SECUNDUM PRAESCIENTIAM DEI PATRIS IN SANCTIFICATIONEM SPIRITUS, IN OBOEDIENTIAM & ASPERSIONEM SANGUINIS IESU CHRISTI.

Ratione status interni felicissimi vocantur electi secundum praescientiam DEI Patris, in sanctificationem Spiritus, in oboedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi. Προσδιορισμὸν κατὰ πρόγνωσιν. Oecumenius secutus Cyrillum lib. de recta fide connectit cum verbis, Apostolus Iesu Christi, ut sit sensus, quod secundum praescientiam DEI Patris sit Apostolus Iesu Christi, sicut PaulusGal. 1. v. 15.se ex utero matris suae segregatum dicit, ut evangelizaret Christum inter gentes, acRom. 1. v. 1.sic loquitur, Paulus servus Iesu Christi vocatus Apostolus segregatus in Evangelium Dei. Sed verba sequentia, in sanctificatione Spiritus, in oboedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi, ostendunt προσδιορισμὸν illum coniungendum esse cum verbo electis, quod faciunt Beda, Lyranus & plerique omnes interpretes, ut sic in textu Graeco h. l. sit quaedam traiectio, cum inter electos secundum praescientiam interseratur advenis dispersis, unde etiam Syrus paraphrastes non sine emphasi illud repetit. v. 2.Qui electi fuerunt in praescientia. ac in versu primo inserit copulativam, Electis & advenis. Electorum nomen accipitur vel de electione aeterna ad salutem, vel de electione temporali quae triplex, ad consortium Ecclesiae, ad communionem renatorum, & ad certum aliquod officium Ecclesiasticum vel politicum. Ratione primae significationis inter eas, qua pro electione temporali accipitur, electi sunt iidem cum vocatis; ratione secundae significationis iidem cum renatis; ratione tertiae significationis iidem cum personis in publico munere, constitutis. Atque haec omnia locum habent, quando nomen electorum de hominibus accipitur, sed in generali significatione etiam tribuitur Christo Esa. 42. v. 1.cap. 43. v. 10.Matth. 12. v. 18. qui dicitur electus DEI servus, tum quia peculiariter est DEO patri dilectus, tum quia in aeterno DEI consilio Mediator & Redemtor generis humani constitutus est. Item sanctis Angelis, 1. Timoth. 5. v. 21. qui dicuntur electi, quia sunt eximii, excellentes, praestantes, DEO dilecti & à malis Angelis separati.

Quia ergo tot modis electorum nomen accipitur, inde Salmeron & alii accipiunt de electione temporali ad consortium Ecclesiae, vel ut ipsi ad verbum DEI audiendum, non ad salutarem verbi auditum. Sed quia electi dicuntur secundum praescientiam DEI patris in sanctificatione Spiritus &c. ex eo manifestum est, nomen electorum hic accipi de electione aeterna ad salutem. Est n. hic locus Apostolicus parallelus loco Paulino 2. Thess. 2. v. 13.Nos debemus gratias agere Deo semper pro vobis, fratres dilecti à Deo, quod elegerit vos Deus ab initio ad salutem in sanctificatione Spiritus & fide veritatis, ubi haec electio notanter dicitur factaεἰς σωτηρίαν & ἄπ᾽ ἀρχῆς i. e. ab aeterno, ante iacta mundi fundamenta, quia principium ibi non intelligitur ἔναρχον sed ἄναρχονMich. 5. v. ult.Hab. 1. v. 12. Codex Regius hoc loco habet, electis κατὰ πρόθεσιν, sicut etiam Rom. 8. v. 28. electi dicuntur κλητοὶ κατὰ πρόθεσιν. Sed reliqui Codices omnes legunt κατὰ πρόγνωσιν, ut sic cum electione πρόγνωσις coniungatur, quod congruit cum loco Apostolico Rom. 8. v. 29.οὓς προέγνω καὶ προώρισε. Per hanc πρόγνωσιν quidam intelligunt aeternum DEI decretum de salvandis electis. 1. Quia ApostolusRom. 11. v. 2.verboπρογινώσκεινin illa significatione uti videtur. Non repulit DEUS plebem suam quam praescivit, id quodv. 7.sic exponitur, electio id consecutu est i. e. electi id assecuti sunt. 2. Quia Petrus in hoc ipso capitev. 20.Christum dicit praecognitum i. e. praeordinatum ante mundi constitutionem.

3. Augustinus in lib. de bono persev. cap. 18. docet, praescientiam, cum in bonis ponitur, esse eandem cum praedestinatione. Inde Erasmus vertit praefinitionem, Lyranus praedestinationem. Sed πρόγνωσις ab ἐκλογῇ hoc loco distinguitur, quod etiam fit in loco parallelo Rom. 8. v. 29. Ergo praescientia non potest praecisè & formaliter accipi de electione. Quod si quis dicere velit, per πρόγνωσιν hîc intelligi non ipsam ἐκλογὴν sed πρόθεσιν iuxta quam facta electio, illi meritò hoc obvertitur, quod πρόγνωσις à προθέσει in articulo de providentia divina distinguatur. Nec potest contrarium ex adductis Scripturae locis demonstrari, quia Rom. 11. v. 2.πρόγνωσις itidem non ponitur absolutè & formaliter pro electione, sed pro praescientia, iuxta quam facta est electio, quae quomodo comparata sit, mox videbimus. Neque Christus à Petro dicitur electus vel praedestinatus electione eâ, quâ credentes in Christum dicuntur praedestinati ad salutem, sed praescitus sive praeordinatus, ut suo loco inferiùs apparebit.

Alii igitur per praescientiam intelligunt specialem DEI dilectionem, inde Estius vertit praedilectionem. Argumenti loco affert illud, quod scire seu cognoscere usitatissimè in Scripturis accipiatur pro diligere, approbare, tanquam suum agnoscere, ergo etiam hoc loco electos dici secundum praescientiam i. e. aeternâ DEI praeordinatione & praedilectione. Atqui quamvis τὸ scire pro notitia approbationis usurpatum, significet idem quod diligere, tamen de praescientia vix occurret exemplum, ubi pro dilectione vel praedilectione usurpetur, cum etiam de malis hominum operibus vox προγνώσεως usurpata extet, Act. 2. v. 23.Πρόγνωσις ergo pro ratione subiectae materiae, quia de electis ad aeternam salutem agitur, significat non solum praevisionem aeternam certorum individuorum & personarum salvandarum, sed etiam ordinationem mediorum, quibus DEUS homines salvare decrevit, quae sunt praedicatio & auditus verbi, institutio & usus Sacramentorum, ac fides ex auditu verbi & usu Sacramentorum haurienda, augenda & conservanda, itemque praescientiam tum fidei ipsius tum μελλόντων πιστεύειν1. Tim. 1. v. 16. Quos enim DEUS ab aeterno praevidit mediis ad salutem à se ordinatis usuros ac per operationem Spiritus sancti in Christum Mediatorem & Salvatorem perseveranter credituros, illos & solos & omnes ad aeternam salutem elegit. Haec explicatio colligitur ex dictis illis Scripturae, quae testantur, intuitum fidei perseverantis ingredi decretum electionis ad salutem. Ergo ut in Christo, ita quoque in fide DEUS nos elegisse dicitur, quia in Christo eligi non potuimus, nisi sub fidei Christum apprehendentis, eiusque beneficia sibi applicantis intuitu. Inde dicitur DEUS elegisse pauperes, divites in fideIac. 2. v. 5. ac fides Christi vocatur fides electorumTit. 1. v. 1. Quos enim DEUS in tempore glorificat & salvat, illos ab aeterno glorificare & salvare constituit. Iam vero solos & omnes perseveranter in Christum credentes DEUS in tempore glorificat & salvat. Ergo solos & omnes perseveranter in Christum credentes, vel ut Apostolus 1. Tim. 1. v. 16. emphaticè loquitur, μέλλοντας πιστεύειν, DEUS ab aeterno glorificare & salvare constituit & per conseq. etiam ad salutem elegit. Aeternae omnino ac immotae veritatis est oraculum illud Apostolicum. Impossibile est DEO placere sine fideHebr. 11. v. 6. cuius pronunciati ratio pendet ex labe originalis peccati, à qua nemo nisi per fidem in Christum liberari potest. Iam vero electi ab aeterno DEO placuerunt & quidem ita placuerunt, ut ad salutem aeternam eos eligeret, qui est summus dilectionis divinae erga homines gradus. Ergo non nisi intuitu fidei in Christum DEO placuerunt & per conseq. non nisi intuitu fidei in Christum sunt electi.

Inde porrò subiungit Apostolus, quod illi, ad quos scribit, electi sint secundùm praescientiam DEI Partis in sanctificationem Spiritus. In Graeco est non εἰς ἁγιασμὸν, sed ἐν ἁγιασμῷin sanctificatione, sicut etiam 2. Thess. 2. v. 13. dicitur: elegit vos DEUS ad salutemέν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, ubi ipsamet vulgata translatio reddidit, in sanctificatione Spiritus. Salmeron exponit de sanctitate passiva, Spiritus nostri, cum voxπνεύματοςnon habeat additum articulum. Idem placet Tossano & aliis. Existimant igitur, his verbis exponi tum electionis finem, quod electio facta sit eo fine, ut essemus sancti & irreprehensibiles coram DEOEph. 1. v. 4.tum electionis signum, quod sanctitati studeant, qui sunt à DEO ad salutem electi.2. Tim. 2. v. 21. Quidam etiam longiùm progrediuntur, quod sanctificatio illa nostri Spiritus i. e. studium sanctitatis sit & medium & meritum aeternae salutis. Estius ambiguus est. Statuit exponi posse vel de Spiritu humano vel de Spiritu divino. Priori modo esse sensum; electis, ut Spiritus vester sanctificetur. Posteriori modo sensum esse, electis per Spiritum sanctum, ut ille vos sanctificet, ac si dixisset, in spiritu sanctificationis, id est, in Spiritu sanctificanteRom 1. v. 4.per speciem quandam hypallages. Sed ex loco parallelo 2. Thess. 2. v. 13. & ex toto huius loci contextu colligitur, per sanctificationem Spiritus non intelligi hoc loco sanctificationem passivam nostri Spiritus, sed sanctificationem activam Spiritus sancti. Praepositio ἐν iuxta usitatum Hebraei sermonis idiotismum ponitur pro διὰ, quo modo etiam Erasmus reddidit, ut sic exprimatur causa instrumentalis salutis, quae est ministerium verbi & Sacramentorum, per quod DEUS fidem in electorum cordibus operatur, sicut Christus dicit Iohan. 17. v. 17.sanctifica eos in veritate, sermo tuus veritas est. Hoc ministerium vocatur sanctificatio Spiritus, quia est ministerium Spiritus 2. Corinth. 3. v. 6. quod DEUS ab aeterno ordinavit, ut esset salutare & efficax medium, per quod homines fide donarentur, inque ea ad salutem conservarentur. Neque vel hoc loco vel 2. Thessal. 2. v. 13. exponitur electionis effectus, qui est nostra per Spiritum S. sanctificatio, ut vult Estius, quem ipsa series Apostolici contextus refellit, cum sanctitas illa Naturae ordine fidem non praecedat sed sequatur. Sed intelligitur medium fidei & sanctificationis nostrae, quod est ministerium verbi & Sacramentorum, per quod DEUS fidem & sanctitatem in cordibus electorum operatur. Cumque ministerium illud Spiritus sancti sit medium salutis ex parte DEI, ideò Petrus ei statim subiungit mediumsalutis ex parte hominum, quando electos nos dicit in obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi. Quidam accipiunt de obedientia Christi activâ i. e. quâ Christus patri suo coelesti oboediens fuit ad mortem usque crucisPhil. 2. v. 9. in quam sententiam etiam Salmeron propendet. Probant hanc expositionem ex eo, quod addatur, & aspersionem sanguinis Christi. Ut ergò intelligitur aspersio sanguinis Christi activa i. e. quâ nos sanguine suo aspergit & mundat, ita quoque intelligi videtur obedientia Christi activa, ut sic & meritum & efficacia, sive quod idem est, & acquisitio & applicatio beneficiorum Christi describatur. Sed hanc expositionem meritò refellit Estius, cum non rectè dicamur electi ad obedientiam, quâ Christus patri suo obedivit, sed potiùs per eam & propter eam. Alii igitur intelligunt de obedientia Christi passivâ i. e. quâ nos Christo oboedimus, quae expositio non solùm probatur Estio, sed etiam Calvino, qui per obedientiam hîc intelligit vitae novitatem. Robur quaeritur huic expositioni ex dictis illis Scripturae, in quibus studium sanctitatis & filialis obedientiae requiritur ab electis. Ut enim creati sumus in Christo Iesu in operibus bonis, quae praeparavit DEUS, ut in illis ambulemusEph. 2. v. 10. ita quoque electi sumus in Christo, ut simus sanctiEphes. 1. v. 4. & in filiali obedientia DEO serviamusLuc. 1. v. 74. Atqui si per sanctificationem Spiritus illud studium sanctitatis & obedientiae intelligi volunt, quomodo per obedientiam illud denuò intelligi potest? Praeterea huic obedientiae subiungitur aspersio sanguinis Christi, quae omnium consensu fit per fidem. Iam vero obedientia filialis non praecedit fidem, sed est eius consequens, oportet enim nos prius fieri DEI filios per fidem, antequam filialem obedientiam ipsi praestemus. Intelligitur ergò nomine obedientiae fides in Christum, quae vocatur etiam alibi obedientia fideiRom. 1. v. 5.Cap. 16. v. 26.obedientia EvangcliiActor. 6. v. 7.Rom. 10. v. 16.obedientia ChristiHebr. 5. v. 9. quae expositio non solùm respondet toti contextui & fidei analogiae, quae unicum medium, per quod oblata in ministerio verbi beneficia Christi apprehendimus, fidem esse docet, sed etiam confirmatur ex loco parallelo 2. Thessal. 2. v. 13. Ut enim ibi media salutis ex parte DEI & ex parte hominum sanctificatio Spiritus & fides veritatis coniunguntur:

ita quoque eodem planè sensu hoc loco electi dicimur in sanctificatione Spiritus, & in obedientiam vel in obedientia sc. fidei; ac sicut Paulus dicto loco fidem illam electorum vocat fidem veritatis vel quia est vera fides, vel quod magis congruit, quia per eam fides habetur veritati Evangelii Marc. 1. v. 14.Actor. 6. v. 7.Rom. 10. v. 16. ita quoque Petrus in hoc ipso capite obedientiam illam vocat obedientiam veritatis, quia per eam veritati obedientia exhibetur. Estius meminit cuiusdam explicationis, per quam προσδιορισμὸς τοῦ αἳματος Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ,ad utrumque membrum referatur in obedientiam sanguinis Christi & aspersionem sanguinis eiusdem. Haec expositio mirificè confirmaret nostram sententiam, quia obedientia sanguinis Christi non potest esse alia, quàm obedientia fidei, quâ verbo Evangelii, in quo beneficia morte & sanguine Christi parta nobis offeruntur, obedimus. Sed quia haec constructio est coactior, ideò rectiùs subintelligimus nomen fidei ex Rom. 1. v. 5. & cap. 16. v. 26. Idem iudicium de illa expositione, cuius itidem Estius meminit, eamque magis probat quàm priorem, quâ προσδιορισμὸς Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ ad utrumque membrum praecedens refertur. In obedientiam Iesu Christi & aspersionem sanguinis eiusdem Iesu Christi, quae expositio itidem à nostra non abluderet, cum Hebr. 5. v. 9.fides dicatur obedientia Christi. Sed non opus est, ut eò descendamus, cum obedientiae nomen etiam absolutè positum iuxta expositionem Paulinam de obedientia fidei rectè accipiatur. Hanc enim sententiam vel maximè confirmat, quod statim subiungitur, & in aspersionem sanguinis Iesu Christi. Per hanc aspersionem sanguinis Christi manifestum est intelligi applicationem beneficiorum morte & sanguine Christi partorum, quae fit per obedientiam illam fidei, sive per fidem, meritum Christi ad iustitiam & remissionem peccatorum sibi applicantem. Quia enim nemo per sanguinem Christi à peccatis mundatur, nisi eo fuerit aspersus i. e. nisi beneficia Christi passione & morte, sive quod idem est effusione sanguinis Christi parta sibi applicet, quae applicatio fit per obedientiam fidei Rom. 3. v. 25.DEUS proposuit Christum propitiatorium per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ideò cum sanctificatione Spiritus Apostolus obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi i. e. fidem, quâ corda nostra CHRISTI sanguine asperguntur & à peccatis mundantur, individuo nexu in negotio electionis & salutis coniungit. Fide enim corda purificanturActor. 15. v. 9.ac sanguis Christi, fide sc. nobis aspersus, emundat conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuisHebr. 9. v. 14. adeoque ab omni peccato nos emundat1. Ioh. 1. v. 7. quâ ratione in phrasi Apostolica occurrit figura, quam vocant ἑνδιαδύο. Respicit autem voculâ aspersionis Apostolus tum ad phraseologian Spiritus Sancti in V. T. Psal. 51. v. 9.asperges me hyssopo & mundabor, (ubi in Hebr. habetur verbum חטאpurificavit, expiavit, peccatum abstulit, sed Chaldaeus rectè per דכי & LXX. per ῥαντίζειν reddiderunt, quia illa expiatio fiebat aspersione sanguinis sacrificiorum.) T. initiatum & credentes à peccatis suis mundantur ac Deo consecrantur, ut velut Spirituales Sacerdotes Apoc. 1. v. 6.Spirituales victimas Deo offerant.Rom. 12. v. 1.

Q. hoc loco 1. Quare electionis statim in Epistolae exordio Petrus mentionem facere voluerit? Resp. quia paulo pòst enumeraturus erat spiritualia beneficia proper Christum in credentes collata, inter quae electio ab aeterno in Christo facta vel maximè eminet.

Q. 2. Unde Apostolus noverat, illos, ad quos scribebat, esse electos? Resp. non à priori ex immediata & peculiari quadam revelatione divina, sed à posteriori, quia vocati erant per Evangelium ad Christi regnum, ac vocationi isti locum dederant credentes in Christum, & fidem suam tum bonorum operum studio tum tolerantiâ persecutionum testatam reddentes.

ἘναντιοΦανείαι 1. Petrus eos, ad quos scribit, vocat electos. At de electione aliorum nemo infallibiliter potest esse certus. Deus novit, qui sunt sui2. Tim. 2. v. 21.Homo videt ea, quae apparent, Dominus autem cor intuetur1. Sam. 16. v. 7. Resp. Petrus aliorum electionem noverat non à priori certitudinaliter, ut loquuntur Scholastici, sed à posteriori probabiliter, non iudicio fidei infallibili, sed iudicio caritatis probabili. Inde cum posteà in cap. 5. v. 12. Sylvanum appellaret fidelem, adiicit προσδιορισμὸν, ὡς λογίζομαι.

2. Petrus eos ad quos scribit, vocat electos. At non omnes ad quos scribit, electi erant. Resp. Ecclesiis, ad quas scribit, electorum elogium competit, non ratione omnium, sed ratione praecipuorum membrorum, perusitatam in Scripturis synecdochen. August. libr. de unit. Eccles. cap. 12. & in libro quem edidit post collationem cum Donatistis cap. 20. Prophetae & Apostoli sic arguere solent reprehensibiles in aliquo populo, qui omnes in aliquo populo arguantur, & sic alloqui laudabiles, qui omnes ibi laudentur.

Ἔλεγχος 1. Electio facta est secundum praescientiam. Ergo non ex absoluto quodam decreto. Ratio consequentiae est, quia praescientia illa respicit fidem in Christum, ut ex collatione locorum parallelorum ostendimus. Contra Calvinianos.

2. Electio facta est secundum praescientiam DEI Patris in sanctificatione Spiritus, in obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi. Ergo non propter merita praevisa. Vis veritatis compulit Estium ut in h. l. sic commentaretur. Electos dicit Apostolus secundum praescientiam, hoc est, aeternâ DEI praedestinatione & dilectione, ut omnis cogitatio meritorum qualiumcunque hanc electionem praevenientium, quae ex parte nostra fingi possunt, excludatur, utque fideles cum gratiarum actione intelligant, se solâ DEI gratia ad salutem esse praedestinatos. Et paulo pòst ad v. 3. sic annotat. Electio non est ex meritis. Salmeron tom. 16. Disp. 1. in Epist. Petri eodem modo. Electio ad finem vitae aeternae possidendum firma est & certa per seipsam & à nostris operibus non pendet.

3. Si aliorum electio potest sciri probabiliter ex iudicio caritatis, multò magis propria electio sciri potest certitudinaliter ex iudicio fidei. Sed illud, teste Petro h. l. & Paulo 1. Thess. 1. v. 4. Ergo.

4. Scriptura peccatorum remissionem & nostri ab illis emundationem constituit in aspersione sanguinis Christi. De aqua lustrali, cuius aspersio in Papatu delicta expurgare creditur, nihil novit.

Έκδίκησις. 1. Calviniani ex hoc loco probare cupiunt, fidem pendere ab electione tanquam à prima causa, cum electi dicamur secundum praescientiam Dei Patris. Piscator in h. l. Sed haec probatio nititur falsâ hypothesi, quod πρόγνωσις significat absolutum decretum.

2. Estius ex hoc loco probare nititur, nostram coram DEO iustitiam non solum in fide & peccatorum remissione, sed etiam in operibus consistere. Obedientiae, inquit, Apostolus addit aspersionem sanguinis Christi i. e. expiationem peccatorum sanguine Christi factam, quae est altera pars nostrae iustificationis, ut innuat, totam nostram iustitiam, quae partim in fide & operatione virtutum, partim in remissione peccatorum consistit, esse divinae electionis. Sed haec probatio nititur falsâ hypothesi, quod per obedientiam intelligatur operatio virtutum, cum de obedientia fidei sit accipienda, quod ipse Estius agnoscit, quando ibidem sic scribit. Vocatur illa remissio peccatorum aspersio sanguinis Christi, quia nemo per Christi sanguinem mundatur à peccatis, nisi eo fuerit aspersus, h. e. nisi per applicatum meritum, quae applicatio fit per obedientiam fidei. Nascitur ex eo tale argumentum. Per quam obedientiam fit applicatio meriti Christi, illa & quidem sola nomine obedientiae ab Apostolo hic intelligitur. Per fidei obedientiam non autem per operationem virtutum fit applicatio meriti Christi. Ergo fidei obedientia & quidem sola nomine obedientiae ab Apostolo hic intelligitur.

3. Photiniani ex hoc loco evincere conantur, electionem factam esse iuxta praevisionem operum: quos enim Deus praevidit rectè usuros libero arbitrio & in praeceptis Christi pro virili in omni vita ambulaturos, illos dicunt ad vitam aeternam electos & ideo quidem electos, quia Christum sint recepturi & eius mandatis obtemperaturi. Catech. Racov. p. 295. Socin. in comm. 1. Ioh. 1. vult per obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi nihil aliud intelligi, quam iustos electos fuisse à Deo, ut Iesu Christi foederis essent participes, & ita obedientia vitam aeternam consequerentur. At 1. connexa quidem sunt in foedus recipi & in symbolum seu confirmationem illius sanguine aspergi Ex. 24. v. 8.Heb. 9. v. 20. sed ex eo inferri nequit, ipsam aspersionem sanguinis significare receptionem in foedus. 2. Peccat Socinus, rationem foederis tantum quaerens in demonstratione exemplari, exclusa Christi satisfactione.

4. Iidem ex hoc loco evincere cupiunt, fidem iustificantem consistere in fiducia & in nova obedientia. Utraque probatio nititur falsâ hypothesi, quod obedientiae nomine intelligatur obedientia vitae sanctae, cum de fidei obedientia Apostolus loquatur.

5. Salmeron in h. l. sic scribit. Aspergitur sanguis Christi super nos, cum in Missae sacrificio offertur pro vivis & mortuis. Sed sanguinis aspersione, quae fit per verbum & Sacramenta, quae sunt media δοτικὰ, ac per fidem, quae est medium ληπτικὸν, Apostolus hîc loquitur; de aspersione, quae fiat per oblationem pro vivis & mortuis, nihil in Scripturis habemus.

6. Piscator ex h. l. evincere cupit, sanguinem Christi cum sensu irae divinae effusum, adeoque solam obedientiam Christi passivam esse illud, quod coram DEI iudicio nobis ad iustitiam imputatur. Sed unius inclusio non est alterius exclusio. Scriptura ideò praecipuè sanguinis i. e. passionis & mortis Christi mentionem facit, quia passio & mors fuit summus obedientiae DEO praestitae gradus.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Electio facta est secundùm praescientiam DEI Patris in sanctificatione Spiritus, in obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Christi. Ergo electionis nostrae fundamentum est gratia DEI in merito Christi fundata, per ministerium verbi & Sacramentorum nobis oblata, fide à nobis apprehensa.

2. Electio facta est in sanctificatione Spiritus. Ergo ministerium verbi, quod est ministerium Spiritus, magni aestimandum, quippe per quod Spir. S. fidem electorum in nobis vult accendere, augere & conservare.

3. Fidei, in qua electi sumus, & per quam iustificamur & salvamur, principium est gratia DEI eligentis; forma consistit in obedientia non legali sed Evangelica, non operum sed notitiae, assensus ac fiducialis apprehensionis; medium est ministerium Spiritus; fructus & effectus remissio peccatorum.

4. Deo patri tribuitur praescientia, Christo aspersio sanguinis, Spiritui S. sanctificatio i. e. ministerium verbi. Habemus ergo insinuatum Trinitatis mysterium. Deus Pater salutem nobis donat per gratuitam electionem; Filius eam promeretur per sanguinis effusionem; Spiritus S. beneficia illa Filii applicat per Evangelii praedicationem.

5. Aspersio sanguinis Ceremonialis in V. T. fuit figura spiritualis aspersionis in N. T. per quam sanguis Christi in verbo & Sacramentis, velut salutaribus aspergillis divinitus ordinatis, in nos respergitur. Qui ab hac aspersione sese subtrahit, à peccatorum suorum immundicie purgari nequit.

6. Fidei obedientia respicit aspersionem sanguinis Christi i. e. verbum Evangelii, in quo beneficia passione & morte Christi parta nobis offeruntur, quod est proprium & adaequatum fidei iustificantis obiectum. Ac vicissim aspersio sanguinis Christi requirit fidem. Hebr. 4. v. 2.

Inscriptioni subiungitur salutatio.

GRATIA VOBIS & PAX MULTIPLICETUR, Χάρις ὐμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πλῃθυνθείη.

Πληθυνθῆναι significat multiplicari, dilatari, incrementum largissimum capere, adimpleri, ut sic tum de multiplicatione in quantitate discreta, tum de augmento in quantitate continua accipiatur. Matth. 24. v. 12.Act. 6. v. 1. & 7.c. 7. v. 17.c. 9. v. 31.c. 12. v. 24.2. Cor. 9. v. 10.2. Petr. 1. v. 2. inde quidam reddunt, multiplicetur, quidam vero impleatur. Similis salutatio extat in Epist. Iudae v. 2.Misericordia vobis & pax & caritasπληθυνθείη, ubi Latina versio reddidit, adimpleatur, cum hoc loco reddiderit multiplicetur. In Epistolis Paulinis ferè omnibus gratia & pax in salutatione iisdem praemissa coniunguntur, omisso verbo πληθυνθείη, & addito gratiae & pacis, tum principio, tum merito. Gratia vobis & pax à DEO patre nostro & Domino Iesu ChristoRom. 1. v. 1.1. Cor. 1. v. 3. &c. ex quo apparet, hanc salutandi formam esse Apostolicam. De Dario quidem Dan. 6. v. 25. legitur, quòd in exordio literarum Regiarum usus fuerit hac salutandi formula. Pax vobis multiplicetur. Sed ea ab hac Apostolica plurimûm variat, ut ex eiusdem explicatione manifestum erit. Per gratiam quidam μετωνυμικῶς intelligunt beneficia ex gratia collata, ad aeternam hominis salutem directa, qualia sunt fides, spes, caritas, ac reliquae virtutes, Itemque per severantia in bonis operibus. Sed rectiùs intelligitur sons illorum beneficiorum omnium, videlicet favor DEI gratuitus, quo in Christo nos complectitur peccata nobis remittens, ex gratia nos iustificans & salvans. Nam 1. in loco parallelo Iudae v. 2.χάρις exponitur per τὸ ἔλεος. 2. Petrus ipse v. 13. huius capitis dicit, gratiam illam offerri in verbo Evangelii, in quo DEUS paternum suum favorem, peccatorum remissionem, iustitiam & vitam aeternam credentibus offert. 3. Pax in hac salutatione à gratiâ distinguitur tanquam fructus & effectus à sua causa. Nomine pacis Hebraei solent omnem felicitatem & prosperitatem complecti, Gen. 43. v. 27.Psal. 119. v. 165.Ierem. 29. v. 7. inde quidam statuunt, per pacem in genere hîc accipi quaevis beneficia corporalia & spiritualia, temporalia & aeterna. Lyranus gratiam à pace sic distinguit, ut gratiam ad praesentem, pacem ad futuram vitam referat. Sed in salutatione Christi Luc. 24. v. 36.Iohan. 20. v. 19. & 21. ac Pauli Apostoli Rom. 1. v. 7.1. Cor. 1. v. 3. &c. pacis nomine intelligitur praecipuum illud gratiae divinae beneficium, quod iustificati fide pacem habemus ad DeumRom. 5. v. 1.quae est pax in DEO & cum DEO. Celebrat igitur Petrus singulare illud Evangelii beneficium, quòd in eo DEI gratia propter Christum Mediatorem offeratur, ut in posterum quietam & tranquillam conscientiam habeamus, utpote DEO per Christum reconciliati, ac precatur horum bonorum conservationem & augmentum.

Q. Quare Apostolus gratiae & pacis multiplicationem illis, ad quos scribit, precetur? Resp. 1. Quia quamvis & gratiae & pacis participes facti essent, tamen bona illa nondum erant perfecta, sed opus erat eorum quotidiano incremento. 2. Quia non possidebant ea immutabiliter, sed poterant ea in hac vita iterum auferri.

ἘναντιοΦανίαGratia vobis multiplicetur. At paternus ille DEI favor, quo nos in Christo complectitur, non multiplicatur, sed idem semper manet. Resp. sicut caritas Dei dicitur effundi in corda nostra per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis,Rom. 5. v. 5. tum quia sensus, illius caritatis in cordibus nostris effusus est, sentimus enim nos â DEO diligi, & gustamus, quàm bonus sit Domivus: tum quia effectus huius caritatis, videlicet donatio Spiritus sancti, in corda nostra effunditur: ita quoque gratia DEI multiplicari dicitur, quando πληροφορία de DEI gratia, bonitate & misericordia, quâ nos in Christo complectitur, augetur, ut in gratia illa DEI magis magisque roborati stemus, ac quando dona ex gratia in nos collata augentur & multiplicantur.

Ἐλεγχος Petrus gratiam & pacem in cordibus credentium multiplicari precatur, h. e. efficacem & intimum divinae gratiae sensum ac pacem conscientiae ipsis optat. Papa de remissione peccatorum & gratia DEI dubitare iubet, quae dubitatio conscientiae paci & sensui divinae gratiae è diametro adversatur.

Ἐκδίκησις. Baronius Anno Christi 45. n. 27. occasione ex hac Petrina salutatione accepta, de benedictione Rom. Pont. quam Apostolicam vocare solent, sic disserit. Quod Petrus Apostolus in fine Epistolae primae, sicut & in exordio eius, gratiam impertiendo salutet, sicut in secunda etiam Epistola fecisse constat, & quod insuper eadem secunda etiam Epistola fecisse constat, & quod insuper eadem salutatione utatur saepè Apostolus Paulus &c. quodque etiam Iohannes eadem salutatione utatur, planè significatur, Apostolorum exemplo in Ecclesiam introductum, ut in Apostolicis literis gratia salutando impartiatur. n. 28. Ex Apostolica igitur traditione & exemplo manavit, ut Romanus Pontifex Apostolicis literis quempiam salutando unà cum Apostolica benedictione gratiam impartiatur. Resp. 1. Gratiae & pacis adprecationem in Epistolis Pontificis Romani praemitti, in se ac per se nemo nostrûm improbat. 2. Hoc vero improbamus, quod sibi ut successori Petri hoc peculiariter competere autumat, cum sit omnibus Episcopis, utpote Apostolorum successoribus commune, gratiam & pacem fidelibus precari. Baronius ipse d. 1. fatetur, Ignatium in Epistola ad Ephes. & caeteros post eum Episcopos Antiochenos eadem salutationis formulâ fuisse usos. Sicut etiam non solus Petrus, sed etiam reliqui Apostoli Paulus, Iacobus & Iudas hac salutationis formâ utuntur. Iam vero non in sede Antiochena, sed in Romana Petri successores unicè quaerunt. 3. Benedictioni huic Pontificiae peculiaris quaedam efficacia ex opere operato adscribitur. Quod si enim benedictio Episcopi, tunsio pectoris, aspersio aquae benedictae &c. sine quocunque alio bono motu sufficit ad venialia remittenda, docente Francisco à Victoria summ. Sacr. poenit. n. 100. p. 63. quantò maior vis ex ipsorum hypothesi erit in Pontificis benedictione, qui omnium Episcoporum caput.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Sine gratia Christi ad pacem reconciliationis nunquam venitur, ideò gratia & pax in salutatione Apostolica ita coniunguntur, ut gratia paci praemittatur. Beda in h. l.

2. Iudaei hodiè in pacis nomine appellant, & retrò in Scripturis sic salutabant. Sed intelligo illum (Apostolum) defendisse officio suo praedicationem creatoris. Quàm maturi pedes evangelizantium bona, Evangelizantium pacem. Evangelizator enim bonorum, i. e. gratiae DEI paci eam praeferendam sciebat. Tertull. lib. 5. adv. Marc. cap. 5. Sensus est, quòd usque ad Christi ascensionem pacis tantùm verbo aliquem salutare moris fuerit, ut in antiquo Testamento plura exempla suppetunt, ut Gen. 43.Iud. 6. & 9.1. Reg. 25.1. Paral. 12.Tob. 12. & in novo de Christo, qui eodem pacis nomine salutare consuevit discipulos Luc. 24.Ioh. 14. & 20. quos ut eodem etiam modo, cum in alienas domos introirent, in eis agentes salutarent, admonuit Marc. 10.Luc. 10. Sed eidem pacis nomine salutationi Apostoli & gratiam addiderunt, imò & praemiserunt, quod videlicet tam sublimis gratiae, restitutae per Christum generationi humanae, annunciatores essent. Baron. d. l.

3. Summa totius Evangelii continetur in hac salutatione Apostolica. In Evangelio enim offertur nobis DEI gratia in Christo ac propter Christum, quam qui fide recipit, pacem ad DEUM, in DEO & cum DEO obtinet.

4. Non sufficit, gratiae divinae & pacis semel participem esse factum, sed conservatione & quotidiano opus est incremento.

5. Inde sancti sibi mutuò precantur donorum spiritualium augmentum.Rom. 1. v. 11.Eph. 1. v. 17.Phil. 1. v. 9.

6. Quòd si aliis bonorum spiritualium incrementum precari debemus, multò magis ad Deum quotidie ingemiscere oportet, ut, quod in nobis coepit opus bonum, perficiat usque in diem Christi Iesu.Psal. 68. v. 29.Phil. 1. v. 6.

## 1:2-4 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place 1. Why the Apostle begins the commemoration of divine benefits from εὐλογία? Resp. This εὐλογία could indeed be referred to the principal scope of the Apostle, on account of which he instituted that commemoration of divine benefits, in this sense.

Because GOD is to be celebrated on account of the benefits bestowed upon us, therefore you ought to persist constant in the truth acknowledged, for GOD is to be celebrated not only by words, but also by deeds, and consequently also by constancy in the truth of the Gospel. But it is more correctly said that the Apostle wished to demonstrate the salutary use of the commemoration instituted by him by this very εὐλογίᾳ, namely, that he might commend to us the magnitude of those benefits, and by his own example excite us to praise and celebrate GOD for this reason.

Q. 2. Why in this very εὐλογίᾳ does he call God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ? Resp. that he may intimate that He, who from eternity was and is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ by Nature, on account of the eternal generation of the Son from the essence of the Father, willed out of ineffable mercy in time to have us as sons by grace, or by gratuitous adoption into sons and heirs, which benefit Christ merited for us. For He, since He is in the unity of person the natural and only-begotten Son of GOD, gave power to become sons of GOD to those who believe in Him John 1. v. 12. so that the same one, who is the Father of Jesus Christ, is also our Father, of Christ indeed by the Nature of eternal generation, but of us by the grace of regeneration, whence the Apostle immediately adds: Blessed be the GOD and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has regenerated us.

Q. 3. In what sense is that hope, to which GOD is said to have regenerated us, called living? Resp. 1. By reason of the object, because it is borne toward the living GOD, and toward Christ, who is eternal life. 1 John 5. v. 20. 2. By reason of the effect, because that hope vivifies the heart, i.e., fills it with spiritual joy, and faith, apprehending Christ the true life, makes us participants of spiritual life. Hab. 2. v. 4. Rom. 1. v. 17. Gal. 3. v. 11. 3. By reason of the adjunct. Human hope is σκιᾶς ὂναρ, is κενὴ vain and empty Wis. 3. v. 11. since it is about vain and transitory things, but the hope into which GOD regenerates us is living and solid, leaning upon a firm foundation, which therefore does not disappoint Rom. 5. v. 5. 4. By reason of the contrary. Faith, through which we are regenerated, is not something dead and ineffective, but living and effective through charity Gal. 5. v. 6. James 2. v. last.

Ἐναντιοφανία. Blessed be God, and the Father of our Lord Jesus C. who has regenerated us. But regeneration is a benefit of the Holy Spirit. Tit. 3. v. 5? Resp. the works of the Trinity to the outside are common to all three persons of the Deity, the order and distinction of the persons being nevertheless preserved. The named person being therefore one, the remaining two are not excluded, but rather included. For the true GOD, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, has revealed himself in such a way that the Holy Spirit proceeds from him and from the Son from eternity, to whom the benefit of regeneration and sanctification is peculiarly attributed.

Ἔλεγχος 1. No one else is the true GOD, than he who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has revealed himself in his word in such a way that from eternity he begat the Son, who in the fullness of time assumed human Nature, in it performed the work of redemption and reconciled us to GOD his Father. As many therefore as are destitute of the knowledge of the Son, are destitute also of the knowledge of the true GOD, John 17. v. 3.1. John 2. v. 23. This is to be opposed to those who ascribe to the more sound Gentiles the true knowledge of the true GOD and salvation.

2. Peter in regeneration uniquely preaches the great mercy of GOD. The Pope teaches that merits of congruity and proper dispositions concur toward our regeneration. Estius in this place Merits are not here simply excluded from the business of salvation, but even the merits themselves are credited to the grace and mercy of the choosing GOD. And yet the grace of GOD and our merits in the business of election, justification and salvation are not subordinated, but opposed. If by grace, then it is no longer of worksRom. 11. v. 6. GOD chose us, that we might be holy, not because we were holyEph. 1. v. 4. he justifies us by faith freely without worksRom. 3. vers. 24. and eternal life is χάρισμα a gratuitous gift of GODRom. 6. last vers.

3. Peter calls that hope, to which GOD regenerates us, living, because it suffuses the heart with vivifying joy. The Pope commands one to doubt concerning the grace of GOD, which doubt cannot consist with that vivifying joy.

4. Peter calls eternal life an inheritance, because it falls to the faithful, who are adopted as sons of GOD by grace, without their own merit. The Pope teaches that eternal life is the merit of our works.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Salmeron in this place Faith and hope, if charity is not present, which makes them and the faithful themselves who have them live, and makes them worthy of the crown of eternal glory, are altogether dead. Resp. Charity is never separated from true and living faith, meanwhile that charity is not the form or life of faith, but its consequent and effect, for faith works i.e. shows itself living and efficacious through charity Gal. 5. v. 6. just as respiration in the body it is a sign and effect of natural life James 2. v. last Christ is the life of faith, because faith apprehending Christ, has eternal life in Christ 1. John 5. v. 20. charity and works testify of the life of faith. 2. Estius in this place asserts that our regeneration is attributed to the resurrection of Christ thence and therefore, because Christ by his own resurrection presents to us a type of rising again to newness of life. Resp. in the same sense and respect that Paul Rom. 4. v. 25. attributes our justification before GOD to the resurrection of Christ, in the same sense and respect Peter in this place attributes our regeneration to the same, as is evident. But that comes to pass. 1. in respect of manifestation, demonstration, and confirmation, because the resurrection of Christ is an evident testimony that satisfaction has been fully made for our sins, and perfect righteousness brought in, whence Jerome in comm. Rom. 4. says: that Christ rose again for this reason, that he might confirm righteousness to those who believe. 2. in respect of application. Christ raised from the dead, ascended into heaven, and sat at the right hand of GOD, that he might offer to the world the benefits obtained by his passion and death through the word of the Gospel, and apply them to believers, and by this reason justify and save them. In respect of this application, Toletus in comm. Rom. 4. 3. acknowledges that Christ is said to have risen again for our justification, in respect of actual absolution from sin. The resurrection of Christ is not only an evident testimony of the full and perfect righteousness acquired by the merit of Christ, but it is also an actual absolution from sins for those who believe in him, who died for our sins, and was raised again for our justification. For just as the heavenly Father, by delivering Christ to death for our sins, condemned sin in his flesh concerning sin, Romans 8. vers. 3. and thus punished our sins in Christ, which were imposed and imputed to him as a sponsor: so also by raising him from the dead, he ipso facto absolved him from our sins imputed to him, and consequently also absolved us in him, so that thus the resurrection of Christ is both the cause and pledge and complement of our justification. Although therefore it is rightly said in its place that the resurrection of Christ is a type and figure of our spiritual resurrection from the death of sin Rom. 6. v. 4. yet neither Paul Rom. 4. v. 25. nor Peter in this place deal with it properly, because both are occupied there in celebrating the benefits of Christ, given and applied to us through faith, but not in an exhortation to the pursuit of piety and new obedience, to which they descend only in the following. We do not deny, That the resurrection of Christ is not only an example and figure but also the cause of our renewal, just as the death of Christ is not only an example of spiritual mortification, but also the efficient cause of the same 2. Cor. 4. v. 12., it cannot be inferred from this that our justification consists formally in that renewal, because distinct benefits must be discussed distinctly; otherwise it could be inferred that our justification also consists in the resurrection of our bodies to eternal life, since that too is a benefit of the resurrection of Christ.

3. Piscator, from the fact that our inheritance is said to be kept for us in the heavens, concludes that heaven is not everywhere. Resp. It is said to be kept in the heavens because it is a heavenly inheritance. Furthermore, that no one of us says that the heaven of the blessed, that is, ποῦ that in which GOD manifests his glory to the blessed, is everywhere, but we say that that majestic heaven, in which GOD is said to dwell, is included in no place, and is excluded from no place.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. As often as the recollection of divine benefits arises in our heart, so often let the praise of GOD burst forth from our mouth.

2. GOD is εὐλογητὸς in himself, because he is good, all-wise, omnipotent, therefore also to be blessed and praised by us.

3. Man blesses man in one way, man blesses GOD in another, and GOD blesses man in another. Man blesses man by praying for any favorable things for him. Man blesses GOD by praising and glorifying GOD. GOD blesses man by heaping every kind of good upon him.

4. The devil made us children of wrath and guilty of eternal death through envy; GOD regenerated us into his children through his mercy.

5. Christ regenerates us through his resurrection, because by the resurrection of Christ all his merits were sealed, and because Christ was therefore raised from the dead, ascended into the heavens, and sat down at the right hand of GOD, so that he might apply to us through faith the benefits obtained by his passion and death.

6. Regeneration is twofold. The former takes place in this life, the latter on the day of judgment. Peter speaks in this place of the former, which takes place both through Baptism John 3. v. 5.Titus 3. v. 5. then through the word. 1. Peter 1. v. 23.James 1. v. 18. Christ speaks of the latter Matthew 19. v. 28. August. book 20 de Civ. Dei chap. 5. That he says in regeneration, he undoubtedly wished the resurrection of the dead to be understood by the name of regeneration. For thus our flesh will be regenerated through incorruption, just as our soul has been regenerated through faith.

7. From the faith of the resurrection of Christ arises a living hope, because Christ rose again for our justificationRomans 4. v. 23. and merited for us a resurrection to a blessed life.

8. That hope is living, because it enlivens the heart and affects it with spiritual joy Romans 14. v. 17. In those, however, in whose hearts Christ raised from the dead does not yet live through faith, they are dead in sins, and destitute of enlivening consolation.

9. Although the providence of GOD is concerned with the whole human race, it is nevertheless occupied particularly with the elect, for whom God has prepared a most ample inheritance from eternity.

10. That inheritance is incorruptible in itself; it is undefiled by another; it is unfading in time. It is incorruptible, because it never fails; so that it is touched neither by old age, nor by disease, nor by any other sadness. It is undefiled, because it receives nothing unclean. It is unfading, because not even in the very minds of the blessed is that heavenly conversation able to become cheapened by long use. John Huss in this place.

11. That inheritance is heavenly. Therefore it is not transitory like earthly inheritances, which pass from one to another. It is heavenly. Therefore it is not divided but whole, that inheritance is one for all and total for each. O excellent inheritance not to be obtained by the death of fathers, nor by the succession of sons, not to be divided between brothers and sisters, not narrower by the multitude of heirs, because its participation is into the same thing, not insufficient, but filled with all good things.

12. That inheritance is kept for us in the heavens. Therefore let us forget those things which are behind in these landsPhilippians 3. v. 14. seeking those things which are aboveColossians 3. v. 1.

13. If it happens that we are deprived of an earthly inheritance, let us console ourselves with the inheritance stored up in the heavens.

Latin:

Quaeritur h. l. 1. Quare Apostolus commemorationem divinorum beneficiorum ordiatur abεὐλογία? Resp. posset quidem haec εὐλογία referri ad principalem Apostoli scopum, propter quem illam divinorum beneficiorum commemorationem instituit, hoc sensu.

Quia DEUS ob beneficia in nos collata celebrandus, ideò in veritate agnita debetis constantes persistere, DEUS enim non solùm verbis, sed etiam factis, ac proinde etiam constantiâ in veritate Evangelii celebrandus. Sed rectiùs dicitur, quòd Apostolus salutarem usum commemorationis à se institutae hac ipsâ εὐλογίᾳ demonstrare voluerit, videlicet ut magnitudinem istorum beneficiorum nobis commendaret, suoque exemplo ad DEUM hoc nominis laudandum ac celebrandum nos excitaret.

Q. 2. Quare in hac ipsaεὐλογίᾳDeum vocet Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi? Resp. ut innuat, eum, qui ab aeterno fuit, & est Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi per Naturam, propter aeternam Filii ex Patris essentia generationem, ex ineffabili misericordia in tempore nos filios habere voluisse per gratiam, sive per gratuitam in filios & haeredes adoptionem, quod beneficium Christus nobis promeruit. Is enim, cum in personae unitate sit Filius DEI naturalis & unigenitus, potestatem dedit filios DEI fieri his, qui credunt in ipsum Ioh. 1. v. 12. ut idem, qui est Pater Iesu Christi, sit etiam noster Pater, Christi quidem, per Naturam aeternae generationis, noster verò per gratiam regenerationis, unde statim subiicit Apostolus. Benedictus DEUS & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui regeneravit nos.

Q. 3. Quo sensu spes illa, ad quam DEUS nos regenerâsse dicitur, vocetur viva? Resp. 1. Ratione obiecti, quia fertur in DEUM vivum, & in Christum, qui est vita aeterna.1. Ioh. 5. v. 20. 2. Ratione effecti, quia spes illa cor vivificat, h. e. spirituali gaudio perfundit, ac fides Christum veram vitam apprehendens vitae spiritualis participes nos facit. Hab. 2. v. 4.Rom. 1. v. 17.Gal. 3. v. 11. 3. Ratione adiuncti. Spes humana est σκιᾶς ὂναρ, est κενὴinanis & vacuaSap. 3. v. 11. cùm sit de rebus vanis ac transitoriis, sed spes, in quam DEUS nos regenerat, est viva & folida, firmo innixa fundamento, quae proinde non confundit Rom. 5. v. 5. 4. Ratione contrarii. Fides, per quam regeneramur, non est mortuum quid & inefficax, sed viva & efficax per caritatem Gal. 5. v. 6.Iacob. 2. v. ult.

Ἐναντιοφανία.Benedictus Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Iesu C. qui regeneravit nos. At regeneratio est beneficium Spiritus S.Tit. 3. v. 5? Resp. opera Trinitatis ad extra sunt omnibus tribus Deitatis personis communia, servato tamen ordine & discrimine personarum. Nominata ergò una persona, reliquae duae non excluduntur, sed potiùs includuntur. Verus enim DEUS, qui est Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, sese sic patefecit, quòd ab illo & à Filio ab aeterno procedat Spiritus sanctus, cui regenerationis & sanctificationis beneficium peculiariter attribuitur.

Ἔλεγχος 1. Nullus alius est verus DEUS, quàm qui est Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui se in verbo suo sic patefecit, quòd ab aeterno genuerit Filium, qui in plenitudine temporis humanam Naturam assumsit, in ea opus redemtionis praestitit ac DEO Patri suo nos reconciliavit. Quotquot ergò destituuntur cognitione Filii, destituuntur etiam cognitione veri DEI, Iohan. 17. v. 3.1. Ioh. 2. v. 23. Opponendum hoc illis, qui gentilibus sanioribus veram veri DEI cognitionem & salutem adscribunt.

2. Petrus in regeneratione unicè praedicat magnam DEI misericordiam. Papa ad nostram regenerationem merita congrui, & dispositiones proprias docet concurrere. Estius in h. l. Non hîc à negotio salutis simpliciter excluduntur merita, sed ipsa etiam merita gratiae & misericordiae DEI eligentis accepta feruntur. Atqui gratia DEI & merita nostra in negotio electionis, iustificationis & salutis non sunt subordinata, sed opposita. Si ex gratia, iam non ex operibusRom. 11. v. 6.Elegit nos DEUS, ut essemus sancti, non quia eramus sanctiEph. 1. v. 4.iustificat nos fide gratis sine operibusRom. 3. vers. 24.ac vita aeterna estχάρισμαgratuitum DEI donumRom. 6. vers. ult.

3. Petrus spem illam, ad quam DEUS nos regenerat, vocat vivam, quia vivifico gaudio cor perfundit. Papa de gratia DEI iubet dubitare, quae dubitatio cum vivifico illo gaudio consistere nequit.

4. Petrus vitam aeternam vocat haereditatem, quia fidelibus in filios DEI ex gratia adoptatis sine ipsorum merito obtingit. Papa docet, vitam aeternam esse operum nostrorum meritum.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Salmeron in h. l. Fides & spes, si caritas non adsit, quae illas & ipsos fideles habentes vivere faciat, & aeternae gloriae coronâ dignos efficiat, mortuae sunt prorsus. Resp. caritas à vera & viva fide nunquam est separata, interim caritas illa non est fidei forma vel vita, sed eius consequens & effectum, fides enim operatur i. e. vivam & efficacem se demonstrat per caritatem Gal. 5. v. 6. sicut respiratio in corpore signum & effectum est vitae naturalis Iac. 2. v. ult. Christus est vita fidei, quia fides Christum apprehendens, in Christo habet vitam aeternam 1. Ioh. 5. v. 20. caritas & opera de fidei vita testantur. 2. Estius in h. l. resurrectioni Christi inde atque ideò regenerationem nostram tribui asserit, quia Christus suâ resurrectione nobis typum praefert resurgendi ad vitae novitatem. Resp. quo sensu ac respectu Paulus Rom. 4. v. 25. resurrectioni Christi tribuit nostram coram DEO iustificationem, eodem sensu ac respectu Petrus hoc loco eidem tribuit nostram regenerationem, ut constat. Fit autem illud. 1. respectu manifestationis, demonstrationis ac confirmationis, quia resurrectio Christi est evidens testimonium, quod pro peccatis nostris plenè satisfactum, & iustitia perfecta adducta, unde Hieron. in comm. Rom. 4. dicit: Christum ideò resurrexisse, ut credentibus iustitiam confirmaret. 2. respectu applicationis. Christus ex mortuis suscitatus, ascendit in coelum, & consedit ad dextram DEI, ut beneficia passione ac morte sua parta, per verbum Evangelii mundo offerret, & credentibus applicaret, atque hac ratione eos iustificaret & salvaret. Respectu huius applicationis, Christum dici propter nostram iustificationem resurrexisse, agnoscit Toletus in comm. Rom. 4. 3. respectu actualis à peccato absolutionis. Christi resurrectio non tantùm est evidens testimonium plenae & perfectae iustitiae Christi merito acquisitae, sed etiam est actualis absolutio à peccatis illis, qui credunt in ipsum, pro peccatis nostris mortuum, & propter iustificationem nostram resuscitatum. Ut enim Pater coelestis Christum propter peccata nostra in mortem tradendo, in carne ipsius de peccato damnavit peccatum, Roman. 8. vers. 3. sicque punivit peccata nostra in Christo, quae ipsi ut sponsori erant imposita atque imputata: ita quoque excitando eum à mortuis, ipso facto absolvit eum à peccatis nostris ipsi imputatis, ac proinde etiam nos in eo absolvit, ut sic Christi resurrectio nostrae iustificationis sit & causa & pignus & complementum. Quamvis ergò suo loco rectè dicatur, Christi resurrectionem esse typum & figuram spiritualis nostrae resurrectionis ex morte peccati Rom. 6. v. 4. de eo tamen nec Paulus Rom. 4. v. 25. nec Petrus hoc loco propriè agunt, quia uterque ibi versatur in celebrandis Christi beneficiis, per fidem nobis donatis & applicatis, non autem in exhortatione ad studium pietatis & novae obedientiae, ad quam in sequentibus demum descendunt. Non negamus, Christi resurrectionem esse non solùm exemplar & figuram sed etiam causam nostrae renovationis, sicut mors Christi non solùm est exemplar spiritualis mortificationis, sed eiusdem etiam causa efficiens 2. Cor. 4. v. 12. vertim ex eo inferri nequit, iustificationem nostram in illa renovatione formaliter consistere, quia de distinctis beneficiis distinctè est disserendum, aliàs inferri posset, etiam in corporum nostrorum ad vitam aeternam resurrectione nostram iustificationem consistere, cum illa quoque sit resurrectionis Christi beneficium.

3. Piscator ex eo, quod haereditas nostra in coelis nobis servari dicitur, colligit, coelum non esse ubique. Resp. dicitur in coelis servari, quia est coelestis haereditas. Porrò coelum beatorum, h. e. ποῦ illud, in quo DEUS gloriam suam beatis manifestat, esse ubique, nemo nostrûm dicit, sed coelum illud maiestaticum, in quo DEUS habitare dicitur, nulli loco inclusum, à nullo loco esse exclusum dicimus.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Quoties in corde nostro exurgit divinorum beneficiorum rec. datio, toties ex ore nostro erumpat DEI laudatio.

2. DEUS est εὐλογητὸς in se, quia bonus, omnisapiens, omnipotens, ergò etiam à nobis benedicendus ac laudandus.

3. Aliter homo homini, aliter homo DEO, aliter DEUS homini benedicit. Homo homini benedicit, quaevis fausta ipsi adprecando. Homo DEO benedicit, DEUM laudando & glorificando. DEUS homini benedicit, omni bonorum genere ipsum cumulando.

4. Diabolus fecit nos irae filios, & mortis aeternae reos per invidiam, DEUS nos in filios fuos regeneravit per suam misericordiam.

5. Christus per resurrectionem suam nos regenerat, quia resurrectione Christi omnia ipsius merita obsignata, & quia Christus ideò ex mortuis suscitatus, in coelos ascendit, & ad dextram DEI consedit, ut beneficia passione & morte suâ parta per fidem nobis applicaret.

6. Duplex est regeneratio. Prior fit in hac vita, posterior in die iudicii. De priore hoc loco Petrus loquitur, quae fit tum per Baptismum Ioh. 3. v. 5.Tit. 3. v. 5. tùm per verbum. 1. Petr. 1. v. 23.Iac. 1. v. 18. De posteriore loquitur Christus Matth. 19. v. 28. August. lib. 20. de Civ. Dei cap. 5. Quod ait in regeneratione, procul dubio mortuorum resurrectionem nomine voluit regenerationis intelligi. Sic enim caro nostra regenerabitur per incorruptionem, quemadmodum est anima nostra regenerata per fidem.

7. Ex fide resurrectionis Christi oritur spes viva, quia Christus propter nostram iustificationem resurrexitRom. 4. v. 23. nobisque beatam ad vitam resurrectionem promeruit.

8. Spes illa est viva, quia cor vivificat & spirituali gaudio afficit Rom. 14. v. 17. In quorum autem cordibus Christus ex mortuis resuscitatus nondum vivit per fidem, illi sunt in peccatis mortui, & vivificâ consolatione destituti.

9. Quamvis providentia DEI versetur circa totum genus humanum, peculiariter tamen circa electos occupata est, quibus Deus ab aeterno haereditatem amplissimam paravit.

10. Haereditas illa est incorruptibilis à se; est incontaminata ab alio; est immarcescibilis tempore. Est incorruptibilis, quia nunquam deficit; ut nec senio, nec morbo, nec alia moestitia tangatur. Est incontaminata, quia nihil immundum recipit. Est immarcescibilis, quia nec in ipsis beatorum mentibus ex longo usu coelestis illa conversatio valet aliquando vilescere. Ioh. Huss. in h. l.

11. Haereditas illa coelestis est. Ergo non transitoria sicut haereditates terrenae, quae transeunt ab uno ad alium. coelestis est. Ergo non divisa sed integra, haereditas illa est omnibus una & singulis tota. O praeclara haereditas non decessu patrum, nec successu filiorum obtinenda, non inter fratres & sorores dividenda, non angustior multitudine haeredum, quia participatio eius in id ipsum, non insufficiens, sed omnibus bonis repleta.

12. In coelis haereditas illa nobis servatur. Ergo obliviscamur eorum quae retrò sunt in his terrisPhil. 3. v. 14.quaerentes ea quae sursum suntCol. 3. v. 1.

13. Si contigat, nos privari haereditate terrena, solemur nos haereditate in coelis repositâ.

## 1:3-4
BLESSED BE THE GOD AND FATHER OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, WHO ACCORDING TO HIS GREAT MERCY HATH REGENERATED US UNTO A LIVING HOPE BY THE RESURRECTION OF JESUS CHRIST FROM THE DEAD. UNTO AN INHERITANCE INCORRUPTIBLE AND UNDEFILED AND THAT FADETH NOT AWAY, RESERVED IN HEAVEN FOR YOU.

Thus far was the προοίμιον, of the Epistle; there follows the ὲργασία itself, the parts of which are two; the διδασκαλικὴ & νουθετικὴ. Διδασκαλικὴ is occupied with the fact that the Apostle demonstrates that the doctrine concerning Christ, which those converted from Judaism had received from the Apostles, is altogether most true and most certain. The Apostle proves this in two ways. 1. By the commemoration of spiritual benefits partly already conferred through it, partly still to be conferred and hoped for. Such benefits are: 1. Spiritual regeneration.

Just as the prologue, consisting of inscription and salutation, was prepared for conciliating benevolence: so the enumeration of those most ample benefits, which the Apostle testifies have been conferred upon believers through the preaching of the Gospel, looks toward procuring attention. The Apostle begins this an enumeration from δοξολογία and the praise of him, from whom those excellent benefits descend to us, Blessed be GOD and the father of our Lord Jesus Christ. With the very same δοξολογία Paul is accustomed to begin his Epistles, when he descends from the inscription and salutation to the ἐργασίαν itself. 2. Corinth. 1. vers. 3.Ephes. 1. v. 3. to which εὐλογίᾳ in other Epistles corresponds εὐχαριστία placed immediately after the salutation Rom. 1. v. 8.1. Cor. 1. v. 4.Phil. 1. v. 3.Col. 1. v. 3.1. Thess. 1. v. 2.2. Thess. 1. v. 3.2. Tim. 1. v. 3.Philem. v. 4. meanwhile, however, εὐλογία extends more widely than εὐχαριστία, when GOD is praised not only by words but also by deeds. Some think εὐλογητὸς is put for εὐλογητέος, to be blessed, to be praised. But it is more correctly said that the verb ἔστω, εὐλογητὸς ἔστω is to be understood blessed and praised be GOD. For that Greek noun corresponds to the ברוך of the Hebrews, which they are accustomed to use when they make mention of GOD, whence they even call God κατ῎ ἐζοχὴν הב רוך that blessed one.Marc. 14. v. 61.Rom. 9. v. 5. Moreover, the blessing of praise is understood, so that the sense may be: Let GOD be praised and extolled on account of the benefits by far the greatest conferred upon us. He then expresses the object of this δοξολογίας, which is God and the father of our Lord Jesus Christ. This is a description of the one true GOD, who has thus revealed himself in his word, that he is the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, i.e., that in the one and undivided essence of the Deity there are three distinct persons: the Father, who from eternity begat the Son, his substantial image; the Son, who begotten from eternity by the Father, in the fullness of time assumed human nature, and in it, by perfecting the work of redemption, was made in a peculiar way our Lord; and the Holy Spirit, who offers and applies to us the benefits obtained by the merit of Christ in the word of the Gospel, to whom the Apostle looks with the little word ἀναγεννήσας, because regeneration is peculiarly attributed to the Holy Spirit. Iohan. 3. v. 5.Tit. 3. v. 5. Bede in this place likewise joins the word GOD with the word Christ, so that the first person of the Deity is called both GOD and the father of our Lord Jesus Christ in a different respect, just as Christ also Ioh. 20. v. 17. says, I ascend to my father and my God. The words of Bede are as follows. When he says God and the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, he calls him the God of the Lord Jesus Christ, because he remembers that the Lord Christ himself was made man, but he names him the father of our Lord, because he does not doubt that the same Lord of ours has always existed as the son of GOD. But the particle καὶ is more correctly accepted as ἐξηγητικῶς, in the way the prefix ו is sometimes used among the Hebrews Gen. 35. v. 12.Exod. 7. v. 11.Ierem. 34. v. 21., examples of which signification also occur in the N. T. Matth. 13. v. 41.Col. 2. v. 8. &c. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ i. e. Blessed be that true GOD, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, hence the Syrian, with the copulative καὶ omitted, rendered it simply. Blessed be GOD the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

The benefit itself, which the Apostle celebrates in the first place, is expressed by the word ἀναγεννήσας.. By the name ἀναγεννήσεως, however, is understood spiritual regeneration, opposed to natural and carnal generation, which was miserably corrupted after the fall of the first-formed, Iohan. 3. v. 6. where Christ says it happens ἄνωθεν v. 3. anew and from above or from the heavens, by the heavenly power of the Holy Spirit Iohan. 1. v. 31.cap. 19. v. 11. for both significations agree with this place; and to happen from water and the Spirit v. 5. whereas the former generation happens from the flesh vers. 6.. The little word ἀνὰ, from which and from the word γεννάω this word is composed, leads us to the former explanation, by which ἄνωθεν in the words of Christ is accepted for anew or from the new, just as Nonnus also rendered δέυτερον, and the Syrian in this place who begat us [consult facsimile image] from the whole, i. e. םחדש from the new, in which respect it is called παλιγγενεσία in other places of Scripture Tit. 3. v. 5.. The word regeneration is accepted in two ways, firstly γενικῶς, so that it embraces the remission of sins and renewal at the same time, secondly εἰδικῶς so that it signifies only the remission of sins and gratuitous justification, in which signification it is distinguished from renewal Tit. 3. v. 5.. Regeneration, strictly, specifically, and properly accepted, is a translation from the state of wrath into the state of grace, which happens through faith in Christ, whose righteousness is imputed to believers and by grace sins are remitted to them. Although indeed renewal is joined to regeneration accepted in this way by an inseparable and immediate connection, through which new and spiritual motions are kindled in man, so that therefore these two benefits of the Holy Spirit are not to be torn apart or separated, nevertheless for many causes they are to be accurately distinguished. For regeneration does not receive more and less any more than carnal generation itself; but renewal does receive more and less 2. Cor. 4. v. 16. Regeneration is justification or washing from sins by the virtue of the blood of Christ, or the remission of sins and salvation, by which a man is made from a son of the Devil and hell a son of GOD and an heir of eternal life. Renovation is spiritual newness or sanctification, through which sin is mortified and man is renewed by the Spirit of his mind. The foundation of renovation is regeneration, the consequence and effect of regeneration is renovation. In regeneration man behaves himself merely passively, and can no more contribute anything to his own regeneration than to his own generation: but in the continuation and increase of renovation man does not behave himself merely passively, but cooperates with the Holy Spirit, not indeed by the natural powers of free will, but by new powers gifted by the Holy Spirit 2. Cor. 7. v. 1.Eph. 4. v. 23. In this place the little word regeneration is taken in its proper and strict signification. Its 1. principal efficient cause is described. Blessed be GOD and the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has regenerated us. As we received natural life from GOD through carnal generation: so also we receive spiritual life from the same through spiritual regeneration. James 1. v. 18. He has voluntarily begotten us. 2. The interior impulsive cause προηγουμένη. According to his great mercy. Just as David Ps. 51. v. 3. asks that GOD might have mercy on him, and remit his sins according to his great mercy and according to the multitude of his mercies, so Peter in this place says, that GOD has regenerated us κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος, because that regeneration includes the remission of our sins, which are many and great. As Paul says Eph. 2. v. 4. GOD who is rich in mercy for his great love, wherewith he loved us v. 5. and when we were dead in sins, has made us alive together with Christ: so also Peter in this place says, that GOD according to his great mercy has regenerated us, because that regeneration includes spiritual vivification. The Syrian in this place uses the word [consult facsimile image] which shows that that mercy is merely gratuitous, which has no respect to our merits, but depends uniquely upon the gratuitous favor of GOD, as Bede comments most beautifully in this place. Since we were begotten to death by our own merits, he regenerated us to life by his mercy. Therefore this mercy of GOD regenerating us is called great. 1. With respect had to GOD himself, who since he is great and infinite, therefore also his mercy is great and

infinite. Sir. 2. v. 23.As great as GOD is, so great is his mercy. 2. With respect had to our misery, into which we had fallen through sins. Great was the foulness of the sin propagated from Adam into us; great was the misery into which the fall of our first parents had cast us headlong; therefore certainly great is the mercy of GOD, according to which he regenerated us, and by this regeneration washed us from sins, and delivered us from our misery. Great was the loss which our first parents, and we in them, had made through the fall, therefore great is the mercy of GOD, which through regeneration restored to us those goods lost through the fall. 3. With respect had to other benefits of GOD. Great is the goodness of GOD, that he gives us natural life through carnal generation: but far greater is the mercy, by which he regenerates us to eternal life. By how much greater a good eternal life is than temporal, by so much greater a benefit is the bestowal of spiritual life through regeneration, than the donation of natural life through carnal generation. Great was the goodness and mercy of GOD, by which he granted to the people of the O. T. various corporal benefits, deliverance from Egypt, sustenance in the desert, introduction into the land of Canaan, victories against enemies: but far greater is the mercy, by which he regenerated us, having been delivered from the captivity of the Devil, and through that regeneration adopted us as his sons, and constituted us heirs of eternal life. 4. With respect had to the fruit and effect of regeneration. This regeneration embraces the remission of sins, the imputation of the righteousness of Christ, the translation from the state of wrath into the state of grace, υἱοθεσίαν and the inheritance of eternal life, which benefits, since they are by far the greatest, therefore also the mercy, from which that regeneration proceeds, is deservedly called great.

3. Formal cause. He regenerated us into a living hope. For ζῶσαν some Codices have ζωῆς, in which way Augustine also seems to have read in book 1 de peccatorum merit. & remiss. chapter 27. into the hope of eternal life, in which way the Syrian Interpreter also translates. Thence some take the name hope μετωνυμικῶς, concerning things which are subject to hope, in which signification this little word is taken Tit. 2. vers. 13.expecting the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of the great GOD and our Savior Jesus Christ, where the latter is ἐξηγητικὸν of the former. This could be confirmed an exposition from the fact that the Apostle seems immediately in v. 4. ἐξηγητικῶς to subjoin what that hope of life is, into which GOD has regenerated us, namely the inheritance of eternal life in the heavens. But because the more approved Codices read εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν,, it is therefore more correctly taken concerning the gift of Hope, than concerning the thing hoped for, of which he treats only in the following v. 4.. The name of hope is sometimes taken for the very confidence proper to justifying faith, and thus to hope in the Lord, to trust in the Lord, to believe in the Lord are taken for ἰσοδυναμοῦσι; but sometimes it is taken for the effect of justifying faith, distinct from faith itself, so that faith is concerning past and present things, but hope is only concerning future things. Although the latter signification of hope is not entirely foreign to this passage, because through hope we expect the plenary possession of the inheritance laid up for us in the heavens, of which the Apostle speaks in v. 4., and GOD has regenerated us by having made for us a most certain hope of obtaining eternal life, as an inheritance promised to sons, yet the former signification seems more congruent to this passage, so that by the name of hope there is noted, or at least connoted, faith, or the fiducial apprehension of the merit of Christ, which is the formal cause of our regeneration. For we are regenerated in such a way that through the word of the Gospel the Holy Spirit kindles faith in our hearts, through which we are adopted as sons of GOD, are transferred from a state of wrath into a state of grace, obtain the remission of sins, are made partakers of spiritual life, and are written as heirs of eternal life, where however it must be warned that we use the term formal cause in a wider signification here for the mode and manner by which we are spiritually regenerated, so that the sense is that this is the mode and this the manner of our regeneration, and therefore also of our justification, that faith embraces Christ, and in Christ the grace of GOD, the remission of sins, υἱοθεσίαν and righteousness availing before GOD. For since regeneration is an action of GOD, therefore, speaking properly and accurately, faith cannot be the formal cause of regeneration, but it consists in the very translation from a state of wrath into a state of grace, and in the adoption to the right of sonship and eternal life. This signification of hope is proposed by the interlinear gloss, when it comments on this passage thus: Through faith Christ rises in us, just as through infidelity He dies in us.

4. Meritorious cause. Through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. Some refer this προσδιορισμὸν to the nearer to a living hope, so that the meaning may be. He has made for us the hope of eternal life through the resurrection of Christ his beloved son, whom he raised from death to eternal life. For because our certainty of our resurrection to eternal life depends upon the resurrection of Christ, and consequently from the resurrection of Christ the hope of life, i. e. of a blessed resurrection to life, arises in our hearts, the Apostle teaches in many places 1. Cor. 15. v. 12. & following. Rom. 8. v. 11. 1. Thess. 4. v. 14. This explanation contains nothing at all that is opposed to the analogy of faith, and it agrees with the Apostolic passage Eph. 2. v. 18. may GOD give you the eyes of your heart enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, v. 19. and what is the supereminent greatness of his power toward us who believe according to the working of the power of his might v. 20. which he worked in Christ, raising him from the dead. But more correctly here προσδιορισμὸς is referred to what is more remote, namely to the word regenerated, in which way the Syrian also arranged it. GOD through his great grace regenerated us through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ into the hope of life. The meaning therefore is that the resurrection of Christ is the meritorious cause of our regeneration, by which we rise from the death of sin to eternal life, just as Paul Rom. 4. v. 25. says, that Christ was delivered for our sins, and rose again for our justification. This exposition is confirmed by the fact that in cap. 3. v. 21.Baptism is said to save us through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Moreover, the merit of Christ is described through the resurrection, because that is an evident argument that sins were fully expiated by his passion and death, and that eternal life was obtained for us by the price of his blood. For because Christ was made our sponsor, and was cast into the prison of the sepulcher on account of the debts of our sins, and in the resurrection was led forth from this prison by the heavenly Father with glory, from that it is most manifestly seen that the heavenly Father was fully and perfectly satisfied for the debts of our sins, so that, if we believe with true faith, and apply to ourselves the benefits obtained by the passion and death of Christ, then that living hope, of which the Apostle speaks, arises, increases, and is confirmed in our hearts through the resurrection of Christ. Some say, thence and therefore we are regenerated through the resurrection of Christ, because the Holy Spirit persuades us of the resurrection of Christ, and instructs us concerning the power and reason of it, and thus kindles faith and hope in our hearts unto regeneration. But that this is said too thinly, will appear from what follows.

5. Final cause. He has regenerated us into an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you. The Apostle had said, that GOD has regenerated us according to his great mercy; but because through this regeneration we are made children of GODJohn 1. v. 12. therefore he most aptly makes mention of the inheritance, to which we have been regenerated. If indeed we are children, then also heirsRom. 8. v. 17. He describes this inheritance magnificently, in order to exaggerate more the benefit of regeneration and adoption into children, for the more ample and august the inheritance is, the greater the benefit the adoption is deservedly judged to be, of which that is the consequent and effect.

First, he calls it ἄφθαρτον incorruptible. This epithet 1. is opposed to earthly inheritances, i.e., those goods which come to men through inheritances in this world. For those, whatever they may be, are nevertheless φθαρτὰ perishable and passing, just as a little later the Apostle calls gold and silver, which are the chief things in earthly inheritances, φθαρτὰ v. 18. but the inheritance, to which GOD has regenerated his children, is incorruptible; its glory and happiness cannot be corrupted. 2. The same is opposed to the inheritance of the land of Canaan, once given to the Israelites. It was a great benefit which GOD granted to his Israelite people in the O.T., by introducing them into the land of Canaan, which is very often called by the name of inheritance in the Scriptures. Levit. 20. v. 24.Deut. 3. v. 18.Psal. 135. v. 12. namely, because Israel was the firstborn son of GODExod. 4. v. 22. to whom, by the grace of adoption, GOD gave the land of Canaan as an inheritance Deut. 9. v. 4. & seqq. But even this inheritance was earthly, and consequently corruptible. 3. He exaggerates the perpetuity of the heavenly blessedness and glory, in that once it is possessed, it cannot again be taken away from the blessed. Earthly inheritances are not only frail and transitory but also ambulatory, for often an inheritance devolves to someone who had never thought of it before. But the heavenly inheritance is incorruptible, and consequently also fixed, firm, and perpetual. 4. He leads us to the meritorious cause of this inheritance, as appears from v. 18. Christ did not redeem us with corruptible gold and silver, but with his precious blood; therefore, he also merited for us not some corruptible and transitory, but an incorruptible and eternal inheritance.

Secondly, he calls this inheritance ἀμίαντον undefiled and undefiled. This epithet is used of Christ Heb. 7. v. 26. as being alien from every stain of sin, of the marriage bed, which is kept chastely and is devoid of pollution, so that the conscience is not defiled by its legitimate use Heb. 13. v. 4. and of worship pleasing and acceptable to GOD James 1. v. 27. μιαίνειν is to defile, to contaminate, thence ἀμίαντος not polluted, nor defiled, therefore καθρὸς καὶ ἀμίαντος are joined by James in the said place, which Plutarch also does in Pericles. 1. Some therefore think that the metaphor is drawn from the modesty of a virgin, not contaminated by any stain of whoredom and lust, just as Wisd. 3. v. 13. a chaste matron is called ἀμίαντος, to whom a body is attributed ἀμίαντον chap. 8. v. 20. which Paul says is holy in body 1. Cor. 7. v. 34. Because, namely, the faithful, betrothed to Christ through faith, have kept their spiritual virginity, consisting in the purity of faith and life, uncontaminated, 2. Cor. 11. v. 2. therefore also the heavenly inheritance, which is given to them, ἀμίαντος, is called. 2. Nor is it absurdly thought that Peter is looking to the passage Wisd. 4. v. 2. where it is said of a chaste and modest woman, she triumphs crowned for eternity ἀμιάντων ἂθλων ἀγῶνα νικήσασα. For those undefiled rewards are distributed to chaste and modest women not only on earth, but also, and even most especially, in heaven. 3. It is said of a temple either guarded or liberated from the violence of enemies, that God kept it ἀμίαντον 2. Macc. 14. v. 36. chap. 15. v. 34. Because, therefore, the inheritance of eternal life, prefigured by the Jerusalem temple, can never again be snatched away from the blessed by any violence of enemies, thence it is deservedly called ἀμίαντος in this place. 4. This epithet is opposed to the pleasures of this age, which an earthly inheritance is accustomed to bring, for those can easily defile a man before God through abuse, but the heavenly inheritance is in itself in every part most pure, admitting no filth or stains, nor shall anything defiled enter into it, Rev. 21. v. 27. whereas into the land of Canaan both the holy and the contaminated entered indiscriminately, and earthly inheritances, even the most ample, sometimes fall to the worst men.

5. It is opposed to earthly joy, which the unexpected possession of an ample inheritance excites. For that is more often contaminated beyond expectation through adversity, or even through a controversy stirred up concerning the inheritance: but the heavenly inheritance of the pious has nothing adverse, nothing troublesome, nothing of disgust, by which its joy and glory might be contaminated.

6. Ἀμίαντος is called by the Greeks a fossil stone, for the most part white, but sometimes ash-colored or reddish or iron-colored, which, when thrown into the fire, is neither consumed nor defiled, but even comes out more splendid, from which they also establish that ἀμίαντον & ἂσβεστον itself is named. Pliny, book 36, Natural History, chapter 19: Amiantus, similar to alum, loses nothing in the fire. This stone is spun into torches, which, when thrown into fires, indeed burn, but, unconquered by the flames, come out from them shining more than they could by water. This is a beautiful image of eternal happiness, which will never perish by fire at any time, whereas, on the contrary, all earthly inheritances are to be corrupted by fire at the end of the age.

Thirdly, it calls ἀμάραντον. μαραίνεσθαι, which signifies to wither, to be rendered withered or flaccid, and is used among other things of flowers, as Eustathius relates; thence ἀμάραντος is peculiarly called a certain flower, named by Galen by the name heliochrysi, with a tawny, bulbous root, a fennel-like stalk, a foot in height, leaves longer than basil, a purple spike, odorless; it is so called because it does not wither, for when plucked it is preserved, and when all flowers have failed, it revives when moistened with water, and when gathered and dried by the warmth of an oven, it is stored away for the garland uses of winter, nor does it lose the brightness and grace of its color. Pliny, book 21, Natural History, chapter 8: It is a wonder in it that it rejoices to be plucked and to be reborn more widely; and it is a wonder that, after all flowers have failed, it revives when moistened with water and makes winter garlands.
