The sum of its nature is in its name, called so because it does not wither. Dioscorides, book 4, chapter 47: Purple amaranth, so called from this, because its flowers never wither. But it is called helichryson because, at the reflection of the sun, it bears before itself the brightness of gold with its leaves blooming in a circle. From this flower that never withers, the metaphor is drawn when Peter calls the heavenly inheritance ἀμάραντον,, which appears from chapter 5, verse 4 of this Epistle, where he calls it the same ἀμαράντινον τῆς δόξης στέφανον.. For it is called a crown or garland amaranthine, which is from amaranth, just as Philostratus also said in the Heroics ἀμαραντίνους στεφάνους.. For that amaranth was accustomed to be used for crowns or garlands is evident not only from the cited passage of Pliny, but also from Tibullus, book 3, elegy 4: As when girls weave white lilies with amaranths. Some establish this distinction between ἀμάραντον & ἀμαράντινον, that ἀμάραντος signifies not Fading; ἀμαράντινον truly unfading, but ἀμαράντινος is not formed from ἀμάραντος, insofar as it is an appellative noun, but insofar as it is the proper name of a certain flower, so that it must be rendered, you shall receive the amaranthine crown of glory, which is from the true and precious amaranth, which is more unfading than that which is from the amaranth. Wis. 6. v. 12. wisdom is called ἀμάραντος, because its possession cannot be taken away. When therefore Peter calls the heavenly inheritance ἀμάραντον, he signifies. 1. That it always retains its vigor, grace, and beauty like the amaranth flower. For just as in eternal life there will be no night Rev. 21. v. 25. so also there will be no winter there adverse to flowers, but perpetual spring. 2. That the joy of eternal life will always be new and fresh, so that weariness of it may never creep upon us, just as the amaranth herb revived when moistened with waters. 3. And that consequently it differs most widely from the pleasures of this age, which like flowers quickly fade. Job 14. v. 2. Ps. 90. v. 6. Ps. 103. v. 5. & 6. 1 Pet. 1 v. 24.

Fourthly, he says this inheritance is kept for us in heaven. τετηρημένην is placed in the perfect form, not in the present form, which would be τηρουμένην: it signifies therefore, that the glory of that heavenly inheritance has already long ago, namely from the origin of the world, nay from all eternity, been prepared, kept, and reserved, just as parents are accustomed to store up and reserve treasures for their children as an inheritance to be entered upon in its own time. Matt. 25. v. 34. possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. 2 Thess. 2. v. 13. GOD chose us from the beginning for salvation. He adds, moreover, that this inheritance is kept in heaven, to show 1. The excellence of this inheritance, that it is not an earthly and transitory but a heavenly and eternal inheritance. 2. The certainty of the same. Not in our hands, but in the hand of GOD is that inheritance kept for us, from whose hand no one, neither we nor that inheritance of ours, will be able to snatch it. Matt. 6. v. 20. John 10. v. 28. 3. The firmness and perpetuity of the same. The inheritance of the land of Canaan was exposed to the violence and depredation of enemies, because it was an inheritance on earth, but the heavenly inheritance will be able to be snatched from us by no violence of enemies, because it is reserved in heaven. An earthly inheritance is often diverted by the cunning of men, but concerning the heavenly inheritance, inasmuch as it is reserved in heaven, this is not to be feared. 4. This member can therefore be taken as αἰτιολογικὸν of the preceding, for from thence and therefore the inheritance of the children of God is incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading, because it is a heavenly inheritance, because it is kept in heaven, in which neither corruption, nor filth, nor fading have any place. 5. At the same time Peter also intimates that the happiness and glory of that inheritance is still invisible to us, for those things which are in the heavens are removed from our eyes and senses, whence he immediately adds v. 5. that salvation or that inheritance is ready to be revealed in the last time, with which agrees that Apostolic saying Colos. 3. v. 3. Your life is hidden with Christ in God, v. 4. when however Christ shall appear, your life, then also you shall appear with him in glory. And likewise that John 1. Epist. 3. v. 2. Now we are the Children of God (and heirs of eternal life), but it has not yet appeared what we shall be.

Finally he adds, that that inheritance is kept for us. The Vulgate version rendered it in us, but most Greek Codices have εἰς ἡμᾶς i. e. ἡμῖν for us, by a customary Hebraism, examples of which also occur in this very Epistle. v. 25. of this chapter, where the word which is preached is εἰς ὑμᾶς. Erasmus rendered it towards you. Jerome lib. 1. against Jovinian. chap. 24. towards you. Augustine cites, kept for you, for not only the Vulgate Latin version, but also many Greek codices have the pronoun of the second person εἰς ὑμᾶς, in which way also Benedict Arias Montanus and D. Luther read in the German version, which reading agrees with v. 5. and 6. following, where Peter changes the first person into the second. For he had said v. 3. blessed be God, who has regenerated us into a living hope, but in v. 6. he says, in which you rejoice, namely, so that he might prepare a way for himself to the following exhortation in v. 13. to which the pronoun of the second person more agrees. Whether therefore in v. 4. we read ἡμᾶς, or ὑμᾶς, the matter comes to the same thing, the former reading agrees more with the preceding v. 3., the latter with the following v. 6., and in both cases the sense is that that heavenly inheritance is kept for those whom God has regenerated and adopted into his children.

Latin:

BENEDICTUS DEUS & PATER DOMINI NOSTRI IESU CHRISTI, QUI SECUNDUM MISERICORDIAM SUAM MAGNAM REGENERAVIT NOS IN SPEM VIVAM PER RESURRECTIONEM IESU CHRISTI EX MORTUIS. IN HAEREDITATEM INCORRUPTIBILEM & INCONTAMINATAM & IMMARCESCIBILEM, CONSERVATAM IN COELIS IN VOBIS.

Hactenus fuit Epistolae προοίμιον, sequitur ὲργασία ipsa, cuius partes duae sunt, διδασκαλικὴ & νουθετικὴ. Διδασκαλικὴ in eo versatur, quod Apostolus demonstrat, doctrinam de Christo, quam conversi ex Iudaismo ab Apostolis acceperint, esse omninò verissimam ac certissimam. Probat hoc Apostolus dupliciter. 1. Commemoratione beneficiorum spiritualium partim iamdum per eam collatorum, partim adhuc conferendorum ac sperandorum. Talia beneficia sunt. 1. Spiritualis regeneratio.

Quemadmodum prooemium, inscriptione & salutatione constans, comparatum fuit ad benevolentiam conciliandam: ita enumeratio amplissimorum illorum beneficiorum, quae per praedicationem Evangelii credentibus collata esse Apostolus testatur, ad comparandam attentionem spectat. Orditur autem Apostolus hanc enumerationem à δοξολογία ac laude illius, à quo eximia illa beneficia ad nos descendunt, Benedictus DEUS & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Eâdem omnino δοξολογία Paulus suas exordiri solet Epistolas, quando ab inscriptione & salutatione ad ipsam ἐργασίαν descendit. 2. Corinth. 1. vers. 3.Ephes. 1. v. 3. cui εὐλογίᾳ in aliis Epistolis respondet εὐχαριστία salutationi proximè subiecta Rom. 1. v. 8.1. Cor. 1. v. 4.Phil. 1. v. 3.Col. 1. v. 3.1. Thess. 1. v. 2.2. Thess. 1. v. 3.2. Tim. 1. v. 3.Philem. v. 4. interim tamen εὐλογία latius patet quàm εὐχαριστία, cum non solùm verbis sed etiam factis DEUS laudetur. εὐλογητὸς quidam pofitum censent pro εὐλογητέος,benedicendus, laudandus. Sed rectius dicitur sub intelligendum verbum ἔστω, εὐλογητὸς ἔστωbenedictus ac laudatus sit DEUS. Respondet enim illud Graecum nomen Hebraeorum ברוך quo uti solent, quando DEI mentionem faciunt, unde etiam Deum κατ῎ ἐζοχὴν vocant הב רוךbenedictum illum.Marc. 14. v. 61.Rom. 9. v. 5. Intelligitur autem benedictio laudis, ut sit sensus. Laudetur & extollatur DEUS ob beneficia longè maxima in nos collata. Exprimit deinde obiectum huius δοξολογίας, quod est Deus & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Descriptio haec est unius veri DEI, qui in verbo suo sese sic revelavit, quod sit pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, i. e. quòd in una & indivisa Deitatis essentia sint tres distinctae personae, Pater qui ab aeterno genuit Filium imaginem suam substantialem; Filius, qui ab aeterno à Patre genitus in temporis plenitudine assumsit humanam naturam, inque ea opus redemtionis perficiendo factus est peculiari ratione noster Dominus; & Spiritus sanctus, qui beneficia Christi merito parta in verbo Evangelii nobis offert atque applicat, ad quem voculâ ἀναγεννήσας Apostolus respicit, quia regeneratio peculiariter tribuitur Spiritui sancto. Iohan. 3. v. 5.Tit. 3. v. 5. Beda in h. l. vocem DEI itidem coniungit cum voce Christi, ut sic prima Deitatis persona diverso respectu & DEUS & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi dicatur, sicut etiam Christus Ioh. 20. v. 17. dicit, Ascendo ad patrem meum & Deum meum. Verba Bedae sic habent. Cùm dicit Deus & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Deum quidem Domini Iesu Christi appellat, quia ipsum Dominum Christum hominem factum fuisse meminit, patrem autem Domini nostri nominat, quia eundem Dominum nostrum DEI filium semper extitisse non dubitat. Sed particula καὶ rectius accipitur ἐξηγητικῶς, quo modo praefixum ו apud Hebraeos interdum usurpatur Gen. 35. v. 12.Exod. 7. v. 11.Ierem. 34. v. 21. cuius significationis exempla etiam in N. T. occurrunt Matth. 13. v. 41.Col. 2. v. 8. &c. Benedictus Deus & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi h. e. Benedictus sit verus ille DEUS, qui est pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, inde Syrus omissâ copulativâ καὶ simpliciter reddidit. Benedictus DEUS pater Domini nostri Ieschua Christi.

Beneficium ipsum, quod primo loco Apostolus celebrat, exprimitur voce ἀναγεννήσας. Intelligitur autem nomine ἀναγεννήσεως spiritualis regeneratio, generationi naturali & carnali, post lapsum protoplastorum miserè corruptae, opposita, Iohan. 3. v. 6. ubi Christus dicit eam fieriἄνωθενv. 3.denuò ac desuper sive è supernis, supernâ Spiritus sancti virtuteIohan. 1. v. 31.cap. 19. v. 11. utraque enim significatio huic loco congruit; ac fieri ex aqua & Spirituv. 5. cum prior generatio fiat ex carnevers. 6. Vocula ἀνὰ ex qua & ex verbo γεννάω haec vox componitur, deducit nos ad priorem explicationem, quâ ἄνωθεν in verbis Christi accipitur pro denuò vel de novo, sicut etiam Nonnus reddidit δέυτερον, ac Syrus h. l. qui genuit nos[consult facsimile image]ab integro, h. e. םחדשde novo, quo respectu in aliis Scripturae locis vocatur παλιγγενεσίαTit. 3. v. 5. Accipitur autem vox regenerationis dupliciter, primò γενικῶς, ut remissionem peccatorum & renovationem simul complectatur, secundò εἰδικῶς ut remissionem peccatorum ac gratuitam iustificationem tantummodò significet, in qua significatione à renovatione distinguitur Tit. 3. v. 5. Regeneratio, strictè, specificè ac propriè accepta, est translatio ex statu irae in statum gratiae, quae fit per fidem in Christum, cuius iustitia credentibus imputatur & ex gratia peccata ipsis remittuntur. Quamvis vero regenerationi hoc modo acceptae indivulso & immediato nexu coniuncta sit renovatio, per quam novi ac spirituales motus in homine accenduntur, ut proinde haec duo beneficia Spiritus sancti non sint divellenda vel separanda, attamen propter multas causas accuratè sunt distinguenda. Regeneratio enim tam non recipit maius ac minus quàm ipsa carnalis generatio; at renovatio maius ac minus recipit 2. Cor. 4. v. 16.Regeneratio est iustificatio seu ablutio a peccatis virtute sanguinis Christi, seu remissio pecatorum & salvatio, quâ ex filio Diaboli & gehennae homo fit filius DEI & haeres vitae aeternae. Renovatio est novitas spiritualis sive sanctificatio, per quam peccatum mortificatur & homo Spiritu mentis suae renovatur. Renovationis fundamentum est regeneratio, regenerationis consequens & effectum renovatio. In regeneratione homo se habet merè passivè, ac tàm non potest aliquid conferre ad sui regenerationem, quàm ad suam generationem: sed in renovationis continuatione & augmento homo non se habet merè passivè, sed cooperatur Spiritui sancto, non quidem naturalibus liberi arbitrii viribus, sed novis à Spiritu sancto donatis viribus 2. Cor. 7. v. 1.Eph. 4. v. 23. Hoc loco regenerationis vocula in propria & stricta significatione accipitur. Illius describitur 1. causa efficiens principalis. Benedictus DEUS & pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui regeneravit nos. Uti à DEO vitam naturalem per generationem carnalem accepimus: ita quoque ab eodem vitam spiritualem per regenerationem spiritualem accipimus. Iacob 1. v. 18.Voluntariè nos genuit. 2. Causa προηγουμένη impulsiva interior. Secundùm misericordiam suam magnam. Sicut David Psal. 51. v. 3. petit, ut DEUS sui misereatur, sibique peccata remittat secundùm magnam suam misericordiam & secundum multitudinem miserationum suarum, ita Petrus h. l. dicit, DEUM nos regenuissèκατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος, quía regeneratio illa peccatorum nostrorum, quae multa & magna sunt, remissionem includit. Sicut Paulus dicit Eph. 2. v. 4.DEUS qui dives est in misericordia propter magnam suam caritatem, quâ dilexit nosv. 5.& cum essèmus mortui in peccatis, convivificavit nos Christo: ita quoque Petrus hoc loco dicit, DEUM secundum magnam misericordiam suam nos regenuisse, quia regeneratio illa spiritualem vivisicationem includit. Syrus h. l. utitur voce [consult facsimile image] quae ostendit, misericordiam illam esse merè gratuitam, quae non habeat respectum ad nostra merita, sed ex gratuito DEI favore unicè dependeat, sicut pulcherrimè Beda in h. l. commentatur. Cum nostris meritis generati essemus ad mortem, suâ misericordiâ nos regeneravit ad vitam. Vocatur igitur haec misericordia DEI nos regenerantis magna. 1. Respectu ad DEUM ipsum habito, qui cum sit magnus & infinitus, ideò etiam ipsius misericordia magna est &

infinita. Sir. 2. v. 23.Quantus est DEUS, tanta est eius misericordia. 2. Respectu habito ad nostram miseriam, in quam per peccata incideramus. Magna erat peccati ab Adamo in nos propagati foeditas; magna erat miseria, in quam lapsus primorum parentum nos praecipites dederat; utique ergò magna est DEI misericordia, secundùm quam nos regeneravit, & hac regeneratione à peccatis nos abluit, atque à miseria nostra nos liberavit. Magna erat iactura, quam primi parentes, & nos in ipsis per lapsum feceramus, magna ergo DEI misericordia, quae per regenerationem amissa illa per lapsum bona nobis restituit. 3. Respectu ad alia DEI beneficia habito. Magna est DEI bonitas, quòd vitam naturalem nobis donat per generationem carnalem: sed longè maior misericordia, quâ nos ad vitam aeternam regenerat. Quantò maius bonum vita aeterna quàm temporalis, tantò maius beneficium collatio vitae spiritualis per regenerationem, quàm donatio vitae naturalis per carnalem generationem. Magna fuit DEI bonitas & misericordia, quâ populo V. T. varia beneficia corporalia, liberationem ex Aegypto, sustentationem in deserto, introductionem in terram Canaan, victorias contra hostes praestitit: sed longè maior misericordia, quâ nos ex Diaboli captivitate liberatos regeneravit, ac per regenerationem illam in filios suos adoptavit, ac haeredes vitae aeternae constituit. 4. Respectu habito ad regenerationis fructum & effectum. Complectitur haec regeneratio peccatorum remissionem, iustitiae Christi imputationem, translationem ex statu irae in statum gratiae, υἱοθεσίαν & vitae aeternae haereditatem, quae beneficia cum sint longè maxima, ideò etiam misericordia, ex qua regeneratio illa proficiscitur, meritò vocatur magna.

3. Causa formalis. Regeneravit nos in spem vivam. Pro ζῶσαν quidam Codices habent ζωῆς, quo modo etiam legisse videtur Augustinus lib. 1. de peccatorum merit. & remiss. cap. 27. in spem vitae aeternae, quo modo etiam vertit Interpres Syrus. Inde spei nomen quidam μετωνυμικῶς accipiunt, de rebus, quae spei sunt subiectae, in qua significatione haec vocula accipitur Tit. 2. vers. 13.expectantes beatam spem & adventum gloriae magni DEI & Salvatoris nostri Iesu Christi, ubi posterius est ἐξηγητικὸν prioris. Confirmari posset haec expositio ex eo, quod Apostolus statim in v. 4.ἐξηγητικῶς subiungere videatur, quaenam sit spes illa vitae, in quam nos DEUS regeneravit, videlicet hereditas vitae aeternae in caelis. Sed quia probatiores Codices legunt, εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν, ideò rectiùs accipitur de Spei dono, quâm de re sperata, de qua in seq. demum v. 4. agit. Sumitur autem spei nomen quandoque pro ipsa fiducia iustificantis fidei propria, & sic pro ἰσοδυναμοῦσι accipiuntur sperare in Dominum, confidere in Dominum, credere in Dominum; quandoque vero pro effectu fidei iustificantis ab ipsa fide distinctus, ita ut fides sit de praeteritis & praesentibus, spes autem tantùm de futuris. Quamvis verô posterior spei significatio ab hoc loco non sit planè aliena, quia per spem expectamus plenariam possessionem hereditatis in coelis nobis repositae de qua Apostolus in v. 4. loquitur, ac regeneravit nos DEUS factâ nobis certissimâ spe consequendae vitae aeternae, tanquam hereditatis filiis promissae, tamen prior significatio huic loco videtur magis congrua, ut sic spei nomine notetur, vel certè connotetur fides, sive fiducialis meriti Christi apprehensio, quae est regenerationis nostrae causa formalis, Regeneramur enim modo eo, ut per verbum Evangelii Spiritus S. in cordibus nostris fidem accendat, per quam in filios DEI adoptamur, ex statu irae in statum gratiae transferimur, peccatorum remissionem consequimur, vitae spiritualis participes reddimur, & heredes vitae aeternae scribimur, ubi tamen monendum, termino causae formalis in latiore significatione nos h. l. uti pro modo ac ratione, quâ spiritualiter regeneramur, ut sit sensus, regenerationis, adeoque etiam iustificationis notrae hunc esse modum & hanc rationem, ut fides amplectatur Christum, & in Christo gratiam DEI, peccatorum remissionem, υἱοθεσίαν & iustitiam coram DEO valentem. Cum enim regeneratio sit actio DEI, ideò propriè & accuratè loquendo fides non potest esse causa formalis regenerationis, sed ea consistit in ipsa translatione è statu irae in statum gratiae, & in adoptione ad ius filiationis ac vitae aeternae. Hanc spei significationem proponit glossa interlinearis, quando in hunc locum sic commentatur. Per fidem Christus resurgit in nobis, sicut per infidelitatem moritur in nobis.

4. Causa meritoria. Per resurrectionem Iesu Christi ex mortuis. Quidam hunc προσδιορισμὸν referunt ad propinquins videlicet ad spem vivam, ut sit sensus. Spem vitae aeternae nobis fecit per resurrectionem Christi dilecti filii sui, quem à morte ad vitam aeternam resuscitavit. Quod enim à Christi resurrectione certitudo nostrae resurrectionis ad vitam aeternam dependeat, ac proinde ex Christi resurrectione spes vitae i. e. beatae resurrectionis ad vitam in cordibus nostris oriatur, multis docet Apostolus1. Cor. 15. v. 12. & seqq. Rom. 8. v. 11.1. Thess. 4. v. 14. Haec explicatio nihil quicquam continet, quod fidei analogiae adversetur, ac congruit cum loco Apostolico Eph. 2. v. 18.det DEUS vobis illuminatos oculos cordis vestri, ut sciatis, quae sit spes vocationis eius, & quae divitiae gloriae haereditatis eius in sanctis,v. 19.& quae sit supereminens magnitudo virtutis eius in nos, qui credimus secundùm operationem potentiae virtutis eiusv. 20.quam operatus est in Christo, suscitans illum à mortuis. Sed rectiùs hic προσδιορισμὸς refertur ad remotius, videlicet ad verbum regeneravit, quo modo etiam Syrus ordinavit. DEUS per gratiam suam magnam regenuit nos per resurrectionem Domini nostri Iesu Christi in spem vitae. Sensus igitur est, quòd resurrectio Christi sit causa meritoria nostrae regenerationis, quâ ex morte peccati ad vitam aeternam resurgimus, sicut Paulus Rom. 4. v. 25. dicit, Christum esse traditum propter peccata nostra, & resurrexisse propter iustificationem nostram. Confirmat hanc expositionem, quòd in cap. 3. v. 21.Baptisma nos dictur salvare per resurrectionem Iesu Christi. Describitur autem meritum Christi per resurrectionem, quia illa est evidens argumentum peccatorum plenè per ipsius passionem & mortem expiatorum, ac vitae aeternae precio sanguinis sui nobis partae. Quia enim Christus sponsor noster factus, & propter peccatorum nostrorum debita in carcerem sepulchri coniectus, in resurrectione à Patre coelesti cum gloria ex hoc carcere eductus fuit, ex eo manifestissimè conspicitur, Patri coelesti pro peccatorum nostrorum debitis plenè & perfectè satisfactum esse, quòd ipsum, si verâ fide credimus, ac beneficia Christi passione & morte parta nobis applicamus, tùm spes illa viva, de qua Apostolus loquitur, per Chrisiti resurrectionem in cordibus nostris oritur, augetur & confirmatur. Quidam dicunt, inde atque ideò nos per resurrectionem Christi regenerari, quia Spiritus sanctus Christi resurrectionem nobis persuadet, ac de vi & ratione illius nos erudit, sicque, fidem & spem in cordibus nostris ad regenerationem accendit. Sed hoc nimis tenuiter dici, ex sequentibus apparebit.

5. Causa finalis. Regeneravit nos in haereditatem incorruptibilem, & incontaminatam & immarcescibilem, conservatam in coelis in vobis. Dixerat Apostolus, DEUM nos regenuisse secundùm magnam, misericordiam; quia vero per hanc regenerationem reddimur DEI filiiIoh. 1. v. 12. ideò aptissimè mentionem facit haereditatis, ad quam regeniti sumus. Si enim sumus filii, utique etiam haeredesRom. 8. v. 17. Magnificè vero hanc haereditatem describit, ut beneficium regenerationis & adoptionis in filios magis exaggeret, quò enim amplior & augustior est haereditas, eò maius beneficium meritò iudicatur adoptio, cuius illa consequens est & effectus.

Primò eam vocat ἄφθαρτονincorruptibilem. Hoc epitheton 1. oppositum est haereditatibus terrenis i. e. bonis illis, quae per haereditates in hoc mundo hominibus obveniunt. Ea enim qualiacunque sint, tamen sunt φθαρτὰperitura ac transitura, sicut paulo pòst Apostolus aurum & argentum, quae in terrenis haereditatibus sunt praecipua, vocat φθαρτὰ v. 18. sed haereditas, ad quam DEUS filios suos regenuit, est incorruptibilis, illius gloria & felicitas corrumpi nequit. 2. Idem oppositum est haereditati terrae Canaan, Israëlitis olim datae. Magnum fuit beneficium, quod DEUS in V. T. populo suo Israëlitico concessit, in terram Canaan ipsos introducendo, quae saepiusculè in Scripturis haereditatis nomine appellatur. Levit. 20. v. 24.Deut. 3. v. 18.Psal. 135. v. 12. nimirùm, quia Israël erat filius DEI primogenitusExod. 4. v. 22. cui ex adoptionis gratia DEUS terram. Canaan in haereditatem dabat Deut. 9. v. 4. & seqq. Sed & haec haereditas fuit terrena, ac proinde corruptibilis 3. exaggerat beatitudinis & gloriae coelestis perpetuitatem, quòd ea semel habita iterum à beatis auferri nequeat. Terrenae haereditates non solùm sunt caducae ac transitoriae sed etiam ambulatoriae, saepè enim haereditas ad aliquem devolvitur, qui de ea nunquam priùs cogitaverat. Sed haereditas coelestis est in corruptibilis, ac proinde etiam fixa, firma & perpetua. 4. Deducit nos ad haereditatis huius causam meritoriam, ut apparet ex v. 18. Christus non redemit nos corruptibilibus auro & argento, sed precioso suo sanguine, ideò etiam non corruptibilem aliquam & transitoriam, sed incorruptibilem & aeternam haereditatem nobis promeruit.

Secundò hanc haereditatem vocat ἀμίαντονincontaminatam ac impollutam. Usurpatur hoc epitheton de Christo Hebr. 7. v. 26. ab omni peccati labe alieno, de cubili coniugali, quod castè servatum est pollutionis expers, ita ut legitimo eius usu conscientia non polluatur Hebr. 13. v. 4. ac de cultu DEO grato & accepto Iacob. 1. v. 27.μιαίνειν est inquinare, contaminare, inde ἀμίαντοςnon pollutus, nec foedatus, propterea καθρὸς καὶ ἀμίαντος à Iacobo d. l. coniunguntur, quod etiam facit Plutarchus in Pericle. 1. Quidam ergo existimant, metaphoram esse ductam à pudicitia virginis, nullâ scortationis ac libidinis labe contaminatae, sicut Sap. 3. v. 13.casta matrona vocaturἀμίαντος,cui tribuitur corpusἀμίαντονcap. 8. v. 20.quod Paulus dicit esse sanctum corpore1. Cor. 7. v. 34.Quia n. fideles Christo per fidem desponsati, spiritualem virginitatem, in fidei & vitae puritate consistentem, incontaminatam servaverunt,2. Cor. 11. v. 2.ideò etiam haereditas coelestis, quae ipsis datur,ἀμίαντος,vocatur. 2. Nec absurdè cogitatur, Petrum respicere ad locum Sap. 4. v. 2. ubi de casta & pudica foemina dicitur, in seculum coronata triumphatἀμιάντων ἂθλων ἀγῶνα νικήσασα. Illa enim impolluta praemia non solùm in terris, sed etiam, ac vel maximè in coelo castis & pudicis foeminis distribuuntur. 3. De templo ab hostium violentia vel custodito vel liberato dicitur, quod Deus illud servaritἀμίαντον2. Maccab. 14. v. 36.cap. 15. v. 34. Quia ergo haereditas vitae aeternae per templum Hierosolymitanum praefiguratae, nulla hostium violentia beatis iterum eripi poterit, indè meritò ἀμίαντος hoc loco vocatur. 4. Opponitur hoc epitheton voluptatibus huius seculi, quas haereditas terrena afferre solet, illae enim per abusum facilè possunt hominem coram Deo inquinare, sed coelestis haereditas in se est omni ex parte purissima, nullas sordes aut maculas admittens, neque quicquam in eam intrabit inquinatum, Apoc. 21. v. 27. cum in terram Canaan promiscuè & sancti & contaminati intrarent, ac haereditates terrenae etiam amplissimae quandoque pessimis hominibus obveniut.

5. Opponitur gaudio terreno, quod amplae haereditatis insperata possessio excitat. Illud enim per adversitatem, vel etiam controversiam de haereditate motam, saepiùs praeter opinionem contaminatur: sed coelestis piorum haereditas nihil adversi, nihil molesti, nihil fastidii habet, quo eius laetitia ac gloria contaminetur.

6. Ἀμίαντος Graecis vocatur lapis fossilis plerunque albus, sed interdum cinereus vel ruffus vel ferreus, qui in ignem coniectus nec absumitur nec inquinatur, sed splendidior etiam evadit, ex quo etiam ἀμίαντον & ἂσβεστον ipsum dictum statuunt. Plinius lib. 36. N. H. cap. 19. Amiantus alumini similis igni nihil deperdit. Filatur hic lapis in taedas, quae ignibus iniectae ardent quidem, sed flammis invictae splendescentes inde magis exeunt quàm possent aquis. Pulchra haec est imago felicitatis aeternae, nullo unquam tempore igni periturae, cum contrà omnes hereditates terrenae in fine seculi igni corrumpendae sint.

Tertiò vocat ἀμάραντον. μαραίνεσθαι significat marcescere, marcidum seu flaccidum reddi, usurpatur inter caetera de floribus, ut tradit Eustathius, inde ἀμάραντος peculiariter vocatur quidam flos, à Galeno heliochrysi nomine appellatus, radice fulva, bulbosa, ferulaceo caule, pedali altitudine, foliis ocimo longioribus, spicâ purpureâ, inodora; sic dictus, quia non marcescit, decerptus enim asservatur & cum defecêre cuncti flores, madefactus aquâ reviviscit, & collectus furnique tepore siccatus reconditur ad coronarios hyemis usus, nec nitorem gratiamque coloris amittit. Plin. lib. 21. Nat. Hist. cap. 8. Mirum in eo, gaudere decerpi & latius renasei; mirumque, postquam defecêre cuncti flores, madefactus aquâ reviviscit & hybernas coronas facit. Summa eius Natura in nomine est, appellato, quoniam non marcescat. Dioscorides lib. 4. cap. 47. Amarantus purpureus ex eo sic dictus, quod flores eius nunquam marcescant. Helichryson vero dictum, quod ad Solis repercussum comantibus in orbem florum foliis fulgorem auri prae se ferat. Ab hoc flore nunquam marcescente ducta est metaphora, quando Petrus haereditatem coelestem vocat ἀμάραντον, id quod ex huius Epist. cap. 5. v. 4. apparet, ubi eandem appellat ἀμαράντινον τῆς δόξης στέφανον. Dicitur enim corona sive sertum amarantinum, quod est ex amaranto, sicut etiam Philostratus in Heroicis ἀμαραντίνους στεφάνους. dixit. Nam adhiberi solitum amarantum coronis sive sertis, constat non solum ex adducto Plinii loco, sed etiam ex Tibullo lib. 3. eleg. 4. Ut cum contexunt amarantis alba puellae Lilia. Quidam inter ἀμάραντον & ἀμαράντινον hoc discrimen constituunt, quod ἀμάραντος significat non marcescens;ἀμαράντινον vero immarcescibile, sed ἀμαράντινος non formatur ex ἀμάραντος, quatenus est nomen appellativum, sed quatenus est nomen certi floris proprium, ut reddendum sit, reportabitis coronam gloriae amarantinam, quae est ex vero & precioso amaranto, quae magis est immarcescibilis, quàm ea, quae est ex amaranto. Sap. 6. v. 12. sapientia vocatur ἀμάραντος, quia eius possessio auferri nequit. Quando ergo Petrus hereditatem coelestem vocat ἀμάραντον, significat. 1. Quòd vigorem, gratiam ac pulchritudinem suam instar floris amaranti semper retineat. Ut enim in vita aeterna non erit noxApoc. 21. v. 25. ita quoque nulla ibi erit hyems floribus adversa, sed ver perpetuum. 2. Quòd gaudium vitae aeternae semper erit novum ac recens, ut eius nunquam nobis obrepat fastidium, sicut herba amarantus madefacta aquis reviviscit. 3. Quodque proinde longissmè differat à voluptatibus huius seculi, quae instar florum citò marcescunt. Iob. 14. v. 2.Psal. 90. v. 6.Psal. 103. v. 5. & 6.1. Petr. 1 v. 24.

Quartò hanc haereditatem dicit conservatam nobis in coelis. τετηρημένην ponitur in forma perfecti, non in forma praesentis, quod esset τηρουμένην: significat igitur, gloriam illam coelestis haereditatis iam olim, videlicet ab origine mundi, imò ab omni aeternitate esse paratam, conservatam & asservatam, sicut parentes liberis suis thesauros in haereditatem suo tempore adeundam reponere & asservare solent. Matth. 25. v. 34.possidete regnum paratum vobis à mundi origine.2. Thes. 2. v. 13.elegit nos DEUS ab initio ad salutem. Addit autem, hanc haereditatem conservari in coelis, ut ostendat 1. Haereditatis huius excellentiam, quod non sit terrena & transitoria sed coelestis & aeterna haereditas. 2. Eiusdem certitudinem. Non in nostris manibus, sed in DEI manu haereditas illa nobis conservatur, ex illius manu nemo vel nos vel haereditatem illam nostram eripere poterit. Matth. 6. v. 20.Iohan. 10. v. 28. 3. Eiusdem firmitatem ac perpetuitatem. Haereditas terrae Canaan erat hostium violentiae ac depraedationi exposita, quia erat haereditas in terra, sed coelestis haereditas nullâ hostium violentiâ nobis poterit eripi, quia asservatur in coelis. Terrena haereditas calliditate hominum saepius intervertitur, sed de coelesti haereditate, utpote in coelis asservata, hoc non est metuendum. 4. Potest ergo hoc membrum accipi tanquam αἰτιολογικὸν praecedentium, inde enim atque ideo haereditas filiorum Dei est incorruptibilis, incontaminata & immarcescibilis, quia est coelestis haereditas, quia in coelo asservatur, in quo nec corruptio, nec sordes, nec marcor ullum habent locum. 5. simul etiam innuit Petrus, felicitatem & gloriam illius haereditatis adhuc nobis esse inconspicuam, quae enim in coelis sunt, ea ab oculis & sensibus nostris sunt remota, unde statim addit v. 5.salutem sive haereditatem illam paratam esse revelari in tempore novissimo, cum quo congruit illud Apostolicum Colos. 3. v. 3.Vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deov. 4.cum autem Christus apparuerit vita vestra, tunc & vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria. Itemque illud Iohannis 1. Epist. 3. v. 2.Nunc Filii Dei (& haeredes vitae aeternae) sumus, sed nondum apparuit, quid erimus.

Denique addit, haereditatem illam conservari nobis. Vulgata versio reddidit in nobis, Sed Graeci Codices plerique habent εἰς ἡμᾶς i. e. ἡμῖν nobis, per usitatum Hebraismum, cuius exempla etiam in hac ipsa Epistola occurrunt. v. 25. huius capitis, quod verbum Evangelizatum est εἰς ὑμᾶς. Erasmus reddidit erga vos. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. cap. 24. ergavos. Augustinus citat, servatam vobis, non solùm enim vulgata versio Latina, sed etiam multi codices Graeci habent pronomen secundae personae εἰς ὑμᾶς, quo modo etiam legit Bened. Arias Montanus & D. Lutherus in vers. Germ. quae lectio congruit cum v. 5. & 6. seqq. ubi Petrus personam primam, mutat in secundam. Dixerat enim v. 3.benedictus Deus, qui regeneravit nos in spem vivam, sed in v. 6. dicit, in quo exultatis, videlicet, ut viam sibi pararet ad sequentem exhortationem in v. 13. cui magis congruit pronomen secundae personae. Sive ergo in v. 4. legamus ἡμᾶς, sive ὑμᾶς, res eodem redit, prior lectio magis congruit cum vers. 3. praecedente, posterior cum v. 6. sequente, ac utrobique sensus est, quod haereditas illa coelestis asservetur illis, quos Deus regeneravit, & in silios suos adoptavit.

## 1:5
WHO ARE KEPT BY THE POWER OF GOD THROUGH FAITH UNTO SALVATION READY TO BE REVEALED IN THE LAST TIME.

The second benefit is divine preservation in dangers. You who are kept by the power of God through faith for salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. The Apostle had said, that we have been reborn into a living hope through the great mercy of God, now he adds, that we are kept by the power of God unto salvation: for it is not enough to have been made a participant of regeneration through faith, but it is required furthermore that we persevere in that faith, which preservation among so many dangers is equally as much a work of divine power and mercy as regeneration, whence in the Greek text τοὺς φρουρουμένους placed in the accusative is expressly joined with the participle ἀναγεννήσας. He had said, that a most ample inheritance is kept in the heavens for believers, now he adds, who are those who shall one day be put into the plenary possession of that inheritance, namely those who persevere in the true faith, through which they have been written as heirs of eternal life. The Apostle also meets a tacit objection. God has begotten us again into an incorruptible inheritance. But many of those who are reborn of water and the Spirit fall away from that inheritance again. What does it profit that the inheritance is kept in heaven, when on earth we are exposed to the snares of enemies and to various dangers altogether? The Apostle answers, you are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation. Some establish that διὰ πίστεως is placed for ἐν πίστει, so that the sense may be, it is to be attributed to divine power as the preserving cause that you remain stable in faith and persevere in standing upon CHRIST the rock of salvation. This sense has nothing inconvenient, meanwhile the customary meaning of the particle διὰ can be best retained, so that the sense becomes, you are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, because divine power preserves us unto salvation not immediately, nor from some absolute decree of God, but mediately through faith. For just as He regenerates us not immediately nor from an absolute decree, but through faith, so also He preserves us unto salvation through faith, for which faith both to be kindled, and to be preserved and increased, the word and Sacraments are divinely constituted means. Therefore the Syrian notably rendered [consult facsimile image] by the power of God and by faith you are kept, using the same preposition [consult facsimile image] in both places, and the copulative and .

Of GOD and faith joining. Meanwhile, there is no doubt that the Apostle, by a singular plan, did not use the particle διὰ, concerning the power of GOD, but ἐν,, lest anyone should think that the divine power is an instrument through which GOD performs that preservation, since it is itself the efficient and preserving cause. The word φρουρεῖσθαι properly signifies to be fortified with garrisons, for φρουρὰ signifies a guard, or a military garrison, φρουρὸς is a guard or a garrison soldier, so called by crasis, as if προυρὸς from προυράω I look forward. Herodian φρουρουμένη καὶ κεκλεισμένη γενναίὡς ἡ πόλις a city well fortified with garrisons. 2. Corinth. 11. v. 32. The Ethnarch of King Aretas ἐφρούρει was guarding the city with a military garrison. Iudith. 3. v. 7. 3. Esdr. 4. vers. 56. is used in the same signification. It is signified, therefore, that the pious are fortified by the power of GOD, as if by a certain most strong garrison, against the assaults and impressions of spiritual enemies, and it is tacitly insinuated that the pious, regenerated by the grace of GOD and written as heirs of eternal life, have in this life various and most powerful enemies who attempt to deprive them of that inheritance of eternal life; for where there is φρουρᾶ or a need for a military garrison, there is fear of hostile violence. But to this violence of enemies is opposed not human, but divine custody, and not just any, but the most vigilant care of GOD, such as is accustomed to be that of soldiers placed in garrisons and watches against hostile irruption. The same metaphorical signification of this word occurs Phil. 4. vers. 7. the peace of GOD φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν shall guard your hearts, against every kind of anxieties and temptations, on which passage Ambrose comments thus: He said this because when one has peace with GOD, he does not fear any adverse mind. For everyone who loves GOD in CHRIST JESUS is safe by the peace of GOD. Galat. 3. vers. 23. before faith came ὑπὸ νόμου ἐφρουρούμεθα we were kept under the guard of the law, where ἐξηγητικῶς is added συγκεκλεισμένη, for cities fortified with military garrisons against enemies are also accustomed to be kept enclosed, as is gathered from the cited passage of Herodian. We are said, however, to be guarded by the power of GOD through faith εἰς σωτηρίαν. because what he had said before εἰς κληρονομίαν, he says here εἰς σωτηρίαν, so that he may show that those illustrious praises are to be understood concerning the inheritance of eternal salvation. Furthermore, προσδιορισμὸν that εἰς σωτηρίαν, some join with the word ἀναγεννήσας, so that by apposition it may be joined with that which He had said εἰς κληρονομίαν and let the sense be, he has regenerated us unto an incorruptible inheritance, that is, unto salvation, or, which is the salvation to be revealed in its own time. Some refer it to the word πίστεως, so that the sense may be, GOD guards you through faith εἰς σωτηρίαν i. e. σωτήριον through that saving faith, by which you believe the promised eternal life and hope that it will come to you in Christ. But anyone sees that that εἰς σωτηρίαν is most simply and without any violence joined with the participle φρουρουμένους, so that the sense may be, by divine power through faith you are guarded unto salvation, lest by the force or fraud of enemies it be snatched away from you and intercepted. Moreover, he says that that salvation is prepared to be revealed in the last time. By time ἔσχατον he understands the end of the age, or the day of judgment, which is otherwise called ἔσχάτη ἡμέρα John 6. v. 39. & seqq. c. 11. v. 24.chap. 12. v. 48. In certain places of Scripture ἔσχατος χρόνος or ἔσχάτη ὥρα is called the last age of the world, which extends from the first to the second coming of Christ, 2. Tim. 3. v. 1.Hebr. 1. v. 1.James 5. v. 3.1. Peter 1. v. 20.2. Peter 3. v. 3.1. John 2. v. 18.Jude v. 18. But in this place the extreme or end of that age is signified, for then the salvation prepared by GOD for believers will be revealed. By the phrase ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι the Apostle looks back to the preceding words τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς. For it signifies that that salvation and inheritance is indeed prepared for us in the heavens, kept and stored up like a most precious treasure, meanwhile not yet revealed, because it is still kept hidden in GOD Col. 3. v. 3. Your life is hidden with Christ in GOD v. 4. but when Christ shall have appeared, your life, then you also shall appear with him in glory; 1. John 3. v. 2. Now we are children of GOD, but it has not yet appeared what we shall be, which places are clearly parallel to this one of ours. But at the end of the age it will be revealed not only to the elect themselves, but also to all Angels and men, who they are for whom that inheritance was prepared by GOD, which in this life is still hidden by reason of the individuals. The riches and glory of that inheritance will also be revealed then, which likewise at this time still lie hidden.

It is asked in this place, since both regeneration is a work of divine power, and preservation among dangers is a work of divine mercy, why does the Apostle attribute regeneration to divine mercy, and preservation to divine power? Resp. these are not to be taken oppositely or exclusively but subordinately ἐξοχικῶς; Therefore, regeneration is truly attributed to divine mercy, and preservation to divine power, because in regeneration divine mercy, and in preservation divine power, exerts itself more and exhibits itself to be seen.

Ἐναντιοφανία. You are kept by the power of GOD through faith unto salvation. But many of the reborn, even among those to whom Peter wrote, fell away from salvation again. Resp. Divine power does not preserve believers in faith unto salvation immediately, nor by an absolute decree, but through the same means by which it first kindled faith in them, namely through the hearing of the word and the use of the Sacraments, to which in the reborn must be added daily prayer for the preservation and increase of faith, and the flight from sins against conscience, by which faith, the grace of GOD, and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit are shaken off.

Ἔλεγχοι. 1. Peter teaches that we are kept by divine power unto salvation. The Pope teaches that perseverance is the merit of our works. For if good works truly merit the increase of grace, eternal life, and the attainment of eternal life itself, and even the increase of glory, as the Council of Trent defines, sess. 6, can. 32, then certainly good works also merit perseverance. Pererius, however, writes more correctly in this regard in Disp. 26, on chapter 14 of John, p. 401: A man cannot properly and worthily merit perseverance in good until the end, but just as the gift of initial grace is gratuitous, and not on account of any merit of man properly so called, so also the preservation of that grace until the end is a gift of GOD, in no way comparable to the merits of man.

2. Peter says, we are kept through faith unto salvation, which he explains in verse nine thus, the end of our faith is the salvation of souls. The Pope teaches, salvation is given on account of the merits of our works.

3. Peter teaches that believers are preserved by divine power unto salvation, from which it follows that they ought not to doubt concerning their perseverance and salvation, but to determine with certainty that they are to be preserved by divine power through faith unto salvation. 2 Tim. 1, v. 12 GOD is able to keep that which is committed unto me. For there are three pillars upon which the certainty of salvation rests. 1. The omnipotence of GOD. 2. The faithfulness of GOD. 1 Cor. 10, v. 13 3. The good will of GOD. Phil. 2, v. 13 Bernard, sermon 3 on the fragments of the seven miseries: I consider three things, in which my whole hope consists, charity of adoption, the truth of the promise, the power of the restoration, etc. I know whom I have believed, and I am certain, because in excessive love He adopted me, because He is truthful in the promise, because He is powerful in the exhibition. The Pope teaches that one must doubt concerning perseverance and salvation. Estius objects, that these things pertain to the elect, not to each one of the faithful. For it is said to individuals, you stand by faith, do not be high-minded, but fear. I respond: individuals and faithful elect are not opposites, but subordinate. Therefore, these things pertain to the elect and to individual true believers, but by a certain reason and order, which we shall explain shortly.

Ἐκδίκησις 1. The Calvinists, from the fact that we are said to be kept by divine power through faith unto salvation, wish to prove that true faith cannot be lost again, but always has perseverance joined to it, and those once reborn cannot fall away from salvation again. I respond: the certainty of election and perseverance is not absolute, depending on an absolute decree of GOD, but is ordered, that is, it respects the means divinely ordained, through which GOD wills to increase and preserve faith, and it depends on the purpose of GOD, manifested to us in the Gospel. That purpose of GOD concerning our salvation is described in the Scriptures in such a way that He wills to preserve by His power through faith unto salvation those who hear the word, use the Sacraments, persist in prayers and the pursuit of piety, and avoid sins against conscience: whence the elect θετικῶς are described in such a way that they remain in the word of ChristJohn 8. v. 31. that they remain in the faith grounded and stableCol. 1. v. 23. that they hold faith and a good conscience1. Tim. 1. v. 19. that they remain faithful even unto deathApoc. 2. v. 10. that they hold the beginning of faith firm unto the endHebr. 3. v. 6. that they persist in goodnessRom. 11. v. 22. ἀρνητικῶς they are described in such a way that they do not withdraw themselves againHebr. 10. v. 38. that they do not fail the grace of Godchap. 12. v. 15. that they do not turn themselves again from the holy commandment2. Peter 2. v. 21.

2. From the fact that salvation is said to be revealed in the last time, the Anabaptists and others gather that the souls of the blessed do not enjoy the beatific vision of God before the day of judgment. I respond: one must distinguish between the salvation of souls, and the salvation of the whole composite. The souls of the blessed arrive at the beatific vision of GOD immediately after death, but the whole composite, and thus the soul united to the body, will aspire to it only at the end of the age. Furthermore, one must distinguish between the possession of salvation, and the revelation of the same. The souls of the pious are made partakers of salvation immediately after death, nay even in have eternal life in this life 1 John 5 v. 12 are saved by grace through faith Eph. 2 v. 8Tit. 3 v. 5 but the revelation of salvation will finally follow on the last day.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. No one is able to be kept in good things by the power of his own liberty, but the help of Him from whom we have received the beginning of a good action must be sought through all things. Bede in this place.

2. Against the adversities of this life we comfort ourselves with salvation stored up in the heavens, and to be revealed in its own time.

3. Our salvation is stored up not in our hands, but in the hands of God; nor is it preserved by human, but by divine power. Therefore Satan will not be able to snatch it from us, much less tyrants and persecutors.

4. The firmer the defense of a city, the greater the confidence in the souls of the citizens surrounded by a siege. But by as much as God is more powerful than man, by so much is the defense of our salvation firmer than any human one.

5. We are kept by divine power unto salvation, but through faith. Therefore let us apprehend by faith the promise concerning the preservation of our salvation to be expected from divine power. He who casts off faith through sins against conscience, renounces the divine power that preserves salvation, and makes shipwreck of salvation.

6. However various and powerful the enemies of our salvation may be; the flesh, which cries out, I will fail; the world, which cries out, I will deceive; Satan, which cries out, I will snatch away; yet divine power is something greater and more powerful than all the violence of those enemies.

Latin:

QUI IN VIRTUTE DEI CUSTODIMINI PER FIDEM IN SALUTEM PARATAM REVELARI IN TEMPORE NOVISSIMO.

Alterum beneficium est, divina in periculis conservatio. Qui in virtute DEI custodimini per fidem in salutem paratam revelari in tempore novissimo. Dixerat Apostolus, nos per magnam DEI misericordiam diam in spem vivam esse regenitos, iam subiungit, per Dei potentiam nos conservari ad salutem: non enim sufficit, regenerationis per fidem esse participem factum, sed requiritur insuper, ut in fide illa perseveremus, quae conservatio inter tot pericula aequè ac regeneratio est opus divinae virtutis & misericordiae, unde in Graeco textu τοὺς φρουρουμένους in accusativo positum cum participio ἀναγεννήσας disertè coniungitur. Dixerat, in coelis amplissimam haereditatem credentibus servari, iam subiungit, quinam in haereditatis illius plenariam possessionem aliquando sint immittendi, videlicet illi, qui in vera fide, per quam haeredes vitae aeternae scripti sunt, perseverant. Occurrit etiam Apostolus tacitae obiectioni. Regenuit nos Deus in haereditatem incorruptibilem. Sed multi eorum, qui ex aqua & Spiritu regeniti, haereditate illâ iterum excidunt. Quid prodest, haereditatem in coelo servari, cum in terra hostium insidiis, ac variis omninò periculis simus expositi? Respondet Apostolus, virtute Dei per fidem custodimini in salutem.διὰ πίστεως quidam positum statuunt pro ἐν πίστει, ut sit sensus, virtuti divina tanquam causae conservanti tribuendum, quod in fide manetis stabiles, ac CHRISTO salutis petrae perseveranter insistitis. Hic sensus nihil habet incommodi, interim usitata significatio particulae διὰ optimè retineri potest, ut fit sensus, virtute DEI per fidem custodimini in salutem, quia virtus divina non immediatè, nec ex absoluto quodam DEI decreto, sed mediatè per fidem nos in salutem conservat. Ut enim non immediatè nec ex absoluto decreto, sed per fidem nos regenerat, ita quoque per fidem nos in salutem conservat, cuius fidei tum accendendae, tum conservandae & augendae media divinitus constituta sunt verbum & Sacramenta. Proinde Syrus notanter reddidit [consult facsimile image]per virtutem Dei & per fidem custodimini, utrobique eandem praepositionem [consult facsimile image] adhibens, & per copulativam virtutem.

DEI & fidem coniungens. Interim dubium non est, Apostolum, singulari consilio de virtute DEI non fuisse usum particulâ διὰ, sed ἐν, ne quis cogitaret, virtutem divinam esse instrumentum, per quod conservationem illam DEUS perficit, cum sit ipsa efficiens & conservans causa. Verbum φρουρεῖσθαι propriè significat praesidiis muniri,φρουρὰ enim significat custodiam, sive praesidium militare,φρουρὸς est custos seu miles praesidiarius, sic dictus per crasin, q. προυρὸς à προυράωprospicio. Herodianus φρουρουμένη καὶ κεκλεισμένη γενναίὡς ἡ πόλιςurbs praesidiis probe munit a.2. Corinth. 11. v. 32.Ethnarcha Regis Aretaeἐφρούρειpraesidio militari muniebat civitatem.Iudith. 3. v. 7. 3. Esdr. 4. vers. 56. in eadem significatione usurpatur. Significatur igitur, pios virtute DEI, velut praesidio quodam fortissimo muniri contra spiritualium hostium oppugnationes & impressiones, ac tacitè insinuatur, pios DEI gratia regenitos & haeredes vitae aeternae scriptos, in hac vita varios & potentissimos hostes habere, qui haereditate illa vitae aeternae ipsos conentur privare, ubi enim φρουρᾶ sive militari praesidio opus, ibi metus est ab hostili violentia. Sed huic hostium violentiae opponitur non humana, sed divina custodia, nec qualiscunque, sed vigilantissima DEI cura, qualis solet esse militum, in praesidiis & excubiis contra hostilem irruptionem collocatorum. Eadem significatio huius verbi metaphorica occurrit Phil. 4. vers. 7.pax DEIφρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶνcustodiat corda vestra, contra omnis generis anxietates & tentationes, in quem locum Ambros. sic commentatur. Hoc ideo dixit, quia cum DEO qui habet pacem, non timet omnem mentem adversam. Tutus enim est pace DEI omnis diligens DEUM in CHRISTO IESU.Galat. 3. vers. 23.priusquam veniret fidesὑπὸ νόμου ἐφρουρούμεθαsub legis praesidio tenebamur, ubiἐξηγητικῶς additur συγκεκλεισμένη, urbes enim praesidiis militaribus contra hostes munitae, solent etiam conclusae teneri, ut ex adducto loco Herodiani colligitur. Dicimur autem virtute DEI per fidem custodiriεἰς σωτηρίαν. quod prius dixerat εἰς κληρονομίαν, hîc dicit εἰς σωτηρίαν, ut ostendat, de haereditate salutis aeternae praeclara illa elogia esse intelligenda. Caeterùm προσδιορισμὸν illum εἰς σωτηρίαν, quidam coniungunt cum verbo ἀναγεννήσας, ut per appositionem iungatur cum eo quod dixerat εἰς κληρονομίαν ac sit sensus, regeneravit nos ad haereditatem incorruptibilem, hoc est, ad salutem, five, quae est salus suo tempore revelanda. Quidam referunt ad vocem πίστεως, ut sis sensus, custodit vos DEUS per fidemεἰς σωτηρίαν i. e. σωτήριονper salvificam illam fidem, quâ vitam aternam promissam creditis & in Christo eam vobis obventuram speratis. Sed quilibet videt, illud εἰς σωτηρίαν simplicissimè & sine ulla violentia coniungi cum participio φρουρουμένους, ut sit sensus, virtute divina per fidem custodimini in salutem, ne per vim vel fraudem hostium ea vobis eripiatur ac intervertatur. Salutem autem illam dicit paratam revelari in tempore novissimo. Per tempusἔσχατον intelligit finem seculi, sive diem iudicii, quod aliàs vocatur ἔσχάτη ἡμέραIohan. 6. v. 39. & seqq. c. 11. v. 24.cap. 12. v. 48. In quibusdam Scripturae locis ἔσχατος χρόνος vel ἔσχάτη ὥρα dicitur ultima mundi aetas, quae à primo usque ad secundum Christi adventum protenditur, 2. Tim. 3. v. 1.Hebr. 1. v. 1.Iacob. 5. v. 3.1. Petr. 1. v. 20.2. Petr. 3. v. 3.1. Ioh. 2. v. 18.Iudae v. 18. Sed hoc loco aetatis illius extremum sive finis significatur, tunc enim salus credentibus à DEO parata revelabitur. Per phrasin ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι respicit Apostolus ad verba praecedentia τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς. Significat enim, salutem ac haereditatem illam esse quidem in coelis nobis paratam, asservatam & preciosissimi thesauri instar repositam, interim nondum revelatam, quia adhuc abscondita in DEO asservatur Col. 3. v. 3.Vita vestra est abscondita cum Christo in DEOv. 4.cùm autem Christus apparuerit vita vestra, tunc & vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria;1. Ioh. 3. v. 2.Nunc filii DEI sumus, sed nondum apparuit quid erimus, quae loca huic nostro sunt planè parallela. In fine autem seculi revelabitur non solùm ipsis electis, sed etiam omnibus Angelis & hominibus, quinam sint quibus illa haereditas à DEO parata, quod in hac vita ratione individuorum adhuc absconditum. Revelabuntor etiam tunc divitiae & gloria illius haereditatis, quae itidem hoc tempore adhuc latent abscondita.

Quaeritur hoc loco, cùm & regeneratio sit divinae virtutis, & conservatio inter pericula sit divinae misericordiae opus, cur Apostolus regenerationem divinae misericordiae, conservationem divinae virtuti tribuat? Resp. haec non sunt accipienda oppositè vel exclusivè sed subordinatè & ἐξοχικῶς; ideò vero divinae misericordiae tribuitur regeneratio, divinae virtuti conservatio, quia in regeneratione divina misericordia, in conservatione divina virtus sese magis exerit ac conspiciendam q. exhibet.

Ἐναντιοφανία.Virtute DEI custodimini per fidem in salutem. Sed multi renatorum etiam inter eos, ad quos Petrus scripsit, salute iterum exciderunt. Resp. Virtus divina non immediatè, nec ex absoluto decreto credentes in fide ad salutem conservat, sed per eadem media, per quae fidem in illis primùm accendit, videlicet per verbi auditum & Sacramentorum usum, ad quae in renatis accedere debet quotidiana oratio, pro fidei conservatione & incremento, ac fuga peccatorum contra conscientiam, quibus fides, DEI gratia & Spiritus sancti inhabitatio excutitur.

Ἔλεγχοι. 1. Petrus docet, nos virtute divinâ custodiri ad salutem. Papa docet, perseverantiam esse operum nostrorum meritum. Quod si enim bona opera verè merentur augmentum gratiae, vitam aeternam, & ipsius vitae aeternae consecutionem, atque etiam gloriae augmentum, ut definit Concil. Trident. sess. 6. can. 32. utique etiam bona opera merentur perseverantiam. Rectiùs tamen hac in parte scribit Pererius Disp. 26. in cap. 14. Ioh. p. 401. Non potest homo propriè ac dignè mereri perseverantiam in bono usque ad finem, sed quemadmodum primae gratiae donatio gratuita est, nec propter ullum hominis meritum propriè dictum, ita & conservatio ipsius gratiae usque ad finem, donum DEI est, meritis hominis nequaquam comparabile.

2. Petrus dicit, per fidem nos custodiri ad salutem, id quod versu nono sic explicat, finem fidei nostrae esse animarum salutem. Papa docet, salutem dari propter operum nostrorum merita.

3. Petrus docet, virtute divinâ credentes conservari ad salutem, ex quo consequens est, quòd de perseverantia ac salute sua non debeant dubitare, sed certò statuere, quòd virtute divinâ perfidem in salutem sint conservandi. 2. Tim. 1. v. 12.potens est DEUS, depositum nostrum servare. Tria enim sunt fulcra, quibus certitudo salutis innititur. 1. DEI omnipotentia. 2. DEI fidelitas. 1. Cor. 10. v. 13. 3. DEI bona voluntas Phil. 2. v. 13. Bernhardus serm. 3. de fragm. septem miser. Tria considero, in quibus tota spes mea consistit, caritatem adoptionis, veritatem promissionis, potestatem redditionis &c. Scio, cui credidi, & certus sum, quia in caritate nimia adoptavit me, quia verax est in promissione, quia potens in exhibitione. Papa docet, de perseverantia & salute esse dubitandum. Excipit Estius, pertinere haec ad electos, non ad unumquemque fidelium. Singulis enim dici, tu fide stas, noli altum sapere, sed time. Resp. singuli & fideles electi non sunt opposita, sed subordinata. Pertinent ergò haec ad electos & singulos verè fideles, sed certâ ratione & ordine, quem mox explicabimus.

Ἐκδίκησις 1. Calviniani ex eo, quod virtute divinâ per fidem ad salutem custodiri dicimur, evincere volunt, veram fidem non posse iterum amitti, sed semper adiunctam habere perseverantiam, ac semel renatos non posse iterum salute excidere. Resp. certitudo electionis & perseverantiae non est absoluta, ex absoluto DEI decreto dependens, sed est ordinata, h. e. respicit media divinitùs ordinata, per quae DEUS fidem vult augere & conservare, ac dependet à DEI proposito, in Evangelio nobis manifestato. Illud propositum DEI de salute nostra in Scripturis sic deseribitur, quòd verbum audientes, Sacramentis utentes, in precibus & studio pietatis persistentes, ac peccata contra conscientiam caventes, velit suâ virtute per fidem ad salutem conservare: unde electi θετικῶς sic deseribuntur, quòd maneant in sermone ChristiIoh. 8. v. 31. quòd permaneant in fide fundati & stabilesCol. 1. v. 23. quòd retineant fidem & bonam conscientiam1. Tim. 1. v. 19. quòd fideles maneant usque ad mortemApoc. 2. v. 10. quòd initium fidei usque ad finem firmum retineantHebr. 3. v. 6. quòd persistant in bonoRom. 11. v. 22.ἀρνητικῶς sic describuntur, quòd se iterum non subducantHebr. 10. v. 38. quòd non desint gratiae Deicap. 12. v. 15. quòd se non avertant iterum à sancto praecepto2. Petr. 2. v. 21.

2. Ex eo, quod salus dicitur revelanda in tempore novissimo, colligunt Anabaptistae & alii, quòd animae beatorum ante diem iudicii non fruantur beatificâ Dei visione. Resp. distinguendum inter salutem animarum, & inter salutem totius compositi. Animae beatorum statim post mortem perveniunt ad beatificam DEI visionem, sed totum compositum, adeoque anima corpori unita, in fine demum seculi ad eam adspirabit. Deinde distinguendum est inter salutis possessionem, & eiusdem revelationem. Piorum animae statim post mortem redduntur salutis participes, quinimò etiam in hac vita habent vitam aeternam 1. Ioh. 5. v. 12. gratiâ salvati sunt per fidem Eph. 2. v. 8.Tit. 3. v. 5. sed revelatio salutis demùm sequetur in die novissimo.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Nullus suae libertatis potentia custodiri valet in bonis, sed illius quaerendum per omnia auxilium, à quo initium bonae actionis accepimus. Beda in h. l.

2. Contra huius vitae adversa solemur nos salute in coelis repositâ, ac suo tempore revelanda.

3. Salus nostra non in nostris, sed in Dei manibus reposita; nec humanâ, sed divinâ virtute conservatur. Ergò Satan eam nobis non poterit eripere, multò minùs Tyranni & persecutores.

4. Quò firmius est urbis praesidium, eò maior fiducia in animis civium obsidione cinctorum. At quantò Deus potentior homine, tantò firmius est salutis nostrae praesidium quovis humano.

5. Virtute divinâ custodimur ad salutem, sed per fidem. Ergò fide apprehendamus promissionem de conservatione nostrae salutis à virtute divinâ. expectandâ. Qui fidem per peccata contra conscientiam excutit, virtuti divinae salutis conservatrici renunciat, & salutis naufragium facit.

6. Utut varii & potentes sint salutis nostrae hostes; caro, quae clamat, ego deficiam; mundus, qui clamat, ego decipiam; Satan, qui clamat, ego eripiam; tamen divina virtus omni hostium istorum violentiâ maius quid est ac potentius.

## 1:6
IN WHICH YOU REJOICE FOR A LITTLE WHILE NOW, IF IT IS NECESSARY TO BE SORROWFUL IN VARIOUS TEMPTATIONS.

The third benefit is solid consolation in adversities. After the Apostle had celebrated that excellent benefit of the Gospel, that those believing in Christ preached in the Gospel are divinely preserved in dangers, he adds another equally great benefit, which is solid consolation in adversities, which he describes by its fruit and effect, which is exultation. Thus therefore the discourse rises. God not only preserves those believing in Christ preached in the Gospel in dangers, but also by the same word of the Gospel in all adversities he comforts. He also meets a silent objection. If they are believers, sons of GOD and co-heirs of Christ, why does He permit so many adversities to befall them, and for them to be saddened in them? The Apostle answers, that GOD not only permits by a salutary counsel that adversities befall believers, but also sends consolation into them, through which they may be preserved and lifted up in adversities. 2. Cor. 1. v. 4. GOD comforts us in all our tribulation &c. v. 5. for as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ our consolation abounds. Finally, since in the verse immediately preceding v. 5. the Apostle made mention of faith, he now adds spiritual joy, which is the fruit of faith. Rom. 5. v. 2. through Christ we have access by faith into grace. v. 3. and not only this, but we also glory in tribulations.

Some refer the particle ἐν ᾧ to what immediately precedes, namely to the last time, so that the sense may be, now indeed you are saddened in afflictions, but then in the time, to wit, the last, you exult i. e. you will exult, so that the present is placed for the future according to the Hebrew idiom. Oecumenius in his commentary and Luther in his German version follow this sense. In welchen ihr euch freuen werdet! This exposition agrees with the words of Christ Luke 6. v. 21. Blessed are you who hunger now, for you shall be satisfied. Blessed are you who weep now, for you shall laugh. But because the Apostle is engaged in an enumeration of the benefits which befall those who believe the Gospel in this life, and because true believers will not only exult on the last day, but also in this life glory and exult in the midst of tribulations Rom. 5. v. 3., therefore the verb ἀγαλλιᾶσθε placed in the present is most rightly said to retain its native meaning, in which way Oecumenius also reads, and many Latin Manuscript Codices render it. From which it is a consequence that the particle ἐν ᾧ is referred not only to the word immediately preceding, namely καιρῷ ἔσχάτῳ, but to the whole complex of the preceding member, and that this little verse is deduced from the preceding πορισματικῶς by a certain manner of inference. Because God according to His great mercy has regenerated you into a living hope, into an incorruptible inheritance &c. reserved in heaven, and because you are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time, therefore you also exult. For those excellent benefits of GOD exhibited to believers in Christ provide a most ample harvest of spiritual joy, and matter for exulting even in this life supply them, as immediately follows v. 8. believing you exult with joy inexpressible. Some take the word ἀγαλλιᾶσθε as placed in the imperative. In which exult. But the Apostle does not yet descend to exhortation, but is still engaged in the enumeration of the spiritual benefits divinely conferred upon those believing the Gospel, therefore it is to be taken in the indicative form ἀγαλλιᾶσθε. There is, however, great emphasis in the word ἀγαλλιᾶσθε.. For it signifies to testify to the internal joy of the heart by countenance, voice, and gestures, and consequently it is more than to rejoice. Hence Christ Matth. 5. vers. 12. joins these two χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, not only rejoice inwardly, but also attest the interior joy of the heart with external motions and signs, show joy with external gestures and leaping. They are also joined 1. Petr. 4. vers. 13.Apoc. 19. vers. 7. meanwhile because external motions without interior affection are hypocritical, therefore τῷ πνέυματι ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι we ought Luc. 1. vers. 47.cap. 10. v. 21. the LXX use for גול which signifies to roll, when someone opens the joy of the heart with leaping, exultation, and other external signs. Psalm. 14. vers. 8.Cant. 1. vers. 3.Esa. 25. vers. 9. in which places and elsewhere here and there ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι καὶ εὐφραίνεσθαι are joined. Likewise for הלל he lifted up his voice on high with jubilation and boasting Esa. 41. vers. 16.Ierem. 49. vers. 4. for עלז he gestured and leaped for joy, 2. Reg 1. v. 20.Psal. 59. v. 6.Psal. 67. v. 5. etc. for עלץ a word of related meaning and writing 1. Paral. 16. v. 32.Psal. 9. v. 2. for רנן he exclaimed for joy Psal. 5. v. 13.Psal. 19. v. 5. etc. The sense therefore is, that the pious, weighing μέγιστα καὶ τίμια those things which in the Gospel are partly promised, partly already given to them 2. Petr. 1. v. 4. may rejoice intimately in their heart, and externally declare that joy of theirs with words and gestures. The Apostle, however, amplifies that exultation by an antithesis of sadness arising from afflictions. ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, he says, ὀλίγον ἄρτι (εἰ δέον ἐστὶ) λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς. τὸ ὀλίγον some think it added to diminish the magnitude of the afflictions, but it is more correctly said that it was added to express the brief duration of the afflictions, just as Luther also rendered it, eine kleine Zeit/ a parallel passage is held 1. Epist. 5 v. 10. THE GOD of all grace who called you into His eternal glory in CHRIST JESUS ὀλίγον having suffered for a short time, He Himself will perfect you, where There is an opposition between αἰώνιον & ὀλίγον.. The sense, therefore, is that those afflictions, by which they are saddened, will not last long, but will cease shortly. Προσδιορισμὸς, εἰ δέον ἐστι is distinguished by a parenthesis from the following expression λυπηθέντες; Moreover, δέον ἐστὶ is placed for δεῖ, Acts 19. verse 36. if it must be so done, if there is need, Luth. Wo es sein soll. The Latins say, if the matter so requires. Peter himself in the following chapter verse 17. explains it thus, εἰ θέλει τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. It is used in the same meaning in Philo in the book on the world. The Vulgate joins this προσδιορισμὸν with the following participle rendered by an infinitive, if it is necessary to be saddened. Bede reads in the commentary in the same way. But by this reasoning the whole sense is rendered more obscure, and in the Greek there is not the infinitive λυποῦσθαι, but the participle λυπηθέντες you exult, having been saddened a little now, that is, even if you are saddened in afflictions, nevertheless you exult. Certain codices, as also the Royal, read λυπηθέντας in the accusative, but the nominative λυπηθέντες agrees more with the context and the most approved codices. By πειρασμοὺς,, through a certain figure of metonymy, are understood afflictions, persecutions, and adversities of every kind, so called from this, that GOD through them tests his faithful in this life James 1. verse 12. 1. Peter 4. verse 12. In this meaning the word πειρασμῶν is accepted Luke 22. verse 28. Acts 20. verse 19. Galatians 4. verse 14. James 1. v. 2. 2. Peter 2. verse 9. Apocalypse 3. verse 10. He calls it πειρασμοὺς ποικίλους, as also James chapter 1. verse 2. because the pious are not pressed in this life by one kind of affliction, but are exposed to various adversities, namely hunger, the plundering of goods, infamy, exile, torments, martyrdom, and thus all things which can happen to someone in body and fortune as adverse in this life. Finally, when believers are said to be saddened in various afflictions, then the particle ἐν is not only χρονικὴ, but also αἰτιολογικὴ, for Peter does not only say this, that at the time of afflictions the pious are saddened, but also that they are affected by pain and sorrow on account of the various and manifold afflictions which happen to them because of the confession of the Gospel.

It is asked here 1. Why does Peter add 'a little now in various afflictions saddened'? Resp. 1. to show that the spiritual joy arising in the souls of the pious from the consideration of the heavenly benefits granted in Christ is not extinguished by external afflictions. 2.

so that he may sprinkle consolation against afflictions, drawn both from the brevity of their duration and from the accompanying intermission, for not only do all afflictions cease with this life, but also in this life a certain respite from afflictions happens quite often. 3. because this Epistle is directed especially to those converted from Judaism, who were still being afflicted by various persecutions from the Jews who were still unbelieving. 1. Thess. 2. vers. 14.

Q. 2. Why does he add εἰ δέον ἐστὶ? Resp. 1. so that he may show that the pious cannot be entirely immune from afflictions in this life. 2. the condition is posited as a cause, for he shows that it does not happen rashly that God sends the cross upon believers in Christ in this life.

Ἐναντιοφανία. You rejoice, being sorrowful. But how can they rejoice and be sorrowful at the same time? Resp. 1. contrary affections can have a place together in remitted degrees, but not in extreme degrees. 2. The pious are sorrowful on account of present afflictions, for they still carry around flesh and blood, nor have they put off human affections; meanwhile, they rejoice in the Spirit, looking toward the joys of eternal life that are to follow Matth. 5. v. 4.Blessed are those who mournv. 12.rejoice and be glad.Rom. 12. v. 12.Rejoicing in hope.2. Cor. 6. v. 10.As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Peter teaches, that the pious are sorrowful for a little while in this life in various afflictions. The Pope teaches, that temporal happiness is a mark of the true Church. Bellarm. lib. de Eccles. cap. 18.

2. Peter teaches that the cross sent by God is to be borne patiently, but not to be rashly sought out. εἰ δέον ἐστὶ, he says. The Pope teaches, that a man can make satisfaction for his sins through scourgings and other laborious works undertaken voluntarily, and that the same are approved by God.

Διδασκαλίαι 1. From the sense of the benefits bestowed upon us by God in Christ and through Christ, spiritual joy arises.

2. Calamities are not only to be tolerated patiently, but also joyfully Act. 5. 41.2. Cor. 8. 2.Iac. 1. 2.Rejoice, inasmuch as you are partakers of Christ's sufferings.1. Pet. 4. 12.

3. The peace of Christ surpasses all understanding Phil. 4. v. 7. because it has a place in a soul that is contrite and sorrowful on account of tribulations.

That which torments is brief, that which delights is eternal. Nothing is long-lasting which ends with this fleeting life. David did not yet spend ten full years in exile, but forty years in the kingdom 2. Sam. 5. v. 4. by this was prefigured the brevity of our sufferings and the perpetuity of the glory that is to follow.

5. Just as Christ says of himself, δεῖ it behooves the Son of Man to suffer many thingsMark 8. v. 31.Luke 9. v. 22. it behooved him to enter into his glory through sufferingLuke 24. v. 26. & 46. so also δέον ἐστί the members of Christ must be subject to the cross in this life. Rom. 8. v. 29. It is not fitting for a member to be delicate under a crucified head.

6. Let evils be αὐτόματα not αὐθαίρετος sent by divine counsel, not drawn on by human rashness.

7. Afflictions do not always nor for all people weigh equally heavily, nor is there a need, since the kinds of afflictions are various, that individuals be exercised by the same ones.

8. As the temptations of the pious are various, so also are the consolations of the Scriptures various and manifold.

Latin:

IN QUO EXULTATIS MODICUM NUNC, SI OPORTET CONTRISTARI IN VARIIS TENTATIONIBUS.

Tertium beneficium est solida in adversis consolatio. Postquam Apostolus eximium illud Evangelii beneficium celebraverat, quod credentes in Christum in Evangelio praedicatum divinitus in periculis conserventur, subiungit aliud aequè magnum beneficium, quod est solida in adversis consolatio, quam describit à fructu & effectu, qui est exultatio. Sic ergò oratio assurgit. Deus credentes in Christum in Evangelio praedicatum non tantùm in periculis conservat, sed etiam eodem Evangelii verbo in omnibus adversis consolatur. Occurrit etiam tacitae obiectioni. Si credentes sunt, DEI filii & coheredes Christi, cur permittit eis tot adversa obtingere, inque, illis contristari? Respondet Apostolus, DEUM non solùm salutari consilio permittere, ut adversa credentibus obtingant, sed etiam consolationem ipsis immittere, per quam in adversis conserventur & erigantur.2. Cor. 1. v. 4.DEUS consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra &c.v. 5.quoniam sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis, ita & per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Denique cum in versu proximè praecedente v. 5. Apostolus fidei mentionem fecerit, iam subiungit laetitiam spiritualem, quae est fidei fructus. Rom. 5. v. 2. per Christum habemus accessum fide in gratiam.v. 3.non solùm autem hoc, sed etiam gloriamur in tribulationibus.

Particulam ἐν ᾧ quidam referunt ad proximè praecedens, videlicet ad tempus novissimum, ut sit sensus, nunc quidem contristati estis in afflictionibus, sed tunc in tempore sc. novissimo exultatis i. e. exultabitis, ita ut praesens iuxta idiotismum Hebraicum ponatur in futuro. Hunc sensum sequitur Oecumenius in comm. ac Lutherus in versione Germ. In welchen ihr euch freuen werdet! congruit haec expositio verbis Christi Luc. 6. v. 21.Beati qui nunc esuritis, quia saturabimini. Beati, qui nunc fletis, quia ridebitis. Sed quia Apostolus versatur in enumeratione beneficiorum, quae in hac vita credentibus Evangelio obtingunt, & quia verè credentes non tantùm in novissimo die exultabunt, sed etiam in hac vita in mediis tribulationibus gloriantur & exultant Rom. 5. v. 3. ideò verbum ἀγαλλιᾶσθε in praesenti positum, rectissimè nativam suam significationem retinere dicitur, quo modo etiam Oecumenius legit, & multi Codices Latini Manuscripti reddunt. Ex quo consequens est, particulam ἐν ᾧ non tantùm proximè praecedens verbum, videlicet καιρῷ ἔσχάτῳ, sed ad totum praecedentis membri complexum referri, ac per modum quendam illationis hunc versiculum ex praecedentibus πορισματικῶς deduci. Quia Deus secundum magnam misericordiam suam regeneravit vos in spem vivam, in haereditatem incorruptibilem &c. conservatam in coelis, & quia in virtute Dei custodimini per fidem in salutem paratam, revelari in tempore novissimo, ideò etiam exultatis. Eximia enim illa DEI beneficia credentibus in Christum exhibita amplissimam laetitiae spiritualis segetem, ac in hac etiam vita exultandi materiam ipsis suppeditant, sicut statim sequitur v. 8. credentes exultatis laetitia inenarrabili. Quidam verbum ἀγαλλιᾶσθε accipiunt ut positum in imperativo. In quo exultate. Sed Apostolus nondum descendit ad exhortationem, sed adhuc versatur in beneficiorum spiritualium credentibus Evangelio divinitus Evangelio collatorum enumeratione, ideò in forma indicativi ἀγαλλιᾶσθε est accipiendum. Magna autem emphasis est in verbo ἀγαλλιᾶσθε. Significat enim internam cordis laetitiam vultu, voce & gestibus testari, ac proinde plus est quàm gaudere. Inde Christus Matth. 5. vers. 12. haec duo coniungit χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, non solùm interius gaudete, sed etiam externis motibus & signis interiorem cordis laetitiam contestemini, externis gestibus ac tripudiis gaudium ostendite. Coniunguntur etiam 1. Petr. 4. vers. 13.Apoc. 19. vers. 7. interim quia exteriores motus sine interiori affectu sunt hypocritici, ideò τῷ πνέυματι ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι debemus Luc. 1. vers. 47.cap. 10. v. 21. LXX. utuntur pro גול quod significat volutari, quando quis tripudio, exultatione, & aliis signis externis gaudium cordis aperit. Psalm. 14. vers. 8.Cant. 1. vers. 3.Esa. 25. vers. 9. in quibus locis & alibi passim ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι καὶ εὐφραίνεσθαι coniunguntur. Item pro הללin altum vocem sustulit cum iubilo & gloriationeEsa. 41. vers. 16.Ierem. 49. vers. 4. pro עלזpraegaudio gestiit ac tripudiavit,2. Reg 1. v. 20.Psal. 59. v. 6.Psal. 67. v. 5. &c. pro עלץ cognatae significationis & scriptionis verbo 1. Paral. 16. v. 32.Psal. 9. v. 2. pro רנןexclamavit prae laetitiaPsal. 5. v. 13.Psal. 19. v. 5. &c. Sensus igitur est, quod pii expendentes μέγιστα καὶ τίμια illa, quae in Evangelio partim promissa, partim iam dum donata ipsis sunt 2. Petr. 1. v. 4. intimè in corde suo gaudeant, & exterius verbis ac gestibus gaudium illud suum declarent. Amplificat autem Apostolus exultationem illam antithesi tristitiae ex afflictionibus ortae. ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, inquit, ὀλίγον ἄρτι (εἰ δέον ἐστὶ) λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς. τὸ ὀλίγον quidam adiectum putant ad diminuendam afflictionum magnitudinem, sed rectiùs dicitur, quod additum sit ad exprimendam brevem afflictionum durationem, sicut etiam Lutherus reddidit, eine kleine Zeit/ locus parallelus habetur 1. Epist. 5 v. 10.DEUS omnis gratiae qui vocavit vos in aeternam suam gloriam in CHRISTO IESUὀλίγονbrevi tempore vos passionem sustinentes ipse perficiet, ubi oppositio est inter αἰώνιον & ὀλίγον. Sensus igitur est, afflictiones illas, quibus contristantur, non diu duraturas, sed brevi desituras. Προσδιορισμὸς, εἰ δέον ἐστι per parenthesin à sequenti dictione λυπηθέντες distinguitur; Ponitur autem δέον ἐστὶ Pro δεῖ,Actor. 19. vers. 36. si ita fieri oportet, si opus sit Luth. Wo es sein soll. Latini dicunt, si res ita ferat. Petrus ipse in cap. seq. vers. 17. sic exponit, εἰ θέλει τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. In eadem significatione usurpatur apud Philonem in lib. de mundo. Vulgata coniungit hunc προσδιορισμὸν cum. participio sequenti per infinitivum reddito, si oportet contristari. Eodem modo legit Beda in comm. Sed hac ratione totus sensus obscurior redditur, ac in Graeco non est infinitivus λυποῦσθαι, sed participium λυπηθέντεςexultatis modicum nunc contristati, id est, etiamsi in afflictionibus contristemini, tamen exultatis. Quidam. Codices ut & Regius legunt λυπηθέντας in accusativo, sed nominativus λυπηθέντες magis congruit contextui & probatissimis Codicibus Per πειρασμοὺς, per figuram quandam metonymiae, intelliguntur afflictiones, persecutiones & omnis generis adversitates, ex eo sic dictae, quod DEUS per illas fideles suas in hac vita probet Iac. 1. vers. 12.1. Petr. 4. vers. 12. In hac significatione vox πειρασμῶν accipitur Luc. 22. vers. 28.Actor. 20. vers. 19.Galat. 4. vers. 14.Iac. 1. v. 2.2. Petr. 2. vers. 9.Apoc. 3. vers. 10. Vocat autem πειρασμοὺς ποικίλους, uti etiam Iacobus cap. 1. vers. 2. quia non uno afflictionum genere pii in hac vita premuntur, sed variis adversitatibus sunt expositi, videlicet inediae, bonorum direptioni, infamiae, exilio, tormentis, Martyrio, adeoque omnibus, quae in corpore & fortunis adversa alicui in hac vita obtingere possunt. Denique quando credentes dicuntur contristati in variis afflictionibus, tunc particula ἐν non solum est χρονικὴ, sed etiam αἰτιολογικὴ, non solùm enim Petrus hoc dicit, quod tempore afflictionum pii contristentur, sed etiam ob varias & multiplices afflictiones, quae ipsis propter confessionem Evangelii accidunt, dolore ac moerore afficiantur.

Quaeritur h. l. 1. Quare Petrus addat modicum nunc in variis afflictionibus contristati? Resp. 1. ut ostendat, spiritualem laetitiam ex consideratione beneficiorum coelestium in Christo donatorum in animis piorum ortam, non extingui per afflictiones externas. 2.
