ut inspergat consolationem adversus afflictiones ductam tùm à durationis brevitate, tùm ab adiuncta intermissione, non solùm enim cum hac vita omnes afflictiones desinunt, sed etiam in hac vita respiratio quaedam ab afflictionibus saepius contingit. 3. quia haec Epistola potissimum ad conversos ex Iudaismo directa est, qui variis persecutionibus à Iudaeis adhuc incredulis affligebantur. 1. Thess. 2. vers. 14.

Q. 2. Quare addatεἰ δέον ἐστὶ? Resp. 1. ut ostendat, pios in hac vita non posse esse ab afflictionibus penitus immunes. 2. conditio ponitur pro causa, ostendit enim non temerè fieri, quod Deus credentibus in Christum crucem in hac vita immittit.

Ἐναντιοφανία.Exultatis contristati. At quomodo exultare simul possunt & contristari? Resp. 1. affectus contrarii in gradibus remissis possunt simul locum habere, non autem in gradibus extremis. 2. Pii tristantur propter afflictiones praesentes, circumferunt enim adhuc carnem & sanguinem, nec exuerunt humanos affectus; interim Spiritu exultant respicientes secutura aeternae vitae gaudia Matth. 5. v. 4.Beati qui lugentv. 12.gaudete & exultate.Rom. 12. v. 12.Spe gaudentes.2. Cor. 6. v. 10.Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Petrus docet, pios modicum in hac vita contristari in variis afflictionibus. Papa docet, felicitatem temporalem esse notam verae Ecclesiae. Bellarm. lib. de Eccles. cap. 18.

2. Petrus docet, crucem divinitus immissam patienter ferendam, non autem temerè accersendam. εἰ δέον ἐστὶ, inquit. Papa docet, hominem per flagellationes & alia opera laboriosa sponte suscepta posse pro peccatis suis satisfacere, eademque Deo probari.

Διδασκαλίαι 1. Ex sensu beneficiorum divinitus nobis in Christo & per Christum collatorum oritur spiritualis laetitia.

2. Calamitates non solum patienter tolerandae, sed etiam laetanter Act. 5. 41.2. Cor. 8. 2.Iac. 1. 2.Communicantes Christi passionibus gaudete.1. Pet. 4. 12.

3. Pax Christi exuperat omnem intellectum Phil. 4. v. 7. quia locum habet in anima contrita & ob tribulationes contristata.

Breve est quod cruciat, aeternum quod delectat. Nihil diuturnum, quod cum hac vita fugaci desinit. David nondum integros annos decem exegit in exilio, quadraginta autem annos in imperio 2. Sam. 5. v. 4. eo praefigurata fuit passionum nostrarum brevitas & gloriae secuturae perpetuitas.

5. Sicut Christus de se ipso dicit, δεῖoportet filium hominis multa patiMarc. 8. v. 31.Luc. 9. v. 22.oportuit ipsum per passionem intrare in gloriamLuc. 24. v. 26. & 46. ita quoque δέον ἐστί membra Christi in hac vita esse cruci subiecta. Rom. 8. v. 29. Non convenit membrum esse delicatum sub capite crucifixo.

6. Mala sint αὐτόματα non αὐθαίρετος divino consilio immissa, non humanâ temeritate attracta.

7. Non semper nec omnibus aequè graves incumbant afflictiones, neque opus est, cum variae sint afflictionum species, ut singuli iisdem exerceantur.

8. Ut variae sunt piorum tentationes, ita quoque variae & multiplices sunt Scripturarum consolationes.

## 1:7
THAT THE PROOF OF YOUR FAITH, BEING MUCH MORE PRECIOUS THAN GOLD, WHICH IS PROVED BY FIRE, MAY BE FOUND UNTO PRAISE AND GLORY AND HONOR AT THE REVELATION OF JESUS CHRIST.

The fourth benefit is the proof of faith through the cross. GOD not only sends consolation into the hearts of the pious in the cross, but also proves their faith through the cross and brings it into the light; therefore, the Apostle joins the benefit of proof to the benefit of consolation. At the same time, he also explains the reason for which he had called the afflictions of the pious πειρασμοὺς, in the preceding verse, namely because through them GOD tests and proves the faith of the pious. This member could therefore be joined with the preceding one, you rejoice in these afflictions knowing that they not only last for a short time, but are also sent by the salutary and paternal counsel of God for an altogether optimal end, namely that your faith may be proved and explored. Τό δοκίμιον τῆσ πίστεως the exploration of faith is placed by a transitive locution through a Hebraism for faith proved, namely by various temptations and afflictions, as is understood from the preceding verse. The pronoun ὑμῶν which is governed by the following noun πίστεως is inserted here by hyperbaton; the natural order is this. Τό δοκίμιον τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν. Furthermore, the Vulgate rendered this whole passage weakly and imperfectly. That the proof of your faith much more precious than gold, which is by fire is tested, may be found. For he omits τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου, which has great emphasis in this place, nor does he express the force of the adversative δὲ.. According to the Greek text, the words should be rendered thus: That the proof of your faith, much more precious than gold, which perishes and yet is tested by fire, may be found. There is, therefore, in the words of the Apostle an argument from the lesser to the greater. If gold, which nevertheless perishes and is corruptible (for as he calls it in this place χρυσίον ἀπολλύμενον,, so afterwards v. 18. he calls it the same φθαρτὸν,, showing that gold is not only corruptible in power, but also perishes in act), if, I say, gold, which nevertheless perishes and is corruptible, is yet so highly esteemed by men that they wish it to be tested by fire, so that it may obtain a just price among them, how much less should it seem a wonder to you that GOD should wish to test your faith through afflictions, so that its light and preciousness may shine forth more brightly before Him. In the words τιμιώτερον χρυσίου some establish an ellipsis, in this way, that the proof of your faith may be more precious than gold i. e. than the proof or exploration of gold, just as 1 John 2. v. 2. He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world, namely, for the sins of the whole world. But there is no need for us to introduce an ellipsis here. For the Apostle compares faith tested by temptations with gold as being more precious, but not the proof of faith with the proof of gold as being more precious. Nor yet, as some wish, must it be said that τιμιώτερον is put for τιμιωτέρας, so that it may agree with the noun πίστεως.. For it is sufficient that it agrees with the word δοκίμιον, so that the sense may be: Your faith, tested by the fire of afflictions, is far more precious than corruptible gold, which is tested by fire. Thus, therefore, in the word ἀπολλυμένου the cause is placed, on account of which faith tested by afflictions is established as more precious than gold tested by fire, namely, because gold, however noble it may be among all metals, is nevertheless corruptible and eventually perishes, but your faith, tested by afflictions, not only perseveres, but is also increased, and through it you are kept unto eternal salvation v. 5. receiving the end of your faith, the salvation of your souls v. 9. What is added, unto praise and honor and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ, that expresses the time when the preciousness of faith tested by temptations will become publicly known to all men, and will bring praise, honor, and glory to the believers, namely, when Christ shall be revealed from heaven in His final coming 2. Thess. 1. v. 7. At the same time, regard is also had to the preceding comparison of faith with gold. For just as gold is then finally held in its own honor, and its price is worthily estimated, when it has first been examined and tested by fire: so faith, tested by the fire of afflictions, brings praise, honor, and glory to man before God. James cap. 1. v. 12. explains this praise and honor of faith thus. Blessed is the man who endures temptation, because when he has been tested, he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him. For God does not honor with mere words, but by the deed itself, i.e., by the gratuitous distribution of the reward.

It is asked in this place, Whether something different is signified here by praise, honor, and glory? ἔπαινος is accustomed to be done by words, τιμὴ by things and deeds, δόξα is a sound judgment concerning someone's virtue. Therefore, in various ways these are accommodated to the honor of believers on the last day. 1. Christ on the day of judgment will praise the believers, saying: I was hungry, and you gave me food, he will glorify the same, saying: Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom; he will honor the same, by separating them from the evil, by placing them at his right hand, and by introducing them into eternal life. 2. The elect on the day of judgment will have praise before men, glory before the Angels, honor before God. 3. They will have praise in the endowments of the glorified body, which the Scholastics call the stole of the body; glory in the endowments of the glorified soul, which the Scholastics call the stole of the soul; honor in the whole composite, when they will be associated with the choirs of Angels. 4. The simplest explanation is sought from the Scriptures. The elect on the day of judgment will have praise, because then there will be praise for everyone from God 1. Cor. 4. v. 5. honor, because the heavenly Father will then honor them Ioh. 12. v. 26.1. Sam. 2. v. 30. glory, because glory and honor will then be to everyone who has worked good Rom. 2. v. 10. then the faithful servants will hear Matth. 25. v. 23. Well done, good and faithful servant, because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many; when Christ, the life of believers, shall appear, then they also shall appear with him in glory Col. 3. v. 4.

Ἐναντιοφανία. Faith will appear much more precious unto praise and glory, at the revelation of Christ. But 1. Cor. 13. v. 8. Charity alone never fails. But knowledge, and thus also faith, will be destroyed. Resp. on the day of judgment faith will not yet cease, because it will be the norm of judgment. He who has believed, and has been baptized, will be saved; but he who has not believed, will be condemned Marc. 16. v. 16. and from good or evil works judgment will be made concerning the of men. by faith or unbelief. As many, therefore, as shall be found on the day of judgment to have persevered in faith until the end of life, to have preserved the same in temptations and persecutions, and to have demonstrated it through the pursuit of good works, they shall obtain honor, praise, and glory from Christ the judge. That γνῶσις is said to be about to cease in eternal life is not to be understood absolutely and simply, as if all knowledge of God whatsoever is to be abolished, but in a certain respect, namely with regard to that which is imperfect in the γνώσει of this life, as the Apostle himself explains v. 10. & 12. While we live here, we know only in part and through a glass, and we must daily progress in the knowledge of God by employing the aids of prophecy or the interpretation of the Scriptures. This imperfect mode of knowledge will cease in the other life, and vision will succeed faith, and facial and intuitive knowledge will succeed enigmatic and speculative knowledge.

Ἔλεγχος, The coming of Christ to judgment is called ἀποκάλυψις in this place & vers. 13.1. Cor. 1. v. 7. ἀποκάλυψις τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀπ᾿ οὐρανοῦ 2. Thess. 1. v. 7. ἐπιφάνεια 1. Tim. 6. v. 14.2. Tim. 4. v. 1. ἐπιφάνεια τῆς παρουσίας 2. Thessal. 2. v. 8. φανέρωσις of Christ Coloss. 3. v. 4.1. Petr. 5. v. 4.1. Ioh. 2. v. 28.cap. 3. v. 2. Therefore the Calvinists err, asserting that Christ according to his human Nature is plainly absent from us. Christ is present to us according to both Natures, according to his infallible promise Matth. 18. v. 20.cap. 28. v. 29. but that presence is invisible, whereas on the day of judgment Christ will be so revealed and manifested that he may be seen by all.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. What the furnace is to gold, what the file is to iron, what the flail is to grain, this is tribulation to a just man. GOD sends calamity, if you are iron, that you may be purged, if gold, that you may be tested. Men are often compared to vessels. Rom. 9. vers. 21. For as with vessels, so also with men, to test by striking what kind of ringing they give back, whether they are broken or whole, full or empty, which tribulation especially brings about.

2. GOD sends the cross to the pious for the recognition of the remnants of sin, for the testing of faith, for the excitation of piety, for the mortification of the old man, for our conformation to the image of CHRIST, for the kindling of the expectation of eternal life.

3. Faith is compared to gold. 1. By reason of its origin, faith arises from the word, which is likewise compared to gold Psal. 19. v. 13.Psal. 119. vers. 127. 2. On account of its dignity. Just as among metals none is more precious than gold, so faith excels all virtues, nay, it procures dignity and weight for the remaining virtues. Gloss on this place. 3. On account of its rarity. Gold is rare, but true faith is far rarer. 4. On account of its virtue. Gold strengthens the heart, faith the soul. 5. On account of its testing. As gold is tested by fire, so faith is tested by temptations. Iob. 23. v. 10.He tests me, that I may come forth as gold.Prov. 17. v. 3.As silver is tested by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord tests hearts. Gold is tested by fire in two ways, first, when it is purged of dross, second, when a judgment must be made concerning its purity; both modes of testing correspond to faith.

4. But faith is far more precious than gold. Gold, when it is tested, is in part worn away; faith, tested by the fire of the cross, is increased. Gold will perish on the last day along with the remaining creatures: faith at the revelation of Christ will yield to the pious in honor and everlasting glory. Gold does not render a man good or better, nor will it be able to deliver in the day of the Lord's wrath Zeph. 1. v. 18. Faith renders a man just and pleasing before GOD, and delivers from the coming wrath of GOD.

5. This is the true honor, which will be obtained by the pious from GOD on the day of judgment 1. Cor. 4. v. 5. worldly honor is a light and transitory thing.

6. Ambrose, book 7, on Luke chapter 10, addresses Christ thus: Although you are everywhere, and standing in our midst, you are not discerned by us, yet there will be a time when all flesh will behold you returning.

The fifth benefit is the love of Christ not yet seen.

Latin:

UT PROBATIO FIDEI VESTRAE MULTO PRECIOSIOR AURO, QUOD PER IGNEM PROBATUR, INVENIATUR IN LAUDEM & GLORIAM & HONOREM IN REVELATIONE IESU CHRISTI.

Quartum beneficium est fidei per crucem probatio. DEUS non solum consolationem in cruce piorum cordibus immittit, sed etiam per crucem fidem eorum probat & in lucem producit, beneficio igitur consolationis subiungit Apostolus beneficium probationis. Simul etiam exponit causam, propter quam piorum afflictiones in versu praeced. vocaverat πειρασμοὺς, nimirùm quia per illas DEUS tentat ac probat fidem piorum. Posset igitur hoc membrum cum praecedente coniungi, exultatis in ipsis afflictionibus scientes, eas non solùm brevi tempore durare, sed etiam salutari & paterno Dei consilio fine omninò optimo immitti, videlicet ut fides vestra probetur & exploretur. Τό δοκίμιον τῆσ πίστεως exploratio fidei locutione transitiva per Hebraismum ponitur pro fide probata, variis videlicet tentationibus & afflictionibus, ut intelligitur ex versu praeced. Pronomen ὑμῶν quod regitur à sequente nomine πίστεως per traiectionem hîc inseritur, ordo naturalis hic est. Τό δοκίμιον τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν. Porrò totum hunc locum vulgata dilutè & imperfectè reddidit. Ut probatio vestrae fidei multò preciosior auro, quod per ignem probatur, inveniatur. Omittit enim τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου, quod magnam hoc loco habet emphasin, nec exprimit vim adversativae δὲ. Iuxta Graecum textum verba sic reddenda. Ut probatio fidei vestrae multò preciosior auro, quod perit & tamen igne probatur, inveniatur. Inest igitur verbis Apostoli argumentum à minori ad maius. Si aurum, quod tamen perit & corruptibile est (ut enim hoc loco vocat χρυσίον ἀπολλύμενον, ita postea v. 18. idem vocat φθαρτὸν, ostendens aurum non solùm potentiâ corruptibile esse, sed etiam actu perire) si, inquam, aurum, quod tamen perit & corruptibile est, tanti tamen ab hominibus aestimatur, ut velint illud igne probari, quò iustum apud ipsos obtinere possit precium, quantò minus mirum videri vobis debet, quod DEUS fidem vestram per afflictiones probare velit, ut eius lux & preciositas coram ipso magis resplendeat. In verbis τιμιώτερον χρυσίου quidam statuunt ellipsin, hoc modo, ut probatio fidei vestrae sit preciosior auro i. e. probatione sive exploratione auri, sicut1 Ioh. 2. v. 2.ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, non pro nostris autem tantùm, sed etiam pro totius mundi sc. peccatis. Sed non opus est, ut ellipsin hîc introducamus. Comparat enim Apostolus fidem per tentationes probatam cum auro tanquam preciosiorem, non autem probationem fidei cum probatione auri tanquam preciosiorem. Nec tamen propterea, ut quidam volunt, dicendum, quòd τιμιώτερονponatur proτιμιωτέρας,ut congruat cum nomineπίστεως. Sufficit enim, quòd congruat cum voce δοκίμιον, ut sit sensus. Fides vestra per ignem afflictionum probata, longè est preciosior auro corruptibili, quod per ignem probatur. Sic ergò in verbo ἀπολλυμένου ponitur causa, propter quam fides afflictionibus probata, preciosior statuatur auro per ignem probato, nimirum, quia aurum, utut sit nobilissimum inter omina metalla, tamen corruptibile est, & tandem perit, fides autem vestra afflictionibus probata, non solùm perseverat, sed etiam augetur, & per eam custo dimini in salutem aeternamv. 5.reportantes finem fidei vestrae salutem animarumv. 9. Quod additur, in laudem & honorem & gloriam in revelatione Iesu Christi, illud exprimit tempus, quando fidei per tentationes probatae preciositas publicè omnibus homnibus innotescet, ac laudem, honorem & gloriam credentibus afferet, videlicet, quando Christus in novissimo suo adventu revelabitur è coelo 2. Thess. 1. v. 7. Simul etiam respectus habetur ad praecedentem fidei cum auro comparationem. Ut enim auro tum demum suus honos habetur, & precium eius dignè aestimatur, quando prius fuerit igne examinatum & probatum: sic fides per ignem afflictionum probata laudem, honorem & gloriam homini apud Deum affert. Iacobus cap. 1. v. 12. hanc fidei laudem & honorem sic explicat. Beatus vir, qui suffert tentationem, quoniam cum probatus fuerit, accipiet coronam vitae, quam promisit Deus diligentibus se. Deus enim non nudis verbis honorat, sed facto ipso i. e. praemii gratuitâ distributione.

Quaeritur hoc loco, An per laudem, honorem & gloriam diversum quid hîc significetur?ἔπαινος solet fieri verbis, τιμὴ rebus & gestibus, δόξα est sanum iudicium de alicuius virtute. Variis ergò modis haec ad credentium in die novissimo honorem accommodantur. 1. Christus in die iudicii credentes laudabit, dicens: Esurivi, & dedistis mihi cibum, eosdem glorificabit, dicens: Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum; eosdem honorabit, à malis eos separando, ad dextram suam collocando, & in vitam aeternam introducendo. 2. Electi in die iudicii laudem habebunt apud homines, gloriam apud Angelos, honorem apud Deum. 3. Laudem habebunt in dotibus glorificati corporis, quas Scholastici vocant stolam corporis; gloriam in dotibus clarificatae animae, quas Scholastici vocant stolam animae; honorem in toto coniuncto, quando Angelorum choris associabuntur. 4. Simplicissima explicatio petitur ex Scripturis. Electi in die iudicii habebunt laudem, quia tunc erit unicuique laus à Deo 1. Cor. 4. v. 5. honorem, quia Pater coelestis eos tunc honorabit Ioh. 12. v. 26.1. Sam. 2. v. 30. gloriam, quia gloria & honor tunc erit omni, qui operatus est bonum Rom. 2. v. 10. tunc audient fideles servi Matth. 25. v. 23.Euge, serve bone & fidelis, quia super paucae fuisti fidelis, super multa te constituam; cum Christus apparuerit credentium vita, tunc & ipsi apparebunt cum eo in gloriaCol. 3. v. 4.

Ἐναντιοφανία.Fides multò preciosior apparebit in laudem & gloriam, in revelatione Christi. At 1. Cor. 13. v. 8.Sola caritas nunquam excidit. Scientia autem, & sic etiam fides destruetur. Resp. in die iudicii fides nondum cessabit, quia norma iudicii erit. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit; qui vero non crediderit, condemnabiturMarc. 16. v. 16. atque ex operibus bonis vel malis iudicium fiet de hominum fide vel incredultiate. Quotquot ergò in die iudicii invenientur, in fide usque ad finem vitae perseverâsse, eandem in tentationibus & persecutionibus conservâsse, ac per bonorum operum studium demonstrâsse, illi à Christo iudice honorem, laudem & gloriam sortientur. Quòd γνῶσις in vita aeterna dicitur cessatura, non est absolutè & simpliciter intelligendum, quasi omnis omninò Dei cognitio sit abolenda, sed secundùm quid, videlicet respectu illius, quod in γνώσει huius vitae est imperfectum, ut Apostolus ipse exponit v. 10. & 12. Dum hîc vivimus, non nisi ex parte & per speculum cognoscimus, ac quotidiè in cognitione Dei nos oportet proficere adhibitis adminiculis Prophetiae seu interpretationis Scripturarum. hic modus cognitionis imperfectus cessabit in altera vita, ac fidei succedet visio, cognitioni aenigmaticae & speculari succedet cognitio facialis & intuitiva.

Ἔλεγχος, Christi adventus ad iudicium vocatur ἀποκάλυψις h. l. & vers. 13.1. Cor. 1. v. 7.ἀποκάλυψις τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀπ᾿ οὐρανοῦ2. Thess. 1. v. 7.ἐπιφάνεια1. Tim. 6. v. 14.2. Tim. 4. v. 1.ἐπιφάνεια τῆς παρουσίας2. Thessal. 2. v. 8.φανέρωσις Christi Coloss. 3. v. 4.1. Petr. 5. v. 4.1. Ioh. 2. v. 28.cap. 3. v. 2. Ergò Calviniani errant, statuentes, Christum secundùm humanam Naturam planè à nobis abesse. Christus secundùm utramque Naturam nobis praesens est, iuxta infallibilem suam promissionem Matth. 18. v. 20.cap. 28. v. 29. sed praesentia illa est invisibilis, in die autem iudicii Christus ita revelabitur & manifestabitur, ut ab omnibus conspiciatur.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Quod fornax auro, quod lima ferro, quod flagellum grano, hoc tribulatio est viro iusto. Immittit DEUS calamitatem, si ferrum es, ut purgeris, si aurum, ut proberis. Homines saepè comparantur vasis. Rom. 9. vers. 21. Ut enim vasa, ita quoque homines pulsu tentare, cuiusmodi tinnitum reddant, fractane sint an integra, plena an vacua, quod praecipuè efficit tribulatio.

2. Immittit DEUS piis crucem ob reliquiarum peccati agnitionem, ob fidei probationem, ob pietatis excitationem, ob veteris hominis mortificationem, ob nostram ad CHRISTI imaginem conformationem, ob accendendam vitae aeternae expectationem.

3. Fides comparatur auro. 1. Ratione originis, oritur fides ex verbo, quod itidem auro comparatur Psal. 19. v. 13.Psal. 119. vers. 127. 2. Propter dignitatem. Sicut inter metalla nullum auro preciosius, ita fides praestat omnibus virtutibus, imò dignitatem, & pondus reliquis virtutibus conciliat. Glossa h. l. 3. Propter raritatem. Rarum est aurum, sed longè rarior vera fides. 4. Propter virtutem. Aurum cor confortat, fides animam. 5. Propter Probationem. Ut aurum igne, ita fides tentationibus probatur. Iob. 23. v. 10.Probat me, ut quasi aurum egrediar.Prov. 17. v. 3.Sicut igne probatur argentum, & aurum camino: ita corda probat Dominus. Bifariam probatur aurum igni, primò, cùm repurgatur à scoria, secundò, cum de eius probitate faciendum iudicium, uterque probationis modus fidei congruit.

4. Longè vero preciosior est fides auro. Aurum, cum probatur, ex parte deteritur, fides per ignem crucis probata augetur. Aurum in novissimo die cum reliquis creaturis interibit: fides in revelatione Christi cedet piis in honorem & gloriam sempiternam. Aurum hominem non reddit bonum vel meliorem, nec poterit liberare in die irae Domini Zeph. 1. v. 18. Fides hominem coram DEO reddit iustum & gratum, ac liberat à ventura DEI ita.

5. Verus honor hic est, qui à DEO piis in die iudicii obtinget 1. Cor. 4. v. 5. mundanus honor res levis est & transitoria.

6. Ambrosius lib. 7. in Lucam cap. 10. Christum sic alloquitur. Licet ubique sis, & stans in medio nostrûm, non cernaris à nobis, erit tamen tempus, quando universa caro te aspiciet revertentem.

Quintum beneficium est Christi nondum visi dilectio.

## 1:8
WHOM WHEN YOU HAVE NOT SEEN, YOU LOVE, IN WHOM EVEN NOW NOT SEEING, YET BELIEVING, YOU REJOICE WITH JOY INENARRABLE AND GLORIFYING.

Among the remaining benefits of the Gospel, it is not the least that, when the love of Christ who suffered and died for us is announced to us in it, a reciprocal love for Christ is kindled in our hearts. The Apostle expresses both the cause and antecedent of this love, which is faith, and the effect and consequent, which is spiritual joy. He also amplifies this love from the circumstance of the object, that they love Christ not yet seen, for to love an appearance contributes the most. 1. John 4. v. 20. Therefore the love of Christ is exaggerated from this, that they love him believing, though not yet seen. οὐκ εἰδότες that is καίπερ, οὐκ εἰδότες. Even though you have not seen him, yet you love him. εἰς ὄν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες, πιστέυοντες δὲ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, though even now you do not see him, yet believing in him you exult. He praises those converted to Christ by a double name, both because in their first conversion to Christ they received him by faith, and from faith received him not yet seen; and because in the progress of Christianity, though he is not even now seen, they adhere to him with such firm faith that from that faith a spiritual joy of the heart arises in them. ἀγαλλιᾶσθε Augustine, book 2, on the Creed to the Catechumens, chap. 7. takes it in the imperative mood. Exult with joy inexpressible. But it is more correctly translated in the indicative mood, you exult, because, as we also warned above, the Apostle has not yet descended to exhortation, but is still occupied in the enumeration of spiritual benefits. The Vulgate Interpreter, as also Luther, rendered it in the future you will exult, looking without doubt to ἀποκάλυψιν of Christ, of whom mention is made in the preceding verse, and to the epithet of joy added, that at some time in the day of judgment and in eternal life they will exult with ineffable joy. But the present tense can also be retained, in which way the Syrian also rendered it, because believers even in this life exult with spiritual joy, feeling a foretaste of heavenly happiness in their heart. The Apostle amplifies this spiritual joy of the pious from the magnitude attached to it, that it becomes ineffable, and from its quality, that it is glorious.

It is asked in this place, 1. In what sense the joy of the pious is called ὰνεκλάλητον? Resp. 1. By reason of the object, because it is concerning the ineffable goods of eternal life, concerning which Augustine, in his book on the triple dwelling, discourses thus. The goods of eternal life are so many, that they exceed all number; so great, that they exceed all measure; so precious, that they exceed all estimation. 2. By reason of the adjunct, because as the peace of GOD, so also that joy surpasses all sense Phil. 4. v. 7. and therefore also all speech. For that which cannot be comprehended by the mind, that also cannot be uttered by the mouth.

2. In what sense the same joy is called δεδοξασμένον? Resp. 1. By reason of the object, for it is concerning glory and heavenly happiness, nay, it is also the beginning and a certain earnest of the glory and happiness that will follow in eternal life.

2. by reason of the adjunct, because it is a glorious, magnificent, stable, and solid joy. For the Hebrews use participles in place of nouns. 3. by reason of the contrary. For it is opposed to worldly and earthly joy, which, since it is empty, momentary, and fleeting, is therefore also usually joined with disgrace and ignominy, for men themselves are ashamed of it a little while later.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Whom when you have not known, (for in the Greek it is εἰδότες) you love. But how can he be loved, whom we have not yet known, since of the unknown, as there is no desire, so also there is no love. Resp. Augustine, book 1 de peccat. merit. & remiss. chapter 27, establishes that regard is had to the time preceding the announcement of the Gospel and conversion. For instead of you have not seen, he has, you were ignorant, i.e., you did not know. The sense therefore would be, whom, when before the preaching of the Gospel you did not even know, you nevertheless received when announced and loved. Estius follows this exposition in his commentary. But it is answered more correctly that the participle εἰδότες, although it otherwise refers to the mind, is in this place contracted to the sense of sight, so that that love is commended by which the faithful love Christ not yet seen. For 1. Peter himself immediately explains that by ὁρῶντες. 2. The Syrian rendered it by [consult facsimile image] he saw. 3. The Royal Codex reads ὶδόντες. instead of εἰδότες 4. The Vulgate version rendered it, whom when you have not seen, you love. It is not permitted for Estius to depart from it on account of the anathema of the Council of Trent. 5. A Synecdoche is customary in the Scriptures, by which under the general name of knowledge is understood in species that which is made through the principal sense, namely sight, just as conversely the sense of seeing is transferred in general to every sense, as Augustine teaches in book 10 Confess. chapter 35. 6. Without doubt Peter looks to the saying of Christ Iohan. 20. vers. 29. Blessed are they who do not see and believe. Rightly, therefore, Luther in the German version rendered it: Welchen ihr nicht gesehen.

2. Whom when you have not seen, you love. But some of the converted Jews, to whom the Apostle writes, had seen Christ in the flesh. Lyranus answers. Although some were still living who had seen the humanity of Christ, yet they had not seen the divinity of Christ. But that saying of Christ Iohan. 20. v. 29. Blessed are they who do not see, and believe, is opposed even to the vision of the humanity. It is more correctly said, therefore, that this Epistle is written not only to those converted from the Jews, but also to the faithful from the Gentiles, and among the converted Jews themselves, to whom Peter writes, there were very few who had seen Christ in the flesh. For Christ did not go to διασπορὰν τῶν ἑλλήνων Ioh. 7. v. 35. but taught chiefly in Judea and Galilee.

Ἔλεγχος. Peter praises those to whom he writes, because they believe in Christ even though they have not seen him, and love him. Therefore, the argument of the Calvinists is absurd and preposterous. The body of Christ is not seen in the holy Supper. Therefore it is not really present. Calvin in Harm. p. 446. When Christ pronounces his body to be palpable (& visible) this passage is skillfully and truly adduced here Ioh. 20. v. 20. Luc. 24 v. 39. Palpate and see, by our men to refute the gross error concerning the local presence of the body, which preposterous men imagine in the S. Supper. D. Mylius in the Misnian Comedy reports that a certain one of the Professors was found at Leipzig, who was not ashamed to say to the Visitors to their face, that they should show him the body of Christ to be seen in the Holy Supper, then he would believe in its presence. And yet 1. Faith is τῶν μὴ βλεπομένων Hebr. 11. v. 1. & we walk here by faith, not by sight 2. Cor. 5. v. 4. If you only believe what you see, what is your faith? But rather, what you do not grasp, what you do not see, courageous faith confirms. 2. It is not even a truth of perpetual necessity in a merely and purely natural body that it is always seen in act, because to be seen or not to be seen in act is an external accident of the body, but by no means its internal and essential property. Distinguish, therefore, between the first act and the second. Any natural body is visible, namely in the first act, but it is not always seen in the second act. 3. But if it is not a truth of perpetual necessity in a merely natural body that it is always seen in act, how much less can it be asserted of glorified bodies that it is necessary that they always be seen in act by the eyes of men not yet glorified, if they are present. 4. If it is not a truth of perpetual necessity in a glorified body that it is always seen in act by eyes not yet glorified, how much less will that have a place in the body of Christ assumed into the hypostasis of the Son of GOD, and raised to the right hand of God? Indeed, it was not even always seen in act in the state of humiliation Luc. 4. vers. 30. Iohan. 8. v. 59. nor after the resurrection. Luc. 24. v. 31. If you say, Christ nevertheless draws an argument from visibility and palpability, by which the presence of his body Let him proveLuke 24. v. 39. I answer: because this argument was less principal, and that proposition, whatever is seen and touched is a body, is not reciprocal, therefore it is by no means permitted to infer from this that those passible qualities are always and necessarily present in the very act, especially since this demonstration was not sought from φύσεως νόμῳ but from ὀικονομίας. τρόπῳ, not from the necessity of nature, but from the disposition of free will. Otherwise, by the same reasoning, it would have to be concluded: Christ, from the fact that he eats and drinks, demonstrated to the disciples the truth of his body. Therefore, to eat and drink is an inseparable property even of a glorified body, which mode of concluding Calvin himself rejects p. 447. And it is well to be noted that Christ himself predicts that the vision and touching of him would not be perpetual, when he declares those blessed who, although they do not see, yet believe.

Ἐκδίκησις Salmeron in his commentary, following Thomas in his opusculum on the Sacraments, chapter 15, adapts this passage to the Sacrament of the Eucharist, and teaches that one must believe that the bread is transubstantiated into the body of Christ, even if this is not seen by the eyes. I answer: 1. We believe in the presence of the body of Christ, even if we do not see it to be present, because we have the word of Christ. We do not believe in transubstantiation, because we do not have the word concerning it. 2. The sense is not deceived regarding its proper object. But the sense testifies that the substance of the bread is still present. Augustine, sermon to the Neophytes: What is seen is bread and the chalice, which even the eyes report. But what faith demands to be instructed in is that the bread is the body, the chalice the blood of Christ. Scotus, 4th book of sentences, dist. 11, q. 3, from Ambrose: In the Sacrament of truth there ought not to be a falsehood. But if the substance of the bread is lacking, there will be a falsehood in the accidents. For external accidents are natural signs of an internal substance.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The light of the faithful is to believe without hesitation the things of the soul which are not seen by bodily sight, and to fix one's desire there, where one cannot bring one's gaze. Leo, sermon 2 on the Ascension of the Lord. Heb. 11. v. 1.

2. There is a twofold sight of Christ, bodily and spiritual. Without spiritual sight, bodily sight is not salutary nor saving; but without bodily sight, spiritual sight is salutary and is saving. Luke 2. verse 30.

3. Faith is not a naked, idle, and cold knowledge, but it inflames the heart to the love of Christ. Those who truly believe in Christ also love him. Peter, in this place: Those who love Christ keep his commandments.

Ioh. 14. v. 15. Therefore he who says that he knows Christ (and believes in him) and does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.1. Iohan. 2. v. 4.

4. True faith in Christ produces spiritual joy. Just as the disciples rejoiced when they saw Christ corporally Ioh. 20. v. 20. so the truly pious rejoice when they see Christ spiritually.

5. Just as the Spirit intercedes for us with inexpressible groanings Rom. 8. v. 26. so also that joy, which the Holy Spirit kindles in our hearts, is inexpressible. Just as ἄῤῥητα are the words which Paul heard in the third heaven, 2. Cor. 12. v. 4. so also ἄῤῥητον is that joy, which is a foretaste of heavenly happiness.

6. The end of earthly joy is occupied by sorrow Prov. 14. v. 13. but the end of heavenly joy is occupied by glory.

The sixth and final benefit is the possession of eternal salvation.

Latin:

QUEM CUM NON VIDERITIS, DILIGITIS, IN QUEM NUNC QUOQUE NON VIDENTES, CREDENTES AUTEM LAETITIA INENARRABILI & GLORIFICANTE.

Inter reliqua Evangelii beneficia non postremum est, quod cum in eo Christi pro nobis passi & mortui dilectio nobis annuncietur, reciproca Christi dilectio in cordibus nostris acconditur. Dilectionis huius exprimit Apostolus tùm causam & antecedens, quod est fides, tùm effectum & consequens, quod est gaudium spirituale. Amplificat etiam hanc dilectionem ex circumstantia obiecti, quòd Christum nondum visum diligant, ad amorem enim plurimum facit aspectus. 1. Iohan. 4. v. 20. proinde dilectio Christi inde exaggeratur, quòd eum nondum visum credentes diligant. οὐκ εἰδότες h. e. καίπερ, οὐκ εἰδότες.Etiamsi non videritis, tamen diligitis. εἰς ὄν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες, πιστέυοντες δὲ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε,cùm ne nunc quidem eum videatis, credentes tamen in eum exultatis. Duplici nomine laudat conversos ad Christum, tùm quòd in prima sua ad Christum conversione fide eum receperint, & ex fide ipsum nondum visum receperint; tùm quòd in Christianismi progressu ne nunc quidem viso fide tam firma adhaereant, ut ex fide illa spirituale cordis gaudium in ipsis oriatur. ἀγαλλιᾶσθε Augustinus lib. 2. de Symb. ad Catechum. cap. 7. accipit in modo praeceptivo. Exultate gaudio inenarrabili. Sed rectius vertitur in modo indicativo, exultatis, quia, ut superius etiam monuimus, Apostolus nondum descendit ad exhortationem, sed versatur adhuc in beneficiorum spiritualium enumeratione. Vulgatus Interpres, uti etiam Lutherus reddiderunt in futuro exultabitis, respicientes dubio procul ad ἀποκάλυψιν Christi, cuius in versu praeced. fit mentio & ad epitheton laetitiae adiectum, quod aliquando in die iudicii & in vita aeterna gaudio ineffabili sint exultaturi. Sed potest etiam praesens tempus retineri, quo modo Syrus quoque reddidit, quia credentes etiam in hac vita laetitiâ spirituali exultant, praegustum coelestis felicitatis in corde sentientes. Hanc spiritualem piorum laetitiam amplificat Apostolus ab adiuncta magnitudine, quod fit ineffabilis, & qualitate, quod sit gloriosa.

Quaeritur hoc loco, 1. Quo sensu gaudium piorum voceturὰνεκλάλητον? Resp. 1. Ratione obiecti, quia est de bonis vitae aeternae ineffabilibus, de quibus August. lib. de tripl. habitac. sic disserit. Bona vitae aeternae tàm multa sunt, ut numerum; tàm magna ut mensuram; tàm preciosa, ut aestimationem omnem excedant. 2. Ratione. adiuncti, quia ut pax DEI, ita quoque gaudium illud exuperat omnem sensum Phil. 4. v. 7. ac proinde etiam omnem loquelam. Quod enim mente non potest comprehendi, illud etiam ore non potest proferri.

2. Quo sensu idem gaudium voceturδεδοξασμένον? Resp. 1. ratione obiecti, est enim de gloria & felicitate coelesti, quin & inchoatio ac quaedam arrha gloriae & felicitatis in vita aeterna secuturae.

2. ratione adiuncti, quia est gaudium gloriosum, magnificum, stabile ac solidum. Hebraei enim participiis utuntur pro nominibus. 3. ratione contrarii. Opponitur enim gaudio mundano & terreno, quod cum sit inane, momentaneum ac fluxum, ideo etiam cum dedecore & ignominia plerunque coniunctum, eius enim paulo pòst ipsosmet homines pudet.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Quem cum non noveritis (in Graeco enim est εἰδότες) diligitis. At quomodo potest is diligi, quem nondum habemus cognitum, cum ignoti, ut nulla cupido, ita quoque nulla dilectio. Resp. Augustinus lib. 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. 27. statuit, respectum haberi ad tempus, annunciationem Evangelii & conversionem praecedens. Nam pro non videritis, habet, ignorabatis i. e. non cognoscebatis. Sensus igitur esset, quem, cum ante Evangelii praedicationem ne quidem noveratis, annunciatum tamen fide recepistis ac dilexistis. Hanc expositionem Estius in comm. sequitur. Sed rectiùs respondetur, participium εἰδότες etsi aliàs ad mentem refertur, hoc tamen loco ad sensum visus contrahi, ut sic commendetur dilectio illa, qua fideles Christum nondum visum diligunt. Nam 1. Petrus ipse statim illud exponit per ὁρῶντες. 2. Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image]vidit. 3. Codex Regius pro εἰδότες legit ὶδόντες. 4. Vulgata versio reddidit, quem cum non videritis, diligitis. Ab ea propter anathema Concilii Tridentini recedere Estio integrum non est. 5. Usitata est in Scripturis Synecdoche, qua generali nomine notitiae intelligitur in specie illa, quae fit per sensum principalem, videlicet visum, sicut vicissim sensus videndi in genere ad omnem sensum transfertur, docente Augustino lib. 10. Confess. cap. 35. 6. Procul dubio respicit Petrus ad dictum Christi Iohan. 20. vers. 29.Beati qui non vident & credunt. Rectè igitur Lutherus in vers. Germ. reddidit: Welchen ihr nicht gesehen.

2. Quem cum non videritis, diligitis. At quidam ex conversis Iudeis, ad quos scribit Apostolus, Christum in carne viderant. Lyranus respondet. Licet aliqui adhuc viverent, qui humanitatem Christi viderant, tamen divinitatem Christi non viderant. Atqui etiam visioni humanitatis opponitur illud Christi Iohan. 20. v. 29.Beati qui non vident, & credunt. Rectiùs ergo dictur, Epistolam hanc non solùm ad conversos ex Iudaeis, sed etiam fideles ex gentibus esse scriptam, & inter ipsos conversos Iudaeos, ad quos Petrus scribit, oppidò paucos fuisse, qui Christum in carne viderant. Christus enim non abiit ad διασπορὰν τῶν ἑλλήνωνIoh. 7. v. 35. sed in Iudaea & Galilaea praecipuè docuit.

Ἔλεγχος. Petrus laudat eos, ad quos scribit, quòd in Christum etiam non visum credant, eumque diligant. Absurdum igitur ac praeposterum est Calvinianorum argumentum. Corpus Christi in sacra Coena non videtur. Ergo non est realiter proesens. Calvinus in Harm. p. 446. Cùm Christus palpabile (& visibile) esse corpus suum pronunciet, scitè & verè adductus est hic locusIoh. 20. v. 20.Luc. 24 v. 39.Palpate & videte, à nostris hominibus ad refellendum crassum errorem de locali corporis proesentia, quam homines praeposteri in S. Caena fingunt. D. Mylius in Comoedia Misnica refert, Lipsiae quendam ex Professoribus repertum fuisse, quem non puduerit Visitatoribus in os dicere, ut monstrent sibi corpus Christi in Sacra Coena videndum, tunc se praesentiam eius crediturum esse. Atqui 1. Fides est τῶν μὴ βλεπομένωνHebr. 11. v. 1. & ambulamus hîc per fidem, non per aspectum2. Cor. 5. v. 4. Si tantùm credis quod vides, quid est tua fides? Quin potiùs quod non capis, quod non vides, animosa firmat fides. 2. Ne quidem in corpore merè & purè naturali perpetuae veritatis est, quòd semper actu videatur, quia actu videri vel non videri est externum corporis accidens, nequaquam vero interna & essentialis eius proprietas. Dist. igitur interactum primum, & secundum. Quodlibet corpus naturale est visibile, scilicet actu primo, non autem semper actu secundo videtur. 3. Quod si in corpore merè naturali non est perpetuae veritatis, quod semper actu videatur, quantò minùs de corporibus glorificatis asseri poterit, quòd necessarium sit, oculis hominum nondum glorificatorum actu ea semper videri, si sint praesentia. 4. Si in corpore glorificato non est perpetuae veritatis, quod ab oculis nondum glorificatis actu semper videatur, quantò minùs in corpore Christi in hypostasin Filii DEI assumto, & ad dextram Dei evecto illud locum habebit? quinimò nec in statu exinanitionis semper actu videbatur Luc. 4. vers. 30.Iohan. 8. v. 59. nec post resurrectionem. Luc. 24. v. 31. Si dicas, Christus tamen à visibilitate & palpabilitate argumentum ducit, quo corporis sui praesentiam probetLuc. 24. v. 39. Resp. quia argumentum hoc erat minus principale & propositio illa, quicquid videtur & palpatur est corpus, non est reciproca, ideò minimè hinc inferre licet, passibiles illas qualitates actu ipso semper ac necessariò inesse, maximè cum haec demonstratio non fuerit petita ex φύσεως νόμῳ sed ex ὀικονομίας. τρόπῳ non ex Naturae necessitate, sed liberae voluntatis dispositione. Alioqui pari ratione concludendum foret. Christus ex eo, quod edit & bibit, discipulis veritatem corporis sui demonstravit. Ergo edere & bibere est corporis etiam glorisicati inseparabile proprium, quem concludendi modum Calvinus ipse repudiat p. 447. ac probè notandum, quod Christus ipse sui visionem & palpationem haud fore perpetuam praedicat, quando beatos eos praedicat, qui licet non videant, tamen credant.

Ἐκδίκησις Salmeron in comm. secutus Thomam in opusc. de Sacrament. cap. 15. hunc locum ad Eucharistiae Sacramentum accommodat, ac panem in Christi corpus transubstantiatum credendum esse docet, etiamsi oculis hoc non videatur. Resp. 1. Praesentiam corporis Christi credimus, etiamsi illud praesens esse non videamus, quia verbum Christi habemus. Transsubstantiationem non credimus, quia de ea verbum non habemus. 2. Sensus circa proprium obiectum non fallitur. Atqui sensus testatur substantiam panis adhuc adesse. August. serm, ad Neoph. Quod videtur, panis est & calix, quod etiam oculi renunciant. Quod autem fides postulat instruendum, panis est corpus, calix sanguis Christi. Scotus 4. sent. dist. 11. q. 3. ex Ambrosio. In Sacramento veritatis non debet esse falsum. At si desit substantia panis, erit falsitas in accidentibus. Accidentia enim externa sunt naturalia signa internae substantiae.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Fidelium lumen est animarum incunctanter credere, quae corporeo non intuitu videntur, & ibi figere desiderium, quò nequeas inferre conspectum. Leo serm. 2. de ascens. Dom. Heb. 11. v. 1.

2. Duplex est Christi intuitus, corporalis & spiritualis. Absque intuitu spirituali corporalis non est salutaris nec salvificus; sed absque intuitu corporali spiritualis salutaris & est salvificus. Luc. 2. vers. 30.

3. Fides non est nuda, otiosa & frigida notitia, sed inflammat cor ad amorem Christi. Qui verè in Christum credunt, eundem etiam diligunt. Petrus h. l. Qui Christum diligunt Mandata eius observant.

Ioh. 14. v. 15. Ergò qui dicit, se nosse Christum (& in eum credere) & mandata eius non observat, mendax est, & veritas non est in eo.1. Iohan. 2. v. 4.

4. Vera fides in Christum parit gaudium spirituale. Sicut discipuli gavisi sunt viso corporaliter Christo Ioh. 20. v. 20. ita verè pii gaudent viso spiritualiter Christo.

5. Sicut Spiritus postulat pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus Rom. 8. v. 26. ita quoque gaudium illud, quod Spiritus sanctus in cordibus nostris accendit, est inenarrabile. Sicut ἄῤῥητα sunt verba, quae Paulus in tertio coelo audivit, 2. Cor. 12. v. 4. ita quoque ἄῤῥητον est illud gaudium, quod est coelestis felicitatis praegustus.

6. Extrema gaudii terreni occupat luctus Prov. 14. v. 13. sed extrema gaudii coelestis occupat gloria.

Sextum & ultimum beneficium est aeternae salutis possesio.

## 1:9
OBTAINING THE END OF YOUR FAITH, THE SALVATION OF SOULS.

Some connect this member with the preceding one in this way, that the cause of that ineffable joy is expressed, namely a certain kind of eternal life, for from that and therefore believers in Christ exult with inexpressible joy, because they are certain that they will at some time obtain the heavenly inheritance. But it is more correctly understood as a benefit distinct from the others, which the Apostle adds to the others for this reason, to show that the benefits of Christ pertain not only to this life, but also to the future life, and that the goal of all the benefits which Christ confers upon believers in this life looks to this, that believers may at some time be made partakers of eternal life, hence the Syrian rendered ἐκβατικῶς, that you may obtain the end of faith, the salvation of souls.

By σωτηρίαν some understand the beginning of salvation, which is conferred in this life upon those who believe in Christ, both because the Apostle says in the present tense κομιζόμενοι obtaining, and because it is called the salvation of souls, but salvation in the present life pertains only to souls, in which we still await the redemption of the body.Rom. 8. v. 23. In this meaning the word σωτηρίας, or rather the verb σώζεσθαι, from which it descends, is taken Roman. 8. vers. 24. ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν Eph. 2. vers. 8by grace you are σεσωμένοι. Tit. 3. vers. 5.According to his great mercy ἒσωμεν ὑμᾶς. He saved us. We are made partakers of this begun salvation in justification itself, just as Paul Roman. 4. vers. 6.

from Psalm 32. v. 1. he proves that blessedness consists in this, that GOD imputes righteousness to us without works. But it is more correctly understood of consummated salvation, which befalls man in eternal life after the death of the body, because the Apostle enumerates this benefit in the last place, as the end and goal of the remaining preceding ones. For this reason GOD regenerates us according to His great mercy, for this reason He guards us by His power in dangers, for this reason He raises us up in adversities with firm consolation, for this reason He tests our faith through adversities, so that He may finally introduce us into the full possession of eternal salvation. Therefore the present κομιζόμενοι must be accepted as placed for the future through the customary enallage of time, about to receive the end of your faith. By τέλος in this place is accepted end or the latest, after which nothing else is expected; such an end of our faith, toward which faith strives as its ultimate goal, is the eternal salvation of souls. Augustine, book 1, on the merit and remission of sins chap. 27. Receiving the Testament of faith the salvation of souls. Without doubt he looks to this, that a Testament is the latest will of a man, whence he placed it for an end.

It is asked in this place. Why does the Apostle call the salvation of souls the end of faith? Resp. 1. to show that all things to be believed, hoped for, and tolerated in Christianity are directed, namely, toward possessing eternal life at some time, whence we also conclude the Symbol of faith with these words. I believe in eternal life. 2. to recall the Jews from carnal thoughts about temporal salvation promised through the Messiah and liberation from earthly enemies to be expected from Him. 3. to supply them with firm consolation in all adversities, namely, that the tribulations of this life are not worthy of eternal life Rom. 8. vers. 18.

Ἐναντιοφανεία. The end of faith is the salvation of souls. And yet not only souls, but also bodies will one day be participants of salvation. Resp. 1. after death souls are the first to be made participants of salvation, therefore it is called the salvation of souls. Nor are bodies excluded from the participation of that salvation, because the souls of the pious, having been made participants of salvation, await the resurrection of bodies for the perfection of blessedness. 2. salvation overflows from the souls of the blessed into the bodies, thence κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν it is called the salvation of souls.

Ἔλεγχος. Peter teaches that eternal salvation is the end of faith. The Pope teaches that salvation is the merit of our works.

Ἐκδίκησις. The Papists establish, and Piscator supports them in this part, that τέλος signifies reward in this place, so that there is a likeness drawn from a laborer who endures labor in the hope of a reward which he is to carry back once the labor is finished. 1. Because the Syrian rendered it by [consult facsimile image] a prize. 2. The Hebrews call a reward אחרית Prov. 23. v. 18. 3. a reward is τέλος, the end and prize of a work. Iac. 5. v. 11. from which they further collect that eternal life is given on account of works, just as a reward is on account of labor. I respond: 1. We deny that τέλος signifies reward in this place. Indeed, every reward is τέλος,, but not every τέλος is a reward. τέλος properly signifies an end, and it is transferred to reward only by a metaphorical signification. Why, therefore, should we wish to depart without necessity from the proper signification of the word? 2. Paul Rom. 6. v. 21. & 22. distinguishes between καρπὸν and τέλος; he calls the καρπὸν of the service rendered to GOD ἁγιασμὸν, τέλος, but eternal life; he calls the καρπὸν of the service rendered to sin shame, but τέλος eternal death. Lest anyone, however, from the word τέλος used concerning death and eternal life, should collect that eternal life is the due reward of piety, just as eternal death is the due reward of impiety, he immediately adds the ἐξηγήσεως cause: the wages of sin is death, but the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. 3. Even if we should grant in the highest degree ἐκ περιουσίας that by τέλος a reward is understood—for that faith which the Apostle mentions ἐργάζεται through love Gal. 5. v. 6., whence it is called ἒργον τῆς πίστεως 1. Thess. 1. v. 3.—from that, however, it by no means follows that eternal life is given out of merit. For not every reward is a reward of merit, but a certain reward of grace is also given. Matth. 5. v. 46. cap. 6. v. 1. Luc. 6. v. 32. Item Psalm. 127. v. 4. Ambrose, book 1, Epistle 1, around the middle: One thing is the reward of liberality and grace, another is the stipend of virtue, another is the remuneration of labor. Lyranus on cap. 10. John: Celestial glory is not properly called a reward, but only broadly, insofar as everything that is rendered as a prize for labor is called a reward. What of the fact that Bellarmine himself argues thus, book 5, on Justification, chapter 3: The end and the reward are not the same. For the end has a relation to the means, whether they be merits or whether they be not. A reward (that is, one that is due and properly and strictly so called) has a relation it pertains to merits alone. Since therefore Peter calls the salvation of souls the end of faith, certainly the salvation of souls is not the reward of merit.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The end of the revealed word is faith in Christ, the end of faith is eternal life. John 20. v. 31. These things are written, that you might believe that Jesus is the Christ, and that believing you might have life in his name.

2. The salvation of souls in this life happens to believers in an incipient way, in the future life in a consummatory way.

3. That we may attain the salvation of souls as the end of faith, faith finally persevering is required. Matt. 10. v. 22. chap. 24. v. 13. Rev. 2. v. 10. Only perseverance is crowned.

4. Of all those benefits which the Apostle has hitherto commemorated, the highest cause is the mercy of GOD; the meritorious cause is the passion of Christ; the ultimate end is eternal life, to which we are led through crosses and afflictions, in which we are confirmed by faith and hope.

Latin:

REPORTANTES FINEM FIDEI VESTRAE SALUTEM ANIMARUM.

Quidam hoc membrum cum praecedente eo modo connectunt, causam illius ineffabilis gaudii exprimi, videlicet certam speciem vitae aeternae, inde enim atque ideò credentes in Christum laetitia inenarrabili exultant, quia certi sunt, se aliquando coelestem haereditatem reportaturos. Sed rectiùs accipitur, ut distinctum à reliquis beneficium, quod Apostolus ideò reliquis subiungit, ut ostendat, Christi beneficia non tantùm ad hanc, sed etiam ad vitam futuram pertinere, & scopum omnium beneficiorum, quae Christus in hac vita credentibus confert, eò spectare, ut credentes aliquando vitae aeternae reddantur participes, inde Syrus reddidit ἐκβατικῶς,ut reportetis finem fidei, salutem animarum.

Per σωτηρίαν quidam intelligunt initium salutis, quod in hac vita credentibus in Christum confertur, tùm quia Apostolus in praesenti dicitκομιζόμενοιreportantes, tùm quia vocatur salus animarum, salus autem in praesenti vita ad solas animas pertinet, in qua corporis redemtionem adhuc expectamus.Rom. 8. v. 23. In hac significatione vox σωτηρίας, vel potiùs verbum σώζεσθαι, à quo descendit, accipitur Roman. 8. vers. 24.ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημενEph. 2. vers. 8gratia estisσεσωμένοι.Tit. 3. vers. 5.Secundùm magnam misericordiam suamἒσωμεν ὑμᾶς.Salvos nos fecit. Huius salutis inchoatae participes reddimur in ipsa iustificatione, sicut Paulus Roman. 4. vers. 6.

ex Psalmo 32. v. 1. probat beatitudinem in eo consistere, quòd DEUS nobis imputat iustitiam sine operibus. Sed rectiùs accipitur de salute consummata, quae post corporis mortem homini in vita aeterna obtingit, quia Apostolus ultimo loco hoc beneficium enumerat, tanquam praecedentium reliquorum finem & scopum. Ideò enim DEUS nos regenerat secundùm magnam suam misericordiam, ideò virtute suâ in periculis nos custodit, ideò in adversis firmâ consolatione nos erigit, ideò fidem nostram per adversa probat, ut in plenam aeternae salutis possessionem tandem nos introducat. Praesens ergò κομιζόμενοι per usitatam temporis enallagen accipiendum pro futuro positum, reportaturi finem fidei vestrae. Per τέλος hoc loco accipitur finis sive novissimum, post quod nihil aliud expectatur, talis finis fidei nostrae, ad quem velut ultimum scopum fides contendit, est aeterna animarum salus. Augustin. libro 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. 27.Percipientes Testamentum fidei salutem animarum. Procul dubio eò respicit, quòd Testamentum sit novissima hominis voluntas, unde pro fine eam posuit.

Quaeritur hoc loco. Quare Apostolus finem fidei appellet Animarum salutem? Resp. 1. ut ostendat, quò omnia credenda, speranda, ac toleranda in Christianismo dirigantur, videlicet ad vitam aeternam aliquando possidendam, unde etiam Symbolum fidei concludimus his verbis. Credo vitam aeternam. 2. ut revocet Iudaeos à cogitationibus carnalibus de salute temporali per Messiam promisâ & liberatione ab hostibus terrenis ab ipso expectanda. 3. ut firmam in omnibus adversis consolationem ipsis suppeditet, videlicet tribulationes huius vitae non esse dignas vitâ aeternâ Rom. 8. vers. 18.

Ἐναντιοφανεία.Finis fidei est salus animarum. Atqui non solùm animae, sed etiam corpora aliquando salutis erunt participia. Resp. 1. post mortem animae primùm salutis participes redduntur, ideò vocatur salus animarum. Nec tamen corpora à participatione illius salutis excluduntur, quia animae piorum salutis participes factae ad beatitudinis perfectionem expectant resurrectionem corporum. 2. salus ex animabus beatorum in corpora quis redundat, inde κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν salus animarum vocatur.

Ἔλεγχος. Petrus docet, salutem aeternam esse finem fidei. Papa docet, salutem esse operum nostrorum meritum.

Ἐκδίκησις. Pontificii statuunt, ac Piscator illis hac in parte suffragatur, τέλοςhoc loco significare mercedem, ut sit similitudo ducta ab operario, qui laborem tolerat spe mercedis, quam labore peracto sit reportaturs 1. quia Syrus reddidit per[consult facsimile image]praemium. 2. Hebraei mercedem vocantאחריתProv. 23. v. 18. 3. merces estτέλος,finis & praemium operis.Iac. 5. v. 11.ex quo porrò colligunt, vitam aeternam dari propter opera, sicut merces propter laborem. Resp. 1. negamus, τέλος hoc loco significare mercedem. Omnis quidem merces est τέλος, sed non omne τέλος est merces. τέλος propriè significat finem, ad mercedem non nisi metaphoricâ significatione transfertur. Eccur igitur absque necessitate à propria vocis significatione recedere velimus. 2. Paulus Rom. 6. v. 21. & 22. inter καρπὸν ac τέλος distinguit, servitii DEI praestiti καρπὸν vocat ἁγιασμὸν, τέλος autem vitam aeternam; servitii peccato praestiti καρπὸν vocat erubescentiam, τέλος vero mortem aeternam. Ne quis vero ex voce τέλος de morte & vita aeterna usurpata, colligat, vitam aeternam esse debitum pietatis praemium, sicut mors aeterna est debita impietatis merces, statim ἐξηγήσεως causâ subiungit, stipendia peccati mors, gratia autem Dei vita aeterna in Christo Iesu Domino nostro. 3. Si vel maximè ἐκ περιουσίας concedamus, per τέλος intelligi mercedem, fides enim illa, cuius meminit Apostolus, ἐργάζεται per caritatem Gal. 5. v. 6. unde vocatur ἒργον τῆς πίστεως1. Thess. 1. v. 3. ex eo tamen minimè sequitur, vitam aeternam dari ex merito. Non enim omnis merces est merces meriti, sed datur etiam quaedam merces gratiae. Matth. 5. v. 46.cap. 6. v. 1.Luc. 6. v. 32. It. Psalm. 127. v. 4. Ambrosius lib. 1. Epist. 1. circa med. Alia est merces liberalitatis & gratiae, aliud virtutis stipendium, alia laboris remuneratio. Lyranus in cap. 10. Iohan. Gloria coelestis non propriè dicitur merces, sed tantummodo largè in quantum omne quod redditur in praemium laboris, dicitur merces. Quid quod ipse Bellarminus sic disserit. lib. 5. de Iustif. cap. 3. Non est idem finis & merces. Nam finis relationem habet ad media, sive sint merita, sive non sint. Merces (debita sc. & propriè ac strictè sic dicta) relationem habet ad sola merita. Cum ergò Petrus salutem animarum vocet finem fidei, utique salus animarum non est merces meriti.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Finis verbi revelati fides in Christum, finis fidei vita aeterna. Ioh. 20. v. 31.Haec scripta sunt, ut credatis, quia Iesus est Christus, & ut credentes vitam habeatis in nomine ipsius.

2. Salus animarum in hac vita credentibus obtingit inchoativè, in futura vita consummativè.

3. Ut finem fidei salutem animarum consequamur, requiritur fides finaliter perseverans. Matth. 10. v. 22.cap. 24. v. 13.Apoc. 2. v. 10. Sola perseverantia coronatur.

4. Beneficiorum illorum omnium, quae Apostolus hactenus commemoravit, causa summa DEI misericordia; meritoria Christi passio; finis ultimus vita aeterna, ad quam per cruces & affilictiones perducimur, in quibus fide & spe confirmamur.

## 1:10
OF WHICH SALVATION THE PROPHETS HAVE INQUIRED AND SEARCHED DILIGENTLY, WHO PROPHESIED OF THE GRACE THAT SHOULD COME UNTO YOU.

We have seen hitherto the former proof, by which the Apostle wished to give confirmation that the doctrine concerning Christ, which those converted from Judaism had received from the Apostles, is altogether most true and most certain. This proof consisted in the enumeration of spiritual benefits, partly already conferred upon believers through this doctrine of the Gospel, partly still to be hoped for. The latter proof consists in the demonstration of the most exact consensus of the Apostolic doctrine with the Prophetic doctrine, the truth of which was indubitable to those converted from Judaism. This proof is completed in v. 10, 11, and 12. Indeed, others bring forward other reasons for the connection.

1. Some think that the Apostle is still engaged in the commemoration of the benefits conferred upon believers through the gospel, and is setting forth a new benefit, which is the illustrious manifestation of the mystery of salvation obtained through Christ, which manifestation is made through the preaching of the Gospel; but this benefit is amplified both by the added study of the Prophets, who accurately searched out this mystery, and especially the time of Christ being exhibited, and by the antithesis, that they ministered this by their study not to themselves, but to us, and by the authority of those through whom this mystery of salvation was made manifest, namely by the Apostles taught and led by the Holy Spirit, then finally from the effect, namely the desire of the Angels, because the sublimity and excellence of the mystery concerning the salvation brought about through Christ is so great, that the Angels themselves desire to look into it.

2. Some establish that the Apostle wishes to amplify the magnitude of the salvation, concerning which he had treated in the verse immediately preceding, from the study of the ancient Prophets.

3. Some proceed thus. The Apostle had hitherto preached the grace exhibited in Christ, now furthermore he teaches how this grace, faith, and salvation had been predicted by the Prophets in the Scriptures of the O. T., and announced everywhere by the Apostles in the N. Test. But it is manifest from the context and from a comparison of 2. Epist. 1. v. 19. & seqq. that the principal scope of the Apostle is that he wished to demonstrate the truth of the Apostolic doctrine from its consensus with the Prophetic doctrine.

By σωτηρίαν the Apostle understands not so much salvation itself, which befell believers even in the O. T. through faith in the promised Messiah, as the clearer manifestation of salvation, promised in the advent of the Messiah. In the compound words ἐκζητεῖν & ἐξερευνᾷν there is great emphasis. Christ uses the simple ἐρευνᾷν Ioh. 5. v. 39., in which Chrysostom, homil. 21. in Genes. & homil. 40. in Iohann., says it is a metaphor drawn from miners of metals, who search the innermost caverns of the earth. Some wish the metaphor to be taken from the sagacity of dogs, so that it signifies to inquire sagaciously into something and to unearth it from its hiding places. For the Etymologicum says ἐρευνᾷν is composed of ἐρέω i. e. ζητέω I seek and εὐνὴ a lair, which word Xenophon, lib. 3. de dict. & fact. Socratis & in lib. de venat., uses concerning the lair of a hare, ἐρευνᾶν concerning a hunter Euripid. in Hecuba, but Plutarch in lib. de curiosit. uses it concerning a dog, but it is better to say the metaphor is drawn from metals, as is evident from Prov. 1. vers. 4. If you seek wisdom as silver and ὡς θησαυροὺς ἐξερευνήσῃς αὐτὴν. It expresses, therefore, both the ardent desire and the singular study of the Prophets in searching out the salvation promised through the Messiah, to be most clearly revealed in his own advent. He adds, however, that he is speaking of those Prophets who prophesied concerning this grace, to be offered to the world in the Gospel in the time of the New Testament, that is, who consigned their prophecies to writing, he refers those to whom he writes to the Prophetic Scriptures, in which he commands them to search and to compare with them the doctrine of the Gospel, just as the Prophets searched in the Mosaic writings, and compared with them the divine revelations. By χάριν some understand the redemption made through Christ, and announced in the Gospel, others the grace of God offered to men in the Gospel. But these expositions are not opposed, but subordinate. The Vulgate rendered it, who prophesied of the grace to come in you, but in the Greek it is οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητέυσαντες, where to come is not added, nor is it in you, but unto you, namely, already bestowed and expended, and manifested and offered to the whole world in the Gospel. The Syrian rendered it, of the grace, which was to be, that it might be given to you.

Latin:

DE QUA SALUTE EXQUISIVERUNT, ATQUE SCRUTATI SUNT PROPHETAE, QUI DE FUTURA IN VOBIS GRATIA PROPHETARUNT.

Vidimus hactenus priorem probationem, quâ Apostolus confirmatum dare voluit, doctrinam de Christo, quam conversi ex Iudaismo ab Apostolis acceperant, esse omninò verissimam & certissimam. Constitit haec probatio enumeratione beneficiorum spiritualium, partim iamdum per hanc Evangelii doctrinam credentibus collatorum, partim adhuc sperandorum. Posterior probatio constat demonstratione exactissimi consensus doctrinae Apostolicae cum doctrina Prophetica, cuius veritas conversis ex Iudaismo erat indubitata. Absolvitur haec probatio v. 10. 11. & 12. Sanè alii alias afferunt connexionis rationes.

1. Quidam existimant, Apostolum adhuc versari in commemoratione beneficiorum per evangelium credentibus collatorum, ac novum exponere beneficium, quòd sit illustris patefactio mysterii salutis per Christum partae, quae patefactio fiat per praedicationem Evangelii; Amplificari autem hoc beneficium tùm ab adiuncto studio Prophetarum, qui hoc mysterium, & praesertim tempus Christi exhibendi, accuratè fuêre perscrutati, tùm ab antithesi, quod non sibi ipsis, sed nobis hoc studio suo ministraverint, tùm ab autoritate eorum, per quos hoc salutis mysterium patefactum, videlicet per Apostolos à Spiritu sancto doctos & ductos, tum denique ab effectu, videlicet desiderio Angelorum, quòd mysterii de salute per Christum parta tanta sit sublimitas & excellentia, ut ipsi Angeli in illud introspicere desiderent.

2. Quidam statuunt, Apostolum amplificare velle magnitudinem salutis, de qua in versu proximè praecedente egerat, à studio veterum Prophetarum.

3. Quidam sic progrediuntur. Apostolus hactenus gratiam in Christo exhibitam praedicaverat, nunc porrò docet, quomodo haec gratia, fides & salus per Prophetas in Scripturis V. T. praedicta, & per Apostolos in N. Test. ubivis fuerit annunciata. Sed manifestum est ex contextu & ex collatione 2. Epist. 1. v. 19. & seqq. principalem Apostoli scopum esse eum, quod veritatem doctrinae Apostolicae ex consensu cum doctrina Prophetica demonstrare voluerit.

Per σωτηρίαν intelligit Apostolus non tàm salutem ipsam, quae credentibus etiam in V. T. per fidem in promissum Messiam, obtigit, quàm clariorem salutis manifestationem, in Messiae adventu promissam. In verbis compositis ἐκζητεῖν & ἐξερευνᾷν magna est emphasis. Simplice ἐρευνᾷν utitur Christus Ioh. 5. v. 39. in quo Chrysostomus homil. 21. in Genes. & homil. 40. in Iohann. dicit, esse metaphoram ductam a fossoribus metallorum, qui intimas terrae cavernas perscrutantur. Quidam volunt, metaphoram à canum sagacitate petitam esse, ut significet sagaciter aliquid inquirere atque è latebris eruere. Etymologicus enim ἐρευνᾷν componi dicit ex ἐρέω i. e. ζητέωquaero &εὐνὴcubile, quam vocem Xenophon. lib. 3. de dict. & fact. Socratis & in lib. de venat. de leporis cubili usurpat, ἐρευνᾶνde venatore Euripid. in Hecuba, Plutarchus autem in lib. de curiosit. usurpat de cane, sed praestat, à metallis ductam dicere metaphoram, ut patet ex Prov. 1. vers. 4.Si quaesieris sapientiam quasi argentum &ὡς θησαυροὺς ἐξερευνήσῃς αὐτὴν. Exprimit igitur tùm ardens desiderium, tùm singulare studium Prophetarum in exquirenda salute per Messiam promissa, in ipsius adventu clarissimè revelanda. Addit autem, se loqui de illis Prophetis, qui Prophetarunt de hac gratia, in Evangelio tempore Novi Testamenti mundo offerenda, id est, qui Prophetias suas scripto consignarunt, remittit enim illos, quibus scribit, ad Scripturas Propheticas, in quibus scrutari & cum illis doctrinam Evangelii conferre iubet, sicut Prophetae in Scriptis Mosaicis scrutati fuêre, & cum illis divinas patefactiones contulerunt. Per χάριν quidam intelligunt redemtionem per Christum factam, & in Evangelio annunciatam, quidam gratiam Dei in Evangelio hominibus oblatam. Sed hae expositiones non sunt oppositae, sed subordinatae. Vulgata reddidit, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetarunt, sed in Graeco est, οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητέυσαντες, ubi non additur futura, nec est in vobis, sed in vos scilicet collata iam & impensa, atque in Evangelio toti mundo manifestata & oblata. Syrus reddidit, de gratia, quae futurum erat, ut vobis daretur.

## 1:10-12 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. To what end does the Apostle make mention of the Prophets? Resp. because he was writing to those to whom the Prophetic Scripture was known and authentic, he therefore commands that they diligently compare the Evangelical doctrine preached by the Apostles with it, and from the most exact harmony of both make a judgment concerning the truth of the Evangelical doctrine.

Q. 2. What kind of scrutiny of the Prophets does Peter understand here? Resp. he looks especially to the time of the coming of the Messiah, when, namely, the fulfillment of the promise concerning the coming of the Messiah is to be expected. Thus the Patriarch Jacob Genes. 49. v. 10. determines the time of the scepter being taken away from the tribe of Judah. Es. 2. v. 4.cap. 11. v. 6. it is predicted that there will be a time of universal peace. Daniel cap. 9. solicitously inquires concerning the time of the coming of of the Messiah, whence he is also called a man of desiresv. 23. and that is manifested to him through the Angel. v. 24.

Q. 3. Why are the scrutiny and the Prophetic prediction joined by the Apostle? Some establish that ἐξερεύνησιν καὶ ἐκζήτησιν the Prophetic is to be understood concerning their private study and desire, by which they wished to know the circumstances and manner of the revelation, and the state of the kingdom of Christ, προφητείαν but that it pertains to their public office, and the writings left to the Church. But it is more correctly said that ἐξερευνήσεως καὶ προφητείας the matter and the object are one and the same. For that which the Prophets had previously scrutinized, that they knew from the revelation of the Holy Spirit, and preached to others by living voice, and finally also consigned to the monuments of letters. Hence the Syriac version in verse 12 notably rendered it thus: And it was revealed to them, whatever they had scrutinized, because they were not inquiring for themselves.

Q. 4. Why does the Apostle speak in the plural τὰς δόξας Χριστοῦ? Some wish that by the name of Christ here is understood not only the head, but also the members, whose glories, like their sufferings, are also multiple and diverse. But the Apostle speaks primarily and principally not of the spiritual and mystical, but of the personal and proper body of Christ, and of the same following its sufferings and glory. He says therefore glories in the plural, because the glory that followed the passion of Christ was multiple, namely, absolute glory, consisting in the collation of glory made to Christ as man, and relative glory, consisting in the acknowledgment, manifestation, and preaching of that glory which was conferred. Absolute glory again was either finite, habitually inhering in Christ, or infinite, consisting in the plenary usurpation of the divine idioms communicated to Christ as man through personal union: likewise, the glory conferred upon Christ was conferred upon him either by reason of the soul, or by reason of the body, or by reason of the whole composite. The ancients say that the glory conferred upon Christ was the glory of the resurrection, the glory of the ascension, the glory of the session at the right hand of GOD, the glory of the name above every name given to him in exaltation, the glory of judicial power.

Q. 5. For what end does the Apostle make mention of the sufferings of Christ and the glories that followed them? Resp. that he may show that they themselves must enter into heavenly glory by the same way of sufferings Act. 14. v. 22. since through faith they are members of the mystical body of Christ, and not unless Christ by following, and by insisting upon his footsteps, they might be able to arrive at the glory of the heavenly kingdom.

Q. 6. Why the Apostle uses the word παρακύψαι? concerning the Angels Resp. 1. That he may show the sublimity of the mysteries revealed in the Gospel, because not even the Angels themselves, beholding GOD face to face, can perfectly comprehend them. 2. That he may set forth the dignity of the same mysteries, because the mysteries revealed in the Gospel are so excellent, that the Angels themselves desire a perfect knowledge of them. 3. That he may kindle in those to whom he writes a zeal for perceiving the mysteries proposed in the Gospel, and for progressing more fully in their knowledge from time to time. For if the Angels desire to look into them, how much more does that befit men. 4. Some think that regard is had to the two Cherubim, who, standing upon the ark of the covenant, by which Christ was prefigured, lowered their faces toward the lid of the ark, as if desiring to look into it Exod. 25. v. 18.

Q. 7. What is the cause of this desire in the Angels? Resp. 1. Because the wonderful and inscrutable wisdom of GOD shines forth in the work of redemption through Christ, therefore they long to look into it more deeply. 2. Because they delight in the salvation of men, to which the work of redemption and the manifestation of the Gospel is directed. Luc. 15. v. 10.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. The Prophets searched, prophesying. But the immediate illumination of the Holy Spirit, from which they prophesied, does not seem to consist with that searching. Resp. Maximus, writing thus on these words of Peter: The nature of man has indeed the power of searching and inquiring about divine things implanted in it by its author, but the grace of the Holy Spirit coming upon it makes the revelations. For it is not permitted to say that grace alone worked the knowledge of mysteries in the Saints without the faculties given by Nature for perceiving knowledge. Therefore they did not attain the knowledge of things and mysteries by natural powers alone without the grace of the Holy Spirit, otherwise the grace of the Holy Spirit would have been superfluous, which would effect nothing for the manifestation of truth. Nor would the grace of the Holy Spirit work into wisdom, without a mind receiving it? But all the saints declare that, if indeed after revelations were made they inquired into the reasons of the things revealed, as Abraham, how he was to possess the land; Moses, David, Daniel and Zechariah, seeking the reason of the visions. Thus Moses was an eminent Prophet, with whom GOD spoke mouth to mouth Num. 12. vers. 8.

Nevertheless, the mouth of the Lord, graciously dwelling in the midst of the two Cherubim, was asking. Luke in the preface to the History of the Gospel testifies that he had attained diligently to all things which pertained to the writing of the Gospel, and that from those who had heard, and seen, and had been ministers of the word.

2. They have been announced to you, through those who have evangelized to you. But Peter himself was in the number of those who had evangelized to them, if not by living voice, yet by this very writing. Response: Peter does not exempt himself by these words from the number of the Apostles through whom the Gospel was preached to the Jews and Gentiles, otherwise he would also exempt himself from the number of those upon whom the Holy Spirit was poured out from heaven, but he speaks thus either by the figure κοινοποιας, as if he were one from the number of those who had been converted by the Apostles Heb. 2. v. 3.1. Thess. 4. v. 15. & 17. or by the figure of synecdoche, because not one nor alone had he preached the Gospel to them.

3. Into which even the Angels desire to look. But those mysteries were not unknown to the Angels, illuminated by the light of divine wisdom, since GOD used their ministry in revealing mysteries of this kind. Response: The Apostle speaks not of the first degree of knowledge, but of a more abundant knowledge of those things which were previously known in part, according to many circumstances. The Angels are so delighted by the mysteries of the Gospel and the kingdom of Christ already known to them beforehand, that they desire to know them ever more fully and perfectly.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Peter That salvation, concerning which the Prophets have searched and prophesied, he calls χάριν. The Pope teaches, that it is not a gratuitous gift, but the merit of our works, that we merit begun salvation by meritorious works from congruity, and consummated salvation by meritorious works from condignity. But merit from condignity or justice is opposed to grace, as Bellarmine rightly teaches in book 2 of penance, chapter 12.

2. The Spirit of Christ was in the Prophets, Therefore Christ already existed while in the O. Testament and filled the Prophets with His Spirit, which is to be opposed to the Photinians, who deny the existence of Christ before his birth from the virgin Mary.

3. The Prophets spoke and wrote from the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. Therefore their Scripture is divine, which is to be opposed to the Photinians and Anabaptists, who disparage the Scriptures of the O. T.

4. The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of Christ. Therefore, He proceeds not only from the Father, but also from the Son. For just as He is called the Spirit of the Father, because He proceeds from the Father, so also He is called the Spirit of the Son and the Spirit of Christ, because He proceeds from the Son, which is to be opposed to the Greeks, who deny the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Son.
