5. The Holy Spirit, who was in the Prophets, revealed the future sufferings and glory of Christ. Therefore, He is true God, because it is the property of the true God alone to reveal future things, which are placed in the power and knowledge of God alone. Isa. 41. v. 21.chap. 45. v. 21.Dan. 2. v. 27. Damas. lib. 2. orth. fid. cap. 4. τὰ μέλλοντα οὐδὲ οἱ Ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐδὲ οἱ δαίμονες ὂιδασιν. This is to be opposed to the Macedonians and Photinians.

Ἐκδίκησις 1. The Photinians, from the fact that Peter says, that the prophets searched concerning the salvation revealed in the New Testament. Also, that it was manifested to the prophets, that not to themselves but to others who would live in the time of the New Testament they manifested it, they gather, that the way of salvation was not manifested in the Old Testament. I respond: 1. We invert the argument. Because the prophets searched concerning that salvation, therefore neither they nor other believers of the Old Testament were excluded from its participation. 2. A clearer manifestation of salvation and a richer grace reserved for the New Testament does not cause us to be able to exclude the pious of the Old Testament entirely from salvation and grace. For the Apostles testify to the contrary Acts 15. v. 11.Rom. 3. v. 21.chap. 4. v. 3. & 6.Heb. 11. v. 10. & 16. 3. Nor does the Apostle say that those things which were predicted by the prophets and consigned to writing did not pertain to them at all, but he expresses the use of the prophetic revelations, that they were not made only for their own sake, and for the sake of the believers of the Old Testament, but also for the sake of those in whose time those things were to be fulfilled which were revealed to them, and which they themselves predicted as future, namely, that they might be confirmed in faith from the comparison of the fulfillment with the prophecies. To this pertains the rule that negative particles are often placed for comparative ones. Gen. 32. v. 28.Ex. 16. v. 8.1. Sam. 8. v. 7. &c. Mark 9. v. 37.Luke 14. v. 12.John 5. v. 30.1. Cor. 1. v. 17. &c. and vice versa.

2. The same Photinians, from the fact that the Spirit of Christ is said in the prophets to have searched for future things, gather, that the Holy Spirit is not true God, and a person distinct from God the Father, because it does not befit infinite wisdom to search. If we wish to respond that the discourse here is not about the Holy Spirit considered in Himself, but about the Holy Spirit dwelling in the prophets, that they searched for future things, they will be able to object, that it is said of the Holy Spirit absolutely and considered in Himself, that He searches the depths of God 1. Cor.

2. v. 10. Resp. 1. We invert the argument. Because the Holy Spirit not only knows the interior recesses of human hearts, which is the property of the one true God 1. Reg. 8. v. 39. but also searches the depths of GOD Himself, whence Paul says of Him 1. Cor. 2. v. 11. the things of God, no one knows except the Spirit of God: and Isaiah cap. 40. v. 13. denies that He is in need of any instruction cap. 40. v. 13. therefore the Spirit is omniscient and all-wise, and consequently true God. 2. Nor can the contrary be proved from the word searching. For when Scripture speaks of GOD, it is accustomed to signify the consequent through the antecedent. Scrutiny and investigation precede knowledge, not indeed in God, but in us, and without it certain knowledge cannot be had, whence it happens that by the same manner of speaking άνθρωποπαθῶς the knowledge of God is indicated. Therefore, just as nothing is detracted from the infinite knowledge and wisdom of God the Father when He is said to search hearts and reins Psalm. 7. v. 10. Ierem. 11. v. 20. so also nothing departs from the divine and infinite knowledge of the Holy Spirit from the fact that He is said to have searched future things in the Prophets, or that the scrutiny of divine depths is attributed to Him.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The Prophets searched concerning the salvation and grace of the New Testament in the Mosaic writings; the Apostles searched in the Mosaic and Prophetic Scriptures. It is therefore our duty, according to the command of the Savior Ioh. 5. v. 39. to search the Mosaic, Prophetic, and Apostolic Scriptures. Clement of Alexandria, book 7, Stromata, fol. 348. δεῖ τὰς γραφὰς ἀκριβῶς διερευνᾶν, they do the contrary of the age οἱ ἐξ ἐπιπολῆς ἀναγινώσκοντες, as he speaks in the same book, f. 322. Beautifully Jobius in the Bibliotheca of Photius, f. 323. Sacred letters seem not unlike golden earth, which does not offer proven gold and profit greater than the labor to all, nor to common people, but only to those who laboriously and knowingly search through it. And just as he does not escape poverty who, handling fossil sand for the sake of ornament, play, or jest, applies no study meanwhile to investigate what lies hidden beneath it: so neither can he escape ignorance nor the reproach of negligence who, adhering only to the letter, does not search the treasure hidden in it, nor study to collect the utility latent in its depth. Chrysostom, homily 40, on John. Christ recalled the Jews not to a simple reading of the Scriptures but to a very diligent investigation. He did not say, read the scriptures, but search. For divine things are in need of the greatest diligence. For in the shadow He spoke not without reason to those greater ones, therefore He commands us to dig deeper, so that we may be able to find those things which lie hidden deep down. For we do not dig up a thing placed on the surface and in readiness, but that which is hidden deeply like a treasure. For he who seeks such things, unless he applies the greatest diligence and labor, will never find the things sought.

2. The scrutiny of the Prophets proves their highest desire, with which they awaited the coming of the Messiah. Psal. 14. v. 7.Esai. 45. v. 8.cap. 64. v. 1.Matth. 13. v. 17.Luc. 10. v. 24. It is therefore fitting for us to receive with rejoicing Him whom they awaited with desire.

3. Just as the Prophets most eagerly desired the first coming of Christ; so it is fitting for us to await the second coming of Christ with desire. Apoc. 22. v. 16. The Spirit and the bride say Come. Therefore, he who has the Spirit of Christ, and is the Bride of Christ, groans daily, Come Lord JESUS.

4. God promised His Gospel through the Prophets in the holy Scriptures Rom. 1. v. 2.cap. 16. v. 26. therefore the righteousness of faith has testimony from the law and the Prophets Rom. 3. v. 21. and what the Prophets in the O. Test. predicted would be, that the Apostles in the N. Test. announce as completed.

5. The Holy Spirit is called Spirit of Christ 1. because He proceeds from the Son just as from the Father. 2. because Christ by His passion and death merited the gift of the H. Spirit for men. 3. because Christ gives the H. Spirit to believers, not only visibly, as in the primitive Church, but also invisibly, as today. The third reason presupposes the second, the second the first. August. tract. 99. in Ioh. If the Spirit did not proceed from the Son, He could not, presenting Himself to the disciples after the resurrection by breathing upon them, say, Receive the Holy Spirit. For what else did that breathing signify, except that the Holy Spirit proceeds also from Him?

6. Spirit of Christ in the Prophets, Spirit of Christ in the Apostles. Thus it appears that the Prophets and Apostles announce the same salvation. Gloss. ordin. h. l.

7. The use of Prophetic Scripture is that we may compare the articles of the Christian religion with it, and be confirmed in faith from their most exact harmony. Act. 17. v. 11.

8. The παθήματα καὶ δόξαι, of Christ are joined together just as Christ Himself joins them most closely, Luc. 24. v. 26. because He did not arrive at glory except through passion Phil. 2. v. 9.Hebr. 2. v. 10. hence gloss. ord.

He interprets the later glories in this place as having been obtained by the preceding sufferings. Tertullian, book on the soldier's crown, chapter 14: Christ tasted honeycombs after gall, nor was He greeted as King of glory by the heavenly ones before He was written as King of the Jews on the cross, having been made a little lower than the angels by the Father, and thus crowned with glory and honor.

9. The Gospel announces two things especially concerning Christ, sufferings and glories, that is, the state of humiliation and exaltation; all things that are announced concerning Christ in the Evangelical History can be referred to these two states.

10. By the same way by which Christ entered into glory, we also must walk, Luke 22. v. 28.Acts 14. v. 22.2. Tim. 2. v. 12.Rev. 1. v. 9. where tribulation, the kingdom, and patience are joined together, and the kingdom is placed in the middle position between tribulation and patience. From this it is not absurdly thought that, in an accommodative sense, both the head and the members can be understood by the name of Christ, because believers as members of the mystical body fulfill τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ σαρκί σου Col. 1. v. 24.

11. It provides great comfort to us in sufferings that the Prophets predicted them, that Christ sanctified them in His own body, that not one kind of glory is to follow them. What else do persecutors do but fashion crowns for the pious? Gregory Nazianzen, oration 1 against Julian: Crowns are prepared for those who engage in the contest, not for those who sit above as spectators.

12. The truth and dignity of the Evangelical doctrine shines forth from the fact that the Prophets confirm it with their testimony, and that not only did they themselves prophesy concerning the mysteries revealed in the Gospel and solicitously search them out, but that even the Angels desire to look into them. Therefore, concerning those things which are confirmed by the consenting suffrage of so many Prophets and Apostles, and indeed even of the Angels themselves, no occasion for doubting remains.

13. Most sweet is the harmony of the Prophetic Church in the O. T., the Apostolic in the N. T., and the Angelic in heaven.

14. Because the Angels rejoice that men are to be joined to them in heavenly glory Luke 15. v. 10., therefore they look into the mysteries of the Gospel and the kingdom of Christ with the greatest desire, and they execute with the greatest joy and alacrity those things which pertain to the propagation of the kingdom of Christ. Eph. 3. v. 8.to me was given the grace of evangelizing among the Gentilesv. 10.that it might be made known now to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places through the Church the manifold wisdom of GOD.1. Tim. 3. v. 16.The Son of GOD manifested in the flesh ὤφθη was beheld with singular delight by the Angels, both when newly born, and when raised from death, and finally when received into heaven.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quo fine Apostolus Prophetarum mentionem faciat? Resp. quia scribebat ad eos, quibus Prophetica Scriptura erat nota & authentica, iubet igitur, ut doctrinam Evangelicam ab Apostolis praedicatam cum ea diligenter conferant, & exactissima utriusque harmonia de veritate doctrinae Evangelicae iudicium faciant.

Q. 2. Quale Prophetarum scrutinium Petrus hîc intelligat? Resp. respicit potissimùm ad tempus adventus Messiae, quando scil. promissionis de adventu Messiae complementum sit exspectandum. Sic Patriarcha Iacobus Genes. 49. v. 10. determinat tempus ablati à tribu Iuda sceptri. Es. 2. v. 4.cap. 11. v. 6. praedicitur fore tempus pacis Universalis. Daniel. cap. 9. solicitè quaerit de tempore adventus Messiae, unde etiam vocatur vir desideriorumv. 23. ac per Angelum illud ipsi manifestatur. v. 24.

Q. 3. Quare scrutinium & vaticinium Propheticum ab Apostolo coniungantur? Quidam statuunt, ἐξερεύνησιν καὶ ἐκζήτησινPropheticam de privato eorum studio ac desiderio intelligendam esse, quâ circumstantias & modum revelationis, statumque regni Christi cognoscere voluerunt,προφητείανverò ad publicum eorum munus, & scripta Ecclesiae relicta pertinere. Sed rectiùs dicitur, ἐξερευνήσεως καὶ προφητείας unam eandemque esse materiam & idem obiectum. Quod enim Prophetae priùs fuêre scrutati, illud ex revelatione Spiritus S. cognoverunt, ac vivâ voce aliis praedicârunt, tandem etiam literarum monumentis consignârunt. Inde Syrus vers. 12. notanter sic reddidit. Et revelatum est illis, quicquid scrutati fuerant, propterea quod non sibiipsis inquirebant.

Q. 4. Quare Apostolus in plurali dicatτὰς δόξας Χριστοῦ? Quidam volunt, Christi nomine hîc intelligi non solùm caput, sed etiam membra, quorum ut passiones ita quoque gloriae sunt multiplices ac diversae. Sed Apostolus primariò ac principaliter non de spirituali & mystico, sed de personali & proprio Christi corpore, eiusdemque passionibus & gloria easdem insecuta loquitur. Dicit ergò glorias in plurali, quia gloria passionem Christi insecuta fuit multiplex, videlicet gloria absoluta, in collatione gloriae Christo homini facta consistens, & gloria relativa, in agnitione, manifestatione & praedicatione illius gloriae collatae consistens. Gloria absoluta iterum fuit vel finita, habitualiter Christo inhaerens, vel infinita, in divinorum idiomatum, per unionem personalem Christo homini communicatorum, plenariâ usurpatione consistens: Gloria item Christo collata, vel ratione animae, vel ratione corporis, vel ratione totius compositi ipsi fuit collata. Veteres dicunt, quòd gloria Christo collata fuerit gloria resurrectionis, gloria ascensionis, gloria sessionis ad dextram DEI, gloria nominis super omne nomen in exaltatione ipsi dati, gloria potestatis iudiciariae.

Q. 5. Quo fine passionum Christi & gloriarum eas insecutarum mentionem Apostolus faciat? Resp. ut ostendat, ipsos eadem viâ passionum in gloriam coelestem ingredi oportere Act. 14. v. 22. cum per fidem sint membra corporis Christi mystici, ac non nisi Christum sequendo, & vestigiis eius insistendo, ad gloriam regni coelestis pervenire possint.

Q. 6. Quare Apostolus de Angelis utatur verboπαρακύψαι? Resp. 1. Ut ostendat mysteriorum in Evangelio revelatorum sublimitatem, quod nec ipsi Angeli, DEUM à facie ad faciem intuentes, ea perfectè comprehendere possint. 2. Ut eorundem mysteriorum exponat dignitatem, quòd mysteria in Evangelio revelata tàm praeclara sint, ut ipsi etiam Angeli perfectam eorum ex optent notitiam. 3. Ut accendat in eis, ad quos scribit, studium percipiendi mysteria in Evangelio proposita, inque eorum cognitione pleniùs subinde proficiendi. Si enim Angeli cupiunt ea introspicere, quantò magis hominibus illud competit. 4. Quidam putant, respectum haberi ad duos Cherubin, qui arcae foederis, per quam Christus praefigurabatur, insistentes, facies suas versus operculum arcae demittebant, velut introspicere desiderantesExod. 25. v. 18.

Q. 7. Quae causa huius desiderii in Angelis? Resp. 1. Quia mirabilis & imperscrutabilis DEI sapientia in opere redemtionis per Christum relucet, ideò eam penitiùs introspicere gestiunt. 2. Quia delectantur hominum salute, ad quam opus redemtionis & Evangelii manifestatio dirigitur. Luc. 15. v. 10.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Prophetae scrutati sunt vaticinantes. Atqui immediata Spiritus sancti illuminatio, ex qua prophetarunt, non videtur cum ille scrutinio consistere. Resp. Maximus in haec verba Petri sic scribens. Vim quidem scrutandi & inquirendi de rebus divinis habet Natura hominis sibi insitam ab autore suo, revelationes vero Spiritus sancti gratia adveniens facit. Nec enim licet dicere, quòd sola gratia operabatur in Sanctis cognitionem mysteriorum sine facultatibus ad percipiendam cognitionem à Natura datis. Non igitur absque Spiritus sancti gratia solis viribus naturalibus cognitionem rerum & mysteriorum consecuti sunt, alioqui supervacanea fuisset Spiritus sancti gratia, quae nihil efficeret ad manifestationem veritatis. Neque gratia Spiritus sancti operaretur in sapientiam, sine mente eam recipiente? Id autem declarant omnes sancti, siquidem post revelationes factas inquirunt rationes revelatorum, ut Abraham, quomodo possessurus sit terram; Moses, David, Daniel & Zacharias, quaerentes rationem visionum. Sic Moses erat eximius Propheta, cum quo DEUS ore ad os loquebaturNum. 12. vers. 8.

nihilo tamen minùs interrogabat os Domini gratiosè habitantis in medio duorum Cherubim. Lucas in praefat. Hist. Evang. testatur, se assecutum omnia diligenter, quae ad Evangelii scriptionem pertinebant, idque ab iis, qui ipsi audierant, & viderant, & ministri fuerant sermonis.

2. Nunciata sunt vobis, per eos, qui evangelizarunt vobis. Atqui Petrus ipse erat in eorum numero, qui evangelizaverat illis, si non vivâ voce, tamen hoc ipso scripto. Resp. non eximit sese Petrus his verbis ex numero Apostolorum, per quos Evangelium Iudaeis & gentibus praedicatum, aliàs etiam sese eximeret ê numero eorum, in quos Spiritus sanctus coelitus est effusus, sed sic loquitur vel per figuram κοινοποιας, quasi unus esset ex numero eorum, qui ab Apostolis conversus Hebr. 2. v. 3.1. Thess. 4. v. 15. & 17. vel per figuram synecdoches, quòd non unus nec solus Evangelium ipsis praedicasset.

3. In quae desiderant etiam Angeli introspicere. Atqui mysteria illa non fuêre Angelis, divinae sapientiae luce collustratis, ignota, cum eorum ministerio in revelandis huiusmodi mysteriis DEUS usus sit. Resp. loquitur Apostolus non de primo cognitionis gradu, sed de uberiore eorum, quae antea ex parte nota, secundùm plures circumstantias cognitione. Angeli mysteriis Evangelii & regni Christi â se iam antê cognitis adeò delectantur, ut subinde pleniùs ac perfectiùs ea nosse cupiant.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Petrus Salutem illam, de qua Prophetae scrutati & vaticinati sunt, vocat χάριν. Papa docet, eam non esse gratuitum donum, sed operum nostrorum meritum, inchoatam salutem nos promereri operibus meritoriis ex congruo, consummatam salutem operibus meritoriis ex condigno. At meritum ex condigno sive iustitia opponitur gratiae, ut rectè docet Bellarminus lib. 2. de poenit. cap. 12.

2. Spiritus Christi fuit in Prophetis, Ergo Christus iam dum in V. Test. extitit ac Spiritu suo implevit Prophetas, quod opponendum Photinianis, negantibus Christi existentiam ante nativitatem ex Maria virgine.

3. Prophetae locuti sunt & scripserunt ex inspiratione Spiritus sancti. Ergo Scriptura ipsorum divina, quod opponendum Photinianis & Anabaptistis, Scripturas V. T. vilipendentibus.

4. Spiritus Sanctus est Spiritus Christi. Ergo non solùm à Patre, sed etiam à Filio procedit. Ut enim dicitur Spiritus Patris, quia à Patre procedit, ita quoque Spiritus Filii & Spiritus Christi dicitur, quia à Filio procedit, quod opponendum Graecis, processionem Spiritus Sancti à Filio negantibus.

5. Spiritus Sanctus, qui fuit in Prophetis, revelavit futuras Christi passiones & gloriam. Ergo est verus Deus, quia solius veri Dei proprium, revelare futura, in solius Dei potestate & scientia posita. Esa. 41. v. 21.cap. 45. v. 21.Dan. 2. v. 27. Damas. lib. 2. orth. fid. cap. 4. τὰ μέλλοντα οὐδὲ οἱ Ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐδὲ οἱ δαίμονες ὂιδασιν. Opponendum hoc Macedonianis & Photinianis.

Ἐκδίκησις 1. Photiniani ex eo, quod Petrus dicit. Prophetas de salute in N. T. revelata scrutatos fuisse. Item. Prophetis manifestatum fuisse, quod non sibi ipsis sed aliis tempore N. T. victuris manifestaverint, colligunt, viam salutis in V. T. non fuisse manifestatam Resp. 1. invertimus argumentum. Quia Prophetae de illa salute scrutati fuêre. Ergo ab eius participatione, nec ipsi nec alii credentes V. T. fuêre exclusi. 2. Clarior salutis manifestatio & uberior gratia N. Test. reservata non efficit, ut à salute & gratia pios V. T. penitus excludere possimus. Contrarium enim testantur Apostoli Act. 15. v. 11.Rom. 3. v. 21.cap. 4. v. 3. & 6.Hebr. 11. v. 10. & 16. 3. Neque dicit Apostolus, ea, quae à Prophetis praedicta & scriptis consignata, nihil ad ipsos attinuisse, sed usum revelationum Propheticarum exprimit, quod non sint factae tantùm propter ipsos, & propter credentes V. Test. sed etiam propter eos, quorum tempore implenda erant, quae ipsis revelabantur, quaeque ipsi futura praedicebant, videl. ut ex collatione complementi cum vaticiniis in fide confirmentur. Hûc pertinet regula, quòd particulae negativae saepe ponantur pro comparativis. Gen. 32. v. 28.Ex. 16. v. 8.1. Sam. 8. v. 7. &c. Marc. 9. v. 37.Luc. 14. v. 12.Ioh. 5. v. 30.1. Cor. 1. v. 17. &c. & vice versa.

2. Iidem Photiniani ex eo, quod Spiritus Christi in Prophetis dicitur futura scrutatus, colligunt, Spiritum S. non esse verum Deum, & distinctam à Deo Patre personam, quia infinitae sapientiae non convenit scrutari. Si respondere velimus, sermonem hîc esse non de Spiritu Sancto in se considerato, sed de Spiritu Sancto in Prophetis habitante, quod illi futura scrutati sint, excipere poterunt, de Spiritu S. absolutè & in se considerato dici, quòd scruetur profunditates Dei 1. Cor.

2. v. 10. Resp. 1. invertimus argumentum. Quia Spiritus Sanctus non solùm novit interiores cordium humanorum recessus, quod est solius veri Dei proprium 1. Reg. 8. v. 39. sed etiam scrutatur ipsius DEI profunditates, unde Paulus de ipso dicit 1. Cor. 2. v. 11.quae Dei sunt, nemo novit nisi Spiritus Dei: ac Esaias cap. 40. v. 13. negat, ipsum ullius instructionis indigere cap. 40. v. 13. ideò Spiritus est omniscius & omnisapiens, & per consequens verus Deus. 2. Nec potest contrarium probari ex verbo scrutandi. Quando enim Scriptura de DEO loquitur, consequens significare solet per antecedens. Scrutinium & indagatio antecedit scientiam, non quidem in Deo, sed in nobis, & absque ea certa notitia haberi nequit, unde fit, ut eodem loquendi genere άνθρωποπαθῶς Dei notitia indicetur. Quemadmodum ergo infinitae Dei Patris scientiae & sapientiae nihil derogatur, quando corda & renes scrutari diciturPsalm. 7. v. 10.Ierem. 11. v. 20. ita quoque Spiritus S. scientiae divinae & infinitae ex eo nihil decedit, quod in Prophetis futura dicitur scrutatus, vel profunditatum, divinarum scrutinium ipsi tribuitur.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Prophetae de salute & gratia N. T. in scriptis Mosaicis; Apostoli in Mosaicis & Propheticis Scriptis scrutati fuere. Nostrum ergo est, iuxta mandatum Salvatoris Ioh. 5. v. 39. Mosaicas, Propheticas & Apostolicas Scripturas scrutari. Clemens Alexandrin. lib. 7. Stromat. fol. 348. δεῖ τὰς γραφὰς ἀκριβῶς διερευνᾶν,evi contrarium faciuntοἱ ἐξ ἐπιπολῆς ἀναγινώσκοντες, ut loquitur lib. eod. f. 322. Pulchrè Iobius in Bibliotheca Photii f. 323. Sacrae literae non dissimiles aureae terrae videntur, quae non omnibus neque vulgaribus, sed laboriosè tantum ac scienter perscrutantibus aurum probatum & lucrum labore maius praebet. Quemadmodum itaque paupertatem non evadit, qui fossilem arenam ornamenti, ludi aut ioci causâ tractans nullum interea studium adhibet, ut quod sub ea absconditum latet, investiget: sic neque ignorantiam neque negligentiae reprehensionem evadere queat, qui soli literae adhaerescens thesaurum in ea reconditum non scrutetur, neque latentem in eius fundo utilitatem colligere studeat. Chrysost. homil. 40. in Ioh. Christus Iudaeos ad Scripturarum non simplicem lectionem sed ad investigationem perquàm diligentem revocavit. Non dixit, legite scripturas, sed scrutamini. Divina enim summâ indigent diligentiá. In umbra enim maioribus illis non abs re locutus est, idcircò effodere profundius iubet, ut quae altè delitescunt, invenire possimus. Non enim rem in superficie & in promtu positam effodimus, sed quae tanquam thesaurus profundè reconditur. Qui enim huiusmodi quaerit, nisi summam adhibeat diligentiam & laborem, nunquam quaesita inveniet.

2. Scrutinium Prophetarum arguit summum ipsorum desiderium, quo Messiae adventum expectarunt. Psal. 14. v. 7.Esai. 45. v. 8.cap. 64. v. 1.Matth. 13. v. 17.Luc. 10. v. 24. Nobis ergo convenit excipere cum tripudio, quem illi expectarunt cum desiderio.

3. Sicut Prophetae primum Christi adventum cupidissimè desiderarunt; ita nobis convenit secundum Christi adventum desideranter expectare. Apoc. 22. v. 16. Spiritus & sponsa dicunt Veni. Ergo qui habet Spiritum Christi, & est Sponsa Christi, quotidie ingemiscit, Veni Domine IESU.

4. Deus Evangelium suum promisit per Prophetas in Scripturis sanctis Rom. 1. v. 2.cap. 16. v. 26. proinde iustitia fidei testimonium habet à lege & Prophetis Rom. 3. v. 21. ac quod Prophetae in V. Test. praedixerunt futurum, illud Apostoli in N. Test. nunciant completum.

5. Spiritus Sanctus vocatur Spiritus Christi 1. quia â Filio aequè ac à Patre procedit. 2. quia Christus sua passione & morte Spiritus S. donationem hominibus promeruit. 3. quia Christus credentibus Spiritum S. donat, non solùm visibiliter, ut in Ecclesia primitiva, sed etiam invisibiliter, ut hodie. Tertia ratio praesupponit secundam, secunda primam. August. tract. 99. in Ioh. Si non à Filio Spiritus procederet, non posset post resurrectionem se repraesentans discipulis insufflando dicere, Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Quid enim aliud significavit illa insufflatio, nisi quod procedat Spiritus Sanctus & de ipso?

6. Spiritus Christi in Prophetis, Spiritus Christi in Apostolis. Ita apparet, quod Prophetae & Apostoli eandem salutem nuncient. Gloss. ordin. h. l.

7. Usus Scripturae Propheticae est, ut articulos Christianae religionis cum ea conferamus, atque ex harmonia eorum exactissima in fide confirmemur. Act. 17. v. 11.

8. Coniunguntur Christi παθήματα καὶ δόξαι, sicut etiam Christus ipse ea arctissimè coniungit, Luc. 24. v. 26. quia non nisi per passionem ad gloriam pervenit Phil. 2. v. 9.Hebr. 2. v. 10. inde glossa ord.

posteriores glorias h. l. interpretatur praecedentibus passionibus comparatas. Tertullianus lib. de corona milit. cap. 14. Christus favos post fella gustavit, nec antea Rex gloriae à coelestibus salutatus est, quàm Rex Iudaeorum praescriptus in cruce, minoratus primùm à Patre modicum quid citra Angelos, & ita gloriâ & honore coronatus.

9. Evangelium duo potissimùm de Christo nunciat, passiones & glorias i. e. statum exinanitionis & exaltationis, ad duos hosce status referri possunt omnia, quae de Christo in Evangelica Historia nunciantur.

10. Eadem viâ, quâ Christus in gloriam ingressus, etiam nobis incedendum, Luc. 22. v. 28.Actor. 14. v. 22.2. Tim. 2. v. 12.Apocal. 1. v. 9. ubi tribulatio, regnum, & patientia coniunguntur, ac regnum inter tribulationem & patientiam medio loco ponitur. Inde haud absurdè cogitatur, Christi nomine in sensu accommodatitio, & caput & membra intelligi posse, quia credentes tanquam membra corporis mystici adimplent τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ σαρκί σουCol. 1. v. 24.

11. Magnum in passionibus nobis praestat solatium, quòd Prophetae illas praedixerunt, quòd Christus in suo corpore eas sanctificaverit, quòd non unum genus gloriae eas consecuturum sit. Quid aliud faciunt persecutores, quàm quòd coronas piis fabricant? Gregor. Nazianz. orat. 1. in Iulian. Coronae in eos comparantur, qui certamine congrediuntur, non qui sursum sedent velut spectatores.

12. Evangelicae doctrinae veritas & dignitas elucet ex eo, quòd Prophetae suo testimonio eam confirmant, quodque non ipsi solùm de mysteriis in Evangelio revelatis vaticinati solicitè eadem fuêre perscrutati, sed quòd etiam Angeli in ea introspicere desiderent. Quae ergò tanto Prophetarum & Apostolorum, imò etiam ipsorum Angelorum consentiente suffragio confirmata, de illis nulla dubitandi superest occasio.

13. Suavissima est consonantia Ecclesiae Propheticae in V. T. est. Apostolicae in N. T. & Angelicae in coelo.

14. Quia Angeli gaudent homines sibi sociandos in coelesti gloria Luc. 15. v. 10. ideò summo cum desiderio mysteria Evangelii & regni Christi introspiciunt, ac summo cum gaudio & alacritate ea, quae ad propagationem regni Christi faciunt, exequuntur. Eph. 3. v. 8.mihi data est gratia evangelizandi in gentibusv. 10.ut innotescat nunc principatibus & potestatibus in coelestibus per Ecclesiam multiformis sapientia DEI.1. Tim. 3. v. 16.Filius DEI in carne manifestatusὤφθηsingulari cum delectatione conspectus est ab Angelis tùm recens natus, tùm à morte excitatus, tùm denique in coelum receptus.

## 1:11
SEARCHING WHAT OR WHAT MANNER OF TIME THE SPIRIT OF CHRIST WHICH WAS IN THEM DID SIGNIFY, WHEN IT TESTIFIED BEFOREHAND THE SUFFERINGS OF CHRIST, AND THE GLORY THAT SHOULD FOLLOW.

The Apostle explains more specifically what the Prophets searched concerning that salvation and grace of the N. T., namely, into what time, near or still far distant; and into what manner of time, quiet or warlike, the Advent of the Messiah ought to fall. In the Greek there is a certain transposition of words to be ordered thus. Ἐρευνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρὸν τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ προμαρτυρούμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν (ἐλευσύμενα.) παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας ὲδήλου (namely πεσεῖσθαι αὐτὰ.) By καιρὸν not simply time, but opportune time and the juncture of time, the time convenient for a thing to be done and executed is properly understood Acts 1. v. 7. which meaning best agrees with this place. τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ the Spirit of Christ, which was in them, namely, προμαρτυρούμενον testifying beforehand, testifying previously. The sense is, that the Spirit of Christ, which was in the Prophets and spoke through them, had testified and predicted both the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that would follow the same, before either those happened, or this was bestowed upon him.

Latin:

SCRUTANTES IN QUOD VEL QUALE TEMPUS SIGNIFICARET IN EIS SPIRITUS CHRISTI, PRAENUNCIANS EAS QUAE IN CHRISTO SUNT PASSIONES, & POSTERIORES GLORIAS.

Specialiùs exponit Apostolus, quid de salute & gratia illa N. T. Prophetae fuerint scrutati, videl. in quod tempus, propinquum aut longè adhuc distans; & in quale tempus, quietum aut bellicosum Adventus Messiae incidere debeat. In Graeco est quaedam verborum traiectio sic ordinanda. Ἐρευνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρὸν τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ προμαρτυρούμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν (ἐλευσύμενα.) παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας ὲδήλου (scil. πεσεῖσθαι αὐτὰ.) Per καιρὸν non simpliciter tempus, sed oportunum tempus & temporis articulus, tempus rei gerendae & exequendae commodum propriè intelligitur Act. 1. v. 7. quae significatio optimè huic loco congruit. τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα ΧριστοῦSpiritus Christi, qui in eis sc. erat,προμαρτυρούμενονpraenuncians, priùs testificans. Sensus est, quod Spiritus Christi, qui erat in Prophetis & per eos loquebatur, testatus fuerit ac praedixerit tum passiones Christi, tum gloriam easdem secuturam, priusquam vel illae acciderent, vel haec ipsi conferretur.

## 1:12
TO WHOM IT WAS REVEALED, THAT NOT UNTO THEMSELVES, BUT UNTO US THEY DID MINISTER THE THINGS, WHICH ARE NOW REPORTED UNTO YOU BY THEM THAT HAVE PREACHED THE GOSPEL UNTO YOU WITH THE HOLY GHOST SENT DOWN FROM HEAVEN; WHICH THINGS THE ANGELS DESIRE TO LOOK INTO.

Some Greek codices in the first place in the words οὐχ ἐαυτοῖς, ὑμῖν δὲ, read ήμῖν in the first person, and it is read thus also in Didymus the Latin. But other more approved and more ancient codices more correctly read ὑμῖν in the second person, for immediately follows ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη ύμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμὲνων ύμᾶς, so that the person is not changed, in which way Oecumenius and all Latin codices read. οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη. Erasmus at this place annotates thus. The Greek discourse is ambiguous. For the sense can be taken here, testifying of the passions and glories of Christ to those to whom the Spirit revealed it, namely the Prophets. It can also be taken here, the passions and glories, through which Christ was revealed to the world, who had previously been unknown. Nor should the Greek article move anyone οἷς, since there preceded παθήματα. Although the former sense in my judgment is simpler, that οἷς the article should be referred to the Christians, who saw that which the Spirit had predicted concerning Christ in the Prophets. For he feels that through afflictions the glory of Christ became known to the world. A third sense can also be taken here, to which Prophets it was revealed both that, that these things which they were preaching were preparing for you, not for themselves, since they knew that they would not happen in their own times. A fourth sense can also be taken here. The Prophets predicted both the death of Christ, and the illumination brought forth by his death, both truly, which is known to those to whom these things have been exhibited. But the thing itself shows that the pronoun οἷς is most simply referred to the Prophets ἐρευνοῦντας, because to them through the Holy Spirit, who was in them, even this was revealed, that not to themselves, but to those who were to live in the New Testament after the coming of the promised Messiah, they ministered those things which they predicted in their own times would be future, but in the New Testament are announced as completed. Some take it specifically concerning the coming of the Messiah, so that the sense may be. The Prophets prophesied concerning these things which have been announced to you in the New Testament, i. e. they learned from the revelation of the Holy Spirit, that Christ, concerning whom they prophesied, was to come not in their own times, but in the fullness of time in the New Testament. Dan. 9. v. 24. cap. 12. v. 9. & 13. Hebr. 11. v. 13. But it is more correctly taken generally concerning the whole doctrine of the Gospel, concerning the person, office, benefits, and kingdom of the Messiah, and the whole state of the New Testament, so that the sense may be. Not unto themselves but unto you did the Prophets minister, predicting those things in the N. Testament to come, which are announced to you as completed in the word of the Gospel, so that, namely, from a comparison of those things which were predicted by the Prophets with those which are announced to you as completed in the Gospel, you might know the immovable truth of the Evangelical doctrine, and be confirmed in the faith. Therefore the Apostle says this: The Prophets of the O. T. of whom I speak, were indeed taken away by death, so that they did not behold face to face the coming of Christ, the work of redemption performed through him, his sufferings and glories, and the state of his kingdom, and as the Epistle to the Hebrews speaks cap. 11. v. 13. all these died according to faith, not having received the promises, but seeing them from afar and greeting them, meanwhile, however, they by no means bore that with difficulty, because this also was revealed to them by the Holy Spirit, that they were ministering not to themselves, but to others coming after several centuries, those things which are now announced in the N. Testament, i. e. that those prophecies were not to obtain their fulfillment in their own times, but only in future times, and therefore they ought to consign them to writing not for themselves, but for the use of others. Furthermore, the Apostle explains through whom those things which were predicted by the Prophets were announced as completed to those to whom he writes in the N. T. Διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ὑμᾶς he says, through those who preached the Gospel to you, that is, through the holy Apostles and their συλλειτούργους. ἐν πνέυματι ἀγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ. in the preaching of the Gospel, which the Vulgate version rendered with the preposition omitted, the Holy Spirit having been sent from heaven. But the Greek text, which alone is authentic, by no means has it added idly. The Apostles evangelized to you and announced as completed those things which were predicted in the O. T. by the Prophets, not by human will, but in the Holy Spirit, or through the Holy Spirit, sent to them from heaven. The sense is that the Apostles, having been most perfectly instructed concerning the mysteries of the faith by the Holy Spirit poured out upon them on the day of Pentecost in the form of tongues of fire, began, by the impulse, power, and efficacy of the same Holy Spirit, to preach the Gospel in the whole world and to explain the mysteries of the Christian faith. Thus Act. 2. v. 14. after the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, Peter immediately preaches at Jerusalem. He performs the same Act. 3. v. 12. Thus Act. 4. v. 8. it is said of Peter, that filled with the Holy Spirit he delivered an apologetic sermon to the Princes of the people and the Elders of Israel. v. 31. it is added, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with confidence v. 33. and with great power they were rendering The Apostle's testimony of the resurrection of Christ. Concerning Stephen it is said cap. 6. v. 10 they could not resist the wisdom and the Spirit, by which he spoke. Finally the Apostle adds εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι. The relative ἃ is variously explained by the ancients. 1. Gregory, homily 8 on Ezekiel, interprets it of GOD absolutely, that the Angels are delighted by his beatific vision. The Angels, he says, see God without weariness, and therefore they are said to have a perpetual desire of seeing him, because by seeing they are not fatigued, book 18 of the Morals, chapter 28. 2. Bede refers it to Christ as man, of whom in v. 11 mention had been made, in this sense, that the Angels rejoice to look into Christ as man, especially now glorified, since in him, and through him, all things in heaven and earth have been restored. Eph. 1. v. 10. 3. The same Bede also applies it to the Holy Spirit, of whom in v. 11. & 12. mention precedes, so that the sense is, that the Angels gaze upon the Holy Spirit together with the Father and the Son as the true GOD with the highest pleasure and never-ending desire. The Ordinary Gloss likewise joins both expositions, into whom, namely, Christ or the Holy Spirit. These expositions take their origin from the fact that certain Greek and Latin Codices read εἰς ὃν, into whom, namely, Christ or the Holy Spirit. But the more approved Greek and Latin Codices read εἰς ἃ, into which, in which way also Ambrose reads, book 4 de Sacram. chapter 2. Isidore, book 1, Epistle 119. 4. Some therefore refer it to the passions and glories of Christ in v. 11. because an Angel was present to Christ in his passion, comforting him Luc. 22. v. 43. that is, speaking with him about the mystery of the passion, and in the history of the resurrection Angels appear in white garments rejoicing with the resurrected Christ Matth. 28. v. 3. Marc. 16. v. 5. Luc. 24. v. 4. But also the athletes of Christ, configured to him through passions, exhibit a spectacle not only to the world and to men, but also to the Angels 1. Cor. 4. v. 5. But because τὰ παθήματα καὶ αἱδόξαι are more remotely distant, therefore. 5. The relative ἃ is more simply referred to those things which were predicted by the Prophets in the O. T. concerning Christ, and announced by the Apostles in the Gospel, of which mention had been made in the words immediately preceding, in which way Irenaeus, a most ancient writer, explains it in book 4, chapter 77, namely concerning the promises of the Prophets, which Christ fulfilled upon arriving. The scope of the Apostle also confirms this exposition, for he is still occupied in commending and confirming the majesty, authority, and truth of the Evangelical doctrine preached by the Apostles, which he demonstrates not only from the benefits which through it are partly bestowed upon believers, and partly certainly promised; and not only from the prophecies of the Prophets, who predicted many centuries before that what is announced in the Gospel would come to pass, but also from the desire of the Angels themselves, who with the greatest zeal yearn to look more deeply into the mysteries of human salvation predicted by the Prophets and announced by the Apostles in the Gospel. παρακύπτειν is indeed properly used of those who incline themselves with the zeal of observing and looking more deeply into things, and who explore all things with the greatest zeal, and look diligently with fixed eyes. Luc. 24. v. 12.Ioh. 20. v. 5. & 11. it is used of John, with his head inclined or bent obliquely, looking into the tomb of Christ; for thus were the tombs constructed among the Jews, that they could not be looked into by one standing erect, but could indeed by one inclined. And because this manner of looking is employed to that end, that a thing may be accurately known, therefore it is used simply for accurate inspection. Iac. 1. v. 25. The LXX Cant. 2. v. 9. use it for שגח, which is to look forward intently, and with observation of the mind. Also for שקף to look forth from on high Gen. 26. v. 8.1. Paral. 15. v. 29.Prov. 7. v. 6. With this exposition, by which through those things which the Angels desire to look into more deeply are understood those things predicted by the Prophets in the O. and announced by the Apostles in the N. T., it does not at all conflict that some say the mysteries of the Gospel are understood, some the mysteries of faith, some the mysteries of the kingdom of Christ, some the mysteries of human salvation, for all these things are contained in the number of those which were predicted by the Prophets and announced by the Apostles as completed; therefore to all those things, but especially to the mystery of redemption performed through Christ, this Petrine word ought to be accommodated.

Latin:

QUIBUS REVELATUM EST, QUIA NON SIBIIPSIS, VOBIS AUTEM MINISTRABANT EA, QUAE NUNC NUNTIATA SUNT VOBIS PER EOS, QUI EVANGELIZARUNT VOBIS SPIRITU SANCTO MISSO DE COELO, IN QUAE DESIDERANT ANGELI PROSPICERE.

Quidam Graeci Codd. priore loco in verbis οὐχ ἐαυτοῖς, ὑμῖν δὲ, legunt ήμῖν in prima persona, ita quoque legitur apud Didymum Latinum. Sed alii Codices probatiores & antiquiores rectiùs legunt ὑμῖν in secunda persona, statim enim sequitur ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη ύμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμὲνων ύμᾶς, ut persona non mutetur, quo modo Oecumenius & omnes Codd. Latini legunt. οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη. Erasmus ad h. l. sic annotat. Sermo Graecus anceps est. Potest enim hic accipi sensus, testificans Christi passiones & glorias iis, quibus revelavit Spiritus, nempe Prophetis. Potest & hic, passiones & glorias, per quas Christus fuit mundo revelatus, qui antea fuerat ignotus. Neque quemquam movere debet articulus Graecusοἷς,cum praecesseritπαθήματα.Quanquam prior sensus meo iudicio simplicior est, utοἷςarticulus referatur ad Christianos, qui viderunt id, quod de Christo praedixerat Spiritus in Prophetis. Sentit enim per afflictiones innotuisse mundo Christi gloriam. Potest & hic tertius accipi sensus, quibus Prophetis revelatum est & illud, quod haec, quae praedicabant, vobis pararent non sibi, cum scirent, ea non eventura suis temporibus. Potest & quartus hic accipi. Prophetae praedixerunt & Christi mortem, & illustrationem morte partam, utrumque verè, quod notum est iis, quibus ea sunt exhibita. Sed res ipsa ostendit, pronomen οἷς simplicissimè referri ad Prophetas ἐρευνοῦντας, quod illis per Spiritum Sanctum, qui in ipsis erat, etiam hoc revelatum sit, quod non sibi, sed illis, qui in N. T. post promissi Messiae adventum victuri erant, ministraverint ea, quae suis temporibus praedixerunt futura, in Novo autem Testamento annunciantur completa. Quidam in specie accipiunt de adventu Messiae, ut sit sensus. Vaticinati fuêre Prophetae de his quae vobis in N. T. annunciata, i. e. ex Spiritus Sancti revelatione didicerunt, quod Christus, de quo vaticinati sunt, non ipsorum temporibus, sed in temporis plenitudine in N. T. sit venturus.Dan. 9. v. 24.cap. 12. v. 9. & 13.Hebr. 11. v. 13. Sed rectiùs generaliter accipitur de tota Evangelii doctrina, de Messiae persona, officio, beneficiis, regno, ac toto N. T. statu, ut sit sensus. Non sibimetipsis sed vobis ministrarunt Prophetae, praedicentes ea in N. Test. futura, quae in verbo Evangelii vobis nunciantur completa, ut scilicet ex comparatione eorum, quae à Prophetis praedicta, cum illis, quae in Evangelio vobis nunciantur completa, doctrinae Evangelicae immotam veritatem cognoscatis, & in fide confirmemini. Hoc ergo dicit Apostolus: Prophetae V. T. de quibus loquor, morte quidem abrepti sunt, quò minus Christi adventum, opus redemtionis per ipsum praestitum, ipsius passiones & glorias ac statum regni eius coram intuerentur, & ut loquitur Epistola ad Hebraeos cap. 11. v. 13.iuxta fidem defuncti sunt omnes isti, non acceptis promissionibus, sed â longè eas aspicientes & salutantes, interim tamen haudquaquam aegrè illud tulerunt, quia & hoc per Spiritum sanctum ipsis revelatum, quod non sibi ipsis, sed aliis post aliquot secula venturis ministrarent ea, quae nunc in V. Test. annunciantur, i. e. quod non suis, sed futuris demum temporibus vaticinia illa complementum sint sortitura, ac proinde non sibi, sed in aliorum usum literis ea consignare debeant. Exponit autem porrò Apostolus, per quos ea, quae â Prophetis praedicta, illis ad quos scribit in N. T. nunciata fuerint completa. Διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ὑμᾶς inquit, per eos qui Evangelium vobis praedicarunt, h. e. per sanctos Apostolos & eorum in Evangelii praedicatione συλλειτούργους. ἐν πνέυματι ἀγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπ᾽ οὐρανοῦ. Vulgata versio omissâ praepositione reddidit, Spiritu S. misso de coelo. Sed Graecus textus, qui solus est authenticus, haudquaquam otiosè eam habet adiectam. Evangelizarunt vobis Apostoli & annunciarunt ea impleta, quae in V. T. à Prophetis praedicta, non arbitrio humano, sed in Spiritu sancto, vel per Spiritum sanctum, ê coelo ipsis missum. Sensus est, quod Apostoli per Spiritum sanctum, die Pentecostes in specie linguarum ignearum super ipsos effusum, de mysteriis fidei perfectissimè instructi, eiusdem Spiritus sancti impulsu, virtute & efficacia Evangelium in toto orbe praedicare, & fidei Christianae mysteria explicare caeperint. Sic Act. 2. v. 14. post Spiritus S. effusionem Petrus Hierosolymis statim concionatur. Idem praestat Act. 3. v. 12. Sic Act. 4. v. 8. de Petro dicitur, quod repletus Spiritu sancto apologeticum sermonem ad Principes populi & Seniores Israël habuerit.v. 31.additur, & repleti sunt omnes Spiritu sancto, & loquebantur verbum Dei cum fiduciav. 33.& virtute magna reddebant Apostoli testimonium resurrectionis Christi. De Stephano dicitur cap. 6. v. 10non poterant resistere sapientiae & Spiritui, quo loquebatur. Tandem subiungit Apostolus εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι. Variè relativum ἃ à veteribus exponitur. 1. Gregorius homil. 8. in Ezech. de DEO absolutè interpretatur, quòd Angeli beatificâ eius visione delectentur. Angeli, inquit, vident Deum sine fastidio, & ideò dicuntur habere perpetuum desiderium videndi illum, quia videndo non fatigantur, lib. 18. moral. cap. 28. 2. Beda refert ad Christum ut hominem, cuius in v. 11. facta erat mentio, sensu eo, quòd in Christum ut hominem, praesertim iam glorificatum Angeli prospicere gaudeant, quippe in quo, & per quem omnia in coelo & terra sunt instaurata.Eph. 1. v. 10. 3. Idem Beda etiam applicat ad Spiritum sanctum, cuius in v. 11. & 12. praecedit mentio, ut sit sensus, quòd Angeli Spiritum sanctum unà cum Patre & Filio verum DEUM summa cum voluptate & desiderio nunquam finiendo intueantur. Glossa ordinaria itidem utramque expositionem coniungit, in quem sc. Christum vel Spiritum sanctum. Hae expositiones originem ducunt ex eo, quod quidam Codices Graeci & Latini legunt εἰς ὃν,in quem, sc. Christum vel Spiritum sanctum. Sed probatiores Codices Graeci & Latini legunt εἰς ἃ,in quae, quo modo etiam legit Ambrosius lib. 4. de Sacram. cap. 2. Isidorus lib. 1. Epist. 119. 4. Quidam ergò referunt ad Christi passiones & glorias inv. 11.quia Angelus in passione Christo adfuit ipsum confortansLuc. 22. v. 43.h. e. de passionis mysterio cum ipso colloquens, ac in resurrectionis Historia Angeli apparent in vestibus candidis Christo resuscitato congaudentesMatth. 28. v. 3.Marc. 16. v. 5.Luc. 24. v. 4.Sed & Christi athletae, per passiones ipsi configurati, spectaculum exhibent non solùm mundo & hominibus, sed etiam Angelis1. Cor. 4. v. 5. Sed quia τὰ παθήματα καὶ αἱδόξαι remotius distant, ideò. 5. Relativum ἃ simplicius refertur ad ea, quae à Prophetis in V. T. de Christo praedicta, & ab Apostolis in Evangelio nunciata, quorum in verbis proximè praecedentibus facta erat mentio, quo modo Irenaeus scriptor antiquissimus exponit lib. 4. cap. 77. videlicet de promissis Prophetarum, quae Christus adveniens implevit. Hanc expositionem confirmat etiam Apostoli scopus, versatur enim adhuc in commendanda & confirmanda Evangelicae doctrinae per Apostolos praedicatae maiestate, autoritate ac veritate, quam demonstrat non solùm ex beneficiis, quae per eam credentibus sunt partim collata, partim certò promissa; & ex Prophetarum vaticiniis, qui idem ante multa secula praedixerunt futurum, quod in Evangelio nunciatur completum, sed etiam ex ipsorummet Angelorum desiderio, qui mysteria salutis humanae à Prophetis praedicta, & ab Apostolis in Evangelio nunciata, summo studio penitiùs introspicere gestiunt. παρακύπτειν enim propriè usurpatur de iis, qui studio intuendi, ac penitiùs introspiciendi se inclinant, quique summo studio omnia explorant, ac diligenter fixis oculis intuentur. Luc. 24. v. 12.Ioh. 20. v. 5. & 11. usurpatur de Iohanne inclinato vel proclinato in obliquum capite transversim sepulchrum Christi introspiciente, ita enim extructa erant apud Iudaeos sepulchra, ut introspici non possent ab erecto, possent vero ab inclinato. Et quia hic modus aspectus eo fine adhibetur, ut accuratè res cognoscatur, ideò simpliciter pro accurata inspectione usurpatur. Iac. 1. v. 25. LXX. Cant. 2. v. 9. utuntur pro שגח, quod est intentè, & cum animi observatione prospicere. Item pro שקףex alto prospicereGen. 26. v. 8.1. Paral. 15. v. 29.Prov. 7. v. 6. Cum hac expositione, quâ per ea, quae Angeli desiderant penitiùs introspicere, intelliguntur praedicta à Prophetis in V. & nunciata ab Apostolis in N. T. minimè pugnat, quod quidam dicunt intelligi mysteria Evangelii, quidam mysteria fidei, quidam mysteria regni Christi, quidam mysteria salutis humanae, haec enim omnia continentur in numero eorum, quae à Prophetis praedicta, & ab Apostolis nunciata sunt completa, ad omnia ergò illa, cumprimis vero ad mysterium redemtionis per Christum praestitae, hoc Petrinum debet accommodari.

## 1:13
WHEREFORE GIRD UP THE LOINS OF YOUR MIND, BE SOBER, AND HOPE PERFECTLY FOR THE GRACE THAT IS BROUGHT UNTO YOU AT THE REVELATION OF JESUS CHRIST.

Thus far we have expounded the former ἐργασίας part of the Apostolic teaching in this Epistle, which was διδασκαλικὴ, there follows the latter, which is νουθετικὴ. For after the Apostle had proved, both by an enumeration of various spiritual benefits and by a demonstration of the most exact agreement with the Prophetic doctrine, that the doctrine concerning Christ preached by the Apostles was most true and most certain, by way of inference he deduces from it an exhortation that they should persevere constant in the profession of that doctrine, and adorn the same with holiness of life and morals. He requires, therefore, from those to whom he writes: 1. Constancy in faith. 2. Holy obedience toward GOD, or the innocence of life and morals. For it is not enough to embrace Christian doctrine by faith, but it is further required to remain constant in the profession of faith; nor is it enough to profess faith with words, but it is further required to demonstrate the same by the testimony of good works. Jas. 2. v. 18. The general and principal Proposition of this Apostolic exhortation is contained in vers. 13. which in the following verses he not only confirms with various arguments, but also divides into various species. The Apostle had said v. 10. that the Prophets had long ago prophesied concerning the grace to be offered to men through the preaching of the Gospel in the N. T., from which the Apostle deduces this exhortation, that the faithful of the N. T. ought to hope perfectly in that grace which is now brought to them. He had said vers. 3. & 4.that GOD according to His great mercy had regenerated them unto an incorruptible inheritance reserved in the heavens, now furthermore he instructs them for the journey, that they may strive in a straight course toward the proposed goal. Διὸ ἀναζωσά μενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ἡμῶν. Before όσφύας must be understood κατὰ. Girded as to the mind like the loins. These things are taken from the words of Christ Luke 12. v. 35.Let your loins be girded, and your lamps burningv. 36.And you yourselves like unto men that wait for Wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding, that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him immediately. In both places there is a metaphor taken from Oriental men, who used long and loose garments, and therefore, whether they were about to make a journey or to undertake some work, in order to be more ready for it, they were accustomed to gird their loins. A parallel passage is that of the Apostle Ephes. 6. v. 14. Stand therefore having girded your loins in truth. For just as in this place the Apostle requires of the faithful that, having girded the loins of their mind, they should hope perfectly for the grace of the Gospel, so Paul there in the same sense requires that they stand having girded their loins in the truth of the Gospel. Moreover, Peter clarifies the metaphor when he adds, having girded the loins τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, so that no one might suspect that the discourse is about the loins of the body. What is signified by this spiritual girding of the loins, the opinions of interpreters vary. Some think that chastity alone is prescribed here, but it is more correctly said that in general some restraint of passions and carnal desires is prescribed. For because a looser garment, not sufficiently tightened and applied, not only presents an impediment to the body in doing work and performing a journey, but is also accustomed to be an indication of a more dissolute mind, whence Macrobius in book 2 of the Saturnalia, chapter 3, records that Sulla, Pompey, and indeed Suetonius often warned the Optimates concerning Caesar, to beware of the ill-girded boy. For Caesar used a looser garment, which he did not apply sufficiently to his body, so that he would drag the hem: from which gesture Sulla thought he perceived not obscurely a certain softness and wickedness of morals: therefore the Apostle, ordering the loins of the mind to be girded, requires of the faithful that they restrain and restrict the mind from every depraved desire hindering the service of God. Such depraved desires, hindering the free and expeditious service of God, are various and diverse, not only carnal lust, but also vicious affections of the flesh, any inordinate love of earthly things, a preposterous fear of adversities, a perverse pursuit of honor and riches, and whatever can present a certain delay to a faithful person on the way of piety traveling to the heavenly fatherland. And because the strength of the body consists in the loins Iob. 40. v. 11. Psalm. 38. v. 8. whence the phrase, gird up your loins like a man Iob. 38. v. 3. cap. 40. v. 2. therefore by the girding of the loins this also can be understood, that believers, instructed by the strength of the Spirit against the depraved concupiscences of the flesh they ought to fight manfully, lest they retard themselves in the course of piety.

Νήφοντες. The Vulgate rendered it sober. Jerome, in his work against Vigilantius, rendered it vigilant, in which way the Syrian also translates it, [consult facsimile image] be awakened. But these expositions do not conflict in the least. For just as τὸ νήφειν is opposed not only to τῷ μεθύειν, which is to be drunk, but is also said of him who is vigilant, prudent, and circumspect, as is evident from that well-known saying of Epicharmus: νῆφε καὶ μέμνησε ἀπιστεῖν: so also among the Latins to be sober is used not only of the sobriety of the body, but also of the sobriety of the mind, namely, vigilance, prudence, and attention, and νήφειν is joined with γρηγορεῖν 1. Thessal. 5. v. 6. 1. Petr. 5. v. 8. Therefore, not only is the intemperance of food or drink, the nurse of lusts, and the immoderate use of delightful things prohibited, but the sobriety and vigilance of the mind are also required, and thus the metaphor previously proposed in the girding of the loins ἐξηγητικῶς is explained. For those who gird their loins are of a vigilant and present mind to undertake some work, Τελείως ἐλπίσατε ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὐμῖν χάριν. The Syrian interpreter joins the little word τελείως with the preceding verb νήφοντες be awakened perfectly, in which way Oecumenius also arranges it. But it is more correctly referred to the following verb ἐλπίσατε, so that the sense may be, perfectly hope in the grace. For χάριν the Syrian reads χαρὰν,, for he rendered it by [consult facsimile image] Because hope is not of a present, but of a future good, it therefore seemed inconvenient to the Syrian Interpreter that we are commanded to hope in the grace, therefore he rendered it, hope in the joy which will come to you in the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ. But in no Greek Codex is χαρὰν, read, nor do the Greek Interpreters mention this reading, and indeed the present φερομένην manifestly contradicts it. By χάριν some understand the gratuitous benefit of salvation, of which the Apostle had treated vers. 9. They therefore maintain that the present φερομένην is placed for the future, so that the sense may be, perfectly hope that heavenly happiness and glory will be given to you by GOD out of grace. But we are compelled by no necessity to change the present into the future. By grace the Apostle understands the grace obtained through Christ, and offered to men in the Gospel, conferred upon those believing through faith, whence he calls it φερομένην, which the Vulgate has not inconveniently rendered, which is offered to you, although in the Greek it is simple, which is brought to you. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian rendered it, in that grace which is to be brought to you. Erasmus more correctly in the present tense, in that grace which is brought to you. In this grace the Apostle commands those to whom he writes to hope perfectly, by which words he requires: 1. Firm confidence. To hope in the Scriptures is sometimes the same as to believe, and hope is used for confidence. 2. Sam. 22. v. 13.1. Paral. 10. v. 14.Iobi. 13. v. 13. etc. To hope therefore perfectly in grace, is to embrace with firm confidence the grace obtained for us through Christ, and to believe firmly that we have in Christ all things which are necessary for us to obtain salvation. 2. Faith ἀνυπόκριτον and sincere. For as it is said of hypocrites, that they serve God with a heart and a heart, and therefore not with a whole and perfect heart: so when the Apostle requires that believers should hope perfectly in the grace given to them, he then wishes all hypocrisy to be excluded, and requires that they hold a true and ἀνυπόκριτον confidence concerning the grace obtained for them through Christ, and that they undoubtedly expect it as revealed and brought from heaven in the word of the Gospel. 3. Perseverance in faith. For since only perseverance is crowned, therefore when the Apostle commands to hope perfectly in grace, he at the same time requires this, that keeping their mind from every depraved desire, they not only apprehend the grace brought to them through the preaching of the Gospel with perfect faith, but also retain it, nor suffer themselves to be moved from it by any threats of enemies or allurements of the flesh, as is said of the Christians in the Apostolic Church, they were persevering in the doctrine of the Apostles. There remains προσδιορισμὸς added, ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Some Latin codices read, in the revelation of Jesus Christ. But more approved and more numerous codices have, in the revelation, in which way it is also in the Greek and in the Syriac version, and in Jerome book 1 against Jovinian. Some understand by ἀποκάλυψιν of Christ that revelation which is to be in the day of the final judgment, when Christ coming visibly to judgment will be manifested to the whole world, who in this life was seen by few, in which sense the word ἀποκαλύψεως is used1. Cor. 1. v. 7.2. Thess. 1. v. 7.& in this very chapter v. 7. They join this προσδιορισμὸν with the more remote, namely with the verb ἐλπίσατε, so that the sense may be: In the grace to you through the preaching of the Gospel Hope perfectly and perseveringly for the grace offered unto the revelation of Jesus Christ, so that ἐν may be set for εἰς, until the day in which Christ shall reveal Himself from heaven in His final coming for judgment. According to this exposition, the Apostle would stir up the faithful to the perseverance of faith and hope, with the promise of glory proposed, of which they shall be participants with Christ at His coming for judgment. Col. 3. v. 4. When Christ shall appear, your life, then you also shall appear with Him in glory. It could also be said that the argument of the exhortation is taken from the revelation of all deeds that will follow on the day of judgment. 1. Cor. 3. v. 13. cap. 4. v. 5. Because on the day of judgment all things shall be manifested, therefore, having girded up the loins of your mind, restrain the depraved concupiscences of the flesh, lest they break forth into external acts and, being manifested to all on the day of judgment, affect you with shame. But it is more correctly said that by ἀποκάλυψιν is understood that manifestation of Christ which occurs in the word of the Gospel in this life, in which way the Blessed Luther also rendered it. In this meaning the word ἀποκαλύψεως is used Luke 2. v. 32. Rom. 16. v. 25. Eph. 1. v. 17. and especially Gal. 1. v. 12. and 16. although there an immediate mode of revelation is understood. According to this exposition, this προσδιορισμὸς is joined here with the immediately preceding word φερομένην, so that the sense may be: Hope perfectly in the grace offered to you in the revelation of Jesus Christ, i.e., in the Gospel, in which and through which Christ is revealed to you, which is what the translation of Erasmus also intends. While Christ is manifested to you. Thus, therefore, in these words is contained the first argument of the proposed exhortation, taken from the knowledge of the divine will, made manifest in Christ and through Christ.

Ἐναντισφάνεια. Hope perfectly in the grace which is offered to you. But Paul denies that he is perfect. Phil. 3. v. 12. And the very conscience of the pious convicts them that faith and hope in them is not perfect. Resp. The faith of the pious is perfect, both by reason of sincerity, because it is immune from the stain of hypocrisy, and by reason of desire and study, by which the pious tend toward perfection, and comparatively with respect to others, who have not yet made such great progress Eph. 4. 4. v. 13. Hebr. 5. v. 3. and by reason of perseverance, as it were perfecting the faith of the pious; but absolute perfection, both of knowledge and of obedience, is denied to them in this life 1. Cor. 13. v. 10.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Peter teaches that one must hope perfectly in the grace procured for us by Christ and offered in the Gospel. The Pope teaches that one must doubt concerning the grace of GOD.

2. Peter teaches that one must hope perfectly in that grace. The Pope teaches that one must hope and place confidence partly in the grace of GOD procured by the merit of Christ, partly in the merits of the saints, and partly in one's own merits. Bellarmine, book 5 on Justification, chapter 7: The Catholic Church teaches that while the chief hope and confidence must be placed in GOD, some may nevertheless also be placed in merits.

3. Peter teaches that whatever is offered to us in the Gospel is grace. The Pope teaches that our merits concur toward the participation of those benefits, if not by condignity, then by congruity.

Ἐκδίκησης. Salmeron on this passage comments thus: Some add 'perfectly' to the word 'hope,' because chastity and sobriety increase that hope and make it persevering. And thus, he says, 'hope perfectly,' against the vain hope of those who, loosening the reins for lust and concupiscence, dare to hope for eternal rewards, frequently having in their mouth that saying, that Christ bore all our crimes upon himself, and that by his stripes we have been saved. I respond: it is a calumny that we teach that eternal rewards are to be hoped for by those who loosen the reins for lust and concupiscence while having in their mouth that saying, that Christ bore all our crimes upon himself. Rather, we teach from the Apostle Gal. 5. v. 4. Those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh with its desires and concupiscences, and Rom. 8. v. 13. If you live according to the flesh, you will die: but if by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you will live. That chastity and sobriety are said to increase hope and make it persevering can be taken in a double sense, namely, either concerning the testimony of good works, which we can gather from chastity, sobriety, and other good works as fruits of faith, that our faith, by which we hope perfectly in grace, is true and living: or concerning the merit of good works, that we ought to place our faith and hope partly in the grace of God procured by the merit of Christ, and partly in our good works as merits of salvation. We accept the former sense; we repudiate the latter.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The bestowing of divine benefits is an obligation and invitation to the pursuit of piety. This is gathered from the illative particle Διὸ.

2. Truly faithful people do not loosen the reins for depraved concupiscences, but gird up the loins of their minds.

3. Τῆς εὐσεβείας γείτων ἡ σωφροσύνη. Truly the body of the pious is chaste, their diet sober, their prayer modest. Nilus in sentent. Exercise purity in the heart, chastity in the body, for both of these make you a temple of God. Tom. 1. Orthod. p. 173.

4. Those about to undertake a journey cast away impediments. But in the spiritual course of piety, the affections of the flesh, the desire for riches, worldly cares, drunkenness, and other things of this kind cast obstacles in the way. Therefore, those things must be cast away,

5. The revelation of Christ, i. e., the knowledge of the divine will made manifest to us in Christ and through Christ, is effective for rendering obedience to God ὁρμητήριον Eph. 5. v. 8.1. Thess. 5. v. 4. & 5.

Latin:

PROPTER QUOD SUCCINCTI LUMBOS MENTIS VESTRAE SOBRII, PERFECTE SPERANTES IN EAM, QUAE OFFERTUR VOBIS, GRATIAM IN REVELATIONE IESU CHRISTI.

Hactenus exposuimus priorem ἐργασίας Apostolicae in hac Epistola partem, quae fuit διδασκαλικὴ, sequitur posterior, quae est νουθετικὴ. Postquam enim Apostolus tùm enumeratione variorum beneficiorum spiritualium, tùm demonstratione exactissimi consensus cum doctrina Prophetica probaverat, doctrinam de Christo ab Apostolis praedicatam esse verissimam & certissimam, per modum illationis ex eo deducit exhortationem, ut in professione illius doctrinae constantes perseverent, eandemque vitae & morum sanctitate ornent. Requirit igitur ab illis, ad quos scribit. 1. In fide constantiam. 2. Sanctam erga DEUM obedientiam, sive vitae ac morum innocentiam. Neque enim sufficit, doctrinam Christianam fide amplecti, sed insuper requiritur, in fidei professione constantem permanere; neque sufficit verbis fidem profiteri, sed insuper requiritur, bonorum operum testimonio eandem demonstrare. Iac. 2. v. 18. Exhortationis huius Apostolicae Propositio generalis ac principalis continetur in vers. 13. quam in sequentibus non solùm variis argumentis confirmat, sed etiam in varias species diducit. Dixerat Apostolus v. 10. Prophetas de gratia per praedicationem Evangelii in N. T. hominibus offerenda, iam olim esse vaticinatos, ex eo Apostolus deducit hanc exhortationem, quòd fideles N. T. perfectè sperare debeant in eam, quae ipsis iam affertur, gratiam. Dixerat vers. 3. & 4.DEUM secundùm magnam suam misericordiam ipsos regeneràsse in haereditatem incorruptibilem reservatam in coelis, iam porrò ad iter eos instruit, ut ad propositam metam recto cursu contendant. Διὸ ἀναζωσά μενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ἡμῶν. Ante όσφύας subaudiendum κατὰ.Mente velut lumbis succincti. Desumta haec sunt ex verbis Christi Luc. 12. v. 35.Sint lumbi vestri succincti, & lucernae ardentesv. 36.Et vos similes hominibus expectantibus Dominum suum, quando revertatur à nuptiis, ut cum venerit, & pulsaverit, confestim aperiant ei. Utrobique est metaphora ab Orientalibus hominibus petita, qui longis & laxis utebantur vestibus, proinde vel iter facturi vel operis aliquid aggressuri, ut ad illud expeditiores essent, lumbos praecingere solebant. Parallelus est locus Apostoli Ephes. 6. v. 14.State ergò succincti lumbos vestros in veritate. Ut enim hoc loco Apostolus requirit à fidelibus, ut succincti lumbos mentis perfectè sperent in gratiam Evangelii, ita Paulus ibi eodem sensu requirit, ut stent succincti lumbos in veritate Evangelica. Declarat autem Petrus metaphoram, quando addit, succincti lumbosτῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, ne de corporis lumbis sermonem esse quis suspicetur. Quid per spiritualem hanc lumborum praecincturam significetur, variant Interpretum sententiae. Quidam putant, solam castitatem hîc praescribi, sed rectiùs dicitur, in genere quamvis passionum & cupiditatum carnalium refrenationem praescribi. Quia enim vestis laxior non satis astricta & applicata, corpori non solùm in opere faciendo, & itinere peragendo impedimentum obiicit, sed etiam animi dissolutioris solet esse indicium, unde Macrobius lib. 2. Saturnalium cap. 3. memorat, Syllam Pompeium, Suetonium vero Optimates saepiùs admonuisse de Caesare, ut malè praecinctum puerum caverent. Utebatur enim Caesar laxiore vestitu, quem corpori non applicabat satis, sic ut laciniam traheret: ex quo gestu mollitiem & improbitatem quandam morum non obscurè sibi videbatur Sylla animadvertere: ideò Apostolus lumbos mentis succingi iubens à fidelibus requirit, ut mentem ab omni prava cupiditate, servitium Dei impediente, refrenent ac restringant. eiusmodi pravae cupiditates, servitium Dei liberum & expeditum impedientes, sunt variae ac diversae, non solùm libido carnalis, sed etiam vitiosi carnis affectus, quicunque inordinatus terrenorum amor, praeposterus adversitatum timor, honoris ac divitiarum studium perversum, & quaecunque fideli in via pietatis ad coelestem patriam peregrinanti remoram quandam obiicere possunt. Ac quia in lumbis consistit corporis robur Iob. 40. v. 11.Psalm. 38. v. 8. unde phrasis, accinge sicut vir lumbos tuosIob. 38. v. 3.cap. 40. v. 2. ideò per cincturam lumborum etiam hoc intelligi potest, quòd credentes Spiritus robore instructi contra pravas carnis concupiscentias viriliter pugnare debeant, ne in pietatis cursu ipsos retardent.

Νήφοντες. Vulgata reddidit sobrii. Hieronymus advers. Vigilant. reddidit, vigilantes, quo modo etiam Syrus vertit, [consult facsimile image]excitamini. Sed hae expositiones minimè pugnant. Ut enim τὸ νήφειν opponitur non solùm τῷ μεθύειν, quod est inebriari, sed etiam dicitur de eo, qui est vigilans, prudens & circumspectus, ut constat ex noto illo Epicharmi dicterio: νῆφε καὶ μέμνησε ἀπιστεῖν: ita quoque apud Latinos sobrium esse, non solùm de sobrietate corporis, sed etiam de sobrietate mentis, vigilantiâ scilicet, prudentiâ & attentione usurpatur, ac νήφειν coniungitur cum γρηγορεῖν1. Thessal. 5. v. 6.1. Petr. 5. v. 8. Non solùm ergò cibi potusve intemperantia, libidinum nutrix, & immoderatus rerum delectabilium usus prohibetur, sed etiam mentis sobrietas ac vigilantia requiritur, sicque metaphora in lumborum cinctura priùs proposita ἐξηγητικῶς explicatur. Qui enim lumbos praecingunt, vigilante & praesente sunt animo ad opus aliquod aggrediendum, Τελείως ἐλπίσατε ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὐμῖν χάριν. Voculam τελείως Syrus interpres coniungit cum praecedente verbo νήφοντεςexcitamini perfectè, quo modo etiam Oecumenius ordinat. Sed rectiùs ad sequens verbum ἐλπίσατε refertur, ut sit sensus, perfectè sperate in gratiam. Pro χάριν Syrus legit χαρὰν, reddidit enim per [consult facsimile image] Quia enim spes non est praesentis, sed futuri boni, ideò inconveniens visum Syro Interpreti, quod sperare iubemur in gratiam, ideò reddidit, sperate in gaudium, quod vobis eveniet in revelatione Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Sed in nullo Codice Graeco legitur χαρὰν, nec meminerunt huius lectionis Graeci Interpretes, quin & praesens φερομένην eidem manifestè repugnat. Per χάριν quidam intelligunt gratuitum beneficium salutis, de quo Apostolus egeratvers. 9. Statuunt igitur, praesens φερομένηνpositum esse pro futuro, ut sit sensus, perfectè sperate, coelestem felicitatem & gloriam ex gratia vobis à DEO datum iri. Sed nullâ cogimur necessitate, ut praesens in futurum commutemus. Per gratiam intelligit Apostolus gratiam per Christum partam, & in Evangelio hominibus oblatam, per fidem credentibus collatam, unde eam appellat φερομένην, quod Vulg. non incommodè reddidit, quae vobis offertur, quamvis in Graeco simplex, quae vobis fertur. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovin. reddidit, in eam, quae deferenda est vobis, gratiam. Erasmus rectiùs in praesenti, in eam, quae ad vos defertur, gratiam. In hanc gratiam perfectè eos, ad quos scribit, Apostolus sperare iubet, quibus verbis requirit. 1. Firmam fiduciam. Sperare in Scripturis quandoque idem est quod credere, ac spes pro fiducia usurpatur. 2. Sam. 22. v. 13.1. Paral. 10. v. 14.Iobi. 13. v. 13. &c. Sperare ergo perfectè in gratiam, est firmâ fiducia amplecti gratiam per Christum nobis partam, ac firmiter credere, nos omnia in Christo habere, quae ad salutem consequendam nobis sunt necessaria. 2. Fidem ἀνυπόκριτον ac sinceram. Ut enim de hypocritis dicitur, quod corde & corde, adeoque non toto & perfecto corde DEO serviant: ita quando Apostolus requirit, ut credentes perfectè sperent in gratiam ipsis datam, tùm omnem hypocrisin vult exclusam, ac requirit, ut veram & ἀνυπόκριτον de parta sibi per Christum gratia fiduciam teneant, eamque in verbo Evangelii caelitus patefactam & delatam indubitatè expectent. 3. In fide perseverantiam. Cum enim sola perseverantia coronetur, ideò quando Apostolus perfectè sperare iubet in gratiam, simul & hoc requirit, ut mentem ab omni prava cupiditate continentes, gratiam per Evangelii praedicationem ipsis delatam, fide perfecta non solum apprehendant, sed etiam retineant, nec ullis vel minis hostium vel blanditiis carnis ab ea sese dimoveri patiantur, sicut de Christianis in Ecclesia Apostolica dicitur, erunt perseverantes in doctrina Apostolorum. Restat προσδιορισμὸς additus, ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Quidam Codd. Latini legunt, in revelationem Iesu Christi. Sed probatiores ac plures Codices habent, in revelatione, quo modo etiam est in Graeco & in versione Syriaca, & apud Hieronymum lib. 1. contra Iovian. Quidam per ἀποκάλυψιν Christi intelligunt illam revelationem, quae in die extremi iudicii futura, quando Christus visibiliter ad iudicium veniens toti mundo manifestabitur, qui in hac vita à paucis visus, quo sensu voxἀποκαλύψεωςusurpatur1. Cor. 1. v. 7.2. Thess. 1. v. 7.& in hoc ipso cap. v. 7. Illi huncπροσδιορισμὸνconiungunt cum remotiori, videlicet cum verboἐλπίσατε,ut sit sensus: In gratiam vobis per praedicationem Evangelii oblatam perfectè & perseveranter sperate usque in revelationem Iesu Christi, ut sicἐνponatur proεἰς,usque in diem, quo Christus ê coelo sese revelabit in novissimo suo adiudicium adventu. Iuxta hanc expositionem Apostolus excitaret fideles ad perseverantiam fidei & spei, proposita promissione gloriae, cuius cum Christo in ipsius ad iudicium adventu futuri sint participes. Col. 3. v. 4.Cum Christus apparuerit vita vestra, tunc & vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria. Posset etiam dici, argumentum exhortationis petitum esse à revelatione omnium factorum in die iudicii secutura. 1. Cor. 3. v. 13.cap. 4. v. 5. Quia in die iudicii omnia manifestabuntur, ideò succincti lumbos mentis pravas carnis concupiscentias refrenate, ne in actus externos prorumpant & in die iudicii omnibus manifestati pudore vos afficiant. Sed rectiùs dicitur, per ἀποκάλυψιν intelligi eam Christi manifestationem, quae fit in verbo Evangelii in hac vita, quo modo etiam B. Lutherus reddidit. In hac significatione usurpatur vox ἀποκαλύψεωςLuc. 2. v. 32.Rom. 16. v. 25.Eph. 1. v. 17. cumprimis vero Gal. 1. v. 12. & 16. quamvis ibi modus revelationis immediatus intelligatur. Iuxta hanc expositionem coniungitur hic προσδιορισμὸς cum proximè praecedente verbo φερομένην, ut sit sensus. Perfectè sperate in gratiam vobis oblatam in revelatione Iesu Christi i. e. in Evangelio, in quo & per quod Christus vobis revelatur, quod ipsum etiam vult Erasmi translatio. Dum vobis manifestatur Christus. Sic ergo in his verbis continetur primum exhortationis propositae argumentum, petitum à, cognitione divinae voluntatis, in Christo & per Christum patefactae.

Ἐναντισφάνεια.Perfectè sperate in gratiam, quae vobis offertur. At Paulus negat, se esse perfectum.Phil. 3. v. 12.ac ipsa piorum conscientia ipsos convincit, quod fides & spes in ipsis non sit perfecta. Resp. fides piorum perfecta tum ratione sincertatis, quia ab hypocriseos labe immunis, tum ratione desiderii & studii, quo pii ad perfectionem tendunt, tum comparatè respectu aliorum, qui nondum tantos fecere progressus Eph. 4.4. v. 13.Hebr. 5. v. 3. tum ratione perseverantiae, fidem piorum quasi perficientis; absoluta autem tum cognitionis, tum obedientiae perfectio ipsis in hac vita denegatur 1. Cor. 13. v. 10.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Petrus docet, perfectè sperandum esse in gratiam à Christo nobis partam & in Evangelio oblatam. Papa docet, dubitandum esse de DEI gratia.

2. Petrus docet, perfectè in illam gratiam esse sperandum. Papa docet, partim in gratiam DEI Christi merito partam, partim in merita sanctorum, partim in merita propria sperandum & fiduciam collocandam esse. Bellarm. lib. 5. de Iustif. cap. 7. Catholica Ecclesia praecipuam quidem spem & fiduciam in DEO ponendam esse, aliquam tamen etiam in meritis poni posse, docet.

3. Petrus docet, quicquid in Evangelio nobis offertur, esse gratiam. Papa docet, ad eorum beneficiorum participationem concurrere merita nostra, si non ex condigno, tamen ex congruo.

Ἐκδίκησης. Salmeron in h. l. sic commentatur. Quidam cum verbo sperate adiungunt perfectè, eò quod castitas & sobrietas auget spem illamque perseverantem efficit. Et sic perfectè sperate, ait, contra vanam eorum spem, qui libidini & concupiscentiae frena laxantes, audent praemia sperare aeterna, in ore frequenter habentes illud, Christum omnia crimina nostra super se portasse, & livore eius nos servatos fuisse. Resp. calumnia est, quod doceamus, praemia aeterna speranda esse illis, qui libidini & concupiscentiae frena laxant in ore habentes illud, Christum omnia crimina nostra super se portasse. Quin potius docemus ex Apostolo Gal. 5. v. 4.Qui Christi sunt, crucifixerunt carnem cum desideriis & concupiscentiis, & Rom. 8. v. 13.Si secundùm carnem vixeritis, moriemini: si autem Spiritu actiones carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis. Quod castitas & sobrietas spem augere dicuntur, illamque perseverantem efficere, duplici sensu accipi potest, videlicet vel de bonorum operum testimonio, quod ex castiate, sobrietate & aliis bonis operibus tanquam fidei fructibus colligere possimus, fidem nostram, quâ perfectè in gratiam speramus, esse veram & vivam: vel de bonorum operum merito, quod fidem & spem nostram partim in gratiam Dei merito Christi partam, partim in nostra bona opera tanquamsalutis merita collocare debeamus. Priorem sensum acceptamus, posteriorem repudiamus.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Beneficiorum divinorum collatio est ad studium pietatis obligatio & invitatio. Colligitur hoc ex particula illativa Διὸ.

2. Verè fideles non laxant frena concupiscentiis pravis, sed fuccingunt lumbos mentium suarum.

3. Τῆς εὐσεβείας γείτων ἡ σωφροσύνη. Verè pii corpus est castum, victus sobrius, oratio pudica. Nilus in sentent. Exerce puritatem in corde, castitatem in corpore, ea enim utraque templum Dei te efficiunt. Tom. 1. Orthod. p. 173.
