4. Iter aggressuri impedimenta abiiciunt. At in spirituali pictatis curriculo remoras obiiciunt affectus carnis, cupiditas divitiarum, curae mundanae, ebrietas & huius generis alia. Ea igitur abiicienda,

5. Revelatio Christi, i. e. cognitio divinae voluntatis in Christo & per Christum nobis patefactae ad obedientiam Deo praestandam est efficax ὁρμητήριονEph. 5. v. 8.1. Thess. 5. v. 4. & 5.

## 1:13-17 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place, 1. whether the Apostle speaks only of the lusts of carnal sins in v. 14. So some wish, moved by the argument that holiness is opposed to those lusts in v. 15. Now indeed holiness is properly and directly opposed to the desires of carnal sins. 1. Thessal. 4. v. 3. & 4. But not only are the defilements of the flesh given, but also those of the Spirit, 2. Cor. 7. v. 1. and any sins committed against conscience defile a man before GOD and render him unclean Matth. 15. v. 19. & 20. whence the Apostle requires holiness of body and Spirit from the faithful. 1. Cor. 7. v. 34.

2. In what sense is God ὰπροσωπολήπτως said to judge? I answer: he is said to accept the face of someone by a Hebrew phrase who does something for the favor of another Gen. 19. v. 21. 1. Sam. 25. v. 35. in judgment he is said to accept the face or person who does not regard the merits of the case, but judges out of favor for the person, having considered his external adjuncts which strike the eyes and render him commendable, but which pertain not at all to the case itself, such as are riches, honor, family, dignity, power, kinship, etc. Lev. 19. v. 15. Deut. 1. v. 17. cap. 16. v. 19. Prov. 18. v. 5. etc. thence August. lib. 2. contra duas Epist. Pelag. c. 7. προσωποληψίαν defines, when not the merits of the cause, but the dignity of the person is attended to. Because therefore such a preposterous affection does not fall upon God at all, thence he is said to judge ἀπροσωπολήπτως. Peter himself explains clearly enough why GOD is said to judge ἀπροσωπολήπτως, namely because he judges according to the work of each one, and not, with the cause about which one ought properly to judge being set aside, does he look only at persons and their external accidents, which pertain not at all to the cause.

ἘναντιοΦανείαι. 1. Not fashioning yourselves according to the former desires in your ignorance. But Peter writes to those converted from the Jews, who before their conversion to Christ had knowledge of the true GOD, whereas ignorance is properly attributed to the Gentiles. Acts 17. v. 30. Gal. 4. v. 8. Resp. 1. We showed above that this Epistle was also written secondarily and less principally to those converted from the Gentiles. 2. Concerning the Jews not yet converted to Christ, the Apostle says 2. Cor. 3. v. 15. that a veil is placed upon their heart. Outside of Christ, true and saving knowledge of GOD has no place, but all things are mere darkness.

2. As he who called you is holy, so be you also holy in all your conversation. But GOD is essentially, most perfectly, and in the highest degree holy, such holiness as does not fall to man. Resp. That comparison is not ὶσότητος, but ὁμοιότητος;, not of equality, but of likeness. Matt. 5. v. 48. Luke 6. v. 36. Caesarius, brother of Gregory Nazianzen, Dial. 3, on the words, Be perfect, etc., he does not command us to extend ourselves to the divine Nature, which is altogether incomparable and surpasses reason and intellect: for that cannot be done, but that we should imitate his kindness and gentleness, etc.

3. It is written: Be holy, for I am holy. But in the Mosaic sayings, it is a matter of ceremonial holiness. Resp. 1. Not of ceremonial holiness alone, but also of moral holiness, which consists in cleanliness from sins committed against the moral law, as the context shows. 2. Ceremonial and external holiness was a type of spiritual and interior holiness, since by it the Israelites were admonished concerning this.

4. If you call upon him as Father, who judges without respect of persons. But John 5. v. 22. The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son. Resp. 1. The Father judges no one, to wit, alone without the Son, but he judges all through the Son. For if both are to be honored, the Father and the Son, and indeed with the same worship of honor, it follows that both judge. Didymus in c. 5. John: The Father, while the Son judges, himself also judges, because the essence and power of the Father and the Son is the same. 2. Hilary, Chrysostom, and Theophylact teach that the Father gave all judgment to the Son by begetting him equal to himself and by giving him from eternity the divine Nature, whose proper attribute it is to judge all things. 3. By judgment in this place is properly understood the government of the whole universe, especially indeed the gathering of the Church and its defense from enemies. John 3. v. 35.chap. 17. v. 2. That judgment the Father gave to the Son, not by emptying Himself of the power of judgment, but by committing its administration ὀικονομικῶς to the Son,

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Men before conversion to Christ are occupied ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ. It is therefore false, the dogma of certain Papists and Calvinists, that the Gentiles could have drawn a salvific knowledge of GOD from the light of Nature.

2. The saints before GOD are not those who have been canonized by the Pope and related into the number of the saints, but those who by a holy calling have been called into the fellowship of the holy Church 1. Cor. 1. v. 2.2. Tim 1. v. 9. and by true faith in Christ apply to themselves holiness and righteousness, and are regenerated, renewed, illuminated, and sanctified through the Holy Spirit, 1. Cor. 6. v. 11.Eph. 4. v. 24.Tit. 3. v. 5. so that they may strive for holiness and, cleansing themselves from every defilement of flesh and Spirit, may perfect sanctification, 2. Cor. 7. v. 1.

3. True holiness does not consist in a peculiar habit, in elective forms of worship, in Monastic profession, etc., as the Pope teaches, but in true faith, exercising itself through the pursuit of good works done according to the norm of the word.

Ἔκδίκησις 1. Pope Innocent, from the words, be holy, for I am holy, wished to prove that Priests ought to be celibate. For thus he writes in Epist. 2. chap. 9. and it is held in c. Tenere dist. 31. The Church ought to hold that in every way Priests and Levites should not mingle with their wives, because they are occupied with the daily necessities of divine ministry. For it is written: Be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy. Epist. 3. chap. 1. and it is held in c. Proposuisti dist. 82. There is a very old authority of the sacred law, guarded from the beginning, that Priests were commanded to dwell in the temple during the year of their service, so that those serving the sacred offerings might claim for themselves divine ministries pure and purged from every stain, nor is it right that those be admitted to sacred offices who also practice carnal intercourse with a wife, because it is written: Be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy. And before Innocent, Siricius in Epist. 1. chap. 7. and it is held in c. Plurimos of the same dist. We have learned that very many Priests of Christ and Levites, after long times of their consecration, have produced offspring both from their own marriages and also from shameful intercourse to have procreated and to defend their crime with this prescription, because in the O. T. the faculty of procreating is read to have been attributed to Priests and Ministers. Let whoever that follower of lusts, that teacher of vices, tell me now, if he thinks that in the law of Moses the reins of luxury were relaxed everywhere for sacred orders by our GOD, why does He warn those to whom the holy of holies was entrusted, saying be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God? But both Pontiffs err gravely in this part. For if those to whom it was said, be holy, ought to abstain from marriage, it would follow that 1. Holiness cannot have a place in marriage. 2. All who are truly pious ought to abstain from marriage, since it was said to all, be holy, as appears from Leviticus and from this Petrine passage. 3. That marriage was forbidden even to Priests in the O. T., all of which are false and absurd. Bellarm. book on matrimony, chap. 5, defends Siricius and Innocent in this way, that they are not speaking of marriage in general, but of the marriage of Priests in particular. But it is manifest that they prove that marriage was forbidden to Priests by this argument, because Priests ought to be holy, whence Vasquez tract. on Matrim. Disp. 2. chap. 8. refutes this subterfuge of Bellarmine.

2. From the fact that Peter commands, that we be holy in all conversation, Estius gathers in his comm. on this place that our holiness and justice does not consist in the mere remission of sins, but also and chiefly in the adornment and operation of virtues. Resp. Our holiness and justice is either imputed or inherent. Imputed holiness and justice consists in the mere remission of sins Rom. 4. v. 6. but inherent holiness and justice consists in the adornment and operation of virtues, which, since it is not yet perfect in this life, therefore we can in no way rely upon it before the judgment of GOD, nor seek the foundation of our justification in it.

3. From the fact that GOD is said to judge without respect of persons according to the work of each, the Pontificians gather the merits of good works. Bellarm. book 5. on Justif. chap. 2. Estius on this place. Resp. 1. From Gregory in Psal. 7. pen. It is one thing to render according to works, another to render according to the merits of works or because of works. For in that which is said according to works, the quality of the works themselves is understood, so that whose works shall have appeared good, his also shall be the glorious retribution. For to that blessed life, in which one lives with God and from God, no labor can be equaled, no works compared, especially since the Apostle says:

They are not worthy &c. 2. This exposition agrees with the sayings of Scripture, in which κατὰ signifies not the cause, but the quality. Matth. 23. v. 3. According to their works do not, i. e. do not do such works as they themselves do. 3. And lest anyone doubt that an explanation of this kind is also proper to this passage, the passage Apoc. 22. v. 12. must be exactly noted, where that κατὰ is explained thus, ὡς τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ ἔσται. Namely, as a tree is judged good or bad by its fruits: so a believer or an unbeliever is judged by GOD from his works. 4. The Apostolic scope also proves this exposition. For Peter wishes this, that at the tribunal of GOD there is no place for respect of persons, but the sincerity of the heart is esteemed, and works are judged by Him not from the external appearance, but from the good or bad quality of the heart.

4. From the fact that Peter commands that the pious should conduct themselves with fear during the time of their sojourn, the Papists gather that one must doubt concerning divine grace. Bellarm. lib. 3. de iustif. cap. 6. I answer: filial fear is one thing, doubt is another. Filial fear is not opposed to confidence, to which doubt is opposed, but it is opposed to carnal security. For that filial fear embraces both a serious humiliation before the judgment of GOD, which arises from the acknowledgment of sins and one's own infirmity, and a filial confidence in the mercy of GOD, without which this fear would not be, nor could it be called filial. Therefore, when the truly pious are commanded to conduct themselves in fear, doubt is not commended to them, but pious solicitude in avoiding falls against conscience, and the flight of security and confidence in one's own powers. For Peter immediately adds v. 18. Knowing that you were redeemed not with corruptible gold and silver, but with the precious blood of Christ &c.

Διδαοκαλίαι. 1. Where υἱοθσσία has a place through faith, there εὐπεισθεία. exerts itself outwardly.

2. Because the pious in their conversion to Christ renounced their former manner of life and its concupiscences, therefore they ought not to configure themselves to them again after their conversion to Christ; because they have put off the old man, therefore they ought not to put him on again, but rather let them say with the bride Cant. 5. v. 3. I have put off my tunic, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them?

3. Ignorance, opposed to the salutary and saving knowledge of GOD, is innate to all men after the fall.

4. Ignorance of Christ is the cause of all impurity and impiety Eph. 4. v. 18.

5. The example of holiness proposed in GOD ought to be both the rule and the impulsive cause of holiness in us.

6. Sin is a defilement of the soul. But by faith the heart is purified Act. 15. v. 9.

7. That is holy which is purged and separated from the filth of the world, whence they judge ἅγιος to be said as if without earth.

8. On those words, You shall be holy, for I am holy, Leo in sermon 8 on the fast of the seventh month notes thus. He commands holiness, and the manner of acquiring it. This is, he says, love me, and abstain from those things which displease me. Do what I love, love what I do. And when that which I command seems to be difficult, have recourse to the one commanding, so that from where the precept is given, help may be provided; I will not deny aid, I who have granted the will.

9. GOD is both father and judge; let the former kindle confidence in us, but the latter fear.

10. An earthly father treats children more indulgently than servants: but the heavenly father receives servants into the status of sons, and excludes disobedient sons from the inheritance.

11. In the Scriptures this title is most often attributed to GOD, that he is ἀπροσωπολήπτης Deut. 10. v. 17.2. Paral. 19. v. 7.Iob. 34. v. 19.Act. 10. v. 34Rom. 2. v. 11.Gal. 2. v. 6.Eph. 6. v. 9.Col. 3. v. 11. and 25. It is to be noted, however, that this ἀπροσωποληψίαν is attributed to GOD on account of justice. Therefore, just as his mercy does not fight with the justice of GOD, so it is not to be deemed προσωποληψία that GOD, on account of a person reconciled to himself by faith in Christ, also holds his works pleasing, or that he distributes his gifts according to his own will.

12. We are pilgrims and strangers in this world. Therefore let us live in the fear of GOD, lest by securely indulging the concupiscences of our flesh, we ourselves also perish with the world that is quickly perishing, but aspiring to our heavenly fatherland, let us be carried there with the whole desire of our heart and zeal for piety.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco, 1. an Apostolus de cupiditatibus peccatorum carnalium tantum loquatur in v. 14. Ita quidam volunt, argumento permoti eo, quòd cupiditatibus illis in v. 15. opponatur sanctitas. Iam verò carnaelium peccatorum desideriis sanctitas propriè & directè opponitur.1. Thessal. 4. v. 3. & 4. Atqui non solùm inquinamenta carnis, sed etiam Spiritûs dantur, 2. Cor. 7. v. 1. ac quaevis peccata contra conscientiam admissa, hominem coram DEO coinquinant & immundum reddunt Matth. 15. v. 19. & 20. unde sanctitatem corporis & Spiritus Apostolus à fidelibus requirit. 1. Cor. 7. v. 34.

2. Quo sensu Deusὰπροσωπολήπτωςdicatur iudicare? Resp. dicitur alicuius faciem accipere phrasi Hebraicâ qui facit aliquid in gratiam alterius Gen. 19. v. 21.1. Sam. 25. v. 35. in iudicio faciem sive personam accipere dicitur, qui non respicit merita causae, sed ex favore iudicat pro persona consideratis externis eius adiunctis, quae in oculos incurrunt & eam commendabilem reddunt, adipsam verò causam minimè pertinent, qualia sunt, divitiae, honor, familia, dignitas, potentia, cognatio &c. Lev. 19. v. 15.Deut. 1. v. 17.cap. 16. v. 19.Prov. 18. v. 5. &c. inde August. lib. 2. contra duas Epist. Pelag. c. 7. προσωποληψίαν definit, quando non causae merita, sed personae dignitas attenditur. Quia ergo eiusmodi praeposterus in Deum affectus minimè cadit, inde ἀπροσωπολήπτως iudicare dicitur. Petrus ipse satis perspicuè exponit, quare DEUS ἀπροσωπολήπτως dicatur iudicare, nimirum quia iudicat secundùm cuiusque opus, non autem postpositâ causâ, de quâ propriè iudicandum, tantùm personas & externa earum accidentia, ad causam minimè pertinentia, respicit.

ἘναντιοΦανείαι. 1. Non configurantes vos prioribus in ignorantia vestra desideriis. Atqui Petrus scribit ad conversos ex Iudaeis, qui ante suam ad Christum conversionem notitiam veri DEI habuerunt, gentilibus autem propriè tribuitur ignorantia.Actor. 17. v. 30.Gal. 4. v. 8. Resp. 1. ostendimus superiùs, hanc Epistolam etiam ad conversos ex gentilibus secundariò & minùs principaliter scriptam fuisse. 2. De Iudaeis nondum ad Christum conversis dicit Aposto lus 2. Cor. 3. v. 15. quod velamen positum sit super cor eorum. Extra Christum non habet locum vera & salutaris DEI cognitio, sed omnia sunt merae tenebrae.

2. Quemadmodum is, qui vocavit vos, sanctus est, ita ipsi quoque in omni conversatione vestra sitis sancti. Atqui DEUS est essentialiter, perfectissimè & in summo gradu sanctus, qualis sanctitas in hominem non cadit. Resp. comparatio illa non est ὶσότητος, sed ὁμοιότητος; non aequalitatis, sed similitudinis. Matth. 5. v. 48.Luc. 6. v. 36. Caesarius Gregor. Nazianz. frater Dial. 3. super verba, Estote perfecti &c. non cum omnino incomparabili & rationem intellectumque superante divina Natura nosmet ut extendamus, iubet: id enim fieri nequit, sed ut illius imitemur benignitatem & facilitatem &c.

3. Scriptum est. Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Atqui in dictis Mosaicis agitur de sanctitate Ceremoniali. Resp. 1. non de sola Ceremoniali, sed etiam morali sanctitate, quae in munditie à peccatis contra legem moralem commissis consistit, ut ostendit contextus. 2. Sanctitas Ceremonialis & externa fuit typus spiritualis & interioris sanctitatis, cum per eam de hac Israelitae admoniti fuerint.

4. Si Patrem invocatis eum, qui sine acceptione personarum iudicat. AtquiIoh. 5. v. 22.Pater non iudicat quenquam, sed omne iudicium Filio dedit. Resp. 1. Pater non iudicat quenquam, scil. solus absque Filio, sed omnes iudicat per Filium. Si enim uterque honorandus est, Pater & Filius, & quidem eodem honoris cultu, consequens est, utrumque iudicare. Didymus in c. 5. Ioh. Pater, iudicante Filio, ipse quoque iudicat, quia eadem est Patris & Filii essentia ac potestas. 2. Hilarius, Chrysostomus & Theophylactus docent, Patrem dedisse Filio omne iudicium, gignendo eum sibi aequalem & dando ei ab aeterno Naturam divinam, cuius attributum proprium est, iudicare omnia. 3. Per Iudicium h. l. propriè intelligitur gubernatio totius universi, praecipuè vero Ecclesiae collectio & ab hostibus defensio. Ioh. 3. v. 35.cap. 17. v. 2. Illud iudicium Pater dedit Filio, non potestate iudicii sese evacuando, sed eius administrationem ὀικονομικῶς Filio committendo,

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Homines ante conversionem ad Christum versantur ἐν ἀγνοίᾳ. Falsum est ergo, quorundam Pontificiorum & Calvinianorum dogma, quod gentiles ex luce Naturae salvificam DEI cognitionem haurire potuerint.

2. Sancti coram DEO sunt, non qui à Papa canonizati, & in numerum sanctorum relati, sed qui vocatione sancta ad Ecclesiae sanctae consortium vocati 1. Cor. 1. v. 2.2. Tim 1. v. 9. verâ fide Christi sanctitatem & iustitiam sibi applicant, ac per Spiritum sanctum regenerantur, renovantur, illuminantur, sanctificantur, 1. Cor. 6. v. 11.Eph. 4. v. 24.Tit. 3. v. 5. ut sanctitati studeant & ab omni inquinamento carnis & Spiritus sese mundantes sanctificationem perficiant, 2. Cor. 7. v. 1.

3. Vera sanctitas non consistit in peculiari habitu, in cultibus electitiis, in professione Monastica &c. ut Papa docet, sed in vera fide, per studium bonorum operum iuxta normam verbi factorum sese exerente.

Ἔκδίκησις 1. Papa Innocentius ex verbis, sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum, probare voluit, Sacerdotes oportere esse coelibes. Sic enim scribit Epist. 2. cap. 9. & habetur c. Tenere dist. 31. Tenere debet Ecclesia, ut omni modo Sacerdotes & Levitae cum uxoribus suis non misceantur, quia ministerii divini quotidianis necessitatibus occupantur. Scriptum est enim. Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum Dominus vester. Epist. 3. cap. 1. & habetur c. Proposuisti dist. 82. Est vetus admodum sacrae legis autoritas, iam inde ab initio custodita, quod in templo anno vicis suae habitare praecepti sunt Sacerdotes, ut servientes sacris oblationibus puros & ab omni labe purgatos sibi vendicent divina ministeria, neque eos ad sacra officia fas sit admitti, qui exercent etiam cum uxore carnale consortium, quia scriptum est. Sancti estote, quia ego sanctus sum, dicit Dominus Deus vester. Et ante Innocentium Siricius Epist. 1. cap. 7. & habetur c. Plurimos dist. ead. Plurimos Sacerdotes Christi atque Levitas post longa consecrationis suae tempora tam de coniugiis propriis, quàm etiam de turpi coitu sobolem didicimus procreasse & crimen suum hac praescriptione defendere, quia in V. T. Sacerdotibus ac Ministris generandi facultas legitur attributa. Dicat mihi nunc quis quis ille est sectator libidinum, praeceptor vitiorum, si existimat, quòd in lege Mosi passim sacris ordinibus à DEO nostro relaxata sunt frena luxuriae, cur eos quibus committebantur sancta sanctorum, praemonet dicens sancti estote, quia ego sanctus sum, Dominus Deus vester? Sed graviter hac in parte uterque Pontifex errat. Si enim illi, quibus dictum est, sancti estote, debent à coniugio abstinere, consequens fuerit 1. In coniugio non posse habere locum sanctitatem. 2. Omnes verè pios à coniugio abstinere debere, cum omnibus dictum sit, sancti estote, ut ex Levitico & ex hoc loco Petrino apparet. 3. Etiam in V. T. Sacerdotibus coniugio fuisse interdictum, quae omnia sunt falsa & absurda. Bellarm. lib. de matrimon. cap. 5. Siricium & Innocentium hoc modo defendit, quòd non de coniugio in genere, sed de coniugio Sacerdotum in specie loquantur. Sed manifestum est, quod coniugio Sacerdotibus interdictum esse probent hoc argumento, quia Sacerdotes debent esse sancti, unde Vasquez tract. de Matrim. Disp. 2. cap. 8. hoc Bellarmini subterfugium refellit.

2. Ex eo, quod Petrus praecipit, ut in omni conversatione simus sancti, colligit Estius in comm. h. l. sanctitatem & iustitiam nostram non consistere in sola remissione peccatorum, sed eitam ac praecipuè in ornatu & operatione virtutum. Resp. sanctitas & iustitia nostra est vel imputata vel inhaerens. Sanctitas & iustitia imputata consistit in sola remissione peccatorum Rom. 4. v. 6. sed sanctitas & iustitia inhaerens consistit ornatu & operatione virtutum, quae cum in hac vita nondum sit perfecta, ideò coram DEI iudicio eâ niti, ac fundamentum nostrae iustificationis in ea quaerere minimè possumus.

3. Ex eo, quod DEUS dicitur sine acceptione personarum secundùm cuiusque opus iudicare colligunt Pontificii bonorum operummerita. Bellarm. lib. 5. de Iustif. cap. 2. Estius in h. l. Resp. 1. Ex Gregorio in Psal. 7. poenit. Aliud est secundùm opera reddere, aliud secundùm operum merita vel propter opera reddere. In eo enim quod secundùm opera dicitur, ipsa operum qualitas intelligitur, ut cuius apparuerint opera bona, eius sit & retributio gloriosa. Illi namque beatae vitae, in qua cum Deo & de Deo vivitur, nullus potest aequari labor, nulla opera comparari, praesertim cum dicat Apostolus:

Non sunt condignae &c. 2. Congruit haec expositio dictis Scripturae, in quibus κατὰ non causam, sed qualitatem significat. Matth. 23. v. 3.Secundùm opera eorum nolite facere, i. e. nolite talia opera facere, qualia ipsi faciunt. 3. Neve quis dubitet, eiusmodi explicationem etiam huius loci propriam esse, exactè notandus locus Apoc. 22. v. 12. ubi illud κατὰ sic exponitur, ὡς τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ ἔσται. Nimirum ut arbor ex fructibus bona vel mala iudicatur: sic fidelis vel infidelis quis à DEO iudicatur ex operibus. 4. Probat etiam hanc expositionem scopus Apostolicus. Hoc enim vult Petrus, apud DEI tribunal non esse personae respectui locum, sed cordis sinceritatem aestimari, ac opera non ex specie externa, sed ex cordis qualitate bona vel mala ab ipso iudicari.

4. Ex eo, quod Petrus iubet, ut cum timore incolatus sui tempore pii conversentur, colligunt Pontificii, dubitandum esse de divina gratia. Bellarm. lib. 3. de iustif. cap. 6. Resp. aliud est timor filialis, aliud dubitatio. Timor filialis non opponitur fiduciae, cui opposita est dubitatio, sed opponitur carnali securitati. Complectitur enim ille timor filialis tùm seriam coram DEI iudicio humiliationem, quae oritur ex agnitione peccatorum & propriae infirmitatis, tùm filialem fiduciam in DEI misericordiam, absque qua hic timor non esset, nec dici posset filialis. Proinde quando verè pii iubentur in timore conversari, non commendatur illis dubitatio, sed pia solicitudo in cavendis lapsibus contra conscientiam, & fuga securitatis & confidentiae in propriis viribus. Statim enim addit petrus v. 18.Scientes, quòd non corruptibilibus auro & argento redemti estis, sed precioso sanguine Christi &c.

Διδαοκαλίαι. 1. Ubi locum habet υἱοθσσία per fidem, ibi exteriùs fefe exerit εὐπεισθεία.

2. Quia pii in sua ad Christum conversione priori vitae generi & eius concupiscentiis renunciarunt, ideò non debent se illis post suam ad Christum conversionem iterum configurare; quia veterem hominem exuerunt, ideò non debent eum iterum induere, sed potiùs dicant cum sponsa Cant. 5. v. 3.Expoliavi me tunica mea, quomodo induar illa? lavi pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo illos?

3. Ignorantia, salutari & salvificae DEI cognitioni opposita, post lapsum omnibus hominibus est innata.

4. Christi ignorantia est omnis impuritatis & impietatis causa Eph. 4. v. 18.

5. Exemplum sanctitatis in DEO propositum, debet esse & regula & causa impulsiva sanctitatis in nobis.

6. Peccatum est animae inquinamentum. Fide autem cor purificatur Act. 15. v. 9.

7. Sanctum est, quod à mundi sordibus purgatum & separatum, inde ἅγιος q. sine terra dictum censent.

8. Ad verba illa, Sancti eritis, quoniam ego sanctus sum, Leo serm. 8. de ieiunio septimi mensis sic annotat. Praecipit sanctitatem, & modum eius acquirendae. Hoc est, inquit, me diligite, & ab illis, quae mihi displicent, abstinete. Facite quod amo, amate quod facio. Et cum videtur difficile esse, quod iubeo, ad iubentem recurrite, ut unde datur praeceptum, praestetur auxilium, non negabo opem, qui tribui voluntatem.

9. DEUS & pater est & iudex, illud in nobis accendat fiduciam, hoc vero timorem.

10. Pater terrenus indulgentiùs tractat liberos, quàm servos: sed pater coelestis servos in filios recipit, & filios immorigeros ab haereditate excludit.

11. In Scripturis DEO saepissimè hoc elogium tribuitur, quòd sit ἀπροσωπολήπτηςDeut. 10. v. 17.2. Paral. 19. v. 7.Iob. 34. v. 19.Act. 10. v. 34Rom. 2. v. 11.Gal. 2. v. 6.Eph. 6. v. 9.Col. 3. v. 11. ac 25. Notandum verò, hanc ἀπροσωποληψίαν DEO tribui propter iustitiam. Ut ergò cum iustitia DEI non pugnat ipsius misericordia, ita non est προσωποληψία deputandum, quod DEUS propter personam fide in Christum sibi reconciliatam, etiam opera eius grata habet, vel quod dona sua pro arbitrio distribuit.

12. Peregrini & advenae sumus in hoc mundo. Ergò in timore DEI vivamus, ne carnis nostrae concupiscentiis securè indulgendo, cum mundo citò pereunte, ipsi quoque pereamus, sed ad patriam nostram coelestem aspirantes, toto cordis desiderio, & pietatis studio illuc feramur.

## 1:14
AS CHILDREN OF OBEDIENCE NOT CONFORMED TO THE FORMER DESIRES OF YOUR IGNORANCE.

The Apostle had said that the grace of God, obtained by the merit of Christ, is offered to believers in the revelation, or through the revelation of Jesus Christ, i. e., in the Gospel, in which Christ is revealed to us, and consequently this knowledge of the divine will ought to be an incitement to the pursuit of piety. The Apostle amplifies this first argument of exhortation from the contrary, namely from the opposite desires of ignorance, in which they remained before their conversion to Christ. He also adds another argument of exhortation from the right of sonship. He had said v. 3. that God according to his great mercy had regenerated believers into a living hope, into an incorruptible inheritance etc. but where there is generation or regeneration, there is sonship, and where there is an inheritance, sonship is presupposed. From there the Apostle connects such an argument of exhortation. Those who have been received into sonship, it behooves them to render due obedience to their father. Malach. 1. vers. 6. Believers have been received into sonship by the heavenly Father. Therefore they ought to render due obedience to their heavenly father. One could also establish a new argument of exhortation in the words, not conformed to the former desires of ignorance, drawn from the prior manner of life. Which manner of life, as being less conformable to the divine will, having been deservedly abandoned by you, you ought not to follow any longer after your conversion to CHRIST. But that former manner of life, which you followed in the former desires of your ignorance, by securely indulging your depraved concupiscences, was deservedly abandoned by you. Therefore. Finally, since the obedience to be rendered to God consists both in the flight from evil works, to which incite depraved desires, then in the pursuit of good works Psal. 34. v. 4. therefore he warns that depraved desires, in which they securely indulged in the former desires of ignorance, must be bridled and mortified, and by the same effort he shows what he wishes to be understood by the girding of the loins.

Τέκνα ὑπακοῆς are called by a Hebrew phrase obedient children, just as υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας are children or unbelieving men Eph. 2. v. 2. cap. 5. v. 6. Col. 3. v. 6. υἱὸς τῆς ἀγάπης is beloved son Col. 1. v. 13. although there it is a passive signification, here an active one. Moreover, this προσδιορισμὸς must be joined with the verb ἐλπίσατε in the preceding verse. Perfectly hope in grace as obedient children. For just as that which apprehends is the antecedent υἱοθεσίας, so the evidence and consequent of it is obedience, owed to God as a heavenly Father. μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοία ἐπιθυμίαις. The Syrian separates this member from the former. Neither associate yourselves again with the former concupiscences, which you desired without knowledge. But it can be joined very well with the former member, since in the Greek it is a participle. As obedient children not fashioning yourselves to the former concupiscences: for true obedience owed to God also requires this, that the former manner of life spent in depraved concupiscences be deserted. The Vulgate rendered: not fashioned. But in the Greek text it is present μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς ἐν τῇ ἀγνοία ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις, i.e. γεγονείαις. The Vulgate rendered to the former desires of your ignorance. But the Greek text is ἐμφατικώτερος. Not fashioning, nor accommodating yourselves to the former desires or concupiscences, in which you securely indulged, when you still stuck in the darkness of ignorance and sins.

Latin:

QUASI FILII OBEDIENTIAE NON CONFIGURATI PRIORIBUS IGNORANTIAE VESTRAE DESIDERIIS.

Dixerat Apostolus, gratiam Dei, Christi merito partam, credentibus offerri in revelatione, seu per revelationem Iesu Christi i. e. in Evangelio, in quo Christus nobis revelatur, ac proinde hanc divinae voluntatis notitiam debere esse incitamentum ad studium pietatis. Hoc primum exhortationis argumentum amplificat Apostolus à contrario, videlicet ab oppositis desideriis ignorantiae, in quibus ante suam ad Christum conversionem haeserunt. Addit etiam alterum exhortationis argumentum à iure filiationis. Dixerat v. 3.Deum secundùm magnam suam misericordiam credentes regenerasse in spem vivam, in haereditatem incorruptibilem &c. ubi autem generatio vel regeneratio, ibi filiatio, ac ubi haereditas, ibi filiatio praesupponitur. Inde Apostolus nectit tale exhortationis argumentum. Qui in filios sunt recepti, illos oportet patri suo debitam obedientiam praestare.Malach. 1. vers. 6. Credentes sunt à Patre coelesti in filios recepti. Ergo debent patri suo coelesti debitam obedientiam praestare. Posset etiam in verbis, non configurati prioribus ignorantiae desideriis, novum statui exhortationis argumentum, à priori vitae genere ductum. Quod vitae genus tanquam voluntati divinae minùs conforme meritò à vobis desertum, illud non debetis ampliùs post vestram ad CHRISTUM conversionem sectari. Atqui prius illud vitae genus, quod in prioribus ignorantiae vestrae desideriis sectati estis, pravis concupiscentiis vestris securè indulgendo, meritò à vobis desertum. Ergo. Denique cum obedientia Deo praestanda consistat tum in fuga malorum operum, ad quae instigant pravae cupiditates, tùm in studio bonorum operum Psal. 34. v. 4. ideò monet, pravas cupiditates, quibus in prioribus ignorantiae desideriis securè indulserunt, refrenandas & mortificandas esse, eademque operâ ostendit, quid per cincturam lumborum intelligi velit.

Τέκνα ὑπακοῆς phrasi Hebraica dicuntur filii obedientes, sicut υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας sunt filii sive homines increduliEph. 2. v. 2.cap. 5. v. 6.Col. 3. v. 6.υἱὸς τῆς ἀγάπης est filius dilectusCol. 1. v. 13. quamvis ibi sit significatio passiva, hîc activa. Coniungendus autem hic προσδιορισμὸς cum verbo ἐλπίσατε in versu praeced. Perfectè sperate in gratiam tanquam filii obedientes. Ut enim ὶsto apprehendens, est antecedens υἱοθεσίας, ita eiusdem indicium & consequens est obedientia, Deo tanquam Patri coelesti debita. μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοία ἐπιθυμίαις. Syrus hoc membrum separat à priori. Neque associetis vos rursus concupiscentiis pristinis, quas concupiscebatis sine scientia. Sed potest optimè cum priore membro coniungi, cum in Graeco sit participium. Tanquam filii obedientes non configurantes vos prioribus concupiscentiis: vera enim obedientia Deo debita etiam hoc requirit, ut pristinum vitae genus in pravis concupiscentiis exactum deseratur. Vulgata reddidit: non configurati. Sed in Graeco textu est praesens μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς ἐν τῇ ἀγνοία ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις, sc. γεγονείαις. Vulgata reddidit prioribus ignorantiae vestrae desideriis. Sed Graecus textus est ἐμφατικώτερος.Non configurantes, nec accommodantes vos prioribus desideriis sive concupiscentiis, quibus securè indulgebatis, cum adhuc in tenebris ignorantiae & peccatorum haerebatis.

## 1:15
BUT ACCORDING TO HIM, WHO CALLED YOU, HOLY, AND YOU YOURSELVES BE HOLY IN ALL CONVERSATION.

This is the third argument of the exhortation, taken from the example of the heavenly Father, by whom they were called. It is fitting for children to insist upon the paternal footsteps. Now indeed the heavenly Father, who called you to the kingdom of his Son, is holy. Therefore it is also fitting that you yourselves be holy. Κατὰ τὸν καλέσοντα ὑμᾶς ἃγιον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἃγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροΦῇ γενήθητε. Κατὰ here is a mark of similitude. Just as he, who called you, is holy, so also you yourselves may be rendered or made holy in all conversation.

By πάσην ἀναστροΦὴν he understands the whole course of the present life and conversation with all kinds of men. Whether you converse with those of the household of faith, or with infidels; whether you have to deal with friends or with enemies, with those of the household or with strangers; whether you live among prosperous things or among adverse things, you should perpetually and among all people strive for holiness.

Latin:

SED SECUNDUM EUM, QUI VOCAVIT VOS, SANCTUM & IPSI IN OMNI CONVERSATIONE SANCTI SITIS.

Tertium hoc est exhortationis argumentum, petitum ab exemplo Patris coelestis, à quo vocati sunt. Filios convenit insistere vestigiis paternis. Iam vero Pater coelestis, qui vos ad regnum Filii sui vocavit, sanctus. Ergò etiam convenit, ut & vos sancti sitis. Κατὰ τὸν καλέσοντα ὑμᾶς ἃγιον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἃγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροΦῇ γενήθητε. Κατὰ hîc est nota similitudinis. Quemadmodum ille, qui vos vocavit, sanctus est, ita & ipsi sancti in omni conversatione reddamini sive efficiamini.

per πάσην ἀναστροΦὴν intelligit totum praesentis vitae decursum & conversationem cum omnis generis hominibus. Sive cum domesticis fidei, sive cum infidelibus conversemini; sive cum amicis, sive cum inimicis, domesticis vel extraneis vobis agendum; sive inter prospera, sive inter adversa degatis, perpetuò & apud quosvis sanctitati studeatis.

## 1:16
BECAUSE IT IS WRITTEN. YOU SHALL BE HOLY, BECAUSE I AM HOLY.

This is a confirmation of the former argument. That you ought to be holy by the example of your heavenly Father is evident from the fact that GOD himself proposes his own holiness for you to imitate. This fourth argument of the exhortation can also be established as being sought from an express divine command. If you desire to hear, obedient children, it is necessary that you show yourselves compliant to the divine command: Now indeed this is the divine command. Be holy, because I am holy. Therefore show yourselves compliant to that command. Nor indeed does God simply command that we be holy, but he adds the reason, because I am holy. The reason for the connection is this. I am your God, you are my people; I am your Father, you are my children, not only in respect of creation, but also in respect of regeneration. It is indeed fair that a people should be assimilated to their GOD, and children to their father, in the conversation of life. Furthermore, the saying cited by the Apostle is repeated several times in Leviticus. Levit. 11. v. 44. after God had handed down the distinction of clean and unclean animals in species, and had commanded that it be observed, he adds γενικῶς. Do not defile your souls with any reptile, nor touch anything of them, lest you be unclean. For I am the Lord your God, be holy, because I the Lord am holy. cap. 19. v. 2. God, about to promulgate precepts partly Moral, partly Ceremonial, premises in general. Be holy, because I the Lord your God am holy. cap. 20. v. 7. God, about to repeat the prohibitions of degrees in contracting marriage, and certain moral laws, premises. Be sanctified, and be holy, because I the Lord your God am. v. 26. After the promulgation of those laws the same is repeated You shall be holy to me, because I the Lord am holy, and I have separated you from other peoples, that you might be mine. cap. 21. v. 8. when certain special precepts concerning the Priest are handed down, it is repeated. Let him be therefore Holy, because I the Lord, who sanctify you, am holy. Peter looks to all and each of these sayings, but especially to Levit. 20. v. 26. in this place, where in the Hebrew the verb of the future tense היותם is held, placed for the imperative, just as in this place. Peter explains that future, which the Vulgate, having followed the Hebrew custom of speaking, retained, by γενέσθε be, or as the Royal codex reads ἔσεσθε,. You shall be holy. In the same place the reason for the connection is also explained, why on account of the holiness of GOD the faithful also ought to strive for holiness, I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be mine, i. e. I have chosen you as a peculiar people, therefore it is fair that you separate yourselves from other peoples by the conversation of your life, and imitate the morals of Him whom you worship, and whose own you are.

Latin:

QUONIAM SCRIPTUM EST. SANCTI ERITIS, QUONIAM EGO SANCTUS SUM.

Confirmatio haec est prioris argumenti. Exemplo Patris vestri coelestis vos debere esse sanctos, patet ex eo, quòd DEUS ipse sanctitatem suam vobis imitandam proponit. Potest etiam quartum hoc statui exhortationis argumentum ab expresso mandato divino petitum. Si audire cupitis filii obedientes, oportet ut mandato divino vos obsequentes praebeatis: Iam vero mandatum divinum hoc est. Estote sancti, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Ergò illi mandato vos obsequentes praestetis. Neque vero simpliciter Deus praecipit, ut simus sancti, sed addit rationem, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Connexionis ratio haec est. Ego sum Deus vester, vos populus meus; ego sum Pater vester, vos filii mei, non solùm respectu creationis, sed etiam respectu regenerationis. Aequum vero est, ut populus DEO suo, & filii patri suo in vitae conversatione assimilentur. Caeterùm dictum ab Apostolo citatum aliquoties in Levitico repetitur. Levit. 11. v. 44. postquam Deus discrimen animalium mundorum & immundorum in specie tradiderat, illudque observari praeceperat, subiungit γενικῶς.Nolite contaminare animas vestras in omni reptili, nec tangatis quicquam eorum, ne immundi sit is. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester, sancti estote, quia ego Deus sanctus sum.cap. 19. v. 2. Deus praecepta partim Moralia, partim Ceremonialia promulgaturus praemittit in genere. Sancti estote, quia ego sanctus sum Dominus vester.cap. 20. v. 7. Deus prohibitiones graduum in matrimonio contrahendo, ac morales quasdam leges repetiturus praemittit. Sanctificamini, & estote sancti, quia ego Dominus Deus Vester.v. 26. Post legum illarum promulgationem idem repetitur Eritis mihi sancti, quia sanctus sum ego Dominus, & separavivos à coeteris populis, ut essetis mei.cap. 21. v. 8. quando traduntur certa quaedam praecepta specialia Sacerdotem concernentia, repetitur. Sit ergò sanctus, quia & ego sanctus sum Dominus, qui sanctifico vos. Ad haec dicta omnia & singula, praecipuè vero ad Levit. 20. v. 26. respicit hoc loco Petrus, ubi in Hebraeo habetur verbum futuri temporis היותם positum pro imperativo, sicut hoc loco. Petrus per γενέσθεestote, vel ut codex Regius legit ἔσεσθε, futurum illud explicat, quod vulgata Hebraicam loquendi consuetudinem secuta retinuit. Eritis sancti. Ibidem etiam exponitur connexionis ratio, quare ob sanctitatem DEI etiam fideles sanctitati studere debeant, Separavi vos a populis, ut essetis mei, i. e. elegi vos in populum peculiarem, aequum igitur est, ut vitae conversatione ab aliis populis vos separetis, & mores eius, quem colitis, & cuius proprii estis, imitemini.

## 1:17
AND IF YOU CALL UPON HIM AS FATHER, WHO WITHOUT RESPECT OF PERSONS JUDGES ACCORDING TO EVERY MAN'S WORK, CONVERSE IN FEAR DURING THE TIME OF YOUR SOJOURNING.

This is the fifth argument of the exhortation, drawn from the integrity of the divine judgment. The bare title of Christian profession will not excuse you before Him, who judges without respect of persons according to every man's work, if, having neglected the study of holiness, you wish to conform yourselves to your former evil concupiscences. Because GOD judges without respect of persons according to the work of each, therefore He will render rewards to those doing well; and punishments to those doing evil. It can also be referred to the amplification of the prior argument. God, who commands, be holy, because I am holy, not only called you, but also adopted you as sons, so that you might address Him in your prayers as Father out of filial confidence according to the institution of Christ. Therefore it is most fair that you insist upon His footsteps in the study of holiness. Moreover, the Apostle meets a tacit objection. The God, whom we worship, is our Father. Therefore He readily indulges, if we have offended in anything, consequently an exact study of holiness is not required. The Apostle answers, He is not only Father and merciful, but also judge and just, judging without respect of persons according to every man's work. Therefore you ought to pursue holiness with all study. The particle εἰ in this place is not conditional, but assertive; not of one doubting, but presupposing a known matter. Because you call upon Him as Father, εἰ ἐπικαλεῖσθε πατέρα. He refers without a doubt to the Lord's Prayer, which Christ taught us to begin with the most sweet name of Father. Because as sons you name the Father in daily prayer, and by naming you invoke him, etc.; for the word ἐπικαλεῖσθαι, signifies both, it is used for naming Matth. 10. v. 3.Luc. 22. v. 3.Act. 1. v. 23. etc., and for invocation Actor. 2. v. 21.cap. 9. v. 14.cap. 22. v. 16. etc. The Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] which likewise signifies both to call and to invoke. The sense therefore is, because you profess yourselves his sons, and in prayers you address him as your Father, who judges without respect of persons according to the work of each, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourning. Up to this point the Apostle had exhorted those to whom he writes to join holiness of life and innocence of morals with constancy of faith; now he shows the manner of holy conduct, namely that they should conduct themselves in fear, having shaken off carnal security. There is also contained in these words a new, and indeed a sixth, argument of exhortation drawn from the condition of the pious in this life. ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τἤς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ὰναστράφητε, understand κατὰ, as v. 13. Through all the time of your sojourning conduct yourselves in the fear of him, namely, who without acceptance of persons judges according to the work of each. παροικία signifies the dwelling of strangers, namely of those who were born elsewhere, for παροικεῖν signifies to arrive as a stranger in some place, for the sake of dwelling in it for a time Hebr. 11. v. 9. or simply to be a stranger and a guest Luc. 24. v. 18.. Budaeus from Gregory of Nazianzus teaches on page 237 that παροικίαν differs from κατοικίᾳ, in that the former is temporary, such as that of tenants, but the latter is stable and perpetual, such as that of natives. Ephes. 2. v. 19. ξένοι καὶ πάροικοι are opposed to συμπολίταις & οἰκείοις.. When therefore the Apostle calls the time of our life in these lands χρόνον παροικίας,, he signifies that we live in the world as strangers and guests, and therefore ought to abstain from carnal desires, lead a holy life, and walk in fear, which argument he explains more fully later in cap. 2. v. 11.. There is a double nerve and connection in this argument, taken from the condition of the pious in these lands. The former is this. The pious are strangers and sojourners in this world, they live indeed in the world, but they are not of the world Ioh. 15. v. 19.. Therefore they also ought not to conform themselves to the world, but to turn their love and appetite away from the world; they ought not to walk according to the former lusts after the manner of this world, but to lead a new life in holiness and in the fear of the Lord. The latter is this. The pious are pilgrims and strangers in this world, they do not obtain a stable and firm dwelling place in this world as an inn for staying Hebr. 13. v. 14. Therefore, they ought to spend the time of their sojourn in these lands, which cannot be long-lasting, in the pursuit of holiness, and live perpetually in the fear of the Lord, so that they may be able to approve themselves and their life to the judge who is soon to be present.

Latin:

ET SI PATREM INVOCATIS EUM, QUI SINE ACCEPTIONE PERSONARUM IUDICAT SECUNDUM UNIUSCUIUSQUE OPUS, IN TIMORE INCOLATUS VESTRI TEMPORE CONVERSAMINI.

Quintum hoc est exhortationis argumentum, ductum ab integritate divini iudicii. Nudus professionis Christianae titulus apud eum, qui sine personarum acceptione secundùm unius cuiusque opus iudicat, non excusabit, si neglecto sanctitatis studio prioribus concupiscentiis pravis vos configurare velitis. Quia DEUS sine acceptione personarum secundùm cuiusque opus iudicat, ideò benè operantibus praemia; malè agentibus poenas retribuet. Potest etiam referri ad amplificationem prioris argumenti. Deus, qui praecipit, sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum, non solùm vos vocavit, sed etiam in filios adoptavit, ut eum ex institutione Christi tanquam Patrem ex filiali fiducia in precibus vestris compelletis. Ergò in sanctitatis studio ipsius vestigiis vos insistere est aequissimum. Occurrit insuper Apostolus tacitae obiectioni. Deus, quem colimus, est noster Pater. Ergò promtè indulget, si quid deliquimus, proinde non requiritur exactum sanctitatis studium. Respondet Apostolus, ipse non solùm pater est & misericors, sed etiam iudex & iustus, sine personarum acceptione secundùm uniuscuiusque opus iudicans. Ergò omni studio sanctitatem debetis sectari. Particula εἰ hoc loco non est conditionalis, sed assertiva; non dubitantis, sed rem notam praesupponentis. Quia patrem invocatis eum, εἰ ἐπικαλεῖσθε πατέρα. Respicit dubio procul ad Orationem Dominicam, quam duleissimo Patris nomine exordiri Christus nos docuit. Quia tanquam filii in oratione quotidiana Patrem nominatis, & nominando invocatis &c. utrumque enim significat verbum ἐπικαλεῖσθαι, pro nominatione usurpatur Matth. 10. v. 3.Luc. 22. v. 3.Act. 1. v. 23. &c. pro invocatione Actor. 2. v. 21.cap. 9. v. 14.cap. 22. v. 16. &c. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] quod itidem significat & vocare & invocare. Sensus igitur est, quia vos profitemini illius filios, & in precibus tanquam Patrem vestrum eum compellatis, qui citra personarum respectum iuxta cuiusque opus iudicat, in timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini. Hactenus exhortatus fuerat eos, ad quos scribit, Apostolus, ad vitae sanctitatem & morum innocentiam cum fidei constantia coniungendam, iam ostendit modum sanctae conversationis, videlicet ut in timore, excussâ securitate carnali, coversentur. Continetur etiam in his verbis novum, adeoque sextum exhortationis argumentum ductum à piorum in hac vita, conditione. ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τἤς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ὰναστράφητε, subintellige κατὰ, ut v. 13. Per omne tempus incolatus vestri conversemini in timore illius, scil. qui absque personarum acceptione iuxta cuiusque opus iudicat. παροικία significat commorationem advenarum, eorum scil. qui alibi nati sunt, παροικεῖν enim significat peregrè advenire in aliquem locum, ad tempus in eo habitandi causâ Hebr. 11. v. 9. vel simpliciter peregrinum & hospitem esse Luc. 24. v. 18. Budaeus ex Gregorio Nazianzeno docet pag. 237. παροικίανita differre àκατοικίᾳ,ut illa sit temporaria, qualis est inquilinorum, haec verò stabilis & perpetua, qualis est indigenarum.Ephes. 2. v. 19.ξένοι καὶ πάροικοι opponuntur συμπολίταις & οἰκείοις. Quando igitur Apostolus tempus nostrae in his terris vitae vocat χρόνον παροικίας, significat, nos tanquam peregrinos & hospites in mundo versari, ac proinde à carnalibus desideriis abstinere, sanctam conversationem ducere, & in timore ambulare debere, quod argumentum in cap. 2. v. 11. uberiùs postmodum explicat. Duplex vero nervus & nexus est in hoc argumento, à piorum in his terris conditione petito. Prior hic est. Pii sunt peregrini & advenae in hoc mundo, vivunt quidem in mundo, non tumen sunt de mundoIoh. 15. v. 19. Ergò etiam non debent se mundo configurare, sed amorem & appetitum à mundo avertere; non debent iuxta priores concupiscentias more huius seculi ambulare, sed novam in sanctitate & timore Domini vitam ducere. Posterior hic est. Piisunt in hoc mundo peregrini & advenae, commorandi diversorium non stabile & firmum habitaculum in hoc mundo obtinent Hebr. 13. v. 14. Ergo tempus sui in his terris incolatus, quod diuturnum esse nequit, in studio sanctitatis transigere, & in timore Domini perpetuò vivere debent, ut iudici mox affuturo se suamque vitam probare possint.

## 1:18-20
KNOWING THAT YOU WERE NOT REDEEMED WITH CORRUPTIBLE THINGS, AS GOLD OR SILVER, FROM YOUR VAIN CONVERSATION OF THE TRADITION OF THE FATHERS. BUT WITH THE PRECIOUS BLOOD OF CHRIST, AS OF A LAMB UNSPOTTED AND UNDEFILED. FOREKNOWN INDEED BEFORE THE FOUNDATION OF THE WORLD, BUT MANIFESTED IN THE LAST TIMES FOR YOU.

The Apostle produces the seventh argument of his exhortation, drawn from the dear price of redemption and the due duty of the redeemed. Those who have been redeemed at a dear price from the miserable captivity in which they were stuck, it is right that they should serve their Redeemer in justice and holiness with fear. Luke 1. v. 74. & 75. For this the law of justice and gratitude requires. Believers in Christ have been redeemed at a dear price from the miserable captivity in which they were stuck, namely the power of the Devil Coloss. 1. v. 13.. Therefore it is right that they should serve their Redeemer Christ in justice and holiness. Bede on this passage: The greater the price is by which you have been redeemed from the corruption of a carnal life, the more you ought to fear, lest perhaps by returning to the corruption of vices you offend the mind of your Redeemer. Regarding the Minor premise, the Apostle first determines that price, that it is the precious blood of Christ. Secondly, he amplifies and exaggerates it in various ways. First, by a comparison of unequals, namely silver and gold, which are otherwise accustomed to be spent by men for the redemption of captives. Secondly, by an exposition of the term from which, or the state in which they were established before redemption, which he calls the vain conversation of the tradition of the fathers. Thirdly, by a description of the Redeemer, that he is an innocent and holy person, which holiness he declares by the likeness of a lamb, offered in sacrifice in the time of the O. Testament, which it was necessary to be unspotted. Fourthly, by a narration of the divine counsel, from which the whole work of our redemption originally descends. GOD entered into this counsel concerning our redemption through the blood of Christ, hidden from all human reason from eternity, and afterwards manifested it to us in the Gospel. Therefore, that work of redemption must be great, which GOD decreed from eternity and revealed in time.

Εἰδότες Knowing, i. e. weighing, in which way the word of knowing is used Psal. 39. v. 5.Psal. 90. v. 12. The sense therefore is, the consideration of the benefit may the liberation provided through Christ impel you to gratitude and a holy manner of life, ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς ἀργυρίῳ ἣ χρυσίῳ ἐλυτρώθητε. In the Latin Codices gold is placed before silver, but in the Greek text and the Syriac and German version silver is more correctly placed before, because in the exaggeration of price, that which is less precious was fitting to be named in the first place. Silver and gold, with which the Kings of this age are accustomed to redeem captives, the Apostle calls φθαρτὰ, because although in the judgment of men they are very precious, nevertheless they are corrupted both by fire and by use, and on the day of judgment they will be utterly annihilated, but the blood of Christ, which He expended for our redemption, is ἄφθαρτος and incorruptible. The Syrian referred that only to silver. You have not been redeemed with silver, [consult facsimile image] which is worn away and corrupted by age, nor with gold, etc. But the Greek Codices more correctly refer it to both, because to be corrupted and to perish by age is common to silver and gold. Ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου. In the preceding v. 14. he had accused the former manner of life of those to whom the Apostle writes ἀγνοίας, now he argues the same ματαιότητος because it profited nothing for justice and salvation, nay rather it rendered them liable to eternal death and destruction, πατροπαράδοτον he calls it the same, which the Vulgate rendered, of paternal tradition; Erasmus more correctly, which you had received from the tradition of the Fathers; with whom agrees that of Augustine in Psal. 146. by the manner of life handed down from the Fathers, because through evil examples they had received it from their ancestors, and through imitation had expressed it in themselves. And because he says that they were liberated from this vain manner of life through the blood of Christ, by that very fact he signifies that it was a heavy yoke of servitude, from which they could not have been liberated by any other reason, except through Christ. Ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ. The construction is to be ordered thus, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἳματι Χριστοῦ ὡς ἀμνοῦ etc. The particle ὡς in this place is not only a mark of similitude, for the blood of Christ is compared with the blood of the lamb, τυπικῶς formerly offered in sacrifice, but also of causality. You have been redeemed with the blood of Christ, as of a lamb, that is, as one who is a lamb, namely that lamb of GOD, taking away the sins of the world Iohan. 1. Vers. 29. prefigured in all those lambs, which were offered in sacrifice in the time of the Old Testament. Thence and Therefore the blood of CHRIST could be the price of your redemption, because CHRIST was ordained by divine decree to be that lamb of GOD taking away the sins of the world, which explanation the Apostle himself adds in v. 20.. Moreover, he calls the blood of Christ τίμιον precious both because it has the value of a price before the judgment of GOD, in which sense Paul also says in 1. Cor. 6. v. 20. & cap. 7. v. 23., ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς you were bought with a great price, and because by reason of the person it is by far most precious, namely the blood of the Son of GOD himself Acts 20. verse 28. 1. John 1. verse 7. to which nothing at all in heaven and on earth can be compared. That which is added ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου, shows firstly the third term of comparison, in which Christ is compared with the lambs accustomed to be offered in sacrifice in the time of the Old Testament, namely with respect to purity and innocence. Secondly, it pertains to exaggerating the dignity of the person. For thence and therefore the blood of Christ was a dear price of our redemption before GOD, both because it is the blood θεανθρώπου, and because it is the blood of an innocent person, entirely immune from every stain of sin. Some wish the name ἄμωμος, which is also used of Christ Heb. 9. v. 14. to be of Greek origin, derived from μωμᾶν, which is to blame, but it is more correctly derived from the Hebrew מום, which the Syrian also uses in this place, which properly signifies some defect of the body Lev. 21. v. 18. concerning a Priest cap. 22. Verse 20. concerning cattle, for from it descends μῶμος, signifying disgrace and reproach, especially if it is used by Poets. For writers of prose use it more concerning a person than a thing. For to the Gentiles Momus was a certain GOD, the mocker and censurer of all the other Gods, of whom mention is made in Plato book 6 of the Republic and elsewhere throughout, likewise he who imitates that GOD, and in the same way mocks the deeds of men as he does those of the Gods, concerning whom Erasmus discourses at length in the Chiliads in the proverb to satisfy Momus. Therefore ἄμωμος is lacking a defect, on account of which one might be censured, unblamable, in whom not even Momus could find anything to censure, which meaning is also gathered from the fact that it is opposed to one having מום, some defect of the body תםים destitute of every bodily defect. Ex. 12. v. 5. A lamb תםים to be chosen for the paschal lamb. Lev. 22. v. 18. & 19. a lamb תםים you shall take, every in which מום you shall not cause a blemish to approach. Joined to this noun ἄμωμος is also ἄσπιλος ὁ μὴ ἔχων σπίλον Ephes. 5. Vers. 27. who has no blemish. Someone can be a lamb ἄμωμος lacking a bodily defect, who nevertheless might not be ἄ σπιλος, if, that is, he has some blemishes. Therefore, so that the purest and most absolute purity, cleanliness, and holiness of Christ, prefigured in the sacrificial lambs of the O.T., might be more expressed, for that reason the Apostle calls him a lamb ἄμωμον καὶ ἄσπιλον. Nazianzen in oration περὶ τοῦ πάσχατος also adds ἀκίβδηλον. Προεγνωσμὲνου Ambrose in book 1 of the faith, chapter 7, renders predestined, but the Greek word properly signifies foreknown or precognized, where, however, it is not understood as simple knowledge, which they call of vision, but joined with a decree and ordination, which they call practical knowledge, by which GOD so knows something from eternity that He wills to give it execution in time, so that thus foreknown in this place is the same as preordained, because GOD in His eternal decree so ordained that the work of redemption ought to be carried out through Christ, His beloved Son, established as Mediator of the human race. The Syrian rendered, who from the beginning was [consult facsimile image] separated, by which word we are sent back to the type of the sacrificial lambs of the O.T., especially the paschal lamb, which were separated from the common flock before they were offered in sacrifice. Πρό καταβολῆς κόσμου before the casting, i.e., of the foundations of the world, i.e., before the foundations of the world were cast, which is a description of eternity John 17. v. 24. Eph. 1. v. 4. because nothing preceded creation except mere and naked eternity. Φανερωθέντος δὲ ὲπ᾿ ἔσχάτων τῶν χρόνων. By Φανέρωσιν some understand manifestation, which was made through the assumption of flesh 1. Tim. 3. v. 16. concerning which Gal. 4. v. 4. Eph. 1. v. 10. Hebr. 1. v. 1. it is treated, but so that at the same time and indeed principally the manifestation made through the preaching of the Gospel is understood, which presupposes the prior manifestation of the Son of GOD in the flesh. For that the manifestation through the Gospel is here principally understood is clear from the added προσδιορισμῷ δι' ύμᾶς and from the collation of parallel passages. Rom. 16. v. 25. according to my Gospel according to the revelation of the mystery kept secret for eternal times v. 26. but now manifested through the Prophetic Scriptures. Eph. 3. v. 9. The Gospel is called the mystery hidden from the ages in GOD. v. 10. but afterwards in time made manifest.

Col. 1. v. 26. The Gospel is the mystery which was hidden from ages and generations, but now is made manifest to his saints. 2. Tim. 1. v. 9. grace was given to us in Christ before the world began v. 10. but is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and ἀφθαρσίαν to light through the Gospel. Tit. 1. v. 2. GOD promised life before the world began v. 3. but hath in due times manifested his word through preaching. The Apostle therefore signifies that Christ was indeed ordained by the decree of GOD before the world was founded, and thus from eternity, to perform the work of redemption, yet He was not immediately exhibited in the flesh from the very beginning of the world, but only in the last times, that is, only in the New Testament was the Son of GOD manifested in the flesh, and the work of redemption having been performed in it and through it, it was manifested to the whole world through the preaching of the Gospel. δί ύμᾶς for your sake, so that you, no less than the rest of the faithful, might be made partakers of salvation through Him; for to that end the Son of GOD came into the world, assumed human flesh, perfected the work of redemption, and offered His benefits to the whole world in the Gospel, so that those embracing those benefits by faith might obtain eternal life in Him; therefore the Apostle adds.

Latin:

SCIENTES, QUOD NON CORRUPTIBILIBUS AURO VEL ARGENTO REDEMTI ESTIS DE VANA VESTRA CONVERSATIONE PATERNAE TRADITIONIS. SED PRECIOSO SANGUINE Q. AGNI IMMACULATI & INCONTAMINATI CHRISTI. PRAECOGNITI QUIDEM ANTE MUNDI CONSTITUTIONEM, MANIFESTATI AUTEM NOVISSIMIS TEMPORIBUS PROPTER VOS.

Septimum producit Apostolus exhortationis suae argumentum, petitum à caro redemtionis precio, ac debito redemtorum officio. Qui caro precio ex misera, in qua haerebant, captivitate sunt redemti, illos aequum est, Redemtori suo in iustitia & sanctitate cum timore servire. Luc. 1. v. 74. & 75. hoc enim requirit lex iustitiae & gratitudinis. Credentes in Christum caro precio ex misera, in qua haerebant, captivitate, videlicet Diaboli potestate Coloss. 1. v. 13. sunt redemti. Ergò aequum est, illos Redemtori suo Christo in iustitia & sanctitate servire. Beda in h. l. Quantò maius est precium, quo redemti estis a corruptione vitae carnalis, tantò ampliùs timere debetis, ne fortè ad corruptelam vitiorum revertendo animum vestri Redemtoris offendatis. Circa Minorem Apostolus primò precium illud determinat, quòd sit preciosus sanguis Christi. Secundò illud amplificat & exaggerat variis modis. Primò collatione imparium, videlicet argenti & auri, quae in redemtionem captivorum solent alioqui ab hominibus expendi. Secundò expositione termini à quo, sive status, in quo ante redemtionem fuêre constituti, quem vocat vanam paternae traditionis conversationem. Tertiò descriptione Redemtoris, quòd sit persona innocens & sancta, quam sanctitatem declarat similitudine agni, tempore V. Test. in sacrificium oblati, quem oportuit esse immaculatum. Quartò enarratione consilii divini, à quo totum redemtionis nostrae opus originaliter descendit. DEUS hoc de redemtione nostra per Christi sanguinem consilium ab omni humana ratione absconditum ab aeterno iniit, ac postea in Evangelio nobis manifestavit. Magnum ergò oportet esse illud redemtionis opus, quod DEUS ab aeterno decrevit, & in tempore patefecit.

ΕἰδότεςScientes, i. e. expendentes, quo modo verbum sciendi usurpatur Psal. 39. v. 5.Psal. 90. v. 12. Sensus igitur est, consideratio beneficii liberationis per Christum praestitae ad gratitudinem & sanctam vitae conversationem vos impellat, ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς ἀργυρίῳ ἣ χρυσίῳ ἐλυτρώθητε. In Codicibus Latinis aurum praeponitur argento, sed in Graeco textu & versione Syriaca ac Germanica argentum rectiùs praeponitur, quia in exaggeratione precii, illud, quod minùs preciosum, conveniebat primo loco nominari. Argentum & aurum, quibus Reges huius seculi solent captivos redimere, Apostolus vocat φθαρτὰ, quia tametsi hominum iudicio sint valdè preciosa, tamen & igne & usu corrumpuntur, ac in die iudicii penitus annihilabuntur, sed Christi sanguis, quem in redemtionem nostram expendit, est ἄφθαρτος & incorruptibilis. Syrus illud tantummodò ad argentum retulit. Non estis redemti argento[consult facsimile image] quod vetustate atteritur ac corrumpitur, nec auro &c. Sed Graeci Codices rectiùs ad utrumque referunt, quia vetustate corrumpi & perire, argento & auro commune est. Ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου. In praecedenti v. 14. priorem eorum, ad quos scribit Apostolus, conversationem accusaverat ἀγνοίας, iam eandem arguit ματαιότητος quia ad iustitiam & salutem nihil profuit, quinimò aeternae morti & exitio eos obnoxios reddidit, πατροπαράδοτον eandem vocat, quod Vulgata reddidit, paternae traditionis; Erasmus rectiùs, quàm ex Patrum traditione acceperatis; cum quo consentit illud Augustini in Psal. 146.à Patribus traditâ conversatione, quia per mala exempla à maioribus suis eam acceperant, ac per imitationem in semetipsis expresserant. Et quia ab hac vana conversatione per Christi sanguinem eos liberatos dicit, eo ipso significat, quòd fuerit grave servitutis iugum, à quo non aliâ ratione, nisi per Christum liberari potuerint. Ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ. Constructio sic ordinanda, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἳματι Χριστοῦ ὡς ἀμνοῦ &c. Particula ὡς h. l. non solùm est nota similitudinis, comparatur enim sanguis Christi cum sanguine agni, τυπικῶς olim in sacrificium oblati, sed etiam causalitatis. Redemti estis sanguine Christi, ut agni, id est, utpote qui sit agnus, videlicet agnus ille DEI, tollens peccata mundi Iohan. 1. Vers. 29. in omnibus illis agnis, qui tempore Vet. Testam. in sacrificium offerebantur, praefiguratus. Inde atque ideo sanguis CHRISTI potuit esse redemtionis vestrae precium, quia CHRISTUS divino decreto fuit ordinatus, ut esset agnus ille DEI tollens peccata mundi, quam explicationem Apostolus ipse in v. 20. subiungit. Vocat autem Christi sanguinem τίμιονpreciosum tùm quòd precii valorem coram DEI iudicio habeat, quo sensu etiam Paulus 1. Cor. 6. v. 20. & cap. 7. v. 23. dicit, ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆςmagno precio emti estis, tum quia ratione personae est longè preciosissimus, ipsius sc. Filii DEI sanguis Actor. 20. vers. 28.1. Ioh. 1. vers. 7. cui nihil quicquam in coelo ac terra comparari potest. Quod additur ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου, illud primò ostendit comparationis tertium, in quo Christus cum agnis tempore Vet. Test. in sacrificium offerri solitis conferatur, videlicet respectu puritatis & innocentiae. Secundò pertinet ad exaggerandam personae dignitatem. Inde enim atque ideo sanguis Christi coram DEO fuit carum redemtionis nostrae precium, tùm quia est sanguis θεανθρώπου, tùm quia est sanguis personae innocentis, ab omni peccati labe penitus immunis. Nomen ἄμωμος, quod de, Christo etiam usurpatur Hebr. 9. v. 14. quidam volunt esse originis Graecae, deductum à μωμᾶν, quod est culpare, sed rectiùs deducitur ab Hebraeo מום, quo etiam Syrus h. l. utitur, quod propriè significat vitium aliquod corporis Lev. 21. v. 18. de Sacerdote cap. 22. Vers. 20. de pecore, ab eo enim descendit μῶμος, significans dedecus ac probrum, praesertim si à Poetis usurpetur. Solutae namque orationis scriptores eo potiùs utuntur de persona quàm de re. Gentilibus enim Momus fuit DEUS quidam, reliquorum Deorum omnium irrisor & reprehensor, cuius apud Platonem lib. 6. de Republ. & alibi passim fit mentio, Item is qui DEUM illum imitatur, eodemque modo facta hominum, quo ille Deorum, irridet, de quo Erasmus in Chiliad. in proverb. Momo satisfacere, multis disserit. Est ergo ἄμωμοςcarens vitio, propter quod reprehendi queat, inculpatus, in quo ne Momus quidem, quod reprehendat, invenire possit, quae significatio etiam colligitur ex eo, quod habenti מום, vitium aliquod corporis opponitur תםים destitutus omni corporis vitio. Ex. 12. v. 5. Agnus תםים in agnum paschalem eligendus. Lev. 22. v. 18. & 19.agnumתםיםaccipietis, omne in quoמוםmacula non appropinquare facietis. Coniungitur huic nomini ἄμωμος etiam ἄσπιλος ὁ μὴ ἔχων σπίλονEphes. 5. Vers. 27.qui non habet maculam. Potest aliquis agnus esse ἄμωμος carens vitio corporis, qui tamen non sit ἄ σπιλος, si scilicet habeat aliquas maculas. Ut ergo purissima & asolutissima Christi puritas, mundities & sanctitas in agnis sacrificalibus V. T. praefigurata magis exprimatur, ideò Apostolus eum vocat agnum ἄμωμον καὶ ἄσπιλον. Nazianzenus in orat. περὶ τοῦ πάσχατος addit etiam ἀκίβδηλον. Προεγνωσμὲνου Ambrosius lib. 1. de fide cap. 7. reddit praedestinati, sed Graeca vox propriè significat, praesciti sive praecogniti, ubi tamen non intelligitur simplex scientia, quam vocant visionis, sed cum decreto & ordinatione coniuncta, quam vocant scientiam practicam, quâ DEUS ita aliquid ab aeterno cognoscit, ut illud in tempore velit executioni dare, ut sic praecogniti hoc loco idem sit, quod praeordinati, quia DEUS in aeterno suo decreto sic ordinavit, quod per Christum dilectum suum Filium Mediatorem humani generis constitutum opus redemtionis peragi debeat. Syrus reddidit, qui ab initio fuit[consult facsimile image]separatus, qua voce remittimur ad typum agnorum sacrificalium V. T. cumprimis agni paschalis, qui priùs ê communi grege separabantur, antequam in sacrificium offerrentur. Πρό καταβολῆς κόσμουante deiectionem, sc. fundamentorum mundi i. e. ante mundi fundamenta iacta, quae est descriptio aeternitatis Ioh. 17. v. 24.Eph. 1. v. 4. quia creationem nihil praecessit nisi mera & nuda aeternitas. Φανερωθέντος δὲ ὲπ᾿ ἔσχάτων τῶν χρόνων. Per Φανέρωσιν quidam intelligunt manifestationem, quae facta est per assumtionem carnis 1. Tim. 3. v. 16. de qua Gal. 4. v. 4.Eph. 1. v. 10.Hebr. 1. v. 1. agitur, sed ut simul & quidem praecipuè intelligatur manifestatio facta per praedicationem Evangelii, quae priorem ilFilii DEI in carne manifestationem praesupponit. Quod enim manifestatio per Evangelium hîc praecipuè intelligatur, patet ex addito προσδιορισμῷ δι' ύμᾶς & ex collatione locorum parallelorum. Rom. 16. v. 25. iuxta Evangelium meum secundùm revelationem mysterii aeternis temporibus taciti vers. 26. manifestati autem nunc per Scripturas Propheticas. Eph. 3. v. 9. Evangelium vocatur mysterium absconditum à seculis in DEO.v. 10.postea autem in tempore patefactum.

Col. 1. v. 26. Evangelium est mysterium quod absconditum fuit à seculis & generationibus, nunc autem manifestatum sanctis eius.2. Tim. 1. v. 9.gratia nobis data est in Christo ante tempora seculariav. 10.nunc autem manifestata per illuminationem Salvatoris Iesu Christi, qui mortem quidem destruxit, illuminatione vero suâ reduxit vitam &ἀφθαρσίανper Evangelium.Tit. 1. v. 2.promisit DEUS vitam ante tempora seculariav. 3.manifestavit autem temporibus suis verbum suum in praedicatione. Significat ergo Apostolus, Christum quidem ante mundum conditum, adeoque ab aeterno fuisse DEI decreto ordinatum ad opus redemtionis peragendum, nec tamen statim iam inde à primâ mundi origine in carne exhibitum, sed novissimis demum temporibus h. e. in Novo demum Testamento Filium DEI in carne esse manifestatum, ac redemtionis opere in ea & per eam peracto toti mundo per Evangelii praedicationem esse manifestatum. δί ύμᾶς propter vos, ut vos non minùs quàm reliqui fideles per ipsum salutis participes reddamini, eo enim fine Filius DEI in mundum venit, carnem humanam assumsit, redemtionis opus perfecit & beneficia sua in Evangelio toti mundo obtulit, ut fide beneficia illa amplectentes vitam aeternam in ipso consequerentur, ideò subiungit Apostolus.

## 1:18-21 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. What is understood by the Apostle by conversation πατροπαράδοτον? Resp. 1. Those who establish that this Epistle was written to the Gentiles, take it concerning the carnal life, or that which was spent securely and insolently in the works of the flesh Gal. 5. v. 19. & 20. which the Apostle Eph. 2. v. 11. & 12. graphically describes thus. You were at one time Gentiles in the flesh, at that time you were without Christ, being aliens from the conversation of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world. c. 4. v. 17. the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their mind v. 18. having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of GOD through the ignorance that is in them because of the blindness of their heart etc. which exposition could be confirmed from cap. 2.of this Epistlev. 10. & 11.That carnal conversation of the gentiles indeed πατροπαράδοτον to be called they judge, for the reason that it had been observed by ancestors in a long series, and handed down to posterity as if good and honest, which reason Augustine brings forward in enarr. Ps. 146. But the gentiles in that carnal conversation followed not so much the tradition of their ancestors, as the impulse and inclination of corrupt Nature. 2. Those who judge this Epistle to have been written to the Jews, explain it in various ways. First, some take it concerning the observation of the Mosaic law joined with the opinion of righteousness being valid before God, and of salvation to be hoped for from the law. If anyone should wish to object to this exposition, that that legal conversation cannot be called vain, since rewards were divinely promised to those observing the law, it can be answered, that the observation of Levitical Ceremonies and Forensic laws in the N. T. is called vain, because they had already been abrogated; but the observation of the moral law is called vain, not absolutely and simply, but in a certain respect, insofar as righteousness subsisting before GOD and eternal life is sought in it, because not only judicial and Ceremonial works, but also moral works are vain and ineffective for justification before GOD. If anyone should wish to object, that the law is not from the tradition of the Fathers, but from divine promulgation, it can be answered, that Circumcision had been divinely instituted, and nevertheless Ioh. 7. v. 22. it is said to be ἐκ τῷν πατέρων,, namely, because both the promulgation of the divine law, and the institution of Circumcision were propagated to posterity through the Fathers or ancestors of the Jews. This exposition therefore we leave in the middle: meanwhile secondly we say, that the Apostle here most especially looks to those corruptions of doctrine and divine worship, which had been brought into the Jewish Church under the name of traditions, which the Prophets, Christ, and the Apostles frequently tax. Esa. 29. v. 13.Ezech. 20. v. 18.Matth. 5. v. 21. & seqq. cap. 15. v. 6.Marc. 7. v. 9.Col. 2. v. 8. And these are those traditions, which as being instituted and received from ancestors the Jews most studiously observed and retained, whence Paul Galat. 1. v. 14. says that he before his conversation to the faith of Christ had been περισσοτέρως ζηλοτὴν τῷν πατρικῶν παραδόσεων But Peter in this place pronounces, that the conversation instituted according to them is ματαίαν, just as Christ Matth. 15. v. 9. & Marc. 7. v. 7. from Es. 29. v. 13. pronounces, μάτην σέβονταί με διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων, namely because the conversation instituted according to those traditions is neither approved by GOD, nor anything to righteousness. it does so, since the origin of the dear is not descended from a divine institution, but from human judgment.

Q. 2. Why does Peter call Christ an unblemished and unstained lamb? Resp. He looks 1. To the Prophecy Isa. 53. v. 7. 2. To the figure of the types of the O. T. Formerly a lamb was offered in the purification of a woman after childbirth Lev. 12. v. 6. in the cleansing of a leper, Lev. 14. v. 10. daily, in the morning and evening two lambs were offered for the continual sacrifice Exod. 29. v. 39. in more solemn feasts more lambs were offered Num. 28. v. 11. All these lambs offered in sacrifice prefigured Christ, to be offered at some time in sacrifice for the sins of the whole world. But especially the Apostle looks to the type of the paschal lamb, through whom Christ was prefigured, the Apostle teaches 1. Cor. 5. v. 7. For just as earlier in v. 2. through the word sprinkling he leads us to the type Exod. 24. v. 8. where the people were sprinkled with the blood of calves and goats previously offered in sacrifice, and by this sprinkling were received into the covenant of GOD: so in this place through the word lamb he leads us to the paschal lamb, slaughtered and eaten once every year with peculiar Ceremonies, with whose blood the lintels and doorposts were sprinkled Ex. 12. v. 7. For that the Apostle looks especially to this type is clear both from the word ἐλυτρώθητε. and from the epithets ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου. For just as the Israelites before their liberation from Egyptian servitude smeared the lintels and posts of their houses with the blood of the Paschal lamb, so that they might be delivered from the striking Angel: so by the blood of Christ we have been delivered from the power of the Devil and the captivity of hell. Just as it was necessary for the paschal lamb to be without spot and blemish Exod. 12. v. 5. so Christ is completely immune from every stain of sin. 1. Pet. 2. v. 22.Heb. 7. v. 26. 3. Because of suitability. For just as a lamb is gentle and innocent, so Christ demonstrated innocence in life, and patience in death. As a lamb clothes us with its fleeces: So Christ has prepared for us a garment of righteousness by his obedience and passion. As all things that are in a lamb have their use and advantage: so whatever is in Christ profits for our salvation.

Q. 3. Why is Christ called προεγνωσμένος πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου? Resp. 1. Because GOD foresaw from eternity that man would not persist in his concreated integrity, but into sin and death would fall, and therefore also out of ineffable mercy, He already from eternity provided for the human race concerning a remedy in Christ the Mediator and Redeemer. 2. Because the Son of GOD in the eternal counsel of the Trinity voluntarily took upon Himself the roles of Mediator and Redeemer. 3. Because whatever is announced to us in the Gospel concerning the benefits of Christ, all that, and thus the whole mystery of our salvation, was from eternity decreed and ordained by GOD.

Q. 4. Why was the Son of GOD sent into the flesh only in the last times, and manifested to the world through the preaching of the Gospel? Resp.
