Although a reason for the divine will, which is the highest reason, cannot be given, there is nevertheless no doubt that this was done by the most wise counsel of GOD. A long-desired gift afterwards exists as far more dear and pleasing.

Q. 5. How are we said to believe in GOD through Christ? Resp. 1. Because Christ manifested the heavenly Father to us in the Gospel. Iohn. 1. v. 14. 2. Because faith, by which we believe in GOD, as the author of our salvation in Christ, and obtained for us through Christ, cannot be had except from the merit of Christ. 3. Because through Christ, nay rather not except through Christ, access lies open to us to GOD. Iohan. 14. v. 6. Outside of Christ GOD is a consuming fire. Christ, however, reconciled us to GOD, so that we might place all our trust in Him.

Q. 6. How is this inferred by way of deduction from the preceding, that your faith and hope might be in GOD? Resp. 1. Some understand by the glory bestowed upon Christ the glorification of Christ, made through the preaching of the Gospel in the whole world, which is a glorification, so to speak, relative. They put forward such a connection. GOD through the universal proclamation of the Gospel declared to the whole world that Christ is His only-begotten Son and true God, so that while you believe and hope in Christ, this faith and hope of yours might not be in a mere and pure man, but in GOD. These things are indeed rightly said, but they do not yet attain that which the Apostle properly intends, because GOD not only glorified Christ relatively through the preaching of the Gospel, but also absolutely through the real bestowal of glory. 2. Some bring forward this reason for the connection. GOD for this reason raised Christ from the dead, and advanced Him into glory, so that looking unto Him, as the exemplar of resurrection and glory, you might believe in the words of GOD, to those believing in the resurrection unto life in Christ promising, and you hoping, you, as members in the mystical body of Christ, would obtain from him the participation of blessed resurrection and glory. These things are likewise rightly said indeed, but insufficiently. For Christ is not only the exemplar, but also the merit of our resurrection to life. 3. It must therefore be said, from the resuscitation and the bestowing of glory, done to Christ the man by the heavenly Father, it is gathered that our faith and hope are in GOD for this reason, because through the resuscitation of Christ, and the bestowing of glory done to him by the heavenly Father, we are most certainly confirmed that for our sins it has been most fully satisfied, and that we are most perfectly reconciled to GOD. For unless Christ our sponsor had provided a most sufficient λύτρον, for the debts of our sins, the heavenly Father would by no means have led him out from the prison of the sepulcher, and crowned him with glory and honor. And from this faith firmly embracing the sufficiency of the satisfaction, arises that hope which looks upon the glory of Christ the head as a certain pledge, that we also, who are his members, are to be resurrected to life and glory in his own time. 4. Furthermore, the Apostle also looks to this, that the heavenly Father gave glory to Christ resurrected from the dead so that, reigning most powerfully at the right hand of the Father, he might effectively and powerfully work faith and hope in GOD in us, might defend and protect his Church against all enemies, and might provide life and salvation to the whole Church, and to all its members. For unless Christ in his resurrection had brought back a glorious triumph from death, the Devil, and all enemies, and now sitting at the right hand of GOD, had all enemies subjected under his feet, neither could the kingdom of grace be preserved, nor be propagated and dilated. Thus therefore, both by reason of merit and by reason of efficacy, it is attributed to Christ resurrected and exalted to the right hand of the Father, that our faith and hope through him is in GOD, whence also the Apostles confirmed their preaching about Christ the Savior most especially from the resurrection and glory of Christ Acts 2. v. 33.chap. 5. v. 31.chap. 10. v. 40. etc.

ἘναντιοΦανείαι. 1. Christ is called the lamb foreknown before the foundation of the world. On the contrary Apoc. 13. v. 8. he is called the lamb slain from the origin of the world. Some respond that it is one thing πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμον to be foreknown, another ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου to be slain; the former describes mere and naked eternity, but the latter time from beginning from the origin of the world. But the phrase ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου is likewise taken for a description of eternity. Matt. 25. v. 34.Rev. 17. v. 8. Therefore Christ is called the lamb slain from the foundation of the world, by reason of the divine decree, as Peter explains in this place, if this phrase is taken for a description of eternity. For GOD from eternity not only foresaw that Christ would be slaughtered like a lamb, but also made this decree, that through this slaughtering of Christ, as an innocent lamb, the work of the redemption of the human race should be accomplished, and those whom He foresaw would believe in Christ that lamb, those He wrote in the book of life, i.e., He elected them to eternal salvation. But if this phrase is taken for time beginning from the origin of the world, then Christ is said to be slain ἀπό καταβολῆς κόσμου. 1. by reason of the promises. 2. by reason of the types. 3. by reason of the efficacy; but not by reason of the external act, which followed only in the fullness of time,

2. Christ was manifested in the last times. But the Son of God was sent in the flesh, and manifested to men through the Gospel, more than one thousand and six hundred years ago. Resp. It is solemn for the Prophets and Apostles to call that whole time, which intervenes from the first coming of the Messiah until His second coming, the last time, nay, the last hour.Isa. 2. vers. 2.Mic. 4. v. 1.1. Cor. 10. v. 11.2. Tim. 3. v. 1.Heb. 1. v. 1.Jas. 5. v. 3.2. Pet. 3. v. 3.1. John 2. v. 18.Jude v. 18. It is called the last time. 1. Because it is the third and final age of the world, according to that ancient distribution of the times of the world, by which two thousand years are attributed to the void, two thousand to the law, and the last two thousand to the Messiah, whence Christ is also said to have appeared ἐν συτελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων. 2. Because after that time, until the end of the world, no other manifestation is to be expected Heb. 1. v. 1.3. Because no other time remains, to which the prior times of the Prophets might be subservient. Thomas Aquinas in chapter 9 of Hebrews, The last age is the present state, after which there is no other state, just as there is no other age after old age. And just as in other ages there is a determined number of years, but not in old age, so it is not determined how long this state of the world ought to last, yet it is the consummation of the ages, because no other state remains.

3. Christ was manifested in the last times for you, who through him believe in God. But the joy from the birth of Christ pertains to all the peopleLuke 2. v. 10.and the manifestation through the Gospel pertains to all nations.Matt. 28. v. 19. Resp. Peter signifies that the manifestation of Christ, both in His advent and in the preaching of the Gospel, does not profit all, but only believers, who embrace the goods offered by faith in the Gospel. John 1. v. 12.

4. GOD raised Christ from the dead. But Christ rose by His own power and raised the temple of His body.John 2. v. 19.chap. 10. v. 18. Resp. 1. If the name of GOD is taken essentially, as it denotes the three persons of the Deity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, every difficulty will be removed. 2. If it is even taken personally, so as to denote only the first person of the Deity, namely the Father, just as Rom. 6. v. 4. Christ is said to have risen from the dead by the glory of the Father, it must be said that by the name of the Father, neither the Son nor the Holy Spirit is excluded, because that power by which the Father raised Christ is common to all three persons of the Deity. But that the resurrection of Christ from the dead is attributed peculiarly to the Father, that happens because 1. Because the Father is the fountain of Divinity, which He communicated from eternity to the Son by generation, and to the Holy Spirit by procession. Therefore, because Christ rose by the power of the Father, communicated to Him by the Father according to the Deity through eternal generation, thence the resurrection is for the most part attributed to the Father. 2. As the very mission of the Son and the confirmation of His office, made by the divine voice from heaven, and the miracles performed by Christ in the days of His flesh, are wont to be assigned to GOD the Father, and all the obedience of Christ is said to have been rendered to GOD the Father Phil. 2. v. 8., so also the resurrection of Christ from the dead is attributed to the Father. 3. Just as the Son is said to have been delivered into death by the Father John 3. v. 16.Rom. 8. v. 32., so also He is said to have raised Him from the dead, so that nevertheless the Son is not excluded from that delivery, who voluntarily underwent death Gal. 2. v. 20., so also the Son is not excluded from that resurrection. 4. We are admonished by this form of speaking concerning the sufficiency of the merit and satisfaction rendered to GOD the Father through Christ. For because the heavenly Father so gloriously brings back from the prison of the sepulcher Christ, who had received into Himself the debts of all our sins and had promised that He would satisfy for them, it becomes manifest from that, that the heavenly Father has been most fully satisfied for those debts. Compare Gregory of Nyssa, oration 2 on the resurrection of Christ.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. We are redeemed οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀλλὰ ἃιματι Χριστοῦ. It is false, therefore, what Curaeus and certain other Calvinists maintain, that the blood of Christ poured out on the altar of the cross has rotted, and Therefore it is not possible for the drink to be given to us to be drunk in the holy Supper by means of the blessed cup.

2. The work of redemption is attributed to Christ alone, both in this place and everywhere else in the Scriptures. Therefore, what the Pope teaches is false, that Mary was Christ's helper in this work of redemption. Mariale Argentinense published in the year 1493, book 1, chapter 5, folio 13, The Lord was with Mary, and she herself was with the Lord in the same labor, and in the same work of redemption. The mother of mercy helped the father of mercies in the work of our salvation, whence it was predicted concerning the first woman, let us make a helper for him. What is it therefore that the Lord says, I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me? It is true, Lord, that there was no man with you, but a woman was together with you. Vincentius Brunius in Meditations on the Feasts of the Blessed Virgin, published at Cologne in the year 1599, page 11, When GOD decreed that his only-begotten Son should assume flesh for the redeeming of the human race, he at the same time also decreed and predestined who ought to be his mother, and the co-worker of our redemption. Osorius, volume 4, sermons, page 530, Christ immolated his flesh on Calvary, Mary her soul. Alphonsus Salmeron, volume 10, tract 41, page 339, Mary stood beneath the cross, so that she might be a co-redemptrix, just as Eve brought in evil together with Adam.

3. Christ alone is our Redeemer. Therefore, what the Pope teaches is false, that a man can rightly be called his own redeemer. Bellarmine, book 1 on purgatory, chapter 14, that saints can be called redeemers, in that they pay a debt of small moment, if it is compared with that debt for which Christ made satisfaction. Schioppius in Apology on Indulgences, chapter 47.

4. We are redeemed by the blood of Christ. Therefore, what the Photinians deny is false, that Christ provided satisfaction for our sins. They say the word redemption is metaphorical, and in this question signifies nothing else than a simple liberation, which was done without the intervening price of satisfaction. And yet where all the requirements of a truly and properly called redemption are given, there a truly and properly called redemption is given. In our spiritual redemption there is given 1. The object of redemption, that is, the captives, who are all men Zech. 9. v. 11.Gal. 3. v. 10. 2. The principal cause, who is Christ our redeemer, our propitiatory Rom. 3. v. 24. and the propitiation for the sins of the whole world 1. John 2. v. 2. 3. The instrumental cause, or the medium of redemption, is the blood of Christ, which is called the blood of the Testament Zech. 9. v. 11.Eph. 1. v. 7.Col. 1. v. 14. and in this place 4. The term from which we are redeemed is captivity, under which are understood the judge himself, or the Lord of the prison, the keeper of the prison, the prison itself, and its adjuncts. The judge is GOD himself angered, or the wrath and judgment of GOD Rom. 5. vers. 9.Gal. 3. v. 13. The keeper of the prison is the Devil, from whom Christ redeemed us. Os. 13. v. 14. The prison is hell, or the pit, in which there is no water Zach. 9. v. 11.Os 13. v. 14. The adjuncts of the prison are the snares of our sins, which Christ has crushed Luc. 1. vers. 74.Hebr. 2. v. 14.5. The term to which is GOD appeased, to whom Christ has redeemed us, and the liberty into which He has asserted us Luc. 1. v. 74.

5. Peter teaches that we have been liberated by the precious blood of Christ from the conversation πατροπαραδότω. The Pope teaches that traditions of faith and morals are to be accepted with an equal affection of piety as the written word of God. The Pharisees and Pseudo-Apostles urged the traditions of the elders; Christ and Peter repudiated them. The Pope therefore insists on the footsteps of those, and thus is not the vicar of Christ, nor is he the true successor of Peter.

6. Peter describes the creation with this phrase πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, which also agrees with other sayings of Scripture. Psalm. 91. vers. 3.Prov. 8. vers 24. It is therefore false, what the Photinians, and with them Vorstius, deny, that it is a firm argument for the Deity of Christ, that He is said to have existed before the world was founded.

7. Peter says, that Christ was manifested for the sake of those who through Him believe in God. It is therefore false, what certain Papists and Calvinists and Photinians teach, that the sounder Gentiles, who neither knew Christ nor believed in Him, were made partakers of eternal salvation.

8. Peter teaches, that glory was given to Christ in time, namely in the resurrection and ascension. Therefore, according to the human Nature, this glory was conferred upon Him, which is to be opposed to the Calvinists, who trifle that one must subsist in the person of the Mediator.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. From the fact that we are said to be redeemed by the blood of Christ, Piscator gathers that the passive obedience of Christ alone is the meritorious cause of our justification. Sibrandus Lubertus supports this in part, when in the catalog of the errors of Vorstius p. 357, he writes, that the active obedience of Christ is indeed not to be separated from the passive, meanwhile the whole humiliation of Christ is not λύτρου the payment of that, but death alone is the price of our redemption. Resp. when Peter in this place, and Scripture elsewhere throughout, it attributes the work of redemption to the death and shedding of the blood of Christ, that is not to be taken exclusively, for the sayings which make express mention of active obedience testify to the contrary, Matth. 5. v. 17.Rom. 5. v. 18.cap. 10. v. 4.Gal. 3. v. 4.Hebr. 10. v. 10. &c. but inclusively, since the active and passive obedience of Christ are joined by a most tight and indissoluble bond, inasmuch as the passion of Christ is active, and the action of Christ is passive. In the passion of Christ shine forth the most illustrious virtues, required in the law, the highest love of GOD, and most ardent affection toward the human race, humility, patience, obedience, trust, invocation, hope &c. and the passion of Christ did not begin only in the garden, but from the first moment of the incarnation, and lasted through the whole course of life. But mention is made so often of death and shed blood, because in death and the shedding of blood, the most perfect obedience of Christ toward God the Father, and most ardent affection toward the human race, most greatly shone forth and beamed. Nowhere did it shine more clearly that the Lord loved us, than in his passion and wounds. Furthermore, death is the final line, the complement and consummation of the obedience which CHRIST rendered to his Father on the cross. Iohan. 19. v. 30.Phil. 2. v. 8.

2. From the fact that Peter says, we have been redeemed by the precious blood, as of a lamb unspotted and undefiled, Christ, the Papists gather, that Christ is our Mediator, not as God and man, but as a just man. Resp. 1. Scripture teaches that the obedience and satisfaction of Christ is meritorious thence and for that reason, both because it is the obedience of a most innocent, most holy, and most pure person Hebr. 7. v. 26. and even most greatly, because it is the obedience of the Son of GOD himself, since that infinite dignity and majesty of the person reconciles infinite force, dignity, and efficacy to the same merit. Ioh. 6. v. 51.Actor. 20. v. 29.Galat. 4. v. 4.1. Iohan. 1. v. 7. &c. 2. That is so certain and evident, that Bellarmine, although he disputes with great effort in book 5 de Christo cap. 2, that Christ is our Mediator only according to his human Nature, nevertheless, convinced by the brightness of the truth, writes in book 2 de Iustif. cap. 5, GOD does not accept as true satisfaction for sin anything except infinite justice, since sin is an infinite offense, but for some justice to be infinite, that is, of infinite price and value, it is not necessary that it be the essential justice of GOD, but it is enough that it be the justice of an infinite person, such as is CHRIST GOD and man. Therefore The obedience, passion, and death of the Son of GOD, although in itself and essentially it was created and finite, nevertheless by reason of the person obeying, suffering, and dying, it was infinite, and by the true rigor of justice it was a propitiation for the sins of the whole world. But if in the work of our redemption and our reconciliation with GOD, a justice of infinite value and price is required, then certainly Christ according to his divine Nature is our Mediator and Redeemer. The reason is that that infinite value and that infinite price of our redemption cannot descend from the human Nature alone. But if therefore in the work of our redemption and our reconciliation with GOD, something is required and concurs which does not flow formally from the humanity of Christ, that is, from the virtue of the humanity by itself and of itself, but from the infinite τοῦ λὸγου Deity in ἀποτελέσματα the Redeemer Christ, then certainly not according to the human nature only, but also according to the divine Nature, Christ is Redeemer and Mediator. But if in the work of redemption the human Nature alone acts, with the activity of the divine Nature excluded, then the obedience of Christ will not be of infinite price, nor a satisfaction for the sins of the whole world, nor will it be able to be imputed to us for righteousness. 3. Therefore, even if Peter did not make mention of the divine Nature of Christ in this place, he would not for that reason exclude it from the work of redemption, since in other sayings of Scripture dealing with the work of redemption, express mention is made of it. 4. What of the fact that the term Christ is a concrete term of the person, expressing both Natures. Athanas. orat. 5. contra Arian. p. 321. Χριστὸς τὸ συναμφότερον νοεῖται. August. in Psal. 44. The name of Christ embraces the anointing Deity and the anointed humanity. Damasc. lib. 3. cap. 4. Χριστὸς ἐστι τὸ συναμφότερον.

3. Schmaltzius in Examinat. 157. errorum err. 69. p. 21. The blood of Christ is called precious, not because it has any value of price, but because it is the blood of the eternal covenant. For precious is opposed to corruptible, whence it is evident that precious is the same as incorruptible. However, the blood of Christ cannot be called incorruptible in itself: for Christ, because he is a Spirit, has no blood, but relatively, because, to wit, it is the blood of an eternal thing, insofar as the new covenant was confirmed through it. Resp. 1. The blood of Christ is called τίμιος, not only in opposition to φθαρτοῦ, but also absolutely and simply, because it is the τιμή, or price of our redemption. 1. Cor. 6. v. 20. and cap. 7. v. 23. ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς. Actor. 20. vers. 29.

GOD redeemed the Church with His own blood. From the comparison of these places it shines forth most evidently that the blood of Christ is the price of our redemption. 2. To be a price, and to be incorruptible, are not opposites, but subordinate. Both belong to the blood of Christ, and render it τίμιον. 3. Because the blood of Christ is the blood of the eternal covenant, it is therefore also the price of our redemption. For the eternal covenant between GOD and the human race, having fallen into sins, could not have been erected unless GOD had been reconciled to the human race through the blood of Christ, hence Zach. 9. v. 11. both are joined. By the blood of thy Testament thou hast sent forth the prisoners. 4. The blood of Christ is incorruptible, because it is the blood of the Son of GOD Himself Actor. 20. v. 29.1. Ioh, 1. v. 7. Although therefore by itself, i. e. from the property of its own Nature, and from essential principles it is not incorruptible, yet from the personal union it is incorruptible. 5. It is false that Christ does not have blood, since He is Spirit, i. e. since His human Nature itself has been changed into Spirit. The human Nature of Christ is spiritual, but not changed into Spirit. Luc. 24. v. 39. 6. That the blood of Christ is called incorruptible, because it is the blood of an eternal thing, insofar as through it the new covenant has been confirmed, is indeed said correctly, but insufficiently, for it is also therefore incorruptible, because, as the proper blood of the Son of GOD it did not see, nor is it going to see corruption. Psalm. 16. v. 10.Actor. 2. v. 27.cap. 13. v. 36.

4. From the fact that Christ is called προεγνωσμένος foreordained and destined to the office of Mediator, Chamier gathers in tom. 3. Panstrat. l. 9. c. 3. §. 5. that Christ could merit nothing from GOD by absolute merit. For since He merited nothing for us, except as Mediator, and He is Mediator from a certain decree of predestination, it is altogether necessary that He merited nothing, except from the eternal decree of predestination. But all these things proceed from that false hypothesis, that GOD chose certain ones to salvation by an absolute decree, and afterwards destined Christ as Mediator for them, when on the contrary rather, πρόγνωσις of the merit of Christ, and of faith in Christ, must be placed under the decree of election.

5. From the fact that Peter says, that Christ was manifested for the sake of believers, the Calvinists gather, that Christ died for the elect alone, and the benefits of Christ, with the intention of communicating them, are offered in the Gospel to the elect alone. Resp. 1. The Apostle here does not speak about the handing over of Christ into death, but about the manifestation of Christ, i.e., both about the manifestation of the Son of GOD in the flesh, and indeed especially about the manifestation through the Gospel. 2. Therefore he says that Christ was manifested for the sake of believers, so that he may signify that the benefits of Christ, which are offered to all in the Gospel, are applied to believers alone, and profit no one, unless they are received through faith. 3. He writes especially to those converted from the Jews, to whom peculiar promises concerning the coming of the Messiah had been made, and for whose sake Christ had primarily come, Matth. 15. v. 24.Rom. 15. v. 8. to whom therefore the Gospel had to be preached first, Act. 13. v. 46. 4. He signifies that every believer ought to embrace the benefits of Christ with such confidence, and be so affected toward the benefit of redemption, that, although it is common to all, he may nevertheless acknowledge that it was provided properly for himself, just as Paul says out of true and firm confidence Gal. 2. v. 20.Christ loved me, and delivered himself for me.

6. From the fact that Peter says, that Christ was manifested in the last times through the Gospel, the Photinians gather, that eternal life was not promised in Christ to the fathers of the O. Testament. Resp. 1. The Gospel is taken either for the joyful message concerning Christ already exhibited, or for the preaching of grace concerning the gratuitous remission of sins on account of Christ, whether still to be expected, or already exhibited. The Gospel taken in the former signification is proper to the N. Testament; but in the latter signification it is common to both Testaments, Act. 15. v. 11.Rom. 4. v. 1. & following. 2. Although the benefit of redemption not yet performed also had a place in the O. Testament, nevertheless after the work was completed, a more abundant fruit of redemption came to men.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The benefit of precious redemption is most effective ὁρμητήριον for holy conversation. For why should we still wish to serve sin, from whose servitude Christ redeemed us at such a dear price? Moreover, it is fitting to give thanks to such a benefactor not only with words, but by the deed itself.

2. The redemption of Christ is our worthiness and exaltation before GOD. Hugo in the book on the pledge of the Bride. I ought no longer to be vile to myself, because I pleased GOD so much, that He chose to die for me, lest He should lose me.

3. The preciousness of the blood of Christ depends not only on His own innocence, but also on the infinite dignity of His person.

4. Christ is entirely uncontaminated and immaculate, both because He was conceived of the Holy Spirit, and born of a virgin, He did not contract the stain of original sin, and because he was never contaminated by any actual sin, even the smallest. Interlinear Gloss. Christ is uncontaminated by original and actual sin.Es. 53. v. 9.2. Cor. 5. v. 21.Hebr. 7. v. 26.1. Petr. 2. v. 22.

5. Hugo in his commentary on chapter 53 of Isaiah brings forward fifteen properties, with respect to which he establishes σύγκρισιν between Christ and the lamb. Among them, however, innocence and patience stand out. In a relative sense, the title of lamb is attributed to Christ on account of a twofold Prophetic prediction, namely both γραφικὴν Esai. 53. v. 7.Ierem. 11. v. 19. and τυπικὴν in the sacrifices.

6. But primarily the paschal lamb was an illustrious type of Christ. 1. With respect to quality. The paschal lamb had to be immaculate and perfect: so also Christ is immune from every stain of sin, whence he is called ἂμωμος καὶ ἂσπιλος. by this. The paschal lamb had to be a male. Christ is that man whom a woman has encompassed, Ierem. 31. v. 22. The lamb had to be a yearling, in a perfect state of age: thus Christ was sacrificed in the very flower of his age. 2. With respect to Sacramental acts, which are 1. Segregation. The paschal lamb was to be sought from the common flock: thus Christ assumed true flesh from the human race. Deut. 18. v. 18. The paschal lamb was segregated on the 10th day of the first month. Christ on the same day entered Jerusalem solemnly and in a peculiar manner through the same gate through which sheep and lambs were accustomed to be led to sacrifices. 2. Slaughtering. 3. Roasting. 4. Eating. 5. Smearing of blood on the doorposts and lintels of the houses. We show the application of the individual members in the place concerning Circumcision and the paschal lamb §. 46. and following.

7. Christ was ordained by the heavenly Father from eternity to be the lamb to be sacrificed for the sins of the world, his immolation was promised in the protevangelium, and foreshadowed in the sacrifices, the same was also sent in the fullness of time, so that he might be sacrificed on the altar of the cross. Peter expresses all these acts in this place, and on account of all and each of these acts he is called the lamb of GOD. Ioh. 1. v. 29.

8. The innocence, gentleness, and patience of Christ proposed to us in the likeness of a lamb, not only pertains to the merit of our redemption, but also exhibits to us an example for imitation, and ought to be an incitement to loving Christ.

9. Jerome in chapter 53 of Isaiah, Not only did Christ redeem us with His blood, but He also covered us with wool, so that He might warm those shivering from infidelity with His garment, according to that, Gal. 3. As many of you as have been baptized have put on Christ. Nazianzen also, in his oration on the holy Passover, among the reasons for which Christ is called a lamb, lists this, that we are clothed by the merits of Christ as if by the fleece of a lamb. Since Blasius de Viega approves these sayings of Nazianzen and Jerome in Apoc. p. 243, he cannot deny the imputation of the righteousness of Christ.

10. We have been chosen in Christ Eph. 1. v. 4. Therefore Christ was first preordained as the lamb, that is, that He might be a victim for our sins.

11. As salvation, so the means of salvation depend upon the ordination of God; it is therefore purely gratuitous.

12. Christ is our Savior not only by merit, but also by efficacy, for through Him we believe.

13. The glory of Christ is twofold; absolute, which had its beginning in the resurrection, its progress in the ascension, and its completion in the sitting at the right hand of GOD; and relative, in the preaching of the Gospel, for through it, it was manifested to the whole world that Christ is the Son of God, and according to His human nature is exalted at the right hand of the Father.

14. The glory given to Christ embraces not only the glorification of His body and the bestowal of finite gifts, but also His exaltation to the infinite right hand of God. For the glory of Christ as man is twofold. The former is habitual and finite, which, with the proportion of degrees preserved, He has in common with the blessed Phil. 3. v. 20. The latter is personal and infinite, which He received from the union and exaltation to the right hand of God.

15. This glory was given to Christ as man so that it might effectively work faith and hope in us, and provide life and salvation to the whole Church and to all its members.

16. Because God ἀκατάληπτος and dwells in light ἀπρόσιτον 1. Tim. 6. v. 16. therefore our faith does not reach God except through Christ; hence Christ is called the image of the invisible God Coloss. 1. v. 15. Heb. 1. vers. 3. not only by reason of essence, but also by reason of the will revealed in the word. That faith in God is therefore true, if we believe in Him through Christ who died and was raised again. John 14. v. 6. Leo, sermon on the passion, Your cross, O Christ, is the source of all blessings, it is the the cause of graces, through which is given to believers virtue from infirmity, glory from reproach, life from death.

17. Faith in the remission of sins obtained through the death of Christ, and offered to us in the Gospel, is confirmed from faith in the resurrection of Christ Rom. 4. v. 24. For just as the heavenly Father, by delivering Christ to death for our sins, condemned sin in his flesh concerning sin Rom. 8. v. 3. and thus punished our sins in Christ, which were imposed and imputed to him as Sponsor: so also by raising him from the dead, he by that very fact absolved him from our sins imputed to him, and absolved us in him, so that thus the resurrection of CHRIST may be the cause, and pledge, and complement of our justification, which consists in the remission of sins.

Latin:

Quaeritur hocloco. 1. Quid per conversationemπατροπαράδοτονab Apostolo intelligatur? Resp. 1. Qui ad gentiles hanc Epistolam scriptam statuunt, accipiunt de vita carnali, sive in operibus carnis securè & protervè exactaGal. 5. v. 19. & 20.quam ApostolusEph. 2. v. 11. & 12.graphicè sic describit. Eratis aliquando gentes in carne, illo tempore eratis sine Christo, alienati à conversatione Israël, & hospites Testamentorum promissionis, spem non habentes & sine Deo in mundo.c. 4. v. 17.gentes ambulant in vanitate sensus suiv. 18.tenebris intellectum habentes obscuratum, alienati à vita DEI per ignorantiam, quae est in illis propter caecitatem cordis eorum &c. quae expositio confirmari posset ex cap. 2.huius Epistolaev. 10. & 11.Illam vero carnalem gentilium conversationemπατροπαράδοτονvocari censent, eò quod à maioribus longâ serie fuerit observata, ac posteris tanquam bona & honesta per manus tradita, quam rationem affert Augustinus in enarr. Ps. 146. Sed gentiles in carnali illa conversatione non tàm maiorum suorum traditionem, quàm Naturae corruptae impetum & inclinationem sequebantur. 2. Qui ad Iudaeos hanc Epistolam scriptam censent, diversimodè explicant. Primò quidam accipiunt de observatione legis Mosaicae cum opinione iustitiae coram Deo valentis, & salutis ex lege sperandae coniuncta. Si quis huic expositioni obvertere velit, conversationem illam legalem non posse vocari vanam, cum observantibus legem divinitùs promissa sint praemia, responderi potest, Ceremoniarum Leviticarum & legum Forensium observationem in N. T. vocari vanam, quia iam erant abrogatae; legis autem moralis observationem vanam vocari, non absolutè & simpliciter, sed certo respectu, quatenus in ea iustitia coram DEO subsistens & vita aeterna quaeritur, quia non solùm opera iudicialia & Ceremonialia, sed etiam opera moralia ad iustificationem coram DEO sunt vana & inefficacia. Si quis obvertere velit, legem non esse ex Patrum traditione, sed ex divina promulgatione, responderi potest, Circumcisionem divinitùs fuisse institutam, ac nihilominus Ioh. 7. v. 22. dici, eam esse ἐκ τῷν πατέρων, nimirum, quia & legis divinae promulgatio, & Circumcisionis institutio per Patres sive maiores Iudaeorum ad posteros fuêre propagata. Hanc ergò expositionem in medio reliquimus: interim secundò dicimus, Apostolum vel maximè hîc respicere ad corruptelas illas doctrinae & cultus divini, quae sub nomine traditionum in Ecclesiam Iudaicam invectae erant, quas Prophetae, Christus & Apostoli saepiùs taxant. Esa. 29. v. 13.Ezech. 20. v. 18.Matth. 5. v. 21. & seqq. cap. 15. v. 6.Marc. 7. v. 9.Col. 2. v. 8. Atque hae sunt illae traditiones, quas utpote à maioribus institutas & acceptas Iudaei studiosissimè observabant & retinebant, unde Paulus Galat. 1. v. 14. se ante suam ad fidem Christi conversationem fuisse περισσοτέρως ζηλοτὴν τῷν πατρικῶν παραδόσεων Sed Petrus hoc loco pronunciat, conversationem iuxta illas institutam esse ματαίαν, perinde ut Christus Matth. 15. v. 9. & Marc. 7. v. 7. ex Es. 29. v. 13. pronunciat, μάτην σέβονταί με διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων, nimirum quia conversatio iuxta illas traditiones instituta nec DEO probatur, nec ad iustitiam quicquam facit, cum carum origo non à divino instituto, sed ab humano arbitrio descendat.

Q. 2. Quare Petrus Christum appellet agnum immaculatum & incontaminatum? Resp. respicit 1. Ad Prophetiam Esa. 53. v. 7. 2. Ad typorum V. T. figuram. Offerebatur olim agnus in purificatione puerperae Lev. 12. v. 6. in mundatione leprosi, Lev. 14. v. 10. quotidiè, manè & vesperi in iuge sacrificium agni duo offerebantur Exod. 29. v. 39. in festis solennioribus plures agni offerebantur Num. 28. v. 11. Omnes hi agni in sacrificium oblati praefigurarunt Christum, pro peccatis totius mundi in sacrificium aliquando offerendum. Cumprimis vero respicit Apostolus ad typum agni paschalis, per quem Christum fuisse praefiguratum, docet Apostolus 1. Cor. 5. v. 7. Utenim superiùs in v. 2. per vocem aspersionis deducit nos ad typum Exod. 24. v. 8. ubi sanguine vitulorum & hircorum in sacrificium priùs oblatorum populus aspergebatur, & hac aspersione in foedus DEI recipiebatur: ita hoc loco per vocem agni deducit nos ad agnum paschalem, quotannis semel peculiaribus Ceremoniis mactatum & manducatum, cuius sanguine superliminaria & postes ostiorum aspergebantur Ex. 12. v. 7. Quòd enim ad hunc typum Apostolus potissimùm respiciat, patet tùm ex verbo ἐλυτρώθητε. tùm ex epithetis ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου. Ut enim Israëlitae ante suam ex Aegyptiaca servitute liberationem sanguine agni Paschalis superliminaria & postes aedium liniebant, ut ab Angelo percussore liberarentur: sic Christi sanguine â potestate Diaboli & captivitate inferni liberati sumus. Quemadmodum agum paschalem oportebat esse sine macula & vitio Exod. 12. v. 5. ita Christus ab omni peccati labe penitùs est immunis. 1. Petr. 2. v. 22.Hebr. 7. v. 26. 3. Propter convenientiam. Ut enim agnus est mansuetus & innocens, ita Christus innocentiam in vita, & patientiam in morte demonstravit. Ut agnus velleribus suis nos vestit: Sic Christus suâ obedientiâ & passione vestem iustitiae nobis paravit. Ut omnia, quae in agno suum habent usum atque commodum: sic quicquid est in Christo, ad nostram proficit salutem.

Q. 3. Quare Christus dicaturπροεγνωσμένος πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου? Resp. 1. Quia DEUS ab aeterno praevidit, hominem in concreata integritate non perstiturum, sed in peccatum & mortem prolapsurum, ideò etiam ex ineffabili misericordia, iam inde ab aeterno prospexit humano generi de remedio in Christo Mediatore & Redemtore. 2. Quia Filius DEI in aeterno Trinitatis consilio partes Mediatoris & Redemtoris in se sponte recepit. 3. Quia quicquid in Evangelio de Christi beneficiis nobis nunciatur, illud omne, adeoque totum salutis nostrae mysterium ab aeterno fuit à DEO decretum & ordinatum.

Q. 4. Quare novissimis demum temporibus Filius DEI in carnem missus, & per Evangelii praedicationem mundo manifestatus? Resp. etsi ratio divinae voluntatis, quae est summa ratio, dari nequit, dubium tamen nullum, quin sapientissimo DEI consilio hoc factum fuerit. Donum diu desideratum postmodùm longè carius & gratius existit.

Q. 5. Quomodo per Christum dicamur credere in DEUM? Resp. 1. Quia Christus Patrem coelestem in Evangelio nobis manifestavit. Iohn. 1. v. 14. 2. Quia fides, quâ in DEUM, ut autorem salutis nostrae in Christo, & per Christum nobis partae credimus, non nisi ex Christi merito haberi potest. 3. Quia per Christum, quinimò non nisi per Christum aditus nobis patet ad DEUM. Iohan. 14. v. 6. Extra Christum DEUS est ignis consumens. Christus autem nos DEO reconciliavit, ut omnem in ipsum fiduciam collocare possimus.

Q. 6. Quomodo per modum illationis ex praecedentibus hoc inferatur, ut fides vestra & spes esset in DEUM? Resp. 1. Quidam per gloriam Christo collatam intelligunt glorificationem Christi, per praedicationem Evangelii in toto mundo factam, quae est glorificatio, ut sic loquar relativa. Illi proferunt talem connexionem. DEUS per Universalem salem Evangelii praedicationem declaravit toti mundo, Christum esse unigentum suum Eilium ac verum Deum, ut dum creditis & speratis in Christum, ist haec fides & spes vestra non sit in mero ac puro homine, sed in DEO. Haec quidem rectè dicuntur, sed nondum assequuntur id, quod Apostolus propriè intendit, quia DEUS non solùm glorificavit Christum relativè per Evangelii praedicationem, sed etiam absolutè per realem gloriae collationem. 2. Quidam hanc afferunt connexionis rationem. DEUS ideò Christum à morte suscitavit, & in gloriam provexit, ut in ipsum, velut exemplar resurrectionis & gloriae aspicientes, crederetis verbis DEI, resurrectionem ad vitam credentibus in Christum promittentis, & speraretis, vos, ut membra in Christi corpore mystico, beatae resurrectionis & gloriae participationem ab ipso consecuturos. Haec itidem rectè quidem dicuntur, sed insufficienter. Christus enim non solùm est exemplar, sed etiam meritum nostrae ad vitam resurrectionis. 3. Dicendum igitur, ex resuscitatione & collatione gloriae, Christo homini à Patre coelesti factâ, colligi, fidem & spem nostram esse in DEUM eâ ratione, quia per resuscitationem Christi, & collationem gloriae ipsi à Patre coelesti factam, certissimè confirmati sumus, pro peccatis nostris plenissimè esse satisfactum, nosque perfectissimè esse DEO reconciliati. Nisi enim Christus sponsor noster, pro peccatorum nostrorum debitis, sufficientissimum praestitisset λύτρον, Pater coelestis nequaquam ex sepulchri carcere eum eduxisset, ac gloriâ & honore eum coronâsset. Atque ex hac fide sufficientiam satisfactionis firmiter amplectente, oritur spes illa, quae gloriam Christi capitis respicit tanquam certum pignus, quod & nos, qui sumus ipsius membra, ad vitam & gloriam suo tempore simus resuscitandi. 4. Deinde etiam eò respicit Apostolus, quòd Pater coelestis Christo ex mortuis resuscitato ideò gloriam dederit, ut ad dextram Patris potentissimè regnans, fidem, & spem in DEUM efficaciter ac potenter in nobis operaretur, Ecclesiam suam adversus omnes hostes defenderet ac tueretur, & vitam ac salutem toti Ecclesiae, atque omnibus eius membris praestaret. Nisi enim Christus in sua resurrectione gloriosum ex morte, Diabolo & omnibus hostibus retulisset triumphum, & nunc ad dextram DEI sedens, omnes hostes pedibus suis subiectos haberet, nec regnum gratiae conservari, nec propagari ac dilatari possit. Sic ergò tùm ratione meriti, tùm ratione efficaciae Christo resuseitato, & ad dextram Patris exaltato tribuitur, quòd fides & spes nostra per ipsum est in DEUM, unde etiam Apostoli suam, de Christo Salvatore praecationem potissimùm ex resurrectione & gloria Christi confirmabant Act. 2. v. 33.cap. 5. v. 31.cap. 10. v. 40. &c.

ἘναντιοΦανείαι. 1. Christus dicitur agnus praecognitus ante constitutionem mundi. ContràApoc. 13. v. 8.dicitur agnus occisus ab origine mundi. Quidam resp. aliud esse πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμον esse praecognitum, aliud ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου esse occisum, illud describit meram ac nudam aeternitatem, hoc vero tempus ab origine mundi incipiens. Sed phrasis ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου itidem accipitur pro descriptione aeternitatis. Matth. 25. v. 34.Apoc. 17. v. 8. Dicitur ergò Christus agnus occisus ab origine mundi, ratione divini decreti, ut hoc loco Petrus explicat, si haec phrasis pro descriptione aeternitatis accipiatur. DEUS enim ab aeterno non solùm praevidit, Christum instar agni fore mactandum, sed etiam hoc decretum fecit, quòd per hanc Christi, tanquam innocentis agni mactationem, opus redemtionis generis humani sit peragendum, & quos praevidit in Christum agnum illum credituros, illos in librum vitae scripsit i. e. ad salutem aeternam eos elegit. Si vero haec phrasis accipiatur pro tempore ab origine mundi incipiens, tunc Christus dicitur occisusἀπό καταβολῆς κόσμου. 1. ratione promissionum. 2. ratione typorum. 3. ratione efficaciae; non autem ratione externi actus, qui in plenitudine demùm temporis fuit secutus,

2. Christus manifestatus temporibus novissimis. At qui ante annos plures quàm mille & sexcentos, Filius Dei in carne fuit missus, & per Evangelium hominibus manifestatus. Resp. solenne est Prophetis & Apostolis, totum illud tempus, quod à primo Messiae adventu, usque ad secundum eius adventum intercedit, vocare novissimum tempus, imò novissimam boram.Esa. 2. vers. 2.Mich. 4. v. 1.1. Cor. 10. v. 11.2. Tim. 3. v. 1.Hebr. 1. v. 1.Iac. 5. v. 3.2. Petr. 3. v. 3.1. Ioh. 2. v. 18.Iud. v. 18. Vocatur autem tempus novissimum. 1. Quia est tertia & ultima mundi aetas, iuxta veterem illam temporum mundi distributionem, quâ duo millia annorum tribuuntur inani duo millia legi, & novissima duo millia Messiae, unde etiam Christus dicitur apparuisse ἐν συτελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων. 2. Quia post illud tempus, usque ad finem mundi, non est alia manifestatio expectanda Hebr. 1. v. 1.3. Quia non restat aliud tempus, cui priora Prophetarum tempora subserviant. Thomas Aquin. in cap. 9. Hebr. Ultima aetas est status praesens, post quem non est alius status, sicut nec post senium alia aetas. Sicut autem in aliis aetatibus est numerus annorum determinatus, non autem in senio, ita non est determinatum, quantum iste status mundi durare debeat, tamen est consummatio seculorum, quia non restat alius status.

3. Christus manifestatus est novissimis temporibus propter vos, quòd per ipsum creditis in Deum. Atqui gaudium ex nativitate Christi pertinet ad omnem populumLuc. 2. v. 10.ac manifestatio per Evangelium pertinet ad omnes gentes.Matth. 38. v. 19. Resp. Significat Petrus, manifestationem Christi tùm in adventu, tùm in Evangelii praedicatione non prodesse omnibus, sed solùm credentibus, fide oblata in Evangelio bona amplectentibus. Ioh. 1. v. 12.

4. DEUS excitavit Christum à mortuis. At Christus propriâ virtute resurrexit & corporis sui templum excitavit.Ioh. 2. v. 19.cap. 10. v. 18. Resp. 1. Si nomen DEI accipiatur essentialiter, prout denotat tres Deitatis personas, Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum sanctum, sublata erit omnis difficultas. 2. Si vel maximè accipiatur personaliter, ut denotet tantùm primam Deitatis personam, videlicet Patrem, sicut Rom. 6. v. 4. Christus dicitur surrexisse à mortuis per gloriam Patris, dicendum, nomine Patris non excludi vel Filium, vel Spiritum sanctum, quia virtus illa, quâ Pater Christum excitavit, est omnibus tribus Deitatis personis communis. Quòd autem Patri peculiariter tribuitur Christi ex mortuis resuscitatio, illud fit propterea 1. Quia Pater est fons Divinitatis, quam ab aeterno communicavie Filio per generationem, & Spiritui sancto per spirationem. Quia ergò Christus resurrexit virtute Patris, per aeternam generationem sibi à Patre secundùm Deitatem communicata, inde resuscitatio Patri utplurimùm tribuitur. 2. Ut ipsa missio Filii & officii eius confirmatio, divinâ voce caelitus facta, & miracula in diebus carnis à Christo facta, DEO Patri assignari solent, ac tota obedientia Christi DEO Patri dicitur praestita Phil. 2. v. 8. ita quoque Patri resuscitatio Christi ex mortuis tribuitur. 3. Sicut Filius à Patre dieitur in mortem traditus Ioh. 3. v. 16.Rom. 8. v. 32. ita quoque ex mortuis eum dicitur suscitasse, ut tamen à traditione illa non excludatur Filius, qui voluntariè mortem subiit Galat. 2. v. 20. ita quoque ab illa refuscitatione Filius non est exclusus. 4. Admonemur hac loquendi forma de sufficientia meriti & satisfactionis per Christum DEO patri praestitae. Quia enim Pater caelestis Christum, qui in se omnium nostrorum peccatorum debita receperat, seque pro illis satisfacturum promiserat, tam gloriosè ex sepulchri carcere reducit, ex eo manifestum fit, Patri coelesti plenissimè pro debitis illis satisfactum. Confer. Gregor. Nyssen. orat. 2. de resurrect. Christi.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Redemti sumus οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀλλὰ ἃιματι Χριστοῦ. Falsum est ergo, quod Curaeus & alii quidam Calviniani statuunt, Sanguinem Christi in ara crucis effusum computruisse, ac proinde non posse nobis in sacra Coena mediante benedicto potu bibendum dari.

2. Soli Christo tribuitur redemtionis opus, & hoc loco & passim alibi in Scripturis. Ergo falsum est, quod Papa docet, Mariam fuisse Christi in hoc opere redemtionis adiutricem. Mariale Argentinense Anno 1493. editum lib. 1. cap. 5. f. 13. Fuit Dominus cum Maria, & ipsa cum Domino in eodem labore, & in eodem opere redemtionis. Mater misericordiae adiuvit patrem misericordiarum in opere nostrae salutis, unde praedictum est de prima muliere, faciamus ei adiutorium. Quid est ergo quod Dominus dicit, Torcular calcavi solus, & de gentibus non fuit vir mecum? Verum est Domine, quòd non fuit vir tecum, sed mulier unà tecum est. Vincentius Brunius in Meditat. festor. B. Virginis Ann. 1599. Colon. edit. p. 11. Cùm DEUS decrevit Filio suo unigenito pro redimendo genere humano, assumendam esse carnem, simul etiam decrevit & praedestinavit, quae deberet esse eius mater, & redemtionis nostrae cooperatrix. Osorius tom. 4. concion. p. 530. Christus in calvaria carnem, Maria immolabai animam. Alphonsus Salmeron Tom. 10. tract. 41. p. 339. Maria stetit sub cruce, ut esset corredemtrix, quemadmodum Eva unà cum Adamo malum invexit.

3. Solus Christus est noster Redemtor. Falsum est ergo, quod Papa docet, hominem sui ipsius redemtorem rectè appellari posse. Bellarm. lib. 1. de purgat. cap. 14. Sanctos appellari posse redemtores, eò quòd debitum parvi momenti persolvant, si cum eo debito conferatur, pro quo Christus satisfecit. Schiopp. in Apol. de Indulg. cap. 47.

4. Sanguine Christi sumus redemti. Falsum ergo est, quod Photiniani negant, Christum pro peccatis nostris satisfactionem praestitisse. Redemtionis vocem dicunt esse metaphoricam, & in hac quaestione nihil aliud significare, quàm simplicem liberationem, quaea absque interveniente satisfactionis precio sit facta. Atqui ubi dantur omnia verè & propriè dictae redemtionis requisita, ibi verè & propriè dicta redemtio datur. In spirituali nostra redemtione datur 1. Obiectum redemtionis h. e. captivi, qui sunt omnes homines Zach. 9. v. 11.Gal. 3. v. 10. 2. Causa principalis, qui est Christus redemtor noster, propitiatorium nostrum Rom. 3. v. 24. & propitiatio pro totius mundi peccatis 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. 3. Causa instrumentalis, sive medium redemtionis est sanguis Christi, qui dicitur sanguis Testamenti Zach. 9. v. 11.Eph. 1. v. 7.Col. 1. v. 14. & hoc loco 4. Terminus à quo, redimimur est captivitas, sub qua intelliguntur ipse iudex, seu Dominus carceris, custos carceris, carcer ipse, eiusque adiuncta. Iudex est ipse DEUS iratus, sive ira & iudicium DEI Rom. 5. vers. 9.Gal. 3. v. 13. Custos carceris est Diabolus, à quo Christus nos redemit. Os. 13. v. 14. Carcer est infernus, seu lacus, in quo non est aqua Zach. 9. v. 11.Os 13. v. 14. Adiuncta carceris sunt laquei peccatorum nostrorum, quos Christus contrivit Luc. 1. vers. 74.Hebr. 2. v. 14.5. Terminus ad quem, est DEUS placatus, cui nos redemit Christus & libertas, in quam nos asseruit Luc. 1. v. 74.

5. Petrus docet, nos precioso Christi sanguine liberatos esse à conversationeπατροπαραδότω. Papa docet, traditiones fidei & morum, pari pietatis affectu, cum scripto Dei verbo acceptandas esse. Pharisaei & Pseudo Apostoli urgebant maiorum traditiones, Christus & Petrus eas repudiabant. Illorum ergo vestigiis Papa insistit, non itaque Christi vicarius, nec Petri verus est successor.

6. Petrus describit creationem hac phrasi πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, quod congruit etiam aliis Scripturae dictis. Psalm. 91. vers. 3.Prov. 8. vers 24. Falsum est ergò, quod Photiniani, & cum eis Vorstius negat, esse firmum Deitatis Christi argumentum, quòd ante mundum conditum dicitur extitisse.

7. Petrus dicit, Christum manifestatum esse propter eos, qui per ipsum credunt in Deum. Falsum est ergò, quòd quidam Pontificii & Calviniani & Photiniani docent, saniores gentiles, qui Christum nec noverunt, nec in eum crediderunt, salutis aeternae factos fuisse participes.

8. Petrus docet, Christo in tempore gloriam datam, videlicet in resurrectione & ascensione. Ergo secundùm humanam Naturam haec gloria illi collata, quod opponendum Calvinianis, in persona Mediatoris subsistendum esse, nugantibus.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Ex eo, quòd Christi sanguine redemti dicimur, colligit Piscator, solam passivam Christi obedientiam esse meritoriam nostrae iustificationis causam. Cui ex parte suffragatur Sibrandus Lubertus, quando in catal. error. Vorstii p. 357. scribit, activam quidem obedientiam Christi, non esse separandam à passiva, interim totam Christi humiliationem non esseλύτρουillius solutionem, sed solam mortem esse redemtionis nostrae precium. Resp. quando Petrus hoc loco, & Scriptura alibi passim, morti & effusioni sanguinis Christi redemtionis opus tribuit, illud non est accipiendum exclusivè, contrarium enim testantur dicta, quae disertam activae obedientiae mentionem faciunt, Matth. 5. v. 17.Rom. 5. v. 18.cap. 10. v. 4.Gal. 3. v. 4.Hebr. 10. v. 10. &c. sed inclusivè, cum arctissimo & indissolubili vinculo activa & passiva obedientia Christi sint coniuncta, siquidem passio Christi est activa, & actio Christi est passiva. In passione Christi relucent praeclarissimae virtutes, in lege requisitae, summus amor DEI, & ardentissima erga genus humanum dilectio, humilitas, patientia, obedientia, fiducia, invocatio, spes &c. ac passio Christi non in horto demum coepit, sed à primo incarnationis momento, ac per totum vitae decursum duravit. Ideò autem toties mortis & fusi sanguinis fit mentio, quia in morte & effusione sanguinis, maximè eluxit & effulsit perfectissima Christi erga Deum Patrem obedientia, & ardentissima erga genus humanum dilectio. Nuspiam illuxit clariùs, quòd nos dilexerit Dominus, quàm in ipsius passione & vulneribus. Praetera mors est ultima linea, complementum & consummatio obedientiae, quam CHRISTUS Patri suo in cruce praestitit. Iohan. 19. v. 30.Phil. 2. v. 8.

2. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, nos redemtos esse precioso sanguine, quasi agni immaculati & incontaminati Christi, colligunt Pontificii, Christum esse nostrum Mediatorem, non ut Deum & hominem, sed ut hominem iustum. Resp. 1. Scriptura docet, obedientiam ac satisfactionem Christi inde atque ideò esse meritoriam, tùm quia est innocentissimae, sanctissimae ac purissimae personae obedientia Hebr. 7. v. 26. tùm vel maximè, quia est ipsius Filii DEI obedientia, quippe infinita illa dignitas ac maiestas personae conciliat infinitam vim, dignitatem & efficaciam eiusdem merito. Ioh. 6. v. 51.Actor. 20. v. 29.Galat. 4. v. 4.1. Iohan. 1. v. 7. &c. 2. Illud tàm certum atque evidens est, ut Bellarminus, quamvis magno conatu disputet lib. 5. de Christo cap. 2. Christum tantùm secundùm humanam Naturam esse nostrum Mediatorem, veritatis tamen fulgore convictus, scribat lib. 2. de Iustif. cap. 5. DEUS non acceptat in veram satisfactionem pro peccato nisi iustitiam infinitam, quoniam peccatum peccatum offensa est infinita, sed ut aliqua iustitia sit infinita, id est, infiniti precii & valoris, non est necesse, ut sit iustitia DEI essentialis, sed satis est, ut sit iustitia personae infinitae, qualis est CHRISTUS DEUS & homo. Itaque obedientia, passio & mors Filii DEI, quamvis in se, & essentialiter fuerit creata & finita, tamen ratione personae obedientis, patientis, & morientis infinita fuit, & ex vero iustitiae rigore propitiatio fuit pro totius mundi peccatis. At si in opere nostrae redemtionis, nostraeque cum DEO reconciliationis, requiritur infiniti valoris & precii iustitia, utique etiam Christus secundùm divinam Naturam est noster Mediator & Redemtor. Ratio est, quia infinitus ille valor, & infinitum illud redemtionis nostrae precium, non potest ab humana Natura sola descendere. Quòd si ergò in opere nostrae redemtionis, nostraeque cum DEO reconciliationis, aliquid requiritur & concurrit, quod non ab humanitate Christi formaliter, h. e. à virtute humanitatis perse, & ex se, sed ab infinita τοῦ λὸγου Deitate in ἀποτελέσματα Christi Redemtoris q. influit, utique non secundùm humanam tantùm, sed etiam secundùm divinam Naturam, Christus est Redemtor & Mediator. Si vero in opere redemtionis sola humana Natura, seclusâ divinae Naturae activitate agit, utique obedientia Christi non erit infiniti precii, nec satisfactio pro totius mundi peccatis, nec imputari nobis poterit ad iustitiam. 3. Quòd si ergò vel maximè Petrus hoc loco non faceret mentionem divinae Christi Naturae, non tamen propterea eam excluderet ab opere redemtionis, cum in aliis Scripturae dictis, de opere redemtionis agentibus, diserta eius fiat mentio. 4. Quid quod vocabulum Christi est concretum personae, utramque Naturam exprimens. Athanas. orat. 5. contra Arian. p. 321. Χριστὸς τὸ συναμφότερον νοεῖται. August. in Psal. 44.Nomen Christi ungentem Deitatem, & unctam humanitatem complectitur. Damasc. lib. 3. cap. 4. Χριστὸς ἐστι τὸ συναμφότερον.

3. Schmaltzius in Examinat. 157. errorum err. 69. p. 21. Sanguis Christi dicitur preciosus, non quòd aliquem valorem precii habeat, sed quòd sit sanguis aeterni foederis. Opponitur enim preciosum corruptibili, unde constat, preciosum esse idem, quod incorruptibile. Incorruptibilis autem Christi sanguis dici non potest per se: Christus enim, quia Spiritus est, nullum habet sanguinem, sed respectivè, quia sc. rei aeternae sit sanguis, quatenus per eum novum foedus confirmatum est. Resp. 1. Christi sanguis dicitur τίμιος, non solùm in oppositione φθαρτοῦ, sed etiam absolutè & simpliciter, quia est redemtionis nostrae τιμή, sive precium. 1. Cor. 6. v. 20. & cap. 7. v. 23.ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς.Actor. 20. vers. 29.

DEUS suo sanguine redemit Ecclesiam. Ex horum locorum collatione evidentissimè elucescit, sanguinem Christi esse redemtionis nostrae precium. 2. esse precium, & esse incorruptibile, non sunt opposita, sed subordinata. Utrumque Christi sanguini competit, eumque τίμιον reddit. 3. Quia Christi sanguis est aeterni foederis sanguis, ideò etiam redemtionis nostrae precium. Neque enim foedus aeternum, inter DEUM, & genus humanum, in peccata prolapsum, erigi potuisset, nisi DEUS per Christi sanguinem generi humano reconciliatus fuisset, inde Zach. 9. v. 11. utrumque coniungitur. In sanguine Testamenti tui emittis vinctos. 4. Incorruptibilis est Christi sanguis, quia est ipsius Filii DEI sanguis Actor. 20. v. 29.1. Ioh, 1. v. 7. Quamvis ergò per se, i. e. ex Naturae suae proprietate, & ex essentialibus principiis non sit incorruptilis, tamen ex unione personali est incorruptibilis. 5. Falsum est, Christum non habere sanguinem, cum sit Spiritus, i. e. cum ipsius humana Natura mutata sit in Spiritum. Spiritualis est Christi Natura humana, non autem in Spiritum mutata. Luc. 24. v. 39. 6. Sanguinem Christi dici incorruptibilem, quia est rei aeternae sanguis, quatenus per eum novum foe dus est confirmatum, rectè quidem dicitur, sed insufficienter, est enim etiam ideò incorruptibilis, quia, ut proprius Filii DEI sanguis non vidit, nec visurus est corruptionem. Psalm. 16. v. 10.Actor. 2. v. 27.cap. 13. v. 36.

4. Ex eo, quod Christus dicitur, προεγνωσμένος praeordinatus & destinatus ad officium Mediatoris, colligit Chamierus tom. 3. Panstrat. l. 9. c. 3. §. 5. Christum nihil potuisse à DEO mereri merito absoluto. Cum enim nihil pro nobis meruerit, nisi Mediator, & Mediator sit ex certo praedestinationis decreto, omninò necesse est, nihil eum meruisse, nisi ex aeterno praedestinationis decreto. Sed haec omnia procedunt ex falsa illa hypothesi, quòd DEUS absoluto decreto quosdam ad salutem elegerit, ac postea Christum Mediatorem illis destinaverit, cum contrà potiùs, πρόγνωσις meriti Christi, & fidei in Christum substernenda sit electionis decreto.

5. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, Christum manifestatum esse propter credentes, colligunt Calviniani, Christum pro solis electis esse mortuum, & beneficia Christi, animo communicandi, solis electis in Evangelio offerri. Resp. 1. Apostolus hîc non loquitur de traditione Christi in mortem, sed de manifestatione Christi, i. e. tùm de Filii DEI in carne manifestatione, tùm vero cumprimis de manifestatione per Evangelium. 2. Ideò vero Christum propter credentes dicit esse manifestatum, ut significet, beneficia Christi, quae in Evangelio omnibus offeruntur, solis credentibus applicari, ac nemini prodesse, nisi per fidem recipiantur. 3. Scribit praecipuè ad conversos ex Iudaeis, quibus peculiares promissiones de adventu Messiae erant factae, & propter quos Christus principaliter venerat, Matth. 15. v. 24.Rom. 15. v. 8. quibus proinde primùm Evangelium oportebat praedicari, Act. 13. v. 46. 4. Significat, quemlibet credentem tantâ fiduciâ Christi beneficia amplecti, atque ita affectum esse debere erga redemtionis beneficium, ut, quamvis illud omnibus sit commune, sibi tamen propriè praestitum esse agnoscat, sicut Paulus ex vera & firma fiducia dicit Gal. 2. v. 20.Christus dilexit me, & tradidit seipsum pro me.

6. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, Christum novissimis temporibus per Evangelium esse manifestatum, colligunt Photiniani, patribus V. Test. non fuisse in Christo promissam vitam aeternam. Resp. 1. Evangelium sumitur vel pro laeto nuncio, de Christo iam exhibito, vel pro concione gratiae, de gratuita peccatorum remissione propter Christum, sive adhuc expectandum, sive iam exhibitum. Evangelium in priore significatione acceptum est N. T. proprium; in posteriore vero significatione utrique Testamento commune, Act. 15. v. 11.Rom. 4. v. 1. & seqq. 2. Quamvis beneficium redemtionis nondum praestitae etiam in V. T. locum habuerit, tamen post peractum opus copiosior redemtionis fructus ad homines provenit.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Beneficium preciosae redemtionis est efficacissimum ὁρμητήριον sanctae conversationis. Eccur enim peccato adhuc velimus servire, à cuius servitute Christus tàm caro precio nos redemit? Tanto insuper benefactori non verbis tantùm, sed ipso facto gratias agere convenit.

2. Christi redemtio est nostra coram DEO dignatio & exaltatio. Hugo in libr. de arrh. Sponsae. Ampliùs mihi vilis esse non debeo, quia tantum DEO placui, ut mori pro me eligeret, ne me perderet.

3. Preciositas sanguinis Christi non tantùm ab ipsius innocentia, sed etiam ab infinita personae dignitate dependet.

4. Christus est prorsus incontaminatus & immaculatus, tùm quia de Spiritu sancto conceptus, & ex virgine natus, non contraxit peccati originalis maculam, tùm quia non fuit ullo peccato actuali, etiam minimo unquam contaminatus. Gloss. interlin. Christus ab originali & actuali peccato incontaminatus est.Es. 53. v. 9.2. Cor. 5. v. 21.Hebr. 7. v. 26.1. Petr. 2. v. 22.

5. Hugo in enarrat. cap. 53. Esai. quindecim proprietates adducit, quarum respectu σύγκρισιν inter Christum & agnum instituit. Inter eas vero eminent innocentia & patientia. In sensu relativo, agni appellatio Christo tribuitur propter praedictionem Propheticam duplicem, videlicet tùm γραφικὴνEsai. 53. v. 7.Ierem. 11. v. 19. tùm τυπικὴν in sacrificiis.

6. Cum primis vero agnus paschalis fuit illustris Christi typus. 1. Respectu qualitatis. Agnus paschalis esse debuit immaculatus & perfectus: ita quoque Christus ab omni peccati labe immunis, unde hâc vocatur ἂμωμος καὶ ἂσπιλος. Agnum paschalem oportuit esse masculum. Christus est vir ille, quem foemina circumdedit, Ierem. 31. v. 22. Agnum oportuit esse anniculum, in perfecto aetatis statu: sic Christus in ipso aetatis flore immolatus. 2. Respectu actuum Sacramentalium, qui sunt 1. Segregatio. Agnus paschalis ex communi grege petendus: sic Christus ex genere humano veram carnem assumsit. Deut. 18. v. 18. Agnus paschalis segregabatur die 10. mensis primi. Christus eadem die Hierosolymam solenniter & peculiari modo per eandem portam, per quam oves & agni ad sacrificia duci solebant, ingressus est. 2. Mactatio. 3. Assatio. 4. Manducatio. 5. Sanguinis in postes & superliminaria aedium illitio. Singulorum membrorum applicationem ostendimus in loc. de Circumc. & agno paschali §. 46. & seqq.

7. Christus à Patre caelesti iam inde ab aeterno fuit ordinatus, ut esset agnus pro peccatis mundi immolandus, eius immolatio in protevangelio fuit promissa, & in sacrificiis adumbrata, idem etiam in plenitudine temporis fuit missus, ut in ara crucis immolaretur. Hos actus omnes Petrus hoc loco exprimit, & propter hos actus omnes ac singulos dicitur agnus DEI. Ioh. 1. v. 29.

8. Christi innocentia, mansuetudo & patientia in similitudine agni nobis proposita, non solùm pertinet ad redemtionis nostrae meritum, sed etiam exhibet nobis imitationis exemplum, & ad Christum amandum debet esse incitamentum.

9. Hieronymus in cap. 53. Esai. Non solùm sanguine suo Christus nos redemit, sed etiam lanis operuit, ut infidelitate algentes suâ veste calefaceret, iuxta illud,Gal. 3.Quotquot baptizati estis, Christum induistis. Nazianzenus etiam orat. in sanct. pascha, inter causas, propter quas Christus dicatur agnus, recenset eam, quòd Christi meritis, tanquam agni vellere induamur. Haec Nazianzeni & Hieronymi dicta cum approbet Blasius de Viega in Apoc. p. 243. non potest imputationem iustitiae Christi negare.

10. Electi sumus in ChristoEph. 1. v. 4. Ergò Christus priùs praeordinatus est agnus i. e. ut esset victima pro peccatis nostris.

11. Ut salus, ita media salutis pendent à Dei ordinatione, est ergò merè gratuita.

12. Christus est Salvator noster non solùm meritô, sed etiam efficaciâ, per ipsum enim credimus.

13. Gloria Christi duplex est; absoluta, quae initium habuit in resurrectione, progressum in ascensione, complementum in sessione ad DEI dextram; ac relativa, in Evangelii praedicatione, per illud enim toti mundo manifestatum, Christum esse Dei Filium, ae secundùm humanam Naturam ad dextram Patris esse exaltatum.

14. Gloria Christo data, non tantùm corporis glorificationem, ac finitorum donorum collationem, sed etiam ad infinitam Dei dextram exaltationem complectitur. Duplex enim est Christi hominis gloria. Prior habitualis & finita, quam servatâ graduum proportione, cum beatis communem habet Phil. 3. v. 20. Posterior personalis & infinita, quam ex unione & exaltatione ad Dei dextram accepit.

15. Haec gloria Christo homini ideò data, ut fidem & spem in nobis efficaciter operatretur, ac vitam & salutem toti Ecclesiae, & omnibus eius membris praestaret.

16. Quia Deus ἀκατάληπτοςac lucem inhabit atἀπρόσιτον1. Tim. 6. v. 16. ideò non nisi per Christum fides nostra ad Deum pervenit, inde Christus dicitur imago Dei invisibilisColoss. 1. v. 15.Heb. 1. vers. 3. non solùm ratione essentiae, sed etiam ratione voluntatis in verbo patefactae. Illa ergò fides in Deum vera, si per Christum mortuum & resuscitatum in ipsum credamus. Ioh. 14. v. 6. Leo serm. de pass. Crux tua, ô Christe omnium fons benedictionum, omnium est causa gratiarum, per quam credentibus datur virtus de infirmitate, gloria de opprobrio, vita de morte.

17. Fides remissionis peccatorum per Christi mortem partae, & in Evangelio nobis oblatae, confirmatur ex fide resurrectionis Christi Rom. 4. v. 24. Ut enim Pater coelestis Christum propter peccata nostra in mortem tradendo, in carne ipsius de peccato damnavit peccatum Rom. 8. v. 3. sicque punivit peccata nostra in Christo, quae ipsi ut Sponsori erant imposita, atque imputata: ita quoque excitando eum à mortuis, ipso facto eum absolvit, à peccatis nostris ipsi imputatis, ac nos in eo absolvit, ut sic CHRISTI resurrectio sit nostrae iustificationis, quae in remissione peccatorum consistit, causa, & pignus, & complementum.

## 1:21
WHO BY HIM DO BELIEVE IN GOD, THAT RAISED HIM UP FROM THE DEAD, AND GAVE HIM GLORY; THAT YOUR FAITH AND HOPE MIGHT BE IN GOD.

Some here establish a new argument of exhortation, taken from the gift of faith and hope, namely, that through Christ they are persuaded of the grace of GOD obtained for them by His death, and consequently hope for eternal life. That grace of GOD is indeed signified by two effects, both that He raised Christ from the dead, and that He gave Him glory through exaltation to His right hand in the heavens. But from the illative particle ὥστε it is gathered that this is an epilogue of the preceding argument. Because Christ, constituted Redeemer before the foundations of the world were laid, was manifested in the last times for the sake of you who believe in GOD through Him, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, therefore your faith also ought to be in GOD, to be supplied for this sentence through the particle δεῖ or χρὴ, your faith and hope ought to be in God

Because of this πίστευοντας. In some copies the past tense πιστεύσαντες, is read, in certain others πιστούς, to which the Vulgate version undoubtedly looked when it rendered: who through him are faithful But the more approved Codices read, πιστέυοντας, who through him believe. εἰς θεὸν τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα. Some wish the latter member to be ἐξηγητικὸν of the former, because in the resurrection GOD gave to CHRIST the man the glory of soul and body. But it is more correctly said that the bestowing of glory is proposed as something distinct from the resuscitation, so that the sense may be: The heavenly Father not only raised Christ from the dead, but also placed him at his right hand, which is the glorification and ὑπερύψωσις that, of which Paul Eph. 1. v. 20. 21. & 22.Phil. 2. v. 9. speak. But especially evident is the former passage to the Ephesians, clearly parallel to this one of ours. We believe according to the operation of the power of his might, which he wrought in Christ, raising him from the dead and setting him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all principality and power and might and dominion and every name that is named, not only in this world but also in that which is to come, and he put all things under his feet. ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ύμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς θεόν. The Vulgate rendered, that your faith and hope might be in GOD, But the Greek Codices constantly read εἰς θεὸν, in which way also the Syriac rendered, [consult facsimile image] and certain Latin Codices have in GOD.

Latin:

QUI PER IPSUM FIDELES ESTIS IN DEO, QUI SUSCITAVIT CUM A MORTUIS & DEDIT EI GLORIAM, UT FIDES VESTRA & SPES ESSET IN DEUM.

Quidam hîc constituunt novum exhortationis argumentum, desumtum â dono fidei & spei, quod sc. per Christum persuasi sint de gratia DEI sibi per mortem eius parta, ac proinde sperent vitam aeternam. Illam vero DEI gratiam significari ex duobus effectis, tùm quod Christum excitaverit à mortuis, tùm quod gloriam ei dederit per exaltationem ad suam dextram in coelestibus. Sed ex vocula illativa ὥστε colligitur, hunc esse epilogum praecedentis argumenti. Quia Christus ante iacta mundi fundamenta constitutus Redemtor, novissimis temporibus manifestatus est propter vos credentes per ipsum in DEUM, qui à mortuis eum excitavit, & gloriam ei dedit, ideo & fides vestra debet esse in DEUM, supplenda enim haec sententia per particulam δεῖ vel χρὴ, fidem & spem vestram oportet esse in Deum

Propter Dosπίστευοντας. In nonnullis exemplaribus legitur praeteritum πιστεύσαντες, in quibusdam πιστούς, quo procul dubio respexit vulgata versio, quando reddidit: qui per ipsum fideles estis Sed probatiores Codices legunt, πιστέυοντας,qui per ipsum creditis.εἰς θεὸν τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα. Quidam volunt, posterius membrum esseἐξηγητικὸνprioris, quia in resurrectione dedit DEUS CHRISTO homini gloriam animae & corporis. Sed rectiùs dicitur, collationem gloriae proponi ut distinctum quid à resuscitatione, ut sit sensus: Pater coelestis non solùm excitavit Christum à mortuis, sed etiam collocavit eum ad suam dextram, quae est glorificatio & ὑπερύψωσις illa, de qua Paulus Eph. 1. v. 20. 21. & 22.Phil. 2. v. 9. loquuntur. Cumprimis vero evidens est locus prior ad Ephesios huic nostro planè parallelus. Credimus nos secundùm operationem potentiae virtutis eius, quam operatus est in Christo, suscitans illum à mortuis & constituens ad dextram suam in coelestibus, supra omnem principatum & potestatem & virtutem & dominationem & omne quod nominatur non solùm in hoc seculo sed etiam in futuro, & omnia subiecit sub pedibus eius. ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ύμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς θεόν. Vulgata reddidit, ut fides vestra & spes esset in DEO, Sed Graeci Codices constanter legunt εἰς θεὸν, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit, [consult facsimile image] & quidam Latini Codices habent in DEUM.

## 1:22
PURIFYING YOUR SOULS IN OBEDIENCE OF CHARITY, IN LOVE OF THE BROTHERHOOD, LOVE ONE ANOTHER FROM A SIMPLE HEART MORE ATTENTIVELY.

Connection. The Apostle returns to the exhortation, begun in v. 13. and continued in v. 15. and 17., that having girded up the loins of their mind they ought to hope perfectly in the grace which is offered to them, that they ought to pursue holiness in their conversation, and conduct themselves in the true fear of God during the time of their sojourn, and thus v. 18. 19. 20. & 21. are to be taken as if enclosed in a parenthesis, in which a certain digression for the sake of exaggerating the benefit of redemption is contained. This connection is gathered from the participle ἡγνικότες, which shows that this little verse is connected with the preceding ones, conduct yourselves in fear purifying your souls. For just as in the preceding ones the Apostle had exhorted those to whom he writes both to constancy of faith and to innocence of life, so also he inculcates both members of the exhortation again in this place, calling constancy in faith the obedience of truth, but embracing innocence of life with charity, as the sum of all other virtues συνεκδοχικῶς. Some establish here the beginning of a new pericope, so that the participle ἡγνικότες is governed by the verb ἀγαπήσατε, and thus they are commanded to show charity from purified souls, that is, from a heart purified by faith, and sincere toward their neighbor. But because he exhorts not only to charity, but also to the obedience of truth, therefore this member is more rightly connected with the preceding ones and

The repetition of the principal proposition is established. For chastising some Latin codices read more correctly making chaste, for in the Greek it is ἡγνικότες.. But not even that version attains the emphasis of the Greek text, because the Greek ἡγνικότες is of the past tense, who have purified, or when you shall have purified your souls, or your souls having been purified, or even by purifying your souls, so that the participle may be resolved into a gerund. For the Apostle does not declare them to be such that they have already purified their souls, but he exhorts them that they should purify their souls. The Syrian rendered it by [consult facsimile image] he sanctified. Now, by purification of souls, is understood: 1. True faith in Christ, by which hearts are purified Acts 15. v. 9., whence the Apostle immediately adds ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ἀληθείας in obedience, or through the obedience of the truth, i.e., through faith, by which you have obeyed the Evangelical truth, and have embraced it. The Vulgate indeed reads in the obedience of charity, but the Greek codices constantly read ἀληθείας, and the Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] which corresponds to the Hebrew אמת, just as Jerome also reads in book 1 against Jovinian, citing this passage with these words: In the obedience of the truth. The sense therefore is, when through faith by which you obey and acquiesce to the truth, you shall have purified your souls. 2. The mortification of depraved concupiscences and carnal inclinations toward hatreds, revenge, lusts, intemperance, etc. For from the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies, Matt. 15. v. 19. Mark 7. v. 21. & 22. all these things are to be mortified by the Spirit, as the Apostle expressly adds, with which the Apostolic passage Rom. 8. v. 13. agrees: If by the Spirit you shall have mortified the deeds of the flesh, you shall live. Gal. 5. v. 16. Walk in the Spirit and you shall not fulfill the desires of the flesh. Truly that προσδιορισμὸς διὰ πνέυματος is not held in the Syriac version, nor in the Latin, nor in Jerome, meanwhile since it is read in all Greek codices, and fits the context most aptly, it is deservedly considered a genuine part. 3. The flight of hypocrisy. Hypocrisy is the hidden poison of the heart, therefore when the Apostle commands to purify souls, he simultaneously requires the flight of hypocrisy, whence he immediately adds εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον indeed if brotherly charity ought to be devoid of simulation, it is necessary that souls be [purified] from to be purified first from the poison of hypocrisy. Thus, therefore, from the exhortation to the constancy of faith, which he had described metaphorically through the chastity of the soul abhorring every false doctrine, and had explained its efficient cause, namely the Holy Spirit, the Apostle passes to the exhortation of charity, which he expresses by the name φιλαδελφίας,, by which word also in other sayings of Scripture, the mutual love of Christians is described, since all are through faith sons of GOD, and consequently brothers to one another. Roman. 12. v. 10.1. Thessal. 4. v. 9.Hebr. 13. v. 1.1. Petr. 3. v. 8.2. Petr. 1. v. 7. The little word εἰς φιλαδελφίαν is governed by the verb ἀγαπήσατε.. Because, therefore, the Apostle does not say ἀγαπήσατε ἐν φιλαδελφίᾳ, but εἰς φιλαδελφίαν,, thence some think that the term to which of charity is described. Love one another into brotherly charity, that is, into one body of brotherly charity. But Oecumenius rightly warns, εἰς, as elsewhere everywhere, so also here it is placed for διὰ, love one another through brotherly charity. But if we wish to retain altogether the proper signification of the particle εἰς, it could be taken ὲκηβατικῶς, love one another into brotherly charity, that is, so that it may become manifest to all that you are brothers to one another and sons of GOD. Furthermore, the charity which the Apostle prescribes, he wishes to be: 1. ἀνυπόκριτον devoid of simulation, the Syrian rendered, which does not accept a face, that is, which does not assume a mask only externally, and transforms itself so that it may appear other than it truly is. What indeed is charity ἀνυπόκριτος, he explains John 1. Epist. 3. v. 18. Let us not love in word nor in tongue, but in work and in truth. 2. καθαρὰν pure and clean; Love, he says, one another from a pure heart, that is, from a heart purified through faith, as is understood from the preceding. A parallel passage exists 1. Timoth. 1. v. 4. The end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned. Some wish charity from a pure heart to be opposed to impure and carnal love, and thus to all that love by which the neighbor is not loved in GOD, under GOD, and for the sake of GOD. But the former explanation agrees more with the text. 3. ὲκτενῆ. Love, he says, one another ἐκτενῶς. Acts 12. v. 5. προσευχή ἐκτενὴς, are constant prayers, and without intermission. Also intense, so that it may be referred to the ardor of souls. Hesychius ἐκτενεῖ explains ἐπιμελεῖ accurate, diligent, attentive. To Suidas ἐκτενὲστερος is ἐνεργηκώτερος, ἐπιμελέστερος. Therefore ἐκτενῶς is intensely and intently Luke 22. vers. 44. Also constantly, continuously not interruptedly,Joel 1. v. 14.Judith 4. v. 10. in which sense also ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ is used, Judith 4. v. 7.Acts 26. v. 7. Hesychius explains not only διατεταμένως, ἐκτεταμένως, but also προθύμως promptly, Suidas, ὀλοψύχως. The LXX use for בחזקה in strength,Jonah 3. v. 8. When therefore Peter requires that we love ἐκτενῶς, he does not only demand an extensive increase of charity, so that we may never cease to love one another, but also an intensive one, so that we may love intensely, ardently, with all our strength. A parallel passage exists in chap. 4. of this Epistle v. 8. τὴν εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἀγάπην ἐκτενῆ ἔχοντες.

Latin:

ANIMAS VESTRAS CASTIGANTES IN OBEDIENTIA CARITATIS, IN FRATERNITATIS AMORE, SIMPLICI EX CORDE INVICEM DILIGITE ATTENTIUS.

Connexio. Redit Apostolus ad exhortationem, in v. 13. caeptam & in v. 15. & 17. continuatam, quòd succincti lumbos mentis suae perfectè sperare debeant in eam, quae ipsis offertur, gratiam, in conversatione sanctitatem sactari, & in vero Dei timore, tempore incolatus sui conversari debeant, sicque v. 18. 19. 20. & 21. velut parenthesi inclusi accipiantur, in qua digressio quaedam ad exaggerandum redemtionis beneficium contineatur. Colligitur haec connexio ex participio ἡγνικότες, quod ostendit, hunc versiculum connecti cum superioribus, conversamini in timore animas vestras castigantes.
