Ut enim in superioribus tùm ad fidei constantiam, tùm ad vitae innocentiam eos, ad quos scribit, Apostolus fuerat exhoratus, ita quoque utrumque exhortationis membrum hoc loco denuò inculcat, constantiam in fide vocans oboedientiam veritatis, vitae vero innocentiam, caritate, tanquam reliquarum virtutum omnium summâ συνεκδοχικῶς complectens. Quidam hîc constituunt novae pericopes initium, ita ut participium ἡγνικότες regatur à verbo ἀγαπήσατε, sicque caritatem ex purificatis animis, hoc est, ex corde fide purificato, & sincero proximo exhibere iubeantur. Sed quia non solùm ad caritatem, verùm etiam ad obaedientiam veritatis exhortatur, ideò rectiùs hoc membrum cum superioribus connectitur &

principalis propositionis repetitio statuitur. Pro castigantes quidam Latini Codices rectiùs legunt castificantes, in Graeco enim est ἡγνικότες. Sed nec dum illa versio emphasin Graeci textus assequitur, quia Graecum ἡγνικότες est praeteriti temporis, qui purificastis, vel cùm purificaveritis animas vestras, vel purificatis animabus vestris, vel etiam purificando animas vestras, ut participium resolvatur in gerundium. Neque enim praedicat eos Apostolus, quod animas fuas iamdum purificaverint, sed exhortatur, ut animas suas purificent. Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image]sanctificavit. Intelligitur autem per purificationem animarum, 1. Vera in Christum fides, quâ corda purificantur Act. 15. v. 9. unde statim addit Apostolus ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ἀληθείαςin obedientia, vel per obedientiam veritatis i. e. per fidem, quâ Evangelicae veritati obedivistis, eamque amplexi estis. Vulgata quidem legit in obedientia caritatis, sed Graeci Codices constanter legunt ἀληθείας, ac Syrus habet vocem [consult facsimile image] quae respondet Hebraeorum אמת quomodo etiam legit Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinianum, citans hunc locum hisce verbis: In obedientia veritatis. Sensus igitur est, cum per fidem quâ obeditis & acquiescitis veritati, animas vestras purificaveritis. 2. mortificatio pravarum concupiscentiarum & inclinationum carnalium ad odia, vindictam, libidines, intemperantiam &c. De corde enim exeunt cogitationes malae, homicidia, adulteria, fornicationes, furta, falsatestimonia, blasphemiae,Mat. 15. v. 19.Marc. 7. v. 21. & 22. haec omnia sunt mortificanda per Spiritum, ut disertè Apostolus addit, cum quo congruit locus Apostolicus Rom. 8. v. 13.Si Spiritu facta carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis.Gal. 5. v. 16.Spiritu ambulate & desideria carnis non perficietis. Sanè προσδιορισμὸς ille διὰ πνέυματος non habetur in versione Syriaca, nec in Latina, nec apud Hieronymum, interim cum in Graecis Codicibus omnibus legatur, & contextui aptissimè congruat, meritò pro genuina parte censetur. 3. Fuga hypocriseos. Hypocrisis est occultum cordis venenum, proinde quando Apostolus animas purificare iubet, simul fugam hypocriseos requirit, unde statim addit εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον quidem si caritas fraterna debet esse simulationis erpers, oportet animas ab hypocriseos veneno priùs purificari. Sic ergò ab exhortatione ad fidei constantiam, quam metaphoricè per castitatem animae abhorrentis ab omni falsa doctrina descripserat, eiusque causam efficientem, Spiritum scil. sanctum exposuerat, transit Apostolus ad exhortationem caritatis, quam exprimit nomine φιλαδελφίας, quâ voce etiam in aliis Scripturae dictis, mutuus Christianorum amor describitur, cum omnes per fidem sint DEI filii, ac proinde invicem fratres. Roman. 12. v. 10.1. Thessal. 4. v. 9.Hebr. 13. v. 1.1. Petr. 3. v. 8.2. Petr. 1. v. 7. Vocula εἰς φιλαδελφίαν regitur à verbo ἀγαπήσατε. Quia ergò Apostolus non dicit, ἀγαπήσατε ἐν φιλαδελφίᾳ, sed εἰς φιλαδελφίαν, inde quidam existimant, describi terminum ad quem caritatis. Diligite vos invicem in fraternam caritatem, hoc est, in unum corpus fraternae caritatis. Sed Oecumenius rectè monet, εἰς, ut alibi passim, ita & hîc poni proδιὰ,diligite vos invicem per fraternam caritatem. Quòd si omninò propriam significationem particulae εἰς retinere velimus, accipi ea posset ὲκηβατικῶς,diligite vos in fraternam caritatem, id est, ut omnibus manifestum fiat, vos esse invicem fratres ac DEI filios. Caeterùm caritatem, quam Apostolus praescribit, vult esse. 1. ἀνυπόκριτονsimulationis expertem, Syrus reddidit, quae non accipit vultum, id est, quae non assumit larvam tantùm externam, seseque transformat, ut alia appareat, quam reverâ est. Quae vero sit caritas ἀνυπόκριτος, exponit Iohannes 1. Epist. 3. v. 18.Non diligamus verbo neque lingua, sed opere & veritate. 2. καθαρὰνpuram & mundam; Diligite, inquit, alii alios ex puro corde, id est, ex corde per fidem purificato, ut ex praecedentibus intelligitur. Locus parallelus extat 1. Timoth. 1. v. 4.Finis praecepti est caritas ex puro corde, & conscientiâ bonâ, & fide non simulatâ. Quidam volunt, caritatem ex puro corde opponi amori impuro ac carnali, adeoque omni illi amori, quo proximus non diligitur in DEO, sub DEO, & propter DEUM. Sed prior explicatio textui magis congruit. 3. ὲκτενῆ.Diligite, inquit, alii alios ἐκτενῶς.Actor. 12. v. 5.προσευχή ἐκτενὴς, sunt preces iuges, & sine intermissione. Item intentae, ut ad ardorem animorum referatur. Hesychius ἐκτενεῖ exponit ἐπιμελεῖaccurato, sedulo, attento. Suidae ἐκτενὲστερος est ἐνεργηκώτερος, ἐπιμελέστερος. Ergò ἐκτενῶς est impensè & intentèLuc. 22. vers. 44. Item iugiter, continuè non interruptè,Ioel. 1. vers. 14.Iudith. 4. vers. 10. quo sensu etiam ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ usurpatur, Iudith. 4. v. 7.Actor. 26. vers. 7. Hesychius exponit non solùm διατεταμένως, ἐκτεταμένως, sed etiam προθύμωςpromtè, Suidas, ὀλοψύχως. LXX. utuntur pro בחזקהin fortitudine,Ion. 3. v. 8. Quando ergò Petrus requirit, ut diligamus ἐκτενῶς, non solùm postulat augmentum caritatis extensivum, ut nunquam desinamus nos invicem diligere, sed etiam intensivum, ut diligamus impensè, ardenter, totis viribus. Locus parallelus extat in cap. 4. huius Epistolae v. 8.τὴν εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἀγάπην ἐκτενῆ ἔχοντες.

## 1:23
BORN AGAIN NOT OF CORRUPTIBLE SEED, BUT INCORRUPTIBLE BY THE WORD OF GOD LIVING & REMAINING FOREVER.

Some wish these things to have been added by the Apostle, to show the faculty of the required love, because spiritual regeneration confers upon man the faculty of loving his neighbor, & of doing what is pleasing to God. But it is more correctly said that the Apostle makes mention of regeneration for this reason, because in the preceding verse he had made mention of φιλαδελφίας. He does not only show, therefore, in what respect he called us brothers, namely, not in respect of the first birth, which is of the flesh, but of the second birth, or regeneration, which is of the Spirit John 3. v. 5. But he also confirms the exhortation to brotherly charity, by an argument drawn from spiritual & heavenly regeneration, in this way: Those who through regeneration have been made spiritual brothers, they also ought to love one another brotherly. But you Christians through regeneration have been made spiritual brothers. Therefore. But if we wish to adapt the argument to the principal proposition, namely to the innocence of life, & the holiness of morals, it can be formed thus. Those who through regeneration have been made children of GOD, they also ought to walk as children of GOD, & to study the holiness of life. But you Christians through regeneration have been made children of GOD. Therefore. Furthermore, the Apostle describes this regeneration from the instrumental cause, namely the seed, from which we are regenerated, which is the word of GOD, and he declares that seed by opposition, that it is not corruptible seed, but incorruptible. By corruptible seed, to which the word of GOD is opposed as incorruptible seed, some understand the seed of crops, with which the word of GOD is compared Matt. 13. v. 19.Mark 4. v. 14. & 28.Luke 8. v. 6. 7. & 11.Col. 1. v. 6.Jas. 1. v. 21. B. Luther understands it concerning human seed, vol. 2. Jena. Germ. f. 333. b. If the old birth is from seed, the new birth also must be from seed. That seed is not flesh and blood, but the eternal word of GOD; that word is that from which we live and are fed, but especially it is the seed from which we are reborn. To which pertains the well-known little verse. We are in the word like an embryo enclosed in the womb. For just as an infant is conceived, born, and carried in the maternal womb: so through the word we are spiritually born, and are carried in the word Isa. 46. v. 3. & 4. Nor indeed is the word only a spiritual womb, in which we are cherished, but also the seed, from which we are spiritually reborn. The Apostle calls this seed incorruptible, in distinction to corruptible seed. Our first birth is from corruptible seed, to which the foulness and uncleanness of sin adheres. Job 14. v. 4.Ps. 51. v. 7.Isa. 64. v. 6. for that which is born of the flesh, is flesh John 3. v. 5. but the second birth, or παλιγγενεσία spiritual, is from incorruptible seed, which is spiritual, pure, and clean, nay, cleansing us from the stain of sin, for that which is born of the Spirit, is Spirit. Furthermore, the Apostle himself explains what he understands by incorruptible seed, when ἐξηγητικῶς he adds, διὰ λόγου θεοῦ ζῶντος καὶ μένοντος εἰς αἰῶνα. These are connected to the preceding by the figure of apposition, though with the phrase changed. For previously he had said ἐκ σπορᾶς; but now he adds, διὰ λόγου, because the word of GOD is not the material of spiritual regeneration, but its instrumental cause. But just as he had previously called the word of GOD incorruptible seed, so in this place he calls it living, and remaining forever, so that he may thus commend the excellence of the word for a double reason. 1. from the added durability. 2. from the effect of vivifying.

Latin:

RENATI NON EX SEMINE CORRUPTIBILI, SED INCORRUPTIBILI PER VERBUM DEI VIVI & PERMANENTIS IN AETERNUM.

Quidam volunt, haec ab Apostolo adiecta, ut ostenderet dilectionis requisitae facultatem, quia regeneratio spiritualis confert homini facultatem diligendi proximum, & faciendi quod Deo gratum. Sed rectiùs dicitur, Apostolum ideò mentionem facere regenerationis, quia in praeced. vers. mentionem fecerat φιλαδελφίας. Non solùm igitur ostendit, quo respectu nos fratres dixerit, videl. non respectu primae nativitatis, quae est ex carne, sed secundae nativitatis, sive regenerationis, quae est ex Spiritu Ioh. 3. v. 5. Sed etiam confirmat exhortationem ad fraternam caritatem, argumento ducto à spirituali & superna regeneratione, hoc modo: Qui per regenerationem facti sunt spirituales fratres, illi etiam debent se invicem fraternè diligere. Atqui vos Christiani per regenerationem facti estis spirituales fratres. Ergò. Quòd si ad principalem propositionem, videlicet ad vitae innocentiam, & morum sanctitatem argumentum accommodare velimus, poterit illud sic informari. Qui per regenerationem facti sunt filii DEI, illi etiam debent ut filii DEI ambulare, & sanctitati vitae studere. Atqui vos Christiani per regenerationem facti estis filii DEI. Ergò. Porrò hanc regenerationem describit Apostolus ex causa instrumentali, videlicet semine, ex quo regeneramur, quod est verbum DEI, ac semen illud declarat ex oppositione, quòd non sit semen corruptibile, sed incorruptibile. Per semen corruptibile, cui verbum DEI, tanquam semen incorruptibile opponitur, quidam intelligunt semen frugum, cum quo verbum DEI confertur Matth. 13. v. 19.Marc. 4. v. 14. & 28.Luc. 8. v. 6. 7. & 11.Col. 1. v. 6.Iac. 1. v. 21. B. Lutherus intelligit de semine humano, tom. 2. Ien. Germ. f. 333. b. Si vetus nativitas est ex semine, etiam novam nativitatem oportet esse ex semine. Semen illud non est caro & sanguis, sed aeternum DEI verbum; verbum illud est, ex quo vivimus & cibamur, cumprimis vero est semen, ex quo renascimur. Quò pertinet notus versiculus. Nos sumus in verbo velut embryo clausus in alvo. Quemadmodum enim infans in utero materno concipitur, nascitur ac gestatur: sic per verbum spiritualiter nascimur, & in verbo portamur Esa. 46. v. 3. & 4. Neque vero verbum est tantùm spiritualis alvus, in qua fovemur, sed etiam semen, ex quo spiritualiter renascimur. Vocat autem Apostolus hoc semen incorruptibile, ad differentiam seminis corruptibilis. Prima nostra nativitas est ex semine corruptibili, cui adhaeret peccati foeditas & immundities. Iob. 14. v. 4.Psalm. 51. v. 7.Esa. 64. v. 6. quod enim ex carne natum, caro est Ioh. 3. v. 5. sed secunda nativitas, sive παλιγγενεσία spiritualis, est ex semine incorruptibili, quod est spirituale, purum ac mundum, imò mundans nos à peccati labe, quod enim ex Spiritu natum, est Spiritus. Caeterùm ipse Apostolus explicat, quid per semen incorruptibile intelligat, quando ἐξηγητικῶς subiicit, διὰ λόγου θεοῦ ζῶντος καὶ μένοντος εἰς αἰῶνα. Haec praecedentibus annectuntur per figuram appositionis, mutatâ tamen phrasi. Priùs enim dixerat ἐκ σπορᾶς; iam vero subiicit, διὰ λόγου, quia verbum DEI non est materia spiritualis regenerationis, sed eius causa instrumentalis. Ut autem priùs verbum DEI vocaverat semen incorruptibile, ita hoc loco vocat illud vivum, & manens in aeternum, ut sic praestantiam verbi duplici ratione commendet. 1. ab adiuncta durabilitate. 2. ab effectu vivificandi.

## 1:24
FOR ALL FLESH IS AS GRASS, & ALL THE GLORY OF IT AS THE FLOWER OF GRASS. THE GRASS WITHERED, & THE FLOWER OF IT FELL AWAY.

He confirms the assertion concerning the durability of the divine word with the testimony of Scripture Isa. 40. v. 6. where that durability is declared from an antithesis. All flesh is as grass, i. e. it not only perishes, but it even perishes quickly: but the word of the Lord abides forever. Meanwhile, because the Apostle had made mention of a double seed in the preceding verse, corruptible, namely, & incorruptible, it is not absurdly established that the Prophetic passage is brought forward not only to confirm the durability of the divine word, but also to declare the nature of both seeds. For by the name of flesh is signified man born of flesh John 3. v. 6.; he, although he may seem to flourish for some time, nevertheless, on account of the adhering corruption of sin, which is likewise signified in the Scriptures by the name of flesh Rom. 8. v. 4. & seqq. Gal. 5. v. 17. &c., is subject to diseases and death, and like grass flourishing indeed in the morning, but in the evening cut down and withered Ps. 90. v. 6., cut down by the sickle of death, he withers, from which it is gathered that even that seed from which he is conceived and born is corruptible. Furthermore, the Apostle brings forward this Prophetic passage from the version of the LXX Interpreters, which has it thus, πᾶσα σὰρξ χόρτος, και πᾶσα δόξα ἀνθρώπου ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου. ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος, καὶ τὸ ἀνθὸς ἐξέπεσε.. The Apostle retained these unchanged, except that he also added the particle of similitude in the former member ὡς χόρτος, and for the sake of greater σαφηνείας clarity added the relative pronoun αὐτοῦ. to the word ἀνθὸς. The Hebrew words are literally thus: All flesh is grass, and all its goodness, as the flower of the field, where for flower χόρτου of hay or grass is placed flower of the field. The grass withered, the flower fell, because the Spirit of the Lord blew upon it; truly the people is grass; which latter parts were omitted by the LXX Interpreters, but are expressed in the version of Theodotion and Symmachus. For ἀνθρώπου in Peter, certain Greek Codices have the relative αὐτῆς, so that it may refer to σάρκα, which agrees more with the Hebrew text. The noun חסד,, signifying goodness in this place, the LXX, looking to the sense, rendered by δὸξαν, so that the antecedent may be understood from the consequent. Whatever is most excellent in a man born of flesh, and still carnal, and of which he is accustomed to boast, that whole and entire thing is frail and transitory like grass, first indeed beautifully flourishing, but soon withering and dried up. The verbs of the past tense ἐξηράνθη καὶ ἐξέπεσε are placed in the Prophetic manner . for things present or things to be shortly, on account of their certainty. It is so certain that the grass will soon wither, that it may deservedly be said to have already withered.

Latin:

QUIA OMNIS CARO UT FOENUM, & OMNIS GLORIA EIUS TANQUAM FLOS FOENI. EXARUIT FOENUM, & FLOS EIUS DECIDIT.

Assertionem de durabilitate verbi divini confirmat testimonio Scripturae Esa. 40. v. 6. ubi durabilitas illa declaratur ex antithesi. Omnis caro ut foenum, i. e. non solùm perit, sed etiam citò perit: verbum autem Domini manet in aeternum. Interim quia Apostolus duplicis seminis in versu praeced. mentionem fecerat, corruptibilis, scil. & incorruptibilis, haud absurdè statuitur, locum Propheticum non solùm ad confirmandam verbi divini durabilitatem, sed etiam ad declarandam utriusque seminis Naturam adduci. Carnis enim nomine significatur homo ex carne natus Iohan. 3. v. 6. is quamvis aliquandiu florere videatur, tamen propter adhaerentem peccati corruptionem, quae itidem carnis nomine in Scripturis significatur Roman. 8. v. 4. & seqq. Galat. 5. v. 17. &c. morbis & morti est obnoxius, ac instar graminis manè quidem florentis, circa vesperam vero decerpti & arescentisPsal. 90. v. 6. falce mortis resectus exarescit, ex quo colligitur, etiam semen illud, ex quo concipitur & nascitur, esse corruptibile. Caeterùm hunc locum Propheticum adducit Apostolus ex versione LXX. Interpretum, quae sic habet, πᾶσα σὰρξ χόρτος, και πᾶσα δόξα ἀνθρώπου ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου. ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος, καὶ τὸ ἀνθὸς ἐξέπεσε. Apostolus haec invariata retinuit, nisi quòd etiam in priore membro addidit particulam similitudinis ὡς χόρτος, ac voci ἀνθὸς maioris σαφηνείας causâ adiecit pronomen relativum αὐτοῦ. Hebraea ad verbum sic habent. Omnis caro herba, & omnis bonitas eius, tanquam flos agri, ubi pro floreχόρτουfoeni sive graminis ponitur flos agri. Aruit herba, cecidit flos, quia Spiritus Domini sufflavit in cum, verè herba, populus; quae posteriora à LXX. Interpp. sunt omissa, sed in Theodotionis & Symmachi versione exprimuntur. Pro ἀνθρώπου apud Petrum, quidam Codices Graeci habent relativum αὐτῆς, ut ad σάρκα referatur, quod magis congruit cum textu Hebraeo. Nomen חסד,bonitatem hoc loco significans, LXX. ad sensum respicientes reddiderunt per δὸξαν, ut ex consequente intelligatur antecedens. Quicquid in homine ex carne nato, & adhuc carnali est praestantissimum, & de quo gloriari solet, illud totum & omne est caducum, & transitorium instar graminis, primùm quidem pulchrè florentis, mox vero arescentis & exiccati. Verba praeteriti temporis ἐξηράνθη καὶ ἐξέπεσε more Prophetico ponuntur pro praesentibus vel paulo pòst futuris propter certitudinem. Tàm certum est, gramen citò exariturum, utiam exaruisse meritò dici possit.

## 1:25
BUT THE WORD OF THE LORD ENDURES FOREVER. AND THIS IS THE WORD WHICH HAS BEEN PREACHED AS GOSPEL UNTO YOU.

He proves the other member of the opposition, that that spiritual seed from which we have been reborn, namely the word of GOD, is incorruptible. Just as a corruptible man has corruptible seed: so, on the contrary, the word of GOD, which is the spiritual seed of our regeneration, is incorruptible, because it is the word of the eternal and incorruptible GOD. Likewise, just as a carnal man is corruptible, because he is born from corruptible seed: so a spiritual man is by a certain reason incorruptible, i.e., he does not die an eternal death, because he is reborn from incorruptible seed. The LXX have τὸ δέ ῥῆμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα,, which agrees more with the Hebrew. The word of our God shall stand forever. Peter, without any variation of sense, put Κυρίου. for τοῦ θεοῦ ἠμῶν. That which is added, and this is the word which has been preached as gospel unto you, was added for the sake of declaring the Prophetic testimony, that it is to be understood that that refers to the preached word. είς ὑμᾶς is put for ὑμῖν through a customary Hebraism. James cap. 1. v. 21. calls λόγον ἒμφυτον, implanted and engrafted into hearts through preaching.

Q. In this place. 1. Why does the Apostle name only souls, when he requires purification from the faithful, since we ought to cleanse ourselves not only from the defilements of the Spirit, but also of the flesh. 2. Cor. 7. v. 1. Resp. The purification of the soul and Spirit also draws with it the cleansing from the defilements of the flesh, just as interior uncleanness is the cause of exterior uncleanness. Therefore, the purification of the soul ought to be commended to us principally and above all things, lest with the hypocrites we pursue an external cleanliness of the body of whatever kind, destitute of the interior cleanliness of the heart, from external offenses.

Q. 2. How is the purification of souls attributed to the obedience of the truth? Resp. By obedience of the truth is understood obedience of faith Rom. 1. v. 5. cap. 16. v. 26. through which hearts are purified Act. 15. vers. 9. because faith the most perfect cleanliness of Christ in the word of the Gospel he embraces the offered [gift], and applies it to himself. Through this faith the Holy Spirit is also given Gal. 3. v. 2. who begins to purge the filth of sin through renewal, so that the faithful man may be clean not only imputatively, but also inchoatively, and may grow daily in that spiritual cleanliness, until at some time the consummation follows in eternal life. 1. Cor. 1. v. 30.cap. 6. v. 11.2. Cor. 7. v. 1.

Q. 3. Whether the participles ζῶντος καὶ μένοντος are to be referred to the nearer, namely to the word θεοῦ, or indeed to the more remote, namely to the word λόγου; Resp. Certainly some of the Calvinists & Photinians, but especially Svencfeldius & Rathmannus, wished that the Apostolic text should be rendered thus, you are reborn through the word of the living GOD, and remaining forever. But that it should rather be rendered in this way, through the living word of GOD, and remaining forever, he shows. 1. The Prophetic testimony, which is immediately subjoined from Isaiah. All flesh is grass, but the word of our GOD remains forever. The Syriac version. You are reborn [consult facsimile image] through the living word of GOD, which remains forever, where the latter participle seems indeed to be referred to God, yet the former to be referred to the word, can be denied by no appearance of truth. 3. The series of words. If the participle ζῶντος were to agree with the noun θεοῦ, Peter would have ordered the words thus, διὰ λόγον θεοῦ ζῶντος. 4. Comparison of parallel passages. To be living is attributed to the word of GOD Ioh. 6. v. 63.Hebr. 4. v. 12. to remain forever is attributed to the same Luc. 21. v. 33.

Q. 4. In what sense is the word of GOD said to be living? Some here establish a metonymy. The word of GOD is said to be living, because it makes men alive to eternal life. But some a metaphor. The word of GOD is living, because it is efficacious, as living and animated things. These things are indeed rightly said in their place, but insufficiently. 1. For both are joined Hebr. 4. v. 12. that ὁ λόγος θεοῦ is ζῶν καὶ ἐνεργὴς. 2. The second act presupposes the first, ἐνέργεια δύναμιν. 3. To the word of GOD is attributed not only ἐνέργεια ζωοποιητικὴ, the action of vivifying, but also δύναμις the power of saving. Rom. 1. v. 16. Therefore the word of GOD is called living, because as the word of the living GOD it obtains an internal force of vivifying, which it effectively exerts in spiritually vivifying men.

Q. 5. Why does Peter follow the version of the LXX Interpreters rather than the Hebrew source? Resp. This is customary for the Evangelists and Apostles in the New Testament, concerning which matter Jerome discourses thus in his questions on Genesis, chapter 46. This is to be observed generally, that wherever the holy Apostles or Apostolic men speak to the peoples, they for the most part make use of those testimonies which had already been published among the nations. But this is to be understood when the version of the LXX Interpreters agrees in sense with the Hebrew text, for thus Jerome himself limits it in chapter 28 of Isaiah. We have observed this in the Old Testament, apart from a few testimonies which Luke alone uses, who had more knowledge of the Greek language, that wherever anything is said from the Old Testament, they do not set them down according to the LXX, but according to the Hebrew, following no one's interpretation, but translating the Hebrew sense in their own speech. In chapter 29 of Isaiah We ought to note that the Evangelists and Apostles did not interpret word for word, nor did they follow the authority of the LXX Interpreters, whose edition was already being read at that time, but as Hebrews and instructed in the law, they used their own words without damage to the senses. In the preface to chapter 54 of Isaiah I know that I have often said that the Apostles and Evangelists, wherever they set down testimonies from the Old Testament, if there is no diversity between the Hebrew and the LXX, are accustomed to use either their own words or those of the LXX Interpreters. But if the sense is otherwise in the Hebrew and otherwise in the old edition, they follow the Hebrew more than the LXX Interpreters. Finally, just as we have shown that they set down many things from the Hebrew which are not held in the LXX, so let our rivals teach, having taken up some testimonies from the LXX which are not in the books of the Hebrews, and the contention is finished. He repeats the same in Epistle 151 to Algasia and elsewhere throughout.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. The word of GOD is living and remaining forever. But 2. Cor. 3. v. 6. the letter kills. Resp. 1. The Apostle here speaks properly of the word of the Gospel, just as he immediately adds. This is the word which is preached among you. That is the word of life John 6. v. 68. chapter 12. v. 50. Acts 5. verse 20. Phil. 2. v. 16. 2. The Law of Moses, of which Paul 2. Cor. 3. v. 6. speaks, in itself and through itself is likewise the word of life Act. 7. v. 38. but by accident, on account of the corruption of Nature, it is the ministry of death. Rom. 7. v. 10.

2. The word of GOD is living. But Hebr. 4. v. 2. the word heard does not profit, not being mixed with faith of those who heard it. Resp. From the removal of a second act, hindered in a certain object, an argument cannot be drawn to the removal of the first act. The Word of GOD in itself and through itself is living, although it does not vivify all things in act.

3. The Word of GOD remains forever. But Ierem. 36. v. 25. The King burned the volume and the words, which Baruch had written from the mouth of Ieremiah. Resp. The written Word of GOD is considered in three ways. 1. By reason of characters and signifying voices. 2. By reason of sense, signified through voices. 3. By reason of sign and signified together, i.e., by reason of voices and sense. In the first signification it is taken Ierem. 36. v. 27. In the second in this place and Ioh. 10. v. 35. Scripture cannot be broken. In the third, 2. Tim. 3. v. 15. & 16. and elsewhere throughout.

Ἒλεγχος. 1. Peter teaches that souls are purified in obedience or through the obedience of truth, i.e., through faith. Act. 15. v. 9. The Pope teaches that true faith can consist with the impure filth of sins.

2. Peter teaches that souls are purified by the obedience of truth. The Pope seeks the purification of souls and bodies in fasts, vigils, and sleeping on the ground. Stapulensis chastises this error in chapter 3 of Colossians.

3. The Word of GOD is an incorruptible seed, from which we are reborn, it is living and vivifying. The Pope, with Swencfeld, teaches that it is a dead letter. Costerus, chapter 3 of the Enchiridion on the Supreme Pontiff, p. 131: Scripture, as a thing without a soul or sense, distracted into various and conflicting opinions, seeks nothing. Greg. de Valend. book 8 of the analysis of faith, chapter 6: The Word of GOD extends much more widely than Scripture, nor is it bound to mute letters. Gretserus in the defense of Bellarmine, vol. 1, p. 413, asserts that Scripture, as far as we are concerned, is truly called a dead letter.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. From the fact that Peter in this place commands to purify souls, Estius gathers that there is free will in spiritual matters. It is signified, he says, the cooperation of the will with GOD, for here to man, Act. 15. vers. 9. the purification of the heart is attributed by GOD. Resp. 1. Peter addresses the reborn, whose free will has already been liberated. But none of us denies that the reborn are θεοῦ συνέργους, yet they act not by their own powers remaining in a corrupted Nature, but by new powers granted by the Holy Spirit. 2. Thence Peter immediately adds, δίὰ πνέυματος, through the operation of the Holy Spirit. Therefore that purification of souls is the work of the Holy Spirit, and of new powers granted by the Holy Spirit.

2. From the fact that Peter says, we are reborn from incorruptible seed, which is the word of GOD, the Anabaptists gather that infants are not capable of regeneration, since they are not capable of the word. Resp. 1. The Apostle speaks about those who had been converted through the preaching of the Gospel, whom we easily concede to be converted through the preached and heard word. 2. From that, however, it cannot be inferred that infants are not reborn through Baptism. For from the removal of one means to the removal of all means, and of the end itself, the consequence is not valid. 3. As in this place Peter calls the word the incorruptible seed, from which we are reborn; so Paul Tit. 3. v. 5. calls Baptism the washing of regeneration and renewal; and Ephes. 5. v. 27. says that Christ cleanses the Church by the washing of water in the word. 4. Therefore the word and the Sacraments, regarding the effect of regeneration, are not opposed, but subordinated, since in the Sacraments there is also the word of GOD, whence they are called the word ὁρατὸν visible. 5. The pious ancients explain that word, of which Peter testifies that it is the means of regeneration, not only of the preached word, but also of the Sacramental word. Bede in this place: Just as the price of the Lord's passion, by which we have been redeemed, is incorruptible, so also the Sacrament of the sacred font, by which we are reborn, is incorruptible, which are so connected to each other that one cannot confer salvation upon us without the other.

3. By the word, from which we are reborn, Swencfeldius and Rathmannus in Bestandiger sehr der Vater p. 109. 112. understand the hypostatic Word, the Son of GOD himself, so that they are not forced to concede that the Word of GOD is living and life-giving. Caietanus and Aretius in their commentaries on this place also go in the same direction. Resp. 1. Peter himself declares clearly enough that he is speaking about the preached word, because ἐξηγήσεως for the sake of this he adds in the last verse: this is the word which has been preached to you, or unto you. 2. Peter does not use the word λόγος, which is sometimes attributed to the Son of GOD in the Scriptures Ioh. 1. v. 1.1. Ioh. 1. v. 1.Apoc. 19. V. 13. but the word ῤῆμα, which is used only of the revealed preached or written word. Damasc. in the disputation of the Christian and the Saracen: I confess only one uncreated Word of GOD, but I do not call all Scripture λόγους, but ῤήματα θεοῦ. 3. The same is proved from parallel places of Scripture. Luc. 8. v. 11. The seed is the word of GOD. Rom. 10. v. 17. Faith is from hearing, hearing through the word of GOD. Iac. 1. v. 18. he voluntarily begat us by the word of truth. Especially pertinent here is the Apostolic place 1. Cor. 4. v. 15. through I have begotten you through the Gospel. Compare B. Luther, vol. 2, Jena, German, f. 333.

4. From the fact that the word is called seed, from which we are reborn, Piscator gathers that true faith, once kindled in hearts, is not extinguished, because the seed received into hearts does not perish. I respond: the word of GOD in itself and by itself is incorruptible seed, but the fructification of this seed in our heart is often hindered and extinguished, whence the Devil is said to snatch this seed from the hearts of certain hearers Matthew 13, v. 19; thence he who is born of God is said not to commit sin, ὅτι because and insofar as his seed remains in him. 1 John 3, v. 9

5. Sixtus Senensis, book 8, Bibliotheca, heresy 9; Iodocus Coccius, vol. 1, Thesaurus, book 6, art. 17, p. 680; from the fact that Peter alleges a testimony from chapter 14 of Ecclesiasticus, v. 19, they prove that the book of Ecclesiasticus is Canonical. I respond: 1. If the Canonical authority of any book were proven from a mere Apostolic allegation, it would follow that the book of Enoch cited by Jude is Canonical. 2. In the Biblical Index of the Vulgate edition, no testimony is taken from Wisdom or Ecclesiasticus, but the words of Peter are said to be cited there from Isaiah 40, v. 7. 3. Claudius Guillandus, Lorinus, Salmeron, Dominicus à Soto, Iustinianus, etc., say that the testimony is taken from Isaiah.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. There are three principal virtues of a truly pious and reborn man: purification of the soul, i.e., cleanliness of heart without any affected malice; obedience of the truth, i.e., faith, from which cleanliness of heart and innocence of life arises; and brotherly love, which is the effect of both, whence the Apostle says that love ought to proceed from a pure heart.

2. Faith is obedience of the truth, by which, namely, we obey from the heart the truth divinely revealed Romans 6, v. 17 you have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine into which you were delivered.

3. Purification of the soul happens in obedience of the truth, because where there is true faith, there the soul struggles with depraved concupiscences, lest they reign in the mortal body Romans 6, v. 12; where, however, the soul is not purified through faith, there it does not walk toward the truth.

4. From true faith is born love of GOD and neighbor Galatians 5, v. 6, whence Peter joins faith and love with the tightest bond. Love of GOD is simultaneously insinuated through the purification of the soul. For he who loves GOD adheres to Him chastely, avoiding spiritual fornication, i.e., idolatry and by fleeing sins against conscience. Love of neighbor is described by φιλαδελφίαν.

5. There is virginity of mind and of the womb; without the former, the latter profits little. Aug. lib. de virg. cap. 18. Virginity of mind consists in the sincerity of faith, and in the purity of the heart from depraved burnings.

6. Love of neighbor ought to be ἀνυπόκριτος & ἐκτενὴς.

7. It is necessary that the same flow from a pure heart. The heart is the fountain of the affections. In order that clear water may be drawn, it is necessary that the fountain be pure.

8. The Word of the Gospel is the means of regeneration and vivification. It regenerates us not only θεωρητικῶς,, so to speak, insofar as it illuminates minds with the knowledge of the divine will, and shows us what is to be believed and done, but also πρακτικῶς, insofar as it bends the will to the assent of the divine testimony, effectively moves and changes the heart, kindles in it faith, by which we embrace the grace of GOD offered in Christ, and in it we peacefully acquiesce, and through this faith we are rendered children of GOD and heirs of eternal life. It vivifies us, not only insofar as it offers to us the favor of GOD to be tasted, and raises us up with vivifying consolation, but also insofar as it makes us participants of spiritual life.

9. The Word of GOD is living, both because it is the word of the living GOD, and because it has an inherent vivifying power, and because the Holy Spirit works through it true and living spiritual motions in hearts. The second follows from the first, the third from the second.

10. The Word of GOD remains forever, not only because the Gospel concerning Christ, perceived by faith, is effective to grant eternal life to believers, but also because in itself, insofar as it embraces the sense and counsel of GOD, it is eternal.

11. As the seed, so the birth; as the birth, so the life, and vice versa. From carnal and corruptible seed arises a carnal and corruptible birth; where there is a carnal birth, there also is a carnal life. From incorruptible seed arises an incorruptible and spiritual birth. Where there is a spiritual birth, there is a spiritual life.

12. We are sown from Adam, corrupted through sin; hence this sowing is corrupt φθαρτὴ,, not only because the body is subject to corruption and death, but also because the soul is miserably defiled by the stain of sin, whence, insofar as we descend from Adam, we are all children of wrathEph. 2. v. 3. subject to death and damnation, and thus damned before they are born.

13. Man by nature is flesh, because, that which is born of the flesh, is flesh,Ioh. 3. v. 6. By the name of flesh, however, not only the fragility of human nature is denoted, but also its corruption through sin.

14. When the Prophet speaks of flesh and its glory, he describes the whole man, such as he is by nature, whence among the works of the flesh even heresies, which are vices of the mind, are referred to by the Apostle, Gal. 5. v. 20.

15. Man, on account of the fleetingness and brevity of life, is rightly compared to hay. Iob. 14. v. 2.Psal. 90. v. 6.Esa. 40. v. 6.Sirac. 14. v. 18.Iac. 1. v. 10. Hay in being born has greenness, in growing vigor, then also a flower, but cut down by the scythe and dried by the heat of the sun, it loses all greenness, vigor, and flower: thus man, through the succession of ages, loses his beauty and is reduced to dust.

16. All the glory of the carnal man is like the flower of the field. Reason devises various ways of happiness, but they are fleeting and vain, and all that glory eventually vanishes.

17. The word of GOD abideth for ever, therefore it is the panacea of immortality. For he who embraces the word by faith, he is saved in the word and with the word unto eternal life. There is no stable and true life except in GOD, but that is not communicated except through the word apprehended by faith 1. Ioh. 2. v. 17. The world passeth away, and the lust thereof. He that doeth the will of GOD, abideth for ever.

18. The word of GOD, through which we are regenerated, vivified, and preserved unto eternal life, is not to be sought in heaven, but as it has been revealed to us on earth, not as it lies hidden closed in the heart of GOD, but as it has proceeded from his mouth and been comprehended in the writings of the Prophets and Apostles, it has become known to us. Roman. 10. vers. 6.Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven?vers. 7.or who shall descend into the deep?vers. 8.The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach.

Summary of the chapter. A continuation of the exhortation to constancy of faith and innocence of life. There are two parts: the former general, from verse 1 up to verse 13, directed to all Christians of whatever status and condition; the latter special, from verse 13 up to the end of the chapter, directed to subjects and servants.

The former part is completed in three members: 1. Proposition. 2. Confirmation. 3. Conclusion or repetition of the proposition. The proposition contains both ἀποτροπὴν regarding vices adverse to Christian charity, and προτροπὴν regarding the zeal of progressing from the word of the Gospel in true faith and holy life. Ἀποτροπὴ is expressed in these words.

Latin:

VERBUM AUTEM DOMINI MANET IN AETERNUM. HOC EST AUTEM VERBUM QUOD EVANGELIZATUM EST IN VOS.

Probat alterum oppositionis membrum, quòd semen illud spirituale ex quo renati sumus, videlicet verbum DEI, sit incorruptibile. Sicut homo corruptibilis habet semen corruptibile: ita ex opposito verbum DEI, quod est semen spirituale nostrae regenerationis, est incorruptibile, quia est aeterni & incorruptibilis DEI verbum. Item sicut homo carnalis est corruptibilis, quia ex corruptibili semine natus est: sic homo spiritualis certâ ratione est incorruptibilis i. e. non moritur aeternâ morte, quia est ex incorruptibili semine renatus. LXX. habent, τὸ δέ ῥῆμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, quod magis congruit cum Hebraeo. Verbum Dei nostri stabit in seculum. Petrus sine ulla sensûs variatione pro τοῦ θεοῦ ἠμῶν posuit Κυρίου. Quod additur, hoc est autem verbum, quod evangelizatum est in vos, declarandi Prophetici testimonii causa est adiectum, quod intelligendum illud sit de verbo praedicato. είς ὑμᾶς ponitur pro ὑμῖν per usitatum Hebraismum. Iacobus cap. 1. v. 21. vocat λόγον ἒμφυτον, per praedicationem cordibus implantatum atque insitum.

Q. Hoc loco. 1. Cur animas tantùm nominet Apostolus, quando purificationem à fidelibus requirit, cum non solùm ab inquinamentis Spiritus, sed etiam carnis nos mundare debeamus.2. Cor. 7. v. 1. Resp. animae ac Spiritus purificatio secum etiam trahit mundationem ab inquinamentis carnis, sicut interior immundities est causa immunditiei exterioris. Propterea animae purificatio praecipuè & ante omnia nobis debet esse commendata, ne cum hypocritis externam qualemcunque corporis ab externis delictis mundiciem destitutam interiore cordis mundicie sectemur.

Q. 2. Quomodo obedientiae veritatis tribuatur purificatio animarum? Resp. per obedientiam veritatis intelligitur obedientia fideiRom. 1. v. 5.cap. 16. v. 26. per quam purificantur corda Act. 15. vers. 9. quia fides perfectissimam Christi munditiem in verbo Evangelii oblatum amplectitur, eamque sibi applicat. Per hanc fidem etiam datur Spiritus sanctus Gal. 3. v. 2. qui sordes peccati per renovationem expurgare incipit, ut homo fidelis non solùm imputativè, sed etiam inchoativè mundus sit, inque spirituali illa mundicie quotidiè crescat, donec aliquando consummatio sequatur in vita aeterna. 1. Cor. 1. v. 30.cap. 6. v. 11.2. Cor. 7. v. 1.

Q. 3. An participiaζῶντος καὶ μένοντοςreferenda sit ad propinquius, videlicet ad vocemθεοῦ,an vero ad remotius, videlicet ad vocemλόγου; Resp. sanè quidam ex Calvinianis & Photinianis, cumprimis vero Svencfeldius & Rathmannus voluerunt, textum Apostolicum sic reddendum esse, renati estis per sermonem DEI vivi, & manentis in aeternum. Sed reddendum potius esse hoc modo, per sermonem DEI vivum, & manentem in aeternum, ostendit. 1. Testimonium Propheticum, quod statim ex Esaia subiicitur. Omnis caro foenum, verbum autem DEI nostri manet in aeternum. Versio Syriaca. Regeniti estis[consult facsimile image]per sermonem vivum DEI, qui manet in aeternum, ubi posterius participium ad Deum quidem referri videtur, prius tamen ad sermonem referri, nullâ veritatis, specie negari potest. 3. Series verborum. Si participium ζῶντος conveniret cum nomine θεοῦ, sic potiùs verba ordinasset Petrus, διὰ λόγον θεοῦ ζῶντος. 4. Collatio locorum parallelorum. Vivum esse tribuitur DEI verbo Ioh. 6. v. 63.Hebr. 4. v. 12.manere in aeternum eidem tribuitur Luc. 21. v. 33.

Q. 4. Quo sensu verbum DEI dicatur vivum? Quidam hîc statuunt metonymiam. Verbum DEI dicitur vivum, quia homines vivificat ad vitam aeternam. Quidam vero metaphoram. Sermo DEI est vivus, quia efficax, utres viva & animata. Haec quidem suo loco rectè dicuntur, sed insufficienter. 1. Utrumque enim Hebr. 4. v. 12. coniungitur, quòd ὁ λόγος θεοῦ sit ζῶν καὶ ἐνεργὴς. 2. Actus secundus praesupponit primum, ἐνέργεια δύναμιν. 3. Verbo DEI non solùm tribuitur ἐνέργεια ζωοποιητικὴ, actio vivificandi, sed etiam δύναμις potentia salvandi. Rom. 1. v. 16. Dicitur ergò verbum DEI vivum, quia ut DEI vivi verbum internam vim vivificandi obtinet, quam in hominibus spiritualiter vivificandis efficaciter exerit.

Q. 5. Quare Petrus versionem LXX. Interpp. potiùs sequatur quàm fontem Hebraeum? Resp. solenne hoc est Evangelistis & Apostolis in N. Test. qua de re sic disserit Hieronymus in quaestionibus super Genesin cap. 46. Hoc generaliter observandum, quòd, ubicunque sancti Apostoli, aut Apostolici viri loquuntur ad populos, iis plerunque testimoniis abutantur, quae iam fuerant in gentibus divulgata. Sed hoc intelligendum, quando LXX. Interpp. versio quoad sensum convenit cum textu Hebraeo, sic enim limitat ipse Hieronymus in cap. 28. Esai. Hoc in veteri observavimus Testamento, absque paucis testimoniis, quibus Lucas solus abutitur, qui magis Graecae linguae habuit scientiam, ubicunque de veteri instrumento quid dicitur, non eos iuxta LXX. sed iuxta Hebraicum ponere, nullius sequentes interpretationem, sed sensum Hebraicum suo sermone vertentes. In cap. 29. Esai.Notare debemus, Evangelistas & Apostolos non verbum interpretatos esse de verbo, nec LXX. Interpretum autoritatem secutos, quorum editio illo iam tempore legebatur, sed q. Hebraeos & instructos in lege, absque damno sensuum suis usos esse sermonibus. in prooem. cap. 54. Esai.Crebrò dixisse me novi, Apostolos & Evangelistas, ubicunque de veteri instrumento ponunt testimonia, si inter Hebraicum & LXX. nulla diversitas sit, vel suis vel LXX. Interpp. verbis uti solitos. Sin autem aliter in Hebraico, aliter in veteri editione sensus est, Hebraicum magis quàm LXX. Interpp. sequi. Denique ut nos multa ostendimus posuisse eos ex Hebraeo, quae in LXX. non habentur, sic aemuli nostri doceant, assumta aliqua de LXX. testimonia, quae non sunt in Hebraeorum libris, & finita contentio est. Idem repetit Epist. 151. ad Algas. & alibi passim.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Verbum DEI est vivum, & manens in aeternum. At2. Cor. 3. v. 6.litera occidit. Resp. 1. Apostolus hîc propriè loquitur de verbo Evangelii, sicutstatim addit. Hoc est verbum, quod praedicatum inter vos. Illud est verbum vitaeIoh. 6. v. 68.cap. 12. v. 50.Actor. 5. vers. 20.Phil. 2. v. 16. 2. Lex Mosis, de qua Paulus 2. Cor. 3. v. 6. loquitur, in se ac per se itidem est verbum vitaeAct. 7. v. 38. sed ex accidente, propter corruptionem Nature est ministerium mortis. Rom. 7. v. 10.

2. Verbum DEI est vivum. AtHebr. 4. v. 2.Non prodest sermo auditus, non admixtus fidei auditorum. Resp. à remotione actus secundi, in certo obiecto impediti, non potest argumentum duci ad remotionem actus primi. Verbum DEI in se ac per se est vivum, licet non omnes actu vivificet.

3. Verbum DEI manet in aeternum. AtIerem. 36. v. 25.Combussit Rex volumen & sermones, quos scripserat Baruch ex ore Ieremiae. Resp. verbum DEI scriptum consideratur tripliciter. 1. Ratione characterum & vocum significantium. 2. Ratione sensûs, per voces significati. 3. Ratione signi & signati simul i. e. ratione vocum & sensus. In prima significatione accipitur Ierem. 36. v. 27. In secunda hoc loco & Ioh. 10. v. 35.Non potest solvi Scriptura. In tertia, 2. Tim. 3. v. 15. & 16. & alibi passim.

Ἒλεγχος. 1. Petrus docet, animas purificari in obedientia sive per obedientiam veritatis i. e. per fidem. Act. 15. v. 9. Papa docet, veram fidem cum impuris peccatorum sordibus consistere.

2. Petrus docet, animas purificari obedientiâ veritatis. Papa purificationem animarum & corporum quaerit in ieiuniis, vigiliis, humicubationibus. Castigat hunc errorem Stapulensis in cap. 3. Coloss.

3. Verbum DEI est semen incorruptibile, ex quo renascimur, est vivum & vivificans. Papa cum Swencfeldio docet, quòd sit litera mortua. Costerus cap. 3. Ench. de summ. Pontif. p. 131. Scriptura, ut res sine anima, vel sensu, in varias pugnantesque, sententias distracta, nihil queritur. Greg. de Valend. lib. 8. anal. fid. cap. 6. Verbum DEI multò latiùs patet quàm Scriptura, neque illud est ad mutas literas alligatum. Gretserus in def. Bellarm. tom. 1. p. 413. adserit Scripturam quoad nos verè dici literam mortuam.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Ex eo, quod Petrus hoc loco iubet purificare animas, colligit Estius, dari liberum arbitrium in spiritualibus. Significatur, inquit, cooperatio voluntatis cum DEO, hîc enim homini,Act. 15. vers. 9.DEO tribuitur cordis purificatio. Resp. 1. Petrus compellat renatos, quorum liberum arbitrium iam est liberatum. Nemo autem nostrûm negat, renatos esse θεοῦ συνέργους, agunt autem non propriis in Natura corrupta adhuc reliquis, sed novis à Spiritu sancto donatis viribus. 2. Inde Petrus statim addit, δίὰ πνέυματος,per operationem Spiritus sancti. Ergo illa animarum purificatio est opus Spiritus sancti, & novarum à Spiritu sancto donatarum virium.

2. Ex eo, quòd Petrus dicit, nos renasci ex semine incorruptibili, quod est DEI verbum, colligunt Anabaptistae, infantes non esse regenerationis capaces, cum non sint capaces verbi. Resp. 1. Apostolus loquitur de illis, qui per praedicationem Evangelii conversi erant quos per verbum praedicatum & auditum converti, facilè concedimus. 2. Ex eo vero non potest inferri, infantes non renasci per Baptismum. Ex remotione enim unius medii ad remotionem omnium mediorum, & ipsius finis, non valet consequentia. 3. Ut hoc loco Petrus verbum vocat semen incorruptibile, ex quo renascimur; ita Paulus Tit. 3. v. 5.Baptismum vocat lavacrum regenerationis & renovationis; ac Ephes. 5. v. 27. dicit, Christum mundare Ecclesiam lavacro aquae in verbo. 4. Ergò verbum & Sacramenta, quoad effectum regenerationis, non sunt opposita, sed subordinata, cum in Sacramentis etiam sit DEI verbum, unde dicuntur verbum ὁρατὸν visibile. 5. Pii veteres verbum illud, de quo Petrus testatur, quòd sit regenerationis medium, exponunt non solùm de verbo praedicato, sed etiam de verbo Sacramentali. Beda in h. l. Sicut incorruptibile est precium Dominicae passionis, quo redemti sumus, ita etiam incorruptibile est Sacramentum fontis sacri, quo renascimur, quae ita sibi invicem connectuntur, ut unum nobis sine altero salutem conferre nequeat.

3. Per verbum, ex quo renascimur, Swencfeldius & Rathmannus in Bestandiger sehr der Vater p. 109. 112. intelligunt Verbum hypostaticum ipsum DEI Filium, ne concedere cogantur, Verbum DEI esse vivum & vivificum. Eodem etiam abeunt Caietanus & Aretius in comm. h. l. Resp. 1. Petrus ipse satis perspicuè declarat, quod de verbo praedicato loquatur, quia ἐξηγήσεως causâ addit versu ult. hoc est verbum, quod praedicatum est in vos, vel ad vos. 2. Petrus non utitur voce λόγος, quae Filio DEI aliquando in Scripturis tribuitur Ioh. 1. v. 1.1. Ioh. 1. v. 1.Apoc. 19. V. 13. sed voce ῤῆμα, quae tantùm de revelato verbo praedicato vel scripto usurpatur. Damasc. in discept. Christiani & Saraceni. Ego solum unum verbum DEI confiteor increatum Ens, omnem autem Scripturam non dicoλόγους, sed ῤήματα θεοῦ. 3. Idem probatur ex parallelis Scripturae locis. Luc. 8. v. 11.Semen est verbum DEI.Rom. 10. v. 17.Fides est ex auditu, auditus per verbum DEI.Iac. 1. v. 18.voluntariè genuit nos verbo veritatis. Cumprimis huc pertinet locus Apostolicus 1. Cor. 4. v. 15.per Evangelium vos genui. Confer B. Lutherum tom. 2. Ien. Germ. f. 333.

4. Ex eo, quod verbum dicitur semen, ex quo renascimur, colligit Piscator, fidem veram semel in cordibus accensam non extingui, quia semen in corda receptum non interit. Resp. verbum DEI in se ac per se est semen incorruptibile, sed fructificatio huius seminis in corde nostro saepè impeditur & extinguitur, unde Diabolus dicitur, semen hoc rapere ex cordibus quorundam auditorumMatth. 13. v. 19. inde qui ex Deo natus est, dicitur non facere peccatum,ὅτιquia & quatenus semen ipsus in eo manet.1. Ioh. 3. v. 9.

5. Sixtus Senensis 1. 8. Bibl. haeres. 9. Iodocus Coccius tom. 1. Thesauri lib. 6. art. 17. p. 680. ex eo, quod Petrus allegat testimonium ex cap. 14. Ecclesiastici v. 19. probant, librum Ecclesiastici esse Canonicum. Resp. 1. Si ex nuda allegatione Apostolica probaretur Canonica alicuius libri autoritas, sequeretur, librum Henoch à Iuda citatum esse Canonicum. 2. In Indice Biblico vulgatae editionis nullum testimonium ex Sapientia vel Ecclesiastico est desumtum, sed verba Petri ibidem dicuntur citata, ex Es. 40. v. 7. 3. Claudius Guillandus, Lorinus, Salmeron, Dominicus à Soto, Iustinianus &c. ex Esaia testimonium desumtum esse dicunt.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Tres sunt praecipuae virtutes hominis verè pii & renati, purificatio animae, i. e. mundicies cordis absque omni affectata malitia; obedientia veritatis, i. e. fides, ex qua mundicies cordis, & vitae innocentia oritur; ac dilectio fraterna, quae utriusque est effectus, unde Apostolus dicit, dilectionem debere proficisci ex puro corde.

2. Fides est obedientia veritatis, quâ sc. veritati divinitùs patefactae ex corde obedimus Rom. 6. v. 17.obedistis ex corde in eam formam doctrinae, in quam traditi estis.

3. Purificatio animae fit in obedientia veritatis, quia, ubi vera fides, ibi anima luctatur cum pravis concupiscentiis, ne dominentur in corpore mortaliRom. 6. v. 12. ubi autem anima non est purificata per fidem, ibi non ambulat ad veritatem.

4. Ex vera fide nascitur dilectio DEI & proximi Galat. 5. v. 6. unde Petrus fidem & dilectionem arctissimo nexu coniungit. Dilectio DEI simul insinuatur per purificationem animae. Qui enim DEUM diligit, castè ei adhaeret, spiritualem scortationem, i. e. idololatriam, & peccata contra conscientiam fugiendo. Dilectio proximi describitur per φιλαδελφίαν.

5. Est virginitas mentis & ventris, absque illa haec parùm prodest. Aug. lib. de virg. cap. 18. Virginitas mentis consistit in fidei sinceritate, & cordis à pravis ustionibus puritate.

6. Dilectio proximi debet esse ἀνυπόκριτος & ἐκτενὴς.

7. Eandem oportet ex puro corde profluere. Cor est fons affectuum. Ut limpida hauriatur aqua, fontem purum esse oportet.

8. Verbum Evangelii est medium regenerationis & vivificationis. Regenerat nos non solùm θεωρητικῶς, ut sic loquar, quatenus mentes illustrat cognitione divinae voluntatis, ac monstrat nobis, quid credendum ac faciendum, sed etiam πρακτικῶς, quatenus flectit voluntatem ad assensum divini testimonii, efficaciter cor movet & immutat, accendit in eo fidem, quâ gratiam DEI in Christò oblatam amplectimur, inque eâ pacatè acquiescimus, & per hanc fidem filii DEI, & heredes vitae aeternae reddimur. Vivificat nos, non solùm quaetenus gustandum nobis praebet DEI favorem, & vivificâ consolatione nos erigit, sed etiam quatenus vitae spiritualis nos participes facit.

9. Vivum est DEI verbum, tùm quia est verbum DEI viventis, tùm quia insitam habet vim vivificam, tùm quia Spiritus sanctus per illud veros & vivos motus spirituales in cordibus operatur. Secundum sequitur ex primo, tertium ex secundo.

10. Verbum DEI manet in aeternum, non solùm, quia Evangelium de Christo, fide perceptum, efficax est, ut credentibus tribuat vitam aeternam, sed etiam, quia in se, quatenus DEI sensum & consilium complectitur, est aeternum.

11. Quale semen, talis nativitas; qualis nativitas, talis vita & vice versâ. Ex semine carnali & corruptibili oritur nativitas carnalis & corruptibilis; ubi nativitas carnalis, ibi etiam vita carnalis. Ex semine incorruptibili oritur incorruptibilis & spiritualis nativitas. Ubi nativitas spiritualis, ibi vita spiritualis.

12. Proseminamur ex Adamo per peccatum corrupto, inde haec satio est corrupta φθαρτὴ, non solùm quia corpus corruptioni & morti obnoxium, sed etiam quia anima peccati labe miserè defoedata, unde quatenus ab Adamo descendimus, sumus omnes filii iraeEph. 2. v. 3. morti & damnationi obnoxii, adeoque priùs damnati, quàm nati.

13. Homo per Naturam caro, quia, quod ex carne natum, caro est,Ioh. 3. v. 6. Carnis autem nomine non solùm Naturae humanae fragilitas, sed etiam eiusdem per peccatum corruptio denotatur.

14. Cum de carne, & eius gloria, Propheta loquitur, totum hominem, qualis est per Naturam, describit, unde inter opera carnis etiam haereses, quae sunt mentis vitia, ab Apostolo referuntur, Gal. 5. v. 20.

15. Homo ob vitae fugacitatem & brevitatem rectè confertur foeno. Iob. 14. v. 2.Psal. 90. v. 6.Esa. 40. v. 6.Sirac. 14. v. 18.Iac. 1. v. 10. Foenum nascendo habet virorem, crescendo vigorem, deinde etiam florem, sed falce resectum, & ardore Solis exiceatum, omnem virorem, vigorem & florem amittit: sic homo per aetatum successionem, amittit decorem, & redigitur in pulverem.

16. Omnis gloria hominis carnalis est sicut flos agri. Ratio excogitat varias felicitatis vias, sed evanidae eae sunt, atque frustraneae, & omnis illa gloria tandem evanescit.

17. Verbum DEI manet in aeternum, ideò est panacaea immortalitatis. Qui enim fide amplectitur verbum, ille in verbo, & cum verbo servatur ad vitam aeternam. Non est stabilis & vera vita, nisi in DEO, ea vero non communicatur, nisi per verbum fide apprehensum 1. Ioh. 2. v. 17. Mundus transit, & concupiscentia eius. Qui facit voluntatem DEI, manet in aeternum.

18. Verbum DEI, per quod regeneramur, vivificamur, & ad vitam aeternam conservamur, non est quaerendum in coelo, sed ut nobis in terris est patefactum, non ut in corde DEI latet clausum, sed ut ab ore eius profectum, ac in Prophetarum & Apostolorum scriptis comprehensum, nobis innotuit. Roman. 10. vers. 6.Ne dixeris in corde, Quis ascendet in coelum?vers. 7.aut quis descendet in abyssum?vers. 8.propè est verbum in ore tuo, & in corde tuo, hoc est verbum fidei, quod praedicamus.

Summa capitis. Exhortationis ad fidei constantiam, & vitae innocentiam continuatio. Partes duae sunt, Prior generalis, à vers. 1. usque ad v. 13. directa ad omnes cuiusvis status & conditionis Christianos Posterior specialis, â v. 13. usque ad finem capitis, ad subditos & servos directa.

Pars prior tribus absolvitur membris. 1. Propositione. 2. Confirmatione. 3. Conclusione sive propositionis repetitione. Propositio continet tùm ἀποτροπὴν à vitiis caritati Christianae adversantibus, tùm προτροπὴν ad studium proficiendi ex verbo Evangelii in fide vera & vita sancta. Ἀποτροπὴ hisce exprimitur verbis.

## 2:1
LAYING ASIDE THEREFORE ALL MALICE AND ALL GUILE, AND HYPOCRISIES AND ENVIES AND ALL EVIL SPEAKINGS.

Connection. 1. Toward the end of the preceding chapter v. 22. the Apostle had exhorted to φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον,, now furthermore he dissuades them from vices opposed to brotherly charity.

2. In v. 23. of the preceding chapter he had made mention of regeneration, through which both as children of GOD and brothers among themselves, he infers from that an admonition concerning the fleeing of vices, which most especially disgrace the children of GOD and spiritual brothers. For that this admonition is deduced by way of inference from the preceding, the particle οὖν. shows.

3. In the previous chapter, he had exhorted in general to the study of piety; now in particular he teaches the manner in which piety is to be exercised and demonstrated.

Explanation of the text. Ἀποθέμενοι οὺν. The Vulgate rendered it in the present Laying aside therefore. But in the Greek it is an aorist, therefore it is more correctly rendered, Having laid aside therefore all malice, as Augustine reads in homily 20 among the fifty, or after you have laid aside, for it signifies that, in the regeneration and renewal made through Baptism, that laying aside of malice has indeed begun to be done, but is still to be continued daily, in which sense also the verb of the present tense rightly agrees with this place. Furthermore, the little word for laying aside, when it is a matter of sending away vices and putting off the old man, is customary for the Apostles, as the parallel passages teach. Eph. 4. v. 22.To put off according to the former conversation the old man.Col. 3. v. 8.But now do you also put away all, anger, indignation &c.Hebr. 12. v. 1.Laying aside every weight, and the sin which surrounds us.Iacob. 1. v. 21.Laying aside all filthiness and abundance of malice. The Syrian in this place rendered [consult facsimile image] Make to cease, by which very thing he explains the metaphor of putting off. Πασαν κακίαν. Some take the noun κακίας as a genus, not only of the subsequent, but also of all other vices, fighting against both tables of the divine law, in which meaning it is usedAct. 8. v. 22. & in this verycap. 2. v. 16. in which sense also Blessed Luther in the first copies rendered it, was bo se ist. The Syrian has the noun [consult facsimile image] from the root [consult facsimile image] he stank. The sense therefore would be: Put away, whatever is evil and wicked, and thus unworthy of a Christian man and name, still remaining in your flesh. But it is more correctly taken as a certain species of vices fighting against Christian charity, 1. For the scope of the Apostle is to enumerate five distinct species of such vices. 2. In other Apostolic sayings it is likewise taken in a special sense, and is placed in the midst of special vices Rom. 1. v. 29.1. Cor. 5. v. 8.Eph. 4. v. 31.Coloss. 3. v. 8.Tit. 3. v. 3.Iac. 1. v. 21. Nor can the contrary be gathered from the little word πᾶσαν, because the same is immediately added to guile and detractions. Therefore a determined Universality of those things which pertain to this species of vice is signified. Furthermore κακίαν Jerome defines in chapter 4 of Eph. malignity, which is felt in tergiversation and craftiness. Augustine in book 50. homil. 20. the love of harming, when someone is delighted by another's evil. In Scripture it is joined with πονηρίᾳ Rom. 1. vers. 29.1. Cor. 5. v. 8. from which according to some it is distinguished thus, that πονηρία is the depravity of the intellect and will, κακία but malice is of the will only. From which arose the distinction between sins of ignorance, of infirmity, and of malice. The sense therefore is: Put away that interior perversity, by which someone deliberately inflicts evil upon a neighbor, and indeed lay it aside in such a way that you strip off all malice, that is, that you perfectly renounce it, which little word ἀπὸ κοινοῦ the Apostle teaches is to be repeated in the remaining vices, when he joins it both to deceit and to slanders.

CHAPTER II.

Lay aside also. 2. Πάντα δόλον. Deceit is opposed to simplicity and truth, whence it is defined as a contrivance of fraud for circumventing someone by words or deeds. Dyers, when they introduce another color to wool, are called by the Greeks δολοῦν, and δόλωνες are hidden daggers and poniards, with which someone deceitfully attacks another. Plutarch in Tiberius. Jurists distinguish between good deceit, by which they understand nothing other than lawful cleverness, especially against an enemy and a robber, and evil deceit, concerning which Ulpian speaks in law 1, ff. de dolo malo. Servius defines evil deceit thus: a certain contrivance for the sake of deceiving another, when one thing is done and another is simulated. Labeo defines it thus: that evil deceit is every craftiness, fallacy, or contrivance applied for the purpose of circumventing, deceiving, or defrauding another. In Cicero, 3. De Officiis, Aquilius says that evil deceit is when one thing was simulated and another was done. For in words deceit is a lie 1. Petr. 2. v. 22., in works it is simulation Act. 13. v. 10., in the heart it is the contrivance of fraud Matth. 26. v. 4.. The sense, therefore, is that the truly pious ought to renounce all kinds of frauds and impostures, by which men of this age are accustomed to circumvent others in dealings and actions, and ought to study the opposite virtue, namely, simplicity and truth.

Lay aside, 3. Ὑποκρίσεις, simulations. This is a vice related to deceit, when someone displays benevolence and love in his countenance which he does not, however, have in his mind; hypocrisy in general is when someone by words, gestures, and external deeds pretends to be someone other than he truly is, but here it is taken specifically concerning the painted simulation of love and benevolence toward a neighbor. Thus Matth. 22. v. 18. Christ calls the disciples of the Pharisees, who were simulating benevolence by external words, hypocrites, and Marc. 12. v. 15. he is said to have seen their hypocrisy. Augustine, in the first place, translates it as adulations, either reading something else, or, which is more likely, putting the species for the genus. For flatterers are the worst hypocrites. The sense, therefore, is that the truly pious ought to renounce the false signification of love toward a neighbor, and ought to study the opposite virtue, namely, candor.

Lay aside. 4. φθόνους envies. Envy is an unjust sorrow conceived from the temporal or spiritual goods of a neighbor, a vice clearly Diabolical, diametrically opposed to Christian charity.

Finally 5. Lay aside πᾶσας καταλαλιὰς. the Vulgate rendered detractions, that is, slanders, by which the reputation and name of an absent neighbor is maliciously detracted. 2. Cor. 12. v. 20. likewise ζῆλοι & καταλαλιαὶ envies & slanders are joined. The emphasis is in the particle added πᾶσας because, as John Huss advises in his commentary on this place, detraction is committed in many ways, either by denying the good, or by obscuring it, or by diminishing it, or by ascribing evil, or by perverting the intention in a good work. Therefore, when the Apostle πᾶσαν κακίαν, πάντα δὸλον καὶ πᾶσας καταλαλιὰς commands to be laid aside, he wishes that no malice, deceit, and malevolence, nor any species of slander, should remain among the pious.

Latin:

DEPONENTES IGITUR OMNEM MALITIAM & OMNEM DOLUM, & SIMULATIONES & INVIDIAS & OMNES DETRECTATIONES.

Connexio. 1. Sub finem capitis praecedentis v. 22. hortatus fuerat Apostolus ad φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον, iam porrò dehortatur eos à vitiis fraternae caritati oppositis.

2. In v. 23. praecedentis capitis mentionem fecerat regenerationis, per quam & DEI filii & fratres inter se effecti, ex eo infert admonitionem de fugiendis vitiis, DEI filios & fratres spirituales maximè dedecentibus. Quòd enim haec admonitio per modum illationis ex praecedentibus deducatur, ostendit particula οὖν.

3. In capite superiore, in genere ad studium pietatis hortatus fuerat, nunc in specie docet modum, quo pietas exercenda sit & demonstranda.

Textus explicatio. Ἀποθέμενοι οὺν. Vulgata reddidit in praesenti Deponentes igitur. Sed in Graeco est aoristus, ideò rectiùs redditur, Depositâ igitur omni malitiâ, prout legit Augustinus homil. 20. inter quinquaginta, vel postquam deposuistis, significat enim, in regeneratione ac renovatione per Baptismum factâ, depositionem illam malitiae fieri quidem caepisse, sed adhuc quotidiè esse continuandam, quo sensu etiam verbum praesentis temporis rectè huic loco congruit. Caeterùm deponendi vocula, quando de nuncio vitiis mittendo & veteri homine exuendo agitur, Apostolis est usitata, ut docent loca parallela. Eph. 4. v. 22.Deponere secundum pristinam conversationem veterem hominem.Col. 3. v. 8.Nunc autem deponite vos omnia, iram, indignationem &c.Hebr. 12. v. 1.Deponentes omne pondus, & circumstans hoc peccatum.Iacob. 1. v. 21.Deponentes omnem immunditiem & abundantiam malitiae. Syrus hoc loco reddidit [consult facsimile image]Cessare faeite, quo ipso deponendi metaphoram explicat. Πασαν κακίαν. Nomen κακίας quidam accipiunt ut genus, non solùm subsequentium, sed etiam omnium aliorum vitiorum, cum utraque divinae legis tabula pugnantium, in qua significatione usurpaturAct. 8. v. 22. & in hoc ipsocap. 2. v. 16. quo sensu etiam B. Lutherus in primis exemplar. reddidit, was bo se ist. Syrus habet nomen [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image] foetuit. Sensus igitur foret. Deponite, quicquid malum atque improbum, adeoque Christiano homine & nomine indignum, in carne vestra adhuc reliquum. Sed rectiùs accipitur, ut species quaedam vitiorum cum caritate Christianâ pugnantium, 1. Scopus enim Apostoli est, enumerare quinque distinctas eiusmodi vitiorum species. 2. In aliis dictis Apostolicis itidem in sensu speciali accipitur, ac in medio vitiorum specialium ponitur Rom. 1. v. 29.1. Cor. 5. v. 8.Eph. 4. v. 31.Coloss. 3. v. 8.Tit. 3. v. 3.Iac. 1. v. 21. Nec potest contrarium ex vocula πᾶσαν colligi, quia eadem statim additur dolo & obtrectationibus. Significatur igitur determinata Universalitas eorum, quae ad hanc vitii speciem pertinent. Porrò κακίαν definit Hieronymus in cap. 4. Eph. malignitatem, quae in tergiversatione & calliditate sentitur. Augustinus in libro 50. homil. 20. nocendi amorem, cum quis malo delectatur alieno. In Scriptura coniungitur cum πονηρίᾳRom. 1. vers. 29.1. Cor. 5. v. 8. à quâ iuxta quosdam ita distinguitur, utπονηρίαsit pravitas intellectus & voluntatis,κακίαverò voluntatis tantùm malitia. Ex quo orta distinctio inter peccata ignorantiae, infirmitatis & malitiae. Sensus igitur est: Deponite interiorem illam perversitatem, quâ quis datâ operâ proximo malum infert, & quidem ita eam deponite, ut omnem malitiam exuatis h. e. ut perfectè eidem renuncietis, quam voculam ἀπὸ κοινοῦ in reliquis vitiis repetendam docet Apostolus, quando & dolo & obtrectationibus eandem coniungit.

CAPUT II.

Deponite etiam. 2. Πάντα δόλον.Dolus opponitur simplicitati ac veritati, unde definitur machinatio fraudis ad aliquem circumveniendum verbis vel factis. Tinctores cum lanae alium colorum inducunt, Graecis dicuntur δολοῦν, ac δόλωνες sunt occultae sicae ac pugiones, quibus alium dolosè quis petit. Plutarch. in Tiberio. ICti distinguunt inter dolum bonum, per quem nihil aliud intelligunt, quàm solertiam licitam praesertim contra hostem & latronem, ac dolum malum, de quo Ulpianus l. 1. ff. de dolo malo. Dolum malum Servius ita definit, machinationem quandam alterius decipiendi causâ, cum aliud agitur, & aliud simulatur. Labeo sic definit, dolum malum esse omnem calliditatem, fallaciam, machinationem ad circumveniendum, fallendum, decipiendum alterum, adhibitam. Apud Ciceronem 3. offic. Aquilius dolum malum esse dicit, cùm aliud esset simulatum, aliud actum. In verbis enim dolus est mendacium 1. Petr. 2. v. 22. in operibus simulatio, Act. 13. v. 10. in corde fraudis machinatio. Matth. 26. v. 4. Sensus igitur est, quòd verè pii omnis generis fraudibus & imposturis, quibus in commerciis & actionibus homines huius seculi alios circumvenire solent, renunciare & virtuti oppositae, videlicet simplicitati ac veritati studere debeant.

Deponite, 3. Ὑποκρίσεις,simulationes. Cognatum hoc est dolo vitium, cum quis benevolentiam & amorem praefert in vultu, quem tamen non habet in animo; Hypocrisis in genere est cum quis verbis, gestibus & factis externis alium se esse simulat, quàm revera est, hîc vero in specie accipitur de fucata amoris & benevolentiae erga proximum simulatione. Sic Matth. 22. v. 18. discipulos Pharisaeorum benevolentiam verbis externis simulantes Christus vocat hypocritas, ac Marc. 12. v. 15. eorum Hypocrisin vidisse dicitur. Augustinus d. 1. vertit adulationes vel aliud quid legens, vel quod verisimilius pro genere ponens speciem. Adulatores enim sunt hypocritae pessimi. Sensus igitur est, quod verè pii falsae amoris erga proximum significationi renunciare, & oppositae virtuti, candori scilicet studere debeant.

Deponite. 4. φθόνουςinvidentias. Invidia est dolor iniustus ex bonis proximi temporalibus, vel spiritualibus conceptus, vitium planè Diabolicum, caritati Christianae diametraliter oppositum.

Denique 5. Deponiteπᾶσας καταλαλιὰς. Vulgata reddidit detractiones, h. e. obtrectationes, quibus proximi absentis famae ac nomini malitiosè detrahitur. 2. Cor. 12. v. 20. itidem ζῆλοι & καταλαλιαὶinvidiae & obtrectationes coniunguntur. Emphasis est in particula adiecta πᾶσας quia, ut monet Iohannes Hussus in comm. h. l. multis modis committitur detractio, aut bonum negando, aut obfuscando, aut diminuendo, aut malum adscribendo, aut intentionem in bono opere pervertendo. Quando igitur Apostolus πᾶσαν κακίαν, πάντα δὸλον καὶ πᾶσας καταλαλιὰς deponi iubet, nihil malitiae, doli ac malevolentiae, nec ullam obtrectationis speciem apud pios vult esse reliquam.

## 2:1-3 Questions and observations
Questions 1. Why did the Apostle wish to make mention of these vices only, when there are still more that are opposed to Christian and brotherly love? Resp. 1. It is the custom of Scripture to understand the whole genus from one or more species; hence also, when the Apostles treat of putting off the old man, they propose certain vices as an example, by which they describe his whole character. Galat. 5. v. 19.Eph. 4. v. 25.Col. 3. v. 8. 2. The vices which are enumerated in this place are so constituted that the later ones are born from the earlier ones. Malice is a depraved desire of harming, which is directly opposed to the source of love. Guile arises from malice, when, namely, a deception is intended out of a desire to harm someone. Simulation arises from guile, and is its daughter or certainly its own sister, when, namely, something else is shown outwardly than what lies hidden inwardly in the mind. Envy is the companion of simulation, when someone is tormented by another's good. From envy proceed detractions, which detract from another's reputation and praise.

Q. 2. What is understood by the Apostle here by the name of milk? 1. Calvin in his commentary on this place establishes that by the name of milk the Apostle comprehends all the affections of spiritual life, so that there is in this part an antithesis between the vices which he recounts and the rational milk: as if he had said, malice and simulation belong to those who, accustomed to the corruptions of the world, have imbibed these vices; the sincere simplicity of infancy, pure from all guile, is fitting. The opinion of Hemmingius is the same. By the name of milk, he says, is signified a manner of living consistent with simple infancy. Cornelius à Lapide on this place: Milk is a symbol of candor, sincerity, and benevolence; for Peter opposes this milk to guile, simulation, and envy; by it, therefore, he signifies that he wishes that Christians in their conversation should not be sour, harsh, and full of gall, but honeyed and milky, that is, candid, amiable, sweet, benign, beneficent, fraternally loving, helping, and promoting one another, so that an allusion is made to Cantic. 5. vers. 1.Esa. 7. vers. 15.cap. 55. vers. 1. 1. Estius establishes that this exposition, by which is understood by milk every kind of Christian virtue, comes to the same thing as that by which are understood by milk the precepts of faith and morals. But the Apostle treats of such milk through which we progress in the knowledge and faith of CHRIST. 2. Clement of Alexandria, book 1, Paedagogus, chapter 6, by verbal milk understands the incarnate Word, namely CHRIST, since the Apostle immediately adds concerning him, if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is sweet. Augustine, tractate 3, on the Epistle Ioh. 1. Our milk is the humble Christ. For he himself is the milk, i.e., nourishment of the little ones and the humble, through him we flee as if to the breast of the Father, that we may suck grace and every good thing from it. His words are milky, i. e. sweet and gracious. Cant. 4. v. 11. 3. Salmero, Estius in h. l. Turrianus lib. 2. de Eucharist. cap. 20. by milk understand the Eucharist. For it was once given to those baptized, even to infants, immediately after Baptism, Dionys. de Hierarch. Eccles. cap. 5. which agrees with that which Peter says, as newborn infants desire the rational milk. For the Eucharist is truly rational milk, because in it the rational man i. e. Christ is present. It has the same spiritual power of nourishing our souls, and before its reception it is necessary to lay aside all malice, guile, envy etc. it itself as the food of minds ought to be taken with such greed as infants suck the nipples of the mother, nay with far greater, says Chrysost, homil. 60. ad pop. Antioch. Through it the sweetness of divine goodness is tasted in its source. 4. Most simply, and according to the mind of the Apostle, by milk is understood the pure doctrine of the Gospel. 1. For the Apostle had compared that v. 23. cap. preceding to an incorruptible seed, through which they had been regenerated, here he compares the same to milk, through which they might be nourished in the spiritual life. 2. At the end of the preceding chapter he had said. This is the word, which has been evangelized to you. That very word of the Gospel, by the example of newborn infants desirous of milk, he wishes them to desire. 3. He calls it τὸ λογικὸν γάλα verbal milk or milk of the word, as Clement of Alexandria explains lib. 1. paedag. cap. 6. so that he may express the subject, which he compares to milk. 4. The word of the Gospel is that salutary medium, through which we are nourished and grow in the spiritual life. Esai. 38. v. 16. Matth. 4. v. 4. 5. Also in other sayings of Scripture the doctrine of the Gospel is compared to milk, Cant. 4. v. 11. cap. 5. v. 1. Esai. 51. v. 1. 1 Cor. 3. v. 2. Hebr. 5. v. 12. etc. 6. But especially the passage Iac. 1. v. 21. pertains here, clearly parallel to this one of ours; Wherefore laying aside all filthiness and abundance of malice, in meekness receive the engrafted word, which can save your souls. 7. The properties of milk agree with the word of the Gospel, as will soon appear. This therefore is the proper and principal exposition, the others are accommodative and less principal.

Q. 3. Why is the Gospel compared to milk? Resp. 1. on account of purity. Maternal milk, which infants suck, is white, pure, having nothing foreign mixed in, thus the word of the Gospel is pure and immaculate. Psal. 19. v. 8. 2. On account of sweetness. of the interior the taste of man perceives its sweetness in temptations, Psal. 19. v. 13.Psal. 119. v. 39. & 103. &c. 3. Because of the power of nourishing, nay even of fattening, which reason of comparison Peter himself expresses. 4. Because of the power of washing. Cant. 5. v. 12. the eyes of the spiritual bride are called dove-like washed with milk, and Thren. 4. v. 7. the Nazarites are said to be brighter than milk. Thus the word of the Gospel cleanses our souls Ioh 15. v. 3. and makes them beautiful and bright. Psal. 51. vers. 9. 5. Because of the power of inducing sleep. Milk induces sleep in infants, and takes away the sense of other things, Psal. 131. v. 2. but also Sisera after a drink of milk is overcome by sleep Iud. 4. v. 19. Thus the doctrine of the Gospel renders the mind quiet and recalls it from earthly things. Clement of Alexandria, book 1, Paedagogus, chapter 6. Certainly you will find nothing that nourishes better, nor that is sweeter than milk, nor that is whiter than milk. It is therefore in every part similar to spiritual nourishment, which is indeed sweet because of grace, nourishing however as life, white however as the day of Christ, and the blood of the Word has been shown to be as milk.

Q. 4. Why it is called milk λογικὸν? Resp. Those who τὸ λογικὸν translate as rational, bring forward various reasons. 1. By reason of origin. The word of doctrine and of the mouth flows forth from the mind, as milk from the breast. 2. By reason of the object, because the word of GOD is received by the rational soul. 3. By reason of the effect, the Word of GOD informs the mind, and makes men truly prudent Psal. 19. v. 9.Matth. 10. v. 16. 4 By reason of the contrary. Lest anyone should think that an infancy devoid of intelligence and full of foolishness is being praised, he commands them to desire rational milk, and that milk, which he commands them to desire, he wishes to be as if seasoned with intelligence, 1. Cor. 14. v. 20. Do not become children in senses, but in malice be infants. Others τὸ λογικὸν translate as spiritual, in which way also the Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] Luth. Geistlich thus therefore the Apostle would signify that he is not speaking of bodily milk, but spiritual, in which sense also Rom. 12. v. 1. rational service is called, which is spiritual, in distinction to the bodily sacrifices prescribed in the O. T. Bodily milk is given to infants not yet having the use of reason, but spiritual milk is given to adults, who can hear, understand, and meditate upon the word of GOD. Some think this was added to express the difference between spiritual and animal doctrine, heavenly and earthly. That in divine mysteries is truly λογικὴ, This truly ἂλογος, 1. Corinth. 1. vers. 20.James 3. vers. 15. & 17. to what does it pertain, which blessed Luther determined to be signified, that the Gospel is not to be received by a carnal sense, but by a spiritual one, namely through faith.
