Some think that by τὸ λογικὸς it is signified prudent, moderate, discreet. But if by τὸ λογικὸν γἁλα one understands τοῦ λόγου γάλα, the whole matter is in the open.

Q. 5. Why it is called milk ἄδολον? Resp. 1. By reason of itself. It is in itself sincere and pure, flowing down to us from the breasts of divine wisdom. 2. By reason of us. Such a word is to be desired, which is not mixed with false doctrine and the corruptions of men, which is not adulterated by human opinions. 2. Cor. 2. v. 17.chap. 4. v. 2. otherwise it will not be pure milk, but wheyey and watery. 3. By reason of the effect, that milk taken by faith renders men ἀδόλους and simple, and therefore such as the Apostle requires in v. 1. no one using it is deceived, as men are otherwise deceived by poisonous drinks and deceitful love potions.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Peter commands all guile to be laid aside. But2. Cor. 12. v. 16.being crafty, I caught you with guile. Resp. 1. Some determine that Paul speaks of good guile. 2. It is more correctly said that the Apostle is reciting an objection of the false Apostles.

2. That Doctor of the Gentiles, D. Paul, argues as carnal and imperfect those who still need the nourishment of milk,1. Corinth. 3. v. 1.I could not speak to you as to spiritual, but as to carnal, as to little ones in Christv. 2.I gave you milk to drink, not meat, for you were not yet able.Hebr. 5. v. 12.when you ought to be masters for the time, you have become such as have need of milk, and not of solid food.v. 13.For everyone who is a partaker of milk is unskillful in the word of justice, for he is a little one.v. 14.but solid food is for the perfect. Peter, however, exhorts all the faithful in general to desire milk. Resp. 1. Those who by the name of milk here understand a manner of living agreeable to the simplicity of infancy, respond that the name of milk in this place is not opposed to perfect food, but to the oldness of the flesh, for milk indeed is of those who are new men. There, says Calvin, they are compared to boys, who in the doctrine of piety are always novices and raw recruits, who stick in the first elements, and never penetrate into a higher knowledge of GOD, and milk is called a coarser and childish form of teaching, when there is never any progress beyond the first rudiments, but here indeed milk is not elementary doctrine so that perpetually who may learn, yet never arrive at the knowledge of the truth, but a way of life, which may savor of a new birth. 2. But because we showed above that by the name of milk the Evangelical doctrine is properly and principally understood here, it must be answered that by the name of milk 1. Corinth. 3. v. 2.Hebr. 5. vers. 12. is understood in particular the Elementary doctrine, and a manner of teaching suitable to the more unlearned and weak, to which is opposed solid food, which is for the perfect: but here by the name of milk in general is understood the Evangelical doctrine, through which both the weak and the perfect are nourished unto eternal life. August. tract. 98. in Iohan. Those very things, which spiritual and carnal persons hear at the same time, they each grasp according to their own measure, the former as little ones, the latter as greater ones, the former as the nourishment of milk, the latter as the solid food. And afterwards. CHRIST crucified is both milk to those who suck, and food to those who are progressing.

3. Incap. 1. v. 13.he commanded them to hope perfectly in that grace which is offered to them. But here he compares them to newborn infants. Resp. Although with respect to the more unlearned and weaker ones some in this life are said to be perfect, who through the habit of knowledge, acquired by diligent meditation on the word through the grace and efficacy of the Holy Spirit, have their senses exercised for the discernment of good and evil Hebr. 5. vers. 14. yet by comparison with the manly and perfect age, which we shall attain only in the future age Ephes. 4. vers. 13. as long as we live here, we are little ones Psalm. 131. vers. 2.1. Corinth. 13. vers. 11. Compare Augustine on Psalm 130, where among other things he says: You will not be separated from milk, as long as you are upon your mother, lest you die of hunger before you are fit to eat bread. And afterwards. Those who eat solid food seem to be perfect, because they understand the equality of the Word with the Father. As yet they do not see as it is to be seen, face to face, as yet in part in a riddle.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Peter says that those to whom he writes are reborn from the incorruptible seed of the word, and yet he commands them to lay aside all malice, all guile, etc. Therefore, renewal is not perfect in this life, but the reborn are still in part carnal Roman. 7. v. 14. sin still dwells in their flesh vers. 18. and clings closely to them in this life Hebr. 12. v. 1. which is to be opposed to the Papists, who decree that through Baptism everything which has the nature of sin is extinguished and abolished in the reborn.

2. We do not bring with us to Christ, when we are reborn through the Gospel, any merit of congruity, as the Papists wish, but a heavy burden of sin, in the laying aside of which it behooves us to be occupied throughout the whole course of this life.

3. Peter appeals to the own experience of the pious, that they have tasted the kindness of GOD. The Pope denies that the pious can be certain in this life that they are in grace before GOD, which cannot be reconciled with the spiritual taste of divine kindness.

4. The Psalmist says, Taste, how sweet Jehovah is. Peter teaches that Christ is He whose sweetness the pious have tasted. Therefore Christ is the true Jehovah. Against the Photinians.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. From the fact that Peter commands to lay aside all malice, all deceit, etc., the patrons of perfection gather that a man in this life can be without sin. Resp. 1. This command lasts through the whole life of a reborn man, nor is it ever so perfectly fulfilled that something of malice does not always remain to be laid aside, 2. James ch. 1. v. 21. explains it thus, Laying aside πὲρισσείαν κακίας, the abundance of malice. Although therefore the exuberant abundance of malice is laid aside, its vicious root nevertheless still remains in this life.

2. From the fact that we are commanded to grow in salvation by the spiritual milk, Cornelius à Lapide gathers the merits of works. He indicates, he says, that Peter, that Christians ought to grow in virtues throughout their whole life until death, through which they will go to salvation and eternal life. For the life of grace grows in act, through the merits of works, but the life of glory grows through the same in hope and right, for greater merits give a greater right to glory, and a greater one at that. Resp. 1. προσδιορισμὸς unto salvation, is not held in the Greek Codices. 2. By milk are not understood Christian virtues, as Cornelius wishes, but the doctrine of the Gospel.

3. Nor is the doctrine of the Gospel γενικῶς accepted, as Estius wishes, when he writes, By the name of milk is understood the Evangelical doctrine, that is, precepts of faith and morals: but the doctrine of the Gospel εἰδικῶς & κυρίως so called, concerning the gratuitous remission of sins on account of Christ, which is the medium of both regeneration and spiritual nutrition. 4. When we are said to grow in virtues unto salvation, then the end of spiritual increase is described, but not the meritorious cause of salvation is expressed. Bernard, Treatise on Grace and Free Choice, col. 1069. If those things which we call our merits are properly named, they are certain seeds of hope, incentives of charity, signs of hidden predestination, presages of future happiness, a way of the kingdom, not a cause of reigning.

3. From the fact that the milk of doctrine is called λογικὸν, and our worship λογικὸς Romans 12, v. 1., Smalcius gathers in his later Disputation 8 against the Augustan Confession of Frantz, p. 421, that nothing is to be believed which is opposed to reason, etc. But what is to be understood by τὸ λογικὸν in this place was explained in question 4.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The first degree of piety is to cease from evil. Psalm 34, v. 15. 1 Peter 3, v. 12. For unless evils are first laid aside, it is by no means possible to have leisure for good works.

2. The whole first birth, which we draw from Adam, is vicious; whatever we have from it must be laid aside.

3. It is not enough to lay aside malice once, but this laying aside and stripping off of the old man must be continued throughout the whole life. Bernard, Epistle 253. Between progress and defect in this state of mortal life no middle ground is found, but just as it is certain that our body itself is continually either growing or decreasing: so it is necessary that the Spirit also either always progresses or fails.

4. The word 'laying aside' used by the Apostle concerning sin shows that sin is a heavy burden, depressing man to hell, unless it is cast off in this life. Ambrose, vol. 2, fol. 532, to Horantianus. No burden is heavier than the pack of sins and the weight of crimes. It depresses the soul, it bows it down even to the earth, so that it cannot raise itself up.

5. The laying aside of the old man with his deeds is the demonstration of a true Christian. Cyprian, Sermon on Zeal and Envy, after he had brought forward the Apostolic passage 1 Corinthians 15, v. 50., adds: We cannot bear the heavenly image unless we show the likeness of Christ in that which we have now begun to be. This is indeed to have changed what you were, and to have begun what you were not, so that the divine birth may shine in you, so that the deifying discipline may correspond to God the Father, so that God may shine in man by the honor and praise of living.

6. Charity is the inseparable property of the truly pious. Therefore, the truly pious ought especially to flee vices contrary to charity. Augustine Book 50. of homilies, homily 20. What is malice, if not the love of harming? What is deceit, if not to do one thing and simulate another? What is flattery, if not seduction by fallacious praise? What is envy, if not hatred of another's happiness? What is detraction, if not a criticism more biting than it is truthful? Malice delights in another's evil. Envy is tormented by another's good. Deceit doubles the heart, flattery the tongue; detraction wounds reputation.

7. It is for the pious to do nothing maliciously or deceitfully, but with a candid mind to direct all actions to the glory of GOD and the utility of the neighbor. John 1. v. 47.

8. It befits Christians to have dove-like simplicityMatt. 10. verse 16. and sheep-likeJohn 10. verse 27. from which all hypocrisy and simulation should be banished. Romans 12. verse 9. Let charity be ἀνυπόκριτος. Origen, homily 25. on Matthew. Hypocrisy is not a good, but a simulation of good, nor is it justice, but a figment of justice; in reality, however, it is the greatest iniquity and the worst evil.

9. Meditation on the communion of saints is the best remedy for envy. For since we are members of one mystical body, let no one envy another's happiness and gifts. Augustine, 15. on the city of GOD, chapter 5. In no way does the possession of goodness become smaller by the arrival or presence of a partner; rather, the possession of goodness becomes so much the broader, the more concordant the charity that possesses it undivided.

10. Detraction is a clearly Diabolical vice, because the Devil received his name from it. Chrysostom gives the reason in 2. homily on 2. Corinthians 1. ἐπειδὴ καὶ θεὸν πρὸς ἀνθρώπους διαβάλλει, καὶ ἡμᾶς πρὸς θεὸν καὶ πάλιν ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς πρὸς ἀλλήλους.

11. The baptized are as newborn infants, because Baptism is the washing of regeneration Tit. 3. verse 5. and the child-bearing of the kingdom of heaven. Chrysostom, homily 25. on John. τό δε ὕδωρ παρείλεται, τὸκος τῷ τικτομένω γενόμενον, ὅπερ γὰρ ἐστὶν ἡ μήτρα τῷ ἐμβρύῳ, τοῦτο τῷ πιστῷ τὸ ὕδωρ. The water taken up becomes a birth for him who is brought forth. For what the womb is to the embryo, that the water is to the faithful. Paulinus. Thence the Priest, parent, leads from the sacred font infants snowy in body, heart, and habit.

12. The reborn are as newborn infants, therefore infantile innocence, purity, humility, obedience, docility, ease, simplicity, and sincerity ought to be commended to them. Matt. 18. v. 3.

13. The Word of the Gospel is the seed from which we are regenerated; and the food and drink of our souls, by which we are nourished. Clement of Alexandria, book 1, Paedagogus, chapter 8. The Word is everything, both father and mother to the infant, and tutor and nourisher. Chrysostom, homily 16 on the Epistle to the Romans. The Word of GOD is as it were the womb of the Church, in which we are not only formed and begotten to Christianity, but also nourished.

14. As the body is increased by nourishment, so also it is fitting that faith should grow by the hearing and meditation of the Gospel. Wine strengthens the body, the Word of GOD the soul. Nilus in Sententiae, volume 1, Orthodox, page 170.

15. The Gospel is milk for the more unlearned, and solid food for the perfect. Fulgentius, sermon on confession. The Scriptures, as the richest of dishes, have what is suitable for every age, what is appropriate for every profession: milky drink, by which infancy may be nourished, and solid food, by which robust youth may receive spiritual increases of virtue.

16. Meditation on the divine benefits exhibited in Christ is a sweet and milky food of the soul, through which we grow to the more solid food, which is hidden in scourges and the cross. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk Exod. 23. v. 19. that is, Christians who are still tender are not to be burdened with the doctrine of the cross, but first to be refreshed with the doctrine of the Gospel. Luther.

17. Seek the simple rudiments of faith first from the breasts of mother Church, that is, from the Doctors of both Testaments; who have either written the divine utterances or even preach them to you with a living voice.

18. Between those breasts, from which the milk of heavenly doctrine is drawn, the beloved bridegroom of the Church ought to dwell like a bundle of myrrh, that is, Christ suffered and crucified ought always to be preached in the Church and the memory of his passion constantly recalled. Cant. 1. v. 13. Luther on this passage.

19. The milk of Evangelical doctrine ought to be ἄδολον, The Doctors of the Church ought to propose it sincerely, the hearers to imbibe it candidly. Just as those who sell milk sometimes adulterate it with added water, so false teachers corrupt the doctrine of the Gospel with human opinions, as if with water less fit for nourishment. Esai. 1. vers. 22. Hence Irenaeus, book 3, chapter 19, says concerning heretics, that they mix gypsum with milk i. e. they infect heavenly doctrine with the poison of their error.

20. Milk does not nourish infants unless it is imbibed and into the of the body is changed in substance: thus the heavenly doctrine is to be received into the heart by faith, and converted into acts and morals. Tertullian, book on the resurrection of the flesh. The Word of GOD is to be sought for the sake of life, to be devoured by hearing, to be ruminated by the intellect, to be digested by faith.

21. Formerly, something of milk and honey was offered to the baptized to taste. Tertullian, book on the soldier's crown, chapter 3, which the Ethiopians still observe today, as appears from their Ritual, by which very thing they wished to express this Apostolic exhortation, as if by a certain type.

22. No one can regenerate himself, just as also no one can generate himself: meanwhile, the reborn person can and ought to desire and take up the milk of the word for his own spiritual growth.

23. The Word of GOD is the hidden manna Apoc. 2. v. 17. no one knows its sweetness, except he who tastes it.

24. Those who are drunk with bodily pleasures or with confidence in their own righteousness do not taste the sweetness of Evangelical doctrine and divine kindness. The Israelites loathed the manna, the taste of which was nevertheless most sweet. Sap. 16. v. 20. Bede. He who tastes nothing of heavenly sweetness in his soul, it is no wonder if he does not avoid defiling it with earthly allurements.

25. Christ is everywhere χρηστὸς useful, beneficial, and sweet to us in calling, receiving, illuminating, and defending us; in the remission of sins, in the pacification of the conscience, in consolation. John Huss on this passage. The Lord is sweet in contemplation for meditatingCant. 2. v. 3.in the spiritual ear for hearingCant. 5. v. 13.in the mouth for speakingPsal. 119. v. 39.in prospect for seeingSir. 23. v. 37.

26. In Christ we can taste the goodness and kindness of GOD. Matt. 11. v. 28. Clement of Alexandria, book 1, pedagogue, chapter 6. The nourishment of infants is the Lord, who is Spirit and word. That nourishment is the Lord Jesus, that is, The Word of GOD, is the incarnate Spirit, the sanctified heavenly flesh. The nutriment is the milk of the Father, by which only little infants are nourished. He therefore who is our beloved and nourisher, the Word, poured out his blood for us, bringing salvation to human Nature, through whom we who have believed in GOD flee to the breast of the Father, which induces forgetfulness of cares, namely the Word. He however alone, as is fitting, supplies to us infants the milk of love.

Latin:

Quaestiones 1. Quare horum duntaxat vitiorum Apostolus mentionem facere voluerit, cum plura adhuc dentur, quae Christianae & fraternae caritati adversantur? Resp. 1. Scripturae mos est, ex una vel pluribus speciebus totum genus intelligere, inde etiam cum de veteri homine deponendo Apostoli agunt, quaedam vitia in exemplum proponunt, quibus totum illius ingenium describunt. Galat. 5. v. 19.Eph. 4. v. 25.Col. 3. v. 8. 2. Vitia, quae hoc loco enumerantur, ita comparata sunt, ut posteriora ex prioribus nascantur. Malitia est prava cupiditas nocendi, quae dilectionis fonti directè adversatur. Dolus à malitia oritur, quando sc. ex cupiditate nocendi alicui fallacia intenditur. Simulatio ex dolo oritur, estque eiusdem filia vel certè germana soror, quando sc. aliud foris ostenditur, quàm in animo latet interiùs. Invidia est simulationis comes, quando quis alieno bono cruciatur. Ab invidia proficiscuntur obtrectationes, quae alienae famae ac laudi detrahunt.

Q. 2. Quid nomine lactis ab Apostolo hîc intelligatur? 1. Calvinus in comm. h. l. statuit, lactis nomine Apostolorum affectus omnes spiritualis vitae comprehendere, ut sit hac in parte antithesis inter vitia, quae recenset & lac rationale: ac si dixisset, malitia & simulatio eorum est, qui mundi corruptelis assuefacti haec vitia imbiberunt, infantiae sincera & omni dolo pura simplicitas convenit. Eadem est sententia Hemmingii. Lactis nomine, inquit, significatur consentanea simplici infantiae vivendi ratio. Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. Lac est symbolum candoris, sinceritatis & benevolentiae, hoc enim lac opponit Petrus dolo, simulationi, invidiae, per illud ergo significat, se velle, ut Christiani in suae conversatione non sint acidi, asperi & fellei, sed mellei & lactei, id est, candidi, amabiles, suaves, benigni, benefici, fraternè invicem diligentes, iuvantes, & promoventes, ut fiat allusio adCantic. 5. vers. 1.Esa. 7. vers. 15.cap. 55. vers. 1. 1. Estius statuit, hanc expositionem, quâ per lac intelligitur omne genus Christianarum virtutum, eodem recidere cum ea, qua per lac intelliguntur fidei ac morum praecepta. Sed de tali lacte Apostolus agit, per quod in cognitione & fide CHRISTI proficimus. 2. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 1. Paedagog. cap. 6. per lac verbale intelligit Verbum incarnatum, videlicet CHRISTUM, cum Apostolus de eo statim subiungat, siquidem gustastis, quoniam suavis est Dominus. August. tract. 3. in Epist. Ioh. 1.Lac nostrum Christus humilis est. Ipse enim est lac i. e. alimentum parvulorum & humilium, per ipsum q. lac ad mammam Patris confugimus, ut ex ea gratiam & omne bonum sugamus. Verba eius sunt lactea i. e. suavia & gratiosa.Cant. 4. v. 11. 3. Salmero, Estius in h. l. Turrianus lib. 2. de Eucharist. cap. 20. per lac intelligunt Eucharistiam. Eà enim olim baptizatis etiam infantibus statim à Baptismo dabatur, Dionys. de Hierarch. Eccles. cap. 5. quod convenit cum eo, quod Petrus dicit, quasi modo geniti infantes lac rationale concupiscite. Verè enim Eucharistia lac rationale, quia in ea homo rationalis i. e. Christus praesens. Eadem spiritualem vim habet animas nostras nutriendi, & ante eius sumtionem omnem deponere oportet malitiam, dolum, invidiam &c. ipsa velut cibus mentium tantâ aviditate sumi debet, quantâ infantes papillas matris sugunt, imò longè maiori, inquit Chrysost, homil. 60. ad pop. Antioch. Per eam dulcedo bonitatis divinae in suo fonte gustatur. 4. Simplicissimè, & ad mentem Apostoli, per lac intelligitur pura Evangelii doctrina. 1. Illam enim comparaverat Apostolus v. 23. cap. praeced. semini incorruptibili, per quod erant regeniti, hîc eandem comparat lacti, per quod in vita spirituali nutriantur. 2. In fine praeced. cap. dixerat. Hoc est verbum, quod evangelizatum est vobis. Illud ipsum verbum Evangelii, exemplo recens natorum infantum lactis cupidorum vult, eos concupiscere debere. 3. Vocat illud τὸ λογικὸν γάλαlac verbale sive lac verbi, ut exponit Clemens Alexandr. lib. 1. paedag. cap. 6. ut exprimat subiectum, quod lacti comparat. 4. Verbum Evangelii est salutare illud medium, per quod in vita spirituali nutrimur ac crescimus. Esai. 38. v. 16.Matth. 4. v. 4. 5. Etiam in aliis Scripturae dictis doctrina Evangelii lacti confertur, Cant. 4. v. 11.cap. 5. v. 1.Esai. 51. v. 1.1 Cor. 3. v. 2.Hebr. 5. v. 12. &c. 6. Cumprimis vero huc pertinet locus Iac. 1. v. 21. huic nostro planè parallelus; Propter quod deponentes omnem immunditiem & abundantiam malitiae in mansuetudine suscipite insitum verbum, quod potest animas vestras salvare. 7. Verbo Evangelii conveniunt proprietates lactis, ut mox apparebit. Haec ergo est expositio propria & principalis, reliquae sunt accommodatitiae & minùs principales.

Q. 3. Quare Evangelium lacti comparetur? Resp. 1. propter puritatem. Lac maternum, quod infantes sugunt, est candidum, purum, nihil alieni admixtum habens, sic verbum Evangelii purum & immaculatum. Psal. 19. v. 8. 2. Propter suavitatem. interioris hominis gustus eius dulcedinem in tentationbus percipit, Psal. 19. v. 13.Psal. 119. v. 39. & 103. &c. 3. Proper vim nutriendi, imò etiam impinguandi, quam comparationis rationem petrus ipse exprimit. 4. Propter vim abluendi.Cant. 5. v. 12. oculi spiritualis sponsae columbini vocantur lacte loti, ac Thren. 4. v. 7. Nazaraei dicuntur nitidiores lacte. Sic verbum Evangelii animas nostras mundat Ioh 15. v. 3. easque speciosas ac nitidas facit. Psal. 51. vers. 9. 5. Propter vim conciliandi somnum. Lac infantibus somnum conciliat, ac rerum aliarum sensum aufert, Psal. 131. v. 2. sed & Sissera post lactis potum somno opprimitur Iud. 4. v. 19. Sic doctrina Evangelii mentem quietam reddit & à terrenis revocat. Clemens Alexandr. lib. 1. paedagog. cap. 6. Nihil certè, quòd melius nutriat, neque quòd sit dulcius lacte, nec quòd candidius lacte inveneris. Est id itaque omni ex parte spirituali nutrimento simile, quod est quidem dulce propter gratiam, nutriens autem tanquam vita, candidum autem ut dies Christi, & sanguinem Verbi ostensum est esse tanquam lac.

Q. 4. Quare vocetur lacλογικὸν? Resp. Qui τὸ λογικὸν vertunt rationale, varias afferunt rationes. 1. Ratione ortus. Verbum doctrinae & oris promanat ex mente, ut lac ex ubere. 2. Ratione obiecti, quia verbum DEI ab anima rationali recipitur. 3. Ratione effecti, Verbum DEI mentem informat, & homines verè prudentes efficitPsal. 19. v. 9.Matth. 10. v. 16. 4 Ratione contrarii. Ne quis putaret, intelligentiae expertem & fatuitatis plenam infantiam laudari, inde lac rationale ipsos concupiscere iubet, ac lac illud, quod appetere iubet, vult esse intelligentiâ quasi conditum,1. Cor. 14. v. 20.Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitiâ parvuli estote. Alii τὸ λογικὸν vertunt spirituale, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] Luth. Geistlich sic ergo Apostolus significaret, se non loqui de lacte corporali, sed spirituali, quo sensu etiam Rom. 12. v. 1.rationale obsequium vocatur, quod est spirituale, ad differentiam corporalium sacrificiorum, in V. T. praescriptorum. Lac corporale datur infantibus nondum rationis usum habentibus, sed lac spirituale datur adultis, quod verbum DEI audire, intelligere & meditari possunt Quidam hoc adiectum putant ad exprimendam differentiam doctrinae spiritualis & animalis, coelestis & terrenae. illa in divinis mysteriis est verèλογικὴ, haec vero ἂλογος,1. Corinth. 1. vers. 20.Iacob. 3. vers. 15. & 17. quò pertinet, quod B. Lutherus significari statuit, Evangelium non esse carnali sensu accipiendum, sed spirituali, videlicet per fidem. Quidam existimant, per τὸ λογικὸςsignificari prudens, moderatum, discretum. Sed si per τὸ λογικὸν γἁλα intelligatur τοῦ λόγου γάλα, res tota est in aprico.

Q. 5. Quare vocetur lacἄδολον? Resp. 1. Ratione sui. Est in se sincerum ac purum ab uberibus divinae sapientiae ad nos promanans. 2. Ratione nostri. Tale verbum appetendum, quod non sit falsâ doctrinâ & corruptelis hominum permixtum, quod non sit humanis opinionibus adulteratum. 2. Cor. 2. v. 17.cap. 4. v. 2. aliàs non erit lac purum, sed serosum & aquosum. 3. Ratione effecti, Lac illud fide assumtum reddit homines ἀδόλους ac simplices, adeoque tales, quales Apostolus requirit in v. 1. nemo illo utens decipitur, ut aliàs venenatis potibus ac philtris dolosis homines decipiuntur.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Petrus deponi iubet omnem dolum. At2. Cor. 12. v. 16.cum essem astutus, dolo vos cepi. Resp. 1. Quidam statuunt, Paulum loqui de dolo bono. 2. Rectiùs dicitur, Apostolum recitare obiectionem Pseudo Apostolorum.

2. Gentium ille Doctor D. Paulus velut carnales & imperfectos eos arguit, qui lactis alimento adhuc indigent,1. Corinth. 3. v. 1.Non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed q. carnalibus tanquam parvulis in Christov. 2.Lac vobis potum dedi, non escam, nondum enim poteratis.Hebr. 5. v. 12.cùm deberetis magistri esse propter tempus, facti estis quibus lacte opus sit, non solido cibo.v. 13.Omnis enim qui lactis est particeps, expers est sermonis iustitiae, parvulus enim est.v. 14.perfectorum autem est solidus cibus. Petrus vero ad lac appetendum in genere omnes fideles hortatur. Resp. 1. Qui lactis nomine hîc intelligunt vivendi rationem simplicitati infantiae consentaneam, respondent, lactis nomen hoc loco non opponi cibo perfecto, sed vetustati carnis, lac quippe eorum est, qui sunt novi homines. Illic, inquit Calvinus, pueris comparantur, qui in pietatis doctrina semper sunt novitii ac rudes tyrunculi, qui in primis Elementis haerent, nec unquam penetrant in altiorem DEI notitiam, atque lac vocatur crassior & pueriles docendi forma, cum ultra prima rudimenta nunquam fit progressus, hîc vero lac non Elementaris est doctrina ut perpetuò quis discat, nunquam ad agnitionem veritatis perveniat, sed vitae ratio, quae novam genituram sapiat. 2. Sed quia superiùs ostendimus, lactis nomine Evangelicam doctrinam propriè & principaliter hîc intelligi, respondendum est, lactis nomine 1. Corinth. 3. v. 2.Hebr. 5. vers. 12. in specie intelligi doctrinam Elementarem, ac modum docendi rudioribus & infirmis convenientem, cui opponitur solidus cibus, qui est perfectorum: hîc vero lactis nomine in genere intelligitur doctrina Evangelica, per quam & infirmi & perfecti ad vitam aeternam nutriuntur. August. tract. 98. in Iohan. Ea ipsa, quae simul audiunt spirituales atque carnales, pro suo quique modulo capiunt, illi ut parvuli, isti ut maiores, illi ut lactis alimentum, isti ut cibi solidamentum. Et postea. CHRISTUS crucifixus, & lac sugentibus, & cibus est proficientibus.

3. Incap. 1. v. 13.iussit eos perfectè sperare in eam, quae offertur ipsis, gratiam. Hîc vero confert eos modò genitis infantibus. Resp. Quamvis respectu rudiorum & infirmiorum quidam in hac vita dicantur perfecti, qui per habitum scientiae, diligenti meditatione verbi per Spiritus sacti gratiam & efficaciam comparatum, exercitatos habent sensus ad discretionem boni & mali Hebr. 5. vers. 14. tamen comparatione virilis ac perfectae aetatis, quam in futuro demum seculo assequemur Ephes. 4. vers. 13. quamdiu hîc vivimus, parvuli sumus Psalm. 131. vers. 2.1. Corinth. 13. vers. 11. Confer Augustinum in Psalm. 130. ubi inter caetera dicit: Alacte non separaberis, quoad usque super matrem tuam es, ne priùs fame moriaris, antequam panem manducare sis idoneus. Et postea. Qui manducant solidum cibum, videntur esse perfecti, quia intelligunt aqualitatem Verbi cum Patre. Adhuc non sic vident, quomodo videndum est, facie ad faciem, aphuc ex parte in aenigmate.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Petrus eos, ad quos scribit, dicit esse renatos ex semine verbi incorruptibili, & tamen iubet eos deponere omnem malitiam, omnem dolum &c. Ergò renovatio non est in hac vita perfecta, sed renati sunt adhuc ex parte carnales Roman. 7. v. 14. peccatum adhuc in carne eorum habitat vers. 18. atque arcte eis in hac vita adhaeret Hebr. 12. v. 1. quod opponendum Pontificiis, qui per Baptismum omne, quod peccati rationem habet, in renatis extingui & aboleri statuunt.

2. Non afferimus nobiscum ad Christum, quando per Evangelium renascimur, meritum aliquod congrui, ut volunt Pontificii, sed grave onus peccati, in quo deponendo per totum vitae huius cursum nos oportet occupari.

3. Petrus provocat ad propriam piorum experientiam, quòd DEI benignitatem gustaverint. Papa negat, pios in hac vita certos esse posse, quòd sint apud DEUM in gratia, quod cum spirituali divinae benignitatis gustu conciliari nequit.

4. Psaltes dicit, Gustate, quàm suavis sit Iehovah. Petrus docet, Christum esse illum, cuius suavitatem pii gustarunt. Ergò Christus est verus Iehovah. Contra Photinianos.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Ex eo, quòd Petrus omnem malitiam, omnem, dolum &c. deponere iubet, colligunt patroni perfectionis, hominem in hac vita esse posse absque peccato. Resp. 1. mandatum hoc durat per totam hominis renati vitam, nec unquam tàm perfectè impletur, quin adhuc aliquid malitiae deponendum semper restet, 2. Iacobus cap. 1. v. 21. illud sic explicat, Deponentesπὲρισσείαν κακίας,abundantiam malitiae. Quamvis igitur exuberans malitiae abundantia deponatur, vitiosa tamen eius radix in hac vita adhuc manet.

2. Ex eo, quòd iubemur lacte spirituali cresoere in salute, Cornelius à Lapide colligit merita operum. Indicat, inquit, Petrus, Christianos in virtutibus crescere debere totâ vitâ usque ad mortem, per quam ibunt ad salutem & vitam aeternam. Vita enim gratiae actu crescit, per operum merita, vita vero gloriae per eadem crescit in spe & iure, maiora enim merita maius dant ius ad gloriam, eamque maiorem. Resp. 1. προσδιορισμὸςad salutem, non habetur in Graecis Codicibus. 2. Per lac non intelliguntur virtutes Christianae, ut vult Cornelius, sed doctrina Evangelii.

3. Nec doctrina Evangelii γενικῶς accepta, ut vult Estius, quando scribit, Lactis nomine intelligitur doctrina Evangelica, h. e. fidei & morum praecepta: sed doctrina Evangelii εἰδικῶς & κυρίως sic dicta, de gratuita peccatorum remissione propter Christum, quae & regenerationis & nutritionis spiritualis est medium. 4. Quando in virtutibus dicimur crescere ad salutem, tunc spiritualis incrementi terminus describitur, non autem causa salutis meritoria exprimitur. Bernhardus tract. de grat. & lib. arbitr. col. 1069. Si propriè appellentur ea, quae dicimus nostra merita, spei quaedam sunt seminaria, caritatis incentiva, occultae praedestinationis indicia, futurae felicitatis praesagia, via regni, non causa regnandi.

3. Ex eo, quòd lac doctrinae vocatur λογικὸν, & cultus noster λογικὸςRoman. 12. v. 1. colligit Smalcius Disp. post. 8. contra August. Conf. Frantzii p. 421. nihil esse credendum, quod rationi adversetur &c. Sed quid per τὸ λογικὸν h. l. intelligendum, expositum fuit q. 4.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Primus pietatis gradus est à malo cessare. Psal. 34. v. 15.1. Petr. 3. v. 12. Nisi enim mala priùs deponantur, bonis operibus vacari minimè potest.

2. Tota nativitas prima, quam ab Adamo trahimus, vitiosa est, quicquid ex illa habemus, deponendum.

3. Non sufficit, semel deponere malitiam, sed hanc veteris hominis depositionem atque exuitionem per totam vitam continuari oportet. Bernh. Epist. 253. Inter profectum & defectum in hoc statu mortalis vitae nihil medium invenitur, sed quomodo ipsum corpus nostrum continuè aut crescere constat, aut decrescere: sic necesse est, & Spiritum aut proficere semper aut deficere.

4. Deponendi vox de peccato ab Apostolo usurpata ostendit, peccatum esse grave onus, hominem ad infernum deprimens, nisi in hac vita abiiciatur. Ambrosius tom. 2. fol. 532. ad Horantianum. Nullum gravius est onus, quàm peccatorum sarcina, & pondus flagitiorum. Deprimit animam, curvat usque ad terram, ne se erigere possit.

5. Veteris hominis cum suis actibus depositio est veri Christiani demonstratio. Cyprianus serm. de zelo & livore, postquam adduxerat locum Apostolicum 1. Cor. 15. v. 50. subiungit. Imaginem coelestem portare non possumus, nisi in eo, quod esse nunc caepimus, Christi similitudinem praebeamus. Hoc est enim mutâsse, quod fueras, & caepisse, quod non eras, ut in te divina nativitas luceat, ut ad Patrem DEUM Deifica disciplina respondeat, ut honore & laude vivendi DEUS in homine clarescat.

6. Caritas est individua verè piorum proprietas. Ergò vitia caritati contraria verè pii cumprimis fugere debent. Augustinus lib. 50. homil. homilia 20. Quid est malitia, nisi nocendi amor? quid dolus, nisi aliud agere, aliud simulare? Quid adulatio, nisi fallaci laude seductio? Quid invidia, nisi odium felicitatis alienae? Quid detractio, nisi mordacior, quàm veracior reprehensio? Malitia malo delectatur alieno. Invidia bono cruciatur alieno. Dolus duplicat cor, adulatio linguam; detractio vulnerat famam.

7. Piorum est, nihil malitiosè vel dolosè agere, sed candido animo actiones omnes ad DEI gloriam & proximi utilitatem dirigere, Ioh. 1. v. 47.

8. Christianos decet simplicitas columbinaMatth. 10. vers. 16. & ovinaIohan. 10. vers. 27. à qua omnis hypocrisis & simulatio exulet. Roman. 12. vers. 9. Caritas sit ἀνυπόκριτος. Origenes homil. 25. in Matth. Hypocrisis non est bonum, sed simulatio boni, nec iustitia, sed figmentum iustitiae; reipsâ autem maxima iniquitas & pessimum malum.

9. Communionis sanctorum meditatio optimum invidiae remedium. Cum enim unius corporis mystici membra simus, nemo alteri felicitatem & dona invideat. August. 15. de civit. DEI cap. 5. Nullo modo fit minor accedente seu permanente consorte possesio bonitatis, imò possessio bonitatis tantò fit latior, quantò concordior eam individua socior, possidet caritas.

10. Obtrectatio vitium planè Diabolicum, quia ab eo Diabolus nomen accepit. Rationem dat Chrysostomus 2. homil. in 2. Corinth. 1. ἐπειδὴ καὶ θεὸν πρὸς ἀνθρώπους διαβάλλει, καὶ ἡμᾶς πρὸς θεὸν καὶ πάλιν ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς πρὸς ἀλλήλους.

11. Baptizati sunt velut modò geniti infantes, quia Baptismus est regenerationis lavacrum Tit. 3. vers. 5. ac puerpera regni coelorum. Chrysost. homil. 25. in Iohan. τό δε ὕδωρ παρείλεται, τὸκος τῷ τικτομένω γενόμενον, ὅπερ γὰρ ἐστὶν ἡ μήτρα τῷ ἐμβρύῳ, τοῦτο τῷ πιστῷ τὸ ὕδωρ.Aqua assumta fit partus ei, qui editus est. Quod enim matrix embryoni, id aqua est fideli. Paulinus. Inde parens sacro ducit de fonte Sacerdos Infantes niveos corpore, corde, habitu.

12. Renati sunt q. modò geniti infantes, ergò commendata ipsis esse debet infantilis innocentia, puritas, humilitas, obedientia, docilitas, facilitas, simplicitas & sinceritas. Matth. 18. v. 3.

13. Verbum Evangelii est semen, ex quo regeneramur; ac animae nostrae cibus & potus, quo nutrimur. Clemens Alexandr. lib. 1. paedagog. cap. 8. Verbum est omnia, infanti & pater & mater, & paedagogus & altor. Chrysost. homil. 16. in Ep. Rom. Verbum DEI est quasi uterus Ecclesiae, in quo non solùm ad Christianismum formamur & gignimur, sed etiam nutrimur.

14. Ut corpus augetur nutrimento, ita quoque fidem auditu & meditatione Evangelii crescere oportet. Vinum roborat corpus, animam DEI verbum. Nilus in sent. tom. 1. orth. p. 170.

15. Evangelium est lac rudioribus, ac cibus solidus perfectis. Fulgentius serm. de confess. Scripturae ut ditissima fercula habent, quod omni aetati congruat, omni professioni conveniat, potum lacteum, quo infantia nutriatur, & cibum solidum, quo robusta iuventus spiritualia virtutis incrementa accipiat.

16. Meditatio divinorum beneficiorum in Christo exhibitorum est suavis & lacteus animae cibus, per quem crescimus ad solidiorem cibum, qui in flagellis & cruce reconditur. Non coquendus est haedulus in lacte matrisExod. 23. v. 19. h. e. Christiani adhuc teneri, non sunt doctrinâ crucis onerandi, sed primò doctrinâ Evangelii recreandi. Lutherus.

17. Simplicia fidei rudimenta primò de matris Ecclesiae uberibus quaerite, hoc est, de utriusque Testamenti Doctoribus; qui divina eloquia vel scripsêre, vel etiam vivâ voce vobis praedicant.

18. Inter ubera illa, ex quibus lac doctrinae coelestis hauritur, dilectus Ecclesiae sponsus instar fasciculi myrrhae debet commorari, h. e. Christus passus & crucifixus semper in Ecclesia debet praedicari & passionis memoria iugiter recoli. Cant. 1. v. 13. Lutherus in h. l.

19. Lac doctrinae Evangelicae debet esse ἄδολον, Doctores Ecclesiae illud debent sincerè proponere, auditores candidè imbibere. Sicut qui lac vendunt, admixtâ aquâ illud quandoque adulterant, ita falsi doctores humanis opinionibus doctrinam Evangelii, velut aquâ ad nutrimentum minùs aptâ corrumpunt. Esai. 1. vers. 22. inde Irenaeus lib. 3. cap. 19. de haereticis dicit, quod gypsum lacti immisceant i. e. erroris sui veneno doctrinam coelestem inficiant.

20. Lac non nutrit infantes nisi imbibatur & in corporis substantiam mutetur: sic doctrina coelestis fide in cor recipienda, inque actus & mores convertenda. Tertull. lib. de resurr. carnis. Sermo DEI in causam vitae appetendus, auditu devorandus, intellectu ruminandus, fide digerendus.

21. Baptizatis olim lactis & mellis quippiam gustandum praebebatur. Tertull. lib. de coron. milit. cap. 3. quod adhuc hodie observant Aethiopes, ut ex ipsorum Rituali apparet, quo ipso hanc Apostolicam exhortationem, velut typo quodam exprimere voluerunt.

22. Nemo potest seipsum regenerare, sicut etiam nemo potest seipsum generare: interim renatus ad spirituale sui incrementum, lac verbi concupiscere & assumere potest ac debet.

23. Verbum DEI est manna absconditum Apoc. 2. v. 17. dulcedinem eius nemo novit, nisi qui gustat.

24. Qui corporalibus voluptatibus, aut propriae iustitiae fiduciâ ebrii, non gustant Evangelicae doctrinae ac divinae benignitatis suavitatem. Israelitae fastidiebant manna, cuius tamen gustus erat suavissimus. Sap. 16. v. 20. Beda. Qui nihil de superna suavitate animo gustat, non est mirum, si hunc terrestribus illecebris sordidare non evitat.

25. Christus ubique nobis χρηστὸς utilis, beneficus ac dulcis in nobis vocandis, recipiendis, illuminandis, defendendis; in peccatorum remissione, in conscientiae pacificatione, in consolatione. Iohannes Hussus in h. l. Dulcis est Dominus in contemplatione ad meditandumCant. 2. v. 3.in aure spirituali ad audiendumCant. 5. v. 13.in ore ad loquendumPsal. 119. v. 39.in prospectu ad videndumSir. 23. v. 37.

26. In Christo gustare possumus DEI bonitatem & benignitatem. Matth. 11. v. 28. Clem. Alexandr. lib. 1. paedag. cap. 6. Alimentum infantium est Dominus, qui est Spiritus & verbum. Alimentum id est Dominus Iesus, h. e. Verbum DEI, est Spiritus incarnatus, caro coelestis sanctificata. Nutrimentum est lac Patris, quo solùm aluntar infantuli. Ipse itaque qui est dilectus & altor noster, Verbum, effudit pro nobis suum sanguinem, salutem humanae Naturae afferens, per quem, qui in DEUM credidimus, ad mammillam Patris, quae curarum oblivionem inducit, nempe Verbum confugimus. Ille autem solus, ut est consentaneum, nobis lac dilectionis infantibus suppeditat.

## 2:2
AS NEWBORN INFANTS DESIRE THE REASONABLE MILK WITHOUT DECEIT, THAT YOU MAY GROW IN IT.

Connection. Ἀποτροπῇ from evil, is added προτροπὴ to good. 1. The Apostle had said in v. 23. cap. preceding that the pious, to whom he writes, were reborn from the incorruptible seed of the word, therefore persisting in the metaphor he calls them newborn infants, and admonishes them, that by the example of infants they should most greedily desire the milk of the Gospel for their spiritual nutrition. Thus, therefore, he compares the word of the Gospel to mother's milk, he compares the spiritually reborn to infants recently born, he compares the zeal of progressing in the knowledge of heavenly doctrine & faith, to the desire for mother's milk, such as is seen in infants recently born; he compares the spiritual progress of the pious to the growth which we see conferred upon infants recently born by mother's milk. 2. Bede refers that προσδιορισμὸν as newborn infants, not only to the following, but also to the preceding, Because you have been reborn recently, & have been made children of GOD through Baptism, be such now through the study of good conversation, as infants recently brought forth are by the Nature of an innocent age, namely ignorant of malice and deceit, in every way ignorant of how to simulate, to envy, to slander, and to be enslaved to other vices of this kind. The Syrian likewise seems to refer to the preceding to refer. For he rendered. Be as infants. [consult facsimile image] that is פתאים or תמימים simple, ignorant of guile and fraud. But the context shows that this pertains properly and principally to the following exhortation concerning desiring the milk of the Gospel. For just as the Apostle had previously compared the word of the Gospel to seed, from which the pious are reborn, so he now compares the same to milk, from which they are spiritually nourished. Secondarily, however, this can also be referred to the preceding things. For infants, although they do not lay aside those vices, nevertheless lack those vices, which is sufficient for the comparison. Infants desiring maternal milk are alien to malice, guile, envy, etc.: so also by their example you ought to lay aside those vices, so that you may grow in faith and holy life from the word of the Gospel. A similar comparison of the pious with infants, with respect to immunity from these vices, exists Matt. 13. v. 3.Mark 10. v. 15.1. Cor. 14. v. 20.

3. The Apostle had said that vices contrary to Christian charity must be laid aside; he therefore shows the means by which that laying aside can be obtained, which is the word. For just as regeneration is perfected through the word, and renewal is begun; so also daily renewal is continued through the word, whence to the prior exhortation concerning laying aside the old man, the Apostle adds this admonition, that they should be studious hearers of the word, and constantly retain the pure doctrine of the Gospel, but flee the corrupt one.

Explanation of the text, ὡς ἀρτιγὲνητα βρέφη. Because they had recently been converted to the faith, regenerated through Baptism and the word, and thus were still weak in faith, he therefore compares them to infants recently born. Τὸ βρέφος they wish it to be said, or ἀπὸ τοῦ φέρφω, which is στρέφω, because it moves in the maternal womb at certain intervals, or ἀπὸ τοῦ τρέφω, which is I nourish, because it especially needs suitable food, by the taking of which it quickly grows. In the Scriptures it is taken both for an infant still enclosed in the maternal womb Luke 1. v. 41. and for an infant recently born Luke 2. v. 12.Acts 7. v. 19. and for him who is already a little older 2. Tim. 3. v. 15. that it is taken in this place in the second signification, the added little word ἀρτιγὲνήτον shows.

Τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, The word ἐπιποθεῖν He expresses a singular zeal and desire for learning, which he compares to the desire for mother's milk, such as is observed in infants, which comparison is without doubt taken from Ps. 131:2. Other sayings of Scripture also show this signification of vehement desire in the word ἐπιποθεῖν Rom. 1:11 2 Cor. 5:2 ch. 9:14 Phil. 1:8 ch. 2:26 etc. The Syriac has the word [consult facsimile image] in the Ethpael, which likewise denotes vehement concupiscence. Phil. 1:23. By τὸ γάλα λογικὸν he understands τὸ γάλα τοῦ λόγου, the milk of the word or the word of the Gospel compared to milk, just as the Syriac has rightly expressed the sense, desire the word itself, as pure and spiritual milk. A similar mode of speaking exists in ch. 1 of this Epistle v. 13 ἀναζωσύμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας girding up the loins of your mind. v. 13 of this chapter he calls κτίσιν ἀνθρωπίντην, men established in the office of Magistrate, ch. 3:8 he calls σκεῦος γυναικεῖον women compared to a vessel, in all of which places the added epithet does not denote an adjoined quality of the thing, but the subject, i.e., the thing itself, of which there is speech, and which is compared to another, so that this mode of speaking seems to have been familiar to Peter. Certain Latin Codices read rational, so that this may be referred to those who are desiring. But without the support of any Greek Codex, whence this error was corrected in the Sixtine edition. The Vulgate rendered ἄδολον without guile, Augustine in book 1 innocent. The Syriac [consult facsimile image] pure and clean, looks to the purity and sincerity of the doctrine, which he most beautifully compares with the sincerity of unadulterated milk. He expresses, therefore, what kind of milk of doctrine they ought to seek, namely, that it be not corrupted by the addition of human opinions and traditions, just as infants seek pure and sincere milk, and not that which is corrupted and adulterated by mixed water. ἵνα ἐν αὐτοῦ αὐξηθῆτε, is to be taken not only ἐκβατικῶς, but also τελικῶς. Therefore you ought to greedily desire the pure milk of the Gospel, so that in it, i.e., through it (according to the customary Hebraism) you may grow. Just as infants from natural instinct desire milk, so that through it they may take bodily growth: so you ought to seek the doctrine of the Gospel with the highest zeal and desire, so that through it you may grow more in spiritual life, and receive spiritual strength and increase. Parallel passage It stands Eph. 4. v. 13. Until we all come into the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of GOD, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ. Certain Latin Codices add, that in it you may grow unto salvation, just as Augustine in his book on the subject and Bede in his commentary also read, just as the Syrian also adds, [consult facsimile image] unto life. But the more approved Greek Codices do not have this προσδιορισμὸν added.

Latin:

SICUT MODO GENITI INFANTES RATIONABILE SINE DOLO LAC CONCUPISCITE, UT IN EO CRESCATIS.

Connexio. Ἀποτροπῇ à malo, subiungitur προτροπὴ ad bonum. 1. Dixerat Apostolus in v. 23. cap. praeced. pios, ad quos scribit, renatos esse ex incorruptibili semine verbi, persistens igitur in metaphora vocat eos modò genitos infantes, atque admonet, ut exemplo infantum lac Evangelii ad spiritualem sui nutritionem avidissimè experant. Sic ergò verbum Evangelii confert lacti materno, spiritualiter renatos comparat infantibus recens natis, studium proficiendi in cognitione doctrinae coelestis & fide, comparat desiderio lactis materni, quale in infantibus recens natis conspicitur; spiritualem piorum profectum confert incremento, quod infantibus recens natis lacte materno conferri videmus. 2. Beda illum προσδιορισμὸν sicut modò geniti infantes, refert non solùm ad sequentia, sed etiam ad praecedentia, Quia renati estis nuper, & filii DEI per Baptismum facti tales modò estote per studium bonae conversationis, quales recenter editi infantes per Naturam innoxia aetatis, ignari videl. malitiae & doli, simulare, invidere, detrahere, aliisque huiusmodi vitiis mancipari omnimodis ignorantes. Syrus itidem videtur ad praecedentia referre. Reddidit enim. Estote tanquam infantes.[consult facsimile image] h. e. פתאים vel תמימיםsimplices, ignari doli ac fraudis. Sed contextus ostendit, propriè & principaliter ad sequentem exhortationem, de lacte Evangelii expetendo, hoc pertinere. Ut enim Apostolus priùs verbum Evangelii comparaverat semini, ex quo pii renascuntur, ita idem iam comparat lacti, ex quo spiritualiter nutriuntur. Secundariò tamen etiam ad praecedentia hoc referri potest. Infantes enim, quamvis vitia illa non deponant, tamen vitiis illis carent, id quod ad comparationem sufficit. Infantes lactis materni appetentes à malitia, dolo, invidia &c. sunt alieni: ita quoque exemplo eorum vitia illa deponere debetis, ut ex verbo Evangelii in fide & vita sancta crescatis. Similis comparatio piorum cum infantibus, respectu immunitatis ab his vitiis, extat Matth. 13. v. 3.Marc. 10. v. 15.1. Cor. 14. v. 20.

3. Dixerat Apostolus, deponenda esse vitia caritati Christianae contraria, ostendit igitur medium, per quod depositio illa obtineri potest, quod est verbum. Ut enim per verbum regeneratio perficitur, ac renovatio inchoatur; ita quoque per verbum renovatio quotidiana continuatur, unde priori exhortationi de veteri homine deponendo, Apostolus subiicit hanc admonitionem, ut verbi sint studiosi auditores, ac puram Evangelii doctrinam constanter retineant, corruptam vero fugiant.

Textus explicatio, ὡς ἀρτιγὲνητα βρέφη. Quia nuper erant ad fidem conversi, per Baptismum ac verbum regeniti, adeoque in fide adhuc infirmi, inde confert eos infantibus recens natis. Τὸ βρέφος dictum volunt, vel ἀπὸ τοῦ φέρφω, quod est στρέφω, quia in utero materno per certa intervalla movetur, vel ἀπὸ τοῦ τρέφω, quod est nutrio, quia alimento inprimis indiget idoneo, quo assumto citò crescit. In Scripturis accipitur, tùm pro infante adhuc in utero materno concluso Luc. 1. v. 41. tùm pro infante recens nato Luc. 2. v. 12.Actor. 7. v. 19. tùm pro eo, qui iam paulo adultior 2. Tim. 3. v. 15. hoc loco in secunda significatione accipi, adiecta vocula ἀρτιγὲνήτον ostendit.

Τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε, Verbum ἐπιποθεῖν singulare studium & desiderium discendi exprimit, quod confert cum desiderio lactis materni, quale in infantibus conspicitur, quae comparatio dubio procul petita, ex Psal. 131. v. 2. Hanc vehementis desiderii significationem in verbo ἐπιποθεῖν ostendunt etiam alia Scripturae dicta Rom. 1. v. 11.2. Cor. 5. v. 2.cap. 9. v. 14.Philipp. 1. v. 8.cap. 2. v. 26. &c. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael, quod itidem vehementem concupiscentiam denotat. Phil. 1. v. 23. Per τὸ γάλα λογικὸν intelligit τὸ γάλα τοῦ λόγου,lac verbi sive verbum Evangelii lacti collatum, sicut Syrus sensum rectè expressit, concupiscite ipsum sermonem, tanquam lac mundum & spirituale. Similis loquendi modus extat cap. 1. huius Epistolae v. 13.ἀναζωσύμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίαςsuccincti mentis vestrae lumbos.vers. 13. huius capitis Magistratus vocat κτίσιν ἀνθρωπίντην, homines in officio Magistratûs constitutos, cap. 3. v. 8.σκεῦος γυναικεῖον vocat mulieres vasi comparatas, in quibus locis omnibus epitheton adiectum non notat adiunctam rei qualitatem, sed subiectum, i. e. rem ipsam, de qua sermo est, & quae alteri confertur, ut hic loquendi modus Petro videatur fuisse familiaris. Quidam Codices Latini legunt rationabiles, ut ad ipsos concupiscentes hoc referatur. Sed sine ullius Graeci Codicis suffragio, unde in Sixtina editione hic error correctus. ἄδολον vulgata reddidit, sine dolo, Augustinus d. 1. innocens. Syrus [consult facsimile image]purum & mundum, respicit ad puritatem & sinceritatem doctrinae, quam cum sinceritate lactis non adulterati pulcerrimè confert. Exprimit igitur, quale doctrinae lac expetere debeant, videlicet, quòd non sit humanarum opinionum ac traditionum additamento corruptum, sicut infantes lac purum & sincerum, non autem aquâ admixtâ corruptum atque adulteratum expetunt. ἵνα ἐν αὐτοῦ αὐξηθῆτε, hoc non solùm ἐκβατικῶς, sed etiam τελικῶς accipiendum. Ideò debetis purum Evangelii lac avidè concupiscere, ut in eo, h. e. per illud (iuxta usitatum Hebraismum) crescatis. Sicut infantes ex instinctu naturali lac appetunt, ut per illud corporis incrementum capiant: ita doctrinam Evangelii summo studio ac desiderio expetere debetis, ut per eam in vita spirituali magis crescatis, ac spirituale robur & incrementum accipiatis. Locus parallelus extat Eph. 4. v. 13.Donec occurramus omnes in unitatem fidei, & agnitionis filii DEI in virum perfectum, in mensuram aetatis plenitudinis Christi. Quidam Codices Latini addunt, ut in eo crescatis in salutem, quomodo etiam legunt Augustinus l. d. & Beda in comment. uti etiam Syrus addit, [consult facsimile image]ad vitam. Sed probatiores Graeci Codices hunc προσδιορισμὸν non habent adiectum.

## 2:3
IF YET YOU HAVE TASTED, THAT THE LORD IS SWEET.

Connection. 1. The Apostle had exhorted the faithful to seek most greedily the milk of Evangelical doctrine. He begins to confirm this exhortation of his from the sweetness of the Gospel already perceived before. You have already tasted before how sweet the Lord is, exhibiting Himself to you to be tasted spiritually in the preaching of the Gospel. Therefore, just as infants, once the sweetness of maternal milk has been tasted, seek it more greedily: so after you have tasted the kindness of GOD from the preached Gospel, and received it by faith, you ought subsequently to seek it with greater desire. 2. Previously he had commended the excellence of Evangelical doctrine from its sincerity and efficacy of nourishing in the spiritual life: now he commends the same from the sweetness and pleasantness by which it commends itself to the new and interior man, which the faithful had already previously experienced by spiritual taste.

Exposition of the text. Εἰπερ ἐγεύσασθε. The Vulgate rendered it adversatively. If yet you have tasted, by which reasoning such would be the connection. I exhort you, that like newborn infants, you seek the most sweet milk of Evangelical doctrine for your spiritual growth. But in vain do I exhort you to seek it, if you have not yet perceived its sweetness by spiritual taste. But the adversative particle 'yet' is not in the Greek Codices, nor in the Syriac paraphrase, nor in all Latin Codices. And τὸ εἴπερ is not of one doubting whether that has been done, but of one supposing that it has been done, so that it is thus accepted as placed for ἐπειδήπερ, since, or if indeed, in a causal sense. Since you have already tasted before the sweetness of Evangelical doctrine, it is fair that you should henceforth seek it. Rom. 8. v. 9. 2. Thessal. 1. v. 6. For you have tasted certain Latin Codices read you taste, but in the Greek it is ἐγεύσασθε, where, however, the present tense and the continuation of spiritual taste is included. Jerome In chapter 40 of Ezekiel, for you have tasted he reads you have believed, because that spiritual tasting is done through faith. But the word for tasting is more emphatic, expressing the spiritual sense of divine sweetness, of consolations, and of spiritual delights, such as arises from true and living faith in the hearts of believers. Heb. 6. verse 4. The Syrian rendered it: [consult facsimile image] If you have tasted and seen, which latter word is repeated from Ps. 34. v. 9. Taste and see, how sweet the Lord is, to which the thing itself makes it manifest that the Apostle is alluding here. Secondarily, he also seems to look back to Isa. 66. v. 11. that you may suck and be satisfied from the breast of his consolations.

ὅτι Χρηστὸς ὁ Κύριος. By τὸν Κύριον in this place is understood Christ, as appears from the following. He calls him by a certain most sweet allusion χρηστὸν, just as Justin also writes allusively in Apol. 2. page 42. We are accused of being Christians. But χρηστὸν, that is to hate what is convenient and good, is unjust. where Sylburgius notes, that there is an allusion to the common custom of his time, by which Christ, because the reason for the name was unknown, was called Chrestus: for otherwise it was not unknown to Peter the Apostle, nor to Justin, that the name of Christ is not derived from χράομαι, but from χριζομαι deduced. For when Peter a little later verse 5. calls Christians a holy Priesthood, he implies, that they themselves, having been anointed by Christ with the fullness of the Holy Spirit, have been anointed into spiritual Priests; and Justin writes in Apol. 1. for Christ p. 35: The Son of GOD is called Χριστὸς κατὰ το κεχρίσθαι καὶ κοσμῆσαι τὰ πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ τὸν θεὸν, and in the Dialogue with Trypho p. 244. ὁ βασιλεῖς πάντες, καὶ οἱ χριστοί ἀπὸ τοὺτου μέτεσχον, και βασιλεῖς καλεῖσθαι καὶ χριστοί, Furthermore, in Psalm 34, from which this sentence is taken, in the Hebrew text there is the name טוב, which signifies good, kind, useful, sweet, which latter meaning the word for tasting shows to be properly suited to this place. The LXX, and Peter the Apostle following them, rendered it χρηστὸν, which signifies him who offers himself to be used by others, who is beneficent, useful, easy towards others, whose conversation is convenient, pleasant, and fruitful. For because Christ is good and kind towards men, therefore also to taste his goodness and kindness is sweet and pleasant. And conversely, because a certain taste of sweetness is perceived from the word of the Gospel, from it is gathered that Christ is good and kind.

Latin:

SI TAMEN GUSTASTIS, QUONIAM DULCIS EST DOMINUS.

Connexio. 1. Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus fideles ad lac Evangelicae doctrinae cupidissimè expetendum. hanc exhortationem suam incipit confirmare ab Evangelii suavitate iam antè perceptâ. Iam antè gustastis, quàm suavis sit Dominus, in Evangelii praedicatione seipsum spiritualiter gustandum vobis exhibens. Ergò quemadmodum infantes, lactis materni dulcedine semel gustata, avidiùs illud expetunt: sic postquam DEI benignitatem ex Evangelio praedicato, & fide recepto gustastis, subinde maiori desiderio illud expetere debetis. 2. Priùs commendaverat doctrinae Evangelicae praestantiam à sinceritate & efficacia nutriendi, in vita spirituali: iam eandem commendat à dulcedine & suavitate, quâ sese novo & interiori homini commendat, quam fideles iam antè spirituali gustu experti erant.

Textus expositio. Εἰπερ ἐγεύσασθε. Vulgata reddidit adversativè. Si tamen gustastis, quâ ratione talis foret connexio. Exhortor vos, ut instar infantum recens natorum, suavissimum doctrinae Evangelicae lac ad spirituale vestrum incrementum expetatis. Sed frustra ad illud expetendum vos exhortor, si dulcedinem eius spirituali gustu nondum percepistis. Sed particula adversativa tamen non est in Graecis Codicibus, nec in paraphrasi Syriaca, nec in omnibus Latinis Codd. Ac τὸ εἴπερ non est dubitantis, an illud factum sit, sed supponentis, quòd factum sit, ut sic accipiatur positum pro ἐπειδήπερ,quandoquidem, vel siquidem, in sensu causali. Siquidem iam antè gustatis doctrinae Evangelicae dulcedinem, aequum est, ut eam porrò expetatis. Rom. 8. v. 9.2. Thessal. 1. v. 6. Pro gustastis quidam Codices Latini legunt gustatis, sed in Graeco est ἐγεύσασθε, ubi tamen praesens tempus, & spiritualis gustus continuatio includitur. Hieronymus in cap. 40. Ezech. pro gustastis legit credidistis, quia gustus ille spiritualis fit per fidem. Sed gustandi verbum magis est emphaticum, exprimens spiritualem sensum divinae suavitatis, consolationum ac delitiarum spiritualium, qualis ex vera & viva fide in cordibus credentium oritur. Hebr. 6. vers. 4. Syrus reddidit: [consult facsimile image]Si gustastis & vidistis, quod posterius verbum repetitum ex Psal. 34. v. 9.Gustate & videte, quàm suavis sit Dominus, ad quem Apostolum hâc alludere res ipsa manifestum facit. Secundariò etiam respicere videtur ad Esa. 66. v. 11.ut sugatis & saturemini ab ubere consolationum eius.

ὅτι Χρηστὸς ὁ Κύριος. Per τὸν Κύριον hoc loco intelligitur Christus, ut apparet ex sequentibus. Illum suavissimâ quadam allusione vocat χρηστὸν, sicut etiam Iustinus Apol. 2. pag. 42. allusivè scribit. Christiani esse deferimur. Atquiχρηστὸν, h. e. commodum & bonum odisse, iniustum est. ubi Sylburgius notat, alludi ad vulgatam eius temporis consuetudinem, quâ Christus ignoratâ nominis ratione vocabatur Chrestus: alioquienim nec Petro Apostolo, nec Iustino ignotum fuit, Christi nomen non àχράομαι,sedχριζομαιdeduci Quando enim Petrus paulo pòst vers. 5. Christianos vocat Sacerdotium sanctum, innuit, ipsos à Christo plenitudine Spiritus sancti uncto, in spirituales Sacerdotes esse unctos; ac Iustinus Apol. 1. pro Christ p. 35. scribit: Filius DEI diciturΧριστὸς κατὰ το κεχρίσθαι καὶ κοσμῆσαι τὰ πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ τὸν θεὸν, ac Dialog. cum Tryphone p. 244. ὁ βασιλεῖς πάντες, καὶ οἱ χριστοί ἀπὸ τοὺτου μέτεσχον, και βασιλεῖς καλεῖσθαι καὶ χριστοί, Caeterùm in Psalmo 34. ex quo haec sententia desumta, in textu Hebraeo habetur nomen טוב, quod significat bonum, benignum, utilem, suavem, quam posteriorem significationem huic loco propriè convenire, verbum gustandi ostendit. LXX. & eos secutus Petrus Apostolus reddiderunt χρηστὸν, quod significat eum, qui se aliis utendum praebet, qui est erga alios beneficus, utilis, facilis, cuius conversatio est commoda, grata & fructuosa. Quia enim Christus erga homines est bonus & benignus, ideò etiam ipsius bonitatem & benignitatem gustare suave est & dulce. Et vicissim, quia ex verbo Evangelii spiritualis quidam dulcedinis gustus percipitur, ex eo colligitur, Christum esse bonum & benignum.

## 2:4-5
TO WHOM COMING, A LIVING STONE, REJECTED INDEED BY MEN, BUT CHOSEN AND HONORED BY GOD. AND YOU YOURSELVES AS LIVING STONES ARE BUILT UP A SPIRITUAL HOUSE, A HOLY PRIESTHOOD, TO OFFER SPIRITUAL SACRIFICES ACCEPTABLE TO GOD THROUGH JESUS CHRIST.

Connection. 1 He brings forward another argument of exhortation from the dignity of the pious, which he expresses by two similitudes, when he compares them with the temple and the Priests of the O. T. Whoever are the spiritual house of GOD, and spiritual Priests, they ought to lay aside all malice, all guile, and therefore all spiritual uncleanness. But truly the faithful, who have approached Christ by faith, are the spiritual house of GOD and spiritual Priests. Therefore they ought to lay aside all malice, all guile, and therefore all spiritual uncleanness. The confirmation of the major can be sought from the fact that the temple of the Old T. by the command of GOD had to be kept clean and not at all polluted Lev. 15. v. 31.cap. 21. v. 12.Num. 19. v. 13. etc. and that the Priests had to be most studious of cleanliness and holiness. Levit. 21. v. 6. Therefore, that the antitype may correspond to the type, the spiritual temple and the spiritual Priests also must be clean.

2. The argument sought from the dignity of the pious can also be formed thus. The greater and more excellent the dignity of the faithful in the N. than of the Jews in the O. T., the more ardently is the pursuit of piety required of them. But now the dignity of the pious in the N. T. is far more illustrious and excellent than that of the Jews in the O. T., because the faithful in the N. T. are a spiritual house built upon the cornerstone Christ, whereas the Jews in the O. T. had an external and material temple; they are also spiritual Priests, whereas the Priests of the Jews offered spiritual victims. Therefore, a more ardent pursuit of piety is required also from the faithful in the N. T.

3. He confirms the exhortation from the salutary beginning of the calling to Christ. When you received the doctrine of the Gospel by faith, you have already come to Christ, and like living stones upon him as the cornerstone you have begun to be built, it is therefore just that you should persevere constantly in this your calling, and by daily progress in the faith approaching CHRIST, you yourselves as living stones may be built up more and more upon him, and thus in the spiritual life may take greater increases from time to time. In this way this verse coheres with the words immediately preceding, in verse 2. that you may grow in it.

4. He had compared the faithful reborn in Christ to newborn infants, and had exhorted them under this name to lay aside malice, which is opposed to infantile innocence and simplicity, now he passes to a related metaphor among the Hebrews and compares them to a spiritual building. For among the Hebrews בנים sons are called from the root בנה he built. For as a house is built from stones, so families are built from children, especially males. And there is a certain sweet wordplay between בנים which sons אבנים which signifies stones. Those therefore whom Peter had previously called בנים newborn infants, he compares them to אבנים חיים living stones, from which the structure of the spiritual house is built.

5. Bede brings forward such a connection. Since in that same Psalm, from which he assumed this verse (namely 34.) it was premised, Approach him and be enlightened, rightly blessed Peter added, To whom approaching as to a living stone.

6. The Apostle had exhorted those to whom he writes to spiritual progress both in true faith and in a holy life. He illustrates the former part of the exhortation with a similitude taken from the Scriptures of the Old Testament, by which he compares Christ to a cornerstone and foundation stone, but the faithful to stones, which are built upon the foundation stone. He exhorts them, therefore, that they may be built up more and more upon this stone, that is, that through faith they may be, as it were, more glued together and coalesce with him. He illustrates the latter part of the exhortation with another similitude, by which he compares the faithful to Priests, and good works to sacrifices. He exhorts them, therefore, that having been constituted and consecrated by GOD as spiritual Priests, they may offer spiritual sacrifices to GOD.

7. The Apostle brings forward not only the dignity of Christians, but also of Christ himself as a place of argument, by which he may confirm his proposed exhortation, while he calls him a living stone indeed rejected by men, but chosen by GOD and honored; the chief cornerstone, elect and precious. For as many Christians as, having been converted to CHRIST by faith, are unwilling to lay aside the filth, malice, guile, hypocrisy, etc., of their former conversation, and thus the old man, they affect with ignominy CHRIST himself, so greatly honored by GOD, and bring infamy upon his name among the unbelieving Gentiles and Jews.

Exposition of the text. To whom προσερχόμενοι, i.e., to the Lord, or CHRIST, whose sweetness you taste. Προσερχόμενοι has the signification of the present tense, for he describes not only the first conversion of those to whom he writes to CHRIST, but also their present state, that they, having already been reborn in CHRIST, approach him more by the daily continuation and increase of faith, and join themselves more closely to him. The Syrian, however, seems to have expressed the signification of the past [consult facsimile image] to whom you have approached, or have been made to approach.

Λίθον ζῶντα. He calls CHRIST a stone, i.e., fundamental and angular, which sustains the whole house of the Church and provides it with firmness, because he had intended to compare believers in CHRIST to a house and to stones built upon a foundation. He takes this appellation, however, from the Old Testament Scripture, namely from the Psalms and the Prophet Isaiah, whose testimonies he brings forward a little later. He does not, however, simply call CHRIST a stone, but adds living, so that he may express the metaphor and hint at the properties and effects of this stone, which not only has life in itself, but also vivifies the stones built upon it, i.e., those adhering to him by faith.

Ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον. By men rejecting this stone he understands not only in particular those foolish architects who rejected this stone, of whom he treats in v. 7 from Psal. 118. v. 22., namely the Chief Priests, Scribes, and Pharisees among the Jewish people, but also in general all unbelievers from among the Jews and Gentiles, who contumaciously reject the benefits of Christ offered to them in the Gospel.

Παρά δε θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν, ἐντιμον. The Vulgate rendered it, elect by GOD, but the Greek sounds rather, elect with GOD, in which way the Syrian also translates [consult facsimile image] ἐκλεκτὸς here is not taken participially, but nominally in that sense in which even Angels are called elect, i. e. eminent, outstanding, excellent1. Tim. 5. v. 21. just as also the Hebrew בחיר & בחור is used Isa. 42. v. 1.Ezek. 23. v. 6. and the substantive םבחר signifies an excellent and outstanding thing Gen. 23. v. 6.Jer. 48. v. 15.2. Kings 3. v. 19. &c. for in a free and right election, that which is worst is not wont to be chosen, but that which is best. The Syrian has the noun [consult facsimile image] which can be translated not only by elect, but also lofty, sublime, and excellent. The added noun ἔντιμος, shows the same thing, which is of the former ἐξήγησις, therefore and thence this stone is elect with GOD, because it is of great price with him, so that there is a certain allusion to outstanding stones, which are of price among men. The Apostle opposes this, however, by a certain prolepsis to the false judgment of the unbelievers rejecting this stone. Although it seems to yield to the ignominy of this stone, that it is rejected by men, or as the Syrian emphatically rendered it, by the sons of men, i. e. by those who excel in dignity among men, nevertheless nothing of its dignity departs from this stone because its own dignity and its own price remains for it with GOD.

καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθον ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε. Just as he had called CHRIST a living stone, so also he calls believers living stones, so that he may show a continuation of the metaphor. Yet he calls CHRIST a living stone and the faithful living stones for a different reason. He calls Christ living in an active signification, because he communicates life to the stones built upon him. He calls the faithful living in a passive signification, because they receive life from the foundational stone Christ, upon whom they are built. Therefore that καὶ αὐτοὶ you yourselves also, is to be referred only to the parity of the thing, but not to the equality of the mode, so that the sense may be: Not only is Christ the living stone foundation of the Church, but also you, as living stones, are built upon him, meanwhile that life belongs to both Christ and you in a different mode. Erasmus takes the word οἰκοδομεῖσθε imperatively, so that it may be a continuation of the exhortation, and may correspond to v. 2. ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε, in which way also the Syriac [consult facsimile image] Tremellius translates, be built. But it is more correctly taken in the indicative mood, in which way Bede reads, and adds: To be built upon He says those; because without our Lord Jesus Christ, namely the living stone, no spiritual building can stand. For the Apostle is engaged in exaggerating the dignity of the pious, because by approaching Christ through faith, they are built up as living stones upon Christ the foundational stone. The Vulgate Interpreter rendered be built up, looking to the sense, but in the Greek it is the simple οἰκοδομεῖσθε, which, however, is to be completed thus from Eph. 2. v. 20. be built up upon him, as upon a foundational stone, which supports the whole structure of the house. Bede warns that some read, be built up upwards, which fits beautifully with the affection of the pious, by which they tend toward heaven Col. 3. v. 1. Peter looks, moreover, both to the Prophecy Esa. 54. v. 11. where the gathering of the Church of the N. T. is likewise compared to a building. Behold I will lay thy stones in carbuncle, and will found thee with sapphires vers. 12. and I will make thy windows of jasper, and thy gates of graven stones, and all thy borders of desirable stones; and to the words of Christ Matth. 16. v. 18. Upon this rock οἰκοδομήσω I will build my Church.

Οἶκος πνευματικὸς. Jerome in chapter 28 of Ezekiel, Leo sermon 3 on the Assumption, Ambrose in chapter 3 of Luke, and Bede in this place read in the accusative case, and plural number. Be built up as spiritual houses, and he adds here. Thus he says that they ought to become spiritual houses, since there is one house of Christ, founded from all the elect Angels and men, just as since there is one Catholic Church spread throughout the whole world, they are often called Churches in the plural on account of the manifold, namely, gatherings of the faithful, distinguished by various tribes, tongues, and peoples. But he soon adds. Nor is it to be passed over, that some Codices have it in the singular. Be built up as a spiritual house, others, be built up upwards into a spiritual house, in which, indeed, the unity itself of the whole most holy Church is more openly commended. But this variety of reading only has a place in Latin Codices. For the Greeks constantly read οἶκος πνευματικὸς in which way the Syrian also translates, be a spiritual temple, and Augustine in Epistle 57 to Dardanus alleges it in the same way. Be built up as a spiritual house, that is, so that you may be a spiritual house. Some add, that the plural number does not sufficiently agree with the matter of which it is treated here, since individual stones are not built into individual houses, but many into one house, since the Church is a congregation of the faithful and the pious. But it cannot be denied, that even individual faithful are a spiritual house of GOD, inasmuch as in whose hearts Christ he dwells through faith Eph. 3. v. 17. and whose bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit 1. Cor. 3. v. 16. Peter, however, looks to the sayings of the O. T. in which the Mosaic tabernacle, and also the Jerusalem temple, is called the house of GOD Exod. 23. v. 19. cap. 34. v. 26. Deut. 23. v. 18. and elsewhere throughout, and he teaches that that external and bodily temple was a figure of the spiritual house, i. e., of the Church in the N. T. to be built from Jews and Gentiles through the word of the Gospel, whence the Syrian, leading us closer to the type, rendered it: Be ye [consult facsimile image] a spiritual temple.

Ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον. In the temple of the Old Testament, priests were divinely appointed and consecrated, so that they might daily offer victims to GOD. Peter adapts this to the faithful of the N. T., and says that they are not only built into a spiritual house, and a temple holy to the Lord, but also into a holy Priesthood, so that they may be spiritual Priests before GOD. The difference, however, is in this, that in the Old Testament only certain persons were chosen for the Priesthood, namely the Levites, but in the New Testament all the truly pious are Priests. Likewise, in the O. T. the priests offered bodily sacrifices, but in the N. T. they offer spiritual sacrifices. In the O. T. they were anointed with external oil, but in the N. T. they are consecrated with spiritual and internal oil, namely the Holy Spirit. In the O. T. the priests were indeed holy, i. e., consecrated and deputed to the priestly office, but not all were endowed with internal holiness. But the spiritual Priests of the N. T. are all holy, not only by external calling, but also by the internal sanctification of the Spirit, for unless they were sanctified by the Spirit, they could by no means offer spiritual sacrifices pleasing to GOD, whence the Apostle notably added, that they are built as a spiritual house, so also as a holy Priesthood. Furthermore, as the name House is aggregative, signifying a structure heaped together from many stones, so also the name Priesthood is collective, signifying the whole assembly, or college of priests, with which explanation it by no means conflicts that some say the abstract is here put for the concrete, just as elsewhere circumcision is wont to be used for circumcised Jews, and foreskin for uncircumcised Gentiles. For thus the faithful are built as a spiritual house and a holy Priesthood, so that individuals also are a spiritual house and holy Priests. But as the name of house is placed figuratively, as the added epithet, spiritual, shows: so also the name of Priesthood is placed figuratively is used, as the added epithet Holy shows, which the Apostle illustrates more clearly when he adds that the end of the consecration to a holy Priesthood is that which the pious ought to ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ.. Such as the Priesthood is, such also are the sacrifices. Since, therefore, the pious in the New Testament are consecrated into spiritual Priests, they therefore also ought to offer spiritual sacrifices, which are good works of every kind, prescribed in the divine law. There is contained, therefore, in these words a tacit exhortation to good works, inasmuch as they are those spiritual sacrifices to the offering of which the pious have been divinely called in Baptism and consecrated by the Holy Spirit. If, therefore, they wish to behave in a manner obedient to their calling and competent to their dignity, they should certainly also perform legitimately the duty of the Priesthood entrusted to them in offering spiritual sacrifices. He also adds a new argument for exhortation when he says, that those sacrifices are acceptable or pleasing to GOD. For whatever is acceptable and pleasing to GOD, that the children of GOD ought to hold uniquely commended to themselves, so that they may perform it as a testimony of filial obedience. Whatever sacrifices spiritual Priests know to be acceptable to GOD and an odor of sweetness before Him, in offering them they ought not to be remiss and sluggish. Finally, whatever is pleasing and acceptable to GOD, that is also rewarded by grace. Let the pious, therefore, by no means think that they are taking vain labor in offering spiritual sacrifices, but let them know that a most generous reward of grace is prepared for them. Προσδιοριμὸν added, διὰ Ιησοῦ χριστοῦ, Bede refers to the whole preceding sentence. Which, he says, he says in the conclusion, through Jesus Christ, pertains to all things which he had premised, because through His grace we are both built up in Him by wise architects, that is, ministers of the New Testament, and we are made spiritual houses through His Spirit, and we are not able to participate in a holy Priesthood and to perform anything good acceptable to God except through Him. Others refer it to the word ἀνενέγκαι because of the parallel passage Heb. 13. v. 15. through Him let us offer the sacrifice of praise &c. But it is more correctly referred to the words immediately preceding εὐπροσδέκτους τῷ θεῷ, in the sense that those spiritual sacrifices are not pleasing to God except in Christ and through Christ; although the meaning remains the same, whether we refer this προσδιορισμὸν to the word to offer or to the noun acceptable. Because, indeed, spiritual Priests are in Christ through faith, therefore also their spiritual sacrifices please God. Conversely, because Christ as our only Mediator and Priest of the New Testament, He offers to GOD the spiritual sacrifices received from the faithful, covers the imperfection and impurity adhering to them with His most perfect obedience, and commends them by His intercession, Apoc. 8. Vers. 1. and following, and thence and therefore those spiritual sacrifices are pleasing and acceptable to the heavenly Father. Thus, therefore, through this προσδιορισμὸν the Apostle meets a tacit objection, and raises up the faithful against doubt.
