For when they acknowledge their own obedience to be imperfect, lacking, and mutilated, and indeed even contaminated by the stains of sins, they sometimes doubt thence whether it is pleasing and acceptable to GOD. The Apostle answers that in Christ, and through Christ, that obedience is pleasing to GOD. He also suppresses the Pharisaical pride concerning the perfection of good works before the judgment of GOD, when he attributes solely to the merit and intercession of Christ that our works, in themselves imperfect and impure, are pleasing to God.

Latin:

AD QUEM ACCEDENTES, LAPIDEM VIVUM, AB HOMINIBUS QUIDEM REPROBATUM, A DEO AUTEM ELECTUM & HONORIFICATUM. ET IPSI TANQUAM LAPIDES VIVI SUPERAEDIFICAMINI DOMUS SPIRITUALIS, SACERDOTIUM SANCTUM, OFFERRE SPIRITUALES HOSTIAS ACCEPTABILES DEO PER IESUM CHRISTUM.

Connexio. 1 Alterum exhortationis argumentum profert à piorum dignitate, quam duabus exprimit similitudinibus, quando confert eos cum templo & Sacerdotibus V. T. Quicunque sunt spiritualis DEI domus, ac spirituales Sacerdotes, illos oportet deponere omnem malitiam, omnem dolum, adeoque omnem immunditiem spiritualem. Atqui verè fideles, qui ad Christum fide accesserunt sunt spiritualis DEI domus & spirituales Sacerdotes. Ergò deponere debent omnem malitiam, omnem dolum, adeoque omnem immunditiem spiritualem. Maioris confirmatio peti potest ex eo, quod templum Vet. T. mandato DEI oportuit servari mundum ac minimè pollui Lev. 15. v. 31.cap. 21. v. 12.Num. 19. v. 13. &c. quodque Sacerdotes mundiciei ac sanctitati studiosissimos esse oportuit. Levit. 21. v. 6. Ut ergò antitypus typo respondeat, etiam spirituale templum, & spirituales Sacerdotes mundos esse oportet.

2. Potest etiam argumentum à dignitate piorum petitum sic informari. Quò maior ac praestantior est dignitas fidelium in N. quàm Iudaeorum in V. T. eò quoque ardentius pietatis studium ab ipsis requiritur. Iam vero piorum in N. T. longè illustrior ac praestantior est dignitas, quàm Iudaeorum in V. T. quia fideles in N. T. super lapidem angularem Christum extructi sunt domus spiritualis, cum Iudaei in V. T. templum externum & materiale habuerint; sunt etiam spirituales Sacerdotes, cum Iudaeorum Sacerdotes spirituales victimas obtulerint. Ergò etiam à fidelibus in N. T. ardentius pietatis studium requiritur.

3. Confirmat exhortationem à salutari vocationis ad Christum initio. Quando Evangelii doctrinam fide recepistis, iamdum ad Christum accedere, ac instar vivorum lapidum super ipsum tanquam angularem lapidem aedificari caepistis, aequum igitur est, ut in hac vocatione vestra constanter pergatis, ac quotidianis in fide profectibus ad CHRISTUM accedentes, ipsi tanquam vivi lapides magis magisque super eum aedificemini, sicque in vita spirituali maiora subinde incrementa capiatis. Hac ratione cohaeret hic versiculus cum verbis proximè praecedentibus, in vers. 2. ut in eo crescatis.

4. Fideles in Christo renatos comparaverat modò genitis infantibus, eosque hoc nomine ad deponendam malitiam, infantili innocentiae & simplicitati oppositam, fuerat exhortatus, iam ad affinem apud Hebraeos metaphoram transit ac spirituali aedificio eos comparat. Hebraeis enim בניםfilii dicuntur à rad. בנהaedificavit. Ut enim ex lapidibus domus, ita ex filiis praesertim masculis familiae aedificantur. Ac suavis quaedam paranomasia est inter בניםquod filiosאבנים quod lapides significat. Quos ergò Petrus prius vocaverat בנים infantes modò genitos, illos confert אבנים חיים lapidibus viventibus, ex quibus spiritualis domus fabrica est extructa.

5. Beda eiusmodi connexionem affert. Quoniam in ipso Psalmo, de quo hunc versiculum assumsit (puta 34.) praemissum est, Accedite ad eum & illuminamini, rectè B. Petrus subdidit, Ad quem accedentes lapidem vivum.

6. Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus eos ad quos scribit ad spiritualem profectum tùm in fide vera, tùm in vita sancta. Priorem exhortationis partem illustrat similitudine ex Scripturis V. Test. petitâ, quâ Christum comparat lapidi angulari & fundamentali, fideles verò lapidibus, qui lapidi fundamentali superaedificantur. Hortatur igitur eos, ut super hunc lapidem magis ac magis aedificentur h. e. ut per fidem magis cum ipso quasi conglutinentur & coalescant. Posteriorem exhortationis partem illustrat alia similitudine, quâ fideles comparat Sacerdotibus, bona opera hostiis. Hortatur igitur eos, ut à DEO Sacerdotes spirituales constituti & consecrati spirituales hostias DEO offerant.

7. Non solùm Christianorum; sed etiam ipsius Christi dignitatem argumenti loco Apostolus adducit, quo propositam suam exhortationem confirmet, dum eum vocat lapidem vivum ab hominibus quidem reprobatum, à DEO autem electum & honorificatum; lapidem summum angularem, electum & preciosum. Quotquot enim Christiani fide ad CHRISTUM conversi pristinae conversationis sordes, malitiam, dolum, simulationem &c. adeoque veterem hominem deponere nolunt, CHRISTUM ipsum à DEO tantoperè honoratum ignominiâ afficiunt, ac nomen eius apud Ethnicos & Iudaeos incredulos infamant.

Textus expositio. Ad quemπροσερχόμενοι, sc. ad Dominum, sive CHRISTUM, cuius suavitatem gustatis.Προσερχόμενοι praesentis temporis significationem habet, neque enim tantùm primam eorum, ad quos scribit, ad CHRISTUM conversionem, sed etiam praesentem eorum statum describit, quòd in CHRISTO iam renati quotidianâ fidei continuatione & incremento magis ad eum accedant, seque arctiùs ei coniungant. Syrus tamen videtur praeteriti significationem expressisse [consult facsimile image]ad quem appropinquastis, vel appropinquare fecistis.

Λίθον ζῶντα. Vocat CHRISTUM lapidem, sc. fundamentalem & angularem, qui totam Ecclesiae domum sustentat, eique firmitatem praestat, quia credentes in CHRISTUM domui ac lapidibus super fundamentum extructis comparare instituerat. Desumit autem hanc appellationem ex Vet. Test. Scriptura, videlicet ex Psalmis & Propheta Esaia, quorum testimonia paulo pòst adducit. Non autem simpliciter CHRISTUM vocat lapidem, sed addit vivum, ut metaphoram exprimat, ac proprietates & effectus huius lapidis innuat, qui non solùm in se vitam habeat, sed etiam Iapides super se extructos, h. e. fide sibi adhaerentes vivificet.

Ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον. Per homines lapidem hunc reprobantes non solùm in specie intelligit stolidos illos architectos, qui hunc lapidem reprobaverunt, de quibus v. 7. ex Psal. 118. v. 22. agit, videlicet Pontifices, Scribas & Pharisaeos in populo Iudaico, sed etiam in genere omnes incredulos ex Iudaeis & gentibus, qui beneficia Christi in Evangelio sibi oblata contumaciter respuunt.

Παρά δε θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν, ἐντιμον. Vulgata reddidit, à DEO electum, sed Graeca potiùs sonant, apud DEUM electum, quo modo etiam Syrus vertit [consult facsimile image]ἐκλεκτὸς hîc non accipitur participialiter, sed nominaliter sensu eo, quo etiam Angeli dicuntur electi, i. e. eximii, praestantes, excellentes1. Tim. 5. v. 21. sicut etiam. Hebraeorum בחיר & בחור usurpatur Esa. 42. v. 1.Ezech. 23. v. 6. ac substantivum םבחר significat rem excellentem ac praestantem Genes. 23. v. 6.Ierem. 48. v. 15.2. Reg. 3. v. 19. &c. nam in libera & recta electione non solet eligi, quod pessimum, sed quod optimum. Syrus habet nomen [consult facsimile image] quod non solùm, verti potest per electum, sed etiam excelsum sublimem, & excellentem. Idipsum ostendit adiectum nomen ἔντιμος, quod prioris est ἐξήγησις, ideò atque inde hic lapis apud DEUM electus, quia in magno apud eum precio, ut sic quaedam allusio sit ad lapides praestantes, qui apud homines in precio. Opponit autem hoc Apostolus per quandam prolepsin falso iudicio incredulorum lapidem huncce reprobantium. Quamvis ad ignominiam huius lapidis cedere videatur, quod ab hominibus, vel ut Syrus emphaticè reddidit, à filiis virorum, i. e. ab illis, qui inter homines dignitate eminent, reprobetur, nihil tamen ex eo dignitati huius lapidis decedit, quia apud DEUM ipsi constat sua dignitas, suumque precium.

καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθον ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε. Sicut CHRISTUM vocaverat lapidem vivum, ita quoque credentes vocat vivos lapides, ut metaphorae continuationem ostendat. Diversâ tamen ratione CHRISTUM vocat lapidem vivum, ac fideles lapides vivos. Christum vocat vivum in significatione activa, quia vitam lapidibus super se extructis communicat. Fideles vocat vivos in significatione passiva, quia vitam à lapide fundamentali Christo, cui superstructi sunt, accipiunt. Proinde illud καὶ αὐτοὶ etiam vos ipsi, tantùm ad rei paritatem, non autem ad modi aequalitatem referendum, ut sit sensus. Non solùm Christus Ecclesiae fundamentum est lapis vivus, sed etiam vos, ut lapides vivi, ei aedificamini, interim modo diverso vita illa & Christo, & vobis competit. Verbum οἰκοδομεῖσθε Erasmus accipit imperativè, ut sit exhortationis continuatio, ac respondeat v. 2.ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε, quo modo etiam Syriacum [consult facsimile image] Tremellius vertit, aedificemini. Sed rectiùs accipitur in modo indicativo, quo modo Beda legit, & addit. Superaedificari illos dicit; quia sine Domino nostro Iesu Christo, lapide scil. vivo, nulla spiritualis aedificatio stare potest. Versatur enim Apostolus in exaggeranda piorum dignitate, quòd per fidem ad Christum accedentes, super Christum lapidem fundamentalem, ut vivi lapides aedificentur. Vulgatus Interpres reddidit super aedificamini, ad sensum respiciens, sed in Graeco est simplex οἰκοδομεῖσθε, quod tamen ita complendum ex Eph. 2. v. 20.aedificamini super eo, tanquam lapide fundamentali, qui totam domus fabricam suffulcit. Beda monet, quosdam legere, sursum aedificamini, quod pulcrè congruit piorum affectui, quo in coelum tendunt Col. 3. v. 1. Respicit autem Petrus, tùm ad Prophetiam Esa. 54. v. 11. ubi collectio Ecclesiae N. T. itidem comparatur aedificio. Ecce ego ponam in carbunculo lapides tuos, & fundabo te in Saphirisvers. 12.& ponam Smaragdum fenestras tuas, & portas tuas in lapides rubinos, & omnes terminos tuos in lapides desiderabiles; tùm ad verba Christi Matth. 16. v. 18.Super hanc petramοἰκοδομήσωaedificabo Ecclesiam meam.

Οἶκος πνευματικὸς. Hieronymus in cap. 28. Ezech. Leo serm. 3. in assumt. Ambrosius in cap. 3. Lucae, & Beda h. l. legunt in casu aceusativo, & numero plurali. Super aedificamini domos spirituales, & addit hic. Ita illos domus spirituales fieri debere dicit, cum sit una domus Christi, ex electis omnibus Angelis & hominibus condita, quomodo cum sit una Ecclesia Catholica toto orbe diffusa, saepè pluraliter appellantur Ecclesiae propter multifaria sc. fidelium conventicula, variis tribubus, linguis & populis discreta. Sed mox subiungit. Nec praetereundum, quod quidam Codices habent in singulari. Super aedifiamini domus spiritualis, alii, sursum aedificamini in domum spiritualem, in quo nimirum unitas ipsa totius sacrosanctae Ecclesiae apertiùs commendatur. Sed haec varietas lectionis tantùm locum habet in Codicibus Latinis. Graeci enim constanter legunt οἶκος πνευματικὸς quo modo etiam vertit Syrus, estote templum spirituale, ac Augustinus Epist. 57. ad Dardanum eodem modo allegat. Aedificamini domus spiritualis, h. e. ita ut sitis domus, spiritualis. Quidam addunt, non satis congruere pluralem numerum rei, de quâ hîc agitur, cum non singuli lapides aedificentur in singulas domus, sed multi in unam domum, cum Ecclesia sit fidelium & piorum congregatio. Sed negari nequit, quòd etiam singuli fideles sint spiritualis DEI domus, quippe in quorum cordibus Christus per fidem habitat Eph. 3. v. 17. & quorum corpora sunt Spiritus sancti templa1. Cor. 3. v. 16. Respicit autem Petrus ad dicta V. T. in quibus tabernaculum Mosaicum, it. templum Hierosolymitanum vocatur domus DEIExod. 23. v. 19.cap. 34. v. 26.Deut. 23. v. 18. & alibi passim, ac docet templum illud externum & corporale fuisse figuram domus spiritualis, i. e. Ecclesiae in N. T. per verbum Evangelii ex Iudaeis & gentibus aedificandae, unde Syrus propiùs ad typum nos deducens reddidit. Estote[consult facsimile image]templum spirituale.

Ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον. In templo Vet. Test. Sacerdotes erant divinitùs constituti & consecrati, ut quotidiè DEO victimas offerrent. Hoc Petrus ad fideles N. T. accommodat, ac dicit, eos non solùm aedificari in domum spiritualem, ac templum Domino sanctum, sed etiam in sanctum Sacerdotium, ut sint coram DEO spirituales Sacerdotes. Discrimen tamen in eo est, quòd in Vet. Test. tantùm certae quaedam personae ad Sacerdotium erant electae, videlicet Levitae, sed in N. Test. omnes verè pii sunt Sacerdotes. Item in V. T. Sacerdotes offerebant hostias corporales, sed in N. Test. offerunt hostias spirituales. In V. T. ungebantur oleo externo, sed in N. Test. oleo spirituali & interno, videlicet Spiritu sancto consecrantur. In V. T. Sacerdotes erant quidem sancti, i. e. consecrati, ac deputati ad munus Sacerdotale, non autem omnes erant internâ sanctitate praediti. Sed spirituales N. T. Sacerdotes omnes sunt sancti, non solùm externâ vocatione, sed etiam internâ Spiritus sanctificatione, nisi enim à Spiritu sanctificati essent, spirituales hostias DEO gratas offerre minimè possent, unde Apostolus notanter adiecit, quòd aedificentur ut domus spiritualis, ita quoque ut Sacerdotium sanctum. Caeterùm ut nomen Domus est aggregativum, significans fabricam ex multis lapidibus congestam, ita quoque Sacerdotii nomen est collectivum, significans totum caetum, seu collegium Sacerdotium, cum qua explicatione minimè pugnat, quòd quidam dicunt, abstractum hîc poni pro concreto, sicut aliàs circumcisio pro circumcisis Iudaeis, praeputium pro incircumcisis gentibus usurpari solet. Ita enim aedificantur fideles domus spiritualis ac Sacerdotium sanctum, ut singuli etiam sint domus spiritualis & sancti Sacerdotes. Ut autem nomen domus figuratè ponitur, uti ostendit adiectum epitheton, spiritualis: ita quoque nomen Sacerdotii figuratè usurpatur, ut ostendit adiectum epitheton Sanctum, quod ipsum clariùs illustrat Apostolus, quando subiungit, finem consecrationis ad sanctum Sacerdotium esse eum, quod pii debeant ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους τῷ θεῷ διὰ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Quale Sacerdotium, tales etiam hostiae. Cum ergò pii in N. T. sint consecrati in spirituales Sacerdotes, ideò etiam spirituales hostias offerre debent, quae sunt omnis generis bona opera, in lege divina praescripta. Continetur igitur in his verbis tacita exhortatio ad bona opera, quippe quae sunt spirituales illae hostiae, ad quas offerendas pii in Baptismo divinitus sint vocati & per Spiritum sanctum consecrati. Quòd si ergò suae vocationi obsequentes, suaeque dignitati competentes se gerere velint, utique etiam in offerendis hostiis spiritualibus Sacerdotii sibi concrediti munere legitimè fungantur. Addit etiam novum exhortationis argumentum, quando dicit, hostias illas esse DEO acceptabiles sive gratas. Quicquid enim DEO acceptabile & gratum, illud filii DEI debent sibi unicè habere commendatum, ut in filialis obsequii testimonium illud praestent. Quascunque etiam hostias Sacerdotes spirituales norunt DEO esse acceptas & odorem suavitatis coram ipso, in illis offerendis non debent esse remissi ac segnes. Denique quicquid DEO gratum & acceptum, illud etiam ex gratia remuneratur. Nequaquam igitur cogitent pii, se in offerendis spiritualibus hostiis vanam operam sumere, sed largissimam gratiae mercedem sibi paratam sciant. Προσδιοριμὸν adiectum, διὰ Ιησοῦ χριστοῦ, Beda ad totam praecedentem sententiam refert. Quod, inquit, in conclusione dicit, per Iesum Christum, ad cuncta, quae praemiserat, pertinet, quia per ipsius gratiam & super aedificamur in illo per architectos sapientes hoc est ministros N. T. & domus spirituales efficimur per Spiritum eius, & Sacerdotio sancto participare & boni aliquid acceptabile Deo gerere non nisi per ipsum valemus. Alii referunt ad verbum ἀνενέγκαι propter locum parallelum Heb. 13. v. 15.per ipsum offeramus hostiam laudis &c. Sed rectiùs refertur ad verba proximè praecedentia εὐπροσδέκτους τῷ θεῷ, sensu eo quod spirituales illae hostiae, non nisi in Christo & per Christum Deo sunt gratae; quamvis idem maneat sensus, sive ad verbum offerre sive ad nomen acceptabiles hunc προσδιορισμὸν referamus. Quia n. spirituales Sacerdotes sunt in Christo per fidem, ideò etiam spirituales ipsorum hostiae Deo placent. Vicissim quia Christus tanquam unicus noster Mediator & Novi Testamenti Sacerdos, spirituales hostias à fidelibus susceptas DEO offert, imperfectionem & immunditiem illis adhaerentem suâ perfectissima obedientia tegit, suaque intercessione eas commendat, Apoc. 8. Vers. 1. & seqq. inde atque ideò hostiae illae spirituales sunt Patri coelesti gratae & acceptae. Sic ergò per hunc προσδιορισμὸν occurrit Apostolus tacitae obiectioni, & erigit fideles contra dubitationem. Cum enim obedientiam suam agnoscant esse imperfectam, mancam & mutilam, quin & peccatorum maculis contaminatam, inde dubitant quandoque, an ea sit DEO grata & accepta. Respondet Apostolus, in Christo, & per Christum obedientiam illam esse DEO gratam. Deprimit etiam fastum Pharisaicum de perfectione bonorum operum coram DEI iudicio, quando Christi merito & intercessioni unicè tribuit, quòd sint opera nostra, in se imperfecta & immunda, Deo grata.

## 2:4-8 Questions and observations
Observations. 1. Access to GOD joined with a taste of goodness. The human mind naturally flees from GOD, because it conceives of Him as a severe judge; it does not approach Him, unless it tastes His goodness in Christ.

2. It is not enough to have approached Christ once by faith, and to have begun to be built upon Him, but continuation and a closer union is required. Those who have begun to be built upon Christ through faith should progress daily in faith, so that they may coalesce more firmly with Christ.

3. One must approach Christ to that end, that we may be built in Him, because He has been placed by God in the Church as a foundational stone; that we may be enlivened by Him, because He has been placed as a living stone.

4. We approach Christ not with bodily steps, but with the affection of a devout mind by believing in Him, by adhering to Him, by placing all the confidence of the heart in Him, by desiring Him, by loving Him.

5. In the same way we are also built upon Him by true faith. Augustine in Psal. 4.You are raised into this structure with pious affection, with sincere religion, with faith, hope, and charity, and to walk is to build him himself.

6. Just as stones in a building are not only built upon a foundation, but are also joined to one another by the glue of lime, so the pious are not only built upon Christ the living stone through faith: but are also joined to one another by the glue of charity. Eph. 4. v. 15. & 16.

7. Peter, named thus from the rock Christ, delights in the metaphor of the rock, and by his own example teaches that all ought to be Peters, that is, living stones built upon Christ by faith.

8. Christ is the living stone οὐσιωδῶς, ἐνεργητικῶς, ποιητικῶς;, believers are living stones παθητικῶς participatively, receptively, passively.

9. Spiritual and eternal life is to be sought only in Christ, the living and fundamental stone of the Church.

10. The comparison of the pious with stones can warn them of many things. First, a stone to be placed in the structure of a house must be hard and firm, so that it may sustain both the incumbent mass and the assaults of storms: so the pious man must be firm and constant, so that he may sustain the winds of persecutions and the waves of temptations. He receives this strength from Christ truly, just as he receives life from him, as from a living stone. Second, a stone to be placed in the structure of a house must first be prepared and hewn before it is applied to the building: so believers in this life must first be hewn by the doctrine of the law, by the rebukes of ministers, and by the iron tool of the cross, so that they may become fit for the spiritual building. Of. 6. v. 5. Author of the imperfect work, homily 40. Just as builders hew knotty stones, and those having twists, with iron, and afterwards place them in the building, otherwise unhewn stones do not cohere with stones: so the doctors of the Church must first circumcise the vices of men, as if they were knots, with sharp rebukes, and thus place them in the building of the Church. Bede on this passage. They are fitted as living stones to a spiritual building, who, through the discretion of a learned Doctor, are squared as if by the blow of an axe, with superfluous acts and thoughts amputated. And this is the difference between the citizens of the militant and the triumphant Church: for the former must first be hewn in this life, but the latter will no longer have need of legal rebukes and the chastisement of the cross, of which thing a type preceded in the construction of Solomon's temple, concerning which 1. Reg. 6.

v. 7. it is said. And the house, when it was in building, was built of stones hewed and made ready, so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building. Thirdly, that preparation and hewing of the stones is done to a certain plumb line, just as the whole structure of the house is also measured to the line of the plumb. Ignatius applies that to the spiritual structure thus in his Epistle to the Ephesians. Christ has founded you upon the rock as chosen stones, fit for the divine building of the Father, lifted up on high by Christ, who was crucified for us, using the Holy Spirit as a plumb line; and drawn up by faith and raised by charity into heaven. Fourthly, the quantity of all stones is not the same, but some are smaller, some larger, yet all are useful for the structure: thus the progress of all the pious is not the same, nor is the same abundance of gifts, man bedarff nicht allein Quadersteine/sondern auch Fullsteine. Fifthly, just as in a building stones rest upon one another and mutually support each other: so in the Church one ought to bear the burden of another Gal. 6. v. 2. Bede in this place. Just as the courses of stones in a wall are supported by one another, so are all the faithful supported by the just who precede them in the Church, and they themselves also support the just who follow through doctrine and tolerance, even to the last just man, who, while he is supported by those before him, will have no one following whom he ought to support. But He who supports the whole building, and is Himself supported by no one, is the Lord Christ, whence He is also called a precious stone by the Prophet, founded in the foundation.

II. The comparison of the Church with a house in general, and with the house of GOD or the Jerusalem temple in particular, is also illustrious, whence it is even called the House of GOD itself. 1. Tim. 3. v. 15.Hebr. 3. v. 6. The foundation, upon which this house is built, is Christ 1. Cor. 3. v. 11.Eph. 2. v. 20. the stones, from which this house is built, are all true believers, as Peter teaches in this place. The cement is the unity of faith Eph. 4. v. 5. and sincere charity, which is the bond of peace Eph. 4. v. 3. and of perfection Col. 3. v. 14. The door of this house is Christ John 10. v. 7. The porter is the Holy Spirit v. 3. the walls are the holy Angels Ps. 34. v. 8. the roof is divine protection Isa. 4. v. 6. the light in this house is the Gospel Ps. 119. v. 105. The architects of this house and of GOD in building this edifice σύνεργοι are all the faithful Doctors of the Church, who are therefore called architects1. Cor. 3. v. 9. & 10. and buildersPs. 118. v. 22. But it behooves architects in building an edifice to direct everything to the norm of the foundational stone: thus the doctrine of Christ ought to be the rule of spiritual edification. Let them not be like those who daub the wall with mortar not rightly mixed Ezech. 13. v. 10. they do that who do not censure the crimes of the hearers, who dissemble and palliate the errors of religion. But this spiritual building is erected through the ministry of the word, and just as a building rises on high by the addition of stones: so the spiritual building of the Church grows by the conversion of many to Christ by a certain προσθέσει as it were, and rises on high, because the truly pious dwell in spirit in the heavens, and seek those things which are above. Col. 3. v. 1.

12. Not only do all the pious and truly believing of all times, places, and nations constitute one spiritual house and one mystical temple, but also individual particular assemblies of the pious, nay even individual true believers are a spiritual temple of God and a spiritual house, belonging to that universal and Catholic temple as certain parts or living stones of it. Ioh. 14. v. 23.1. Cor. 3. v. 16.cap. 6. v. 19.2. Cor. 6. v. 18. Clement of Alexandria, book 2 of the Stromata, cites a saying of Barnabas, a companion of Paul. Before we believed in God, the corruptible and fragile dwelling of our heart was a temple truly made by hand, because it was full of idolatry, and was of demons, because we did those things which were contrary to God. But take heed, that the temple of God may be built gloriously. How? By receiving the remission of sins and hoping in the name of Christ, let us become new and created anew, in that God truly dwells in our dwelling. How? When the word of his Son, the calling of his promise, the wisdom of the justifications, and the mandates of the doctrine dwell in us.

13. Just as Christ is the temple of GodCol. 2. v. 9. our Priest and King, so he makes the pious the temples of God, and spiritual Priests and Kings before God. Apoc. 1. v. 6.cap. 5. v. 10. Irenaeus, book 4, chapter 20, p. 245. All the just have the priestly order.

14. They are called and are indeed Priests, and truly holy and spiritual. 1. Because they are anointed to the spiritual Priesthood by Christ the high Priest, not indeed with external oil, as the Priests of the O.T., but with the oil of gladness or the Holy Spirit. Psalm. 45. vers. 8. 2 Because they are members of Christ the Priest. Augustine, book 20 of the City of God, chapter 10, after he had brought forward the passage of Apoc. 20. They shall be Priests of God and of Christ, he adds. It was not said only of Presbyters and Bishops, who are now properly called Priests in the Church, but just as we call all Christians because of the mystical chrism: so all are Priests, since they are members of one Priest. 3. Because they offer spiritual sacrifices to GOD. As a sign of this matter, some think that the paschal lamb was slaughtered for sacrifice by the whole multitude of the Israelites. Philo lib. 3. de vita Mosis. At the Paschal time, not as at other times do common men bring victims to the altar to be slaughtered by the Priests, but the law commanding it, the whole nation sacrifices, while each one slaughters a victim for himself with his own hands. 4. Because as the Priests of the O. Test. were ordered to abstain from legal impurities: so they ought to guard themselves studiously from every spiritual impurity, since they are a holy Priesthood. 5. Because at some time in eternal life they will offer themselves entirely to the perpetual praise of GOD as if in a perennial sacrifice. Apocal. 20. vers. 6.

15. The spiritual sacrifices, which the pious offer to GOD in the N. Test., are various. First, they offer themselves to GOD as a pleasing sacrifice, through the denial of self, and the mortification of the flesh. Roman. 12. vers. 1. Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to GOD, your reasonable service. On which words Origen comments thus in lib. 9. in Epist. Rom. Those who mortify their members, offer a living sacrifice reasonably, and fulfill the law of sacrifices, which is in Leviticus, according to spiritual understanding. If they conquer pride, they sacrifice a calf; if they overcome wrath, a ram; if lust, a goat; if they cut off the wandering and slippery flights of thoughts, doves and turtledoves. Gregor. homil. 22. in Ezech. The altar of burnt offering is the mind of one living well. A living sacrifice is a body afflicted for the Lord. A sacrifice, because it is already dead to this world, living because it performs all the good things that it can. Psalm. 51. v. 19. A sacrifice pleasing to GOD is a troubled spirit. A sacrifice of a contrite heart pleases GOD more than a slaughtered beast. August. lib. 10. de Civit. DEI cap. 5. 2. Prayers and thanksgivings, Psal. 50. vers. 14. & 23. Psal. 54. vers. 8. Psal. 107. vers. 22. Psal. 116. vers. 17. Psal. 141. vers. 2 Hebr. 5. vers. 7. cap. 13. vers. 15. Apoc. 5. vers. 8. cap. 8. vers. 4. Iustinus in Dial. cum Tryphone pag. 270. Supplications at the same time and thanksgivings, which are performed by the worthy, I myself would also affirm to be the only perfect and dear victims to GOD. Tertull. lib. adv. Iudaeos pag. 104. He names some sacrifices as temporal of earthly offerings, others as spiritual of praise and thanksgiving. Augustinus in Psal. 94. If we are the temple of GOD, our soul is the altar of GOD. A sacrifice of GOD what is? We place a sacrifice upon the altar, when we praise GOD. 3. Alms Phil. 4. v. 18.Heb. 13. v. 16. 4. Death endured for the sake of the confession of the Gospel is likewise a sacrifice Phil. 2. v. 7.2. Tim. 4. ver. 6. Augustine, book 10 of The City of God, chapter 4. When we approach GOD, our heart is His altar, and we are appeased by His only-begotten Priest (Vives reads, we appease Him by His only-begotten Priest) we slay bloodless victims to Him, when we strive even unto blood for His truth. Irenaeus, book 4, chapter 34, p. 263. It behooves us to make an offering to GOD, and to be found grateful in all things to the Creator GOD with a pure mind, and faith without hypocrisy, in firm hope, in fervent love, offering the first-fruits of those things which are His creatures, and the Church alone offers this pure offering to the Creator, offering to Him with thanksgiving from His creature. 5. Nay, every obedience which the pious perform from the Spirit and faith, whether it be internal or external, is a spiritual victim. Origen on Leviticus, homily 9, chapter 16. Each one has in himself his own burnt offering, and he himself lights the altar of his own burnt offering, so that it may always burn. If I renounce all that I possess, and take up my cross, and follow Christ, I have offered a burnt offering to the altar of GOD, or if I deliver my body to be burned, having charity, and attain the glory of martyrdom, I have offered myself as a burnt offering to the altar of GOD. If I love my brothers, so that I lay down my soul for my brothers, if I strive for justice, for truth even unto death, I have offered a burnt offering to the altar of GOD: If I mortify my members from all concupiscence of the flesh, if the world is crucified to me, and I to the world, I have offered a burnt offering to the altar of my GOD, and I myself am made the Priest of my own victim. Lactantius, book 6 of the Institutes, chapter 24. Whoever obeys all the heavenly precepts, this is truly a worshiper of God, whose sacrifices are the meekness of the mind and an innocent life and good acts, all of which he who exhibits, sacrifices as often as he has done something good and pious. Augustine, book 10 of The City of GOD, chapter 4. We burn the sweetest incense, when we burn in His sight with pure and holy love, we vow and render to Him His gifts in us, and ourselves, we dedicate and consecrate to Him the memory of His benefits with solemnities, feasts, and appointed days, lest ungrateful forgetfulness should creep in with the passage of time, we sacrifice to Him a victim of humility and praise on the altar of the heart with the fire of fervent charity. chapter. 6. A true sacrifice is every work which is done so that we may adhere to GOD in a holy society, referred, that is, to that end of good by which we may be truly blessed. And afterwards. Man himself to the name of GOD consecrated and devoted to GOD, in so far as it dies to the world, that it may live to GOD, is a sacrifice, etc. Our body also, when we chastise it through temperance, if we do this, as we ought, for the sake of GOD, so that we do not present our members as weapons of iniquity for sin, but as weapons of righteousness for GOD, is a sacrifice. If therefore the body, which the soul uses as an inferior like a servant, or like an instrument, when its good and right use is referred to GOD, is a sacrifice, how much more is the soul itself, when it refers itself to GOD, so that, kindled by the fire of His love, it may lose the form of secular concupiscence, and, being subjected to Him as to an unchangeable form, may be reformed, pleasing Him from this, that it has received from His beauty, it becomes a sacrifice.

16. Those spiritual sacrifices are not pleasing and acceptable to GOD except in Christ, and through Christ; for the denial of oneself is not perfect, good works are contaminated by the stain of clinging sin, so that therefore they may please GOD, it is necessary that they be done out of faith in Christ, through which the clinging imperfection and uncleanness may be covered. Lyranus in h. l. warns, that therefore at the end of prayers it is added, through our Lord Jesus Christ, so that it may be signified that not only are our prayers heard for the sake of Christ, but also that they are pleasing to GOD in Him, and through Him. This must be opposed to the diffidence and carnal doubt, by which the pious are sometimes tempted, whether their mutilated and lacking obedience even pleases GOD.

17. Because the spiritual sacrifices of the faithful, and their good works, are pleasing to GOD, therefore He will also reward them most bountifully, by which stimulus we ought to shake off the torpor of the flesh, and excite ourselves to the study of good works.

18. GOD alone is the principal architect of His spiritual house Ps. 48. v. 9. GOD has founded it forever. He Himself places a stone in Zion. He indeed uses the ministry of men for this building, meanwhile all power and efficacy, every success depends solely upon Him.

19. Without our Lord Jesus Christ, namely the living and fundamental stone, no spiritual building can stand, says Bede in v. 4. Hence it was necessary for this stone to be divinely placed in Zion, before other stones were built upon it.

20. Those alone are built upon Christ by true faith who maintain the unity of the Church, and outside the Church that spiritual building has no place, because this stone is placed in Zion.

21. We are those leaning upon Christ the living stone with true and constant faith beyond the danger of a further fall. The interlinear Gloss on this passage: He who believes in Christ shall not be confounded, that is, he shall neither blush at his fall in the present, nor shall he be empty of reward in the future.

22. If he who believes in Christ is not confounded. Therefore, by the contrary sense, he who does not believe shall be put to shame. No one can stand before the judgment of GOD, unless in Christ, and through Christ, because on account of sin it is necessary for all to be put to shame.

23. Not only the common crowd of men repudiates Christ, but also those who are great in this world, and established in eminence of dignity, both Ecclesiastical and Political. If we see the same thing happening still today, let us not be scandalized.

24. Christ is repudiated not only by words, but also by deeds, indeed more by deeds than by words.

25. Just as those foolish builders rejected Christ in their building: so also He Himself in His coming rejected them from being received into the building of His house in the heavens. Bede on this passage: Those who reject Christ in this age, will be rejected by Him in the future.

26. To the judgment of the world rejecting Christ must be opposed the judgment of GOD, who constitutes this stone as the foundation.

27. Vain and void are all the attempts of enemies against Christ. Even against their will and struggling in vain, Christ remains the foundational gift of the Church. He has been placed as the head of the building and King of His people, until He puts all enemies as the footstool of His feet.

28. No middle or third way is given here. As many as do not wish to be built upon this stone will be dashed and crushed by Him, when the stone cut out of the mountain without hands shall break in pieces the clay and the iron, and the brass, and the silver, and the gold, that is, all the kingdoms of this world, Dan. 2. v. 45.

Latin:

Observationes. 1. Accessus ad DEUM cum gustu bonitatis coniunctus. Mens humana naturaliter DEUM sugit, quia eum ut severum iudicem concipit; non accedit ad eum, nisi in Christo eius bonitatem gustet.

2. Non sufficit fide ad Christum semel accessisse, ac super eum aedificari caepisse, sed continuatio & arctior unio requiritur. Qui caeperunt aedificari super Christum per fidem, quotidie in fide proficiant, ut firmiùs cum Christo coalescant.

3. Eo fine ad Christum accedendum, ut in ipso aedificemur, quia positus est à Deo in Ecclesia ut lapis fundamentalis; ut ab ipso vivisicemur, quia positus est ut lapis vivus.

4. Ad Christum accedimus non passibus corporeis, sed affectu devotae mentis in eum credendo, ipsi adhaerendo, in ipsum omnem cordis siduciam collocando, ipsum desiderando, ipsum amando.

5. Eodem modo etiam super ipsum verâ fide aedificamur. Augustinus in Psal. 4.Erigeris in hanc fabricam affectu pio, religione sincera, fide, spe, caritate, & ipsum aedificare ambulare est.

6. Quemadmodum lapides in aedificio non solùm aedificantur super fundamentum, sed etiam calcis glutine invicem coniunguntur, ita pii Christo vivo lapidi per fidem non tantùm superaedificantur: sed caritatis quoque glutine invicem coniunguntur. Eph. 4. v. 15. & 16.

7. Petrus à petra Christo sic denominatus, metaphorâ petrae delectatur, ac suo exemplo docet, omnes debere esse Petros h. e. vivos lapides super Christum fide aedificatos.

8. Christus est lapis vivus οὐσιωδῶς, ἐνεργητικῶς, ποιητικῶς; credentes sunt vivi lapides παθητικῶς participativè, receptivè, passivè.

9. Vita spiritualis & aeterna, non nisi in Christo vivo & fundamentali Ecclesiae lapide quaerenda.

10. Comparatio piorum cum lapidibus de multis eos monere potest. Primò, Lapidem in fabrica domus collocandum oportet esse durum & firmum, ut & molem incumbentem & tempestatum insultus sustineat: sic pium oportet esse firmum & constantem, ut persecutionum ventos, & tentationum fluctus sustineat. Hoc robur accipit à Christo verâ sicut & vitam ab ipso accipit, ut lapide vivo. Secundò, lapidem in fabrica domus collocandum oportet priùs praeparari ac dolari, antequam aedifieio adhibetur: sic credentes in hac vita per doctrinam legis, per reprehensiones ministrorum, per ferramentum crucis priùs dolari oportet, ut spirituali aedificio fiant apti. Of. 6. v. 5. Autor operis impers. homil. 40. Sicut aedificatores nodosos lapides, & habentes tortuositates ferro dolant, postea vero ponunt eos in aedificio, alioqui non dolati lapides lapidibus non cohaerent: sic Ecclesiae doctores vitia hominum, q. nodos, acutis increpationibus primùm circumcidere debent, & sic in Ecclesiae aedificatione collocare. Beda in h. l. Tanquam lapides vivi ad spirituale, aedificium aptantur, qui per discretionem eruditi Doctoris amputatis actibus, & cogitationibus superfluis velut ictu quadrantur securis. Atque hoc est discrimen inter cives Ecclesiae militantis & triumphantis: illos enim in hac vita priùs dolari oportet, hi vero legalibus reprehensionibus & castigatione crucis non ampliùs indigebunt, cuius rei typus in extructione templi Salomonis praecessit, de qua 1. Reg. 6.

v. 7. dicitur. Domus autem cum aedificaretur, de lapidibus dolatis atque perfectis aedificata est, & malleus, & securis, & omne ferramentum non sunt audita in domo, cum aedificaretur. Tertiò, illa lapidum praeparatio & dolatio fit ad certum perpendiculum, sicut etiam tota domûs structura ad lineam perpendiculi exigitur. Illud ad spiritualem structuram sic applicat Ignatius in Epist ad Ephesios. Christus fundavit vos super petram ut lapides electos, aptos ad divinum aedificium Patris, sublatos in altum per Christum, qui pro nobis crucifixus est, perpendiculo usos Spiritu sancto; fide vero subductos & caritate elevatos in coelum. Quartò, non omnium lapidum eadem quantitas, sed quidam sunt minores, quidam maiores, omnes tamen ad structuram utiles: sic piorum non est idem omnium profectus, eadem donorum copia, man bedarff nicht allein Quadersteine/sondern auch Fullsteine. Quintò quemadmodum in aedeficio lapides sibi invicem incumbunt, seseque mutuò portant: sic in Ecclesia alter debet alterius portare onus Gal. 6. v. 2. Beda in h. l. Sicut ordines lapidum in pariete portantur alii ab aliis, ita portantur fideles quique à praecedentibus in Ecclesiaiustis, portant & ipsi sequentes iustos per doctrinam & tolerantiam usque ad ultimum iustum, qui cum à prioribus portetur, quem portare debeat, ipse sequentem non habebit. Qui autem omne aedificium portat, & ipse à nemine portatur, Dominus est Christus, unde & lapis preciosus à Propheta vocatur, in fundamento fundatus.

II. Illustris etiam est comparatio Ecclesiae cum domo in genere, & domo DEI sive templo Hierosolymitano in specie, unde etiam ipsa Domus DEI dicitur. 1. Tim. 3. v. 15.Hebr. 3. v. 6. Fundamentum, super quod haec domus extruitur, est Christus 1. Cor. 3. v. 11.Eph. 2. v. 20. lapides, ex quibus haec domus extruitur, sunt omnes verè credentes, ut Petrus h. l. docet. Caementum est fidei unitas Eph. 4. v. 5. & sincera caritas, quae est vinculum pacis Eph. 4. v. 3. & perfectionis Col. 3. v. 14. Ostium huius domus Christus Ioh. 10. v. 7. Ostiarius Spiritus sanctus v. 3. muri sunt sancti Angeli Psal. 34. v. 8. tectum divina protectio Esai. 4. v. 6. lux in hâc domo, Evangelium Psal. 119. v. 105. Architecti huius domus ac DEI in extruendo hoc aedificio σύνεργοι sunt omnes fideles Ecclesiae Doctores, qui propterea dicuntur architecti1. Cor. 3. v. 9. & 10. & aedificantesPsal. 118. v. 22. Architectos vero in extruendo aedificio omnia ad normam lapidis fundamentalis dirigere oportet: sic doctrina Christi debet esse spiritualis aedificationis regula. Non sint similes illis, qui incrustant parietem calce non rectè mixta Ezech. 13. v. 10. illud faciunt, qui non taxant scelera auditorum, qui religionis errores dissimulant ac palliant. Erigitur autem hoc spirituale aedificium per ministerium verbi, & sicut aedificium accessione lapidum in altum exsurgit: sic aedificium Ecclesiae spirituale conversione multorum ad Christum quadam veluti προσθέσει crescit, ac in altum surgit, quia verè pii animo in coelis habitant, & ea quae sursum sunt, quaerunt. Col. 3. v. 1.

12. Non solùm omnes pii & verè credentes omnium temporum, locorum & gentium unam domum spiritualem, ac unum templum mysticum constituunt, sed etiam singuli caetus particulares piorum, quinimò singuli verè credentes sunt spirituale DEI templum ac domus spiritualis, ad universale & Catholicum illud templum, velut eius quaedam partes seu vivi lapides pertinentes. Ioh. 14. v. 23.1. Cor. 3. v. 16.cap. 6. v. 19.2. Cor. 6. v. 18. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 2. Stromat, citat dictum Barnabae comitis Pauli. Antequam crederemus Deo, domicilium corruptibile & fragile cordis nostri erat templum verè manu factum, quia erat plenum idololatriâ, & erat daemonum, propterea quòd faceremus quae erant Deo contraria. Sed attendite, ut templum Dei gloriosè aedificetur. Quomodo? accipiendo remissionem peccatorum & sperando in nomen Christi, fiamus novi & denuò creati, eò quod in domicilio nostro verè Deus habitat. Quomodo? quando habitat in nobis sermo Filii ipsius, vocatio promissionis ipsius, sapientia iustificationum & mandata doctrinae.

13. Sicut Christus est Dei templumCol. 2. v. 9. Sacerdos & Rex noster, sic pios facit DEI templa, ac spirituales Sacerdotes & Reges coram Deo. Apoc. 1. v. 6.cap. 5. v. 10. Irenaeus lib. 4. cap. 20. p. 245. Omnes iusti Sacerdotalem habent ordinem.

14. Dicuntur autem & sunt Sacerdotes, & quidem sancti ac spirituales. 1. Quia ad spirituale Sacerdotium à Christo summo Sacerdote uncti, non quidem oleo externo, ut V. T. Sacerdotes, sed oleo laetitiae sive Spiritu sancto. Psalm. 45. vers. 8. 2 Quia sunt membra Christi Sacerdotis. Augustinus lib. 20. de Civ. DEI. cap. 10. postquam adduxisset locum Apoc. 20. Erunt Sacerdotes Dei & Christi, subiungit. Non utique de solis Presbyteris & Episcopis dictum est, qui propriè iam vocantur in Ecclesia Sacerdotes, sed sicut omnes Christianos dicimus propter mysticum Chrisma: sic omnes Sacerdotes, quoniam membra sunt unius Sacerdotis. 3. Quia offerunt DEO spirituales hostias. In huius rei signum agnum paschalem à tota Israëlitarum multitudine in sacrificium fuisse mactatum, quidam existimant. Philo lib. 3. de vita Mosis. Tempore Paschali non ut alias plebeii homines victimas adducunt ad altare mactandas à Sacerdotibus, sed iubente lege tota gens sacrificat, dum pro se quisque mactat hostiam suis manibus. 4. Quia ut V. Test. Sacerdotes ab immunditiis legalibus abstinere iussi erant: sic ab omni immunditie spirituali debent studiosè sibi cavere, cum sint sanctum Sacerdotium. 5. Quia aliquando in vita aeterna seipsos totos ad perpetuam DEI laudem q. in perenne sacrificium offerent. Apocal. 20. vers. 6.

15. Spirituales hostiae, quas pii in N. Test. DEO offerunt, variae sunt. Primò offerunt seipsos DEO in gratum sacrificium, per sui ipsius abnegationem, & carnis mortificationem. Roman. 12. vers. 1.Exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, DEO placentem, rationabile obsequium vestrum. in quae verba sic commentatur Origenes lib. 9. in Epist. Rom. Qui membra sua mortificant, hostiam viventem rationabiliter offerunt, & legem sacrificiorum, quae in Levitico est, secundùm spiritualem intelligentiam complent. Si superbiam vincunt, immolant vitulum; si iracundiam superant, arietem; si libidinem, hircum; si vagos & lubricos cogitationum resecant volatus, columbas & turtures. Gregor. homil. 22. in Ezech. Altare holocausti est mens bene viventis. Hostia vivens est corpus Domino afflictum. Hostia, quia iam huic mundo est mortuum, vivens quia cuncta, quae praevalet, bona operatur.Psalm. 51. v. 19.Sacrificium DEO gratum Spiritus contribulatus. Plus DEO placet sacrificiùm contriti pectoris, quàm trucidati pecoris. August. lib. 10. de Civit. DEI cap. 5. 2. Preces & gratiarum actiones, Psal. 50. vers. 14. & 23.Psal. 54. vers. 8.Psal. 107. vers. 22.Psal. 116. vers. 17.Psal. 141. vers. 2Hebr. 5. vers. 7.cap. 13. vers. 15.Apoc. 5. vers. 8.cap. 8. vers. 4. Iustinus in Dial. cum Tryphone pag. 270. Supplicationes simul & gratiarum actiones, quae à dignis peraguntur, solas perfectas esse, & DEO caras victimas, ipse quoque affirmaverim. Tertull. lib. adv. Iudaeos pag. 104. Sacrificia alia temporalia nominat terrenarum oblationum, alia spiritualia laudis & gratiarum actionis. Augustinus in Psal. 94.Si nos sumus templum DEI, ara DEI anima nostra est. Sacrificium DEI quid est? imponimus in ara sacrificium, quando DEUM laudamus. 3. Eleemosynas Phil. 4. v. 18.Hebr. 13. v. 16. 4. Mors propter confessionem Eunagelii tolerata itidem est sacrificium Phil. 2. v. 7.2. Timoth. 4. vers. 6. Augustinus lib. 10. de C. D. cap. 4. Cùm ad DEUM accedimus, eius altare est cor nostrum, eius unigenito cum Sacerdote placamur (Vives legit, eius unigenito Sacerdote eum placamus) ei cruentas victimas caedimus, quando usque ad sanguinem pro eius veritate certamus. Irenaeus lib. 4. cap. 34. p. 263. Oportet nos oblationem DEO facere, & in omnibus gratos inveniri fabricatori DEO in sententia pura, & fide sine hypocrisi, in spe firma, in dilectione ferventi, primitias earum, quae sunt eis, creaturarum offerentes, & hanc oblationem Ecclesia sola puram offert fabricatori, offerens ei cum gratiarum actione ex creatura eius. 5. Quinimò omnis obedientia, quam pii ex Spiritu & fide praestant, sive fit interna, sive externa est spiritualis hostia. Origenes in Leviticum homil. 9. cap. 16. Unusquisque habet in se holocaustum suum, & holocausti sui ipse succendit altare, ut semper ardeat. Ego si renunciem omnibus, quae possideo, & tollam crucem meam, & sequar Christum, holocaustum obtuli ad altare DEI, aut si tradidero corpus meum, ut ardeam, habens caritatem, & gloriam Martyrii consequar, holocaustum meipsum obtuli ad altare DEI. Si diligam fratres meos, ita ut animam meam ponam pro fratribus meis, si pro iustitia, pro veritate usque ad mortem certavero, holocaustum obtuli ad altare DEI: Si membra mea ab omni concupiscentia carnis mortificavero, si mundus mihi crucifixus sit, ego mundo, holocaustum obtuli ad altare DEI mei, & ipse meae hostiae Sacerdos efficiar. Lactantius lib. 6. Instit. cap. 24. Quisquis omnibus praeceptis coelestibus obtemperat, hic est verè Dei cultor, cuius sacrificia sunt mansuetudo animi & vita innocens & actus boni, quae omnia qui exhibet, toties sacrificat, quoties bonum aliquid & pium fecerit. Augustinus lib. 10. de Civ. DEI cap. 4. Suavissimum adolemus incensum, cum in eius conspectu puro sanctoque amore flagramus, ei dona eius in nobis, nosque ipsos vovemus & reddimus, ei beneficiorum eius solennitatibus, festis & diebus statutis dicamus, sacramusque memoriam, ne volumine temporum ingrata subrepat oblivio, ei sacrificamus hostiam humilitatis & laudis in ara cordis igne fervidae caritatis. cap. 6. Verum sacrificium est opus omne, quod agitur, ut sanctâ societate inhaereamus DEO, relatum sc. ad illum finem boni, quo veraciter beati esse possimus. Et postea. Ipse homo DEI nomini consecratus & devotus DEO, in quantum mundo moritur, ut DEO vivat, sacrificium est &c. corpus etiam nostrum, cum per temperantiam castigamus, si hoc, quemadmodum debemus, propter DEUM facimus, ut non exhibeamus membra nostra arma iniquitatis peccato, sed arma iustitiae DEO, sacrificium est. Si ergò corpus, quo inferiore tanquam famulo, vel tanquam instrumento utitur anima, cum eius bonus & rectus usus ad DEUM refertur, sacrificium est, quantò magis anima ipsa, cum se refert ad DEUM, ut igne amoris eius accensa formam concupiscentiae secularis amittat, eique tanquam incommutabili formae subdita reformetur, hinc ei placens, quod ex eius pulchritudine acceperit, fit sacrificium.

16. Spirituales illae hostiae, non nisi in Christo, & per Christum sunt DEO gratae & acceptae, abnegatio enim suiipsius non est perfecta, bona opera sunt adhaerentis peccati labe contaminata, ut ergò DEO placeant, ex fide in Christum ea fieri opertet, per quam adhaerens imperfectio & immundities tegatur. Lyranus in h. l. monet, propterea in fine orationum adiici, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, ut non solùm preces nostras propter Christum exaudiri, sed etiam in ipso, & per ipsum DEO gratas esse significetur. Opponendum hoc diffidentiae & dubitationi carnali, quâ pii quandoque tentantur, an etiam mutila & manca illorum obedientia DEO placeat.

17. Quia spirituales hostiae fidelium, ac bona ipsorum opera DEO grata, ideò etiam ea largissimè remunerabitur, quo stimulo torporem carnis excutere, & ad studium bonorum operum nos excitare debemus.

18. Solus DEUS est spiritualis domus suae architectus principalis Ps. 48. v. 9. DEUS fundavit eam in aeternum. Ipse ponit lapidem in Sion. Utitur quidem ad hoc aedificium hominum ministerio, interim omnis vis & efficacia, successus omnis ab ipso unicè dependet.

19. Sine Domino nostro Iesu Christo, lapide sc. vivo & fundamentali, nulla spiritualis aedificatio stare potest, inquit Beda in v. 4. inde in Sion hunc lapidem divinitùs poni oportuit, antequam alii lapides ei superaedificarentur.

20. Illi soli verâ fide super Christum aedificantur, qui Ecclesiae unitatem tuentur, ac extra Ecclesiam non habet locum spiritualis illa aedificatio, quia hic lapis in Sione positus est.

21. Christo lapidi vivo verâ & constante fide innitentes sumus extra lapsûs periculum. Glossa interlin. in h. l. Qui in Christum credit, non confundetur, h. e. neque in praesenti de casu erubescet, neque in fnturo vacuus erit praemio.

22. Si credens in Christum non confunditur. Ergò à contrario sensu, qui non credit, pudefiet. Nemo potest coram DEI iudicio consistere, nisi in Christo, & per Christum, propter peccatum omnes oportet pudefieri.

23. Non modò vulgus hominum Christum repudiat, sed etiam, qui in hoc mundo magni, & in eminentia dignitatis, tùm Ecclesiasticae, tùm Politicae constituti. Si idem adhuc hodiè fieri videamus, non scandalizemur.

24. Christus non solùm verbis, sed etiam factis, imò magis factis, quàm verbis repudiatur.

25. Sicut stolidi illi aedificantes in sua aedificatione Christum reprobaverunt: sic & ipse in suo adventu reprobavit, eos accipere in aedificationem domus suae in coelis. Beda in h. l. Qui Christum reprobant in hoc seculo, reprobabuntur ab eo in futuro.

26. Iudicio mundi Christum reprobantis opponendum est iudicium DEI, hunc lapidem in fundamentum constituentis.

27. Inanes atque irriti sunt omnes hostium conatus contra Christum. Ipsis invitis ac frustra renitentibus Christus manet fundamentalis Ecclesiae munus. Collocatus est in caput aedificii ac Regem populi sui, donec omnes inimicos ponat scabellum pedum suorum.

28. Nullum hîc datur medium sive tertium. Quotquot nolunt super hunc lapidem aedificari, ab eo collidentur & conterentur, quando lapis de monte abscissus, sine manibus comminuet testam & ferrum, & aes, & argentum, & aurum, h. e. omnia huius mundi regna, Dan. 2. v. 45.

## 2:6
FOR WHICH REASON THE SCRIPTURE CONTAINS. BEHOLD I LAY IN SION A CHIEF CORNER STONE, ELECT, PRECIOUS, AND HE THAT SHALL BELIEVE IN HIM, SHALL NOT BE CONFOUNDED.

Connection. The Apostle had said that Christ is the foundational stone, upon which believers are built up, so that they may become a spiritual house; and likewise a stone elect and precious before GOD. He confirms the same thing with a Prophetic testimony Esai. 28. v. 16. in which all these things are contained in express words.

Exposition of the text. Διὸ καὶ περιέχει ἐν τῇ γραφῇ. Robertus Stephanus notes that in one Greek Codex there is περιέχει ή γραφὴ: but without doubt this was derived from the Latin version into that Greek Codex, which it is established has also been done in certain other places. For the Latin Interpreter, having neglected the preposition ἐν,, rendered it: For which reason the Scripture contains. But because the verb περιέχειν is active, which does not seem to be joined conveniently enough with the preposition ἐν,, thence this passage has been rendered in various ways here.

1. Some understand the noun ὁ θεὸς, which is had in the verse immediately preceding. GOD, who is the principal author of Prophetic Scripture, contains or proposes this in Scripture. 2. Some refer it to Christ, that living stone elect and precious before God so that the sense may be. That stone, of which I have spoken, contains in Scripture. i. e. By the testimony of Scripture it is described thus, that it contains and connects in itself two peoples, as two walls, while it is called the cornerstone. Which exposition is confirmed from this, that περιέχειν properly means, to embrace and hold from all sides, and that a similar phrase occurs Heb. v. 16. nowhere does he assume Angels or Angelic Nature, viz. in Scripture. i. e. Scripture nowhere testifies that the Son of God was about to assume Angelic Nature. 3. Since περιέχειν it signifies also to excel, thence some, with the discourse likewise referred to Christ, render it thus. Whence also that stone excels, or is excellent in Scripture i. e. By the testimony of Scripture this stone is declared excellent and distinguished. Erasmus makes mention of both expositions. 4. It is answered most simply, that the word περιέχειν is placed neutrally in a passive signification for περιέχεται, just as the Syrian also rendered [consult facsimile image] it is said in Scripture. For the scope of the Apostle is to signify that he wishes to cite a saying of Scripture in confirmation of the preceding things. Acts 23. v. 25. concerning the Epistle of Claudius Lysias to the Governor Felix it is said that it was περιέχουσα τὸν τόπον τοῦτον, that this had comprised, that these things had been contained in it, which are subjoined in the same place. Thence περιοχὴ is called the argument of some book, or the sum of those things which are written in some book, comprised in few words. But especially the passage Acts 8. v. 32. pertains here, where περιοχὴ is called some chapter, or section of Scripture, for which signification they judge that this reason can be given, that since περιοχὴ properly signifies a complex, and that which can be contained in one circuit, by the best reason those sections can also be so called, as if you would say a part comprised by certain limits and distinct from the rest.

Furthermore, the Prophetic passage brought forward from Isaiah 28. v. 16. according to the Hebrew sources has it thus. Therefore thus said the Lord GOD. Behold I lay in Sion a stone, a stone of fortification or of a citadel, of a corner of price or precious, of a founded foundation. He who believes, shall not hasten or let him hasten. The LXX rendered it thus. Διὰ τοῦντο οὕτω λέγει Κύριος. ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τα θεμέλια Σιὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἀκρογωνιᾶιον, ἔντιμον εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁ πιστέυων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.

From this it appears that the Apostle cites the testimony of the Prophet neither in the same words, nor in the same order, in which it is read either in the Hebrew text or among the LXX, yet he retains the meaning itself unchanged. For what is here called a stone in the Hebrew text אבן בחן a stone of fortification or of a citadel, that the Apostle omits here, but on the contrary he calls it ἐκλεκτὸν, which is not held in the Hebrew. What is said in the Greek version πολυτελῆ & εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῶν, Peter likewise omits. But in order that the sense of the Prophetic saying may be more illustrious, its connection with the preceding things must be noted, to which the Prophet himself recalls us, saying לכן therefore thus says the Lord; and otherwise the laws of genuine interpretation require this, that when any saying of the O. T. is cited in the New, it should not be considered torn from the context, but as ὕφος καὶ εἶρμος ἀκολουθίας requires. The Prophet prophesies in that chapter both about the destruction of the Israelite kingdom and about the devastation of the kingdom of Judah, to be sent upon both on account of most grave sins, but lest they should think that on that account the promise concerning the Messiah would be void, or the Church would perish entirely, therefore he promises that he will send his Son at a defined time, who is to be the fundamental stone, sustaining the whole building of the Church to be gathered from Jews and Gentiles. God also complains in the same place about the incredulity of the Jewish people refusing to depend upon divine promises, and about their vain confidence, by which they trusted in human and fig-tree supports. Intending to bring a remedy to both evils, he proposes his infallible decree concerning the promised Son the Messiah to be sent into the flesh, in whom, as the fundamental stone of the Church to be perpetually preserved, whoever is to recline with true faith, he pronounces that he will not be confounded or put to shame. ἰδοὺ is a little word of one exciting to a worthy consideration of this prophecy. τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον. I myself place or will place this stone. Not by the judgment or counsel of men will this stone be placed, but by a divine and therefore immovable decree. In the Hebrew it is יסר I found or I place in the place of a foundation, from which root descends the name מוסר of a foundation, which the Prophet uses a little later in the commendation of this stone. I will place him, however, in Sion LXX, ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν I will send into the foundations of Sion i. e. so that he may be a foundation. By the name Sion in the mystical sense the Church of the N. T. is understood, since the citadel and city of David built on Mount Sion was its type: therefore this stone is promised to be placed in Sion, that is, in the Church of the New Testament, which shall be built upon this stone as an immovable foundation. At the same time, however, regard is had to the fact that Christ is to preach the Gospel in Judea, whose metropolis was Jerusalem built upon Mount Zion, and is to perform miracles and accomplish the work of redemption, and that the doctrine of the Gospel is first to be preached at Jerusalem, and from there is to be propagated into the whole world. Ps. 110. v. 2.Es. 2. v. 3.Mich. 4. v. 2. Through this preaching of the Gospel, that stone, established by divine decree, shall also be founded in spiritual Zion, i.e., in the Church and in the hearts of men believing the Gospel, so that they may be built up upon it as living stones and not be moved forever. Peter, following the thread of prophetic Scripture, adorns this stone with three distinguished epithets. First, he calls it ἀκρογωνιαῖον indeed the chief cornerstone. Erasmus rendered it, to be placed at the highest corner. In the Hebrew stone פנת of the corner. Now that is called a cornerstone or angular stone, which, placed at the extreme corner of the foundation, supports and joins two walls leaning upon it. Therefore, Christ is called the cornerstone for a double reason: first, because He is the foundation of the Church, whence it is added in the Prophet that He is a stone מוסר מוסד of a founded foundation, i.e., well founded, which the Apostle omitted, since it is implicitly contained in the ἀκρογωνιαὶου appellation Eph. 2. v. 20.; and second, because He joins the Jews and the Gentiles, as two diverse walls, into one spiritual building Eph. 2. v. 14., which Apostolic passage is parallel to this one of ours. 2. ἐκλεκτὸν, of which above. 3. ἔκτιμον. In the Hebrew it is יקרת from the root יקר it was heavy in weight, authority or price, it was honorable and precious. In the Hebrew it is added that this stone is אבן בחן which the Vulgate Interpreter rendered tried, for בחן signifies he tried, he explored Gen. 42. v. 15.Zachar. 13. v. 9.Mal. 3. v. 15. in which way Luther also rendered it, einen bevehrten Stein. For it is called a tried stone or a stone of probation, both because it is tried above others, and therefore also precious, and because the whole building is to be tested by it as by a plumb line, and the whole mass of the structure is to be measured by it as a rule, so that all things may accurately correspond to it. But because בחן also signifies a fortress and a fortification Esa. 23. vers. 13., since it ought to be tried, strong and firm, therefore Pagninus and Arias Montanus rendered it a stone of the fortress, or of the fortification, as strength and firmness of this stone is signified. To these honorific praises of this fundamental and corner stone, the Apostle adds from the Prophet its salutary use, on account of which GOD placed it in spiritual Sion, i. e., in the Church.

καὶ ὀ πιστεύων ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθήσεται. The Apostle follows in this part the version of the LXX Interpreters, who rendered the Prophetic saying in the same way, except that in certain Codices προσδιορισμὸς ἐπ´ αὐτᾧ is omitted. In the same way Paul alleges this passage Rom. 9. v. 33. & cap. 10. v. 11. except that in the subject he adds a note of Universality. The Vulgate rendered it in both places, he who will have believed in him, shall not be confounded, that is, shall not be put to shame. Moreover, it is shown in these words, both the salutary use of this stone in the Church, and the manner by which it becomes salutary to men. The salutary use consists in this, that it prohibits from confusion. The manner, that we ought to lean upon it by faith, lest it be necessary for us to be put to shame. By what reason these can be accommodated to the metaphor of the stone is in some way obscure. Perhaps not without reason the parable of Christ Matth. 7. v. 24. can be accommodated here: A house built upon a rock, because it is well founded, therefore it is overturned neither by rains, nor by rivers, nor by winds: but a house built upon sand is overturned and collapses by rains, rivers, and winds. And since Christ in the same place calls him foolish who builds upon sand, it is understood from that, that besides the damage of the collapsed house, he also gains shame and confusion among others. This can be accommodated to the spiritual building. All men after the fall, since they are sinners, lack the glory before GOD Rom. 3. v. 23. cannot stand before GOD through their own righteousness, but confusion of face is owed to them, Dan. 9. vers. 7. and as long as they are outside of Christ, they build upon sand, and bear such fruits in which they blush Rom. 6. v. 21. but GOD in Sion, i. e., in the Church placed a corner stone, elect and precious, he who believes in him, i. e., as Peter himself follows in the preceding verse 5. 10., who as a living stone is built upon him by true faith, he builds upon the rock, therefore he is not confounded, he has a firm and stable foundation, and has erected a firm and stable structure, therefore he does not waver nor vacillate, nor does he have need to tremble at the insults of rains, rivers, and winds, but persists immovable and firm. καὶ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ´ αὐτῷ, οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.

When the rain descends, that is, the temptations which are from the demons existing in the air, and the winds of ambition and vainglory blow, which are sent by the world, and the rivers of concupiscences come upon that house, which burst forth from the flesh, and rush upon it, it did not fall, but stood, because it was founded upon the rock or Christ, says Weidn. in loc. fid. praecip. tract. 2. p. 383. Moreover, he who is built by faith upon Christ, that firm rock, he persists against all the insults of death, the Devil, and hell, nor is there any reason why he should fear to be put to shame before GOD or men. Bede shows yet another reason for the connection. Nobly, he says, does the speech of the Prophet and the Apostle agree here, by which it is said, those approaching the living stone, or believing in him, are not confounded by that verse of the Psalm, in which, when it had been said, approach him, and be enlightened, it was immediately subjoined, and your faces shall not blush. Although indeed the version of the LXX Interpreters cited by Peter in this place differs in words from the Hebrew text, nevertheless as to the meaning the agreement is most beautiful. He who believes, says the Prophet, shall not hasten. Isaiah says simply, He who believes, but the LXX Interpreters and Peter following them, complete that with the expressed object of faith. He who believes in him, whom προσδιορισμὸν the connection of these words with the preceding promise concerning that cornerstone and foundational stone being placed in the Church shows. Some take the future shall not hasten as placed in the manner of the Hebrews for the imperative, by which reason an exhortation would be proposed in these words. He who believes those things which I say about the foundational stone being placed in Zion, let him not hasten, so that he may see them (as ἐξηγήσεως for the sake of Pagninus adds) i. e. let him not hasten to the promised thing, impatient of delay, as if it ought to be exhibited immediately, nor if it be deferred, should he cast away hope, but let him wait patiently. This exposition seems to be confirmed from the context. For there precedes v. 10. precept upon precept, line upon line, where μιμητικῶς the voices of those are repeated who refused to wait for the fulfillment of the divine promises, and on account of the delay of the fulfillment were rendered impatient, as also from Habac. 2. v. 3. But it is more correctly taken as a promise, and the future is left in its proper signification. He who believes, shall not hasten, i. e. he will not have need to flee to other remedies, or to flee out of anxiety and trepidation of heart, just as on the contrary it is said of those who follow another, Psalm. 16. v. 4.they multiplied their troublesome labors, afterwards they hastened. For those who seek their salvation elsewhere than in Christ, namely in their own works, or in other fabricated Saviors, they perpetually fluctuate as if uncertain of their own salvation, and their end at last is confusion Phil. 3. v. 19. but those who believe in Christ, in whom alone GOD has deposited our salvation Acts 4. v. 12. they are not frustrated of the expected salvation, but most certainly attain it in its own time. And by this reasoning the word shall be put to shame, which the Apostles use from the version of the LXX Interpreters, most beautifully agrees with the word shall hasten, which the Prophet uses. For those who are suffused with shame take to flight, and immediately withdraw themselves from the sight of men. This exposition is confirmed from the following verse. For because those who do not believe in Christ are not put to shame, from that Peter infers. To you therefore who believe he is honor, i. e. because by faith you are built into this stone, therefore shame and ignominy are not to be feared by you, but honor and glory are to be expected. It is also confirmed from the Pauline allegation Rom. 9. v. 31. and following. Israel pursuing the law of righteousness, did not arrive at the law of righteousness. Why? because not from faith, but as if from works, for they stumbled at the stone of stumbling, as it is written. Behold I place in Sion a stone of stumbling, and a rock of scandal, and everyone who believes in him, shall not be confounded, i. e. to the unbelieving indeed this stone is a stone of stumbling and confusion, but to the believing it is salutary, prohibiting them from confusion, which passage is plainly parallel to this one of ours. The same shines forth from the allegation Rom. 10. v. 11 where after the Apostle had said. With the heart, it is believed unto righteousness, he adds, for the Scripture says, everyone who shall have believed in him, shall not be confounded, all of which manifestly show that not an exhortation, but a promise is contained in these words of the Prophet and the Apostles.

Latin:

PROPTER QUOD CONTINET SCRIPTURA. ECCE PONO IN SION LAPIDEM SUMMUM ANGULAREM, ELECTUM, PRECIOSUM, & QUI CREDIDERIT IN EUM, NON CONFUNDETUR.

Connexio. Dixerat Apostolus, Christum esse lapidem fundamentalem, cui credentes superstruantur, ut fiant domus spiritualis; Itemque lapidem electum & preciosum apud DEUM. idipsum confirmat testimonio Prophetico Esai. 28. v. 16. in quo istaec omnia disertis verbis continentur.

Textus expositio. Διὸ καὶ περιέχει ἐν τῇ γραφῇ. Robertus Stephanus monet, in uno Codice Graeco haberi περιέχει ή γραφὴ: sed procul dubio hoc deductum ex versione Latina in Codicem illum Graecum, quod etiam in aliis quibusdam locis factum esse constat. Latinus enim Interpres neglectâ praepositione ἐν, reddidit. Propter quod continet Scriptura. Quia vero verbum περιέχειν activum est, quod non satis commodè videtur coniungi cum praepositione ἐν, inde variè hic locus fuit redditus.

1. Quidam subintelligunt nomen ὁ θεὸς, quod in versu proximè praecedente habetur. DEUS, qui est principalis Scripturae Propheticae autor, hoc continet sive proponit in Scriptura. 2. Quidam referunt ad Christum, vivum illum apud Deum electum & preciosum lapidem, ut sit sensus. Lapis ille, de quo locutus sum, continet in Scriptura. i. e. Scripturae testimonio sic describitur, quod contineat & connectat in se duos populos, tanquam duos parietes, dum vocatur lapis angularis. Quae expositio confirmatur ex eo, quòd περιέχεινpropriè sit, undique amplecti & tenere, quòdque similis phrasis occurrat Heb. v. 16. nuspiam Angelos sive Angelicam Naturane assumit, sc. in Scriptura. h. e. Scriptura nuspiam testatur, Filium Dei assumturum Naturam Angelicam. 3. Cùmπεριέχεινsignificet etiam excellere, inde quidam sermone itidem ad Christum relato sic reddunt. Unde etiam excellit, sive eximius est ille lapis in Scripturâ i. e. Scripturae testimonio hic lapis excellens & eximius declaratur. Utriusque expositionis mentionem facit Erasmus. 4. Simplicissimè respondetur, verbum περιέχειν poni neutraliter in significatione passiva pro περιέχεται, sicut & Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]dicitur in Scriptura. Scopus enim Apostoli est, significare, quòd dictum Scripturae in confirmationem praecedentium velit citare. Actor. 23. v. 25. de Epistola Claudii Lysiae ad Praesidem Felicem dicitur, quòd fuerit περιέχουσα τὸν τόπον τοῦτον, quòd haec fuerit complexa, quòd haec fuerint in ea contenta, quae ibidem subiunguntur. Inde περιοχὴ vocatur argumentum alicuius libri, seu summa eorum, quae in aliquo libro scripta sunt paucis comprehensa. Cumprimis vero huc pertinet locus Act. 8. v. 32. ubi περιοχὴ vocatur capitulum aliquod, sive sectio Scripturae, cuius significationis hanc rationem dari posse censent, quòd cum περιοχὴ propriè significet complexionem, ac quod uno ambitu contineri potest, optimâ ratione possint istae sectiones sic etiam vocari, quasi partem dicas certis terminis comprehensam & à reliquis dictinctam.

Caeterum locus Propheticus ex Esaiae 28. v. 16. adductus iuxta fontes Hebraeos sic habet. Idcircò sic dixit Dominus DEUS. Ecce ego fundo in Sion lapidem, lapidem munitionis sive arcis, anguli precii sive preciosi, fundamenti fundati. Qui credit, non festinabit vel festinet. LXX. sic reddiderunt. Διὰ τοῦντο οὕτω λέγει Κύριος. ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τα θεμέλια Σιὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἀκρογωνιᾶιον, ἔντιμον εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁ πιστέυων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.

Ex quo apparet, Apostolum Prophetae testimonium nec verbis iisdem, nec eodem ordine, quibus vel in Hebraeo textu, vel apud LXX. legitur, citare, ipsam tamen sententiam invariatam retinere. Quod enim hic lapis vocatur in textu Hebraeo אבן בחןlapis munitionis sive arcis, illud Apostolus hîc praetermittit, contrà vero eum vocat ἐκλεκτὸν, quod non habetur in Hebraeo. Quod in Graeca versione dicitur πολυτελῆ & εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῶν, itidem Petrus praetermittit. Ut autem sensus Prophetici dicti sit illustrior, notanda eius cum, praecedentibus connexio, ad quam ipse Propheta nos revocat, dicens לכןidcircò sic dicit Dominus; ac alioqui leges genuinae interpretationis hoc requirunt, ut quando dictum aliquod V. T. in Novo citatur, illud non consideretur à contextu avulsum, sed prout ὕφος καὶ εἶρμος ἀκολουθίας requirit. Vaticinatur Propheta in illo capite tùm de regni Israëlitici excidio, tùm de regni Iuda vastatione, propter peccata gravissima utrique immittendis, sed ne cogitarent propterea promissionem de Messia fore irritam, vel Ecclesiam penitus interituram, ideò promittit, se Filium suum tempore definito missurum, qui futurus sit fundamentalis lapis, totum aedificium Ecclesiae ex Iudaeis & gentibus colligendae sustentans. Conqueritur etiam ibidem Deus de incredulitate populi Iudaici renuentis pendere à divinis promissionibus, ac de vana eiusdem fiducia, quâ confidebat humanis & ficulneis praesidiis. Utrique malo remedium allaturus proponit infallible suum decretum de Filio promisso Messia in carnem mittendo, in quem velut fundamentalem Ecclesiae perpetuò conservandae lapidem, quisquis vera fide recubiturus sit, eum non consusum vel pudefactum iri pronunciat. ἰδοὺ vocula est excitantis ad dignam prophetiae huius considerationem. τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον.Ego ipse pono vel ponam hunc lapidem. Non hominum arbitrio vel consilio hic lapis ponetur, sed divino ac proinde immoto decreto. In Hebraeo est יסרfundo vel fundamenti loco pono, ex qua radice descendit nomen מוסרfundamenti, quo paulo pòst Propheta in commendatione huius lapidis utitur. Ponam autem eum in Sion LXX, ἐμβαλῶ εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν immittam in fundamenta Sion i. e. ut sit fundamentum. Nomine Sionis in sensu mystico Ecclesia N. T. intelligitur, quippe cuius typus fuit arx & civitas Davidis in monte Sion extructa: promittitur igitur hic lapis in Sion ponendus, h. e. in Ecclesia N. T. quae super hunc lapidem, velut immotum fundamentum aedificabitur. Simul tamen eò respectus habetur, quòd Christus in Iudaea, cuius metropolis erat Hierosolyma in monte Sionis extructa, sit Evangelium praedicaturus, miracula editurus, & opus redemtionis peracturus, quodque Evangelii doctrina Hierosolymis primùm praedicanda, exinde in totum terrarum orbem sit propaganda. Ps. 110. v. 2.Es. 2. v. 3.Mich. 4. v. 2. Per hanc Evangelii praedicationem lapis ille divino decreto firmatus, ac fundatus etiam in Sione spirituali, i. e. in Ecclesia & in cordibus hominum Evangelio credentium fundabitur, ut super ipsum velut lapides vivi extruantur, nec commoveantur in aeternum. Tribus vero insignibus elogiis Petrus filum propheticae Scripturae secutus, hunc lapidem exornat. Primò vocat eum ἀκρογωνιαῖον quidem summangularem. Erasmus reddidit, in summo ponendum angulo. In Hebraeo lapisפנתanguli. Dicitur autem lapis anguli sive angularis, qui in extremo angulo fundamenti positus, duos parietes sibi innitentes sustinet & coniungit. Duplici igitur ratione Christus vocatur lapis angularis, tùm quia est Ecclesiae fundamentum, unde apud Prophetam subiungitur, quòd sit lapis מוסר מוסדfundamenti fundati, i. e. probè fundati, id quod Apostolus praetermisit, cum in ἀκρογωνιαὶου apellatione implicitè contineatur Eph. 2. v. 20. tùm quia Iudaeos & gentes, tanquam duos parietes diversos in unum spirituale aedificium coniungit Eph. 2. v. 14. qui locus Apostolicus est huic nostro parallelus. 2. ἐκλεκτὸν, de quo superiùs 3. ἔκτιμον. In Hebr. est יקרת à rad. יקרgravis fuit pondere, autoritate vel precio, honorabilis ac preciosus fuit. In Hebraeo additur, quòd hic lapis sit אבן בחן quod vulgatus Interpres reddidit probatum,בחן enim significat probavit, exploravitGen. 42. v. 15.Zachar. 13. v. 9.Mal. 3. v. 15. quo modo etiam Lutherus reddidit, einen bevehrten Stein. Vocatur enim lapis probatus sive probationis, tùm quia prae aliis probatus est, ac proinde etiam preciosus, tùm quia totum aedificium ad eum, tanquam ad amussim probandum, tota structurae moles ad eum tanquam regulam exigenda, ut, omnia accuratè illi respondeant. Quia vero בחן etiam significat arcem & munitionem Esa. 23. vers. 13. quippe quae debet esse, probata, fortis & firma, ideò Pagninus & Ariaemontanus reddiderunt lapidem arcis, sive munitionis, ut robur & firmitas huius lapidis significatur. Hisce honorificis lapidis huius fundamentalis & angularis encomiis subiungit Apostolus ex Propheta salutarem eiusdem usum, propter quem in Sione spirituali, i. e. in Ecclesia DEUS illum posuit.

καὶ ὀ πιστεύων ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθήσεται. Sequitur hac in parte Apostolus versionem LXX. Interpp. quae Propheticum, dictum eodem modo reddidit, nisi quod in quibusdam Codicibus προσδιορισμὸς ἐπ´ αὐτᾧ omittitur. Eodem modo allegat hunc locum Paulus Rom. 9. v. 33. & cap. 10. v. 11. nisi quod in subiecto addit notam Universalitatis. καὶ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ´ αὐτῷ, οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται. Vulgatus utrobique reddidit, qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur, id est, non pudefiet. Ostenditur autem in his verbis, tùm salutaris huius lapidis in Ecclesia usus, tùm modus, quo hominibus fit salutaris. Usus salutaris in eo consistit, quòd prohibeat à pudefactione. Modus, quòd fide ei inniti debeamus, ne pudefieri nos oporteat. Quâ ratione haec ad metaphoram lapidis accommodari possint, quodammodo est obscurum. Fortè haud abs re huc accommodari potest parabola Christi Matth. 7. v. 24. Domus aedificata super petram, quia probè fundata, ideò nec à pluviis, nec à fluminibus, nec à ventis evertitur: sed domus super arenam aedificata à pluviis, fluminibus & ventis everitur atque corruit. Cùmque Christus ibidem eum appellet stolidum, qui super arenam aedificat, ex eo intelligitur, quòd praeter damnum collapsae domus, etiam pudorem & confusionem apud alios lucretur. Hoc potest ad spirituale aedificium accommodari.
