Bellarminus in praefat. controv. 3. generalis de Romano Pontifice dictum Propheticum Esai. 28. v. 16. applicat ad Romanum Pontificem, quem existimat vocari lapidem, propter Sedis Romanae firmitatem divinitus fundatam; angularem verò, ad demonstrandum discrimen inter Pontificem Iudaeorum & Christianorum. Ille enim lapis quidem & fundamentum erat, sed non lapis angularis. Neque enim parietes duos, sed unum tantùm sustentabat. Sed Romanus Pontifex lapis angularis est. Nam & Iudaei & gentes q. parietes duo simul coniuncti, atque unam Christianam Ecclesiam facientes, ab hoc uno angulari lapide continentur. Quinimò in exemplari Manuscripto negaverat, dictum Propheticum de Christo intelligi posse, sed de Pontifice Romano unicè intelligendum esse, cum sequatur apud Prophetam, ponam lapidem in fundamento fundatum i. e. fundamentum post fundamentum, sive fundamentum secundarium, quod Christo competere non potest. In excuso autem exemplari corrigit se ac verba quaedam interserit. Etsi, inquit, non dubitamus, haec praecipuè de Christo intelligenda esse, tamen ad Petrum quoque (& Petri successorem Pontif. Rom.) non ineptè referri possunt. Atqui 1. ostendimus superiùs q. 6. ex immotis fundamentis, per lapidem angularem & fundamentalem solum Christum intelligendum esse. Quid clarius dicto Apostolico 1. Cor. 3. v. 11.Fundamentum aliud nemo ponere potest, praeter id quod positum, quod est Christus Iesus. 2. Bellarminus ipse lib. 1. de Christo Cap. 4. ex hoc loco Prophetico argumentum pro afferenda Christi Divinitate format, quod vocat indissolubile agnoscere igitur cogitur, de solo Christo id exponendum. 3. Neque hic lapis dicitur fundatus in alio fundamento, sed dicitur fundamentum fundationis, fundatio fundatissima, totum aedificium fundans & continens. Repetitio enim apud Hebraeos rem intendit.

8. Salmero in h. l. sic commentatur. Qui credit, non festinet, sc. ad palmam vitae aeternae obtinendam, quia longa adhuc restat via, sed patienter agat & viam mandatorum currat, quod est contra Lutheranos, qui unâ & folâ fide putant omnia perfecta & completa, quae quidem fides digna est confusione & illusione. Resp. 1. ostendimus superiùs, verbum יחיש rectiùs accipi in forma enunciandi, quàm imperandi. 2. Cur discedit à versione vulgata, quae in Conc. Trid. pronunciata est authentica. Illa vero reddidit, non confundetur. 3. Credentes in via mandatorum divinorum debere currere, nemo nostrum negat. Sed bona illa opera iuxta Dei mandata facta, sunt via regni, non causa regnandi. 4. Vera fides in Christo iustitiam & salutem unicè quaerit, interim in studio bonorum operum ad palmam obtinendam decurrit, quae non habent rationem causae meritoriae, sed ordinis divinitus constituti. 5. Ipsimet Pontificii concedunt, solâ fide palmam vit. aet. obtineri posse, sinon detur tempus benè operandi.

9. Locum Davidicum de lapide ab aedificantibus reprobato, Calvinus in sensu literali exponit de Davide, à Saule & Consiliariis eius ac regni Proceribus primùm reiecto, postmodùm vero in Regem evecto. Sic enim commentatur in Ps. 118.Iam David collecto animo calumniis insultat, quibus iniustè & praeter meritum fuerat gravatus &c. Nihil moror, inquit, quod reiectus fuerim à maximis quibusque quando reipsa apparuit, Dei iudicio me fuisse electum. Concinnâ vero metaphorâutitur, sese lapidi comparans, ipsos vero Ecclesiae primores architectis. Calvinum sequuntur Musculus & Mollerus in Ps. 118. Piscator in h. l. Petrinum. Testimonium illud sumtum ex Ps. 118. v. 22.ubi exponitur decretum Dei, tùm de Davide constituendo Rege populi Dei externo, tùm de Christo, per Davidem praefigurato, constituendo Rege Ecclesiae spirituali. In eandem opinionem inclinat Salmero Iesuita. Quin & Chaldaica versio eò abit, quae sic habet. Iuniorem ex filiis Isai despexerunt aedificatores, meruit verò, ut constitueretur Rex & Dominus. Resp. 1. repetenda sunt argumenta, quibus superiùs ostendimus, per lapidem angularem solum Christum intelligi. 2. Christus ex hoc loco argumentum ducit contra Sacerdotes & Scribas Matt. 21. v. 42. At si ex mystico sensu illud petitum fuisset, utique non fuisset apud Sacerdotes & Scribas efficax. 3. Ideò vero magni apud eos fuit ponderis, quia ipsimet sensu literali & genuino de Messia hîc sermonem esse intellexerunt, ut constat ex R. Salomone in comm. Mich. 5. 4. Describuntur in hoc Psalmo ipsa verba, quibus populus Hierosolymitanus Christum excepit, quando regium suum ingressum in urbem Hierosolymam celebravit.

10. Ex eo, quòd Christus dicitur lapis offensionis, & petra scandali, colligunt Calviniani absolutum decretum reprobationis. Resp. Christus positus est in resurrectionem sive erectionem ut homines in luto peccati & mortis demersi, in hoc lapide sese erigant, Luc. 2. v. 34. sed hominum culpâ ac vitio contingit, ut quibusdam positus sit in ruinam, quia sc. nolunt apprehendere hunc lapidem, ut erigantur, sicut Ioh. 3. v. 19. dicitur: Hoc est iudicium, quòd lux venit in mundum, & homines magis dilexerunt tenebras, quàm lucem. Hoc modo Petrus ipse explicat, quando dicit: Lapis offensionis est his, qui verbo offendunt, nec credunt. Vis veritatis Calvino ipsimet extorsit, ut in hunc locum Petrinum sic commentaretur. Cùm Christus nobis in fundamentum datus sit, illi accidentale est, esse petram scandali. Proprium eius munus est, nos in spirituale templum Deo aptare, fit autem hominum vitio, ut in ipsum impingant, quia sc. incredulitas homines in certamen cum Deo committit.

11. Ex verbis εἰς ὅ καὶ ἐτέθησαν Calviniani colligunt, Deum non solùm ad damnationem, sed etiam ad causas damnationis hominem reprobasse, imò creasse. Beza in Glossis marginalibus huius loci, quosdam ad hoc conditos esse, dicit, ut offenderent: quae perversio quibusdam ita, placuit, ut in Bibliis Latinis Anno 91. Francofurti editis, ipsi textui eam inserere non fuerint veriti. Sic enim vertunt, vel potiùs pervertunt hunc locum. Iis qui offendunt ad sermonem immorigeri, ad quod etiam conditi fuerunt. Piscator in h. l. Tollit Apostolus scandalum, (quod oriebatur ex incredulitate maximae partis Iudaeorum) commemoratione voluntatis Dei, in qua nimirùm tanquam iustâ & sanctâ omnibus piis est acquiescendum, hoc significat, ubi dicit, incredulos illos, qui ad sermonem Evangelii offendunt, ad hoc ipsum esse positos, id est, à Deo praedestinatos. Resp. 1. genuinum huius loci sensum exposuimus superiùs. 2. Hemmingius Bezanam illam perversionem, ex professo refellit. Quidam novus interpres, inquit, ita reddidit. Immorigeri, ad quod etiam conditi erant, & interpretatur, quòd ideò conditi fuerint, ut essent immorigeri, h. e. quòd creati fuerint ab optimo DEO ad certam damnationem. Verùm praeter id, quodἐτέθησανvertit, conditi sunt, contra vocis Graecanicae Naturam, vim facit huic loco. Nam suprà dixit Apostolus, hunc lapidem Christum fuisse ab aedificantibus reprobatum, quòd nequaquam verum fuisset, nisi hic lapis his oblatus antea. Deinde verbum DEI & promissionem factam populo Iudaico, malè pervertit. Nam verbum DEI & promissio testatur, Iudaicum populum cum conditione fuisse electum.Exod. 19.Si audiveritis vocem, meam &c. proinde audientes vocem DEI, & credentes Evangelio, quod proponitur universo orbi, sunt DEI peculium. Qui vero non audierint, nec crediderint Evangelio, reprobi sunt, & suâ culpâ damnati. 3. Τὸ ἐτέθησαν vertere per conditi sunt, non solùm repugnat significationi huius verbi Grammaticae, sed etiam ipsius creationis Naturae. DEUS enim in Adarno omnes homines condidit ad imaginem, suam, ac proinde in iustitia & sanctitate veritatis Ephes. 4. v. 24. & ad vitam immortalem ac aeternam, Sap. 2. v. 23. August ad artic. sibi falsò impositos resp. ad 3. Omnium quidem hominum DEUS creator est, sed nemo ab eo ideò creatus est, ut pereat, quia alia causa est nascendi, & alia pereundi. Ut nascantur homines, creatoris est beneficium; ut pereant, praevaricatoris est vitium. Damasc. lib. 2. orth. sid. cap. 29. Non ad puniendum nos plasmavit DEUS, sed ut efficiat nos bonitatis suae participes, ut bonus; peccantes autem puniri vult, ut iustus. 4. Si vel maximè τὸ ἐτέθησαν referatur ad proximè praecedens membrum, οἱ προκόκτουσι τῷ λόγῳ, nondum tamen sequitur, à DEO illos esse, positos ad incredulitatem, quia Petrus absolutè dicit ἐτέθησαν, non autem addit, à DEO positi sunt. Aretius in h. l. Quis illos sic posuit, ut essent vasa irae ad interitum coagmentata? non DEUS certè, qui boni autor est & ordinis, non mali autἀταξίας,sed Satan tales posuit, & innata malitia, nec est opus in causarum peccati inquisitione, aliò progredi, quàm ad Naturam nostram. Latent enim in nobis, non in DEO eius causae. Tossanus in h. l. Sicut DEUS novit numerum credentium & electorum, quibus Christus est electus, & preciosus lapis: sic novit etiam numerum incredulorum & reproborum, quibus Christus est lapis offensionis. Quamvis vero DEUS non sit autor & causa incredulitatis, & inobedientiae hominum, per quam semetipsos in aeternum exitium praecipitant, nihil tamen fit absque DEI praevisione, qui omnia dirigit ad nominis sui gloriam, ut iustitia in damnatis, quos propter incredulitatem punit, & misericordia in electis, quos ex gratia salvat, agnoscatur & celebretur. Salmero in h. l. Est haec positio voluntaria, positi sunt à seipsis. 5. Quòd si vel maximè ex hypothesi concedamus, à DEO positos dici, non tamen dicerentur positi ad impingendum in hunc lapidem Christum, ex absoluto decreto, sed iusto DEI iudicio, antegressum verbi contemtum & incredulitatem punientis.

Examinanda vero hoc loco sunt argumenta, quibus evincere cupiunt, reprobos ad incredulitatem, absoluto DEI decreto, esse, positos. 1. Verbumτιθέναι, inquit Piscator, ita usurpaturIohan. 15. v. 16. Resp. non de positione ad fructus malos, sed de positione, ad fructus bonos proferendos ibi agitur. Ego elegi vos, & posui vos, ut eatis & fructum afferatis. August. de praedest. DEI cap. 2. Inprimis nefas est dicere, Deum aliquid nisi bonum praedestinare. Leo in Epist. ad Petrum Antiochenum. Credo Deum tantùm praedestinasse bona, praeseivisse autem bona & mala. Prosper in resp. ad Gall. praedestinatio Dei semper in bono est. Fulgent. lib. 1. ad Monim. Non sicut praedestinavit Deus sanctos ad iustitiam accipiendam, sic praedestinavit iniquos ad iustitiam amittendam &c. Nunquam Deus ad hoc hominem potuit praedestinare, quod ipse disposuit & praecepto prohibere, & misericordiâ diluere, & iustitiâ punire.

2. Actor. 13. v. 47.voxτιθέναιeodem sensu usurpatur. Resp. imò verò de electis ibi sermo est, non de reprobis. Crediderunt, quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam aeternam. Quod si ad priorem versiculi partem digitum intendit Piscator, ibi itidem non agitur de reprobis, sed de Christo electorum capite. Posui te in lucem gentium. Quid quod ex v. 46. praecedente manifestè colligitur, incredulos Iudaeos non esse à DEO positos ad incredulitatem, sed ad audiendum verbum, & fide illud amplectendum.

3. Rom. 9. v. 17.In hoc ipsum excitavite, ut ostendam in te virtutem meam. IlludExod. 9. v. 16.sic exprimitur. Idcircò posui te. Resp. in Hebraeo est, stare te feci, conservavi te, nolens te ilicò ob tuam, impietatem exterminare. Nequaquam vero Pharao dicitur positus ad reluctandum, sed ut in eo DEUS virtutem suam ostenderet. Describitur igitur salutaris sinis, ad quem pervicacem illam & voluntariam Pharaonis duritiem DEUS voluit dirigere, videlicet ut tanto tamque potente Rege everso, & Israëlitis ex servitute eius liberatis, ac potenti manu eductis DEUS suam potentiam illustraret.

4. Cap. eiusd. v. 22.vasa irae dicunturκατηρτισμέναin interitum. Resp. Apostolus non dicit, quòd DEUS vasa irae aptet, sed quòd vasa illa irae ad interitum aptata cum multa patientia sufferat. Iam verò quod quis multâ cum patientia suffert, ipse non fecit. DEUS vasa irae invenit, non facit; vasa gratiae non invenit, sed facit. Fulgent. lib. 1. ad Monim. Notum est, iram DEI dici non posse, nisi ubi creditur hominis iniquitas praecessisse. Dici ergò nequite, DEUM ex absoluto odio quosdam creare, ut sint vasa irae.

5. 1. Thess. 3. v. 3.nemo moveatur in tribulationibus. Ipsi enim scitis, quòd in hoc positi simus. Resp. tribulationes sunt pars ordinis divinitùs constituti, quo DEUS electos ad salutem perducit, Act. 14. v. 22. sed peccata non sunt pars ordinis à DEO constituti, quo reprobos perducit ad damnationem. Mala poenae à DEO immittuntur, non autem mala culpae à DEO inspirantur.

6. Epist. eiusd. cap. 5. v. 9.Non posuit nos DEUS in iram, sed in acquisitionem salutis. Resp. ad iram, i. e. ad exitium sive interitum μετωνυμικῶς irae nomine expressum, DEUS iusto iudicio reprobos posuit, i. e. aeternis poenis subiicere decrevit, sed ad causas irae, i. e. ad peccandum eos non posuit, nec praedestinavit.

7. Epist. Iud. v. 4.προγεγραμμένοιad iudicium. Resp. Oecumenius hoc sensu accipit, quòd de talibus, deque eorum impietate & iudicio, sive condemnatione ante Iudam scripserint Petrus & Paulus, imò Christus ipse eos vivis coloribus depinxerit. Matth. 24. v. 24.2. Tim. 3. v. 1.2. Petr. 2. v. 1. & seqq. quin & Prophetae in suis aemulis Pseudo Prophetis mores haereticorum descripserunt. Ier. 14. v. 14.cap. 28. v. 15.Zach. 13. v. 4.Thren. 2. v. 14. Quòd si vel maximè praescripti ad iudicium dicantur respectu reprobationis, quo modo Clemens Alexandrinus & Beda exponunt, non tamen sequeretur, eos ex absoluto decreto ad causas damnationis esse praedestinatos, disertè enim additur, εἰς τοῦτο κρῖμαad hoc iudicium sive poenam, i. e. ad condemnationem aeternam, quam impietate & pertinaciâ sunt promeriti.

8. A DEO hoc dicitur factum, quòd aedificantes lapidem illum reprobaverint.Psal. 118. v. 23. Musculus in illum locum. Resp. imò vero à Domino hoc factum dicitur, ut lapis ille voluntaria Pontificum malitiâ reprobatus fieret in caput anguli. 2. Quam interpretationem confirmat noster Apostolus v. 4. quando hunc lapidem dicit ab hominibus quidem reprobatum, apud DEUM autem electum & honorificatum, nimirum quia à Deo factus est in caput anguli. 3. Quamvis ratione permissionis & determinationis ad salutarè sinem providentia divina ad hanc ipsam lapidis reprobationem, i. e. Messiae passionem concurrerit Act. 2. v. 23.cap. 4. v. 28. nequaquam tamen statuendum, quod vel infallibili quodam & absoluto Dei decreto, vel occulto Dei impulsu Hierosolymitani Proceres ad reprobationem Messiae fuerint pertracti, sed distinguendum est inter ipsum factum reprobationis & crucifixionis Christi, & inter eiusdem salutarem finem. Factum ipsum fuit iniquum atque impium, ad quod Deus Iudaeos nec impulit, nec illud approbavit Ioh. 13. v. 2.Act. 2. v. 23. sed severissimè temporalibus & aeternis poenis vindicavit. Quia vero Deo futurorum praescio mala voluntas Procerum Iudaicorum ab aeterno fuit cognita, ideo quod illi erant facturi pessimè, illud ad redemtionem generis humani ipse convertit optimè & sapientissimè. 4. Hanc distinctionem monstrat David ipse, quando reprobationem huius lapidis non Deo, sed stolidis aedificantibus, adeoque ipsi Diabolo homicidae, cuius organa in hac parte fuerunt, tribuit: constitutionem autem lapidis in caput anguli Deo autori assignat. August. in h. l. Psalmi. A Domino factus est Christus caput anguli. Quamvis enim hoc non esset factus, nisi passus esset, non tamen hoc ab iis, à quibus passus est, factus est. Nam illi, qui aedificabant, reprobabant, sed in eo, quod Dominus occultè aedificabat, fecit in caput anguli, quod illi reprobaverunt.

## 2:9
BUT YOU ARE A CHOSEN GENERATION, A ROYAL PRIESTHOOD, A HOLY NATION, A PECULIAR PEOPLE, THAT YOU SHOULD SHOW FORTH THE VIRTUES OF HIM, WHO CALLED YOU OUT OF DARKNESS INTO HIS MARVELOUS LIGHT.

Connection. 1. The Apostle returns to exaggerating the dignity and happiness of the pious, which he had begun to proclaim in v. 4, but on the occasion of that, because he had said that the pious, like living stones, were built upon Christ the living and fundamental stone, he had digressed through an inserted parenthesis to describe the condition of this living and fundamental stone. And from this dignity of the pious he deduces and confirms the argument of his exhortation proposed at the beginning of the chapter.

2. Because in the verses immediately preceding he had dealt with the rejection of the unbelieving Jews, who, because they had rejected the Messiah, were rejected by God, he thence proclaims the happiness of the faithful converted to Christ from among the Jews and Gentiles, because by approaching Christ and being built upon him as a living stone by true faith, they have been made a peculiar people of God and a holy assembly. Above all, he celebrates that highest benefit of God bestowed upon the Gentiles, that through the preaching of the Gospel they were called to the fellowship of the Church, and substituted in the place of the Jews, they are now reckoned as the people of God.

3. Again he separates the faithful, to whom he writes, from the unbelievers who reject Christ and are in turn rejected by him, lest, seduced by their example, they fall away from the true faith, and because the greatest part of the Jews stumbled against that cornerstone, they themselves also depart from Christ, and thus fall from the dignity and happiness divinely bestowed upon them.

4. On the contrary, he exhorts them to the glorification of God and the pursuit of a holy life, that they may show themselves grateful for the benefits received. For he draws the argument of his exhortation from the commemoration of two greatest benefits, namely, election to eternal life and calling to the fellowship of the Church.

Exposition of the text. The Apostle adorns those believing in Christ with four excellent titles. 1. He calls them γένος ἐκλεκτὸν.. The word Election, when used of men, signifies first in general to select someone to perform public duties, whether Ecclesiastical or Political. Exod. 18. vers. 25.Deut. 18. Vers. 5.1. Sam. 10. v. 24.Luc. 6. v. 13.Actor. 1. Vers. 24. Then, in species and a stricter signification, it is used either of the whole assembly of the Church, which God gathers to Himself from all peoples and nations through the word and chooses as a peculiar people; or of the true and living members of the Church, who by true faith adhere to Christ the head of the Church and persevere in it until the end of life. The former election is temporal, the latter eternal. Some therefore maintain that the Apostle is speaking here only of the former election, which with vocation is the same, in which sense the Israelites in the O. T. are said to be chosen by GOD.Deut. 3. v. 37.GOD loved your fathers, and chose their seed after them.cap. 7. v. 6.The Lord your GOD chose you, that you might be to him a peculiar people from all peoples that are upon the earth.cap. 10. v. 15.Behold the heaven of the Lord your GOD is, and the heaven of heavens, the earth and all things that are in it, and yet the Lord was joined to your fathers and loved them, and chose their seed after them, that is, you from all nations.cap. 14. v. 2.GOD chose you, that you might be to him a peculiar people.Esai. 43. v. 20.I gave waters in the desert, that I might give drink to my chosen peoplev. 21.I formed this people for myself. But it is more correctly said that the Apostle speaks not only of this temporal election to the fellowship of the Church, but also and chiefly of the eternal election to eternal life. 1. For he adds the name of a race, through which he leads us to the second birth, or spiritual regeneration, of which he had treated in v. 23. of the preceding chapter, by which not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of GOD they were bornIoh. 1. v. 13.and were made into sons and heirs of GOD, and indeed co-heirs of Christ adoptedRom. 8. v. 17. the race of GOD himself, in a far more sublime way than that by which all men are otherwise called the race of GOD on account of the benefit of creation. Act. 17. v. 28. Thus, therefore, on account of the regeneration made from an incorruptible seed, i. e., through the living word of God, he calls them a chosen race. 2. He opposes this to those who, through the rejection of the chosen stone, have been made reprobate. But to the reprobate are directly opposed the elect in Christ to eternal life. 3. He compares the dignity and happiness of believers with the dignity and happiness of the Israelitic people in the O. T., and intimates that the former is far greater than the latter. The Israelitic people had been chosen for a terrestrial possession, hence with the election of that people, in the places just cited, the leading out from the land of Egypt and the promise of the land of Canaan are perpetually conjoined, but believers are chosen not for any terrestrial possession, but for a heavenly inheritance, prefigured by the land of Canaan, without any merit of their own. 4. He signifies that not the unbelieving Jews, who descended from the Patriarchs through carnal generation, but those believing in Christ are the true and genuine sons of the Patriarchs, and consequently that the covenant of grace entered into with the Patriarchs and all the spiritual benefits annexed to it pertain not to the unbelieving Jews, but to those converted from the Jews and the nations Matth. 3. v. 9.Rom. 4. v. 11.cap. 9. v. 6. and following 2. He calls them a royal Priesthood. This is taken from Exod. 19. v. 6.

You shall be to me ממלכת כהנים a kingdom of priests or a priestly one, which the LXX rendered by the transposition βασὶλειον ίεράτευμα, which Peter follows in this place. He had previously called the believers ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον v. 9. now he calls them ἱεράτευμα βασίλειον, so that he may signify that they were not only made spiritual Kings by Christ, but also spiritual Priests, just as this phrase is explained Apoc. 1. v. 6.cap. 5. v. 10.cap. 20. v. 6. in which way the Chaldean also rendered Exod. 19. v. 6. You shall be to me Kings and Priests. The sense therefore is that just as in the Israelite people there was once both a kingdom and an external Priesthood divinely constituted: so truly pious people and believers in the N. Testament are a royal Priesthood and a priestly kingdom, that is, spiritual Kings and Priests. 3. ἔθνος ἄγιον. This likewise is taken from Moses, with whom it is frequent and solemn that the Israelite people are called a holy people. Exod. 19. v. 6.Deut. 7. v. 6.cap. 14. v. 2. etc. But the Israelites were called a holy people, both because they were separated from the unclean gentiles and elected into a holy people of GOD, and because in the Ceremonial laws GOD had prescribed to them an external, legal, and Ceremonial holiness in the choice of foods, in various readings, etc., by which they were to be reminded of internal and spiritual holiness, whence also this clause is frequently prefixed or added to the promulgation of the Ceremonial laws: You shall be holy, or be holy, because I also am holy, Exod. 22. v. 31.Levit. 11. v. 44. & 45.cap. 20. v. 26.Num. 15. v. 40. But when truly pious people and believers are here called a holy people, regard is had to the interior and spiritual holiness, prefigured by that legal and external holiness. Ioh. 17. v. 17.Eph. 1. v. 4.cap. 5. v. 27.Hebr. 13. v. 12. etc. Especially therefore the Apostle here looks to the prophecy of Isaiah cap. 62. v. 11. Say to the daughter of Sion, Behold your salvation comes. v. 12. And they shall call them a people of holiness or a holy people, the redeemed of the Lord. But by singular counsel the Apostle does not call believers λαὸν ἅγιον, but ἔθνος ἅγιον, in which way the LXX also rendered the Heb. גוי Exod. 19. v. 6. when Esai. 62. v. 11. it is עם הקדש To carnal and incredulous Jews the name of the nations was very hateful, for they judged the nations to be hated by GOD and abominable, but to Jews converted to the faith of Christ it was pleasing, because they rejoiced from the heart concerning the calling of the nations to the kingdom of Christ predicted in the O. T., and Peter by this very name admonishes them, because in the N. T. there is no longer a distinction between Jews and Gentiles, but all are one in Christ. Gal. 3. Vers. 28.Col. 3. v. 11. 4. λαὸν εἱς περιποὶησιν The Vulgate rendered a people of acquisition. This is also taken from Moses. Exod. 19. Vers. 5. You shall be to me סגלה a peculiar treasure above all peoples. Deut. 7. v. 6. The Lord your GOD chose you to be to him a people of peculiar treasure above all peoples, which is repeated cap. 14. v. 2.cap. 26. v. 18.Mal. 3. v. 17. סגלה signifies to the Hebrews a dear, precious thing, which is held in the place of a treasure. Eccles. 2. v. 8. The Chaldean rendered You shall be to me חביבין beloved, because precious things and treasures are wont to be dear. The LXX rendered λαὸς περιούσιος a peculiar people, because סגלה is used by the Rabbis for the property and innate force of a thing. Theodosius and Symmachus translated λαὸς ἐξαὶρετος. Lyranus. You shall be to me amiability. Pagninus You shall be to me as a beloved treasure, as some precious κειμήλιον, which is highly esteemed and diligently preserved. Paul Tit. 2. v. 14. following the LXX Interpreters likewise renders λαὸν περιούσιον. Peter in this place expresses the sense, translating λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν a people for acquisition i. e. an acquired possession. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] a redeemed assembly, which, to wit, Christ acquired and redeemed with his own blood. GOD had liberated the Israelites from Egyptian servitude and captivity, and had claimed them for himself as his own, as it were, possession and thus as a peculiar treasure, hence he calls them a people of acquisition or of acquired possession and claiming. Because therefore that corporal benefit of liberation from the hand of Pharaoh was a figure of the spiritual liberation, by which CHRIST, having snatched us from the power of Satan, asserted us as a people proper and peculiar to himself, hence Peter calls believers λαὸν εἰς περιποὶησιν. Actor. 20. vers. 28. GOD with his own blood περιποιήσατο acquired his Church. Ephes. 1. vers. 14. The Holy Spirit is the pledge of our inheritance εἰς ὰπολύτρωσιν τῆς περιποιήσεως unto the redemption of acquisition, that is, of acquired possession, as Erasmus rendered, while we are vindicated into the liberty which CHRIST merited and acquired for us. 1. Thess. 5. vers. 9. GOD has not set us unto wrath, but unto the acquisition of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, 2. Thess. 2. vers. 14. GOD called us through the Gospel to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ,Heb. 10. v. 39.we are of faith unto the obtaining of the soul. When therefore Peter calls believers λαὸν εἰς περιποίησιν, he admonishes them concerning the benefit of election, redemption, vocation, adoption, and glorification, as can be understood from a comparison of parallel sayings. Ambrose in his exposition of Psal. 118. octonary 6, and Augustine in book 1 of De peccatorum meritis et remissione, chapter 27, read, a people in adoption, which some think was changed from that which was formerly written, a people in acquisition. But from the things said, it is clear that the reading of Ambrose and Augustine in no way departs from the scope and sense. Thus, therefore, those four epithets, (a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for an acquisition) which in the Old Testament are attributed by Moses to the Israelite people, chosen by GOD as a peculiar possession before all nations, heaped with many benefits, and adorned with various prerogatives, the Apostle attributes to the Christian people of the New Testament, since the corporal benefits bestowed upon the Israelite people were types of the spiritual benefits to be bestowed upon the Christian people in the New Testament, and consequently far inferior to them. He also expresses the end of that περιποιήσεως, for which GOD claimed them for Himself as a peculiar people, namely that they might announce the virtues of Him who called them out of darkness into His admirable light. Bede thinks that regard is had to chapter 15 of Exodus, in which is described the Song of praise, which the Israelites composed after their leading out of Egypt through the Red Sea, to the glory of GOD the liberator. Just as (he says) those who were liberated from Egyptian servitude sang a triumphal song to the Lord through Moses after the crossing of the Red Sea and the drowning of Pharaoh's army: so also it behooves us, after the remission of sins received in Baptism, to repay thanks worthy of heavenly benefits. For the Egyptians, who afflicted the people of GOD, because they are interpreted as darkness or tribulations, aptly signify the sins following us, but deleted in Baptism. The liberation also of the children of Israel, and their being led to the land once promised to the fathers, corresponds to the mystery of our redemption, through which we tend toward the light of the heavenly mansion, with the grace of Christ illuminating and leading us, the light of whose grace that pillar of cloud and fire also showed, which defended them, both in that whole journey, from the darkness of the nights, and led them in an ineffable way to the promised seats of the fatherland. Nor is it undeservedly considered that the Apostle also looked to chapter 43 of Isaiah, in which the prophecy concerning the vocation of the Gentiles to the fellowship of the Church It is added v. 7. Everyone who is called by my name, I have created him for my glory. And after the Prophet had proposed the benefit of the liberation from Egypt, and the leading through the Red Sea, and the desert into the land of Canaan, as a type of the spiritual liberation that was to follow in the New Testament, he adds v. 21. This people I have formed for myself, they shall declare my praise. LXX. λαὸν μου ὅν περιποιησάμην τάς ἀρετάς μου διηγεῖσθαι. Nor is it absurdly established that the Apostle requires the announcement of divine virtues from believers for this reason, because a little before he had called them a holy and royal priesthood, for the duty of priests among other things is also this, that they ought to announce the word of GOD, and glorify his name. By virtues in this place are not understood δυνάμεις, which the Vulgate Interpreter expressed elsewhere by the name of virtues, Matt. 7. vers. 22. chap. 11. v. 20. chap. 24. v. 29. etc. But ἀρεταὶ opposed to vices. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] praises, because virtues deserve praise, and praises are attributed to someone, they certainly ought to be attributed on account of virtues. Cornelius à Lapide explains it concerning virtues, which Christ works in us, by inspiring into us humility, charity, patience etc., which virtues wonderfully commend the glory of Christ. But it is manifest from the text that the Apostle is speaking about the virtues of him who called us, not about the virtues of those who were called. Salmero explains it concerning the virtues of Christ, which he exhibited to be seen in full splendor in the days of his flesh, namely concerning Christ's love, patience, obedience, humility. Others take it concerning the benefits which Christ bestowed upon the Church in the time of his conversation on these lands, and still bestows upon the same today. But because the Apostle is dealing with the benefit of the calling, which is not appropriated peculiarly to Christ, but is attributed to GOD, therefore it is more correctly understood by virtues as the attributes of GOD, which shine forth in the work of gratuitous calling, and in the whole business of our salvation, namely the goodness, wisdom, and power of GOD, in which sense he also uses the name of virtue Peter 2. Epist. 1. vers. 3. by the glory and virtue of him who called us. The LXX use the name ἀρετῆς for הור, which signifies celebrity, glory, majesty, strength, and power Habac. 3. vers. 2. Zach. 6. v. 13. Also for תהלה, which signifies praise and glory Isa. 42. vers. 8. and 12. chap. 43. v. 21. chap. 63. v. 7. These virtues of GOD, in which the majesty and glory of GOD consist, the pious are commanded ἐξαγγέλλειν publicly to announce and to proclaim, to bring to the notice of others, and by this reason also to excite others to glorify GOD. The LXX use for ספר he recounted, he narrated, he numbered in order, Psal. 9. v. 14. Psal. 55. v. 8. etc., which verb the Syrian also uses in this place. The Apostle uses the related verb καταγγίλλειν in the same meaning 1. Corinth. 11. v. 26. when he commands to announce the death of the Lord. But in order that Peter may more excite the faithful to announce the praise of GOD, he commemorates some one benefit of GOD from those which he had hitherto enumerated in the 1st and 2nd chapters, which is the benefit of the calling, of which he makes mention cap. 1. v. 12. and 15. He understands, however, the calling joined with the assent of the one called, and therefore he considers it not only as it exists on the part of GOD calling, but also on the part of the man called. Of this calling he expresses both the term from which, and the term to which. The term from which, are darknesses, through which are understood: 1. Darkness of ignorance, in which the Gentiles especially remained before their calling to Christ. 2. Darkness of errors and superstitions, indeed of idolatries, in which they were likewise immersed before their calling. 3. Darkness of sins and impieties, which are called by the Apostle the unfruitful works of darkness. Eph. 5. v. 11. 4. Darkness of misery and death, not only temporal, but also eternal. 5. And thus the whole kingdom of the Devil, which the Apostle calls the power of darkness, Col. 1. v. 13. For the Holy Spirit embraces all these things when he attributes Darkness to men after the fall before their calling to the kingdom of Christ. Esa. 9. v. 2. cap. 60. v. 1. Matth. 4. v. 16. Luc. 1. v. 79. Iohan. 1. v. 5. cap. 8. vers. 12. Actor. 26. v. 18. Rom. 13. v. 12. Ephes. 5. v. 8. 1. Thessal. 5. v. 4. 1. Iohan. 2. v. 8. From which it can also be understood with little effort what ought to be understood by the marvelous light of GOD, which is the term to which of this calling. Some take it as said of Christ, who is GOD from GOD, light from light, that true light, which illuminates every man coming into this world, Ioh. 1. v. 9. the light of the world, Ioh. 8. v. 12. He is truly the marvelous light, since no one can comprehend his eternal birth from the Father. Some explain it of the light of faith and divine recognition. But the opposition shows not only faith in Christ, and saving recognition of GOD, but also the grace and blessing of GOD, the consolation of the Holy Spirit, the hope of eternal life, and thus all the benefits which in the kingdom of Christ, which is the kingdom of light, are distributed to believers, to be understood in this place by the name of light. This light is truly admirable, both because it wonderfully illuminates the mind to consider the wonders of the divine law, Psal. 119. v. 18. and because it is worthy of admiration and praise, because GOD has called those sitting in darkness to that light, and because it wonderfully leads us to eternal life. The Apostle also seems to look back to the pillar of fire, which led the Israelites, liberated from Egyptian slavery, through the desert into the land of Canaan, a type of the heavenly inheritance, concerning which Sap. 10. v. 17. He led them in a wonderful way, and was to them for a covering by day, and for a flame of stars by night. cap. 18. v. 3. for which reason you gave them a pillar of burning fire, a guide indeed of an unknown journey, and a harmless sun of an honorable hospitality.

Latin:

VOS AUTEM GENUS ELECTUM, REGALE SACERDOTIUM, GENS SANCTA, POPULUS ACQUISITIONIS, UT VIRTUTES ANNUNCIETIS EIUS, QUI DE TENEBRIS VOS VOCAVIT IN ADMIRABILE LUMEN SUUM.

Connexio. 1. Redit Apostolus ad exaggerandam piorum dignitatem, & felicitatem, quam v. 4. praedicare caeperat, sed occasione eâ, quòd pios velut lapides vivos super Christum lapidem vivum & fundamentalem extrui dixerat, per interiectam q. parenthesin ad describendam lapidis huius vivi ac fundamentalis conditionem digressus fuerat. Atque ex hac piorum dignitate argumentum exhortationis suae in principio capitis propositae deducit & confirmat.

2. Quia in vers. proximè praecedentibus de reiectione incredulorum Iudaeorum egerat, qui propterea quod Messiam reprobaverant, à Deo reprobati fuêre, inde fidelium ex Iudaeis & gentibus ad Christum conversorum felicitatem praedicat, quòd ad Christum accedentes & verâ fide super ipsum tanquam lapidem vivum extructi populus DEI peculiaris & sanctus caetus fuerint facti. Cumprimis summum illud Dei benesicium gentilibus praestitum celebrat, quòd per praedicationem Evangelii ad consortium Ecclesiae vocati, & in locum Iudaeorum substituti, iam populus Dei censeantur.

3. Denuò fideles, ad quos scribit, ab incredulis Christum reprobantibus & ab ipso vicissim reprobatis separat, ne eorum exemplo seducti à vera fide deficiant, & quia maxima Iudaeorum pars in lapidem illum angularem impegit, etiam ipsi à Christo discedant, sicque dignitate & felicitate, divinitus in se collatâ excidant.

4. Contrà vero ad DEI glorificationem & studium sanctae vitae ipsos hortatur, ut pro acceptis beneficiis sese gratos praestent. Exhortationis enim argumentum ducit à commemoratione duorum maximorum beneficiorum, electionis sc. ad vitam aeternam & vocationis ad Ecclesiae consortium.

Textus expositio. Credentes in Christum quatuor eximiis elogiis ornat Apostolus. 1. Vocat eos γένος ἐκλεκτὸν.Electionis vox de hominibus usurpata significat primò in genere aliquem seligere ad munia publica obeunda, sive Ecclesiastica, sive Politica. Exod. 18. vers. 25.Deut. 18. Vers. 5.1. Sam. 10. v. 24.Luc. 6. v. 13.Actor. 1. Vers. 24. Deinde in specie & strictiori significatione usurpatur vel de toto Ecclesiae coetu, quem ex omnibus populis & gentibus DEUS sibi per verbum colligit & in populum peculiarem eligit; vel de veris & vivis Ecclesiae membris, quae verâ fide Christo Ecclesiae capiti adhaerent & in ea ad finem usque vitae perseverant. Prior electio est temporalis, posterior aeterna. Quidam ergò statuunt, Apostolum hîc loqui dê priore tantùm electione, quae cum vocatione est eadem, quo sensu Israelitae in V. T. dicuntur à DEO electi.Deut. 3. v. 37.dilexit DEUS patres tuos, & elegit semen eorum post eos.cap. 7. v. 6.Te elegit Dominus DEUS tuus, ut sis ei in populum peculiarem de cunctis populis, qui sunt super terram.cap. 10. v. 15.En Domini DEI tui coelum est, & coeli coelorum, terra & omnia quae in ea sunt, & tamen patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus & amavit eos, elegitque semen eorum post eos, id est, vos de cunctis gentibus.cap. 14. v. 2.elegit te DEUS, ut sis ei in populum peculiarem.Esai. 43. v. 20.Dedi in deserto aquas, ut darem potum populo electo meov. 21.populum istum formavi mihi. Sed rectiùs dicitur, Apostolum non solùm de hac temporali electione ad Ecclesiae consortium, sed etiam ac praecipuè de aeterna electione ad vitam aeternam loqui. 1. Addit enim nomen generis, per quod deducit nos ad secundam nativitatem, sive spiritualem regeneratione, de qua egerat v. 23. cap. praeced. quâ non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex DEO natiIoh. 1. v. 13.& in filios ac haeredes DEI, cohaeredes vero Christi adoptatiRom. 8. v. 17. facti sunt ipsius DEI genus, longè sublimiori modo, quàm quo aliàs propter beneficium creationis homines universi dicuntur genus DEI. Act. 17. v. 28. Sic ergò propter regenerationè ex semine incorruptibili i. e. per verbum Dei vivum sactam, vocat eos genus electum. 2. Opponit hoc illis, qui per reprobationem electi lapidis facti sunt reprobi. Reprobis autem directè opponuntur electi in Christo ad vitam aeternam. 3. Credentium dignitatem & felicitatem confert cum populi Israelitici in V. T. dignitate & felicitate, & illam hac longè ampliorem esse innuit. Israeliticus populus ad terrenam possessionem electus erat, inde cum electione illius populi, in locis modò citatis, eductio ex terra Aegypti, & promissio terrae Canaan perpetuò coniunguntur, sed credentes non ad terrenam aliquam possessionem, sed ad coelestem haereditatem, per terram Canaan praefiguratam, absque ullo suo merito sunt electi. 4. Significat, non incredulos Iudaeos, qui per carnalem generationem à Patriarchis descendebant, sed credentes in Christum esse veros & genuinos Patriarcharum filios, ac proinde non ad incredulos Iudaeos, sed ad conversos ex Iudaeis & gentibus pertinere foedus gratiae cum Patriarchis initum & omnia beneficia spiritualia ei annexa Matth. 3. v. 9.Rom. 4. v. 11.cap. 9. v. 6. & seqq. 2. Vocat eos regale Sacerdotium. Desumtum hoc ex Exod. 19. v. 6.

Eritis mihiממלכת כהניםregnum Sacerdotum sive Sacerdotale, quod LXX. reddiderunt per transpositionem βασὶλειον ίεράτευμα, quos Petrus hoc loco sequitur. Priùs vocaverat credentes. ἱεράτευμα ἅγιονv. 9. iam vocat eos ἱεράτευμα βασίλειον, ut significet, illos non solùm à Christo factos esse spirituales Reges, sed etiam spirituales Sacerdotes, sicut haec phrasis exponitur Apoc. 1. v. 6.cap. 5. v. 10.cap. 20. v. 6. quo modo etiam Chaldaeus reddidit Exod. 19. v. 6.Eritis mihi Reges & Sacerdotes. Sensus igitur est, quod quemadmodum in populo Israelitico olim fuit & regnum & Sacerdotium externum divinitus constitutum: ita verè pii & credentes in N. Test. sint regium Sacerdotium & Sacerdotale regnum h. e. spirituales Reges & Sacerdotes. 3. ἔθνος ἄγιον. Hoc itidem desumtum ex Mose, apud quem populum Israeliticum vocari populum sanctum, frequens est & solenne. Exod. 19. v. 6.Deut. 7. v. 6.cap. 14. v. 2. &c. Dicebantur autem Israelitae populus sanctus, tùm quia erant ab immundis gentilibus separati & in populum DEI sanctum electi, tùm quia in legibus Ceremonialibus externam, legalem & Ceremonialem sanctitatem in delectu ciborum, in variis lectionibus &c. DEUS ipsis praescripserat, quâ de interna & spirituali sanctitate moneri debebant, unde etiam promulgationi legum Ceremonialium haec clausula frequenter praemittitur vel subiicitur: Sancti eritis, vel sancti estote, quoniam & ego sanctus sum,Exod. 22. v. 31.Levit. 11. v. 44. & 45.cap. 20. v. 26.Num. 15. v. 40. Sed quando verè pii & credentes hîc dicuntur populus sanctus, respectus habetur ad interiorem & spiritualem sanctitatem, per legalem illam & externam sanctitatem praefiguratam. Ioh. 17. v. 17.Eph. 1. v. 4.cap. 5. v. 27.Hebr. 13. v. 12. &c. Cumprimis ergò Apostolus hîc respicit ad vaticinium Esaiae cap. 62. v. 11.Dicite filiae Sion, Ecce salus tua venit.v. 12.Et vocabunt eos populum sanctitatis sive sanctum, redemtos Domini. Singulari autem consilio Apostolus credentes non vocat λαὸν ἅγιον, sed ἔθνος ἅγιον, quo modo etiam LXX. reddiderunt Heb. גויExod. 19. v. 6. cum Esai. 62. v. 11. sit עם הקדש Iudaeis carnalibus & incredulis nomen gentium erat valde invisum, iudicabant enim gentes esse DEO exosas & abominabiles, sed Iudaeis ad Christi fidem conversis illud erat gratum, quia de vocatione gentium ad regnum Christi in V. T. praedictâ animitus laetabantur, ac Petrus hoc ipso nomine eos admonet, quòd in N. T. non ampliùs sit distinctio inter Iudaeos & gentes, sed omnes esse unum in Christo. Gal. 3. Vers. 28.Col. 3. v. 11. 4. λαὸν εἱς περιποὶησιν Vulgata reddidit populum acquisitionis. Desumtum & hoc ex Mose. Exod. 19. Vers. 5.Eritis mihiסגלהpeculium prae omnibus populis.Deut. 7. v. 6.elegit te Dominus DEUS tuus ad existendum ei in populum peculii prae omnibus populis, quod repetitur cap. 14. v. 2.cap. 26. v. 18.Mal. 3. v. 17.סגלה Hebraeis significat rem caram, preciosam, quae thesauri loco habetur. Eccles. 2. v. 8. Chaldaeus reddidit. Eritis mihiחביביןdilecti, quia res preciosae & thesauri solent esse cari. LXX. reddiderunt λαὸς περιούσιοςpopulus peculiaris, quia סגלה à Rabinis usurpatur pro rei proprietate & vi innata. Theodosius &Symmachus verterunt λαὸς ἐξαὶρετος. Lyranus. Eritis mihi amicabilitas. Pagninus Eritis mihi tanquam thesaurus dilectus, velut preciosum aliquod κειμήλιον, quod magni aestimatur ac diligenter asservatur. Paulus Tit. 2. v. 14. secutus LXX. Interpretes itidem reddit λαὸν περιούσιον. Petrus hoc loco sensum exprimit, vertens λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν populus in acquisitionem i. e. acquisitam possessionem. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] coetus redemtus, quem sc. Christus suo sanguine acquisivit & redemit. Israelitas liberaverat DEUS exservitute & captivitate Aegyptiaca, eosdemque in propriam, q. possessionem adeoque in peculium sibi vendicaverat, inde vocat eos populum acquisitionis sive acquisitae possessionis & vendicationis. Quia ergò corporale illud beneficium liberationis è manu Pharaonis fuit figura spiritualis liberationis, qua CHRISTUS nos è potestate Satanae ereptos in populum sibi proprium ac peculiarem nos asseruit, inde Petrus credentes vocat λαὸν εἰς περιποὶησιν.Actor. 20. vers. 28.DEUS proprio suo sanguineπεριποιήσατοacquisivit Ecclesiam suam.Ephes. 1. vers. 14.Spiritus sanctus est pignus haereditatis nostraeεἰς ὰπολύτρωσιν τῆς περιποιήσεωςin redemtionem acquisitionis, id est, acquisitae possessionis, ut Erasmus reddidit, dum in libertatem vindicemur, quam CHRISTUS nobis promeruit & acquisivit. 1. Thess. 5. vers. 9.Non posuit nos DEUS ad iram, sed in acquisitionem salutis per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum,2. Thess. 2. vers. 14.Vocavit nos DEUS per Evangelium ad acquisitionem gloriae Domini nostri Iesu Christi,Hebr. 10. v. 39.sumus fidei in acquisitionem animae. Quando igitur Petrus credentes vocat λαὸν εἰς περιποίησιν, admonet illos de beneficio electionis, redemtionis, vocationis, adoptionis & glorificationis, ut ex collatione dictorum parallelorum intelligi potest. Ambrosius in expos. Psal. 118. octon. 6. Augustinus lib. 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. 27. legunt, populus in adoptione, quod quidam putant, mutatum ex eo, quod olim scriptum, populus in adeptione. Sed ex dictis, patet, Ambrosii & Augustini lectionem à scopo & sensu minimè recedere. Sic ergò quatuor illa epitheta, (genus electum, Regale Sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus in acquisitionem) quae in V. Test. populo Israëlitico à DEO prae cunctis gentibus in peculium electo, multis beneficiis cumulato, ac variis praerogativis ornato à Mose attribuuntur, Apostolus populo Christiano N. T. tribuit, cum corporalia beneficia populo Israëlitico praestita fuerint typi spiritualium benesiciorum, in N. Test. populo Christiano praestandorum, ac proinde illis longè inferiora. Exprimit etiam finem illius περιποιήσεως, propter quem DEUS in populum peculiarem eos sibi vendicarit, videlicet ut annuncient virtutes eius, qui de tenebris vocavit eos in admirabile lumen suum. Beda existimat, respectum haberi ad caput 15. Exodi, in quo describitur Canticum laudis, quod Israëlitae post eductionem ex Aegypto per mare rubrum, in gloriam DEI liberatoris composuerunt. Sicut (inquit) hi, qui de Aegyptiacâ servitute liberati sunt, per Mosen carmen triumphale post transitum maris rubri, & demersum Pharaonis exercitum Domino decantarunt: ita & nos oportet post acceptam in Baptismo remissionem peccatorum dignas beneficiis coelestibus rependere gratias. Namque Aegyptii, qui populum DEI affligebant, quia tenebrae vel tribulationes interpretantur, aptè per sequentia nos peccata, sed in Baptismate deleta significant. Liberatio quoque filiorum Israël, & ad promissam olim patriam perductio congruit mysterio nostrae redemtionis, per quam ad lucem supernae mansionis illustrante nos ac ducente Christi gratiâ tendimus, cuius lucem gratiae etiam illa nubis & ignis columna monstravit, quae eos, & in toto itinere illo, à tenebris defendit noctium, & ad promissas patriae sedes inenarrabili modo perduxit. Nec immeritò etiam censetur Apostolus respexisse ad cap. 43. Esaiae, in quo prophetiae de vocatione gentium ad Ecclesiae consortium subiungitur v. 7.Omnis qui vocatur in nomine meo, ad gloriam meam creavi eum. Ac postquam Propheta beneficium liberationis ex AEgypto, ac deductionis per mare rubrum, & desertum in terram Canaan, tanquam spiritualis liberationis in N. T. secuturae typum proposuerat, subiungit v. 21.Populum istum formavi mihi, laudem meam enarrabunt. LXX. λαὸν μου ὅν περιποιησάμην τάς ἀρετάς μου διηγεῖσθαι. Nec absurdè statuitur, Apostolum propterea annunciationem divinarum virtutum à credentibus requirere, quia eos paulo ante vocaverat sanctum & regale Sacerdotium, Sacerdotum enim munus inter coetera etiam hoc est, quòd verbum DEI annunciare, & nomen eius glorificare debeant. Per virtutes hoc loco non intelliguntur δυνάμεις, quas alibi virtutum nomine Vulgatus Interpres expressit, Matth. 7. vers. 22.cap. 11. v. 20.cap. 24. v. 29. &c. Sed ἀρεταὶ vitiis oppositae. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]laudes, quia virtutes laudem merentur, & laudes alicui tribuuntur, tribui certè debent propter virtutes. Cornelius à Lapide exponit de virtutibus, quas Christus in nobis operatur, humilitatem, caritatem, patientiam &c. nobis aspirando, quae virtutes mirificè commendant gloriam Christi. Sed manifestum est ex textu, Apostolum loqui de virtutibus eius, qui nos vocavit, non de virtutibus eorum, qui-vocati sunt. Salmero exponit de virtutibus Christi, quas in diebus carnis suae pleno fulgore conspiciendas exhibuit, videlicet de Christi dilectione, patientiâ, obedientiâ, humilitate. alii accipiunt de beneficiis, quae Christus tempore conversationis suae in his terris Ecclesiae praestitit, & adhuc hodiè eidem praestat. Sed quia Apostolus de beneficio vocationis agit, quod non appropriatur peculiariter Christo, sed DEO tribuitur, ideò rectiùs per virtutes intelliguntur attributa DEI, quae in opere gratuitae vocationis, & in toto negotio salutis nostrae relucent, videlicet DEI bonitas, sapientia ac potentia, quo sensu etiam nomine virtutis utitur Petrus 2. Epist. 1. vers. 3. eius qui vocavit nos gloriâ & virtute. LXX. nomine ἀρετῆς utuntur pro הור, quod celebritatem, gloriam, maiestatem, robur ac potentiam significat Habac. 3. vers. 2.Zach. 6. v. 13. Item pro תהלה, quod laudem & gloriam significat Esa. 42. vers. 8. & 12.cap. 43. v. 21.cap. 63. v. 7. Has DEI virtutes, in quibus DEI maiestas & gloria consistit, iubentur pii ἐξαγγέλλειν publicè annunciare ac depraedicare, in aliorum notitiam perducere, & hac ratione etiam alios ad DEUM glorificandum excitare. LXX. utuntur pro ספרrecensuit, enarravit, ordine numeravit,Psal. 9. v. 14.Psal. 55. v. 8. &c. quo verbo etiam Syrus hoc loco utitur. Cognatum verbum καταγγίλλειν in eadem significatione usurpat Apostolus 1. Corinth. 11. v. 26. quando mortem Domini annunciare iubet. Ut autem ad laudem DEI annunciandam fideles magis excitet Petrus, unum aliquod DEI beneficium ex iis, quae hactenus in 1. & 2. capite enumeraverat, commemorat, quod est beneficium vocationis, cuius mentionem facit cap. 1. v. 12. & 15. Intelligit autem vocationem cum assensu vocati coniunctam, ac proinde eam considerat, non tantùm ut se habet ex parte DEI vocantis, sed etiam ex parte hominis vocati. Huius vocationis exprimit, tùm terminum à quo, tùm terminum ad quem. Terminus à quo, sunt tenebrae, per quas intelliguntur. 1. Tenebrae ignorantiae, in quibus ante vocationem suam ad Christum gentiles cumprimis haeserunt. 2. Tenebrae errorum ac superstitionum, imò idololatriarum, quibus itidem ante vocationem immersi fuêre. 3. Tenebrae peccatorum & impietatum, quae ab Apostolo vocantur infructuosa opera tenebrarum. Eph. 5. v. 11. 4. Tenebrae miseriae & mortis, non solùm temporalis, sed & aeternae. 5. Adeoque totum Diaboli regnum, quod Apostolus vocat potestatem tenebrarum, Col. 1. v. 13. Haec enim omnia Spiritus sanctus complectitur, quando hominibus post lapsum ante vocationem ad regnum Christi Tenebras tribuit. Esa. 9. v. 2.cap. 60. v. 1.Matth. 4. v. 16.Luc. 1. v. 79.Iohan. 1. v. 5.cap. 8. vers. 12.Actor. 26. v. 18.Rom. 13. v. 12.Ephes. 5. v. 8.1. Thessal. 5. v. 4.1. Iohan. 2. v. 8. Ex quo etiam facili negotio intelligi potest, quid per lumen DEI admirabile, quod est vocationis huius terminus ad quem, intelligi debeat. Quidam accipiunt de Christo dictum, qui est DEUS de DEO, lumen de lumine, lux illa vera, quae illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum,Ioh. 1. v. 9.lux mundi,Ioh. 8. v. 12. Is verè est lumen admirabile, cum aeternam ipsius à Patre nativitatem nemo comprehendere possit. Quidam exponunt de lumine fidei & agnitionis divinae. Sed oppositio ostendit non solùm fidem in Christum, & salvificam DEI agnitionem, verùm etiam DEI gratiam & benedictionem, Spiritus sancti consolationem, spem vitae aeternae, adeoque omnia beneficia, quae in regno Christi, quod est regnum lucis, credentibus distribuuntur, luminis nomine hoc loco intelligi. Hoc lumen est verè admirabile, tùm quia mirabiliter mentem illustrat, ad consideranda mirabilia legis divinae, Psal. 119. v. 18. tùm quia admiratione & laude dignum, quòd DEUS ad illud lumen sedentes in tenebris vocaverit, tùm quia ad vitam aeternam mirabiliter nos deducit. Videtur etiam Apostolus respicere ad columnam ignis, quae Israelitas ex Aegyptiaca servitute liberatos, per desertum in terram Canaan, coelestis haereditatis typum, deduxit, de qua Sap. 10. v. 17.Deduxit eos in via mirabili, & fuit illis in velamentum die, & in flammam stellarum nocte.cap. 18. v. 3.propter quae ignis ardentis columnam ducem quidem ignoti itineris. Solem autem non laedentem honorifici hospitii praestitisti.

## 2:9-12 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Whether the pronoun ὑμεῖς in v. 9. is to be taken collectively, or distributively? Resp. it does not indeed conflict with the analogy of faith, if it is taken distributively, because individual believers are a race an elect and Royal Priesthood, meanwhile it is more consistent with the text if it is taken collectively concerning the faithful gathered into one assembly, or concerning the Church of Christ, which is the congregation of the saints, for immediately it is subjoined. You are a holy nation, a people of acquisition, v. 9. and who once were not a people, but now are the people of GOD, v. 10. and it precedes v. 5. You yourselves as living stones are built up into a spiritual house.

Q. 2. Why is the Israelite people called a kingdom of Priests or a Priestly kingdom? Resp. 1. Because the kingdom of this people was not profane from works and arms, but sacred, consisting of Priests, sacred things, and divine things. 2. Kings and Priests among all peoples are the highest, and more honorable than the rest. It is signified, therefore, that the Israelites were elected and selected by GOD from all nations, so that they might be preeminent before all peoples, and they themselves peculiarly consecrated. 3. Respect is had at the same time to Christ, who is that true King and Priest, who was to be born from the Jewish people according to the promise of GOD. Fagius in chapter 19 of Exodus. 4. The Israelites were not subject to Kings first in the manner of other profane nations, but they used GOD as King, and for their liberty they were individually like Kings. Afterwards from their own assembly GOD chose Kings and Priests, determining the Priesthood to the tribe of Levi, the kingdom to the tribe of Judah.

Q. 3. Why are the faithful called a Royal Priesthood, that is, Kings and Priests? Resp. Why they are called Priests, the Apostle himself explained v. 5. They are called Kings 1. Because they command their vicious affections, they do not permit sin to have dominion in their mortal body, but they dominate the flesh and its concupiscences. 2. Because they are subject to GOD through faith and holy obedience, but to serve GOD is to reign. 3. They are members of Christ, King and Priest, therefore from the head, and in their head Christ, they themselves are deservedly reckoned also as Kings and Priests. Didymus of Alexandria in his exposition upon the 7th Canonical Epistle, after he showed that Christ is King and Priest, he subjoins. These things therefore being dispensed, it was necessary for those dispersed by Him, who is at once King and Priest, to be an elect race, and Royal at the same time, and Priestly, since their Father indeed possesses both headships, it is necessary that they, as if from a King, be a Royal race, and as if from a Priest, a Priestly race. 4. Christ reigns in them through the Holy Spirit, says Ambrose in chapter 1 of the Apocalypse, and in them He conquers sin, the world, and the Devil. 5. They are children of GOD, of the highest King, are brothers and co-heirs of Christ, who is King of Kings and Lord of lordsApoc. 19. 16. and will one day reign with him in the heavens. Matth. 19. 28.Luc. 22. 30.1. Cor. 6. 2.Apoc. 3. vers. 21.6. They are anointed as Kings for a spiritual kingdom, not with external oil, but with the Holy Spirit, who is the oil of gladnessPsal. 45. v. 8. Lactantius, book 4 of the Institutes, chapter 7: It was commanded to the Jews that they should prepare a sacred ointment, with which those who were called to the Priesthood or to the kingdom could be anointed. And just as now for the Romans the garment of purple is a sign of assumed royal dignity, so for them the anointing of the sacred ointment conferred the name and royal power.

Q. 4. Does Peter take the Prophetic saying concerning those converted from Judaism, or indeed concerning those converted from Gentilism? Resp. 1. Some wish that the prediction of the Prophet pertains to the Israelites alone dispersed among the nations: to whom the Prophet, after the announced divorce, promises the grace of reconciliation, which promise Peter teaches is now fulfilled through the calling to the kingdom of Christ, so that the sense may be: You who until now were not the people of God, inasmuch as you did not have the true and saving knowledge of God and divine things, and were entangled in the corruptions of the nations, now you are the people of God. Calvin in this place: After Hosea in the name of GOD announced the divorce to the Jews, he gives them hope of future reconciliation; this Peter warns is fulfilled. They were dispersed, entangled in the corruptions of the nations, hence by reason of their former state they are called not a people. Strength can be sought for this exposition from the fact that the Prophet incap. 1. v. 6. & 7. distinguishes between the house of Israel and Judah, and afterwardscap. 2. v. 1. (or as others distinguish incap. 1. v. 10.) and subjoins this prophecy C. 2. v. 22., whence Origen, Chrysostom, and other Greek Fathers interpret this passage concerning the spiritual restoration of the ten tribes. 2. Some wish that the prediction of the Prophet pertains to those converted from the Gentiles alone, as is gathered from the parallel passage Deut. 32. v. 21. and from the Apostolic allegation Rom. 9. v. 25. where Paul teaches that not only Jews, but also the nations have been called by God to the fellowship of the Church in the New Testament. To that, that Hosea seems to speak about the Israelites, they respond from Augustine, book 18 of the City of GOD, chapter 28: the people of the nations themselves also are spiritually in the sons of Abraham, and through this they are rightly called Israel. 3. Cajetan establishes that what was predicted by the Prophet concerning the Gentile people, the same Peter adapts in his own words to the people of the circumcision. For the Apostle does not say that the Prophet wrote these things about those whom he addresses.

4. Some wish the prophecy of Hosea to pertain in the literal sense to the Jews, and in the mystical to the Gentiles, and therefore, just as the Apostle adapts those things which are said in the literal sense concerning the Jews Exod. 19. to those converted from the Gentiles, so also in this place he adapts the prophecy of Hosea, which treats in the literal sense of the Jews, in the mystical sense to those converted from the Gentiles. We have warned above that Peter is writing this Epistle principally indeed to those converted from the Jews, meanwhile, however, also directing his speech secondarily to those converted from the Gentiles, nor is it new or unusual in the Scriptures for one and the same prophecy to be adapted in diverse ways. For although it may seem to belong uniquely or principally to those converted from the Gentiles that they are called by GOD from darkness into his marvelous light, Es. 42. v. 6 cap. 49. v. 6. Luc 2. v. 32. Actor. 13. v. 47. Eph. 5. v. 8. yet it is manifest from Esai. 9. v. 1. cap. 60. v. 1. Matth. 4. v. 16. Iohan. 1. vers. 5. that this very thing can also be referred to the Jews.

Q. 5. What are those detractions and slanders to which the Apostle testifies that Christians were formerly subject in this place? Resp. 1. Some accept those detractions concerning the calumny by which Christians were said to devour human flesh, taking the occasion from the mystery of the Eucharist, of which calumny Justin mentions Apol. 1. Eusebius lib. 5. Histor. cap. 1. & seqq. Oecumen. in comm. h. l. Unbelieving servants accused their Christian masters that they prepared Thyestean banquets. 2. Some accept them concerning the calumny by which they called Christ a magician, and lied that Christians practiced magical arts. August. lib. 1. de cons. Evang. cap. 9. They think Christ was therefore most wise, because he knew I know not what illicit things, which not only the Christian discipline, but even the administration of the earthly Republic itself condemns by law. lib. 18. de C. D. cap. 53. He records that Peter was proclaimed a magician by the pagans. Ioh. Hussus in comm. h. l. The pagans imposed upon Christians that they practiced the magic art. 3. Some expound them concerning the calumny by which John the Evangelist was said to have magnified the deeds of Christ beyond the truth. 4. Some concerning the crime of infanticide, with which Christians were burdened by the Gentiles. Ludov. Vives in comm. lib. 18. de Civ. Dei cap. 53. Tertullian shows in his Apologetic that infanticides were accustomed to be cast at Christians, who clears this most false and most impudent crime, although the Cataphrygians and Pepuzians, two kinds of men of a heresy especially lost and desperate, were accustomed to the tender body of an infant through to prick all the limbs, so that the flour might be soaked with the blood thus expressed, with which they would make bread for the use of the Eucharist, as Augustine narrates to Quodvultdeus etc. The Euchites and Gnostics used to do something similar to drive away demons, as is read in Michael Psellus. But these were held to be as much Christian as the magical arts and the rites of worshipping demons. 5. Some concerning the calumny by which Christians were said to use promiscuous sex in their mysteries and assemblies, of which Justin makes mention Apol. 2. to which accusation the Gnostics, disciples of Simon Magus, had likewise given occasion, practicing base and nefarious things in their conventicles, as witnessed by Epiphanius in the heresy against the Gnostics. 6. Some take it concerning the calumnies to which Christians were liable from the Jews converted to Christ, to whom this Epistle was principally written. For they were accused because of the seditions often stirred up by their own ancestors against the Romans, that under the pretext of religion and liberty they denied the due obedience to Ethnic Princes and Magistrates. 7. It is more correctly taken in a general sense concerning any detractions and calumnies with which Christians were indiscriminately burdened by Gentiles and Jews not yet converted, many of which Tertullian, Justin, and from them Eusebius book 4, chapter 7, recount.

Q. 6. What is understood by the Apostle by the day of visitation? Resp. 1. Bede by the day of visitation understands the day of the final judgment, in which the impious, having seen the glory of the just, will acknowledge the justice of GOD even against their will. In the time, he says, of retribution, let the incredulous acknowledge even now how great a glory is to be given to you by GOD, when they shall have perceived you instantly following Him amidst opposing dangers. Sap. 5. v. 3. & following. To this some refer the passage 1. Pet. 5. v. 6. Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in the time of visitation. But there the name έπισκοπῆς. is not held in the Greek. But the context shows that it is a matter of the visitation which happens in this life, for the Apostle says, observing you from your good works. 2. Some take it concerning the visitation through the cross and calamities, in which sense this little word is accepted here and there in the Prophets. Esai. 10. v. 3. What will you do in the day of visitation and calamity? Ierem. 6. v. 15. in the time of their visitation they shall fall. Ezech. 9. v. 1. the visitations of the city have approached. Os. 9. v. 7. The days of visitation have come, the days of retribution have come. This visitation can, however, be referred either to the detractors themselves, in the sense that God through the cross leads them to the acknowledgment of sin, so that they may no longer detract from the innocent; or to the Christians suffering calumnies beyond merit, in that sense, that the patience of the faithful, which shines forth in adversities, confounds all the calumnies of detractors. To this exposition can be referred what the Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] probation, because visitation through the cross is made for probation. 3. Some understand of the visitation of grace, which is made outwardly through the preaching of the word, inwardly through salutary conversion, in which sense the name of visitation is used Luc. 19. v. 44. to which can be referred those sayings of Scripture, in which visitation is taken for some peculiar bodily or spiritual benefit. Gen. 21. v. 1. cap. 50. v. 24. Exod. 3. v. 16. 1. Sam. 2. v. 21. Psal. 80. v. 15. Luc. 1. v. 68. & 78. cap. 7. v. 16. The sense therefore will be, when God will visit such detractors through grace & convert them to the faith of Christ, then their eyes closed in calumnies will be opened, so that they may acknowledge your innocence and glorify GOD. This exposition offers a useful observation, that the work of our conversion draws its origin from the visitation of divine grace, when GOD looks upon us with a fatherly eye and draws us to Himself. For unless GOD visited men out of grace, and looked upon them just as Christ once looked upon Peter with the benign illumination of His countenance, the good conversation of the faithful would never profit toward their conversion, since it is only an occasion, but not an adequate cause of conversion. 4. Oecumenius & Arias Montanus following him explain of the inquiry of those who spoke evil of Christians. For when an inquiry is made by them concerning the life of Christians, where things are found to be otherwise than was their suspicion, not only are they put to shame, but they are also corrected themselves, & GOD is glorified by them. This exposition can be proved from the preceding word ἐποπτέυσαντες, when persecutors & calumniators inquire more accurately about your deeds & words, & by this reason visit you, then they will acknowledge your innocence. 5. It is most simply taken of that divine visitation, by which GOD brings the innocence of the pious into the light in various ways, by moving the hearts of calumniators to a more accurate inquiry, by confounding the lies of informers, by giving grace & efficacy to the clear Apologies of the faithful, by bringing their good works into the light, by subjecting persecutors to punishments etc. Whence Luther rightly rendered, Wenns nun an den Tag kommen wird/ & noted in the margin: Neither virtue nor vice remain hidden forever. 1. Timoth. 5. vers. 25.

There is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hidden, that shall not be known.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. The pious are commanded to announce the virtues of GOD. But virtues in God do not seem to be able to have a place, since they do not even have a place in the blessed, inasmuch as in them no depraved concupiscence remains to be restrained. Resp. 1. The Scholastics say, that virtues are in God not formally, but eminently. Virtues in GOD are not habits added to the essence, but are essential attributes of GOD; nor are they occupied with moderating certain interior affections, but with exterior objects. 2. As regards virtues in the blessed, they distinguish between the material and the formal. Thomas 1. 2 q. 67. art. 1. There is in moral virtues something which is formal, and something which is material. The material in them is the inclination of the appetitive part toward passions or operations according to some mode. But because that mode is determined by reason, therefore the formal in all virtues is the very order of reason. As to the material, moral virtues will not remain, because there will be no concupiscence there to be restrained; as to the formal they will remain, in that the reason of each one will be most upright concerning those things which pertain to him according to that state, and the appetitive power will be moved entirely according to the order of reason. Bonav. 3. sent. dist. 33. Cardinal virtues will have other acts in the fatherland than on the way. Justice there excludes obliquity, prudence error, fortitude molestation, temperance all lust: on the way they fight against vices, in the fatherland they rejoice over the victory.

2. I beseech you, as strangers and pilgrims to abstain from fleshly desires. But the prodigal son was a pilgrim, and yet he did not abstain from fleshly concupiscences, Luc. 15. v. 13. Resp. 1. The Apostle treats of those who are pilgrims spiritually, i. e. who acknowledge that they are pilgrims and strangers in this world, whether they dwell in their native land or live elsewhere in other places. 2. The Apostle speaks of the right, what pilgrims ought to do, not of the fact, what they always do. Those who acknowledge themselves to be pilgrims and strangers in this life, they consider that through sin they have been reduced to this miserable condition, so that they are exiles from the heavenly kingdom; they acknowledge also that fleshly concupiscences lead them away from the way which leads us to the heavenly fatherland, and because they are carried with the whole desire of their heart to that heavenly fatherland, thence they do not have desires tenaciously fixed on earthly things. A pilgrim abstains from all things which can be an impediment to the journey:

The faithful man, therefore, considering himself a pilgrim on earth and striving toward the heavenly fatherland, abstains from fleshly lusts, which he knows to be not only an impediment to him on the way, but also a poison to his life.

3. The Apostle commands to abstain from fleshly lusts. But Paul Rom. 7. v. 14. complains that he is still carnal and sold under sin, and consequently that he is not entirely immune and free from depraved lusts in this life. Resp. To abstain from depraved lusts, is not to be entirely without them, to which perfection we cannot aspire in this life, but not to consent to them, nor to carry them out in deed, but to turn one's ears away from them as from the worst counselors, to mortify and crucify them. Gal. 5. v. 24. August. tract. 41. in Iohannem. The Apostle does not say, let there not be sin, but let it not reign in your body. As long as you live, it is necessary for sin to be in your members, at least let its reign be taken away from it. Bernh. serm. 6. de adventu Domini col. 12. I say to you, that kind of sin which so often disturbs us, I speak of lusts and evil desires, ought to be and can be repressed by the grace of GOD, so that it does not reign in us, but it is not cast out except in death.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Only the faithful are called a chosen race. It is false, therefore, what Huberus teaches, that all men, and thus even unbelievers, are elect.

2. GOD calls us out of darkness into his light. Therefore, whatever is outside the light of the word is mere gloom and darkness in spiritual matters. By what appearance, therefore, can a saving knowledge of GOD be ascribed to the more sound Heathens who are destitute of the light of the word?

3. Our calling is merely gratuitous, election is merely gratuitous, justification is merely gratuitous. It is false, therefore, that there is given a merit of congruity in calling and justification.

4. Faith is a marvelous light. Therefore it is knowledge. It is false, therefore, what Bellarminus argues in lib. 1. de Iustif. cap. 7. in fin. that faith is better defined by ignorance than by knowledge.

5. The Apostle exhorts the pious to abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. It is false, therefore, what the Calvinists maintain, that the regenerate cannot fall from the grace of GOD, for to what end would there be need for this exhortation?

6. The end of good works is not established as our merit before GOD, but that the mouth of slanderers may be stopped. It is false, therefore, what the Papists teach, that good works are to be done for that reason, so that we may merit an increase of grace and glory before the judgment of GOD.

Ἐκδίκηςις. 1. Salmero, intending to demonstrate that the Apostle does not speak here of election to eternal life, uses this argument, because GOD would not reveal that election for our benefit. Resp. 1. By this reasoning, in no saying of Scripture at all, which speaks of certain specific men, would there be any dealing with election to eternal life. What then will become of those most sweet sayings? John 15. v. 16. You have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and have appointed you, that you should go, and should bring forth fruit, and your fruit should remain. v. 19. Because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. Rom. 8. v. 38. I am sure that neither death, nor life, nor Angels, nor Principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come. vers. 39. nor might, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature shall be able to separate us from the love of GOD, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. Ephes. 1. v. 4. he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. 1. Thess. 5. v. 9. GOD hath not appointed us unto wrath, but unto the purchasing of salvation by Christ. 2. Thessal. 2. v. 13. We ought to give thanks to GOD always for you, brethren beloved of GOD, that GOD hath chosen you firstfruits unto salvation in sanctification of the Spirit, and faith of the truth. 2. The mystery of election is revealed in the Scriptures by the Holy Spirit in such a way that we may be warned that filial fear must be joined with the confidence of grace and salvation, lest carnal security creep into our souls instead of the security of the Spirit. 1. Corinth. 10. v. 12. Phil. 2. v. 12. Bernh. serm. 3. in Psalmum. I wish you to be joyful, but not yet secure; rejoicing in the Spirit, but nevertheless still fearing, and guarding against relapse. 3. Lorinus in h. l. writes thus. Ambrose should be read, or rather Prosper 1. de voc. gent. cap. 3. & 5. in what way this passage agrees with the election of the predestined.

2. Cornelius à Lapide [interprets] the words of the Apostle, You are a chosen generation, thus παραφράξει: You, O individual believers, are a chosen generation, whom, namely, GOD has chosen for Himself, and who in turn have chosen GOD, by consenting to and cooperating with His election and calling, as Moses teaches Deut. 26. v. 17. & 18. Lorinus in h. l. The chosen one is said to choose, while he responds to the one choosing, and embraces the offered means of salvation, Deut. 26. v. 17. Resp. 1. The cause of eternal election is not given in men, but it is always and everywhere attributed to GOD alone. Indeed, an opposition is added John 15. v. 16. You have not chosen me, but I have chosen you. 2. Of temporal election and calling to the fellowship of the Church the cause likewise is nowhere attributed to men, but to Divine grace alone. 3. For man who is to be converted does not have natural powers by which he can consent to and cooperate with the divine election and calling, but for that he receives new and spiritual powers in conversion from GOD. 4. After his conversion he cooperates with GOD, namely with those new powers gifted by the Holy Spirit, concerning which συνεργεία the cited passage Deut. 26. v. 17. treats; for the Papists themselves admit that the fulfillment of the law, of which Moses speaks there, can only have a place in the reborn. 5. The same state after conversion is treated in Ios. 24. v. 15. Choose today whom you wish to serve, etc.

3. Salmero maintains, The Apostle rendered the words of Moses, You are a priestly kingdom, in this way, You are a royal priesthood, so that he might signify that the priesthood in the N. T. is more excellent than the kingdom. Peter, (he says) did not say, as Moses did, a priestly kingdom, for in that people the kingdom was the principal thing, to which a carnal priesthood succeeded for offering carnal sacrifices. But now the priesthood is spiritual, to which royal carnal power is added. Cornelius à Lapide on chapter 29 of Exodus, and on this place of Peter. Peter elegantly and prudently inverts the words of Moses, because, namely, in the Synagogue of the Jews the kingdom stood out above the priesthood, but in the Church of Christ the priesthood stands out above the kingdom, and the kingdom is referred to the priesthood, as the spiritual to the temporal. And afterwards. Caietanus, Catharinus, and Salmero say the priesthood of Christians is Royal, because it directs Kings, and commands them. For Pontiffs are spiritual Kings, and are set over Kings; because they direct their temporal power to a spiritual end. Resp. 1. Estius refutes this fiction on this place, writing thus. You are a royal priesthood. Taken from the words which GOD ordered to be said to the people, Exod. 19. and that according to the version of the LXX. where we have, with Jerome as interpreter, a priestly kingdom, for that which is in the Hebrew, a kingdom of priests. Whence vanishes the argument which some make from this place for the distinction which they think must be established between the old and new priesthood, saying that in the O. T. royal power was superior to the priestly, because it was said in Exodus, a priestly kingdom, but now the priesthood is prior and more important than royal power, because Peter, with the speech inverted, says a royal priesthood, as if there the priesthood were an accessory to the kingdom, but here the kingdom is an accessory to the priesthood, and this is the prerogative of the New Testament over the old. It vanishes, I say, this argument, because Peter uses the very words of Moses, which had been said to the ancient people, but he referred to them as they were held in the Greek version, which was in use by the faithful. Whether that distinction truly exists, however, and whether it should not rather be said with other most learned Theologians that even under the old law the Priesthood was prior to and more worthy than the Royal power, is not for this place to inquire. This passage, however, is to be compared with that which is said inApocal. 1. & 5.that GOD made us a kingdom & Priests, in Greek Kings & Priests, not without an allusion to the passage of Exodus. For also in Exodus the Chaldean version has, Kings Priests, not From which it appears that Blessed Peter also wishes to signify the same thing, namely that all Christians are Kings & Priests. 2. Lorinus comments on this passage thus. In Exodus there are the same Greek words, for which the Interpreter. You shall be to me a priestly kingdom. In Hebrew. A kingdom of Priests. In Chaldean. You shall be before me Kings Priests. Wherefore the annotation of Hugo and Thomas the Englishman seems superfluous, that a Royal Priesthood is said here to intimate the prerogative of the new Testament with respect to the old, since in the New the Priesthood excels the kingdom, as the Spirit does the body.
