Primaticcius followed, saying the same opinion that in the Old Testament the royal dignity was superior to the Priestly. And afterwards. I do not think there is a distinction, whether we say Royal Priesthood or kingdom of Priests, as Salmeron, Catharinus & Fevardentius nevertheless also wished; whatever it may be, whether in the old Testament the royal dignity was greater, which I by no means concede. For Peter, as he is accustomed, and other Apostles, used words from the edition of the LXX. 3. Priesthood is more excellent than the kingdom in spiritual matters; the kingdom is more excellent than the Priesthood in political matters.

4. The same Cornelius à Lapide applies the words of the Apostle to the Roman Pontiff. The priestly kingdom of the Church, he says, is seen primarily in Bishops & the Episcopacy &c. But most of all the same is seen in the supreme Pontiff & the Pontificate, whose highest and most ample power extends itself everywhere through the whole world, by which he also commands Kings, whence also Kings prostrate themselves as suppliants to him, and lay down their scepters, and he can deprive Kings who are rebellious to the Church of their kingdom, as he has often deprived them &c. Therefore let not heretics wonder if the Pontiff has royal purple, a diadem, a bodyguard, riches, honor, adoration, for he has a Royal Priesthood. Resp. The Apostle is not speaking of the Roman Pontiff alone, but of all the truly faithful; he calls them Kings & Priests, i.e. spiritual ones. Therefore from this Petrine passage in vain is sought the foundation of the Royal power, together with the Priestly power, to be joined in the Roman Pontiff.

5. The same Cornelius in this place applies it to the Mass-priests. The Church, he says, is the Royal Priesthood of Christ, etc., because its victim is royal, excellent, and divine, namely Christ, who on the altar of the cross offered himself as a royal sacrifice for us, and daily offers himself to God on the altar of the Eucharist through priests: and because the manner of offering is royal, both because it is performed not by slaughtering and butchering, as Aaron and the others used to do, but by the sublime and secret operation of the Holy Spirit, by consecrating and transubstantiating bread into the body of Christ: and because with a royal, liberal, munificent spirit, and with full love and worship, a royal gift is offered to God the King. Response: Peter does not speak specifically of Mass-priests, but generally of all truly pious and Christian people, whom he calls Kings and Priests, not because of any external sacrifice, but because they offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to GOD through Christ, as he himself explains verse 4.

6. The same Cornelius in this place applies it to Monks. Religion, he says, is a Royal Priesthood, because in it religious persons offer themselves entirely to GOD as spontaneous victims, indeed as burnt offerings; Thus Thomas 22. q. 186. art. 7. teaches that religious persons are burnt offerings, because they hand over all their things to God, namely wealth through the vow of poverty, the body through the vow of chastity, the will and judgment through the vow of obedience. Response: Peter does not treat of Monks, who were not even known by name in the Apostolic Church, but generally of all truly pious and Christian people, to all and each of whom he attributes this eulogy. Therefore, the sayings of the ancients, which Cornelius adduces, pertain to all the truly pious. Augustine, book 10 de Civ. Dei, chapter 6: Man himself, consecrated and devoted to the name of GOD, in so far as he dies to the world that he may live to GOD, is a sacrifice. Gregory, 9 moral. chapter 31: We indeed offer ourselves as a sacrifice to GOD, when we dedicate our life to divine worship.

7. From the fact that Peter says the pious have been called out of darkness into his marvelous light, the Calvinists gather that there is a twofold calling, efficacious and inefficacious, since only the pious are efficaciously called by God. Response: We do not deny the distinction between an efficacious and an inefficacious calling; meanwhile, we say that it must be rightly explained. The Calvinists attribute the cause, on account of which the calling is inefficacious among some, to the absolute decree of reprobation, when nevertheless it is to the own fault of men, to those refusing to give place to the divine calling, is to be attributed solely, Matth. 23. v. 36.Luc. 7. v. 30.2. Thess. 2. v. 10.

8. I object, because Peter calls depraved concupiscence carnal desires, some of the Papists gather, that it is not a sin, unless the consent of the will is added. Bellarm. lib. 5. de amiss. gratiae cap. 7. arg. 2. When the Apostle says Rom. 7. For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwelleth no good thing, he teaches quite openly that concupiscence in a justified man is not properly a sin, which can make one guilty. For he says that such an evil is not in himself, but in his flesh. However, it is agreed that the flesh is not capable of sin properly so called. I answer, by the name of flesh in this and similar sayings of Scripture is not understood the body, nor only the lower faculties of the soul, but the whole man, insofar as he is still constituted under the oldness of the flesh. The mind with the Apostle signifies the whole man, insofar as he is renewed. Therefore also the flesh denotes the whole man, insofar as he is not yet renewed. The Apostle attributes to the flesh φρόνημα Rom. 8. v. 6. νοῦν, Col. 2. v. 18. heresies and idolatry Gal. 5. v. 21. which certainly pertain to the higher faculties of the soul. Rightly therefore writes Salmero in h. l. The Apostle calls carnal desires, which are of the old man, even if they are most spiritual sins, such as anger, envy, heresy. Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. Understand carnal desires not only of gluttony and lust, but also of anger, envy, pride. For all these are works of the flesh i. e. of concupiscence, which resides not only in the flesh, but also in the soul and mind, as the Apostle teaches Gal. 5. vers. 19. Bellarmine himself d. l. In many places of divine Scripture without doubt by the flesh are understood all powers both lower and higher corrupted by sin. Whence also we see Gal. 5. heresies numbered among the works of the flesh. And so we do not deny, that the mind also was corrupted by sin lib. eiusd. cap. 15. §. It must be known. Augustine in all the books written directly against the Pelagians, when in almost every chapter he names concupiscence more often: he almost always takes the name of concupiscence for the vice of the lower part, which is rebellious to the higher. Furthermore, it must not be denied that a similar vice is found also in the higher part. For that part of the soul also is prone to covet honors, vain glory and other vanities, and even if we are unwilling, it sometimes brings forth such desires. Wherefore Blessed Paul in Epist. Gal. 5. when he had said, that the flesh lusts against the Spirit, immediately enumerating the works of the flesh, he not only named fornication drunkenness & other things of that kind, but also idolatry, heresies, enmities, etc., which St. Augustine diligently noted book 14 of The City of God, chapters 2, 3, and 4, where he demonstrates that flesh is sometimes taken for the whole man, such as he is without the grace of GOD after the fall of Adam, and that he is called carnal who lives according to himself, not according to GOD.

Observations. 1. The dignity of believers surpasses all the splendor of human titles. They are named Christians from Christ. Therefore, just as Christ is the Son of God, King and Priest, so they too are sons of God, Kings and Priests.

2. The pious are chosen out of the world John 15, v. 19. Therefore, let them not conform themselves to the world Rom. 12, v. 2. Justin in the Epistle to Diognetus: The soul indeed dwells in the body, yet it is not of the body, and Christians dwell in the world, yet they are not of the world. The invisible soul is placed in the visible body as in a garrison: and Christians are known to remain in the world, but their piety remains invisible.

3. The pious are a chosen race. Therefore, let them conduct themselves in a manner worthy of their divine race, and let them walk as children of God Eph. 5, v. 1. They are Kings. Therefore, let them rule over the desires of the flesh and vicious affections. They are Priests. Therefore, let them offer themselves through self-denial as a spiritual sacrifice to GOD. Rom. 12, v. 1. They are a holy nation. Therefore, let them cleanse themselves from all defilement of the flesh and Spirit 2 Cor. 7, v. 1. They are a people of acquisition. Therefore, let them be zealous for good works Tit. 2, v. 14.

4. In former times, a crown was placed upon the baptized, as a sign of the royal dignity conferred upon them through Baptism. Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 40: Embrace Baptism with honor, so that it may adorn you, and weave a crown of graces for your head, and protect you with a crown of delights. Chrysostom, homily to the baptized: Remember me when you feel the crown more splendid than the rays of the Sun upon your head. For the same purpose, they were also anointed with oil as a sign of the kingdom and spiritual Priesthood. Clement of Rome, book 3 of the Apostolic Constitutions, chapter 15: The Bishop shall anoint his head in Baptism, just as Kings and Priests were anointed before, not indeed that those who are now baptized are also ordained Priests, but that they are made by Christ Christians, a Royal Priesthood, a holy nation, the Church of GOD, the pillar and foundation of the present light, who were once not a people, but now are beloved and elect, upon whom His name has been invoked.

5. The truly pious are holy, because they have been called with a holy calling 2 Tim. 1, v. 9, they are sanctified through the word and Sacraments, they are sprinkled sanctified by the blood of Christ and the Holy Spirit, 1. Cor. 6. vers. 11. they are holy in this life imputatively and inchoatively; in the future life they will be holy consummatively. Heb. 12. v. 22. The head of the Church is Christ, Holy of holies, Dan. 9. v. 24. the ruler and governor is the Holy Spirit.

6. Christ bought the Church for Himself as a peculiar possession with His own blood Acts 20. v. 28. Rev. 5. v. 9. therefore let us live for Him, who died for us, that He might claim us as His own peculiar possession. 2. Cor. 5. v. 15. Oecumenius in this place beautifully distinguishes between κτίσμα & κτῆμα. All, he says, are God's κτὶσμα, creature, but κτῆμα, that is, a possession to Him alone, who through their good work have been deemed worthy of that thing.

7. The ineffable goodness of God shines forth from the fact that He has called us out of darkness into light. If God were to meet those seeking light studiously, it would be a great benefit, but it is far more excellent that He rescued us from the abyss of darkness, i.e., of blindness and ignorance.

8. A bright mirror and irrefutable document of gratuitous calling is proposed in the calling of the Gentiles to the fellowship of the Church. For no one can think that they merited this by their own works.

9. The darkness of ignorance, of sins, and of miseries, in which all men after the fall remain by Nature, leads them to eternal darkness: just as the light of the Gospel leads believers to eternal light.

10. The Gospel is an admirable light, absurd to reason, and one that makes the light of reason foolish in spiritual matters.

11. All the benefits of God have this goal proposed for themselves, that His virtues may be acknowledged and proclaimed, that is, that the glory of God may be propagated through us.

12. But because God has not honored us with mere words, but has heaped great benefits upon us, therefore we ought to glorify Him not only with our tongue, but with our whole life, and not only celebrate His virtues with words, but also express them with our very life. Lact. lib. 5. Instit. cap. 10. The most religious worship of God is to imitate Him.

13. The pious have been called to the light. Therefore let them walk as children of light, Eph. 5. v. 8. and let them cast off the works of darkness. Rom. 13. v. 12.

14. That they are the people of God, who were once not a people, is of mercy; that they are not the people of God, who were once a people, is of justice.

15. Those who have obtained mercy from GOD, and are beloved by GOD, they are also deservedly called and considered by us as most dear.

16. The Apostle beseeches the faithful, but does not compel them tyrannically. By his example, let the Ministers of the Church not lord it over the faith of their hearers, 2. Cor. 1. v. 24.

17. Just as the Israelites wandered through the desert before they arrived in the promised land of Canaan: So the pious must pass through the desert of this world, and must fight with various enemies.

18. Thence and therefore the desires of the flesh supplant us, because we remain still entangled in the world, nor do we aspire to the heavenly fatherland with the whole desire of our heart.

19. Every man is a stranger by being born, because he is compelled to migrate by dying. August. q. 91. in Levit. Whether on account of the soul, which God forbid that it should be thought to be from the earth, it could deservedly be said, I am a sojourner, or an inhabitant, or a stranger on the earth: or according to the whole man, because he was once a citizen of Paradise, where certainly he who was saying these things was not, or what is freer from all controversy, not every man can say this, but he to whom the eternal fatherland in the heavens is promised &c. Therefore let us call ourselves sojourners on earth, because we have found the heavenly fatherland, from whence we have received a pledge, and to which arriving we shall never migrate from thence. The same conc. 8. in, Psal. 118.

20. A pilgrim looks upon all things as foreign, thence he does not set his heart upon them; he esteems them as things not pertaining to himself, and passes by: thus the pious look upon all earthly things as foreign, therefore they use the world so that they do not abuse it. 1. Corinth. 7. v. 31. August. serm. 26. de verb. Apost. We use temporal things according to the necessity of our pilgrimage, but we do not fix our joys in them, lest we be undermined by their slipping away. We use this world as not using it, that we may come to Him who made this world, and remain in Him, enjoying His eternity. A pilgrim, content with food and clothing, attends to his journey, does not desire superfluous things, lays aside heavier burdens which can be a hindrance to him, strives uniquely toward the fatherland and the goal of his journey, patiently tolerates the labors of the journey, softens the inconveniences of lodgings with the hope of a better lot to follow in the fatherland, inflicts injury on no one, shows himself solicitous in all things, guards against dangers with the greatest zeal, prepares himself for the journey with shoes, clothes, and a staff: all these things can be adapted to spiritual pilgrims. Bernh. de nostro bene vivendi cap. 7. All things which are in this world are contrary to the servants of GOD, so that while they feel these adverse things, they may sigh for the heavenly kingdom with the greatest desire. He shines with great grace before GOD, who is contemptible to this world. For in truth it is necessary that those things which the world hates, should be loved by GOD. Holy men are pilgrims and strangers in this age, whence Peter is rebuked because he wished a tabernacle to be made on the mountain, because for the saints there is no tabernacle in this world, for whom there is a fatherland and home in heaven. Bede in h. l. This is accustomed to differ in this life between the elect and the reprobate, that the elect, now pilgrims and exiles, await a fatherland in the future, and are delighted by fleeting joys in the present so much the less, by how much they hope to receive joys without end in the future, and to reign eternally with Christ. But truly the reprobate have a fatherland here, for which alone they know how to gape with the desires of life, and therefore, after this life they will be relegated into perpetual exile, where, lacking all pleasures, they may suffer only adversities in torments.

21. The life of man upon earth is a warfare,Iob. 7. v. 1. not only with external enemies, but one must also fight with an internal and domestic enemy, namely with the depraved concupiscences of the flesh, which duel, since it is continuous and lasts until the very end of life, is by far the most dangerous. We fear bodily enemies, we cherish spiritual ones.

22. The desires of the flesh fight against the salvation of the soul. Therefore, those who indulge in carnal concupiscences fall away from the salvation of the soul. Bede in h. l. While the flesh is enervatedly subjugated to flattering concupiscences, now the army of vices is firmly armed against the soul.

23. No fight is harder than against the flesh, no victory more glorious than over the flesh. Tertull. lib. ad Martyr. cap. 3. The living GOD stands as the agonothete of the conflict and of the victories of his own: the Holy Spirit as Xystarches: Christ Jesus as Epistates: the crown, of eternity: the prize, the citizenship of angelic substances in the heavens: glory, for ages of ages.

24. First of all, account must be taken of a conscience and mind pure before GOD, and afterwards also of reputation and an honest conversation among men.

25. The pious are subject in this life not only to real injuries, but also to verbal ones, namely the calumnies of the impious. Those calumnies are more troublesome to the pious than stripes and chains.

26. The evil-speaking and sinister words of the impious ought to be for us stimuli to live well. He who has many observers of his life institutes the manner of his life more cautiously.

27. The best remedy and most firm shield against calumnies is innocence of life. The Apology of the pious is not in words, but in life. It goes ill with me, if my speech defends me rather than my life.

28. Truth pressed by calumnies at length emerges into the light, and by its rays attracts others to the love of itself. Justin, Apol. 2, records concerning himself, that when he was still a gentile, he thought it impossible that Christians could pursue those prodigious pleasures of which they were accused, who so constantly underwent death for Christ. Eusebius, lib. 2, Hist., cap. 9, reports, that the torturer of St. James the Apostle, having considered his charity and patience, was converted to the faith. Bede, lib. 1, Hist. Angl., cap. 7, is witness, that Alban, when he was a pagan, was made a Christian from the consideration of a certain cleric, living holily and religiously. That the Iberian peoples of Spain were converted to Christ by the obedience, patience, devotion, and virtue of a certain captive Christian, record Eusebius, lib. 10, cap. 10, and Rufinus, lib. 1, cap. 10. Truly, examples move more than words.

29. We must not labor primarily for our own sake, so that men may speak well of us, but that GOD may be glorified in us,Galat. 1. v. 24.

30. Not only for the sake of GOD, and for our own sakes, but also for the sake of our neighbor, we ought to strive for holiness of life and good works, so that by honest conversation we may stop the mouths of slanderers, and by our example provoke others to conversion and piety.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. An pronomenὑμεῖςinv. 9.sit collectivè, an distributivè accipiendum? Resp. non quidem pugnat cum fidei analogia, si distributivè accipiatur, quia singuli fideles sunt genus electum ac Regale Sacerdotium, interim textui magis congruit, si accipiatur collectivè de fidelibus in unum caetum collectis, sive de Ecclesia Christi, quae est congregario sanctorum, statim enim subiungitur. Vos estis gens sancta, populus acquisitionis,v. 9.ac qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem populus DEI,v. 10. ac praecedit v. 5.Vos ipsi tanquam lapides vivi super aedificamini domus spiritualis.

Q. 2. Quare populus Israëliticus vocetur regnum Sacerdotum vel Sacerdotale? Resp. 1. Quia regnum huius populi non fuit prophanum ex operibus & armis, sed sacrum ex Sacerdotibus, rebus sacris, & divinis constans. 2. Reges & Sacerdotes apud omnes populos summi, & prae caeteris honoratiores sunt. Significatur ergò, Israelitas à DEO ex omnibus gentibus electos ac selectos esse, ut sint prae omnibus populis praecipui, ipsique peculiariter consecrati. 3. Respectus simul habetur ad Christum, qui est verus ille Rex & Sacerdos, qui ex populo Iudaico secundùm promissionem DEI erat nasciturus. Fagius in cap. 19. Exodi. 4. Israëlitae non more aliarum gentium prophanarum Regibus primùm erant subditi, sed DEO Rege utebantur, ac pro libertate sua singuli instar Regum erant. Postea ex ipsorum caetu DEUS Reges & Sacerdotes eligebat, Sacerdotium ad tribum Levi, regnum ad tribum Iuda determinans.

Q. 3. Quare fideles dicantur Regale Sacerdotium, id est, Reges & Sacerdotes? Resp. Quare Sacerdotes dicantur, exposuit ipse Apostolus v. 5. Reges dicuntur 1. Quia imperant vitiosis suis affectibus, non permittunt peccato dominium in mortali suo corpore, sed carni & concupiscentiis eius dominantur. 2. Quia DEO per fidem & sanctum obsequium subditi sunt, DEO autem servire, regnare est. 3. Sunt membra Christi, Regis & Sacerdotis, proinde à capite, & in capite suo Christo meritò censentur etiam ipsi Reges & Sacerdotes. Didymus Alexandrinus in exposit. sup. 7. Canon. Epist. postquam ostendit, Christum esse Regem & Sacerdotem, subiungit. His itaque dispensatis necessarium erat dispersos ab eo, qui simul Rex & Sacerdos est, electum esse genus, & Regale simul atque, Sacerdotale, Patre siquidem eorum utrumque habente principatum, necesse est, eos tanquam ex Rege Regale, & tanquam ex Sacerdote Sacerdotale esse genus. 4. Christus per Spiritum sanctum in ipsis regnat, inquit Ambrosius in cap. 1. Apocal. & in ipsis peccatum, mundum, Diabolum vincit. 5. Sunt filii DEI, summi Regis, sunt fratres & cohaeredes Christi, qui est Rex Regum & Dominus dominantiumApoc. 19. 16. ac cum ipso aliquando in coelis dominabuntur. Matth. 19. 28.Luc. 22. 30.1. Cor. 6. 2.Apoc. 3. vers. 21.6. Unguntur ut Reges ad spirituale regnum, non oleo externo, sed Spiritu sancto, qui est oleum laetitiaePsal. 45. v. 8. Lactant. lib. 4. Instit. cap. 7. Erat Iudaeis praeceptum, ut sacrum conficerent unguentum, quo perungi possent ii, qui vocabantur ad Sacerdotium vel ad regnum. Et sicut nunc Romanis indumentum purpurae insigne est regiae dignitatis assumtae, sic illis unctio sacri unguenti nomen ac potestatem regiam conferebat.

Q. 4. An dictum Propheticum Petrus accipiat de conversis ex Iudaismo, an vero de conversis ex gentilismo? Resp. 1. Quidam volunt, praedictionem Prophetae ad solos Israelitas pertinere in gentibus dispersos: quibus Propheta post indictum repudium gratiam reconciliationis promittat, quam promissionem per vocationem ad Christi regnum Petrus nunc impletam doceat, ut sit sensus. Qui hactenus non fuistis Dei populus, quippe, qui veram & salutarem Dei rerumque devinarum notitiam non habuistis, ac gentium corruptelis impliciti fuistis, nunc estis Dei populus. Calvinus in h. l. Postquam Oseas DEI nomine repudium Iudaeis indixit, spem illis facit futurae reconciliationis, hoc Petrus impletum monet. Erant dispersi, corruptelis gentium impliciti, inde ratione prioris status vocantur non populus. Huic expositioni robur quaeri potest ex eo, quod Propheta incap. 1. v. 6. & 7.distinguat inter domum Israel & Iuda, ac posteacap. 2. v. 1.(vel ut alii distinguunt incap. 1. v. 10.) & C. 2. v. 22.hanc prophetiam subiungit, unde Origenes, Chrysostomus & alii Patres Graeci de spirituali decem tribuum reductione hunc locum interpretantur. 2. Quidam volunt, praedictionem Prophetae ad solos conversos ex gentilibus pertinere, ut colligitur ex loco paralleloDeut. 32. v. 21.& ex allegatione ApostolicaRom. 9. v. 25.ubi Paulus docet, à Deo ad Ecclesiae in N. T. consortium non solùm Iudaeos, sed etiam gentes vocatos esse. Ad illud, quòd Oseas videatur loqui de Israelitis, respondent ex Augustino lib. 18. de Civ. DEI cap. 28. ipse quoque populus gentium spiritualiter est in filiis Abrahae, ac per hoc rectè dicitur Israel. 3. Caietanus statuit, quae de populo gentili à Propheta praedicta, eadem Petrum suis verbis accommodare populo circumcisionis. Neque enim dicit Apostolus, Prophetam haec scripsisse de iis, quos alloquitur.

4. Quidam volunt Prophetiam Oseae in sensu literali ad Iudaeos, mystico ad gentiles pertinere, ac proinde, sicut Apostolus ea, quae in sensu literali de Iudaeis dicunturExod. 19.ad conversos ex gentibus accommodat, ita quoque hoc loco Prophetiam Oseae, quae in sensu literali de Iudaeis agit, in sensu mystico ad conversos ex gentibus accommodare. Monuimus superiùs, Petrum principaliter quidem ad conversos ex iudaeis hanc Epistolam scribere, interim tamen secundariò etiam ad conversos ex gentibus sermonem dirigere, nec novum vel insolitum in Scripturis, unam eandemque Prophetiam diversimodè accommodari. Quamvis enim conversis ex gentilibus hoc unice vel praecipuè convenire videatur, quòd sint à DEO vocati de tenebris in lucem admirabilem, Es. 42. v. 6cap. 49. v. 6.Luc 2. v. 32.Actor. 13. v. 47.Eph. 5. v. 8. tamen ad Iudaeos hoc ipsum etiam referri posse, manifestum est ex Esai. 9. v. 1.cap. 60. v. 1.Matth. 4. v. 16.Iohan. 1. vers. 5.

Q. 5. Quae sint illae detractiones & obtrectationes, quibus Christianos olim fuisse obnoxios, Apostolus hoc loco testatur? Resp. 1. Quidam illas detractiones accipiunt de calumnia, quâ Christiani dicebantur humanas carnes devorare, occasione sumta ex mysterio Eucharistiae, cuius calumniae meminerunt Iustinus Apol. 1. Eusebius lib. 5. Histor. cap. 1. & seqq. Oecumen. in comm. h. l. Infideles servi accusabant Dominos suos Christianos, quod Thyestaeas caenas praepararent. 2. Quidam accipiunt de calumniâ, quâ Christum vocabant Magum, & Christianos Magicas artes exercere mentiebantur. August. lib. 1. de cons. Evang. cap. 9. Christum proptere a sapientissimum fuisse putant, quia nescio, quae illicita noverat, quae non solùm disciplina Christiana, sed etiam ipsa terrenae Reipubl. administratio iure condemnat. lib. 18. de de C. D. cap. 53. Petrum à paganis Magum fuisse proclamatum memorat. Ioh. Hussus in comm. h. l. Imponebant pagani Christianis, quòd Magicam artem exercerent. 3. Quidam exponunt de calumnia, quâ Iohannes Evangelista Christi gesta supra veritatem magnificasse dicebatur. 4. Quidam de crimine infanticidii, quo Christiani à gentilibus praegravabantur. Ludov. Vives in comm. lib. 18. de Civ. Dei cap. 53. Infanticidia solita obiici Christianis, ostendit Tertullianus in Apologetico, qui id crimen falsissimum atque impudentissimum purgat, quanquam Cataphryges & Pepuziani, duo hominum genera haeresis cumprimis perditae ac desperatae, infantis tenellum corpus soliti erant per omnia membra compungere, ut sic expresso sanguine farina maceraretur, qua conficerent panem in Eucharistiae usum, ut August. ad Quodvult Deum &c. narrat. Simile quiddam Euchetae & Gnostici faciebant ad Daemones pellendos, ut legitur apud Michaëlem Psellum. Sed haec tàm sunt habita Christiana, quàm Magicae artes & Daemonum colendorum ritus. 5. Quidam de calumnia, quâ Christiani dicebantur in mysteriis & conventibus suis uti promiscua Venere, cuius meminit Iustinus Apol. 2. cui criminationi occasionem itidem praebuerant Gnostici, Simonis Magi discipuli, in conventiculis suis turpia & nefaria exercentes, teste Epiphanio in haeres. adv. Gnosticos. 6. Quidam accipiunt de calumniis, quibus obnoxii erant Christiani ex Iudaeis ad Christum conversi, ad quos principaliter haec Epistola scripta. Illi enim ob seditiones ab ipsorum maioribus contra Romanos saepius excitatas accusabantur, quòd religionis ac libertatis praetextu Principibus ac Magistratibus Ethnicis debitum denegent obsequium. 7. Rectiùs in genere accipitur de quibusvis obtrectationibus & calumniis, quibus Christiani promiscuè à gentilibus & Iudaeis nondum conversis onerabantur, quarum plurimas Tertullianus, Iustinus & ex illis Eusebius lib. 4. cap. 7. recensent.

Q. 6. Quid per diem visitationis ab Apostolo intelligatur? Resp. 1. Beda per diem visitationis intelligit diem extremi iudicii, in quo impii conspecta iustorum gloriâ DEI iustitiam vel inviti agnoscent. In tempore, inquit, retributionis quanta sit vobis gloria per DEUM donanda, iam nunc agnoscant increduli, cum vos instanter inter obstantia pericula illum sequi perspexerint.Sap. 5. v. 3. & seqq. Hûc quidam referunt locum1. Pet. 5. v. 6.Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei, ut vos exaltet in tempore visitationis. Sed ibi non habetur in Graeco nomenέπισκοπῆς. Sed contextus ostendit, agi de visitatione, quae fit in hac vita, dicit enim Apostolus, ex bonis operibus vos considerantes. 2. Quidam accipiunt de visitatione per crucem & calamitates, quo sensu haec vocula in Prophetis passim accipitur.Esai. 10. v. 3.Quid facietis in die visitationis & calamitatis?Ierem. 6. v. 15.in tempore visitationis suae corruent.Ezech. 9. v. 1.appropinquaverunt visitationes urbis.Os. 9. v. 7.Venerunt dies visitationis, venerunt dies retributionis, Potest autem haec visitatio referri vel ad ipsos obtrectatores, sensu eo, quòd Deus per crucem eos ad agnitionem peccati perducat, ut innocentibus non amplius detrahant; vel ad Christianos calumniis praeter meritum obnoxios, sensu eo, quòd patientia fidelium, quae in adversitatibus eluceseit, confundat omnes obtrectatorum calumnias. Ad hanc expositionem referri potest, quod Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]probationem, quia visitatio per crucem fit ad probationem. 3. Quidam intelligunt de visitatione gratiae, quae fit exterius per verbi praedicationem, interius per salutarem conversionem, quo sensu nomen visitationis usurpaturLuc. 19. v. 44.quò referri possunt dicta illa Scripturae, in quibus visitatio de peculiari quodam beneficio corporali vel spirituali accipitur.Gen. 21. v. 1.cap. 50. v. 24.Exod. 3. v. 16.1. Sam. 2. v. 21.Psal. 80. v. 15.Luc. 1. v. 68. & 78.cap. 7. v. 16. Sensus igitur erit, cùm Deus obtrectatores eiusmodi per gratiam visitabit & ad Christi fidem convertet, tunc aperientur ipsorum oculi in calumniis clausi, ut innocentiam vestram agnoscant ac DEUM glorificent. Praebet haec expositio utilem observationem, quòd conversionis nostrae opus à visitatione divinae gratiae originem trahat, cum DEUS paterno oculo nos respicit & ad se trahit. Nisi enim DEUS ex gratia homines visitaret, eosque sicut olim Christus Petrum benigna vultus sui illuminatione respiceret, nunquam bona fidelium conversatio ad ipsorum conversionem proficeret, cum ea duntaxat sit occasio, non autem causa adaequata conversionis. 4. Oecumenius & eum secutus Arias Montanus exponunt de inquisitione eorum, qui de Christianis malè loquebantur. Cum enim fit ab illis inquisitio de vitae Christianorum, ubi res contrario modo se habere reperiuntur, quàm fuerit eorum suspicio, non solùm pudefiunt, sed etiam ipsi corriguntur, & DEUS ab ipsis glorificatur. Haec expositio probari potest ex verbo praecedente ἐποπτέυσαντες, quando persecutores & calumniatores de vestris factis & dictis accuratiùs inquirunt, & hac ratione vos visitant, tunc inno centiam vestram agnoscent. 5. Simplicissimè accipitur de visitatione illa divinâ, quâ DEUS piorum inno centiam variis modis in lucem producit, corda calumniatorum ad accuratiorem inquisitionem movendo, mendacia delatorum confundendo, luculentis fidelium Apologiis gratiam & efficaciam dando, bona eorum opera in lucem producendo, persecutores poenis subiiciendo &c. Unde Lutherus rectè reddidit, Wenns nun an den Tag kommen wird/ & in margine annotavit: Nec virtus nec vitium perpetuo manent occulta.1. Timoth. 5. vers. 25.

nihil est opertum, quod non reveletur; & occultum, quod non sciatur.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Pii iubentur annunciare virtutes DEI. Atqui virtutes in Deo non videntur habere posse locum, cum ne quidem in beatis locum Habeant, quippe in quibus nulla concupiscentia prava refrenanda adhuc superest. Resp. 1. Scholastici dicunt, in Deo virtutes esse non formaliter, sed eminenter. Virtutes in DEO non sunt habitus essentiae superadditi, sed sunt essentialia DEI attributa; nec occupantur circa affectus quosdam interiores moderandos, sed circa obiecta exteriora. 2. Quod attinet virtutes in beatis, distinguunt inter materiale, & formale. Thomas 1. 2 q. 67. art. 1. Est in virtutibus moralibus aliquid q. formale, & aliquid q. materiale. Materiale in illis est inclinatio partis appetitivae ad passiones vel operationes secundùm modum aliquem. Sed quia modus iste determinatur à ratione, ideò formale in omnibus virtutibus est ipse ordo rationis. Quantum ad materiale, non manebunt virtutes morales, quia non erit ibi concupiscentia refrenanda; quantum ad formale manebunt, in quantum ratio uniuscuiusque rectissima erit circa ea, quae ad ipsum pertinent secundùm statum illum, & vis appetitiva omninò movebitur secundùm ordinem rationis. Bonav. 3. sent. dist. 33. Virtutes cardinales habebunt alios actus in patria, quàm in via. Iustitia ibi excludit obliquitatem, prudentia errorem, fortitudo molestiam, temperantia omnem libidinem: in via pugnant contra vitia, in patria gaudent de victoria.

2. Obsecro vos, tanquam advenas & peregrinos abstinere à carnalibus desideriis. At filius prodigus fuit peregrinus, nec tamen à carnalibus concupiscentiis abstinuit,Luc. 15. v. 13. Resp. 1. Apostolus agit de peregrinis spiritualiter talibus, i. e. qui agnoscunt, se esse peregrinos & advenas in hoc mundo, sive in patria terra degant, sive extra eam alibi locorum vivant. 2. Apostolus loquitur de iure, quid peregrini facere debeant, non de facto, quid semper faciant. Qui se in hac vita peregrinos & advenas esse agnoscunt, illi expendunt, quòd per peccatum in hanc miseram conditionem sint redacti, ut sint à regno coelesti extorres; agnoscunt etiam, quòd carnales concupiscentiae ipsos abducant à via, quae in patriam coelestem nos deducit, ac quia toto cordis desiderio feruntur ad coelestem illam patriam, inde non habent desideria rebus terrenis tenaciter affixa. Peregrinus abstinet ab omnibus, quae itineri possunt esse impedimento:

fidelis ergò peregrinum in terra se aestimans, & ad coelestem patriam contendens abstinet à carnalibus concupiscentiis, quas scit, sibi non tantum impedimento esse ad viam, sed etiam veneno ad vitam.

3. Apostolus iubet abstinere à carnalibus concupiscentiis. At Paulus Rom. 7. v. 14. conqueritur, se adhuc carnalem esse, & sub peccato venundatum, ac proinde à pravis concupiscentiis in hac vita non esse penitus immunem ac liberum. Resp. abstinere à pravis concupiscentiis, non est prorsus illis carere, ad quam perfectionem in hac vita aspirare non possumus, sed in eas non consentire, nec opere illas exsequi, sed ab illis velut pessimis consultoribus aures avertere, eas mortificare & crucifigere. Gal. 5. v. 24. August. tract. 41. in Iohannem. Non dicit Apostolus, non sit, sed non regnet peccatum in corpore vestro. Quamdiu vivis, peccatum necesse est esse in membris tuis, saltem illi regnum auferatur. Bernh. serm. 6. de adventu Domini col. 12.Dico vobis, genus illud peccati, quod toties conturbat nos, concupiscentias loquor & desideria mala, reprimi quidem debet & potest per gratiam DEI, ut non regnet in nobis, sed non eiicitur, nisi in morte.

Ἐλεγχος. 1. Soli fideles dicuntur genus electum. Falsum igitur est, quod Huberus docet, omnes homines, adeoque etiam incredulos esse electos.

2. DEUS vocat nos de tenebris ad lumen. Ergò quicquid est extra verbi lucem, in spiritualibus est mera caligo ac tenebrae. Quâ igitur specie sanioribus Ethnicis luce verbi destitutis, salvifica DEI cognitio adscribi potest?

3. Vocatio nostra est merè gratuita, electio merè gratuita, iustificatio merè gratuita. Falsum ergò est, dari meritum congrui in vocatione & iustificatione.

4. Fides est lumen admirabile. Ergò est notitia. Falsum igitur, quod Bellarminus disputat lib. 1. de Iustif. cap. 7. in fin. Fidem meliùs definiri per ignorantiam, quàm per notitiam.

5. Hortatur Apostolus pios, ut abstineant à carnalibus concupiscentiis, quae militant adversus animam. Falsum ergò est, quod Calviniani statuunt, renatos non posse excidere gratiâ DEI, quorsum enim opus foret hac exhortatione?

6. Finis bonorum operum non statuitur nostrum coram DEO meritum, sed ut calumniatoribus os obstruatur. Falsum igitur, quod Pontificii docent, ideò facienda esse bona opera, ut augmentum gratiae & gloriae coram DEI iudicio mereamur.

Ἐκδίκηςις. 1. Salmero demonstraturus, Apostolum hîc non, loqui de electione ad vitam aeternam, utitur hoc argumento, quia non detegeret DEUS illam electionem propter nostram utilitatem. Resp. 1. hac ratione in nullo omninò Scripturae dicto, quod de certis quibusdam hominibus loquitur, de electione ad vitam aeternam ageretur. Quid ergò fiet suavissimis illis dictis? Iohan. 15. v. 16.Non me elegistis, sed ego elegi vos, & posui vos, ut eatis, ut fructum afferatis, & fructus vester maneat.v. 19.Quia de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus.Rom. 8. v. 38.Certus sum, quòd neque mors, neque vita, neque, Angeli, neque, Principatus, neque, virtutes, neque, instantia, neque, futura.vers. 39.neque, fortitudo, neque, altitudo, neque, profundum, neque, creatura alia poterit nos separare à caritate DEI, quae est in Christo Iesu Domino nostro.Ephes. 1. v. 4.elegit nos in Christo ante iacta mundi fundamenta.1. Thess. 5. v. 9.non posuit nos DEUS ad iram, sed ad acquisitionem salutis per Christum.2. Thessal. 2. v. 13.Nos debemus DEO gratias agere semper pro vobis, fratres dilecti à DEO, quòd elegerit vos DEUS primitias in salutem in sanctificatione Spiritus, & fide veritatis. 2. Mysterium electionis in Scripturis eo modo à Spiritu sancto revelatum, ut moneamur, cum fiducia gratiae & salutis coniunctum esse debere timorem filialem, ne pro securitate Spiritus securitas carnalis animis nostris obrepat.1. Corinth. 10. v. 12.Phil. 2. v. 12. Bernh. serm. 3. in Psalmum. Qui habitat. Laetos vos esse volo, sed nondum securos; gaudentes in Spiritu, sed tamen paventes adhuc, & caventes à recidiva. 3. Lorinus in h. l. sic scribit. Legendus Ambrosius, vel potiùs Prosper 1. de voc. gent. cap. 3. & 5. quo pacto hîc locus electioni congruat praedestinatorum.

2. Cornelius à Lapide verba Apostoli, Vos estis genus electum, sic παραφράξει:Vos, ô singuli fideles, estis genus electum, quos sc. DEUS sibi elegit, & qui vicissim DEUM elegistis, electioni & vocationi eius consentiendo & cooperando, uti docet Moses Deut. 26. v. 17. & 18. Lorinus in h. l. Electus dicitur eligere, dum eligenti respondet, & oblata salutis media amplectitur,Deut. 26. v. 17. Resp. 1. Electionis aeternae causa non datur in hominibus, sed ea soli DEO semper & ubique tribuitur. Quinimò additur oppositio Ioh. 15. v. 16.Non vos me elegistis, sed ego elegivos. 2. Electionis temporalis ac vocationis ad Ecclesiae confortium causa itidem nuspiam tribuitur hominibus, sed soli Divinae gratiae. 3. Homo enim convertendus non habet vires naturales, quibus electioni & vocationi divinae consentire & cooperari possit, sed ad id novas ac spirituales vires in conversione à DEO accipit. 4. Post sui conversionem cooperatur DEO, videlicet novis illis & à Spiritu sancto donatis viribus, de qua συνεργεία agit adductus locus Deut. 26. v. 17. fatentur enim ipsimet Pontificii, impletionem legis, de qua Mose ibi loquitur, non nisi in renatis locum habere posse. 5. De eodem statu post conversionem agitur Ios. 24. v. 15.Eligite hodiè, cui servire velitis &c.

3. Salmero statuit, Apostolum verba Mosis, Vos estis regnum Sacerdotale, propterea sic reddidisse, Vos estis regale Sacerdotium, ut significaret, Sacerdotium in N. T. esse regno praestantius. Petrus (inquit) non dixit, sicut Moses, regnum Sacerdotale, nam in populo illo principale erat regnum, cui succedebat carnale Sacerdotium ad offerendas hostias carnales. Nunc vero spirituale est Sacerdotium, cui regia carnalis potestas accedit. Cornelius à Lapide in cap. 29. Exodi, & in h. l. Petri. Petrus verba Mosis eleganter & prudenter invertit, quia sc. in Synagoga Iudaeorum regnum eminebat Sacerdotio, in Ecclesia vero Christi Sacerdotium eminet regno, & regnum refertur ad Sacerdotium, q. spirituale ad temporale. Et postea. Caietanus, Catharinus, & Salmero Christianorum Sacerdotium dicunt esse Regale, quia Reges dirigit, iisque, imperat. Pontifices enim esse Reges spirituales, ac Regibus praeesse; quia eorum potestatem temporalem dirigunt ad finem spiritualem. Resp. 1. Commentum hoc refellit Estius in h. l. sic scribens. Vos estis regale Sacerdotium. Sumtum ex verbis, quae DEUS iussit ad populum dici,Exod. 19.idque iuxta versionem LXX. ubi nos habemus, Interprete Hieronymo, regnum Sacerdotale, pro eo, quod in Hebraeo est, regnum Sacerdotum. Unde evanescit argumentum, quod ex hoc loco faciunt nonnulli pro discrimine, quod statuendum putant inter Sacerdotium vetus & novum, dicentes, in V. T. regiam potestatem fuisse Sacerdotali superiorem, quia dictum sit in Exodo, regnum Sacerdotale, nunc autem Sacerdotium Regali potestate esse prius ac potius, quia Petrus sermone converso dicat Sacerdotium regale, tanquam illic Sacerdotium fuerit accessorium regno, hîc autem regnum sit accessorium Sacerdotio, atque hanc esse praerogativam Novi Testamenti prae veteri. Evanescit, inquam, hoc argumentum, quia Petrus ipsa Mosis verba, quae ad veterem populum dicta fuerunt, referre voluit, sed retulit ut habebantur in versione Graeca, quae erat in usu fidelium. An autem verè consistat illud discrimen, ac non potiùs cum aliis doctissimis Theologis dicendum sit, etiam sub lege veteri Sacerdotium fuisse Regali potestate prius ac dignius, non huius est est loci disquirere. Conferendus est autem hic locus cum eo, quodApocal. 1. & 5.dicitur DEUS nos fecisse regnum & Sacerdotes, Graecè Reges & Sacerdotes, non sine allusione ad locum Exodi. Nam & in Exodo Chaldaea versio habet, Reges Sacerdotes, non Ex quibus apparet, etiam B. Petrum idipsum velle significare, scilicet omnes Christianos esse Reges & Sacerdotes. 2. Lorinus in h. l. sic commentatur. In Exodo sunt eadem vocabula Graeca, pro quibus Interpres. Eritis mihi in regnum Sacerdotale. Hebraicè. Regnum Sacerdotum. Chaldaicè. Eritis coram me Reges Sacerdotes. Quocirca superflua videtur annotatio Hugonis & Thomae Anglici, Regale Sacerdotium hîc dici ad innuendam praerogativam novi Testamenti respectu veterus, quoniam in Novo Sacerdotium praemineat regno, sicut Spiritus corpori. Secutus est Primaticcius, eandem sententiam dicens in Vet. Test. regalem dignitatem Sacerdotali superiorem fuisse. Et postea. Non arbitror, discrimen esse, seu Regale Sacerdotium seu regnum Sacerdotale dicamus, ut voluit tamen etiam Salmeron, Catharinus & Fevardentius; quicquid sit, an in vetere Testamento maior esset regia dignitas, quod minimè concedo. Nam Petrus, ut solet ipse, aliique Apostoli, verbis usus est ex editione LXX. 3. Sacerdotium in spiritualibus praestantius regno; regnum in politicis praestantius Sacerdotio.

4. Idem Cornelius à Lapide applicat verba Apostoli ad Pontificem Romanum. Sacerdotale regnum Ecclesiae, inquit, inprimis cernitur in Episcopis & Episcopatu &c. Maximè vero idipsum cernitur in summo Pontifice & Pontificatu, cuius summa & amplissima quaqua versum est potestas per totum orbem sese extenens, quâ etiam Regibus imperat, unde & Reges se ei supplices prosternunt, suaque sceptra substernunt, ac Regès Ecclesiae rebelles regno privare potest, uti saepe privavit &c. Non ergò mirentur haeretici, si Pontifex regalem, habeat purpuram, diadema, satellitium, opes, honorem, adorationem, habet enim Regale Sacerdotium. Resp. Apostolus non liquitur de solo Pontifice Romano, sed de omnibus verè fidelibus; illos vocat Reges & Sacerdotes, sc. spirituales. Ergò ex hoc loco Petrino frustra quaeritur fundamentum Regalis potestatis unà cum Sacerdotali in Pontifice Romano coniungendae.

5. Idem Cornelius h. l. applicat ad sacrificulos Missaticos. Ecclesia, inquit, est Christi Sacerdotium Regale &c. quia victima eius est regalis, eximia & divina, puta Christus, qui in ara crucis q. regalem hostiam pro nobis obtulit se, atque indies in altari Eucharistiae per Sacerdotes se offert Deo: & quia modus offerendi est regalis, tùm quia non mactando & laniendo, uti faciebat Aaron & caeteri, sed sublimi & arcana operatione Spiritus sancti, consecrando & transsubstantiando panem in corpus Christi, peragitur: tùm quia regali, liberali, munifico animo, plenoque amore & cultu q. regium donum Regi Dea offertur. Resp. Petrus non loquitur in specie de sacrificulis Missaticis, sed in genre de omnibus verè piis & Christianis, quos vocat Reges & Sacerdotes, non propter externum aliquod sacrificium, sed quia spirituales victimas per Christum DEO acceptas offerunt, uti ipse exponit vers. 4.

6. Idem Cornelius h. l. applicat ad Monachos. Religion, inquit, est Regale Sacerdotium, quia in ea Religiosi se totos q. victimas spontaneas, imo q. holocausta DEO offerunt; Sic Thomas 22. q. 186. art. 7. docet, Religiosos esse holocausta, quia omnia sua Deo tradunt, nimirum opes per votum paupertatis, corpus per votum castitatis, voluntatem & iudicium per votum obedientiae. Resp. Petrus non agit de Monachis, qui in Ecclesia Apostolica ne nomine quidem noti fuêre, sed in genere de omnibus verè piis & Christianis, quibus omnibus ac singulis hoc elogium tribuit. Proinde ad omnes verè pios pertinent dicta veterum, quae Cornelius adducit. August. lib. 10. de Civ. Dei cap 6. Ipse homo DEI nomini consecratus ac devotus, in quantum mundo moritur, ut DEO vivat, sacrificium est. Gregor. 9. moral. cap. 31. Nos quippe ipsos sacrificium DEO offerimus, cum vitam nostram divino cultui dedicamus.

7. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, pios vocatos esse de tenebris ad lumen admirabile, Calviniani colligunt, duplicem esse vocationem, efficacem & inefficacem, cum soli pii efficaciter à Deo vocentur. Resp. discrimen inter vocationem efficacem & inefficacem non negamus, interim illud rectè explicandum dicimus. Causam, propter quam vocatio apud quosdam sit inefficax, Calviniani tribuunt absoluto decreto reprobationis, cum tamen propriae hominum culpae, vocationi divinae locum dare renuentium, unicè sit tribuenda, Matth. 23. v. 36.Luc. 7. v. 30.2. Thess. 2. v. 10.

8. Exeo, quòd Petrus pravam concupiscentiam vocat desideria carnalia, quidam ex Pontificiis colligunt, eam non esse peccatum, nisi accedat voluntatis consensus. Bellarm. lib. 5. de amiss. gratiae cap. 7. arg. 2. Quando Apostolus dicitRom. 7.Scio enim quia non habitat in me, id est, in carne mea bonum, satis apertè docet, concupiscentiam in homine iustificato non esse propriè peccatum, quod reum facere possit. Dicit enim huiusmodi malum non esse in se, sed in carne sua. Constat autem carnem non esse capacem peccati propriè dicti. Resp. carnis nomine in hoc & similibus Scripturae dictis non intelligitur corpus, nec inferiores tantùm animae facultates, sed totus homo, quatenus sub carnis vetustate adhuc constitutus est. Mens apud Apostolum significat totum hominem, quatenus est renovatus. Ergò & caro notat totum hominem, quatenus nondum est renovatus. Carni tribuit Apostolus φρόνημαRom. 8. v. 6.νοῦν,Col. 2. v. 18. haereses & idololatriam Gal. 5. v. 21. quae ceretè ad superiores animae facultates pertinent. Rectè ergò scribit Salmero in h. l. Apostolus vocat carnalia desideria, quae sunt veteris hominis, etiamsi maximè spiritualia sint peccata, ut iram, invidiam, haeresin. Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. Carnalia desideria intellige non tantùm, gulae & libidinis, sed & irae, invidiae, superbiae. Haec enim omnia sunt opera carnis i. e. concupiscentiae, quae non tantùm in carne, sed & in anima ac mente residet, uti docet ApostolusGal. 5. vers. 19.Bellarminus ipse d. l. In multis locis divinae Scripturae sine dubio per carnem intelliguntur omnes potentiae tùm inferiores, tùm superiores per peccatum corruptae. Unde etiam videmusGal. 5.inter opera carnis haereses numerari. Itaque non negamus, etiam mentem per peccatum fuisse corruptam lib. eiusd.cap. 15.§. Sciendum. Augustinus in omnibus libris contra Pelagianos directè scriptis, cum in singulis ferè capitibus concupiscentiam saepius nominet: semper ferè pro vitio partis inferioris, quae rebellis est superiori, concupiscentiae nomen accipit. Caeterùm negandum non est, etiam in parte superiore simile vitium inveniri. Nam ea quoque animae pars propria est ad concupiscendos honores, inanem gloriam & alias vanitates, & etiamsi nolimus, interdum parit eiusmodi desideria. Quocirca B. Paulus in Epist. Gal. 5.cùm dixisset, carnem concupiscere adversus Spiritum, statim enumerans opera carnis, non solùm nominavit fornicationem ebrietatem & alia id genus, sed etiam idololatriam, haereses, inimicitias &c. quod diligenter notavit S. Augustinus lib. 14. de Civ. Dei cap. 2. 3. & 4. ubi demonstrat, carnem interdum accipi pro toto homine, qualis est sine gratiae DEI post lapsum Adami, & eum dici carnalem, qui secundùm seipsum, non secundùm DEUM vivit.

Observationes. 1. Dignitas credentium superat omnem humanorum titulorum splendorem. Denominantur à Christo Christiani. Ergô ut Christus Dei filius, Rex & Sacerdos, ita ipsi quoque sunt Dei filii, Reges & Sacerdotes.

2. Pii sunt electi de mundo Ioh. 15. v. 19. Ergò non conforment sese mundo. Rom. 12. v. 2. Iustinus in Epist ad Diognet. Habitat quidem anima in corpore, non est tamen de corpore, & Christiani in mundo habitant, non sunt tamen de mundo. Inaspectabilis anima in corpore aspectabili tanquam in praesidio collocata est: & Christiani in mundo manere cognoscuntur, sed eorum pietas manet inaspectabilis.

3. Pii sunt genus electum. Ergò divino genere sese dignos gerant, & ut filii Dei ambulent. Eph. 5. v. 1. Sunt Reges. Ergò concupiscentiis carnis & vitiosis affectibus imperent. Sunt Sacerdotes. Ergò seipsos per abnegationem sui in sacrificium spirituale DEO offerant.Rom. 12. v. 1. Sunt gens sancta. Ergò mundent se ab omni inquinamento carnis & Spiritus 2. Cor. 7. v. 1. Sunt populus acquisitionis. Ergò sint Zelotae in bonis operibusTit 2. v. 14.

4. Baptizatis olim corona fuit imposita, in signum regiae dignitatis per Baptismum ipsis collatae. Gregor. Nazianz. Orat. 40. Baptismum honore complectere, ut te ornet, capitique tuo gratiarum coronam nectat & coronâ delitiarum te protegat. Chrysost. homil. ad babtiz. Mementote mei, quando coronam Solis raediis splendidiorem sentietis in capite. Eodem fine etiam unguento delibuti fuêre in signum regni & Sacerdotii spiritualis. Clemens Romanus lib. 3. Constit. Apost. cap. 15. Episcopus in Baptismo caput eius unget, sicut priùs ungebantur Reges & Sacerdotes, non quidem quodqui nunc babtizantur, etiam Sacerdotes ordinentur, sed quòd fiant à Christo Christiani, Regale Sacerdotium, gens sancta, Ecclesia DEI, columna & firmamentum praesentis luminis, qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem dilecti & electi, super quos invocatum est nomen eius.

5. Verè pii sunt sancti, quia vocati sunt santâ vocatione2. Tim. 1. v. 9. sunt per verbum & Sacramenta sanctificati, sunt aspersi sanguine Christi, & Spiritu sancto santificati, 1. Cor. 6. vers. 11. sancti sunt in hac vita imputativè & inchoativè in futura vita sancti erunt consummativè. Heb. 12. v. 22. Ecclesiae caput est Christus, Sanctus sanctorum,Dan. 9. v. 24. rector & gubernator Spiritus sanctus.

6. Christus suo sanguine Ecclesiam sibi in peculium emit Actor. 20. v. 28.Apoc. 5. v. 9. illi ergò vivamus, qui pro nobis mortuus est, ut nos in peculium suum assereret. 2. Cor. 5. v. 15. Oecumenius in h. l. pulcrè distinguit inter κτίσμα & κτῆμα.Omnes, inquit, sunt DEIκτὶσμα,creatura, sedκτῆμα,id est, possessio illi soli, qui per bonam suam operationem dignati eâ re fuerint.

7. Ineffabilis Dei bonitas ex eo elucet, quòd nos vocaverit è tenebris ad lucem. Si Deus studiosè quaerentibus lumen occurreret, magnum esset beneficium, sed longè excellentius, quod ex abysso tenebrarum, i. e. caecitatis & ignorantiae nos eruit.

8. Gratuitae vocationis illustre speculum, & irrefragabile documentum proponitur in vocatione gentium ad Ecclesiae consortium. Nemo enim cogitare potest, illos suis operibus hoc esse promeritos.

9. Tenebrae ignorantiae, peccatorum & miseriarum, in quibus post lapsum omnes homines per Naturam haerent, ducunt eos ad tenebras aeternas: sicut lumen Evangelii credentes ducit ad lucem aeternam.

10. Evangelium est lumen admirabile, rationi absurdum, & lumen rationis in spiritualibus infatuans.

11. Omnia Dei beneficia hunc sibi propositum habent scopum, ut virtutes eius agnoscantur ac praedicentur, h. e. ut gloria Dei per nos propagetur.

12. Quia autem, Deus non nudis verbis nos honoravit, sed magnis beneficiis cumulavit, ideò non solâ linguâ, sed totâ vitâ nostrâ ipsum glorificare debemus, ac virtutes eius non solùm verbis celebrare, sed etiam vitâ ipsâ exprimere. Lact. lib. 5. Instit. cap. 10. Religiosissimus Dei cultus est imitari.

13. Pii vocati sunt ad lumen. Ergò ambulent, ut filii lucis,Eph. 5. v. 8.opera autem tenebrarum abiiciant,Rom. 13. v. 12.

14. Quòd sint populus Dei, qui aliquando non populus, misericordiae est; quòd non sint populus Dei, qui aliquando populus, iustitiae est.

15. Qui apud DEUM misericordiam consecuti, & à DEO dilecti, illi etiam à nobis meritò dicuntur & censentur carissimi.

16. Apostolus fideles obsecrat, non autem Tyrannicè cogit. Eius exemplo Ministri Ecclesiae non dominentur fidei auditorum suorum, 2. Cor. 1. v. 24.

17. Sicut Israëlitae peregrinabantur per desertum, antequam in promissam terram Canaan pervenirent: Sic piis per desertum huius mundi transeundum, cumque variis hostibus pugnandum.

18. Inde atque ideò carnis desideria nos supplantant, quia, mundo adhuc impliciti haeremus, nec ad patriam coelestem toto cordis desiderio aspiramus.

19. Omnis homo advena est nascendo, quia compellitur migrare moriendo. August. q. 91. in Levit. Sive propter animam, quae absit, ut putetur ex terra, meritò dici potuerit inquilinus, vel incola, vel advena ego sum in terra: sive secundùm totum hominem, quia Paradisi aliquando civis fuit, ubi utique, non erat, qui ista dicebat, sive quod est ab omni controversia liberius, non omnis homo possit hoc dicere, sed cui patria promissa est aeterna in coelis &c. Ideò ergò nos in terra inquilinos dicamus, quia supernam patriam, unde pignus accepimus, & quò pervenientes nunquam inde migremus, invenimus. Idem conc. 8. in, Psal. 118.

20. Peregrinus omnia q. aliena intuetur, inde eis cor non apponit; q. sed ad se non pertinentia aestimat, ac pertransit: sic pii omnia terrena aspiciunt ut aliena, proinde mundo sic utuntur, ut non abutantur. 1. Corinth. 7. v. 31. August. serm. 26. de verb. Apost. Utimur temporalibus secundùm peregrinationis nostrae necessitatem, sed non in eis gaudia nostra figimus, ne illis labentibus subruamur. Utimur autem hoc mundo tanquam non utentes, ut veniamus ad eum, qui fecit hunc mundum, & in eo maneamus, eius aeternitate perfruentes. Peregrinus victu & amictu contentus iter suum curat, supervacua non appetit, sarcinas graviores, quae inepedimento ipsi esse possunt, deponit, ad patriàm & propositum itineris scopum unicè contendit, labores itineris patienter tolerat, incommoda hospitiorum spe secuturae melioris sortis in patria lenit, nulli iniuriam infert, solicitum in omnibus sese exhibet, à periculis summo studio cavet, ad iter se praeparat calceis, vestibus & baculo: haec omnia ad spirituales peregrinos accommodari possunt. Bernh. de nostro bene vivendi cap. 7. Omnia, quae in hoc mundo sunt, servis DEI contraria sunt, ut dum ista adversa sentiunt, ad coeleste regnum cum summo desiderio suspirent. Magnâ apud DEUM refulget gratiâ, qui huic mundo contemtibilis est. Nam rever à necesse est, ut quae mundus odit, diligantur à DEO. Sancti viri peregrini sunt, & hospites in hoc seculo, unde reprehenditur Petrus, quòd tabernaculum in monte fieri voluerit, quia sanctis in hoc mundo tabernaculum non est, quibus in coelo patria & domus est. Beda in h. l. Hoc distare in hac vita inter electos & reprobos solet, quòd electi peregrini nunc & exules patriam expectant in futuro, tantoque, minus in praesenti gaudiis delectantur caducis, quanto futum sine fine gaudia se sperant accipere, & in aeternum cum Christo regnare. At vero reprobi hic habent patriam, cuius solum vitae desideriis norunt inhiare, ideoque, post hanc vitam in exilium relegabuntur perpetuum, ubi cunctis carentis voluptatibus sola in tormentis patiantur adversa.

21. Militia est vita hominis super terram,Iob. 7. v. 1. non tantùm cum exterioribus hostibus, sed etiam cum interno & domestico hoste ipsi pugnandum, cum pravis seil. carnis concupiscentiis, quòd duellum, cum sit continuum, & ad finem usque vitae duret, est longè periculosissimum. Hostes corporales metuimus, spirituales fovemus.

22. Desideria carnis pugnant contra animae salutem. Qui ergò concupiscentiis carnalibus indulgent, animae salute excidunt. Beda in h. l. Dum concupiscentiis blandientibus caro enerviter subiugatur, iam vitiorum exercitus firmiter adversus animam armatur.

23. Nulla durior pugna, quàm contra carnem, nulla gloriosior victoria, quàm de carne. Tertull. lib. ad Martyr. cap. 3. Stat conflictus, & victoriae suorum agonothetes DEUS vivus: Xystarches, Spiritus sanctus: Epistates, Christus Iesus: corona, aeternitatis: bravium, Angelicae in coelis substantiae politia: gloria, in secula seculorum.

24. Primùm omnium conscientiae & animi coram DEO puri, postmodum etiam famae & honestae apud homines conversationis ratio habenda.

25. Pii non solùm iniuriis realibus, sed etiam verbalibus, calumniis scilicet impiorum in hac vita sunt subiecti. Calumniae illae piis magis sunt molestae, quàm verbera & vincula.

26. Impiorum maledicentia & sinistri sermones debent nobis esse stimuli ad bene vivendum. Qui multos vitae observatores habet, vitae rationem cautiùs instituit.

27. Optimum contra calumnias remedium & scutum firmissimum vitae innocentia. Piorum Apologia non in verbis, sed in vita. Malè mecum agitur, si me oratio potiùs, quàm vita, defendat.

28. Veritas calumniis pressa in lucem tandem emergit, & ad sui amorem radiis suis alios allicit. Iustinus Apol. 2. de se commemorat, quòd cum adhuc gentilis esset, cogitârit, impossibile esse, Christianos prodigiosas illas, quarum rei agebantur, sectari voluptates, qui tàm constanter pro Christo mortem obirent. Eusebius lib. 2. Hist. cap. 9. resert, quod tortor D. Iacobi Apostoli, considerata eius caritate & patientiâ, ad fidem sit conversus. Beda lib. 1. Hist. Angl. cap. 7. testis est, Albanum, cum esset paganus, ex consideratione cuiusdam Clerici, sanctè & religiosè viventis, Christianum factum. Iberos Hispaniae populos obedientiâ, patientiâ, devotione & virtute captivae cuiusdam Christianae ad Christum esse conversos, memorant Eusebius lib. 10. cap. 10. & Ruffinus lib. 1. cap. 10. Nimirum plùs movent exempla, quàm verba.

29. Non nostrâ causâ potissimùm laborandum, ut homines benè de nobis loquantur, sed ut DEUS in nobis glorificetur,Galat. 1. v. 24.

30. Non solùm propter DEUM, & propter nos ipsos, sed etiam propter proximum vitae sanctitati & bonis operibus studere debemus, ut honestâ conversatione maledicorum ora obstruamus, ac nostro exemplo ad conversionem & pietatem alios provocemus.

## 2:10
WHO AT ONE TIME WERE NOT A PEOPLE, BUT NOW ARE THE PEOPLE OF GOD: WHO HAD NOT OBTAINED MERCY, BUT NOW HAVE OBTAINED MERCY.

Connection. 1. Because the Apostle had said that those to whom he writes were called by the kindness of GOD from darkness to admirable light, he therefore adds a testimony of Scripture, by which he might prove that that calling had been divinely foretold, and that the same is merely gratuitous.

2. He had called them a people for an acquisition or peculiar, he shows therefore that they themselves formerly had not been the people of GOD, and thus he opposes their present state to their former one, so that he may excite them to a grateful memory of so great a benefit. Formerly you were not the people of GOD, but now you are a peculiar people.

3. He had adorned them with distinguished praises, by calling them a chosen race, a royal Priesthood, a holy nation, a people for an acquisition. Lest therefore they should think that they had arrived at such great dignity by their own merits, he shows that that covenant of grace, into which they were received, is merely gratuitous, and that there is no other reason why GOD should account them as His own, except because, having had mercy on them, He adopted them freely.

Exposition of the text. Some think that regard is had to Deut. 32. v. 21. where after the enumerated benefits, provided to the Israelite people, Moses adds a prophecy concerning the calling of the Gentiles. I will make them jealous with a non-people, i. e. in those, who are not a people, I will make them angry with a foolish nation. But it is more correctly said that regard is had to Os. 2. vers. 23.

I will have mercy on her that had not obtained mercy, and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my GOD. Paul also brings forward this Prophetic passage Rom. 9. vers. 25. as an illustrious prophecy concerning the calling of the Gentiles, and joins to it another from the same Prophet cap. 1. vers. 10. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living GOD. But in both places, namely both in the Petrine allegation and in the Pauline allegation, the order of the Prophetic saying is changed, without any variation of sense. The Prophet puts the mention of mercy first, and thus proceeds from the cause to the effect, since it was by the gratuitous mercy of GOD that the Gentiles were called to the fellowship of the Church, and became the people of GOD. Paul and Peter place the mention of mercy after the calling, and thus proceed from the effect to the cause. Because the Gentiles before their calling are said absolutely not to be a people, some seek an emphasis in this, that a dispersed people is not in reality a people, since this name signifies a collection of men into one Republic. But it is more correctly said that the name of GOD is to be supplied from the latter member, because with Hosea GOD speaks thus: I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people. The Syrian rendered it: Who before were not reckoned a people, but now are the people of GOD: also there was no mercy towards you, but now mercy has been poured out upon you.

Latin:

QUI ALIQUANDO NON POPULUS, NUNC AUTEM POPULUS DEI: QUI NON CONSECUTI MISERICORDIAM, NUNC AUTEM MISERICORDIAM CONSECUTI.

Connexio. 1. Quia Apostolus dixerat, eos ad quos scribit, DEI benignitate vocatos esse à tenebris ad lumen admirabile, ideò subiicit testimonium Scripturae, quo probet, vocationem illam fuisse divinitùs praedictam, eandemque esse merè gratuitam.

2. Vocaverat illos populum in acquisitionem sive peculiarem, ostendit igitur, ipsos olim non fuisse DEI populum, sicque praesentem eorum statum opponit pristino, ut ad gratam tanti beneficii memoriam eos excitet. Quondam non eratis DEI populus, nunc autem estis populus peculiaris.

3. Ornaverat eos insignibus elogiis, vocando genus electum, regale Sacerdotium, gentem sanctam, populum in acquisitionem. Ne igitur existimarent, suis meritis se ad tantam pervenisse dignitatem, ostendit foedus illud gratiae, in quod recepti sunt, esse merè gratuitum, nec aliam esse causam, cur eos DEUS pro suis reputet, nisi quia illorum misertus gratis eos adoptaverit.

Textus expositio. Quidam existimant, respectum haberi adDeut. 32. v. 21.ubi post enumerata beneficia, populo Israëlitico praestita, Moses subiungit vaticinium de vocatione gentium. Zelare eos faciam in non populo, i. e. in illis, qui non sunt populus, in gente stulta irasci faciam eos. Sed rectiùs dicitur, respectum haberi ad Os. 2. vers. 23.

Miserebor eius, quae fuit absque misericordia, & dicam non populo meo, populus meus es tu, & ipse dicet, DEUS meus, scil. es tu. Hunc locum Propheticum adducit etiam Paulus Rom. 9. vers. 25. tanquam illustre vaticinium de vocatione gentium, eidemque coniungit alterum ex eodem Propheta cap. 1. vers. 10.Et erit in loco, ubi dictum est eis, Non populus meus vos, ibi vocabuntur filii DEI viventis. Utrobique autem, videlicet tùm in allegatione Petrina, tùm in allegatione Paulina, mutatur ordo dicti Prophetici, sine ulla sensus variatione. Propheta praemittit mentionem misericordiae, sicque progreditur à causa ad essectum, cum gratuitâ DEI misericordiâ factum fuerit, ut gentes vocarentur ad Ecclesiae consortium, & fierent DEI populus. Paulus & Petrus mentionem misericordiae subiiciunt vocationi, sicque progrediuntur ab effectu ad causam. Quod gentiles ante suam vocationem dicuntur absolutè non populus, in eo quidam quaerunt emphasin, quòd populus dispersus reverà non sit populus, cum hoc nomen significet collectionem hominum in unam Rempublicam. Sed rectiùs dicitur, ex membro posteriore supplendum esse nomen DEI, quia apud Oseam DEUS sic loquitur. Dicam non populo meo, populus meus es tu. Syrus reddidit. Qui antea non reputabamini populus, nunc autem populus DEI: etiam non erat ergae vos misericordia, nunc autem effusa est super vos misericordia.

## 2:11
DEARLY BELOVED, I BESEECH YOU AS STRANGERS AND PILGRIMS, ABSTAIN FROM FLESHLY LUSTS, WHICH WAR AGAINST THE SOUL.

Connection. 1. Having set forth the various arguments of his exhortation, the Apostle repeats his principal proposition, and dissuades those to whom he writes from evil works, but on the contrary exhorts them to good works, just as he had also exhorted them at the beginning of the chapter, that they should lay aside all malice and desire the rational milk. He describes evil works from the efficient cause, which are the desires of the flesh, or depraved concupiscences, still remaining in the flesh of the regenerate. He describes good works from that part which falls into the senses of men, namely from an external honest conversation.

2. Having shown the foundation of salvation, which is Christ, to whom by faith as living stones believing they have been built up, and having set forth the highest dignity and happiness of Christians, which they obtain from the benefit of election, redemption, vocation, adoption, and promised glorification, by a method used by the Apostles he exhorts them to the flight of evils and the pursuit of good works, warning that they should respond to such great dignity with a holy conversation.

3. He had said that they had obtained mercy. Therefore, by that very mercy of GOD, by which they had been called into the peculiar people of GOD, and by which alone that which he asks could be performed, he adjures and beseeches them that they show themselves obedient to the admonition about to be added.

4. Bede here establishes the beginning of special exhortations, and judges these words to be directed to the free, to whom a special exhortation directed to subjects and servants is later added. Up to this point, he says, Blessed Peter has instructed the Church generally, explaining either the benefits by which divine piety has deigned to call us to salvation, or the gifts by which it once honored the Jews, but now honors us. Hence he skillfully exhorts the diverse persons of the faithful, lest by living carnally they render themselves unworthy of such great grace of the Holy Spirit, lest those who are distinguished by the Royal and Priestly title, being subdued by the malice of vices, degenerate from the glory of the nobility once granted or promised to them. Therefore, he addresses first the free and servants, then women and men specifically, and after the interlocution of the general exhortation, also how the Elders and adolescents ought to conduct themselves. He aptly teaches the free to abstain from carnal desires, because the liberty of a more relaxed life is accustomed to tolerate greater dangers of titillating allurements, which war against the soul. But it is more correctly established that these pertain to a general exhortation common to all the pious, because it concerns everyone that they are sojourners and pilgrims in this world.

Exposition of the text. He calls the faithful to whom he writes ἀγαπητοὺς beloved, with which form of address the other Apostles also frequently use in their Epistles, Rom. 12. v. 19.1 Cor. 10. v. 14.cap. 15. v. 58.2. Cor. 12. v. 19.Phil. 2. v. 12.cap. 4. v. 1.Hebr. 6. v. 9.Iac. 1. v. 16. & 19.cap. 2. v. 5.1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. & 21.cap. 4. v. 1.7. & 11.Iudae v. 3.17. & 20. and Peter repeats the same several times in this and the later Epistle. 1. Epist. 4. vers. 12.2. Epist. 3. v. 1.8.14. & 17. in which part they follow Christ their Master, who called his Apostles τεκνία his beloved children Ioh. 13.

v. 33. by which appellation John is especially delighted in his Epistles. He calls them beloved, because having obtained mercy from GOD, and having been adopted by Him into sons, he may deservedly hold them for brothers, and by that very φιλαδελφίαν, to which he was about to exhort them, cap. 1. v. 22. he may demonstrate it. He also looks back to the spiritual regeneration through the word, of which he had made mention cap. 1. v. 23. for since he had begotten them in Christ through that word 1. Cor. 4. v. 15. thence he calls them his beloved children. παρακαλεῖν signifies both to pray and to exhort. The Vulgate Latin version, as also the Syriac, embraces the former meaning; Luther in the German version embraces the latter. Both are sufficiently congruent and can be joined without absurdity. I exhort, and if it is lawful, I beseech. This is the first argument of the exhortation. It is fair that you should leave room for my petition, since I am your Apostle, sincerely loving you in Christ. Ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους. Both words were explained in the preceding chapter, the former indeed v. 17. the latter truly v. 1. The Vulgate Interpreter rendered the little word παρεπιδήμους, at the beginning of the Epistle as strangers, but here he translates it as pilgrims, the meaning of both words being almost the same. For it denotes those who, as pilgrims and newcomers, dwell in some place. Cyprian, lib. 1. Epist. 5. reads guests. Augustine, conc. 8. in Psal. 118. What is in Greek πάροικος some of ours have interpreted as tenant, some as inhabitant, some even as stranger. Tenants not having a house of their own dwell in another's. Inhabitants, however, or strangers are at any rate considered newcomers. Although Peter calls the converted Jews to whom he writes by the name παρεπιδήμους, in a different sense in v. 1. than in this place, for there he calls them παρεπιδήμους διασπορᾶς because they lived dispersed among the nations outside their native land, but here he calls converted Jews and Gentiles in general strangers and pilgrims, because they are pilgrims and guests in this world, there is no doubt, however, that the Apostle alludes to the first verse cap. 1. with this appellation. You are strangers of the dispersion, exiled from your native land; let this condition of yours remind you that you are spiritually strangers and pilgrims in this world. This is the second argument of the exhortation. You are guests and pilgrims in this world. Therefore do not love the world, nor those things which are in the world, namely the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. 1. Ioh. 2. v. 15. & 16. Conduct yourselves in this world as in a land of exile. Therefore do not covet those things which are worldly, which are most highly esteemed in the world and by the world, namely pleasures, honors, riches. For pilgrims and strangers do not conform themselves to the region in which they are only journeying for a time, nor do they set the end of their desires in the land of exile, but they perpetually aspire toward their homeland. Nor is it absurdly thought that Peter by these words recalls them to the examples of the holy Patriarchs. Abraham, the father of all believers, calls himself a stranger and a sojournerGen. 23. v. 4. Moses was a stranger in a strange landExod. 2. v. 22. The Israelites were strangers in the land of Egypt,Deut. 10. v. 19. David says of himself Ps. 39. v. 13. I am a stranger with thee and a sojourner, as all my fathers were.Ps. 119. v. 19. I am a stranger in the earth, and of himself and the whole Israelite people he says, 1 Chron. 29. v. 15. We are strangers before thee and sojourners, as were all our fathers. Concerning all the Patriarchs, the Epistle to the Hebrews 11. v. 13. speaks thus. These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but seeing them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.v. 14. For they that say such things declare plainly that they seek a country.v. 15. And truly, if they had been mindful of that country from whence they came out, they might have had opportunity to have returned.v. 16. But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly. Just as therefore the holy Patriarchs, when they called themselves strangers and sojourners, testified that they were aspiring toward the heavenly homeland from the exile of this world, so also the Apostle exhorts believers, that as their spiritual children, panting for the heavenly homeland, they should hold their depraved lusts in contempt. Ἀπέχενσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμίων, The Vulgate rendered the pronoun you, which is not in the Greek text, nor is it necessary for the completion of the sentence, whence it is also omitted in certain Latin Codices. For ἀπέχεσθαι to abstain, certain Codices have ἀπέ χεσθε abstain in the imperative, in which way the Syriac also rendered it. [consult facsimile image] separate yourselves. But the infinitive ἀπέχεσθαι agrees more with the text, because this verb coheres with the preceding παθκαλῶ in which way Clement of Alexandria also reads and arranges it in book 3 of the Stromata 2. By τὰς σαρκικὰς ἐπιθυμίας some understand in particular carnal lusts. But more correctly in general are understood any depraved and illicit of the lusts of the flesh, which after the fall of the first-formed are implanted in individual men from carnal generation, and still cling in the flesh of the reborn, and through it exert themselves, and solicit men to the works of the flesh. The Apostle recounts a fairly long catalog of them Gal. 5. v. 19. 20. & 21. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] [consult facsimile image] the desires of the body, by which word he also uses in the explanation of the commandment concerning not coveting Roman. 7. v. 7. Concerning these carnal lusts the Apostle says that they war against the soul. Some by the name of soul here understand the salvation of the soul. They think, therefore, that carnal lusts are said to fight against the soul for this reason, because the vicious affections of the flesh, however much the soul may assent to them, tend toward its destruction; and that those carnal desires, although they are pleasing to the senses, nevertheless wage a destructive war against the salvation of man. But it is more correctly said, by a phrase also used by the remaining Apostles, that by the soul is understood the whole new and inner man, insofar as he is renewed by the Holy Spirit, just as by the flesh is understood the whole man, insofar as he is still constituted under the oldness of the flesh, in part carnally sold under sin. Roman. 7. v. 14. Just as therefore Paul says, in the reborn the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh, and consequently there is a hostile fight between the flesh and the Spirit, Galat. 5. v. 17. so also Peter says in this place, carnal desires fight against the soul, i. e. against the inner man, against the Spirit, against the mind, (for these are all ἰσοδυναμοῦντα, to Paul in the description of this hostile fight) thence also Peter uses the same word στρατουεσθαι which Paul used in describing this fight of the Spirit and the flesh. Roman. 7. v. 23. I see another law in my members ἀντιστρατευόμενον to the law of my mind. Iacobi. 4. vers. 1. Whence are wars and strifes among you? are they not hence from your lusts, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευόι των, which war in your members. This is the third argument of the exhortation. Carnal lusts war against the soul. Therefore you ought deservedly to abstain from them, lest, namely, you fulfill them in deed.

Latin:

CARISSIMI, OBSECRO TANQUAM ADVENAS & PEREGRINOS, ABSTINERE VOS A CARNALIBUS DESIDERIIS, QUAE MILITANT ADVERSUS ANIMAM.

Connexio. 1. Expositis variis exhortationis suae argumentis, principalem propositionem Apostolus repetit, ac dehortatur eos, ad quos scribit, ab operibus malis, contrà vero hortatur eos ad opera bona, sicut etiam in principio capitis hortatus fuerat, ut malitiam omnem deponerent & lac rationale concupiscerent. Opera mala describit à causa efficiente, quae sunt desideria carnis, sive pravae concupiscentiae, in carne renatorum adhuc reliquae. Opera bona describit à parte ea, quae in sensus hominum incurrit, videlicet ab externa honesta conversatione.

2. Ostenso salutis fundamento, quod est Christus, cui per fidem tanquam vivi lapides credentes superaedificati sunt, & expositâ summâ Christianorum dignitate ac felicitate, quam ex beneficio electionis, redemtionis, vocationis, adoptionis & promissae glorificationis obtinent, methodo Apostolis usitata exhortatur eos ad fugam malorum & studium bonorum operum, monens ut tantae dignitati sancta conversatione respondeant.

3. Dixerat eos misericordiam consecutos. Per illam ipsam ergò DEI misericordiam, per quam in populum DEI peculiarem vocati erant, ac per quam unicè praestari poterat, quod rogat, eos obtestatur & obsecrat, ut admonitioni subiungendae sese obsequentes praestent.

4. Beda hîc statuit initium specialium exhortationum, atque haec dicta censet ad liberos, quibus postea subiiciatur specialis exhortatio ad subditos & servos directa. Hucusque, inquit, B. Petrus generaliter Ecclesiam instituit, explicans vel beneficia, quibus nos divina pietas ad salutem vocare, vel dona, quibus aliquando Iudaeos, nunc autem nos honorare dignatus est. Hinc diversas fidelium personas solerter hortatur, ne se tanta sancti Spiritus gratiâ carnaliter vivendo reddant indignos, ne qui Regali ac Sacerdotali vocabulo sunt insigniti, vitiorum malitiâ subacti à condonatae vel promissae olim sibi nobilitatis gloriâ degenerent. Itaque primò liberos & servos, deinde mulieres & viros specialiter alloquitur, ac post interlocutionem generalis exhortationis Seniores quoque & adolescentes qualiter sese agere debeant. Aptè autem liberos docet à carnalibus abstinere desideriis, quia solet libertas vitae remissioris maiora illecebrarum titillantium tolerare pericula, quae militant adversus animam. Sed rectius statuitur, quòd haec ad generalem exhortationem omnibus piis communem pertineant, quia ad omnes spectat, quòd sintadvenae & peregrini in hoc mundo.

Textus expositio. Fideles ad quos scribit, vocat ἀγαπητοὺςdilectos, quâ compellatione etiam reliqui Apostoli in suis Epistolis frequenter utuntur, Rom. 12. v. 19.1 Cor. 10. v. 14.cap. 15. v. 58.2. Cor. 12. v. 19.Phil. 2. v. 12.cap. 4. v. 1.Hebr. 6. v. 9.Iac. 1. v. 16. & 19.cap. 2. v. 5.1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. & 21.cap. 4. v. 1.7. & 11.Iudae v. 3.17. & 20. ac Petrus eandem aliquoties in hac & posteriore Epistola repetit. 1. Epist. 4. vers. 12.2. Epist. 3. v. 1.8.14. & 17. qua in parte sequuntur Christum Magistrum suum, qui Apostolos suos vocavit τεκνίαdilectos suos filios Ioh. 13.

v. 33. quâ apellatione Iohannes in suis Epistolis cumprimis delectatur.
