For whoever does not carry his cross, and come after Christ, cannot be a disciple of Christ,Luc. 14. vers. 27. Leo serm. 5. de nativitate Christi. In vain are we called Christians, if we are not imitators of Christ, who therefore said He was the way, so that the conversation of the master might be the form of the disciple, and the servant might choose that humility which the Lord followed.

8. The mode of imitation consists in this, that by the example of Christ, who was placed under the burden of the cross, we exercise our trust, Psal. 16. v. 2. Psal. 22. v. 1. obedience toward God, spontaneous Phil. 2. v. 8. patience, Esai. 53. v. 7.hope of liberation, Psal 16. v. 10. and invocation, Hebr. 5. v. 7.

9. Meanwhile, that imitation is not perfect and absolute in every respect in this life. For just as painters and students cannot attain the ὑπογραμμὸν prescribed to them by their masters, so too we shall never be able to reach the pinnacle of the virtues proposed to us in Christ for imitation.

10. Christ not only taught us by word, but also by example; He not only taught, but also did Act. 1. v. 1. so that true preachers may teach not only with the tongue but also with their life. 1. Tim 4. v. 12. August. lib. 4. de doctr. Christ. cap. 27. The life of the teacher has greater weight so that he may be heard obediently, than any greatness of diction.

11. Christ alone out of all men, and among all men, is entirely ἀναμάρτητος, Ioh. 8. v. 46. cap. 14. v. 30. 2. Cor. 5. v. 21. Hebr. 7. v. 26. 1. Ioh. 3. v. 5. but our righteousness, both habitual and actual, is not perfect, but contaminated by the stain of sin.

12. The patience of Christ was most pure and most perfect, entirely void of any desire for vengeance; but ours is imperfect and unclean, for when injuries are received, our minds immediately boil over with a desire for vengeance.

13. GOD is a just judge and a most equitable avenger. If we deposit our injury with Him, He will assert our innocence and will inflict vengeance upon our persecutors. Tertull. lib. de patient. How much is permitted to patience, that it should have God Himself as a debtor, because if you deposit an injury with God, He Himself will be the avenger.

14. On the contrary, however, he who, provoked by injuries, immediately leaps to vengeance, raises himself into the place of God, and snatches to himself what is proper to God. Deut. 32. v. 35. Rom. 12. v. 9.

15. The passion of Christ is not only a most lucid mirror of virtues and an example proposed to us for imitation, Iohan. 13. vers. 15. but also and chiefly our merit and a most full satisfaction for our sins. CHRIST came into these lands, not only that He might be our Teacher, who would show us the way of salvation both by word and example, but also that He might be our Mediator and

The Redeemer, who might procure eternal salvation for us by the price of his own blood.

16. Christ therefore died, that he might mortify sin in us; in the death of Christ our old man is crucified, that we may walk in newness of life.Rom. 6. v. 4. Where the death of Christ flourishes to expiate and forgive sins, there it is at the same time efficacious for the mortification of the flesh. Clement of Alexandria, book 3 of the Paedagogus, chapter 12. We have as a limit (a boundary of sinning) the cross of the Lord, to which we are co-crucified, and are restrained from former sins.

17. True life is to live to GOD and to righteousness; but to live to sin, is death.1. Tim. 5. v. 6. Bernard, Epistle 105. A good death, if you die to sin, that you may live to righteousness. It is necessary that this death should go before, that that secure one may follow. While you live in the flesh, die to the world, that after the death of the flesh you may begin to live to GOD.

18. The wounds of Christ are the health and medicine of our soul. Tauler, Meditations on the life of Christ, chapter 8. That we might live, it behooved him to die; that we might be gladdened, he himself was saddened; that we might be healed, he himself was wounded; that we might be cleansed, he himself shed blood. The blood of the Physician was poured out, and it was made the medicine of the sick man. Ambrose, alleging this Prophetic and Apostolic passage, by whose stripe you are healed, writes in his book on the Holy Spirit, chapter 8. The wound of Christ is our medicine.

19. We are by Nature strangers to the way of salvation, and we follow the pathless ways of errors and sins, until Christ gathers us from that dispersion.

20. It is frequent in the Scriptures for us to be compared to sheep, before conversion indeed to wandering sheep,Psal. 119. versu ult.Ezech. 34. v. 5.Luc. 15. v. 4. but after conversion, to sheep hearing the voice of their shepherd.Ioh. 10. v. 4. & 27.

21. What our condition is before our conversion to Christ is most beautifully described by this similitude of sheep. A sheep is a foolish animal: thus before conversion we are destitute of true wisdom, which consists in the saving knowledge of GOD. Sheep are liable to various diseases, and as those learned in Nature maintain, to as many diseases as men: thus before conversion we are spiritually sick, and we are in need of the healing of the soul. Wandering sheep are destitute of a shepherd, and are separated from the flock: thus before conversion from Christ and

we are separated from the assembly of the saints. Nothing is more miserable than a lost little sheep, which would have to perish in the jaws of the wolf, unless it were sought by the Shepherd and restored to the flock: thus we would all be the prey of the infernal wolf, unless Christ the true shepherd sought us, and brought us to his flock. Wandering sheep are at length deprived of saving pastures, and perish from hunger: thus we would all have to perish from hunger, unless Christ led us to the saving pastures of the Gospel.

22. As our misery is depicted in the wandering sheep, so the goodness and mercy of Christ the shepherd is depicted in the Shepherd seeking the wandering sheep. Luke 15. verse 1. Hence everywhere in the Scriptures Christ is called shepherd,Ezek. 34. v. 23.John 10. v. 11.Heb. 13. v. 20. For he himself provides pastures in the present of temporal graces, and grants us the pastures of eternal life, says Bede in this place. As a shepherd leads sheep to pastures, so Christ feeds us with spiritual and Sacramental food, he feeds us with saving teachings, and the examples of his most holy life, he feeds us with the preaching of Evangelical doctrine, and the internal consolation of the Holy Spirit. As a shepherd watches over the sheep, so also Christ guards us with a watchful eye, lest the infernal wolf snatch us from his hand.John 10. v. 28. As a shepherd defends his sheep against wolves and thieves: so also we are safe under the custody of Christ the shepherd from the incursion of the infernal wolf. As a shepherd heals the diseased sheep, lifts the lambs into his bosom, leads those that are nursing: Thus Christ provides the same benefits to spiritual sheep. Isa. 40. v. 11.Ezek. 34. v. 16. As a shepherd seeks the wandering sheep, so Christ does the same. Ezek. in the said place. Luke 15. v. 1. Thence to the manger of the born Christ, shepherds were the first of all to be called, because clearly the true shepherd of our souls had come into the world, and as Christ was dying on the Echinades islands a voice was heard, that the great Pan was dead. Euseb. book 5 of the preparation of the Gospel, chapter 9. Pan, however, was the GOD of shepherds.

23. Christ is at once the shepherd and Bishop of our souls: Thus the pastors and teachers of the Church should be Bishops i.e. watch for the souls of the hearers, committed to their faith.Heb. 13. verse 17. Isidor. Pelusiota book 1, Epistle 149, p. 39. Let a Bishop have it perceived from the name itself, that it behooves him to watch, and to be an eye on every side, looking out for all things, and neglecting nothing. John Huss in this place. Let Bishops see if they themselves also watch as if for souls about to render an account. Bernard, book 2, on consideration, to Eugene, chapter 6, Does the chair flatter you? It is a watchtower; from there, finally, you oversee, with the name of Bishop sounding to you not lordship, but duty.

4. The Apostle in the preceding verse proposed Christ to us as Priest and lamb, who offered himself to GOD as a sacrifice for our sins; here he proposes him to us to be considered as the Shepherd seeking his sheep, for whom he offered himself as a sacrifice, restoring the sought ones to the flock, feeding the restored ones with the word of the Gospel, and placing the fed ones into eternal tabernacles. Epiphanius, heresy 88, Christ offered himself for the whole world, he himself the victim, he himself the sacrifice, he himself the Priest, he himself the altar, he himself God, he himself man, he himself King, he himself Pontiff, he himself sheep, he himself lamb, having been made all things in all things for us, so that he might become life for us in all ways.

25. Let us not despair of the conversion of others, who like sheep are still wandering from the Lord's flock, but let us strive to obtain and promote it from Christ the faithful Shepherd with pious prayers. Prosper, in the sentences of Augustine, sentence 184, One must not despair of the wicked, but one must pray more zealously for them, that they may become good: because the number of the saints is always increased from the number of the impious. Those who are goats today, can be sheep tomorrow. Those who are tares today, can be wheat tomorrow.

Summary of the Chapter. A continuation of the Apostolic exhortation to holiness of life and morals. There are two parts of the chapter. 1. Special exhortation to married persons, and indeed first to wives, secondly to husbands, from the beginning of the chapter up to v. 9. 2. General exhortation to all Christians, established in whatever state of life, from v. 9 up to 19. To the latter part is added παρέκβασις, a certain digression concerning the benefits of Christ in the N. T. and his ascension to the heavens, and exaltation to the right hand of the Father, from 19 to the end of the chapter.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quare Apostolus servos in omni timore subditos heris suis esse velit. Resp. Quidam voculam omnis accipiunt distributivè pro quantitate discreta, cum multiplex sit timor, qui in servis esse debeat, utpote primò timor poenae, ne ab heris, si inobedientes sint, puniantur, secundò timor culpae, ne Deum inobedientiâ suâ offendant; tertiò timor scandali, ne inobedientiâ suâ heros ad odium fidei Christianae provocent. Sed monuimus superiùs, Apostolum non requirere timorem poenae, qui est timor servilis, sed timorem culpae, qui est filialis. Rectius ergò vocula πάντι accipitur pro quantitate continua, cum omni timore i. e. cum multa reverentia. Exigit enim Apostolus purum, plenum ac voluntarium reverentiae affectum, quo ex officio suo obedientiam heris se debere agnoscant. Col. 3. v. 22.

Q. 2. An servis liceat à dominis inclementibus fugere? Distinguendum inter mancipia & libertos. Mancipia non erant sui iuris, sed possessio Domini, unde ex fuga retrahebantur, sed liberti fugere possunt, si vitae vel incolumitatis membrorum periculum illis immineat. August. tract. 15. in Iohannem: Unusquisque servus Dei non peccat, si se cesserit in alium locum, ridens furorem per sequentium se, aut quaerentium in malum animam suam. Videretur autem servus Dei peccare, si faceret, nisi in faciendo Dominus praecessisset. Fecit hoc ille Magister bonus, ut doceret, non quod timeret.

Q. 3. Quid per conscientiam DEI Apostolus hîc intelligat in v. 19. Resp. 1. Caietanus sic exponit. Si quis propter DEI conscientiam sustinet tristitias i. e. propter applicationem scientiae, quam habet de iis, quae sunt DEO grata. 2. Gagnaeus hanc expositionem reiicit, ipse vero sic exponit. Si quis propter DEI conscientiam sustinet, id est, propter Deum, qui & servilis patientiae & herilis malitiae conscius est, ac utriusque erit iudex & vindex, ut servi patientiam praemiis coelestibus ornet, heri vero saevitiam flammis infernalibus puniat. Conscientia ergò DEI est innocentia coram DEO acuni DEO patens. 3. Quidam sic exponunt. Si quis propter Dei conscientiam sustineat tristitias i. e. quia est veri Dei cultor; eo nomine hero suo exosus, quòd fidem Christianam profiteatur. Quando enim servi ad Christum convertebantur, ab heris Ethnicis in odium fidei Christianae plagis ac verberibus mulctabantur, si ergò propter Dei conscientiam patiebantur i. e. propter Deum & Dei cultum, ex pura conscientia profectum; patiebantur haec omnia propterea quod bonâ conscientiâ Deo servire studerent in fide Christiana, quam amplexi erant ac profitebantur. Huic expositioni à quibusdam obvertitur, quòd Petrus nondum agere videatur de afflictione Christianorum propter fidem Christianam ipsis illata, de qua demum in seqq. capp. agat. 4. Quidam Dei conscientiam intelligunt eam, quae solius Dei gloriam spectat, eidemque sese totam addicit. Fideles servi ab iniustis dominis illatas iniurias patienter tolerantes, patiebantur propter Dei conscientiam, quia in servitio ac tota vita sua Dei solius honorem spectabant, nec hominum sed Dei respectu officio suo fungebantur. 5. Simplicissimè respondetur, conscientiam Dei esse conscientiam ad Deum, ut Lutherus reddidit, vel de Deo, quando scilicet aliquis conscius est, id DEUM velle, idque DEO gratum esse, quod agit. Sic servi patiebantur propter DEI conscientiam, quia iniurias iniustè sibi illatas patienter tolerabant, non tantùm ne graviora incurrerent incommoda, nec ut herorum suorum vel aliorum hominum gratiam sibi conciliarent, sed quia noverant, hanc esse Dei voluntatem, ut iniurias patienter sustineant, patientiam illam esse opus DEO gratum & acceptum, quod etiam temporalibus & aeternis praemiis sit remuneraturus. Obediebant ergò etiam durissimis herorum imperiis, & mores ipsorum asperrimos tolerabant, ut conscientiae satisfacerent, ut bonâ conscientiâ coram DEO ambularent & ipsius voluntati obtemperarent, sicque non hominum, sed Dei timore in officio continebantur.

Q. 4. Quid Christus DEO iudici dicatur tradidisse? Resp. 1. Glossa ordinariâ Didymo accipit de persecutoribus & hostibus Christi. Tradebat suos per secutores DEO Patri pro eis orando. Pater dimitte illis, quia nesciunt, quid faciunt,Luc. 23. vers. 34. 2. Quidam de ipso Christo accipiunt. Tradidit seipsum DEO Patri in voluntarium sacrificium, fuit obediens suo Patri usque ad mortem crucis,Phil. 2. vers. 8. 3. Quidam subintelligunt nomen vindictae, ut sit sensus. Christus non vindicavit seipsum, sed vindictam commisit DEO Patri, qui dicit. Mihi vindicta, ego retribuam,Deuter. 32. vers. 35.Roman. 12. v. 19. 4. Simplicissimè accipitur de causa ipsa. Christus pro peccatis nostris passiones varias sustinens, causam suam DEO commendabat, liberationem ex angustiis petens, pro crucifixoribus intercedens, & pertinaces ac incorrigibiles DEI iudicio committens, παριδίδον enim non tantùm significat tradidit, sed etiam commisit ac commendavit. Ierem. 11. v. 20.In te devolvi causam meam.

Q. 5. Quis per iustè iudicantem intelligatur? Oecumenius accipit de τῷ λόγῳDEO Verbo inhabitanti in Christo. Sed Augustinus tractat. 21. in Iohan. ac Didymus in comm. rectiùs intelligunt de DEO Patre, à quo in mortem erat traditus,Roman. 8. vers. 32.& cum quo per preces egit in passione,Matth. 26. v. 39.Hebr. 5. vers. 7. interim certum est Patris ac λόγου esse unam Deitatis essentiam.

Q. 6. Quâ ratione vitae sanctitas sit consequens mortis Christi? Resp. 1. Ποιητικῶς. Christus suâ morte non tantùm promeruit nobis peccatorum remissionem, sed etiam Spiritus sancti donationem, qui peccatum in carne nostra mortificat. 2. Ὑποδειγματικῶς.Roman. 6. v. 4.Consepulti sumus cum Christo per Baptismum in mortem, ut quomodo Christus surrexit à mortuis per gloriam Patris, ita & nos in novitate vitae ambulemus. Ambrosius in 2. Cor. 5.Crucifige peccatum, ut moriare peccato. Qui enim peccato moritur, DEO vivit. Vivamus ei, qui proprio Filio non pepercit, ut in illius corpore nostras crucifigeret passiones. Pro nobis enim mortuus est Christus, ut nos in illius corpore redivivo moreremur. Mortua est ergò in illo non vita nostra, sed culpa.

Q. 7. Quare Apostolus Christum animarum duntaxat Pastorem & Episcopum vocet? Resp. Christus, ut verus cum Patre & Spiritu sancto DEUS, etiam corpora nostra cibo corporali pascit ad hanc vitam, & ut noster Mediator ac Redemtor non solùm animas, sed etiam corpora nostra perducit ad vitam aeternam, interim Apostolus animarum duntaxat mentionem facere voluit. 1. Ut distingueret Christum spiritualem animarum Pestorem & Medicum à corporum Pastoribus ac Medicis. Christus est animarum nostrarum Pastor & Episcopus, quia spirituali cibatione ac defensione custodit nos ad salutem aeternam. 2. Ut significaret, Christum animarum nostrarum curam agere, easque ad se recipere, quando corpora nostra à persecutoribus occiduntur, Matth. 10. v. 28.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Quae est gloria, si peccantes & colaphizati suffertis?v. 20.Atqui patientia etiam in poenis promeritis suam habet laudem ac mercedem. Resp. Petrus non loquitur absolutè, sed comparatè. Non significat, eum qui pro delictis suis poenas vel à DEO vel à Magistratu DEI ministro illatas patienter sustinet, omni omninò patientiae mercede apud DEUM cariturum, sed negat, esse ex suo genere magnum & illustre aliquod patientiae opus, cui singularis gloria debeatur, quale est, si quis ob bona opera, vel certè praeter meritum illatas iniurias patienter sustineat. Tenuis & obscura laus est, iustam poenam aequo animo ferre, si comparetur cum laude ex afflictionibus iniustè illatis, sed patienter toleratis orta.

2. Si benefacientes & patientes sustinetis, haec est gratia apud Deum, versu eod. At qui gloria coram DEO in poenis non habet locum. Resp. Sanè Interpres Syrus voculam κλέος hîc repetit ex membro priore. Sed Graeci Codices omnes legunt. Haec est gratia apud Deum. Singulari igitur consilio vox χάριτος ab Apostolo ex versu praeced. repetitur, cum antithesis huius versiculi vocem κλέος requirere videretur. Significat enim, non posse nos de patientia in afflictionibus etiam iniustè illatis coram DEO gloriari, cum pertineat ad obedientiam DEO multis nominibus debitam, cum non sit opus nostrum, sed gratiae & Spiritus efficaciter in nobis operantis, cum sit imperfecta & vitiosis affectibus in infirmitate huius carnis contaminata. In nullo gloriandum, quia nihil nostrum est. 1. Cor. 4. v. 7.

3. Christus reliquit nobis exemplum, ut sequamur vestigia eius.v. 21.Atqui Christus ambulavit super mare, coecis visum, surdis auditum restituit, in quo eum sequi minimè possumus. Resp. distinguendum inter opera Christi miraculosa, & virtuosa, sive virtutes. Petrus non proponit nobis in exemplum imitationis opera Christi miraculosa ac heroica, sed patientiam, obedientiam & innocentiam. Christus in quibusdam operibus est nobis mirabilis, in quibusdam imitabilis.

4. Reliquit nobis exemplum, ut sequamur vestigia eius,v. 21.AtquiEccles. 2. v. 12.Quid est homo, ut sequi possit Regem factorem suum. Resp. Ioh. Huss. distinguit inter divinam, & humanam Christi Naturam; non illam, sed hanc in exemplum imitationis nobis proponi. Rectiùs respondetur, in Hebraeo ibi aliter legi. Quid est homo, qui venturus est post Regem, quod iam fecerunt ipsum, ubi non de coelesti, sed terreno Rege sermo est.

5. Christus non fecit peccatum.v. 22.Atqui Christus factus est pro nobis peccatum,2. Cor. 5. v. 21.DEUS Christum pro nobis fecit peccatum. Resp. aliud est Christum fecisse peccatum, aliud Christum pro nobis factum esse peccatum. Illud denotat peccati inhaesionem & operationem, hoc vero peccati imputationem, factam pro peccatis oblationem, & poenarum peccatis nostris debitarum tolerationem. Illud accipitur ἐνυπαρκτικῶς, hoc vero λογιστικῶς. August. lib. 2. contra Pelag. & Coelestinum cap. 32. DEUS fecit Christum pro nobis peccatum, i. e. sacrificium, per quod dimitterentur peccata nostra, quoniam peccata vocantur sacrificia pro peccatis. Fulgentius de fide ad Petrum cap. 26. Christus sine peccato conceptus, sine peccato mortuus, peccatum pro nobis factus est, i. e. sacrificium factus pro peccatis nostris.

6. Christus non fecit peccatum,v. 22.Atqui Christus non solùm à peccatis actualibus, sed etiam ab originali liber. Resp. 1. τό facere peccatum, non ponitur exclusivè pro solis actualibus peccatis, sed inclusivè, ut includat etiam originale peccatum, ex quo tanquam venenato fonte actualia peccata oriuntur. 2. Quòd enim Petrus dicit, Christum non fecisse peccatum, illud Paulus sic effert 2. Cor. 5. v. 21.Christum non novisse peccatum, ubi Chrysostomus notat, Apostolum non dixisse, qui peccatum non fecerat, sed qui peccatum non noverat, quidem usque adeò ipsum fuisse à peccatoribus segregatum, ut ne de facie quidem peccatum noverit.Hebr. 7. v. 26. Vocatur ὅσιος, ἄκακος, ἀμίαντος, κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῆν ἁμαρτωλῶν. 3. Pétrus notanter addit ex Esaia, quòd non sit inventus dolus in ore Christi. Iam vero qui linguâ non delinquit, hic perfectus est, inquit Iacobus cap. 3. v. 2. Ergò eo ipso summa & perfectissima innocentia Christi denotatur. 4. Augustinus ex remotione peccati actualis colligit remotionem peccati originalis, lib. 5. contra Iulianum cap. 15. sic disserens. Profectò peccatum etiam maior fecisset, si parvulus habuisset. Nam propterea nullus est hominum praeter ipsum, qui peccatum non fecerit grandioris aetatis accessu, quia nullus est hominum praeter ipsum, qui peccatum non habuerit infantilis aetatis exortu.

7. Cùm malediceretur, non regessit maledictav. 23.AtquiIoh. 8. v. 44.dicit ad Iudaeos sibi maledicentes. Vos ex patre Diabolo estis. Resp. 1. Non fuit haec recriminatio, quia nihil simile priùs ei obiectum fuerat, sed fuit vera & iusta accusatio. 2. Non ex vitioso privatae vindictae affectu, sed ex animo salutis ipsorum cupidissimo hoc protulit, ut ad peccatorum agnitionem, & consequenter ad conversionem & salutem ipsos perduceret, Iohannes Hussus in h. l. Caritativa correctio non est contumelia, sed ex odio procedens, praesertim si sit in propriam vindictam.

8. Cùm pateretur, non comminabatur.v. 23.AtquiMatth. 11. v. 20.dicit. Vaetibi Chorazin, vae tibi Bethsaida.Matth. 23. v. 13. & seqq. Vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei.cap. 26. v. 64.Veruntamen dico vobis, à modò videbitis Filium hominis sedentem à dextris DEI, & venientem in nubibus coeli. Resp. 1. Non denunciavit vae sive aeternam maledictionem Pontificibus, Scribis & Pharisaeis ipso passionis tempore, sed ante passionem, ne non ex Zelo iustitiae, sed affectibus irae & odii commotus id fecisse videretur. 2. Denunciavit illis DEI iudicium, non propter se, nec ex impatientia vel studio vindictae, sed propter ipsos & ex caritate, ut eos à scelere, & consequenter à damnatione revocaret.

9. Tradebat iudicanti iustè.v. 23.At Christus nuspiam legitur, causam vindictam suam DEO commendasse. Resp. non postulavit vindictam, sed veniam, quando pro interfectoribus deprecator factus conversionem ipsorum petiit, Luc. 23. v. 34. unde sanguis ipsius dicitur loquiκρείττοναmeliora, quàm sanguis Abelis,Hebr. 12. vers. 24.Sanguis enim Abel postulavit ultionem,Genes. 4. v. 10. Christi vero sanguis reconciliationem & expiationem.

10. Eratis sicut oves errantes.v. 25.Atqui ante conversionem non erant oves, sed haedi. Respondet 1. Beda in h. l. Quomodo & oves dicit & errantes, cum hi qui in errore vitam ducunt, haedorum potiùs, quàm ovium nomine censeantur, nisi quia novit Dominus qui sunt eius, qui & multos diu malè conversantes sustinet, quos tamen in ovium suarum numero salvandos esse praevidet. 2. Simpliciùs respondetur, homines ad Christum non conversos comparari ovibus, non ratione simplicitatis, innocentiae, patientiae & reliquorum simulachrorum virtutum, sed ratione stoliditatis, periculi & miseriae, in qua versantur oves pastore destitutae, & praedae luporum expositae, unde non simpliciter comparantur ovibus, sed ovibus errantibus.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Haec est gratia apud DEUM, si benefacientes & patientes sustinetis. Falsum est ergò, quod Papa docet, patientiam & reliquas piorum virtutes ex condigno mereri coelestia praemia. Gratia enim ac merces ex gratia opponuntur mercedi ex debito, sive mercedi meriti. Rom. 4. v. 4.

2. Christus passus est pro nobis, non tantùm propter nos & in nostram utilitatem, sed etiam pro nobis ac nostro loco, quia poenas peccatis nostris debitas sustinuit, & hac ratione pro peccatis nostris satisfecit. 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. quo sensu etiam peccata nostra in corpore suo super lignum dicitúr sustulisse, videlicet ut in sacrificium pro illis seipsum offerret. Falsum est ergò, quod Photiniani statuunt, Christi passionem & mortem non esse satisfactoriam & meritoriam, sed duntaxat exemplarem.

3. Christus peccata nostra pertulit in corpore suo super lignum. Ergò peccata nostra coram Dei iudicio efficaciter ipsi fuêre imputata. Falsum igitur est, quod Pontificii hanc peccatorum nostrorum imputationem Christo factam esse negant. Excipiunt, Christum ideò dici pro nobis factum peccatum2. Cor. 5. v. 21.& peccata nostra pertulisse in corpore suo super lignum, quia se ipsum obtulit in sacrificium pro peccatis nostris. Resp. Christum factum esse pro peccatis nostris sacrificium, praesupponit, imputationem peccatorum nostrorum Christo esse factam. Inde enim atque ideò Christus seipsum in sacrificium pro peccatis nostris obtulit, quia peccata nostra per imputationem in se translata suscepit. Probamus hoc 1. Ex phrasi Prophetica Es. 53. v. 4. & seqq. ubi Christus non solùm nostros dolores & poenas peccatis nostris debitas, sed etiam nostros languores & nostra peccata tulisse aliquoties dicitur, ac emphaticè additur, quòd Pater coelestis fecerit in ipsum quem agmine facto incurrere iniquitates omnium nostrûm. 2. Ex phrasi Apostolica Christus non solùm dicitur pro nobis factus maledictumGal. 3. v. 13. quae phrasis respicit poenam peccatis nostris debitam, sed etiam factus pro nobis peccatum.2. Cor. 5. v. 21. quae phrasis respicit imputationem peccatorum nostrorum Christo factam. 3. Ex collatione huius loci Petrini cum loco Apostolico Hebr. 7. v. 27. Ut enim hoc loco dicitur, quod Christus in corpore suo ἀνένεγκεν ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, ita ibi dicitur ἑαυτὸν ἀνένεγκας. Ergò quando crucem ascendit, non solùm se ipsum in sacrificium DEO oblaturus ascendit, sed etiam peccata nostra sibi imposita & imputata in crucem secum ascendere fecit, ut Syrus hoc loco notanter reddidit, atque ea unà cum corpore suo, & in corpore suo tanquam grande onus sibi impositum in crucem sustulit. Athanas. orat. 4. contra Arian. efferens peccata nostra in crucem unà cum corpore suo. 4. Ex dicto Iohannis Baptistae Ioh. 1. v. 29.Eccè agnus DEIὁ αἴρωνpeccatum mundi. Significat autem αἴρειν non solùm tollere & è medio auferre, sed etiam in se recipere & Dortare. 5. Ex versione Graeca Esai. 53. v. 4. ubi in textu Hebraeo dicitur. Verè languores nostros ipse tulit, & dotores nostros ipse portavit. Sed LXX. interpretes reddiderunt. Ipse peccata nostra portat & pro nobis dolet, peccatorum imputationem & poenarum tolerationem tanquam antecedens & consequens pulcherrimè coniungentes. 6. Ex typo hirci emissarii Lev. 16. v. 21.Sacerdos positâ utraque manu super caput hirci confiteatur omnes iniquitates filiorum Israel, & universa delicta atque peccata eorum, quae imponens capiti eius emittet illum per hominem paratum in desertum.v. 22. cumque sic portaverit omnes iniquitates eorum in terram solitariam. 7. Chrysostomus in 2. Cor. 5. & ex eo Theodoretus. Eum qui nihil deliquerat pro delinquentibus supplicio affici permisit. Atqui id non dixit, sed aliud multò maius. Quidnam? eum, qui non norat peccatum, qui erat ipsissima iustitiae, peccatum effecit h. e. tanquam peccatorem condemnari permisit, tanquam maledictum mori. 8. Christum factum esse pro nobis peccatum λογιστικῶς i. e. imputata illi esse nostra peccata, agnoscunt Ruardus Tapperus Decanus Lovaniensis art. 8. tom. 2. p. 27. Barradius tom. 4. Conc. Evangel. lib. 6. cap. 3. in sept. passion. praecellentia.

4. Sicut Christo peccata nostra imputata, ita iustitia Christi per fidem nobis imputatur, quia Christus dicitur factus pro nobis peccatum, ut nos redderemur iustitia DEI i. e. coram Deo iusti in ipso. August. enarr. 2. in Psal. 22.Delicta nostra sua delicta fecit, ut iustitiam suam nostram iustitiam faceret. in Enchir. cap. 41. Ipse ergò peccatum, ut nos iustitia, nec nostra, sed DEI simus: nec in nobis, sed in ipso, sicut ipse peccatum non suum, sed nostrum; nec in se, sed in nobis constitutum similitudine carnis peccati, in qua crucifixus est, demonstravit. Fallunt ergò Pontificii, quando Christi iustitiam per fidem imputari posse negant. Salmero tom. 15. p. 20. Bellarm. lib. 2. de iustificat. cap. 7.

5. Christus dicitur peccata nostra in corpore suo sustulisse. Ergò pro omnibus in universum peccatis plenissimè satisfecit. Falsum igitur est quod Thomas opusc. 58. de Sacr. altar. & Ambrosius Catharinus in lib. de incruento sacrificio disputant, corpus Dominipro debito originali semel oblatum esse in cruce, sediugiter in altari offerri pro quotidianis nostris delictis.

6. Christus dicitur peccata nostra in corpore suo sustulisse super lignum, quia poenas peccatis nostris debitas in cruce sustinuit. Falsum igitur est, quod Christum pro sola culpa & poena aeterna satisfecisse, pro poena autem temporali nobis ipsis satisfaciendum esse Pontificii dictitant. Concil. Trid. sess. 6. cap. 14. sess. 14. cap. 12. Bellarminus lib 4. de poenit. cap. 2.

7. Petrus dicit, Christum peccata nostra in corpore suo sustulisse super lignum. Seipsum ergò ac sua peccata Petrus includit, ac pro illis etiam Christum satisfecisse innuit, ut Beda in h. l. observat. Non ait peccata vestra, sed etiam se addito, qui peccata nostra, inquit, ipse pertulit in corpore suo super lignum. Falsum ergò est, quod Pontificii docent, renatos legem DEI perfectè implere posse. Quod si enim Petrus Apostolus peccata sua à Christo expiata docuit, utique se peccatorem professus est, & consequenter etiam legis divinae transgressorem.

8. Eramus sicut oves errantes. Ergò non potuimus nostris viribus in viam redire & ad Dominum converti. Falsum est ergò Pelagianorum & SemiPelagianorum, Synergistarum dogma.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lyranus verba Apostoli. Haec est gratia, si propter DEI conscientiam sustinet quis tristitias, sic explicat. Haec est res gratiosa, quia est supererogationis. Illius vestigiis insistens Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. sic commentatur. Haec est gratia, i. e. gloria vestra, unde explicans subdit. Quae est enim gloria. Sic Paulus gloriam suam esse ait, non Evangelizare, ad hoc enim necessitas praecepti DEI eum obligabat, sed Evangelizare sine sumtu i. e. gratis, hoc enim erat opus liberale & illustre supererogationis, & consilii, non praecepti.1. Cor. 9. v. 16. Resp. 1. Haec expositio directè adversatur scopo Apostoli. Gratiae enim nomen opinionem de opere supererogationis ac merito penitus excludit. 2. Adversa praeter meritum illata sustinere, non est opus consilii & supererogationis, à solis Monachis requisitum, sed est opus praecepti ab omnibus Christianis requisitum, quia serviilli, quos Petrus specialiter hîc alloquitur, non erant Monachi. 3. Aliud est gloriari in Domino, aliud gloriari coram Domino. Prius est Christianorum, posterius fastuosorum hypocritarum. 1. Cor. 1. v. 31. Gloriari in Deo, non nisi à solo Deo est. Haec proinde gloria non facit superbos, sed humiles; non contemnit proximum, sed diligit; non praefert se aliis, sed subiicit in timore DEI & caritate. 4. Aliud est gloriari contra homines, aliud gloriari coram DEO. Apostolus contra homines videlicet Pseudo Apostolos gloriabatur, quod ex Evangelii praedicatione non susceperit mercedem, coram DEO autem non gloriabatur, sed sese humiliabat.

2. Ex eo, quòd Christus pro nobis passus, dicitur exemplum nobis reliquisse, ut sequamur eius vestigia, colligit Cornelius à Lapide proprias satisfactiones. Notent hoc, inquit, molles haeretici, qui fidem Christi sequi volunt, non passionis vestigia, dicentes, solam fidem in Christum sufficere ad salutem, Christum enim pro nobis planè satisfecisse, quare nulla esse bonorum operum merita, satifactiones nullas. Audiant hi, quod hîc intonat S. Petrus & ex eo Gregorius in1. Reg. 9. v. 24.Remansit, inquit, quia non omnia nostra Christus explevit, per crucem quidem suam omnes redemit, sed remansit, ut qui redimi & regnare cum eo nititur, crucifigatur. Hoc profectò residuum viderat, qui dicebat, Si compatimur & conregnabimus2. Tim. 2. v. 12.& adimpleo ea, quae desunt passionum Christi in carne mea.Coloss. 1. v. 24. Resp. 1. Petrus non loquitur de afflictionibus sponte in satisfactionem pro peccatis assumtis, vel à Sacerdotibus impositis, sed de passionibus ab aliis illatis, quas exemplo Christi patienter ferendas esse docet. Alloquitur enim servos, qui ab iniquis dominis plagas praeter meritum tolerabant.

2. Vestigia passionis Christi sequimur, ac sequi debemus, non pro peccatis nostris satisfaciendo, haec enim gloria soli Christo competit, qui torcular solus calcavit,Es. 63. v. 3.& purgationem peccatorum nostrorum per seipsum fecit,Hebr. 1. v. 3. sed crucem divinitus impositam patienter ferendo. 3. Quod Cornelius dicit, Deum sanxisse, ut passionis Christi precium per passiones nostras nobis applicemus, illud sine ullo Scripturae testimonio dicitur. Scriptura nuspiam proponit passiones, vel patientiam in passionibus tanquam medium, per quod fructus passionis Christi nobis applicetur, sed soli fidei hanc applicationem ubique tribuit. 4. Debemus ergò cum Christo pati, & per crucem ipsi conformari, Rom. 8. v. 29. non ad satisfactionis complementum, sed ad imitationis exemplum. 5. Guilielmus Estius & Benedictus Iustinianus in comm. Coloss. 1. expositionem illam Cornelii à Lapide ex professo refellunt. Rectè enim monet Lyranus ibid. Passiones Christi dici dupliciter, uno modo in corpore proprio, in quo Christus sustinuit famem, sitim & mortem, & sic accipiendo nihil esse implendum: alio modo prout patitur in membris suis, quae sunt fideles, & sic Apostolum ibidem loqui. Ac Thomas p. 3. q. 48. art. 5. resp. ad 3. inquit. Passiones Sanctorum proficiunt Ecclesiae, non quidem per modum redemtionis, sed per modum exempli & exhortationis, secundùm illud, sive tribulamur pro vestra exhortatione & salute.

3. Ex eo, quod Christus dicitur nobis reliquisse exemplum, ut sequamur eius vestigia, colligunt Pontificii, ieiunium quadrage simale. Resp. monuimus superiùs, Petrum non loqui de operibus Christi miraculosis, sed virtuosis. Iam vero ieiunium quadragesimale pertinet ad opera Christi miraculosa. Martinus Delrius part. 1. Disquisit. Magicar. lib. 2. q. 4. quaedam in rebus divinis sunt credenda, ut Trinitas; quaedam admimtione honoranda, ut Christi & sanctorum miracula; quaedam imitanda, ut mansuetudo & caritas Christi. Velle imitari in illis prodigiosis effectis, animi stulti est ac superbi. Interim non negamus, exemplum temperantiae & ieiunii Christiani in Christi facto nobis propositum.

4. Ex eo, quòd Petrus probat, CHRISTUM esse ἀναμάρτητον,quia non fecit peccatum, nec inventus est dolus in ore eius, Pelagiani colligebant, nullum dari originis peccatum. Quòd si enim daretur peccatum originis, Petrus non potuisset ex remotione unius speciei procedere ad remotionem generis. Respondet. 1. Augustinus lib. 5. contra Iulianum cap. 15. Illud sanè magnum verumque dixisti, cùm posuisses testimonium Apostoli Petri dicentis. Qui peccatum non fecit, notandum esse, quòd iudicaverit Apostolus sufficere ad ostendendum, in Christo nullum fuisse peccatum, ut doceret, inquit, quia qui non fecit, habere non potuit. Omninò verissimum est. Profecto enim peccatum etiam maior fecisset, si parvulus habuisset, nam propterea nullus est hominum praeter ipsum, qui peccatum non fecit grandioris aetatis accessu, quia nullus est hominum praeter ipsum, qui peccatum non fecerit infantilis aetatis exortu. 2. Quidam respondent, testimonium hoc productum ex Esa. 53. v. 9. in quo de toto genere humano priùs erat dictum, v. 6.Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus, unus quisque in viam suam declinavit, ubi etiam parvuli comprehenduntur, qui peccati originalis labem habent, & in pravam viam declinant. 3. Hieronymus in cap. 53. Es. rectè monet, de nullo homine post protoplastorum lapsum dici posse illud Propheticum, quòd peccatum non fecerit, quia docente Iobo cap. 28. v. 4. nemo mundus à sordibus, ne si unius quidem diei vita eius fuerit super terram. Quamvis enim infantes nondum peccent προαιρετικῶς, tamen non sunt penitus liberi à peccatis actualibus, cum fomes peccati in illis non sit otiosus ac torpidus.

5. Ex eo, quôd Petrus probat, Christum etiam originalis peccati expertem esse, quia peccatum non fecit, colligit Salmero in h. l. Mariam esse sine originali peccato conceptam. Si regula Augustini vera est, inquit, ut verissimam & solidissimam puto, necessariò sequitur, B. Mariam Deiparam peccatum originale non contraxisse aut habuisse, cùm omne peccatum etiam actuale, imò veniale ab omnibus Patribus, & ab ipso Thoma removetur, ex quo coepit uti libero arbitrio. Quod si à levibus & minimis peccatis defenditur, cur non potiùs ab originali, quod facit irae filium, & praedam Daemonis? hoc argumentum apud me est magni momenti, neque novi, quomodo à contrariam sententiam tenentibus benè dissolvi possit. Resp. 1. Scriptura testatur, B. Mariam non caruisse peccatorum actualium naevis & infirmitatibus, Matth. 12. v. 46.Marc. 3. v. 20.Luc. 2. v. 23.43.49.cap. 8. v. 20.Iohan. 2. v. 4. Ergò contrario modo potiùs inferendum, quòd ipsa quoque fuerit peccato originali obnoxia. 2. Falsum est, quòd omnes Patres Mariam à peccatis actualibus liberent. Chrysostomus homil. 12. in Matth. importunitatem, ambitionem ac vanam gloriam ei tribuit, in-comm. Psal. 13.dubitationis gladium tempore passionis animam ipsius pervasisse, scribit. in comm. Iohan. 2.ambitionis ac gloriae humanae affectum illi assignat. Quibus similia inveniuntur apud Origenem homil. 17. in Lucam, August. in qq, v. & N. T. q. 73. Theophylactum in cap. 2. Lucae. 3. in Christo locum habet haec collectio. Christus non fecit peccatum. Ergò etiam ab originali peccato liber est, tùm quia Christus sine virili semine, ex peculiari Spiritus sancti obumbratione, est conceptus, tùm quia in aliis Scripturae dictis planè ἀναμάρτητος statuitur. Sed in Maria haec collectio non valet, quia neutra connexionis ratio in ea locum habet.

6. Ex eo, quòd Christus dicitur, in cruce peccata nostra expiâsse, ut peccatis mortui, iustitiae vivamus, colligit Estius, sanctificationem ac renovationem esse alteram iustificationis nostrae partem, ad quam velut finem prior pars, quae in remissione peccatorum consistit, ordinatur. Resp. concedimus, effectum & fructum mortis Christi esse non solùm peccatorum nostrorum remissionem, sed etiam nostram sanctificationem & renovationem: Concedimus & hoc, remissionem peccatorum ordinari ad sanctam vitae conversationem, tanquam ad finem, sed ex neutro horum sequitur, iustificationem nostram in sanctificatione & renovatione consistere. Distincta enim sunt beneficia Christi, iustificatio & sanctificatio: iustificatio consistit in remissione peccatorum, non in sanctificatione ac renovatione, quae est iustificationis consequens. Quòd si omnia mortis Christi beneficia pertinerent ad nostram coram DEO iustificationem, consequens fuerit, etiam resuscitationem ad vitam aeternam esse nostrae iustificationis partem, quia Christus morte suâ resuscitationem ad vitam aeternam nobis promeruit.

Observationes didascalicae. 1. In Christo Iesu non est servus, nec liber, sed omnes sunt unus in Christo,Galat. 3. v. 28.Col. 3. v. 11. Ergò Evangelium non tollit discrimen inter servos & dominos in politia, sed in Christo per fidem eos coram DEO exaequat. Etiam servorum, si fideles sint, conditio non displicet,Iob. 31. v. 15.

2. Servi heris suis debent obedientiam, quae etiam complectitur iniuriarum tolerantiam. Christus, fidelis DEI servus, obediens factus est Patri suo coelesti ad mortem usque crucis,Phil. 2. v. 8. eius exemplum fidelibus imitandum.

3. Duram quidem provinciam sustinent servi sub iniquis dominis, ὡς ἀργάλεον πρᾶγμ᾽ ἐστιν ὧ ζεῦ καὶ θεοὶ δοῦλον γενέσθαι παραφρονοῦντος δεσπότου, inquit Carion servus apud Aristophanem, de difficili & moroso Chremylo conquestus; sed quia DEUS hoc onus servis imposuit, aequo animo est ferendum, ac heris etiam durissima imperantibus & inferentibus promtè obtemperandum.

4. Iniuriae patienter ferendae. Haec tolerantia DEO grata est, quam etiam gratuitâ mercede remunerabitur.

5. Eadem est pars officii divinitus nobis iniuncti. Vocati enim sumus in hac vita ad crucem patienter ferendam, in futura vita ad gloriam consequendam.

6. Christus in passione exemplum patientiae, caritatis, mansuetudinis & obedientiae perfectissimum nobis proposuit, nobis ergò incumbit, ut ipsum velut viae ducem sequamur, & vestigiis eius insistamus. Matth. 16. v. 24.Luc. 9. v. 23.Iohan. 15. v. 20.Roman. 8. v. 29. Beda in h. l. Audis, quia Christus passus est pro nobis, & gaudes, quia pro te mortuus est, attende quod sequitur, relinquens nobis exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia eius, exemplum tribulationum, delitiarum, contumeliarum, flagellorum, dolorum, opprobriorum, spinarum, crucis, --nerum mortis.

7. Imitationis huius non solùm magna dignitas, quid enim magis honorificum, quàm Christo capiti per crucem conformari, & stigmata Christi in corpore suo portare,Galat. 6. vers. 17. sed etiam magna utilitas, qui enim mortificationem Christi in corpore suo circumferunt, in illorum corpore etiam vita Christi manifestabitur,2. Corinth. 4. vers. 10. qui cum Christo in hoc mundo moriuntur, illi cum ipso vivent in futuro seculo, qui cum ipso sustinent, etiam cum ipso aliquando regnabunt,2. Timoth. 2. vers. 11. & 12. qui conformes redduntur imagini Christi crucifixi, illi aliquando conformes reddentur imagini Christi glorificati,Roman. 8. vers. 29. ac summa omninò necessitas. Qui enim non baiulat crucem suam, & venit post Christum, non potest esse Christi discipulus,Luc. 14. vers. 27. Leo serm. 5. de nativitate Christi. Frustrà appellamur Christiani, si imitatores non simus Christi, qui ideò se viam dixit esse, ut conversatio magistri forma esset discipuli, & illam humilitatem eligeret servus, quam sectatus est Dominus.

8. Modus imitationis consistit in eo, ut exemplo Christi sub crucis onere constituti, exerceamus nostram ergo Deum fiduciam,Psal. 16. v. 2.Psal. 22. v. 1.obedientiam erga Deum spontaneam Phil. 2. v. 8.patientiamEsai. 53. v. 7.spem liberationisPsal 16. v. 10. invocationem, Hebr. 5. v. 7.

9. Interim imitatio illa in hac vita non est perfecta & omnibus numeris absoluta. Ut enim pictores & discipuli non possunt assequi ὑπογραμμὸν à Magistris sibi praescriptum: ita quoque ad fastigium virtutum, in Christo ad imitationem nobis propositarum, nunquam poterimus pertingere.

10. Christus non solùm docuit nos verbo, sed etiam exemplo; non solùm docuit, sed etiam fecit Act. 1. v. 1. sic veri praedicatores non solùm linguâ sed etiam vitâ doceant. 1. Tim 4. v. 12. August. lib. 4. de doctr. Christ. cap. 27. Habet ut obedienter audiatur, quantacunque granditate dictionis maius pondus vita docentis.

11. Solus Christus ex omnibus hominibus, & inter omnes homines est prorsus ἀναμάρτητος,Ioh. 8. v. 46.cap. 14. v. 30.2. Cor. 5. v. 21.Hebr. 7. v. 26.1. Ioh. 3. v. 5. nostra vero iustitia tùm habitualis tùm actualis non est perfecta, sed peccati labe contaminata.

12. Patientia Christi fuit purissima & perfectissima, ab omni vindictae cupiditate prorsus vacua; nostra vero imperfecta & immunda, iniuriis enim acceptis animi nostri statim ebulliunt vindictae cupiditate.

13. DEUS est iudex iustus & vindex aequissimus. Apud illum si iniuriam deposuerimus, innocentiam nostram asseret, & vindictam persecutoribus nostris irrogabit. Tertull. lib. de patient. Quantum licet patientiae, ut Deum ipsum debitorem habeat, quia si apud Deum iniuriam deposueris, ipse ultor erit.

14. Contrà verò, qui iniuriis lacessitus, protinus ad vindictam prosilit, in Dei locum sese evehit, ac quod Dei proprium est, ad se rapit. Deut. 32. v. 35.Rom. 12. v. 9.

15. Christi passio non solùm est lucidissimum virtutum speculum, & exemplum ad imitationem nobis propositum,Iohan. 13. vers. 15. sed etiam ac praecipuè nostrum meritum ac plenissima pro peccatis nostris satisfactio. Venit CHRISTUS in has terras, non solùm ut esset noster Doctor, qui & verbo & exemplo viam salutis nobis monstraret, sed etiam ut esset noster Mediator &

Redemtor, qui sanguinis sui precio salutem aeternam nobis compararet.

16. Christus ideò mortuus est, ut peccatum in nobis mortificaret; in Christi morte vetus noster homo crucifixus, ut in novitate vitae ambulemus.Rom. 6. v. 4. Ubi viget mors Christi ad peccata expianda & condonanda, ibi simul ad carnis mortificationem est efficax. Clemens Alexandrin. lib. 3. paedagog. cap. 12. Limitem (terminum peccandi) habemus crucem Domini, cui concrucifigimur, & à peccatis prioribus reprimimur.

17. Vera vita est, DEO & iustitiae vivere; peccato autem vivere, mors est,1. Tim. 5. v. 6. Bernhardus Epist. 105. Bona mors, si moriaris peccato, ut iustitiae vivas. Haec mors necesse est ut praecurrat, ut sequatur illa secura. Dum vivis in carne, morere mundo, ut post mortem carnis DEO vivere incipias.

18. Christi vulnera sunt animae nostrae sanitas ac medicina. Taulerus meditat. vitae Christi cap. 8. Ut nos viveremus, ipsum mori oportuit; ut nos exhilararemur, ipse tristatus est; ut nos sanaremur, ipse vulneratus est; ut nos mundaremur, ipse fudit sanguinem. Fusus est sanguis Medici, & factus est medicamentum aegroti. Ambrosius hunc locum Propheticum & Apostolicum, cuius livore sanati estis, allegans lib. de Spiritu sancto cap. 8. scribit. Plaga Christi nostra medicina est.

19. Alieni sumus per Naturam à via salutis, & errorum ac peccatorum avia sequimur, donec Christus ex dispersione illa nos colligat.

20. Frequens est in Scripturis nos conferri ovibus, ante conversionem quidem ovibus errantibus,Psal. 119. versu ult.Ezech. 34. v. 5.Luc. 15. v. 4. post conversionem verò, ovibus vocem pastoris sui audientibus.Ioh. 10. v. 4. & 27.

21. Qualis sit conditio nostra ante nostram ad Christum conversionem, pulcherrimè describitur hac ovium similitudine. Ovis est animal stolidum: sic ante conversionem destituti sumus verâ sapientiâ, quae in salvifica DEI cognitione consistit. Oves variis morbis sunt obnoxiae, & ut Naturae consulti volunt, tot morbis, quot homines: sic ante conversionem spiritualiter aegrotamus, ac sanatione animae indigemus. Oves errantes destituuntur pastore, & à grege separantur: sicante conversionem à Christo &

coetu sanctorum sumus separati. Nihil miserius perditâ ovicula, cui in faucibus lupi pereundum, nisi à Pastore quaesita gregi restitueretur: sic omnes essemus infernalis lupi praeda, nisi Christus verus pastor nos quaereret, & ad gregem suum adduceret. Oves aberrantes tandem salutaribus pascuis destituuntur, & fame pereunt: sic nobis omnibus fame pereundum esset, nisi Christus ad salutaria Evangelii pascua nos deduceret.

22. Ut in ovibus errantibus nostra miseria, ita in Pastore, ovem errantem quaerente, Christi pastoris bonitas & misericordia depingitur. Luc. 15. vers. 1. inde passim in Scripturis Christus vocatur pastor,Ezech. 34. v. 23.Ioh. 10. v. 11.Hebr. 13. v. 20.Ipse enim pascua in praesenti temporalium praestat gratiarum, ac pascua nobis donat vitae aeternae, inquit Beda in h. l. Sicut pastor oves ad pascua ducit, sic Christus pascit nos cibo spirituali & Sacramentali, pascit nos salutaribus documentis, & sanctissimae vitae suae exemplis, pascit nos Evangelicae doctrinae praedicatione, & internâ Spiritus sancti consolatione. Sicut pastor pro ovibus vigilat, sic & Christus vigilanti oculo nos custodit, ne infernalis lupus, nos ex ipsius manu rapiat.Ioh. 10. v. 28. Sicut pastor oves suas contra lupos & fures defendit: sic & nos sub Christi pastoris costodia ab incursu infernalis lupi tuti sumus. Sicut pastor morbidas oves sanat, agnos in sinum suum levat, lactantes ducit: Sic Christus spiritualibus ovibus eadem beneficia praestat. Esai. 40. v. 11.Ezech. 34. v. 16.Sicut pastor ovem errantem requirit, ita Christus idem facit. Ezech. d. l. Luc. 15. v. 1. Inde ad praesepe nati Christi, pastores primi omnium sunt vocati, quia scilicet verus animarum nostrarum pastor in mundum venerat, ac Christo moriente in Echinadis insulis vox audita fuit, magnum Pana esse mortuum. Euseb. lib. 5. de praeparat. Evang. cap. 9. Pan autem erat DEUS pastorum.

23. Christus est simul animarum nostrarum pastor & Episcopus: Sic Ecclesiae pastores & doctores sint Episcopi i. e. vigilent pro animabus auditorum, fidei suae commissorum.Hebr. 13. vers. 17. Isidor. Pelusiota lib. 1. Epist. 149. p. 39. Episcopus ex ipso nomine perspectum habeat, quòd speculari eum oporteat, atque omni ex parte oculum esse, omnia prospicientem, neque quicquam negligentem. Iohan. Hussus in h. l. Videant Episcopi, si & ipsi vigilant quasi pro animabus rationem reddituri. Bernhardus lib. 2. de consid. ad Eugenium cap. 6. Blanditur cathedra? specula est, inde denique superintendis, sonante tibi Episcopi nomine non dominium, sed officium.

4. Apostolus in versu praecedente Christum nobis proposuit ut Sacerdotem & agnum, qui se ipsum DEO pro peccatis nostris in sacrificium obtulit, hîc eum nobis considerandum proponit ut Pastorem oves suas, pro quibus in sacrificium sese obtulit, quaerentem, quaesitas gregi restituentem, restitutas verbo Evangelii pascentem, ac pastas in aeterna tabernacula collocantem. Epiphanius haeresi. 88. Christus pro toto mundo obtulit se, ipse victima, ipse sacrificium, ipse Sacerdos, ipse altare, ipse Deus, ipse homo, ipse Rex, ipse Pontifex, ipse ovis, ipse agnus, omnia in omnibus pro nobis factus, ut nobis vita omnibus modis fieret.

25. Conversione aliorum, qui instar ovium à grege Dominico adhuc aberrant, non desperemus, sed piis precibus à Christo fideli Pastore eam impetrare & promovere studeamus. Prosper in sent. Augustini sent. 184. Non est desperandum de malis, sed pro ipsis, ut boni fiant, studiosiùs supplicandum est: quia numerus sanctorum semper est de numero auctus impiorum. Qui hodiè sunt haedi, cras oves esse possunt. Qui hodiè Zizania, eras triticum esse possunt.

Summa Capitis. Exhortationis Apostolicae ad vitae & morum sanctitatem continuatio. Partes capitis duae sunt. 1. Exhortatio specialis ad personas coniugatas, & quidem primò ad uxores, secundò ad maritos, ab initio cap. usque ad v. 9. 2. Exhortatio generalis ad omnes Christianos, in quovis vitae statu constitutos, à v. 9. usque ad 19. Parti posteriori subiungitur παρέκβασις, digressiò quaedam de Christi beneficiis in & N. T. eiusdemque ad coelos ascensione, & ad dextram Patris exaltatione, à 19. usque ad finem capitis.

## 2:15
FOR SO IS THE WILL OF GOD, THAT BY DOING GOOD YOU MAY MAKE SILENT THE IGNORANCE OF FOOLISH MEN.

Connection. 1. He proposes a twofold argument for his exhortation. The first is sought from the will of GOD, to which he had also previously referred the hearers v. 13. Be subject for the Lord's sake. The second is from the consequent utility. Through this obedience you will stop the mouths of slanderers. Some, however, because of the particle οὓτως prefer to refer these words, so is the will of GOD, only to what follows, in this sense. It is the will of GOD that by obedience rendered to the Magistrate the mouths of slanderers be stopped by you.

2. The Apostle meets a silent objection. For lest anyone should object that unbelievers are not worthy that the children of GOD should have regard for them in composing their life and morals, therefore Peter warns that the faithful are bound by the command of GOD himself, so that they may remove and cut off every occasion of speaking evil from unbelievers, especially slanderers.

3. Bede refers it to leaders or governors, of whom mention had been made in the preceding verse. This therefore, he says, is the praise of the good, to which he says leaders are sent by the King, while the good, by acting well, use the ignorance of imprudent leaders for their own perpetual praise. The ordinary Gloss in the same way. So that those ignorant leaders, how you may use them for good, and through them earn praise, may not find what they may blame in you, while you even honor and suffer them. But the Apostle's sentiment is general, pertaining to any slanderers whatsoever.

4. The Apostle had said earlier that one must strive for honest conversation, so that in that which slanderers disparage Christians as evildoers, they may glorify GOD from good works observed in the day of visitation. Here he simply says that the faithful ought to render obedience to the Magistrate, so that by doing good they may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men. He expresses less, therefore, than he had said earlier, in this sense. If you cannot even at most obtain by your innocence and obedience that others, by the sight of it, be converted to GOD and glorify him himself, which outcome is often intercepted by the malice of the Devil and the obstinacy of men, you will nevertheless be able to obtain this, that the mouths of slanderers be stopped.

Exposition. ὃτι οὔτως ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, so is the will of GOD, i. e. this is the will of GOD, Matth. 7. v. 12.cap. 9. v. 33. ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν doing good, or by doing good to stop the mouths of slanderers. The Syrian rendered it, that by your good works you may stop. Τὸ φιμοῦν is formed from φίμος, which is properly a kind of bond, by which the mouths of wild beasts and dogs are bound, so that they may not bite; or of oxen, so that they may not trample the crops and devour the fruits, which the Greeks otherwise call πάριστόμιον or παραστόμιον,, the Latins a muzzle and a halter, which the latter indeed differs from a muzzle, yet meanwhile, when tightly constricted, it performs the duty of a muzzle, Deut. 25. v. 4.Esa. 37. v. 29.Ezech. 39. v. 11.Sirac. 20. v. 29.1. Corinth. 9. v. 9.1. Tim. 5. v. 18. Thence φιμοῦν,, with Hesychius as expositor, is δεσμεύειν ἐμφρόττειν, ἐπιστομίζειν, to occlude the mouth, to gather with a muzzle, or as Pliny speaks in book 18, chapter 19, to muzzle with baskets, and φιμοῦσθαι is in that way to be muzzled, and by metaphor to be struck dumb. Matth. 22. vers. 12. & 34.Marc. 1. vers. 25.cap. 4. v. 39.Luc. 4. vers. 35. & 39. The Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] he closed, he obstructed, he stopped up. Τὴν τὡν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν. Clement of Alexandria in book 6 of the Stromata, chapter 3, for ἀγνωσία reads ἐργασίαν, an occupation, so that the tongues of slanderers may not have that in which they might exercise their strength. But the Greek Codices constantly read ἀγνωσίαν,, in which way also the Vulgate Interpreter translates, and the Syrian, rendering it, the mouths of those who do not know GOD. Therefore, the Apostle attributes two vices to the detractors of the pious. The first is ἀγνωσὶα ignorance; the Syrian takes it determinately concerning the ignorance of GOD, others explain it concerning the ignorance of the Gospel. Thus, therefore, it would be signified that the cause of speaking evil in the unbelieving is that they are ignorant of GOD and His word, just as Christ also says concerning the persecutors, Iohan. 16. v. 3. These things they will do to you, because they have not known the Father nor me. It could also be understood concerning the ignorance of the state of the pious, in that sense, that slanderers, being less correctly informed about the life and morals of Christians, judge sinisterly concerning them. The latter is ἀφροσύνη foolishness, for because true wisdom consists in the knowledge of GOD, therefore the unfaithful are deservedly considered foolish, as being destitute of the true knowledge of GOD. It can also for that reason be called imprudence joined by the Apostle with ignorance, because those who are ignorant of GOD easily stumble in words and deeds through imprudence, and thus ignorance is the mother of imprudence, or for that reason, because those who weigh all things less prudently and exactly, with blind judgment blurt out foolish and irrational speeches against the innocent, just as the infidels used to slander those converted from the Jews, as if they were contemners of the Magistrate, prone to sedition and refractory to the laws, by which reasoning imprudence is the mother of ignorance. But because by ἀγνωσίαν τῶν ἀπρόεων ἀνθρτώπων are understood men ignorant of GOD, with the abstract placed for the concrete, thence the Syrian, having followed the sense, rightly rendered it, that you may stop the mouths of foolish men, who do not know GOD.

Latin:

QUIA SIC EST VOLUNTAS DEI, UT BENEFACIENTES OBMUTESCERE FACIATIS IMPRUDENTIUM HOMINUM IGNORANTIAM.

Connexio. 1. Duplex proponit exhortationis suae argumentum. Prius petitum à DEI voluntate, ad quam etiam antea auditores remiserat v. 13. Subiecti estote propter Dominum. Posterius à consequente utili. Per hanc obedientiam calumniatorum ora obstruetis. Quidam tamen propter particulam οὓτως verba isthaec, sic est voluntas DEI, tantùm ad sequentia referre malunt, hoc sensu. Voluntas DEI est per obedientiam Magistratui praestitam calumniatorum ora à vobis obstrui.

2. Occurrit Apostolus tacitae obiectioni. Ne quis enim exciperet, infideles non esse dignos, quorum rationem habeant filii DEI in vita & moribus componendis, ideò Petrus monet, DEI ipsius mandato fideles obstringi, ut infidelibus, praesertim calumniatoribus omnem maledicendi occasionem demant atque amputent.

3. Beda refert ad duces sive praesides, quorum in versu praecedente facta erat mentio. Haec ergò, inquit, est laus bonorum, ad quam duces à Rege dicit missos, dum ignoratia ducum imprudentium boni ad laudem suam perpetuam benè agendo utuntur. Glossa ordin. eodem modo. Ut duces illi ignorantes, quomodo eis in bonum utamini, & per eos laudem mere amini, non inveniant, quod in vobis vituperent, dum etiam ipsos honoratis & patimini. Sed Apostoli sententia generalis est, ad quosvis calumniatores pertinens.

4. Dixerat Apostolus superiùs, ideò honestae conversationi studendum, ut in eo, quod calumniatores detrahunt Christianis, tanquam maleficis ex bonis operibus considerates DEUM glorificent in die visitationis. Hîc simpliciter dicit, ideò debere fideles Magistratui obedientiam praestare, ut benefacientes obmutescere faciant imprudentium hominum ignorantiam. Minùs ergò exprimit, quàm superiùs dixerat, hoc sensu. Si vel maximè non potestis vestrâ innocentiâ & obedientiâ hoc obtinere, ut alii eius intuitu ad DEUM convertantur, ipsumque glorificent, qui eventus Diaboli malitiâ, & hominum pertinaciâ saepiùs intervertitur, hoc tamen obtinere poteritis, ut calumniatoribus ora obstruantur.

Expositio. ὃτι οὔτως ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ,sic est DEI voluntas, i. e. haec est voluntas DEI, Matth. 7. v. 12.cap. 9. v. 33.ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν benefacientes, sive benefaciendo obturare calumniatorum ora. Syrus reddidit, ut bonis vestris operibus obturetis.Τὸ φιμοῦν formatur à φίμος, quod propriè est vinculi genus, quo ferarum canumque ora obligantur, ne mordeant; boum, ne segetes atterant, ac fruges devorent, quod Graeci aliàs vocant πάριστόμιον vel παραστόμιον, Latini camum & capistrum, quod posterius quidem differt à camo, interim tamen arctè constrictum, cami vicem praestat, Deut. 25. v. 4.Esa. 37. v. 29.Ezech. 39. v. 11.Sirac. 20. v. 29.1. Corinth. 9. v. 9.1. Tim. 5. v. 18. Inde φιμοῦν, Hesychio expositore, est δεσμεύειν ἐμφρόττειν, ἐπιστομίζειν,os occludere, camo colligere, vel ut Plinius loquitur lib. 18. cap. 19. fiscellis capistrare, ac φιμοῦσθαι est eo modo capistrari, & per metaphoram obmutescere.Matth. 22. vers. 12. & 34.Marc. 1. vers. 25.cap. 4. v. 39.Luc. 4. vers. 35. & 39. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image]clausit, obstruxit, obturavit.Τὴν τὡν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 6. stromat. cap. 3. pro ἀγνωσία legit ἐργασίαν,occupationem, ut linguae calumniatorum non habeant, in quo vires suas exerceant. Sed Graeci Codices constanter legunt ἀγνωσίαν, quo modo etiam vertit vulgatus Interpres, ac Syrus reddens, ora eorum, qui non norunt DEUM. Duo ergò obtrectatoribus piorum Apostolus tribuit vitia. Prius est ἀγνωσὶα ignorantia, Syrus accipit determinatè de ignorantia DEI, alii exponunt de ignorantia Evangelii. Sic ergò significaretur, causam maledicendi in incredulis esse eam, quòd DEUM & verbum eius ignorant, sicut & Christus dicit de persecutoribus, Iohan. 16. v. 3.Haec facient vobis, quia non noverunt Patrem neque me. Posset etiam intelligi de ignorantia status piorum, sensu eo, quòd calumniatores de vita & moribus Christianorum minùs rectè informati, sinistrè de illis iudicent. Posterius est ἀφροσύνη stultitia, quia enim vera sapientia in DEI cognitione consistit, ideò infideles meritò censentur stolidi, utpote verâ DEI cognitione destituti. Potest etiam propterea dici imprudentia cum ignorantia ab Apostolo coniuncta, quia qui DEUM ignorant, in verbis & factis facilè per imprudentiam impingunt, & sic ignorantia est mater imprudentiae, vel propterea, quòd qui minùs prudenter & exactè omnia perpendunt, caeco iudicio sermones stolidos & irrationabiles contra innocentes effutiunt, sicut infideles calumniabantur conversos ex Iudaeis, quasi Magistratûs essent contemtores, ad seditionem proni & legum refractarii, quâ ratione imprudentia est mater ignorantiae. Quia verò per ἀγνωσίαν τῶν ἀπρόεων ἀνθρτώπων intelliguntur homines DEUM ignorantes, abstracto posito pro concreto, inde Syrus sensum secutus rectè reddidit, ut obturetis orastultorum, qui DEUM non norunt.

## 2:16
AS FREE AND NOT AS HAVING LIBERTY AS A CLOAK OF MALICE, BUT AS SERVANTS OF GOD.

Connection. 1. Certain of those who had been converted to Christ were abusing the pretext of a double liberty for the sake of sinning. Those indeed who had been converted from the Jews, because they were the peculiar people of GOD, to whom a special promise was made, that they ought not to be aliens and strangers subject to the authority of the Magistrate. Deut. 17. verse 15. hence those boastful voices John 5. verse 33. We are the seed of Abraham and have never served anyone. On account of this promise they desired to be free from the obedience, tributes, and laws of the Ethnic Magistrate. But those who had been converted from the Gentiles, through the liberty obtained by Christ, thought that they were liberated from the law in such a way that they could do whatever they pleased. To both, but especially to the former pretext of liberty, Peter opposes this exhortation, for he writes especially to those converted from the Jews.

2. He therefore meets a tacit objection. We are free, as being sprung from a free people and asserted into liberty by the Messiah. Therefore we ought not to obey the Magistrate, especially an Ethnic one. Peter answers by distinguishing between spiritual liberty and carnal license. You are indeed free, but that liberty, as being spiritual, ought not to be changed into carnal license, nor ought you to abuse that liberty as a cloak of malice. Through Christ you have been liberated from the servitude of sin, so that in the future you may be servants of GOD. Because therefore GOD requires obedience toward the Magistrate, therefore the liberty obtained through Christ by no means removes that obedience.

Exposition. Ὡς ἐλέυθεροι. Bede joins this member with participle άγαθοποιοῦντας in the verse immediately preceding. As free, he says, they do good, who the more liberty they enjoy among men, the more strictly, nay the more freely, they are subjected to divine service. But Chrysostom and Oecumenius more correctly connect it with the verb ὑποτάγητε in v. 13. For the construction in the Greek text does not allow the former, and the matter itself testifies that the Apostle is meeting an objection to the precept concerning subjection toward the Magistrate, not to the precept of doing good that was opposed. The Syrian rendered it, as sons of liberties, in a Hebrew phrase. Καὶ μὴ ὡσ ὲπικάλυμμα ἒχοντες τῆς κακὶας τὴν ἐλευθεριαν. Just as a foul and deformed face is sometimes covered by a beautiful veil, so those who under the pretext of liberty deny obedience to the Magistrate cover their malice with the specious veil of liberty. The Syrian rendered it. And not as men, to whom their liberty has been made a covering of their malice. ἀλλ ᾿ὡς δοῦλοι θεοῦ. Bede connects this part with the following verse but as the servants of God honor all. But it is more harmonious to connect it with the preceding. You are indeed free, but yet servants to God, and in that which you render obedience to the Magistrate, you serve God, inasmuch as He commanded that obedience, therefore being obedient to the Magistrate on account of GOD, you serve not men but GOD. But to serve GOD is so far from conflicting with liberty, that it is true and supreme liberty.

Latin:

QUASI LIBERI & NON QUASI VELAMEN HABENTES MALITIAE LIBERTATEM, SED SICUT SERVI DEI.

Connexio. 1. Quidam eorum, qui ad Christum conversi erant, duplicis libertatis praetextu ad peccandum abutebantur. Illi quidem, qui ex Iudaeis conversi erant, quòd essent populus DEI peculiaris, cui specialis promissio facta, quòd non debeant esse alienigenae & peregrini Magistratus imperio subditi. Deut. 17. vers. 15. hinc gloriabundae istae voces Iohan. 5. vers. 33.Semen Abrahae sumus & nemini servivimus unquam. Propter hanc promissionem ab obedientia, tributis & legibus Magistratus Ethnici liberi esse cupiebant. Hi verò, qui ex gentilibus conversi erant, per libertatem à Christo partam, existimabant, se à lege eâ ratione liberatos, ut quicquid liberet, agere possent. Utrique, praesertim vero priori libertatis praetextui Petrus hanc exhortationem opponit, scribit enim praecipuè ad conversos ex Iudaeis.

2. Occurrit igitur tacitae obiectioni. Sumus liberi, utpote ex libero populo & in libertatem à Messia asserto oriundi. Ergò non debemus Magistratui, praesertim Ethnico, obedire. Respondet Petrus distinguendo inter spiritualem libertatem, & carnalem licentiam. Estis quidem liberi, sed libertas illa, utpote spiritualis, non debet mutari in licentiam carnalem, nec debetis libertate illa abuti pro velamine malitiae. Per Christum à peccati servitute liberati estis, ut in posterum sitis DEI servi. Quia ergò DEUS obedientiam erga Magistratum requirit, ideò libertas per Christum parta obedientiam illam minimè tollit.

Expositio. Ὡς ἐλέυθεροι. Beda coniungit hoc membrum cum participio άγαθοποιοῦντας in versu proximè praecedente. Quasi liberi, inquit, bona faciunt, qui quò maiore apud homines libertate utuntur, eò arctius, imò liberius divino famulatui subiugantur. Sed Chrysostomus & Oecumenius rectiùs coniungunt cum verbo ὑποτάγητε in v. 13. Prius enim non permittit constructio in textu Graeco, ac res ipsa testatur, Apostolum occurrere obiectioni praecepto de subiectione erga Magistratum, non autem praecepto benefaciendi oppositae. Syrus reddidit, q. filii libertatum, phrasi Hebraeâ. Καὶ μὴ ὡσ ὲπικάλυμμα ἒχοντες τῆς κακὶας τὴν ἐλευθεριαν. Sicut foeda & deformis facies pulchro velamine quandoque tegitur, ita illi, qui praetextu libertatis obedientiam Magistratui denegant, specioso libertatis velamine suam tegunt malitiam. Syrus reddidit. Et non tanquam homines, quibus facta est libertas eorum operimentum malitiae eorum.ἀλλ ᾿ὡς δοῦλοι θεοῦ. Beda hanc partem coniungit cum versu seq. sed sicut servi Dei omnes honorate. Verùm concinnius est cum praecedentibus eam connectere. Estis quidem liberi, sed tamen servi Deo, in eo autem quod Magistratui obedientiam praestatis, Deo servitis, quippe qui obedientiam illam praecepit, proinde Magistratui propter DEUM obedientes, non hominibus sed DEO servitis. DEO autem servire tantùm abest ut cum libertate pugnet, ut sit vera ac summa libertas.

## 2:17
HONOR ALL. LOVE THE BROTHERHOOD. FEAR GOD. HONOR THE KING.

Connection. 1. Some think that the Apostle is returning to the general exhortation concerning the honest conversation to be followed among the Gentiles proposed in v. 12., and is distributing the same into four main heads, as it were, that they ought to show honor to all, love to the brethren, fear to God, and special honor of obedience to the King.

2. Some wish that, being about to conclude the former special exhortation concerning the obedience to be rendered to the Magistrate, he wished to intersperse certain other special exhortations, related to the former, and to add other special precepts worthy of the conversation of Christians.

3. But the matter itself testifies that the Apostle is still engaged in the exhortation to render obedience to the Magistrate. He concludes this little verse by the repetition of the exhortation proposed in v. 13. Honor the King, because the honor to be shown to the King includes the subjection required in the same place. Therefore this is a brief conclusion of what immediately precedes, and because the Apostle joins the honor owed to all, the love to be bestowed upon the brothers, and the fear to be shown to GOD, with the special honor of obedience owed to the King, he signifies that neither can God be truly feared, nor can his right be rendered to each one, nor can civil society be preserved, unless the political order binding the Magistrate and subjects to one another is inviolably kept, and the obedience owed to the Magistrate is rendered.

4. The Apostle also signifies that that honor of obedience, which is owed and deferred to Kings, ought to arise from the true fear of God and the love of men, and therefore is perpetually joined with them. He who truly and from the heart fears God, the author of the Magistrate, he also will not deny the honor of obedience to the King or Magistrate, because GOD has commanded this honor to be deferred to the King. Conversely, he who loves his brothers, and embraces the whole human race with the affection of humanity, benevolence, and love that is fitting, he likewise will not deny the honor of obedience to the Magistrate, because the Magistrate is instituted for the salvation of the human race and the advantage of the brothers, i.e., the Church. 1. Tim. 2. v. 1. & 2.

5. The Apostle joins such propositions, which in appearance seem to fight, but in reality are most excellently joined and connected among themselves, so that one cannot subsist without the other. They seem to fight in the first appearance, the honor owed to all, and the honor owed to the King alone; the fear of God and the honor of the King; the love of the brotherhood and the honor of the King, but if we weigh all these with an accurate balance of the mind according to the norm of the divine word, fraternal charity, the fear of God, and the obedience to be rendered to the Magistrate are joined to one another in an inseparable bond.

Exposition. 1. Πάντας τιμήσατε. The Jews despised the gentiles Rom. 14. v. 3. and among the Jews themselves the rich despised the poor, Iacob. 2. v. 3. the Apostle opposes a remedy to this evil, saying honor all i. e. Reverently acknowledge the gifts of God in others, think well and honorably of all, honor even those who are inferior to you either by reason of gifts or by reason of status, and thus preserve mutual concord, because nothing is more adverse to concord than contempt of the neighbor. A parallel passage exists Rom. 12. v. 10. τῆ τιμῆ άλλήλους προηγούμενοι. Phil. 2. v. 3.In humility let each esteem others better than themselves.

2. Τήν άδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε. The name of the brotherhood is taken collectively for the whole multitude of brothers, just as nobility is used for the whole assembly of nobles. The Apostle uses this word in the same signification in chapter 5 of this Epistle v. 9., whence the Syrian rightly rendered it, Love your brothers. He understands brothers, however, not with respect to carnal generation, but with respect to spiritual regeneration, concerning which he had said C. 1. v. 23., being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, etc. Therefore he repeats the precept φιλαδελφίας, proposed in the same place v. 22., and commands that the union of Christians, as brothers in Christ, must be fostered in a special way by the duties of charity. Hence this precept is subjoined to the preceding one, as a special to a general; we ought to honor and love all men, meanwhile embracing the Church and the citizens of the Church with a special love, and rendering our love attested by brotherly duties. Gal. 6. v. 10. Let us work good unto all, but especially unto those who are of the household of the faith. A passage parallel to this one of ours exists Rom. 12. v. 10. τῆ φιλαδελφὶα εἰς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι, which φιλαδελφίας precept is joined in that same place with the precept concerning attributing honor to others. Bede thinks this precept concerning loving the brothers pertains to depressing pride in the minds of superiors. To love the brotherhood, he says, he commands the free, so that they may also recall that those who are subject to them by temporal condition have been made brothers to them in Christ. Cornelius à Lapide explains this Apostolic precept thus, that the pious ought to love and frequent the assembly and gathering of the faithful for common prayers, sermons, and Synaxes Hebr. 10. v. 25.. But it is manifest φιλαδελφίαν that it is commanded by the Apostle.

3. Τὸν θεὸν φοβεῖσθε The Syrian rendered it, fear GOD. By the name of fear, some establish that the entire worship of GOD, indeed the whole study of piety is comprehended, namely both the true acknowledgment of GOD, and filial trust, and serious invocation of GOD; and likewise the acknowledgment of our infirmity, and serious humiliation before GOD, as also charity toward the neighbor, and all kinds of duties owed to Him. But the name of fear is more rightly taken in a special signification concerning filial fear and reverence, which GOD of all our actions he acknowledges as inspector, and reveres him as the supreme Lord and judge. The Apostle inserts this precept, however, so that he may establish certain limits of subjection and honor owed to the Magistrate, and teach that one must obey GOD rather than men, Acts 5. verse 29. Therefore, if the Magistrate commands something that is contrary to the will of GOD, he intimates that we ought to be recalled from it by the fear of him who is King of Kings, and Lord of lords,1. Tim. 6. verse 15.

4. Τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε. The Vulgate rendered it. Honor the King. But in the Greek it is the same verb as the one above in the first special precept. πάντας τιμήσατε, τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε, just as the Syrian also has the verb [consult facsimile image] in both places. A special honor is understood, however, as owed to the King, indeed to all Magistrates, namely the honor of compliance, for then Magistrates are honored in the due manner, when the excellence of the office, to which they have been divinely raised, is acknowledged, and honor is deferred to them in reality, that is, both by obedience toward the laws promulgated by the Magistrate, and by the payment of tributes.

Q. in this place. 1. Why does Peter call Magistrates a human κτίσιν? Ans. 1. By reason of the subject, because from men, and thus from the common lot of men, they are divinely chosen and raised to the dignity and power of a Magistrate. 2. By reason of the instrumental cause, because they are mostly raised through men to the principate which they bear, especially if they are inferior Magistrates. 3. By reason of the term to which, because the power of the Magistrate was instituted for the benefit of human society, and is still preserved for the same end. Luth. vol. 2. Ien. Germ. fol. 181. Ubrigkeit wird weltliche Ordnung genennet/weil solcher Stand zu menschliche/weltliche/politische Ordinantz von Gott geordnet/nicht aber in geistlichen himlischen Sachen/wie der Eehrstand.

Q. 2. Does the Apostle speak of the preceptive will of GOD, or indeed of the absolute? Ans. it can indeed be understood also of the absolute will, that GOD has so disposed, that through the innocence of the good the mouths of the calumniators may be stopped, and their slanderous tongues may grow faint, Tit. 2. verse 8. meanwhile the Apostle speaks properly of the preceptive will of GOD, GOD among other causes of good works also for this end [demands] their serious zeal from the faithful he requires that, by rendering obedience to the Magistrate and by applying themselves to good works of every kind, they should cut off every occasion of slandering from the enemies of the Evangelical truth.

Q. 3. Why does the Apostle begin with the mention of liberty? Resp. 1. That he may meet a tacit objection. Christians have been made free through Christ. Therefore they are not bound to obey the Magistrate. The Apostle answers that spiritual liberty ought not to be a cloak of malice and of carnal license. 2. That he may show that the pious ought to obey Princes and their laws spontaneously and liberally, not constrainedly and servilely. 3. That he may insert a new argument for the exhortation to obedience. The pious are freed from sins through Christ, that they may henceforth serve righteousness, Rom. 6. v. 22. of that righteousness the obedience owed to the Magistrate is not the least part. Therefore liberty itself ought to be an incitement to rendering obedience to the Magistrate.

Q. 4. In what sense does the Apostle not want liberty to be a cloak of malice? Resp. Some establish that regard is had to the white garment which the baptized received in Baptism. For it was a symbol not only of innocence and joy, but also of the liberty obtained through Christ and conferred upon the baptized through this Sacrament. Because to slaves, when they were manumitted and gifted with liberty, a white garment was given. Tertull. lib. 5. contra Marc. That which he says, with what liberty Christ has manumitted us, does he not constitute him the manumitter who was the Lord? For he did not manumit the slaves of others with a white garment. Augustine lib. 4. de Symbolo ad Catechum. cap. 9. gives this reason for the white garment given in Baptism, that the soul, clothed with the liberty of a new life, may be able to fight bravely against the Devil with divine help. The LXX use for the covering of the tabernacle of the covenant prepared from hyacinthine skins, Exod. 26. v. 14. cap. 36. v. 16. Just as those external coverings covered the tabernacle, most beautiful within, in which GOD himself dwelt by his grace: so the exterior conversation of the pious ought not to be a covering of interior malice, but rather of a heart sanctified and adorned with faith and other virtues, because it is a most beautiful temple of GOD.

Q. 5. Why does the Apostle command that honor be deferred specifically to the King? Resp. 1. Because the King is ὑπερέχων, therefore also, as a certain chief species or part, he is taken out from the common number of the rest, and it is commanded that honor be deferred to him above all. 2. The honor owed to the King includes the compliance which the Apostle had already commanded to be deferred to him before.

There is therefore a repetition of the prior exhortation proposed in v. 13. 3. The King or Emperor at that time was not only a Gentile, but also covered in all crimes, and a persecutor of the true Church. The Apostle therefore repeats this precept concerning honoring the King with obedience, lest on account of diversity of religion, impropriety of life, and cruelty, he might seem to some less worthy of honor.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. The magistrate is a human κτίσις. But there is no power, except from GOD,Rom. 13. v. 1. Resp. The magistrate is called human κτὶσις by reason of the instrumental cause, because he is for the most part constituted by men.
