But because ulcers and apostemes did not have a place in the body of Christ, therefore the first signification has no place here it has, in which it is used for a bruise, that is, a swelling rising from a blow, or the trace of a blow on the skin. The same is signified by the Greeks μώλωψ, whence πληγὴ μάστιγος is said to make μώλωπας Sirach 28. verse 18. when μώλωψ is ὁ ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς αἱματώθης τόπος.. Peter alludes, however, with this name to the bruises or weals of blows, which Christian servants were suffering from Heathen and unjust masters, saying this. That you may patiently sustain the blows and beatings brought upon you by harsh and morose masters, that highest benefit conferred upon you by Christ ought to move you, because for your sake he willed to be beaten with scourges in the manner of servants, that he might heal the wounds of your souls: on account of his holy weals you ought also to tolerate your own weals with an even mind. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] his spots, by which he understands the sprinkling of his blood, by which his whole body was spotted.

Latin:

QUI PECCATA NOSTRA IPSE PERTULIT IN CORPORE SUO SUPER LIGNUM, UT PECCATIS MORTUI IUSTITIAE VIVAMUS, CUIUS LIVORE SANATI ESTIS.

Connexio. 1. Quia Apostolus passionis Christi mentionem fecerat, hac occasione digreditur ad expositionem finis, propter quem Christus eam sustinuit, quem constituit duplicem, principalem & minùs principalem, Principalis finis est peccatorum nostrorum expiatio, minùs principalis sancta fidelium conversatio.

2. Utrumque hunc finem velut salutarem effectum specialiter accommodat ad servos, quos alloquitur, dicens, cuius livore sanati estis. Livorem & vibices nominatim commemorat, quia servi ab iniquis Dominis flagellabantur, ex quibus flagellis vibices reportabant. Monet igitur eos, ut exemplo Christi iniustè flagellati vibices patienter tolerent.

3. Verbo sanationis docet, servos fideles utrumque beneficium ex passione Christi consecutos esse, videlicet peccatorum remilsionem, & Naturae per peccatum corruptae instaurationem. Utrumque beneficium debere ipsis incitamentum esse ad sanctam conversationem, cuius pars non postrema est obedientia erga heros, & patiens iniuriarum tolerantia. Ideò enim peccata nobis propter Christum sunt remissa, & Natura nostra per Christum sanata ac renovata, ut inposterum peccato nuncium mittamus & iustitiae vivamus.

4. Potest etiam talis dari connexio. Dixerat Apostolus v. 22. Christum fuisse omnis planè peccati tàm originalis quàm actualis expertem, iam ostendit causam, propter quam Christum Mediatorem nostrum oportuerit esse sanctum, innocentem, impollutum, segregatum à peccatoribus Hebr. 7. v. 26. videlicet ut idoneus esset, qui pro aliorum peccatis satisfaceret, & passione sua totum genus humanum Patri coelesti reconciliaret.

5. Dixerat Apostolus, Christum pro nobis passum reliquisse nobis exemplum, ut sequamur eius vestigia. Ne quis igitur cogitaret, hunc vel solum vel praecipuum esse passionis Dominicae finem, ideò subiicit, Christum peccata nostra pertulisse in corpore suo super lignum. Docet proinde, non nudum patientiae exemplum in Christi passione nobis proponi, sed etiam passionem ipsius esse meritoriam ac satisfactoriam pro nostris peccatis, quin & hanc vim esse passionis & mortis Christi, ut carnem nostram mortificet, ut inposterum peccatis mortui iustitiae vivamus.

6. Opponit Apostolus servorum iniquis dominis subiectorum impatientiam, & Christi Servatoris, cuius fidem profitentur, patientiam: Illam significat esse multis modis noxiam, non solùm servulis ipsis, sed etiam aliis, quibus exemplo suo nocent: hanc vero dicit fuisse multis modis salutarem, non solùm ipsi Christo, qui per passionem intravit in gloriam, sed etiam toti generi humano, pro cuius peccatis satisfecit, ac cumprimis verè in Christum credentibus, in quibus peccatum mortificavit, ut inposterum iustitiae vivant.

7. Occurrit servorum querelis. Livor & vibices praesuppo. nunt plagas, verbera, contusiones &c. hoc ergò vult Petrus dicere. Non est quod de vestris plagis, verberibus, flagellis conqueramini, Christus itidem eiusmodi flagella & quidem longè duriora sustinuit. Nihil oberit saluti vestrae etiam durissima servitus, in Christo salus vobis reposita, ad quam passiones praeter meritum illatae vos promovent, tantum abest, ut eam intervertant.

Expositio ὁς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον, Respicit Apostolus ad cap. 53. Esaiae, quod etiam in praecedentibus citaverat. v. 4.Verè languores nostrosהוא נשאipse tulit, & dolores nostrosסבלםbaiulavit eos,v. 6.fecit Dominus incurrere in eum iniquitatem omnium nostrûm.v. 11.iniquitates ipsorumהוא יסבלipse baiulabit.v. 12.peccata multorumנשאtulit, ubi LXX. non solùm habent verbum Φέβειvers. 4.ἀνοίσειv. 10. sed etiam ἀνήνεγκενv. 12. quo Petrus hoc loco utitur. Respicit etiam ad dictum Iohannis Baptistae Ioh. 1. v. 29.Ecce agnus DEI,ὁ αἴρωνferens & auferens, in se suscipiens, & tollens peccatum mundi. Vocula αὐτὸς magnam habet emphasin, unde toties eam Propheta repetit. Verè languores nostrosהואipse tulitvers. 4.והוא& ipse vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras.v. 5.והוא& ipse afflictus estv. 7.iniquitates ipsorumהואipse baiulabitv. 11.והוא& ipse peccatum multorum tulitv. 12. Remittit autem nos Propheta, & cum eo Apostolus ad primam promissionem Evangelicam de semine mulieris contrituro caput serpentis, cui additur vaticinium de passione, & ipse insidiabitur calcaneo eius. Gen. 3. v. 15.Inimicitiam ponam inter te & inter mulierem, & inter semen tuum, & inter semen eius,הוא αὐτὸςconteret tibi caput, & tu conteres ei calcaneum. Significat etiam, Christum ipsum in persona propria, & quidem solùm pro peccatis nostris plenam satisfactionem praestirisse, sicut dicitur Esa. 63. v. 3.Torcular calcavi solus ego.cap. 43. v. 25.Ego egoהואipse sum qui deleo praevaricationes tuas. LXX. ἐγὼ εἰμὶ αὐτὸς.Hebr. 1. v. 3.purgationem peccatorum nostrorum fecitδι' έαυτοῦ,per seipsum; non obtulit alienum sacrificium, sicut Sacerdotes Veteris Test. sed ipse in corpore suo peccata nostra pertulit, non imposuit ea hirco piaculari, Lev. 16. v. 21. sed ipse in se ea suscepit, ut pro eis in sacrificium seipsum Patri coelesti exhiberet. Verbum ἀνήνεγκεν formatum ab ἀναφέρομαι propriè significat in altum tollere, sursum tollere, sustollere, ut sic ἀνήνεγκεν sit idem, quod ἄνωσε ἤνεγκεν,Matth. 17. vers. 1.Marc. 9. vers. 2. usurpatur de elevatione in montem, Luc. 24. v. 51. de elevatione in coelum. Remittit igitur nos Apostolus primò ad sacrificia V. T. de quibus verbum, ἀναφέρειν usurpatur Hebr. 7. v. 27.Iacob. 2. vers. 21. & à LXX. Interpp.

passim. Ut enim reatus peccatori debitus in V. T. transferebatur in victimam, quae peccatoris loco offerebatur: sic Christus peccata nostra, & maledictionem peccatis nostris debitam in se suscepit, ut peccata nostra expiaret, & maledictionem peccatis nostris debitam à nobis auferret. Inde Lutherus rectè reddidit. Christus hat unsere Su nde selbst geopffert. Secundò ad crucem, in qua Christus seipsum DEO Patri in sacrificium pro peccatis nostris obtulit, undè etiam disertè addit Apostolus ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον. Crux Christi fuit sublime illud altare, in quod Christus seipsum in sacrificium oblaturus ascendit, sicut Isaac in holocaustum DEO offerendus in montem sublimem ducebatur, Genes. 22. v. 2. & sicut V. T. sacrificia altari imponebantur. Inde etiam verbum ἀνήνεγκεν de hoc sacrificio Christi in ara crucis pro peccatis nostris oblato alibi à Spiritu sancto usurpatur. Hebr. 7. v. 27.εἁυτὸν ἀνενέγκας,cap. 9. vers. 28.Christus semel oblatusεἰ τὸ ἑολλῶν ὲνεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας. Tertiò ad locum Esa. 53. v. 4. ubi pro eo, quod est in Hebraeo, verè languores nostros ipse tulit, LXX. habent. Ipse peccata nostra pro nobis portat. Syrus emphasin huius verbi duobus vocabulis exprimere conatus est, [consult facsimile image]portavit peccata omnia[consult facsimile image]& ascendere fecit illa cum corpore suo ad crucem.[consult facsimile image] Syris est, portavit, gestavit, tanquam grande onus ac pondus, cum Hebraeis שקל significet, ponderavit, libravit. Significatur igitur, quod peccata nostra, tanquam onus gravissimum & nudo homini intolerabile, Christus in se susceperit, & cum, ac sub hoc peccatorum nostrorum omnium, sive totius humani generis onere in crucem ascenderit, quod onus tàm duriter eum pressit, ut in cruce clamaret, Deus mi, ut me dereliquisti![consult facsimile image] est idem, quod העולהascendere fecit,Marc. 9. v. 1.Hebr. 13. v. 20. à rad. [consult facsimile image]ascendit,Ioh. 7. v. 8.Matth. 13. v. 2. Significatur igitur, quòd pondus peccatorum nostrorum in se susceptum Christus nondum deposuerit, cùm lignum crucis ascenderet, sed quòd peccata nostra secum in crucem sustulerit, ac in cruce mortem sustinens, plenissimam satisfactionem pro illis praestiterit. Nec praetermittendum, quòd Apostolus dicat, Christum sustulisse τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, ubi vocula ἡμῶν est valdè emphatica. Non solùm enim significat, Christum non propter sua, quae non habebat, v. 22. sed propter nostra peccata crucem ascendisse, sed etiam mutatione illa personae secundae (quâ Apostolus in praecedentibus usus fuerat, v. 20. 21.) in primam insinuat, Christum non solùm pro servis, quos peculiariter hîc alloquitur, sed etiam pro tota Ecclesia, imò pro toto genere humano esse passum. Beda observat, quòd Petrus seipsum includat, ac pro suis etiam peccatis Christum in ara crucis mortuum esse asserat. Cum supra, inquit, ad servos specialiter fecerit sermonem, nunc generaliter admonet, ut etiam Domini in memoriam revocent, quid pro illis DEUS & Dominus sustinuerit. Imò totam Ecclesiam instruit, quid pro eius liberatione suus autor pertulit. Non enim ait peccata vestra, sed etiam se addito, qui peccata, inquit, nostra ipse pertulit in corpore suo super lignum. Indefinitam propositionem, quòd Christusτὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶνsustulerit, Syrus rectè exposuit per universalem, quòd omnia peccata nostra portaverit, quia Ioh. 1. v. 29. dicitur tulisse peccatum mundi, & 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. dicitur, propitiatio pro totius mundi peccatis. Quod autem peccata nostra dicitur sustulisse in corpore suo, non est accipiendum exclusivè, q. in solo suo corpore poenas peccatis nostris debitas sustulerit, sed per corpus συνεκδοχικῶς intelligitur tota Christi humana Natura, corpore & animâ constans, quia etiam sanctissima eius anima laboravit, Esa. 53. v. 11. ac Christus animam pro delicto posuit,v. 10.& in mortem effudit,v. 12. ideò autem specialiter sit mentio corporis, quia illud visibiliter in cruce, de qua Petrus loquitur, pependit & dolores, quos Christus in corpore sustinuit, magis in oculos & sensus incurrunt. Per τὸ ξύλον determinatè intelligi illud crucis lignum, cui Christi corpus affixum fuit, articulus adiectus ostendit, unde Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image] quod crucifixionem ac crucem significat, ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις απογινόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν. Verbum ἀπογινόμενοι Ambrosius reddidit separati, seorsim facti. Sed procul dubio Petrus eo exprimere voluit Paulinum ἀποθάνοντνες,Rom. 6. v. 10. ut enim ibi Apostolus coniungit, mortuum esse peccato, & vivere DEO, quod postea v. 22. exponit, liberatum esse à peccato, ac servum factum DEO; ita quoque Petrus hoc loco coniungit, peccato esse mortuum, & vivere iustitiaeἀπογάνεσθαι ergò hîc est è medio tolli, defungi, quasi dicas defieri, significatione eâ, quâ hoc verbum opponitur τῷ fieri, ac τῷ vivere, ut subiecta antithesis ostendit. Dativus ἁμαρτίαις hîc exprimit rem, cui aliquid adimitur, significatur enim, quòd peccatis simus mortui, i. e. dominio & iugo eorum exemti, ne illud ampliùs in nobis dominetur & vivat, nec nos illi vivamus, sed iustitiae, ad quam Christus suâ morte nos reformavit. Quando autem Apostolus hoc loco dicit, Christum ideò pro peccatis nostris in ara crucis mortuum, ut peccatis mortui, iustitiae vivamus, significat, Christum non solùm ideò in cruce mortuum, ut peccata nostra expiaret, eorumque condonationem nobis impetraret, quod beneficium pertinet ad iustificationem & regenerationem, sed etiam ut peccatum in nobis mortificaret, & ad vitam iustitiae & sanctae conversationis nos reformaret, quod beneficium pertinet ad sanctificationem & renovationem. Repetit etiam principalem propositionem, ac tacitam proponit exhortationem, ut quia per Christum, & in Christo sumus peccatis mortui, id est, à peccatorum reatu ac dominio liberati, inposterum nihil commercii cum peccato habeamus, sed iustitiae vivamus, hoc est, opera iustitiae exerceamus, cùmque servorum erga dominos obedientia, & in perferendis iniuriis patientia illius iustitiae quaedam pars sit, ideò hoc ipso eos ad obedientiam & patientiam hortatur. οὗν τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἰάθητε. Desumtum hoc ex Esa. 53. vers. 5.In livore eius medicatum est nobis, hoc est, livor eius fuit nobis sanitas. LXX. μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν Petrus pronomen relativum bis repetit οὗ τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ, per usitatum Hebraeis pleonasmum, ac primam personam mutat in secundam, quia generalem Prophetae sententiam specialiter applicat ad eos, ad quos scribit. Voculam livoris Glossa interlinearis inscitè accipit de invidia Iudaeorum; livore eius sanati estis, inquit, vel carne eius facta livida in passione, vel quia pro sola invidia Iudaei eum morti adiudioarunt. Petrus enim hîc non agit de Iudaeorum invidia, sed de vulneribus ac plagis, quas Christus in corpore suo sustinuit. Hebraeum חבורה quo Propheta utitur, significat livorem, ulcus aut apostema, in quo collectus est sanguis, aut sanies à rad. חברconsociatus, collectus fuit.Genes. 4. v. 23.Exod. 21. v. 25.Psalm. 38. v. 6.Esa. 1. v. 6. Quia vero in corpore Christi ulcera & apostemata locum non habuerunt, ideò prima significatio hic locum habet, quâ usurpatur pro livore, id est, tumore ex plaga surgente, sive vestigio plagae in cute. Idem significat Graecis μώλωψ, unde πληγὴ μάστιγος dicitur facere μώλωπαςSirac. 28. vers. 18. cùm μώλωψ sit ὁ ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς αἱματώθης τόπος. Alludit autem Petrus hoc nomine ad livores seu vibices plagarum, quas servi Christiani patiebantur ab Ethnicis & iniquis dominis, hoc dicens. Ut plagas & verbera à duris & morosis dominis illata patienter sustineatis, permovere vos debet summum illud beneficium à Christo in vos collatum, quod propter vos more servorum flagris caedi voluerit, ut animarum vestrarum vulnera sanaret: propter illius sanctas vibices etiam vestras vibices aequo animo tolerare debetis. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] maculis eius, per quas intelligit aspersionem sanguinis eius, quo totum eius corpus fuit maculatum.

## 2:25
FOR YOU WERE AS SHEEP GOING ASTRAY, BUT YOU ARE NOW CONVERTED TO THE SHEPHERD AND BISHOP OF YOUR SOULS.

Connection. 1. Because the Apostle in the preceding words had brought forward some sayings concerning the passion of Christ from chapter 53 of Isaiah, on this occasion he also brings forward certain things from verse 6 of that chapter, in which the most miserable condition of the whole human race, for whose sins Christ suffered, is described. All we like sheep have gone astray, we have turned every one to his own way.

2. The Apostle adds, however, that they are converted to the true Shepherd of souls, Christ, and thus he brings a new argument, by which he recalls not only servants, but in general all Christians, from impatience and the desire for private vengeance. Before conversion you committed many things, which by no means became the pious, but after you were truly converted to Christ, it is just that you conduct yourselves worthy of your calling and conversion. Eph. 4. v. 1. walk worthy of the vocation wherewith you are called.

3. Luther gives this reason for the connection. We once stuck in the same mire of misery in which those who afflict you are established. The Heathen yesterday are destitute of the saving knowledge of GOD, hence they are deservedly compared to wandering sheep, and yet your condition was once the same. It is better therefore for their conversion to make vows to GOD, rather than to return curses for curses and to render evil for evil. He who converts you can also convert your masters.

4. Bede comments on this place thus. The Apostle touches upon the Evangelical parable, where the pious Shepherd, having left the ninety-nine sheep in the desert, comes to visit the one that had wandered. For what is said there, that having found it he placed it upon his shoulders rejoicing, this the blessed Peter has set forth here, saying: Because he himself bore our sins in his body upon the tree. Because, indeed, he wished so to redeem us, that he might have the tree, upon which he might take away our sins, hanging upon his shoulders.

5. Such a connection can also be established. Because from the immense and unmerited mercy of God you have been converted to the true Shepherd of souls, Christ, you who were formerly wandering sheep, therefore it is just that for the sake of gratitude you should henceforth conduct yourselves as obedient sheep, and piously and patiently serve in your calling Christ, to whom you have been converted. Christ is your Shepherd, you are his sheep; it is fitting, therefore, that you should imitate the example of your shepherd in bearing the cross.

6. He repeats the effect of the passion of Christ, namely the salvation of souls obtained through Christ, which he amplifies by the antithesis of their former miserable state.

7. Peter had said, that we have been healed by the bruise of Christ, now furthermore he expresses the disease from which we have been healed. For as wandering sheep languish and fail for want of good pasture: so, alienated from Christ and entangled in the byways of errors and sins, we did not know true righteousness, so far were we from obtaining it.

Exposition. Ἠτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα πλανώμενα. Isaiah speaks in the first person. All we like sheep have gone astray, Peter changes the first person into the second, so that he may accommodate the Prophetic sentence to his purpose, and direct it specifically to the servants whom he addresses. You were like wandering sheep destitute of a shepherd, torn by the thorns of vices, as the interlinear gloss has it, and wandering through the precipices of vices. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν. You were once turned away from GOD through errors, idolatries, and every kind of sin, which were distancing you from GOD Esai. 59. v. 2. but now you have been converted from your errors and sins to Christ, that true Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. Shepherd Christ he calls him, because he feeds us with the word of the Gospel in this life, and eventually leads us to the pastures of eternal happiness. He calls him Bishop, that is, Inspector, Superintendent, curator, and visitor, because he bears diligent care for our salvation, considering our necessities and infirmities with a watchful eye. By the name of Shepherd, he refers us to the prophecies of the O.T. in which the name of Shepherd is attributed to GOD or to the promised Messiah. Ps. 23. v. 1.Isa. 40. v. 11.Ezek. 34. v. 23.chap. 37. v. 24. By the name of Bishop, he refers us to the Prophetic passage Ezek. 34. v. 11. Behold, I myself will seek my sheep and will visit them, v. 12. As a shepherd visits his flock in the day when he shall be in the midst of his scattered sheep: so will I visit my sheep. where in the version of the LXX Interpreters the word ἐπισκέψομαι, is held, from which the name of Bishop is derived. Some understand King by Shepherd, because to feed sometimes signifies to rule, and Kings are called shepherds of peoples. But we are compelled by no necessity to depart from the customary meaning.

Latin:

ERATIS ENIM SICUT OVES ERRANTES, SED CONVERSI ESTIS NUNC AD PASTOREM & EPISCOPUM ANIMARUM VESTRARUM.

Connexio. 1. Quia Apostolus in praecedentibus verbis aliquot dicta de passione Christi ex cap. 53. Esaiae ad duxerat, hac occasione etiam adducit quaedam ex versiculo 6. illius capitis, in quo miserrima totius generis humani, pro cuius peccatis Christus passus est, conditio describitur. Omnes nos tanquam ovis erravimus, unusquisque ad viam suam conversi sumus.

2. Addit autem Apostolus, quòd conversi sint ad verum animarum Pastorem Christum, & sic novum affert argumentum, quo ab impatientia & vindictae privatae studio non modò servos, sed in genere omnes Christianos revocat. Ante conversionem multa commisistis, quae pios minimè decebant, postquam vero ad Christum conversi estis, aequum est, ut vocatione & conversione vestra dignos vos geratis. Eph. 4. v. 1. dignè ambuletis vocatione, quâ vocati estis.

3. Lutherus hanc tradit connexionis rationem. In eodem olim miseriae luto haesimus, in quo illi, qui vos affligunt, constituti sunt. Destituuntur heri Ethnici salutari DEI cognitione, inde meritò comparantur ovibus errabundis, atqui eadem fuit olim etiam vestra conditio. Satius igitur est pro conversione eorum ad DEUM vota facere, quàm maledicta maledictis regerere ac mala pro malis reddere. Qui vos convertit, etiam dominos vestros convertere potest.

4. Beda in h. l. sic commentatur. Tangit Apostolus Evangelicam parabolam, ubi pius Pastor relictis nonaginta novem ovibus in deserto venit visitare unam, quae erraverat. Nam quod ibi dictum est, quia hanc inventam imposuerit in humeros suos gaudens, hoc isthic beatus Petrus praemisit dicens. Quia peccata nostra ipse portavit in corpore suo super lignum. Quia nimirum ita nos redimere voluit, ut lignum, in quo peccata nostra tolleret, pendens in humeris haberet.

5. Potest etiam talis statui connexio. Quia ex immensa & indebita Dei misericordia ad verum animarum Pastorem Christum conversi estis, qui priùs eratis oves errantes, ideò aequum est, ut gratitudinis causa inposterum vos geratis, ut oves obedientes, ac piè & patienter in vocatione vestra Christo, ad quem conversi estis, serviatis. Christus Pastor vester est, vos illius oves, decet igitur ut pastoris vestri exemplum in cruce ferenda imitemini.

6. Effectum passionis, Christi repetit, videl. salutem animarum per Christum partam, quam amplificat antithesi pristini status miseri.

7. Dixerat Petrus, nos livore Christi sanatos esse, iam porrò exprimit morbum à quo sanati sumus. Ut enim oves errantes inopiâ boni pabuli languescunt ac deficiunt: sic à Christo alieni & errorum ac peccatorum aviis impliciti veram iustitiam nesciebamus, tantùm abest, ut eam obtineremus.

Expositio. Ἠτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα πλανώμενα. Esaias loquitur in prima persona. Omnes nos tanquam oves erravimus, Petrus primam personam mutat in secundam, ut sententiam Propheticam instituto suo accommodet, ac specialiter ad servos, quos alloquitur, dirigat. Eratis sicut oves errantes destituti pastore, dilacerati spinis vitiorum, ut habet glossa interlinearis ac per abrupta vitiorum vagantes.Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπιστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν ποιμένα καὶ ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν.Aversi olim fuistis à DEO per errores, idololatrias & omnis generis peccata, quae vos elongabant à DEOEsai. 59. v. 2.nunc vero ab erroribus & peccatis vestris conversi estis ad Christum verum illum Pastorem & Episcopum animarum vestrarum. Pastorem Christum vocat, quia verbo Evangelii in hac vita nos pascit, & ad pascua aeternae felicitatis aliquando perducit. Episcopum eum vocat i. e. Inspectorem, Superintendentem, curatorem ac visitatorem, quia assiduam salutis nostrae curam gerit, oculo vigilante necessitates & infirmitates nostras considerans. Pastoris nomine remittit nos ad vaticinia V. T. in quibus Pastoris nomen DEO vel promisso Messiae tribuitur. Ps. 23. v. 1.Esa. 40. v. 11.Ezech. 34. v. 23.cap. 37. v. 24.Episcopi nomine remittit nos ad locum Propheticum Ezech. 34. v. 11.Ecce ego ipse requiram oves meas & visitabo eas,v. 12.Sicut visitat Pastor gregem suum in die, quando fuerit in medio ovium suarum dissipatarum: sic visitaebo oves meas. ubi in versione LXX. Interpp. habetur verbum ἐπισκέψομαι, ex quo nomen Episcopi deductum. Quidam per Pastorem intelligunt Regem, quia pascere interdum significat regere, ac Reges dicuntur pastores populorum. Sed nullâ necessitate cogimur, ut ab usitata significatione discedamus.

## 3:1
LIKEWISE AND WIVES BE SUBJECT TO THEIR OWN HUSBANDS, THAT IF ANY DO NOT BELIEVE THE WORD, THEY MAY BE WON WITHOUT THE WORD BY THE CONVERSATION OF THE WIVES.

Connection. 1. By the particle ὁμοίως the Apostle connects this exhortation directed to Christian wives with the preceding exhortation directed to Christian servants, and thus passes from δεσποτικῷ government to γαμικὸν. government.

2. Therefore, just as in the preceding chapter he had commanded subjection, reverence, and obedience to subjects toward even an ethnic Magistrate, and to servants toward even gentile masters: so he mandates to wives subjection, reverence, and obedience toward even infidel husbands.

3. In the preceding chapter 12. he had exhorted in general all the Christians to whom he wrote, that they should lead an honest conversation among the gentiles, he now requires it specifically from the faithful spouse.

Disposition. The Apostle confirms the exhortation to obedience, to be rendered by a Christian wife even to an infidel husband, from the useful consequence, which is the conversion of the infidel husband to the Christian religion.

Exposition of the text. ὁμοίως. The Apostle expresses his exhortation through λόγον συγκρίσεως. Just as I commanded subjects, that they should render due obedience to a Magistrate even if infidel, and to servants, that they should show themselves compliant to their masters even σκολιοῖς: so I command you wives, that you should exhibit due subjection and obedience to husbands even if infidel, whether they be gentiles or Jews.

CHAPTER III.

By τὰς γυναῖκας the Apostle understands specifically married women, as appears from the context. Therefore, in this place it is not only a name of Sex, but also of a certain status, namely, the conjugal one.

Ὑποτασσόμεναι namely ἒστωσαν. Let them be or be you subject, as the Syrian has it, for the Apostle frequently changes the person in exhortations of this kind. The middle voice of the verb in this place denotes a reciprocal action. Parallel passages to this Apostolic exhortation are held. Eph. 5. 23. & 25.Col. 3. 18.1. Tim. 2. 11.Tit. 2. 5.

Τοῖς ὶδίοις ἀνδράσιν, to their own husbands, not to adulterers, says the interlinear gloss; to their own, not to strange husbands. He therefore admonishes wives of chastity, to be joined with obedience toward their husbands. A parallel passage is held. 1. Cor. 7. 2.

Ἵνα καὶ εἴτινες ἀπειθοῦσι τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσωνται. By τὸν λόγον he understands the word of GOD, namely the Evangelical doctrine concerning Christ, λόγω ὑποστατικῷ. By τοὺς ἀπειθοῦντας τῷ λόγῳ he understands infidel husbands, who are such by incredulity, as they call it, positive, that is, to whom the word of the Gospel was indeed announced, but they were unwilling to have faith in it, whose mind is averse to the Christian religion, which is not unknown to them, and repugnant to the faith. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] who do not acquiesce or obey the word, who do not suffer themselves to be persuaded. Fulgentius Epist. 2. to Galla chap. 11. τῷ λόγῳ adds the word of GOD. Ἄνευ λόγου. An elegant ἀντανάκλασις. In the former place λόγος is taken for the doctrine of the Gospel, but in the latter for the public preaching of the word. Ioh. Huss. Without the word of public preaching. For the sense is that by the pious and holy conversation of Christian wives, infidel husbands are rendered well-disposed and affected toward the Christian religion, even if they do not hear the preaching of the Gospel. Some refer to the wives, in this sense, even if the wives themselves do not force the doctrine of the Gospel upon them, for the reason that husbands bear it with annoyance to be taught by wives. But it is more correctly taken generally concerning the public preaching of the Evangelical word, from which women are excluded, 1. Cor. 14. 34. 1. Tim. 2.

v. 12. & 34. and which such unbelieving husbands have rejected. The Syriac rendered [consult facsimile image] without labor, or what is more likely, it plainly omitted this προσδιορισμὸν, for that without labor, pertains to the word you may gain, since gain seems to be obtained without labor. The same adds to the word ἀναστροφῆς placed indeterminately ἐξηγητικῶς [consult facsimile image] through your honest and good conversations. The Greek scholia of Oecumenius have Without a word, that is, with every word and contradiction ceasing, by which reason it is referred to the men, that they have no word by which they can contradict. Concerning the word κερδηθήσωνται, to Christ is to be understood. For the sense is that it will come to pass that through the holy conversation of Christian wives, unbelieving husbands may be led to the Christian faith, and thus be gained for Christ, having been made, namely, citizens of the kingdom of grace in this life, and of the kingdom of glory in the future life, of which the former is called the kingdom of Christ, but the latter the kingdom of GOD. Ephes. 5. v. 5. Some understand to the Church, but the matter returns to the same thing, and both explanations can be joined in this way, so that the soul and salvation of unbelieving husbands, as a certain huge gain, may be acquired, and may accrue to Christ and the Church. By the name of gain is insinuated both the price of souls and the holy delight which those perceive who strive for the conversion of others. 2. Cor. 1. v. 14. Phil. 4. vers. 1. The metaphor seems to be taken from the Savior's parable about the servants who acquire gain through the talents entrusted to them by their master, Matth. 25. vers. 14. & following. Luc. 19. vers. 12. & following. Christ uses the same metaphorical form of speaking, Matth. 18. v. 15. & Paul 1. Cor. 9. v. 19. & following. Phil. 3. v. 8. The Syriac has the word [consult facsimile image] acquired, obtained. A place parallel to this one of ours stands in 1. Cor. 7. v. 16. For how do you know, O wife, if you will save your husband; or how do you know, O husband, if you will save your wife, where κερδαίνειν is explained by σώζειν.. An illustrious example is proposed in Monica, who, when she had conducted herself most modestly in her whole life with her husband Patricius in such a fervent manner, at the end of his life she gained him for GOD, and she did not lament in him, now a believer, what she had tolerated in him when he was not yet a believer. August. lib. 9. Confess. c. 9.

Latin:

SIMILITER & MULIERES SUBDITAE SINT VIRIS SUIS, UT & SI QUI NON CREDUNT VERBO, PER MULIERUM CONVERSATIONEM SINE VERBO LUCRIFIANT.

Connexio. 1. Per particulam ὁμοίως connectit Apostolus hanc exhortationem ad uxores Christianas directam, cum praecedente exhortatione ad servos Christianos directa, sicque à regimine δεσποτικῷ transit ad regimen γαμικὸν.

2. Ut ergò in cap. praecedente praeceperat subditis subiectionem, reverentiam & obedientiam erga Magistratum etiam Ethnicum, & servis erga dominos etiam gentiles: ita mandat uxoribus subiectionem, reverentiam & obedientiam erga maritos etiam infideles.

3. In cap. praecedente 12. exhortatus fuerat in genere omnes Christianos, ad quos scripsit, ut honestam conversationem inter gentiles ducerent, eam speciatim à coniuge fideli iam requirit.

Dispositio. Exhortationem ad obedientiam, marito etiam infideli ab uxore Christiana praestandam, confirmat Apostolus à consequente utili, quod est conversio mariti infidelis ad religionem Christianam.

Textus expositio. ὁμοίως. Effert Apostolus exhortationem suam per λόγον συγκρίσεως. Quemadmodum praecepi subditis, ut debitam Magistratui etiam infideli obedientiam praestent, & servis, ut heris suis etiam σκολιοῖς sese obsequentes praebeant: ita vobis uxoribus praecipio, ut maritis etiam infidelibus, sive gentiles sint sive Iudaei, debitam subiectionem & obedientiam exhibeatis.

CAPUT III.

Per τὰς γυναῖκας intelligit Apostolus in specie mulieres coniugatas, ut apparet ex contextu. Ergò hoc loco non solùm est nomen Sexus, sed etiam certi status, videlic. coniugalis.

Ὑποτασσόμεναι sc. ἒστωσαν.Sint vel sitis subditae, ut habet Syrus, frequenter enim Apostolus in huiusmodi exhortationibus personam mutat. Verbi vox media hoc loco notat actionem reciprocam. Loca parallela huic Apostolicae exhortationi habentur. Eph. 5. 23. & 25.Col. 3. 18.1. Tim. 2. 11.Tit. 2. 5.

Τοῖς ὶδίοις ἀνδράσιν,suis viris, non adulteris, inquit glossa interlinearis; propriis, non alienis maritis. Admonet ergò uxores castitatis, cum obedientia erga maritos coniungendae. Locus parallelus habetur. 1. Cor. 7. 2.

Ἵνα καὶ εἴτινες ἀπειθοῦσι τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσωνται. Per τὸν λόγον intelligit verbum DEI, videlicet doctrinam Evangelicam de Christo, λόγω ὑποστατικῷ. Per τοὺς ἀπειθοῦντας τῷ λόγῳ intelligit maritos infideles, qui tales sunt incredulitate, ut vocant, positivâ, h. e. quibus verbum Evangelii quidem annunciatum, sed illi noluerunt ei fidem habere, quorum animus est à religione Christiana, ipsis non incognita, aversus & fidei repugnans. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]qui non acquiescunt vel obtemperant verbo, qui non patiuntur sibi persuaderi. Fulgentius Epist. 2. ad Gallam cap. 11. τῷ λόγῳ addit vocem DEI. Ἄνευ λόγου. Elegans ἀντανάκλασις. Priore loco sumitur λόγος pro doctrina Evangelii, posteriore vero pro publica verbi praedicatione. Ioh. Huss. Sine verbo praedicationis publicae. Sensus enim est, Christianarum uxorum piâ & sanctâ conversatione maritos infideles erga Christianam religionem benè animatos & affectos reddi, etiamsi non audiant praedicationem Evangelii. Quidam referunt ad uxores, hoc sensu, etiamsi ipsae uxores eis non ingerant doctrinam Evangelicam, eò quod molestè ferant viri, ab uxoribus doceri. Sed rectiùs generaliter accipitur de publica verbi Evangelici praedicatione, à qua foeminae sunt exclusae, 1. Cor. 14. 34. 1. Tim. 2.

v. 12. & 34. quamque infideles eiusmodi mariti repulerunt. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]sine labore, vel quod verisimilius est, hunc προσδιορισμὸν planè omisit, nam illud sine labore, pertinet ad verbum acquiratis, cum lucrum videatur sine labore obtingere. Idem voci ἀναστροφῆς indeterminatè positae addit ἐξηγητικῶς[consult facsimile image]per honestas & bonas conversationes vestras. Scholia Graeca Oecumenii habent Sine verbo, h. e. cessante omni verbo, & contradictione, quâ ratione refertur ad viros, quòd nullum habeant verbum, quo contradicere possint. Circa verbum κερδηθήσωνται subaudiendum est, Christo. Sensus enim est, fore, ut per sanctam Christianarum uxorum conversationem mariti infideles perducantur ad fidem Christianam, sicque Christo lucrifiant, facti scil. cives regni gratiae in hac, & regni gloriae in futurâ vitâ, quorum illud vocatur regnum Christi, hoc vero regnum DEI. Ephes. 5. v. 5. Quidam subintelligunt, Ecclesiae, sed res eodem redit, ac potest utraque explicatio coniungi hoc modo, ut infidelium maritorum anima & salus, velut ingens quoddam lucrum acquiratur, & Christo ac Ecclesiae accedat. Lucri nomine insinuatur tùm precium animarum, tùm sancta delectatio, quam percipiunt illi, qui aliorum conversioni student. 2. Cor. 1. v. 14.Phil. 4. vers. 1. Metaphora desumta videtur ex parabola Salvatoris de servis, qui per talenta ab hero sibi concredita lucrum acquirunt, Matth. 25. vers. 14. & seqq. Luc. 19. vers. 12. & seqq. Utuntur eadem loquendi formâ metaphoricâ Christus, Matth. 18. v. 15. & Paulus 1. Cor. 9. v. 19. & seqq. Phil. 3. v. 8. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image]acquisivit, comparavit. Locus huic nostro parallelus extat 1. Cor. 7. v. 16.Unde enim scis mulier, si virum salvum facies; aut unde scis vir, si mulierem salvam facies, ubi κερδαίνειν exponitur per σώζειν.Exemplum illustre proponitur in Monica, quae cum in omni vita sese cum Patritio viro ita fervido gessisset modestissimè, iam in extrema vita eius lucrata est illum DEO, nec in eo iam fideli planxit, quod in nondum fideli toleraverat. August. lib. 9. Confess. c. 9.

## 3:1-7 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Whether by συνοικεῖν κατὰ γνῶσιν is understood the moderate use of marriage? Salmero and others establish it thus 1. Because as the Hebrews κατ᾽ εὐφημισμὸν καὶ ἀστεισμὸν describe conjugal intercourse by ידע he knew, Genes. 4 v. 1. cap. 19 v. 8. Jud. 19 v. 25. for which in the same signification the verb γινώσκειν is placed Matth. 2 v. 25. Luc. 1 v. 35. so the noun γνώσεως seems to allude to the same. 2. Just as the verb ὁμιλεῖν Judith 12 v. 11. in the History of Susanna vers. 53. is placed for conjugal intercourse, in which signification it can also be taken Prov. 5 v. 19. so the verb συνοικεῖν corresponding to it can be taken in the same sense. Nay, there exists a manifest place in which συνοικεῖν is used in that sense, Deut. 22 v. 13. so also it seems to be used, Deut. 24 v. 1. as also the cognate verb συνοικίζειν, Deut. 21 v. 13. so that Lorinus was false, who denies that the verb συνοικεῖν is found used in this signification in the Scriptures. 3. This Petrine passage seems parallel to the Apostolic saying 1. Corinth. 7 v. 5. Do not defraud one another, unless perhaps by consent for a time, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer. 4. Jerome book 1 against Jovinian cap. 4, Augustine in Psalm 146, Bede and Oecumenius in this place explain it in the same way. 5. Salmero adds a reason, but a very slippery one. Women are accustomed to study chastity more than men, therefore Peter commands that men in this part should defer to some wives. Thus therefore the sense would be, that wives are to be used chastely and temperately, not to be abused for superfluous, much less unspeakable and preposterous lusts, and at certain times on account of more serious exercises of piety one must abstain from intercourse. We do not simply disapprove of this exposition, as is evident from what was said in the place concerning Marriage §. 435, meanwhile we add that the Interlinear Gloss, Hugo, Lyranus, Carthusianus etc. more correctly explain this place generally concerning domestic conversation according to, that is, to be instituted according to that form of holy and honest life, which knowledge dictates must be kept. Thus therefore the effect is understood from the cause by metonymy, since knowledge drawn from the norm of the divine word is of all honesty and

for the sake of holiness. But especially the Apostle requires conjugal harmony, without which GOD cannot be rightly invoked, since quarrels, dissensions, and brawls are contrary to the fervor of prayer. Thus, therefore, this Petrine passage is parallel to the Apostolic statement 1. Timoth. 2. vers. 8. I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands without anger and disputation. Lorinus on this passage: Lyranus mentions that exposition (concerning rendering the debt according to conscience, not in the passions of desire 1. Thessal. 4. v. 5.) but he prefers another concerning domestic cohabitation, in which the woman indeed ought to be subject, but the man to preside according to knowledge, so that he may treat his wife as a companion, not as a handmaid, etc. The Carthusian agrees, so that discreet and circumspect men may act, and not scandalize and offend their wives, because they are more prone to evil. The mind of Gagnaeus and other more recent authors is the same, to whom I more willingly acquiesce, etc. Certainly, for the most part, husbands are more free and importunate than wives in demanding the debt. Guillandus on this passage: He prescribes the duties of husbands, repressing the arrogance, command, and tyranny of certain men, who shout, the husband is the head of the woman, therefore we have the power of life and death over every command, we can command our wives in any matter, even according to our lust, they must obey us. But the Apostle has placed a bridle on men of this sort, saying: Husbands, cohabit with your wives according to knowledge.

Q. 2. Whether by the honor to be bestowed upon wives is understood the moderate use of marriage? Lorinus, although he takes τὸ συνοικεῖν κατὰ γνῶσιν generally concerning the prudence by which husbands ought to preside over their wives and cohabit with them humanely and harmoniously, nevertheless understands the honor to be bestowed upon wives specifically concerning the moderate use of marriage. I will grant, he says, that these things are more willingly understood concerning coitus, and are honestly said by Peter, which our Turrianus also feels concerning dogmatic characters, just as the same thing is accustomed to be denoted by other honest words, such as the word of knowing Matth. 2. v. 25. Luc. 1. v. 34. The same reason applies to the word of entering or going in. Ps. 51. v. 1. He follows in this part Jerome, Bede, and Oecumenius, who likewise expound these words concerning the moderate use of the matrimonial act. He brings forward these reasons 1. because Paul 1. Thessal. 5. vers. 4. & 5. speaks in the same way. This is the will of God, your sanctification, that you abstain from fornication, and that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honor, not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles who do not know GOD, and

that no one should overreach, nor circumvent his brother in business, for God has not called us to uncleanness, but to sanctification, where honor signifies abstinence or the moderate use of marriage, business the act itself, vessel the wife, and both the immoderate use of one's own spouse and that of another is cautioned against, as Jerome explains in chapter 4. Eph. 2. Petronius and Plautus in the Poenulus use the name of vessel for the female obscenity, which the Apostle Paul calls weaker, less noble, and uncomely 1. Cor. 12. v. 22. 23. Hugo notes that it is called a cistern Isa. 51. 1. and a cavern. Prov. 5. v. 15. 3. To the exposition by which the moderate use of marriage is understood through honor, words of contrary meaning are favorable, such as shame Phil. 3. 19. (where glory signifies the impulse of lust, shame the shameful things themselves, which those who burn with lust in those whose god is their belly, that is, who gorge themselves) and ignominy Isa. 20. v. 4. Ez. 16. v. 7. Rom. 1. 26. and that which is recently known is named נחרפת reproached, from the root חרף Lev. 19. v. 20. The sense, therefore, would be that husbands ought to use their wives honestly and chastely. Although we do not simply reject this exposition, as is clear from what was said in the place concerning marriage §. 435, nevertheless we add that this member is more correctly taken generally, in the sense that husbands ought not to hold their wives in low esteem, and treat them as servants or slaves, but attribute to them the honor that is fitting, by acknowledging that they were given to them by God as companions of their life and bed, and therefore treat them humanely and kindly. Oecumenius adds a certain species of this honor, that husbands ought not to demand an exact account of those things which are entrusted to them in the family, nor prohibit them from alms. This is also a certain species of the honor owed, that because of the infirmities adhering to this sex they ought not to be despised, but their infirmities should be covered by conjugal love, and lighter errors should be forgiven. In the reasons brought forward by Lorinus for establishing a special explanation concerning the moderate use of marriage, some things can be desired. By τὸ σκεῦος 1. Thess. 4. v. 4. the body of each man is more correctly understood, which is the dwelling place and instrument of the soul, than the wife, for this is a general precept of chastity, concerning not only the married, but also the celibate. By τὸ πρᾶγμα business v. 6. the conjugal act is understood very absurdly. For the Apostle in these words no longer treats of the sixth commandment, but subjects the virtues of the seventh commandment, as the phrases μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐν τῷ πράγματι τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτού. manifestly show; he therefore prohibits frauds in contracts, so that you may not circumvent your neighbor in anything out of a desire to have more or through avarice.

The exposition of the Apostolic passage Phil. 3. v. 19. is also absurd; for by glory the Apostle does not understand the impulse of lust, nor by shame the shameful parts of the body, but that glory which the Pseudo-Apostles were seeking among the Jews with their blandishments and flatteries, or which they arrogated to themselves by boasting of their lineage and peculiar gifts 2. Cor. 11. v. 12., which he teaches will finally end in most shameful ignominy. The Hebrew נחרפת the Targum rendered אחידא betrothed. The LXX διαπεφυλαγμὲνη guarded, through the L. which passes from freedom to servitude, and even if it is taken most of all concerning marriage, it can be rendered, manifested or known to the husband, for חרף among other things also signifies manifested, uncovered. Thence Lorinus himself finally adds: If we wish to take honor in a broader signification, and this is true, the wife is to be held in honor and treated honorably in words and deeds.

Q. 3. Why are wives compared to vessels? Some bring forward a general reason, that by vessels creatures are understood. 2. Tim. 2. vers. 20. Some think regard is had to bodies, which are the organs of the indwelling soul, through which it exerts natural, vital, and animal actions. 1. Sam. 21. vers. 5. the vessels of the young men were holy. 1. Thessal. 4. vers. 4. let everyone know how to possess his vessel in honor and sanctification. Isidore of Pelusium, book 2, Epistle 4, adapts to this the Apostolic passage 2. Corinth. 4. vers. 7. we have this treasure in earthen vessels, which he explains not only concerning the mortal body made from earth of the preachers, in which as in an earthen vessel the treasures of the divine word are exhibited to men, but also concerning the simplicity of words in Scripture, it is more correctly explained concerning the infirmity of the flesh still adhering to the reborn in this life. It is answered most simply that wives are compared to vessels because by divine creation and ordination they are a help to the husband, which is before him Genes. 2. vers. 18., they are instruments divinely ordained for the generation and education of children, and likewise for the administration of family affairs.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Husbands ὁμοίως likewise dwell with their wives according to knowledge. But in the preceding exhortation directed to wives, the Apostle had dealt with unequal marriage, but here he speaks of such a marriage in which the husband and wife are Christians, as is gathered from the words, as fellow-heirs of the grace of life, and that your prayers be not hindered. Resp. B. Luther judges that the discourse is still concerning unequal marriage, According to this hypothesis, it must be established that the relative pronoun ὑμῶν is to be referred not to both spouses, but only to the believer, in this sense: You Christian husbands, dwell with your wives, even the unbelieving ones, according to knowledge, that you may be able to lift up holy hands to GOD without wrath and disputing, 1. Tim. 2. vers. 8. But if we should wish to establish even most strongly that the discourse is about an equal marriage, we shall be able to respond that the little word ὁμοίως is to be taken with respect to parity in marriage, but not with respect to the same profession of the Christian faith.

2. Husbands, ὁμοίως dwell with your wives. But subjection belongs to wives, and lordship to husbands. v. 1. Resp. Some explain the particle ὁμοίως as in turn, conversely. But the customary meaning can be retained, in which it is also taken in v. 1 of this chapter. Regard, however, is had: 1. To the conjugal bond, by reason of which husband and wife are equals and are bound to equal things. 1. Cor. 7. vers. 4. The wife has not power of her own body, but the husband. ὁμόιως Likewise also the husband has not power of his own body, but the wife. 2. To the equal weight of the commandment. Just as wives, by the ordination of GOD, ought to be subject to their husbands, so husbands, by the same ordination of GOD, should dwell with their wives according to knowledge, and use this lordship prudently and courteously. Bede on this passage: He says 'likewise,' provoking the husbands to imitation, because he had already commanded the wives above, saying, let the husbands consider your chaste conversation in the fear of GOD. 3. To the equal benefit of obedience. Just as wives, by their subjection and modesty, entice and invite unbelieving husbands to embrace the Christian religion: so husbands, by prudent cohabitation with their wives and humane conversation with them, gain this, that no impediment is cast in the way of their prayers.

3. Giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel. But servile subjection was imposed upon the wife as a punishment for sin Gen. 3. v. 16. on account of which she ought to fear her husband Eph. 5. v. 33. Resp. Masterly lordship is not attributed to the husband over the wife, nor is servile subjection imposed upon the wife toward the husband, but it is signified that, after the fall, the husband's rule will sometimes be harsh and troublesome to the woman. Nor do the fear, which the wife owes to the husband by the commandment of the Apostle Paul, and the honor, which the husband owes to the wife by the commandment of the Apostle Peter, fight against each other, because honor in the place of an object has not only a superior but also an equal, nay, and an inferior. Rom. 12. vers. 10. in honor preventing one another. Although, therefore, a wife may be honored by her husband through harmonious cohabitation, gentle governance, and prudent conversation, she ought not on that account to consider herself absolute from the subjection and fear to be shown to her husband. The love and honor of spouses ought to be reciprocal, yet neither weakens the lordship of the husband or the subjection of the wife.

4. As being co-heirs of the grace of life. But some women are not co-heirs of grace and life with their husbands, for the unfaithful are excluded from the communion of grace, and those persevering in sins from the communion of glory. Resp. It suffices for the argument of honor to be shown to wives that grace and life are offered to them no less than to men in the word of the Gospel, and that access to it lies open in this age.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. The Apostle describes marriage as a holy kind of life and pleasing to GOD, in which pious spouses can be co-heirs of eternal life. He also teaches that spouses can cohabit with one another in such a way that their prayers are not hindered. But the Roman Pope, who boasts himself the successor of Peter, speaks thus in the Canon Law. c. Whatever is blind. 32. q. 2. The presence of the Holy Spirit is not given at the time in which conjugal acts are performed, c. Marriages caus. & quaest. the same. Lawful marriages indeed lack sin, yet at that time in which conjugal acts are performed, the presence of the Holy Spirit will not be given, even if he who complies with the duty of generation appears to be a Prophet. c. Know 33. q. 4. Whoever renders the debt to their wife cannot be free for prayer, nor ought they to eat of the flesh of the Lamb. c. Nuptials caus. 32. q. 1. Scripture, on the first and third and fourth and fifth and sixth day, the works of each day being completed, said: And God saw that it was good. On the second day He withdrew this entirely, granting us the understanding that the double number, which divides from unity and prefigures the covenants of weddings, is not good. Whence also in the ark of Noah all animals, whatsoever enter in pairs, are unclean; an odd number is clean. The Roman Pontiff confirmed the Revelations of Bridget, in which lib. 1. c. 26. Christ is introduced speaking thus to spouses: When spouses come to the bed, then immediately My Spirit departs from them, and an impure spirit approaches. Gretser in Virgidemia p. 48. cites and approves the words of Pope Sixtus lib. de castit. To marry is of almost all men. Nothing gentile (excellent) It is to wish to exercise yourself in that which all do; and to have that which even the worst obtain, but to be silent about men, wild beasts also live luxuriously, and birds also mate, it is no great thing to have something in common with pigs and dogs, rather follow the life of GOD, and of His Angels. In these words the holy cohabitation of pious spouses is not obscurely compared by the Pontiff to the mixing of pigs and dogs.

2. The Apostle calls eternal life an inheritance. Therefore it is not given out of merit as a wage to servants, but out of grace υἱοθεσίας, as an inheritance to sons. Likewise, the Apostle calls eternal life grace, as Estius acknowledges in his commentary. Therefore it is not given on account of the merits of works, but out of grace on account of Christ, in whom GOD adopts us as sons, For if it is by grace, it is no longer by works, otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is by works, it is no longer by grace, because a work would no longer be a work Rom. 11. v. 6. A passage parallel to this one of ours is found Rom. 6. v. 23. χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν χριστῷ, on which Chrysostom, homily 10 on the Epistle to the Romans, comments thus. Eternal life is neither a debt, nor a retribution for labors, but a gratuitous gift of divine bounty. It is false, therefore, that the Council of Trent, confirmed by the Roman Pontiff, decreed in session 6, chapter 16, that eternal life is to be proposed to those who work well until the end, and who hope in GOD, both as a grace mercifully promised to the sons of GOD through Christ Jesus, and as a reward to be faithfully rendered for their good works and merits according to the promise of GOD Himself. Likewise: that nothing is lacking to the works of the reborn, so that they should not be considered to have fully satisfied the divine law for the state of this life, and to have truly merited eternal life. To the exception, that eternal life is given out of grace and out of merits at the same time, and that it is therefore said to be given out of grace, because those meritorious works, on account of which it is given, are gifts of grace, we have responded in its proper place.

3. Augustine, book 5 against Julian, chapter 7, refutes Julian the Pelagian from this Apostolic passage, who maintained, as often as concupiscence stirs itself in spouses, it is to be sated greedily and to reign securely. That he warned, he says, the Apostle, that each one should not possess his vessel in the disease of desire, you think is to be understood not of marriage, but of fornication, and thus you take away all the honesty of temperance from the intercourse of spouses, so that no one seems to himself to possess his vessel in the disease of desire, however much he may have been able to rage with lust in the genitals of his wife. For if any is to be held there you were able to consider the measure, and there to reprehend the excess of concupiscence, and to say that it was the disease of desire signified by the Apostle, and not improperly to deny that his own vessel was called each one's own spouse. Which word the Apostle Peter also uses in the same matter, where he warns that husbands should give honor to their wives as to the weaker vessel, as to co-heirs of grace, adding and saying: And see that your prayers be not hindered. Just as the Apostle also prescribes its times of praying for conjugal temperance, and according to indulgence grants that intercourse which is performed with a spouse, not indeed for the sake of offspring, but which is done with the intention of pleasure. Let Christian marriages hear this, not you, who wish that in them, which you defend, concupiscence should never be curbed, but as often as it has moved itself, it should be satisfied greedily, and reign securely.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Hugo gathers from this place, that vessel and little vessel are said of a wife with a different respect, who by reason of the marriage bed is equal to the husband, but lesser by reason of care, and because she behaves herself passively in generation. And yet 1. in the Greek is held the noun σκεῦος, which is not a diminutive. 2. Ambrose, book on Paradise, chapter 4, renders it simply, as to the weaker vessel. 3. The form of a diminutive noun does not always import a diminution of the thing, as appears from the words tabernacle, spectacle, habitation, etc.

2. Estius in this place and in 1 Corinthians 7, verse 4, and other Papists approve those harsher things pronounced by Jerome against marriage, that by the conjugal duty prayers are hindered. Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 4, I pray you, what is that good, which prohibits praying, which does not permit the body of the Lord to be received, etc.? When I fulfill the duty of a husband, I do not fulfill the duty of a Christian. Martianus Victor amended and substituted of the continent. The same Apostle commands in another place that we should always pray; if one must always pray, therefore one must never serve marriage, since as often as I render the debt to my wife, I cannot pray. The Apostle Peter, having experience of conjugal bonds, see how he informs the Church, what he teaches Christians. Likewise, husbands living with wives according to knowledge, etc., that your prayers be not hindered. Behold, in the same sense, because also by the same Spirit he says that prayers are hindered by the conjugal duty, etc. If we abstain from intercourse, we give honor to our wives; if we do not abstain, it is clear that insult is contrary to honor. book of the same, chapter 19, But also this must be inferred. If a layman and any faithful person cannot pray, unless he lacks the conjugal duty, to a Priest, to whom sacrifices must always be offered for the people, it must always be prayed. If one must always pray, therefore one must always abstain from marriage, in Apolog. ad Pammach. cap. 6. Why do they not dare to go to the Martyrs? (who use marriage) why do they not enter the Churches? Similar things occur in Bede in h. l. If we abstain from intercourse, we bestow honor. If we do not abstain, it is clear that intercourse is contrary to honor. He mentions that prayers are hindered by the conjugal duty, because as often as I render the debt to my wife, I cannot pray. But if, according to another sermon of the Apostle, one must pray without ceasing, therefore I must never serve marriage, lest I be hindered at any hour from prayer, to which I am ordered to always insist. Guilielmus Estius in 1. Cor. 7. proves this with such an argument. The conjugal act, by which the soul is in a certain way entirely immersed in the flesh, renders a man inept for prayer, by which the mind must be elevated to God. Resp. 1. The Apostle in this place does not say that prayers are hindered by the conjugal act, but by the quarrels and dissensions of spouses. 2. Paul 1. Corinth. 7. v. 4. does not speak of any prayer whatsoever, but of that solemn one, which was instituted for a certain time on account of a special case of adversity, to which the faithful gathered publicly, such as on Sundays and solemn days, to which fasts were joined. 3. This is gathered from the very words of the Apostle, the emphasis of which Theophylactus correctly weighs. For the Apostle does not say, that you may pray, but that you may be free for prayer and fasting. A parallel passage exists Ioel. 2. v. 16. 4. Estius himself acknowledges that the Apostle speaks not of any, but of that solemn prayer. 5. As with food, so also the moderate use of marriage in itself, and by itself, does not hinder prayers, otherwise pious spouses could not conduct themselves in conformity with the Apostolic precept, 1. Thess. 5. v. 17. ἀδιαλείπτως προσέυχεσθε. 6. Bellarminus lib. de matrim. cap. 5. §. 41. argues, that through the conjugal act the grace of the Holy Spirit can be acquired, when that act is an act of justice or obedience, or charity. But if the grace of the H. S. can be acquired through the conjugal act, certainly through it, when it is conducted in the due manner, prayers are not hindered. Erasmus in argum. l. adv. Iovinian. Virvesius in Conf. Aug. art. 23. Espensaeus lib. 1. de contin. cap. 9. acknowledge that Jerome, in the heat of the dispute on this argument, progressed further than was fitting, and spoke too harshly. 7. Estius in h. l. comments thus. The Apostle does not permit the use of the marriage bed to be interrupted for the sake of prayer when one or the other requests it, but only by consent &c. Item: If someone is joined to his wife only for the sake of rendering the debt it shall be, he is not prohibited from receiving the Eucharist on the same day. Gregory, in his 10th response to the questions of Augustine, Bishop of the English, grants this even to him who unites with his spouse solely for the desire of procreating offspring. Since, he says, it ought not to be prohibited by us from receiving, he who, placed in the fire, does not know how to burn.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Although the husband is the head of the woman, 1. Corinth. 11. v. 3. both are nevertheless equally obligated to chastity and conjugal fidelity, to the pursuit of harmony, and to mutual love. 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. Hence the son of Sirach requires of spouses that they be συμπεριφερόμενοι, bearing with one another, namely by deferring mutual honor to each other, by bearing mutual defects, by helping with mutual duties, and by showing mutual love.

2. That the woman was made from the side of the man, is also sufficiently signified from this, how dear the union of husband and wife ought to be. August. lib. 12. de civ. DEI cap. 26. Certainly the woman was not formed from the feet of the man, so that she might be held in the place of a handmaid, nor from the head of the man, so that she might be held as a mistress, but from the side of the man, so that she might be recognized as a partner in life. In the book Musar. c. 74. Therefore the woman was taken from one of the ribs of the man, and she is flesh of his flesh, so that he may be merciful, and spare her when angry, and remember that she is a member of his members.

3. By no means, therefore, is a tyrannical, nor absolute, nor masterly authority over the wife given to the husband, but γαμικὸν καὶ ἐπιεικές. Therefore let him use this dominion prudently, and let him not treat his wife harshly, imperiously, rigidly, importunately, and inhumanely, but blandly, courteously, and humanely. Sirac. 4. v. 35. Do not be as a lion in your house, overturning your household. 1. Cor. 7. vers. 3. Let the husband render to the wife due benevolence. Eph. 5. v. 29. Husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies; he who loves his own wife, loves himself. Col. 3. v. 19. Husbands love your wives, and do not be bitter against them.

4. It is a sign of prudence in a husband if he treats his wife humanely; but of imprudence, if he rushes at her with blind impulse and shows himself bitter.

5. The husband owes the wife instruction, the exhibition of honor, true love, the rendering of the debt, and peaceful speech. Iohan. Huss. in h. l.

6. Husbands, dwell with your wives. Therefore let them not desert them, nor follow after others, 1. Cor. 7. v. 10.

7. Then at last husbands dwell with their wives according to knowledge, that is to say, prudently, if they render due honor to them. In the book Musar, chapter 74. R. Hanina says. Let a man always render honor to his wife. For there is no blessing for a man, except because of his wife, as it is said. And he did well to Abraham because of her. Ibid. He who loves his wife as his own body, and honors her more than his own body, etc., of him the Scripture says. And you shall know that peace will be in your tabernacles.

8. Then at last husbands render due honor to their wives, if they acknowledge that they were given to them by God as companions in life and in the marriage bed, if they tolerate their weaknesses and treat them humanely, if they consider in them the divine condescension, that through faith they have been adopted by God as daughters and heirs of eternal life.

8. Just as in the human body more abundant honor is bestowed upon the weaker and less noble members, 1. Cor. 12. v. 22. & 23. so it befits husbands to have greater care for their wives as weaker vessels, and to treat them more humanely and gently. Weaker vessels, like Venetian glass, must be handled cautiously and gently.

10. Ambrose, in his book on Paradise, chapter 4, gathers from this passage, that honor is to be imparted to him from whom help is provided.

11. A wife is an instrument divinely created for the help of man, she is a vessel useful for the generation and education of children and for the administration of family affairs. B. Luther on this passage.

12 All the pious in general are vessels of grace and honor, the impious are vessels of wrath and ignominy and disgrace.Rom. 9. v. 22.2. Timoth. 2. vers. 22.

13. Pious spouses are not only equals and partners in marriage, but also participants of the same grace in this life, and co-heirs in the heavenly kingdom. Gal. 3. v. 28. There is neither male nor female, for you are all one in CHRIST. This is a great ὁρμητήριον. of Christian and conjugal concord. Lyranus on this passage: Since husband and wife are co-heirs of the future life, they ought to live socially and amicably in the present.

14. As many as heap insults upon the female sex, against God himself the Creator of this sex, against Christ its Redeemer and are injurious to the Holy Spirit, their sanctifier. God calls and promotes women equally as men through the word of the Gospel to the kingdom of grace in this life, and the kingdom of glory in the life to come.

15. The concord of spouses is pleasing to GOD and to men Sirac. 25. v. 1. since it is a soothing of conjugal troubles and an aid to pious prayers: The discord of spouses is most adverse to God, since it dissolves the bond of conjugal love required by God, and is an impediment to prayers.

16. Just as this reason brought forward by the Apostle, that spouses therefore ought to be in concord, lest their prayers be hindered, deservedly settles domestic disturbances and the dissensions of spouses: So it ought to cast a bridle upon all pious people in common life, lest they contend with one another in mutual hatreds. Matth. 5. vers. 23. & 24.Marc. 11. vers. 25.1. Tim. 2. v. 8.

17. A wife ought to be a help to her husband and to join her efforts with his, not only in economic matters, but also in prayers and other exercises of piety 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. It is therefore fitting for a pious mother of a family to institute daily and fixed exercises of domestic prayers, and to accustom her children and the whole family to offer morning and evening sacrifices of prayers to God. Psal. 55. vers. 18. to read a Biblical chapter to them or to see that it is read, and to summon them to the recitation of prayers before and after food.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. An perσυνοικεῖν κατὰ γνῶσινintelligatur moderatus coniugii usus? Ita statuit Salmero & alii 1. Quia ut Hebraei κατ᾽ εὐφημισμὸν καὶ ἀστεισμὸν congressum coniugalem describunt per ידעcognovit,Genes. 4. v. 1.cap. 19. v. 8.Iud. 19. v. 25. pro quo in eadem significatione ponitur verbum γινώσκεινMatth. 2. v. 25.Luc. 1. v. 35. ita nomen γνώσεως ad eundem videtur alludere. 2. Sicut verbum ὁμιλεῖνIudith. 12. v. 11. in Hist. Susannae vers. 53. pro congressu uxorio ponitur, in qua significatione etiam accipi potest Prov. 5. v. 19. ita verbum συνοικεῖν ei correspondens eodem sensu accipi potest. Quinimò extat manifestus locus, in quo συνοικεῖν eo sensu usurpatur, Deut. 22. v. 13. ita quoque videtur usurpari, Deut. 24. v. 1. ut & cognatum verbum συνοικίζειν,Deut. 21. v. 13. ut sic falsus fuerit Lorinus, qui negat, verbumσυνοικεῖνin hac significatione in Scripturis usurpatum inveniri. 3. Videtur hic locus Petrinus parallelus dicto Apostolico 1. Corinth. 7. v. 5.Nolite fraudare invicem, nisi fortè ex consensu ad tempus, ut vacetis ieiunio & orationi. 4. Eodem modo exponunt Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. cap. 4. Augustinus in Psal. 146. Beda & Oecumenius in h. l. 5. Salmero addit rationem, sed valde lubricam. Solent mulieres prae viris castitati studere, ideò Petrus praecipit, ut viri hac in parte nonnullis uxoribus deferant. Sic ergò foret sensus, uxoribus castè & temperanter utendum, non ad superfluas, nedum infandas & praeposteras libidines abutendum, ac certis temporibus propter pietatis exercitia magis seria à congressu abstinendum. Hanc expositionem non simpliciter improbamus, ut patet ex dictis in loco de Coniug. §. 435. interim addimus, quòd Glossa interlinearis, Hugo, Lyranus, Carthusianus &c. rectiùs h. l. generaliter explicent de conversatione domestica secundùm, h. e. secundùm eam sanctae & honestae vitae formam, quam scientia servandam dictat, instituenda. Sic ergò ex causa intelligitur effectus per metonymiam, siquidem scientia ex norma verbi divini hausta, est omnis honestatis &

sanctitatis causa. Cumprimis vero Apostolus coniugalem concordiam requirit, absque qua DEUS ritè invocari nequit, cum iurgia, dissidia & rixae fervori orationis sint contraria. Sic ergò locus hic Petrinus parallelus est dicto Apostolico 1. Timoth. 2. vers. 8.Volo ergo viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira & disceptatione. Lorinus in h. l. Meminit Lyranus expositionis illius (de reddendo debito secundùm conscientiam, non in passionibus desiderii 1. Thessal. 4. v. 5.) sed mavult aliam de cohabitatione domestica, in qua mulier quidem debet esse subiecta, vir autem praeesse secundùm scientiam, ut uxorem tractet tanquam sociam, non quasi ancillam &c. Consentit Carthusianus, ut discreti atque circumspecti viri agant, neque scandalizent & offendant uxores, quia sunt proniores ad malum. Mens eadem Gagnaei & recentiorum aliorum, quibus libentius acquiesco &c. Certè plerunque viri quàm uxores in exigendo debito sunt liberiores & importuniores. Guillandus in h. l. Maritorum officia praescribit, reprimens quorundam supercilium, imperium & Tyrannidem, qui clamitant, vir est caput mulieris, habemus ergò vitae & necis potestatem omni imperio, imperitare possumus uxoribus nostris in quavis re, etiam iuxta nostram libidinem, ab illis parendum est nobis. Sed viris huiusmodi frenum imposuit Apostolus, dicens: Viri cohabitate uxoribus secundùm scientiam.

Q. 2. An per honorem uxoribus impertiendum intelligatur moderatus coniugii usus? Lorinus etsi τὸ συνοικεῖν κατὰ γνῶσιν generaliter accipit de prudentia, quâ mariti uxoribus praeesse, iisque humaniter & concorditer debent cohabitare, tamen honorem uxoribus impertiendum specialiter intelligit de moderato coniugii usu. Concedam, inquit, libentius haec intelligi de coitu, & honestè dici à Petro, quod etiam sentit Turrianus noster de dogmat. character. sicut solet res eadem honestis aliis vocabulis denotari, ut verbo cognoscendiMatth. 2. v. 25.Luc. 1. v. 34.Eadem ratio de verbo ingrediendi aut intrandi.Ps. 51. v. 1.Sequitur hac in parte Hieronymum, Bedam & Oecumenium, qui itidem de matrimonialis actus usu moderato haec verba exponunt. Rationes affert hasce 1. quia Paulus1. Thessal. 5. vers. 4. & 5.eodem modo loquitur. Haec est voluntas Dei sanctificatio vestra, ut abstineatis à fornicatione, & sciat unus quisque, vas suum possidere in sanctificatione & honore, non in passione desiderii, sicut gentes, qui ignorant DEUM, &

ne quis supergrediatur, neque circumveniat in negotio fratrem suum, non enim vocavit nos Deus in immunditiam, sed in sanctificationem, ubi honor significat abstinentiam usumvè coniugii moderatum, negotium actum ipsum, vas uxorem, & cavetur tùm immodicus propriae coniugis usus, tùm quivis alienae, ut explicat Hieronymus in cap. 4. Eph. 2. Vasculi nomine Petronius & Plautus in Penulo utuntur pro obsceno muliebri, quod Paulus Apostolus infirmius, ignobilius, inhonestum vocat1. Cor. 12. v. 22. 23.Hugo notat dici cisternamEsai. 51. 1.& cavernam.Prov. 5. v. 15.3.Expositioni quâ per honorem moderatus coniugii usus intelligitur, favent contrariae significationis voces, utpote confusioPhil. 3. 19.(ubi gloria significat impetum libidinis, confusio pudenda ipsa, quae libidine flagrant in iis, quorum Deus venter est, hoc est, qui se ingurgitant) & ignominiaEs. 20. v. 4.Ez. 16. v. 7.Rom. 1. 26.& quod recens cognita nominaturנחרפתexprobata, à rad.חרףLev. 19. v. 20.Sensus igitur foret, maritos debere uxoribus honestè & castè uti. Quamvis v. hanc expositionem non simpliciter repudiemus, ut patet ex dictis loc. de coniug. §. 435. tn. addimus, rectiùs etiam hoc membrum generaliter accipi, sensu eo, quòd mariti non debeant uxores suas vilipendere, easque ut servas vel mancipia tractare, sed honorem convenientem ipsis tribuere, agnoscendo, quòd in vitae torivè socias divinitus sibi datae sint, ac proinde humaniter & comiter eas tractare, Oecumenius speciem quandam huius honoris subiungit, quod mariti non debeant rationem eorum, quae in familia ipsis concredita, exactè repetere, nec ab eleemosynis eas prohibere. Est & haec quaedam honoris debiti species, quòd propter infirmitates huic sexui adhaerentes non debeant contemni, sed earum infirmitates ex amore coniugali tegi, atque errata leviora usdonari. In rationibus à Lorino pro stabilienda speciali explicatione de moderato coniugii usu adductis quaedam desiderari possunt. Per τὸ σκεῦος1. Thess. 4. v. 4. rectiùs intelligitur cuiusque hominis corpus, quod est animae habitaculum & instrumentum, quàm uxor, est enim praeceptum hoc castitatis generale, non solùm coniuges, sed etiam caelibes concernens. Per τὸ πρᾶγμα negotium v. 6. perquam absurdè intelligitur actus coniugalis. Apostolus n. in his verbis non amplius de sexto praecepto agit, sed virtutes septimi praecepti subiicit, ut manifestè ostendunt phrases μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐν τῷ πράγματι τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτού. prohibet igitur fraudes in contractibus, ne quidq. desiderio plus habendi sive per avaritiam circumvenias proximum.

Absurda quoque est expositio loci Apostolici Phil. 3. v. 19. per gloriam enim non intelligit Apostolus libidinis impetum, nec per confusionem pudendas corporis partes, sed gloriam illam, quam Pseudo Apostoli quaerebant apud Iudaeos suis blanditiis & adulationibus, vel quam sibi arrogabant gloriatione de suo genere & peculiaribus donis 2. Cor. 11. v. 12. quam in turpissimam ignominiam tandem desinere docet, Hebraeum נחרפת Targum reddidit אחידאdesponsata. LXX. διαπεφυλαγμὲνηcustodita, per L. quae ex libertate ad servitutem transit, ac si vel maximè de coniugio accipiatur, reddi potest, viro manifestata sive cognita, חרף enim inter caetera etiam significat manifestavit, detexit. Inde Lorinus ipse tandem subiicit. Si velimus honorem accipere in latiore significatione, & hoc verum est, habendam in honore uxorem atque verbis & satis honorificè tractandam.

Q. 3. Quare uxores comparentur vasis? Quidam generalem afferunt rationem, quòd per vasa intelligantur creaturae.2. Tim. 2. vers. 20. Quidam putant respectum haberi ad corpora, quae sunt animae inhabitantis organa, per quae actiones naturales, vitales & animales exerit.1. Sam. 21. vers. 5.fuerunt vasa puerorum sancta.1. Thessal. 4. vers. 4.quilibet sciat, vas suum possidere in honore & sanctificatione. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 2. Epist. 4. huc accommodat locum Apostolicum 2. Corinth. 4. vers. 7.habemus thesaurum hunc in vasis fictilibus, quem exponit non solùm de mortali atque ex terra facto corpore concionatorum, in quo ceu vase fictili verbi divini thesauri hominibus exhibentur, sed etiam de verborum in Scriptura simplicitate, rectiùs exponitur de infirmitate carnis renatis in hac vita adhuc adhaerente. Simplicissimè respondetur, uxores comparari vasis, quia ex divina creatione & ordinatione sunt viri adiutorium, quod qt. coram ipso Genes. 2. vers. 18. sunt instrumenta ad generationem & educationem liberorum, itemque ad rei familiaris administrationem divinitùs ordinata.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Viriὁμοίωςsimiliter cohabitent uxoribus secundum scientiam. Atqui in praecedente exhortatione ad uxores directa, egerat Apostolus de impari coniugio, hîc vero loquitur de tali coniugio, in quo maritus & uxor sunt Christiani, ut colligitur ex verbis, tanquam coheredibus gratiae vitae, & ne impediantur orationes vestrae. Resp. B. Lutherus censet, adhuc sermonem esse de impari coniugio, iuxta hanc hypothesin statuendum, pronomen relativum ὑμῶν non ad utrumque coniugem, sed duntaxat ad fidelem referendum esse, sensu eo. Vos mariti Christiani secundum scientiam uxoribus vestris etiam infidelibus cohabitate, ut possitis sanctas manus ad DEUM levare sine ira & iurgiis,1. Tim. 2. vers. 8. Quòd si vel maximè statuere velimus, de pari coniugio sermonem esse, respondere poterimus, voculam ὁμοίως respectu paritatis in coniugio, non autem respectu eiusdem professionis fidei Christianae accipiendam esse.

2. Viriὁμοίωςuxoribus cohabitent. Atqui uxoribus subiectio, maritis dominium competit.v. 1. Resp. Quidam particulam ὁμοίως exponunt vicissim, è diverso. Sed potest usitata significatio retineri, in qua etiam v. 1. huius capitis accipitur. Respectus autem habetur. 1. Ad coniugale vinculum, cuius ratione maritus & uxor sunt pares & tenentur ad aequalia. 1. Cor. 7. vers. 4.Mulier sui corpori potestatem non habet, sed vir.ὁμόιως similiter autem & vir sui corporis potestatem non habet, sed mulier. 2. Ad aequale praecepti momentum. Quemadmodum uxores ex DEI ordinatione maritis suis debent esse subiectae, ita viri ex eadem DEI ordinatione uxoribus suis secundùm scientiam cohabitent, ac prudenter & comiter hoc dominio utantur. Beda in h. l. Similiter dicit, viros ad imitationem provocans, quia iam suprà uxoribus praeceperat, dicens, considerent viri in timore DEI castam vestram conversationem. 3. Ad par obedientiae commodum. Quemadmodum uxores subiectione & modestiâ suâ viros infideles ad amplexandam Christianam religionem alliciunt & invitant: sic mariti ex prudente cum uxoribus suis cohabitatione, & humana cum ipsis conversatione, hoc lucrantur, quod nullum precibus ipsorum obiicitur impedimentum.

3. Quasi infirmiori vasculo muliebri tribuentes honorem. Atqui uxori inpoenam peccati servilis subiectio impositaGen. 3. v. 16.propter quam virum timere debetEph. 5. v. 33. Resp. non tribuitur marito dominium herile in uxorem, nec uxori imponitur servilis subiectio erga maritum, sed significatur, post lapsum durum & molestum mulieri quandoque futurum viri imperium. Neque pugnant invicem timor, quem uxor marito ex praecepto Apostoli Pauli debet, & honor, quem maritus ex praecepto Apostoli Petri uxori debet, quia honor obiecti loco non tantùm habet superiorem sed etiam aequalem, imò & inferiorem. Rom. 12. vers. 10.honore vos invicem praevenientes. Quamvis ergò uxor à marito honoretur per concordem cohabitationem, mansuetam gubernationem & prudentem conversationem, non tamen propterea uxor à subiectione & timore marito exhibendo sese absolutam censere debet. Amor & honor coniugum debet esse reciprocus, neuter tamen dominium mariti vel uxoris subiectionem labefactat.

4. Tanquam coheredibus gratiae vitae. At quaedam mulieres non sunt cum maritis suis gratiae & vitae coheredes, infideles enim à gratiae, per severantes in peccatis à gloriae communione excluduntur. Resp. sufficit ad argumentum honoris uxoribus exhibendi, quòd ipsis non minùs ac viris gratia & vita in verbo Evangelii offeratur, atque ad eam in hoc seculo pateat aditus.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Describit Apostolus coniugium tanquam vitae genus sanctum & DEO gratum, in quo pii coniuges possunt esse vitae aeternae cohaeredes. Docet etiam, coniuges posse invicem eo modo cohabitare, ut non impediantur ipsorum preces. Sed Papa Romanus, qui se Petri successorem iactitat, in iure Canonico sic lotur. c.
