Quicquid caeus. 32. q. 2. Non datur praesentia Spiritus sancti tempore eo, quo coniugales actus geruntur, c. Connubia caus. & quaest. iisdem. Connubia legitima carent quidem peccato, non tamen tempore illo, quo coniugales actus geruntur, praesentia Spiritus sancti dabitur, etiamsi Propheta videatur esse, qui officio generationis obsequitur. c. Sciatis 33. q. 4. Quicunque uxori debitum reddunt, vacare non possunt orationi, nec de carnibus Agni comedere debent. c. Nuptiae caus. 32. q. 1. Scriptura in primo & tertio & quarto & quinto die & sexto expletis operibus singulorum dierum dixit. Et vidit Deus, quòd bonum esset. In secundo die hoc omninò subtraxit, nobis intelligentiam tribuens, non esse bonum duplicem numerum, qui ab unione dividat & praefiguret foedera nuptiarum. Unde & in arca Noae omnia animalia, quaecunque bina ingrediuntur, immunda sunt, impar numerus est mundus. Pontifex Romanus confirmavit Revelationes Brigittae, in quibus lib. 1. c. 26. Christus ad coniuges sic loqui introducitur. Cùm coniuges veniunt ad lectum, tunc statim discedit ab eis Spiritus meus, & appropinquat Spiritus impurus. Gretserus in Virgidemia p. 48. adducit & approbat verba Sixti Papae lib. de castit. Nubere omnium penè hominum est. Nihil gentile (excellens) est, id te exercere velle, quod cuncti; & illud habere, quod etiam pessimi consequuntur, sed ut de hominibus taceam, luxuriantur & ferae pecudes, & volucres quoque nubunt, nihil magnum cum porcis & canibus aliquid habere commune, DEI potius, & Angelorum eius vitam sectare. In his verbis sancta piorum coniugum cohabitatio porcorum & canum commixtioni non obscurè à Pontifice comparatur.

2. Vitam aeternam vocat Apostolus hereditatem. Ergò non datur ex merito ut merces servis, sed ex gratia υἱοθεσίας, ut hereditas filiis. Item vitam aeternam vocat Apostolus gratiam, uti Estius in comm. agnoscit. Ergò non propter operum merita datur, sed ex gratia propter Christum, in quo DEUS nos in filios adoptat, Si enim ex gratia, iam non ex operibus, alioquin gratia iam non est gratia. Si autem ex operibus, iam non ex gratia, quia opus iam non esset opus Rom. 11. v. 6. Locus huic nostro parallelus habetur Rom. 6. v. 23.χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν χριστῷ, in quem Chrysostomus homil. 10. in Epist. Rom. sic commentatur. Vita aeterna neque debitum est, neque laborum retributio, sed divini muneris donum gratuitum. Falsum est ergò, quòd Concilium Tridentinum à Pontifice Romano confirmatum, statuit sess. 6. cap. 16. benè operantibus usque in finem, & in DEO sperantibus proponendam esse vitam aeternam, & tanquam gratiam filiis DEI per Christum Iesum misericorditer promissam, & tanquam mercedem ex ipsius DEI promissione bonis ipsorum, operibus & meritis fideliter reddendam. Item: renatorum operibus nihil deesse, quò minùs legi divinae pro huius vitae statu plenè satisfecisse, & vitam aeternam verè promeruisse censeantur. Ad exceptionem, quòd vita aeterna detur ex gratia & ex meritis simul, quodque propterea dicatur ex gratia dari, quia meritoria illa opera, propter quae datur, sunt gratiae dona, suo loco respondimus.

3. August. l. 5. contra Iulianum c. 7. ex hoc loco Apostolico refellit Iulianum Pelagianum, statuentem, quoties commoveret se in coniugibus concupiscentia, satiandam avidè & regnare securam. Quòd monuit, inquit, Apostolus, ne in morbo desiderii vas suum quisque possideat, non de coniugio, sed fornicatione accipiendum putas, atque ita temperantiae totam honestatem de concubitu coniugum aufers, ut nemo sibi videatur in morbo desiderii suum vas possidere, quantacunque libidine in uxoris genitalibus potuerit insanire. Si enim ullum ibi tenendum existimare modum potuisti, & illic concupiscentiae reprehendere excessum, eumque dicere ab Apostolo significatum morbum desiderii, & non improbè negare, suum vas dictum fuisse cuique coniugem suam. Quo verbo in eadem re etiam Petrus Apostolus utitur, ubi monet, ut viri uxoribus suis tanquam vasi infirmiori tribuant honorem, velut coheredibus gratiae, adiungens, & dicens: Et videte, ne impediantur orationes vestrae. Sicut & Co Apostolus eius tempora praescribit orandi temperantiae coniugali, & secundùm veniam concedit, quamvis cum coniuge non utique illum prolis, sed qui fit voluptatis intentione concubitum. Hunc audiant Christiana coniugia, non te, qui vis in eis, quam defendis, nunquam frenari concupiscentiam, sed quotiescunque se commoverit, satiari avidam, regnare securam.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Hugo ex hoc loco colligit, vas & vasculum diverso respectu dici de uxore, quae ratione tori aequalis est viro, minor ratione curae, & quia se passivè habet in generatione. Atqui 1. in Graeco habetur nomen σκεῦος, quod non est diminutivum. 2. Ambrosius, lib. de Parad. cap. 4. simpliciter reddit, tanquam vasi infirmiori. 3. forma nominis diminutivi non semper importat diminutionem rei, ut apparet ex verbis tabernaculum, spectaculum, habitaculum &c.

2. Estius in h. l. & in 1. Corinth. 7. vers. 4. ac alii Pontificii approbant duriora illa Hieronymi contra coniugium pronunciata, quòd officio coniugali impediantur orationes. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovin. cap. 4. Oro te, quale illud bonum, quod orare prohibet, quod corpus Domini accipi non permittit &c.? Quando impleo officium mariti, non impleo officium Christiani. Martianus Victor emendavit & substituit continentis. Iubet idem Apostolus in alio loco, ut semper oremus, si semper orandum est, nunquam ergo coniugio serviendum, quoniam quotiescunque uxori debitum reddo, orare non possum. Petrus Apostolus experimentum habens coniugalium vinculorum, vide, quo modo informet Ecclesiam, quid doceat Christianos. Similiter viri cohabitantes uxoribus secundùm scientiam &c. ut non impediantur orationes vestrae. Ecce eodem sensu, quia & eodem Spiritu impediri dicit orationes officio coniugali &c. Si abstinemus nos à coitu, honorem tribuimus uxoribus, si non abstinemus, perspicuum est, honori contrariam esse contumeliam. lib. eiusd. cap. 19. Sed & hoc inferendum. Si Laicus & quicunque fidelis orare non potest, nisi careat officio coniugali, Sacerdoti, cui semper pro populo offerenda sunt sacrificia, semper orandum est. Si semper orandum est, ergò semper carendum matrimonio, in Apolog. ad Pammach. cap. 6. Quare ad Martyres ire non audent? (qui coniugio utuntur) quare non ingrediuntur Ecclesias? Similia occurrunt apud Bedam in h. l. Si abstineamus nos à coitu, honorem, tribuimus. Si non abstineamus, perspicuum est, honori contrarium esse concubitum. Impediri orationes officio coniugali commemorat, quia quotiescunque uxori debitum reddo, orare non possum. Quod si iuxta alium Apostoli sermonem sine intermissione orandum est, nunquam ergò mihi coniugio serviendum, ne ab oratione, cui semper insistere iubeor, ullâ horâ praepediar. Guilielmus Estius in 1. Cor. 7. hoc probat eiusmodi argumento. Coniugalis actus, quo animus quodammodo totus carni immergitur, ineptum reddit hominem ad orationem, quâ mens ad Deum elevanda est. Resp. 1. Apostolus hoc loco non dicit, actu coniugali impediri orationes, sed rixis & dissidiis coniugum. 2. Paulus 1. Corinth. 7. v. 4. non loquitur de quacunque oratione, sed de solenni illa, quae ob specialem adversitatis casum certo tempore instituebatur, ad quam fideles publicè conveniebant, veluti Dominicis & solennibus diebus, cui coniuncta erant ieiunia. 3. Colligitur hoc ex ipsis Apostoli verbis, quorum emphasin Theophylactus rectè expendit. Neque enim dicit Apostolus, ut oretis, sed ut orationi & ieiunio vacetis. Locus parallelus extat Ioel. 2. v. 16. 4. Agnoscit ipse Estius, Apostolum non de quacunque, sed de folenni illa oratione loqui. 5. Ut cibi, ita quoque coniugii usus moderatus in se, ac per se non impedit preces, aliàs pii coniuges non possent se conformes gerere praecepto Apostolico, 1. Thess. 5. v. 17.ἀδιαλείπτως προσέυχεσθε. 6. Bellarminus lib. de matrim. cap. 5. §. 41. disputat, per actum coniugalem acquiri posse gratiam Spiritus sancti, quando actus iste est actus iustitiae vel obedientiae, vel caritatis. Atqui si per actum coniugalem potest acquiri gratia Spiritus S., utique per illum, debito modo se habentem, non impediuntur preces. Erasmus in argum. l. adv. Iovinian. Virvesius in Conf. Aug. art. 23. Espensaeus lib. 1. de contin. cap. 9. agnoscunt, Hieronymum ardore disputationis in hoc argumento longiùs, quàm par erat, progressum, & duriùs locutum. 7. Estius in h. l. sic commentatur. Apostolus nec orationis causâ permittit, usum tori coniugalis alterutro petente intermitti, sed tantùm ex consensu &c. Item: Si tantùm debiti reddendi gratiâ quis uxori commixtus fuerit, non prohibetur eodem die Eucharistiam percipere. Gregorius ad interrogationes Augustini Anglorum Episcopi resp. 10. id concedit etiam illi, qui solo procreandae sobolis desiderio coniugi miscetur. Quoniam, inquit, à nobis prohiberi non debet accipere, qui in igne positus, nescit ardere.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Quamvis vir sit mulieris caput,1. Corinth. 11. v. 3. uterque tamen coniugam ad castitatem & fidem coniugalem, ad studium concordiae & amorem mutuum aequaliter obligatur. 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. Inde Siracides à coniugibus requirit, ut sintσυμπεριφερόμενοι, simul se ferentes, videlicet mutuum honorem sibi deferendo, mutuos defectus ferendo, mutuis officiis iuvando, amorem mutuum exhibendo.

2. Quòd foemina ex latere viri facta est, etiam hinc satis significatum, quàm cara mariti & uxoris debeat esse coniunctio. August. lib. 12. de civ. DEI cap. 26. Nimirum mulier non est formata ex pedibus viri, ut habeatur loco ancillae, nec ex capite viri, ut habeatur velut domina, sed ex latere viri, ut agnoscatur vitae socia. In libro Musar. c. 74. Ideò sumta fuit mulier de una ex costis viri, & caro est de carne eius, quò clemens sit, eique parcat iratus, & recordetur, ipsam esse membrum de membris eius.

3. Nequaquam igitur Tyrannicum, nec absolutum, nec herile imperium in uxorem marito datum, sed γαμικὸν καὶ ἐπιεικές. Prudenter igitur hoc dominio utatur, nec durè, imperiosè, rigidè, importunè & inhumaniter, sed blandè, comiter & humaniter uxorem tractet. Sirac. 4. v. 35.Noli esse sicut leo in domo tua, evertens domesticos tuos.1. Cor. 7. vers. 3.Uxori vir debitam benevolentiam reddat.Eph. 5. v. 29.Viri debent diligere uxores suas ut corpora sua; qui suam uxorem diligit, seipsum diligit.Col. 3. v. 19.Viri diligite uxores, & nolite amari esse adversus illas.

4. Signum prudentiae in viro, si humaniter uxorem tractet; imprudentiae verò, si caeco impetu in eam ruat, ac amarulentum sese praebeat.

5. Maritus uxori debet instructionem, honoris exhibitionem, veram dilectionem, debiti redditionem, pacificam locutionem. Iohan. Huss. in h. l.

6. Viri cohabitent uxoribus. Ergò non deserant eas, nec alienas sectentur, 1. Cor. 7. v. 10.

7. Tunc demum mariti secundùm scientiam h. e. prudenter cum uxoribus cohabitant, si debitum honorem illis tribuant. In libro Musar cap. 74. R. Hanina dicit. Semper homo honorem tribuat uxori. Nam non est benedictio homini, nisi propter uxorem eius, sicut dicitur. Et Abrahamo benefecit propter eam. Ib. Qui amat uxorem suam, sicut corpus suum, & honorat eam plusquam corpus suum &c. de eo Scriptura dicit. Et scies, quod pax erit in tabernaculis tuis.

8. Tunc demum mariti debitum honorem uxoribus tribuunt, si agnoscant, eas divinitùs in vitae torique socias sibi esse datas, si infirmitates earum tolerent & humaniter eas tractent, si considerent in illis divinam dignationem, quod per fidem in filias & vitae aeternae heredes à Deo sint adoptatae.

8. Sicut in corpore humano infirmioribus & ignobilioribus membris abundantior honor apponitur, 1. Cor. 12. v. 22. & 23. ita maritos decet uxorum tanquam vasorum infirmiorum maiorem curam habere, easdemque humaniùs & molliùs tractare. Vasa debiliora, ut vitra Veneta, cautè & molliter tractanda.

10. Ambrosius lib. de Paradiso cap. 4. ex hoc loco colligit, quod honor impartiendus ei, à quo praesto est auxilium.

11. Uxor est instrumentum divinitùs conditum in viri adiutorium, est vas utile ad generationem & educationem liberorum & ad rei familiaris administrationem. B. Lutherus in hunc locum.

12 Omnes pii in genere sunt vasa gratiae & honoris, impii sunt vasa irae & ignominiae ac dedecoris.Rom. 9. v. 22.2. Timoth. 2. vers. 22.

13. Pii coniuges non solùm sunt compares & consortes in coniugio, sed etiam eiusdem gratiae in hac vita participes, & in coelesti regno coheredes. Gal. 3. v. 28.Non est masculus nec foemina, omnes enim unus estis in CHRISTO. Magnum hoc est Christianae & coniugalis concordiae ὁρμητήριον. Lyranus in h. l. Ex quo vir & uxor sunt coheredes vitae futurae, debent in praesenti socialiter & amicabiliter vivere.

14. Quotquot in foemineum sexum convitia congerunt, in Deum ipsum sexus huius Creatorem, in Christum eiusdem Redemtorem & in Spiritum S. eiusdem sanctificatorem sunt iniurii. Deus foeminas aequè ac viros per verbum Evangelii ad regnum gratiae in hac vitâ, & regnum gloriae in futura vitâ vocat & promovet.

15. Concordia coniugum DEO & hominibus placet Sirac. 25. v. 1. cum sit aerumnarum coniugalium lenimentum & piarum precum adminiculum: Discordia coniugum Deo vel maximè adversa, cum dissolvat amoris coniugalis divinitùs requisiti vinculum, ac sit precum impedimentum.

16. Sicut haec ratio ab Apostolo adducta, quòd coniuges ideò debeant esse concordes, ne impediantur ipsorum preces, domesticas turbas & coniugum dissidia meritò componit: Sic omnibus piis in vita communi eadem frenum iniicere debet, ne mutuis odiis invicem certent. Matth. 5. vers. 23. & 24.Marc. 11. vers. 25.1. Tim. 2. v. 8.

17. Uxor debet esse viri adiutorium ac socias operas ei iungere, non solùm in re oeconomica, sed etiam in precibus & aliis pietatis exercitiis 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. Convenit ergò piae matrifamilias, quotidiana & stata precum domesticarum exercitia institnere, ac liberos suos & totam familiam ad matutina & vespertina precum sacrificia Deo offerenda assuefacere. Psal. 55. vers. 18. caput Biblicum ipsis praelegere vel praelegendum curare, & ad precum ante ac post cibum recitationem eos convocare.

## 3:2
CONSIDERING IN FEAR YOUR CHASTE CONVERSATION.

Connection. 1. The Apostle had said in the preceding verse, that unbelieving husbands can be won over by the conversation of Christian wives without a word: now furthermore he explains what that conversation ought to be, if it is to obtain that desired effect, the conversion and salvation of husbands, namely chaste and holy. It is therefore a fuller exposition of the organic cause or occasion through which unbelieving husbands are rendered more equitable and better disposed toward the Christian religion.

The Apostle had exhorted v. 1. Christian wives to ὑποταγὴν or subjection, to be rendered in words and deeds: now furthermore he exhorts them to ἁγνὴν καὶ καλὴν ἀναστροφὴν, to a chaste and holy conversation, likewise to be exhibited in words and deeds. Lyranus in this place: The Apostle instructs women, first concerning due subjection, secondly concerning honest composition.

Exposition of the text. ἐποπτεύσαντες, namely husbands. Hugo and Lyranus refer it to the wives: but the masculine in the Greek text shows that this must be referred to the husbands, denoted by the word τινες in the preceding verse. The Vulgate rendered it, considering. But the Greek is properly, when they shall have considered or looked upon. Moreover ἐποπτεύειν signifies accurate inspection and consideration, as is gathered from this Epistle chap. 2. v. 12. which place is parallel to this one of ours, nor does this word occur elsewhere in the New Testament. 2. Pet. 1. v. 16. the noun ἐπόπτης is had in the same signification. The LXX use the cognate word ἐπόπτεσθαι for חזה he saw, he looked through, Mic. 4. v. 11. which the Syrian also uses in this place, for צפה he spied out, Ps. 5. v. 4. as also for ראה he saw, he apprehended with his eyes or mind, Ps. 34. v. 20. Ps. 117. v. 7. Mic. 7. v. 10.

Ἐν φόβῳ. Some refer this προσδιορισμὸν to the preceding word ἐποπτεύσαντες, but the series of the text in the Greek source shows that it must be referred to the following, namely to ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν. For it is said τὴν ἐν φόβῳ for τὴν μετὰ φόβου, namely οὖσαν ἀναστροφὴν. Furthermore, this fear is explained in three ways by the Interpreters. Some For they interpret of the fear of husbands, by which, namely, husbands, considering the chaste conduct of their wives, revere and love them, and thence are enticed to their emulation and consequently to Christianity. Cornel. à Lapide in h. l. But this exposition rests upon a hypothesis just now repudiated. Some interpret of the fear of GOD, in this sense, that Christian wives ought to declare the fear of GOD (which is the foundation of pious and chaste conduct) by speech, countenance, attire, gestures, and conduct. Glossa interlin. in h. l. Considering in fear the holy conduct, that is, held in the fear of GOD preserved. It is most simply interpreted as reverence toward husbands, by which wives, on account of the divine command, revere the husband, and solicitously take care lest they offend him even in the smallest matter. A parallel passage exists Eph. 5. v. 33. where the Apostle likewise joins fear or reverence with subjection toward husbands. v. 23. Let wives be subject to their own husbands as to the Lord v. 33. Let the wife fear her husband. It is possible, however, for the second exposition to be joined with this third one, since that reverence ought to be joined with the fear of God.

By τὴν ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν is understood, 1. that wives ought to keep their conjugal faith whole and unblemished for their husband, and abstain from adulterous meetings. 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. 2. That they ought to be chaste not only in body, but also in mind: for as piety, so also chastity is often harmed by the countenance. Iob. 31. v. 1. Matth. 5. v. 28. thence mention is made of eyes full of adultery Ezech. 6. vers. 9. which are full of adultery 2. Petr. 2. v. 14. etc. 3. That they ought to abhor libidinous meetings contrary to Nature, or against honesty. Rom. 1. v. 26. For to those were Christian wives enticed by infidel husbands.

Ὑμῶν. Lyranus annotates thus on this little word. The mode of speaking is changed here from the third person to the second, which happens frequently in Holy Scripture. Ioh. Huss. in almost the same way. He turns his speech to the women, so that from the mode of speaking, which is more familiar, he may entice them to good.

Latin:

CONSIDERANTES IN TIMORE CASTAM CONVERSATIONEM VESTRAM.

Connexio. 1. Dixerat Apostolus in versu praecedente, maritos infideles per uxorum Christianarum conversationem sine verbo lucrifieri posse: iam porrò exponit, qualis debeat esse illa conversatio, si exoptatum illum effectum, maritorum conversionem & salutem obtinere debeat, videlicet casta & sancta. Est ergò uberior expositio causae organicae vel occasionis, per quam mariti infideles erga Christianam religionem aequiores & melius affecti redduntur.

Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus v. 1. uxores Christianas ad ὑποταγὴν sive subiectionem, verbis & factis praestandam: iam porrò exhortatur eas ad ἁγνὴν καὶ καλὴν ἀναστροφὴν, ad castam & sanctam conversationem, itidem verbis & factis exhibendam. Lyranus in h. l. Informat Apostolus mulieres, primùm de debita subiectione, secundò de honesta compositione.

Textûs expositio. ἐποπτεύσαντες, scilicet mariti. Hugo & Lyranus referunt ad uxores: sed masculinum in textu Graeco ostendit ad maritos, per vocem τινες in versu praeced. denominatos, hoc referendum esse. Vulgata reddidit, considerantes. Sed Graecum propriè est, ubi consideraverint sive inspexerint. Significat autem ἐποπτεύεινaccuratam inspectionem & considerationem, ut colligitur ex huius Epist. cap. 2. v. 12. qui locus huic nostro parallelus, neque alibi in Nov. Test. hoc verbum occurrit. 2. Petr. 1. v. 16. habetur nomen ἐπόπτης in ead. significatione. Cognato verbo ἐπόπτεσθαι LXX. utuntur pro חזהvidit, perspexit,Mich. 4. vers. 11. quo etiam Syrus h. l. utitur, pro צפהspeculatus est,Psal. 5. vers. 4. ut & pro ראהvidit, oculis vel animorem aliquam apprehendit,Psal. 34. v. 20.Psal. 117. v. 7.Mich. 7. v. 10.

Ἐν φόβῳ. Quidam hunc προσδιορισμὸν referunt ad verbum praecedens ἐποπτεύσαντες, sed series textûs in fonte Graeco ostendit, referendum esse ad sequentia, videlicet ad ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν. Dicitur enim τὴν ἐν φόβῳ pro τὴν μετὰ φόβου, scil. οὖσαν ἀναστροφὴν. Coeterùm timor hic tripliciter ab Interpretibus exponitur. Quidam enim accipiunt de timore maritorum, quo scilicet mariti, considerantes castam uxorum conversationem, eas reverentur & amant, indeque ad earum amulationem & consequenter ad Christianismum alliciuntur. Cornel. à Lapide in h. l. Sed haec expositio nititur hypothesi modò repudiatâ. Quidam accipiunt de timore DEI, sensu eo, quòd uxores Christianae timorem DEI (qui piae & castae conversationis fundamentum est) sermone, vultu, habitu, gestibus, conversatione declarare, debeant. Glossa interlin. in h. l. Considerantes in timore sanctam conversationem, hoc est, habitam in timore DEI conservato. Simplicissimè accipitur de reverentia erga maritos, quâ uxores propter mandatum divinum maritum reverentur, ac solicitè cavent, ne eum etiam in re minima offendant. Locus parallelus extat Eph. 5. v. 33. ubi Apostolus itidem timorem sive reverentiam cum subiectione erga maritos coniungit. v. 23.Mulieres viris suis subditae sint sicut Dominov. 33.Uxor timeat virum. Potest tamen cum hac tertiâ expositione secunda coniungi, cum reverentia illa debeat esse cum timore Dei coniuncta.

Per τὴν ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν intelligitur, 1. quod uxores fidem coniugalem integram & illibatam marito servare, & ab adulterinis congressibus abstinere debeant. 1. Cor. 7. v. 4. 2. Quòd non solùm corpore, sed etiam animo debeant esse castae: ut enim pietas, ita quoque castitas vultu saepè laeditur. Iob. 31. v. 1.Matth. 5. v. 28. inde mentio fit oculorum fornicantiumEzech. 6. vers. 9. qui pleni sunt adulterii2. Petr. 2. v. 14. &c. 3. Quod à libidinosis congressibus praeter Naturam, aut contra honestatem abhorrere debeant.Rom. 1. v. 26. Ad illos enim à maritis infidelibus alliciebantur uxores Christianae.

Ὑμῶν. Lyranus ad hanc voculam sic annotat. Mutatur hic modus loquendi de persona tertia ad secundam, quod fit frequenter in Sacra Scriptura. Ioh. Huss. eodem ferè modo. Convertit sermonem suum ad mulieres, ut ex modo loquendi, qui magis familiaris est, alliciat eas ad bonum.

## 3:3
WHOSE ADORNING LET IT NOT BE THE OUTWARD PLAITING OF HAIR, OR THE WEARING OF GOLD, OR THE PUTTING ON OF APPAREL.

Connection. 1. Προτροπῇ or the exhortation to subjection and obedience, the Apostle subjoins ἀποτροπὴν or the dehortation from luxury in clothing.

2. The Apostle had exhorted in the preceding verse Christian wives to chaste conversation, now he subjoins a dehortation from excessive cultivation of external adornment, inasmuch as it is accustomed to pave the way for adulterous loves.

3. He had commanded wives that by due subjection, and chaste conversation, and thus by manners, words, and deeds, they should endeavor to make their husbands better, and invite them to embrace the Christian faith, now he demands that they also soothe their minds with moderation of dress.

4. The Apostle had required from Christian wives first ὑποταγὴν καὶ φόβον, second καλὴν ἀναστροφἣν, third ἀγνείαν, now he sets forth the fourth virtue of pious wives, namely the moderation of the external cultivation of the body and dress, for he teaches with what cultivation and adornment they ought especially to commend themselves to their infidel husbands, namely not with the exterior, which is expensive to husbands and pernicious to chastity, but with the interior, which is precious before God.

5. B. Luther offers such a connection. The Apostle had shown how Christian wives ought to conduct themselves toward infidel husbands, now he further teaches how they should conduct themselves toward others in common life and conversation, namely, that they ought to adorn themselves soberly, and thus he opposes to honest and chaste conversation the common vice of women; namely, pomp in dress.

Disposition of the text. He illustrates the dehortation from luxury in dress by an enumeration of some parts, which are the plaiting of the hair, the putting around of gold, and the wearing of cloaks.

Exposition of the text. ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν etc. The Vulgate rendered it rather obscurely. Whose adorning let it not be the outward plaiting of the hair, or the wearing of gold, or the putting on of apparel. In the Greek all things are clearer, if the little word κόσμος placed in the last place is joined with the relative pronoun ὧν, placed in the beginning. Whose adornment may it be, not that external one, which is situated in the plaiting of the hair, and the putting around of gold or the wearing of cloaks. The Syrian here begins a new sentence, with the relative pronoun omitted, thus rendering the text. Neither be ye adorned with external adornments, etc. Furthermore, so that the Apostle may the more severely rebuke the immoderate zeal for adorning bodies, which is familiar to the female sex, and recall Christian wives from it, he recounts three species of that vanity, under which he synecdochically includes all other things pertaining to female attire, a list of which, quite long, Isaiah weaves cap. 3. v. 16. & following.

The first species is ἐμπλοκὴ τριχῶν. In certain Greek Codices it is read as διαστολὴν, ἐν πλοκῇ τριχῶν in the plaiting of the hair. Which reading Ambrose seems to have followed in exhort. ad virgin. where he cites this passage thus, in the plaiting of the hair. But most all read, ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν. Which reading the same Ambrose follows in Epist. 27. as does Fulgentius in Epist. 2. cap. 11. The sense comes to the same thing. Ἐμπλέκεσθαι is to be implicated, to be knotted 2. Tim. 2. v. 4. 2. Petr. 2. v. 20. therefore ἐμπλοκαί τριχῶν are knots and plaitings, or implications of the hair, as Fulgentius renders it lib. 2. cap. 11. called braids; 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. of which female pride has devised various species. For some women curl their hair with art, some twist it back, knot it, and arrange it into ringlets, some separate them into curls and horns with curling irons, some even attach foreign and artificial hair to themselves, some let down hair from the forehead. Hieron. ad Demetriadem. Exod. 35. v. 22. Num. 31. v. 50. ἐμπλόκιον is referred to among female ornaments, and corresponds to the Hebrew כומז which some translate as a female girdle, pendant, or bossed ornament, some as a bracelet, some as a pair of drawers. Es. 3. v. 17. is likewise referred to among female ornaments, and corresponds to the Hebr. שביסים which others translate as brooches, others as ribbons, others as little wheels or circles, others as hairnets. The Syrian in this place as also 1. Tim. 2. vers. 9. ἐμπλοκὴν renders by [consult facsimile image] which signifies such binding, twisting, implication, by which hairs are twisted into ringlets, from the root [consult facsimile image] he spun, he bound, he wrapped, he knotted, Ioh. 19. v. 12.

The second species of female attire is περίθεσις χρυσίων. Gagnaeus determines that it should be read περιθέσεως ἣ ἐνδύσιως χρυσίων ἱματίων, so that χρυσίων may be an adjective, in this sense, that the attire and adornment of women ought not to be in the clothing and garment of golden vestments.

But we are compelled by no necessity to depart from the common and received reading. The plural τὰ χρύσια placed absolutely denotes any golden ornaments whatsoever, such as necklaces, chains, bracelets, rings, earrings, frontlets. For just as Paul 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. joins πλέγματα, χρυσὺν καὶ μαργαρίτας; so Peter in this place joins ἐμπλοκὴν τριχῶν the affected curling of the hair, and περίθεσιν χρυσίων the putting around of golden ornaments, with which women are accustomed to decorate their heads, necks, breasts, hands, and fingers, and indeed even to distinguish their garments with golden borders and fringes. But especially by this περίθεσιν χρυσίων (inasmuch as it is joined with ἐμπλοκῇ τριχῶν) are denoted nets, and other ornaments of the same kind interwoven with gold, which are accustomed to be placed upon the hair or the head, as also golden threads and ribbons, with which they were accustomed to bind and knot their hair.

The third species is ἔνδυσις ἱματίων.. By τὰ ἱμάτια sometimes in general are understood garments Matth. 11. v. 8.cap. 27. vers. 35. etc., sometimes in particular cloaks, which are thrown over the inner garments on the outside. Matth. 9. v. 20.cap. 21. v. 7. etc. Both significations can have a place here. The general is proved from the parallel passage 1. Tim. 2. vers. 9. μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν, ἣ χρυσῷ, ἣ μαργαρίταις, ἣ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ.. The special is proved from the fact that mention of garments in general had already been made before under the name χρυσίων.. The sense therefore is that Christian wives ought not to clothe themselves with a cloak, or with any other more precious garment. For that the epithet of precious things is to be understood is clear from the parallel passage 1. Tim. 2. v. 9., whence the Syrian added ἐξηγήσεως for the sake of clarity, translating the Apostolic passage thus: Do not be adorned with the devising of gold, or of sumptuous garments. Lyranus on this passage annotates thus: It is called the clothing of garments by excellence, just as the rose is called the flower of flowers. For women are accustomed to put on so many clothes, and to adorn themselves with so many tunics, veils, cloaks, and those silk, fine linen, precious and sumptuous, that the adornment of one could suffice for many women.

Latin:

QUARUM NON SIT EXTRINSECUS CAPILLATURA AUT CIRCUMDATIO AURI, AUT INDUMENTI VESTIMENTORUM CULTUS.

Connexio. 1. Προτροπῇ sive exhortationi ad subiectionem & obedientiam, subiungit Apostolus ἀποτροπὴν sive dehortationem à luxu in vestitu.

2. Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus in versu praeced. uxores Christianas ad castam conversationem, iam subiungit dehortationem à nimio externi ornatus cultu, quippe qui adulterinis amoribus viam sternere solet.

3. Praeceperat uxoribus, ut debitâ subiectione, & castâ conversatione, adeoque moribus, dictis, & factis maritos suos meliores reddere, & ad fidem Christianam amplectendam invitare conentur, iam exigit, ut etiam moderatione vestitus animos eorum demulceant.

4. Requisiverat Apostolus ab uxoribus Christianis primò ὑποταγὴν καὶ φόβον, secundò καλὴν ἀναστροφἣν, tertiò ἀγνείαν, iam quartam piarum uxorum virtutem exponit, videlicet moderationem externi corporis cultus ac vestitus, docet enim quo cultu & ornatu sese potissimum maritis suis infidelibus commendare debeant, videlicet non exteriore, qui maritis est dispendiosus & castitati perniciosus, sed interiore, qui coram Deo preciosus.

5. B. Lutherus eiusmodi profert connexionem. Ostenderat Apostolus, quomodo uxores Christianae erga maritos infideles sese gerere debeant, iam porrò docet, quomodo erga alios in communi vita & conversatione sese gerant, videlicet, quod sobriè se ornare debeant, sicque bonestae & castae conversationi opponit vulgare foeminarum vitium; videlicet pompam in vestitu.

Textus dispositio. Dehortationem â luxu in vestitu illustrat enumeratione aliquot partium, quae sunt plicatura capillorum, circumpositio auri, & amictus palliorum.

Textus expositio. ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν &c. Vulgata subobscurè reddidit. Quarum non sit extrinsecus capillatura, aut circumdatio auri, aut indumenti vestimentorum cultus. In Graeco omnia planiora, si vocula κόσμος ultimo loco posita coniungatur cum pronomine relativo ὧν, in principio posito. Quarum ornatus sit, non externus ille, qui situs in plicatura capillorum, & circumpositione auri aut amictu palliorum. Syrus novam hic inchoat sententiam, omisso pronomine relativo, sic reddens textum. Neque ornemini ornatibus externis &c. Caeterùm ut immodicum studium in ornandis corporibus foemineo sexui familiare Apostolus eò magis perstringat, & ab eo uxores Christianas revocet, tres vanitatis illius species recenset, sub quibus synecdochicè comprehendit reliqua omnia, ad cultum muliebrem pertinentia, quorum catalogum benè longum texit Esaias cap. 3. v. 16. & seqq.

Prima species est ἐμπλοκὴ τριχῶν. In quibusdam Codicibus Graecis legitur per διαστολὴν, ἐν πλοκῇ τριχῶνin plicatura capillorum. Quam lectionem secutus videtur Ambros. in exhort. ad virgin. ubi hunc locum sic citat, in plicatu capillorum. Sed plerique omnes legunt, ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν. Quam lectionem sequitur idem Ambrosius Epist. 27. ut & Fulgentius Epist. 2. cap. 11. Sensus eodem redit. Ἐμπλέκεσθαι est implicari, innodari2. Tim. 2. v. 4.2. Petr. 2. v. 20. ergò ἐμπλοκαί τριχῶν sunt nodi & plicaturae, sive implicationes capillorum, ut reddit Fulgent. lib. 2. cap. 11. plegmata dicta;1. Tim. 2. v. 9. quorum varias species muliebris fastus excogitavit. Quaedam enim foeminae capillos arte crispant, quaedam eos retorquent, innodant, & in cincinnos componunt, quaedam in cirros & cornua calamistris eos discriminant, quaedam etiam alienos & factitios crines sibi apponunt. quaedam à fronte crines demittunt. Hieron. ad Demetriadem. Exod. 35. v. 22.Num. 31. v. 50.ἐμπλόκιον refertur inter ornamenta muliebria, ac respondet Hebraeo כומז quod quidam vertunt cingulam, pendulam, vel bullatam muliebrem, quidam dextrale, quidam subligaculum.Es. 3. v. 17. itidem refertur inter ornamenta muliebria, ac respondet Hebr. שביסים quod alii fibulas, alii vittas, alii rotulas seu circulos, alii reticula vertunt. Syrus hoc loco ut & 1. Tim. 2. vers. 9.ἐμπλοκὴν reddit per [consult facsimile image] quod significat eiusmodi nexionem, retorsionem, implicationem, qua crines torquentur in cincinnos, à rad. [consult facsimile image]filavit, nexuit, involvit, innodavit,Ioh. 19. v. 12.

Secunda cultus muliebris species est περίθεσις χρυσίων. Gagnaeus legendum esse statuit περιθέσεως ἣ ἐνδύσιως χρυσίων ἱματίων, ut χρυσίων sit adiectivum, sensu eo, quòd cultus & ornatus mulierum non debeat esse in amictu & indumennto vestimentorum aureorum.

Sed nullâ cogimur necessitate, ut à communi & recepta lectione discedamus Plurale τὰ χρύσια absolutè positum denotat quaevis ornamenta aurea, qualia sunt monilia, catenae, dextrocheria, annuli, inaures, frontalia. Ut enim Paulus 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. coniungit πλέγματα, χρυσὺν καὶ μαργαρίτας; ita Petrus hoc loco coniungit ἐμπλοκὴν τριχῶν affectatam capillorum crispaturam, & περίθεσιν χρυσίων circumpositionem aureorum ornamentorum, quibus foeminae capita, colla, pectora, manus ac digitos suos solent decorare, quin & vestes limbis & fimbriis aureis distinguere. Cumprimis vero per hanc περίθεσιν χρυσίων (utpote cum ἐμπλοκῇ τριχῶν coniunctam) denotantur reticula, eiusdemque generis ornamenta alia auro intexta, quae capillis aut capiti imponi solent, ut etiam aurea fila ac vittae, quibus capillos colligare & innodare consueverunt.

Tertia species est ἔνδυσις ἱματίων. Per τὰ ἱμάτια quandoque in genere intelliguntur vestimenta Matth. 11. v. 8.cap. 27. vers. 35. &c. quandoque in specie pallia, quae vestimentis interioribus exteriùs superiniiciuntur. Matth. 9. v. 20.cap. 21. v. 7. &c. Utraque significatio hîc locum habere potest. Generalis probatur ex loco parallelo 1. Tim. 2. vers. 9.μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν, ἣ χρυσῷ, ἣ μαργαρίταις, ἣ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ. Specialis probatur ex eo, quòd vestimentorum in genere iam antè fuerat facta mentio sub nomine χρυσίων. Sensus igitur est, quòd Christianae uxores non debeant se pallio, seu quocunque alio vestimento preciosiore vestire. Subintelligendum enim esse epitheton preciosorum, patet ex loco parallelo 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. unde Syrus ἐξηγήσεως causâ addidit, locum Apostolicum sic vertens. Ne ornemini excogitatione auri, aut vestimentorum sumtuosorum. Lyranus ad h. l. sic annotat. Dicitur indumentum vestimentorum per excellentiam, sicut rosa dicitur flos florum. Solent enim foeminae tot induere vestes, totque tunicis, peplis, palliis, iisque sericis, byssinis, preciosis & sumtuosis se ornare, ut unius ornatus multis foeminis sufficere possit.

## 3:4
BUT THE HIDDEN MAN OF THE HEART IN THE INCORRUPTIBILITY OF A QUIET & MODEST SPIRIT, WHICH IS RICH IN THE SIGHT OF GOD.

Connection. 1. The Apostle proceeds by ἄρσιν καὶ θέσιν, and opposes to the excessive & preposterous zeal for external adornment the care and cultivation of the inner man.

2. He commends the fifth & sixth virtue of the female sex, namely πραότητα καὶ ἡσυχίαν.

3. He connects his exhortation, by which the Apostle urges Christian wives to gentleness & tranquility of mind, to the preceding by antithesis, calling those virtues the internal and hidden man, which he opposes to the external adornment of the body.

Disposition of the text. The Apostle confirms his exhortation with a double argument, the former of which is sought from the constancy & durability of those virtues, namely gentleness & tranquility, implying by a silent antithesis that the external adornment of the body is corruptible, & fleeting, indeed momentary: The latter is taken from the excellence & preciousness of those virtues, when he says that that inner adornment is precious before GOD.

Exposition of the text. Ἀλλ᾽ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος. By the hidden man he understands the Christian virtues, which the Holy Spirit works in man through regeneration & renewal, by the example of Paul, who distinguishes one and the same man into inner and outer, Romans 7. verse 22.2. Corinthians 4. verse 16. denoting by the nomenclature of the inner man the spiritual renewal in the reborn man, whence elsewhere for the inner and outer man he puts the old and the new man. Romans 6. v. 6.Colossians 3. v. 9. & 10. whence he joins the renewal of the Spirit, & the putting on of the new man, Ephesians 4. v. 23. & 24. The Vulgate in this place renders it less conveniently hidden, for κρυπτὸς is a noun, not a participle, therefore it is more correctly rendered hidden. The Apostle seems entirely to look to a parallel passage, Romans 2. v. 28. For he is not a Jew, who is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh.

v. 29. But ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, he who is a Jew in secret, and circumcision of the heart, in the Spirit, not in the letter, whose praise is not of men, but of GOD. For in both places we have the man κρυπτὸν, in both places mention is made καρδίας, and what Paul says, that the praise of the secret man is from GOD, Peter explains that in this way, that that secret man is πολυτελὴς before GOD. The little word καρδίας is added ἐξηγητικῶς, for the Apostle declares whom he means, that secret man, namely the interior one, because Christian virtues, signified by the appellation of the secret and interior man, have a place in the heart, regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit: The Syrian rendered it, adorn yourselves in the secret son of man of the heart, where by the secret son of man of the heart he understands the internal man, who is created according to GOD,Eph. 3. v. 24. whom Paul calls the new, internal and spiritual one, and opposes to him the old, external and carnal one. Cajetan wants the hidden man of the heart in incorruptibility to be a description of the immortal man, who has an immortal soul lying hidden in the body and a heart, i. e. the will. But that in incorruptibility pertains to that which follows, of a quiet and modest Spirit.

Έν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ πρᾴεος καὶ ἡσυχίου πνεύματος. The article ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ, must be understood here, viz. κείμενος. The Vulgate rendered it, in the incorruptibility of a quiet and modest Spirit. But the Greek properly has, which is in the incorruption of a meek and quiet Spirit. Jerome, book 1 against Jovinian, cites this passage thus, in the incorruption of a mild and silent Spirit. By incorruption the Apostle understands the integrity and firmness of the Spirit, or of the spiritual and interior man, just as Paul also prays for the Ephesians, that they may be strengthened with power through the Spirit of GOD into the interior man,Eph. 3. v. 16. And likewise the purity and holiness of the Spirit, or of the mind regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit. But especially τὸ ἄφθαρτον πνεύματος is opposed to the exterior adornment of the body, which is corruptible and perishable, so that the sense may be: Whose adornment may not be that exterior and corruptible one, which consists of gold, silver, pearls, gems, silk garments, and other corruptible things, 1. Petr. 1. v. 18. and which is applied and placed around the corruptible body, but that which is concerned with the interior man, and consists in the virtues of the mind and Spirit, which will never perish at any time. By this very thing, therefore, as if by a certain new argument the Apostle dissuades Christian wives from luxury in dress, when he opposes the incorruption of the Spirit and the cultivation of the inner man to fleeting and perishable things, which are applied to the adornment of the body. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian, Bede, and the gloss on this passage establish that τὸ ἄφθαρτον πνεύματος, is opposed to the corruption of virginity, so that the sense may be: Because your outer man is corrupted, and you have ceased to have the blessedness of integrity, which is proper to virgins, imitate the incorruption of the Spirit through abstinence, and what you cannot do with the body, perform with the mind. For Christ seeks these riches and these ornaments of your union. But as ἁγιασμὸς of body and soul cannot be denied to pious spouses, 1. Timoth. 2. vers. 15. so also they are ἄφθαρτοι, in body and soul before GOD immune from spiritual corruption, as long as they remain incorrupt in true faith and holy life, as long as they are free from adulterous loves and illicit flames of burning, and seek that the infirmities adhering to them be pardoned and covered by the grace of GOD on account of the merit of Christ. For they are not excluded from the number of those who are said not to have defiled themselves with women, Apoc. 14. v. 4. and who are said through ἀφθαρσίαν, or in ἀφθαρσίᾳ to seek eternal life, Rom. 2. v. 7. but ἡ κοίτη the marriage bed is ἀμίαντος, Hebr. 13. vers. 4. therefore also the bodies of pious spouses. By πνεῦμα πρᾳές the Apostle denotes the ease of manners and the gentleness of mind, which is opposed to envy, wrath, pride, etc.

By πνεῦμα ἡσύχιον he understands: 1. Tranquility of mind, so that they are not agitated by any storms of depraved desires, 2. Taciturnity, so that they do not snarl at their husbands; and 3. Modesty opposed to levity, petulance, inconstancy, and garrulity, which vices are accustomed to accompany an excessive zeal for external adornment and the neglect of the inner man. John Huss on this passage annotates thus, in the incorruptibility of a quiet and modest Spirit, quiet from the operation of evil, keeping a measure in the operation of good; quiet in adversity, modest in prosperity. The Syrian rendered it, in a Spirit of gentleness, which is not corrupted. B. Luther rendered it unverructet mit sanfftem und stillem Geist/ and in the margin annotates, that they may be pure and upright in faith. It is also to be noted that the little word πνεύματος is placed without an article, and thus according to the rule of Didymus of Alexandria, which however is not absolutely universal, it is hinted at the discourse is about the gifts and effects of the Holy Spirit in a man, regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit,John 7. v. 39.Rom. 7. v. 6.chap. 8. v. 4. & 9.

ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πολυτελὲς. Some Latin Codices read, which is rich in the sight of GOD. But it is more correctly translated, which is precious before GOD, for it refers to the immediately preceding word πνεύματος πολυτελὲς. The Vulgate rendered it, rich, but it is more correctly translated, precious. Nor is it a substantive, otherwise the article Τὸ, would be added, but it refers to πνεῦμα, so that the sense may be: Which Spirit, that is, the mind of pious wives adorned with the meekness and quietness of the Spirit, is precious in the sight of GOD. But even if, as some Interpreters wish, it is referred not to the noun Spirit, but to the whole complex of the preceding discourse, the sense nevertheless remains the same, whence the Syrian ἐξηγητικῶς rendered it. (This is) adorned precious before GOD. Without a doubt the Apostle looks to a parallel passage, 1. Timothy 2. v. 9.Likewise also women in decent apparel, adorning themselves with shamefacedness and sobriety, not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, ἣ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ. For he opposes this προσδιορισμὸν through a certain tacit occupation to the perverse judgment of the world and of haughty women. Although the world considers external adornment of the body to be precious, yet before GOD it is esteemed as nothing, whereas on the contrary the meekness and gentleness of the Spirit are precious before GOD, which therefore pious women ought most studiously to pursue.

Latin:

SED QUI ABSCONDITUS EST CORDIS HOMO IN INCORRUPTIBILITATE QUIETI & MODESTI SPIRITUS, QUOD EST IN CONSPECTU DEI LOCUPLES.

Connexio. 1. Procedit Apostolus per ἄρσιν καὶ θέσιν, ac nimio & praepostero externi ornatus studio opponit interioris hominis curam atque culturam.

2. Quintam & sextam foeminei sexus virtutem commendat, videl. πραότητα καὶ ἡσυχίαν.

3. Exhortationem suam, quâ uxores Christianas ad animi lenitatem & tranquillitatem Apostolus hortatur, praecedenti per antithesin annectit, virtutes illas vocans internum & occultum hominem, quem externo corporis cultui opponit.

Textûs dispositio. Confirmat Apostolus suam exhortationem duplici argumento, quorum prius petitum à virtutum illarum, lenitatis scilicet & tranquillitatis constantiâ & durabilitate, per tacitam antithesin innuens, externum corporis cultum esse corruptibilem, & caducum, imò momentaneum: Posterius desumtum à virtutum illarum praestantia & preciositate, quando dicit, interiorem illum ornatum esse coram DEO preciosum.

Textûs expositio. Ἀλλ᾽ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος. Per occultum hominem intelligit virtutes Christianas, quas Spiritus sanctus per regenerationem & renovationem in homine operatur, exemplo Pauli, qui unum eundemque hominem distinguit in interiorem & exteriorem, Roman. 7. vers. 22.2. Corinth. 4. vers. 16. interioris hominis nomenclatura renovationem spiritualem in homine renato denotans, unde alibi pro interiore & exteriore homine veterem & novum hominem ponit. Roman. 6. v. 6.Col. 3. v. 9. & 10. unde renovationem Spiritus, & induitionem novi hominis coniungit, Ephes. 4. v. 23. & 24. Vulgata hoc loco minùs commodè reddit absconditus,κρυπτὸς enim nomen est, non participium, proinde rectiùs redditur occultus. Videtur omninò Apostolus respicere ad locum parallelum, Rom. 2. v. 28.Non enim, qui in manifesto Iudaeus est, neque quae in manifesto, in carne est circumcisio.

v. 29. Sed ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ,qui in occulto Iudaeus est, & circumcisio cordis, in Spiritu, non litera, cuius laus non ex hominibus, sed ex DEO. Utrobique enim habemus hominemκρυπτὸν,utrobique fit mentioκαρδίας, ac quod Paulus dicit, laudem occulti hominis esse ex DEO, illud Petrus sic exponit, quòd occultus ille homo sit πολυτελὴς coram DEO. Vocula καρδίας additur ἐξηγητικῶς, declarat enim Apostolus, quem dicat, occultum illum hominem, videlicet interiorem, quia virtutes Christianae, occulti & interioris hominis appellatione significatae, locum habent in corde, per Spiritum sanctum regenerato ac renovato: Syrus reddidit, ornate vos in filio hominis occulto cordis, ubi per filium hominis occultum cordis intelligit internum hominem, qui secundùm DEUM creatus est,Eph. 3. v. 24. quem Paulus vocat novum, internum & spiritualem, eique opponit, veterem, externum & carnalem. Caietanus hominem cordis absconditum in incorruptibilitate vult esse descriptionem hominis immortalis, qui habet latentem in corpore animam immortalem & cor, i. e. voluntatem. Verùm illud in incorruptibilitate pertinet ad illud, quod sequitur, quieti & modesti Spiritus.

Έν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ πρᾴεος καὶ ἡσυχίου πνεύματος. Subintelligendus hîc articulus ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ, scil. κείμενος. Vulgata reddidit, in incorruptibilitate quieti & modesti Spiritus. Sed Graeca propriè habent, qui est in incorruptione mansueti & quieti Spiritus. Hieron. lib. 1. contra Iovin. locum hunc sic citat, in incorruptione mitis & silentis Spiritus. Per incorruptionem intelligit Apostolus integritatem & firmitatem Spiritus, sive spiritualis & interioris hominis, sicut etiam Paulus Ephesiis precatur, ut corroborentur virtute per Spiritum DEI in hominem interiorem,Eph. 3. v. 16. Itemque puritatem & sanctitatem Spiritus, sive animi per Spiritum sanctum regenerati ac renovati. Cumprimis vero τὸ ἄφθαρτον πνεύματος opponitur exteriori corporis ornatui, qui est corruptibilis & caducus, ut sit sensus: Quarum ornatus sit non ille exterior & corruptibilis, qui constat auro, argento, margaritis, gemmis, vestibus sericis, & aliis rebus corruptibilibus, 1. Petr. 1. v. 18. quique adhibetur & circumponitur corpori corruptibili, sed qui versatur circa hominem interiorem, & consistit in virtutibus animi & Spiritus, nullo unquam tempore perituris. Hoc ipso igitur velut novo quodam argumento dehortatur Apostolus uxores Christianas à luxu in vestitu, quando incorruptionem Spiritus ac culturam hominis interioris opponit rebus fluxis & caducis, quae ad corporis ornatum adhibentur. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. Beda & gloss. in h. l. statuunt, τὸ ἄφθαρτον πνεύματος,opponi corruptioni virginitatis, ut sit sensus: Quia exterior vester homo corruptus est, & beatitudinem integritatis, quae propria est virginum, habere destitistis, imitamini incorruptionem Spiritus per abstinentiam, & quod corpore non potestis, mente praestate. Has enim Christus divitias, & hos vestrae coniunctionis quaerit ornatus. Sed ut piis coniugibus ἁγιασμὸς corporis & animae denegari nequit, 1. Timoth. 2. vers. 15. ita quoque corpore & anima coram DEO sunt ἄφθαρτοι, à spirituali corruptione immunes, quamdiu in fide vera & vita sancta manent incorrupti, quamdiu ab adulterinis amoribus, & illicitis ustionum flammis sunt liberi, ac infirmitates sibi adhaerentes per gratiam DEI propter Christi meritum condonari ac tegi petunt. Neque enim exclusi sunt ab eorum numero, qui dicuntur, cum mulieribus se non inquinasse,Apoc. 14. v. 4. & qui dicuntur per ἀφθαρσίαν, sive in ἀφθαρσίᾳquaerere vitam aeternam,Rom. 2. v. 7. sed ἡ κοίτη coniugalis lectus est ἀμίαντος,Hebr. 13. vers. 4. ergò & coniugum piorum corpora. Per πνεῦμα πρᾳές denotat Apostolus morum facilitatem, ac animi mansuetudinem, quae opponitur invidiae, iracundiae, superbiae &c.

Per πνεῦμα ἡσύχιον intelligit. 1. Animi tranquillitatem, ut nullis exagitentur pravarum cupiditatum procellis, 2. Taciturninitatem, ne maritis suis ogganniant; ac 3. modestiam levitati, petulantiae, inconstantiae, & garrulitati oppositam, quae vitia comitari solent nimium externi ornatus studium, & interioris hominis neglectum. Iohannes Huss. ad h. l. sic annotat, in incorruptibilitate quieti & modesti Spiritus, quieti ab operatione mali, modum servantis in operatione boni; quieti in adversis, modesti in prosperis. Syrus reddidit, in Spiritu lenitatis, qui non corrumpitur. B. Lutherus reddidit, unverructet mit sanfftem und stillem Geist/ & in margine annotat, ut sint in fide purae & rectae. Notandum & illud, quòd vocula πνεύματος ponatur sine articulo, sicque iuxta regulam Didymi Alexandrini, quae tamen non est absolutè Universalis, innuatur sermonem esse de Spiritus sancti donis & effectis in homine, per Spiritum sanctum regenito & renovato,Ioh. 7. v. 39.Rom. 7. v. 6.cap. 8. v. 4. & 9.

ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πολυτελὲς. Quidam Codices Latini legunt, quod est in conspectu DEI locuples. Sed rectiùs vertitur, qui est coram DEO preciosus, refertur enim ad proximè praecedentem vocem πνεύματος πολυτελὲς. Vulgata reddidit, locuples, sed rectiùs vertitur, preciosus. Nec est substantivum, aliàs adderetur articulus Τὸ, sed refertur ad πνεῦμα, ut sit sensus: Qui Spiritus, hoc est, animus piarum maritarum mansuetudine & quietudine Spiritus ornatus est in conspectu DEI preciosus. Quod si vel maximè, ut quidam Interpp. volunt, non ad nomen Spiritus, sed ad totum praecedentis orationis complexum referatur, idem tamen manet sensus, unde Syrus ἐξηγητικῶς reddidit. (Hic est) ornatus coram DEO preciosus. Dubio procul respicit Apostolus ad locum parallelum, 1. Timoth. 2. v. 9.Similiter & mulieres in habitu decente, cum verecundia & sobrietate ornantes se, non in tortis crinibus, aut auro, aut margaritis,ἣ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ. Opponit enim hunc προσδιορισμὸν per tacitam quandam occupationem perverso mundi & mulierum fastuosarum iudicio. Etsi mundus externum corporis ornatum existimat esse preciosum, tamen coram DEO nihili aestimatur, contra vero mansuetudo & lenitas Spiritus sunt coram DEO preciosae, quas proinde studiosissimè piae foeminae sectari debent.

## 3:5
FOR AFTER THIS MANNER IN THE OLD TIME THE HOLY WOMEN ALSO, WHO TRUSTED IN GOD, ADORNED THEMSELVES, BEING IN SUBJECTION UNTO THEIR OWN HUSBANDS.

Connection. He confirms both exhortations, both to reverence and subjection toward husbands, and to the pursuit of interior adornment, by the example of holy women, from whom they drew their origin by reason of the flesh.

Exposition of the text. Οὕτω γὰρ πότε καὶ αἱ ἁγίαι γυναῖκες, ἐκόσμουν εἁυτὰς, the sense is. Because you were begotten from holy ancestors, namely from holy matriarchs, therefore it is fair that you insist upon their footsteps and adorn yourselves in that manner in which they themselves once adorned themselves. For those women did not solicitously pursue the external cultivation of the body, but, applying themselves to the care of the inner man, they adorned themselves with holy virtues, especially with meekness and the gentleness of the Spirit.

Αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν. The Vulgate rendered it, hoping. But the Greek words properly have, who hoped in GOD, for it is an aorist and the article ἀναφορικὸς. is added. That they are said to have hoped in GOD, the interlinear gloss determines to be opposed to the excessive study of external adornment. Hoping, it says, in GOD, not in the adornment of garments. It is more correctly said that regard is had to the interior and hidden adornment of the heart, of which mention had been made in the immediately preceding article. For just as everywhere in the Scriptures the whole worship of GOD is expressed by the name of fear, so the name of hope is used in this place synecdochically for all virtues flowing from fear and trust in GOD, so that the sense may be: Those holy women adorned themselves interiorly, placing all trust and hope in the living GOD, who is the principal and primary part of that interior adornment. Moreover, this member can be referred either to the preceding, in this sense: they were holy women because their hope was in GOD, and their only care was to please GOD; or to the following, in this sense: because they hoped in GOD, they therefore adorned themselves interiorly with obedience toward their husbands, with chastity, and with a meek and quiet Spirit.

Ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ίδίοις ἀνδράσιν, subject or subjecting themselves to their own husbands, namely with a meek and quiet Spirit, which is to be repeated from the preceding verse. Thus, finally, they judged themselves to be beautifully adorned, if they showed themselves obedient and compliant to their husbands. The Syriac adds a copulative, they adorned themselves and were subject to their husbands. The little word ἀνδράσιν the Syriac rendered by [consult facsimile image]. Moreover, [consult facsimile image] signifies not only husband, but also lord, which signification fits this place beautifully, as is gathered from the following verse.

Latin:

SIC ENIM ALIQUANDO & SANCTAE MULIERES SPERANTES, IN DEO ORNABANT SE, SUBIECTAE PROPRIIS VIRIS.

Connexio. Utramque exhortationem tùm ad reverentiam & subiectionem erga maritos, tùm ad studium interioris ornatus confirmat exemplo sanctarum foeminarum, ex quibus ratione carnis originem ducebant.

Expositio textus. Οὕτω γὰρ πότε καὶ αἱ ἁγίαι γυναῖκες, ἐκόσμουν εἁυτὰς, sensus est. Quia progenitae estis ex sanctis maioribus, ex sanctis scilicet matriarchis, ideò aequum est, ut earum vestigiis insistatis & eo modo vos ornetis, quo ipsae quondam sese exornaverunt. Illae vero non externum corporis cultum solicitè sectatae sunt, sed interioris hominis curae incumbentes, sanctis virtutibus, mansuetudine cumprimis & lenitate Spiritus, sese exornarunt.

Αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν. Vulgata reddidit, sperantes. Sed Graeca propriè habent, quae speraverunt in DEUM, est enim aoristus & additur articulus ἀναφορικὸς. Quod dicuntur sperasse in DEUM, illud glossa interlinearis nimio externi ornatus studio oppositum esse statuit. Sperantes, inquit, in DEO, non in ornatu vestium. Rectiùs dicitur, respectum haberi ad interiorem & occultum cordis ornatum, cuius in proximè praecedente articulo facta erat mentio. Ut enim passim in Scripturis nomine timoris totus DEI cultus exprimitur, ita spei nomen hoc loco synecdochicè pro omnibus virtutibus, ex timore & fiducia in DEUM promanantibus, usurpatur, ut sit sensus. Sanctae illae mulieres interiùs sese ornabant, omnem fiduciam & spem in DEO vivo collocantes, qui est interioris illius ornatus pars principalis & primaria Potest autem hoc membrum referri vel ad praecedentia, sensu eo, ideò erant sanctae mulieres, quia illarum spes erat in DEO, & unica earum cura DEO placere; vel ad sequentia, hoc sensu, quia sperabant in DEUM, ideò interius se ornabant obedientiâ erga maritos, castitate ac Spiritu mansueto & quieto.

Ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ίδίοις ἀνδράσιν,subiectae vel subiicientes se propriis viris videlicet cum mansueto & quieto Spiritu, quod repetendum ex versu praecedente. Ita demum se pulchrè ornatas iudicabant, si obedientes & obsequentes maritis suis sese exhiberent. Syrus addit copulativam, ornabant se & subiectae erant maritis suis. Voculam ἀνδράσιν reddidit Syrus per [consult facsimile image] Significat autem [consult facsimile image] non solùm maritum, sed etiam dominum, quae significatio huic loco pulchrè congruit, ut colligitur ex versu sequente.

## 3:6
AS SARAH OBEYED ABRAHAM, CALLING HIM LORD, WHOSE DAUGHTERS YOU ARE, DOING GOOD AND NOT FEARING ANY DISTURBANCE.

Connection. 1. From the general example of the holy women of the O.T. he passes to the special example of Sarah, the wife of Abraham, and by the same he confirms his exhortation.

2. He had said that holy women in the O.T. were subject to their own husbands; he confirms that with the example of Sarah, insinuating that the same judgment is to be made concerning the remaining matriarchs.

3. He shows what the ἄναστροφὴ, of Christian married women ought to be, of which he had made mention v. 1., namely, that they ought to be ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μεγαλόψυχοι.

Disposition of the text. The Apostle in this verse: 1. Proves the obedience of Sarah toward Abraham from the external effect, namely, from the honorable title by which she honored her husband. 2. Applies this example of Sarah to Christian women, especially those who had been converted from Judaism to the Christian religion, whom he therefore calls daughters of Sarah. 3. Adds a limitation, that they are to be considered true and genuine daughters of Sarah only then, if they strive for good works, and rest in the protection of GOD with great confidence and strength of mind.

Exposition. Ὡς Σάῤῥα ὑπήκουσε τῷ Ἀβραὰμ, κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα. When the Apostle mentions that Sarah was obedient to her husband Abraham, he sends us to the History of Abraham, described in Gen. 12. and the following chapters, in which many and significant examples of obedience rendered by Sarah to her husband are commemorated, namely, that she followed her husband, setting out from the region of Ur of the Chaldeans, her fatherland, to foreign lands, that she was his constant and undivided companion on the journey in exile and pilgrimage through the land of Canaan, that by the command of her husband she even exposed herself to the danger of her modesty, saying that she was his sister; content, if it were necessary, to risk her modesty rather than her husband his safety, as Ambrose speaks in 1 de Abrah. c. 2, that she brought the contempt brought upon her by the handmaid Hagar to her husband and committed it to him to be avenged, that she obeyed her husband commanding the preparation of food to be set before guests, and thus hastened to put that command into effect. Hence the interlinear gloss to the word obeyed in this place rightly adds, even in those things which seemed burdensome.

Κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα. The passage exists Gen. 18. v. 12. when Sarah heard that a son was to be born to her within the space of a year, she laughed, saying within herself, After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure ואדני and my lord is old. Drusius, book 9, passes over it. From the book Musar, chapter 7, f. 73, he cites a similar passage. A good wife stands before her husband, and serves him, and calls him her lord. Which we learn from Sarah, who called Abraham her husband her lord, when she said, my lord is old. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] my lord, which approaches more closely to the Hebrew text. Moreover, this obedience and subjection of Sarah is exaggerated from the fact that, although she herself had been called by GOD Sarah, that is, lady, and it was commanded to Abraham that he should no longer call her Sarai, i.e., my lady, but simply Sarah, i.e., lady, nevertheless, out of sincere and humble compliance, she called her husband her lord.

Ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκνα whose daughters you have become, that is, spiritual ones. For although some of those married women to whom Peter writes were also daughters of Sarah by reason of carnal generation, namely those who had been converted from Judaism to Christianity, the Apostle nevertheless treats in this place principally of spiritual filiation, 1. because he addresses not only those converted from Judaism, but also from Gentilism. 2. because he calls only those daughters of Sarah who are zealous for good works. 3. because he says that they were not born, but have become daughters of Sarah. Hence the gloss on this passage rightly notes: Whose daughters you have become by imitation of faith, even if not by succession of lineage.

Ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι. Some take this προτρεπτικῶς, that the Apostle continues to exhort Christian wives to the pursuit of good works, but it is to be taken properly and principally διακριτικῶς and διοριστικῶς: for the Apostle shows that those alone are to be held as true and spiritual daughters of Sarah who are zealous for good works. By ἀγαθοποιΐαν, some understand in particular beneficence and munificence toward one's neighbor, in which meaning the word ἀγαθοποιεῖν is used Luc. 6. v. 33. & 35. which exposition could be confirmed from the fact that the Apostle is occupied with the example of Sarah, who was prompt and compliant to her husband in doing good to guests arriving from abroad. Gen. 18. v. 6 But it is more correctly taken generally concerning the pursuit of good works, in in which meaning our Apostle perpetually uses this word 1. Epist. 2. v. 14.15. & 20. cap. 3. v. 17.cap. 4. v. 19. whence the Syrian rightly rendered it, [consult facsimile image] [consult facsimile image] in good works, which exposition agrees more with the following words, and is proven from the parallel passage 1. Tim. 2. vers. 10.

Καὶ μὴ φοβούμενοι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν. The Vulgate rendered it. And not fearing any perturbation. But πτόησις properly does not signify perturbation, but dread or consternation from πτοεῖσθαι, which is to be made afraid or to be consternated.Luke 21. v. 9.When you shall hear of wars and seditions, μὴ πτοηθῆτε do not be afraid (for which Matthew says μἠ θροεῖσθζ c. 24. v. 6.) Luke c. 24. v. 37. πτοηθέντες καὶ ἒμψοβοι γενόμενοι, where the latter is ὲξηγητικὸν of the former, the LXX use the word πτοεῖσθαι for חרר which signifies he was terrified, he feared with movement of the bodyEx. 19. v. 16.Amos 3. v. 6. for חתת he was consternated in mind or strength of body.1. Chron. 22. v. 13.cap. 28. v. 20. For מסס thus he was so terrified, that his heart was liquefiedJosh. 7. v. 5. for ערץ he was broken in spirit, he dreadedDeut. 31. v. 6. for פחד he was terrified, he trembled with fear of sudden evilJob 23. v. 15. & for רגז he trembled, he was disturbedHab. 3. v. 6. In the same meaning profane writers also use this word. Plutarch in Alcibiades. πτοηθέντος τοῦ ὄρτυγος the quail being terrified & frightened. The same in Publicola, ἳππους πτοηθέντας he calls horses consternated & terrified. Among Pollux συνωνύμως are placed ἐπτοημένος, ἐκπεπληγμένος, τεθορυβημένος, ἐξεστηκὼς to wit τῷ δέει. From all of which it is gathered, that by πττόησιν sudden dread & consternation is understood here, whence also the Syrian rendered it by [consult facsimile image] dread. However, this φόβος πτοήσεως is explained in various ways by the Interpreters. 1. Some think that regard is had to the immediately preceding word ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι, you are daughters of Sarah, while you do good also, when you are not terrified by any dread i.e. if you are not compelled or driven by fear but of your own accord & freely apply yourselves to good works. The sense therefore would be, wives ought not to be compelled by the terror of husbands to do good, but rather be impelled by the promptness of their own mind to perform their duty, and not be upright by the terror of punishment, but by the love of virtue.

2. Some connect ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι, with the word, but in another sense. While you are zealous for good works, there is no reason for you to fear any evil, for example, that you might displease your husbands if you do not walk about adorned and dressed up, or that they might treat you servilely if you show yourselves obedient to them in all things, or that your husbands might be troublesome to you with unjust reproaches and threats. For your obedience will win for you the love and honor of your husbands. But it is more correctly understood as a certain peculiar property of Christian wives, who are truly daughters of Sarah. However, different expositions also occur according to this hypothesis.

1. B. Luther in his commentary on this passage understands it of that perverse and inordinate fear by which women, placed in dangers or adversities, flee to superstitious and magical arts.

2. Gagnaeius understands it of the dread on account of supervening afflictions and persecutions, which were frequent in the primitive Church.

3. Erasmus interprets it of the dread by which women are accustomed to be dismayed about things of small, or even of no, moment on account of the fragility of their sex.

4. Some understand it of the disturbances and tumults which women are sometimes accustomed to stir up in the household over a frivolous matter.

5. It is most simply understood generally, that he teaches that timidity contrary to faith, from which sudden dread and excessive dismay arises, is absent from holy women, and the Apostle also wishes it to be absent; for he says in general, μὴ φοβούμενοι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν, not terrified by any dread, where before μηδεμίαν is understood κατὰ, and the double negation denies more strongly in the Greek manner. Indeed, it is customary in the Scriptures for dread and fear μετωνυμικῶς to signify not only GOD, who is to be feared and reverently worshipped, Gen. 31. v. 42. but also sudden evil, which is the cause of dread. Psalm 53. v. 6. There they feared a fear, where there was no fear, i.e., evil, the cause of dread. Psalm 91. v. 5. You shall not fear from the fear of the night. Prov. 1. v. 26. When your dread comes, i.e., the evil for fear of which you are terrified. Prov. 3. v. 25. You shall not be afraid of sudden dread, i.e., of sudden evil, where likewise φοβεῖν πτόησιν are joined, as in this place. The rule can also be applied here: Among the Hebrews, words of act or affection are accustomed to be put for the object.

Job 3. verse 25.the fear which I feared, has come upon me, i. e. the evil which I feared. Psalm 106. verse 12.they praised his praise, i. e. his praiseworthy name. v. 14.they lusted a lust in the desert, i. e. they lusted after illicit things. Titus 2. v. 13.expecting the blessed hope, i. e. heavenly blessedness and glory, which we expect by faith. Thus therefore also in this place, Christian wives are not held by any terror, that is, they so trust in the favor, protection, help, and gracious presence of God, that they do not fear any evil for themselves in a preposterous manner, but with firm confidence of heart they rely solely upon God. Thus therefore with ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ is joined true faith, and confidence of heart, which animates Christian wives against sudden and unexpected terrors, for a double reason. 1. because the source and foundation of ἀγαθοποιΐας is true faith, and firm confidence in Christ. 2. because Christian wives by faith have been made true and spiritual daughters of Sarah, just as Romans 4. verse 12.children of Abraham are called those who follow the footsteps of the faith of Abraham.

Q. in this place. 1. Why does the Apostle, after the precepts delivered to subjects and servants in the preceding chapter, not admonish the Magistrate and masters of their duty? Indeed Paul Ephesians 6. v. 9.Colossians 4. v. 1. after he had prescribed to servants the due tasks of their duty, also admonishes masters what they owe to servants. But Peter in this place mentions only servants, because he writes especially to those converted from the Jews placed in the dispersion, 1. Epistle 1. v. 1. among whom there were many servants, but few masters.

2. Why does he exhort Christian wives to subjection toward their husbands so laboriously? Resp. Just as the Apostles were falsely burdened with this calumny, that they taught that subjects owed no obedience to an Ethnic Magistrate, and servants to infidel masters: so also it was detracted from them, that they taught that Christian wives ought to be separated from infidel husbands through divorces. The occasion of the calumny was that Christian matrons, by the institution of the Apostles, refused to endure the abominable lusts of their husbands which were contrary to the law of Nature, and some even divorced them on this account. Eusebius book 4. Ecclesiastical History chapter 17. from the Apology of Justin the Philosopher and Martyr brings forward these things. A certain woman had lived with a husband given to lasciviousness, to which she herself had also been given previously. After she had known the doctrine of Christ, she returned to repentance and the chastity of life, and attempting to persuade her husband to repent in a similar way, she explained to him the doctrine which threatens the future punishment of eternal fire to those living intemperately and not according to right reason. But he, persisting in those same lascivious acts of his, alienates his wife from himself by his illicit deeds. For she was saying that it would be illicit henceforth to share the same bed with that man who, against the law of Nature and beyond what is fair and right, sought ways for his pleasure from every quarter. But since she was recalled from that opinion by the persuasions of friends, who advised that she should still live with her husband, because there was hope that it would come to pass that he would one day return to himself, she remained in that marriage by restraining herself. But when that man was reported to have set out for Alexandria and to be perpetrating worse things, lest she be rendered a partner in crimes and impious outrages if she persisted in his marriage and used the same cohabitation and bed with him, having given a bill of divorce, she is separated and departs. Chrysostom, book 1 against those who disparage the Monastic life, records that Paul, having converted Nero's mistress, whom he was desperately in love with and held in delights, had alienated her from Nero's friendship, and that consequently Nero had called Paul a corrupter, a scoundrel, and a flagitious man, and had thrown him into chains, and afterwards had demanded of him that he cease to give such counsels and admonitions to the girl, which, when he could not obtain from Paul, he killed him. But that which is recorded in the book which is circulated under the name of Linus concerning the passion of Peter and Paul, that the wife of Albinus, having been so taught by Peter, had repudiated the bed of her husband for the love of chastity, even with the husband protesting, and that Agrippa the prefect had therefore said to Peter: You have much confidence, O wicked one, in the common people whom you circumvent, and in the women who by your persuasion depart from the marital bed, that shows that writing, which is in no way consistent with the truth and less in conformity with the Apostolic doctrine 1. Corinth. 7. vers. 10., and which reeks with a full mouth of Manichaeism, to be supposititious, which Baronius acknowledges in the year 66, n. 14, year 69, n. 6, year 80, n. 4, Bellarmine, 2. d. R. P. cap. 9. and de script. Eccles. p. 55. Therefore, in order that Peter might meet these calumnies of the gentiles, he exhorts Christian wives to render obedience to their husbands, even if they are infidels, just as he had also diluted other calumnies of the gentiles in the preceding passages.

Q. 3. Why does he address by name those wives who are married to infidel husbands? Resp. There were many unequal marriages at that time, as is gathered from Acts 16. vers. 1. 1. Cor. 7. v. 12. & 13. Because, therefore, Christian wives joined to infidel husbands had more color for shaking off they seemed to have the yoke of marital obedience, therefore he specifically reminds them of their duty, and brings forward a special reason why they ought to obey their husbands with greater zeal, namely, that they might entice them to the love of the Christian religion by their compliance. Meanwhile, he leaves it to be understood that if wives owe obedience to unbelieving husbands, they are much more obligated to it who are married to Christian husbands.

Q. 4. Why does he address Christian wives before husbands? Resp. 1. Because in the preceding chapter he had dealt with the subjection which subjects owe to the Magistrate, and servants to their masters, therefore he wished to continue the exhortation of subjection. 2. Because women, on account of the infirmity of their sex v. 8., were more in need of that exhortation.

Q. 5. Whether the wife would have been subject to the husband even before the fall in the state of integrity? Resp. among the paternal chastisements imposed upon Eve and her daughters themselves after the fall, the dominion of the husband is also included, Genes. 3. vers. 16. from which it seems to be gathered that that subjection did not have a place before the fall: conversely, however, 1. Corinth. 11. v. 8. among the arguments by which obedience is to be persuaded to wives, it is included that the man is from the woman, and that the man is the head of the woman, v. 3. Therefore, one must distinguish between obedience that is voluntary, sweet, and harmonious: and subjection that is involuntary, difficult, and troublesome. Likewise between rule that is free, voluntary, and pleasant, such as the husband's would have been over the wife even before the fall: and rule that is involuntary, harsh, and troublesome, such as it is today after the fall. Before the fall there would have been a certain prerogative and eminence of dignity in the husband, but such dominion of power as was given to husbands over wives after the fall, and such subjection of the female sex as obtains today, would not have had a place in the state of integrity, since the husband would have done nothing through anger or importunity, nor would the will of the wife have departed in a different direction from the will of the husband, but both would have most quietly consented in the holy will of GOD, which most beautiful harmony has been miserably disrupted by the fall. August. lib. 11. de Genes. ad liter. cap. 27.

Q. 6. Why does he specifically require meekness and gentleness of Spirit from wives in v. 4.? Resp. because meekness and gentleness are especially required in persevering through the importunity of husbands, especially unbelieving ones, if wives ought to be subject to them with a calm mind.

Q. 7. Whether by the Spirit v. the same the Holy Spirit, the third person of the Deity, is to be understood? Athanasius in his Epistle to Serapion establishes it thus, with this argument, that it properly belongs to the Holy Spirit, what Peter predicates of him in this place, namely that he is rich with GOD, as being a sharer of the same divinity with him. He therefore thinks the sense is such. Those who keep themselves pure and incorrupt have the Holy Spirit dwelling within, who, since he is quiet and modest, makes them also quiet and modest. To which it could be referred, that meekness and gentleness are fruits of the SpiritGal. 5. vers. 22. Idacius brings forward the same exposition in his book against Varimadus, responding, that modesty is spoken of the Holy Spirit, just as it is of the Father, according to a certain place of Jeremiah from the LXX edition, and of Christ2. Cor. 10. vers. 1. according to the Vulgate version. But Ambrose in book 1 of his Offices, chapter 18, more correctly understands it of the spirit of man, regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit, which is the best ornament of women, if it has been endowed with meekness, gentleness, and other virtues. For it is placed πνεῦμα without the article, and what is called πνεῦμα πρᾳὲς, in this place 1. Corinth. 4. vers. 21.Galat. 6. v. 1. is called πνεῦμα πρᾳότητος.

Q. 8. Why does he propose the examples of holy women to Christian wives? Resp. because there is altogether great power in examples, especially among the female sex μιμητικὸν.

9. Why does he bring forward the example of Sarah in particular? Resp. he writes especially to women converted from Judaism, therefore from all the holy women of the Old Testament he brings forward Sarah, as the parent of the whole Israelite race. He makes use of this example Esaiae cap. 51. v. 1. Look unto the rock, whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit, whence ye are diggedv. 2. Look unto Abraham, your father, and unto Sarah, that bare you. Where by the name of rock those sterile and worn-out spouses are understood, for the reason that it was an equally great miracle for Isaac to be born from them, as if God had raised up a son to Abraham from stonesMatth. 3. v. 9. Regard is also had to the multiplication of posterity. For as many stones are dug out from a quarry: so all the Israelites were propagated in great number from those parents through succession.

Peter also follows in this part the example of the Apostle Paul, who introduces Abraham as the spiritual Father of all believers Rom. 4. v. 11. & 12.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. By the particle ὁμοίως the Apostle compares the subjection of wives toward husbands to the subjection of servants toward masters v. 1. but v. 8. he commands husbands to bestow honor upon wives as upon a weaker vessel: Resp. The particle ὁμοίως is not a mark of total equality, but of similarity and proportion. For the Apostle does not equate wives in subjection to servants, since a wife was not formed from the feet, but from the side of the man, and therefore is the companion of the husband, not a servant, but he imports a similarity of the precept and a certain proportion of subjection. Just as servants owe obedience to masters, by reason of servile subjection: so wives owe obedience to husbands, by reason of conjugal subjection. Masters command servants δεσποτικῶς, husbands wives γαμικῶς.

2. Let women be subject to their husbands, that even if any do not believe the word, they may be won over by the conduct of the women without the word v. 1.
