But Rom. 10. 17. faith is from hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Resp. 1. The words of the Apostle are to be understood not of total conversion, but of the occasion of conversion. He teaches that the holy conduct of Christian wives is a certain occasion of conversion for unbelieving husbands and a certain silent invitation to embrace the Christian faith. For when husbands who are still unbelievers notice that their wives, converted to Christ, are obedient to them out of the teachings of the Christian religion, chaste, not at all desirous of external adornment, gentle, quiet, studious of good works, courageous in dangers and adversities, they begin to think more honestly about the Christian religion, and to be of a more favorable mind toward it, which is as it were the first step toward conversion, or certainly the removal of an impediment, namely, a preconceived hatred toward the Christian faith. 2. Therefore, Peter by no means establishes immediate conversion through interior inspirations and Enthusiasms, but teaches that GOD leads those who show themselves docile to the knowledge of Christ through certain steps. 3. When he asserts that unbelieving husbands can be won over without the word, he does not simply and absolutely exclude the word from the means of conversion, but speaks of the word of public preaching, from which unbelieving husbands are previously alienated, before they are as it were enticed to it by the holy conduct of their wives.

3. Let the adorning of pious women not be the plaiting of hair, or the wearing of gold, or the putting on of costly garments.v. 3. But yet,Gen. 24. v. 22. the servant of Abraham adorns Rebecca, the bride of Isaac, with a golden necklace and bracelets.Psal. 45. v. 20. & seqq. the spiritual adornment of the Bride of Christ is described in metaphorical words taken from the bodily adornment of a Royal Bride.Ezech. 16. v. 12. & 13.Ose. 2. v. 8. & 13. necklaces, bracelets, earrings, and similar ornaments of women are referred to among the gifts of GOD. Esther was adorned with royal garmentsEsth. 2. v. 17. Judith arranged the hair of her head, and placed a mitre upon her head, and put on the garments of her gladness, she took bracelets, and lilies, and earrings, and rings, and adorned herself with all her ornaments.Matth. 6. v. 29. Christ commends the royal adornment of Solomon. Resp. The Apostolic prohibition, conformable to the Pauline 1. Tim. 2. v. 9., is not to be taken simply, but with a determination, if indeed women exalt themselves above their lot and condition with sumptuous and luxurious attire, if they are too devoted to the external cultivation of the body, and are little or not at all solicitous about the internal cultivation of the mind and spiritual adornment. This is evident from the antithesis placed below, by which the Apostle admonishes women to expend greater care upon the adornment of the Spirit, which is precious before GOD, than upon the external adornment of the body, which is corruptible and fleeting. For the Apostolic negation is to be taken comparatively, according to the customary rule. Among the Hebrews, negative words are often placed for comparative ones.Gen. 32. v. 28.Exod. 16. v. 8.1. Sam. 8. v. 7.Prov. 8. v. 10.Ierem. 7. v. 22.Luc. 14. vers. 12.1. Tim. 2. v. 14. &c. The Apostle Paul in the parallel passage 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. so disapproves of braided hair, gold, pearls, and costly clothing, that he permits καταστολὴν κόσμιον attire that is adorned, modest, and honest with shamefacedness and sobriety. Therefore, the Apostle by no means forbids every external adornment whatsoever, with which either women or even men, by reason of status, region, age, time, &c., decently clothe and adorn themselves, but he forbids all care and thought from being placed in external adornment, and teaches that the internal cultivation of the mind and spiritual adornment must be preferred by far to the external cultivation of the body. Hence Basil in Moral Constitutions, chapter 5, rule 73, rightly explains the words of Peter thus: women ought not to study to be too exquisite in the elegance of bodily adornment, but rather to confer all their care upon good works. Jerome, book 1 against the Pelagians: Everywhere, O Pelagius, pass over the mediocre ὑπερβολικῶς and pursue the great. Whence you add that the glory of garments and ornaments are contrary to God. What enmities, I ask, are there against God, if I have a cleaner tunic, if a Bishop, Presbyter, and Deacon, and the rest of the Ecclesiastical order proceed in the administration of sacrifices in a white garment? Beware Clerics, beware Monks, widows and virgins you are in danger, unless the common people see you as filthy and ragged.

4. The adornment of Christian wives ought not to be in gold and precious garments v. 3. And yet through this adornment wives commend themselves to their husbands. Which moderate desire of pleasing husbands Paul does not disapprove.1. Cor. 7. v. 33.lest, namely, men cast their mind and eyes upon other women. Resp. If a wife adorns herself decently and moderately with that end, that she may please her husband, that is by no means disapproved by the Apostle, but if by an excessive desire for external adornment she strives to please other men. Augustine Epist. 73. to Possidius. I do not wish, however, that you have a hasty opinion in prohibiting ornaments of gold or clothing, except for those who, being neither married nor desiring to be married, ought to think how they may please God. But those think of the things that are of the world, how they may please, either husbands their wives or wives their husbands, except that it does not befit women to bare their hair, whom the Apostle even commands to cover their head, nor does it befit married women. But to be painted with pigments, by which one may appear either redder or whiter, is an adulterous deception, by which I do not doubt that even the husbands themselves do not wish to be deceived, to whom alone women are permitted to be adorned according to indulgence, not according to command.

5. The Apostle approves of Sarah's subjection from the fact that she called Abraham her husband lord.v. 7.And yet even disobedient and refractory wives can call their husbands Lords. Resp. The Apostle does not conclude from the address alone, but joins with it a real exhibition of obedience, a clear proof of which is described in that very cap. 18. Genes. to which the Apostle refers us, namely, that at the command of her husband Sarah hastened to prepare food for guests who were still unknown.

6. Sarah obeyed Abraham.v. 7. And yet Gen. 16. v. 5.she accuses her husband as acting unjustly toward her. Resp. Chrysost. hom. 38. in Gen. That Sarah had a just cause for complaining, for it was unworthy that Hagar the handmaid should be puffed up against the primary spouse and mistress, and not be restrained by Abraham on this account. But if any infirmity concurs in this little matter, as the same Chrysostom wishes, from that it is gathered that the obedience even of the pious in this life is not perfect in all respects.

7. You have become daughters of Sarah, doing good.v. 7.And yet through the pursuit of good works we cannot arrive at spiritual υἱοθεσίαν, but through faith in Christ.Rom. 4. v. 12. Resp. 1. The Apostle joins confidence, resting in the mercy of GOD promised on account of Christ, to the pursuit of good works, as we showed in the exposition of the text. Therefore, he brings forward the pursuit of good works, not as a υἱοθεσίας medium of spiritual life, but as a necessary consequence and effect of true faith in Christ. 2. The Theological rule must be repeated here. Active verbs are often to be explained declaratively, and things are then said to be done when they are manifested as done. August. lib. 83. qq. q. 69. A thing is said to be done when it is declared or predicted as done.Iob. 9. v. 31.my garments will abhor me, i. e. they will show that I am abominable. Esa. 43. vers. ult.I have contaminated the holy Princes, i. e. I have declared them contaminated, when I ordered them to die. Especially pertinent here are two N. T. sayings, Matth. 5. v. 44.Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you &c.v. 45.that you may be sons of your Father, i. e. that you may declare in reality that you are genuine sons of the heavenly Father. Ioh. 15. v. 8.In this is my Father glorified, that you bear much fruit, and become my disciples, i. e. that by bearing copious fruit you may declare that you are my disciples.

Ἒλεγχος. 1. The Apostle prescribes precepts of a holy life to married people; there is deep silence in the Apostolic writings concerning monks and votary nuns who place perfection in this kind of their life. Therefore, monasticism, such as flourishes today in the Papacy, does not enjoy divine institution, nor Apostolic approbation. Fulgentius Epist. 3. cap. 8. Paul did not so ascribe holiness of body and Spirit to virgins,1. Cor. 7. v. 34.that he would either take it away from the married or deny it to widows. He proves this from the fact that Peter does not hesitate to call married faithful women Holy.

2. The Apostles prescribe their duties not only to virgins and widows, but also to married people, and Peter teaches in this place that even married women can and ought to strive that they may be adorned inwardly before GOD, and may please Him. They show, therefore, that even the married state pleases GOD. This must be opposed to the Papists, who in various ways derogate from the dignity of marriage, as by calling it uncleanness and pollution, by establishing it as an impediment to piety, by heaping insults upon celibacy and marriage, by forbidding marriage to the whole Ecclesiastical order, by tolerating concubinage and wandering lusts in Ecclesiastical persons rather than permitting honest marriage to them, by demanding and accepting vows of celibacy from persons less suited for it, by tolerating public brothels to the disgrace of marriage, and by separating spouses joined by God from one another, all of which things see proved in the treatise on the Church §. 251, and the treatise on marriage §. 51.

3. The Apostle does not command that faithful women joined in marriage to unfaithful husbands should depart from them, but that they should lead a life worthy of the Christian life, and by this means strive to win their husbands for Christ. Paul commands the same 1. Corinth. 7. v. 12. and following. This must be opposed to the Canonists, who count diversity of religion among the impediments not only prohibiting marriage from being contracted, but also dissolving it once contracted; and to Bellarmine, who in his book on marriage, chapter 23, forms in the third place a proposition of this kind: Marriage between a believer and an unbaptized unbeliever is void by the custom of the Christian people, obtaining the force of law; and by the practice used in some places in the Papacy.

4. Chastity pleasing to GOD also has a place in marriage, because the Apostle requires chaste conversation from wives. Therefore, that which the Pontiff says about married Priests in c. We decree, dist. 28, must be disapproved: Since they ought to be the temple, and vessels of the Lord, and the sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, it is unworthy for them, by taking wives, to serve beds and impurities; as well as what Bellarmine writes in his book on marriage, chapter 5: that it can be said not badly of married people: Those who are in the flesh cannot please God; which same thing he in his book on Monks, chapter 9, for establishing the celibacy of Monks brings forward the passage Apoc. 14. These are they who have not been defiled with women, from which it follows by a contrary sense that married men are defiled with women; and what he writes in his book on Clerics, chapter 19: that even the marriage of saints is not exercised without a certain pollution and baseness, and that the conjugal act makes the soul itself in a certain way carnal; and in the same book, chapter 18, that the conjugal act renders the whole man carnal and inept for divine things.

5. Those finally are the true and genuine daughters of Sarah, who believe in Christ, and from faith strive for good works. This must be opposed This is opposed to the preposterous boasting of the Jews, by which they perpetually brag of the propagation of their race from holy ancestors, and especially from Abraham Matt. 3. v. 9.John 8. v. 33., to whom that saying of Christ is deservedly opposed John 8. v. 39. If you were Abraham's children, you would do the works of Abraham; as also those Pauline ones Rom. 2. v. 28. not he who is a Jew in the manifest &c. chap. 4. v. 11. Abraham is the father of all believers &c. chap. 9. v. 6. Not all who are of Israel, they are Israelites, v. 7. nor because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children, v. 8. but those who are reckoned as children of the promise in the seed. Gal. 3. v. 7. Those who are of faith, they are the children of Abraham.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Cornelius à Lapide on v. 1 notes thus: Peter ordains so explicitly that wives should be subject to their husbands, because a rumor was being spread by the Gentiles, though a false one, that Christians, as if they were children of Christ, wished to exempt themselves from all servitude and subjection, and especially wives from the company of their spouses, and that partly because the lustful Gentiles were abusing their wives preposterously against Nature, but the Apostles forbade this, that they should not permit it to their wives &c. and partly because many virgins betrothed by their parents to infidel men would recoil from their betrothals and betrothed men before the marriage was consummated, on account of love or a vow of virginity, which they heard being so celebrated by the Apostles. But there exists no trace in the Apostolic writings that the Apostles separated betrothed women from infidel betrothed men, or demanded or received a vow of virginity. The examples of Flavia, Thecla, Iphigenia, Susanna &c. which Cornelius brings forward, are not taken from approved writers, but from supposititious ones, the writings of Linus, Abdias, Metaphrastes, and others.

2. The Anabaptists, Enthusiasts, Weigelians &c. abuse those words of the Apostle, that if any do not believe, they may be won without the word v. 1., to disparage the external ministry of the word, as if it were not an instrument necessary by the ordination of GOD, and efficacious for exciting and nourishing faith in the hearts of men. But we showed above that Peter is speaking only of the occasion by which infidel husbands are led to think more honestly about the Christian religion, so that they no longer hate the public assemblies in which the word of the Gospel is preached, but attend them, and in the progress of time conceive faith from the word, and embrace the Christian religion.

3. Cajetan establishes that the precept of Peter concerning the neglect of external adornment, v. 3, is temporary, given only to the primitive Church, in which women who were worshippers of Christ renounced all allurements. But the precept This is moral and perpetual, pertaining to the degrees and states of women of every time, as appears from the antithesis below, and from the parallel Apostolic passage. 1. Tim. 2. v. 9.

4. Estius on verse 4 comments thus. The Apostle shows whom he calls the hidden man, namely him who consists in the mind or the part of reason, by which we are properly men, whom the Apostle calls the interior one. 2. Cor. 4. v. 16. Lorinus on this passage: The hidden and interior man is therefore according to his superior part, which is reason and will, and not patent to the senses of men. And yet by the name of hidden and interior man is not understood absolutely and simply the mind or soul of man, but the mind renewed by the Holy Spirit, and thus the whole man consisting of body and soul, insofar as he is regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit. For that ornament, which the Apostle here commends to the female sex, is not only interior, but also spiritual, therefore it has a place only in those women who are regenerated and renewed by the Holy Spirit, whence the Apostle notably adds that that hidden man of the heart consists in the incorruption of a meek and quiet spirit, showing that meekness, gentleness, and other virtues, in which the exterior ornament consists, are effects and fruits of the Holy Spirit Galat. 5. v. 22. whence Lorinus adds. Nevertheless, speaking more properly, the old man imports guilt and punishment; the new man justice and glory. The new man includes the perfection of the interior.

5. Salmero establishes that πτόησιν in v. 7. can be accepted as lust. For he comments on that verse thus. Some say, πτόησιν is the excessive ardor of lust in women. And thus Aristotle book 4 on the generation of animals concludes, that women after many births are finally freed from this ardor. For the woman is confounded in spirit, when the suffocations of the womb prove it. And thus he teaches, that those doing rightly ought to fear no burning lust, since the grace of God provides for them that which Nature grants to women after many births. We reply, we concede that πτόησιν among profane writers is sometimes accepted for that erotic affection, by which women burn with excessive and as it were stupid lust for the Venereal thing, in which way Budaeus interprets the passage adduced from Aristotle, book 4 on the generation of animals, chapter 5, which in Greek has it thus. Ἒστι γὰρ τὰ καταμήνια σπέρμα ἄπεπτον, διὸ καὶ τῷν γυναικῶν ὅσαι πρὸς τὴν ὁμιλίαν ἀκρατεῖς τὴν τοιάυτην, ὃταν πολυτοκήσωσι, πάυονται τῆς πτοήσεως, ἐκκεκριμένη γὰρ ἡ σπερματικὴ περίττωσις οὐκέτι ποιεῖ τῆς ὁμιλίας τάυτης ἐπιθυμίαν, from which it appears that Salmeron translated it with obscure and foreign words. Among Plato σωφροσύνη is described thus, that it is τὸ περιτὰς ἐπιθυμίας μὴ ἐπτοῆσθαι.. Among Euripides it is held ἐπτοήθης ἒρωτι you are struck with the gadfly of love even to stupor. But this πτοήσεως meaning nowhere occurs in the Scriptures, and is entirely foreign to this place. For what sense would there be here, you have become daughters of Sarah doing good and fearing no heat of lust. Thence Cornelius à Lapide, criticizing Salmeron with his name suppressed, annotates thus on this place. Less chastely some take the perturbation as of lust, which the Greek word πτόησις signifies among Aristotle, indeed. Do not fear that lust is to be inflamed in you through obsequiousness toward a husband, because those things beget charity, not desire. Lorinus on this place. I admit the notion of the Greek word handed down by the Philosopher for that excessive and as it were astonished and stupid lust περὶ τὰ ἀφροδίσια, but I do not think it is to the point, nay I judge it unworthy of so great an Apostle, even to indicate a matter so little honest. That also μηδεμίαν argues a more general fear. Finally it should rather have been said πτοούμεναι which word would correspond to the name πτόησις, and has a similar use, which φοβούμεναι.

6. Cornelius à Lapide from v. 7. tries to prove, that marriage is a Sacrament, for thus he annotates to it. Do not fear perturbations i. e. the troubles of marriage. For if you do good, and live worthily of marriage, God by His grace makes them easy for you. For this grace is an effect of the Sacrament of matrimony prepared by God for spouses, so that they may bravely sustain the burdens of matrimony, and being well conscious to themselves may fear nothing. Resp. We concede that to pious spouses grace is given by God, by which they may be able to sustain the burdens of matrimony bravely, and to be in this kind of life with a quiet mind. But from that it cannot be inferred that marriage is a Sacrament divinely ordained, for neither is that grace given through marriage itself, but through prayers made from faith by pious spouses; nor does any grace constitute a Sacrament, but that which is proper to the Gospel and includes the remission of sins.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. There is proposed here a mirror of virtues which pious women ought to contemplate daily, and to which they ought to conform themselves and their life. Such virtues are: 1. Subjection, through which they may temper their own will to the will of the husband. 2. Reverence toward the husband, by which they may solicitously take care not to offend the husband by deed, word, or even gesture. 3. Chastity in manners, words, gestures, and in their whole conversation. 4. Fear of GOD, which is the foundation of a pious and chaste conversation. 5. Humility, that they may not be too eager for the external adornment of the body. 6. Meekness, that they may not be back-talkers or murmurers when they are rebuked by their husbands. 7. Tranquility, that they may not be curious about the affairs of others, that they may not run about to inquire into the affairs of others, that they may not be troublesome to their husbands or others with their garrulity. Prov. 7. vers. 11. &c. 8. Affability, that they may address their husbands gently. 9. Kindness and a zeal for doing good. 10. Strength of mind, that they may not be too fearful, but in dangers and adversities be endowed with great confidence of a mind resting in GOD. Prov. 31. v. 10.Sirac. 26. v. 2.

2. The causes are by far very many, which ought to exhort women to subjection. v. 1. These are the more important: 1. Creation 1. Cor. 11. 8. The man is not of the woman, but the woman of the man. v. 9. neither was the man created for the woman, that is to say, that he might serve her, as if she were more excellent, but the woman for the man. 1. Tim. 2. v. 13. Adam was first formed, then Eve. 2. Transgression. 1. Tim. 2. v. 14. Adam was not seduced, that is to say, first and immediately by the Devil, but the woman being seduced was in the transgression i. e. she was the first to transgress the commandment of God, and persuaded Adam, so that he himself also might transgress the same. 3. The ordination of God. Gen. 3. v. 16. thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. 1. Cor. 14. v. 33. It becomes women to be subject, as also the law saith. 4. The dignity of the husband. 1. Cor. 11. vers. 3. the head of the woman is the man, insofar as he excels in sex, and is constituted her Lord. vers. 7. the man is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man. The Apostle looks to that part of the divine image which was situated in dominion. Just as God is the lord of the whole world and commands all creatures, so the father of the family is the Lord of the house, and commands the woman and the household. Glory is taken for the representation of divine majesty and domination. The man is the glory of GOD i. e. he represents the majesty and dignity of God, obtaining the highest rank in the government of the household, and having dominion over the wife in the name of GOD. By the name of glory could also be understood power and excellence men, because power produces authority and glory. Augustine q. 153. in Genesis There is a natural order among men, that women should serve men, because even there this is justice, that the weaker reason should serve the stronger, and this is a clear justice in dominations and servitudes, that those who excel in reason should excel in domination. 5. God's approval. If a woman obeys her husband, she can determine with certainty from faith that this obedience of hers is pleasing to God, for those works which God commands are pleasing to Him. Johannes Huss in this place Women ought to be subject to men for five reasons. The first is the transgression of God's command. For from the woman's transgression the perdition of men and the misery of this life took its origin. Whence GOD said to her as a punishment for the transgression. Because you have done this, you shall be under the power of a man. The second is the elation of pride. August. A woman elated, obeying the persuasion of the serpent, despised the commands of God, and on account of this she deserves to be subject to the power of a man. The third is the fragility and instability of Nature, and therefore they ought to obey more constant men, and not rule men, but be ruled by men. The fourth is the passion of modesty, which is more present in women, from which when a woman fails, she is very prone to malice, from which she ought to be restrained by a man, Sirac. 26. In a daughter not taking heed i. e. not modest, there is firm custody. 1. Tim. 2. Women with modesty and sobriety. The fifth is the clamor and litigation of words. Prov. 9. A foolish and clamorous woman &c.

3. That subjection of wives has a certain limitation, lest for the sake of husbands they sin against GOD and His holy word, whence Paul wishes wives to be subject to their husbands in the Lord. Col. 3. v. 18. which phrase embraces two things, first that they ought to be subject to their husbands according to the command and ordination of GOD, who willed them to be subject to their husbands. Secondly that they ought to be subject under GOD, lest from this obedience toward husbands they do anything against GOD. Ephes. 6. vers. 1. Beda in this place It is to be noted, that Peter desires good and honest women to be subject to unbelieving husbands on the condition that they not only do nothing evil at their command, but also persist so insuperable in chaste conversation, that they themselves may be able to be an example of chastity and faith to their husbands.

4. When the Apostle wishes wives to be subject to their own husbands, he prohibits adultery, and denies that they have power over their own body. 1. Corinth. 7. v. 8. He declares the same thing more clearly, when in v. 2. he requires chaste conversation from them. This chastity is ἁγιασμὸς that μετὰ σωφροσὺνης, which Paul requires of them in the parallel passage 1. Tim. 2. v. 15. Plutarch mentions in his problems, that it was formerly the custom for fire and water to be brought before a new bride, to signify that she ought to be chaste and pure, for fire purges, and water cleanses.

5. If in an unequal marriage the Apostle requires subjection and reverence toward husbands from wives, how much more ought that to have a place between spouses who are both Christian. Thus concludes Hieron. Epist. ad Celantiam.

6. Unbelief is defined by disobedience toward the word of the Gospel, ἡ ἀπιστία is defined by ἀπειθείαν, just as faith is defined by obedience toward the Gospel. Rom. 1. vers. 5.cap. 16. vers. 26.1. Petr. 1. v. 2. & 22.

7. All Christians, but especially and in a certain peculiar way the ministers of the Church, are servants of ChristRom. 1. v. 1.Gal. 1. v. 10. etc. therefore they ought to strive solicitously that they may gain many for Christ with the talent of the word entrusted to them, Matth. 25. v. 16. which zeal the Apostle proclaims of himself 1. Cor. 9. v. 19. & following.

8. Not only Christian wives, but all Christians whatsoever, of whatever sex, age, and status they may be, ought to strive for a chaste and holy conversation, so that by their example they may entice others to the love of true religion. For whose conversation is pleasing, his religion cannot be displeasing.

9. Just as the pursuit of good works invites and entices others to embrace the doctrine of the Gospel: So the wickedness of life and morals deters unbelievers more from the same and alienates their minds, concerning which matter God complains most gravely. Esai. 52. v. 5.Ezech. 36. v. 23.Rom. 2. v. 24. the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you.

10. Τὰ ἔργα have greater force for the conversion of others than ψιλοὶ λόγοι. Chrysost. homil. 19. in Epist. Hebr. The voice of the work is more efficacious than that of speech, says Iohan. Hufs. from Bernard in this place. The manner of living is worth more than the manner of speaking. August. Epist. 112. Men prefer examples to words, because it is easy to speak, but difficult to perform. Lactant. lib. 4. Instit. cap. 23. It is best to teach by example rather than by words. Hilarius can. 5. in Matth.

11. Regarding the external adornment of the body, φιλοκόσμῳ is sinned against in many ways by the female sex, namely through superfluity, novelty, preciousness etc. 1. They are too indulgent toward that external cultivation, so that in the meantime they neglect the internal and spiritual adornment. Those who are anxiously occupied in the cultivation of the body, neglect the cultivation of the soul. Cato once said. 2. If they are too delighted by that adornment, when they ought rather to delight and rejoice in the Lord, Ps. 37. v. 4. Phil. 4. v. 4. etc. 3. If they exceed the limits of modesty and moderation in the world of women, and make excessive expenditures for that purpose. Two things are to be observed in clothing, convenience and decorum. There are two parts of decorum, mediocrity and modesty; excessive elegance and superfluous splendor, and thus every excess arises from a vice of the soul. 4. If they are proud on account of external adornment. Esa. 3. v. 16. He who boasts of a garment is like a thief who boasts of a branding iron, because the garment is a sign of guilt. They ought to follow the footsteps of Esther, who c. 14. v. 16. prays thus: You, Lord, know my necessity, that I abhor the sign of my pride and glory, which is upon my head, in the days of my ostentation, and I detest it as a menstruous cloth, and I do not wear it in the days of my silence. 5. If in adorning themselves they do not have regard for place and time Ps. 35. v. 13. Matth. 22. v. 11. Rom. 2. v. 15. 6. If they strive by this adornment to please other men, and entice them to the adultery of the eyes and heart. The observed complication of hair, and nets interwoven with golden threads are like a net, by which they catch unwary men.

12. Hence among the pious ancients there are held most grave pronouncements against the pursuit of external adornment. Cyprian in the tract on the dress of virgins: If you adorn yourself too sumptuously, and walk notably through the public, entice the eyes of youth to yourself, draw the sighs of young men after you, nourish the lust of concupiscence, kindle the fuel of sin, so that even if you yourself do not perish, you nevertheless destroy others, and offer yourself as a sword and poison to those who see you, you cannot be excused, as if you were of a chaste and modest mind. Your wicked dress and shameless adornment refute you etc. The insignia of ornaments and clothes and the allurements of cosmetics befit none but prostitutes and shameless women, and there is almost no one whose dress is more precious than those whose modesty is cheap. Clothed in silk and purple, they cannot put on Christ; adorned with gold and pearls and necklaces, they have lost the ornaments of the body and the breast. Tertullian in the tract on the dress of women, chapter 7: What does such a burdensome weight of adorning the head contribute to salvation? Why is it not permitted for your hair to be at rest, now bound up, now relaxed: now raised up, now let down? Some are eager to restrain it in curls, others, so that they may slip away wandering and winged, not with good simplicity. You afflict yourselves furthermore with I know not what enormities of stitched and woven hairpieces, now in the manner of a gallery, as if a sheath for the head and a lid for the crown, now pushed back toward the neck. It is a wonder that one contends against the precepts of the Lord. It has been pronounced that no one can add to his stature. You clearly add to the weight certain cakes, by attaching the bosses of shields to your necks. If you are not ashamed of the enormity, be ashamed of the defilement, lest you place the spoils of another's head, perhaps unclean, perhaps guilty and destined for hell, upon a holy and Christian head. In this detestation of excessive and artificial adornment, the whole book on the dress of women, as also another on female attire, is consumed. Clement of Alexandria, book 2, Paedagogus, chapter 10, says: that the true ornament of a woman is modesty, and those who adorn themselves with gold imitate the barbarians, who bind evildoers with gold. Is not, he says, a golden necklace a bond for the neck, and necklaces, and those things which take the place of chains? Hence also ἁλύσεις, i.e., they are called chains. Chrysostom, homily 21 to the people of Antioch: Do you wish to adorn your face? Adorn it not with pearls, but with modesty and honesty, and thus your husband will see a more pleasing appearance. That adornment, indeed, is often accustomed to cast suspicion of jealousy, and enmities, and contentions, and fights, etc. But adornment with modesty expels every wicked suspicion, and reconciles marriage more firmly than any bond, etc. Regarding the cult of pearls, it is a Satanic display. For you have taken gold, not to bind your body, but to save and nourish the poor. Gregory of Nazianzus, oration 11, concerning his sister Gorgonia: Gold did not adorn her, nor yellow hair, nor knots and impostures of hair, making the precious head a stage with the greatest insanity, nor the magnificence of flowing and translucent clothing, nor the splendors of stones, coloring the nearby air, nor the arts and deceptions of painters, etc. One blush pleased her, which modesty brings; one whiteness, which abstinence produces. Augustine, Epistle 73 to Possidius: The true ornament of Christians, both men and women, is not only no lying paint, but not even the display of gold and clothing, but good morals. Gregory on the words Luke 16 There was a rich man, etc. If the cultivation of precious clothing were not a fault, the Gospel reading would never have said so vigilantly that the rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen, was buried in hell. Moreover, even the Gentiles disapproved of that excessive zeal for external adornment in women as if it were innate. Bede in this place brings forward the saying of Pythagoras, that the true ornaments of matrons are modesty, not clothes. Plutarch in the Laconica cites the saying of Gatetis: Adornment is, that which adorns; but that which makes a woman more adorned, adorns. But neither gold, nor an emerald makes a woman more adorned, but whatever things have a signification of gravity, modesty, and chastity. Ovid, book 3, on the art of loving.

What shame it is to carry one's wealth upon one's body.

13. But above all, the pious ancients inveigh sharply against those who do not shrink from staining either their face or their hair with a foreign color. For if the Apostle forbids the braiding of hair, how much more does he forbid staining the face with white lead and vermilion? Cyprian, on the dress of virgins. The sinners and apostate angels, when they had fallen down to earthly contagions and had withdrawn from heavenly vigor, taught men both to stain their eyes with a surrounding blackness, and to infect their cheeks with a lie of redness, and to change their hair with adulterous colors, and to assault all the truth of the face and head with the attack of their corruption, etc. And I think that not only virgins or widows, but also married women and all women whatsoever ought to be admonished that the work of GOD and His creation and formation ought in no way to be adulterated by the application of a yellow color, or black powder, or redness, or finally any cosmetic that corrupts the native features. GOD says: Let us make man in our image and likeness, and does anyone dare to change and convert what GOD has made? They lay hands upon GOD when they strive to reshape and transfigure that which He has formed, not knowing that everything that is born is the work of GOD, and whatever is changed is of the Devil. If any artist of painting had marked the face and appearance and quality of the body of someone with a rival color, and if another were to lay hands upon the image already formed and already painted, as if he were more skilled, to reshape it, it would seem a grave injury and a just indignation to the former artist. Do you think that you will carry off with impunity the audacity of such wicked rashness and the offense to God the artist? For even if you are not unchaste and incestuous toward men with alluring cosmetics, by having corrupted and violated those things which are of GOD, you are held to be worse than an adulteress: that you think you are being adorned, that you think you are being groomed, that is an attack upon the divine work, it is a prevarication of the truth, etc. Do you not fear, I pray, you who are such a one, lest when the day of resurrection comes, your artist may not recognize you? That He may remove and exclude you when you come to His rewards and promises? That He may say, rebuking with the vigor of a censor and judge: This is not my work, nor is this our image; you have polluted your skin with a false cosmetic, you have changed your hair with an adulterous color, your face has been assaulted by a lie, your figure has been corrupted, your attire is foreign It is, you will not be able to see GOD, since you do not have eyes which GOD made, but which the Devil infected; you have followed him, you have imitated the glowing and painted eyes of the serpent, adorned by your enemy, destined to burn forever with him. Tertull. de cultu foeminarum cap. 5. They offend against God, who anoint their skin with medicaments, stain their cheeks with redness, and smear their eyes with wheat-flour. The molding of God is displeasing to them, of course; in themselves they refute and rebuke the artificer of all things. For they rebuke him when they amend, when they add, certainly taking these additions from the opposing artificer, that is, the Devil. For who would show how to change the body, except him who also transformed the Spirit of man with malice? He undoubtedly devised such talents, so that in a way he might lay hands upon God in us. What is born is the work of God. Therefore, what is fashioned is the business of the Devil. How wicked it is to superimpose the talents of Satan upon a divine work! cap. 7. Would that I, most miserable, on that day of Christian exultation, might lift my head even between your heels, to see whether you rise again with white lead and purple-dye and saffron, and in that arrangement of the head, or whether Angels might lift up such a painted thing into the clouds to meet Christ. If they are now good, and are of God, then they will also meet the rising bodies, and will recognize their own places. Gregory Nazianzen begins his poem against women adorning themselves too ambitiously thus. Μὴ κεφαλὰς πυργοῦτε νόθοις καὶ οκαμοῖσι γυναῖκες. Beware, O women, lest you fortify your head with bastard and adulterous hairs, as if with certain towers, and delicately display your soft necks from your shoulders: nor that you anoint the forms of God with foul colors, so that you now wear not faces, but masks, etc. It is to be feared that God, being angry, might address you thus. Come tell me, O strange woman, who at last and from where is your shaper and creator? I did not paint you with white lead, but I fashioned an image of myself. How does it happen, therefore, that instead of a dear image I have an idol? Jerome to Laeta concerning the instruction of a daughter. Neither load your head with gems, nor redden your hair, and mix into it something of the fires of Gehenna. Augustine Epist. 73. to Possidius. To be painted with fictions, so that one might appear either redder or whiter, is an adulterous deception, by which I do not doubt that even husbands themselves do not wish to be deceived. John Huss in h. l. In those ornaments in which prejudice is done to Nature, as in the painting of the face, nothing excuses; but in others, it excuses feminine adornment, if it is not for the sake of pride or vanity, or of provoking others to incontinence, but so that the custom of the place or the degree of dignity may be observed, or so that a husband may be recalled from fornication.

14. If the Apostle disapproves of an excessive zeal for external adornment in women, how much more will he detest it in men, whom Tertullian in his book de veland. virgin. says have professed openly effeminacy. The same author in de cultu foeminarum chapter 8: And in men for the sake of women, and in women for the sake of men, the desire to please is innate by a vice of Nature, and this sex also recognizes for itself its own illusions of form: to cut the beard more sharply, to pluck it out, to arrange the hair, to dispose of it, even to color the grayness, to remove every first down of the whole body; also to distinguish it with womanly pigment, to smooth the rest with the roughness of some powder, then to consult the mirror on every occasion, to inspect it most of all, when however, with God known, the desire to please having been taken away through the vacation of luxury, all those things are refused as idle, as hostile to modesty. For where God is, there is modesty, there is gravity, its helper and companion. By what pact, therefore, shall we treat of modesty without its instrument, i. e. without gravity, or how shall we apply gravity to the administration of modesty? unless severity is carried about both in the face, and in dress, and in the contemplation of the whole man? Gregory, homily 6 in Evang.: Consider what a fault it is for men to desire this, which the Pastor of the Church (Peter) took care to forbid even to women!

15. Interior and spiritual adornment is to be preferred by a very long way to external bodily adornment. Tertullian de cultu foeminarum chapter 13: Come forth now, built up with the medicines and ornaments of the Apostles, taking whiteness from simplicity, redness from modesty, painting your eyes with bashfulness and the silence of the Spirit, inserting the word of God into your ears, binding the yoke of Christ to your necks. Submit your head to your husbands, and you will be sufficiently adorned. Occupy your hands with wool, fix your feet at home, and you will please more than in gold. Clothe yourselves with the silk of probity, the fine linen of holiness, the purple of modesty. Thus pigmented, you will have God as your lover.

16. That interior adornment consists chiefly in this, that we put on Christ by faith,Galat. 3. vers. 27. and thus our heart is purified by faith,Actor. 15. vers. 9. by this faith the heart is stabilized, so that it may be peaceful, quiet, and tranquil, and not doubt concerning the grace of GOD. Hebr. 13. vers. 9. From this faith proceed good works, even external ones, diverse and various according to the calling of each. Therefore, the true adornment of Christian women is not silken, or jeweled, or golden, but spiritual and interior. Virtues are most precious pearls and gems, which most greatly adorn the female sex before God, the Angels, and pious men.

17. There is nothing that more adorns the female sex than a settled and placid disposition, meekness and gentleness of spirit, bashfulness and modesty, temperance and humility. Hence Ambrose, book 2, on virgins, describes a woman pleasing to God and men thus: Nothing stern in the eyes, nothing forward in words, nothing shameless in action, no gesture too broken, no gait too loose, no voice too petulant, so that the very appearance of the body might be an image of the mind, a figure of probity.

18. The true and incorruptible riches of a pious man are spiritual and interior. For the interior man, raising himself above all earthly things and despising the same, possesses God Himself and is an heir of the eternal kingdom. Ambrose, book 4, Epistle 27, Truly rich is he who in the sight of God can appear rich ( who is rich in GodLuc. 21. v. 21.) in whose sight the earth is small, the world itself is narrow. But God knows only him to be rich who is rich for eternity, who stores up not the fruits of works, but of virtues. But who is rich before God, if not the quiet and modest Spirit, which is never corrupted? Does he not seem rich to you who has peace of mind, the tranquility of rest, so that he desires nothing, is agitated by no storms of desires, etc. That is peace truly rich, which surpasses every mind. Rich is peace, rich is modesty, rich is faith (for to the faithful the whole world is a possession) rich is simplicity, for there are also riches of simplicity, which discusses nothing, thinks nothing contracted or fraudulent, but pours itself out with pure affection. Rich is goodness, which if anyone has kept, he is fed on the riches of the heavenly inheritance, etc. The same, book 1 of duties, chapter 18, Great therefore is modesty, which, since it is also more remiss of its own right, usurping nothing for itself, claiming nothing, and in a certain way more contracted within its own powers, is rich before God, before whom no one is rich. Modesty is rich, because it is a portion of God. Augustine, book 1 of the City of God, chapter 10, The saints lost all things which they had. Did they lose faith? Did they lose piety? Did they lose the goods of the interior man, who is rich before God? These are the riches of Christians, with which the Apostle said he was opulent, poor on the outside, rich on the inside. Great gain is piety with sufficiency. Blessed Luther in this place, The believer has all things which Christ has; faith brings all the goods of Christ to us; therefore he is truly rich who believes in Christ and from faith studies the cultivation of the interior man.

19. In Scripture, not only the New but also the Old Testament, examples of virtues are proposed, especially in the holy Patriarchs and Matriarchs, which are to be imitated according to the manner and measure of one's calling. Heb. 11. vers. 4. & seqq.

20. The examples of the ancestors ἀξιομίμητα contain a great ὁρμητήριον. for piety and holiness.

21. Just as the sons of Abraham, so also the daughters of Sarah are reckoned in two ways, by flesh and by Spirit; by carnal generation, and by the imitation of faith and virtues. Carnal generation avails nothing at all before God, unless the imitation of faith and virtues is added. Matt. 3. v. 9.John 8. v. 39. Didymus in this place As anyone doing the work of Abraham and having his faith becomes his son: so the faithful women doing good have Sarah as their mother.Luke 13. v. 16.

22. Those who are made sons of Abraham through faith, and those who are made daughters of Sarah through faith, will inherit heavenly glory and happiness with Abraham and Sarah. Rom. 3. v. 17.Gal. 3. v. 9. Those who are of faith will be blessed with faithful Abraham.

23. Abraham's wife called her husband lord, but she herself was in turn honored by her husband, who called her Sarai i.e., my lady. Naturally, wives who honor their husbands and reverently submit themselves to them are honored by their husbands. In the book Musar, chapter 6, folio 73, it is read thus: A certain wise woman was saying to her daughter when she was leading her to the bridal chamber: My daughter, stand before your husband and serve him. If you are a handmaid to him, he himself will be a servant to you and will honor you as a mistress or lady. But if you exalt yourself against him, he will be a Lord to you and then you will become vile in his eyes as one of the handmaids. Publius Syrus.

A chaste matron commands her husband by obeying.

24. The female sex is easily accustomed to be disturbed and terrified by fear, either because of the inconveniences of their own household affairs, or because of evils commonly happening to Christians; moreover, it is prone to superstitions, so that in adversities and dangers it runs to diviners and seeks counsel from them, but the Apostle wishes pious women to be free and alien from this fear.

25. Hope in God and faith in Christ free the pious from inordinate and preposterous fear, as the connection of verses 6 and 7 shows, hence with David they say with a strong and undaunted spirit Ps. 23. vers. 4. Even if I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I will not fear evils, because you are with me The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear.Ps. 27. v. 1. God is my rock and my salvation, my refuge, I shall not be moved greatly.Psal. 62. v. 3. & 7.

Latin:

SICUT SARA OBEDIEBAT ABRAHAE, DOMINUM EUM VOCANS, CUIUS ESTIS FILIAE, BENEFACIENTES & NON PERTIMENTES ULLAM PERTURBATIONEM.

Connexio. 1. Ab exemplo generali sanctarum V. T. foeminarum transit ad exemplum speciale Sarae coniugis Abrahami, eodemque suam confirmat exhortationem.

2. Dixerat, sanctas mulieres in V. T. subiectas fuisse propriis: viris, illud confirmat exemplo Sarae, idem iudicium de reliquis matriarchis faciendum esse insinuans.

3. Ostendit, qualis debeat esse maritarum Christianarum ἄναστροφὴ, cuius mentionem fecerat v. 1. videlicet, quòd debeant esse ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μεγαλόψυχοι.

Textus dispositio. Apostolus in hoc versiculo. 1. Obedientiam Sarae erga Abrahamum probat ex effectu externo, videl. ex honorifica appellatione, quâ maritum suum honoravit. 2. Exemplum istud Sarae applicat ad mulieres Christianas, praesertim eas, quae ex Iudaismo ad Christianam religionem erant conversae, quas proptereà vocat Sarae filias. 3. Addit limitationem, quod tùm demum verae & genuinae Sarae filiae sint censendae, si bonis operibus studeant, & in DEI protectione magnâ animi fiduciâ & robore acquiescant.

Expositio. Ὡς Σάῤῥα ὑπήκουσε τῷ Ἀβραὰμ, κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα. Quando Apostolus Saram marito suo Abrahae obsequentem fuisse memorat, remittit nos ad Historiam Abrahae, Gen. 12. & cap. seqq. descriptam, in qua multa eademque insignia obedientiae à Sara marito suo praestitae exempla commemorantur, videl. quòd secuta fuerit maritum, ex Ur Chaldaeorum regione patria ad peregrinas terras proficiscentem, quòd assidua & indivisa itineris comes ipsi fuerit in exilio & peregrinatione per terram Canaan, quòd iussu mariti etiam pudoris periculo sese exposuerit, dicens se esse sororem; contenta, si ita esset necesse, se periclitari pudore, quàm virum salute, ut loquitur Ambros. 1. de Abrah. c. z. quòd contemtum ab ancilla Agar sibi illatum ad maritum detulerit, eique vindicandum commiserit, quòd marito praeparationem cibi hospitibus apponendi praecipienti obtemperaverit, adeoque praeceptum istud effectui dare festinaverit. Inde glossa interlinearis ad verbum obediebat h. l. rectè addit, etiam in his, quae gravia videbantur.

Κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα. Locus extat Gen. 18. v. 12.cùm audiret Sara ex se intra anni spacium natum iri filium, risit, intra se dicendo, Postquam senui, erit mihi voluptasואדני& dominus meus senuit. Drusius lib. 9. praeterit. ex libro Musar cap. 7. f. 73. citat similem locum. Uxor bona stat coram marito suo, & ministrat ei & vocat eum dominum suum. Quod ex Sara discimus, quae Abrahamum maritum vocabat dominum suum, cum diceret, dominus meus senuit. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]dominum meum, quod propiùs ad textum Hebraeum accedit. Exaggeratur autem haec obedientia & subiectio Sarae ex eo, quòd cum ipsa à DEO vocata esset Sara h. e. domina, ac Abrahae demandatum, ut non ampliùs eam vocaret Sari, i. e. dominam meam, sed simpliciter Saram i. e. dominam, nihilo tamen minus ex sincero & humili obsequio maritum suum vocarit dominum suum.

Ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκναcuius filiae factae estis, puta spirituales. Quamvis enim quaedam illarum maritarum, ad quas Petrus scribit, etiam ratione carnalis generationis erant Sarae filiae, illae scilicet, quae ex Iudaismo ad Christianismum erant conversae, Apostolus tamen hoc loco principaliter de Spirituali filiatione agit, 1. quia non solùm conversas ex Iudaismo, sed etiam ex gentilismo alloquitur. 2. quia illas solùm filias Sarae vocat, quae bonis operibus student. 3. quia dicit, illas non natas, sed factas esse Sarae filias. Inde glossa ad h. l. rectè annotat. Cuius filiae factae estis imitatione fidei, etsi non successione generis.

Ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι. Quidam hoc accipiunt προτρεπτικῶς,quòd Apostolus pergat uxores Christianas exhortari ad studium bonorum operum, sed propriè ac principaliter accipiendum est διακριτικῶς ac διοριστικῶς: ostendit enim Apostolus, eas demum esse veras & spirituales Sarae filias habendas, quae bonis operibus student. Per ἀγαθοποιΐαν, quidam in specie intelligunt beneficentiam ac munificentiam erga proximum, in qua significatione verbumἀγαθοποιεῖνusurpaturLuc. 6. v. 33. & 35.quae expositio confirmari posset ex eo, quòd Apostolus occupetur in exemplo Sarae, quae promta & obsequiosa fuit marito ad benefaciendum hospitibus peregrè adventantibus.Gen. 18. v. 6 Sed rectiùs accipitur generaliter de studio bonorum operum, in qua significatione Apostolus noster hac voce perpetuò utitur 1. Epist. 2. v. 14.15. & 20. cap. 3. v. 17.cap. 4. v. 19. unde Syrus rectè reddidit, [consult facsimile image][consult facsimile image]in operibus bonis, quae expositio magis congruit verbis sequentibus, & probatur ex loco parallelo 1. Tim. 2. vers. 10.

Καὶ μὴ φοβούμενοι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν. Vulgata reddidit. Et non pertimentes ullam perturbationem. Sed πτόησις propriè non significat perturbationem, sed pavorem vel consternationem à πτοεῖσθαι, quod est pavefieri vel consternari.Luc. 21. v. 9.Cùm audiveritis praelia & seditiones,μὴ πτοηθῆτεnolite pavefieri (pro quo Matthaeus dicit μἠ θροεῖσθζc. 24. v. 6.) Luc. c. 24. v. 37.πτοηθέντες καὶ ἒμψοβοι γενόμενοι, ubi posterius est ὲξηγητικὸν prioris, LXX. verbo πτοεῖσθαι utuntur pro חרר quod significat expavit, timuit cum motu corporisEx. 19. v. 16.Amos 3. v. 6. pro חתתconsternatus fuit animo vel robore corporis.1. Paral 22. v. 13.cap. 28. v. 20. Pro מסס ita expavefactus est, ut cor fuerit liquefactumIos. 7. v. 5. pro ערץanimo fractus est, formidavitDeut. 31. v. 6. pro פחדexpavit, metu mali repentini trepidavitIob. 23. v. 15. & pro רגזcontremuit, conturbatus estHab. 3. v. 6. In eadem significatione hoc verbo etiam profani scriptores utuntur. Plutarchus in Alcibiade. πτοηθέντος τοῦ ὄρτυγοςexpavefactâ & exterritâ coturnice. Idem in Publicola, ἳππους πτοηθέντας vocat equos consternatos & pavefactos. Apud Pollucem συνωνύμως ponuntur ἐπτοημένος, ἐκπεπληγμένος, τεθορυβημένος, ἐξεστηκὼς scil. τῷ δέει. Ex quibus omnibus colligitur, per πττόησιν subitum pavorem & consternationem hîc intelligi, unde & Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image]pavorem. Variis autem modis hic φόβος πτοήσεως ab Intepretibus exponitur. 1. Quidam respectum haberi putant ad proximè praecedens verbum ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι,estis Sarae filiae, dum benefacitis etiam, cum non terremini ullo pavore h. e. si non coactae aut metu adactae sed sponte & liberè bonis operibus incumbatis. Sensus igitur foret, uxores non debere terrore maritorum cogi ad benè operandum, sed proprii potius animi promtitudine impelli ad officium praestandum, nec poenae terrore, sed virtutis amore esse probas.

2. Quidam coniungunt cum verbo ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι, sed alio sensu. Dum bonis operibus studetis, non est quod quidquam mali metuatis, verbi causâ, ne maritis displiceatis, si minùs exornatae & comtae incedatis, vel ne serviliter vos tractent, si obsequentes ad omnia vosmet eis exhibeatis, vel ne iniquis obiurgationibus & comminationibus mariti vobis sint molesti. Obsequium enim vestrum conciliabit vobis maritorum amorem & honorem. Sed rectiùs accipitur, ut peculiaris quaedam proprietas Christianarum uxorum, quae verè sunt Sarae filiae. Occurrunt autem etiam iuxta hanc hypothesin diversae expositiones.

1. B. Lutherus in comm. h. l. accipit de perverso & inordinato illo timore, quo mulieres in periculis vel adversis constitutae confugiunt ad superstitiosas & Magicas artes.

2. Gagnaeius intelligit de pavore ob supervenientes afflictiones & persecutiones, quae in primitiva Ecclesia erant frequentes.

3. Erasmus interpretatur de pavore, quo solent de rebus exigui, imò nullius momenti consternari mulieres ob sexus fragilitatem.

4. Quidam accipiunt de turbis & tumultibus, quos ob rem frivolam quandoque concitare solent mulieres in Oeconomia.

5. Simplicissimè accipitur generaliter, quòd timiditatem fidei contrariam, ex qua subitus pavor & nimia consternatio oritur, à sanctis foeminis abesse doceat, ac abesse etiam velit Apostolus, in genere enim dicit, μὴ φοβούμενοι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν, non territae ullo pavore, ubi ante μηδεμίαν subauditur κατὰ, & gemina negatio more Graeco fortiùs negat. Usitatum vero est in Scripturis, per pavorem & timoremμετωνυμικῶς significari non solùm DEUM, qui est timendus & reverenter colendus, Genes. 31. v. 42. sed etiam malum subitum, quod est pavoris causa. Psalm. 53. v. 6.Ibi paverunt pavorem, ubi non erat pavor, i. e. malum pavoris causa. Psal. 91. v. 5.non timebis à timore nocturno.Prov. 1. v. 26.cùm venerit pavor vester, i. e. malum, cuius metu expavescitis. Prov. 3. v. 25.Non pavebis à repentino pavore, i. e. à malo repentino, ubi itidem φοβεῖν πτόησιν coniunguntur, ut hoc loco. Potest etiam hûc accommodari regula. Apud Hebraeos vocabula actus vel affectus poni solent pro obiecto.

Iob. 3. vers. 25.timor, quem timebam, evenit mihi, i. e. malum, quod timebam. Psal. 106. vers. 12.laudaverunt laudem eius, i. e. nomen eius laudabile. v. 14.concupiverunt concupiscentiam in deserto, i. e. res illicitas concupiverunt. Tit. 2. v. 13.expectantes beatam spem, i. e. coelestem beatitudinem & gloriam, quam fide expectamus. Sic ergò etiam hoc loco, uxores Christianae non tenentur ullo pavore, h. e. ita confidunt in Dei favore, praesidio, auxilio & gratiosâ praesentiâ, ut à nullo malo praeposterè sibi timeant, sed firmâ cordis fiduciâ in Deum unicè recumbant. Sic ergò cum ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ coniungitur vera fides, & cordis fiducia, quae contra subitos & repentinos pavores Christianas uxores animat, duplici ratione. 1. quia fons & fundamentum ἀγαθοποιΐας est vera fides, & firma in Christum fiducia. 2. quia uxores Christianae fide factae sunt verae & spirituales Sarae filiae, sicut Roman. 4. vers. 12.filii Abrahae dicuntur, qui sectantur vestigia fidei Abrahae.

Q. hoc loco. 1. Quare Apostolus post praecepta subditis & servis in cap. praeced. tradita, Magistratum, & heros sui non admoneat officii? Sanè Paulus Ephes. 6. v. 9.Coloss. 4. v. 1. postquam servis debita officii sui munia praescripserat, etiam heros admonet, quid servis debeant. Sed Petrus hoc loco servorum duntaxat meminit, quia potissimùm scribit ad conversos ex Iudaeis in dispersione positis, 1. Epist. 1. v. 1. inter quos multi erant servi, pauci vero domini.

2. Quare uxores Christianas ad subiectionem erga maritos tàm operosè hortetur? Resp. Sicut Apostoli hac calumniâ falsò onerabantur, quòd docerent, subditos Magistratui Ethnico, & servos dominis infidelibus nullam debere obedientiam: ita quoque detrahebatur ipsis, quod docerent, uxores Christianas à maritis infidelibus per divortia separari debere. Occasio calumniae erat ea, quòd matronae Christianae ex instituto Apostolorum, abominandas, & legi Naturae contrarias maritorum libidines perpeti recusabant, quaedam etiam hoc nomine ab illis divertebant. Eusebius lib. 4. Histor. Eccles. cap. 17. ex Iustini Philosoph. & Martyris Apolog. haec adducit. Mulier quaedam vixerat cum marito lasciviis dedito, quibus & ipsa anteà dedita fuerat. Ea postquam Christi doctrinam cognovisset, ad resipiscentiam & vitae castimoniam rediit, ac viro ut consimiliter resipisceret, persuadere conata, doctrinam illi exposuit, quae futurum sempiterni ignis supplicium intemperanter & non rectâ ratione viventibus comminatur. Ille vero iisdem lasciviis suis immorando, illicitis actibus suis uxorem abs se alienat. Dicebat enim illa, illicitum deinceps futurum, ut cum eo viro eodem uteretur cubili, qui contra Naturae legem, & praeter aequum & fas, voluptati suae undecunque vias quaereret. Quoniam vero amicorum persuasionibus ab ea sententia revòcabatur, qui consulebant, ut adhuc marito conviveret, quod spes esset, fore ut aliquando ad se rediret, seipsam cohibendo in eo coniugio manebat. Cum vero vir ille Alexandriam profectus peiora perpetrare nunciaretur, ne consors scelerum & impiorum flagitiorum redderetur, si in coniugio illius perduraret, & eodem cum illo contubernio, cubilique uteretur, dato repudii libello separatur ac discedit. Chrysostomus lib. 1. contra vituperat. vitae Monast. memorat, Paulum pellicem Neronis, quam deperibat, & in delitiis habebat, conversam ad Christum à Neronis amicitia abalienasse, ac proinde Neronem, Paulum corruptorem, nebulonem & flagitiosum nominasse, & in vincula coniecisse, ac postea ab eo poposcisse, ut puellae huiusmodi consilia & monita dare desineret, quod cum à Paulo impetraere non potuisset, eum necasse. Quòd vero in libro, qui sub nomine Lini de passione Petri & Pauli circumfertur, memoratur, uxorem Albini ita à Petro edoctam repudiasse thorum viri ob amorem castitatis etiam reclamante marito, atque Agrippam praefectum Petro propterea dixisse: Multa tibi fiducia est, ô scelerate, in plebibus, quas circumvenis, & in foeminis, quae tuâ persuasione à maritali thoro discedunt, illud veritati minimè consentaneum, & doctrinae Apostolicae, 1. Corinth. 7. vers. 10. minùs conforme ostendit scriptum illud Lini, Manichaeismum pleno ore redolens, esse supposititium, quod agnoscunt Baronius ann. 66. n. 14. ann. 69. n. 6. ann. 80. n. 4. Bellarm. 2. d. R. P. cap. 9. & de script. Eccles. p. 55. Hisce ergò gentilium calumniis ut occurreret Petrus, uxores Christianas ad oboedientiam maritis etiam infidelibus praestandam tàm solicitè exhortatur, sicut etiam alias gentilium calumnias in superioribus diluerat.

Q. 3. Quare nominatim compellet uxores eas, quae maritis infidelibus coniugatae? Resp. erant tunc temporis multa coniugia disparia, ut colligitur ex Actor. 16. vers. 1.1. Cor. 7. v. 12. & 13. Quia ergò uxores Christianae infidelibus maritis iunctae plus coloris ad excutiendum obedientiae maritalis iugum habere videbantur, ideò nominatim illas sui admonet officii, ac peculiarem causam profert, cur maiori studio viris suis parere debeant, nempe ut eos ad religionis Christianae amorem obsequio suo alliciant. Interim intelligendum relinquit, si uxores maritis infidelibus obedientiam debent, multò magis ad eam obligari, quae maritis Christianis nuptae.

Q. 4. Quare uxores Christianas priùs compellet, quàm maritos? Resp. 1. Quia in praecedente capite egerat de subiectione, quam subditi Magistratui, & servi dominis suis debent, continuare ergò voluit subiectionis exhortationem. 2. Quia foeminae ob sexus infirmitatem v. 8. exhortatione illâ magis indigebant.

Q. 5. An etiam ante lapsum in statu integritatis uxor fuisset viro subiecta? Resp. inter paternas castigationes, Evae & ipsius filiabus post lapsum impositas, etiam dominium viri refertur, Genes. 3. vers. 16. ex quo colligi videtur, subiectionem illam ante lapsum non habuisse locum: vicissim vero 1. Corinth. 11. v. 8. inter argumenta, quibus obedientia uxoribus persuadenda, refertur, quòd vir sit ex muliere, quodque vir caput mulieris, v. 3. Distinguendum igitur inter obedientiam voluntariam, suavem & concordem: ac inter subiectionem invitam, difficilem & molestam. Item inter imperium liberum, voluntarium ac iucundum, quale fuisset viri in uxorem etiam ante lapsum: & inter imperium involuntarium, durum & molestum, quale est hodiè post lapsum. Ante lapsum quaedam praerogativa & eminentia dignitatis fuisset in viro, sed tale dominium potestatis, quale post lapsum maritis in uxores datum, & talis subiectio foeminei sexus, qualis hodiè obtinet, non habuisset locum in statu integritatis, siquidem maritus nihil per iracundiam vel importunitatem egisset, nec voluntas uxoris à voluntate mariti in diversum abiisset, sed in sancta DEI voluntate uterque quietissimè consensisset, quae pulcherrima harmonia per lapsum miserè est disrupta. August. lib. 11. de Genes. ad liter. cap. 27.

Q. 6. Quare in specie mansuetudinem & lenitatem Spiritus ab uxoribus requirat in v. 4.? Resp. quia mansuetudo & lenitas in perferenda maritorum praesertim infidelium importunitate vel maximè requiruntur, si uxores aequo animo illis subiectae esse debeant.

Q. 7. An per Spiritum v. eod. intelligatur Spiritus sanctus tertia Deitatis persona? Athanasius in Epist. ad Serapionem ita statuit, argumento eo, quòd Spiritui sancto propriè competat, quod Petrus de eo h. l. praedicat, videlicet quòd sit dives apud DEUM, utpote eiusdem cum ipso divinitatis consors. Sensum ergò existimat esse talem. Qui se puros & incorruptos custodiunt, inhabitantem habent Spiritum sanctum, qui cum sit quietus & modestus, ipsos etiam facit quietos & modestos. quò referri posset, quòd mansuetudo & lenitas sint fructus SpiritusGal. 5. vers. 22. Eandem expositionem profert Idacius lib. contra Varimodum respondens, de Spiritu sancto dici modestiam, sicut de Patre, iuxta quendam locum Ieremiae ex editione LXX. & de Christo2. Cor. 10. vers. 1.iuxta vulgatam versionem. Sed Ambrosius lib. 1. offic. cap. 18. rectiùs accipit de spiritu hominis per Spiritum sanctum regenito ac renovato, qui est optimus mulierum ornatus, si mansuetudine, lenitate ac aliis virtutibus fuerit praeditus. Ponitur enim πνεῦμα sine articulo & quod hoc loco vocatur πνεῦμα πρᾳὲς, illud 1. Corinth. 4. vers. 21.Galat. 6. v. 1. vocatur πνεῦμα πρᾳότητος.

Q. 8. Quare exempla sanctarum mulierum uxoribus Christistianis proponat? Resp. quia magna omninò vis in exemplis, praesertim apud sexum foemineum μιμητικὸν.

9. Quare in specie Sarae exemplum adducat? Resp. scribit potissimùm ad mulieres ex Iudaismo conversas, ex omnibus ergò sanctis V. Test. foeminis Saram adducit, ut totius generis Israelitici parentem. Facit hoc exemplo Esaiae cap. 51. v. 1.Respicite ad petram, unde excisi estis & ad cavernam putei, de quo praecisi estisv. 2.Respicite ad Abraham, Patrem vestrum & ad Saram, quae peperit vos. ubi petrae nomine coniuges illi steriles & effoeti intelliguntur, propterea quod aequè magnum fuit miraculum ex illis nasci Isaacum, ac si Deus ex lapidibus suscitasset Abrahae filiumMatth. 3. v. 9. Respectus etiam habetur ad multiplicationem posteritatis. Ut enim ex latomia lapides plurimi eruuntur: sic Israelitae omnes ab illis parentibus magno numero per successionem sunt propagati.

Sequitur etiam hac in parte Petrus exemplum Apostoli Pauli, qui Abrahamum ut spiritualem omnium credentium Patrem introducit Rom. 4. v. 11. & 12.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Per particulamὁμοίωςApostolus subiectionem uxorum erga maritos comparat subiectioni servorum erga dominos v. 1. sed v. 8. maritis praecipit, ut honorem impertiant uxoribus tanquam vasculo infirmiori: Resp. particula ὁμοίως non est nota omnimodae aequalitatis, sed similitudinis ac proportionis. Neque enim Apostolus uxores in subiectione aequat servis, cum uxor non ex pedibus, sed ex latere viri sit formata, ac propterea sit mariti socia non serva, sed similitudinem praecepti & proportionem quandam subiectionis importat. Sicut servi debent obedientiam heris, ratione subiectionis servilis: sic uxores debent obedientiam maritis, ratione subiectionis coniugalis. Domini imperant servis δεσποτικῶς, mariti uxoribus γαμικῶς.

2. Mulieres subditae sint viris, ut & si qui non credunt verbo, per mulierum conversationem sine verbo lucrifiantv. 1. Atqui Rom. 10. 17.fides est ex auditu, auditus a. per verbum Dei. Resp. 1. non de totali conversione, sed de conversionis occasione verba Apostoli sunt accipienda. Sanctam maritarum Christianarum conversationem maritis infidelib. docet esse quandam conversionis occasionem & tacitam quandam ad fidem Christianam amplectendam invitationem. Quando enim mariti adhuc infideles animadvertunt, uxores suas ad Christum conversas ex documentis Christianae religionis esse sibi obsequentes, castas, externi ornatus minimè cupidas, mansuetas, quietas, bonorum operum studiosas, in periculis & adversis animosas, de Christiana religione honestiùs sentire, & aequiore erga eam animo esse incipiunt, qui est primus q. ad conversionem gradus, vel certè remotio impedimenti, videlicet praeconcepti erga Christianam fidem odii. 2. Nequaquam igitur immediatam conversionem per interiores afflatus & Enthusiasmos Petrus stabilit, sed DEUM per gradus quosdam ad cognitionem Christi, eos qui se dociles exhibent, perducere docet. 3. Quando sine verbo maritos infideles lucrifieri posse asserit, non simpliciter & absolutè excludit verbum à conversionis mediis, sed de verbo publicae praedicationis loquitur, à quo mariti infideles priùs sunt alieni, antequàm sanctâ uxorum conversatione ad illud quasi alliciantur.

3. Ornatus piarum foeminarum non sit plicatura capillorum, vel circumdatio auri, vel induitio vestimentorum preciosorumv. 3.AtquiGen. 24. v. 22.servus Abrahae monili aureo & armillis Rebeccam Isaaci sponsam ornat.Psal. 45. v. 20. & seqq. spiritualis ornatus Sponsae Christi describitur verbis metaphoricis ab ornatu corporali Regiae Sponsae petitis.Ezech. 16. v. 12. & 13.Ose. 2. v. 8. & 13.torques, armillae, inaures & similia mulierum ornamenta, inter dona DEI referuntur. Esther ornabatur vestibus regiisEsth. 2. v. 17. Iudith discriminabat crinem capitis sui, & imponebat mitram super caput suum, & induebat se vestimentis iucunditatis suae, assumebat dextraliola, & lilia, & inaures, & annulos, & omnibus ornamentis suis se ornabat.Matth. 6. v. 29.commendat Christus regium Salomonis ornatum. Resp. prohibitio Apostolica conformis Paulinae 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. non simpliciter, sed cum determinatione est accipienda, si nimirum foeminae supra sortem & conditionem suam, sumtuoso & luxurioso habitu sese efferant, si externo corporis cultui nimis deditae sint, de interiore animi cultu & spirituali ornatu nihil vel parum solicitae. Patet hoc ex antithesi subiectâ, quâ Apostolus foeminas admonet, ut ornatui Spiritus coram DEO precioso maiorem curam impendant, quàm externo corporis ornatui, qui corruptibilis est & caducus. Namque Apostolica negatio comparatè accipienda, iuxta usitatam regulam. Apud Hebraeos verba negantia saepè ponuntùr pro comparatis.Gen. 32. v. 28.Exod. 16. v. 8.1. Sam. 8. v. 7.Prov. 8. v. 10.Ierem. 7. v. 22.Luc. 14. vers. 12.1. Tim. 2. v. 14. &c. Apostolus Paulus in loco parallelo 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. sic improbat tortos crines, aurum, margaritas, vestem preciosam, ut permittat καταστολὴν κόσμιον habitum ornatum, modestum & honestum cum verecundia & sobrietate. Nequaquam igitur omnem omninò externum ornatum Apostolus interdicit, quo vel foeminae vel etiam viri ratione statûs, regionis, aetatis, temporis &c. decenter se vestiunt & ornant, sed omnem curam & cogitationem in ornatu externo poni prohibet, & interiorem animi cultum ac spiritualem ornatum, externo corporis cultui longissimè anteferendum esse docet. inde Basilius in moralib. constitut. cap. 5. regul. 73. verba Petri rectè sic explicat: mulieres non debere nimis exquisitae in ornatu corporis elegantiae studere, potiusque curam omnem in bona opera conferre. Hieronymus lib. 1. adv. Pelag. Ubique ó Pelagi, mediocriaὑπερβολικῶςtranseas & magna secteris. Unde adiungis, gloriam vestium & ornamentorum Deo esse contrariam. Quae sunt, rogo, inimicitiae contra Deum, si tunicam habuero mundiorem, si Episcopus, Presbyter & Diaconus, & reliquus ordo Ecclesiasticus in administratione sacrificiorum cum candidâ veste processerint? Cavete Clerici, cavete Monachi, viduae & virgines periclitamini, nisi sordidas vos atque pannosas vulgus aspexerit.

4. Ornatus uxorum Christianarum non debet esse in auro & vestibus preciosis v. 3. Atqui per hunc ornatum commendant se uxores maritis. quod moderatum maritis placendi studium non improbat Paulus.1. Cor. 7. v. 33.ne scil. viri ad alienas mulieres animum & oculos adiiciant. Resp. Si fine eo uxor sese decenter & moderatè ornet, ut marito placeat, illud ab Apostolo minimè improbatur, sed si nimio externi ornatus studio alienis viris placere satagat. Augustinus Epist. 73. ad Possidum. Nolo tamen de ornamentis auri vel vestis praeproperam habeas in prohibendo sententiam, nisi in eos, qui neque coniugati, neque coniugari cupientes cogitare debent, quomodo placeant Deo. Illi autem cogitant, quae sunt mundi, quomodo placeant vel viri uxoribus vel uxores maritis, nisi quod capillos nudare foeminas, quas etiam caput velare Apostolus iubet, nec maritatas decet. Fucari autem figmentis, quò vel rubicundior, vel candidior appareat, adulterina fallacia est, quâ non dubito etiam ipsos maritos se nolle decipi, quibus solis permittendae sunt foeminae ornari secundùm veniam, non secundùm imperium.

5. Sarae subiectionem Apostolus probat ex eo, quòd Abrahamum maritum suum vocarit dominum.v. 7.Atqui etiam immorigerae & refractariae uxores maritos vocare possunt Dominos. Resp. Apostolus non concludit ex sola compellatione, sed realem obedientiae exhibitionem cum ea coniungit, cuius illustre documentum in illo ipso cap. 18. Genes. ad quod Apostolus nos remittit, describitur, videl. quòd iussu mariti Sara festinaverit praeparare cibos hospitibus adhuc ignotis.

6. Sara obediebat Abrahae.v. 7. Atqui Gen. 16. v. 5.maritum accusat tanquam iniquè secum agentem. Resp. Chrysost. hom. 38. in Gen. Saram iustam habuisse conquerendi causam, indignum enim erat, ut Agar ancilla efferretur adversus primariam coniugem ac dominam, neque hoc nomine ab Abrahamo coërceretur. Quod si quid infirmitatis in hoc fribusculo concurrit, ut vult idem Chrysostomus, ex eo colligitur, obedientiam etiam piorum in hac vitâ non esse numeris omnibus perfectam.

7. Factae estis Sarae filiae benefacientes.v. 7.Atqui per studium bonorum operum non possumus ad spiritualemυἱοθεσίανpervenire, sed per fidem in Christum.Rom. 4. v. 12. Resp. 1. Apostolus studio bonorum operum coniungit fiduciam, in misericordia DEI propter Christum promissa acquiescentem, ut in expositione textus ostendimus. Proinde studium bonorum operum adducit, non tanquam υἱοθεσίας spiritualis medium, sed tanquam verae in Christum fidei necessarium consequens & effectum. 2. Repetenda hîc regula Theologica. Verba activa saepè exponenda sunt declarativè, ac res tunc fieri dicuntur, quando factae manifestantur. August. lib. 83. qq. q. 69. Tunc fieri aliquid dicitur, quando factum declaratur aut praedicitur.Iob. 9. v. 31.abominabuntur me vestimenta, i. e. abominabilem esse ostendent. Esa. 43. vers. ult.Contaminavi Principes sanctos, i. e. contaminatos declaravi, quando mori illos iussi. Cumprimis huc pertinent duo N. T. dicta, Matth. 5. v. 44.Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite his, qui oderunt vos &c.v. 45.ut sitis filii Patris vestri, i. e. ut reipsa declaretis, vos esse genuinos Patris coelestis filios. Ioh. 15. v. 8.In hoc clarificatus est pater meus, ut fructum plurimum afferatis, & efficiamini mei discipuli, i. e. ut copiosum ferendo fructum declaretis, vos esse meos discipulos.

Ἒλεγχος. 1. Coniugibus sanctae vitae praecepta Apostolus praescribit, de Monachis & Monialibus votariis, perfectionem in hoc vitae suae genere collocantibus, altum in Apostolicis scriptis est silentium. Ergò Monachatus, qualis hodiè in Papatu viget, non gaudet institutione divinâ, nec approbatione Apostolicâ. Fulgentius Epist. 3. cap. 8. Paulus non sic adscripsit virginibus sanctitatem corporis & Spiritus,1. Cor. 7. v. 34.ut illam vel coniugatis demeret, vel viduis abnegaret. Probat hoc ex eo, quòd Petrus non ambigit coniugatas fideles appellare Sanctas.

2. Apostoli non solùm virginibus & viduis, sed etiam coniugibus sua praescribunt munia, ac Petrus hoc loco docet, etiam coniugatas posse ac debere studere, ut interiùs coram DEO sint ornatae, ipsique placeant. Ostendunt ergò, etiam coniugalem statum DEO placere. Opponendum hoc Pontificiis, qui variis modis coniugii dignitati derogant, utpote immunditiem & pollutionem illud vocando, impedimentum pietatis illud statuendo, caelibatum contumelia coniugil laudando, toti ordini Ecclesiastico coniugio interdicendo, concubinatum & vagas libidines in personis Ecclesiasticis potiùs tolerando, quàm honestum coniugium ipsis permittendo, vota caelibatus à personis ad eum minùs idoneis exigendo ac suscipiendo, lupanaria publica in coniugii dedecus tolerando, & coniuges divinitùs coniunctos invicem separando, quae omnia probata vide tractat. de Eccles. §. 251. tractat. de coniugio §. 51.

3. Apostolus non praecipit, ut mulieres fideles maritis infidelibus in matrimonio coniunctae ab illis discedant, sed ut vitam Christianâ vitâ dignam agant, & hac ratione maritos suos Christo lucrari studeant. Idem praecipit Paulus 1. Corinth. 7. v. 12. & seqq. Opponendum hoc Canonistis, qui inter impedimenta matrimonium non solùm contrahendum prohibentia, sed etiam contractum dissolventia numerant religionis diversicatem; Bellarmino, qui lib. de matrim. cap. 23. format tertio loco eiusmodi propositionem. Matrimonium inter fidelem & infidelem non baptizatum, irritum est ex more populi Christiani, vim legis obtinente; & praxi in Papatu alicubi usitatâ.

4. Etiam in coniugio locum habet castitas DEO grata, quia ab uxoribus castam conversationem Apostolus requirit. Improbandum ergò, quod de Sacerdotibus coniugatis Pontifex c. Decernimus, dist. 28. dicit. Cùm ipsi templum, & vasa Domini, & sacrarium Spiritus sancti esse debeant, indignum est, eos ducendo uxores cubilibus & immunditiis deservire; quod Bellarminus lib. de matrim. cap. 5. scribit, non malè dici posse de coniugatis: Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt; quod idem lib. de Monachis cap. 9. pro stabiliendo Monachorum caelibatu adducit locum Apoc. 14.Hi sunt, qui cum mulieribus non sunt coinquinati, ex quo sequitur à contrario sensu, coniugatos cum mulieribus inquinari; quod lib. de Clericis cap. 19. scribit; Etiam sanctorum matrimonium sine pollutione quadam & turpitudine non exerceri, & actum coniugalem animam ipsam facere quodammodo carnalem; ac lib. eiusd. cap. 18. actum coniugalem reddere totum hominem carnalem & ineptum ad divina.

5. Illae demum sunt verae & genuinae Sarae filiae, quae in Christum credunt, & ex fide bonis operibus student. Opponendum hoc praeposterae Iudaeorum gloriationi, quâ propagationem sui generis ex sanctis maioribus, praesertim vero ex Abrahamo perpetuò iactitant, Matth. 3. vers. 9.Iohan. 8. v. 33. quibus meritò opponitur illud Christi Ioh. 8. v. 39.Si filii Abrahae essetis, opera Abrahae faceretis; uti etiam illa Paulina Roman. 2. v. 28.non qui in manifesto Iudaeus est &c.cap. 4. v. 11.Abraham est pater omnium credentium &c.cap. 9. v. 6.Non omnes qui ex Israël, illi sunt Israëlitae,v. 7.neque quia semen sunt Abrahae, omnes filii,v. 8.sed qui filii promissionis aestimantur in semine.Gal. 3. v. 7.Qui ex fide sunt, illi sunt filii Abrahae.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Cornelius à Lapide ad v. 1. sic annotat. Sancit Petrus tàm disertè, ut uxores maritis sint subditae, eò quòd per gentiles spargeretur rumor, sed falsus, Christianos quasi Christi filios velle se eximere ab omni servitute & subiectione, ac praesertim uxores à consortio coniugum, idque partim ex eo, quòd luxuriosi gentiles uxoribus praeposterè contra Naturam abutebantur, hoc autem uxoribus ne permitterent, vetabant Apostoli &c. partim ex eo, quod multae virgines à parentibus desponsatae viris infidelibus, ante consummatum matrimonium à Sponsalibus & Sponsis resilirent, ob amorem vel votum virginitatis, quam adeò ab Apostolis celebrari audiebant. Atqui nullum in Apostolicis scriptis extat vestigium, quòd Apostoli Spòsas à Sponsis infidelibus separaverint, vel votum virginitatis exegerint aut susceperint. Exempla Flaviae, Theclae, Iphigeniae, Susannae &c. quae Cornelius adducit, non sunt petita ex probatis scriptoribus, sed ex supposititiis, Lini, Abdiae, Metaphrastae & aliorum scriptis.

2. Verbis illis Apostoli, ut si qui non credunt, sine verbo lucrifiantv. 1. abutuntur Anabaptistae, Enthusiastae, Weigeliani &c. ad extenuandum ministerium verbi externum, quasi non sit organum ex ordinatione DEI necessarium, & efficax ad fidem in cordibus hominum excitandam & alendam.
