Sed ostendimus superiùs, Petrum loqui tantùm de occasione, quâ mariti infideles adducuntur, ut honestiùs de Christiana religione sentiant, publicos congressus, in quibus verbum Evangelii praedicatur, non ampliùs odio habeant, sed iis intersint, & progressu temporis ex verbo fidem concipiant, & Christianam religionem amplectantur.

3. Caietanus statuit, praeceptum Petri de neglectu ornatus externi, v. 3. esse temporarium, primitivae duntaxat Ecclesiae datum, in qua mulieres Christi cultrices omnia lenocinia à se abdicabant. Sed praeceptum hoc morale est & perpetuum, ad omnis temporis gradus & status foemineos pertinens, ut apparet ex antithesi subiecta, & ex loco Apostolico parallelo. 1. Tim. 2. v. 9.

4. Estius ad vers. 4. sic commentatur. Ostendit Apostolus, quem dicat absconditum hominem, sc. eum, qui in mente seu parte rationis consistit, quâ propriè homines sumus, quem Apostolus vocat interiorem.2. Cor. 4. v. 16. Lorinus in h. l. Est igitur absconditus & interior homo secundùm partem suam superiorem, quae est ratio ac voluntas, nec patens hominum sensibus. Atqui nomine occulti & interioris hominis non intelligitur absolutè & simpliciter mens sive animus hominis, sed mens per Spiritum sanctum renovata, adeoque totus homo corpore & animâ constans, quatenus est per Spiritum sanctum regenitus & renovatus. Ornatus enim ille, quem Apostolus foemineo sexui hîc commendant, non folùm est interior, sed etiam spiritualis, proinde in illis solùm foeminis locum habet, quae sunt per Spiritum sanctum regenitae ac renovatae, unde notanter Apostolus subiicit, quòd occultus ille homo cordis consistat in incorruptione mansueti & quieti Spiritus, ostendens mansuetudinem, lenitatem & alias virtutes, in quibus ornatus exterior consistit, esse Spiritus sancti effectus & fructus Galat. 5. v. 22. inde Lorinus subiicit. Nihilo minùs magis propriè loquendo, vetus homo importat culpam & poenam; novus iustitiam & gloriam. novus homo perfectionem interieris includit.

5. Salmero per πτόησιν in v. 7.libidinem accipi posse statuit. Sic enim ad illum vers. commentatur. Quidam aiunt,πτόησινesse nimium ardorem libidinis in foeminis. Et ita Aristoteles lib. 4. de generat. animal. colligit, foeminas post multos partus tandem liberari ab hoc ardore. Animo enim consternatur mulier, cum suffocationes vulvae coarguunt. Et ita docet, rectè facientes nullam ardentem libidinem metuere debere, cum gratia Dei illis praestet id, quod post multos partus Natura foeminis concedit. Resp. concedimus, πτόησιν apud profanos scriptores quandoque accipi pro erotico illo affectu, quo nimia & veluti stupida rei Venereae libidine foeminae flagrant, quo modo locum adductum ex Aristot. lib. 4. de generat. animal. cap. 5. Budaeus interpretatur, qui in Graeco sic habet. Ἒστι γὰρ τὰ καταμήνια σπέρμα ἄπεπτον, διὸ καὶ τῷν γυναικῶν ὅσαι πρὸς τὴν ὁμιλίαν ἀκρατεῖς τὴν τοιάυτην, ὃταν πολυτοκήσωσι, πάυονται τῆς πτοήσεως, ἐκκεκριμένη γὰρ ἡ σπερματικὴ περίττωσις οὐκέτι ποιεῖ τῆς ὁμιλίας τάυτης ἐπιθυμίαν, ex quo apparet Salmeronem verbis obscuirs & alienis eum vertisse. Apud Platonem σωφροσύνη sic describitur, quòd sit τὸ περιτὰς ἐπιθυμίας μὴ ἐπτοῆσθαι. Apud Euripidem habetur ἐπτοήθης ἒρωτιamoris oestro ad stuporem usque perculsus es. Sed haec πτοήσεως significatio nuspiam in Scripturis occurrit, & ab hoc loco prorsus aliena est. Ecquis enim hic foret sensus, factae estis Sarae filiae benefacientes & nullum libidinis ardorem pertimescentes. Inde Cornelius à Lapide Salmeronem suppresso nomine perstringens ad h. l. sic annotat. Minùs castè aliqui perturbationem accipiunt libidinis, quam significat Graecumπτόησιςapud Aristotelem, quidem. Ne timeatis per obsequia erga maritum inflammandam in vobis libidinem, quia illa caritatem pariunt, non cupiditatem. Lorinus in h. l. Admitto notionem Graeci vocabuli traditam à Philosopho pro nimia illa velutque attonita & stupida libidineπερὶ τὰ ἀφροδίσια,verùm non arbitror ad rem esse, imò indignum iudico tanto Apostolo, rem adeò parùm honestam vel indicare. Illud quoqueμηδεμίανarguit magis generalem timorem. Postremò dicendum potius fuissetπτοούμεναιquod verbum responderet nominiπτόησις,habetque similem usum, quemφοβούμεναι.

6. Cornelius à Lapide ex v. 7. probare conatur, coniugium esse Sacramentum, sic enim ad eum annotat. Nolite timere perturbationes i. e. molestias coniugii. Si enim benefaciatis, digneque coniugio vivatis, Deus suâ gratiâ eas vobis facit faciles. Haec enim gratia est effectus Sacramenti matrimonii coniugibus à Deo praeparata, ut matrimonii onera fortiter sustineant, sibique benè consciae nihil timeant. Resp. Concedimus piis coniugibus gratiam à Deo dari, qua matrimonii onera fortiter sustinere, & quieto animo in hoc vitae genere possint esse. Sed ex eo inferri nequit, coniugium esse Sacramentum divinitùs ordinatum, neque enim gratia illa datur per ipsum coniugium, sed per preces ex fide à piis coniugibus factas; nec quaevis gratia constituit Sacramentum, sed quae est Evangelii propria & remissionem peccatorum includit.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Proponitur hîc speculum virtutum, quod piae foeminae quotidie intueri, & ad illud sese ac vitam suam conformare debent. Tales virtutes sunt. 1. Subiectio, per quam voluntati mariti suam attemperent. 2. Reverentia erga maritum, quâ solicitè caveant, ne maritum facto, verbo vel etiam nutu offendant. 3. Castitas in moribus, verbis, gestibus & tota conversatione. 4. Timor DEI, qui piae & castae conversationis est fundamentum. 5. Humilitas, ne nimium studeant externo corporis ornatui. 6. Mansuetudo, ne sint responsatrices vel obmurmuratrices, cum à maritis obiurgantur. 7. Tranquillitas, ne sint alienarum rerum curiosae, ne discursent ad inquirendum res alienas, ne suâ garrulitate maritis vel aliis sint molestae. Prov. 7. vers. 11. &c. 8. Comitas, blandè compellent maritos. 9. Benignitas & benè operandi studium 10. Robur animi, ne sint nimis meticulosae, sed in periculis & adversis magnâ animi in DEO acquiescentis fiducia praeditae. Prov. 31. v. 10.Sirac. 26. v. 2.

2. Causae sunt longè plurimae, quae mulieres ad subiectionem exhortari debent. v. 1. Potiores hae sunt. 1. creatio 1. Cor. 11. 8.Vir non est ex muliere, sed mulier ex viro.v. 9.non est creatus vir propter mulierem, ut scil. illi serviret, tanquam praestantiori, sed mulier propter virum.1. Tim. 2. v. 13. Adam primus formatus est, deinde Eva. 2. transgressio. 1. Tim. 2. v. 14.Adam non est seductus, scil. primùm & immediatè à Diabolo, mulier autem seducta fuit in praevaricatione i. e. prima transgressa est Dei mandatum, & Adamo persuasit, ut ipse quoque idem transgrederetur. 3. Dei ordinatio. Gen. 3. v. 16.ad virum desiderium tuum, & ipse dominabitur tibi.1. Cor. 14. v. 33.Mulieres decet esse subditas, sicut & lex dicit. 4. viri dignatio. 1. Cor. 11. vers. 3.caput mulieris vir, quatenus sexu praestat, & Dominus eius constitutus est.vers. 7.vir est imago & gloria Dei, mulier autem gloria viri est. Respicit Apostolus ad partem illam divinae imaginis, quae in dominio erat sita. Sicut Deus est totius mundi dominus & omnibus creaturis imperat, sic paterfamilias est Dominus domus, & mulieri ac domesticis imperat. Gloria accipitur pro repraesentatione maiestatis & dominationis divinae. Vir est gloria DEI i. e. repraesentat maiestatem & dignitatem Dei, supremum obtinens gradum in oeconomiae gubernatione, & nomine DEI habens dominium in uxorem. Posset etiam gloriae nomine intelligi potestas & excellentia viri, quia potestas parit autoritatem & gloriam. Augustinus q. 153. in Genes. Est ordo naturalis in hominibus, ut serviant foeminae viris, quia & illic iustitia est haec, ut infirmior ratio serviat fortiori, & haec in dominationibus & servitutibus clara iustitia est, ut qui excellunt ratione, excellant dominatione. 5. Dei approbatio. Si mulier paret marito, potest ex fide certò statuere, hanc suam obedientiam placere Deo, quae enim opera Deus praecipit, ea sunt ipsi grata. Iohannes Huss in h. l. Mulieres debent viris subiici propter quinque. Primum est praecepti Dei transgressio. Nam à mulieris transgressione sumsit originem hominum perditio & miseria huius vitae. Unde dixit ei DEUS in poenam transgressionis. Quia hoc fecisti, sub viri potestate eris. Secundum est superbiae elatio. August. Mulier elata per suasioni serpentis obediens, praecepta Dei contemsit, & propter hoc meretur viri subiici potestati. Tertium est Naturae fragilitas & instabilitas, & ideò viris constantioribus debent obedire, nec viros regere, sed à viris regi. Quartum est verecundiae passio, quae plus inest mulieribus, à qua cûm mulier deficit, est ad malitiam valde prona, à qua debet per virum cohiberi,Sirac. 26.In filia non advertente i. e. non verecunda firma custodia.1. Tim. 2.Mulieres cum verecundia & sobrietate. Quintum est verborum clamatio & litigatio.Prov. 9.Mulier stulta & clamosa &c.

3. Subiectio illa uxorum habet certam limitationem, ne in gratiam maritorum peccent contra DEUM & sanctum illius verbum, unde Paulus uxores maritis vult esse subiectas in Domino.Col. 3. v. 18. quae phrasis duo complectitur, primò quod subiectae viris esse debeant iuxta mandatum & ordinationem DEI, qui eas viris subiectas esse voluit. Secundo quòd subiectae esse debeant infra DEUM, ne ex hac erga viros obedientia quicquam contra DEUM agant. Ephes. 6. vers. 1. Beda in h. l. Notandum, quòd Petrus eâ conditione desiderat, mulieres bonas & honestas viris incredulis subdi, ut non solùm nihil mali ad imperium eorum faciant, verùm etiam tàm casta conversatione persistant insuperabiles, ut ipsi etiam viris exemplo possint esse castitatis & fidei.

4. Quando Apostolus uxores viris propriis subditas esse vult, adulterium prohibet, easque corporis sui potestatem habere negat. 1. Corinth. 7. v. 8. Idipsum manifestiùs declarat, quando in v. 2.castam conversationem ab illis requirit. Haec castitas est ἁγιασμὸς ille μετὰ σωφροσὺνης, quem Paulus in loco parallelo ab illis exigit 1. Tim. 2. v. 15. Plutarch. in problem. memorat, novae nuptae praeferri olim solitum ignem & aquam, ut significaretur, eam castam & puram esse debere, ignis enim purgat, aqua lustrat.

5. Si in coniugio dispari Apostolus subiectionem & reverentiam erga maritos ab uxoribus requirit, quantò magis inter coniuges utrinque Christianos illa locum habere debet. Ita concludit Hieron. Epist. ad Celantiam.

6. Incredulitas definitur per in obedientiam erga sermonem Evangelii, ἡ ἀπιστία definitur per ἀπειθείαν, sicut & fides definitur per obedientiam erga Evangelium. Rom. 1. vers. 5.cap. 16. vers. 26.1. Petr. 1. v. 2. & 22.

7. Omnes Christiani, cumprimis vero & peculiari quadam ratione ministri Ecclesiae, sunt servi ChristiRom. 1. v. 1.Gal. 1. v. 10. &c. solicitè igitur operam dare debent, ut talento verbi sibi concredito multos Christo lucrifaciant, Matth. 25. v. 16. quod studium de se praedicat Apostolus 1. Cor. 9. v. 19. & Seqq.

8. Non uxores solùm Christianae, sed omnes omninò Christiani cuiuscunque sint sexus, aetatis ac status, castae & sanctae conversationi studere debent, ut exemplo suo ad verae religionis amorem alios alliciant. Cuius enim placet conversatio, eius non potest displicere religio.

9. Sicut studium bonorum operum alios ad amplectendam Evangelii doctrinam invitat & allicit: Sic vitae ac morum improbitas ab eadem incredulos magis deterret & animos ipsorum alienat, quâ de re gravissimè Deus conqueritur. Esai. 52. v. 5.Ezech. 36. v. 23.Rom. 2. v. 24.nomen Dei per vos blasphematur inter gentes.

10. Τὰ ἔργαad aliorum conversionem maiorem vim habent, quàmψιλοὶ λόγοι. Chrysost. homil. 19. in Epist. Hebr. Efficacior est vox operis quàm sermonis, inquit Iohan. Hufs. ex Bernhardo in h. l. Plus valet vivendi, quàm loquendi modus. August. Epist. 112. Homines malunt exempla, quàm verba, quia loqui facilè est, praestare difficile. Lactant. lib. 4. Instit. cap. 23. Optimum est exemplo potius docere, quàm dictis. Hilarius can. 5. in Matth.

11. Circa externum corporis ornatum multis modis à sexu foemineo φιλοκόσμῳ peccatur, videl. per superfluitatem, novitatem, preciositatem &c. 1. Nimiùm indulgent externo isti cultui, ut interim negligant ornatum interiorem ac spiritualem. Qui anxiè occupantur in cultu corporis, animi cultum negligunt. Dicebat olim Cato. 2. Si ornatu illo nimiùm delectentur, cùm in Domino potiùs delectari & gaudere debeant,Ps. 37. v. 4.Phil. 4. v. 4. &c. 3. Si modestiae & moderationis limites in mundo muliebri excedant, ac nimios in eam rem sumtus faciant. Duo in vestitu sunt spectanda, commoditas & decorum. Decori partes duae sunt, mediocritas & modestia; nimia elegantia & superfluus splendor, adeoque excessus omnis ex animi vitio oritur. 4. Si propter externum ornatum superbiant. Esa. 3. v. 16.Qui gloriatur de vestimento, similis est furi, qui gloriatur de cauterio, quia vestimentum est reatus signum. Estheris debent insistere vestigiis, quae c. 14. v. 16. sic orat. Tu Domine scis necessitatem meam, quòd abominer signum superbiae & gloriae meae, quod est super caput meum, in diebus ostentationis meae, & detester illud quasi pannum menstruatae, & non portem in diebus silentii mei. 5. Si in ornando se non habeant rationem loci ac temporis Ps. 35. v. 13.Matth. 22. v. 11.Rom. 2. v. 15. 6. Si studeant hoc ornatu placere viris alienis, & ad oculorum ac cordis adulterium eas alliciant. Aspectata capillorum complicatio, & reticula aureis filis intertexta sunt instar retis, quo capiunt homines incautos.

12. Inde apud pios veteres gravissima contra externi ornatus studium habentur pronunciata. Cyprianus tract. de habitu virginum. Si te sumtuosius comas, & per publicum notabiliter incedas, oculos in te inventutis illicias, suspiria adole scentum post te trahas, concupiscendi libidinem nutrias, peccandi fomenta succendas, ut etsi ipsa non pereas, alios tamen perdas, & velut gladium te, & venenum videntibus praebeas, excusari non potes, quasi mente casta sis & pudicâ. Redarguit te cultus improbus & impudicus ornatus &c. Ornamentorum ac vestium insignia & lenocinia fucorum, non nisi prostitutis & impudicis foeminis congruunt, & nullarum ferè preciosior cultus est, quàm quarum pudor vilis est. Serico & purpurâ indutae Christum induere non possunt, auro & margaritis & monilibus adornatae ornamenta corporis & pectoris perdiderunt. Tertullianus in tract. de cultu foeminarum cap. 7. Quid tanta ornandi capitis onerositas salutem subministrat? quid crinibus vestris quiescere non licet, modò substrictis, modò relaxatis: modò suscitatis, modò elisis? Aliae gestiunt, in cincinnis coërcere, aliae, ut vagi & volucres elabantur, non bona simplicitate. Affligitis praeterea nescio quas enormitates sutilium atque textilium capillamentorum, nunc in galeri modum, quasi vaginam capitis, & operculum verticis, nunc in cervicem retrò suggestum. Mirum quòd contra Domini praecepta contenditur. Ad mensuram neminem sibi adiicere posse, pronunciatum est. Vos planè adiicitis ad pondus collyridas quasdam, scutorum umbilicos cervicibus adstruendo. Si non pudet enormitatis, pudeat inquinamenti, ne exuvias alieni capitis forsitan immundi, forsan nocentis & gehennae destinati sancto & Christiano capiti suppares. In hac detestatione ornatus nimii & ascititii totus liber de cultu foeminarum, ut & alius de habitu muliebri consumitur. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 2. Paed. c. 10. dicit: verum mulieris ornamentum esse verecundiam, eas quae se auro ornant, imitari barbaros, qui maleficos auro vinciunt. An non, inquit, colli vinculum est torques aureus, moniliaque, & quae catenarum locum obtinent? hinc &ἁλύσεις, i. e. catenae appellantur. Chrysost. homil. 21. ad popul. Antioch. Vis ornare faciem? orna non margaritis, sed modestiâ & honestate, sicque vir gratiorem cernet aspectum. Ille nempe ornatus, & Zelotypiae suspicionem iniicere saepè solet, & inimicitias, & contentiones, & pugnas &c. Modestiâ autem ornatus omnem quidem improbam suspicionem expellit, omni autem vinculo firmius coniugium conciliat &c. Circa margaritarum cultum insania est pompa Satanica. Aurum enim cepisti, non ut corpus vincias, sed ut pauperes salves, & enutrias. Gregor. Nazianz. orat. 11. de Gorgonia sorore sua. Non illam aurum ornavit, non flavae comae, non crinium nodi & imposturae, preciosum caput summa cum insania scenam efficientium, non circumfluae & pellucidae vestis magnificentia, non lapidum splendores, propinquum aërem colorantes, non pictorum artes & praestigiae &c. unus illi rubor placebat, quem pudor affert; unus candor, quem parit abstinentia. Augustinus Epist. 73. ad Possidium. Verus ornatus maximè Christianorum & Christianarum, non tantùm nullus fucus mendax, verùm ne auri quidem vestisque pompa, sed boni mores sunt. Gregorius super verba Luc. 16.Erat dives &c. Si cultus preciosarum vestium culpa non esset, nunquam lectio Evangelica tàm vigilanter dixisset, quòd dives in inferno sepultus, qui induebatur purpurâ & bysso. Quin & gentiles nimium illud externi ornatus studium foeminis quasi innatum improbarunt. Beda in h. l. adducit dictum Pythagorae, vera ornamenta matronarum pudicitiam esse, non vestes. Plutarchus in Laconicis citat dictum Gatetis. Ornatus est, quod ornat; ornat autem quod mulierem ornatiorem facit. Sed nec aurum, nec Smaragdus mulierem ornatiorem facit, sed quaecunque gravitatis, modestiae & pudicitiae significationem habent. Ovid. lib. 3. de arte amandi.

Quis pudor est, census corpore ferre suos.

13. Cumprimis vero acriter invehuntur pii veteres in eas, quae vel faciem vel capillos alieno colore fucare non reformidant. Quòd si enim capillos complicare prohibet Apostolus, quantò magis faciem cerussa ac minio fucare prohibet? Cyprianus de habitu virginum. Peccatores & apostatae Angeli, quando ad terrena contagia devoluti, à coelesti vigore recesserunt, & oculos circumducto nigrore fucare, & genas mendacio ruboris inficere, & mutare adulterinis coloribus crinem, & expugnare omnem oris & capitis veritatem corruptelae suae impugnatione docuerunt &c. Nec virgines tantùm aut viduas, sed & nuptas puto & omnes omninò foeminas admonendas, quòd opus DEI & factura eius & plasma adulterari nullo modo debeat, adhibito flavo colore vel nigro pulvere, vel rubore, aut quolibet denique lineamenta nativa corrumpente medicamine. Dicit DEUS. Faciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram, & audet quisquam mutare & convertere quod DEUS fecit? Manus DEO inferunt, quando illud, quod ille formavit, reformare & transfigurare contendunt, nescientes, quia opus DEI est omne quod nascitur, Diaboli quodcunque mutatur. Si quis pingendi artifex vultum alicuius & speciem & corporis qualitatem aemulo colore signasset, & signato iam consummatoque simulachro manus alius afferret, ut iam formata, iam picta quasi peritior reformaret, gravis prioris artificis iniuria & iusta indignatio videretur. Tu te existimas impunè laturam tàm improbae temeritatis audaciam Dei artificis offensam? Ut enim impudica circa homines & incesta fucis lenocinantibus non sis, corruptis, violatisque quae DEI sunt, peior adulterâ detineris: Quod ornari te putas, quod putas comi, impugnatio est ista divini operis, praevaricatio est veritatis &c. Non metuis, oro, quae talis es, ne cum resurrectionis dies venerit, artifex tuus te non recognoscat? ad sua praemia & promissa venientem removeat & excludat? increpans vigore censoris & iudicis dicat? Opus hoc meum non est, nec haec imago nostra est, cutem falso medicamine polluisti, crinem adultero colore mutasti, expugnata est mendacio facies, figura corrupta est, cultus alienus est, DEUM videre non poteris, cum oculi tibi non sint, quos DEUS fecit, sed quos Diabolus infecit, illum tu sectata es, rutilos atque depictos serpentis oculos imitata es, de inimico tuo compta, cum ipso semper arsura. Tertull. de cultu foeminarum cap. 5. In Deum delinquunt, quae cutem medicaminibus ungunt, genas rubore maculant, oculos siligine collinunt. Displicet illis nimirum plastica Dei, in ipsis redarguunt, reprehendunt artificem omnium. Reprehendunt enim, cum emendant, cum adiiciunt, utique ab adversario artifice sumentes additamenta ista, id est, Diabolo. Nam quis corpus monstraret mutare, nisi qui & hominis Spiritum malitiâ transfiguravit? ille indubitatè huiusmodi ingenia concinnavit, ut in nobis quodammodo manus Deo inferret. Quod nascitur, opus Dei est. Ergò quod fingitur, Diaboli negotium est. Divino operi Satanae ingenia superducere, quàm scelestum est! cap. 7. Utinam miserrimus ego in illo die Christianae exultationis vel inter calcanea vestra caput elevem, videre, an cum cerussa & purpurisso & croco, & in illo ambitu capitis resurgatis, an taliter expictam Angeli in nubila sublevent obviam Christo. Si nunc bona, & Dei sunt, tuno quoque occurrent resurgentibus corporibus, & sua loca agnoscent. Gregorius Nazianzenus carmen suum contra mulieres ambitiosiùs se ornantes sic exorditur. Μὴ κεφαλὰς πυργοῦτε νόθοις καὶ οκαμοῖσι γυναῖκες.Cavete; ô mulieres, ne caput vestrum nothis & adulterinis crinibus, tanquam turribus quibusdam muniatis, mollia colla è scapulis delicatè ostentatis: neu Dei formas foedis coloribus inungatis, sic ut iam non facies, sed larvas gestetis &c. Verendum est, ne Deus iratus sic te alloquatur. Dic age, ô aliena mulier, ecquis tandem & undenam est tuus fictor & procreator? non te depinxi canis, sed imaginem mei finxi. Quî fit igitur, ut pro cara imagine idolum habeam? Hieronymus ad Laetam de institutione filiae. Nec caput gemmis oneres, nec capillum irruffes, & ei aliquid de Gehennae ignibus admisceas. August. Epist. 73. ad Possidium. Fucari figmentis, quò vel rubicundior vel candidior appareat, adulterina fallacia est, quâ non dubito etiam ipsos maritos se nolle decipi. Ioh. Huss in h. l. In illis ornamentis, in quibus fit praeiudicium Naturae, sicut in pictura faciei, nihil excusat, in aliis vero ornatum muliebrem excusat, si non sit causa superbiae vel vanitatis, vel provocandi alios ad incontinentiam, sed ut servetur mos loci vel gradus dignitatis, vel ut revocetur vir à fornicatione.

14. Si nimium externi ornatus studium in foeminis Apostolus improbat, quantò magis in viris illud detestabitur, quos Tertullianus in lib. de veland. virgin. apertam professos dicit mulierositatem. Idem de cultu foeminarum cap. 8. Et viris propter foeminas, & foeminis propter viros, vitio Naturae ingenita est placendi voluntas, propriasque praestigias formae & hic sexus sibi agnoscit, barbam acriùs caedere, intervellere, circumdare capillum, disponere, etiam colorare caniciem, primam quamque subducere totius corporis lanuginem; pigmento quoque muliebri distinguere, caetera pulveris cuiusdam asperitudine levigare, tùm speculum omni occasione consulere, maximè inspicere, cum tamen cognito Deo adempta placendi voluntate per luxuriae vacationem omnia illa ut otiosa, ut hostilia pudicitiae recusantur. Nam ubi Deus, ibi pudicitia, ibi gravitas adiutrix & socia eius. Quo ergò pacto pudicitiam sine instrumento eius i. e. sine gravitate tractabimus, quomodo autem gravitatem administrandae pudicitiae adhibebimus? nisi & in facie, & in cultu & in totius hominis contemplatione severitas circumferatur? Gregorius homil. 6. in Evang. Pensate quae culpa sit, hoc etiam viros appetere, quo curavit Pastor Ecclesiae (Petrus) & foeminas prohibere!

15. Interior & spiritualis ornatus externo corporis ornatui longissimè anteferendus. Tertullianus de cultu foeminarum cap. 13. Prodite vos iam medicamentis & ornamentis exstructae Apostolorum, sumentes de simplicitate candorem, de pudicitia ruborem, depictae oculos verecundia & Spiritus taciturnitate, inserentes inaures sermonem Dei, annectentes cervicibus iugum Christi. Caput maritis subiicite, & satis ornatae eritis. Manus lanis occupate, pedes domi figite, & plusquàm in auro placebunt. Vestite vos serico probitatis, byssino sanctitatis, purpurâ pudicitiae. Taliter pigmentatae Deum habebitis amatorem.

16. Interior ille ornatus potissimùm in eo consistit, ut fide Christum induamus,Galat. 3. vers. 27. sicque fide cor nostrum purificetur,Actor. 15. vers. 9. hac fide cor stabilitur, ut sit pacatum, quietum & tranquillum, nec de gratia DEI dubitet. Hebr. 13. vers. 9. ex hac fide procedunt bona opera, etiam externa, pro cuiusque vocatione diversa & varia. Verus igitur Christianarum foeminarum ornatus non est sericus, vel gemmeus, vel aureus, sed Spiritualis & interior. Virtutes sunt preciosissimae margaritae & gemmae, quae foemineum sexum coram Deo, Angelis, & piis hominibus maximè condecorant.

17. Nihil est quod magis ornet sexum foemineum, quàm ingenium fedatum & placidum, mansuetudo & lenitas spiritus, verecundia & pudor, modestia & humilitas. Inde Ambrosius lib. 2. de virginit. foeminam Deo & hominibus placentem sic describit. Nihil torvum in oculis, nihil in verbis procax, nihil in actu inverecundum, non gestus fractior, non incessus solutior, non vox petulantior, ut ipsa corporis species simulachrum fuerit mentis, figura probitatis.

18. Verae & incorruptibiles pii hominis divitiae sunt spirituales & interiores. Interior enim homo super omnia terrena sese elevans, eademque contemnens, Deum ipsum possidet, ac haeres est aeterni regni. Ambrosius lib. 4. Epist. 27. Verè dives qui in conspectu Dei potest dives videri ( qui in Deo divesLuc. 21. v. 21.) in cuius conspectu terra exigua, mundus ipse angustus est. Sed solum illum Deus divitem novit, qui sit dives aeternitati, qui non operum, sed virtutum fructus recondat. Quis autem ante Deum dives, nisi quietus & modestus Spiritus, qui nunquam corrumpitur? Nonne tibi videtur dives, qui habet pacem animi, tranquillitatem quietis, ut nihil concupiscat, nullis exagitetur cupiditatum procellis &c. Ea est pax verè dives, quae superat omnem mentem. Dives pax, dives modestia, dives fides (fideli enim totus mundus possessio est) dives simplicitas, sunt enim & divitiae simplicitatis, quae nihil discutit, nihil contractum aut fraudulentum putat, sed puro se fundit affectu. Dives bonitas, quam si quis servaverit, pascitur in divitiis coelestis hereditatis &c. Id. lib. 1. officiorum cap. 18. Magnaigitur modestia, quae cum sit etiam iuris sui remissior, nihil sibi usurpans, nihil vendicans & quodammodo intra vires suas contractior, dives est apud Deum, apud quem nemo dives. Dives est modestia, quia portio Dei est. August. 1. de civ. Dei cap. 10. Sancti amiserunt omnia, quae habebant. Nunquid fidem? nunquid pietatem? nunquid interioris hominis bona, qui est ante Deum dives? hae sunt opes Christianorum, quibus opulentus dicebat Apostolus, foris pauper, intus dives. Est magnus quaestus pietas cum sufficientia. B. Lutherus in h. l. Credens habet omnia, quae Christus habet, fides omnia Christi bona nobis adducit, verè igitur dives, qui in Christum credit, & ex fide interioris hominis culturae studet.

19. In Scriptura non N. solùm sed etiam V. T. proponuntur exempla virtutum, praesertim in sanctis Patriarchis & Matriarchis, quae pro vocationis modo atque modulo imitanda. Hebr. 11. vers. 4. & seqq.

20. Exempla maiorum ἀξιομίμητα magnum ad pietatem & sanctitatem continent ὁρμητήριον.

21. Ut Abrahae filii, ita quoque Sarae filiae bifariam censentur, carne & Spiritu; carnali generatione, & fidei ac virtutum imitatione. Carnalis generatio coram Deo nihil quidquam valet, nisi accedat fidei ac virtutum imitatio. Matth. 3. v. 9.Ioh. 8. v. 39. Didymus in h. l. Sicut quis opus faciens Abrahami & habens eius fidem, filius eius fit: ita bonafacientes fideles foeminae matrem habent Saram.Luc. 13. v. 16.

22. Qui per fidem Abrahae filii, & quae per fidem Sarae filiae redduntur, cum Abrahamo & Sara coelestem gloriam & felicitatem hereditabunt. Rom. 3. v. 17.Gal. 3. v. 9.Qui ex fide sunt, benedicentur cum fideli Abrahamo.

23. Abrahae uxor maritum suum vocabat dominum, sed ipsa vicissim à marito honorabatur, qui vocabat eam Sarai i. e. domina mea. Nimirum uxores, quae maritos suos honorant, iisque reverenter sese subiiciunt, à maritis suis honorantur. In libro Musar cap. 6. fol. 73. sic legitur. Sapiens quaedam foemina dicebat filiae suae cum eam duceret ad thalamum: Mea filia, sta coram viro tuo & ministra ei. Si fueris ei ancillá, ipse tibi servus erit & honorabit te, ut heram sive dominam. Sed si extuleris te contra eum, erit tibi Dominus & tunc vilesces in oculis eius ut una ancillarum. Publius Syrus.

Casta ad virum matrona parendo imperat.

24. Sexus foemineus facilè solet turbari & pavore exanimari vel ob rei familiaris incommoda propria, vel ob mala Christianis communiter accidentia; pronus insuper est ad superstitiones, ut in adversitatibus ac periculis ad divinatrices currat & ab illis consilium deposcat, sed ab hoc pavore pias foeminas Apostolus vult esse liberas & alienas.

25. Spes in Deum ac fides in Christum liberant pios ab inordinato & praepostero timore, ut ostendit connexio v. 6. & 7. inde cum Davide forti & imperterrito animo dicunt Psal. 23. vers. 4.Etsi ambulavero in valle umbrae mortis, non timebo mala, quoniam tu mecum esPs. 27. v. 1.Dominus est illuminatio & salus mea, quem timebo.Psal. 62. v. 3. & 7.Deus petra mea & salus mea, refugium meum, non movebor vehementer.

## 3:7
YE HUSBANDS LIKEWISE, DWELLING TOGETHER ACCORDING TO KNOWLEDGE, GIVING HONOR UNTO THE WEAKER VESSEL, AS UNTO THE CO-HEIRS OF THE GRACE OF LIFE, THAT YOUR PRAYERS BE NOT HINDERED.

Connection. 1. From the precepts which were prescribed to wives, the Apostle makes a transition to the precepts to be delivered to husbands. The particle ὁμοίως. shows this connection.

2. Between spouses there is a mutual relationship. 1. Cor. 7. v. 2. Therefore, those whom God has joined in an indissoluble covenant Matth. 19. v. 6. the Apostle did not wish to separate in delivering the precepts of life and morals.

Disposition. The Apostle puts forward six arguments by which he exhorts husbands to treat their wives humanely and to converse with them prudently. The first is sought from the prerogative of the male sex. Men are endowed with greater knowledge than women. Therefore, let husbands dwell with their wives according to that knowledge.

The second from the indissolubility of marriage. Husband and wife, by God's institution, ought to dwell together, as being joined by an indissoluble bond. Therefore, let concord flourish between them, which cannot happen unless husbands treat their wives humanely.

The third from the utility of the female sex. Wives are vessels, that is, instruments fit for salutary uses, namely the generation and education of children, and for the administration of domestic affairs. Therefore, let them be treated modestly and humanely by their husbands.

The fourth from the infirmity of the same sex. Wives are weak vessels; therefore, let them be treated tenderly and softly, lest by harsher treatment they be broken like a weak vessel dashed against a stone.

The fifth from the dignity of Christian wives. They are co-heirs of life; therefore, let husbands bestow appropriate honor upon them.

The sixth from the consequent inconvenience. Prayers are hindered by the quarrels and brawls of spouses. Therefore, husbands ought not to treat their wives too harshly, lest occasion be given to dissensions and quarrels.

Exposition of the text, Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως. As Paul Eph. 5. v. 33.

Col. 3. v. 18. & 19.1. Tim. 2. v. 8. & 9. joins the duties of husbands and wives, so also Peter in this place prescribes their own duties to both. Paul 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. through the particle ὡσάυτως, Peter in this place through the particle ὁμοίως connects those duties, which the Vulgate rendered in both places by similarly.

Οἱ ἄνδρες through ἀντίπτωσιν or an Atticism is placed for ὦ ἄνδρες. for the Apostle addresses husbands, as is evident from the end of the verse, hence the Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] And You husbands.

Συνοικοῦντες, viz. ἔστε, cohabit with your wives, not with others. κατὰ γνῶσιν, according to knowledge, by which through the benefit of Nature you excel the female sex. Moreover, the noun is placed for the adverb, according to knowledge, i. e. knowingly, prudently & humanely.

Ώς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ. The adjective γυναικείω denotes the subject, namely the woman, who is compared to a vessel. A similar mode of speaking exists 1. Petr. 2. v. 2. & 13. In the word σκεῦος is a Hebraism; because the Hebrews by the name כלי denote any instrument of a vessel, by which something is prepared, consumed & perfected. Therefore the Apostle alludes to the primeval institution of marriage, in which the wife is called a helper for the man, who is before him, i. e. who is at hand for him for various uses in the administration of family affairs Gen. 2. v. 18. The Vulgate version rendered little vessel, but in the Greek there is no diminutive, whence Ambrose in the book on Paradise chapter 4 simply rendered vessel. Moreover, the woman is called σκεῦος ἀσθενέστερον the weaker vessel, viz. both in body and in mind, with respect had to the man, to whom the Apostle attributes greater knowledge and greater strength of body and mind.

Ἀπονέμοντες τιμὴν. The Vulgate renders, imparting, which some explain as distributing in part, when honor is to be paid totally to GOD alone.

But ἀπαιδεύτως these things are noted, since nothing is being treated here concerning total or partial honor. In the Greek it is ἀπονέμοντες distributing or deferring honor, viz. to the female sex, especially that which is convenient for wives, lest they be held in the place of handmaids, but that they be treated courteously and humanely as companions of life and the marriage bed. The Syrian rendered, as weak vessels hold them in price.

Ώς καὶ συγκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς. Thus some Codices read, especially the Royal and the Veronese, so that ταῖς γυναιξὶ, is understood, namely συνοικοῦντες.. Thus also Jerome reads in book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 4. But other Codices have the nominative ὡς καὶ συγκληρονόμοι,, namely ὄντες,, so that it may be referred to the men, in this sense, that they, just as the women, have been called to the inheritance of eternal life, so that they ought to strive for it equally by living piously and holily, and consequently treat their wives honestly according to the law of God, and live together with them harmoniously. The sense returns to the same thing in both cases, and even if we should read συγκληρονόμοι in the nominative, it can still be referred to the wives in the same way, by rendering the text thus: As also they are co-heirs of grace, namely the women. Thus also the Syrian translates: For the reason that they themselves also will be heirs with you. But also regarding the latter words a variety of reading occurs. For some Codices read χάριτος ζωῆς.; the Royal inserts ποικίλης,, in which way Jerome also reads in book 1 against Jovinian, chapter 4, citing this passage thus: As co-heirs of manifold grace, which reading agrees with v. 10. C. 4. of this Epistle, as also with the nature of the thing itself. For the graces are manifold, in which women are partners of men, of which some pertain to the use of common life, others to the heavenly kingdom of God. The Complutensian Codex in place of ζωῆς reads ζώσης,, as co-heirs of living grace, because that grace brings life and salvation. In certain Codices a conjunction is placed between manifold grace and life, so that thus the benefits of grace and glory may be joined, since through the former access is opened to the latter. The common reading is χάριτος ζωῆς.. Moreover, it is called grace of life through a certain species of metonymy, eternal life to be given from grace. The Syrian χάριν explains by τὸ χάρισμα & ἐξηγήσεως, in place of, adds τῆς αἰωνίου.. For thus he rendered the text: for the reason that they themselves also will be heirs with you [consult facsimile image] of the gift of life, which is into eternity.

Ἐις τὸ μὴ ἐκκόπτεσθαι τὼς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν. For ἐκκόπτεσθαι the Complutensian, Royal, and two other Codices read ἐγκόπτεσθαι without a significant variation of sense, for ἐκκόπτειν is to cut out, or to cut off, Matt. 3. v. 10.cap. 5. v. 30. etc. Likewise to cut between, to divert, as ἐκκόπτειν ὕδατος ἀγωγοὺς to cut between or to divert the water conduits, In Herodian book 7 Έγκόπτειν likewise is to cut off, to impede a course and journey, to inhibit. Acts 24 v. 4. Rom. 15 v. 22. Galat. 5 vers. 7. 1. Thessal. 2 v. 18. The Syriac rendered it. And that you may not be [consult facsimile image] stumbling, or even shaken in your prayers.

Latin:

VIRI SIMILITER, COHABITANTES SECUNDUM SCIENTIAM Q. INFIRMIORI VASCULO MULIEBRI IMPARTIENTES HONOREM, TANQUAM & COHAEREDIBUS GRATIAE VITAE, UT NON IMPEDIANTUR ORATIONES VESTRAE.

Connexio. 1. A praeceptis, quae uxoribus praescripta, transitum facit Apostolus ad praecepta maritis tradenda. Hanc connexionem monstrat particula ὁμοίως.

2. Inter coniuges est mutua relatio. 1. Cor. 7. v. 2. Quos ergò indissolubili foedere Deus coniunxit Matth. 19. v. 6. eos in tradendis vitae & morum praeceptis Apostolus seiungere noluit.

Dispositio. Profert Apostolus sex argumenta, quibus maritos hortatur, ut uxores suas humaniter tractent & prudenter cum illis conversentur. Primum petitum est à sexus virilis praerogativa. Viri maiore scientiâ praediti sunt quàm mulieres. Ergò mariti uxoribus secundùm illam scientiam cohabitent.

Alterum à coniugii indissolubilitate. Vir & uxor ex Dei instituto debent cohabitare, utpote indissolubili vinculo coniuncti. Ergò vigeat inter eos concordia, quod fieri nequit, nisi mariti humaniter uxores tractent.

Tertium à foeminei sexus utilitate. Uxores sunt vasa h. e. instrumenta ad usus salutares, videlicet liberorum generationem & educationem, atque ad rei familiaris administrationem apta. Ergò modestè & humaniter à maritis tractentur.

Quartum ab eiusdem sexus infirmitate. Uxores sunt vasa infirma, teneriter ergò ac molliter tractentur, ne duriore tractatione instar vasis infirmi lapidi allisi frangantur.

Quintum ab uxorum Christianarum dignitate. Sunt illae coheredes vitae, ergò mariti convenientem honorem illis tribuant.

Sextum à consequente incommodo. Impediuntur preces per coniugum rixas & iurgia. Ergò mariti non debent uxores duriùs tractare, ne dissidiis & rixis detur occasio.

Expositio textus, Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως. Sicut Paulus Eph. 5. v. 33.

Col. 3. v. 18. & 19.1. Tim. 2. v. 8. & 9. maritorum & uxorum officia coniungit, ita quoque Petrus hoc loco utrisque sua praescribit munia. Paulus 1. Tim. 2. v. 9. per particulam ὡσάυτως, Petrus hoc loco per particulam ὁμοίως officia illa connectit, quam vulgata utrobique reddidit per similiter.

Οἱ ἄνδρες per ἀντίπτωσιν sive Atticismum ponitur pro ὦ ἄνδρες. alloquitur enim Apostolus maritos, ut patet ex fine versiculi, inde Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] Et Vos viri.

Συνοικοῦντες, scil. ἔστε,cohabitatè uxoribus vestris, non alienis. κατὰ γνῶσιν,secundùm scientiam, quâ Naturae beneficio sexum foemineum praecellitis. Ponitur autem nomen pro adverbio, secundùm scientiam, h. e. scienter, prudenter & humaniter.

Ώς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ. Nomen adiectivum γυναικείω notat subiectum, nempe mulierem, quae vasi comparatur. Similis loquendi modus extat 1. Petr. 2. v. 2. & 13. In voce σκεῦος est Hebraismus; quia Hebraei nomine כלי vasis quodvis instrumentum, quo aliquid paratur, consummatur & perficitur, denotant. Alludit igitur Apostolus ad primaevam coniugii institutionem, in qua uxor dicitur viri adiutorium, quod est coram ipso, i. e. quod ad varios usus in rei familiaris administratione ipsi praestò est Gen. 2. v. 18. Vulgata versio reddidit vasculo, sed in Graeco non habetur diminutivum unde Ambrosius lib. de Paradiso cap. 4. simpliciter reddidit vasi. Vocatur autem mulier σκεῦος ἀσθενέστερονvas infirmius, sc. & corpore, & animo, respectu habito ad virum, cui maiorem scientiam ac maius corporis & animi robur Apostolus tribuit.

Ἀπονέμοντες τιμὴν. Vulgata reddit, impartientes, quod quidam exponunt in parte tribuentes, cum soli DEO totaliter sit honor impendendus.

Sed ἀπαιδεύτως haec annotantur, cum de totali vel partiali honore nihil hîc agatur. In Graeco est ἀπονέμοντεςtribuentes vel deferentes honorem, sc. foemineo sexui, praesertim uxoribus convenientem, ne loco ancillarum habeantur, sed ut vitae torique sociae comiter ac humaniter tractentur. Syrus reddidit, tanquam vasa debilia in precio eas habete.

Ώς καὶ συγκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς. Ita legunt quidam Codices, praesertim Regius ac Veronensis, ut subintelligatur ταῖς γυναιξὶ, scil. συνοικοῦντες. Ita quoque legit Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. cap. 4. Sed alii Codices habent nominativum ὡς καὶ συγκληρονόμοι, scilicet ὄντες, ut ad viros referatur, sensu eo, quòd illi aequè ac mulieres vocati sint ad hereditatem vitae aeternae, ut ad eam piè & sanctè vivendo pariter contendere, ac proinde uxores honestè secundùm legem Dei tractare, ac concorditer cum ipsis conversari debeant. Sensus utrobique eodem redit, ac si vel maximè legamus συγκληρονόμοι in nominativo, tamen itidem ad uxores referri potest, textum sic reddendo. Tanquam & coheredes sint gratiae, scil. mulieres. Ita quoque vertit Syrus. Eò quod etiam ipsae vobiscum heredes erunt. Sed & circa posteriora verba occurrit varietas lectionis. Quidam enim Codices legunt χάριτος ζωῆς. Regius inserit ποικίλης, quo modo etiam legit Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinianum cap. 4. locum hunc sic citans. Sicut coheredibus multiplicis gratiae, quae lectio congruit cum v. 10. C. 4. huius Epistolae, uti etiam cum rei ipsius Natura. Multiplices enim sunt gratiae, in quibus mulieres virorum sunt sociae, quarum aliae ad communis vitae usum, aliae ad coeleste Dei regnum pertinent. Complutensis Codex loco ζωῆς legit ζώσης, tanquam coheredibus vivae gratiae, quia gratia illa vitam & salutem affert. In quibusdam Codicibus inter gratiam multiplicem & vitam interponitur copula, ut sic beneficia gratiae & gloriae coniungantur, cum per illa ad haec pateat accessus. Communis lectio est χάριτος ζωῆς. Dicitur autem gratia vitae per speciem quandam metonymiae vita aeterna ex gratia danda. Syrus χάριν exponit per τὸ χάρισμα & ἐξηγήσεως loco, addit τῆς αἰωνίου. Sic enim reddidit textum; eò quod & ipsae vobiscum heredes erunt[consult facsimile image]doni vitae, quae est in aeternum.

Ἐις τὸ μὴ ἐκκόπτεσθαι τὼς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν. Pro ἐκκόπτεσθαι Complutensis, Regius & alii duo Codices legunt ἐγκόπτεσθαι sine insigni sensus variatione, ἐκκόπτειν enim est excidere, vel excindere,Matth. 3. v. 10.cap. 5. v. 30. &c. Item intercidere, intervertere, ut ἐκκόπτειν ὕδατος ἀγωγοὺςintercidere sive intervertere aequae ductus, apud Herodianum lib. 7. Έγκόπτειν itidem est intercidere, cursum & iter impedire, inhibere.Actor. 24. v. 4.Rom. 15. v. 22.Galat. 5. vers. 7.1. Thessal. 2. v. 18. Syrus reddidit. Et ne sitis[consult facsimile image]impingentes, vel etiam labefactati in precibus vestris.

## 3:8
FINALLY, BE YE ALL OF ONE MIND, COMPASSIONATE, LOVERS OF THE BRETHREN, MERCIFUL, MODEST, HUMBLE.

Connection. 1. From this verse 8 begins the latter part of the chapter, which is a general exhortation directed to all Christians in whatever state of life.

2. The Apostle conveniently passes or rather returns from a special exhortation to a general one, so that he may show that with GOD there is no respect of προσωποληψίαν, but in every nation (and in whatever state of life) he that feareth him and worketh righteousness, is acceptable to him, as our Apostle speaks Act. 10. v. 34. & 35. He signifies, therefore, not only spouses, to whom he had hitherto delivered precepts, but also the unmarried, and not only servants, of whom he had treated in chapter 2, but also that children can please God and become heirs of eternal life if they believe in Christ and strive for good works out of faith. Hence Bede comments on this passage thus: Because he was teaching diverse persons, conditions, and sexes with a distinction appropriate to them, now he admonishes all in common to have one heart and one soul in the cause of the Lord's faith.

3. He had spoken about the interior adornment of married women in verse 4; now he adds the spiritual adornment of all the pious. He had shown above how faith and the interior man ought to be affected toward God; now he demonstrates how he ought to be affected toward men.

4. The Apostle had exhorted those to whom he writes to brotherly love and concord chap. 1. v. 22.chap. 2. v. 17.; now, therefore, he summarizes certain things that are most necessary for fostering love and concord.

5 Some think that the Apostle previously addressed wives and mothers separately, but now he is admonishing both spouses of their duty. But the matter itself testifies that the Apostolic exhortation pertains not only to spouses, but in general to all Christians.

Disposition. 1. Lyranus proceeds thus: The Apostle here returns to instructing all in common, ordering them first toward verse 9, secondly toward God verse 15, thirdly toward oneself in the following chapter. The first part is subdivided into two, because first he orders them in the bestowal of good verse 9, secondly in the enduring of evil v. 1.

2. The Apostle exhorts Christians to homiletic virtues, which are parts of the love owed to one's neighbor and contribute to leading a life quietly and tranquilly. The virtues enumerated in this verse can also be ordered according to the series of virtues that are required in the fifth commandment of the Decalogue.

Exposition of the text. Τὸ δὲ τέλος. Some Latin codices very ineptly read, in faith, which reading also occurs in Lyranus, who comments on this passage thus: Faith is taken in one way as it is a Theological virtue, and thus it leads them to the unity of the Church, so that there may be no schisms among them: in another way as it is a moral virtue, and thus faith is the same as fidelity, and in this way it leads them to the unity of mutual fidelity. In the same way they read Bede, Thomas Anglicus, Hugo, Dionysius the Carthusian, Titelmann, John Benedict, etc. But all the Greek codices read τὸ δὲ τέλος But the end i.e. finally, lastly, or at the end, in which way the more correct Latin codices also have it. The Syriac rendered it, [consult facsimile image] at length, finally, from the root [consult facsimile image] he filled, he finished, he perfected.

Πάντες ὁμόφρονες, namely ἔστε This is the first Christian virtue pertaining to charity ὁμοφρόνησις or ὁμόνοια concord, which embraces agreement in the truth of faith and the holiness of life. ὁμόφρονες are called those who τὰ ὅμοια φρονοῦσι, whose heart is one and soul is one Act. 4. v. 32. who are united to one another by the glue of faith and charity, indeed one Gal. 3. v. 28. even if by reason of a diverse calling their external works are not the same. The Syriac rendered it. Be you all [consult facsimile image] in unanimity, consent, and concord. Parallel passages exist Rom. 12. v. 16. τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς ἀλλήλους φρονοῦντες. cap. 15. v. 5. May God give you τὸ αὐτὸ φροεῖν ἐν ἀλλήλοις according to Christ Jesus v. 6. that ὁμοθυμαδὸν with one mouth you may glorify GOD. 1. Cor. 1. v. 10. I beseech you brethren by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing, and there be no schisms among you, but that you be perfect in the same mind and in the same judgment. 2. Cor. 13. vers. 11. τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, εἰρηνέυετε. Eph. 4. v. 3. Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Phil. 2. vers. 2. Fulfill my joy, ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες, σύμψυχοι τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες. Phil. 3. v. 16. τῷ αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν κανόνι, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν. From these parallel passages it is gathered most excellently of all, what kind of unity and agreement of minds Peter requires of Christians in this place, namely that which includes the truth of faith, and has sincere charity joined to it.

Συμπαθεῖς. This is the second virtue, to which the Apostle exhorts, namely συμπάθεια, by which one looks upon the misery of others as one's own, and which one draws into oneself by compassion. The Greeks say, συμπάθεια ἔστι πάθος τινὸς διὰ πάθους ἑτέρου. For just as Paul Rom. 12. v. 15. & 16. τὸ κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων and τὸ αὐτὸ ἐις ἀλλήλους φρονεῖν, Phil. 2. v. 1. κοινωνίαν πνέυματος and σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτειρμοὺς joins together: so also Peter, gladly insisting on the footsteps of his Apostle, associates ὁμοφρόνησιν & συμπάθειαν in an unbroken bond, for where ὁμόνοια, is, there also follows συμπάθεια ὁμόνοια, he makes it so that the pious are members of one mystical body, now indeed when one member suffers, all the members suffer with it, 1. Cor. 12. v. 26. which is properly συμπάθεια, συμπαθεῖς for they are those who are touched by a mutual affection, who are affected by the evils of their neighbor as if they were their own. The Syrian περιφραστικῶς, be grieving with those who grieve. Some prefer to render it, similarly affected, so that it may be referred as much to the good as to the evil of the neighbor, but the Greek is properly used for compassion in evils. Parallel passages exist Rom. 12. v. 15. Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep. 1. Cor. 12. v. 26. If one member suffers anything, all the members suffer with it, or if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice with it. vers. 27. But you are the body of Christ. Hebr. 10. v. 34. You have had compassion on my bonds. cap. 13. v. 3. Remember those in bonds, as if bound with them.

φιλάδελφοι. This is the worn virtue which the Apostle requires from the pious, namely φιλαδελφία, by which one embraces a neighbor, especially a companion of the faith, with brotherly love. The concrete noun φιλάδελφοι the Vulgate rendered, lovers of the brotherhood (that is, of the brothers), just as also cap. 1. vers. 22. φιλαδελφίαν it translates by love of the brotherhood. Some prefer to render it, endowed with brotherhood. But the matter returns to the same thing, for he who loves the brotherhood or the brothers, and holds the companions of the faith as brothers, he is also endowed with brotherly charity. The Syrian did not express the emphasis of the word, for he rendered it simply, loving one another, when nevertheless the Apostle requires some higher degree of charity, by which we ought to embrace the companions of the faith above the rest of men. Parallel passages are Roman. 12. v. 10. τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ εὶς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι. 1. Thessal. 4. v. 9. Concerning φιλαδελφία you have no need that I write to you, for you yourselves are taught by GOD to love one another. Hebr. 13. v. 1. ἡ φιλαδελφία let it remain. 1. Petr. 1. v. 22. Purifying your souls εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον, cap. 2. v. 17. τὴν ἀδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε 2. Petr. 1. v. 7. Minister in piety τὴν φιλαδελφίαν, in φιλαδελφίᾳ τὴν ἀγάπτην.

Ἐσπλαγχνοι. This is the fourth virtue which the Apostle prescribes, as excellent as the former ones, the offspring of charity, namely εὐσπλαγχνία, by which someone is inclined and prone to mercy, from εὐ, which denotes ease in composition, and the noun σπλάγχνα, which denotes bowels, especially the heart, the most excellent of all human bowels. By the name of heart, however, μετονυμικῶς are understood motions of the heart, and principally indeed that heroic motion of the heart, by which one is moved to show mercy. An example of εὐσπλαγχνίας is proposed in parents, especially mothers, who see their children placed in distress. In them, natural affections are so effective that all their bowels are as it were moved. 1. Reg. 3. v. 26. נכמרו רחמיה they grew warm or her bowels were moved (the mother's) for her son, whom the King had ordered to be divided by the sword. By this word רחם he loved vehemently, he had mercy, from which is formed the noun רחם which properly signifies the womb, which cherishes and loves the infant; the Syrian also uses this in this place, rendering the Greek εὐσπλαγχνοι, thus, Be ye [consult facsimile image] merciful, full of bowels, endowed with the affection of uterine mercy, Ierem. 31. v. 20. my bowels have sounded for him, I will surely have mercy upon him. Luth. Mein Hertz bricht mir gegen ihm/Dass ich mich sein erbarmen muss.

Places parallel to this Apostolic exhortation exist Proverb. 12. vers. 10. the righteous man knoweth the souls of his beasts, but the bowels of the wicked are cruel, τὰ σπλάγχνα ἀνελεήμονα. Ephes. 4. vers. 32. Be ye εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοὶ, εὔσπλαγχνοι Phil. 2. v. 1. εἴ τινα σπλάγχνα και οἰκτειρμοὶ, where εὐσπλαγχνία is likewise joined with ὁμοφονήσει. Coloss. 3. vers. 12. Put on σπλαγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν, χρηστότητα, from which places it appears that such mercy is required, which shows itself kind and beneficent in the very work toward one's neighbor. 1. Iohan. 3. v. 17. He that shall have the substance of the world, and shall see his brother in need of it, and shall shut his bowels from him, how doth the charity of GOD abide in him?

Φιλόφρονες. A great variety of reading occurs here. 1. Two Royal Codices, and as many others, read ταπεινόφρονες, humble, in which way the Vulgate also rendered it, modest humble, and Coloss. 3. vers. 12. σπλάγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν & ταπεινοφροσύνη are joined. For mercy toward one's neighbor without true humility inclining and lowering itself to the neighbor's misery has no place, and it is the chief bond of concord, when each one thinks modestly of himself. Gloss. interlin. Of these things do not be proud, doing all things with moderation. 2. The Dionysian Codex, and Gagnaeus following it, read φιλοταπεινόφρονες, lovers of humility. 3. Most Codices read φιλόφρονες, in which way Oecumenius also reads, who nevertheless joins this third reading with the first, either because he reads these two joined in the same Codices, or he found them individually in different ones, and therefore in his exposition he judged that both readings should be joined, for he explains two virtues separately, the one, which the Latin Interpreter calls affability, the other, which he calls humility or modesty of mind. From which, however, Cornelius à Lapide ἀπαιδεὺτως infers, that the Greek text in this place is corrupt. Furthermore φιλόφρονες are called as if τὰ φίλαφρονοῦντες, who are friendly-minded, who study to do those things which are friendly and pleasing to another. Budaeus rendered, who are easy and accommodating to the custom of life, so that it is opposed to σκολιοῖς hard, morose, difficult, and intractable. And because the ease of manners also has the affability of speech joined to it, therefore φιλόφρονες some render, courteous, affable. Acts 28. verse 7. Publius for three days φιλοφρόνως received us into hospitality, showed himself courteous and affable, and exhibited to us all the duties of humanity. 2. Maccab. 2. verse 9. When Heliodorus had come to Jerusalem, φιλοφρόνως he was kindly received by the high Priest. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] meek and humble, for it corresponds to the Greek ταπεινῷ & πρᾴῳ Matt. 11. verse 29. chap. 21. verse 5. 2. Corinth. 7. verse 6. 1. Thessal. 2. verse 7. etc. since these two are joined to each other by a kind of bond, for he who is humble, he is also courteous and meek. Luther renders Freundlich.

Therefore this is the fifth virtue, which the Apostle requires from those who desire to pursue charity, and to lead a tranquil life, namely φιλοφρόννησις, which is the sweetness of manners in common life, courtesy, affability, and humanity. A parallel passage exists Ephes. 4. verse 32. Be one to another χρηστοὶ ἔυσπλαγχνοι, where ἡ χρηστότης τῇ φιλοφρονήσει he answers. Col. 3. v. 12. Put on σπλάγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν, χρηστότητα, ταπεινοφροσύνττιυ, πρᾳότητα, μακροθυμίαν, which are all the virtues comprehended by Peter under the name φιλοφρονήσεως.

Latin:

IN FINE AUTEM OMNES UNANIMES, COMPATIENTES, FRATERNITATIS AMATORES, MISERICORDES, MODESTI, HUMILES.

Connexio. 1. Ab hoc versu 8. incipit posterior pars capitis, quae est exhortatio generalis ad omnes Christianos in quovis vitae statu directa.

2. Convenienter autem transit vel potius redit Apostolus à speciali exhortatione ad generalem, ut ostendat, apud DEUM non habere unumπροσωποληψίαν,sed in omni gente (& in quovis vitae statu) qui timet eum & operatur iustitiam, esse illi gratum & acceptum, ut noster Apostolus loquitur Act. 10. v. 34. & 35. Significat ergò, non solùm coniuges, quibus hactenus praecepta tradiderat, sed etiam caelibes, nec solùm servos, de quibus in cap. 2. egerat, sed etiam liberos Deo placere, & vitae aeternae heredes fieri posse, si in Christum credant, & ex fide bonis operibus studeant. Inde Beda in h. l. sic commentatur. Quia superiùs diversas personas, conditiones & sexus congruâ sibi discretione docebat, iam nunc omnes communiter admonet, in fidei Dominicae causâ unum cor & unam habere animam.

3. Dixerat de interiore ornatu maritarum vers. 4. iam subiungit spiritualem ornatum omnium piorum. Ostenderat superiùs, quomodo fides & interior homo erga DEUM debeat esse affectus, iam demonstrat, quomodo erga homines affectus esse debeat.

4. Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus eos, ad quos scribit, ad fraternam caritatem & concordiam cap. 1. v. 22.cap. 2. v. 17. iam ergò summatim quaedam recenset, quae maximè ad fovendam caritatem & concordiam necessaria.

5 Quidam existimant, Apostalum priùs seorsim uxores & matrios compellasse, iam vero utrumque coniugem officii sui admonere. Sed res ipsa testatur, exhortationem Apostolicam non solùm ad coniuges, sed in genere ad omnes. Christianos pertinere.

Dispositio. 1. Lyranus sic progreditur. Apostolus hîc revertitur ad informandum omnes communiter, ordinando primò eos ad vers. 9. secundò ad Deum vers. 15. tertiò ad seipsum cap. seq. Prima pars subdividitur in duas, quia primò ordinat eos in collatione boni vers. 9. secundò in perpessione mali v. 1.

2. Hortatur Apostolus Christianos ad virtutes homileticas, quae sunt partes caritatis proximo debitae, & faciunt ad vitam quietè & tranquillè traducendam. Possunt etiam virtutes in hoc versiculo enumeratae iuxta seriem virtutum, quae in quinto Decalogi praecepto requiruntur, ordinari.

Textus expositio. Τὸ δὲ τέλος. Quidam Codd. Latini ineptissimè legunt, in fide, quae lectio etiam apud Lyranum occurrit, qui in h. l. sic commentatur. Fides accipitur uno modo, ut est virtus Theologica, & sic inducit eos ad unitatem Ecclesiae, ut non sint inter eos schismata: alio modo ut est virtus moralis, alis, & sic fides est idem quod fidelitas, & hoc modo inducit eos ad unitatem fidelitatis mutuae. Eodem modo legunt Beda, Thomas Anglicus, Hugo, Dionysius Carthusianus, Titelmannus, Ioh. Benedictus &c. Sed Graeci Codd. omnes legunt τὸ δὲ τέλοςFinis autem i. e. denique, postremò, sive in fine, quo modo etiam Codices Latini correctiores habent. Syrus reddidit, [consult facsimile image]tandem, finaliter, à rad. [consult facsimile image]implevit, finivit, perfecit.

Πάντες ὁμόφρονες, scil. ἔστε Prima haec est virtus Christiana ad caritatem pertinens ὁμοφρόνησις vel ὁμόνοια concordia, quae complectitur consensionem in fidei veritate & vitae sanctitate. ὁμόφρονες dicuntur, qui τὰ ὅμοια φρονοῦσι, quorum est corunum & anima una Act. 4. v. 32. qui fidei & caritatis glutine invicem sunt uniti, imò unus Gal. 3. v. 28. etiamsi pro ratione diversae vocationis opera eorum externa non sint eadem. Syrus reddidit. Sitis omnes[consult facsimile image]in unanimitate, consensu & concordia. Loca parallela extant Rom. 12. v. 16.τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς ἀλλήλους φρονοῦντες.cap. 15. v. 5.Deus det vobisτὸ αὐτὸ φροεῖν ἐν ἀλλήλοιςsecundùm Christum Iesumv. 6. ut ὁμοθυμαδὸν uno ore glorificetis DEUM. 1. Cor. 1. v. 10.Obsecro vos fratres per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut idipsum dicatis omnes, & non sint in vobis schismata, sitis autem perfecti eâdem mente & eadem sententiâ.2. Cor. 13. vers. 11.τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, εἰρηνέυετε.Eph. 4. v. 3.Soliciti estote servare unitatem Spiritus in vinculo pacis.Phil. 2. vers. 2.Implete gaudium meum,ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖτε, τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες, σύμψυχοι τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες.Phil. 3. v. 16.τῷ αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν κανόνι, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν. Ex his locis parallelis omnium optimè colligitur, qualem unitatem & animorum consensionem Petrus hoc loco à Christianis requirat, eam scil. quae fidei veritatem includit, & sinceram caritatem coniunctam habet.

Συμπαθεῖς. Haec est altera virtus, ad quam Apostolus hortatur, videl. συμπάθεια, quâ aliorum miseriam quis aspicit ut suam, eamque compassione in se quem trahit. Graeci dicunt, συμπάθεια ἔστι πάθος τινὸς διὰ πάθους ἑτέρου. Ut enim Paulus Rom. 12. v. 15. & 16.τὸ κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων ac τὸ αὐτὸ ἐις ἀλλήλους φρονεῖν,Phil. 2. v. 1.κοινωνίαν πνέυματος ac σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτειρμοὺς coniungit: ita quoque Petrus, Co Apostoli sui vestigiis libenter insistens, ὁμοφρόνησιν & συμπάθειαν indivulso nexu còsociat, ubi enim ὁμόνοια, ibi quoque sequitur συμπάθεια ὁμόνοια facit, ut pii sint unius corporis mystici membra, iam vero quando membrum unum patitur, compatiuntur omnia membra, 1. Cor. 12. v. 26. quod propriè est συμπάθεια, συμπαθεῖς enim sunt, qui muto tanguntur affectu, qui proximi malis afficiuntur ut suis. Syrus περιφραστικῶς,sitis dolentes cum iis, qui dolent. Quidam malunt reddere, similiter affecti, ut tàm ad bona, quàm ad mala proximi referatur, sed Graecum de compassione in malis propriè usurpatur. Loca parallela extant Rom. 12. v. 15.Gaudete cum gaudentibus, flete cum flentibus.1. Cor. 12. v. 26.Si quid patitur unum membrum, compatiuntur omnia membra, sive gloriatur unum membrum, congaudent omnia membra.vers. 27.Vos autem estis corpus Christi.Hebr. 10. v. 34.Vinculis meis compassi estis.cap. 13. v. 3.Mementote vinctorum, tanquam simul vincti.

φιλάδελφοι. Terita haec est virtus, quam Apostolus à piis requirit, videl. φιλαδελφία, quâ quis fraterno amore proximum, fidei praesertim socium, complectitur. Nomen concretum φιλάδελφοι vulgata reddidit, fraternitatis (h. e. fratrum) amatores, sicut etiam cap. 1. vers. 22.φιλαδελφίαν per fraternitatis amorem vertit. Quidam reddere malunt, fraternitate praediti. Sed res eôdem redit, qui enim fraternitatem sive fratres amat, ac fidei socios pro fratribus habet, is etiam fraternâ caritate praeditus est. Syrus emphasin vocis non expressit, simpliciter enim reddidit, amantes unus alium, cum tamen Apostolus superiorem aliquem caritatis gradum requirat, quo fidei socios prae reliquis hominibus complecti debemus. Loca parallela sunt Roman. 12. v. 10.τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ εὶς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι.1. Thessal. 4. v. 9. De φιλαδελφίαnon necesse habetis vobis scribere, ipsi enim à DEO edocti estis, vos diligere invicem.Hebr. 13. v. 1.ἡ φιλαδελφίαmaneat.1. Petr. 1. v. 22.Animas vestras castificantesεἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον,cap. 2. v. 17.τὴν ἀδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε2. Petr. 1. v. 7.Ministrate in pietateτὴν φιλαδελφίαν, in φιλαδελφίᾳ τὴν ἀγάπτην.

Ἐσπλαγχνοι. Haec est quarta virtus, quam Apostolus praescribit, praeclara aequè ac priores, caritatis soboles, videlicet εὐσπλαγχνία, quâ quis ad misericordiam propensus est ac pronus, ab εὐ, quod in compositione facilitatem notat, & nomine σπλάγχνα, quod viscera notat, praesertim cor omnium humanorum viscerum praestantissimum. Cordis autem nomine μετονυμικῶς intelliguntur motus cordis, ac principaliter quidem heroicus ille motus cordis, quo ad miserendum commovetur. Exemplum εὐσπλαγχνίας proponitur in parentibus, praesertim matribus, quae liberos suos in angustiis vident constitutos. In illis storgae naturales tàm efficaces sunt, ut omnia ipsorum viscera quasi commoveantur. 1. Reg. 3. v. 26.נכמרו רחמיהincaluerunt sive commota sunt viscera eius (matris) super filio suo, quem Rex iusserat gladio dividi. Hac voce רחם vehementer dilexit, misertus est, ex quâ formatur nomen רחם quae propriè significat matricem, quae infantem fovet & diligit, utitur etiam Syrus hoc loco, Graecum εὐσπλαγχνοι, sic reddens, Estote[consult facsimile image]misericordes, viscerosi, uterinae misericordiae affectu praediti,Ierem. 31. v. 20.sonuerunt viscera mea propter eum, miserendo miserebor eius. Luth. Mein Hertz bricht mir gegen ihm/Dass ich mich sein erbarmen muss.

Loca huic exhortationi Apostolicae parallela extant Proverb. 12. vers. 10.novit iustus iumentorum suorum animas, viscera autem impiorum crudelia,τὰ σπλάγχνα ἀνελεήμονα.Ephes. 4. vers. 32.Estoteεἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοὶ, εὔσπλαγχνοιPhil. 2. v. 1.εἴ τινα σπλάγχνα και οἰκτειρμοὶ, ubi εὐσπλαγχνία cum ὁμοφονήσει itidem coniungitur. Coloss. 3. vers. 12.Induiteσπλαγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν, χρηστότητα, ex quibus locis apparet, eiusmodi miseri cordiam requiri, quae benignam & beneficam ipso opere erga proximum sese praestet. 1. Iohan. 3. v. 17.Qui habuerit substantiam mundi, & viderit fratrem suum eâ indigere, & clauserit viscera sua ab eo, quomodo caritas DEI manet in eo?

Φιλόφρονες. Magna hîc occurrit lectionis varietas. 1. Duo Codices Regii, aliique totidem legunt ταπεινόφρονες,humiles, quo modo etiam Vulgata reddidit, modesti humiles, ac Coloss. 3. vers. 12.σπλάγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν & ταπεινοφροσύνη coniunguntur. Misericordia enim erga proximum absque vera humilitate ad proximi miseriam sese inclinante ac demittente non habet locum, ac praecipuum concordiae vinculum est, cum de se modestè quisque sentit. Gloss. interlin. De his ne superbiatis, omnia cum modo facientes. 2. Codex Dionysianus, eumque secutus Gagnaeus legunt φιλοταπεινόφρονες,amantes humilitatis. 3. Plerique Codices legunt φιλόφρονες, quo modo etiam legit Oecumenius, qui tamen hanc tertiam lectionem cum prima coniungit, vel quia haec duo coniuncta in iisdem Codicibus legit, vel singula in diversis invenit, ac proinde in expositione utramque lectionem coniungendam censuit, exponit enim duas separatim virtutes, alteram, quam Latinus Interpres vocat affabilitatem, alteram, quam humilitatem sive animi modestiam vocat. Ex quo tamen Cornelius à Lapide ἀπαιδεὺτως infert, textum Graecum hoc loco esse corruptum. Caeterùm φιλόφρονες dicuntur quasi τὰ φίλαφρονοῦντες, qui sapiunt amica, qui student facere ea, quae alteri amica sunt & grata. Budaeus reddidit, qui ad vitae consuetudinem sunt faciles atque commodi, ut opponatur σκολιοῖςduris, morosis, difficilibus & intractabilibus. Et quia morum facilitas etiam sermonis comitatem coniunctam habet, ideò φιλόφρονες quidam reddunt, comes, affabiles.Actor. 28. vers. 7.Publius per triduumφιλοφρόνωςnos hospitio excepit, comem & affabilem sese praebuit, ac omnia humanitatis officia nobis exhibuit.2. Maccab. 2. vers. 9.Heliodorus cum venisset Hierosolymam,φιλοφρόνωςbenignè à summo Sacerdote fuit exceptus. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]mansueti & humiles, respondet enim Graecorum ταπεινῷ & πρᾴῳMatth. 11. vers. 29.cap. 21. vers. 5.2. Corinth. 7. vers. 6.1. Thessal. 2. vers. 7. &c. cum haec duo fororio quisi vinculo sint invicem coniuncta, qui enim humilis est, ille etiam comis est & mansuetus. Lutherus reddit Freundlich.

Quinta ergò haec est virtus, quam Apostolus requirit ab iis, qui caritatem sectari, & vitam tranquillam ducere cupiunt, videl. φιλοφρόννησις, quae est suavitas morum in vita communi, comitas, affabilitas, & humanitas. Locus parallelus extat Ephes. 4. vers. 32.Estote invicemχρηστοὶ ἔυσπλαγχνοι, ubi ἡ χρηστότης τῇ φιλοφρονήσει respondet. Col. 3. v. 12.Induiteσπλάγχνα οἰκτειρμῶν, χρηστότητα, ταπεινοφροσύνττιυ, πρᾳότητα, μακροθυμίαν, quae virtutes omnes nomine φιλοφρονήσεως à Petro comprehenduntur.

## 3:8-14 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. Why does the Apostle repeat the commandment so often φιλαδελφίας and of related virtuesv. 8.? Resp. 1. To show that love is the sum of the whole law,Matth. 22. v. 39.Rom. 13. v. 8. and a brief compendium of all the duties which we owe to our neighbor. Jerome, book 3, on the Epistle to the Galatians, chapter 6. Blessed John the Evangelist, when he was staying at Ephesus until extreme old age, and could scarcely be carried to the church between the hands of his disciples, and could not weave his voice into many words, was accustomed to utter nothing else at each gathering except this: Little children, love one another. At length the disciples and brothers who were present, affected with weariness because the same things were always being heard, said: Master, why do you always say this? He replied with a sentiment worthy of John: Because it is the commandment of the Lord, and if it alone is done, it suffices. 2. To accuse the sluggishness of our flesh, which needs more frequent stimuli to expend love upon our neighbor. 3. To show that he is a genuine disciple of Christ, because Christ likewise perpetually inculcated the commandment of love to his Apostles, and commended this warning to them as if by a Testament. Ioh. 13. v. 34.

Q. 2. Is it rightly added in certain Latin Codices, after the word unanimes, be in prayer v. 8.? The Roman Church indeed reads it so in the Office of the Mass for the 5th Sunday after Pentecost, thus beginning the Epistle reading: All be unanimous in prayer. So also Albinus reads in Epistle 1, Vitriacus in sermon 2 on the 5th Sunday after Pentecost, as also Hugo in his commentary, who refers this προσδιορισμὸν to the following noun, compassionate. And yet 1. The Greek text reads simply ὁμόφρονες, συμπαθεῖς. 2. Nor does the Syriac paraphrase have this addition. 3. Nor do the more correct Latin Codices. 4. Lyranus, the Carthusian, and almost all more recent interpreters reject it from the text. 5. Peter wishes the pious to be consenting not only in prayer, but also in faith and all honest things. He who collected the Ecclesiastical office added that ὲξηγήσεως of his own accord, because that is most fitting for the faithful gathered into an Ecclesiastical assembly, which others afterwards inserted into the text of Scripture.

Q. 3. Why does the Apostle in v. 9. to a double negative commandment or ἀποτροπῇ, that evil is not to be rendered for evil, nor reviling for reviling, oppose only a single affirmative commandment, or a single ἀροτροπὴν when he says, τουναντίον δὲ εὐλογοῦντες? Resp. By the name εὐλογίας συνεκδοχικῶς he also includes εὑποΐιαν or εὐεργεσίαν, because we ought not only to pray well for our neighbor with words, but also to do good to him in reality. For thus this commandment The Apostolic [teaching] is explained in the parallel passage Matth. 5. v. 44. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who slander and persecute you.

Q. 4. What is the connection of the Apostolic argument in v. 9. Knowing that you were called to this, that you might possess a blessing as an inheritance. Resp. 1. The pious, when harmed by a neighbor, ought to call to mind that GOD did not pour out His curse upon them, even though they had deserved it just as much as other men, but rather blessed them with every heavenly blessing Eph. 1. vers. 4. by which very thing they recognize themselves to be warned not to return curses to those who are worthy of a curse, but rather to pray for eternal happiness for them from the heart. 2. The pious cherish a certain hope that it will come to pass that on the day of judgment they will one day hear from Christ, Come, you blessed of my Father, possess by right of inheritance the kingdom prepared for you &c. Matth. 25. v. 34. for they know that they have been called by grace so that they might possess that blessing as an inheritance, therefore they show themselves to be children of blessing and worthy of this blessing, by blessing the neighbor even him by whom they were affected with injury. 3. The pious know clearly that if they desire to attain at some time the blessing, which consists in the possession of heavenly goods, to which they have been divinely called by grace, they are bound to bless their neighbors also, praying to God with earnest groans that they too, having been converted from sin, may aspire together with them to the inheritance of that heavenly blessing. 4. Unless we forgive our neighbor, neither does GOD forgive us Matth. 6. v. 15. Those who repay insults with insults, evils with evils, do not forgive their neighbor. Therefore neither does God forgive them. But those to whom God does not forgive sins cannot attain the inheritance of blessing, consequently those who desire to inherit the blessing forgive their neighbor and bless him.

Q. 5. Whether the Greek text in v. 10. is corrupt? Piscator determines it so in this place, writing thus. The Greek of the Psalm has. τίς ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὁ θέλων ζωὴν, ἀγαπῶν ἡμέρας ἰδεῖν ἀγαθὰς. From the collation of which words it seems that it should be read in Peter in this way. ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν, ἀγαπῶν ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς, for which, from an unobserved asyndeton, it seems some sciolist has substituted these things. ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾷν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς, namely by changing ἀγαπῶν in ὰγαπᾷν, and thus by creating a pleonasm that is less convenient. But no necessity compels us to acknowledge a corruption of the text here. For we have warned above that it is a Hebrew phrase. He who wishes to love life, i. e. he who is seriously held by the desire and love of life. Peter used a certain διαιρέσει and transposition of words, as appears from a collation of the Hebrew text, but nothing at all is lost from the sense.

Q. 6. Whether it is a matter of peace with one's neighbor alone in verse 11.? Scripture commends a triple peace to us. 1. Peace with GOD. 2. Peace of conscience or with our own heart. 3. Peace with one's neighbor. Therefore some take the Davidic and Apostolic saying concerning all these species of peace, so that it is a general admonition, that everyone ought to pursue peace with GOD, peace with himself, and peace with one's neighbor, because peace with one's neighbor, if it ought to be true and stable, must arise from peace with GOD. For just as we ought to love our neighbor in GOD, and for the sake of GOD, and under GOD: so also in GOD, for the sake of GOD, and under GOD, we ought to live peaceably with our neighbor. Even infidels and the unregenerate can pursue peace with one's neighbor, but peace with GOD and peace of conscience is the interior and proper possession of Christians, who also alone will eventually arrive at that which alone is true peace in heaven. But the circumstances of the text show that it is directly and principally a matter here of exterior peace with one's neighbor: yet in an accommodative sense this saying can be extended also to interior peace with GOD.

Q. 7. In what sense τὸ to decline from evil, and to do good are joined with the pursuit of peace and concord in v. 11.? John Huss brings forward such a connection. Let him decline from evil, because it is the expeller of peace; let him do good, through the disposition of its subject; let him seek peace through the manifestation of its action; let him pursue it through the continuation of time. If we take the first member specifically concerning evil and good with respect to one's neighbor, that we ought not to render evil for evil, but rather good for evil, the connection is manifest. For to render evil for evil is not a means of preserving or recovering peace, but to render good for evil is. But if we truly take the first member generally concerning any evil prohibited in the divine law, and concerning any good prescribed in the same, it must be said that the Apostle insinuates by this connection, that the pursuit of peace without obedience toward the remaining precepts of the Decalogue cannot long subsist, since virtues are connected to one another, and are as it were one copulative.

Q. 8. Why in the exhortation to patience does the Apostle make mention of the face of the Lord, i. e. of the divine wrathv. 12.? Resp. 1. To show that GOD will be the avenger of injuries inflicted upon the pious without merit, who will not perpetually suffer the wicked and persecutors to run riot according to their own lust. 2. To forewarn what will happen if they wish to repay evil with evil and avenge themselves, namely that they will have GOD against them. 3. To teach that divine providence extends itself not only to the good, but also to the wicked.

Q. 9. What is understood by the eyes and ears of the Lordvers. 12.? Clement of Alexandria in his commentary explains it as the multiform observation of the Holy Spirit. Basil in Psalm. 33. as the Angels, of whom some as eyes have undertaken the care of watching over us, others of receiving our prayers. But from the antithesis of the face of the Lord, and from the comparison of other places of Scripture, it is gathered that by the eyes of GOD his fatherly favor is understood, and by the ears the readiness to hear ἀνθρωποπαθῶς. For those whom we love, we direct our eyes toward them, and we receive their speech with ready ears. 1. Reg. 8. v. 9.2. Paral. 6. vers. 20.Neh. 1. v. 6.Psal. 33. v. 18.Prov. 15. v. 3.Ierem. 5. v. 3. &c.

Q. 10. In what sense does the Apostle sayv. 13. Who is it who may harm you, if you have been emulators of the good? Resp. 1. Some take it concerning the power of harming. There is no one who can harm you, i. e. inflict true harm, if you pursue with the greatest zeal what is good in the eyes of the Lord, because for the pious all things work together for good,Rom. 8. v. 28. and whatever external evils befall them, it profits them for the progress of the inner man, and the salvation of the soul. 2. But some concerning the will to harm. There is no one who would wish to harm you, if you pursue the good, because we see it happen for the most part in practice, that those who, having been affected by injury, bless, guard their tongue from evil, strive to do good to all, and pursue peace, soothe the minds of their enemies, and reconcile the same to themselves, and by this reason are less exposed to the injuries of the wicked. Both explanations can be joined without any absurdity.

Q. 11. In what respect are the pious, even if they suffer, nonetheless blessed Are they to be calledv. 14.? Resp. 1. because in miseries they rejoice with a good conscience, since they know that they do not suffer as evildoers, but as Christians. 2. because by faith they await liberation, or at least the mitigation of calamities. 3. because God knows how to compensate for the adversities of this life with various goods. 4. because the promise concerning the heavenly inheritance remains for them valid and firm. They are therefore blessed not only with respect to hope, but also with respect to the thing itself.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Finally, however, be all of one mind v. 8. And yet the Apostle proposes still more precepts in what follows. Resp. 1. some have rendered it, in sum, because love is τέλος or τελείωσις, the fulfillment & consummation of the law, or as the Apostle speaks, ἀνακεφαλαίωσις Rom. 13. v. 9. 2. The Apostle concludes the preceding treatment with this little word τελικῇ, showing that then at last not only subjects & servants, wives & husbands, but also all Christians in general will rightly perform their duty, if they have ὁμόνοιαν, συμπάθειαν, φιλαδελφίαν and related virtues most highly commended to themselves.

2. Not rendering evil for evil.v. 9. And yet Lev. 24. vers. 19.If a man shall give a blemish to his neighbor, as he has done, so let it be done to him.v. 20.breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, according to what he shall have given a blemish to a man, so shall it be given to him. Similar things occur Exod. 21. v. 24.Deut. 19. v. 21. Resp. the divine law deals with public vengeance, which God exercises through the Magistrate. The Apostle speaks of private vengeance, which Moses likewise prohibits. Levit. 19. v. 18.Do not seek vengeance, nor be mindful of the injury of your citizens. LXX. Let not your hand take vengeance. Conversely, not only Moses, but also Paul establishes the public vengeance of the Magistrate. Rom. 13. v. 4.The Magistrate is God's avenger for wrath to him who does evil; which our Apostle repeats 1. Epist. 2. v. 14.

3. He who wishes to love life, & to see good days &c. let him turn away from evil, & do good.v. 10. & 11.And yet the pious often experience the contrary, they do good, but evils are inflicted upon them.Iob. 21. v. 7.Psal. 73. vers. 13. & seqq. Ierem. 12. v. 1.Habac. 1. v. 3. Resp. 1. good days in this age, & blessed life in the future are joined together. But if even in the greatest degree good days do not fall to them in this age, most certainly, however, in the future age a blessed life will fall to them.
