Promises concerning the rewards of piety in this life are to be understood with the exception of the cross & divine εὐδοκὶας. The principal rewards are deferred to the future life. 2. The pious in the cross sustain themselves with the promise of divine help, they rely on the testimony of a good conscience, and they are certain that all things work together for their good. Therefore, they can be tranquil in the midst of waves or tempests.

4. He who wishes to see good days, let him restrain his tongue.vers. 10. But Isa. 6. v. 5.Woe to me, because I have been silent. Resp. 1. The Psalmist, and Peter from him, do not say simply and absolutely, let him restrain his tongue, but they add προσδιορισμὸν from evil, and his lips, that they speak no guile. 2. A time to speak, and a time to keep silence.Eccl. 3. v. 7. and one sins not only by speaking, but also by keeping silent, when, namely, the glory of God and the salvation of one's neighbor require a confession. 1. Cor. 9. v. 16.Woe to me, if I do not preach the Gospel.Psal. 57. v. 2.Do you indeed speak justice, you mutes? 3. In the Hebrew it is נדמיתי in the Niphal, which signifies, I have been reduced to silence, I have perished, I have been cut off,Zeph. 1. v. 11.Obad. 1. v. 7. in which way Luther also rendered it. Ich vergehe.

5. Let him turn away from evil, and do goodv. 11.But it is said of Jobchap. 1. v. 1.That man was perfect, and upright, and fearing GOD, and he withdrew from evil. Therefore he first did good, and only afterwards turned away from evil. Resp. 1. Man is considered either in the act of conversion, or in the state after conversion. In the act of conversion, it is required that he first turn away from evil through the recognition and detestation of sin, before he can do good through the gracious indwelling of the Holy Spirit; it is required that he first turn away from the path of iniquity, before he can insist upon the path of the divine commandments. But in the state after conversion, he first does good through the vivification of the Spirit, before he turns away from evil through the mortification of the flesh. 2. Τὸ to do good is understood either of the interior love and zeal for the good, which precedes the turning away from evil: or of the exterior exercise of good works, which follows the turning away from evil. Origen in chapter 2 of Romans says of Job, although others are accustomed to begin almost from abstinence from evil, and to mix certain evils in the exercise of good things, yet Job was exceptional in this part, because while doing good things he simultaneously abstained from every evil.

6. The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteousv. 12.ButAmos 9. v. 4.I will set my eyes upon them for evil, and not for good. Resp. are attributed to GOD paternal and kind eyes, which God places upon the righteous for good. Jer. 24. v. 6. I will set my eye upon them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. There are also attributed to Him angry eyes, which He places upon the wicked for evil. The same judgment holds for the face of the Lord, which is likewise taken for good and evil, from the fact that Amos 9. v. 4. it is said, I will set my eyes upon them for evil, that Jer. 44. v. 11. is rendered thus. Behold I will set my face against you for evil.

7. And who is he that will harm you, if you be followers of that which is good? v. 13. But 2. Tim. 3. v. 12. All that will live godly in Christ Jesus, shall suffer persecution. Resp. 1. Peter speaks primarily of the state of Christians outside the times of persecution on account of the confession of faith. Paul speaks of the time when persecution is stirred up on account of the profession of religion. 2. Peter looks to this, that the pious by their innocence and patience can bend the minds of the wicked, by whom they are harmed, toward moderation, and reconcile them to themselves, so that they may desist from inflicting injuries without merit.

8. And who is he that will harm you, if you be followers of that which is good? v. 13. And yet the pious are often afflicted by the wicked, even if they strive as much as possible to appease them with benefits and compliance. Resp. 1. If the words of the Apostle are taken concerning the power of harming, it is manifest that the wicked cannot inflict any harm upon the souls of the pious. For although they inflict many evils upon them, they can in no way subvert their salvation, but rather they promote it. 2. If they are taken concerning the will to harm, they must be explained concerning that which happens for the most part. For we see that it happens for the most part and commonly, that those who strive for beneficence and innocence soften the minds of their enemies. 3. But because the contrary sometimes happens, therefore Peter, as if by a certain correction, adds, But and if you suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are you.

9. And who is he that will harm you, if you be followers of that which is good? v. 13. And yet the wicked harm both themselves and others by their example. Resp. The Apostle does not simply deny that those harmful men do harm, but he denies that they harm the pious, upon whom they inflict persecution, because, namely, they can neither kill their soul, nor inflict any harm upon them.

10. And be not afraid of their terror vers. 14. And yet it is said of Joseph, hearing that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither. Matt. 2. vers. 22. Resp. 1. In the pious there is not always the equal strength of the Spirit, but sometimes they tremble in adversity out of the infirmity of the flesh. 2. It is not simply forbidden to fear enemies and persecutors, but to fear in such a way that trust in God and the confession of the truth are cast aside on that account, and thus to fear persecutors more than GOD himself. Matth. 10. vers. 28. Do not fear those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul; μᾶλλον δὲ φοβηθῆτε, but rather or more fear him, who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

II. Do not be troubled. But Christ says of himself. Iohan. 12. vers. 27. My soul is troubled. Resp. Peter speaks of such a perturbation, with which diffidence and ἀταξία, affections are joined, such as has no place in Christ. Iohan. 11. v. 33. it is said of Christ, ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτὸν, from which the pious ancients gather, that Christ was not troubled in that way in which we are accustomed to be troubled in sudden terrors, namely, against our opinion and will, but that he himself willingly took up that affection, when and where he wished, yet without any ἀταξίᾳ καὶ ἀνομὶᾳ. Aug. tract. 49. in Ioh. You are troubled against your will, Christ was troubled because he willed it, it was in his power to be affected thus or so, or not to be affected. Confer. Damascen. lib. 3. Orthod. fid. cap. 23.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Peter requires that all be συμπαθεῖς φιλάδελφοι, ἔυσπλαγχνοι. vers. 8. He therefore condemns the Stoic ἀπάθειαν, such as is observed in certain Monks, who cast off filial affection toward parents and brotherly affection toward blood relatives, perpetually having that of Jerome in their mouth. Walk over your trampled father, in this kind of thing the only piety is to be cruel. Confer. Luth. in h. l.

2. Peter seriously requires that no one return evil for evil, nor insult for insult, but on the contrary, that we bless. v. 9. It is therefore erroneous what the Scholastics dispute, that to love enemies is a counsel. Certainly Christ Matth. 5. vers. 44. commands to love enemies for this reason, that we may be sons of the heavenly Father i. e. that we may demonstrate ourselves to be genuine sons of GOD. Therefore he who does not love an enemy is not a genuine son of the heavenly Father.

3. Peter calls eternal life an inheritance. It is therefore false what the Papists teach, that it is given out of merit, because an inheritance is given by right of sonship, but not on account of the merits of works.

4. Peter requires, that he who wishes to love life and see good days should turn away from evil and do good. It is therefore erroneous that some deny that good works are necessary for the reborn. Change your life, if you wish to receive life. Pursue good in the days of your life, if you seek to see good days.

5. Peter teaches, that the eyes of the Lord are open upon the just, and his ears unto their prayers, but the face of the Lord is upon those who do evil. Most gravely, therefore, do they err who deny divine providence. Erasmus in Symb. catech. 2. They err more shamefully who deny providence than those who deny God himself, just as you would more lightly be indignant at one who thought you were not born, than at one who believed you did not have senses or a human mind.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lorinus on verse 9 annotates thus. This blessing does not consist only in this, that we pray well, which we can do inwardly in our soul, and indeed ought to do, insofar as it is permitted to exclude no one from common prayer, but also and indeed properly in benevolent words. This second is not always so necessary, and it can happen that the adversary rather despises and is more indignant. Resp. 1. Christ Matth. 5. vers. 44. joins these in an inseparable bond. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you. Therefore εὐλογία is equally necessary as the love of an enemy. 2. Peter opposes this εὐλογίαν to ἀντιλοιδορίᾳ, by which insults are repelled with insults. Certainly, therefore, the obligation of this affirmative precept is equal to that of the negative precept. 3. To εὐλογὶαν it also pertains that we pray for our enemies, as Christ teaches, Matth. 5. v. 44. and yet, by Lorinus's own admission, it is permitted to exclude no one from common prayer. 4. It is by accident that benevolent words nourish contempt among enemies and increase indignation. For the most part, by a soft answer, the anger of another is accustomed to be broken Prov. 15. v. 1. and the adversary is provoked to praise God and his doctrine, grace, goodness, etc., and at the same time is persuaded that there is another life better than this one. For unless he hoped for that one, he would not so easily bear the injuries which others value highly; no one is able to perform a thing so difficult without the grace of almighty God; God must be judged good, for whose sake one might bless even an adversary, as Lorinus rightly annotates in the same place. Greater account must be taken of these salutary consequences than of that accidental effect.

2. From the fact that we are forbidden to render evil for evil, the Anabaptists and Photinians gather that the right of the sword over criminals does not belong to the magistrate. Response: The Apostle is speaking about private persons and private vengeance. The magistrate exercises vengeance against evildoers, not out of a desire for vengeance, but out of a zeal for justice.

3. Estius on verse 10 annotates thus: What David can be seen to have said according to the letter concerning longevity and temporal happiness, which the O.T. promised to those keeping the law, that is transferred or rather extended by Peter according to the spiritual sense to the happiness of eternal life, which the N.T. promises, which sense was also and indeed principally intended by the Holy Spirit, and also by David himself as a son of the N.T. Response: Not only the New, but also the Old Testament contains the promise of eternal life, though for a different reason. The Old Testament promises eternal life under the condition of perfect obedience to be rendered to the divine law: the New, however, promises eternal life to be given freely to those believing in Christ.

4. From the fact that Peter says, he who wishes to love life, and to see good days, let him turn away from evil and do good, the Papists attempt to prove that eternal life is given from the merit of good works. Response: This is a description of the subject, what kind of people those ought to be who strive for the proposed prize of eternal life, but not a description of the meritorious cause for which eternal life is given.

5. From the fact that eyes, ears, face, etc. are attributed to God, the Audaeans gathered that God is corporeal. Epiph. heresy 70. Tripart. book 10. chapter 7. Against whom the pious ancients rightly urged: 1. If these were to be taken properly, a monstrous figure of a body would have to be attributed to God, because seven eyes are ascribed to him Zach. 3. vers. 9. 2. GOD not only receives into himself a likeness from human members, but sometimes also from birds, sometimes from senseless things, certain dissimilar likenesses are drawn. Gregory, book 32. moral. chapter 4. Wings are attributed to him Psal. 17. vers. 8. he is compared to a lion, a bear. 3. Everything corporeal is composite, but GOD is most simple, and therefore is a Spirit Ioh. 4. v. 24. Therefore ανθρωποπαθῶς, συμβολικῶς & κατὰ συγκατάβασιν these things are said, which are to be understood θεοπρεπῶς & κατὰ ἀναφορὰν. Chrysost. oration 18. vol. 5. f. 104. μὴ πρόσεχε τῇ εὐτελείᾳ τῶν λεξεων, ἀλλά λάβε θεοπρεπῇ τὰ νοήματα. Do not attend to the vileness of the words, But gather from thence senses worthy of God. Damasc. lib. 1. orth. fid. cap. 14. πὰντα τὰ σωματικῶς εἰρημένα ἐπὶ θεοῦ κεκρυμμένην ἔχει τινὰ ἔυνοιαν ἐκ τῷν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς ἐκδιδάσκουσαν.

6. Lorinus on v. 14. annotates thus: The crown of justice is rendered to patience, even out of justice, on account of the worthiness of the patient one with the grace of GOD and the covenant and promise. 2. Timoth. 4. vers. 8. Resp. 1. The words of the Apostle are clear, Roman. 8. v. 18. The sufferings of this time are not worthy &c. 2. Eternal life is called the crown of justice, both with respect had to the merit of CHRIST, and to the truth of the divine promise.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. A minister of the Church in general and in particular should exhort his hearers to the study of piety. Actor. 20. v. 31.

2. Between ὁμόνοιαν, συμπάθειαν, φιλαδελφίαν, εὐσπλαγχνίαν, φιλοφρόνησιν and the remaining virtues pertaining to the love of neighbor, there is a certain most beautiful connection; for they are joined to one another by a sisterly bond, since the one is also the mother of the other. Where φιλαδελφία, is, there ὁμόνοια, is; where ὁμόνοια, is, there συμπάθεια is &c.

3. Ὁμόνοιαν or unanimity and concord the Apostle commends in the first place, because it is a spiritual bond, by which the pious are joined as members of one mystical body. Concord is a divine virtue, because there is one will of the three persons of the divinity, and the same undivided essence; it is an Angelic virtue, because among so many myriads of Angels no one is found to disagree with another; it is a truly Christian virtue, because Christians are joined through faith with CHRIST the head, and through charity with the remaining members of the mystical body; it is a human virtue, because GOD for this reason made the whole human race descend from one blood, that it might be a perpetual memorial of unity. Actor. 17. vers. 26.

4. We cannot all do one and the same work, it behooves each one to work for himself and his own condition or vocation, the servant does one thing, the master another; the husband one thing, the wife another, but that is required of us, that we think altogether the same thing, endowed with similar judgment and similar affection, thus it will come to pass, that there may indeed be many hands, but one heart and one soul. Before God the work of one believer is not better than the work of another believer, but through faith before God all things are equal. The consideration of this matter keeps men in unity and concord. Luth. in h. l. In the life of Macarius it is recorded that it was revealed to him that by all his prayer, fasting, and pursuit of virtues he had not yet reached the condition of two women who had lived with their husbands in the same house for fifteen years in peace and concord, so that one never said a harsh word to the other.

5. Among the truly pious there ought to be συμπάθεια, not only in evils, but also in goods, since they are members of one body.Roman. 12. v. 4.1. Cor. 12. v. 26. Through this συμπάθειαν in evils he who suffers is relieved, says Lyranus in h. l. A parity of strength with the suffering neighbor ought to exhort us to it. We either are, or have been, or can be what this one is. Hebr. 13. vers. 3. Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body. Examples of συμπαθείας are proposed to us in Job chap. 30. v. 25. Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor? in Paul 2. Corinth. 11. vers. 29. Who is weak, and I am not weak? but especially in CHRIST Hebr. 4. vers. 15. We have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities.

6. Φιλαδελφία ought to be most highly commended to the pious, since they are sons of one heavenly Father, and therefore spiritual brothers, and co-heirs of eternal life.

7. Ἐῖυσπλαγχνία is the genuine daughter of charity, which invites not only to helping brothers with all duties, but also to tolerating their infirmities and forgiving offenses to them, as the interlinear gloss notes to h. l. August. book 9 of the City of God chap. 5 Mercy is a certain compassion in our heart for another's misery, by which, if we can, we are compelled to assist. For this movement serves reason when mercy is so approved that justice is preserved, whether it is given to the needy, or when it is granted to the penitent.

6. The courtesy and modesty of manners are joined by a certain most beautiful συζυγίᾳ. He who thinks modestly of himself shows himself courteous and affable to his neighbor. Bernard serm. on chap. 12 of the Apoc. A great sign &c. Meekness and humility are as it were foster-sisters, hence also Christ declares himself to be both meek and humble,Matt. 11. v. 29.

9. To return evil for good is Diabolical; to return evil for evil, and good for good, is human; to return good for evil is an Angelic, nay, a divine work.

10. To retort abuse with abuse is to cleanse mud with mud.

11. Lactantius, book 6 of the Institutes, chapter 18, places this among the Christian precepts. Let a blessing respond to a curse, nor let an evil word proceed from the mouth of a man who utters a good word. Ambrose in his exhortation to Virgins: Wishing to separate us from the scourge of the tongue, the Apostle warns that we should not return a curse for a curse, but rather, when we are cursed, we should return the grace of a blessing. Augustine in Psal. 92.When, upon hearing an insult, anger begins to rise so as to return evil for evil, remember the words of the Apostle. Not returning evil for evil, nor a curse for a curse. By remembering these words you break your anger, you maintain fortitude, &c.

12. Christians are a people of blessing or a blessed people, they are the blessed of the heavenly Father,Matth. 25. v. 45. nay, they are blessing itself, i.e., blessed in the highest degree and in various ways, Genes. 12. v. 2. Because therefore GOD has removed the curse from them, and has heaped upon them every kind of blessing, therefore they bless even the neighbor who curses them. They are children of the free woman,Gal. 4. v. 22. therefore they stand with the children of the free woman to bless. Deut. 27. v. 12.

13. Let us often recall to our memory the grace of the divine calling, so that we may strive to remain in it through the constancy of faith, and to respond to it through the holiness of life. Eph. 4. v. 1.Walk worthily of the vocation wherewith you are called. It is surely fitting for everyone to be most occupied and most versed in that thing to which he has been singularly called.

14. Just as for GOD to bless is to do good, so also the blessing of GOD is the benefit of GOD: hence eternal life, which is the sum of all goods, is called the blessing of GOD.

15. What each one desires to find in the future, let him strive to meditate upon and do in the present, namely, to bless both the Creator and his neighbor with a sincere voice, and to render himself also worthy of both divine and fraternal blessing. Bede in this place.

16. They who bless shall inherit a blessing: but they that are cursed they are excluded from the heavenly kingdom,1. Cor. 6. v. 10. The blessedness of the saints consists for the greatest part in blessing, i. e. in the glorification of GOD and perpetual jubilation Psal. 84. v. 5. the cursed shall not be admitted into that holy fellowship.

17. To a man living well, and using his tongue well, temporal and eternal happiness, a quiet and tranquil life in this and the future age is promised. Principally this promise pertains to the future life, yet in its own way it can also be referred to this life.

18. No one receives a blessed life, unless he who loves it: no one loves it, unless he who aspires to it with the greatest zeal: no one aspires to it, unless he who applies faith to the divine promise, and seeks that life solely in Christ.

19. The blessed shall see good days, because the blessedness of eternal life consists either solely or certainly for the most part in the beatific vision of GOD. Greg. Nyssen. lib. de virginit. The dignity of seeing God is the supreme pinnacle of all hope, and the end, head, and sum of all desire and ineffable goods. August. q. 114. in Genes. The vision of GOD will be the highest reward of the blessed lib. de spiritu & anima cap. 55. The vision of GOD is the whole of eternal life. If the wicked were to see the face of GOD, they would be free from punishments.

20. The days of this age are evil, since this age also, when it is the measure of the world placed in the wicked one, is assimilated to the Nature of the world, which it measures out. Good days are not of this, but of the future age, and those which the sensible Sun completes here are deciduous and perish. Basilius in Psalm. 33.Days are always evil in the age, always good in GOD, and not to be sought here, but elsewhere, from Eph. 5. v. 16.

21. Sin, which is committed through tongues, is almost the most prone and multiform of all, whence David in the first place hands down this precept to his sons, whom he wishes to teach the fear of GOD. Basil. d. l. Psal. 39. v. 2.I said, I will guard my ways, that I may not sin with my tongue. I will put a muzzle on my mouth. Socrat. lib. 4. Histor. Eccles. cap. 18. reports, there was a certain Hermit, Pambo by name, a man indeed especially religious, but plainly illiterate, who approached a Doctor, and desired to learn a Psalm from him: but when he had heard this verse of the Psalm, he did not wish to know more, and said that this verse was sufficient for him, so that he might express it in life and morals. Six months having elapsed from then, he did not return to the Master, and being asked the cause of his absence, he replied that he had not yet been able to accustom his tongue to the precept of the Psalm. Afterwards Having been asked by another for nineteen years whether he had yet grasped a little verse of the Psalm, he said at last, I have learned it. Sir. 22. vers. 33. Who will set a guard over my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, that I may not fall by them, and my tongue destroy me? Sirach. 28. vers. 28. Make doors for your mouth. vers. 30. When you surround your possessions with a hedge, why do you not much more prepare a door and bars for your mouth? And when you weigh your gold and silver, why do you not also examine your words by weighing them in a balance? Iacob. 3. vers. 5. the tongue is indeed a small member, and boasts great things. Behold how small a fire, which sets a great forest ablaze. etc.

22. Two vices of the tongue are especially to be avoided: Evil-speaking, which burdens one's neighbor with insults and contumelies; and Fraudulence, which brings forth one thing with the mouth, but carries another thing locked in the breast. To the former is opposed εὐλογία,, to the latter candor, devoid of bitterness and simulation Ps. 12. v. 3. their lips are divided, they have spoken with a heart and a heart v. 4. the Lord will destroy all deceitful lips.

23. There are two parts of justice: to decline from evil, and to do good. Virtue teaches to avoid evils, to pursue goods. Psalm. 37. vers. 27. Decline from evil and do good. Esai. 1. v. 16. Cease to act perversely vers. 17. learn to do good. Amos. 5. v. 15. Hate evil and love good. Rom. 12. vers. 9. ἀποστυγοῦντος τὸ πονηρὸν, κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ. Jerome Epist 14. to Celantia. There are two kinds of commandments, in which the whole of justice is enclosed: the one of forbidding, the other of commanding: there rest is ordered, here zeal; there the mind is restrained, here it is incited; here to have done, there not to have done is culpable: this double precept is equally commanded by right to all in any purpose, in any rank it is an equal sin either to admit what is forbidden, or not to do what is commanded.

24. It is not therefore sufficient to decline from evil, but it is required furthermore also to do good. Not only that tree is cut down, and cast into the fire, which bears bad fruit; but also that which brings forth no fruit. Matth. 3. vers. 10. cap. 7. Vers. 19. Let the goats set on the left terrify us, not because they robbed, but because they did not feed. Matth. 25. v. 33. On which passage the Author of the imperfect work comments thus. If for that which men do not do well, they are condemned, do you think what punishments they will pay for that which they sin? For God therefore made man, that he may do good, and it may pertain to the glory of GOD, not only so that he may not sin.

25. First it is necessary to extirpate vices, then to introduce virtues, just as a farmer first frees a garden from briars and thorns, before he commits fruit-bearing seeds to it.

26. Let everyone strive to live peaceably with his neighbor, as much as can indeed be done with a good conscience. Rom. 12. v. 18. We ought to love truth and peace, Zach. 8. v. 16. first indeed and before all things truth, then also peace.

27. Peace with one's neighbor is a rare beast, it is circulated in a German proverb. To catch this beast, the virtues enumerated above are required, ὁμόνοια, συμπάθεια, φιλαδελφία, εὐσπλαγχνία, φιλοφρόνησις, which are like hunting dogs that seek out this beast.

28. It is not enough to seek peace, unless we pursue it with all zeal when it is found and fleeing. Jerome in Epist. ad Rustic. The Prophet does not say: If peace follows you, receive it; but even if it flees from you, follow it, as for instance, if, which is human, you have had a dispute with someone, if indeed he invites you first to peace, peace follows you, receive it with joy: but if he, who is evil, remains in evil, peace is hidden from your eyes, you as a son of peace knock at the door of peace &c. Chrysostom in chapter 5 of Matthew on the words: Blessed are the peacemakers.

29. Augustine in Psal. 33. warns, that peace is to be sought not here, but by following where He has gone before, who is our peace Eph. 2. v. 14. for neither with God, nor with neighbor, nor with ourselves, while we live, can perfect peace be obtained. The same author in lib. de Continent. cap. 7. Perfect peace will then be ours, when our Nature, inseparably clinging to its creator, nothing in us resists us.

30. The best consolation against the injuries of wicked men is that the pious know that they have God favoring them, hearing their prayers, and avenging the injuries brought upon them.

31. By the eyes of GOD open upon the just is denoted not only His providence, but also His paternal benevolence. Nothing is dearer than the eyes, says Augustine, homil. 1. de serm. Dom. in monte cap. 14. because therefore GOD embraces the just with paternal love, for that reason He is also said to have His eyes open upon them, to direct them toward them, and to fix them upon them. Psal. 32. v. 8. In the Hebrew it is, I will direct you with my eyes.

32. As the eyes of the Lord are open upon the righteous: so also are his ears open to their prayers, and intent upon them. Isa. 58. v. 9.John 16. v. 23. &c.

33. Bede, in chapter 16 of John, recounts the causes for which our prayers are sometimes not heard in this order. 1. When we ask against the help of salvation, then the grace of the benefit, which we ask ineptly, is denied by the merciful Father. 2. When we indeed ask for things useful for salvation, but we do not ask rightly. 3. When we pray for those sinning, that they may repent, even if we ask healthfully, yet their own perversity stands in the way so that we do not obtain it. 4. It also happens sometimes that we seek things entirely salutary with both solicitous prayers and devout actions, and yet we do not immediately obtain what we ask, but the effect of our petition is deferred to the future. Bernard, sermon 49 on the manner of living well. Prayer is hindered in two ways from obtaining what it requests, if a man still commits evils, or if he does not forgive from the whole heart the one sinning against him.

34. As GOD looks upon the righteous with paternal and benign eyes: so he directs his angry face against the impious, who will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord2. Thess. 1. v. 9.a fiery river will absorb them, which goes out from the face of the LordDan. 7. v. 10.God sets and hardens his face against themLevit. 17. v. 10.chap. 20. v. 3. &c.

35. The best prophylactic against injuries is the pursuit of good works and kindness toward one's neighbor. For those who are occupied in doing good and benefiting others win the minds of men to themselves, so that they cease to harm them.

36. Therefore, the fruit of a pious and holy life, in which we strive to deserve well of all, is accustomed to be a quiet and tranquil conversation in the world.

37. Who are emulators of the good, no one can harm them. In a certain Ecclesiastical Collect it is said. No adversity will harm us, if no iniquity dominates. Chrysostom wrote an entire book on this sentiment. No one is harmed except by himself, which exists in volume 5 of his works. In it he demonstrates with many things that neither losses, nor poverty, nor calumnies harm the good, nor diseases, nor chains, nor exiles, nor servitude, nor any of the other things which are commonly judged to be evils. Chrysostom sent this book to Olympias, and in Epistle 4 he admonished her to unfold it diligently, for it would be the remedy for every evil &c. Augustine or whoever else the author of the sermon on Peter and Paul. If GOD shall deliver you from yourself, the evil man, nothing will harm you, whoever else the evil man may be. Bede in his commentary on this passage cites the said book of Chrysostom, and adds: Those things which happen to us from adversaries through insulting words, through the loss of temporal goods, through torments of the body, can by no means harm the faithful, but rather bring the palm of patience to those who endure them equanimously, and on the contrary, they harm those who inflict them greatly by accumulating eternal punishment. John Huss on this passage: No one can harm those who possess the holiness of life.

38. Indeed, the good of the pious, being internal, is so constituted that no one can take it away from them. Luke 17. v. 21. The kingdom of GOD is within you. Matt. 6. v. 20. Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where thieves do not break through, nor steal. What else can persecutors do than take away money? But that was soon to be left behind anyway; than afflict the body? But that is subject to diseases anyway; than kill the body? But that was soon to die anyway.

39. To suffer for righteousness, that is finally glorious for a pious man. Augustine, book 3 against Cresconius, chapter 38, and elsewhere passim. It is not the punishment, but the cause, that makes a martyr. Matt. 5. v. 10. Blessed are they who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Augustine against the Epistle of Parmenianus, chapter 9. Righteousness is not certain from suffering, but suffering is glorious from righteousness. And therefore the Lord, lest anyone should cast mists before the unskilled in this matter, and seek the praise of martyrs in the condemnation of their own merits, did not say generally, Blessed are they who suffer persecution, but added a great distinction, by which true piety is separated from sacrilege. For He says, Blessed are they who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake.

40. The pious, on account of afflictions and persecutions, are not more unhappy before God, nor does anything depart from their blessedness through them, but rather some gain accrues to them. 2 Cor. 1. verse 5. As the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also our consolation abounds through Christ.

41. He who fears God and trusts in Him does not fear the threats of men. Ps. 27. v. 1. The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life, of whom shall I be afraid? Ps. 56. v. 5. In GOD I have hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me? Hilary in his Apology to Constantius. Would that you, Almighty God and creator of all things, but Father of our one Lord Jesus Christ, had granted this to my age and time, that this ministry of my confession in You and in Your Only-Begotten I would have fulfilled it in the Neronian and Decian times. Nor would I, burning through the mercy of the Lord and of GOD thy son Jesus Christ, have feared the rack, I who would have known of Isaiah sawn asunder: nor would I have feared the fires, among which I would have remembered the Hebrew boys singing; nor would I have avoided the cross and the breaking of my legs, after I remembered the thief translated into Paradise: nor would I have trembled at the depth of the sea and the Pontic tide absorbing the rheum, when through Jonah and Paul thou hadst taught that for the faithful there is life in the sea. Chrysostom, when he was being driven from the city, was saying within himself in his Epistle to Cyriacus. If indeed the Queen wishes me to act as an exile, let her act for exile. The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof. If she wishes to saw, let her saw, Isaiah suffered the same. If she wishes to cast me into the sea, I will remember Jonah. If she wishes to throw me into the furnace, those three boys suffered the same. If she wishes to throw me to the wild beasts, let her throw, I will remember Daniel thrown into the den of lions. If she wishes to stone me, let her stone; I will have as a companion Stephen the proto-Martyr. If she wishes to take my head, let her take it: I have as a companion John the Baptist. If she wishes to take away my substance, let her take it: naked I came out of my mother's womb, naked also I shall return.

42. Just as the highest of evils, which the law threatens, is a fearful heart, and full of dread Lev. 26. v. 36.Deut. 28. v. 65. so the greatest of goods, which Christ has merited for us, and offers in the Gospel, is a heart certain of the grace of GOD, and therefore tranquil in all adversities and dangers Ioh. 14. v. 1.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quaere Apostolus toties repetat praeceptumφιλαδελφίας& cognatarum virtutumv. 8.? Resp. 1. Ut ostendat, dilectionem esse summam totius legis,Matth. 22. v. 39.Rom. 13. v. 8. ac breve compendium omnium, quae proximo debemus, officiorum. Hieronymus lib. 3. in Epist. Galat. cap. 6. Beatus Iohannes Evangelista, cum Ephesi moraretur usque ad ultimam senectutem, & vix inter discipulorum manus ad Ecclesiam deferretur, nec posset in plura vocem verba contexere, nihil aliud per singulas solebat proferre collectas, nisi hoc. Filioli alter alterum diligite. Tandem discipuli & fratres, qui aderant, taedio affecti, quod eadem semper audirentur, dixerunt. Magister, quare semper hoc loqueris? Qui respondit dignam Iohanne sententiam; quia praeceptum Domini est, & si solùm fiat, sufficit. 2. Ut carnis nostrae torporem accuset, quae frequentioribus ad dilectionem proximo impendendam indiget stimulis. 3. Ut ostendat, se genuinum Christi discipulum, quia Christus itidem praeceptum dilectionis Apostolis suis perpetuò inculcavit, ac monitum hoc quasi per Testamentum ipsis commendavit. Ioh. 13. v. 34.

Q. 2. Rectène addatur in quibusdam Codicibus Latinis, post vocem unanimes, in oratione estote v. 8.? Ita quidem legit Ecclesia Romana in Officio Missae Dominic. v. post Pentecosten, sic inchoans lectionem Epistolicam. Omnes unanimes in oratione estote. Ita quoque legit Albinus Epist. 1. Vitriacus serm. 2. in Dom. 5. post Pentecosten, uti etiam Hugo in comment. qui refert hunc προσδιορισμὸν ad sequens nomen, compatientes. Atqui 1. Graecus textus simpliciter legit ὁμόφρονες, συμπαθεῖς. 2. Nec Syriaca paraphrasis hoc additamentum habet. 3. Nec correctiores Codices Latini. 4. Lyranus Carthusianus, & recentiores Interpp. plerique omnes à textu reiiciunt. 5. Petrus vult pios esse consentientes non solùm in oratione, sed etiam in fide & omnibus rebus honestis. Qui officium Ecclesiasticum collegit, de suo illud ὲξηγήσεως causa addidit, quia congregationis in caetum Ecclesiasticum fidelibus illud maximè convenit, quod postmodùm alii in textum Scripturae inserverunt.

Q. 3. Quare Apostolus in v. 9. duplici praecepto negativo siveἀποτροπῇ,quod non sit reddendum malum pro malo, nec convitium pro convitio, unicum duntaxat affirmativum praeceptum, sive unicamἀροτροπὴνopponat, quando dicit,τουναντίον δὲ εὐλογοῦντες? Resp. εὐλογίας nomine συνεκδοχικῶς complectitur etiam εὑποΐιαν sive εὐεργεσίαν, quòd non solùm verbis debeamus benè precari proximo, sed reipsâ etiam ipsi benefacere. Ita namque hoc praeceptum Apostolicum exponitur in parallelo loco Matth. 5. v. 44.Diligite inimicos vestros, benedicite devoventibus vos, benefacite his, qui oderunt vos, & orate pro calumniantibus & persequentibus vos.

Q. 4. Quis sit nexus argumenti Apostolici inv. 9.Scientes, quia in hoc vocati estis, ut benedictionem hereditate possideatis. Resp. 1. Pii à proximo laesi in memoriam sibi revocare debent, quòd DEUS non effuderit super ipsos suam maledictionem, etiamsi eam aequè ac caeteri homines fuerint promeriti, sed potiùs omni benedictione coelesti ipsis benedixerit Eph. 1. vers. 4. quo ipso se moneri agnoscant, ne maledicta regerant illis, qui maledictione digni sunt, sed aeternam potiùs felicitatem ex animo illis adprecentur. 2. Pii spem certam fovent, fore, ut in die iudicii aliquando à Christo audiant, Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete hereditatis iure regnum vobis paratum &c.Matth. 25. v. 34. norunt enim, se ex gratiâ vocatos esse, ut benedictionem illam hereditate possideant, ergò benedictionis filios & hac benedictione dignos se ostendunt, proximo benedicentes etiam illi, à quo iniuriâ fuêre affecti. 3. Pii praeclarè norunt, si benedictionem, quae in possessione coelestium bonorum consistit, ad quam divinitùs ex gratia vocati sunt, aliquando consequi cupiunt, semet obstrictos esse, ut etiam proximis benedicant, Deum seriis gemitibus precantes, ut illi quoque à peccato conversi ad coelestis illius benedictionis hereditatem unà cum ipsis aspirent. 4. Nisi proximo remiserimus, nec DEUS nobis remittitMatth. 6. v. 15. Qui convitia convitiis, mala malis pensant, proximo non remittunt. Ergò nec Deus illis remittit. Quibus autem Deus non remittit delicta, non possunt benedictionis hereditatem consequi, proinde qui benedictionem hereditare cupiunt, proximo remittunt eique benedicunt.

Q. 5. An textus Graecus in v. 10. sit corruptus? Ita statuit Piscator in h. l. sic scribens. Graeca Psalmi habent.τίς ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὁ θέλων ζωὴν, ἀγαπῶν ἡμέρας ἰδεῖν ἀγαθὰς. Ex quorum verborum collatione videtur apud Petrum legendum hoc modo. ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν, ἀγαπῶν ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς, pro quibus ex non animadverso asyndeto videtur sciolus aliquis reposuisse ista. ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾷν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς, mutando scilicet ἀγαπῶν in ὰγαπᾷν, atque ita efficiendo pleonasmum minùs commodum. Sed nulla nos cogit necessitas, ut corruptelam textus hîc agnoscamus. Monuimus enim superiùs, esse phrasin Hebraeam. Qui vult diligere vitam, i. e. qui vitae desiderio & amore seriò tenetur. Usus est Petrus quadam διαιρέσει & traiectione verborum, ut apparet ex collatione textus Hebraei, sed sensui nihil omninò decedit.

Q. 6. An de sola pace cum proximo agatur in vers. 11.? Triplicem pacem Scriptura nobis commendat. 1. Pacem cum DEO. 2. Pacem conscientiae sive cum corde nostro. 3. Pacem cum proximo. Quidam ergò dictum Davidicum & Apostoltcum accipiunt de omnibus hisce pacis speciebus, ut sit generalis admonitio, quòd quilibet debeat sectari pacem cum DEO, pacem cum semetipso, & pacem cum proximo, quia pacem cum proximo, si vera & stabilis esse debet, oriri oportet ex pace cum DEO. Ut enim in DEO, & propter DEUM, & sub DEO proximum diligere debemus: ita quoque in DEO, propter DEUM, & sub DEO, cum proximo pacificè vivere debemus. Pacem cum proximo etiam infideles & non renati sectari possunt, sed pax cum DEO, & pax conscientiae interior est propria Christianorum possessio, qui etiam soli ad eam, quae sola est in coelo vera pax, aliquando pervenient. Sed circumstantiae textus ostendunt, directè ac principaliter hîc agi de pace exteriore cum proximo: in sensu tamen accommodatitio extendi potest hoc dictum etiam ad pacem interiorem cum DEO.

Q. 7. Quo sensu τὸ declinare malum, & facere bonum cum studio pacis & concordiae coniungantur inv. 11.? Iohannes Huss. profert eiusmodi connexionem. Declinet à malo, quia est pacis expulsivum; faciat bonum, per eius subiecti dispositionem; inquirat pacem per eius actionis manifestationem; per sequatur eam per temporis continuationem. Si prius membrum accipiamus specialiter de malo & bono respectu proximi, quòd non debeamus mala pro malis, sed potiùs bona pro malis reddere, connexio est manifesta. Nam mala pro malis reddere non est pacis conservandae vel recuperandae medium, sed bona pro malis reddere. Si vero prius membrum accipiamus generaliter de quovis malo in lege divina prohibito, & de quovis bono in eadem praescripto, dicendum erit, Apostolum hac connexione insinuare, quòd studium pacis absque obedientia erga reliqua Decalogi praecepta non possit diu consistere, cum virtutes sint sibi invicem connexae, & sint quasi una copulativa.

Q. 8. Quare in exhortatione ad patientiam Apostolus vultus Dominici, i. e. irae divinae mentionem faciatv. 12.? Resp. 1. Ut ostendat, DEUM fore iniuriarum piis praeter meritum illatarum vindicem, qui non perpetuò passurus sit, malos & persecutores pro sua libidine grassari. 2. Ut praemoneat, quid futurum sit, si mala malis rependere ac semetipsos vindicare velint, nimirum quòd DEUM habituri sint sibi adversum. 3. Ut providentiam divinam non solùm ad bonos, sed etiam ad malos sese extendere doceat.

Q. 9. Quid per oculos & aures Domini intelligaturvers. 12.? Clemens Alexandrinus in comm. exponit de multiformi Spiritus sancti speculatione. Basilius in Psalm. 33.de Angelis, quorum aliqui velut oculi curam susceperint nos invisendi, alii preces nostras excipiendi. Sed ex antithesi vultus Dominici, & ex collatione aliorum Scripturae locorum colligitur, per oculos DEI paternum ipsius favorem, ac per aures exaudiendi promtitudinem ἀνθρωποπαθῶς intelligi. Quos enim diligimus, ad illos oculos dirigimus, & eorum sermonem promtis auribus excipimus. 1. Reg. 8. v. 9.2. Paral. 6. vers. 20.Neh. 1. v. 6.Psal. 33. v. 18.Prov. 15. v. 3.Ierem. 5. v. 3. &c.

Q. 10. Quo sensu Apostolus dicatv. 13.Quis est, qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis? Resp. 1. Quidam accipiunt de nocendi facultate. Nemo est, qui nocere vobis possit, h. e. verum nocumentum inferre, si quod bonum est in oculis Domini summo studio sectemini, quia piis omnia cooperantur in bonum,Rom. 8. v. 28.ac quicquid externorum malorum ipsis obtingit, ad interioris hominis profectum, & animae salutem ipsis proficit. 2. Quidam vero de nocendi voluntate. Nemo est, qui nocere vobis velit, si bonum sectemini, quia plerunque usu venire videmus, ut qui iniuriâ affecti benedicunt, linguam suam à malo custodiunt, omnibus benefacere student, & pacem sectantur, animos inimicorum suorum demulceant, eosdemque sibi concilient, & hac ratione minùs obnoxii sint improborum iniuriis. Potest utraque explicatio sine ulla absurditate coniungi.

Q. 11. Quo respectu pii, etiamsi patiantur, nihilo minùs beati dicanturv. 14.? Resp. 1. quia in aerumnis gaudent bonâ conscientiâ, cùm sciant, se non pati ut maleficos, sed ut Christianos. 2. quia fide expectant liberationem, vel certè mitigationem calamitatum. 3. quia Deus variis bonis huius vitae adversitates compensare novit. 4. quia promissio de coelesti hereditate ipsis manet rata ac firma. Sunt ergò beati non solùm respectu spei, sed etiam respectu rei.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. In fine autem sitis denique omnes unanimes v. 8. Atqui Apostolus plura adhuc in sequentibus proponit praecepta. Resp. 1. quidam reddiderunt, in summa, quia dilectio estτέλος sive τελείωσις,impletio & consummatio legis, sive ut Apostolus loquitur,ἀνακεφαλαίωσιςRom. 13. v. 9. 2. Concludit Apostolus hac voculâ τελικῇ praecedentem tractationem, ostendens, tùm demum non solùm subditos & servos, uxores & maritos, sed etiam in genere omnes Christianos suo rectè functuros officio, si ὁμόνοιαν, συμπάθειαν, φιλαδελφίαν & cognatas virtutes sibi habeant maximè commendatas.

2. Non reddentes malum pro malo.v. 9. Atqui Lev. 24. vers. 19.Vir cum dederit maculam in proximum suum, secundùm quod fecit, sic fiat illi.v. 20.fracturam pro fractura, oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente, iuxta quod dederit maculam in hominem, sic dabitur in eum. Similia occurrunt Exod. 21. v. 24.Deut. 19. v. 21. Resp. lex divina agit de vindicta publica, quam Deus per Magistratum exercet. Apostolus loquitur de vindicta privata, quam Moses itidem prohibet. Levit. 19. v. 18.Ne quaeras ultionem, nec memor sis iniuriae civium tuorum. LXX. Non ulciscatur manus tua. Vicissim publicam Magistratus vindictam non solùm Moses, sed etiam Paulus stabilit. Rom. 13. v. 4.Magistratus est Dei vindex ad iram illi, qui malum facit; quod repetit noster Apostolus 1. Epist. 2. v. 14.

3. Qui vult vitam diligere, & dies videre bonos &c. declinet à malo, & faciat bonum.v. 10. & 11.Atqui pii saepè contraria experiuntur, bona faciunt, sed mala ipsis inferuntur.Iob. 21. v. 7.Psal. 73. vers. 13. & seqq. Ierem. 12. v. 1.Habac. 1. v. 3. Resp. 1. coniunguntur dies boni in hoc seculo, & vita beata in futuro. Quod si vel maximè in hoc seculo dies boni ipsis minimè obtingunt, certissimè tamen in futuro seculo vita beata ipsis obtinget. Promissiones de praemiis pietatis in hac vita intelligendae sunt cum exceptione crucis & divinae εὐδοκὶας. Praecipua praemia differuntur in futuram vitam. 2. pii in cruce fustentant se promissione auxilii divini, nituntur testimonio bonae conscientiae, & certi sunt, omnia sibi in bonum cooperari. Possunt ergò esse in mediis undis sive tempestatibus tranquilli.

4. Qui vult dies videre bonos, coërceat linguam suam.vers. 10. At Esa. 6. v. 5.Vae mihi, quia tacui. Resp. 1. Psalmographus, & ex eo Petrus non simpliciter & absolutè dicunt, coërceat linguam suam, sed addunt προσδιορισμὸνà malo, & labia sua, ne loquantur dolum. 2. Tempus est loquendi, & tempus tacendi.Eccl. 3. v. 7. nec solùm peccatur loquendo, sed etiam tacendo, quando scil. gloria Dei, & salus proximi confessionem requirit. 1. Cor. 9. v. 16.Vae mihi, si non Evangelizavero.Psal. 57. v. 2.Num verè muti estis loqui iustitiam? 3. In Hebraeo est נדמיתי in Niphal, quod significat, in silentium redactus sum, perii, excisus sum,Soph. 1. v. 11.Obad. 1. v. 7. quo modo etiam Luth. reddidit. Ich vergehe.

5. Declinet à malo, & faciat bonumv. 11.Atqui de Iobo diciturcap. 1. v. 1.Erat vir ille perfectus, & rectus, & timens DEUM, & recessit à malo. Ergò priùs fecit bonum, postea demum declinavit à malo. Resp. 1. consideratur homo vel in actu conversionis, vel in statu post conversionem. In actu conversionis requiritur, ut priùs declinet à malo per peccati agnitionem ac detestationem, antequam facere possit bonum per Spiritus sancti gratiosam inhabitationem; requiritur, ut priùs avertatur à via iniquitatis, antequam insistere possit viae mandatorum divinorum. Sed in statu post conversionem priùs facit bonum per Spiritus vivificationem, quàm declinet à malo per carnis mortificationem. 2. Τὸ bonum facere, vel intelligitur de interiore amore ac studio boni, quod praecedit declinationem à malo: vel de exteriore bonorum operum exercitio, quod sequitur declinationem à malo. Origenes in cap. 2. Rom. de Iobo dicit, licet soleant caeteri ferè inchoare à mali abstinentia, & in exercitio bonorum mala quaedam permiscere, tamen Iobum hac in parte eximium fuisse, quod agens bona simul ab omni malo abstineret.

6. Oculi Domini super iustosv. 12.AtAmos 9. v. 4.Ponam oculos meos super eos in malum, & non in bonum. Resp. tribuuntur DEO oculi paterni & benigni, quos ponit Deus super iustos in bonum. Ierem. 24. v. 6.Ponam oculum meum super eos in bonum, & reducam eos in terram hanc. Tribuuntur etiam ipsi oculi irati, quos ponit super impios in malum. Idem iudicium de facie Domini, quae itidem in bonum & malum sumitur, inde quod Amos 9. v. 4. dicitur, ponam oculos meos super eos in malum, illudIerem. 44. v. 11. sic redditur. Ecce ego ponam faciem meam in vobis in malum.

7. Quis est, qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis?v. 13. At 2. Tim. 3. v. 12.Omnes, qui piè vivere volunt in Christo Iesu, persecutionem patientur. Resp. 1. Petrus loquitur potissimùm de statu Christianorum extra tempora persecutionis ob fidei confessionem. Paulus de tempore, quo movetur propter religionis professionem persecutio. 2. Petrus eò respicit, quod pii suâ innocentiâ & patientiâ possint animos improborum, à quibus laeduntur, ad moderationem flectere, eosque sibi conciliare, ut ab iniuriis praeter meritum inferendis desistant.

8. Quis est, qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis v. 13. Atqui pii saepe numero ab improbis affliguntur, etiam si beneficiis & obsequio eos placare vel maximè studeant. Resp. 1. Si de nocendi facultate verba Apostoli accipiantur, manifestum est, improbos non posse animabus piorum ullum inferre nocumentum. Quamvis enim mala multa illis inferant, salutem tamen eorum minimè intervertere poslunt, sed eam potiùs promovent. 2. Si de nocendi voluntate accipiantur, explicanda sunt de eo, quod utplurimùm contingit. Plerunque enim ac communiter ita fieri videmus, ut qui beneficentiae & innocentiae student, animos inimicorum suorum emolliant. 3. Quia vero contrarium quandoque contingit, ideò Petrus quasi per correctionem quandam subiicit, Sed & si patiamini propter iustitiam, beati.

9. Quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis v. 13. At qui improbi & sibiipsis & aliis exemplo nocent. Resp. non simpliciter negat Apostolus, noxios illos homines nocere, sed negat eos piis nocere, quibus persecutionem inferunt, quia scilicet nec animam eorum occidere, nec ullum eis nocumentum inferre possunt.

10. Timorem eorum ne timueritisvers. 14.At qui de Iosepho dicitur, audiens quòd Archelaus regnaret in Iudaea pro Herode patre suo, timuit illuc ire.Matth. 2. vers. 22. Resp. 1. In piis non semper viget aequale Spiritus robur, sed quandoque ex infirmitate carnis in adversis trepidant. 2. non est simpliciter prohibitum, ab hostibus & persecutoribus timere, sed eo modo timere, ut fiducia in Deum & confessio veritatis propterea abiiciatur, adeoque persecutores plus timere quàm ipsum DEUM. Matth. 10. vers. 28.Nolite timere eos, qui occidunt corpus, animam autem non possunt occidere;μᾶλλον δὲ φοβηθῆτε,potiùs autem sive maius timete eum, qui potest & animam & corpus perdere in gehenna.

II. Non turbemini. At Christus de seipso dicit.Iohan. 12. vers. 27.Anima mea turbata est. Resp. Petrus loquitur de tali perturbatione, cum qua coniuncta est diffidentia & affectuum ἀταξία, qualis non habet locum in Christo. Iohan. 11. v. 33. de Christo dicitur, ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτὸν, ex quo colligunt pii veteres, Christum non fuisse eo modo perturbatum, quo nos in subitis pavoribus perturbari solemus, videl. praeter opinionem & voluntatem, sed ipsum sponte affectum illum suscepisse, quando & ubi voluit, sine omni tamenἀταξίᾳ καὶ ἀνομὶᾳ. Aug. tract. 49. in Ioh. Turbaris tu nolens, turbatus est Christus, quia voluit, in illius potestate erat, sic vel sic affici, vel non affici. Confer. Damascen. lib. 3. Orthod. fid. cap. 23.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Petrus requirit, ut omnes sint συμπαθεῖς φιλάδελφοι, ἔυσπλαγχνοι.vers. 8. Damnat ergò Stoicam ἀπάθειαν, qualis animadvertitur in quibusdam Monachis, qui filialem erga parentes & fraternum erga consanguineos asfectum exuunt, perpetuò illud Hieronymi in ore habentes. Per calcatum perge pati, sola in hoc genere pietas est, esse crudelem. Confer. Luth. in h. l.

2. Petrus seriò requirit, ut nemo reddat malum pro malo, nec convitium pro convitio, sed contrà, ut benedicamus. v. 9. Erroneum igitur est, quod Scholastici disputant, diligere inimicos esse consilium. Certè Christus Matth. 5. vers. 44. ideò inimicos diligere praecipit, ut simus filii Patris coelestis i. e. ut nos genuinos DEI filios demonstremus. Ergò qui inimicum non diligit, non est genuinus Patris coelestis filius.

3. Petrus vitam aeternam vocat hereditatem. Falsum est ergò quod Pontificii docent, eam dari ex merito, quia hereditas datur iure filiationis, non autem propter merita operum.

4. Petrus requirit, ut declinet à malo & faciat bonum, qui vult vitam diligere & dies videre bonos. Erroneum igitur est, quod quidam negant, bona opera esse renatis necessaria. Muta vitam, si vis accipere vitam. Bonum in diebus vitae tuae sectare, si dies bonos expetis videre.

5. Petrus docet, oculos Domini esse apertos super iustos, & aures eius in preces eorum, vultum autem Domini esse super facientes mala. Gravissimè igitur errant, qui providentiam divinam negant. Erasmus in Symb. catech. 2. Turpius errant, qui negant providentiam, quàm qui Deum ipsum negant, quemadmodum levius indignareris illi, qui putaret te non esse natum, quàm qui crederet, tibi non esse sensus aut mentem humanam.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lorinus ad vers. 9. sic annotat. Benedictio haec non tantùm consistit in eo, ut bene precemur, quod intus facere possumus in anima nostra, & vero debemus, quatenus neminem à communi oratione licet excludere, sed etiam & quidem propriè in verbis benevolis. Hoc secundum non est adeò semper necessarium, fierique potest, ut potiùs contemnat & magis indignetur adversarius. Resp. 1. Christus Matth. 5. vers. 44. indivulso nexu haec coniungit. Diligite inimicos vestros, benedicite his, qui devovent vos. Ergò εὐλογία aequè necessaria ac dilectio inimici. 2. Petrus hanc εὐλογίαν opponit ἀντιλοιδορίᾳ, quâ convitia convitiis repelluntur. Utique ergò praecepti huius affirmativi aequalis est obligatio ac praecepti negativi. 3. ad εὐλογὶαν etiam pertinet ut pro inimicis oremus, docente Christo, Matth. 5. v. 44. atqui fatente Lorino â communi oratione neminem licet excludere. 4. ex accidente est, quod verba benevola contemtum apud inimicos alunt, & indignationem augent. Utplurimùm responsione molli frangi solet alterius ira Prov. 15. v. 1. & provocatur adversarius ad laudandum Deum eiusque doctrinam, gratiam, bonitatem &c. simul etiam persuadetur, aliam esse hac meliorem vitam. Nam nisi illam speraret, non tàm facilè, quas alii magnifaciunt, ferret iniurias. rem adeo difficilem praestare nemo sine omnipotentis Dei gratia valet; bonum oportet iudicari Deum, propter quem benedicat quis etiam adversario, ut Lorinus ibidem rectè annotat. Horum salutarium consequentium maior habenda ratio, quàm accidentarii illius effectus.

2. Ex eo, quod malum pro malo reddere prohibemur, colligunt Anabaptistae & Photiniani, Magistratui non competere ius gladii in facinorosos. Resp. Apostolus loquitur de privatis personis & privata vindicta. Magistratus vindictam in maleficos exercet, non ex cupiditate vindictae, sed ex zelo iustitiae.

3. Estius ad v. 10. sic annotat. Quod David secundum literam dixisse videri potesi de longaevitate & felicitate temporali, quam servantibus legem promittebat V. T. id à Petro iuxta sensum spiritualem transfertur seu potiùs extenditur ad felicitatem vitae aeternae, quam promittit N. T. qui sensus etiam & quidem principaliter à Spiritu Sancto fuit intentus, nec non ab ipso David tanquam N. T. filio. Resp. Non solùm N. sed etiam V. T. continet promissionem vitae aeternae, diversâ tamen ratione. Vetus Testamentum promittit vitam aeternam sub conditione perfectae obedientiae legi divinae praestandae: Novum vero promittit vitam aeternam credentibus in Christum gratis dandam.

4. Ex eo, quod Petrus dicit, qui vult diligere vitam, & dies videre bonos, declinet à malo & faciat bonum, Pontificii evincere conantur, vitam aeternam dari ex merito bonorum operum. Resp. est haec descriptio subiecti, quales oporteat esse eos, qui ad propositum vitae aeternae brabeum contendunt, non autem descriptio causae meritoriae, propter quam vita aeterna datur.

5. Ex eo, quod Deo tribuuntur oculi, aures, facies &c. colligebant Audaeani, Deum esse corporeum. Epiph. haeres. 70. Tripart. lib. 10. cap. 7. Contra quos pii veteres rectè urgebant. 1. Si haec propriè accipienda essent, monstrosam corporis figuram Deo tribuendam esse, quia adscribuntur ei septem oculiZach. 3. vers. 9. 2. DEUM non solùm ab humanis membris similitudinem in se recipere, sed aliquando etiam ab avibus, aliquando ab insensatis rebus dissimiles quasdam similitudines trahi. Gregor. lib. 32. moral. cap. 4. Tribuuntur ei alaePsal. 17. vers. 8.comparatur leoni, urso. 3. Omne corporeum esse compositum, DEUM autem esse simplicissimum, ac proinde esse SpiritumIoh. 4. v. 24.Ergòανθρωποπαθῶς, συμβολικῶς & κατὰ συγκατάβασινhaec dicuntur, quae sunt intelligendaθεοπρεπῶς & κατὰ ἀναφορὰν. Chrysost. orat. 18. tom. 5. f. 104. μὴ πρόσεχε τῇ εὐτελείᾳ τῶν λεξεων, ἀλλά λάβε θεοπρεπῇ τὰ νοήματα.Ne attende vilitati verborum, sed sensus Deo dignos inde collige. Damasc. lib. 1. orth. fid. cap. 14. πὰντα τὰ σωματικῶς εἰρημένα ἐπὶ θεοῦ κεκρυμμένην ἔχει τινὰ ἔυνοιαν ἐκ τῷν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς ἐκδιδάσκουσαν.

6. Lorinus ad v. 14. sic annotat. Patientiae redditur corona iustitiae debita etiam ex iustitia ob patientis cum DEI gratia & pacto promissoque condignitatem.2. Timoth. 4. vers. 8. Resp. 1. verba Apostoli sunt diserta, Roman. 8. v. 18.Non sunt condignae passiones huius temporis &c. 2. Vita aeterna dicitur corona iustitiae, tùm respectu habito ad meritum CHRISTI, tùm ad promissionis divinae veritatem.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Minister Ecclesiae in genere & specie auditores suos ad pietatis studium exhortetur. Actor. 20. v. 31.

2. Inter ὁμόνοιαν, συμπάθειαν, φιλαδελφίαν, εὐσπλαγχνίαν, φιλοφρόνησιν & reliquas virtutes ad caritatem proximi pertinentes, est pulcherrima quaedam connexio; sororio enim vinculo sibi invicem sunt coniunctae, quando & una alterius esi mater. Ubi φιλαδελφία, ibi ὁμόνοια, ubi ὁμόνοια, ibi συμπάθεια &c.

3. Ὁμόνοιαν sive unanimitatem & concordiam Apostolus primo loco commendat, quia est vinculum spirituale, quo pii velut unius corporis mystici membra coniunguntur. Concordia est virtus divina, quia trium personarum divinitatis est una voluntas, & eadem indivisa essentia; est virtus Angelica, quia inter tot Angelorum myriadas nullus ab altero dissidere invenitur; est virtus verè Christiana, quia Christiani per fidem cum CHRISTO capite, & per caritatem cum reliquis mystici corporis membris coniunguntur; est virtus humana, quia DEUS ideò ex uno sanguine fecit totum genus humanum descendere, ut esset perpetuum unitatis memoriale. Actor. 17. vers. 26.

4. Non possumus omnes unum idemque operis facere, unum quemque pro se & sua conditione sive vocatione operari oportet, aliud servum, quàm herum; aliud maritum, quàm uxorem, sed illud à nobis requiritur, ut idem omninò sentiamus, simili iudicio, similique affectu praediti, ita fiet, ut multae quidem sint manus, sed unum cor & anima una. Coram Deo opus unius credentis non est melius opere alterius credentis, sed per fidem coram Deo omnia sunt paria. huius rei consideratio homines retinet in unitate & concordia. Luth. in h. l. In vita Macarii ipsi revelatum memoratur, quod omni suâ oratione, ieiunio & studio virtutum nondum pervenisset ad conditionem duarum foeminarum, quae cum maritis suis in eadem domo per quindecim annos vixerant inpace & concordia, adeò ut nunquam una alteri verbum aserius dixerit.

5. Inter verè pios debet esse συμπάθεια, non tantùm in malis, sed etiam in bonis, cùm sint unius corporis membra.Roman. 12. v. 4.1. Cor. 12. v. 26.Per hancσυμπάθειανin malis allevatur ille, qui patitur, inquit Lyranus in h. l. Ad eam nos hortari debet paritas fortis cum patiente proximo. Aut sumus, aut fuimus, aut possumus, esse quod hic est. Hebr. 13. vers. 3.Mementote vinctorum tanquam simul vincti & laborantium, sive malè habentium, tanquam & ipsi in corpore adhuc commorantes. Exempla συμπαθείας nobis proponuntur in Iobo cap. 30. v. 25.Flebam super, eo, qui afflictus erat, & compatiebatur anima mea pauperi; in Paulo 2. Corinth. 11. vers. 29.Quis infirmatur, & ego non infirmor? cumprimis vero in CHRISTO Hebr. 4. vers. 15.Non habemus Pontificem, qui nos possit compati infirmitatibus nostris.

6. Φιλαδελφία piis debet esse maximè còmmendata, cum sint unius Patris coelestis silii, ac proinde fratres spirituales, & vitae aeternae coheredes.

7. Ἐῖυσπλαγχνίαest genuina caritatis filia, quae non modò ad fratres omnibus officiis iuvandos, sed etiam ad infirmitates eorum tolerandas & offensas eis condonandas invitat, ut gloss. interlin. ad h. l. annotat. August. lib. 9. de civ. Dei cap. 5 Misericordia est alienae miseriae quaedam in corde nostro compassio, quâ utique si possumus, subvenire compellimur. Servit enim motus iste rationi, quando ita probetur misericordia, ut iustitia conservetur, sive cum indigenti tribuitur, sive cùm ignoscitur poenitenti.

6. Morum comitas & modestia sunt pulcerrimâ quadam συζυγίᾳ coniunctae. Qui de se modestè sentit, comem & affabilem sese proximo exhibet. Bernhardus serm. in cap. 12. Apoc. Signum magnum &c. Mansuetudo & humilitas sunt velut sorores collactaneae, inde etiam Christus se mitem simul & humilem esse pronunciat,Matt. 11. v. 29.

9. Mala pro bonis reddere, est Diabolicum; mala pro malis, bona pro bonis reddere, humanum; bona pro malis reddere, Angelicum, imò divinum opus.

10. Convitium convitio regerere, est lutum luto purgare.

11. Lactantius lib. 6. Instit. cap. 18. inter praecepta Christiana ponit. Maledictioni benedictio respondeat, nec verbum malum procedat ex ore hominis, qui edit verbum bonum. Ambros. in exhortat. ad Virg. A flagello linguae nos separare cupiens Apostolus monet, ut non reddamus maledictum pro maledicto, sed magis, cum maledicitur nobis, benedictionis referamus gratiam. Augustinus in Psal. 92.Cùm audito convitio ira coeperit surgere, ut reddat malum pro malo, recordare verba Apostoli. Non reddentes malum pro malo, neque maledictum pro maledicto. His verbis recordatis frangis iram, tenes fortitudinem &c.

12. Christiani sunt populus benedictionis sive benedictus, sunt benedicti Patris coelestis,Matth. 25. v. 45. imò sunt ipsa benedictio, i. e. in summo gradu & variis modis benedicti, Genes. 12. v. 2. Quia ergò DEUS maledictionem ab ipsis sustulit, & omnigenâ benedictione illos cumulavit, ideò proximo etiam maledicenti benedicunt. Sunt filii liberae,Gal. 4. v. 22. ergò cum filiis liberae stant ad benedicendum. Deut. 27. v. 12.

13. Gratiam divinae vocationis saepè in memoriam nobis revocemus, ut in ea per fidei constantiam permanere, eidemque per vitae sanctitatem respondere studeamus. Eph. 4. v. 1.Ambuletis dignè vocatione, quâ vocati estis. Decet prosectò unumquemque in ea re esse occupatissimum & versatissimum, ad quam singulariter est vocatus.

14. Sicut DEI benedicere est benefacere, ita quoque DEI benedictio est DEI beneficium: inde vita aeterna, quae est omnium bonorum summa, DEI benedictio vocatur.

15. Quod quisque in futuro invenire desiderat, hoc in praesenti meditari & agere satagat, & conditorem videlicet & proximum sincerâ voce benedicere, & seipsum etiam divinâ pariter & fraternâ benedictione dignum reddere. Beda in h. l.

16. Benedicentes benedictionem hereditate consequuntur: maledicti è regno coelesti excluduntur,1. Cor. 6. v. 10. Beatitudo sanctorum maxima ex parte consistit in benedictione, i. e. in DEI glorificatione & iubilo perpetuo Psal. 84. v. 5. in sanctum illud consortium non admittentur maledicti.

17. Homini benè viventi, & linguâ suâ benè utenti temporalis & aeterna felicitas, vita quieta & tranquilla in hoc & futuro seculo promittitur. Principaliter haec promissio pertinet ad futuram vitam, suo tamen modo etiam ad hanc vitam referri potest.

18. Nemo accipit vitam beatam, nisi qui diligit eam: nemo diligit eam, nisi qui summo studio ad eam aspirat: nemo ad eam aspirat, nisi qui promissioni divinae fidem adhibet, & in Christo vitam illam unicè quaerit.

19. Beati videbunt dies bonos, quia beatitudo vitae aeternae vel unicè vel certè maximè in DEI visione beatifica consistit. Greg. Nyssen. lib. de virginit. Dignitas videndi Deum supremum est omnis spei fastigium, & omnis desiderii ac bonorum ineffabilium finis, caput & summa. August. q. 114. in Genes. DEI visio summum erit beatorum praemium lib. de spiritu & anima cap. 55. Visio DEI est tota vita aeterna. Si mali DEI faciem viderent, poenis carerent.

20. Dies huius seculi mali sunt, quoniam & hoc seculum, cùm sit mensura mundi in maligno positi, Naturae assimilatur mundi, quem dimetitur. Dies boni non sunt huius, sed futuri seculi, & quos Sol hîc sensibilis peragit, decidui sunt & dispereunt. Basilius in Psalm. 33.Dies semper mali in seculo, semper boni in DEO, & non híc quaerendi, sed alibi, ex Eph. 5. v. 16.

21. Peccatum, quod per linguas committitur, omnium ferè propensissimum & multiforme est, unde David primo loco hoc praeceptum tradit filiis, quos vult timorem DEI docere. Basil. d. l. Psal. 39. v. 2.Dixi, custodiam vias meas, ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Ponam ori meo capistrum. Socrat. lib. 4. Histor. Eccles. cap. 18. refert, fuisse quendam Eremitam, Pambonem nomine, virum quidem apprimè religiosum, sed planè illiteratum, qui accesserit ad Doctorem, & Psalmum ab eo discere cupiverit: cum vero versiculum hunc Psalmi audivisset, plures cognoscere noluit, istumque versum sibi sufficere dixit, ut illum vitâ & moribus exprimeret. Sex inde elapsis mensibus ad Magistruum non rediit, & causam absentiae rogatus, se nondum linguam suam ad Psalmi praeceptum assue facere potuisse, respondit. Post annos novendecim ab alio interrogatus, iamne versiculum Psalmi percepisset, vix tandem, inquit, illum addidici.Sir. 22. vers. 33.Quis dabit ori meo custodiam, & super labia mea signaculum certum, ut non cadam ab ipsis, & lingua mea perdat me?Sirach. 28. vers. 28.Ori tuo facito ostia.vers. 30.Cùm sepem circumdes tuis possessionibus, cur non multò magis ori tuo ianuam & repagula paras? cumque aurum & argentum tuum ponderes, cur non etiam verbatua in libra ponderando examinas?Iacob. 3. vers. 5.lingua modicum quidem membrum, & magna iactat. Ecce quàm exiguus ignis, quae magnam sylvam incendit. &c.

22. Duo potissimùm linguae vitia sunt cavenda, Maledicentia, quae convitiis & contumeliis proximum onerat; & Fraudulentia, quae aliud ore profert, aliud in pectore clausum gerit. Illi opponitur εὐλογία, huic candor, amariciei & simulationis expers Ps. 12. v. 3.labia eorum divisa, in corde & corde locuti suntv. 4.disperdet Dominus universa labia dolosa.

23. Duae sunt iustitiae partes, declinare à malo, & bonum facere. Virtus docet cavere mala, fectari bona. Psalm. 37. vers. 27.Declina à malo & fac bonum.Esai. 1. v. 16.Quiescite perversè agerevers. 17.discite benefacere.Amos. 5. v. 15.Odite malum & diligite bonum.Rom. 12. vers. 9.ἀποστυγοῦντος τὸ πονηρὸν, κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ. Hieronymus Epist 14. ad Celanciam. Duo sunt genera mandatorum, in quibus clauditur tota iustitia, prohibendi unum, iubendi alterum: ibi otium imperatur, hîc studium; ibi coërcetur animus, hic incitatur; hîc fecisse, illic non fecisse culpabile est: hoc duplex praeceptum aequè omnibus iure mandatum est in quovis proposito, in quovis gradu aequale peccatum est vel prohibita admittere, vel iussa non facere.

24. Non ergò sufficit à malo declinare, sed requiritur insuper etiam bonum facere. Non illa solùm arbor excinditur, & in ignem mittitur, quae malos; sed etiam, quae nullos profert fructus.Matth. 3. vers. 10.cap. 7. Vers. 19. Terreant nos hoedi ad sinistram constituti, non quia rapuerunt, sed quia non paverunt. Matth. 25. v. 33. in quem locum Autor imperfecti operis sic commentatur. Si pro eo, quod benè non faciunt homines, condemnantur, putas, quales poenos exolvent pro eo, quod peccant? Deus enim ideò hominem fecit, ut benefaciat, & ad gloriam DEI pertineat, non ideò tantùm ut non peccet.

25. Primò oportet extirpare vitia, deinde virtutes inferere, sicut agricola sentibus & spinis hortum priùs liberat, antequam frugifera semina ipsi committat.

26. Quilibet cum proximo pacificè vivere studeat, quantum quidem bonâ conscientiâ fieri potest. Rom. 12. v. 18.Veritatem & pacem diligere debemus,Zach. 8. v. 16. primùm quidem & ante omnia veritatem, deinde etiam pacem.

27. Pacem cum proximo raram esse feram, Germanico circumfertur proverbio. Ad hanc feram capiendam requiruntur virtutes superiùs enumeratae, ὁμόνοια, συμπάθεια, φιλαδελφία, εὐσπλαγχνία, φιλοφρόνησις, quae sunt velut canes venatici, qui hanc feram inquirunt.

28. Non sufficit, pacem quaerere, nisi inventam fugientemque omni studio persequamur. Hieronym. in Epist. ad Rustic. Non dicit Propheta. Si pax te sequatur, suscipe illam; Sed etsi te fugerit, sequere eam, ut puta, si, quod humanum est, cum aliquo feceris litem, siquidem ille te prius invitat ad pacem, pax te sequitur, cum gaudio suscipe eam: quod si ille, qui malus, permanet in malo, pax absconditur ab oculis tuis, tu quasi filius pacis pulsa ianuam pacis &c. Chrysostomus in cap. 5. Matth. super verba. Beati pacifici.

29. August. in Psal. 33. monet, quaerendam pacem non hîc, sed sequendo, quò is praecessit, qui est pax nostraEph. 2. v. 14.nam neque cum Deo, neque cum proximo, neque nobiscum, dum vivimus, pax perfecta obtineri potest. Idem lib. de Continent. cap. 7. Pax perfecta tunc erit nobis, quando Natura nostra creatori suo inseparabiliter cohaerente, nihil nobis repugnat ex nobis.

30. Optimum contra improborum hominum iniurias solatium est, quod pii sciunt, se habere Deum sibi faventem, preces suas exaudientem, & iniurias sibi illatas ulciscentem.

31. Per oculos DEI apertos super iustos non tantùm denotatur eius providentia, sed etiam paterna eiusdem benevolentia. Oculis nihil carius, inquit August. homil. 1. de ferm. Dom. in monte cap. 14. quia ergò DEUS iustos paterno amore complectitur, ideò etiam oculos suos super ipsos apertos habere, in eos dirigere & super illos firmare dicitur. Psal. 32. v. 8. In Hebraeo est, dirigam te oculis meis.

32. Ut oculi Domini super iustos sunt aperti: ita quoque aures eius ad preces ipsorum sunt apertae, iisque intentae. Esai. 58. v. 9.Ioh. 16. v. 23. &c.

33. Causas, propter quas preces nostrae quandoque non exaudiuntur, Beda in cap. 16. Ioh. recenset hoc ordine. 1. Quando petimus contra auxilium salutis, tunc à misericorde Patre beneficii gratia, quod ineptè petimus, denegatur. 2. Quando utilia quidem ad salutem petimus, sed non rectè petimus. 3. Quando pro peccantibus, ut resipiscant, oramus, etsi salubriter petimus, ipsorum tamen perversitas, ne impetremus, obsistit 4. Fit etiam aliquando, ut salutaria prorsus & precibus solicitis & devotis quaeramus actionibus, nec tamen statim obtineamus, quae petimus, sed in futurum petitionis nostrae differatur effectus. Bernhardus serm. 49. de mod. ben. viv. Duobus modis oratio impeditur, ne impetret, quod postulat, si adhuc homo mala committit, aut si peccanti in se ex toto corde non dimittit.

34. Ut oculis paternis ac benignis DEUS intuetur iustos: ita iratam sitam faciem dirigit contra impios, qui poenas dabunt exitium aeternum à facie Domini2. Thess. 1. v. 9.absorbebit eos fluvius igneus, qui egreditur à facie DominiDan. 7. v. 10.Deus ponit & obfirmat faciem suam contra illosLevit. 17. v. 10.cap. 20. v. 3. &c.

35. Optimum iniuriarum prophylacticum bonorum operum & benignitatis erga proximum studium. Qui enim benè agendo & aliis benefaciendo occupantur, animos hominum sibi conciliant, ut nocere ipsis desinant.

36. Piae igitur & sanctae vitae, in qua conamur de omnibus benè mereri, fructus esse solet, quieta & tranquilla in mundo conversatio.

37. Qui sunt aemulatores boni, illis nemo nocere potest. In Collecta quadam Ecclesiastica dicitur. Nulla nobis nocebit adversitas, si nulla dominetur iniquitas. Chrysostomus integrum librum scripsit de hac sententia. Nemo laeditur nisi à seipso, qui extat tom. 5. operum. In eo multis demonstrat, non damna, non paupertatem; non calumnias bonis nocere, non morbos, non vincula, non exilia, non servitutem, non quidvis aliorum, quae vulgò censentur mala. Hunc librum Chrysostomus misit ad Olympiadem, eamque Epistola 4. admonuit, ut diligenter eum evolveret, eum enim fore omnis mali pharmacum &c. Augustinus vel quicunque alius autor serm. 2. de Petro, Paulo. Si DEUS liberaverit te à teipso homine malo, nihil tibi nocebit, quisquis alius fuerit homo malus. Beda in comm. h. l. allegat dictum librum Chrysostomi, & addit. Ea quae nobis ab adversariis per verba contumeliosa, per damna rerum temporalium, per tormenta corporis accidunt, fidelibus nequaquam nocere possunt, sed palmam magis patientiae aequanimiter tolerantibus afferunt, & contrà illis, qui irrogant, poenam accumulando aeternam plurimùm nocent. Ioh. Huss. in h. l. Habentibus sanctitatem vitae nemo nocere potest.

38. Nimirum bonum piorum, utpote internum, ita comparatum est, ut nemo illud ipsis auferrre possit. Luc. 17. v. 21.Regnum DEI intra vos est.Matth. 6. v. 20.Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in coelo, ubi fures non effodiunt, nec furantur. Quid aliud facere possunt persecutores, quàm auferre pecuniam? at illa mox alioqui erat relinquenda; quàm corpus affligere? at illud morbis alioqui obnoxium; quàm corpus occidere? at illud brevi alioqui erat moriturum.

39. Propter iustitiam pati, illud demum homini pio gloriosum. August. lib. 3. contra Crescon. cap. 38. & alibi passim. Martyrem facit non poena, sed causa.Matth. 5. v. 10.Beati, qui per secutionem patiuntur, propter iustitiam, ipsorum enim est regnum coelorum. Aug. contra Epist. Parmen. cap. 9. Non ex passione certa est iustitia, sed ex iustitia passio gloriosa est. Ideoque Dominus, ne quisquam in hac re nebulas offunderet imperitis, & in suorum damnatione meritorum laudem quaereret Martyrum, non generaliter ait, Beati, qui persecutionem patiuntur, sed addidit magnam differentiam, quà vera à sacrilegio pictas secernatur. Ait enim, Beati, qui per secutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam.

40. Pii ob afflictiones & persecutiones non sunt coram Deo infeliciores, neque quid quam ipsorum beatitudini per eas decedit, sed potiùs lucri aliquid ipsis accedit. 2. Cor. 1. vers. 5.Sicut abundant passiones Christi in nobis: ita & per Christum abundat consolatio nostra.

41. Qui Deum timet, ipsique confidit, non timet hominum minas. Psal. 27. v. 1.Dominus est illuminatio mea & salus mea, quem timebo? Dominus protector vitae meae, à quo trepidabo?Psal. 56. v. 5.In DEO speravi, non timebo, quid faciat mihi homo? Hilarius in Apol. ad Constantium. Utinam istud potiùs omnipotens Deus & universorum creator, sed unius Domini nostri Iesu Christi pater aetati meae & tempori praestitisses, ut hoc confessionis meae in te atque in Unigenitum tuum ministerium Neronianis, Decianisque temporibus explessem. Nec ego per misericordiam Domini, & DEI filii tui Iesu Christi calens eculeum metuissem, qui dissectum Esaiam scissem: nec ignes timuissem, inter quos Hebraeos pueros cantare meminissem; nec crucem & fragmenta crurum meorum vitassem, postquam in Paradisum translatum latronem recordarer: nec profundum maris & Pontici aestus absorbentem rheumam trepidassem, cum per Ionam & Paulum docuisses, fidelibus esse in mari vitam. Chrysostomus cum à civitate fugaretur, dicebat intra seipsum in Epist. ad Cyriacum. Siquidem vult Regina me exulem agere, agat in exilium. Domini est terra, & plenitudo eius. Si vult secare, secet, idem passus est Esaias. Si vult in pelagus me mittere, Ionae recordabor. Si vult in caminum iniicere, idem passi sunt tres illi pueri. Si me feris vult obiicere, obiiciat, Danielis in lacum leonibus obiecti reminiscar. Si me lapidare vult, lapidet; socium habebo Stephanum proto Martyrem. Si caput tollere vult, tollat: habeo socium Ioh. Baptistam. Si substantiam vult auferre, auferat: nudus exivi ex utero matris meae, nudus etiam revertar.

42. Sicut summum malorum, quae lex minatur, est cor pavidum, & formidine plenum Lev. 26. v. 36.Deut. 28. v. 65. ita maximum bonorum, quae Christus nobis promeruit, inque Evangelio offert, est cor de gratia DEI certum, ac proinde in omnibus adversis & periculis tranquillum Ioh. 14. v. 1.

## 3:9
NOT RENDERING EVIL FOR EVIL, NOR CURSE FOR CURSE, BUT CONTRARIWISE BLESSING, BECAUSE UNTO THIS YOU ARE CALLED, THAT YOU MAY POSSESS A BLESSING BY INHERITANCE.

Connection. 1. This is the sixth virtue to which the Apostle exhorts Christians, namely, the tolerance of injuries & εὐλογία, by which the truly pious return a blessing for injuries and curses.

2. The virtues enumerated in the preceding verse all pertain to Christian and brotherly charity, but the desire for private vengeance is extremely opposed to that. Therefore, lest the pious allow themselves to be driven to a desire for vengeance by the injuries and calumnies of their adversaries, the Apostle requires patience from them, without which charity can by no means be preserved.

3. Lyranus proceeds thus. Here consequently the Apostle orders the faithful in the suffering of evil, in which one can be disordered in two ways, in one way by audacity in paying back in turn, in another way by falling into pusillanimity through fear. He removes the first v. 10. the second v. 13. The first part is subdivided into two, because first he warns not to pay back in turn v. 10. secondly he introduces for this the authority of Scripture v. 11.

Disposition of the text: First, the Apostle distributes the injuries which are inflicted upon the pious by the adversaries of heavenly truth into two species, that some are real, some are verbal. He commands that both are to be patiently tolerated by the pious. Secondly, he amplifies his exhortation with an antithesis and a certain exaggeration. The pious ought not only not to render evil for evil, nor curse for curse, but moreover even to bless those by whom they have been harmed. Thirdly, he adds two arguments for the exhortation. The former is sought from the will of GOD, GOD has called you to this, that you may prove your patience in enduring the injuries of adversaries. The latter from the salutary consequence, which is the inheritance of divine blessing. Both arguments can, however, be conveniently joined, so that the reason for the exhortation is said to be sought from that signal benefit of GOD, who, when we were still His enemies, altogether worthy of temporal and eternal curse, called us through the Gospel into the kingdom of grace, so that He might not only take the curse away from us, but also confer upon us the heavenly blessing, and thus the inheritance of all spiritual and heavenly goods. Eph. 1. v. 3.Gal. 3. v. 8. & following.

Exposition of the text, Μὴ ὰποδιδόντες κακὸν αντὶ κακοῦ ἣ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας. The Christians were living in the midst of infidels, who were troublesome to them both by deeds and by words; he therefore warns them, lest out of a desire for vengeance they repay evil deeds with evil deeds and revilings with revilings. Interlinear Gloss: Not rendering evil for evil in act, nor curse for curse in words.
