The way of theology is certainly far greater than human wisdom, and all the more so, because it is a greater thing to receive divine matters by faith than to scrutinize their reasons. Caesarius, brother of Nazianzen, Dialogue 3. The dogmas of Christians are certainly contained and supported by faith, not by reasonings, through which very many have utterly lost their mind. Jacobus Faber in his commentary on Richard, Book 1 on the Trinity, chapter 1. To seek reasoning in faith is to hold a shade before a weak eye, lest it be dazzled by a more distinguished light. Therefore, he who can behold those things which are of faith without reasoning sees and knows far more distinctly than he who demands and seeks reasoning, just as he recognizes the Sun more sincerely whom such great brilliance does not dull while looking directly at it, than he who, in order to see it, places his hand before his sight and casts a shadow.

7. The same man, in the said place, writes thus: With Wycliffe, the heretics of this time hate Scholastic and positive theology, and deny that it is necessary for the Church, but rather pernicious. Conformable to this is that of Possevin, Book 1, Bibliotheca, p. 126, where he says that they especially loathe Scholastic theology in order to cover up their ignorance. Response: We do not simply disapprove of the knowledge and moderate use of Scholastic theology, but the manifold abuse of the same, which some of the Papists themselves acknowledge with us. The Scholastics err entirely: 1. concerning the principle of disputing, because they mix philosophy with theology, and in the highest mysteries of faith, with logical, physical, and metaphysical principles, etc., having omitted or only lightly touched upon the sayings of Scripture, they fetch their conclusions. They follow a most corrupt Latin version, having omitted the Hebrew and Greek sources; they violently and plainly twist the Scriptures outside of their scope; they dispute from the sayings of the Fathers as if from a proper principle of theology, and they almost equate their authority with the authority of Scripture. 2. Concerning the object of disputing, because they propose idle, curious, thorny, useless, absurd, superstitious, and impious questions. 3. Concerning the manner of disputing, because a certain monstrous lust for contradicting is everywhere obvious among them: they dispute topically and skeptically about those things which are defined in the Scriptures; they rashly define abstruse questions not defined in the Scriptures; they use obscure terms, words, and phrases, etc.

8. Estius on v. 17 notes thus: It is possible that the particle ὡς in the Greek text was omitted long ago, either through the carelessness or the ignorance of scribes who thought it superfluous. He certainly posits that it was once read twice ὡς κακοποιῶν & ὡς ἐπηρεάζοντες. Ibid. It may seem to have been added as if for evildoers from the preceding chapter vers. 12. Resp. 1. In the former suspicion, Estius corrects the Greek text from the Syriac version; in the latter, from the Latin Vulgate version. But this is to prefer the streams to the fountains and to judge the latter by the former. 2. No necessity compels us to acknowledge any corruption in the Greek text, since the sense is perfectly consistent. 3. Repetitions are not unusual for Peter in this Epistle.

9. Lorinus on v. 17 notes thus: It is indeed good to bear the punishments owed to sins, and if anyone tolerates them patiently, he satisfies and merits, but it is better not to have deserved them. Resp. Patience in punishments brought on by sins pleases God, but it does not appease God; it is a work pleasing to God, but neither satisfactory nor meritorious.

10. Bellarmine, book 4 de Christo, ch. 13; Gretser, vol. 2, defens. p. 323, by τὸ πνεῦμα in v. 18. understand Christ's soul, in this sense, Christ mortified in the flesh, vivified in the Spirit in his passion, because the flesh remained dead, but the soul could not be killed, but remained alive. For that is said to be vivified which is not killed 1. Reg. 27. 2. Reg. 8. Act. 7. etc. Resp. 1. If by Spirit Christ's soul is understood, then Christ will be said to be vivified by his soul either actively or passively. Not actively, since because the soul is a Spirit always living and incapable of death, it had no need to vivify itself. They do indeed reply, those things are also said to be vivified which are left in life. Exod. 1. 17. 1. Sam. 27. v. 11. But that applies only to those things which can die, for whose life we spare, whom we permit to live, he can be killed. But neither with respect to the body can the soul be said to have vivified actively, because the soul did not bring the body back to life by itself through its own power, but through a communicated τοῦ Λόγου power. Nor passively, because the soul of Christ was not dead, therefore it was not in need of vivification. Aug. Ep. 99 to Enod. That Jesus had been mortified in soul i.e., by that Spirit which is of man, who would dare to say, since there is no death of the soul except sin, from which he was entirely immune when he died for us etc. In that thing he was vivified, in which he had been dead. Therefore it was said of the flesh. For it itself revived with the soul returning, because it itself was dead with the soul departing. Therefore he is said to have been mortified in the flesh, because he died according to the flesh alone, but made alive by the Spirit, because by that Spirit working, in whom he was coming to those to whom he was preaching, the flesh itself also, having been made alive, rose again, in which way he comes to men. 2. Then Estius refutes this explanation. Some, he says, interpret the Spirit as the soul of Christ, etc., so that the sense may be, Christ according to the Spirit, i.e., according to the soul, did not die, but remained alive. For to make alive, for that which is to keep alive, is a phrase of Scripture, etc. But what is great, if the soul of Christ remained living while the flesh was dying, when the soul does not die even in the worst of men, as it is by nature immortal? Wherefore it does not even contribute to the consolation of the pious, who are afflicted here, that their souls survive after death, unless some more blessed life is to follow by the example of Christ, which is proposed here. Estius indeed accepts the Spirit likewise as the soul, but he brings forward another explanation, about which later. 3. Lorinus refutes the same exposition, noting thus at this place. It does not please me what Hesselius (called John of Louvain) hands down, that Christ is said to have been made alive by the Spirit in the passion, because the soul cannot be killed when the flesh is dead. (In the margin are noted Bellarm. lib. 4. de Christo cap. 15. Pererius lib. 9. in Genes. Disp. 9. num. 66.) For this is common to every soul: although I am not ignorant that the word to make alive is used for that which is not to kill, etc. But in this place I follow rather the simple sense and the reasoning of Augustine, that Christ is properly said to have been made alive according to that part in which he had truly died, i.e., according to the flesh and in the flesh: for nothing stands in the way, and thus all things cohere.

11. Cajetan expounds that made alive by the Spirit concerning the blessedness of the soul of Christ, and concerning his triumph against the demons. He thinks indeed, that Christ is said to have been made alive by the Spirit, because he was blessed according to the Spirit and triumphed over the demons, which act of being made alive accrued to him when he died in the flesh. But Lorinus rightly judges this exposition to be too remote. For τὸ to be made alive according to the Spirit is opposed to τῷ to be put to death according to the flesh. Therefore, as by being put to death is understood death, so by being made alive is understood resurrection from the dead, of which we do not deny that the blessedness of the soul and the triumph over the demons are consequences.

12. Isidorus Clarius wishes that what preceded, he died for sins, the just for the unjust, be explained more in this way. Christ did this, that he might offer us to God, which he was also able to do. For although he was affected by death, on account of the nature of the flesh received, yet by the Spirit and divinity (since God is a Spirit Ioh. 4. v. 24.) he always lives, whence he is also able to save by himself those who approach through him to GodHeb. 7. v. 25. Resp. We willingly embrace this exposition, insofar as it understands the divinity of Christ through the Spirit, but we say that by vivification is directly and properly understood the communication or restoration of life, just as by mortification is understood the taking away of life. Meanwhile, we do not deny that the continuation of life followed that restoration of life, because Christ, having been raised from the dead, dies no more; death no longer has dominion over him. Rom. 6. v. 9.

13. Estius explains being put to death in the flesh and made alive in the Spirit concerning the opposition of carnal and spiritual life. Christ, he says, is said to be made alive in the Spirit, i.e., in soul, because he was made into a life-giving Spirit, namely, when he rose from death to immortal life, just as Paul speaks.1. Cor. 15. v. 46. The first man Adam was made a living soul, the last Adam a life-giving Spirit. But Christ is said to have been made into a life-giving Spirit, i.e., having a life-giving Spirit, when his soul began to supply perpetual and immortal life to his body without the aid of food, as if sufficient of itself to provide and preserve life for the body, so that what was previously an animal body was made in this way Spiritual, which sense fits this passage well, so that Christ is understood to be made alive in the Spirit through the resurrection, because then he began to live with an immortal life, for which the presence of the soul alone without the aids of food sufficed for him, which is also what will happen in the rest of the elect, of whom Christ is the firstfruits. In almost the same way, Cornel. à Lapide, who prefers this exposition to the others, says: Christ was made alive in the Spirit, when by the power of the Spirit, i.e., of his soul, he rose from the dead. For then the soul, having entered the flesh as if it were the instrument of his divinity, animated and vivified it again, and communicated a new immortal and glorious life to it. Resp. 1. τὸ to be made alive in the Spirit is not here opposed to τῷ to live in the flesh or according to the flesh, as 1. Cor. 15. v. 46. τὸ to be made into a life-giving Spirit is opposed to τῷ to have been made into a living soul, but to be made alive in the Spirit is opposed to that which is to be put to death in the flesh. 2. Therefore, one species of life is not opposed to another species of life, but the communication or restoration of life is opposed to the taking away of life. Directly, therefore, and properly by τὸ to be made alive in the Spirit is understood the resurrection from the dead effected by the power of the divinity of Christ, who is Spirit, as Athanasius in Bede, Augustine in sermon 14 on the words of the Apostle, ch. 16, and Epist. 99, and Oecumenius in his commentary rightly explain. 3. To be made into the life-giving Spirit, according to Estius, is common to Christ the head with the pious as members, to be resurrected at some time to immortal life, but the scope of Peter is to preach such a thing about Christ, which pertains to him alone. For just as it pertains to him alone to suffer for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God: so also it pertains to him alone to be so mortified in the flesh, that he is vivified in the Spirit, i.e., by the power of the Godhead personally indwelling, and thus by his own power to be resurrected from the dead. 4. Meanwhile, we do not deny that spiritual and immortal life is a consequence of that resurrection, since Christ was resurrected not to this life, but to heavenly life.

14. Lorinus brings forward the exposition of Clement of Alexandria, book 6 of the Stromata, that Christ is said to be vivified in the Spirit, because he lives in us and in our spirits, by obtaining and bestowing upon us the gift of faith, through which we are said to live in a peculiar way, Rom. 1. v. 17. Hebr. 2. v. 4. cap. 10. v. 38. Galat. 3. v. 11. and of charity and other virtues with sanctifying grace. I respond: Just as by τὸ to be mortified in the flesh the mortification of Christ's flesh is understood, so by τὸ to be vivified in the Spirit the vivification of Christ's flesh is understood, as the opposition shows. Furthermore, the Apostle does not speak of vivification actively, but passively, when nevertheless according to the hypothesis of Clement of Alexandria he ought rather to have said ζωοποιῶν than ζωοποιηθεὶς.. Therefore, the Apostle speaks directly and properly about the life of Christ himself, which was restored to him in the resurrection; meanwhile, we do not deny that Christ, having been resurrected from the dead, makes us participants of spiritual life through faith and lives in us. Gal. 2. v. 20.

Didactic observations. 1 He who erects a holy tabernacle to God in his heart through true and living recognition of divine goodness and faith, he truly sanctifies God. But he who sanctifies God, shall be sanctified by God. 2. Cor. 6. v. 26.

2. God is not sanctified by external adornment or hypocritical worship, but by the interior affection of the heart and spiritual worship. Psal. 45. v. 10. Luc. 17. v. 20. Ioh. 4. v. 24.

3. Confession of faith is not arbitrary, but necessary, to be performed by all the pious altogether for the glory of God. Matth. 10. 32. & 33. for it is an inseparable consequence of true faith, Psal. 116. 10. I believed, therefore I have spoken. 2. Cor. 4. 13. having the same Spirit of faith, we also believe, and therefore we speak. The seed of faith germinates in the heart through the confession of faith in the mouth.

4. That confession of faith ought to be so constituted, that what we profess to believe, we can confirm from the Scriptures, for this is to render an account of one's faith. Chrysostom, homily 16 on John: It is absurd that a physician, a tanner, a weaver, and all workmen in general, should each fight for the profession of his own art, but a Christian cannot bring forward any account of his religion. And yet those arts, when neglected, result in a loss of money, but the contempt of this brings detriment to the soul, and yet we labor under such misery, such madness, that we apply all our care and thought to those things, but we count as nothing the necessary things and the firmest bulwark of our salvation. This does not allow the Gentiles to recognize their error and to mock. For when they, relying on a lie, do everything to defend the ignominy of their dogmas, but we, the worshippers of truth, cannot even open our mouths to protect our own, what cause is there that they should not condemn the excessive weakness of our doctrine, that they should not suspect fraud and stupidity in us, that they should not curse Christ as a liar and one who abuses the stupidity of the multitude by his own fraud? We are the cause of this blasphemy, I say, we who are unwilling to watch over the pious discourses of our religion, but apply all our care to these contentions as if they were superfluous and perishable things, etc. If the Gentiles, in order to speak against our religion, have watched so much: with what pardon are we worthy, unless we seem to repel such insults against us? Peter commands this to us, for he says, being ready always to give satisfaction to every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you, etc. He has similar things in sermon 3 on Lazarus.

5. We ought to be ready for the defense to everyone asking for a reason of faith, whether he be an adversary or desirous of learning. Bede in this place: In two ways we ought to render an account to those asking for a reason of our hope and faith, so that we may both intimate the just causes of our faith and hope to all, whether they ask faithfully or unfaithfully, and always keep the profession of our faith and hope itself unblemished, even among the pressures of adversaries, showing through patience how reasonably we have learned that it must be kept, for the love of which we fear neither to suffer adversity nor to undergo death. Lyranus in this place: That satisfaction is made in two ways. In one way to the simple in faith, who asks to be more fully instructed by one more advanced in faith. In another way to the infidel, who considers the faith unreasonable. The first satisfaction is through charitable doctrine (of which one of the ancients says, let us not deny rational money to one wishing to borrow it) but the second is through a reasonable defense of the faith by showing that it contains all holiness, etc.

6. Meanwhile, it is one thing to answer if you have been questioned, another to throw oneself rashly into dangers among the impious without necessity, where a confession is not sought. Certainly, our confession ought not to be subject to the caprice and insolence of men, but to serve the glory of God and the salvation of one's neighbor.

7. By a twofold reason, confession and the rendering of an account of faith through it are required by the Doctors of the Church: first, generally, because they are Christians; second, specially, because they are doctors of the Church, whose proper duty it is to defend the truth of the faith against its attackers. Tit. 1. v. 9. Chrysost. homil. 35. in Matth. He is a traitor to the truth who either does not speak it freely or does not sufficiently defend it. Gregory, part 2, Pastoral care, chapter 11, adapts to this the type Exod. 25. concerning the staves in the ark of the covenant. By the ark he understands the Church, by the staves the Doctors of the Church. To carry the ark with staves, he says, is for good Doctors to lead the Holy Church to the unrefined minds of the infidels by preaching; these staves are commanded to be always in the rings, and never to be drawn out from them, because it is necessary that those who keep watch for the office of preaching should not depart from the study of Sacred reading. For to this end the staves are commanded to be always in the rings, so that when the opportunity requires the ark to be carried, no delay in carrying is generated by the inserting of the staves: because, clearly, when something spiritual is sought from a Pastor by his subjects, it is very shameful if he then seeks to learn when he ought to resolve the question. But let the staves adhere to the rings, so that the Doctors may always meditate on the sacred utterances in their hearts, and lift the ark of the Testament without delay, so that they may immediately teach whatever is necessary. Whence the first Pastor of the Church well admonishes the other pastors, saying, be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you, as if he were saying openly, that no delay may hinder the carrying of the ark, let the staves never depart from the rings.

8. Yet one must not answer all questions proposed by anyone, but only to those asking about useful and necessary matters. The Apostle 1. Tim. 1. v. 4. ζητήσεις ἀπεράντους opposes τῇ οὶκονομίᾳ θεοῦ τῇ ἐν πίστει cap. 6. v. 4. and says that from questions and λογομαχίαις envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings arise. 2. Tim. 2. Vers. 23. he commands to avoid foolish and unlearned questions, because they generate fights, which precept he repeats Tit. 3. v. 9. Athanasius in the life of Anthony records of him, that he was accustomed to ask those who came to him to question him about certain things, whether they came from Egypt or from Jerusalem, that is, whether they are about to set forth empty things, or truly useful and salutary ones.

9. Furthermore, confession should not be made with importunity, immodesty, or pride, by which a good cause is deformed, but in true humility, gentleness, modesty, and reverence; with fear toward God, and meekness toward men. For unless the fear of God underlies it, the human mind is raised into arrogance; unless the soul is composed toward meekness, contentions immediately boil over. Confession ought not to be biting and bitter, but gentle, and joined with the decorum of gravity.

10. Nay, more, not only is reverence required in issuing a confession toward God, lest we conduct ourselves hypocritically or negligently in setting forth the faith: but also toward Superiors, especially Magistrates, who demand a confession of faith from us, lest we seem to despise them. Act. 7. v. 2.cap. 22. v. 1.cap. 26. v. 2.

11. Unless faith resides within in the heart, the tongue will chatter in vain: whence Peter requires, that we give an account of the hope or faith that is in us. Therefore, let faith take root in the heart, so that it may then bring forth the fruit of confession.

12. A good conscience and a holy life ought to be joined to a holy confession. August. Epist. 211. ad Probam. It seems to me that the manner of living is worth more in this inquiry than the manner of speaking. For those who have learned from the Lord Jesus Christ to be meek and humble of heart, progress more by thinking and praying than by reading and hearing.

13. If all accuse you, it suffices for absolution if your conscience alone excuses you before God; but if all praise you, it suffices for condemnation if your conscience accuses you before God.

14. The pious in this life are exposed to various calumnies of adversaries, by which very thing they are conformed to the image of Christ. Matth. 10. Vers. 25.If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more those of his household.

15. There is no better method of refuting the calumnies of adversaries than when we blunt them with the innocence of our life. It is kingly to do good, and to be spoken ill of, Alexander the Great used to say: we ought to say it in this way παροιμιάζειν. It is Christian to do good, and to be spoken ill of, and thus to dispel the mists of calumnies with the Sun of truth and holiness.

16. The mouths of calumniators are not only obstructed by the good conversation of the pious, so that they are forced to be silent 1. Petr. 2. vers. 15.

but the slanderers themselves are confounded, and are forced to blush, which is that most just punishment which the Royal Prophet imprecates upon them several times. Psalm. 25. v. 3.Psalm. 35. v. 4. & 26.Psalm. 40. v. 15. & 16.Psal. 70. v. 3.Psal. 71. v. 13. & 24.Psal. 83. vers. 18.Psal. 86. Vers. 18.Psal. 109. v. 28.Psal. 119. v. 78.Psal. 129. v. 5. Confusion and blushing is a great punishment for an honorable man, whence what is said in Hebrew Ezech. 17. v. 53., bear thy confusion, the LXX rendered, τὴν βάσανον σου thy torment.

17. It does not irk the Apostle to inculcate more often those things which are necessary, hence what he had already said before in chap. 2. v. 15. he repeats again in this place, by the example of Paul Phil. 3. v. 1. To write the same things to you ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρὸν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλὲς.

18. If for the confession of faith something adverse must be endured, the testimony of conscience is sufficient. 1. Petr. 4. v. 15. & 16. Great is the consolation in innocence itself.

19. In this life no one is entirely immune from adversity, it is therefore better to suffer undeservedly for righteousness, than to sustain the punishments due to evildoers. Beda in h. l. This sentence of the Apostle elegantly argues the foolishness of those who, when they are rebuked by brothers for faults, or even are restrained by punishments, tolerate it altogether patiently: but when without fault they suffer either the insults of words, or the losses of things, or any adversities from their neighbors, they immediately break out into anger, and those who until now seemed innocent, through impatience and murmuring render themselves guilty.

20. If it is better to suffer for doing good than to suffer for doing evil. Therefore it is simply good to suffer for doing good. Matth. 5. v. 10. Blessed are they who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake. Blessed here in hope, there in reality. Behold how much they lost? for the dung of the world the kingdom of heaven; for a little sadness, infinite joy; for a fleeting life they received eternal life, says Ioh. Huss. in h. l.

21. The best consolation in persecutions and adversities is to remember that it is not without the will of God, and that the same are paternal when they befall us. Iob. 1. v. 21. The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord. Matth. 10. v. 29. Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing, and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. v. 30. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. August. lib. 22. contra Faustum cap. 20. When those doing good suffer from the will of the Spirit of GOD, it is not spared to the just: but when evildoers are spared, sinners are not spared, yet according to His will both come to pass, who says: I will not spare the just, nor the sinner, the former by scourging him as a son, the latter by punishing him as an impious one.

22. The cross is not to be rashly summoned and sought, but when imposed by GOD it is to be patiently borne.

23. Tyrants and not even the Devil himself can rage as much as they want and as long as they want, but as much and as long as God wants. Tyrants and Devils do what they can with God permitting; what they can, they do not do with God prohibiting, Ioh. Gerson. lib. 3. de consol. Theol. Pros. 4. God holds the infernal lion bound, lest he rage as much as he would want: not he, but the one holding him back, is to be entreated.

24. Since God embraces the truly pious with fatherly love, as His beloved sons, and nevertheless permits the cross to be brought upon them in this life, nay, sends it, it is manifest from this that the cross is sent to them for the benefit of the pious, for God is so good that He would not permit any evil to happen to the good, unless He knew how to elicit a greater good from it.

25. The cross is troublesome and adverse to the flesh, therefore the pious are deservedly recalled so often to look upon the example of Christ, so that when they know themselves to be members of Christ through faith, they may know that they must be conformed to the same as their head through the cross.

26. When the Apostle says that Christ suffered once, he teaches the perfection of the sacrifice and merit of Christ; when he says Christ suffered for sins, he teaches the efficacy and fruit of the passion of Christ; when he says the just suffered for the unjust, he declares the innocence of the suffering Christ; when he says Christ suffered so that He might bring us to God, he shows the final cause of the passion; when he says Christ was put to death in the flesh, he shows according to which Nature Christ suffered and how far He obeyed His heavenly Father; when he says He was made alive in the Spirit, he proposes for us to consider the joyful ἒκβασιν of the passion; and thus in one bundle he embraces the whole doctrine concerning the passion of Christ.

27. When we suffer for the sake of righteousness, let us comfort ourselves, because Christ suffered, to whose image it behooves us to be conformed in this life; because He suffered for us, so that He might free us from eternal death and reconcile us to His Father, therefore it is fair that we also suffer for Him, that is, for His glory by confessing His doctrine; because the just suffered for the unjust, therefore it is fair that we patiently bear the cross imposed upon us, since we are indeed innocent before the world, but not before God;

that he was indeed put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit, that is, resurrected to life and glory. Therefore, just as the outcome of the passion and death of Christ was happy, since the palm of life and glory finally followed that passion: so also the life of Christ will be manifested in us, if we carry about the mortification of Christ in our flesh.2. Cor. 4. v. 10.

28. The fruit of the passion of Christ is that through it he has expiated our sins, reconciled us to the heavenly Father, and brought back fugitives and the lost to the Father and the heavenly home, and has offered us as a pleasing sacrifice in himself to God.

29. If we were to be brought to GOD through the passion of Christ, therefore we all have turned aside like wandering sheepEsa. 53. Vers. 6. from the true GOD, from the knowledge of the true GOD and his legitimate worship; our turning aside is the case, but Christ's is the restoration and bringing back. Os. 13. Vers. 9. which ἀναγωγὴ embraces not only reconciliation with GOD, but also the illumination of the Holy Spirit, sanctification, and introduction into heavenly glory.

30. If Christ suffered for us for this reason, that he might offer us to GOD as a pleasing sacrifice, it is right that we present our bodies to God as a living and spiritual sacrifice.Rom. 12. v. 1. Through Christ let us offer a sacrifice of praise to GOD.Hebr. 13. v. 15. And let us surrender ourselves entirely to the service of GOD, so that GOD in turn may offer himself to us as to sons, Hebr. 12. v. 7. Christ offers himself to you, you offer yourself to Christ. Christ has brought you to GOD, beware lest you flee from him again through voluntary sins.

31. Between the passion of Christ and our own, there is a great difference indeed. Christ suffered to expiate the sins of others: we, however, through suffering can expiate neither our own nor others' sins; the passion of Christ alone is λύτρον, ours is either τιμωρία, or δοκιμασία, or μαρτυρίον. Christ suffered, the just for the unjust; we are not perfectly just by reason of inherent or actual justice, but are still contaminated by the filth of sins. Christ suffered that he might bring us to GOD; we are led through sufferings into the kingdom of heaven.Actor. 14. Vers. 22. Christ is the leader of the way, and he has opened the way for us; we follow him with the Spirit leading, through whom he draws us to himself and after himself.

32. Thence and therefore Christ was able to suffer for the unjust. 1. Because he is just, i. e. he is immune from every stain of sin. If by his own sins he had been contaminated, he could by no means have washed away the sins of others. 2. Because He is Christ, that is, θεάνθρωπος GOD and man in the unity of person, for the name of Christ embraces both the anointing Deity and the anointed humanity.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quid per sanctificationem DEI intelligatur? Resp. 1. Beda in h. l. sic commentatur. Quid est Deum sanctificare in cordibus nostris, nisi sanctitatem eius, quàm incomprehensibilis gloriae sit, intimo cordis affectu intueri? 2. Fulgentius lib. 2. ad Thrasimundum cap. 14. Is Christum sanctificat, qui de Christo, quae sancta sunt, cogitat; quae cogitatio cogitantem sanctificat, & sanctificando conservat. Confirmat hoc ex Cypriano, qui petitionem illam orationis Dominicae, Sanctificetur nomen tuum, ita declarat, ut nobis donum sanctificationis divinae conferatur, atque ut qui in Baptismo sanctificati sumus, in eo quod esse coepimus, per severemus. Eodem modo orationem Dominicam exponit Ambrosius lib. 5. de Sacram. c. 4. Quid est sancrificetur nomen tuum? Quasi optemus, ut sanctificetur ille, qui ait. Estote sancti, quia ego sanctus sum, q. aliquid ei ex nostra precatione sanctificationis accedat? Non; sed sanctificetur in nobis, ut ad nos eius sanctificatio possit pervenire. 3. Augustinus lib. 2. de serm. Dom. in monte, Bernh. serm. 6. quadrag. sic explicant. Quando petimus sanctificari nomen DEI, tùm hoc petimus, ut innotescat omnibus nomen DEI, & ab omnibus sanctificetur. 4. Haec omnia suo quidem loco rectè dicuntur, interim manifestum est, cum variis modis DEUS sanctificetur, Petrum συνεκδοχικῶς certum sanctificationis modum hîc intelligere. Lyranus igitur explicationem quaerit in verbis sequentibus, & exponit hanc sanctificationem Dei de benè firmanda fide in cordibus, unde postea fiat, ut satisfacere possimus obiicientibus contra eam. Dominum, inquit, sanctificate, i. e. firmate, sanctum enim in una significatione idem est quod firmum. 5. Sed ex praecedente antithesi, terrorem eorum ne timueritis, nec conturbemini; & ex addito προσδιορισμῷin cordibus vestris, rectiùs colligitur explicatio, cum in textu Hebraeo Esa. 8. v. 13. addatur. Dominum exercituum sanctificate, ipse sit timor vester, & pavor vester. Sensus igitur hic est. Sanctificate DEUM in cordibus vestris per veram fiduciam in DEI omnipotentiam, ac paternum eius praesidium: filiali fiduciâ in eius bonitatem recumbite, certò persuasi, ipsum sinceros sui cultores & intrepidos nominis sui confessores contra iniurias malorum hominum tueri & velle & posse. Hac fiducia cordis DEUS sanctificatur. 1. Quia in iudiciis suis rectus & sanctus agnoscitur, quando iusto suo iudicio malorum hominum iniuriis & violentiae nos exponit, etiamsi id non videamur gravioribus delictis promeriti. Psal. 119. v. 137. Lutherus in comm. h. l. Quando bonum & sanctum duco, quicquid à DEO immittitur, tunc sanctifico ipsum. 2. Quia hac ratione laus veritatis, sapientiae & bonitatis ipsi tribuitur, quòd promissa sua servare, nosque clementer tueri velit, & modum auxilii invenite possit.

Q. 2. Quare addat Apostolus, sanctificate Dominum in cordibus vestris? Resp. 1. Ut nos deducat ad interiorem cordis fiduciam, quâ praecipuè sanctificatur DEUS. 2. Ut ostendat, externam sanctificationem sine interna nihil prodesse.

Q. 3. Quo modo ad fidei rationem reddendam parati esse debeamus? Resp. Beda in h. l. Duobus modis de spe & fide nostra rationem poscentibus reddere debemus, ut & iustas fidei ac spei nostrae causas omnibus intimemus, sive fideliter sive infideliter quaerentibus, & ipsam fidei ac spei nostrae professionem illibatam semper teneamus, etiam inter pressuras adversantium, ostendentes per patientiam, quam rationabiliter eam servandam didicerimus, pro cuius amore nec adversa pati, nec mortem subire formidemus.

Q. 4. Quare Petrus fidei confessionem vocet Apologiam? Resp. 1. Quia tùm temporis infame erat Christianorum nomen. Vocabatur à gentilibus & Iudaeis secta nefaria, ac multa Christianis obiiciebantur crimina, ut monuimus superiùs cap. 2. vers. 12. 2. Quia ipsis fidei Christianae articulis multa obiiciebantur ab adversariis, quibus à Confessoribus Apologeticum responsum erat opponendum. Oecumenius in h. l. Quoniam gentiles spem Christianorum vanam esse dicebant, ideò Christiani meditatas responsiones in promtu habere debebant, ad refellendas eorum calumnias convenientes.

Q. 5. Quare Chrysostomus homil. 34. in Matth. hanc sententiam, parati ad defensionem omni poscenti vos rationem spei &c. Christo tribuat? Quidam hîc agnoscunt ἁμάρτημα μνημονευτικὸν, cum homil. 16. in Ioh. eam Petro rectè tribuat. Commodiùs respondetur, Chrysostomum respectum habere ad causam principalem, per Petrum enim Christus nobis loquitur Luc. 10. v. 16. Apostoli in praedicatione fuerunt os Christi, in scriptione manus Christi. Item ad cognatam Christi sententiam Matth. 10. v. 32. & 33.

Q. 6. Quare bonam conscientiam & conversationem Apostolus ad fidei consessionem requiratv. 16.? Resp. 1. quia conscientia bona loquendi praebet fiduciam. Actor. 23. v. 1. 2. Confessionis veritas nititur fundamento verbi divini, ad eiusdem normam quoque vita conformanda, utrumque si nobis curae, cordique erit, conscientiam habebimus bonam. Ut enim bona conscientia habeatur, necesse est, ut fidei & actionum nostrarum fundamentum ponamus DEI verbum. 3. Si vita professioni fidei non respondeat, non modo nullus fructus, sed etiam scandalum atque incommodum sequetur. Psal. 50. v. 16.Impio dixit Deus, cur recitas statuta mea, & assumis testamentum meum per os tuum. 4. Paulus itidem 1. Tim. 1. v. 5.cor purum, conscientiam bonam, & fidem non fictam coniungit, ac disertè addit v. 6.eos, qui ab his aberrant, convertiεἰς ματαιολογίαν cap. eiusd. v. 19. iterum coniungit fidem & bonam conscientiam, ac disertè addit, eos, qui repellunt bonam conscientiam, circa fidem naufragium facere.

Q. 7. An confusio calumniatorum in hoc seculo vel in die iudicii secutura significetur? Beda in comm. utramque explicationem coniungit. Conscientiam, inquit, habentes bonam, ut qui fidem ac spem coelestium, quam videre nequeunt, in vobis irrident, videant opera vestra bona, & per haec confundantur, quae apertè esse bona, negare non valent. Vel certè ita sentiendum. Curate benefacientes, ut qui vestrae bonae conversationi detrahunt, adveniente tempore retributionis futurae confundantur, videntes vos cum Christo coronari, sese autem cum Diabolo damnari. Nimirum confusio calumniatorum certissimè sequetur in die iudicii, Sap. 5. vers. 2. interim DEUS etiam in hac vita variis modis piorum inno centiam in lucem producit, & calumniatores eorum pudore afficit, ut ostendimus superiùs in explicat. cap. 2. v. 12. q. 6.

Q. 8. Quo sensu bona piorum conversatio dicatur esse in Christo? Resp. 1. quia iuxta Christi doctrinam instituitur. Eph. 4. v. 17.Hoc dico & testificor in Domino, ut iam non ambuletis, sicut & gentes ambulant in vanitate sensus sui &c.v. 19.qui seipsos tradiderunt impudicitiae &c.v. 20.Vos autem non ita didicistis Christum.v. 21.Si tantùm illum audistis, & in ipso edocti estis, sicut est veritas in Iesu. 2. quia in religione Christiana vita haec lancta ducitur. 3. quia non solùm Christo doctore & autore, sed etiam Christo ductore & directore agitur. Spiritus Christi, qui credentibus in Christum datur, impellit eos ad bonorum operum studium. 4. Sicut Christus de bonis operibus piorum dicit, quòd sint facta in Deo,Iohan. 3. v. 21. quia proficiscuntur à Dei Spiritu, quia Deo teste fiunt, quia iuxta normam mandati divini fiunt, quia ad Dei gloriam sunt directa, sicque efficienter, finaliter & obiectivè sunt in Deo facta: ita quoque Petrus dicit, sanctam piorum conversationem institui in Christo iisdem ferè respectibus.

Q. 9. Quare satiùs sit benefacientes, quàm malefacientes pati? Resp. 1. qui ob benefacta patitur, fruitur pacata conscientiâ; qui ob malefacta, sentit lancinantis conscientiae morsus. 2. qui patienter tolerat poenam, ob peccata sibi inflictam, non destituitur quidem patientiae suae praemio: interim longè maiora manebunt eos praemia, qui iniurias & adversitates, ob fidei confessionem vel iustitiae studium, adeoque praeter meritum, imò contra meritum sibi illatas, patienter tolerant. 3. Qui benefacientes sive ob benefacta patiuntur, magis conformantur CHRISTO, & sanctis Dei hominibus. Psalm. 44. vers. 22.Roman. 8. vers. 36.Propter te mortificamur totâ die, aestimati sumus velut oves occisionis.Matth. 5. vers. 10.Beati, qui per secutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam &c.v. 11.Beati estis, cum maledixerint vobis homines, & persecuti vos fuerint, & dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes propter me.vers. 12.gaudete & exultate &c. sic enim persecuti sunt Prophetas, qui fueruntante vos. 2. Cor. 4. v. 11.semper nos, qui vivimus, in mortem tradimur propter Iesum, ut & vita Iesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali1. Tim. 4. v. 10.In hoc laboramus & maledicimur, quod speramus in Deum vivum. Inde etiam Petrus confirmationis loco statim subiicit. Quia & Christus passus est pro peccatis, iustus pro iniustis quidem eius exemplo, imò imagini conformamini, si benefacientes sive ob benefacta passiones sustineatis. 4. Beda idipsum probat exemplis trium personarum, quae in Scripturis dicuntur coecitate percussae. Ut flagellorum, inquit, distantia in disparibus meritis longè dispar appareat, videamus unà eademque coecitatis molestiâ Tobiam, Saulum, Elymam fuisse percussos. Sed Tobiam ob hoc, ut virtus patientiae eius latiùs in exemplum cunctis claresceret.Tob. 2. v. 11. & seqq. Saulum ob hoc, ut de Saulo persecutore in Paulum mutaretur Apostolum.Actor. 9. v. 8.Elymam verò, ut dignas suae perfidiae poenas luens, ab eorum quoque qui credituri erant, dementatione cessaret.Act. 13. v. 11.Et mihi si detur optio, malim cum tanto patre (Tobia) sive divinis sive humanis subiacere iustus verberibus, quàm ab iniustitia verborum vi ad iustitiae studia trahi: rursumque malim à culpa flagello retrahi, (cum Paulo) quàm pro insanabili pondere peccatorum aeternae ultioni subiici (cum Elyma.) Glossa ordin. ad h. l. sic annotat. Qui iustus patitur, Christum imitatur. Qui flagellis corripitur, latronem imitatur, qui cum Christo in cruce cognito Paradisum intravit. Qui nec flagellis corrigitur, sinistrum latronem imitatur, qui propter peccata ascendit in crucem, & post crucem ivit in tartara.

Q. 10. Quare addat Apostolus, si voluntas Dei velit? Resp. 1. ut ostendat, malos nihil adversi vel incommodi piis afferre posse, nisi Deus permittat & frenum quasi ipsis laxet. 2. ut moneat, pios non debere respicere ad causas secundas, sed ad primam causam, ac quaecunque ipsis obtingunt bona vel mala, prospera vel adversa, velut ex Dei manu, grato & promto animo suscipere. Iob. 1. vers. 21.Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit.Sir. 11. vers. 14.Bona & mala, vita & mors, paupertas & divitiae à Deo sunt. 3. ut doceat, quòd non debeamus temerè nobis ipsis tribulationes accersere, vel malis sponte nos obiicere.

Q. 11. Quare Apostolus geminatè loquatur. Si voluntas Dei velit? Resp. 1. voluntas Dei quandoque significat beneplacitum Dei. Ps. 30. vers. 6.Vita in voluntate eiusvers. 8.in voluntate tua sive iuxta beneplacitum suum constituisti montem meum roboreMalachiae 1. vers. 10.Non est mihi voluntas in vobis. Innuit ergò Apostolus, bono ac salutari Dei consilio piis crucem immitu. 2. significat, DEO non solùm permittente, sed etiam volente immitti calamitates. Neque enim permittit invitus vel coactus, sed volens. 3. Dei voluntas non est aliquid realiter distinctum ab essentia, sed Dei voluntas est ipse Deus volens. Quando ergò Apostolus dicit, si voluntas Dei velit, sensus est, si Deus velut, si Deus bona suâ voluntate statuat, vobis passiones immittendas esse.

Q. 12. Quare notanter addat Apostolus, Christum semel passum esse? Resp. 1. ut ostendat passionis Christi brevitatem, quam statim secuta est aeterna gloria, in quo latet argumentum exhortationis ad patientiam, ut ostendimus superiùs. 2. ut perfectionem sacrificii à Christo in passione & cruce oblati ostendat, qua in parte sacrificiis legalibus quotidiè iterandis illud opponitur. Hebr. 7. v. 27.cap. 9. vers. 12.25. & seqq. cap. 10. vers. 1. & seqq. 3. ut doceat, Christum non amplius passioni ac morti fore obnoxium, sed ut victorem mortis ad Dei dextram in aeternum regnare. Roman. 6. vers. 9. & 10.

Q. 13. Quare notanter addat, Christum esse passum iustum pro iniustis Resp. 1. ut eò efficacius sit argumentum exhortationis. Sic enim à maiori ad minus concludit Apostolus. Si Christus cùm esset perfectissimè iustus, non dubitavit pro iniustis pati, quantò minùs nos passiones in hac vita debemus recusare, cum non simus omnibus modis innocentes. 2. ut commendet Christi erga nos caritatem & patris coelestis benignitatem. Rom. 5. vers. 8.Commendat Deus caritatem suam erga nos, quoniam cum adhuc peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est.Gal. 2. v. 20.Christus dilexit me & tradidit seipsum pro me.Apoc. 1. v. 5.Christus dilexit nos & lavit nos à peccatis nostris suo sanguine. ut causam exponat, quare passio Christi potuerit expiare nostra peccata, nimirum quia ipse fuit perfectissimè iustus ac in personae unitate Dei filius. Hebr. 7. v. 27.Talis decebat ut esset nobis Pontifex sanctus, innocens, impollutus &c.

Q. 14. Quâ ratione Christus dicatur ideò passus, ut nos Deo adduceret? Si verbum προσάγειν accipiatur in significatione sacrificandi, tribus modis Christus in passione & per passionem suam nos Deo adduxit, quos superiùs in expositione textus recensuimus. Si usitata significatio verbi προσάγειν retinetur; potest haec adductio referri. 1. ad tempus praeteritum. Christus ideò passus est, ut nos Deo adduceret i. e. ut nos Patri suo coelesti reconciliaret, hanc enim reconcialitionem cum Patre coelesti esse effectum sive fructum passionis & mortis Christi, constat ex Rom. 5. v. 10.2. Cor. 5. v. 19.Eph. 2. vers. 16.Col. 1. vers. 20. Potest huc accommodari typus Exod. 19. v. 17.Moses tanquam V. T. Mediator in promulgatione legis adducebat populum Israëliticum in occursum Dei, velut Sponsam ad Sponsum, ut Rabini ad illum locum annotant: Christus Mediator N. T. adduxit nos in sua passione ac per suam passionem ad Deum, factus nobis Sponsus sanguinumExod. 4. v. 25. ut nos DEO reconciliaret, à quo in Sponsam dilectam reciperemur. 2. ad tempus praesens. Christus ideò passus, ut nos Deo quotidie adduceret, ut per ipsum tanquam Mediatorem divinitùs constitutum habeamus aditum in precibus nostris Rom. 5. v. 1.Iustificati fide pacem habemus ad Deum per Dominum nostrum I. C.v. 2.per quem habemus accessum fide in gratiam istam, in qua stamus. Confer Ephes. 2. v. 18.c. 3. v. 12. Ipse enim solus est via, per quam possumus ad Deum accedere, nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per ipsumIoh. 14. v. 6. Eâ etiam ratione Christus nos quotidie adducit, quatenus per Spiritum suum sanctum peccatum in nobis mortificat, ac similitudine morum & affectuum Deo nos propinquos reddit, quae tamen renovatio ac imaginis divinae reformatio in hac vita est tantùm inchoata. 3. ad tempus futurum. Christus ideò passus est, ut aliquando in die iudicii nos sisteret Patri suo perfectè renovatos & gloriosos, ac in vitam aeternam secum introduceret, cum Deo in aeternum victuros in summa felicitate ac gloria. 1. Cor. 15. v. 24.cùm tradiderit regnum Deo & patriEphes. 5. v. 26.Christus dilexit Ecclesiam & seipsum tradidit pro ea,v. 27.ut illam sanctificaret, mundans lavacro aquae in verbo.v. 28.ut exhiberet ipsam sibi gloriosam, Ecclesiam non habentem maculam aut rugam, aut aliquid huiusmodi, sed ut sit sancta & immaculata. Ad hunc locum Pauli videtur Petrus verbo προσάγειν simul respexisse. In hac vita offert nos Christus Deo tanquam sacrificium, dum gratia & Spir. suo peccatum in nobis mortificat. In futura vita offeret tanquam holocaustum, quando peccatum penitus erit abolitum, ac perfectè renovati Deo serviemus.

Q. 15. Quare Petrus denuò passionis Dominicae mentionem faciat? Iam antè aliquoties in hac Epistola passionis Christi meminerat.

cap. 1. 2. & 19.cap. 2. v. 21. & seqq. ac porrò eiusdem mentione facturus erat c. 4. v. 1. & 13. quo ipso ostendit, se non posse satiari commemoratione passionis Dominicae, unde se vocat testem passionum Christi cap. 5. v. 1. Passio enim Christi non solùm est redemtionis nostrae meritum, & omnis vivificae consolationis fundamentum, sed etiam perfectissimum omnium virtutum Christianarum exemplum, quod imitatione nostra in hac vita non possumus perfectè exprimere.

Q. 16. An per Spiritum intelligatur Spiritus sanctus, tertia Deitatis persona? Ita statuit Athanasius, citatus à Beda in comm. h. l. qui Spiritus sancti divinitatem ex his Petri verbis probat. Sanè hoc inquit, quod dicitur vivificatus Spiritu sancto, Athanasius Alexandriae Pontifex non ad hominis Spiritum, qui mortificatâ carne meliùs vivificatur, dicente Propheta de Domino, ut vivificet Spiritum humilium & vivificet cor contritorum: sed ad gratiam potiùs refert Spiritus sancti, qui mortificantibus carnem suam vitam tribuit aeternam. Utitur enim & hoc testimonio contra Arianos, qui aequalitati S. Trinitatis contradicunt, astruens, quia individuâ operationis unitate, quâ vivificat Pater, vivificet Filius, vivificet Spiritus sanctus; Pater videlicet & Filius; quia scriptum est. Sicut enim pater suscitat mortuos, & vivificat: Sic & Filius, quos vult, vivificat. Spiritus vero sanctus, ut hoc testimonio declaratur, quo dicitur de Filio, ut nos offerret Deo, mortificatos quidem carne, vivificatos autem Spiritu. Ideoque quorum una operatio, horum dispar esse substantia vel essentia non potest. Resp. 1. ex opere vivificationis Spiritui sancto attributo Rom. 8. vers. 11. rectè probatur Spiritus sancti divinitas, eiusdemque cum Patre & Filio aequalitas. 2. hoc autem loco non agitur de vivificatione, quâ nos per Spiritum sanctum vivificamur, vel ad vitam spiritualem, vel ad vitam corporalem; sed de vivificatione, quâ Christus ex mortuis vivificatus est. 3. Ab hac vivificatione ac resuscitatione non quidem excludi potest Spiritus sanctus, cum sit eiusdem essentiae & potentiae cum Patre & Spiritu sancto, ac proinde, ut Pater Christum resuscitavit, ut Christus seipsum resuscitavit, ita quoque Spiritus sanctus Christum resuscitavit, ut colligi potest ex Rom. 8. v. 11. 4. Interim Spiritus nomen hoc loco non accipitur determinatè pro tertia Trinitatis persona, sed indeterminatè pro Deitate ac divina virtute, quae Patri, Filio & Spiritui sancto communis est. Nam & hîc locum habet regula Nazianzeni orat. 4. de Theol. Id, quod agit, est una tribus personis communis Deitas. 5. Quòd si determinatè nomen Spiritus accipere velimus, de divina Natura Filii potiùs accipiendum, ut ostendit antithesis. Christus mortificatus est carne, i. e. secundùm humanam Naturam passus est & mortuus: sed vivificatus est Spiritu, id est, divinâ suâ Naturâ seipsum ex mortuis resuscitavit, quâ tamen determinatione nec Pater nec Spiritus sanctus excluduntur, quippe unius & eiusdem cum Filio essentiae, aequalis potentiae & gloriae.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Sanctificate Dominum Deum in cordibus vestris.v. 15. At Ex. 31. v. 13.Ego Dominus, qui sanctifico vos. Resp. Aliter sanctificat Deus hominem; aliter homo sanctificat Deum, Deus sanctificat hominem effectivè, sanctum illum faciendo; homo sanctificat Deum obiectivè ac relativè, sanctum illum agnoscendo ac praedicando, honorem sanctitatis ei tribuendo, promissis eius tanquam veracis & sancti fidem habendo.

2. Parati semper ad defensionem.v. 15. Atqui 1. Cor. 12. v. 28.Nunquid omnes doctores.Tit. 1. v. 9.à solo Episcopo requiritur, ut sit potens, & exhortari in doctrina sana, & eos, qui contradicunt arguere. Resp. quilibet pro modo vocationis & donorum debet fidei suae rationem reddere, ac de iis, quae ad fidei confessionem pertinent, interrogantibus respondere. Ut in vita naturali staturae corporeae: ita quoque in vita spirituali cognitionis Christi dantur certi gradus & incrementa. Ephes. 4. v. 13. & 14. August. lib. 14. de Trin. cap. 1. Scientiâ, quâ fides defenditur, non pollent fideles plurimi, quamvis polleant ipsâ fide plurimum. Aliud est enim scire tantummodo, quid homo credere debeat propter adipiscendam vitam beatam, quae non nisi aeterna est: aliud autem scire, quemadmodum hoc ipsum & piis opituletur, & contra impios defendatur, quam proprio vocab. scientiam appellare videtur Apostolus. 1. Cor. 12. v. 8.

3. Parati ad defensionem omni petenti rationem. At Matth. 7. v. 6.Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque margaritas porcis. Resp. parati quidem debent esse pii ad fidei suae rationem reddendam omni petenti, interim actu ipso tùm demum fidei suae rationem reddant, si gloria divini nominis illud requirat, ac fructus inde speretur, vel in eo, cui respondetur, vel in aliis. Quando interrogantur ab illis, qui sunt empactae ac virulenti blasphematores veritatis, tunc locum habet regula Christi. Nolite sanctum dare canibus. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 2. στρωματ. f. 156. Sancta canibus impertiri vetamur, quamdiu bestiae manserint. Neque enim convenit, ut iis, qui quantum ad mores sunt invidi, perturbati, etiamnum infideles & impudentes ad latratum adversus quaestionem propositam, divinum & purum fluentum aquae vivae infundatur. Inde Paulus Col. 4. v. 5. praecipit, ut pii in sapientia ambulent ad eos, qui foris sunt, tempus redimentes, acv. 6.ut sermo ipsorum semper sit in gratia sale conditus, ut sciant, quomodo oporteat eos unicuique respondere; in quae verba Chrysostomus homil. 11. in Epist. ad Coloss. sic commentatur. Propterea adiicitur ad eos, qui foris sunt, ut discamus, quòd adversus nostra membra non tantâ nobis opus est cautione, quantâ adversus extraneos. Non sunt enim pariae etiam inter inimicos & hostes, & inter amicos.

4. Estote semper parati ad defensionem omni petenti rationem eius, quae in vobis est spei.v. 15. At Matth. 10. v. 19.Marc. 13. v. 11.Luc. 12. v. 11.Cùm duxerint vos ad praesides, nolite praemeditari, quomodo aut quid loquamini, dabitur enim vobis in illa hora. Resp. prohibet Christus nimiam solicitudinem cum diffidentia & pusillanimitate coniunctam; Petrus requirit debitam praeparationem, cum fiducia divini auxilii coniunctam. Oecumenius ex Chrysostomo homil. 34. in Matth. respondet, Dominum in Evangelio de Martyrio locutum, Petrum autem de doctrina extra tamen Martyrii causam. Sed & Petri & Christi praeceptum generale est, non solùm tempus Martyrii, sed etiam confessionis respiciens. Certè Petrus v. 14. praeced. expressè mentionem fecerat persecutorum, ac in hoc ipso loco disertè dicit. Estote semper parati. Ergò etiam tempore Martyrii.

5. Meliùs est benefacientes pati, quàm malefacientesvers. 17.At graviùs peccat, qui praeter, imò contra meritum alteri iniurias infert. Resp. loquitur Apostolus de eo, qui patitur, non qui infert passionem. Qui benefacientem praeter meritum iniuriâ afficit, sibiipsi longè magis nocet.

6. Christus pro peccatis mortuus est, iustus pro iniustis, ut nos Deo offerret. AtHeb. 9. v. 14.Christus per Spiritum aeternum seipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo.Iohan. 17. v. 19.Ego meipsum sanctifico pro eis. Resp. Christus seipsum Patri coelesti in sacrificium offerendo etiam credentes in se sanctificatos Deo obtulit, & Patri suo coelesti eos reconciliavit. Proinde ut ipse mortificatus carne, vivificatus spiritu, ita quoque pios oportet carne mortificari: Spiritu autem vivificari, ut sint gratum Deo sacrificium.Rom. 6. v. 4.cap. 12. v. 1.

7. Christus mortificatus carne, vivificatus Spiritu. Atqui non solùm vivificatio, sed etiam oblatio in morte facta est per Spiritum.Hebr. 9. v. 14. Resp. aliud est mori, aliud pro peccatis rotius mundi mori, sive quod idem est, offerre se in sacrificium pro peccatis totius mundi. Illud est humanae Naturae proprietas, cuius respectu Christus rectè dicitur mortificatus carne. Hoc vero est actio θεανδρικὴ, ac tale ἀποτέλεσμα, ad quod utriusque Naturae ἐνέργεια concurrit, cuius respectu Christus per Spiritum aeternum semetipsum DEO obtulisse dicitur.

Ἒλενχος. 1. Apostolus pios semper paratos esse iubet ad fidei rationem reddendam. Errant igitur Helcesaitae, qui referente Origene in Psalm. 82. & ex eo Eusebio lib. 6. Hist. Eccles. cap. 37. indifferens esse dicebant, sive quis consiteatur, sive neget, & eum qui intelligit, in necessitatibus ore negaturum, non corde.

2. Estote semper parati ad defensionem. Errant ergò Iesuitae, quando in Colloquio Ratisbonensi suam de iudice controversiarum aperire sententiam diu fuêre tergiversati. Cumque eis opponeretur hic locus Apostolicus, responderunt, fidei quidem rationem reddendam, sed quando necessarium sit: tunc autem esse necessarium, quando Magistratus id exegerit, ut ex Relatione Tanneri constat. Eodem fere modo Perkinsus lib. 2. de casibus consc. cap. 13. q. 1. sensum dicti Apostolici hunc esse scribit, tùm demum rationem fidei esse reddendam, quando ab iis, qui in autoritate constituti sunt, velut à Principibus examinantur. Sed verba Apostoli sunt clarissima, quòd fidei ratio sit reddenda cuilibet petenti, modò rem seriam agat in loco ac tempore competente. Nam ut cuivis tentatori & exploratori respondeatur, quod Perkinsus obiicit, vel ut à dormiente, vel cibum capiente id fiat, ut Tannerus nugatur, necesse non est, quod quilibet intelligit.

3. Etiam Laici, quos ita vocant, parati esse debent ad rationem fidei reddendam. Praeceptum enim Petri generale est, non solùm ad Ecclesiae Ministros, sed etiam ad auditores pertinens. Errant ergò Pontificii, qui Laicos à Scripturae lectione & controversiarum diiudicatione arcent, ac fide tantùm implicitâ eos contentos esse iubent. Excipit Salmero tom. 16. Disput. 5. in 1. Petr. 1.Hoc praeceptum non omnibus competere, sed quibusdam, etiam Laicis ex dono DEI, qui noverunt de fide propositis quaestionibus respondere. Alioquin ad Episcopos, Praedicatores & Sacerdotes spectare. Resp. quamvis sint gradus divinae cognitionis, ac discretio Spirituum, ut & sermo scientiae, quâ fides adversus haereticos propugnatur, sit peculiare donum Spiritus sancti 1. Corinth. 12. v. 8. & 10. tamen suo modo ac modulo etiam auditoribus competit cavere sibi à Pseudoprophetis, ac proinde ex fructibus eos cognoscere.Matth. 7. v. 15. & 16.observare eos, qui dissensiones & offendicula praeter doctrinam, quam didicerunt, faciunt, & ab illis declinare,Roman. 16. v. 17.omnia probare, quod bonum est, tenere1. Thessal. 5. vers. 21.probare Spiritus an sint ex DEO,1. Iohan. 4. v. 1. exemplo Beroënsium à Spiritu sancto laudatorum, qui quotidiè scrutabantur Scripturas, an haec ita se haberent, quae à Paulo & Barnaba ipsis annunciabantur.Actor. 17. v. 11. 2. In Ecclesia primitiva omnes fere praedicatores extitisse, quia gratiam Spiritus sancti, ac donum linguarum acceperant,Actor. 2.& erant per diversa loca dispersi, ut fidem illam in alios spargerent & propagarent. Resp. in Ecclesia primitiva non fuit sublatum discrimen praedicatorum & auditorum, sed in ea itidem locum habuit illud Apostolicum 1. Corinth. 12. v. 29.Nunquid omnes DoctoresEphes. 4. v. 11.Posuit alios Pastores & Doctores. Quamvis vero pii in primitiva Ecclesia extraordinario modo peculiarium Spiritus sancti donorum participes fuerint facti, Actor. 10. vers. 44. & 46. quae hodiè non habent locum in omnibus Christianis, tamen vocatio generalis omnium Christianorum hoc requirit, ut per media ordinaria, videl. per studiosum verbi auditum, lectionem, meditationem, ac pias preces fundamentalium fidei articulorum notitiam sibi acquirant, eamque pro modo suae vocationis, & pro mensura Spiritus sibi dati ex verbo Dei propugnent. 3. Haec verba ad eos tantùm referenda esse, qui id quod praecipitur, praestare possunt, ut cum Iohannes 1. Epist. 4. ait, probate Spiritus, si ex DEO sint, non omnes alloquitur. Eódem tendit illud, omnia probate, quod bonum est tenete.1. Thess. 5. Resp. imò vero praecepta haec sunt generalia, quae ad omnes Christianos spectant, cum utraque Epistola omnibus Christi fidelibus sit inscripta. Omnes ergò pio studio conari debent, ut hoc praestare possint. Possumus hoc probare ex ipso iure Canonico. c. Oves caus. 2. q. 7. ex Eusebio Papa. Oves, qui pasiori suo commissae sunt, eum non reprehendere, nisi à recta fide exorbitaverit, debent. c. Sicuti caus. & quaest. iisdem. A Laicis Clerici meritò quandoque reprehenduntur. c. Nolite caus. 11. q. 3. ex Chrysostomo. Sicut Sacerdos debitor est, ut veritatem, quam audivit à Deo, liberè praedicet: sic Laicus debitor est, ut veritatem, quam audivit quidem à Sacerdotibus probatam in Scripturis defendat fiducialiter. Atqui si oves Pastorem â recta fide exorbitantem reprehendere debent, utique oportet eas esse gnaras Scripturae, ut de doctrina Pastoris iudicium ferre possint. Si Laicus veritatem, quam audivit probatam in Scripturis, fiducialiter defendere debet utique attendere debet, an quod Sacerdos praedicat, in Scripturis probetur. Cornelius à Lapide excipit. Petrus responsionem exigit, non disput ationem, eamque dandam infidelibus in origine Ecclesiae, non haereticis confirmata iam fide omnium seculorum consensu. Resp. imò vero ὰπολογίαν Petrus requirit, quae locum non habet, ubi fidei fundamentum nondum est cognitum. Iubet etiam pios ad apologiam paratos esse semper & omni poscenti. Ergò etiam haeretico & hac nostra aetate.

4. Apostolus dicit, melius esse benefacientes pati, si voluntas Dei velit, quàm malefacientesv. 17. Errantigitur, qui sponte sibi accersunt tribulationes, ut olim Circumcelliones ac Donatistae, hodie Anabaptistae & Monachi superstitiosi.

5. Apostolus dicit, Christum esse passumv. 18. Christi nomen, est nomen personae. Falsum ergò est, quod Calviniani statuunt, passionem Christi esse solius carnis passionem. Orthod. cons. p. 18. & 122. Quamvis enim in primo genere communicationis idiomatum passiones & actiones, quae in Scripturis Christo tribuuntur, distinguantur ex diversitate Naturarum, ex quibus persona Christi constat Rom. 1. v. 3. & 4.cap. 9. v. 5.1. Tim. 3. v. 16.1. Petr. 4. v. 1. tamen ob personae unitatem de Christo & divina & humana verè & propriè praedicantur. Athanasius apud Cyrill. in Apol. Sicut proprium Domini dicimus esse corpus, ita & corporis passiones propriae eius dicuntur, etiamsi non contingant secundum divinitatem eius, alioqui alterius esset corpus, alterius dicerentur passiones. Si autem caro Verbi caro est, necessarium & passiones carnis dici eius, cuius & caro est. Vigil. lib. 2. contra Eutych. Theodoret, Dial. 3. Quae sunt propria Naturarum, siunt communia personae.

6. Christus dicitur semel passus. Falsum igitur est, quòd Origenes dicitur sensisse, ut est in v. Synodo & refert Niceph. l. 17. Hist. Eccl. c. 27. Christum iterum ac saepius passurum in aëre pro Daemonibus, Hieron. ad Avitum de Origene sic scribit: Ad extremum intulit, quòd & cogitasse sacrilegium est, pro salute Damonum Christum etiam in aere & in supernis locis esse passurum.

7. Christus semel passus est, h. e. non habet necessitatem quotidiè, quemadmodum Sacerdotes V. T. priùs pro suis delictis hostias offerre, deinde pro populi, hoc enim fecit semel se offerendo, Hebr. 7. v. 27.per proprium sanguinem introivit semel in sancta aeternâ redemtione inventâHebr. 9. v. 12.semel in consummatione seculorum ad destructionem peccati per hostiam suam apparuit.v. 26.Unâ oblatione consummavit in sempiternum sanctificatos.Hebr. 10. v. 14.Ergò non opus est, ut denuò in Missa offeratur. In eo ipso enim Sacrificium, Christi opponitur sacrificiis Levit cis, quòd illa quotidiè repetebantur, Christus autem semel fuerit oblatus. Ambrosius lib. 10. in Lucam ex h. l. Apostolico probat, fructum mortis Christi esse perpetuum. Christus, inquit, semel quidem pro peccato populi mortuus est, sed quotidiè peccata populi redemturus. Excipit Lorinus in h. l. Christus semel se obtulit oblatione cruenta in cruce, & pridiè quàm pateretur incruentè in Coenainstituendo Sacramentum Eucharistiae, ac relinquendo Ecclestae saecrificium visibite. Eandem hostiam offerimus quotidie per sacrificium incruentum, quia non potest Ecclesia consistere absque vero Sacerdotio & sacrificio, & decuit fieri quotidie memoriam eruenti & praeterea per dictam hostiae oblationem sive incruentum sacrificium fructus cruenti, quod fuit universalis ac sufficiens causa salutis omnium & remissionis peccatorum, magis magisque ad nos provenit, applicatur, efficientiam habet. Resp. 1. Distinctio inter sacrificium Christi cruentum & incruentum destituitur Scripturae fundamento. 2. Imò pugnat cum Scriptura, quippe quae unicum asserit externum & propriè dictum sacrificium, à Christo in cruce oblatum, celebrat duntaxat post illius sacrificii veri in cruce oblationem, eiusdem efficaciam, & Christi pro nobis intercessionem. Si sacrificium Christi in cruentum in prima Coena fuit propitiatorium pro peccatis mundi, quid opus erat sacrificio cruento in cruce? Ubi peccatorum remissio, ibi non ampliùs oblatio pro peccato.Hebr. 10. v. 18. Praeterea Scriptura pro oppositis habet incruentam, & tamen realem pro peccatis oblationem, quia absque sanguinis effusione negat fieri remissionem. Heb. 9. v. 1214. & 22. partâ quoque per Christum remissione negat ampliùs locum esse oblationi pro peccato. Hebr. 10. v. 18. 3. Eccelesiam non posse consistere absque externo & visibili sacrificio quotidie repetendo, falsum est. Sufficit in N. T. sacrificium Christi in cruce oblatum, quo finem imposuit omnibus externis V. T. sacrificiis. 4. Memoriam cruenti sacrificii in Ecclesia fieri concedimus. At commemoratio sacrificii non est statim visibile & externum sacrificium. 5. Fructus cruenti sacrificii applicatur nobis per verbum & Sacramenta, quae sunt media divinitùs instituta, non autem per aliud quoddam externum & visibile sacrificium.

8. Christus semel passus est pro peccatis h. e. perfectè pro omnibus totius mundi peccatis & pro omnibus peccatorum poenis satisfecit. Ergò non requiritur nostra satisfactio, quam tamen Pontificii exigunt. Excipiunt quidem, Christum pro culpa & poenaaeterna, nos pro poenis temporalibus satisfacere, Item Christi satisfactionem per nostram satisfactionem nobis applicari. Sed haec omnia continent principii petitionem & sibi mutuò adversantur,

9. Fructus passionis Christi non solùm est exemplum, sed etiam satisfactio pro peccatis ac meritum redemtionis. Dicitur enim passus pro peccatis, iustus pro iniustis, ut factâ peccatorum expiatione nos DEO reconciliaret. Errant ergò Photiniani, qui satisfactionem illam Christi passione praestitam protervè negant. Excipiunt, Christum dici pro peccatis nostris mortuum. Iam vero non potuisse loco seu vice peccatorum nostrorum mori. Ergò quando pro nobis mortuus dicitur, non loconostrûm, sed dunt axat nostri causa mortuus esse intelligitur. Resp. non est omninò eadem significatio particulae Pro in his propositionibus, Christus mortuus est pro nobis, &, Christus mortuus est pro peccatis nostris. In priori praepositio Pro additur personae, & exponitur τὸ ὑπὲρ, per τὸ ἀντὶ, quod propriè vicem alterius & permutationem notat. Matth. 20. v. 28.Marc. 10. v. 45. In posteriori additur rei, & exponitur per περὶ & ὑπέρ. Christus mortuus est pro nobis, ut nostro loco sese sisteret, ut poenas peccatorum nostrorum in se recipiendo nos redimeret: pro peccatis nostris mortuus est, ut ea expiaret & tolleret.

10. Ex eo, quòd Christus dicitur passus pro peccatis, ut nos Deo adduceret, Augustinus lib. 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. 7. & Epist. 99. contra Pelagianos probat, infantes non consequi salutem sine Baptismo & Christo. Posterius effatum generale esse admittimus, priori autem limitationem addimus, videlicet casum necessitatis extraordinarium esse excipiendum.

Ἐκδίκησις. 1. Lorinus in v. 1 sic commentatur. Quòd imperandi modo per sanctificate, indicat arbitrii libertatem, quemadmodum & formapetitionis, Sanctificetur nomen tuum, atque aliarum impersonaliter expressarum, cooperationem nostram cum gratia divina. Resp. agitur hîc de renatis, qui ita aguntur à Spiritu sancto, ut etiam ipsi agant. Cooperantur autem gratiae non naturalibus, sed novis à Spiritu sancto donatis viribus.

2. Ex eo quòd Petrus dicit, estote parati ad defensionem omni petenti rationem, colligit Salmero etiam rationem in rebus fidei quaerendam. Illud verum est, inquit, B. Petrum apud Clement. lib. 1. Recogn. tradidisse, optimum esse non tantùm fide apprehendere mysteria, quae in Scripturis continentur, sed etiam rationem aliquam habere ad confirmanda ea. Verba Petri haec sunt. Noli putare nos, quòd ex fide sola recipienda esse dicamus, sed ex ratione adferenda. Neque enim tutum est, nudaehaec fidei absque ratione committere, cum utique veritas ratione non careat. Et ideo qui haec ratione munita susceperit, perdere eam nunquam potest; qui vero absque assertionibus ea suscipit, simplicis sermonis assensu, neque servare ea tutò potest, neque, sivera sint, certus est, quia qui facilè credit, facilè & recedit: qui autem rationem quaesivit eorum, quae credidit & accepit, quasi vinculis quibusdam rationis ipsius colligatus, nunquam ab his, quae credidit, divelli aut separari potest. Et ideò quantò quis propensior fuerit, in expetenda ratione, tantò erit sirmior in conservanda fide. Resp. 1. libros Recognitionum meritò repudiant Sixtus Senensis lib. 2. Biblioth. in verbo Clemens; Baronius ann. 44. n. 42. ann. 51. n. 53. anno 102. num. 21. Iohan. Driedo de Eccles. dogm. & Script. part. 5. lib. 4. cap. 5. p. 602. Bellarminus lib. 2. de Rom. Pont. c. 2. Pererius in Genes. lib. 2. q. 1. &c. Inde Lorinus in h. l. adducturus idem dictum Clementis, praemittit Clemens Romanus, si tamen non alius potius in l. Recognit. inducit Petrum loquentem. 2. Per rationem in rebus fidei intelligitur vel articulorum fidei confirmatio ex Scripturis, vel eorundem probatio ex rationis principiis. In priore significatione coucedimus utile esse, imò etiam necessarium, rationes fidei in promtu habere. 3. Id quod meritò opponitur Pontificiis, qui carbonariam & implicitam fidem commendant. 4. In posteriore significatione rationis nomine accepto negamus, ea quae sunt merae & purae fidei, posse ex ratione probari, cum fides sit supra rationem. Alphonius de Castro lib. 5. advers. haeres. verbo DEUS, haeresi 5. Cùm Trinitatis & unitatis mysterium tàm aeltum sit, ut humanum & Angelicum superet intellectum, hîc oportet captivare intellectum nostrum sub obsequium fidei. Quapropter superfluum est, imò ridiculum, rationibus & argumentis hoc agere, sed solis Scripturarum testimoniis. Et postea. Quantò magis nitimur ad hoc mysterium solâ ratione investigandum, tantò minùs cognoscimus, & ob hoc ipsum Deum à nobis avolare facimus. 5. Audiat Salmero seipsum tom. 2. tract. 2. p. 5. ubi de mysterio Trinitatis sic disserit. Si quid sit, quod nobis contra rationem naturalem videatur, & tamen ad credendum proponatur, debemus operam dare, ut intellectum nostrum captivemus sub obsequium Christi. Ut enim sensus subiiciendus est rationi, & q. captivus cogendus in eius assensum: ita intellectus noster superiori fidei lumini cedere debet & obedire, ut magis certo ac maiori. tom. 15. Disput. 10. in cap. 11. Hebr. Non est necesse, ut examines ea, quae fidei sunt, & quae non videntur, ad exiguum iudicium & modicum lumen rationis humanae &c. Nam animalis homo non potest spiritualiter percipere, quae spiritualiter examinantur, id est, quae lumine spirituali debent examinari, & non rationis lumine. Ut enim bruta animantia, dum seipsa considerant, quae hominis & rationis sunt, capere non possunt, quia illa destituuntur, quae ipsis superior est: ad eum modum homo quamvis sagax & acutus, quae fidei sunt, & quorum ipsa est argumentum sive ostensio, percipere & coniectare non valet. 6. Sed & societatis suae hominem Bellarminum audiat lib. 2. de Sacram. cap. 11. § Adhaec. Tenemur quidem rationem reddere eius, quae in nobis est, spei1. Petr. 3.sed id facere tenemur ex principiis fidei, non ex Metaphysica. Nam 5. Augustinus lib. 3. de peccat. merit. & remis cap. 4. Ego, inquit, loquens de argumentis contra modum traductionis peccati originalis, etiamsi istorum argumenta solvere non valeam, video tamen inhaerendum esse divinis titeris. Et in Epist. 29. ad Hieron. dicit, se cum interrogatur, quomodo peccatum Adaeprogagetur in posteros, respondere solitum. Hoc ut alia multa, me ignorare confiteor.

3. Lorinus ad v. 15. sic annotat. Apologiam fidei condere, non nisi benè docti possunt ac etiam debent, cum nefas sit cuivis de rebus fidei cum adversariis disputare, ut eleganter ostendit Iacobus Simancas, multos citans de Cathol. Instit. tit. 20. Resp. concedimus, Apologiam fidei fundamentalem contra haereticos vel infideles condere, ad officium Doctoris Ecclesiae pertinere Tit. 1. v. 9. interim eiusmodi apologiam edere, qualem Petrus h. l. requirit, ad omnes omninò Christianos pertinet, unde Lorinus ipse statim subiungit. Iohannes mandat omnibus, ut probent Spiritus 1. Epist. 4. vers. 1. (observa hoc contra Salmeronem, idipsum negantem) & tamen Paulus discutionem Spirituum scribit peculiare quoddam donum esse,1. Cor. 12. v. 10.Pro modulo suo quisque Spiritus probare & rationem reddere debent, sed aliqui magis ex officio & perfectiùs utrumque faciunt.

4. Estius ad eundem vers. sic annotat. Non hoc ita accipiendum, ac si velit Petrus, omnes Christianos esse Theologos, qui norint de dogmatibus fidei, aut docendo, aut respondendo disserere. Sunt rationes quaedam generales, quibus utounque tueri se poterat quilibet Christianus adversus paganos, & quaerentibus satisfacere, velut quòd religio Christiana praenunciata sit à Prophetis, quòd innumeris miraculis à Christo & Apostolis eius confirmata, quòd doceat iustitiam, innocentiam & beneficientiam usque ad dilectionem inimicorum &c. Resp. non sufficit, generales quasdam rationes tenere, quibus Christiana religio defendatur, sed oportet etiam fundamentales fidei articulos unumquemque tenere, ac de iis rationem reddere posse. Praecipit enim Salvator, ut hunc in finem quilibet Scripturas scruteturIohan. 5. v. 39. exemplo Beroënsium, qui de singulis dogmatibus à Paulo & Barnaba propositis Scripturas consulebant,Actor. 17. vers. 11. Paulus praecipit, ut verbum DEI opulenter in nobis habitet in omni sapientiaColoss. 3. v. 16.ut omnia probentur, & ex omnibus quod bonum est teneatur.1. Thess. 5. v. 21. unde etiam gratias DEO agit, quòd Corinthii in omnibus divites facti in Christo in omni verbo & omni scientia1. Corint. 1. v. 5. ac David beatos pronunciat, qui in lege Domini meditantur die & noctePsalm. 1. v. 2. Quid quòd Estius ipse vi veritatis convictus subiungit. Quanquam & rationes sive argumenta quaedam magis specialia fidelibus ad respondendum in promtu esse, prout talium capaces sunt, vehementer expedit.

5. Idem Estius ibid. sic scribit. Ad hunc modum etiam hodiè nequaquam desunt rationes & argumenta generalia velut principia quaedam, quibus instructos esse oporteat fideles adversus haereticos fidem nostram Catholicam oppugnantes, aut de ea disputare volentes. Eam scil. Ecclesiam Christi esse unam, eamque visibilem manifestam; ab Apostolis ad vos usque successione Episcoporum continuatam, in qua tot sancti fuêre diversis temporibus Martyres & Confessores, quorum fanguine, doctrinâ, miraculis fides Catholica iam olim consignata sit atque sancita. Ad eam Ecclesiam audiendam, quòd ipsa columna sit, & firmamentum veritatis Scripturam sacram nos remittere, quod probat ex1. Ioh. 4. v. 1. & 6. Eodem ferè modo Cornelius à Lapide in h. l. Laicirogati ab haereticis, cur credant v. g. Christum esse praesentem in Eucharistia, respondeant, quia id credit & credidit Ecclesiae omni seculo, quae est columna & firmamentum veritatis. Resp. 1. Ecclesiam esse unam & visibilem, concedimus, sed visibilem Ecclesiam ab omni prorsùs errore perpetuò immunem fore, nuspiam promissum. 2. Potest Deus Catholicam electorum Ecclesiam, quae invisibilis est, conservare, etiamsi visibilis Ecclesia erroribus quibusdam ad tempus involvatur. 3. Romana Ecclesia nullam accepit promissionem de absoluto quodam non errandi privilegio. 4. Nec localis & personalis, sed doctrinalis successio nobis commendata. 5. Fides verè Catholica Martyrum & Confessorum sanguine, doctrinâ, miraculis confirmata in Scripturis nobis proponitur. 6. Ecclesiam matrem audire iubemur, quatenus & quamdiu illa audit vocem Patris coelestis. Fides nostra ultimatè non resolvitur, nec resolvi debet in Ecclesiam, sed in Dei verbum. 7. Apostolos audire debent, qui Spiritus probare volunt, inquit Iohannes. Atqui Apostolos non possumus audire, nisi in eorum scriptis, sicut divitis epulonis fratres Prophetas non poterant audire, nisi in ipsorum scriptis. Luc. 16. vers. 29. Quo respectu & sensu Ecclesia dicatur columna & firmamentum veritatis, suo loco fuit expositum. art. de Eccles. §. 116.

6. Lorinus ad h. l. sic annotat. Laudabile admodùm Theologorum studium & meritorium in excogitandis pro fide, quam tenent mordicùs, rationibus colligit ex hoc loco B. Thomas 2. 2. q. 2. art. ult. ut in eadem fide, erga quam summopere afficiuntur, & quam nihilominus, si aliae rationes deessent, Iequerentur ob sufficienter sibi propositam ab Ecclesia divinam revelationem, magis confirmentur ipsi, ac sibi magis in eadem complaceant. Resp. rationes illae non possunt magis confirmare fidem, quàm divina revelatio, quae omni demonstratione firmior. Basilius in Psal. 115. tom. 1. p. 300. Fides est una omnium, quam omnium Dei verborum ducem esse oportet. Fides, inquam, non demonstratio. Fides supra omnem rationem scientiarum, disciplinarumvè animum ad consensum trahit. Fides denique non geometricis aut necessariis nititur probationibus, sed Spiritus sancti operationibus animis inditur. Theologiae mysterium ex fide, minimè rationibus probata aedificium quaerit. Chrysostomus homil. 4. in 1. Corinth. col. 347. Via Theologiae profectò longè est, quàm humanae sapientiae maior, eòque magis, quò maius est res divinas fide accipere, quàm earum rationes per scrutari. Caesarius frater Nazianzeni Dial. 3. Christianorum certè dogmata fide continentur, & fulciuntur, non ratiocinationibus, per quas plurimi prorsus mentem amiserunt. Iacobus Faber in comment. super Richardum 1. de Trinit. cap. 1. In fide ratiocinationem quaerere, est debili oculo umbraculum subtendere, ne perstringatur ab insigniori lumine. Ergò qui potest absque ratiocinatione illa, quae sunt fidei, intueri, longè insigniùs videt & cognoscit, quàm qui ratiocinationem efflagitat & quaerit, ut is sinceriùs Solem agnoscit, quem tantus fulgor non hebetat ex adverso contuentem, quàm qui ut illam videat, manum visui opponit ac obumbrat.

7. Idem d. l. sic scribit. Oderunt cum Wiclefo huius temporis baeretici Scholasticam & positivam Theologiam, negantque necessariam Ecclesiae, sed potiùs pernitiosam. Huic conforme est illud Possevin. lib. 1. Bibl. p. 126. ubi ob tegendam inscitiam praecipuè Theologiam Scholasticam aversari dicit. Resp. non simpliciter improbamus cognitionem & moderatum usum Theologiae Scholasticae, sed multiplicem eiusdem abusum, quem quidam ex ipsis Pontificiis nobiscum agnoscunt. Errant omninò Scholastici. 1. circa disputandi principium, quia Philosophiam cum Theologia commiscent, ac in summis fidei mysteriis, principiis Logicis, Physicis, Metaphysicis &c. praetermissis vel leviter duntaxat attactis Scripturae dictis, conclusiones suas accersunt. Sequuntur versionem Latinam corruptissimam, praetermissis Hebraicis ac Graecis fontibus; violenter ac planè extra scopum Scripturas torquent; ex Patrum dictis tanquam ex proprio Theologiae principio disputant, eorumque autoritatem Scripturae autoritati fermè exaequant. 2. Circa disputandi obiectum, quia proponunt quaestiones otiosas, curiosas, spinosas, inutiles, absurdas, superstitiosas & impias. 3. circa disputandi modum, quia immanis quaedam contradicendi libido ubique apud ipsos obvia: quae in Scripturis definita sunt, de illis Topicè & scepticè disputant; quaestiones abstrusas in Scripturis non definitas temerè definiunt; terminis utuntur obscuris, verbis ac phrasibus &c.

8. Estius ad v. 17. sic annotat. Fieri potest, ut particulaὡςin textu Graeco iam olim vel incuria vel imperitia scribentium, qui superfluam putarint, omissa fuerit. Nimirum statuit, eam bis fuisse olim lectam ὡς κακοποιῶν & ὡς ἐπηρεάζοντες. Ibid. Additum videri potest tanquam malefactoribus ex cap. praecedentevers. 12. Resp. 1. in priore suspicione corrigit Estius textum Graecum ex versione Syriaca; in posteriore ex versione Latina vulgata. Hoc vero est rivulos praeferre fontibus & ex illis hosce aestimare. 2. Nulla nos cogit necessitas, ullam in textu Graeco agnoscendi corruptelam, cum sensus optimè sibi constet. 3. Petro in hac Epistola repetitiones non sunt inusitatae.

9. Lorinus ad v. 17. sic annnotat. Bonum quidem, supplicia ferre peccatis debita, & si patienter quis toleret, satisfacit ac meretur, at meliùs non commeruisse. Resp. patientia in poenis per peccata accersitis placet Deo, sed non placat Deum; est opus Deo gratum, sed nec satisfactorium nec meritorium.

10. Bellarminus l. 4. de Christo c. 13. Gretserus. tom. 2. defens. p. 323. per τὸ πνεῦμα in v. 18. intelligunt Christi animam, sensu eo, Christum carne mortificatum, Spiritu vivificatum in passione, quia caro mortua mansit, anima vero non potuit occidi, sed mansit viva. Vivificari enim dicitur, quod non occiditur1. Reg. 27.2. Reg. 8.Act. 7. &c. Resp. 1. Si per Spiritum intelligitur Christi anima, tùm Christus dicetur animâ vivificatus vel activè, vel passivè. Non activè, cum enim anima sit Spiritus semper vivens ac mortis incapax, seipsam vivificare non habuit opus. Regerunt quidem, etiam ea dici vivificari, quae in vita relinquuntur.Exod. 1. 17.1.
