Sam. 27. v. 11. Atqui id illis demum competit, quae mori possunt, cuius enim vitae parcimus, quem vivere permittimus, ille potest occidi. Sed nec respectu corporis dici potest anima activè vivificasse, quia anima corpus non per se suâ virtute, sed communicatâ τοῦ Λόγου potentiâ in vitam reduxit. Nec passivè, quia enim anima Christi non erat mortua, ergò nec vivificationis indiga. Aug. Ep. 99. ad Enod. Quod fuerat anima mortificatus Iesus h. e. eo Spiritu qui hominis est, quis aude at dicere, cum mors animae non sit, nisi peccatum, à quo ille omninò immunis fuit, cum pro nobis moreretur &c. In ea re vivificatus est, in qua fuerat mortuus. Ergò de carne dictum est. Ipsa enim revixit anima redeunte, quia ipsa erat mortua animâ recedente. Mortificatus ergò carne dictus est, quia secundum solam carnem mortuus est, vivificatus autem Spiritu, quia illo Spiritu operante, in quo ad quos veniebat & praedicabat, ipsa etiam caro vivificata surrexit, in quo modo ad homines venit. 2. Inde Estius hanc explicationem refellit. Quidam, inquit, Spiritum interpretantur animam Christi &c. ut sit sensus, Christus secundùm Spiritum i. e. animam non est mòrtuus, sed vivus permansit. Nam vivificare, pro eo quod est vivum servare, phrasis est Scripturae &c. Sed quid magnum, si anima Christi moriente carne vivens permansit, quando nec in pessimis hominibus anima moritur, ut quae naturâ sit immortalis? Quare nec facit ad consolationem piorum, qui hîc affliguntur, quòd post mortem supersint eorum animae, nisi beatior aliqua vita secutura sit exemplo Christi, quod hic proponitur. Accipit quidem Estius itidem Spiritum pro anima, sed aliam affert explicationem, de qua postea. 3. Refellit eandem expositionem Lorinus, ad h. l. sic annotans. Non placet, quod Hesselius (Iohannes à Lovanio dictus) tradit, dici vivificatum Christum Spiritu in passione, quia carne mortuâ anima occidi non poterit. (In margine notantur Bellarm. lib. 4. de Christo cap. 15. Pererius lib. 9. in Genes. Disp. 9. num. 66.) Etenim hoc omni animae commune est: quamvis non ignorem, vivificandi verbum usurpari pro eo, quod est non occidere &c. Verùm hoc loco sequor potius sensum simplicem & Augustini rationem, ut propriè dicatur vivificatus Christus secundum eam partem, in qua fuerat verè mortuus h. e. secundum carnem & in carne: nihil enim obstat, & sic omnia cohaerent.

11. Caietanus illud vivificatus Spiritu exponit de beatitudine animae Christi, ac de triumpho ipsius contra Daemones. Existimat enim, Christum dici vivificatum Spiritu, quia beatus erat secundùm Spiritum & triumphavit de Daemonibus, qui vivificationis actus ei accesserit, quando mortuus est carne. Sed hanc expositionem Lorinus rectè censet esse nimis remotam. Nam τὸ vivificari secundùm Spiritum, opponitur τῷ mortificari secundùm carnem. Ergò ut per mortificationem intelligitur mors, ita per vivificationem resurrectio à mortuis, cuius consequerís beatitudinem animae & triumphum de Daemonibus esse non negamus.

12. Isidorus Clarius vult magis explicari, quod praecessit, mortuus ess pro peccatis, iustus pro iniustis, hoc pacto. Id fecit Christus, ut nos offerret Deo, quod & potuit. Nam etsi morte affectus est, ob carnis Naturam acceptam, Spiritu tamen ac divinitate (siquidem Deus Spiritus estIoh. 4. v. 24.) semper vivit, unde & salvare potest per seipsum accedentes per ipsum ad DeumHebr. 7. v. 25. Resp. hanc expositionem, quatenus per Spiritum intelligit Christi divinitatem, libenter amplectimur, sed per vivificationem directè & propriè intelligi dicimus vitae communicationem sive restitutionem, sicut per mortificationem intelligitur vitae ablatio. Interim non negamus, illam vitae restitutionem secutam esse vitae continuationem, quia Christus ex mortuis suscitatus, non ampliùs moritur, mors illi ultra non dominatur. Rom. 6. v. 9.

13. Estius mortificari carne & vivificari Spiritu exponit de vitae carnalis & spiritualis oppositione. Christus, inquit, dicitur vivificatus Spiritu i. e. animâ, quia factus est in Spiritum vivificantem, tunc scil. quando à morte resurrexit ad vitam immortalem, quemadmodum Paulus loquitur.1. Cor. 15. v. 46.factus est primus homo Adam in animam viventem, novissimus Adam in Spiritum vivificantem. Dicitur autem Christus factus in Spiritum vivificantem i. e. habens Spiritum vivificantem, quando anima eius coepit perpetuam & immortalem vitam, corporiipsius subministrare absque subsidio alimenti, tanquam per se ad vitam corpori praestandam conservandamque sufficiens, ut quod priùs erat corpus animale, factum fuerit hacratione Spirituale, qui sensus huic loco benè convenit, ut vivificatus Spiritu intelligatur Christus per resurrectionem, quia tunc vivere coepit vitâimmortali, ad quam sola sine ciborum adminiculis ei sufficiebat animae praesentia, quod & in reliquis futurum est electis, quorum primitiae Christus. Eodem ferè modo Cornel. à Lapide, qui hanc expositionem reliquis praefert, Christus inquit, vivificatus est Spiritu, quando virtute Spiritus i. e. animae suae à mortuis resurrexit. Tunc enim anima, quasi instrumentum divinitatis eius carnem ingressa, eam rursum animapit & vivificavit, novamque vitam immortalem & gloriosam ei communicavit. Resp. 1. τὸvivificari Spiritu hîc non opponitur τῷvivere carne vel secundum carnem, sicut 1. Cor. 15. v. 46.τὸ fieri in Spiritum vivificantem opponitur τῷ factum esse in animam viventem, sed vivificari Spiritu opponitur ei, quod est mortificari carne. 2. Ergò vitae una species non opponitur alteri vitae speciei, sed vitae communicatio sive restitutio opponitur vitae ablationi. Directè igitur & proprièperτὸvivificari Spiritu intelligitur resuscitatio ex mortuis facta virtute Deit atis Christi, qui est Spiritus, ut Athanasius apud Bedam, Augustinus ser. 14. de verb. Apost. c. 16. & Epist. 99. & Oecumenius in comm. rectè exponunt. 3. Fieri in in Spiritum vivificantem iuxta Estium commune est Christo capiti cum piis tanquam membris, ad vitam immortalem aliquando resuscitandis, sed scopus Petri est, tale quid de Christo praedicare, quod ipsi soli competit. Ut enim ipsi soli competit, pati pro peccatis, iustum pro iniustis, ut nos Deo adduceret: ita quoque ipsi soli competit, ita mortificari carne, ut vivificetur Spiritu i. e. virtute Deitatis personaliter inhabitantis, & sic propria virtute ex mortuis resuscitari. 4. Interim non negamus, vitam spiritualem & immortalem esse resuscitationis illius consequens, cum Christus non ad hanc, sed ad coelestem vitam resuscitatus sit.

14. Lorinus adducit expositionem Clementis Alexandrini lib. 6. stromat. Christum dici vivificatum Spiritu, quia in nobis vivit & in Spiritibus nostris, per fidem sc. obtinendo ac tribuendo nobis fidei munus, per quod peculiariter vivere dicimur,Rom. 1. v. 17.Hebr. 2. v. 4.cap. 10. v. 38.Galat. 3. v. 11.& caritatis aliarumque virtutum cum gratia sanctificante. Resp. Sicut per τὸmortificari carne intelligitur carnis Christi mortificatio, ita per τὸ vivificari Spiritu intelligitur carnis Christi vivificatio, ut oppositio ostendit. Praeterea Apostolus non loquitur de vivificatione activè, sed passivè, cum tamen iuxta Clementis Alexand. hypothesin debuisset potiùs dicere ζωοποιῶν quàm ζωοποιηθεὶς. Directè igitur & propriè loquitur Apostolus de vita ipsius Christi, quae in resuscitatione ipsi restituta, interim non negamus, Christum ex mortuis resuscitatum vitae spiritualis per fidem nos participes facere & in nobis vivere. Gal. 2. v. 20.

Observationes didascalicae. 1 Qui per veram & vivam divinae bonitatis agnitionem & fidem sanctum Deo tabernaculum in corde suo erigit, is verè Deum sanctificat. Qui autem Deum sanctificat, à Deo sanctificabitur. 2. Cor. 6. v. 26.

2. Deus non sanctificatur externo ornatu vel cultu hypocritico, sed interiore cordis affectu & cultu spirituali. Psal. 45. v. 10.Luc. 17. v. 20.Ioh. 4. v. 24.

3. Confessio fidei non est arbitraria, sed necessaria, ab omnibus omninò piis ad Dei gloriam praestanda. Matth. 10. 32. & 33. est enim inseparabile consequens verae fidei, Psal. 116. 10.Credidi, propter quod locutus sum.2. Cor. 4. 13.habentes eundem Spiritum fidei & nos credimus, propter quod & loquimur. Semen fidei in corde germinat per confessionem fidei in ore.

4. Confessio illa fidei ita comparata esse debet, ut quod credere nos profitemur, ex Scripturis possimus confirmare, hoc enim, est Fidei suae rationem reddere. Chrysostomus homil. 16. in Ioh. Absurdum est, quòd Medicus, coriarius, textor, & omnes generatim opifices, quisque pro artis suae professione pugnet, Christianus autem non possit ullam religionis suae afferre rationem. Atqui artes illae neglectae ad pecuniam damnum referunt, huius autem contemtus animae detrimentum affert, & tamen tantâ miserià, tantâ insaniâ laboramus, ut in illas omnem curam cogitationemque adhibeamus, necessaria autem & salutis nostrae munimento firmissima pro nihilo ducimus. Hoc non sinit gentiles recognoscere errorem suum atque deridere. Nam cum ipsi mendacio nixi omnia faciant, ut dogmatum suorum ignominiam defendant, nos autem veritatis cultores ne hiscere quidem ad nostra tutanda possimus, quae causa est, quin doctrinae nostrae nimiam damnent imbecillitatem, quin fraudem & stultitiam in nobis suspicentur, quin Christo tanquam mendaci & multitudinis stultitiâ fraude suâ abutenti maledicant? Huius nos causa blasphemiae, nos inquam, qui nolumus piis religionis nostrae sermonibus invigilare, sed his contentis veluti supervacuis caducis rebus curam omnem adhibemus &c. Si gentiles, ut contra religionem nostram loquerentur, tantopere invigilarunt: quâ nos veniâ dignamur, nisi huiusmodi contra nos insultus propulsare videamur? Hoc nobis Petrus praecipit, inquit enim, parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea, quae in vobis est spe &c. Similia habet conc. 3. de Lazaro.

5. Parati esse debemus ad defensionem omni poscenti rationem fidei, sive sit adversarius, sive discendi cupidus. Beda in h. l. Duobus modis de spe & fide nostra rationem poscentibus reddere debemus, ut & iustas fidei ac spei nostrae causas omnibus intimemus, sive fideliter, sive infideliter quaerentibus, & ipsam fidei ac spei nostrae professionem illibatam semper teneamus, etiam inter pressuras adversantium, ostendentes per patientiam, quam rationabiliter eam servandam didicerimus, pro cuius amore nec adversapati, nec mortem subire formidemus. Lyranus in h. l. Satisfactio illa fit dupliciter. Uno modo fidei simplici, qui petit à magis provecto in fide pleniùs erudiri. Alio modo infideli, fidem irrationabilem reputanti. Prima satisfactio est per doctrinam caritativam (de qua quidam veterum dicit, volenti mutuò accipere rationales pecunias non denegemus) secunda vero per fidei rationabilem defensionem ostendendo, quod continet omnem sanctitatem &c.

6. Interim aliud est respondere, si interrogatus fueris, aliud citra necessitatem apud impios temerè in pericula sese coniicere ubi non expetitur confessio. Nimirum confessio nostra non debet hominum libidini & proterviae esse subiecta, sed Dei gloriae & saluti proximi inservire.

7. Duplici ratione ab Ecclesiae Doctoribus confessio, & per eam fidei ratio reddenda exigitur, tùm generali, quia sunt Christiani, tùm speciali, quia sunt Ecclesiae doctores, quorum proprium munus est, fidei veritatem adversus eius impugnatores propugnare. Tit. 1. v. 9. Chrysost. homil. 35. in Matth. Proditor est veritatis, qui aut non liberè pronuneiat, aut non sufficienter eam defendit. Gregorius part. 2. Pastoral. curae cap. 11. huc accommodat typum Exod. 25. de vectibus in arca foederis. Per arcam Ecclesiam, per vectes Ecclesiae Doctores intelligit. Vectibus arcam portare, inquit, est bonis Doctoribus Sanctam Ecclesiam ad rudes infidelium mentes praedicando deducere, qui vectes semper iubentur esse in circulis, nec unquam ab eis extrahi, quia necesse est, ut qui ad officium praedicationis excubant, à Sacrae lectionis studio non recedant. Ad hoc namque vectes esse in circulis semper iubentur, ut cum portari arcam oportunitas exigit, de intromittendis vectibus portandi tarditas nulla generetur: quia videlicet cum spirituale aliquid à subditis Pastor inquiritur, ignominiosum valde est, si tunc quaerat discere, cum quaestionem debet enodare. Sed circulis vectes inhaereant, ut Doctores semper in suis cordibus eloquia sacra meditentur, Testamenti arcam sine mora elevent, si quicquid necesse est, protinus doceant, Unde benè primus Pastor Ecclesiae pastores caeteros admonet, dicens, parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscentivos rationem de ea, quae in vobis est spe, ac si apertè dicat, ut ad portandam arcam nulla mora praepediat, vectes nunquam à circulis recedant.

8. Nec tamen ad omnes quaestiones à quibusvis propositas, sed de utilibus & necessariis rebus quaerentibus respondendum, Apostolus 1. Tim. 1. v. 4.ζητήσεις ἀπεράντους opponit τῇ οὶκονομίᾳ θεοῦ τῇ ἐν πίστειcap. 6. v. 4. ex quaestionibus & λογομαχίαις dicit oriri invidiam, contentionem, blasphemias, suspiciones malas.2. Tim. 2. Vers. 23.stultas & otio sas quaestiones depitare iubet, propterea quòd pugnas generent, quod praeceptum repetit Tit. 3. v. 9. Athanasius in vita Antonii de ipso memorat, quod ex illis, qui interrogaturi de quibusdam ad se veniebant, quaerere fuerit solitus, an ex Aegypto venirent, an ex Hierosolyma, id est, an res inanes, an vero utiles ac salutares proposituri sint.

9. Confessio insuper non fiat cum importunitate, immodestia, superbia, quibus bona causa deformatur, sed in vera humilitate, lenitate, modestia, reverentia; cum timore erga Deum, & mansuetudine erga homines. Nisi enim Dei timor subsit, in fastum mens humana erigitur; nisi ad mansuetudinem animus sit compositus, statim ebulliunt contentiones. Confessio non debet esse mordax & acerba, sed lenis, & cum decoro gravitatis coniuncta.

10. Quinimò non solùm in edenda confessione reverentia requiritur erga Deum, ne hypocriticè aut negligenter in fide exponenda versemur: sed etiam erga Superiores, praesertim Magistratus, qui fidei confessionem à nobis exigunt, ne illos conteninere videamur. Act. 7. v. 2.cap. 22. v. 1.cap. 26. v. 2.

11. Nisi intus in corde resideat fides, frustra garriet lingua: unde Petrus requirit, ut rationem reddamus, eius quae in nobis est spei sive fidei. In corde igitur radices agat fides, ut deinde confessionis fructum proferat.

12. Confessioni sanctae coniuncta esse debet bona conscientia & vita sancta. August. Epist. 211. ad Probam. Mihividetur plus valere in hac inquisitione vivendi, quàm loquendi modum. Nam qui didicerunt à Domino Iesu Christo mites esse & humiles corde, plus cogitando & orando proficiunt, quàm legendo & audiendo.

13. Si omnes te accusent, ad absolutionem sufficit, si sola apud Deum conscientia te excuset; sed si omnes te laudent, ad condemnationem sufficit, si conscientia apud Deum te accuset.

14. Pii in hac vita variis adversariorum calumniis sunt expositi, quo ipso imagini Christi conformantur. Matth. 10. Vers. 25.Si patremfamilias Beelzebub vocaverunt, quantò magis domesticos eius.

15. Nulla melior ratio confutandi calumnias adversariorum, quàm cum eas vitae innocentiâ retundimus. Regium est benefacere, & malè audire, dicebat Alexander Magnus: nos debemus illud hoc modo παροιμιάζειν. Christianum est benefacere, & malè audire, adeoque calumniarum nebulas Sole veritatis & sanctitatis dispellere.

16. Calumniatorum ora non solùm per bonam piorum conversationem obstruuntur, ut obmutescere cogantur 1. Petr. 2. vers. 15.

sed ipsi etiam calumniatores confunduntur, & erubesoere coguntur, quae est iustissima illa poena, quam Regius Propheta ipsis aliquoties imprecatur. Psalm. 25. v. 3.Psalm. 35. v. 4. & 26.Psalm. 40. v. 15. & 16.Psal. 70. v. 3.Psal. 71. v. 13. & 24.Psal. 83. vers. 18.Psal. 86. Vers. 18.Psal. 109. v. 28.Psal. 119. v. 78.Psal. 129. v. 5. Confusio & erubescentia homini ingenuo est magna poena, unde quod Ezech. 17. v. 53. in Hebraeo dicitur, porta confusionem tuam, LXX. reddiderunt, τὴν βάσανον σουtormentum tuum.

17. Non piget Apostolum, ea, quae necessaria, saepiùs inculcare, inde quod iam ante dixerat cap. 2. v. 15. hoc loco denuò repetit, exemplo Pauli Phil. 3. v. 1.Eadem vobis scribereἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρὸν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλὲς.

18. Si ob fidei confessionem aliquid adversi sustinendum, sufficit conscientiae testimonium. 1. Petr. 4. v. 15. & 16. Magna consolatio in ipsa innocentia.

19. In hac vita nemo penitùs immunis ab adversitate, satiùs igitur est, propter iustitiam pati immerentem, quàm debita malefactorum sustinere supplicia. Beda in h. l. Haec sententia Apostoli illorum stultitiam eleganter arguit, qui cum pro culpis arguuntur à fratribus, vel etiam poenis coërcentur, patienter omninò tolerant: at cum absque culpa vel verborum contumelias, vel damna rerum, vel adversa quaeque patiuntur à proximis, mox adiracundiam prorumpunt, & qui hactenus videbantur innoxii, per impatientiam se & murmurationem noxios reddunt.

20. Si melius est benefacientem pati, quàm malefacientem pati. Ergò simpliciter bonum est benefacientem pati. Matth. 5. v. 10.Beati, qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam. Beati hîc in spe, illic in re. Ecce quantum perdiderunt? pro mundi stercoribus regnum coelorum; pro modicatristitia, infinitum gaudium; pro vita labili vitam aeternam receperunt, inquit Ioh. Huss. in h. l.

21. Optima in persecutionibus & adversitatibus consolatio, meminisse eius, quòd non sine Dei voluntate, eademque paterna illae nobis obtingant. Iob. 1. v. 21.Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit, sit nomen Domini benedictum.Matth. 10. v. 29.Nonne duo passeres asse veneunt, & unus ex illis non cadit super terram sine Patre vestro.v. 30.Vestri autem & capilli capitis numerati sunt. August. lib. 22. contra Faustum cap. 20.Cùm ex voluntate Spiritus DEI patiuntur benefacientes, non parcitur iustis: cum autem malefacientes, non parcitur peccatoribus, secundùm illius tamen voluntatem fit utrumque, qui ait. Non parcam iusto, nec peccatori, illum flagellando ut filium, hunc puniendo ut impium.

22. Crux non est temerè accersenda & quaerenda, sed à DEO imposita patienter ferenda.

23. Non possunt Tyranni ac ne ipse quidem Diabolus saevire quantum volunt & quam diu volunt, sed quantum & quamdiu Deus vult. Tyranni & Diaboli faciunt, quod possunt permittente Deo; quod possunt, non faciunt prohibente Deo, Ioh. Gerson. lib. 3. de consol. Theol. Pros. 4. Tenet Deus ligatum leonem infernalem, ne furat, quantum vellet: non ille, sed detinens eum, rogandus est.

24. Cum verè pios paterno amore Deus complectatur, ut filios suos dilectos, ac nihilominus crucem in hac vita ipsis inferri permittat, imò immittat, ex eo manifestum est, ad piorum utilitatem crucem ipsis immitti, Deus enim tam bonus est, ut nihil mali bonis accidere permitteret, nisi ex eo maius bonum elicere nosset.

25. Crux carni molesta est & adversa, meritò igitur pii ad respiciendum Christi exemplum toties revocantur, ut cum se noverint Christi membra per fidem, eidem tanquam capiti sese conformandos sciant per crucem.

26. Quando Apostolus dicit, Christum semel passum, perfectionem sacrificii & meriti Christi docet; quando pro peccatis Christum passum dicit, efficaciam & fructum passionis Christi docet; quando iustum pro iniustis passum dicit, innocentiam Christi patientis declarat; quando Christum passum esse dicit, ut nos Deo adduceret, causam finalem passionis monstrat; quando Christum carne mortificatum dicit, secundùm quam Naturam Christus passus sit & quousque Patri suo coelesti obedierit, ostendit; quando vivificatum Spiritu dicit, laetam passionis ἒκβασιν nobis considerandam proponit; sicque uno fasciculo totam de passione Christi doctrinam complectitur.

27. Cum propter iustitiam patimur, solemur nos, quòd Christus passus, cuius imagini in hac vita nos oportet conformari; quòd passus sit pro nobis, ut nos à morte aeterna liberaret ac Patri suo reconciliaret, aequum ergò est, ut & nos pro illo patiamur, hoc est, ad ipsius gloriam confitendo eius doctrinam; quòd passus sit iustus pro iniustis, aequum ergò est, ut nos crucem impositam patienter feramus, cum innocentes quidem simus coram mundo, non autem coram Deo;

quod mortificatus quidem sit carne, vivificatus autem Spiritu i. e. ad vitam & gloriam resuscitatus. Ut ergò felix fuit passionis & mortis Christi exitus, cum vitae & gloriae palma tandem fuerit passionem illam insecuta: sic & in nobis vita Christi manifestabitur, si mortificationem Christi in carne nostra circumferamus,2. Cor. 4. v. 10.

28. Fructus passionis Christi est, quòd peccata nostra per eam expiaverit, Patri coelesti nos reconciliaverit, ac fugitivos ac perditos ad patrem & domum coelestem reduxerit, nosque ut gratum sacrificium in seipso Deo obtulerit.

29. Si DEO per passionem Christi adducendi fuimus, ergò omnes à vero DEO, à veri DEI cognitione & legitimo eius cultu, velut oves errantes declinavimusEsa. 53. Vers. 6. nostra est declinatio, Christi vero est restitutio ac reductio. Os. 13. Vers. 9. quae ἀναγωγὴ complectitur non solùm reconciliationem cum DEO, sed etiam illuminationem Spiritus sancti, sanctificationem, & in gloriam coelestem introductionem.

30. Si Christus ideò pro nobis passus est, ut nos DEO tanquam gratum sacrificium offerret, aequum est, ut corpora nostra exhibeamus Deo tanquam hostiam viventem ac spiritualemRom. 12. v. 1. Per Christum offeramus hostiam laudis DEO.Hebr. 13. v. 15. & totos nos in DEI obsequium tradamus, ita DEUS vicissim se nobis offeret tanquam filiis, Hebr. 12. v. 7. Christus se tibi, tu te Christo. Christus DEO te adduxit, cave ne ab eo per peccata voluntaria iterum profugias.

31. Inter passionem Christi & nostram, magnum omninò discrimen. Christus passus est pro aliorum peccatis expiandis: nos verò per passionem nec nostra nec aliorum peccata expiare possumus; sola Christi passio est λύτρον, nostra est vel τιμωρία, vel δοκιμασία, vel μαρτυρίον. Christus passus est iustus pro iniustis, nos non sumus perfectè iusti ratione iustitiae inhaerentis vel actualis, sed sordibus peccatorum adhuc contaminati. Christus passus est, ut nos DEO adduceret, nos per passiones ducimur in regnum coelorum.Actor. 14. Vers. 22. Christus viae dux est, ac viam nobis aperuit, nos ipsum sequimur ducente Spiritu, per quem nos ad se & post se trahit.

32. Inde atque ideò Christus pro iniustis pati potuit. 1. Quia iustus est, i. e. ab omni peccati labe immunis est. Si peccatis propriis contaminatus fuisset, aliena abluere minimè potuisset. 2. Quia Christus est, h. e. θεάνθρωπος DEUS & homo in personae unitate, Christi enim nomen & ungentem Deitatem & unctam humanitatem complectitur.

## 3:16
HAVING A GOOD CONSCIENCE, THAT IN THAT, WHEREIN THEY SPEAK EVIL OF YOU, THEY MAY BE ASHAMED, WHO FALSELY ACCUSE YOUR GOOD CONVERSATION IN CHRIST.

Connection. 1. This is the eighth virtue to which the Apostle exhorts the faithful, namely, the innocence of life, of which he had also made some mention in the preceding verses. v. 10. He that will love life and see good days, v. 11. let him refrain from evil and do good. vers. 12. the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous etc. but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil. v. 13. And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good.

Speech has little authority without life, therefore the Apostle joins a good conscience to the profession of faith, of which it was treated in the preceding verse. It is the integrity of conscience alone that gives confidence of speaking in confession. For he who excellently concerning Evangelical doctrine they can discourse, meanwhile they can be accused of impiety from a dissolute and flagitious life, they prostitute doctrine to the calumnies of the impious, and what they build with one hand, they destroy with the other.

3. The pious ought not only to καλῶς λέγειν, but also τὰ καλὰ πράττειν.. This is not only required, that the pious embrace the true religion, persevere constant in it, and intrepidly profess it, but also that they adorn the doctrine with the innocence and holiness of life, lest they contaminate the purity of faith with the impurity of life and morals; for this reason the Apostle advises that both a good conscience and a good conversation be joined to the exhortation to the confession of faith.

4. All hypocrisy and simulation ought to be absent from confession, therefore the Apostle requires a good conscience from those professing the Christian faith, and from those responding when they are questioned about it, so that such confessors may be internally what they conduct themselves as externally. Lyran. in h. l. having a good conscience, so that there may be a good disposition internally and externally.

5. This member also pertains to the exhortation concerning the confession of faith to be issued. For the Apostle confirms his exhortation from the useful consequence. If, when questioned by adversaries, you render an account of your hope, if you issue a confession of faith placidly and reverently, if you bring to it a good conscience and a good conversation in Christ, it will come to pass that your calumniators, put to shame, will be forced to be silent.

Disposition. He explains a twofold fruit of confession, a good conscience before God, and a good reputation before men. He also commends a twofold zeal to the faithful, namely, first, the zeal of a good conscience. Secondly, the zeal of a holy conversation.

Exposition of the text. Συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθὴν. This member is joined with the noun ἕτομοι, namely ἔστε,, and it can be understood both assertively or indicatively, if you are always prepared to issue a confession of your faith with modesty and reverence, you will have a good conscience: and imperatively or preceptively, be so prepared to issue a confession, that you may have a good conscience and not act here with a feigned mind, nor indulge in shameful deeds and crimes that devastate the conscience.

῞Ινα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλῶσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν χρηστῷ ἀναστροφήν. He repeats what he had said above cap. 2. v. 12.. Having your conversation good among the Gentiles, ἳνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτέυσαντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεόν. Likewise, what he had said specifically about subjects cap. eiusd. v. 15. For so is the will of God, that by doing well you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men. The Syrian in this place expressed the Apostolic sentiment in such a way that he repeated the particle of likeness ὡς, in this manner, that they who speak against you as of evil men may blush as men who slander your good conversations, which are in Christ. The sense is: It will come to pass that those who speak ill of you as of evildoers, they in turn, as slanderers of your good conversation, will be ill-spoken of, and from that will blush. Προσδιορισμὸν in the Greek text is added ὡς κακοποιῶν, the Vulgate version omitted, rendering it simply thus, that in that wherein they speak against you, they may be confounded. But it is held in all Greek Codices, as also in the Syriac paraphrase and in the parallel place 1. Epist. 2. v. 12.. The word καταλαλεῖν properly signifies to detract from someone's fame, to disparage Iac. 4. v. 11. and καταλαλιαὶ are disparagements 2. Cor. 12. v. 20. 1. Petr. 2. v. 1. etc. ἐπηρεάζειν is to infest, to slander. Matth. 5. vers. 44. Luc. 6. v. 28. The LXX Interpreters nowhere use this word. Budaeus renders it, to inconvenience, to offend, and testifies, that it is often taken by Demosthenes for creating trouble for someone, in whose work, however, he renders it to disparage in this place of the oration against Midias. ἣ πρὰξεσιν ἐχούσαις φιλοτιμίαν ἐπηρεάζων, or disparaging his actions flowing from munificence. The Scholiast of Thucydides ἐπηρεάζοι explains βλάπτοι.. But what the Apostle calls ἀναστροφὴν ἀγαθὴν, in this place, he called ἀναστροφὴν καλὴν, in the preceding chapter v. 12. and in this 3rd chapter 2. ἀναστροφὴν ἀγνὴν,, which word the Royal Codex also has in this place. The Syrian both in this place and cap. 2. vers. 12. rendered it in the plural, your conversations [consult facsimile image] decorous and beautiful, pleasing to GOD and men. For to the Syrians [consult facsimile image] to be beautiful μετωνυμικῶς signifies ἀρέσκειν to please.Matt. 14. v. 6.John 8. v. 29.Rom. 8. v. 8. &c. What the Apostle understands by good conversation in Christ, will be explained in the questions.

Latin:

CONSCIENTIAM HABENTES BONAM, UT IN EO, QUOD DETRAHUNT VOBIS, CONFUNDANTUR, QUI CALUMNIANTUR VESTRAM BONAM IN CHRISTO CONVERSIONEM.

Connexio. 1. Octava haec est virtus, ad quam Apostolus fideles exhortatur, videl. vitae innocentia, cuius etiam in praecedentibus mentionem aliquam fecerat. v. 10.Qui vult vitam diligere & dies videre bonos,v. 11.declinet à malo & faciat bonum.vers. 12.oculi Domini super iustos &c. vultus autem Domini super facientes mala.v. 13.Et quis est, qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis.

Parùm autoritatis habet sermo absque vita, ideò fidei professioni, de qua in versu praeced. actum, coniungit Apostolus bonam conscientiam. Sola conscientiae integritas est, quae in confessione dat loquendi fiduciam. Qui enim praeclarè de Evangelica doctrina possunt disserere, interim ex vita dissoluta & flagitiosa impietatis argui possunt, doctrinam prostituunt impiorum calumniis, ac quod unâ manu aedificant, alterâ destruunt.

3. Pii non tantùm debent καλῶς λέγειν, sed etiam τὰ καλὰ πράττειν. Non hoc tantùm requiritur, ut pii veram religionem amplectantur, in ea constantes perseverent, & intrepidè eam profiteantur, sed etiam ut vitae innocentiâ ac sanctitate doctrinam ornent, ne fidei puritatem vitae ac morum impuritate contaminent, hanc ob causam exhortationi ad fidei confessionem coniungendam monet Apostolus & conscientiam bonam & conversationem bonam.

4. A confessione omnis hypocrisis & simulatio debet abesse, ideò à profitentibus fidem Christianam, ac de ea cum interrogantur, respondentibus Apostolus requirit bonam conscientiam, ut confessores tales sint interiùs, quales sese gerunt exteriùs. Lyran. in h. l. conscientiam habentes bonam, ita ut sit bona dispositio interiùs & exteriùs.

5. Pertinet etiam hoc membrum ad exhortationem defidei confessione edenda. Confirmat enim Apostolus exhortationem suam â consequente utili. Si ab adversariis interrogati rationem spei vestrae reddatis, si placidè & reverenter confessionem fidei edatis, si ad eam afferatis bonam conscientiam, & bonam in Christo conversationem, futurum, ut calumniatores vestri pudefacti obmutescere cogantur.

Dispositio. Duplicem confessionis exponit fructum, bonam conscientiam apud Deum, & bonam famam apud homines. Duplex etiam fidelibus commendat studium, videlicet primò studium bonae conscientiae. Secundò studium conversationis sanctae.

Expositio textus. Συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθὴν. Coniungitur hoc membrum cum nomine ἕτομοι scil. ἔστε, ac potest intelligi tùm assertivè sive indicativè, si parati semper estis ad fidei vestrae confessionem cum modestia & reverentia edendam, habebitis bonam conscientiam: tùm imperativè sive praeceptivè, ita parati sitis ad confessionem edendam, ut bonam conscientiam habeatis neque quidquam animo simulatorio hîc agatis, neve flagitiis ac sceleribus, conscientiam vastantibus, indulgeatis.

῞Ινα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλῶσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν χρηστῷ ἀναστροφήν. Repetit, quod superiùs cap. 2. v. 12. dixerat. Conversationem vestram inter gentes habentes bonam,ἳνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτέυσαντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεόν. Item, quod in specie de subditis dixerat cap. eiusd. v. 15.Sic est voluntas Dei, ut benefacientes obmutescere faciatis imprudentium hominum ignorantiam. Syrus hoc loco sententiam Apostolicam sic expressit, ut particulam similitudinis ὡς tanquam repeteret, hoc modo, ut ii, qui loquuntur de vobis tanquam de hominibus malis erubescant tanquam viri, qui calumniantur conversationes vestras bonas, quae sunt in Christo. Sensus est. Ita futurum, ut qui malè de vobis loquuntur tanquam maleficis, ipsi vicissim tanquam calumniatores bonae vestrae conversationis malè audiant, atque ex eo erubescant. Προσδιορισμὸν in textu Graeco adiectum ὡς κακοποιῶν, Vulgata versio omisit, simpliciter sic reddens, ut in eo quod detrahunt vobis, confundantur. Sed habetur in omnibus Codicibus Graecis, uti etiam in Syriaca paraphrasi & in loco parallelo 1. Epist. 2. v. 12. Verbum καταλαλεῖν propriè significat famae alicuius detrabere, obtrectareIac. 4. v. 11. ac καταλαλιαὶ sunt obtrectationes2. Cor. 12. v. 20.1. Petr. 2. v. 1. &c. ἐπηρεάζειν est infestare, calumniari.Matth. 5. vers. 44.Luc. 6. v. 28. LXX. Interpp. hoc verbo nuspiam utuntur. Budaeus reddit, incommodare, offendere, ac testatur, à Demosthene saepe accipi promolestiam alicui creare, apud quem tamen reddit obtrectare in hoc orationis in Midian loco. ἣ πρὰξεσιν ἐχούσαις φιλοτιμίαν ἐπηρεάζων,aut eius actiones à munificentia manantes obtrectans. Scholiastes Thucydidis ἐπηρεάζοι exponit βλάπτοι. Quam verò Apostolus hoc loco vocat ἀναστροφὴν ἀγαθὴν, eam cap. praeced. v. 12. vocavit ἀναστροφὴν καλὴν, & in hoc 3. cap. 2. ἀναστροφὴν ἀγνὴν, quam vocem etiam hoc loco Regius Codex habet. Syrus & hoc loco & cap. 2. vers. 12. reddidit in plurali, conversationes vestras[consult facsimile image]decoras & pulchras, DEO & hominibus placentes. Syris enim [consult facsimile image]pulchrum esseμετωνυμικῶςsignificatἀρέσκειν placere.Matth. 14. v. 6.Iohan. 8. v. 29.Rom. 8. v. 8. &c. Per conversationem bonam in Christo, quid Apostolus intelligat, in quaestionibus explicabitur.

## 3:17
FOR IT IS BETTER, IF THE WILL OF GOD SHOULD WILL IT, TO SUFFER FOR DOING GOOD, THAN FOR DOING EVIL.

Connection. 1. He interposes a new argument for the exhortation to patience, taken from the will of GOD. Since adversities do not befall the pious by chance, nor are they rashly invited, but are sent upon them by the good will of GOD, they are to be borne with a more equable mind.

2. He also meets a tacit objection. Those who are compelled to endure slanders and detractions from wicked men, and especially from enemies of Christian doctrine, sometimes break out into these words. I would not bear reproaches and slanders so gravely and annoyingly, if I had deserved them: Peter answers, it is better that you have not deserved it, so that by doing good and hearing evil you may prove yourself a true Christian.

3. The Apostle therefore joins the afflictions of the pious with the sufferings of wicked men, and says that the afflictions of the former are better, because the pious suffer only outwardly in the flesh, while inwardly they have a good conscience, but the wicked are afflicted both inwardly and outwardly, inasmuch as a depraved conscience strikes them with a silent lash.

4. He had said above, verse 13. Who is it that will harm you, if you are zealous for good? But because even those who are studious of good works, and pursue peace with their neighbor, are exposed to slanders and persecutions either on account of the profession of the Christian faith or the pursuit of justice, therefore the Apostle consoles them, with the advantage of this suffering proposed. In this way, the words of the Apostle are referred not only to the nearest sentence, but to the whole complex. He had spoken of the necessity of giving a confession of faith, which at that time was most dangerous; now he adds that it is much better, if they sustain any inconvenience for the defense of a good cause and the pursuit of justice, to suffer thus unjustly, than if they were punished for their own crimes.

5. What he had proposed specifically to servants in cap. praeced. v. 19. & 20., that he repeats in this place, and adapts in general to all Christians, since in this part the reason for servants and all Christians is equal. For this is grace, if for conscience of God one endures sorrows, suffering unjustly. For what glory is it, if sinning and being buffeted you endure it? But if doing good and suffering you endure it, this is grace with God.

Disposition. Against the afflictions brought upon the pious by persecutors and impious men, the Apostle consoles them with a double argument. 1. From the quality of those afflictions. Since in this life one must suffer entirely, it is better that we suffer in a just and good cause, and thus for the sake of GOD, than in an unjust business. It is more noble to suffer unworthy things for the sake of justice, than worthy punishments for one's own iniquity. To do well and suffer evils is far better than to do evil, and therefore suffer evils. 2. From the paternal will of God. Those afflictions are not sent upon the pious without the permission and good will of God, therefore they are to be taken up with a patient, nay, a grateful mind.

Exposition of the text. Κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας etc. The Vulgate rendered it. For it is better that doing good. But in the Greek it is held simply. For it is better doing good for you to suffer, whence in more correct Latin copies the particle that is rightly omitted as if it were redundant and superfluous. Κρεῖττον The Syrian expressed it through [consult facsimile image] it helps you, it profits you. τὸ πάσχειν is again placed here absolutely for any kinds of passions, which is frequent for Peter in this Epistle cap. 2. Vers. 19. 20. 21. & 23.cap. 3. Vers. 14. & 18.cap. 4. Vers. 1.15. & 19.cap. 5. Vers. 10. ἀγαθοποιοῦντες πάσχειν are said both in this place and cap. 2. Vers. 20. who suffer for the sake of justice, as Peter explains Vers. 14.who do not suffer as murderers, or as thieves, or as evildoers etc. but as Christianscap. 4. Vers. 15. & 16.who not only did nothing evil οὐδὲν ἄτοπον through which they might have summoned such passions upon themselves, as punishments owed for their crimes.Luc. 23. Vers. 41. but also by their good deeds and zeal for justice have deserved the contrary, who are afflicted by impious men not only beyond, but even against their merit.

He opposes to them κακοποιοῦντας, whom he calls cap. 4. v. 15. κακοποιοὺς, who draw upon themselves the punishments due to their crimes, just as the Caecias wind draws clouds. The Syrian rendered this by circumlocution in this way: It is better for you, when doing good works, to suffer evils, and not when you yourselves do evils. Peter adds προσδιορισμὸν, εἰ θέλει τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. as the Hebrews are accustomed to say: אם ירצה השם if it be the will and good pleasure of GOD, which they write by Sigla or by the initial letters of these words in this way איה The Syrian rendered it simply: If only it be so or it brings [consult facsimile image] the will or good pleasure of GOD. Augustine, book 22 against Faustus, ch. 20, reads: If the Spirit of GOD wills. This is to be imputed either to a faulty codex, or it must be established that Augustine read τὸ πνεῦμα. instead of τὸ θέλημα For that which some establish, that Augustine substituted the Spirit of GOD for the will of GOD because the gifts of grace and mercy are attributed to the Holy Spirit, that is sought from too far away. A parallel passage exists cap. 4. v. 19. οἱ πάσχοντες κατὰ τὸ θέλημα θεοῦ etc. Augustine, book on the gift of perseverance, ch. 2, accepts it thus: If GOD shall have granted this gift, that one should suffer for Him. But it is accepted more simply in this way: If it pleases GOD to permit persecutions and calamities, in which sense the same Augustine explains it in book 22 against Faustus, ch. 20.

Latin:

MELIUS EST ENIM BENEFACIENTES, SI VOLUNTAS DEI VELIT, PATI, QUAM MALEFACIENTES.

Connexio. 1. Interponit exhortationis ad patientiam, novum argumentum, à voluntate DEI sumtum. Cum adversitates piis non casu obtingant, neque temerè accersantur, sed bonâ DEI voluntate ipsis immittantur, aequiore animo sunt ferendae.

2. Occurrit etiam tacitae obiectioni. Qui calumnias & obtrectationes ab hominibus improbis, praesertim vero doctrinae Christianae hostibus perferre coguntur, quandoque in haec erumpunt verba. Non adeò graviter ac molestè convicia ac calumnias ferrem, si essem promeritus: respondet Petrus, satiùs est, te non esse meritum, ut benefaciens ac malè audiens te verum Christianum probes.

3. Consert ergò Apostolus piorum afflictiones cum impiorum hominum passionibus, atque illorum afflictiones meliores dicit, quia pii tantùm foris carne patiuntur, intus habent bonam conscientiam, impii vero & intus & extra affliguntur, quippe quos conscientia prava surdo verbere caedit.

4. Dixerat superiùs, vers. 13.Quis est, qui vobis noceat, si boni aemulatores fueritis? Quia vero etiam illi, qui sunt bonorum operum studiosi, ac pacem cum proximo sectantur, calumniis & persecutionibus vel propter fidei Christianae professionem vel iustitiae studium, sunt expositi, ideò Apostolus illos consolatur, proposito passionis huius commodo. Hac ratione verba Apostoli non ad proximam tantùm sententiam, sed ad totum complexum referuntur. Dixerat de necessitate edendi confessionem fidei, quae illo tempore erat maximè periculosa, iam subiungit, multò esse meliùs, si quid incommodi pro bonae causae defensione ac iustitiae studio sustineant, sic iniustè pati, quàm si ob flagitia sua plectantur.

5. Quod in cap. praeced. v. 19. & 20. Servis in specie proposuerat, illud hoc loco repetit, & in genere ad omnes Christianos accommodat, cum hac in parte sit servorum & Christianorum omnium aequalis ratio. Haec est gratia, si propter Dei conscientiam sustinet quis tristitias, patiens iniustè. Quae enim est gloria, si peccantes & colaphizari suffertis? Sed si benefacientes & patientes sustinetis, haec est gratia apud Deum.

Dispositio. Contra afflictiones praetermeritum piis à persecutoribus & hominibus impiis illatas, consolatur eos Apostolus duplici argumento. 1. ab afflictionum illarum qualitate. Quandoquidem in hac vita omninò patiendum, satiùs est, ut in causa iusta & bona, adeoque propter DEUM patiamur, quàm in negotio iniusto. Nobilius est, indigna pati propter iustitiam, quàm digna propter iniquitatem propriam supplicia. Benè agere & mala pati longè melius est, quàm malè agere, & propterea mala pati. 2. à paterna Dei voluntate. Afflictiones illae non sine permissione, ac bona Dei voluntate piis immittuntur, ergò patienti imò grato animo sunt suscipiendae.

Textus expositio. Κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας &c. Vulgata reddidit. Meliùs est enim ut benefacientes. Sed in Graeco simpliciter habetur. Meliùs est enim benefacientes vos pati, unde in correctioribus exemplaribus Latinis particula ut veluti supervacanea ac superflua rectè omittitur. Κρεῖττον Syrus expressit per [consult facsimile image]iuvat vos, proficit vobis.τὸ πάσχειν denuò hîc absolutè ponitur pro quibusvis passionum generibus, quod Petro in hac Epistola frequens cap. 2. Vers. 19. 20. 21. & 23.cap. 3. Vers. 14. & 18.cap. 4. Vers. 1.15. & 19.cap. 5. Vers. 10.ἀγαθοποιοῦντες πάσχειν dicuntur & hoc loco & cap. 2. Vers. 20. qui patiuntur propter iustitiam, ut exponit Petrus Vers. 14.qui non patiuntur ut homicidae, aut ut fures, aut ut malefici &c. sed ut Christianicap. 4. Vers. 15. & 16.qui non solùm nihil maliοὐδὲν ἄτοπονfecerunt, per quod sibi eiusmodi passiones accersiverint, tanquam debitas flagitiorum suorum poenas.Luc. 23. Vers. 41. sed etiam bonis suis factis & studio iustitiae contrarium promeruerunt, qui non solùm praeter, sed etiam contra suum meritum ab impiis hominibus affliguntur.

Illis opponit κακοποιοῦντας, quos cap. 4. v. 15. vocat κακοποιοὺς, qui flagitiis suis debitas sibi attrahunt poenas, sicut Caecias nubes. Syrus per circumscriptionem reddidit hoc modo. Iuvat vos, cum facientes opera bona, sustinetis mala, & non cum facitis ipsi mala. Addit autem Petrus προσδιορισμὸν, εἰ θέλει τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. Hebraei solent dicere. אם ירצה השםsi sit DEI voluntas & beneplacitum, quod per Sigla sive per initiales harum vocum literas scribunt hoc modo איה Syrus simpliciter reddidit. Si modò ita sit vel ferat[consult facsimile image]voluntas sive beneplacitum DEI. Augustinus lib. 22. contra Faust. c. 20. legit. Si Spiritus DEI velit. id quod vel mendoso Codici imputandum, vel statuendum, quòd Augustinus pro τὸ θέλημα legerit τὸ πνεῦμα. Quod enim quidam statuunt, Augustinum propterea pro voluntate DEI substituisse Spiritum DEI, quia Spiritui sancto tribuuntur dona gratiae & misericordiae, id nimis longè petitum. Locus parallelus extat cap. 4. v. 19.οἱ πάσχοντες κατὰ τὸ θέλημα θεοῦ &c. August. lib. de bono persev. cap. 2. sic accipit. Si concesserit DEUS hoc donum, ut patiatur quis pro ipso. Sed simpliciùs accipitur hoc modo. Si DEO placet permittere persecutiones ac calamitates, quo sensu exponit idem Augustinus lib. 22. contra Faustum cap. 20.

## 3:18
BECAUSE CHRIST ALSO DIED ONCE FOR SINS, THE JUST FOR THE UNJUST, THAT HE MIGHT OFFER US TO GOD, BEING PUT TO DEATH INDEED IN THE FLESH, BUT BROUGHT TO LIFE IN THE SPIRIT.

Connection. 1. He adds another argument for the exhortation to patience, taken from the example of Christ. For just as cap. 2. preceding vers. 19. 20. & 21. when he had exhorted servants in particular to patience, he had joined these two arguments, that it is grace before GOD to suffer evils while doing good, and that Christ left us an example of patience: so in this general exhortation to patience directed to all Christians, he likewise joins these two arguments.

2. This example of Christ was very suitable and appropriate to the Apostle's purpose. He had said that it is better for those doing good to suffer, than for those doing evil. He confirms this most strongly by the example of Christ, who suffered for the unjust, the just one.

3. He amplifies this argument from the example of Christ, sought from the end of the Lord's passion, from the fact that Christ suffered for this reason, that He might bring us to GOD; since therefore we have been brought to GOD, it is fair that we should suffer for the sake of justice and good deeds, but not for evil deeds.

4. In order to console the pious who are subject to afflictions more effectively by the example of Christ, he joins to the passion and death of Christ ἔκβασιν the most joyful thing, when he says that Christ was put to death indeed in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit; from which he leaves it to be understood that the outcome of our passions will be similar, just as Paul shows this application 2. Tim. 2. v. 11. εἰς συναπεθάνομεν, καὶ συζήσομεν. 2. Cor. 4. v. 11. For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh.

Disposition. The Apostle amplifies the passion of Christ, in which he proposes to us an example and argument of patience, 1. from the brevity of the passion. Christ suffered once, His passion was brief, if it is compared to the state of glory, into which He entered after the passion, and through the passion, in which He will also live forever. Rom. 6. v. 9. Christ rising from the dead, dies no more, death no longer has dominion over Him. An argument of exhortation to patience lies hidden in this. Just as Christ's passion was brief, so our passions also are brief and momentary. 2. Cor. 4. v. 17. τὸ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως. 2. from the end of the passion. Christ suffered for our sins, i.e., that He might make satisfaction for our sins; He also suffered, that He might bring us to GOD, i.e., that He might reconcile us with His heavenly Father, and introduce us into heavenly glory to live with Him forever. An argument of exhortation to patience also lies hidden in this. Christ suffered for us; when we were still unjust and sinners. It is therefore fair that we show ourselves grateful to Christ, and for His glory bear patiently the injuries brought upon us by evil men. Christ expiated our sins, and redeemed us from them. Therefore it is fair that we beware of sins, and consequently also of the sin of impatience. Christ suffered, that He might bring us to GOD. Therefore let us not abhor the way of tribulation, through which Christ leads us to GOD and heavenly glory. Act. 14. v. 22. 3. From the innocence of the suffering person joined to it. Christ the just one suffered for the unjust, not for His own, but for our sins. There lies also in it an argument of exhortation to patience. If Christ, when He was perfectly just and innocent, nevertheless suffered voluntarily for the unjust, how much less ought we to refuse sufferings, who are not entirely innocent, but corrupted and depraved by sin. 4. from the joyful outcome of the passion. Christ was indeed put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit, i.e., He struggled out of death and raised Himself to life. There lies also in it an argument of exhortation. Just as Christ entered into life and glory through passion, Luc. 24. v. 26. so we also shall be partakers of glory and the kingdom, if we are partakers of sufferings. Apoc. 1. v. 9. Thus, therefore, almost every word of this verse contains weights of arguments by which we ought to be moved to patience.

Exposition of the text. ὅτι καὶ χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἔπαθε. The emphasis is in the particle καὶ even Christ Himself θεάνθρωπος, from whom we Christians are named, suffered. The little word ἅπαξ the Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] at one time, through a Hebraism. περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν is in this place the same as ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν on account of sins or ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτωλῶν for sinners, just as the Apostle himself explains a little later ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων: for the abstract is put for the concrete, not without emphasis, for it is insinuated that we, however great we are, by nature today after the fall are nothing else than sin. Rom. 5. v. 6. Christ died ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν, where περὶ is likewise explained by ὑπὲρ. & ἁμαρτιῶν through ἀσεβῶν. A passage parallel to this one of ours is held 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. Christ is the propitiation περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετερῶν δὲ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου. The Syrian rendered it in the same way through [consult facsimile image] which signifies a certain exchange and transfer. Christ suffered for sins, for sinners, in the place of sinners. It is therefore hinted that Christ transferred our sins onto Himself, and in the place of us all took their punishments upon Himself, just as the Apostle explains in the preceding second chapter v. 24.. Christ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῶ σώματι αὐτοῦ ὲπὶ τὸ ξύλον. And Hebr. 9. v. 28. Christ ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, which places are parallel to this one of ours regarding the matter. To the word ἁμαρτιῶν two Royal and another Codex add ἡμῶν, which in the way that even certain Latin codices read, for our sins. And indeed it is certain that this προσδιορισμὸν must be entirely understood, because Christ suffered not for his own sins, which he had none, but for our sins, whence this προσδιορισμὸς is added by Peter chap. 2. v. 21. & 24.chap. 4. v. 1. but in this place it is added neither in the more approved Greek codices, nor in the Syriac version. For ἔπαθε two Royal codices & another substitute ἀπέθανε he died, in which way not only the Vulgate version, but also the Syrian rendered it. Christ for sins [consult facsimile image] died. But the remaining Greek codices consistently read ἔπαθε, which reading the context also approves, for the Apostle here treats of the passion, and proposes to us the example of patience in the passion of Christ. Meanwhile we do not deny that the end of the passion is included at the same time, namely death, for Christ was made obedient to his Father even unto death, even the death of the cross,Phil. 2. v. 8. and Peter adds the little word ἅπαξ, which Paul uses peculiarly concerning the death of Christ Rom. 6. v. 10.Hebr. 9. v. 26.

Δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων. He explains what he had said before, that Christ suffered for sins, and he exaggerates the love and kindness of Christ, because when he was perfectly just, he did not hesitate to suffer for the unjust. The Syrian also in this place, as also in the words immediately preceding, has the preposition [consult facsimile image] whose emphasis we weighed a little before. A parallel passage exists Rom. 5. v. 6.For why did Christ, when we were yet weak, according to the time die for the ungodly?vers. 8.when we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

Ἵνα ἡμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ θεῷ. Certain codices read ὑμᾶς you, in which way also Augustine reads in book 1 de peccat. merit. & remiss. chapter 7, of which reading Bede also makes mention. But the more approved codices read in the first person ἡμᾶς. τὸ προσάγειν the Vulgate version accepts it in the meaning of sacrificing, if indeed it rendered, that he might offer us to GOD, in which way also B. Luther translates, auff das er ans Gott opfferte. In Greek it is properly, that he might lead us to GOD, or as Augustine in Epistle 99 & book 1 de merit. & remiss. chapter 27, cites, that he might lead us to God, for that is what προσάγειν. properly signifies Luke 9. vers. 41.

Acts 12. v. 6.ch. 16. v. 20. The Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] that he might bring you near to GOD. It is signified, therefore, that Christ brought us back like wandering sheep into the way, reconciled us to His heavenly Father, and prepared for us free access to Him, just as Paul explains this προσαγωγὴν several times. Rom. 5. v. 2. Through Christ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἔσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν τάυτην, Eph. 2. v. 17. Christ coming preached peace to you, who were far off, and to them that were near. v. 18. for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. ch. 3. v. 12. In Christ we have τὴν παῤῥησίαν καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐν πεποιθήσει διὰ τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ. Meanwhile, it is not absurd to explain this bringing as a bringing by way of an offering and a gift. For the word προσάγειν is used most frequently concerning the bringing of victims to sacrifice Lev. 4. v. 4. & 14. ch. 8. v. 14. ch. 14. v. 2. Num. 6. v. 12. 2. Chron. 29. verse 31. Mal. 1. verse 8. But Christ is said to have offered us to GOD as a sacrifice, both because in His body He offered us as members of His mystical body, and as victims incorporated into Himself to GOD, when he bore our sins in his body upon the wood of the cross 1. Pet. 2. v. 24. and because He reconciled us to GOD through His sacrifice; for to those for whom the sacrifice ἱλαστικὸν is offered, to them GOD is reconciled: and because he made us spiritual Priests to GOD and his Father Rev. 1. verse 6. that we may offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to GOD by Jesus Christ. 1. Pet. 2. verse 5.

Θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκὶ, ζωοποιηθεὶς δὲ τῷ πνέυματι. Certain Latin Codices read in the fourth case, put to death indeed in the flesh, but brought to life in the Spirit, so that this may refer to the pronoun ἡμᾶς immediately preceding. Bede follows this reading in his commentary, who annotates thus at this place: Concerning this mortification of the flesh and vivification of the Spirit, which those have who labor for the Lord through patience, the Apostle Paul also speaks. And if our outward man is corrupted, yet that which is within is renewed day by day. 2. Cor. 4. v. 16. Christ therefore offers us to GOD the Father, when we rejoice to be immolated for Him through the mortification of the flesh, that is, He shows our praiseworthy life in the sight of the Father. Or certainly He offers us to GOD, when He introduces us, freed from the flesh, into the eternal kingdom. which the interlinear Gloss repeats from Bede. Lyranus at this place: Put to death in the flesh i. e. made insensible to the desires of the flesh; brought to life But in the Spirit, that is, made sensible and mobile to follow the Spirit. Suarez tom 2. Disp. 43 sect. 3. prefers that reading because of the authority of the Complutensian Codices, and on account of the version of the Council of Ephesus made by Peltanus. Gagnaeus says, the sense of this Latin version is very congruent, that he might offer us to God mortified in the flesh, but vivified in the Spirit. Meanwhile he rightly adds, unless by the fault of a scribe mortificatos was put for mortificatus, and vivificatos for vivificatus. For the reading in the fourth case is altogether faulty, since it should be read in the first case mortificatus, vivificatus. For 1. all Greek Codices have θανατωθεὶς, ζωοποιηθεὶς. 2. The Syrian also translates it thus. He is dead in the body, and lived in the Spirit. 3. The Greek Fathers read it thus, Clement of Alexandria lib. 6. stromat. and in comm. h. l. Epiphanius heresy 51. and 77. Didymus in fragment. of this Epistle. Oecumenius in comm. h. l. 4. The Latin Fathers also read it in the same way, Jerome in cap. 54. of Isaiah, where for mortificatus he reads occisus. Augustine Epist. 59. and 99. and serm. 14. de verb. Apost. cap. 16. Rufinus in exposit. Symboli &c. 5. The Roman edition of the Latin version corrected and restored the nominative &c. whence the more approved Latin Codices read mortificatus, vivificatus.

Σαρκὶ is put for ἐν σαρκὶ in the flesh, as the Apostle speaks a little later cap. 4. v. 1. χριστοῦς παθόντος ἐν σαρκὶ, where however certain Codices likewise read παθόντος σαρκὶ. Rom. 1. v. 3. that is rendered κατὰ σάρκα. For as Christ is of the seed of David κατὰ σάρκα; so also he suffered and died κατὰ σάρκα. By the name of Flesh, however, according to the common phrase of Scripture, is understood the whole human Nature of Christ, in which Christ sustained passion and death, Ioh. 1. v. 14. For although the soul of Christ, as an immortal Spirit, was not dead nor could it die, it nevertheless sustained the most grievous agonies in the passion, whence it is said to have labored Esai. 53. v. 11. and περίλυπος to have been even unto death Matth. 26. vers. 38. and in death it was separated from the body.

Τῷ πνὲυματι is put for διὰ πνέυματος by the Spirit, namely of the Deity, as Oecumenius ἐξηγήσεως rightly adds for a cause, which explanation is gathered from a parallel place 2. Corinth. 13. vers. 4. Although Christ was crucified ὲξ ἀσθενείας, yet he lives by the power of GOD. As therefore he lives ἐκ δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ, so also it is rightly understood ζωοποιηθεὶς made alive, raised from death to life ἐκ δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ. The same is shown by the antithesis σαρκὸς και πνεύματος. For as by the flesh the human Nature of Christ is understood: so by the Spirit the divine Nature of Christ is understood, through which He raised Himself from death to life. To this pertain all the sayings of Scripture in which not only is Christ said to have raised Himself, for instance according to His divinity John 2. v. 19.chap. 10. v. 17. & 18. but also the Father is said to have raised Him, Romans 6. verse 4.chap. 8. v. 11.Hebrews 13. v. 20. because that divine Nature of the Son, through which He was raised from death, is common to Him with the Father, nay, one and the same. Therefore, there occurs here ἀντιθέσεως ἀνομαλία. For σαρκὶ in the former member of the sentence denotes the receiving subject, in the sense that Christ suffered and died according to His human Nature; but τῷ πνεύματι in the latter member of the sentence does not denote the subject, but the efficient cause, that Christ raised Himself from death according to His divine Nature.

Latin:

QUIA & CHRISTUS SEMEL PRO PECCATIS MORTUUS EST, IUSTUS PRO INIUSTIS, UT NOS OFFERRET DEO, MORTIFICATUS QUIDEM CARNE, VIVIFICATUS AUTEM SPIRITU.

Connexio. 1. Aliud exhortationis ad patientiam subiungit argumentum, petitum ab exemplo Christi. Quemadmodum enim cap. 2. praecedente vers. 19. 20. & 21. quando in specie servos exhortatus fuerat ad patientiam, coniunxerat haec duo argumenta, quòd sit gratia apud DEUM, benefacientem mala sustinere, & quòd Christus patientiae exemplum nobis reliquerit: ita in hac generali ad patientiam exhortatione ad omnes Christianos directa, itidem haec duo argumenta coniungit.

2. Hoc exemplum Christi erat instituto Apostoli valdè accommodatum atque congruum. Dixerat, meliùs esse benefacientes pati, quàm male facientes. hoc validissimè confirmat exemplo Christi, qui iustus pro iniustis passus est.

3. Amplificat hoc argumentum ab exemplo Christi, petitum ex passionis Dominicae fine, ex eo, quòd Christus ideò passus sit, ut nos adduceret DEO; cum ergò DEO simus adducti, aequum est, ut propter iustitiam & benefacta, non autem propter mala facta patiamur.

4. Ut exemplo Christi pios afflictionibus obnoxios efficacius soletur, cum passione & morte Christi coniungit ἔκβασιν laetisfimam, quando dicit, Christum mortificatum quidem carne, vivificatum autem Spiritu; ex quo intelligendum relinquit, nostrarum passionum similem fore eventum, sicut Paulus ostendit hanc applicationem 2. Tim. 2. v. 11.εἰς συναπεθάνομεν, καὶ συζήσομεν.2. Cor. 4. v. 11.Semper enim nos, qui vivimus, in mortem tradimur propter Iesum, ut & vita Iesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali.

Dispositio. Passionem Christi, in qua exemplum & argumen tum patientiae nobis proponit, amplificat Apostolus 1. à passionis brevitate. Christus semel passus est, brevis fuit ipsius passio, si comparetur ad statum gloriae, in quam post passionem, & per passionem ingressus est, in qua etiam vivet in aeternum. Rom. 6. v. 9. Christus resurgens ex mortuis, non ampliùs moritur, mors illi ultra non dominatur. Latet in eo argumentum exhortationis ad patientiam. Sicut Christi passio fuit brevis, ita nostre quoquae passiones sunt breves & momentaneae. 2. Cor. 4. v. 17.τὸ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς θλίψεως. 2. à passionis fine. Christus passus est pro peccatis nostris, i. e. ut pro peccatis nostris satisfaceret; passus etiam est, ut nos DEO adduceret, i. e. cum Patre suo coelesti nos reconciliaret, & secum in aeternum victuros in gloriam coelestem introduceret. Latet etiam in eo exhortationis ad patientiam argumentum. Christus passus est pro nobis; cum adhuc essemus iniusti & peccatores. Aequum igitur est, ut gratos nos Christo praestemus, & ad ipsius gloriam iniurias à malis illatas patienter feramus. Christus peccata nostra expiavit, & ab iis nos redemit. Ergò aequum est, ut à peccatis, ac proinde etiam à peccato impatientiae caveamus. Christus passus est, ut nos DEO adduceret. Ergò non abhorreamus à via tribulationis, per quam Christus nos ad DEUM & gloriam coelestem ducit. Act. 14. v. 22. 3. Ab adiuncta patientis personae innocentia. Christus iustus pro iniustis passus, non pro suis, sed pro nostris peccatis. Latet etiam in eo exhortationis ad patientiam argumentum. Si Christus, cum esset perfectè iustus & innocens; nihilo tamen minùs pro iniustis sponte passus est, quantò minùs nos debemus recusare passiones, qui non sumus prorsus innocentes, sed peccato corrupti ac depravati. 4. à laeto passionis eventu. Christus mortificatus quidem carne, vivificatus autem Spiritu i. e. ex morte eluctatus est, & seipsum ad vitam resuscitavit. Latet etiam in eo exhortationis argumentum. Sicut Christus per passionem in vitam & gloriam est ingressus,Luc. 24. v. 26.ita & nos participes erimus gloriae & regni, si passionum participes simus.Apoc. 1. v. 9. Sic ergò singula penè huius versiculi verba continent argumentorum pondera, quibus ad patientiam debemus permoveri.

Textus expositio. ὅτι καὶ χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἔπαθε. Emphasis est in particula καὶ etiam Christus ipse θεάνθρωπος, à quo Christiani denominamur, passus est. Voculam ἅπαξ Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]uno tempore, per Hebraismum. περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν est hoc loco idem, quòd ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶνpropter peccata seu ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτωλῶνpro peccatoribus, sicut paulo post Apostolus ipse exponit ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων: abstractum enim ponitur pro concreto, non sine emphasi, insinuatur enim, nos quanti quanti sumus, per Naturam hodie post lapsum nihil aliud esse, quàm peccatum. Rom. 5. v. 6.Christus mortuus estὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν, ubi περὶ itidem exponitur per ὑπὲρ. & ἁμαρτιῶν per ἀσεβῶν. Locus huic nostro parallelus habetur 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2.Christus est propitiatioπερὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετερῶν δὲ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου. Syrus reddidith. l. per [consult facsimile image] quod permutationem ac translationem quandam significat. Christus passus est pro peccatis, pro peccatoribus, loco peccatorum. innuitur ergò, Christum peccata nostra in se transtulisse, ac nostrûm omnium loco poenas eorum in se suscepisse, sicut in praecedente capite secundo v. 24. explicat Apostolus. Christusτὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῶ σώματι αὐτοῦ ὲπὶ τὸ ξύλον. Et Hebr. 9. v. 28.Christusἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, quae loca huic nostro quoad rem sunt parallela. Ad vocem ἁμαρτιῶν Regii duo & alius Codex adiiciunt ἡμῶν, quo modo etiam quidam Codd. Latini legunt, pro peccatis nostris. Et sanè certum est, hunc προσδιορισμὸν omninò subintelligendum, quia Christus non pro suis, quae nulla habebat, sed pro nostris peccatis passus est, unde hic προσδιορισμὸς à Petro additur cap. 2. v. 21. & 24.cap. 4. v. 1. sed hoc loco nec in Graecis Codicibus probatioribus, nec in Syriaca versione adiicitur. Pro ἔπαθε Regii duo Codd. & alius substituunt ἀπέθανεmortuus est, quo modo etiam non solùm vulgata versio, sed etiam Syrus reddidit. Christus pro peccatis[consult facsimile image]mortuvus est. Sed Graeci Codd. reliqui constanter legunt ἔπαθε, quam lectionem etiam probat contextus, de passione enim Apostolus hîc agit, & exemplum patientiae in passione Christi nobis proponit. Interim non negamus, includi simul passionis terminum, videlicet mortem, Christus enim factus fuit obediens Patri suo usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis,Phil. 2. v. 8. ac Petrus adiicit voculam ἅπαξ, quâ Paulus peculiariter de Christi morte utitur Rom. 6. v. 10.Hebr. 9. v. 26.

Δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων. Exponit quod priùs dixerat, Christum passum esse pro peccatis, & exaggerat Christi amorem ac benignitatem, quòd cum esset perfectè iustus, pro iniustis pati non dubitaverit. Syrus etiam hoc loco, ut & in verbis proximè praecedentibus habet praepositionem [consult facsimile image] cuius emphasin paulo ante expendimus. Locus parallelus extat Rom. 5. v. 6.Ut quid enim Christus, cum adhuc essemus infirmi, secundùm tempus pro impiis mortuus est?vers. 8.cùm adhuc essemus peccatores, Christus pro nobis mortuus est.

Ἵνα ἡμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ θεῷ. Quidam Codd. legunt ὑμᾶς vos, quo modo etiam legit Augustinus lib. 1. de peccat. merit. & remiss. cap. 7. cuius lectionis etiam meminit Beda. Sed probatiores Codd. legunt in prima persona ἡμᾶς. τὸ προσάγειν vulgata versio accipit in significatione sacrificandi, si enim reddidit, ut nos offerret DEO, quo modo etiam B. Lutherus vertit, auff das er ans Gott opfferte. In Graeco propriè est, ut nos DEO adduceret, vel ut Augustinus Epist. 99. & lib. 1. de merit. & remiss. cap. 27. citat, ut adducat nos ad Deum, id enim propriè significat προσάγειν.Luc. 9. vers. 41.

Actor. 12. v. 6.cap. 16. v. 20. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image]ut appropinquare vos faceret DEO. Significatur ergò Christus nos velut oves errantes in viam reduxerit, Patri suo coelesti nos reconciliaverit, & liberum ad ipsum aditum nobis paraverit, sicut hanc προσαγωγὴν Paulus aliquoties explicat. Rom. 5. v. 2.Per Christumτὴν προσαγωγὴν ἔσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν τάυτην,Eph. 2. v. 17.Christus veniens evangelizavit vobis pacem, qui longè fuistis, & iis, qui prope.v. 18.quoniam per ipsum habemus accessum ambo in uno Spiritu ad Patrem.cap. 3. v. 12.In Christo habemusτὴν παῤῥησίαν καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐν πεποιθήσει διὰ τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ. Interim absurdum non est, hanc adductionem exponere de adductione per modum oblationis ac doni. Usurpatur enim verbum προσάγειν frequentissimè de adductione victimarum ad sacrificium Lev. 4. v. 4. & 14.cap. 8. v. 14.cap. 14. v. 2.Num. 6. v. 12.2. Paralip. 29. vers. 31.Mal. 1. vers. 8. Dicitur autem nos Christus DEO in sacrificium obtulisse, tùm quia in corpore suo nos tanquam membra corporis sui mystici, & hostias sibi incorporatas DEO obtulit, quando peccata nostra in corpore suo super lignum crucis sustulit1. Petr. 2. v. 24. tùm quia nos per sacrificium suum DEO reconciliavit. pro quibus enim sacrificium ἱλαστικὸν offertur, illis DEUS reconciliatur: tùm quia nos fecit spirituales Sacerdotes DEO & Patri suoApoc. 1. vers. 6.ut offeramus spirituales hostias acceptas DEO per Christum Iesum.1. Petr. 2. vers. 5.

Θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκὶ, ζωοποιηθεὶς δὲ τῷ πνέυματι. Quidam Codices Latini legunt in casu quarto, mortificatos quidem carne, vivificatos autem Spiritu, ut referatur hoc ad pronomen ἡμᾶς proximè praecedens. Hanc lectionem sequitur Beda in comment. qui ad h. l. sic annotat. De hac mortificatione carnis & vivificatione Spiritus, quam habent hi, qui pro Domino per patientiam laborant, dicit & Apostolus Paulus. Et si exterior homo noster corrumpitur, sed tamen is, qui intus est, renovatur de die in diem.2. Cor. 4. v. 16.Offert ergò nos DEO Patri Christus, cum per mortificationem carnis pro illo immolari gaudemus, id est, vitam nostram laudabilem in conspectu Patris ostendit. Vel certè offert nos DEO, cum absolutos carne in aeternum nos regnum introducit. quae ex Beda repetit Glossa interlinearis. Lyranus in h. l. Mortificatos carne i. e. insensibiles factos ad desideria carnis; vivificatos Autem Spiritu, id est, sensibiles & mobiles factos ad sequendum Spiritum. Suarez tom 2. Disp. 43 sect. 3. praefert illam lectionem propter autoritatem Complutensium Codicum, & ob versionem Concilii Ephesini factam à Peltano. Gagnaeus dicit, sensum huius Latinae versionis esse valde congruum, ut nos offerret Deo mortificatos carne, vivificatos autem Spiritu. Interim rectè addit, nisi vitio librarii mortificatos positum pro mortificatus, & vivificatos pro vivificatus. Omnino enim vitiosa est lectio in casu quarto, cùm in casu primo legendum sit mortificatus, vivificatus. Nam 1. omnes Codices Graeci habent θανατωθεὶς, ζωοποιηθεὶς. 2. Ita quoque vertit Syrus. Mortuus est in corpore, & vixit in Spiritu. 3. Ita legunt Graeci Patres, clemens Alexandrinus lib. 6. stromat. & in comm. h. l. Epiphanius haeresi 51. & 77. Didymus in fragment. huius Epist. Oecumenius in comm. h. l. 4. Eodem modo etiam Patres Latini legunt, Hieronymus in cap. 54. Esaiae, ubi pro mortificatus legit occisus. Augustinus Epist. 59. & 99. & serm. 14. de verb. Apost. cap. 16. Ruffinus in exposit. Symboli &c. 5. Romana editio versionis Latinae correxit & nominativum restituit &c. unde Codd. Latini probatiores legunt mortificatus, vivificatus.

Σαρκὶ ponitur pro ἐν σαρκὶin carne, ut paulo post Apostolus loquitur cap. 4. v. 1.χριστοῦς παθόντος ἐν σαρκὶ, ubi tamen quidam Codd. itidem legunt παθόντος σαρκὶ.Rom. 1. v. 3. illud redditur κατὰ σάρκα. Ut enim Christus est ex semine Davidis κατὰ σάρκα; ita quoque passus est & mortuus est κατὰ σάρκα.Carnis autem nomine iuxta vulgatam Scripturae phrasin intelligitur tota Natura humana Christi, in qua passionem & mortem Christus sustinuit, Ioh. 1. v. 14. Quamvis enim anima Christi, utpote immortalis Spiritus, non fuerit mortua nec potuerit mori, illa tamen gravissimos angores in passione sustinuit, unde dicitur laborasseEsai. 53. v. 11. ac περίλυποςfuisse usque ad mortemMatth. 26. vers. 38. & in morte fuit à corpore separata.

Τῷ πνὲυματι ponitur pro διὰ πνέυματος per Spiritum, videlicet Deitatis, ut Oecumenius ἐξηγήσεως causâ rectè addit, quae explicatio colligitur ex loco parallelo 2. Corinth. 13. vers. 4. Etsi Christus crucisixus est ὲξ ἀσθενείας, tamen vivit ex virtute DEI. Ut ergò vivit ἐκ δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ, ita quoque rectè intelligitur ζωοποιηθεὶς vivificatus, ex morte in vitam resuscitatus ἐκ δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ. Idem ostendit antithesis σαρκὸς και πνεύματος. Ut enim per carnem Natura Christi humana: ita per Spiritum Natura Christi divina intelligitur, per quam seipsum ex morte in vitam resuscitavit. Quò pertinent omnia Scripturae dicta, in quibus non solùm Christus seipsum dicitur resuscitasse, puta secundùm suam divinitatem Iohan. 2. v. 19.cap. 10. v. 17. & 18. sed etiam pater ipsum resuscitasse dicitur, Roman. 6. vers. 4.cap. 8. v. 11.Hebr. 13. v. 20. quia divina illa Filii Natura, per quam à morte suscitatus est, est ipsi cum Patre communis, imò una atque eadem. Occurrit ergò hîc ἀντιθέσεως ἀνομαλία. Nam σαρκὶ in priore membro sententiae notat subiectum recipiens, sensu eo, quòd Christus secundùm humanam suam Naturam passus sit ac mortuus; sed τῷ πνεύματι in posteriore sententiae membro non notat subiectum, sed causam efficientem, quòd Christus secundùm divinam suam Naturam sese ex morte suscitaverit.

## 3:19-20
IN WHICH ALSO HE WENT AND PREACHED TO THE SPIRITS WHO WERE IN PRISON. WHO HAD BEEN UNBELIEVING SOMETIME, WHEN THEY WAITED FOR THE PATIENCE OF GOD IN THE DAYS OF NOAH, WHEN THE ARK WAS BEING BUILT, IN WHICH A FEW, THAT IS, EIGHT SOULS WERE SAVED THROUGH WATER.

Connection. Those who interpret this passage concerning the descent of Christ to the underworld bring forward a connection of this kind. 1. The Apostle proves that Christ, having been put to death in the flesh, was nevertheless made alive in the Spirit from the fact that in the Spirit, that is, in which as to his soul he came into the prison of hell, and there preached to the spirits. Corn. à Lap. in h. l.

2. The same man connects the text in this way. The Apostle had said v. praeced. 18. that Christ the just died for the unjust, that he might bring us to GOD. Because therefore Christ died for the unjust, not only of his own age and the following, but also for those who preceded the incarnation, for instance those who were in the time of Noah, for that reason he descended to them into hell, that he might liberate them from there, and impart to them the fruit of his death, for instance blessedness and the vision of GOD. Estius connects it in almost the same way. In order to show, he says, that the virtue of the passion of Christ, of which he was speaking, not only pertains to the living, but also penetrates to the dead, as being evidently of him who is prepared to judge the living and the dead, therefore he makes mention of the descent of Christ to the underworld, which was done according to the Spirit, that is, the soul. But we have shown above that by the Spirit here is understood not the soul, but the divinity of Christ. Furthermore, that Christ descended to the underworld for that end, that he might liberate those who were in the time of Noah from hell, and impart to them the fruit of his death, namely blessedness, is asserted without the suffrage of Scripture, nay, against Scripture.

3. The Apostle had made mention of the passion, death, and vivification of Christ, he therefore adds the doctrine concerning the descent of Christ to the lower regions, which immediately followed that vivification and immediately preceded the resuscitation, just as also v. 21. he later makes mention of the resurrection, and v. 22. of the placement at the right hand of GOD, which followed the ascension into the heavens, so that in this way he might join together the principal acts pertaining to the office of Redemption performed by Christ.

4. Some provide this reason for the connection. The Apostle had spoken about the Spirit of Christ, according to which He did not die, or according to which He was recalled to life; now he attaches other effects of this Spirit, and in general he recounts three. The first effect looks to the impious and the damned. The second to the pious and the elect. The third to the person of Christ Himself. The first is declared in the descent to the lower regions. The second through the resurrection. The third in the ascension to the heavens. Hence there are as many articles in the Creed concerning this matter.

5. It is probable, says Estius, that many of those who had despised or neglected the preaching of Noah denouncing destruction to sinners, which Peter here calls being disobedient, upon the coming and flooding of the deluge conceived repentance out of fear, a true one indeed, but imperfect, according to thatPsal. 77. v. 34.When He slew them, they sought Him; whose spirits, therefore, were thrust into prison in the lower regions and detained in it, until they were liberated by Christ descending to the same places. But the reason the Apostle makes special mention of the spirits of those who perished in the deluge is because never did such a great multitude of men perish at once and descend according to their souls to the lower regions, so that from such a notable part the whole might be understood. But this reason for the connection rests upon a false hypothesis concerning the limbo of the Fathers and purgatory, from which Christ is feigned to have liberated certain souls in His descent to the lower regions.

Those who interpret this passage concerning the preaching of Christ through Noah also bring forward various reasons for the connection.

1. Because there is the greatest force in examples, therefore the Apostle proposes a comparison of the times of Noah and of Christ exhibited in the flesh, or of the time in which the Apostles taught by living voice and by writings. Just as in the time of Noah the Spirit of Christ preached to men, most of whom indeed did not believe the preached word, and on that account their spirits are now detained in the prison of outer darkness, where they pay the just penalties for their stubbornness: but others, like Noah with his family, were saved through the midst of the waters of the deluge in the ark, and received the rewards of their obedience: So the same Spirit of Christ in the Apostles and their successors preaches to men, most of whom the preached word do not obey, but persecute his confessors, who will one day experience the same lot as those unbelievers who lived in the time of Noah; some, however, have faith in the preaching of the Gospel, who will be led through the midst of the waves of persecutions to the harbor of salvation by the benefit of Baptism, just as Noah was preserved with his own in the ark.

2. The Apostle had said that Christ was put to death in the flesh, and made alive in the Spirit. The mortification of the flesh or the passion and death of Christ is an argument of true humanity: the vivification of the Spirit or the resurrection of Christ is an argument of true Deity. For unless Christ in the unity of his person were true God, he could not have made himself alive from death by divine power essentially proper to himself. The Apostle confirms this Deity of Christ more evidently when he teaches that Christ, in that very Spirit according to which he was made alive, that is, according to his divinity, had long ago performed the office of teaching in the times of Noah. Beda in h. l. He who coming in the flesh in our times preached the way of life to the world, he himself also before the flood preached by the Spirit, coming to those who were then unbelievers and lived carnally. For he himself was in Noah through the Holy Spirit, and in the other saints who were then, and through their good conversation he preached to the wicked men of that age, so that they might be converted to better things.

3. Lyranus brings forward such a connection. The Apostle here introduces an example to the purpose concerning Christ, in whom an example could not be placed, as far as the first condition of faith is concerned, namely its confirmation in the heart of the believer. For in him there was no faith, but clear vision from the instant of conception, but as far as the other two are concerned, namely as far as the derivation of faith into others and the suffering of adversities on account of its truth, he places an example concerning Christ, and first as far as the last (condition) is concerned, so that he may connect himself to the immediately preceding letter, he says. Because Christ also suffered, and in him he gave us an example. Then he places an example concerning the other condition, namely concerning the derivation of faith and preaching. And first he places the example, secondly he infers a corollary.
