Concerning the first, it must be known that the preaching of Noah, calling the sinners of his time to repentance, so that they would not perish in the flood, was a figure of the preaching of Christ through himself and his disciples until the end of the world, calling sinners to repentance, so that they do not perish in the final judgment, on account of which he places an example of this through a place from the lesser, making an argument that if he called those to repentance, much more strongly he has called and will call others.

4. The Apostle had said that a good conscience and holy conversation must be joined with the confession of faith.v. 16.Furthermore, to it now He exhorts everyone by proposing the example of those who, in the flood, made shipwreck of salvation on account of a despised conscience and good conduct.

5. The Apostle had exhorted to patience and long-suffering verse 17, by the example of Christ, who suffered hard and dire things for us beyond merit v. 18. now furthermore he exhorts to the same by the example of Noah, whom 2. Epist. 2. v. 5. he calls a herald of righteousness, indeed of God himself, who awaited the conversion of the antediluvian men for one hundred years.

6. He adds consolation to the exhortation. For having made a comparison of the times of Noah, in which God, having destroyed the impious through the flood, miraculously preserved the pious Noah with his own, he consoles the pious, that the Lord wishes to save them also through Baptism unto eternal life.

7. On the occasion of the word Spirit, he digresses into the history concerning the spirits of men who lived in the days of Noah, and on this occasion he commemorates two illustrious benefits bestowed upon the antediluvian world, the former of which is the preaching of the word, the latter the preservation of Noah from the waters of the flood.

Disposition. The Apostle amplifies the benefit of preaching. 1. By a description of the present state, that those spirits to whom the preaching was made in the times of Noah of old, are now established in prison. 2. By a description of the past state, that they were incredulous to the divine preaching, which incredulity of theirs is exaggerated by the long delay of that time, during which God awaited their conversion, and warned them of the punishment of the flood that was to follow through the construction of the ark. The Apostle amplifies the benefit of preservation. 1. By a description of the fewness of those to whom that happened. For only eight souls were saved in the ark. 2. By a description of the means through which they were preserved in the flood, which was the wooden ark, lifted up by the waters of the flood.

Exposition of the text. ἐν ᾧ Oecumenius explains it causally, on account of which, therefore, wherefore. But among the Greeks this is less customary, who more frequently use the formula ἐφ ᾧ in this signification Roman. 5. v. 12. 2. Cor. 5. v. 4. meanwhile we do not ignore nor deny that ἐν ᾧ is used in a causal signification Rom. 8. v. 3. which could also be accommodated to this passage, if we wish to take it concerning the descent of Christ to the underworld. Bede refers it to those words of the verse immediately preceding, that he might bring us to God. That, however, he says, the Apostle says, in which, signifies in that which he had set forth before, that he might offer us to God. Because even then, if any had wished to believe at the preaching of the Lord, which he extended through the life of the faithful, he rejoiced to offer them also to God the Father. If any were disparaging the good, as if they were evildoers, these were confounded when the flood came. For it can be understood of both, what he says, in which, that is, both to those who were shut up in the flesh, coming in the Spirit he preached, so that through this same preaching of his, both a crown of praise might be born for the believers, and confusion for those who had persisted in unbelief. But the relative ᾧ is most simply referred to the immediately preceding τὸ πνεῦμα, in which namely the Spirit, or according to which Spirit, or in respect of which. Through this προσδιορισμὸν, what is said about the whole person of Christ is demonstrated to be understood according to his divine Nature. The Syrian rendered it by the copulative particle O.

Καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασι πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν. Bede brings forward a double reading. The former is this, in which also to those who were shut up in the flesh, coming in the Spirit he preached, where those weighed down by carnal desires are called shut up in prison, Hugo and the Carthusian likewise read in the flesh. But the Greek text protests against this reading, as do the more approved Latin Codices, which make no mention of the flesh, although some of the ancient Interpreters understand the flesh by the name of prison. The latter has it thus. In which also to those who were in prison coming in the Spirit he preached. But this reading also departs from the Greek text, inasmuch as it does not read in the singular, but in the plural τοῖς πνεύμασι, nor does it express the past tense, they were in prison, but says indefinitely and indeterminately τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασι. After the word φυλακή in certain Codices is interposed κατακεκλεισμένοις, which the Syrian Interpreter also reads. Bede and Albert add the same thing, according to the testimony of Dionysius the Carthusian. Rufinus in the exposition of the Creed ἐξηγητικῶς added, to the spirits who were shut up in prison. But the more approved Greek Codices omit that, nor is it held in the Latin vulgate version. Robertus Stephanus makes mention of a certain Greek Codex, which reads κατακεκλεισμένοις, but it is believed that it was conformed to some Latin exemplar. The Syrian rendered it in this way. And he preached to those souls, which are or were included in Sheol. And yet in this version certain things are added, which are not in the Greek text; certain things are omitted, which are held in it. For no mention of inclusion is made in the Greek text, as we have already warned before: ἐν ᾧ is omitted and the participle πορευθεὶς. Lucas Brugensis maintains that πνεύματι has been changed into πνεύμασι, and the former the reading is to be preferred, so that the sense is, that Christ coming in the Spirit preached to those who were in prison. But as many Greek Codices as are extant, Cyril in his book on the faith to Theodosius, Oecumenius, etc., read πνεύμασι.. Augustine in Epistle 99, Jerome in chapter 54 of Isaiah, Rufinus in his exposition of the Creed read Spirits, for that Christ came in the Spirit, the Apostle had already indicated before through the relative ᾧ. The Vulgate rendered it: In which also coming he preached to those spirits who were in prison. But in the Greek it is said indefinitely τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ,, as we have likewise already warned before, which can be supplied by the present Are, or by the past Were. And τὸ πορευθεὶς is not a participle of the present, but of the past tense, nor does it properly signify to come, but to set out, whence the Vulgate Interpreter himself a little later v. 22. rendered it having set out. By τὴν φυλακὴν is understood the infernal prison, in which meaning this little word is used Apoc. 20. v. 7. and the passage Matth. 5. v. 25. can with a certain respect be accommodated here, where prison is proposed as a type of hell. Compare Matth. 18. v. 30. Luc. 12. v. 58. whence also the Syrian rendered it by Sheol. By τὰ πνεύματα are understood souls, just as also Hebr. 12. v. 23. Spirits are called souls separated from bodies; and the Syrian in this place likewise rendered it by [consult facsimile image]. But the Apostle was more pleased with the word πνευμάτων, than ψυχῶν on account of the antanaclasis, because he had made mention of πνεύματος in the preceding verse. The sense therefore is this: Christ in the Spirit, that is, in his divinity, or according to his divine Nature, having set out, preached through Noah, to wit, the herald of righteousness, to the antediluvian men, whose souls are in the prison of hell, to wit, of those who were unwilling to have faith in this preaching, as follows immediately, v. 20.

Ἀπειθήσασι πότε. The Vulgate rendered it: Who were incredulous at one time. The Greek word is properly used in the Scriptures of those who obstinately refuse to have faith in the truth manifested and sufficiently declared, who do not suffer themselves to be persuaded. But those are understood who were unwilling to give place to the admonitions proposed through Noah, so that they might do penance. The Syrian rendered it, [consult facsimile image] who did not acquiesce, who did not consent, who were not persuaded, to wit, that those things were true which Noah was proposing to them in the name of God.

Ὅτε ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ μακροθυμία. The Vulgate rendered it, when the patience of God was waiting. But in the Greek it is the nominative, when the patience of God was waiting, i.e., for the repentance and amendment of the antediluvian men; for He had prefixed for them 120 years as a space for repentance. Gen. 6. 3. Moreover, it is said that the patience of God was waiting, when God, because of His gentleness and μακροθυμίᾳ, waits patiently, just as Peter himself explains in 2 Epist. 3. 9. ὁ Κύριος μακροθυμεῖ εἰς ἡμᾶς. In the same way, see when the patience of God was waiting, Jerome, Augustine, Epist. 99, Idacius lib. 9 against Varimadus, Bede, and Dionysius the Carthusian in his commentary read it; and indeed the Syrian Interpreter, who ἐξηγητικῶς rendered it thus, when the long-suffering of God was commanding that an ark be made because of the expectation of their conversion. There is therefore an error here in the Latin Vulgate version, which was removed in the Roman Missal corrected by Clement VIII in the Epistle for the Friday of Easter week. Furthermore, for ὅ τε some Greek Codices read ὅ τι because, but the more approved Codices consistently read ὅ τε, which fits the context better, in which way the Syrian also reads, who rendered it [consult facsimile image] when, and Oecumenius in his commentary.

For ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο the Complutensian, the Royal 3, and another Codex read ἀπεξεδέχετο, and Robert Stephanus noted that not a few Codices read it so, which reading could be confirmed from the fact that Paul delights in the use of the compound word ἀπεκδέχεσθαι Rom. 8. 19. & 23.1. Cor. 1. 7.Gal. 5. 5.Phil. 3. 20.Hebr. 9. 28. But more and more approved Codices read ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο, in which way Oecumenius also seems to have read, which verb Paul uses likewise, although less frequently. 1. Cor. 11. 33.c. 16. 11.Hebr. 11. 10. Erasmus and Gagnaeus explain that word ὲξεδέχετο passively, when the long-suffering of God was being awaited, in which way Rupert also reads in his 4th book on Genesis c. 17. But τὸ ἐκδέχεσθαι, even if it is middle in voice, it is nevertheless always taken actively Ioh. 5. 3.Act. 17. 16.1. Cor. 11. 33.c. 16. 11.Heb. 11. 10. in which way Jerome also reads in c. 54. Isaiah, Augustine Epist 99, Idacius against Varimadus; when the patience of God was waiting, which active meaning also fits this passage better, because the patience or long-suffering of God was waiting for the conversion of men, and it was not being awaited by men, unless we take it thus with the Ordinary Gloss following the Vulgate version. Those antediluvian men were not using the patience of GOD for repentance, but were waiting for it, as if it were always going to last, which however is somewhat harsh.

ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶε in the days of Noah that is, in the times of Noah. This can be referred both to the preceding member, when the long-suffering of God was waiting, and to the following member, when the ark was being built.

Κατασκευαζομένης κιβωτοῦ. The Vulgate rendered it, when the ark was being built. In the Greek it is, when the ark was being prepared, see in testimony of the coming flood. Gen. 6. v. 14. κιβωτὸν The LXX Interpreters in the O.T. call that most famous vessel, which Noah built by the special command of God as the flood was impending, which represented the form of an ark. Gen. 6. v. 14. & seqq. cap. 7. v. 1. & seqq. cap. 8. vers. 1. & seqq. cap. 9. vers. 10. & 18. which appellation Matthew also uses cap. 24. vers. 38. Luke cap. 17. vers. 27. Paul Hebr. 11. vers. 7. Moses calls it תבה building, house, construction, from the root בנה he built. Profane writers also use the name κιβωτοῦ for ark or chest. Athen. lib. 3. ὡς τι μέγα κειμήλιον ἀπετίθεντο ἐν ταῖς κιβωτοῖς. Dioscor. lib. 3. cap. 26. concerning wormwood δοκεῖ δὲ περιπαττόμενον εἰς τὰς κιβωτούς ἄβρωτα τηρεῖν τὰ ἱμάτια. The Syrian in this place retained the Greek appellation [consult facsimile image].

Ἐις ἣν ὀλιγαι (τουτέστιν ὀκτὼ) ψυχαὶ διεσώθησαν. The Syrian connects this member with the former in this way, & eight souls only entered into it & were saved. He thought, therefore, that the sentence was to be completed by the word [consult facsimile image] entered. But the Greek εἰς ἣν can be taken as placed for ἐν ᾗ in which, in which way the Vulgate Interpreter also translates, by which reasoning there will be no ellipsis in the text. For ὀλίγαι the Royal and another Codex read ὀλίγοι, in which way the Vulgate version also seems to have read, which rendered it, few, as also the interlinear gloss, which adds, few who believed in God. The Syrian in its place put an exclusive, eight souls only. By ὀκτὼ ψυχὰς are understood eight humans according to the synecdoche customary in the Scriptures Acts 2. 41.cap. 7. v. 14. who were Noah and his wife, the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth and their wives, Gen. 7. 7. That in the version of the LXX Interp. Gen. 5. v. 15. & seqq. Methuselah is said to have been 167 years old when he begat Lamech, and afterwards to have lived 882 years, which sum is one thousand and forty-nine years, from which it follows that Methuselah lived some years after the flood, and thus not eight souls only were saved in the ark, they acknowledge there to be an error in that, August. lib. qq. in Genes. q. 2. & lib. 15. de Civ. Dei cap. 15. Hieronym. in lib. de trad. Hebr. which is to be corrected from the Hebrew text, which has a smaller number.

Δι' ὕδατος. Some, among whom is Gagnaeus, think that διὰ is put for ὰπὸ, through, for from, so that the sense may be, they were saved from the water, namely, lest they should be submerged by the waters of the flood together with the others. But examples of this meaning are very rare. Some retain the customary meaning, & explain it in this way, they were saved through water that is, by the benefit of the water lifting up the ark. For the water which extinguished the others, by lifting the ark on high, caused that those who were in it were not extinguished together with the others. This explanation could be most beautifully accommodated to ἀντίτυπον of water in Baptism, of which the Apostle makes mention in the following verse, since through it our old man is extinguished, but the new is preserved for eternal life. But this effect of the water was accidental. Some establish that διὰ is placed for ἐν, in which way it is accepted Rom. 4. vers. 11. with a different meaning, however, so that time may be noted, since here it describes a place. The passage 2. Epist. 3. vers. 5. approaches more closely The earth consists δι' ὕδατος i. e. ἐν μἐσῳ ὕδατος in the midst of waters, So also in this place They were saved in water i. e. in the midst of the waters, for above the rain was descending, below were the waters of the flood, inundating and devastating everything. But this little word could also denote time, they were saved in water i. e. at that time, in which the waters of the flood inundated and extinguished all the remaining men. It is most simply explained in this way, they were saved in water i. e. notwithstanding the water of the flood, in which sense the little word διὰ is almost used 1. Tim. 2. v. 15. The woman shall be saved διὰ τεκνογονίας, notwithstanding the generation of children, even if she generates children in marriage, concerning which Apostolic passage Bellarmine lib. de Matrim. cap. 2. writes thus. The Apostle does not wish to signify that the generation of children is the cause of salvation, but that the woman in the state of matrimony, or in the state of generating children, will be safe, if she shall have remained in faith. Therefore that through the generation of children is put for that, in the generation of children, which phrase is most frequent in the Scriptures. In place of proof he brings forward these sayings. Act. 15. v. 21. Moses is read through every Sabbath i. e. in every Sabbath. cap. 26. v. 11. through all the Synagogues i. e. in all the Synagogues. Rom. 4. 11. that he might be the father of believers through uncircumcision i. e. in uncircumcision. But the former two sayings are not sufficiently are pertinently accommodated here, because in the Greek text there is not διὰ but κατὰ.. The third saying pertains properly here, that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised, because uncircumcision is not the cause that Abraham was the father of all them that believe, but existing in uncircumcision he was made the father of all them that believe through faith. Moreover, other sayings can be joined. Acts 14. verse 22. διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων through much tribulation, that is, in many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of heaven; tribulations cannot hinder salvation, but rather promote it, just as water lifting up the ark promoted the preservation of those who were in it. 2. Cor. 6. v. 8. by honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report. Gal. 4. v. 13. through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you. Eph. 6. v. 18. by all prayer and supplication i. e. in all prayer.

Latin:

IN QUO & HIS, QUI IN CARCERE ERANT SPIRITIBUS VENIENS PRAEDICAVIT. QUI INCREDULI FUERANT ALIQUANDO, QUANDO EXPECTABANT DEI PATIENTIAM IN DIEBUS NOAE, CUM FABRICARETUR ARCA, IN QUA PAUCI, HOC EST, OCTO ANIMAE SALVAE FACTAE SUNT PER AQUAM.

Connexio. Qui de Christi ad inferos descensu locum hunc accipiunt, proferunt huiusmodi connexionem. 1. Probat Apostolus, Christum mortificatum carne, vivificatum tamen fuisse Spiritu ex eo, quòd Spiritu, i. e. quo ad animam venerit in carcerem inferni, ibique Spiritibus praedicarit. Corn. â Lap. in h. l.

2. Idem connectit textum hoc modo. Dixerat Apostolusv. praeced. 18.Christum iustum mortuum esse pro iniustis, ut nos DEO adduceret. Quia ergò Christus mortuus est pro iniustis, non tantùm sui aevi & sequentis, sed & pro iis, qui in carnationem praecesserunt, puta qui fuerunt tempore Noë, idcirco descendit ad eos in infernum, ut eos inde liberaret, eisque suae mortis fructum, puta beatitudinem & visionem DEI impertiret. Eodem ferè modo Estius connectit. Ut ostenderet, inquit, virtutem passionis Christi, de quâ loquebatur, non solùm ad vivos pertinere, sed etiam ad in feros penetrare, tanquam videlicet eius, qui paratus est iudicare vivos & mortuos, ideo mentionem facit descensus Christi ad inferos, qui secundùm Spiritum i. e. animam factus. Atqui ostendimus superiùs, per Spiritum hî intelligi non animam, sed divinitatem Christi. Praeterea Christum eo fine ad inferos descendisse, ut eos, qui fuerunt tempore Noae, ex inferno liberaret, eisque mortis suae fructum; beatitudinem sc. impertiret, sine Scripturae suffragio, imò contra Scripturam asseritur.

3. Apostolus mentionem fecerat passionis, mortis & vivificationis Christi, subiungit ergò doctrinam de descensu, Christi ad inferos, qui vivificationem illam proximè fuit insecutus ac reluscitationem immediatè antegressus, sicut etiam v. 21. postea mentionem facit resurrectionis, & v. 22. collocationis ad dextram DEI, quae secuta fuit ascensionem ad coelos, ut hac ratione praecipuos actus ad officium Redemtionis à Christo peractum pertinentes coniungat.

4. Quidam hanc tradunt connexionis rationem. Dixerat Apostolus de Spiritu Christi, secundùm quem non fuit mortuus, aut secundùm quem ad vitam revocatus, nunc alia effecta huius Spiritus attexit, ac ingenere tria recenset. Primus effectus ad impios & dammatos spectat. Secundus ad pios & electos. Tertius ad ipsam Christi personam. Primus declaratus est in descensu ad inferos. Secundus per resurrectionem. Tertius in ascensione ad coelos. Inde totidem articuli in Symbolo de hoc negotio.

5. Probabile esse dicit Estius, multos ex iis, qui praedicationem Noae denunciantis interitum peccatoribus contemserant aut neglexerant, quod hîc Petrus vocat, fuisse incredulos, superveniente & inundante diluvio poenitentiam ex timore concepisse, veram quidem illam, sed imperfectam, iuxta illudPsal. 77. v. 34.Cùm occideret eos, quaerebant eum; quorum proinde Spiritus in carcerem apud inferos detrusi fuerunt & in eo detenti, donec Christo ad eadem loca descendente liberarentur. Ideò vero Apostolum de Spiritibus eorum, qui diluvio perierunt, speciatim meminisse, quia nunquam tanta hominum multitudo simul periit & secundùm animas ad inferna descendit, ut ex parte tàm notabili totum intelligatur. At haec connexionis ratio nititur falsâ hypothesi de limbo Patrum ac purgatorio, ex quo Christus in suo ad inferos descensu animas quasdam liberasse fingitur.

Qui de praedicatione Christi per Noahum hunc locum accipiunt, varias & ipsi connexionis rationes afferunt.

1. Quia maxima vis in exemplis, ideò proponit Apostolus collationem temporum Noae, & Christi in carne exhibiti, seu temporis, quo Apostoli docuerunt viva voce & scriptis. Quemadmodum tempore Noae Spiritus Christi praedicavit hominibus, quorum plerique quidem verbo praedicato non crediderunt, & propterea eorum Spiritus nunc detinentur in carcere exteriorum tenebrarum, ubi iustas suae pervicaciae luunt poenas: alii verò ut Noa cum familia suaper medias diluvii aquas in arca servati, obedientiae, suae praemia reportarunt: Sic idem Christi Spiritus in Apostolis & eorum successoribus praedicat hominibus, quorum plerique verbo praedìcato non obtemperant, sed confessores eius persequuntur, qui eandem cum incredulis illis, qui tempore Noahi vixerunt, sortem aliquando experientur; quidam vero Evangelii praedicationi fidem babent, qui per medios persecutionum fluctus ad portum salutis beneficio Baptismi perducentur, sicut Noabus cum suis in arca conservatus.

2. Dixerat Apostolus, Christum esse mortificatum carne, & vivificatum Spiritu. Mortificatio carnis sive passio & mors Christi est argumentum verae humanitatis: vivificatio Spiritus sive resuscitatio Christi est argumentum verae Deitatis. Nisi enim Christus in personae unitate esset verus Deus, non potuisset seipsum divinâ virtute essentialiter sibi propriâ ex morte vivificare. Hanc Deitatem Christi evidentiùs confirmat Apostolus, quando docet, Christum in illo ipso Spiritu, secundùm quem vivificatus est, h. e. secundùm divinitatem suam iamdum temporibus Noae docendi officio fuisse functum. Beda in h. l. Qui nostris temporibus in carne veniens, iter vitae mundo praedicavit, ipse etiam ante diluvium eis, qui tunc increduli erant, & carnaliter vivebant, Spiritu veniens praedicavit. Ipse enim per Spiritum sanctum erat in Noë, caeterisque, qui tunc fuêre sanctis, & per eorum bonam conversationem, pravis illius aevi hominibus, ut ad meliora converterentur, praedicavit.

3. Lyranus eiusmodi connexionem profert. Apostolus hîc ad propositum inducit exemplum de Christo, in quo non potuit poni exemplum, quantum ad primam fidei conditionem, sc. eius confirmationem in corde credentis. nam in eo non fuit fides, sed elara visio ab instanti conceptionis, sed quantum ad alias duas, sc. quantum ad fidei derivationem in alios & sufferentiam adversorum propter eius veritatem ponit exemplum de Christo, & primò quantum ad ultimam (conditionem) ut continuet se literae immediatè praecedenti, dicit. Quia & Christus passus est, & in eo dedit nobis exemplum. Deinde ponit exemplum de alia conditione, sc. de derivatione fidei & praedicatione. Et primò ponit exemplum, secundò infert corollarium. Circa primum sciendum, quòd praedicatio Noae vocando ad poenitentiam peccatores sui temporis, ne perirent in diluvio, fuit figura praedicationis Christi per se & discipulorum usque in mundi finem, vocando peccatores ad poenit entiam, ne pereant in finali iudicio, propter quod de hoc ponit exemplum per locum à minori faciens argumentum, quòd si illos vocavit ad poenitentiam, multò fortiùs vocavit & vocabit alios.

4. Dixerat Apostolus, cum confessione fidei coniungendam esse bonam conscientientiam & sancta conversationem.v. 16.Ad eam iam porrò omnes hortatur proposito exemplo eorum, qui in diluvio salutis naufragium fecerunt ob contemtam conscientiam & conversationem bonam.

5. Exhortatus fuerat Apostolus ad patientiam & longanimitatem vers. 17. exemplo Christi, pro nobis dura ac dira praeter meritum passiv. 18.iam porrò ad eandem exhortatur exemplo Noahi, quem 2. Epist. 2. v. 5.vocat praeconem iustitiae, imò ipsius Dei, qui hominum antediluvianorum conversionem centum annis expectavit.

6. Exhortationi subiungit consolationem. Facta enim collatione temporum Noae, in quibus Deus deletis per diluvium impiis pium Noah cum suis mirabiliter conservavit, solatur pios, quòd ipsos etiam Dominus per Baptismum ad vitam aeternam servare velit.

7. Occasione vocabuli Spiritus digreditur in Historiam de Spiritibus hominum, qui vixerunt in diebus Noae, & hac occasione commemorat duo illustria beneficia, in mundum antediluvianum collata, quorum prius est verbi praedicatio, posterius Noae ab aquis diluvii conservatio.

Dispositio. Praedicationis beneficium amplificat Apostolus. 1. Descriptione status praesentis, quòd Spiritus illi, quibus olim temporibus Noae praedicatio facta, iam sint in carcere constituti. 2. Descriptione status praeteriti, quòd fuerint divinae praedicationi increduli, quae incredulitas ipsorum exaggeratur diuturna illius temporis morâ, quo Deus ipsorum conversionem expectavit, & per arcae extructionem de secutura diluvii poena eos praemonuit. Conservationis beneficium amplificat Apostolus. 1. Descriptione paucitatis eorum, quibus illud obtigit. Octo enim duntaxat animae in arca sunt salvatae. 2. Descriptione medii, per quod in diluvio conservati sunt, quod fuit arca lignea, ab aquis diluvii elevata.

Textus expositio. ἐν ᾧ Oecumenius exponit causaliter, propter quod, idcirco, quamobrem. Sed apud Graecos hoc minùs usitatum, qui frequentiùs in hac significatione utuntur formulâ ἐφ ᾧRoman. 5. v. 12.2. Cor. 5. v. 4. interim non ignoramus nec negamus, ἐν ᾧ in significatione causali usurpari Rom. 8. v. 3. quae etiam ad hunc locum posset accommodari, si de descensu Christi ad inferos eum accipere velimus. Beda refert ad illa verba vers. proximè praecedentis, ut nos adduceret Deo. Quòd autem, inquit, Apostolus dicit, in quo, significat in eo, quod praemiserat, ut nos offerret Deo. Quia & tunc si qui ad praedicationem Domini, quam per vitam fidelium praetendebat, credere voluissent, & ipsos offerre Deo Patri gaudebat. Si qui autem detrahebant de bonis, tanquam de malefactoribus, hi veniente diluvio confundebantur. Nam & de utroque potest intelligi, quod ait, in quo, id est, & eis, qui in carne conclusi erant, Spiritu veniens praedicavit, ut per eandem suam praedicationem & credentibus corona laudis, & iis, qui in incredulitate perstitissent, confusio nasceretur. Sed relativum ᾧ simplicissimè refertur ad proximè praecedens τὸ πνεῦμα,in quo scilicet Spiritu, sive secundùm quem Spiritum, sive cuius respectu. Per hunc προσδιορισμὸν, quod de tota Christi persona dicitur, secundùm divinam eius Naturam accipiendum esse demonstratur. Syrus reddidit per particulam copulativam O.

Καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασι πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν. Beda duplicem profert lectionem. Prior haec est, in quo & iis, qui in carne conclusi erant, Spiritu veniens praedicavit, ubi conclusi carcere vocantur carnalibus desideriis aggravati, Hugo & Carthusianus itidem legunt in carne. Sed reclamat huic lectioni textus Graecus, ut & probatiores Codd. Latini, qui nullam carnis mentionem faciunt, licet quidam veterum Interpretum carceris nomine carnem intelligant. Posterior sic habet. In quo & iis, qui in carcere erant Spiritu veniens praedicavit. Sed & haec lectio à textu Graeco discedit, quippe qui non in singulari, sed in plurali legit τοῖς πνεύμασι, nec exprimit tempus praeteritum, erant in carcere, sed indefinitè & indeterminatè dicit τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασι. Post vocem φυλακή in quibusdam Codicibus interponitur κατακεκλεισμένοις, quod Syrus Interpres etiam legit. Addunt idipsum Beda & Albertus, teste Dion. Carthusiano. Ruffinus in expos. Symb. ἐξηγητικῶς addidit, Spiritibus qui erant in carcere conclusi. Sed probatiores Codices Graeci illud omittunt, nec habetur in versione Latina vulgata. Robertus Stephanus mentionem facit cuiusdam Codicis Graeci, qui legitκατακεκλεισμένοις, sed is ad Latinum aliquod exemplar conformatus creditur. Syrus reddidit hoc modo. Et praedicavit animabus illis, quae inclusae sunt vel fuerunt in Scheol. Atqui in hac versione quaedam adduntur, quae non sunt in textu Graeco; quaedam omittuntur, quae in eo habentur. Inclusionis enim nulla fit mentio in textu Graeco, ut iam ante monuimus: omittitur ἐν ᾧ & participium πορευθεὶς. Lucas Brugensis statuit πνεύματι mutatum esse in πνεύμασι, ac priorem lectionem esse praeferendam, ut sit sensus, Christum Spiritu venientem praedicasse illis, qui in carcere. Sed quotquot extant Codd. Graeci, Cyrill. lib. de fide ad Theodos. Oecumenius &c. legunt πνεύμασι. Augustinus Epist. 99. Hieronymus in cap. 54. Esai. Ruffinus in expos. Symb. legunt Spiritibus, quòd enim Spiritu venerit Christus, iam ante indicaverat Apostolus per relativum ᾧ Vulgata reddidit. In quo & his, qui in carcere erant Spiritibus veniens praedicavit. Sed in Graeco indefinitè dicitur τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ, uti itidem iam antè monuimus, quod suppleri potest per praesens Sunt, vel per praeteritum Erant. Ac τὸ πορευθεὶς non est praesentis, sed praeteriti temporis participium, nec propriè significat venire, sed proficisci, unde ipse vulgatus Interpres paulo pòst v. 22. reddidit profectus. Per τὴν φυλακὴν intelligitur carcer infernalis, in qua significatione haec vocula usurpatur Apoc. 20. v. 7. ac potest certo respectu huc accommodari locus Matth. 5. v. 25. ubi carcer ut inferni typus proponitur. Confer Matth. 18. v. 30.Luc. 12. v. 58. unde & Syrus reddidit per Scheol. Per τὰ πνεύματα intelliguntur animae, sicut etiam Hebr. 12. v. 23.Spiritus vocantur animae à corporibus separatae; ac Syrus hoc loeo itidem reddidit per [consult facsimile image] Magis vero delectatus fuit Apostolus voce πνευμάτων, quàm ψυχῶν propter antanaclasin, quia πνεύματος in versu praeced. mentionem fecerat. Sensus igitur hic est. Christus in Spiritu, h. e. divinitate suâ, sive secundùm divinam suam Naturam profectus praedicavit per Noahum sc. praeconem iustitiae hominibus antediluvianis, quorum animae sunt in inferni carcere, eorum scil. qui praedicationi huic fidem habere noluerunt, sicut statim sequitur, v. 20.

Ἀπειθήσασι πότε. Vulg. reddidit. Qui increduli fuerunt aliquando. Graeca vox propriè in Scripturis usurpatur de iis, qui veritati manifestatae, & sufficienter declaratae fidem habere pertinaciter renuunt, qui non patiuntur sibi persuaderi. Intelliguntur autem illi, qui admonitionibus per Noahum propositis locum dare noluerunt, ut poenitentiam agerent. Syrus reddidit, [consult facsimile image]qui non acquieverunt, qui non consenserunt, qui non fuerunt persuasi, sc. vera esse, quae Noahus Dei nomine ipsis proponebat.

Ὅτε ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ μακροθυμία. Vulgata reddidit, quando expectabant Dei patientiam. Sed in Graeco est nominativus, quando expectabat Dei patientia, sc. hominum antediluvianorum poenitentiam & emendationem; praefixerat enim illis 120. annos ad spacium poenitentiae. Gen. 6. 3. Dicitur autem Dei patientia expectare, quando Deus pro sua lenitate & μακροθυμίᾳ patienter expectat, sicut Petrus ipse exponit 2. Epist. 3. 9. ὁ Κύριος μακροθυμεῖ εἰς ἡμᾶς. Eodem modo, vid. quando expectabat Dei patientia, legunt Hieronymus, Augustinus, Epist. 99. Idacius lib. 9. contra Varimadum, Beda, Dionys. Carthus. in com. quin & Syrus Interpres, qui ἐξηγητικῶς sic reddidit, cum longanimitas Dei praeciperet, ut fieret arca propter expectationem conversionis eorum. Mendum igitur hîc est in vulgata versione Latina, quod sublatum in Missali Romano per Clementem VIII. correcto in Epist. feriae 6. paschalis. Caeterum pro ὅ τε nonnulli Codices Graeci legunt ὅ τιquia, sed probatiores Codd. constanter legunt ὅ τε, quod contextui magis congruit, quo modo etiam legit Syrus, qui reddidit [consult facsimile image]cùm & Oecumenius in comm.

Pro ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο Complutensis, Regius 3. & alius Codex legunt ἀπεξεδέχετο, ac Robertus Stephanus annotavit, Codices non paucos ita legere, quae lectio 9firmari posset ex eo, quòd Paulus usu vocis compositae ἀπεκδέχεσθαιdelecteturRom. 8. 19. & 23.1. Cor. 1. 7.Gal. 5. 5.Phil. 3. 20.Hebr. 9. 28. Sed plures & probatiores Codd, legunt ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο, quo modo etiam legisse videtur Oecumenius, quo verbo Paulus itidem utitur, licet minùs frequenter. 1. Cor. 11. 33.c. 16. 11.Hebr. 11. 10. Verbum illud ὲξεδέχετο Erasmus & Gagnaeus exponunt passivè, cum expectaretur Dei longanimitas, quo modo etiam legit Rupertus l. 4. in Genesin c. 17. Sed τὸ ἐκδέχεσθαι, etsi voce sit medium, tamen activè semper accipitur Ioh. 5. 3.Act. 17. 16.1. Cor. 11. 33.c. 16. 11.Heb. 11. 10. quo modo etiam legunt Hieron. in c. 54. Es. August. Epist 99. Idacius contra Varimadum; quando Dei patientia expectabat, quae significatio activa magis etiam huic loco congruit, quia Dei patientia sive longanimitas conversionem hominum expectabat, non autem ab hominibus ea expectabatur, nisi cum Glossa ordinaria vulgatam versionem secuta sic accipiamus. Homines illi antediluviani non utebantur patientia DEI ad poenitentiam, sed expectabant eam, quasi semper esset duratura, quod tamen est duriusculum.

ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶεin diebus Noë h. e. temporibus Noë. Potest hoc referri tum ad praecedens membrum, quando Dei longanimitas expectabat, tum ad sequens membrum, cùm fabricaretur arca.

T. vocant Navigium illud celeberrimum, quod peculiari Dei mandato Noë fabricavit diluvio imminente, quod formam arcae repraesentavit. Ἐις ἣν ὀλιγαι (τουτέστιν ὀκτὼ) ψυχαὶ διεσώθησαν. Syrus hoc membrum cum priore connectit hoc modo, & octo animae tantùm ingressae sunt in eam & salvatae sunt. Existimavit igitur, sententiam complendam esse per verbum [consult facsimile image]ingressae sunt. Sed Graecum εἰς ἣν potest accipi positum pro ἐν ᾗin qua, quo modo etiam vertit Interpres vulgatus, quâ ratione nulla in textu erit ellipsis. Pro ὀλίγαι Regius & alter Codex legunt ὀλίγοι, quo modo etiam vulgata versio legisse videtur, quae reddidit, pauci, ut & glossa interlinearis, quae addit, pauci qui crediderunt Deo. Syrus eius loco exclusivam posuit, octo tantùm animae. Per ὀκτὼ ψυχὰς intelliguntur octo homines iuxta Synecdochen in Scripturis usitatam Actor. 2. 41.cap. 7. v. 14. qui fuerunt Noah & ipsius uxor, tres Noae filii, Sem, Cham & Iaphet & eorum uxores, Gen. 7. 7. Quod in versione LXX. Interp. Gen. 5. v. 15. & seqq. Methusalem dicitur fuisse annorum 167. cum genuit Lamech, ac postea vixisse 882. annis, quae summa est mille ac quadraginta novem annorum, ex quo sequitur, Methusalem vixisse aliquot annis post diluvium, sicque non octo tantùm animas in arca servatas, in eo mendum esse agnoscunt August. lib. qq. in Genes. q. 2. & lib. 15. de Civ. Dei cap. 15. Hieronym. in lib. de trad. Hebr. quod corrigendum ex textu Hebraeo, qui minorem habet numerum.

Δι' ὕδατος. Quidam, inter quos Gagnaeus, existimant, διὰponi proὰπὸ,per, pro ab, ut sit sensus, salvatae sunt ab aqua, ne scilicet aquis diluvii unà cum aliis immergerentur. Sed exempla huius significationis sunt rarissima. Quidam retinent usitatam significationem, & exponunt hoc modo, salvatae sunt per aquam h. e. beneficio aquae arcam sublevantis. Aquaenim quae caeteros extinxit, arcam in sublime elevans effecit, ne, qui in eaerant, unà cum aliis extinguerentur. Haec explicatio posset pulcerrimè accommodari ad ἀντίτυπον aquae in Baptismo, cuius in seq. vers. Apostolus mentionem facit, quippe per quam vetus noster homo extinguitur, novus autem ad vitam aeternam conservatur. Sed hic effectus aquae fuit accidentarius. Quidam διὰ positum statuunt proἐν,quo modo accipiturRom. 4. vers. 11.diversâ tamen significatione, ut notetur tempus, cum hîc locum describat. Propiùs accedit locus 2. Epist. 3. vers. 5.Terra consistitδι' ὕδατος i. e. ἐν μἐσῳ ὕδατοςin medio aquarum, Ita quoque hoc loco Salvatae sunt in aqua i. e. in medio aquarum, superiùs enim pluvia descendebat, inferiùs erant aquae diluvii, inundantis & omnia devastantis. Sed & tempus haec vocula denotare posset, salvatae sunt in aqua i. e. eo tempore, quo aquae diluvii inundaverunt & reliquos homines universos extinxerunt. Simplicissimè exponitur hoc modo, salvatae sunt in aqua i. e. non obstante aquae diluvio, quo ferè sensu vocula διὰ usurpatur 1. Tim. 2. v. 15.Salvabitur mulierδιὰ τεκνογονίας, non obstante filiorum generatione, etiamsi in coniugio liberos generet, de quo loco Apostolico Bellarminus lib. de Matrim. cap. 2. sic scribit. Non significare vult Apostolus, filiorum generationem esse causam salutis, sed mulierem in statu matrimonii, sive in statu generandi filios salvam fore, si permanserit in fide. Ergò illud per filiorum generationem positum est pro eo, in filiorum generatione, quae phrasis in Scripturis est frequentissima. Probationis loco adducit haec dicta. Act. 15. v. 21.Moses per omne Sabbatum legitur i. e. in omni Sabbato. cap. 26. v. 11.per omnes Synagogas i. e. in omnibus Synagogis. Rom. 4. 11.ut sit pater credentium per praeputium i. e. in praeputio. Sed priora duo dicta non satis pertinenter huc accommodantur, quia in Graeco textu non est διὰ sed κατὰ. Tertium dictum propriè huc pertinèt, ut sit pater omnium credentium per praeputium, quia praeputium non est causa, ut Abraham esset pater omnium credentium, sed in praeputio existens pater omnium credentium factus est per fidem. Coniungi autem possunt alia dicta. Actor. 14. vers. 22.διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεωνper multas tribulationes, id est, in multis tribulationibus oportet nos intrare in regnum coelorum, tribulationes non possunt impedire salutem, sed eam potiùs promovent, sicut aqua arcam elevans eorum, qui in ea erant, conservationem promovit. 2. Cor. 6. v. 8.per gloriam & ignominiam, per infamiam & bonam famam.Gal. 4. v. 13.per infirmitatem carnis evangelizavi vobis.Eph. 6. v. 18.per omnem orationem i. e. in omni oratione.

## 3:19-22 Questions and observations
It is asked in this place. 1. What is to be understood by the preaching of Christ, made to the Spirits in prison? Augustine, Epist. 99 to Evodius, alleging this apostolic place, and joining it with the same which is held in the following chapter, v. 6. for this cause also was the gospel preached to the dead, etc., exclaims. Whom would this depth not move! And after he had brought forward an acute and ingenious exposition of these words, he adds. Whoever is displeased by this exposition of the words of Peter, or whoever even if he is not displeased, it does not suffice for him, let him seek to understand them according to the underworld; who if he shall have been able to resolve those things by which I mentioned above that I am moved, so that he takes away their doubt, let him share it with me also, which if it shall have been done, those words will be able to be understood in both ways. Luther in chapter 7 of Genesis confesses that he doubts how this place is to be understood. tom. 2. Ien. f. 341. He asserts it to be of such great obscurity as hardly occurs in any other place of Scripture, especially of the N. T. Arias Montanus says, this place has been estimated by Interpreters as more difficult than all the places of the whole N. T. We shall therefore enumerate the principal expositions of this place. 1. Some already of old wished to gather from this place that the spirits of certain impious ones were both converted and liberated from the underworld by the preaching of Christ descending to the underworld, whom Augustine refutes. 2. The Papists wish to prove purgatory from this place. 3. Some also the limbo of the Fathers. Concerning these three perversions of the text, as being in conflict with the analogy of faith, it will be treated in ἐκδικήσει. 4. Augustine, Epist. 99 to Evodius, discourses thus concerning this place. Consider, lest perhaps all that which the Apostle Peter says concerning the Spirits shut up in prison, who had not believed in the days of Noah, does not pertain to the underworld at all, but rather to those times, the form of which he transferred to these times. For that deed had been a form of things to come, so that those who now do not believe the Gospel, while the Church is being built among all nations, may be understood to be similar to those who then did not believe, when was being built. the ark. But those who have believed, and are made safe through Baptism, are to be compared to those who were then made safe in the same ark through water. Whence he says: Thus also Baptism in a similar form makes you safe. To this likeness of form, therefore, let us also adapt the rest concerning the unbelievers, and let us not suspect that the Gospel was preached or is still being preached among the dead for the sake of making them believers and setting them free, as if a Church were established there. Therefore, to that sense which moves you, those seem to have been drawn who believed that Peter meant this, because he said that it was preached to the spirits shut up in prison, as if souls could not be understood as spirits, who were then in prison and were shut up in the darkness of ignorance as if in a prison, from which kind of prison he desires to be freed who says: Bring my soul out of prison, that it may confess to thy name.Psal. 141.which elsewhere is called the shadow of death.Luc. 1.from which they were certainly freed not among the dead, but here, of whom it is written: To them that sat in the shadow of death, light is sprung up.Esai. 9.But in those days of Noah it was preached in vain, because they did not believe, when the patience of GOD waited for the time of one hundred years, during which that same ark was being built. For its very construction was in a way a preaching; just as now those who are like them do not believe, who are shut up under the same form in the darkness of ignorance as if in a prison, looking in vain at the Church being built in the whole world, with the judgment impending like the flood, by which all the unbelievers then perished.Luc. 17.But because that event also signified a future thing, therefore it signified there the flood and baptism to the faithful, and punishment to the unfaithful. Afterwards he responds to the objection. Nor let it move one to hinder this understanding, that the Apostle Peter said that the same Christ preached to those shut up in prison, who once had not believed in the days of Noah, so that we should not therefore think this must be understood because Christ had not yet come at that time. For he had not yet come, namely in the flesh, as he came when afterwards he was seen on earth, and conversed with men. Baruch 3. Nevertheless, from the beginning of the human race, either to convict the wicked as to Cain, and before him to Adam himself, and his wife, or to console the good, or to admonish both, so that some might believe for their salvation, and others might not believe to their punishment, he himself certainly came not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, speaking to whom he wished, as he wished, through suitable visions. But what I said: He came in the Spirit, and he himself indeed the Son in the substance of the Godhead, since he is not a body, is certainly Spirit. But what does the Son do without the Holy Spirit, or without the Father, since all works are inseparable? Of the Trinity? The very words of Scripture themselves, concerning which the matter is, sufficiently indicate this, as I think, to those who attend diligently. Put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit. In which Spirit coming he preached also to those Spirits who had been incredulous at one time in the days of Noah, since before he came in the flesh to die for us, which he did once, he often came before in the Spirit to whom he wished, admonishing them by visions as he wished, certainly in the Spirit, by which Spirit he was also made alive, when in his passion he had been put to death in the flesh. For what is it that he was made alive in the Spirit, except that the same flesh, by which alone he had been put to death, rose again by the life-giving Spirit! Therefore, this is the opinion of Augustine, that by the spirits in prison those incredulous ones who lived in the time of Noah are to be understood, whose spirits, that is, souls were in the flesh, and as if shut up in the prison of the darkness of ignorance, and that Christ preached to them not in the flesh, because he was not yet incarnate, but in the Spirit, that is, according to his divinity. Beda in his commentary, Thomas part 3, q. 53, art. 2, ad 3, Hugo, the Glossa ordinaria, and Lyranus follow this exposition of Augustine, who expressly adds, that the Doctors commonly expound this passage in this way, although he himself later applies it to limbo. Bellarmine, book 4, de Christo cap. 13., attacks this exposition with the following arguments. 1. The common opinion of the Fathers is to the contrary, who expound it concerning the descent of Christ into hell. Resp. We do not simply disapprove of that exposition, as will appear later; meanwhile, we consider the exposition of Augustine, to which Lyranus grants this praise, that it is the common exposition of the Doctors, and which Carthusianus, Titelmannus, Iohan. Benedictus, etc., among the Papists themselves embrace, to be more congruent to the text, insofar as this preaching is established as having been done in the times of Noah. 2. Christ is said to have gone in the Spirit to preach to the spirits. But the Spirit, which is here distinguished against the flesh, does not seem to be able to signify anything other than the soul. Resp. We showed above ἐκδικ. 10. that by the Spirit is not signified the soul, but the divinity. 3. That word coming he preached, if it is understood of the soul, can be taken properly, but if of the divinity, it cannot be taken properly. Furthermore, the word πορευθεὶς in the last verse is again used concerning Christ, and is taken properly. Resp. It is nothing new for one and the same word to be taken in different ways in one and the same chapter, or even verse, Iohan. 4. v. 13. & 14.2. Corinth. 5. v. 21.Galat. 5. vers. 4. & 5.

In this place Christ is said to have gone in the Spirit, but in v. 22. the word πορευθεὶς, is placed absolutely; therefore the meaning is varied. 4. By the spirits who were in prison, it does not seem possible to understand living men, unless St. Peter is intentionally affecting an impropriety. Resp. We admit that Augustine's exposition labors under this difficulty, therefore regarding this member we prefer to it the exposition which will be subjoined a little later. 5. If this passage is understood concerning the preaching done in the days of Noah, it does not appear to what end that narrative is inserted here. Resp. Indeed, we have brought forward more than one reason for the connection above.

5. Akin to this exposition of Augustine is that by which the preaching of Christ is likewise understood as that which was done in the times of Noah, but by prison is not understood the body, in which the souls of the incredulous dwelt in this life, but hell, into which they were thrust after this life and the separation made from the body. We judge this exposition to be most conformable to the text, since in the Greek text it is not held that those spirits were in prison in the times of Noah, as the Vulgate translation has it, but it is said simply τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνέυμασι, viz. οὐσι, to the spirits in custody, viz. at that time, in which Peter wrote, constituted. Salmero indeed urges that the word preached, since it is of the past tense, shows that a word of the past tense is also to be understood here, who were in prison. But this proof is very weak; the condition of those to whom Christ preached in the time of Noah is described, not what it was at the time of that preaching, but what it was at the time of this Apostolic writing. For this exposition is confirmed 1. from the fact that Peter in 1 Epist. 1. vers. 11. says that the Spirit of Christ was in the Prophets, and consequently also in Noah the herald of righteousness, through whom He preached to the antediluvian men. 2. God says in Moses Gen. 6. v. 3. My Spirit shall not contend any longer with those men, because they are flesh. Peter seems to allude to this Mosaic passage when he says that Christ by His Spirit formerly speaking in Noah preached to the disobedient men then indeed living, but now dead and damned. 3. This exposition agrees with the analogy of faith, which teaches that the Son of GOD was always present to the human race, and preached repentance through the Patriarchs and Prophets, whence He is also called ὁ λὸγος Maimerah. 4. The same agrees with the Apostolic scope, as we showed above. 5. It agrees with the series of the text. Christ For it is said in the Spirit in which he was made alive, he went and preached to the spirits in prison. Now indeed, by the Spirit in which Christ was made alive, his divinity itself is understood. Therefore, it is a question here of such a preaching as pertains to Christ according to his divinity. 6. Gagnaeus compares this passage with the words of Peter, Acts 2. Repent, and let each one of you be baptized. Peter shows, he says, that Christ, who coming in the flesh in the last times, preached to us, did not then first begin to exist, but was the same who in the Spirit in the days of Noah preached to the men of that time concerning repentance and the impending flood: and for that reason this kind of passage was brought forward by Peter, in order to show that just as in the time of Noah those who remained incredulous, and neither did penance, nor received themselves into the ark, and did not believe in Christ preaching in the Spirit through Noah, perished: so those who now have not believed in Christ coming to us in the flesh, or done penance, or been baptized, will perish. Winckelmann says, this exposition is the simplest. Among the Papists, Andrad. lib. 2. Defens. Trident. embraces the same. Christ, he says, coming himself long ago in the Spirit, preached to those spirits who now in prison are already paying the deserved penalties of their infidelity, inasmuch as they never wished to have faith in Noah, who was advising rightly and building the ark by the command of God. It is objected to this exposition. 1. That Peter speaks of Christ, which is the name of a person, not of Λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ. Resp. On account of the identity of the person, those things which pertain to Λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ are rightly attributed to Christ, John 8. v. 38. 2. That this going and preaching was done after Christ's death and vivification. Resp. One must distinguish between different predicates. Vivification was indeed done after death, but the preaching was done in the times of Noah, nor does the Apostle in this place regard the series of time, but the identity of the subject or person. 3. That the property of the word πορευθεὶς does not pertain to τῷ λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ, and v. 22. is to be taken concerning a properly spoken going. Resp. πόρευσις is frequently attributed to the incorporeal God, so that some peculiar manifestation through words or deeds may be denoted by it. Gen. 11. v. cap. 18. v. 21. Deut. 20. v. 4. Psal. 18. v. 10. Psal. 144. v. 5. Isa. 45. v. 2. Hos. 5. v. 14. John 14. v. 23. 4. That the opposition of flesh and Spirit does not permit the name of Spirit to be taken concerning the ministry of the word. Resp. By the flesh of Christ his humanity is signified, by the Spirit his divinity, and thus the opposition stands perfectly well, for he was put to death in the flesh, made alive in the Spirit, Rom. 1. v. 4. 2. Cor. 13. v. 4. in this Spirit coming through Noah he preached. 5. That the preaching through the Prophets is attributed in the Scriptures not to the second, but to the third person of the Godhead. Resp. It is attributed to Christ no less than to the Holy Spirit, who is therefore called ὁ Λόγος. 6. That men existing in the time of Noah cannot be called Spirits, unless we wish to depart too far from the text and the letter. Resp. Those disobedient ones at that time, in which the Son of God preached through Noah, were living men, but at that time, in which Peter was writing, they were Spirits, or separated souls, established in the prison of hell. Moreover, the Apostle in this very chapter v. 20. calls living animated persons souls. Compare Acts 2. v. 41.chap. 3. v. 22. 7. That no reason can be given why Peter should have wished to make mention of the preaching done in the times of Noah, having passed over that which was done in earlier and later times. Resp. We gave the reason above. Estius says, that Peter remembered the times of Noah for this reason, because he wished to make a way for himself to the following digression concerning the Sacrament of Baptism, of which the ark of Noah and the water of the flood was a type. We also can bring forward the same thing for the assertion of this exposition.

6. Some interpret this departure as the going of Christ into Paradise, and τὰ πνεύματα concerning the blessed souls, but they take the word φυλακῆς concerning heavenly custody in this sense. Christ having died according to the flesh, but having been raised through divine power, having departed into the place of the blessed, manifested himself, and preached his victory to the blessed souls, who were in heavenly custody, who indeed formerly in the times of Noah, not having faith in the threats concerning the universal flood, were divinely punished by the penalty of the flood and perished according to the body, yet having performed repentance according to the Spirit or soul, they migrated to the blessed seats. But 1. it is very harsh and unusual for the Scriptures to take the name φυλακῆς for heaven and Paradise, since it is always taken in a bad sense Matt. 5. v. 25.chap. 25. v. 36.39.43. & 44.Acts 5. v. 19.chap. 8. v. 9.chap. 12. v. 4.chap. 16. v. 23.Apoc. 20. v. 7. 2. Those spirits, to whom the preaching was done, are called ἀπειθήσαντες unbelieving and disobedient; of whom it cannot be certainly affirmed that they afterwards performed true and serious repentance and were saved. 3. The Apostle finally treats of Christ's πορεύσει into heaven v. 22..

7. Osiander explains the words of Peter thus, Christ died on the cross, as to the body; but alive as to the soul; he approached the souls of those who were suffocated in the flood, who then when Noah was preparing the ark, to be persuaded did not suffer themselves that God was so angry with the world that He wished to destroy it with a universal flood, and therefore they did not seriously repent until the waters of the flood rushed in and they saw that they had to die. Wherefore God did not indeed damn them, because they had not departed without repentance, but yet because they had for a long time spurned the pious admonitions of Noah, it therefore pleased the Lord that He would not immediately admit their souls into His sight after death, but would detain them somewhere as if in custody, though not in torment, until Christ, after the price of redemption had been paid, should announce the grace of God to them and transfer them with Himself into heaven. To establish this opinion, the distinction between ἀπειθεῖς καὶ ἀπίστους, between the unpersuadable and the incredulous is urged. All ἄπιστοι are also ἀπειθεῖς, but not the contrary; for it can happen that the faithful and the elect do not believe certain particular threats of God, which portend the destruction and devastation of this or that place, who nevertheless are not on that account immediately called ἄπιστοι. Related is the exposition of those who maintain that Peter means this, that the redemption obtained by Christ profited the dead who had been incredulous for a long time in the time of Noah, yet had finally repented, a little before they were submerged by the flood. Therefore, they had paid the penalties of contumacy in the flesh, yet were saved by the benefit of Christ, so that they would not perish eternally. 1. Pet. 4. 6. And yet. 1. Scripture does not acknowledge any third place between heaven and hell. 2. The text expressly does not add, that those to whom it was preached had afterwards performed true and serious repentance. 3. Scripture does not seem to observe the distinction between ἀπειθεῖς & ἀπίστους, but perpetually understands by ἀπειθοῦντας the incredulous and impenitent. John 2. v. 26. Acts 14. v. 2. Rom. 7. v. 8. Heb. 3. v. 18. and in this very Epistle, and in this very chapter vers. 14. Peter attributes salvation to the one family of Noah, and consigns the rest to destruction.

8. Johannes Hesselius, called of Louvain, thinks that the calling of the Gentiles through Apostolic preaching is described here by Peter, as if explaining what he had said, that Christ died for the unjust. For the Prophets describe the infidel nations as bound, darkened, and shut up with iron bars and gates of bronze. Isa. 42. vers. 7. chap. 49. vers. 9. In almost the same way, Socinus the Photinian explains in the explanation of certain places of Scripture, edited at Raców, Year 618, page 113, of the same place: Christ, he says, although He was killed on account of the infirmity of the flesh and tasted death; yet by divine force and power He was afterwards restored to immortal life, and through the same divine force and power, when He had departed from here to the Father, having sent out His disciples through the whole world and

to his ministers, who might proclaim and openly testify to his victory over death, he clearly preached and revealed the truth even to the minds and souls of those men, who were held captive as if in a certain prison by the force of malice and ignorance, as if by the wrath of God, and were at one time stubborn. Which happened no differently than when, in the age of Noah, the gentleness and clemency of God awaited the repentance of stubborn men, whom the ark, which was being constructed by Noah himself according to divine prescription, sufficiently warned of their own duty and of the divine punishment that was impending. But 1. the name Spirit is unaccustomed to be understood of men living in the flesh. 2. This sentence distinguishes those unbelievers, to whom Christ preached, from those who were in the time of Noah, whom Peter nevertheless establishes as the same. 3. Nor can a reason be given why Peter, dealing with the Apostles, should immediately leap to the time of Noah.

9. Arias Montanus interprets spirits included in prison as eight souls included in the ark, which was like a prison. That Christ preached to them in the Spirit through Noah, the author of the said family, who persuaded them to believe and to betake themselves into the ark, from where also, by the command of the same Christ, they went out when the flood was finished. But 1. by spirits are not understood living men, but the souls of dead men, to whom, established in the prison of hell, Christ preached, when they were still living in the flesh in the times of Noah. 2. Those spirits are said to have been unbelieving, when Noah was building the ark. But by this reasoning Noah himself would have been an unbeliever. 3. Peter distinguishes the eight souls or men saved in the ark from those unbelievers.

10. Calvin, book 2 of the Institutes, chapter 16, § 9, and in the Psychopannychia, explains it thus: that Christ preached to the spirits of the deceased, both good and bad, not that he came to them through the presence of his soul, but that he caused them to feel the effect of his passion and death; and the good indeed received joy, but the bad indeed sorrow. He translates the word φυλακῆς as a watchtower, in which the souls of the pious are said to have been, because they were in continuous expectation of the passion of Christ, they were intent in the hope of promised salvation, as if from afar from a watchtower, in which watches are kept, they were awaiting it. Resp. 1. By this exposition, the real descent of Christ to the underworld is removed. 2. Spirit is explained by a forced gloss concerning efficacy and virtue, when it is distinguished from flesh and opposed to it. 3. Peter emphatically says, Christ πορευθεὶς preached. But for exerting efficacy there was no need of πορέυσει. 4. φυλακὴ is nowhere used for expectation, φυλάττω custody, thence φυλακὴ custody, which little word is translated to signify all things which pertain to custody and protection, such as prisons, sentries, and watches. The fourth watch of the night is usedMatth. 14. v. 25.Marc. 6. v. 48.Matth. 24. v. 43.Luc. 2. v. 8.cap. 12. v. 38. for custody or sentries,Actor. 12. v. 10. 5. The use of a watchtower and of watches is not to wait, but to guard and observe, lest the enemy devise any traps. 6. Peter does not distinguish between good and evil spirits, but absolutely calls them ἀπειθεῖς. Calvin saw these difficulties, therefore he replies, that the name of prison can also be retained. For just as the pious of the Old Testament, while they lived, the law was a certain stricter custody for them, in which they were detainedGal. 3. v. 15. so after death it was necessary for them to be constrained by a solicitous desire for Christ, because the Spirit of liberty had not yet been fully exhibited. Therefore, the anxiety of expectation was for them like a prison. But even if the argument, sought from the meaning of the little word φυλακῆς, were solved by this reasoning, nevertheless the remaining arguments would still stand. For whence does Calvin prove that the souls of the pious in the Old Testament after death did not immediately aspire to the beatific vision of God, but were constrained by a solicitous desire for Christ? Why also does the Apostle call those spirits constituted in φυλακῇ incredulous? Calvin excepts, that mention was made of the incredulous because the pure worshippers of God were mixed with the incredulous; therefore, it signifies that it did not harm the holy Fathers that they were almost overwhelmed by the multitude of the impious. But the Apostle does not deal with a certain mixture of the incredulous and the faithful, but says that those very spirits placed in φυλακῇ, to whom Christ preached, had once been incredulous.

II. Most of the ancients accept this passage concerning the descent of Christ to the underworld, in this sense. Christ was put to death in the flesh, because the union of soul and body was dissolved in death, but he was made alive in the Spirit, because through his divine virtue and power the soul was in turn united to the body and life was restored to it.2. Corinth 13. v. 4.in which divine virtue, according to the soul and according to the manner of a glorified and spiritual body, he went forth as a glorious conqueror, and descended to the spirits condemned and constituted in the prison of hell, who had once been incredulous, and because of their incredulity had come into this place, and he preached to them, that is, he refuted their incredulity, and manifested his divine majesty and victory. We do not simply repudiate this exposition, provided it is observed: 1. that by the Spirit, in which Christ is said to have gone to the spirits in prison, one does not understand properly and directly the soul, but the divine power, through which the body was vivified and glorified. 2. By the prison is not understood Limbo or Purgatory; but the very hell of the damned. 3. That Christ did not descend for the reason that He might convert certain damned ones by His preaching, and liberate them from hell, but that He might reproach them for their unbelief, and manifest His majesty to the demons and the damned souls. This exposition is proven. 1. Because it agrees with the series of the text, as we showed above. 2. πορευθεὶς v. 22. is accepted concerning the ascension of Christ into heaven. Therefore it is likely that v. 19. is accepted concerning the descent of Christ to hell. 3. Just as in His ascension Christ showed His glory and majesty to the spirits of the just: so in His descent to the lower regions He showed His glorious victory and majesty to the spirits of the damned, to those indeed for glorification and exultation: but to these for ignominy and confusion. 4. Most of the Fathers explain it thus, Athanasius in the Epistle to Epictetus, Bishop of the Corinthians, whom Epiphanius cites in heresy 77 of the Dinceritae. The body of Christ was placed in the monument, when He Himself went to preach also to the spirits in prison, as Peter said. Cyril on the true faith to Theodosius. The soul, having obtained a coupling and union with the Word, indeed descended into hell: but using divine virtue and power, He appeared also to the spirits who were there. Afterwards he adds the words of Peter. Ambrose on Eph. 4. The devil having been triumphed over, He descended into the heart of the earth, so that His showing might be a preaching to the dead, so that as many as were desirous of Him might be liberated. Bellarmine in book 4 of Christ, chapter 13, says that similar things occur in Clement of Alexandria, book 6 of the Stromata, Athanasius in the book on the Incarnation, which begins, The custom of a pious man, Cyril on the true faith to the Queens and book 12 on John, chapter 36, Hilary on Psal. 118. upon the words, My eyes have failed for Thy word. Ambrose on C. 10. Rom. Rufinus in the exposition of the Creed. Oecumenius on this place, but it cannot be denied that most of them incline toward that opinion, that Christ in His descent to the lower regions by His preaching converted and liberated certain ones. Some also do not make express mention of this Apostolic place. 5. Justin in the Dialogue with Trypho, and Irenaeus book 3, chapter 23, cite certain words of Isaiah from the version of the LXX Interpreters, which are not found in the Hebrew, very similar to these words of St. Peter, so that it is credible that St. Peter received them from there. These words are, however: The holy Lord of Israel remembered His dead, who had slept in the land of burial, and He descended to them to evangelize salvation, which is from him, that he might save them. It is objected against this exposition, 1. the name φυλακῆς is not to be taken of hell. Resp. Nay, truly it is expressly used of it Apoc. 20. v. 7., as is evident from v. 3., and a prison also in the Hist. Evang. is proposed as a type of hell, Matth. 5. v. 25.C. 18. v. 30.Luc. 12. v. 58., hence the Syrian in this place rendered it [consult facsimile image] in hell. 2. that the preaching is not said to have been done in hell sufficiently conveniently. Resp. The preaching is understood not so much as verbal, as real, (just as Hebr. 12. v. 24. speech is not verbal, but real) by which Christ preached to the souls of the impious not for conversion and liberation, as he had done in his ministry in these lands, but for their refutation and confusion, so that they might understand with their great evil that they had spurned this herald of justice, who had once preached to them through Noah. For just as in the final judgment the impious in their bodies are to see the judge himself, and are to feel punishments from the face of the Lord 1. Thess. 1. v. 9.Apocal. 1. v. 7., so also their souls, constituted outside their bodies, beheld him as a glorious conqueror in hell, and by this vision the torment in them was increased. The sense therefore is this: Christ by divine power descended to the lower regions, and there appeared to the Spirits condemned for unbelief, not that he might liberate them from there, nor that he might grant them a time for repentance, Hebr. 9. v. 27. but that he might show them that he had now come in the flesh, and had provided the price of redemption, which they had once in the times of Noah, when it was preached to them concerning him, stubbornly despised. Thus therefore Christ showed to the damned in hell the glory of his triumph in his descent to it; to men living on earth he demonstrated the same in his glorious resurrection, to the blessed Spirits in heaven in his glorious ascension to heaven. 3. that Christ descended to the lower regions not only in Spirit or soul, but in his whole and entire humanity after ζωοποίησιν and the union of soul and body. Resp. By Spirit is properly understood the divine power of Christ, consequently also the soul united to the body, because it is immediately premised that Christ, having been vivified in Spirit, had set out into hell. 4. that Christ performed this descent not after, but before his resurrection. Resp. One must distinguish between ζωοποίησιν, καὶ ἀνάστασιν, Rom. 14. v. 9. The former preceded the descent of Christ to the lower regions, but the latter followed it.

Q. 2. What is understood by φυλακὴν ? 1. The Papists the limbo of the Fathers or purgatory. 2. Calvin a watch or a watchtower. 3. Augustine Epist. 99. to Evodius, the body which is the prison of the soul. 4. Certain ones they accept concerning the blindness of the mind. John Huss. Who were in the prison of the flesh, or of sin, or of error, or of this exile, not being able to go out by themselves. Interlinear Gloss concerning the prison of darkness and of infidelity, and concerning carnal desires. 5. It is most simply expounded concerning hell, as the Greek Scholia ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ. and the Syrian [consult facsimile image] expound in hell.

Q. 3. Who are those Spirits to whom Christ preached? 1. Some understand good spirits, i. e. the souls of the pious of the O. T. to whom liberation from limbo was preached and granted. They urge the word preaching, which is for the most part taken in a good sense, and for which they think the word evangelizing is put in the following chapter, v. 6, for the wicked are not capable of the Gospel, as being addicted to damnation. But it is still in question whether the same thing is understood in this place by the word preaching, which is understood by the word evangelizing in the following chapter. 2. Some take it concerning good and evil indiscriminately, to whom the sentence of liberation was announced for the former, and of damnation for the latter. But that some were liberated from hell or limbo in the descent of Christ is said gratuitously. 3. Some take it concerning men still living in the flesh, but κατάχρησις this is harsher. 4. It is most simply taken concerning the Spirits, i. e. the damned souls of the impious, because they are called ἀπειθεῖς, and are said to be in prison, viz. of hell. Angelus Ps. 7. in the Symbol, chapter 20, as cited by Lorinus, understands by unbelievers the damned, who existed under Noah, and were extinguished in the flood: but by the remaining words, those who were in prison, in general all without exception. But the context shows that the discourse is about the same persons in both cases.

Q. 4. What is denoted by the preaching made to the Spirits? Resp. 1. Those who defend limbo expound it concerning the preaching of liberation. Bellarm. lib. 4. de Christo cap. 13. §. Argumenta. The preaching of Christ was nothing else than a message of liberation. But we shall examine the exposition concerning limbo a little later. 2. Those who take the passage concerning the descent of Christ to the lower regions expound it concerning the manifestation of the glorious victory of Christ and the denunciation and confirmation of the damnation of the impious. Christ, descending to the lower regions, declared himself to have been exhibited to the world by a certain more illustrious manifestation, and proposed to the impious that dire and mournful sermon, if not by words, yet in reality, viz. by the appearance of his glory, that the merit of his passion and death now no longer pertains to them, since they were unwilling to receive that which was offered in the word of the Gospel by faith, and consequently that by this presence of his, those punishments of which he had warned were more confirmed Noah & other Prophets. τὸ πότε indicates the time of Noah, not the time of Christ's preaching in hell. They had once mocked Noah as a delirious old man; Christ testified to them that Noah had threatened true things. 3. It is most simply explained concerning the preaching of repentance, because the Son of GOD, through Noah, by the threat of the imminent flood, invited those who lived in the times of Noah to repentance, Gen. 6. v. 3. To this must be referred that our Apostle 2. Epist. 2. v. 5. calls κήρυκα τῆς δικαιοσὺνης a herald of righteousness (where he uses a noun derived from the verb κηρύττω, which is had here); therefore he preached righteousness to them by the command of Christ, which consists in the remission of sins Luke 1. v. 77. and is obtained by faith in the promised Messiah, of which faith true contrition is the antecedent, and the pursuit of good works is the consequent. Noah preached in the name of the Messiah, and thus the Son of GOD through Noah preached repentance and the remission of sins, Luke 24. vers. 47. so that they might acknowledge their sins, seriously grieve for them, believe in the promised Messiah, amend their life, and apply their mind to the pursuit of righteousness.

Q. 5. Why does the Apostle produce the example of those who lived in the times of Noah? Resp. The Son of GOD was present to the human race from the beginning, and through a continuous series of times preached to the world through the Patriarchs and Prophets; therefore, what is said about the impious who lived at the time of the flood pertains to the impious of all ages. Peter, however, wished to make mention of the antediluvian men in particular. 1. Because the example was most suited to the purpose of Peter, since in it the long-suffering of GOD, the constancy and patience of Noah, and the destruction of the impious that followed shine forth more brightly. 2. Both things are most clearly shown in this example: that GOD most severely punishes the contemners and persecutors of the word, but miraculously preserves the faithful confessors of the word. 2. Pet. 2. v. 5. GOD did not spare the original world, but kept Noah, the eighth, a herald of righteousness, bringing a flood upon the world of the impious. v. 9. The Lord knows how to rescue the pious from temptation, but to reserve the iniquitous for the day of judgment to be punished. 3. The Apostle looks to the greatest sin of the world, the measure of which was never more copiously filled than at the time of the flood, Gen. 6. v. 5. & 12. & to the most severe punishment of sinners; for never did such a multitude of men perish at once, and descend according to their souls to hell. 4. The Apostle wished to prepare for himself a way to a digression concerning the efficacy of Baptism, which is the instrument of our salvation and preservation unto eternal life.

Q. 7. Does the little word ἅπαξ in the Greek text redundate? To some it seems so. 1. Because it is not held in all Greek Codices, for it is absent from those which read ἀπεξεδέχετο. 2. It does not exist in the Syriac paraphrase. 3. It does not seem to be acknowledged by the Latin Fathers citing this passage. 4. Nor does it seem to contribute to the proposed matter. But the more approved Greek Codices have it, which is sufficient. By this little word Peter wished to signify that which GOD once did in a figure, now, that is, in the time of the N. T., he does daily in the thing signified by the figure. Which opposition of the particle ἅπαξ in verse 20. and the particle νῦν in v. 21. shows that the little word ἅπαξ is genuine to the text.

Q. 8. Did certain ones placed outside the ark in the flood and submerged by the waters perform serious repentance, and become partakers of eternal salvation? Resp. Pererius maintains, that all who were suffocated in the flood were plunged into hell, with the exception of infants alone, who were reborn by the Sacrament of that time, and he gathers this from the fact, that the Holy Spirit commemorates of Noah alone, that he was just in that generation, Gen. 6. v. 9. cap. 7. v. 1. Lorinus on this passage: It seems to be admitted gratuitously that there was repentance of some among those who were submerged by the flood. ibid. We cannot divine that some performed repentance. And afterwards: In the following Epistle chapter 2, the same is repeated together with the destruction of the Sodomites and the Angels, who all seem to have perished. Some prove this from the fact that Peter here proposes the preservation at the time of the flood as a type of spiritual preservation unto eternal life, and attributes it only to those who were in the ark. But on the contrary, Chrysostom, Jerome, and others more rightly maintain, that not only infants, but also some adults, when they saw the daily increase of the waters, remembered the Noachic preaching, performed true repentance, and escaped the punishment of eternal damnation. 1. Because the Prophetic oracle is of perpetual and immovable truth. Esai. 55. vers. 11. The word, which goes forth from my mouth, shall not return to me void. 2. In public and universal punishments it is accustomed to happen that some, namely those who perform repentance, sustain the destruction of the flesh, so that their Spirit may be saved. 1. Corinth. 5. vers. 5. 3. Chrysostom warns, that GOD out of mercy did not send down the rain all at once, but over forty days, so that men might still have The space of conversion. 4. Just as not all who were saved bodily in the ark attained eternal salvation; for there was the impious Ham in the ark: so not all who were punished bodily outside the ark were damned with eternal death. 5. Some add our Apostolic passage compared with 1. Petr. 4. v. 6. from which they gather, that the outcome of those who were destroyed by the universal flood was unequal, since the spirits or souls of some came into prison, namely those who did not do penance, but others attained eternal life, namely those who were led to penance by the chastisement of the body. 6. Estius adduces the passage Psal. 78. v. 34. It is probable, he says, according to that, When he slew them, they sought him, and returned &c. that many of those who had despised or neglected the preaching of Noah announcing destruction to sinners, which here Peter calls having been incredulous, upon the flood coming on and inundating, conceived true, but imperfect, penance from fear. But the Royal Psalmist speaks there of the Israelites in the desert, not of antediluvian men.

Q. 9. In what respect does the Apostle deny that Baptism is the putting away of the filth of the flesh? 1. Some think, that respect is had to Circumcision, the type of Baptism, which was the removal of the filth of the flesh i. e. of the filthy and unclean flesh, namely the foreskin, to which they refer the Apostolic passage Coloss. 2. vers. 11. You are circumcised with circumcision not made by hand in the putting off of the body of the sins of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ. But circumcision just as much as Baptism was an efficacious means of regeneration, of the remission of sins and of salvation, and therefore it can likewise be said of it, that it was not the putting away of the filth of the flesh i. e. that it was not instituted for the external cleansing of the body. 2.
