The series of the articles of faith in the Creed must be held entirely, he ascended into heaven, he sits at the right hand of God, which series this Apostolic passage confirms. 2. That which some have taught, that Christ in the womb of his mother sat at the right hand of God, in that we recognize a certain ἀκυρολογίαν. The convenient sense, however, is that through this placement at the right hand of God, they understand the communication of divine idioms to the flesh of Christ made at the first moment of the incarnation.

23. Estius in this place comments thus. Under the names of the three Angelic Orders, which are expressed here, Blessed Peter wished the rest also to be included, such as principalities, dominations, thrones, which Paul names elsewhere &c. But whether the opposing powers, that is, the evil Angels, are also included, does not appear. For their perfect subjection, namely so great that they are no longer permitted to harm the kingdom of Christ, is finally to be in the day of judgment. Ps. 110. 1. Cor. 15. Lorinus in this place: The Apostle speaks of the spontaneous subjection of the good Angels, since he makes mention of the departure into heaven and of the session of Christ at the right hand of the Father or at the highest place of dignity in heaven, below which without doubt are all the holy Angels. Resp. 1. Paul describes the exaltation of Christ thus Phil. 2. v. 9. For which cause God also ὑπερύψωσε and has given him a name which is above every name, v. 10. that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth, on which words Chrysostom, Theophylact, and Oecumenius comment thus. The whole world, and Angels, and men, and Demons are subject to him. Thomas Aquinas in this place: Subjection is twofold, one voluntary, the other involuntary. All holy Angels are subject to Christ voluntarily, but Demons and the damned not so, but rather involuntarily. 2. Eph. 1. v. 21. Christ is said to be constituted at the right hand of God above every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come. To that name also belong the evil Angels. 3. Paul Hebr. 2. v. 8. concludes thus. In that he hath subjected all things to him, he left nothing not subject to him, certainly therefore by the name of Angels συνεκδοχικῶς being placed, all creatures, and consequently also evil Angels are understood. 4. To that, which the perfect subjection of the Devil and death is finally to be in the day of judgment, the Apostle answers in the same place, But now we see not yet all things subject to him. It must be distinguished, therefore, between the subjection itself, and the manifestation and plenary execution of the subjection. 5. Titelmann and Arias Montanus understand this Petrine passage concerning both subjections, both the spontaneous one of the good Angels, and the forced one of the evil Angels.

24. Lorinus to this place writes thus. That Christ as man is said to have had the Angels subject to himself, it seems to follow from this that he was the cause of the grace and glory of the Angels: and that this was especially made known, when he ascended into heaven and obtained a higher place there, leaving all things below himself; Paul says, that he was constituted above every principality and power, and calls him the head of the whole body of the Church which is composed, namely, of Angels, not only of menCol. 1. v. 16.Ephes. 1. v. 22. whence Thomas proves, that one mystical body is composed of men and Angels, because both are ordained through grace, which they received from the influx of the same Christ as head, to the same end of eternal life. p. 3. q. 8. art. 4. &c. Since the merits of Christ were foreseen and he was predestined, before the grace and glory of the Angels were foreseen, and before they were predestined, for he is the firstborn of every creatureCol. 1. v. 15.and the beginning of the ways of the LordIob. 40. v. 14.it is credible that God also ordained the merits of the same Christ to this effect, to which without doubt they themselves had the condignity of value, being infinite: and that pertained to his honor, and thus a certain greater reason of justice and mercy was preserved with respect to the Angels, so that, namely, grace and glory might be conferred upon them on account of the merits of Christ &c. Similar things occur in Gregor. Valent. book on Christ vol. 2. p. 164. where he argues, that Christ also merited grace and blessedness for the Angels; Blasius de Viegas in chapter 1 of the Apocalypse p. 24. where he writes, that grace and glory were given to the Angels on account of the foreseen merits of Christ, and Suarez vol. 1. Disp. 42. sect. 1. Cornel. à Lapide in this place Serious Theologians probably judge that the Angels also obtained grace and glory from the merits of Christ, for this pertained to the dignity of Christ, and to the greater association of the Church, which consists of Angels just as of men. Where he establishes Christ as the Mediator of the Angels also, and he strives to confirm the same with many reasons. Resp. 1. If man had not sinned, the Son of GOD would not have been incarnated, as is demonstrated in his place with many arguments. Therefore the Angels did not receive grace and glory from the foreseen merits of Christ. The connection is proved, because if the Angels had received the grace of GOD from the foreseen merits of Christ, the Son of GOD would have had to be incarnated, even if man had not fallen. 2. Scripture nowhere asserts that the Angels received grace in their first creation from the foreseen merits of Christ, but attributes this to the mere and absolute goodness of GOD. 3. The first men received grace in their first creation not from the foreseen merits of Christ, but from the gratuitous and absolute kindness of GOD. 4. The foreseeing of the Angelic fall is prior to the foreseeing of the Adamic fall. The foreseeing of the Adamic fall is prior to the decree of sending the Son into the flesh. Therefore, the foreseeing of the angelic fall is also prior to the decree of sending the Son into the flesh. Now, indeed, the will to give grace to the angels is prior to the foreseeing of the angelic fall, because God decreed to give grace to the angels before permitting that they should lose grace through sins. Therefore, the will to give grace to the angels is also prior to the decree of sending the Son into the flesh. Compare Becanus, vol. 1, Theol. Scholast. on the Angels, chap. 2, q. 4, p. 350, where he shows that the foundations of those who establish that grace and glory were given to the angels on account of the foreseen merits of Christ are not certain. 5. Christ is the head of the angels and of men, but in different ways. With respect to men, he is a homogeneous head and of the same nature as men, and regarding the internal influx of grace, neither of these has a place in the angels, of whom he is the head by reason of dominion, power, excellence, and external direction. Ephes. 1. v. 22. Christ is called head over all things in this respect, yet he is not the Mediator of all creatures. 6. The angels are citizens of the triumphant Church and, in a sound sense, also parts Hebr. 12. v. 23. but they are not members of the militant Church properly so called, since they are neither joined to the Church by external society, which consists in the profession of faith and the use of the Sacraments, nor do they have internal communion with it, speaking properly, inasmuch as they are destitute of the bond of that communication, namely, that true and living faith which apprehends the righteousness of Christ and through it incorporates us into Christ, nor do they fight against Satan, the world, and the flesh in the way that reborn men, the true and living members of the militant Church, do. 7. Although the merits of Christ are infinite, nevertheless they are efficacious only to that effect to which they were divinely ordained; otherwise, it could be inferred that Christ also merited something for the evil angels, just as he merited something for evil men. 8. By a ἀπαιδεύτως it is transferred to CHRIST, which Iobi 40. vers. 14. is asserted concerning Behemoth.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. The Son of GOD was always present to the human race, and spoke to it both immediately through interior revelations made to holy men, and mediately through the public preaching of the Patriarchs and Prophets, whence he is called ὁ λόγος.

2. When the Son of GOD in the fullness of time assumed human nature, and performed the ministry of preaching in it, he is said to have come in the flesh 1. Ioh. 4. v. 2. nevertheless, he had already several times before. had come and had preached to men, namely in the Spirit. Bede in this place: He who coming in the flesh in our times preached the way of the journey to the world, he himself also before the flood preached to those who were then unbelieving and living carnally, coming in the Spirit. For he himself was in Noah through the Holy Spirit, and in the others who were then holy, and through their good conversation he preached to the depraved men of that age, so that they might be converted to better things.

3. Those who in this life were unwilling to receive the preaching of grace by faith and to go out from the spiritual prison of impiety and carnal desires, their spirits were thrust into the prison of hell, and thus they were cast down from darkness into darkness and from prison into prison.

4. A prison is commonly called an evil dwelling. Truly hell is the worst dwelling. A prison is a place of custody, in hell the damned are shut up, so that no exit is open to them. 2. Petr. 2. v. 4. God did not spare the sinning Angels, but σειραῖς ζόφουταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τετηρημένους. Jude Epist. 4. δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρηκεν εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας. A prison is a place of torments. Hell is likewise a place βασάνου Luke 16. v. 28. A prison is a place of squalor, horror, putrefaction, stench, etc. Hell is a lake of most foul-smelling sulfur. Apoc. 20. v. 10.

5. The fountain and head of all sins is unbelief, through which a man draws upon himself temporal and eternal punishments.

6. The μακροθυμία of GOD shines forth among other things from this, that for a hundred years he awaited the conversion of the antediluvian men, while the ark was being prepared. These riches of kindness, ἀνοχῆς καὶ μακροθυμίας ought to lead us to repentance Rom. 2. v. 4.

7. From this μακροθυμία of God, Peter 2. Epist. 3. v. 9. gathers that God does not wish any to perish, but all to return to repentance.

8. The very patience of God was his preaching, when Noah, insisting for a hundred years on the works of the ark, showed by the daily execution of the work what was to happen to the world. Bede in this place.

9. Those who placed their labor in the construction of Noah's ark, yet themselves entered it not at all, exhibit a type of those Doctors of the Church who show the way of salvation to others, yet themselves become not at all participants in it.

10. Noah signifies Christ, who gives rest to the souls of his faithful Matt. 11. v. 28. Ordinary Gloss in this place

11. That God miraculously preserved Noah with his family in the ark at the time of the flood, from this Peter gathers this doctrine 2. Epist. 2. v. 9. The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.

12. God always gathers for Himself some Church and preserves for Himself a holy seed even in the most corrupt times of the world. All flesh had corrupted his way Gen. 6. v. 12. Noah, however, was a just man in his generations. v. 9.

13. The ark, in which Noah was saved with his family, was a type of the Church, in which Baptism is preached and administered as the means of our salvation. Augustine, book on the unity of the Church, chapter 5. There is no doubt to any of us, with the faith of the events preserved through the ark of Noah, that the house of the just man was delivered from the flood while the sinners were destroyed, that the Church was also prefigured, which perhaps would seem a conjecture of human ingenuity, if the Apostle Peter did not say this in his Epistle. In the same place he mentions that a Donatist Bishop, through the pitch with which the ark was smeared inside and out Gen. 6. v. 14. understood that Baptism should not be believed to go outside the Church, or that which was given outside the Church should be accepted. Augustine refutes that, and says it is more aptly explained concerning charity, which ought to be among us toward all. The same, book 15 of the City of God, chapter 27. The ark of Noah is without doubt a figure of the city of God wandering in this age. that is, of the Church, which is made safe through the wood, on which hung the Mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus. The members of the comparison can be established in various ways, most of which are enumerated in the place concerning the Church § 25, to which these can be added. Just as the ark grew into one house from the joining or gluing together of many timbers: so the Church is gathered into one body from many men of various nations and orders. Bede on this passage The very construction of the ark from smoothed timbers signifies the construction of the Church, which is made from the collection of faithful souls by the architects of the word.

14. The same ark was also a type of Baptism. Jerome in the Dialogue against the Luciferians. The raven is sent out from the ark, and does not return, and afterwards the dove announces peace to the earth; so also in the Baptism of the Church, the foulest bird having been expelled i. e. the Devil, the dove of the Holy Spirit announces peace to our earth. Just as Noah obtained life through death, when he was enclosed in the ark no differently than in a sepulcher, and was saved with a small family while the whole world was perishing: so today the mortification, which in Baptism is prefigured, is our entry into life, nor is salvation to be hoped for, unless we are separated from the world. August. lib. 12. contra Faustum cap. 14. Noah with his own is freed through water and wood, just as the family of Christ through Baptism, marked by the passion of the cross. (The ark and the cross are of wood, through both is salvation, through the wood of the ark temporal salvation, through the wood of the cross eternal salvation) lib. eiusd. cap. 17. That besides the ark all flesh, which the earth sustained, was consumed by the flood, signifies that besides the society of the Church, the water of Baptism, although it be the same, not only does not avail for salvation, but rather avails for destruction. Beda in h. l. That the water of the flood did not save those placed outside the ark, but killed them, without doubt prefigured that every heretic, although having the Sacrament of Baptism, is to be submerged to the infernal regions not by other things, but by the very waters by which the ark is lifted to heaven.

15. The water of the flood likewise can be considered as a type of Baptism. Psal. 29. v. 10. Cyrillus lib. 6. in Ioh. cap. 14. By the waters of the flood the sins of the whole world were expiated, and those who were hidden in the ark were made safe through water: this bore the type of Baptism, through which all filth of sins is laid aside and the oldness of life is taken away. Ambros. de iis, qui initiantur mysteriis cap. 3. in med. Do you see the water? Do you see the wood? Do you behold the dove and do you doubt about the mystery? Therefore it is water, in which the flesh is submerged, so that every sin may be washed away. Every vice is buried there. It is the wood, on which the Lord Jesus was affixed, when he suffered for us. It is the dove, in whose form the Holy Spirit descended etc. who inspires in you peace of soul and tranquility of mind. Beda in h. l. The Apostle says the form of Baptism is assimilated to the ark and the waters of the flood. 1. Through water the ark with Noah and his sons was lifted on high: thus through Baptism we are carried upward and are made citizens of the kingdom of heaven. Baptism is the child-bearer of the kingdom of heaven. 2. Just as water by itself did not save Noah, but through the medium of the ark: So the water of Baptism by itself does not save, but through the medium of the ark, i. e. Christ Jesus and his passion. All the power of Baptism descends from the passion of Christ, from the wood of the cross. 3. The waters of the flood suffocated everything in which there was a living soul: So Baptism is the mortification of our sins and of the old Adam. Gloss. interlin. in h. l. By those who were submerged in the flood, the mortification of the flesh is signified: by those who were saved in the ark, the vivification of the Spirit is signified. 4. Just as God in that universal cataclysm as it were renewed the world, when he submerged the earth and kept Noah with his own alive in the ark: so Christ through the medium of Baptism creates a new man, whom he preserves for life. For Baptism is the washing of regeneration and renewal.Tit. 3. v. 5. 5. Just as the water of the flood and the blood of men suffocated by the water concurred, so that sin might be destroyed: so in Baptism the water and the blood of Christ blot out sin. 6. As in the flood the water destroyed the blood, in which is life: so in Baptism the water, through the blood of Christ, in which is true life, preserves the life of men. 7. Just as the flood consumed not only adults, but also infants: so through Baptism not only the sins of adults, but also of infants are abolished. There is, however, a difference in this. That was a flood of wrath, but this is a flood of grace. That mortified the living: this vivifies the dead.

16. Bede in this place That with the whole world perishing, a few, that is, eight souls were saved through water, signifies that in comparison to the perishing Gentiles, Jews, heretics, and false believers, the number of the elect is much smaller. John Huss in this place The fewness of those to be saved was prefigured in the time of the law of Nature, when all perished in the flood except eight, who were saved in the ark. Likewise it was prefigured in the time of the Mosaic law Num. 14. because of all whom Moses led out of Egypt through the desert, almost out of the other six hundred thousand, only two entered the land of promise, Joshua and Caleb. Likewise it was prefigured in the time of Prophecy, when the children of Israel were led into captivity, and a few were left in the land of promiseOs. 11.I will leave a few of them. But in the time of grace it was more expressed and announced.Matth. 20.Many are called, few are chosen.

17. The very number eight of souls, which were made safe through water, signifies that the holy Church received the washing of Baptism into the Sacrament of the Lord's resurrection, so that just as He Himself rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, so also we, purged from sins through the water of regeneration, might walk in newness of life. For on the eighth day, that is, after the seventh of the Sabbath, the Lord rising from the dead showed both an example to us of the future resurrection and the mystery of a new conversation; by which, placed on earth, we might lead a heavenly life. Bede in this place.

18. Baptism is ὄχημα πρὸς οὐρανὸν, βασιλείας πρόξενος Cyril of Jerusalem, preface to the Catecheses, is a Sacrament of new life and eternal salvation. Augustine, book 2 against Cresconius, ch. 13, is a vehicle to God, a pilgrimage with Christ, a support of faith, a perfection of the mind, a key to the heavenly kingdom, a change of life, a driving away of servitude, a loosening of bonds, The conversion of composition into a better state, etc. Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 40 on Holy Baptism.

19. Baptism is not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the cleansing from the filth of the soul. Nicene Creed: I confess one Baptism for the remission of sins. Cyril of Jerusalem, Preface to the Catecheses: Baptism is the remission of sins and the death of sin. Ambrose, Book 1 on Penance, Chapter 7: In Baptism is the remission of all sins. Bede, Book 1 on John, Chapter 3: The sinner descends into the font, he ascends purified; he descends a son of death, he ascends a son of the resurrection; he descends a son of transgression, he ascends a son of reconciliation; he descends a son of wrath, he ascends a son of mercy; he descends a son of the Devil, he ascends a son of GOD.

20. From that which Peter says, that Baptism does not take away the filth of the body, the pious ancients gather that by Christian Sacraments the faithful are not freed from miseries and afflictions in this age. Augustine, in Enchiridion, Chapter 66: We see even little children after the laver of regeneration tormented by the affliction of various evils, so that we may understand that all that is done by the saving Sacraments pertains more to the hope of future goods than to the retention or attainment of present ones.

21. In the Sacraments, the promise and the faith of the promise look to one another, from which obedience cannot be separated. Moreover, these two are as a mutual covenant between those stipulating with one another, of GOD promising grace and of man believing the promise.

22. In this stipulation, GOD makes a covenant with the baptized, and by the covenant gives him a good conscience, i.e., His grace, the remission of sins, righteousness, and eternal life; He also promises that He will be his God, i.e., Father, protector, defender, Savior. The baptized in turn promises, either by himself or through godparents, that he wishes to acknowledge, invoke, and worship this true God from the Word, and to preserve a good conscience until the end of life.

23. Baptism both saves us and is the interrogation of a good conscience. Therefore, it provides both. First, it is an efficacious instrument of grace and salvation, through which grace obtained through Christ is offered to men and conferred upon believers: it is also a seal of divine promises, through which the grace conferred upon believers is sealed in them.

24. Because Baptism is the stipulation of a good conscience, it ought therefore to be a perpetual memorial for us, so that, mindful of the promise made in Baptism, we may retain faith and a good conscience 1 Tim. 1, verse 18

lest, sinning against conscience, we make shipwreck of the faith. Gregory, oration 40. Baptism is a covenant entered into with GOD for a second life and a purer way of living, etc.; therefore, we ought all to be in the greatest fear, and to guard our souls with all diligence, lest we be found to have violated this covenant. Ambrose, book on those who are initiated into the mysteries, chapter 2. Repeat what you were asked, recognize what you have promised; you have renounced the Devil and his works, the world and its luxury and its pleasures; your voice is held not in the tomb of the dead, but in the book of the living.

25. The resurrection of Christ is the confirmation of our faith and of the good conscience resulting from it. For it is a public testimony that full satisfaction has been made for our sins, that the heavenly Father is perfectly reconciled to us, and that the heavenly goods have been most sufficiently acquired for us by the λύτρῳ of Christ; hence also our Apostle teaches that by the resurrection of Christ we have been begotten again into a living hope, 1. Epist. 1. v. 3.

26. Just as Christ after his passion and death rose again and ascended into the heavens: So we, having been baptized into the death of Christ, Rom. 6. v. 3. and incorporated into him through Baptism, will one day be received with him into heavenly glory. Iohn. 14. v. 3. Bede in this place: Just as Christ, rising again, ascended into heaven: so also he has marked out for us through Baptism the way of salvation and the kingdom, the entrance to the heavenly fatherland.

27. The πόρευσις of Christ into heaven is the happy conclusion of his entire journey accomplished on these lands. Bernard, sermon 2 on the ascension.

28. Christ did not ascend into heaven in the way that Enoch and Elijah did, because after his ascension into the heavens he sat down at the right hand of GOD, a thing which can be said of neither Enoch nor Elijah, indeed of no Angel Hebr. 1. v. 13., whence it is said that he ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things, Eph. 4. v. 10. and was made higher than the heavens themselves. Hebr. 7. v. 26.

29. Christ not only sat down at the right hand of GOD in his ascension Marc. 16. v. 19., but is still at the right hand of GOD, as our Apostle speaks, and when he returns for judgment, he will sit at the right hand of the power of GOD. Matth. 26. vers. 64. For this session at the right hand of GOD, which embraces the most present and most powerful dominion of heaven and earth, is subject to no variation or change.

30. To him who overcomes, Christ will grant to sit with him on his throne, just as he himself overcame and sat with his Father on his throne Apocal. 3. v. 21.. The throne of the Father on which CHRIST sits is the omnipotent of GOD. virtue and infinite majesty, the sustainer and governor of all things. The throne of Christ, in which the elect shall sit, is the communication of happiness and heavenly glory.

31. Angels are called powers and virtues; because they excel in great power, and God works most powerfully through them, but Christ is made superior to them, inasmuch as he is exalted to the right hand of the almighty God.Eph. 1. v. 20.Phil. 2. v. 9.Hebr. 1. v. 13.

32. That there are thrones or dominions, or Principalities and powers in the heavenly arrangements, I most firmly believe, and that they differ in some way, I hold with undoubted faith, but what these are and how they differ among themselves, I do not know. Aug. ad Oros. contra Piscator. cap. 11. Confer Eph. 1. v. 21.Col. 1. v. 16.

33. The exaltation of Christ to the right hand of God is our highest consolation. For because all things are subject to him, therefore he will be able to protect us against all enemies, nor will anything be able to separate us from himRom. 8. v. 38. nay rather, just as all things are compelled to serve Christ, so also all things are compelled to serve us in Christ and to promote our salvation. Roman. 8. v. 28.

Summary of the Chapter, A general exhortation to innocence of life and patience. Parts are established by some as three. First, a dehortation from sins and the Ethnic manner of living, from the beginning up to v. 7. 2. An exhortation to certain special virtues, from verse 7 up to 12. 3. Consolation in the cross and in persecutions, to be sustained on account of the confession of faith, from v. 12 up to the end of the chapter. More neatly, two parts are established, both of which are exhortatory. The former indeed to the mortification of the flesh and innocence of life, from the beginning up to v. 12. The latter to sustaining persecution and showing patience in the cross, from v. 12 up to the end of the chapter. Lyranus in h. l. He orders the faithful 1. by reason of themselves. 2. by reason of their neighbor.

Latin:

Quaeritur hoc loco. 1. Quid per praedicationem Christi, Spiritibus in carcere factam, intelligendum veniat? Augustinus Epist. 99. ad Evodium allegans hunc locum apostolicum, eundemque cum eo, qui habetur cap. seq. v. 6. propter hoc & mortuis evangelizatum est. &c. coniungens, exclamat. Quem non moveat ista profundit as! Ac postquam verborum horum expositionem acutam & ingeniosam protulisset, subiungit. Haec expositio verborum Petri, cui displicet, vel cui etiamsi non displicet, non tamen sufficit, quaerat ea secundùm inferos intelligere; qui si valuerit illa, quibus me moveri supra commemoravi, ita solvere, ut eorum auferat dubitationem, impartiat & mihi, quod si factum fuerit, poterunt illa verbautroque modo intelligi. Lutherus in cap. 7. Genes. fatetur, se dubitare, quomodo hic locus intelligendus veniat. tom. 2. Ien. f. 341. tantae obscuritatis eum esse asserit, quanta vix in ullo alio Scripturae, praesertim N. T. loco occurrit. Arias Montanus dicit, hunc locum omnibus totius N. T. locis difficiliorem ab Interpretibus aestimatum. Enumerabimus igitur praecipuas huius loci expositiones. 1. Quidam iam olim ex hoc loco colligere voluerunt, Spiritus quorundam impiorum Christi ad inferos descendentis praedicatione & conversos & ex inferno liberatos fuisse, quos refellit Augustinus. 2. Pontificii ex hoc loco probare volunt purgatorium. 3. Quidam etiam limbum Patrum. De his tribus textus perversionibus, utpote cum fidei analogia pugnantibus, in ἐκδικήσει agetur. 4. Augustinus Epist. 99. ad Evodium de hoc loco sic disserit. Considera, ne fortè totum illud, quod de conclusis in carcere Spiritibus, qui in diebus Noë non crediderant, Petrus Apostolus dicit, omninò ad inferos non pertineat, sed ad illa potius tempora, quorum formam ad haec temporatranstulit. Illa quippe res gesta forma fuerat futurorum, ut ii, qui modò non credunt Evangelio, dum in omnibus gentibus aedificatur Ecclesia, illic intelligantur esse similes, qui tunc non crediderunt, cum fabricaretur arca. Illi autem qui crediderunt, & per Baptismum salvi fiunt, illis comparentur, qui tunc in eadem arca salvi facti sunt per aquam. Unde ait. Sic & vos simili forma Baptismus salvos facit. Ad hanc igitur forma similitudinem caetera etiam de incredulis coaptemus & non suspicemur, quòd apud inferos ad faciendos fideles atque liberandos Evangelium praedicatum sit vel adhuc etiam praedicetur, q. & ibi sit Ecclesia constituta. Ad illum ergò sensum, quite movet, ideò videntur attracti, qui hoc Petrum sensisse crediderunt, quia dixit conclusis in carcere Spiritibus praedicatum, q. animae non possint intelligi Spiritus, qui tunc erant in carcere atque ignorantiae tenbris velut carcere claudebantur, de quali carcere se desiderat liberari ille, qui dicit. Educ de carcere animam meam, ut confiteatur nomini tuo.Psal. 141.quae alibi umbra mortis appellatur.Luc. 1.de qua non utique apud inferos, sed hîc liberati sunt, de quibus scriptum est. Qui sedebant in umbra mortis, lumen ortum est eis.Esai. 9.Illis autem in diebus Noae frustra praedicatum est, quia non crediderunt, cum expectaret DEI patientiaper tempus centum annorum, quibus arca eadem fabricata est. Nam eius etiam fabricatio quodammodo praedicatio fuit; sicut modò similes eorum non credunt, qui sub eadem forma ignorantiae tenebris velut carcere concluduntur, frustra intuentes, Ecclesiam toto mundo construi, imminente iudicio tanquam diluvio, quo tunc omnes increduli perierunt.Luc. 17.Sed quia ea res gesta etiam futuram rem significabat, ideò ibi diluvium & baptismum significavit fidelibus, & insidelibus poenam. Postea respondet ad obiectionem. Nec moveat ad impediendum intellectum istum, quòd eundem Christum dixit Apostolus Petrus praedicasse illis in carcere conclusis, qui quondam non crediderant in diebus Noae, ut ideò non arbitremur hoc intelligendum, quiaillo tempore nondum venerat Christus. Nondum enim venerat, scilicet in carne, sicut venit, quando posthaec in terra visus est, & cum hominibus conversatus. Baruch. 3. Veruntamen ab initio generis humani vel ad arguendos malos sicut ad Cain, ac prius adipsum Adamum, uxoremque eius, vel ad consolandos bonos vel ad utrosque admonendos, ut alii ad salutem suam crederent, alii ad poenam suam non crederent, ipse utique non in carne, sed in Spiritu veniebat, visis congruis ad loquens, quos volebat, sicut volebat. Quod autem dixi. In Spiritu veniebat, & ipse quidem Filius in substantia Deitatis, quoniam corpus non est, utique Spiritus est. Sed quid facit Filius sine Spiritu sancto, vel sine Patre, cum inseparabilia sint omnia opera Trinitatis? Ipsa quoque Scripturae verba, de quibus agitur, satis hoc, ut puto, indicant eis, qui diligenter attendunt. Mortificatus carne, vivificatus Spiritu. In quo Spiritu adveniens praedicavit & illis Spiritibus, qui increduli fuerant aliquando in diebus Noë, quoniam priusquam veniret in carne pro nobis moriturus, quod semel fecit, saepe antea veniebat in Spiritu ad quos volebat, visis eos admonens sicut volebat, utique in Spiritu, quo Spiritu & vivificatus est, cum in passione esset carne mortificatus. Quid est enim, quod vivificatus est Spiritu, nisi quod eadem caro, quâ sola fuerat mortificatus, vivificante Spiritu resurrexit! Augustini ergò sententia haec est, per Spiritus in carcere conclusos, intelligendos esse incredulos, qui vixerunt tempore Noë, quorum Spiritus, h. e. amimae erant in carne, atque ignorantiae tenebris velut in carcere conclusae, Christumque iis non in carne, quia nondum erat incarnatus, sed in Spiritu, id est, secundùm divinitatem praedicasse. Sequuntur hanc Augustini expositionem Beda in comment. Thomas part. 3. q. 53. art. 2. ad 3. Hugo, Glossa ordinaria & Lyranus, qui disertè addit, Doctores communiter passum istum sic exponere, quamvis ipse eum postea applicet ad limbum. Impugnant hanc expositionem Bellarminus lib. 4. de Christo cap. 13. seqq. argumentis. 1. Paturm communis sententia est in contrarium, qui exponunt de descensu Christi ad inferos. Resp. expositionem illam non simpliciter improbamus, ut postea apparebit; interim Augustini expositionem, cui Lyranus hoc elogium defert, quòd sit communis Doctorum expositio, & quam ex ipsis Pontificiis amplectuntur Carthusianus, Titelmannus, Iohan. Benedictus &c. textui magis congruam existimamus, quatenus haec praedicatio temporibus Noae facta statuitur. 2. Christus dictur profectus Spiritu ad praedicandum Spiritubus. At Spiritus, qui hîc distinguitur contra carnem, non videtur posse significare aliud, quàm animam. Resp. ostendimus superiùsἐκδικ. 10. per Spiritum non significari animam, sed divinitatem. 3. Illud veniens praedicavit, si de anima intelligatur, accipi poterit propriè, at si de divinitate non potest accipi propriè. Praeterea verbumπορευθεὶςin versu ult. denuò de Christo usurpatur, ac propriè accipitur. Resp. novum, non est, unum idemque verbum in uno eodemque capite, imò versiculo diversimodè accipi, Iohan. 4. v. 13. & 14.2. Corinth. 5. v. 21.Galat. 5. vers. 4. & 5.

hoc loco Christus dicitur Spiritu profectus, sed in v. 22. absolutè ponitur verbum πορευθεὶς, variatur ergò significatio. 4. Per Spiritus, qui in carcere erant, non videtur posse intelligi homines viventes, nisi de industria S. Petrus affectet improprietatem. Resp. fatemur Augustini expositionem hac difficultate laborare, ideò quoad hoc membrum praeferimus ei expositionem, quae paulo pòst subiicietur. 5. Si hic locus intelligatur de praedicatione facta in diebus Noë, non apparet, quorsum hîc sit inserta ista narratio. Resp. imò vero connexionis rationem non unam adduximus superiùs.

5. Huic Augustini expositioni affinis est ea, quâ praedicatio Christi itidem intelligitur de ea, quae temporibus Noae facta est, sed per carcerem non intelligitur corpus, in quo animae incredulorum in hac vita habitarunt, sed infernus, in quem post hanc vitam, & factam à corpore separationem detrusae fuerunt. Hanc expositionem iudicamus textui maximè conformem, cum in textu Graeco non habeatur, quòd Spiritus illi temporibus Noae fuerint in carcere, ut habet vulgata translatio, sed simpliciter dicatur, τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνέυμασι, sc. οὐσι,Spiritibus in custodia eo sc. tempore, quo Petrus scripsit, constitutis. Salmero quidem urget, quòd verbum praedicavit, cùm sit praeteri temporis, ostendat, verbum praeteriti temporis & híc subintelligendum, qui erant in carcere. Sed haec probatio est admodùm infirma, describitur conditio eorum, quibus Christus tempore Noae praedicavit, non qualis fuerit tempore illius praedicationis, sed qualis fuerit tempore Apostolicae huius scriptionis. Confirmatur enim haec expositio 1. ex. eo, quòd Petrus 1. Epist. 1. vers. 11. dicit, Spiritum Christi fuisse in Prophetis, ac proinde etiam in Noaho iustitiae praecone, per quem hominibus antidiluvianis praedicavit. 2. Deus apud Mosen dicit Gen. 6. v. 3.Spiritus meus non contendet ampliùs cum illis hominibus, quia caro sunt. Ad hunc locum Mosaicum Petrus videtur alludere, quando dicit. Christum Spiritu suo olim in Noaho loquente praedicasse hominibus immorigeris tunc quidem vivis, nunc autem mortuis & damnatis. 3. Congruit haec expositio cum fidei analogia, quae docet, Filium DEI semper adfuisse generi humano, ac per Patriarchas & Prophetas poenitentiam praedicasse, unde etiam vocatur ὁ λὸγος Maimerah. 4. Congruit eadem cum scopo Apostolico, ut ostendimus superiùs. 5. Congruit cum serie textus. Christus enim dicitur in Spiritu eo, quo vivificatus est, profectus Spiritibus in carcere praedicasse. Iam vero per Spiritum, quo Christus vivificatus est, intelligitur ipsius divinitas. Ergò de eiusmodi praedicatione hîc agitur, quae Christo secundùm divinitatem competit. 6. Gagnaeus hunc locum confert cum verbis Petri, Actor. 2.Poenitentiam agite, & baptizetur unus quisque vestrum. Ostendit, inquit, Petrus, quòd Christus, qui novissimis temporibus veniens in carne, praedicavit nobis, non tunc primò coepit esse, sed idem erat, qui in Spiritu diebus Noae hominibus eius temporis praedicabat at poenitentiam & diluvium instans: atque ob id huiusmodi locum à Petro adductum esse, ut ostendat, quòd sicut tempore Noë ii, qui increduli permanserunt, nec poenitentiam egerunt, neque se in arcam receperunt, & in Spiritu per Noë praedicanti Christo non crediderunt, perierunt: ita qui nunc venienti ad nos in carnem Christo non crediderunt, aut poenitentiam egerunt, neque baptizati sunt, peribunt. Winckelmannus dicit, hanc expositionem esse simplicissimam Ex Pontificiis eandem amplectitur Andrad. lib. 2. Defens. Trident. Christus, inquit, in Spiritu iam olim ipse veniens praedicavit Spiritibus illis, qui nunc in carcere meritas iam infidelitatis suae poenas luunt, quippe qui Noae recta monenti & arcam iussu Dei construenti fidem habere nunquam voluerunt. Obiicitur huic expositioni. 1. Petrum loqui de Christo, quod est nomen personae, non deΛόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ. Resp. propter identitatem personae Christo rectè tribuuntur, quae Λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ competunt, Ioh. 8. v. 38. 2. Factam esse hanc profectionem & praedicationem post Christi mortem & vivificationem. Resp. distinguendum est inter diversa praedicata. Vivificatio quidem facta est post mortem, sed praedicatio temporibus Noae facta est, nec respicit Apostolus hoc loco seriem temporis, sed identitatem subiecti sive personae. 3. Proprietatem verbiπορευθεὶςnon competereτῷ λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ, ac v. 22.de propriè dicta profectione accipi. Resp. πόρευσις Deo incorporeo saepiùs tribuitur, ut peculiaris aliqua manifestatio per verba vel facta per eam denotetur. Gen. 11. v. cap. 18. v. 21.Deut. 20. v. 4.Psal. 18. v. 10.Psal. 144. v. 5.Esa. 45. v. 2.Oseae 5. v. 14.Ioh. 14. v. 23. 4. Oppositionem carnis & Spiritus non permittere, ut nomen Spiritus de verbi ministerio accipiatur. Resp. per carnem Christi humanitas, per Spiritum eiusdem divinitas significatur, sicque optimè sibi constat oppositio, carne enim mortificatus est, Spiritu vivificatus,Rom. 1. v. 4.2. Corinth. 13. v. 4. in hoc Spiritu veniens per Noahum praedicavit. 5. Praedicationem per Prophetas non secundae, sed tertiae Deitatis personae in Scripturis tribui. Resp. Christo non minùs, quàm Spiritui sancto tribuitur, qui propterea vocatur ὁ Λόγος. 6. Homines tempore Noae existentes non posse vocari Spiritus, nisi à textu & litera nimis longè recedere velimus. Resp. immorigeri illi tempore eo, quo Filius Dei per Noahum praedicavit, fuerunt homines vivi, sed tempore eo, quo Petrus scribebat, fuerunt Spiritus, sive animae separatae, in carcere inferni constitutae. Quin & personas viventes animatas Apostolus hoc ipso capite v. 20. vocat animas. Confer. Actor. 2. v. 41.cap. 3. v. 22. 7. non posse dari rationem, cur Petrus praedicationis factae temporibus Noahi mentionem facere voluerit, praetermissa eâ, quae anterioribus & posterioribus temporibus facta. Resp. rationem dedimus superiùs. Estius dicit, Petrum ideò temporum Noae meminisse, quia viam sibi facere voluerit ad sequentem digressionem de Sacramento Baptismi, cuius typus fuit arca Noahi & aqua diluvii. Idem & nos pro assertione huius expositionis afferre possumus.

6. Quidam hanc profectionem interpretantur de abitu Christi in Paradisum, &τὰ πνεύματαde animabus beatis, vocem autemφυλακῆςde custo dia coelesti accipiunt hoc sensu. Christus mortuus ex infirmitate, resu scitatus autem per potentiam divinam profectus in locum beatorum sese manifestavit, victoriamz, suam praedicavit beatis animabus, quae erant in custodia coelesti, quaez, olim quidem temporibus Noae comminationibus de universali diluvio fidem non habentes poenâ diluvii divinitus correpti secundùm corpus perierunt, poenitentiâ tamen actâ secundùm Spiritum sive animam ad beatas sedes transmigrarunt. Atqui 1. perquam durum & Scripturis insolitum φυλακῆς nomen de coelo ac Paradiso accipere, cum semper in malam partem accipiatur Matth. 5. v. 25.cap. 25. v. 36.39.43. & 44.Act. 5. v. 19.cap. 8. v. 9.cap. 12. v. 4.cap. 16. v. 23.Apocal. 20. v. 7. 2. Spiritus illi, quibus praedicatio facta, dicuntur ἀπειθήσαντες increduli & immorigeri; de quibus certò affirmari nequit, quòd postea veram & seriam poenitentiam egerint & salvati sint. 3. de Christi in coelum πορεύσειv. 22. demum agit Apostolus.

7. Osiander verba Petri sic explicat, Christus mortuus in cruce, quoad corpus; vivus autem quo ad animam; accessit ad animas eorum, qui in diluvio suffocati sunt, quod tunc cum Noë arcam pararet, persuaderi sibi non patiebantur, Deum adeò ir asci mundo, ut eum diluvio universali perdere vellet, itaque non agebant seriò poenitentiam, donec aquae diluvii ingruerent & sibi moriendum esse viderent. Quare Deus eos non quidem damnavit, quia non sine poenitentia decesserant, sed tamen quia pias admonitiones Noahi longo tempore spreverant, ideo placuit Domino, ut eorum animas post mortem non statim in conspectum suum admitteret, sed alicubi tanquam in custodia, non tamen in cruciatu detineret, donec Christus post praestitum redemtionis precium illis gratiam Dei annunciaret, & in coelum secum transferret. Pro stabilienda hac sententia urgetur discrimen inter ἀπειθεῖς καὶ ἀπίστους,inter impersuasibiles & incredulos. Omnesἄπιστοιsunt etiamἀπειθεῖς,sed non contrà; fieri enim potest, ut fideles & electi non credant peculiaribus quibusdam Dei comminationibus, quae huius vel illius loci interitum ac devastationem portendunt, qui tamen non propterea statim dicunturἄπιστοι. Affinis est eorum expositio, qui statuunt, Petrum hoc velle, quòd redemtio à Christo parta profuerit mortuis, qui tempore Noae diu fuerant increduli, tamen resipuerant demum, paulo ante quàm diluvio mergerentur. Illos ergò poenas contumaciae dedisse in carne, servatos tamen Christi beneficio, ne aeternum perirent.1. Pet. 4. 6. Atqui. 1. Scriptura non agnoscit locum aliquem tertium inter coelum & infernum. 2. textus disertè non addit, illos quibus praedicatum est, posteaveram & seriam poenitentiam egisse. 3. Discrimen inter ἀπειθεῖς & ἀπίστους Scriptura non videtur observare, sed per ἀπειθοῦντας incredulos & impoenitentes perpetuò intelligere. Ioh. 2. v. 26.Actor. 14. v. 2.Rom. 7. v. 8.Hebr. 3. v. 18. & in hac ipsa Epistola, inque hoc ipso capite vers. 14. Petrus uni familiae Noahi salutem tribuit, reliquos exitio addicit.

8. Iohannes Hesselius à Lovanio dictus existimat, vocationem gentium per praedicationem Apostolicam à Petro hîc describi velut explicante quod dixerat, Christum pro iniustis mortuum. Nam Prophetae describunt gentes infideles tanquam vinctos, obtenebratos, vectibus ferreis & portis aereis conclusos.Esai. 42. vers. 7.cap. 49. vers. 9. Eodem ferè modo explicat Socinus Photinianus in explicat. quorundam locor. Script. edit. Racov. Ann. 618. per 113. d. l. Christus, inquit, licet propter infirmitatem carnis necatus fuerit & mortem gustaverit; divinâ tamen vi atque potentiâ ad immortalem vitam postmodum est restitutus, per eandem vero divinam vim atque potentiam cum hinc ad Patrem profectus esset, dimissis per universum orbem discipulis &

ministris suis, qui tantem eius adversus mortem victoriam praedicarent & palam testarentur, eorum etiam hominum mentibus & animis clarè concionatus est & veritatem patefecit, quae malitiae & ignorantiae vi quasi quodam carcere tanquam irae Dei captivi detinebantur & contumaces fuerunt aliquando. Quod non secùs accidit, atque cum aetate Noae Dei lenitas atque clementia hominum contumacium resipiscentiam expectaret, quos arca, quae ab ipso Noa ex divino praescripto construebatur, ipsorum officii & divini, quod imminebat, supplicii satis admonebat. Atqui 1. nomen Spiritus de hominibus in carne viventibus accipi insolens est. 2. Incredulos illos, quibus Christus praedicavit, haec sententia ab illis, qui erant tempore Noae, distinguit, quos tamen Petrus eosdem statuit. 3. Nec potest dari ratio, quare Petrus de Apostolis agens mox transiliat ad tempus Noae.

9. Arias Montanus Spiritus in carcere inclusos interpretatur octo animas in arca inclusas, quae erat velut carcer. Iis praedicasse Christum in Spiritu per Noë autorem dictae famitiae qui per suasit, ut crederent & in arcam se reciperent, unde & eiusdem Christi iussu finito diluvio sunt egressae. Atqui. 1. per Spiritus non intelliguntur homines vivi, sed animae hominum mortuorum, quibus in carcere inferni constitutis Christus praedivacit, cùm. temporibus Noae adhuc in carne viverent. 2. Spiritus illi dicuntur increduli fuisse, cum Noë fabricaret arcam. At hac ratione Noahus ipse fuisset incredulus. 3. Octo animas sive homines in arca servatos Petrus ab incredulis illis distinguit.

10. Calvinus lib. 2. Instit. cap. 16. §. 9. & in Psychopannych. sic explicat, Christum praedicasse Spiritibus defunctorum & bonis & malis, non quòd ad eos venerit per animae praesentiam, sed quòd effecerit, ut sentirent effectum suae passionis & mortis; & boni quidem gaudium receperint, mali vero moerorem. Vocemφυλακῆς vertit per speculam, in qua animae piorum dicuntur fuisse, quia erant in continua expectatione passionis Christi, erant in spe promissae salutis intentae, quasi eminus è specula, in qua vigiliae aguntur, eam expectarent. Resp. 1. per hanc expositionem tollitur realis Christi ad inferos descensus. 2. Spiritus coactâ quadam glosâ de efficacia & virtute explicatur, cum â carne distinguatur, eique opponatur. 3. Petrus emphaticè dicit, Christusπορευθεὶςpraedicavit. Atqui ad efficaciam exerendam nulla opus erat πορέυσει. 4. φυλακὴ nuspiam ponitur pro expectatione,φυλάττωcustodio, inde φυλακὴcustodia, quae vocula traducitur ad significanda omnia, quae ad ad custodiam & tutelam pertinent, qualia sunt carceres, excubiae, vigiliae. provigilia noctis usurpaturMatth. 14. v. 25.Marc. 6. v. 48.Matth. 24. v. 43.Luc. 2. v. 8.cap. 12. v. 38. pro custodia sive excubiis,Actor. 12. v. 10. 5. usus speculae & vigiliarum non est expectare, sed custodire & observare, ne quid insidiarum hostis moliatur. 6. Petrus non distinguit inter spiritus bonos & malos, sed absolutè vocat ἀπειθεῖς. Vidit Calvinus has difficultates, ideò regerit, posse etiam carceris nomen retineri. Sicut enim pii V. T. dum vivebant, lex illis quaedam arctior fuit custodia, in qua detinebanturGal. 3. v. 15. ita post mortem solicito Christi desiderio constringi oportuit, quia nondum Spiritus libertatis plenè exhibitus erat. Ergò expectationis anxietas illis fuit veluti carcer. Sed si vel maximè argumentum, à significatione voculae φυλακῆς petitum, hac ratione esset solutum, nihilò tamen minùs starent adhuc argumenta reliqua. Unde enim probat Calvinus, animas piorum in V. T. post mortem non statim ad beatificam Dei visionem aspir asse, sed solicito Christi desiderio constrictas fuisse? Eccur etiam Apostolus incredulos vocat Spiritus illos in φυλακῇ constitutos? Excipit Calvinus, incredulorum ideo factam esse mentionem, quia permixti fuêre puri Dei cultores incredulis, significat ergò, nihil nocuisse sanctis Patribus, quod impiorum multitudine penè obruti fuerint. Atqui Apostolus non agit de quadam incredulorum & fidelium mixtione, sed illos ipsos Spiritus in φυλακῇ positos, quibus Christus praedicavit, dicit fuisse olim incredulos.

II. Plerique ex veteribus hunc locum accipunt de descensu Christi ad inferos, hoc sensu. Christus mortificatus est carne, quia animae & corporis unio in morte fuit soluta, sed vivificatus Spiritu, quia per divinam eius virtutem & potentiam anima corpori vicissim fuit unita ac vita eirestituta.2. Corinth 13. v. 4.in qua divina virtute secundùm animam & secundùm modum glorificati ac spiritualis corporis tanquam gloriosus triumphator profectus est, & descendit ad Spiritus damnatos in carcere inferni constitutos, qui increduli aliquando fuerant, & propter incredulitatem suam in hunc locum venerant, iisque praedicavit, h. e. incredulitatem ipsorum redarguit, ac divinam suam maiestatem & victoriam manifestavit. Hanc expositionem non simpliciter repudiamus, modò observetur. 1. per Spiritum, in quo Christus dicitur profectus ad Spiritus in carcere, non intelligi propriè ac directè animam, sed divinam virtutem, per quam corpus fuit vivificatum & glorificatum. 2. per carcerem non intelligi limbum vel purgatorium; sed ipsum infernum damnatorum. 3. Christum non ideò descendisse, ut damnatos quosdam praedicatione suâ converteret, & ex inferno liberaret, sed ut incredulitatem eis exprobraret, & maiestatem suam Daemonibus & damnatis animabus manifestaret. Probatur haec expositio. 1. quia congruit cum serie textus, ut ostendimus superiùs. 2. πορευθεὶςv. 22. accipitur de ascensu Christi in coelum. Ergò versimile est v. 19. accipi de descensu Christi ad infernum. 3. Sicut in ascensione sua Christus suam gloriam & maiestatem spiritibus iustorum ostendit: sic in descensu ad inferos suam gloriosam victoriam & maiestatem Spiritibus damnatorum ostendit, illis quidem in glorificationem & exultationem: his vero in ignominiam & confusionem. 4. Patres plerique ita exponunt, Athanasius in Epist. ad Epictetum Corinthiorum Episeopum, quem citat Epiphanius haeresi 77. Dinceritarum. Corpus Christi erat in monumento positum, quando ipse ivit ad praedicandum etiam Spiritibus in carcere, ut Petrus dixit. Cyrillus de recta fide ad Theodosium. Anima ad Verbum copulam & unionem sortita descendit quidem in infernum: divina autem virtute & potestate utens etiam Spiritibus, qui illic erant, apparuit. Postea subiungit verba Petri. Ambrosius in Eph. 4.Triumphato Diabolo descendit in cor terrae, ut ostensio eius praedicatio esset mortuorum, ut & quotquot eius essent cupidi, liberarentur. Bellarminus lib. 4. de Christo cap. 13. dicit, similia occurrere apud Clement. Alexandrinum lib. 6. stromat. Athanas. lib. de Incarnatione, qui incipit, Mos pii hominis, Cyrillum de recta fide ad Reginas & lib. 12. in Ioh. cap. 36. Hilarium in Psal. 118. super verba. Defecerunt oculi mei in eloquium tuum. Ambrosium in C. 10. Rom. Ruffinum in exposit. Symb. Oecum. in h. l. sed negari non potest, plerosque ipsorum in eam declinare opinionem, quòd Christus in suo ad inferos descensupraedicatione suâ quosdam converterit & liberaverit. quidam etiam non faciunt disertam huius loci Apostolici mentionem. 5. Iustinus in Dial. cum Triphone, & Irenaeus l. 3. C. 23. citant verba quaedam Esaiae ex LXX. Interpp. versione, quae in Heb. non inveniuntur, similima istis verbis S. Petri, ut credibile sit, inde S. Petrum accepisse. Sunt a. haec verba. Commemoratus est Dominus sanctus Israël mortuorum suorum, qui dormierant in terra sepelitionis, & descendit ad eos evangelizare salutem, quae est ab eo, ut salvaret eos. Obvertitur huic expositioni, 1. nomenφυλακῆςnon accipi de inferno. Resp. imò vero Apoc. 20. v. 7. disertè de eo usurpatur, ut constat ex v. 3. ac carcer etiam in Hist. Evang. ut typus inferni proponitur, Matth. 5. v. 25.C. 18. v. 30.Luc. 12. v. 58. inde Syrus h. l. reddidit [consult facsimile image]in inferno. 2. praedicationem non satis commodè in inferno dici factam. Resp. intelligitur praedicatio non tàm verbalis, quàm realis, (sicut Hebr. 12. v. 24. loquela non verbalis, sed realis) quâ Christus non ad conversionem & liberationem animabus impiorum praedicavit, sicut in ministerio suo in his terris fecerat, sed ad ipsorum confutationem & confusionem, ut magno suo cum malo hunc praeconem iustitiae, qui per Noahum olim ipsis praedicaverat, se sprevisse intelligerent. Ut enim in iudicio extremo impii in suis corporibus ipsum iudicem conspecturi sunt, & poenas à facie Domini sensuri 1. Thess. 1. v. 9.Apocal. 1. v. 7. ita quoque animae eorum extra corpora constitutae ipsum ut gloriosum triumphatorem in inferno conspexerunt, & hac visione cruciatus in iis fuit auctus. Sensus igitur hic est: Christus divinâ virtute ad inferos descendit, & ibi apparuit Spiritibus ob incredulitatem damnatis, non ut eos inde liberaret, neque ut tempus resipiscendi illis concederet, Hebr. 9. v. 27. sed ut eis ostenderet, nunc se in carne venisse, & redemtionis precium praestitisse, quod illi olim temporibus Noae, cum de eo ipsis praedicaretur, praefractè contemsissent. Sic ergò Christus damnatis in inferno gloriam triumphi sui ostendit in sua ad eum descensione; hominibus in terra viventibus eandem demonstravit in gloriosa resurrectione, beatis in coelo Spiritibus in gloriosa ad coelum ascensione. 3. Christum non solùm in Spiritu sive anima, sed in tota atque integra humanitate postζωοποίησινac animae & corporis unionem ad inferos descendisse. Resp. per Spiritum propriè intelligitur divina Christi virtus, consequenter etiam anima corpori unita, quia immediatè praemittitur, quòd Christus Spiritu vivificatus in infernum fuerit profectus. 4. Christum hoc descensu non post, sed ante resurrectionem perfunctum esse. Resp. distinguendum inter ζωοποίησιν, καὶ ἀνάστασιν,Rom. 14. v. 9. Illa descensum Christi ad inferos praecessit, haec vero secuta est.

Q. 2. Quid perφυλακὴνintelligatur? 1. Pontificii limbum Patrum vel purgatorium. 2. Calvinus vigiliam vel speculam. 3. Augustinus Epist. 99. ad Evodium, corpus quod est animae carcer. 4. Quidam accipiunt de coecitate mentis. Ioh. Huss. Qui in carcere carnis, vel peccati, vel erroris, vel huius exilii erant, non valentes per se egredi. Gloss. interlin. de carcere tenebrarum & infidelitatis, ac de carnalibus desideriis. 5. Simplicissimè exponitur de inferno, ut exponunt Scholia Graeca ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ. Syrus [consult facsimile image]in inferno.

Q. 3. Quinam sint illi Spiritus, quibus Christus praedicavit? 1. Quidam intelligunt Spiritus bonos, i. e. animas piorum V. T. quibus praedicata & praestita sit ex limbo liberatio. Illi urgent verbum praedicandi, quod in bonam partem utplurimùm accipitur, ac pro quo c. seq. v. 6. poni putant verbum evangelizandi, mali enim non sunt capaces Evangelii, utpote damnationi addicti. Sed adhuc in quaestione est, an idem h. l. intelligatur verbo praedicandi, quod cap. seq. intelligitur verbo Evangelizandi. 2. Quidam accipiunt de bonis & malis promiscuè, quorum illis liberationis, his damnationis sententia fuerit denunciata. Sed ex inferno vel limbo quosdam liberatos esse in descensu Christi, gratis dicitur. 3. Quidam de hominibus in carne adhuc viventibus accipiunt, sed κατάχρησις haec est durior. 4. Simplicissimè accipitur de Spiritibus, i. e. animabus damnatis impiorum, quia vocantur ἀπειθεῖς, & dicuntur esse in carcere sc. inferni. Angelus Pasl. 7. in Symb. cap. 20. recitante Lorino, per incredulos intelligit damnatos, qui extiterunt sub Noa, & extincti sunt in diluvio: sed reliquis verbis his, qui in carcere erant, in genere omnes omninò. Verùm contextus ostendit, utrobique de iisdem sermonem esse.

Q. 4. Quid per praedicationem Spiritibus factam denotetur? Resp. 1. Qui limbum propugnant, exponunt de praedicatione liberationis. Bellarm. lib. 4. de Christo cap. 13. §. Argumenta. Praedicatio Christi nihil fuit aliud, quàm nuncium liberationis. Sed expositionem de limbo paviò pòst excutiemus. 2. qui de descensu Christi ad inferos locum accipiunt, exponunt de manifestatione gloriosae Christi victoriae & denunciatione ac confirmatione damnationis impiorum. Christus ad inferos descendens illustriori quadam patefactione sese iam exhibitum mundo declaravit, ac impiis diram ac lugubrem illam concionem, si non verbis, tamen reipsâ, apparitione sc. suae gloriae proposuit, quòd passionis & mortis suae meritum iam porrò nihil ad eos pertineat, cum in verbo Evangelii oblatum illum fide recipere noluerint, ac proinde praesentiâ hac sua magis confirmari poenas illas, de quibus monuerat Noë & alii Prophetae.τὸ πότεtempus Noae indicat, non tempus praedicationis Christi in inferno. Deriserant illi olim Noahum tanquam delirum senem, Christus ipsis attestatus est, vera comminatum Noahum. 3. Simplicissimè exponitur de praedicatione poenitentiae, quia Filius DEI per Noahum comminatione imminentis diluvii eos, qui vixerunt temporibus Noae, invitavit ad poenitentiam, Genes. 6. v. 3. Huc referendum, quòd Apostolus noster 2. Epist. 2. v. 5. vocat κήρυκα τῆς δικαιοσὺνηςpraeconem iustitiae (ubi usurpat nomen ex verbo κηρύττω, quod hîc habetur, deductum) ergò praedicavit illis ex Christi mandato iustitiam, quae consistit in remissione peccatorum Luc. 1. v. 77. ac fide in promissum Messiam obtingit, cuius fidei antecedens est vera contritio, consequens studium bonorum operum. Praedicavit Noahus in nomine Messiae, adeoque Filius DEI per Noahum praedicavit poenitentiam & remissionem peccatorum, Luc. 24. vers. 47. ut peccata sua agnoscerent, seriò de illis dolerent, in promissum Messiam crederent, vitam emendarent, & animum ad iustitiae studium applicarent.

Q. 5. Quare Apostolus exemplum illorum producat, qui temporibus Noae vixerunt? Resp. Filius DEI ab initio adfuit generi humano, ac continuâ temporum serie per Patriarchas & Prophetas mundo praedicavit, proinde quod de impiis, qui tempore diluvii vixerunt, dicitur, id ad omnium aetatum impios pertinet. Voluit autem Petrus in specie hominum antediluvianorum mentionem facere. 1. Quia exemplum maximè accommodatum fuit ad propositum Petri, quippe in quo DEI longanimitas, Noae constantia & patientia, ac impiorum eversio secuta magis elucent. 2. Utrumque in hoc exemplo manifestissimè ostenditur, DEUM contemtores & persecutores verbi gravissimè punire, fideles autem verbi confessores mirabiliter conservare. 2. Petr. 2. v. 5.DEUS originali mundo non pepercit, sed octavum Noë iustitiae praeconem custodivit, diluvium mundo impiorum inducens.v. 9.Novit Dominus pios de tentatione eripere, iniquos vero in diem iudicii reservare cruciandos. 3. Respicit Apostolus ad maximum mundi peccatum, cuius mensura nunquam copiosiùs quàm diluvii tempore fuit completa, Genes. 6. v. 5. & 12. & ad gravissimum peccatorum supplicium; nunquam enim tanta hominum multitudo simul periit, & secundùm animas ad infermum descendit. 4. Voluit Apostolus sibi viam parare ad digressionem de efficacia Baptismi, qui salutis nostrae & conservationis ad vitam aeternam organum.

Q. 7. An voculaἅπαξin textu Graeco redundet? Ita quibusdam videtur. 1. Quia non habetur in omnibus Codicibus Graecis, abest enim ab illis, qui legunt ἀπεξεδέχετο. 2. Non extat in paraphrasi Syriaca. 3. Non videtur agnita à Latinis Patribus, hunc locum citantibus. 4. Nec ad rem propositam facere videtur. Sed probatiores Codd. Graeci eam habent, quod sufficit. Petrus hac vocula significare voluit, id quod semel DEUS fecit in figura, nunc, h. e. tempore N. T. quotidiè ipsum facere in re per figuram significata. Quae oppositio particulae ἅπαξ in vers. 20. & particulae νῦν in v. 21. ostendit, voculam ἅπαξ esse textui genuinam.

Q. 8. An quidam in diluvio extra arcam positi & aquis submersi seriam egerint poenitentiam, & salutis aeternae participes facti fuerint? Resp. Pererius statuit, omnes, qui in diluvio suffocati fuerunt, in infernum demersos esse, exceptis solis infantibus, qui Sacramento illius temporis renati fuerint, idque colligit ex eo, quòd de solo Noah Spiritus sanctus commemorat, ipsum in generatione illa fuisse iustum,Gen. 6. v. 9.cap. 7. v. 1. Lorinus in h. l. Gratis videtur admitti aliquorum poenitentia inter eos, qui diluvio submersi. ibid. Non possumus divinare, aliquos egisse poenitentiam. Et postea. Sequenti Epistolâ capite 2. idem repetitur simul cum interitu Sodomitarum & Angelorum, qui videntur omnes periisse. Quidam id probant ex eo, quòd conservationem tempore diluvii Petrus hîc proponit, ut typum spiritualis conservationis ad vitam aeternam, eamque solis illis, qui in arca fuerunt tribuit. Contra vero Chrysostomus, Hieronymus & alii rectiùs statuunt, non solùm infantes, sed etiam aliquos adultos, cum aquarum incrementum quotidianum viderent, concionis Noaiticae recordatos veram poenitentiam egisse, ac supplicium aeternae damnationis effugisse. 1. Quia perpetuae & immotae veritatis est oraculum Propheticum.Esai. 55. vers. 11.Verbum, quod egreditur ex ore meo, non revertetur ad me vacuum. 2. In poenis publicis & universalibus ita contingeresolet, ut quidam, videlicet illi, qui poenitentiam agunt, carnis interitum sustineant, ut Spiritus eorum salvus fiat.1. Corinth. 5. vers. 5. 3. Chrysostomus monet, DEUM ex misericordia non simul & semel, sed per dies quadraginta pluviam demisisse, ut homines adhuc haberent spacium conversionis. 4. Sicut non omnes, qui corporaliter in arca servati, salutem aeternam sunt consecuti; fuit enim in arca impius Cham: sic non omnes, qui fuêre extra arcam corporaliter puniti, morte aeternâ sunt damnati. 5. Quidam addunt locum nostrum Apostolicum collatum cum 1. Petr. 4. v. 6. ex quo colligunt, disparem fuisse eventum illorum, qui diluvio universali sunt deleti, cum aliorum Spiritus seu animae venerint in carcerem, eorum scilicet, qui non egerunt poenitentiam, aliorum vero vitam aeternam consecutae fuerint, eorum sc. qui castigatione corporis ad poenitentiam sunt adducti. 6. Estius adducit locum Psal. 78. v. 34.Probabile est, inquit, iuxta illud, Cùm occideret eos, quaerebant eum, & revertebantur &c. multos ex iis, qui praedicationem Noae denunciantis interitum peccatoribus contemserant aut neglexerant, quod hîc Petrus vocat incredulos fuisse, superveniente & inundante diluvio poenitentiam ex timore concepisse veram, sed imperfectam. Sed Psaltes Regius ibi loquitur de Israëlitis in deserto, non de hominibus antediluvianis.

Q. 9. Quo respectu Apostolus neget, Baptismum esse depositionem sordium carnis? 1. Quidam putant, respectum haberi ad Circumcisionem Baptismi typum, quae erat ablatio sordium carnis h. e. sordidae & immundae carnis, videlicet praeputii, quò referunt locum Apostolicum Coloss. 2. vers. 11.Circumcisi estis circumcisione non manufactain exuitione corporis peccatorum carnis, in circumcisione Christi. Sed circumcisio aequè ac Baptismus fuit efficax medium regenerationis, remissionis peccatorum & salutis, ac proinde de ea itidem dici potest, quòd non fuerit depositio sordium carnis i. e. quòd non fuerit ad externam corporis mundationem instituta. 2. Quidam volunt, respectum haberi ad ablutiones Leviticas, de quibus PaulusHebr. 9. vers. 13.dicit, quòd sanctificaverint inquinatosπρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα. 3. Posset etiam cogitari, Apostolum respicere ad crebras illas lotiones, quibus Pharisaei & Iudaei ex traditione maiorum utebantur, Matth. 15. v. 2.Marc. 7. v. 3. & 4. quibus ita confidebant, ut propterea Baptismum Iohannis repudiarent. Luc. 7. v. 30. Thomas Anglicus in h. l. putat. respectum haberi ad Baptismum Iohannis, qui fuerit tantùm in aqua. Sed Iohannis Baptisma aequè fuit efficax regenerationis Sacramentum, ac Baptismus Apostolorum 4. Simplicissimè respondetur, Apostolum respicere ad vulgarem sordium carnis ablutionem, quae sit in balneo vel podoniprio. Docet enim, Baptismum non esse institutum ad externam corporis ablutionem, sed ad internam cordis mundationem, quae consistitin regeneratione & renovatione, Eph. 5. v. 27.Tit. 3. v. 5.

Q. 10. Quodnam sitἐπερώτημα τῆς ἀγαθῆς. συνειδὴσεως? Resp. 1. ἐπερώτημα propriè significat interrogationem. Quidam ergò per interrogationem bonae conscientiae velut per consequens intelligunt, antecedens, videlicet remissionem peccatorum, ex cuius siducianascitur bona conscientia, quâ fretus fidelis audacter interrogat de ipsius erga se favore per Christi mortem sibi conciliato, ac per eius resurrectionem confirmato. Huc referri potest, quòd interrogatio apud Hebraeos quandoque usurpatur in vehementi asseveratione Gen. 13. v. 8.Ezech. 22. v. 2. Significatur ergò, quod conscientia à labe peccati per Baptismum mundata possit asseveranter dicere, & coram DEO, se esse puram & bonam. 2. Affinis huic expositioni est ea, qua per hoc ὲπερώτημαbonae conscientiae quidam significari putant, Baptismi effectum hunc esse, ut conscientia, hoc lavacro aquae in verbo mundata à peccatis, iam Deum interroget i. e. invocet, dicens Abba pater.Rom. 8. v. 15. 3. Oecumenius per ἐπερώτημα intelligit pignus & arrhabonem, quia Baptismus testis est conscientiae nostrae, quòd simus in gratia DEI propter Christum; ac obsignat foedus gratiae & promissionem salutis, ut baptizali fiducialiter possint DEUM in precibus suis compellare. Huius loci est observatio illa, quod LXX. vocabulo ἐπερωτᾷν utuntur, quando Israëlitae in V. T. dicuntur interrogare os Domini sedentis super Cherubim, ut certi redderentur, quomodo DEUS in tali casu affectus esset erga ipsos. Baptismus igitur est interrogatio, quâ inter Deum & peccatorem agitur de bona conscientia erga Deum propter Christum, hoc est, quomodo Deus erga baptizatum affectus sit, quid conscientia de gratia Dei promittere sibi debeat. Ad hanc interrogationem Historia de Baptismo Christi monstrat responsionem. D. Chemnic. in Harmon. cap. 17. pag. 16. 4. Quidam vertunt per stipulationem, sensu eo, quòd Baptisma sit solennis quaedam conventio, confoederatio & mutua obligatio, quâ DEUS homini suam gratiam offerat, applicet & obsignet, ac vicissim conscientia de gratia Dei certior reddita stipuletur, se credere remissionem peccatorum, & ad obsequium se Deo astringat. Hûc respicit B. Lutherus, quando ἐπερώτημα reddit per foedus. Lyranus refert ad interrogationes, quae patrimis in Baptismo proponuntur, ad quas nomine baptizati respondent. Conscientiae bonae interrogatio. Nam à baptizando quaeritur: Credis in Deum, & respondet, Credo, perse, si est adultus, vel per patrimos, si est parvulus. Stipulatio enim est verborum conceptio, quibus is, qui interrogatur, daturum facturumz, se, quod interrogatus est, respondet, qualis in Baptismo sit, quando baptizando dicitur Credis, Abrenuncias &c.Actor. 8. v. 37. Nicetas annotat. 3. in Nazianzeni orationem. 40. In quorum numero Baptismus quoque est, qui quidem, at Petri verbis ut ar, non sor dium carnis depositio est, sed conscientiae bonaeinterrogatio ad Deum. Interrogati enim in Baptismo, quomodo se habeat conscientia nostra erga Deum, & quam in eum fidem habeamus, respondemus nos ipsius partibus adiungi, atque ut uno verbo dicam, fidei Symbola profitemur. At hae expositiones non sunt oppositae, sed subordinatae, ac possunt optimâ ratione coniungi. 6. Syrus Interpres paulo longiùs abiit à textu Graeco, quia reddidit, confitentes: Deum in conscientia pura. 7. Quidam simpliciter intelligunt animum benè conscium, ut qui per internam interrogationem facto sui ipsius examine nihil in se reperiat, quod indignum reddat fructu Baptismi. Sed manifestum est, Apostolum loqui de effectu Baptismi, 8. Suarez. P. 3. q. 62. Disp. 7. sect. 1. censet, hîc tantùm significari, qua dispositione accedendum sit ad Baptismum, sc. ut rogemus & cupiamus per Baptismum mundari non corpus, sed conscientiam. Sed Apostolus non loquitur de dispositione baptizandorum, sed de Baptismi effectu.

Q. 11. Quare addat Apostolusεἰς θεὸν? Resp. 1. Quia conscientiae cum DEO, & quidem solo DEO res est. Solus DEUS videt & novit, an conscientia sit bona. 2. Tota res in Baptismo agitur coram DEO i. e. teste DEO. 3. Lyranus in h. l. Fides caritate formata (per caritatem efficax) facit conscientiam bonam in Deum tendentem. 4. Lutherus reddidit, cum DEO, quia foedus gratiae in Baptismo initur inter Deum & baptizatum.

Q. 12. Quare addat Apostolusδι' ἀναστάσεως Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ; Monuimus superiùs, quosdam hunc προσδιορισμὸν coniungere cum verbo σώζει, ut verba intermedia, οὐ σαρκὸς ἀπόθεσις ῥύπου, ἀλλὰ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς θεὸν, includantur parenthesi, uti fit in editione Lugdunensi. Quomodo autem Baptismus:

per resurrectionem Christi dicaturnos salvare, diversimodè exponut, 1. Quidam sic progrediuntur. Christi resurrectio formam quandam nobis exhibet resurgendi ad iustitiam & vitae novitatem, ad quam regeneramur & renovamur in Baptismo, ut quemadmodum Christus resurrexit à mortuis, ita & nos in novitate vitae ambulemus,Rom. 6. v. 4. Sed hic secundarius est resurrectionis Dominicae fructus. 2. Christus resurrexit propter nostram iustificationemRom. 4. v. ult.baptizamur autem in mortem (& resurrectionem) ChristiRom. 6. v. 3. Ergò fructus iustitiae & salutis per mortem & resurrectionem Christi nobis partae in Baptismo & per Baptismum nobis communicatur, inde etiam Petrus dicit, nos regenitos esse in spem vivam per resurrectionem Christi,1. Epist. 1. v. 3. Beda in h. l. Sicut ipse resurgens à mortuis ascendit in coelum, & sedet ad dextram Dei: sic etiam & nobis per Baptismaviam salutis & regni coelestis introitum patere signavit. Hugo & Thomas: Qui Baptismo renascitur, simul quodam modo resurgit, mortuus & veluti sepultus & suffocatus in peccatis, quae ei remittuntur. 3. Per resurrectionem Christi συνεκδοχικῶς etiam passio & mors Christi denotantur, cum terminus passionis & mortis fuerit resurrectio. Dicitur ergò Baptismus nos salvare per resurrectionem Christi, quia vis Baptismi nos regenerantis & renovantis descendit ex passione, morte & resurrectione Christi. 4. Quidam sic exponunt. Baptismus nos salvat per resurrectionem Christi i. e. virtute Christi Mediatoris, qui pro peccatis nostris mortuus est & resurrexit propter nostram iustificationem Sed rectiùs hic προσδιορισμὸς refertur ad proximè praecedens, videlicet ad interrogationem bonae conscientiae, quia fiduciam nostram de remissione peccatorum, ex qua oritur bona conscientia, confirmat Christi resurrectio, quae testatur, Christum esse victorem peccati, Diaboli, mortis & inferni. Quo enim sensu Apostolus dixit superiùs, Deum secundùm suam misericordiam nos regenuisse in spem vivam per resurrectionem Christi, 1. Epist. 1. v. 3. eodem sensu hoc loco dicit, interrogationem bonae conscientiae fieri per resurrectionem Christi i. e. bonam conscientiam niti resurrectione Christi, quippe quae est publicum testimonium, pro peccatis nostris plenè esse satisfactum, nos Deo perfectè esse reconciliatos, mortem in victoria esse absorptam & omnia, quae ad salutem nostram promerendam spectabant, esse perfectè consummata.

Q. 11. Secundùm quam Naturam Christus sit in dextra Dei? Resp. secundùm divinam est ipsa Dei dextra, secundùm humanam in tempore est ad Dei dextram collocatus. Coniungit Apostolus profectionem in coelos, & sessionem ad dextram Dei. Iam vero secundùm humanam Naturam Christus prosectus est in coelum. Ergò secundùm eandem sedet ad Dei dextram. Beda in h. l. Nulli dubium est, quin Filio Dei semper fuerint Angeli & omnes patriae coelestis virtutes ac potestates subiectae, quem cum Patre & Spiritu sancto unum sine initto Deum laudant, tremunt, adorant. Sed necessariò admonendum B. Petrus aestimavit, quòd assumta humanitas in tantam sit gloriam resurgendo sublimata, ut incomparabili culmine omni Angelicae dignitatis potentiae praeferatur. Iuxta quod & Psalmista cùm diceret de ipso Patri: Minuisti eum paulo minus ab Angelis, continuò subiecit, Gloriâ & honore coronasti eum, & constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum, omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius.

Q. 12. Quare nominatim Angelos, potestates & virtutes Christo dicat subiectas? Hoc non est accipiendum exclusivè vel restrictivè, quasi ex omnibus creaturis soli Angeli, & ex omnibus Angelis soli hi tres ordines Christo fuerint subiecti, sed cumulativè, & extensivè, quòd non solùm Angeli, sed omnes omninò creaturae in collocatione ad dextram Dei Christo subiectae fuerint. Psal. 8. v. 7.1. Cor. 15. v. 27.Ephes. 1. v. 20. & 21.Hebr. 2. v. 8. quia qui dicit maius, includit minus; & qui est Dominus Angelorum, ille etiam est Dominus inferiotum creaturarum.

Ἐναντιοφανείαι. 1. Christus in Spirituπορευθεὶςpraedicavit temporibus Noaev. 19. Atqui Matth. 4. v. 17.Exinde coepit Iesus praedicare. Resp. 1. Petrus loquitur de Λόγῳ ἀσάρκῳ, Matthaeus de ἐνσάρκῳ. 2. distinguendum inter praedicationem mediatam per Noahum, & immediatam; de illa Petrus, de hac Matthaeus loquitur.

2. Homines antediluviani fuêre increduliv. 19.& tamen praeparatum fuit vastum illud arcae aedificium,v. 20. Resp. 1. etsi fidem negarent comminationibus Divinis per Mosen denunciatis, tamen lucri gratiâ operas suas ad arcam constituendam Noaho locabant. 2. August. lib. 15. de C. D. c. ult. dicit, spacium centum annorum in eo consumtum, paucitatem compensavit fabricantium.

3. Baptismanos salvat.v. 21.At in solo Deo est efficacia salvandi.Esa. 43. v. 3. Resp. distinguendum inter causam salutis principalem, & instrumentalem. Deus non salvat nos immediatè, sed mediatè per verbum & Sacramenta, quae sunt media ex parte Dei; & per fidem, quae est medium ex parte nostra.

4. Christus est ad dextram Dei subiectis ei Angelis,v. 22.Atqui etiam in statu exinanitionis Angelici servierunt,Matth. 4. v. 11. Resp. Subiectio illa, quantum attinet ad potestatem Christo homini datam, facta est in primo incarnationis momento, quam exeruit, quando voluit, & ubi voluit: sed in potestatis istius plenarium usum introductus est, postquam in coelum ascendit, & ad dextram Patris coelestis consedit.

Ἔλεγχος. 1. Christus in Spiritu temporibus antediluvianis per Noahum praedicavit. v. 19. Ergò non solùm est homo verus, sed etiam in personae unitate verus Deus, nec existendi initium coepit in nativitate ex virgine, sed extitit ante Mariam, ante Mosen, ante AbrahamumIoh. 8. v. 58. imò ante mundi exordium, adeoque ab aeterno. Opponendum hoc Photinianis, Deitatem & aeternitatem Christi negantibus.

2. Dei patientia temporibus Noae expectavit hominum conversionem. Ex eo Petrus hoc infert consectarium 2. Epist. 2. v. 9. Non tardat Dominus promissum, sicut quidam tarditatem esse existimant, sed patienter agit propter nos, nolens aliquos perire, sed omnes ad poenitentiam reverti. Opponendum hoc architectis absoluti decreti reprobationis, contra quos sic concludimus. Quorum conversionem Deus patienter expectat, illos non vult absoluto quodam odio perire. Atqui etiam eorum, qui in peccatis suis securè pergunt, conversionem Deus patienter expectat. Ergò

3. In arca Noae octo tantùm animae erant, quarum ambitu tota in terris visibilis Ecclesia continebatur. Ergò amplitudo ac multitudo non est propria & perpetua Eccle siae nota. contra Bellarminum lib. 4. de Eccles. cap. 7. Rectè Salmero tom. 12. comment. in Act. Apost. tract. 9. super verba. Erat autem turba hominum ferè centum & viginti. Vides, quàm parvo numero tunc existeret Ecclesia, quae tamen mox in omnes mundi partes & gentes propaganda erat. Veritas enim Eccle siae Dei in multitudine non consistit, ut primitiva docet &c.

4. Noahus cum familia in arca per annum integrum fuit conclusus, ventorum procellis, & fluctuum verticibus obnoxius, sed divinâ benignitate & potentiâ in diluvio conservatus. Ergò felicitas temporalis non est nota Ecclesiae, sed divina in persecutionibus conservatio. Contra Bellarminum lib. 4. de Ecclesia cap. 18. ubi felicitatem temporalem decimam quintam Ecclesiae notam constituit, qui tamen lib. eiusdem cap. 6. §. Iam vero &c. ex loco hoc Apostolico sic disserit. Constat, Ecclesiam ex per secutionibus crevisse. Ut enim aquae diluvii palatia Regum obruebant, atque deiiciebant; arcam verò Noë semper magis ac magis attollebant: ita per secutiones regna temporalia facilè destruunt, Christi regnum, quod est Ecclesia, non modò non destruunt, sed etiam illustrant &c.

5. Quemadmodum omnes homines extra arcam constituti in diluvio perierunt, soli autem illi, qui in arcam divino iussu fuerant ingressi, sunt conservati: sic in sola Ecclesia adversùs diluvium irae divinae conservari possumus, extra eam nil nisi mors & interitus, quò pertinet versus Nazianzeni, Ζητῶ Νῶε Κιβωτὸν, ὅπως μύρον αἴνον ἀλύζω. Cyprianus de simplicit. praelat. p. 164. Si potuit evadere, qui extra arcam Noae fuit, & qui extra Ecclesiam foris fuerit, evadet. Opponendum hoc omnibus illis, qui sanioribus gentilibus extra Ecclesiam spem salutis faciunt.

6. Baptisma nos salvat, inquit Apostolus. Ergò efficacia Baptismi etiam in futurum se extendit. Petrus post Baptismum perceptum in gravissimum abnegationis peccatum erat prolapsus, nihilo tamen minùs, consolationem ac certitudinem salutis suae petit ex Baptismo. Nemo salvatur, cui non remittuntur peccata praeterita, praesentia & futura. At credentes per Baptismum salvantur. Ergò credentibus per Baptismum remittuntur peccata praeterita, praesentia & futura. Inde etiam Spiritus sanctus in Scripturis de efficacia Baptismi loquitur verbis praeteriti, praesentis & futuri temporis, Tit. 3. v. 5.Galat. 3. v. 27.Ephes. 5. v. 26.Marc. 16. vers. 16. ut ostendat, Baptismi efficaciam non esse restringendam ad illud temporis momentum, in quo baptizamur, sed per totam vitam se extendere. Opponendum hoc Pontificiis, qui negant, Baptismi efficaciam in futurum se extendere. Bellarm. lib. de Bapt. cap. 18. Excipit Lorinus, Petrum non conferre Baptismum cum peccatis, sed Christi tempus cum tempore Noae, ut quemadmodum sub Noë octo salvos fecit diluvium per arcam, sic nunc salvet credentes Baptismus Christi. Deinde quotidiè salvari aliquos & mundari per Baptismum, sed à pectatis praeteritis immediatè, licet mediatè etiam à futuris, quatenus per characterem baptismalem datur ius ad poenitentiae Sacramentum. Resp. 1. Petrus non solùm confert tempus Christi cum tempore Noae, sed etiam perpetuam Baptismi in Nov. Testam. denotat efficaciam, quòd illis, qui hoc Sacramentum susceperunt, sit perpetuum medium salutis, sicut Ioh. 1. v. 29. Christus dicitur agnus DEI tollens peccata mundi, quia vis passionis Christi perpetuò durat. 2. Concedimus, Baptismum non immediatè à peccatis praeteritis, vel praesentibus, vel futuris mundare, sed mediante fide, quae in hoc Sacramento accenditur, augetur, & confirmatur, quae fidei confirmatio per totam vitam ex Baptismo peti potest. 3. Baptismus ideò salvat, quia per eum recipimur in foedus gratiae. Atqui foedus illud durat per totam vitam, ac si vel maximè ex eo per peccata excidamus, tamen per poenitentiam ad illud iterum patet nobis aditus.

7. Baptismus non est depositio sordium carnis, inquit Apostolus. Ergò non habet locum analogia Calvinianorum, quòd quemadmodum exterior Baptismus abluit sordes corporis, itae interior Baptismus Spiritûs tollat sordes animae; quòdque interior ablutio peccatorum per sanguinem Christi, per ablutionem externam in Baptismo tantùm significetur.

8. Baptismus est interrogatio bonae conscientiae ad Deum per resurrectionem Christi, adeoque fide acceptus prodest, ex qua fide bona conscientia oritur. Falsum est ergò, quod Pontificii docent, Baptismum prodesse ex opere operato. August. tract. 80. in Iohan. 1. inde ista tanta virtus aquae, ut corpus tangat, & cor abluat, nisi faciente verbo? non quia dicitur, sed quia creditur. Nam & in ipso verbo aliud est sonus transiens, aliud virtus manens. Hoc est verbum fidei, quod praedicamus, ait Apostolus &c. Unde in Actis Apostolorum legimus. Fide mundans corda eorum. Et in Epistola sua B. Petrus. Sic & vos, inquit, Baptisma salvos facit, non carnis depositio sordium, sed conscientiae bonae interrogatio &c. serm. 30. de verb. Dom. Deinde quid ostendit vobis? Quia & Baptismum, qui semel adhibetur, per fidem mundat. Fides autem intus est, non foris. Unde dicitur & legitur in Actis Apostolorum, fide mundans corda eorum.
