Veteres, inquit, non tantum fronte, in qua residet pudor, in Confirmatione ungebant & signabant cruce, ad intrepidè profitendam fidem & crucem, sed etiam alia membra. Id etiamnum servant Graeci, qui ungunt frontem, oculos & dorsum in formâ Crucis. Aethiopes verò, ut habet eorum Rituale seu ordo Baptismi, ungunt non tantùm oculos, frontem & dorsum in formam crucis, sed & nares, labia, pectus, stomachum, tibias, genua & pedes, ut significent (nota benè, ut significent, ergò significationis tantum causa hoc fit) obsignanda esse omnia membra, omnes sensus, omnes actiones Christiani, 4. gratiam Spiritus sancti in Baptismo datam & fidem in Christum crucifixum veteres dicunt esse illud signaculum, quo ad pugnam spiritualem roboramur. Ambros. l. 4. de Spiritu S. c. 6. Spiritu signamur, ut splendorem & imaginem eius & gratiam tenere possimus, quod est utique spirituale signaculum.

4. Verba Apostoli ὁ παθὼν ἐν σαρκὶ Erasmus refert ad Christum, reddit enim, qui patiebatur. Salmero eandem adducit expositionem, eamque minimè repudiat. Tertium, inquit, dubium diluimus duplici ratione Primùm quidem, ut intelligamus de Christe, qui non desiit à suis ullis peccatis, sed à nostris, quae tamen in corpore suo super lignum expianda portavit, nolens ultrà ea in se suscipere, ut iterum morimur, cui satis fuit semel mori pro omnibus peccatis. Sequitur, sed voluntate Dei, quod reliquum est in carne vivat temporis. Christus enim suscitatus in carne nova, vivens in hoc mundo per quadraginta dies nobis adfuit. Et significat tempus vitae nostrae à Baptismo ad mortem usque docens vitam spiritualem quam vivere debemus. Subiungit tamen. Alius apertus sensus & idoneus, quo hoc argumentum faciliùs solvitur, est, ut referamus ad hominem Christo insitum & baptizatum &c. Lorinus in h. l. sic commentatur. Tota oratio habet homonymiam, quam vidit Carthusianus, ut vel de Christo, vel de imitatione Christi possit intelligi. Sed primo modo, qui Titelmanno placet atque Salmeroni, quem idem iure postponit, secundo traditurque passim à caeteris non solùm exposit oribus, verùm etiam Hieronymo lib. 1. contra Iovinian. & Augustino lib. de fide & operibus cap. 10. homil. 20. ex quinquag. homil. & in editione Syra, non desiit Christus à peccatis, quasi peccaverit unquam, sed quia semper abstinuit vel potius quoniam desiit pro nobis peccatum esse2. Cor. 5. v. 21.ac dici, h. e. hostia pro peccato cruenta & quod mortuus est, peccato mortuus est semelRom. 6. v. 10. Socinus itidem utramque expositionem coniungit. Sic enim scribit Epist. 3. ad Schmalz. p. 518. Quatenus illa verba, passus est in carne, ad Christum referuntur, significant eius mortem & crucis passionem, ut sit sensus, illum per crucis passionem liberatum fuisse ab iis, quae poenae peccatorum esse solent. Quatenus vero refertur ad nos, significat, nos per interemptionem seu abiectionem carnalium desideriorum à peccando cessare. Resp. 1. In Graeco est perfectum παθὼν ergò minùs rectè redditur, qui patiebatur. 2. Christus non desiit à peccatis, quia nunquam coepit peccare. Si excipiant, Christum desiisse à peccatis, quae in se susceperat expianda. Resp. esse hanc valde duram catachresin. Is propriè dicitur à peccato cessare, qui cùm peccaverit hactenus, non ampliùs peccat. Si excipiant, Christum desiisse à peccatis, qui liberatus est à poenis peccatorum, resp. etiam hoc coactum esse, neque enim à proprietate literae ad metonymiam transeundum, nisi ipsa nos cogat necessitas. Si excipiant Christum dici desiisse à peccato, quia abolevit peccatum, resp. Si abolendi vis esset in verbo πέπαυται, construeretur cum accusativo. Sic enim Graeci loquuntur, πάυω τὴν δυστυχὶανtollo infelicitatem;πάυω βοηθείανtollo auxilium;πάυω νόσον,tollo morbum. Quando autem cum genitivo construitur, tunc propriè significat cessare, ut πάυομαι τῆς μαχῆς,recipio me à pugna;πάυομαι τῆς ἀρχῆςdepono Magistratum;πάυομαι ἁμαρτίαςdesino à peccato, quòd propriè peccatori convenit. 4. Nec satis commodè Christo tribui potest, quòd sequitur v. 2.ut iam non desideriis hominum, sed voluntati Dei, quòd reliquum est temporis, in carne vivat. Christus enim nunquam vixit desideriis hominum, nec vixit in carne, postquam peccato mortuus est semel, sed per suam resurrectionem ingressus est in vitam spiritualem & coelestem, dies carnis ipsius finiti sunt in ipsa morte. Hebr. 5. v. 7.2. Cor. 5. v. 16.

5. Salmero ad v. 1. sic commentatur. Christo satis fuit semel mori pro omnibus peccatis, quia ut Paulus dixitHebr. 10.Voluntariè peccantibus nobis post adeptam notitiam veritatis, iam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia, ut scil. omnia eiusmodi peccata expurget, ut in Baptismo facit, sed ipse novus peccator satisfacit Deo per poenitentiam, si velit ipsi reconciliare. Potest enim is qui in gratiam rediit, pro peccato admisso satisfacere. Resp. 1. Nuspiam in tota Scriptura occurrit hoc discrimen, quod Christus satisfecerit pro peccatis nostris ante Baptismum commissis; nobis autem ipsis pro peccatis post Baptismum commissis per poenitentiam satisfaciendum esse, sed Scriptura semper loquitur generaliter. Ioh. 1. v. 29.Ecce agnus Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi.Ioh. 1. v. 7.Sanguis Iesu Christi Filii DEI emundat nos ab omnibus peccatis.cap. 2. v. 2.Propitiatio est pro totius mundi peccatis. Rectè omninò Bellarminus lib. 3. de poenit. cap. 4. §. Altera solutio. Scriptura ubique, cum absolutè de peccatis loquitur, de omnibus peccatis intelligi solet & debet; & si liceret exponere de quibusdam, non de omnibus, ab surdissimae sententiae in divinis literis invenirentur. Subsumimus. Scriptura quando de satisfactione per Christum pro peccatis nostris praestita loquitur, indefinitè & absolutè loquitur, ut constat, Esai. 53. v. 5.1. Petr. 2. v. 24. &c. Ergò de omnibus peccatis id accipiendum. 2. Peccatum est infinitum malum, quia committitur contra infinitum bonum. Ergò ad satisfactionem pro peccato requiritur infinita vis, efficacia ac dignitas, quae in renatorum operibus vel passionibus non habet locum. Bellarm. lib. 2. de Iustif. cap. 5. Deus non acceptat in veram satisfactionem pro peccato, nisi iustitiam insinitam, quoniam peccatum offensa est infinita.

4. Bellarm. ibidem subiungit. Ut aliqua iustitia sit infinita, id est, insiniti precii & voloris &c. satis est ut sit iustitia personae infinitae, qualis est Christus DEUS & homo. Itaque obedientia, passio & mors Filii Dei, quamvis in se & essentialiter fuerit creata & finita, tamen ratione per sonae obedientis, patientis & morientis infinita fuit, & ex vero iustitiae rigore propitiatio fuit pro totius mundi peccatis. Atqui si satisfactio Christi est infiniti precii ac valoris, utique pro omnibus omninò peccatis est sufficiens. Item. Si ad iustitiam & satisfactionem infinitam requiritur, ut sit iustitia & satisfactio personae infinitae, sequitur, neminem hominum pro peccatis satisfacere posse, cum nullus homo sit infinitus. 4. Dictum Apostolicum Hebr. 10. non de quibusvis peccatis actualibus post Baptismum commissis, sed de certa peccati specie, videlicet de peccato in Spiritum sanctum loquitur.

6. Lorinus ad v. 3. sic annotat. Cavendus error haereticorum huius temporis, ipsammet concupiscentiam, eiusque motus omnes peccata esse. Iacobus à concupiscentia i. e. à potentia concupi scendi docet nos abstrahi & illici per suggestionem, & delectationem, cum conceperit per aliquem imperfectum consensum, tunc parere peccatum: si autem peccatum consummatum fuerit per plenum consensum, generare mortem &c. Augustinus crebrò testatur, concupiscentiam, quantumlibet ferveat, ebulliat, tumultuetur in carne, non esse peccatum, coram DEO, donec accesserit voluntatis consensus, dici tamen peccatum, quoniam ex originali peccato est & ad peccandum inclinat, praecepto autem, non concupisces, prohiberi pravum voluntatis consensum. lib. 6. contra Iulian. cap. 5. & 7. lib. 2. de nupt. & concup. cap. 23. 25. 26. lib. 1. contra duas Epist. Pelag. cap. 13. & alibi. Resp. 1. Concedimus per ἐπιθυμίας in textu Apostolico hoc loco intelligi concupiscentias pravas, ad quas voluntatis consensus accedit, loquitur enim de peccatis actualibus mortalibus, quae non consistunt cum fide & Dei gratia. Ex eo verò inferri nequit, concupiscentiam pravam, ad quam nondum accedit voluntatis consensus, non esle peccatum, sed hoc tantùm sequitur, eam non esse peccatum actuale, mortale, excutiens fidem & DEI gratiam. 2. Concupiscentia prava, ad quam nondum accedit consensus, non solùm vocatur peccatum, quod concedunt Pontificii, sed etiam convenit ei definitio peccati 1. Ioh. 3. v. 4. tradita, cùm sit ἀνομία,Rom. 7. v. 7. Itemque peccati proprietates & effecta ut suo loco demonstratur. 3. Iacobus loquitur de concupiscentia in genere non restricta ad fideles, sed generalissimè considerata. Quod si ergò ex loco Iacobi evinci posset, concupiscentiam non esse peccatum, consequens fuerit, concupiscentiam non solùm in renatis, sed etiam in non renatis non esse peccatum. 4. Distinguit Apostolus peccatorum gradus & de peccato actuali mortali, quaerit, unde oriatur? respondet autem ex concupiscentia prava, non à Deo oriri. Quamvis igitur concupiscentia prava in renatis habitualiter inhaerens & primi concupiscentiae motus, quibus per Spiritum resistitur, non sint actualia mortalia peccata, ex eo tamen inferri nequit, quod nullo modo sint peccata, ex negatione enim unius speciei ad negationem generis non valet consequentia. 5. Proinde maior propositio in argumento Lorini restringenda hoc modo. Quod gignit peccatum, non est peccatum scilicet illud ipsum quod gignit. Concupiscentia gignit peccatum scilicet actuale mortale, regnans in homine & saucians conscientiam. Ergò non est peccatum scilicet tale. Nisi haec restrictio addatur, negari poterit ipsum originale peccatum. 6. Augustinus concupiscentiam pravam non solùm vocat peccati causam & poenam, sed etiam peccatum. Quid clariùs loco illo classico lib. 6. contra Iulian. cap. 3. Sicut coecitas cordis quam solus removet illuminatur Deus & peccatum est, quo in Deum non creditur, & poenapeccati, quâ cor superbum digna animadversione punitur & causa peccati, cum aliquid coeci cordis errore committitur: ita concupiscentia carnis, adversus quam bonus concupiscit Spiritus & peccatum est, quia inest illi obedientia contra dominatum mentis, & poenapeccati est quiareddita est meritis inobedientis & causa peccati est defectione consentientis vel contagione nascentis.

7. Gregorius de Valentia lib. 2. de Idolol. cap. 7. p. 718. ex eo quod Petrus dicit, ἐν ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαιςin illicitis idolorum cultibus, colligit, aliquem esse licitum idolorum & simulachrorum cultum, inde Disp. 6. q. 2. de idolol. punct. 1. Idololatriam definit, quod sit cultus, quo honor divinus tribuitur alicui creaturae sicut Deo. Hanc definitionem punct. 3. sic exponit, eum divinos honores creaturae conferre, ut Deo, qui eam divino cultu sic prosequitur, ut eo, quantum in se est, velit illi opinionem conciliare talem, qualis reverâ in solam DEI maiestatem competit: ex quo colligit punct. 6.

Catholicos Romanenses idololatras non esse, cum sic honorent imagines ut minimè tamen creaturae adhibeant divinum honorem sicur Deo. Resp. 1. vocula illicitis non est διακριτικὴ distinctiva, per quam idololatria licita ab illicita distinguatur, sed est ὁριστικὴ & ἐξηγητικὴ circumscriptiva, per quam omnis idololatria statuitur illicita. 2. Estius rectè monet ἀθεμίτοις propriè vertendum esse in nefariis idolorum cultibus. Per hanc versionem in fumum abit collectio Gregorii. Ecquis enim ex eo, si quis scortationes vocaret nefarias sive nefandas, colligere velit, esse quandam scortationem licitam? 3. appendix illa definitionis Gregorianae est planè supervacanea. Quandocunque creaturae alicui divinus honor exhibetur, eo ipso creatura ista in DEI locum evehitur, ac pro DEO habetur, siquidem divinus honor non est, nisi is qui DEO debetur, ac proinde oblato tali honore ipsa divinitas revera attribuitur, vel certè ex immota consequentia attribui intelligitur. 4. Perinde se habet Gregorii definitio, ac si quis definire velit adulterium, concubitum cum altero, qui non sit coniux tanquam cum coniuge, ac proinde adulterum non esse, quae commisceatur ei, quem non habet pro coniuge, sed eam tantùm, quae alteri ceu coniugi sese prostituat.

8. Piscator ad v. 4. sic annotat. Huius admonitionis usus hodie est adversus blasphemiam eorum, qui cum vident nos improbare ac reprehendere compotationes & saltationes illas in nuptiis aliisque conviviis aut solemnitatibus usitatas, dicunt Spiritum Zvinglianum seu Calvinisticum esse Spiritum melancholicum, quo nimirum innuunt Diabolicum. Resp. 1. non eo nomine taxamus Calvinianos, quod compotationes & saltationes lascivas, inverecundas, libidinosas &c. improbant, eas enim nos aequè ac ipsi improbamus. 2. Sed hoc improbamus, quod omnes omninò choreas socias toto genere vitiosas, illicitas, profanas & Christiano indignas esse asserunt. Marloratus in cap. 14. Matth. Aretius loco 169. Iohan. Münster in tract. Von dem ungottseligen Tantz. 3. Nos certis adhibitis conditionibus choreas non tantùm solitarias, sed etiam socias iuvenili praesertim aetati concessas statuimus, videlicet si in iis teneatur modus, nec nimis sint frequentes, si fiant in praesentia honestarum personarum, si instituantur tantùm delectationis gratiâ, non autem ex levitate aliqua, vel libidinis excitandae, alende aut augendae gratiâ instituantur. 4. Quod Spiritum Calvinisticum vocamus melancholicum, hoc sit non tàm propter chorearum prohibitionem, quàm propter absoluti decreti reprobatorii assertionem.

9. Lorinus ad eund. vers. sic commentatur. Omnes ferè nostri temporis haeetici, ac praeterea parùm casti Catholici arbitrantur ac dictitant, aut impossibilem continentiam hominibus, aut minimè ab iis custodiri, qui profiteantur eam. Metiuntur sc. alios ex suamet libidine. Resp. 1. Extant publicae totius orbis & ipsorum Pontificiorum scriptorum querelae de fructibus coacti coelibatus Sacerdotalis & Monachalis. Georg. Cassander in consult. art. 23. Videmus hoc decreto de coelibatu Sacerdotali, usque adeo castitatem & continentiam in Clero non confirmari, ut per illud ad omne libidinis & flagitii genus fenestra aperta esse videatur. Et postea. Eò iam res rediit, ut vix centesimum invenias, qui ab omni commercio foeminarum abstineat. Legatus Alberti Bavariae Ducis in orat. habita in Concilio Tridentino inter caetera haec protulit. Clerus noster gulae libidinibusque indulget, ac quasi velit in contemtum DEI hominumque omni genere vitiorum se coopertum potiùs palam agnosci, quàm minima aliquâ in re emendatum animadverti, ut caetera Cleri vitia, quae cum populo habet communia, taceantur, at certè libido illa nimis libera atque notoria, propter quam is nunc potissimùm infamis habetur, à plebe irritatoque populo alienissima esse iudicatur. 2. Bellarminus lib. de Clericis cap. 21. ad argum. quod Coelibatus Clericorum (coactus in personis ad eum minùs idoneis) prodigiosas libidines pariat, mundum concubinis & Ecclesiam scandalis repleat, inter caetera sic respondet. Non admittimus tot (nota, tot) esse concubinarios & impuros inter Ecclesiasticos, quot haeretici dicunt, qui omnes alios ex se metientes, nullos putant esse castos. Certè plurimi sunt, qui quotidie celebrant & de quibus nulla mala suspicio auditur (nota, nulla suspicio auditur) 3. Nos coelibatum spontaneum in personis idoneis dono continentiae divinitùs instructis, non solùm non improbamus, sed etiam commendamus. Proinde non simpliciter eam dicimus esse impossibilem, aut minimè ab iis custodiri, qui eam profiteantur.

Διδασκαλίαι. 1. Christi passio & mors principaliter ac primeriò est meritum ac donum, secundariò & minus principaliter est exemplum, quo de peccatorum & affectuum mortificatione admonemur. Rom. 6. v. 2. & seqq. Col. 2. v. 12.cap. 3. v. 3. & 5.

2. Multis ergò nominibus Christi passio & mors sunt ὁρμητήρια ad peccati odium & sanctae vitae studium. Christus passus est pro nobis, i. e. pro peccatis nostris. Peccata nostra fuerunt Christo acerbissimae illius passionis & mortis causa. Aequum igitur est, ut odio habeamus peccata atque ab illis desistamus, cum tantos Christo attraxerint cruciatus. Christus passus est pro nobis, ut pro peccatis nostris satisfactione praestitâ Dei iram peccatis nostris debitam à nobis averteret, nosque ipsi reconciliaret. Conciliatâ Dei gratia datur Spiritus S. qui peccatum in nobis mortificat, ac peccato dominium adimit. Christus passus est pro nobis carne. Ergò & nos debemus pati in carne, i. e. carnem mortificare & à peccato desistere. Ut in Christo patiente caro fuit mortua; sic in nobis mortificari debent carnis vitia.

3. Omne quidem mortis genus potuisset esset typus mortificandae nostrae carnis, sed maximè quod crucifixione in Christo perfectum, typum illius spiritualis mortificationis exhibet pulcherrimum. Qui enim crucifigitur, eius membris potestas sese ad arbitrium movendi adimitur.Rom. 6. v. 10.Vetus noster homo simul crucifixus est.Gal. 2. v. 19.Cum Christo crucifixus sum cruciv. 20.Vivo autem iam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus.cap. 6. v. 14.Per Christum mundus mihi crucifixus est, & ego mundo. Bernhardus serm. 6. de peregrino mortuo & crucifixo. Non solùm mortuus mundo, sed & crucifixus, quod est ignominiosum genus mortis. Ego illi, pariter & ipse mihi. Omnia quae mundus amat, crux mihi sunt, delectatio carnis, honores, divitiae, vanae hominum laudes. Quae vero mundus crucem reputat, illis affixus sum, illis adhaereo, illa toto amplector affectu.

4. Neque vero passio & mors Christi tantùm ut exemplum spiritualis mortificationis proponitur, sed etiam ut eiusdem causa efficiens, quatenus mors & resurrectio Christi in renatis efficax est ad mortificationem carnis & novitatem vitae Rom. 6. v. 4. Mortificatio carnis proficiscitur ex virtute mortis Christi, quae in Baptismo nobis offertur, & per fidem confertur.

5. Tota hominis Christiani in his terris vita est spiritualis quaedam militiaIob. 7. v. 1. in qua contra carnis illecebras, Diaboli insidias & mundi decipulas est pugnandum, hanc ad rem animo forti & infracto instructos nos esse convenit.

6. Memoria passionis Christi cum vera in Christum crucifixum fide coniuncta est maximum robur & munimentum piorum contra tot insultus hostium. Hebr. 12. v. 3.Recogitate eum, qui talem sustinuit à peccatoribus adversus seipsum contradictionem, ut ne fatigemini animis vestris deficientes. In Graeco est ἀναλογίσασθε, seriò expendite & considerate analogiam sive proportionem, quae est inter contradictionem illam, quam Christus propter vos à peccatoribus sustinuit, atque eam, quam vos sustinetis, persecutionem.

7. Quod si namque Christi pro nobis passi beneficia ac meritum fide nobis applicamus, inde robur Spiritus consequimur, ut non solùm animo imperterrito crucem feramus, sed etiam carnem cum suis concupiscentiis mortificemus. Gal. 5. v. 27.Qui Christi sunt, crucifixerunt carnem cum suis passionibus & affectibus. Per haec opera, inquit Lutherus in comm. h. l. fides sit fortior, si corpus coërceatur, non fiat lascivum.

8. Signum & effectum mortificatae carnis est cessatio à peccatis, si non amplius cupiditatibus hominum, sed voluntati DEI vivitur. Sicut in Natura corruptio unius est generatio alterius, sic si vetus homo in nobis moritur, vivit novus. Rom. 6. v. 5. 6. &c.

9. Duae sunt sanctificationis nostrae partes. Fuga & odium peccati, ad quod humanae cupiditates nos impellunt: ac studium operis boni in lege divina à nobis requisiti. Ephes. 4. v. 22. & 23.Col. 3. v. 9.& 10.1. Petr. 3. v. 11.

10. Voluntas Dei in verbo patefacta est sanctae vitae regula, Rom. 12. v. 2. definit enim Petrus cessationem à peccato, quando homo divinae voluntati suam conformat, eo ipso innuens, nihil esse in vita rectum, sanctum, compositum ac Deo gratum, quod ab hac regula in diversum abit.

11. Omne tempus vitae perditur, quod non Dei servitio & voluntati eius adimplendae consecratur. August. in Manuali. Perdit quod vivit, quite Deum non diligit; qui curat vivere, non propter te Domine, nihil est & pro nihilo est, qui tibi vivere recusat, mortuus est, qui tibi non sapit, desipit.

12. Quando totum vitae tempus reliquum divinae voluntati conformandum esse praecipit Apostolus in studio pietatis & sanctitatis perseverandum esse docet. Gregorius in Ps. 32.Nihil est bonum, quod incipimus, nisi perseveranti illud fine compleamus. Bernh. de pass. Domini c. 14. Virtus boni operis perseverantia est. Huic soli redditur coronaiustitiae. Quid enim prodest esse bonum, esse sapientem, esse potentem, si non perseveraverit usque ad finem? Alphabeti Hebraici extrema litera est Thau. Haec Ezech. 9. v. 6. est signum liberationis & vitae. Omnem, super quem videritis Thau, non occidatis. Qui ab aeterna morte liberari cupit, vitamque consequi immortalem, fidem & pietatis studium ad vitae usque finem sectetur.

13. Acerrimus ad ambulandum in via Domini & benè currendum stimulus, in mentem sibi revocare, quod quis magnâ vitae parte extra viam aberraverit.

14. Nexus argumenti Apostolici est firmissimus. Ante conversionem securè peccatis indulsimus. Ergò post conversionem à peccatis desistere debemus. Contrariorum enim efficientium effecta sunt contraria. Tenebrae ignorantiae trahunt secum tenebras peccatorum; lux salutaris θεογνωσίας secum affert operalucis, Rom. 6. v. 19.Sicut exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiae & iniquitati ad iniquitatem: ita nunc exhibete membra vestra servire iustitiae in sanctificationem.c. 13. v. 11.Scientes tempus, quia horaiam est, nos de somno surgere.1. Cor. 6. v. 11.Et haec quidam fuistis, sed abluti estis &c.1. Thess. 5. v. 6.Omnes filii lucis estis & filii dieiv. 6.igitur non dormiamus, sicut coeteri.2. Petr. 2. v. 20.Sirefugientes &c.

15. Utile est prius vitae genus, quod ante conversionem sectati sumus, saepius in memoriam nobis revocare, ut magnitudo beneficii in conversione nobis praestiti magis appareat, ac pudor recordatione flagitiorum incussus ad eorum detestationem nos magis permoveat.

16. Tres sunt peccatorum actualium gradus, Primus peccatum aggredi; secundus in illo ambulare ac progredi; tertius in eo sedere, eique se totum tradere. Ps. 1. v. 1.Peccata impiorum sunt funesProv. 5. v. 22. quia iniquae cogitationi consensum; consensui opus; operi consuetudinem; consuetudini necessitatem; necessitati excusationem; excusationi defensionem, defensioni impoenitentiam; impoenitentiae desperationem adiiciunt.

17. Pii ambulant in via divinorum mandatorum: impii in via peccatorum; illi semper magis magisque ascendunt, hi semper magis magisque descendunt. Prov. 18. v. 3. iuxta vulg transl. Impiu cùm in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit.

18. Peccata, quae hoc loco Apostolus recenset, sunt suo genere mortalia, inde in catalogo eorum ponuntur, propter quae gentiles ex regno Dei excluduntur.

19. Etiam interna peccati desideria cum consensu voluntatis coniuncta licet in opus externum exire prohibeantur, ad vitam gentilium pertinent, & ex ipso Naturae lumine, damnabilia esse agnoscuntur. Cic. lib. 1. officiorum. Bene Pericles, cum haberet Collegam in Praetura Sophoclem Poëtam, hique de communi officio convenissent & casu puer formosus praeteriret, dixissetque Sophocles, ô puerum pulobrum? Pericles subiecit. At enim praetorem, Sophocles, decet, non solùm manus, sed etiam oculos continentes habere. Philemon Poetahominem bonum, quem Deus diligit, oportere, ait, alienum nihil aspicene, vel conoupiscere, non foeminam praestantem, non domum, non possessionem, non puerum aut ancillam, non equos aut boves, aut iumentorum aliquid, non filum acus.

20. Vitia gulae fomentum suppeditant libidinibus, inde Apostolus ἀσελγείας, οἰνοφλυγίας, κώμους ac πότους coniungit. c. Venter dist. 35. ex Hieronymo. Venter mero aestuans citò despumat in libidinem. distinct. 14. in princ. itidem ex Hieronymo. Venter & genitalia sibimetipsis vicina sunt, ut ex vicinitate membrorum confoederatio intelligatur vitiorum. Hinc Nabuzardan Princeps coquorum muros Ierusalem destruxisse legitur, quia venter, ubi multitudo coquorum deservit, aedificia virtutum ad solum redigit. Camerarius part. 1. Succisiv. cap. 94. Prudens antiquitas in persuasione fuit signum Virginis vitem aversari.

21. Idololatria est spirituale adulterium, quam proinde tàm non ferre potest Deus in homine, quàm maritus adulterium in uxore. Sap. 14. v. 27.ἡ τῶν ἀνωνύμων εἰδώλων θρησκεία παντὸς ἀρχὴ κακοῦ καὶ αιτία καὶ πέρας ἐστιν. Duplex vero est idololatriae species. Prior ex ratione cultus, cum verus Deus colitur non divinè h. e. non eo modo, quo se coli in verbo suo praecepit. Posterior ex obiecto, cum religiosè colitur id, quod non est verus Deus.

22. Qui in peccatorum coeno haerent, omnes eodem contaminatos esse iudicant & optant. Ecclesiastae. 10. v. 3.Etiamsi insipiens in via stultè ambulet, omnes stultos aestimat.

23. Qui unà currunt in vitiorum stadio, consequentur eadem impietatis suae supplicia. Esai. 5. v. 18.Vae qui trahitis iniquitatem in funibus vanitatis & quasi funibus plaustri peccatum. Qui unà currunt in virtutum stadio, consequentur eadem pietatis suae praemia. 1. Cor. 9. v. 24.Qui in stadio currunt, omnes quidem currunt, sed unus accipit prabeum, sic currite, ut comprehendatis.

24. Mundi utpote excoecati & immundi perversum est iudicium de sancta piorum conversatione, habent eos pro ludibrio ac deridiculo, imò pro περικαθάρμασι ac περιψήμασι.1. Cor. 4. v. 13. cùm tamen sint luminaria in medio nationis pravae & perversae lucentia. Matth. 5. v. 14.Phil. 2. v. 15.

25. Quando ergò videmus, mundum h. e. homines mundanos & carnalibus moribus nostris ad honestatem & gravitatem compositis offendi, non debemus propterea magnopere commoveri, vel etiam permoveri, ut eandem cum ipsis vitiorum semitam ingrediamur. Rom. 12. v. 2.Nolite conformari huic seculo, sed reformemini in novitate sensus vestri.

26. Mundani homines non solùm piorum conversatione offenduntur, sed etiam incipiunt eos odisse & calumniari; nec subsistunt in odio personae, sed progediuntur ad blasphemiam ipsius religionis, ac si illius prosessores vitam à communi humanitate abhorrentem sectari coguntur. Sed huic odio mundi opponamus favorem Dei, ac fatius esse ducamus sustinere in hac vita probra, quàm in iudicio ignis aeterni tormenta.

27. Ἐν τῇ ἀσωτία ἀνάχησις,In luxuria confusio.Prov. 23. v. 29.Cui ve? cui gemitus? cuirixae? cui querelae? cui sine causa vulnera? cuirubedo oculorum? nonne his, qui sectantur vinum & student calicibus epotandis? Ambros. de Elia & ieiunio cap. 16. Ebrietas est fomentum libidinis, incentivum insaniae, venenum insipientiae Per hanc hominesvocem amittunt, colore variantur, oculis ignescunt, ore anhelant, fremunt naribus, in furore ardescunt.

28. Iustum illud iudicium, quod Christus in consummationeseculi exercebit, ad omnes hostium insultus sustinendos, ac convitia ipsorum contemnenda nos animare potest ac debet. Ipse innocentiam nostram in lucem producet, ipse causam nostram asseret, ipse iustè damnabit eos, qui in hac vita nos iniustè actemerè damnant.

29. Iusto huic iudici rationem reddere, eius demque tribunalisese srstere cogeretur, velint, nolint, etiam impii, in quocunque sublimitatis gradu in hoc seculo fuerint constituti.

30. In hoc decretorio die & universali panegyri vivi & mortui adeoque omnes homines iudicabuntur. Actor. 10. vers. 42.2. Tim. 4. vers. 1. Maximus Taurinensis homil. in expos. Symb. Vivi iudicandi referuntur ac mortui, ut omnium hominum esse apud Deum cura credatur.

31. Meditatio huius iudicii excitet in nobis serium timorem Dei. Gregorius lib. 14. moral. cap. 30. Vitari terror iudicis non nisi ante iudicium potest, modò non cernitur, sed precibus placatur. Cum verò in illo tremendo examine sederit & videri potest & placariiam non potest, quia facta pravorum, quae diu sustinuit tacitus, simul omniareddet ir atus. August. in Soliloq. cap. 14. Magna nobis indita est necessitas iustè rectèque cuncta facimus ante oculos iudicis cuncta cernentis.

32. Quia ipse paratus est iudicare, nos simus parati iudicari Matth. 25. vers. 10.Et vos estote parati.Luc. 12. vers. 35.Sint lumbi vestri praecincti &c. Ephrem de beatit. animae cap. 3. Tanquam messis seculi finis ad metendum pervenit, & Angeli accincti & praeparati falces tenent manibus, Domini expectantes imperium. August. Epist. 3. Semper ante oculos versetur ultimus dies, & cum diluculo surrexerimus, non ad vesperam nos confidamus pervenire, & cum in lectulo membra nostra deposuerimus, de lucis non confidamus adventu.

## 4:2
THAT HE MAY LIVE THE REST OF HIS TIME IN THE FLESH NO LONGER FOR THE DESIRES OF MEN, BUT FOR THE WILL OF GOD.

Connection. 1. ἔκθεσις this is of the verse immediately preceding. For the Apostle shows how he who suffers in the flesh can and ought to desist from sin.

2. There are two parts of our renewal, the mortification of the flesh, and the vivification of the Spirit. He had dealt with the mortification of the flesh in the preceding verse; he deals with the vivification of the Spirit in this verse, when he commands that we conform our life henceforth to the will of God. By a like reason Paul also joins both parts of renewal, and teaches that the pattern of both is set forth in the death and resurrection of Christ, Rom. 6. v. 3. As many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death, v. 4. therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. v. 5. For if we have been united together in the likeness of His death, certainly we also shall be in the likeness of His resurrection, etc.

3. It is the duty of the reborn not only to mortify the flesh with its lusts, but also to renounce the world and its pleasures. Peter had dealt with the former in the preceding verse; in this verse he deals with the latter, when he commands: that they should no longer live for the desires of men, which Paul calls not to be conformed to this world Rom. 12. v. 2.

Disposition. The Apostle illustrates the holy conversation of the pious, which is the effect of spiritual mortification. 1. By the opposition between the desires of men and the will of God, and the norm of conversation: he commands that not the former, but the latter ought to be established. 2. By the determination of the duration, we mean that we ought to spend the whole remaining time of our life in holiness and justice conformable to the divine will.

Exposition of the text. Ἐις τὸ μηκέτι ἀνθρώπων ἐπιθυμίαις, ἀλλὰ θελήματι θεοῦ τὸ ἐπίλοιπον ἐν σαρκὶ βιῶσαι χρόνον. The Syrian arranges the text thus. That he may no longer live for the rest of the time in the flesh to the lusts of the sons of men, but to the will of God. Jerome in book 1 against Jovinian reads. That he may spend the remaining time in the flesh in the will of God. The Apostle speaks of him, who has suffered in the flesh, i.e., who has spiritually died and been crucified with Christ through the mortification of carnal lusts. He says that he suffers in the flesh to this end, that in the future he may no longer live according to the desires of men, but according to the will of God, which is the vivification of the Spirit consequent to spiritual mortification. When our old man dies, the new one arises; when the flesh is mortified, the Spirit lives.

By τὰς ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπων he understands depraved lusts, depraved desires, which men not yet reborn by the Holy Spirit are accustomed to follow, which 1. Cor. 3. v. 3. calls walking according to man. To these he opposes τὸ θέλημα θεοῦ the holy will of God revealed in the law, and he commands that we establish as the norm of our life, not the desires of our flesh, nor the will of the world or of carnal men, but the will of God, to whom we ought to surrender ourselves entirely, if we wish to approve our life and morals to Him. A parallel passage exists Rom. 12. v. 2. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is the good and acceptable and perfect will of God. In the word σαρκὸς ἀντανάκλασις. occurs again. For it signifies not the human Nature of Christ, devoid of every stain, as it is taken in the former part of the preceding verse; nor the viciousness of Nature, which we draw from Adam and the remnants of which remain in the reborn even after regeneration, as it is taken in the latter part of the preceding verse, but the condition of this present and mortal life, so that the sense may be: All the time that is remaining to you in this temporal life, you ought to spend in fulfilling the divine will. Hence the Syrian rendered it, how much time he is in the body, i.e., as long as the soul journeys in the dwelling of the body in this temporal life. Examples of this meaning exist 2. Corinth. 10. v. 3. Walking in the flesh we do not war according to the flesh. Galat. 2. v. 20. That I now live in in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of GodPhil. 1. v. 22.to live in the flesh is fruit for me of the work.vers. 24.to remain in the flesh is more necessary for me for your sake.Hebr. 5. v. 7.Christ in the days of his flesh offered up prayers and supplications.

Latin:

UT IAM NON DESIDERIIS HOMINUM, SED VOLUNTATI DEI QUOD RELIQUUM EST IN CARNE VIVAT TEMPORIS.

Connexio. 1. ἔκθεσις hae est versiculi proximè praecedentis. Ostendit enim Apostolus, quomodo is, qui patitur in carne, à peccato desistere possit ac debeat.

2. Duae sunt renovationis nostrae partes, mortificatio carnis, & vivificatio Spiritus. De mortificatione carnis egerat vers. praecedente, de vivificatione Spiritus agit in hoc versiculo, quando voluntati Dei vitam inposterum conformare praecipit. Pari ratione etiam Paulus utramque renovationis partem coniungit, & utriusque exemplar in Christi morte & resurrectione propositum esse docet, Rom. 6. v. 3.Quicunque baptizati sumus in Christum Iesum, in mortem ipsius baptizati fumusv. 4.consepulti enim sumus cum illo per Baptismum in mortem, ut quomodo Christus resurrexit à mortuis per gloriam Patris, ita & nos in novitate vitae ambulemus.v. 5.Si enim complantati facti sumus similitudini mortis eius, simul & resurrectionis erimus &c.

3. Renatorum est, non solùm carnem cum concupiscentiis suis mortificare, sed etiam mundo & eius voluptatibus renunciare. De priore egerat Petrus versu praecedente, in hoc vers. agit de posteriore, quando praecipit; ut non amplius vivant hominum desideriis, quod Paulus vocat non configurari mundoRom. 12. v. 2.

Dispositio. Sanctam piorum conversationem quae spiritualis mortificationis effectus, illustrat Apostolus. 1. oppositione inter desideria hominum & voluntatem Dei, ac normam conversationis: non illa, sed hanc debere statui praecipit. 2. determinatione durationis, quòd totum vitae nostrae tempus reliquum in sanctitate & iustitia voluntati divinae conformi transigere debeamus.

Textus expositio. Ἐις τὸ μηκέτι ἀνθρώπων ἐπιθυμίαις, ἀλλὰ θελήματι θεοῦ τὸ ἐπίλοιπον ἐν σαρκὶ βιῶσαι χρόνον. Syrus textum sic ordinat. Ut non deinceps concupiscentiis filiorum hominis vivat, quanto tempore est in corpore, sed voluntati Dei. Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovinian. legit. In Dei voluntate reliquum in carne tempus exigat. Loquitur Apostolus de eo, qui passus est in carne, i. e. qui spiritualiter cum Christo mortuus & crucifixus per concupiscentiarúm carnalium mortificationem. Illum dicit eo fine pati in carne, ut in posterum non amplius vivat iuxta hominum desideria, sed iuxta Dei voluntatem, qui consequens spiritualis mortificationis est vivificatio Spiritus. Quando vetus noster homo moritur, exurgit novus; quando caro mortificatur, vivit Spiritus.

Per τὰς ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπων intelligit pravas concupiscentias, prava desideria, quae homines nondum per Spiritum S. renati sectari solent, quod 1. Cor. 3. v. 3. vocat secudùm hominem ambulare. Illis opponit τὸ θέλημα θεοῦ sanctam Dei voluntatem in lege patefactam, ac praecipit, ut normam vitae nostrae statuamus, non carnis nostrae desideria, nec mundi sive carnalium hominum voluntatem, sed Dei voluntatem, qui nos totos mancipare debeamus, si vitam & mores ipsi probare velimus. Locus parallelus extat Rom. 12. v. 2.Nolite conformari huic seculo, sed reformemini renovatione mentis vestrae, ut probetis, quae sit voluntas ac Dei bona & beneplacens & perfecta. In voceσαρκὸς denuò occurrit ἀντανάκλασις. Significat enim non humanam Christi Naturam, omnis labis expertem, prout accipitur in priore vers. praeced. parte; nec vitiositatem Naturae, quam ex Adamo trahimus & cuius reliquiae etiam post regenerationem in renatis supersunt, prout accipitur, in posteriore vers. praeced. parte, sed praesentis & mortalis huius vitae conditionem, ut sit sensus. Omne tempus, quod in hac vita temporali vobis reliquum, divinae voluntati implendae debetis impendere. Inde Syrus reddidit, quanto tempore est in corpore, i. e. quamdiu anima in corporis domicilio in hac vita temporali peregrinatur. Exempla huius significationis extant 2. Corinth. 10. v. 3.In carne ambulantes non secundùm carnem militamus.Galat. 2. v. 20.Quod nunc vivo in carne, in fide vivo filio DeiPhil. 1. v. 22.vivere in carne mihi fructus operis.vers. 24.permanere in carne mihi magis necessarium propter vos.Hebr. 5. v. 7.Christus in diebus carnis suae preces & supplicationes obtulit.

## 4:3
FOR THE TIME PAST IS SUFFICIENT TO HAVE CONSUMMATED THE WILL OF THE GENTILES FOR THOSE WHO HAVE WALKED IN LASCIVIOUSNESS, LUSTS, EXCESS OF WINE, REVELINGS, BANQUETINGS, AND UNLAWFUL IDOLATRIES.

Connection. 1. He had said in the preceding verse that the remainder in the flesh, i.e., the time of life that still remains, is not to be spent according to the desires of men, but according to the will of God; he declares that by the antithesis of the former life spent before conversion to Christ according to the will of the Gentiles.

2. Moreover, in this opposition is contained an argument of exhortation, taken from the circumstance of time. You have already consecrated a good part of your life to the world and the flesh, nay, even to the Devil himself; it is fair that you should consecrate the remaining part of your life to God, by conforming it solely according to His will.

3. It can also be said that the argument is drawn from the quality of the persons. Before your conversion to Christ, when you were still moving in the thick darkness of ignorance by the perpetration of the most grievous sins, you conformed yourselves to the will of the Gentiles; but now, illuminated by the saving knowledge of God, it is fitting to change your life and morals; this time demands other morals. You have been changed through renewal, therefore you also ought to change your life. The Gentiles are carried by a blind impulse, where wicked lust leads them, but you have renounced gentilism and have given your names to Christ. Therefore, you ought not to conform the remainder of your life to the will of the Gentiles.

4. John Huss arranges the Apostolic text thus. From the mortification of the flesh we obtain four utilities, which the Apostle touches upon in the present. First, we obtain the conformation of Christ our head, so that just as He suffered for us, so also we may suffer for Him. As to this, the Apostle says. Christ therefore having suffered in the flesh, do you also be armed with the same thought. Secondly, we obtain the expulsion of sins, concerning which the Apostle says: He who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sins. Thirdly, we obtain the fulfillment of the divine will, which is the will of God, our sanctification, etc.; concerning this the Apostle says, that he no longer should live the rest of his time in the flesh for the desires of men, but for the will of God. Fourthly, we obtain the reformation of our mind, so that if in the past we conformed ourselves to this world by living according to the desires of the flesh, now for the future we ought to conform ourselves to God. Regarding this, the Apostle says, for the time past is sufficient, etc.

Disposition. The Apostle first describes in general the life led before conversion to Christ, namely, that they confirmed it to the Gentiles. Secondly, by an enumeration of some vices in particular ἐξηγητικῶς he declares what that life of the Gentiles was like.

Exposition of the text. Ἀρκετὸς γὰρ ἡμῖν ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος τοῦ βίου τὸ θέλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατεργάσεσθαι. The Vulgate rendered it: For the time past is sufficient to have fulfilled the will of the Gentiles. But the Greek properly has it thus: For it is sufficient for us, the time past of life to have worked the will of the Gentiles. Erasmus, looking to the sense, translates it thus: For it is enough for us that in the past time of life we have committed the will of the Gentiles. The Syriac in this manner: For that time which has passed is sufficient, in which you worked the will of the Gentiles. Augustine, Epist. 99 to Evodius, cites the passage with these words: For the time past is sufficient to have fulfilled the will of men.

The pronoun ἡμῖν the Vulgate, as also Augustine, omits, without a doubt because it seemed harsh for Peter to count himself through ἀνακοίνωσιν among those who once perpetrated such grave crimes of this kind. Some respond that it is an enallage of persons, by which the pronoun of the first person is placed for the pronoun of the second person, such as also occurs in Hebr. 2. v. 3. It is answered more simply that the reading of certain Codices, and specifically the Royal one, which has ὑμῖν in the second person, is to be preferred. For 1. in the following verse 4, the pronoun of the second person μὴ συντρεχόντων ὑμῶν. is likewise held; 2. in v. 1. preceding, the Apostle likewise speaks in the second person, καὶ ὑμεῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἔννοιαν ὁπλίσασθε. 3. The Syriac also in this place rendered it in the second person: The time which has passed is sufficient, in which you worked the will of the Gentiles. 4. Cajetan indeed he says, that Peter numbers himself with others, although he was not such, so that the admonition might be more easily admitted: and Cornelius à Lapide on this passage annotates thus. Out of modesty and so that the rebuke may be milder, Peter numbers himself with the Gentiles, when he himself was not a Gentile, much less did he live like a Gentile. It would be a preposterous humility if Peter had wished to number himself with the assembly of those who, having followed the will of the Gentiles, walked in luxuries. The reason is far different when Isaiah ch. 64. v. 6. and Daniel c. 9. v. 5. confess sins before God in their own name and in the name of the whole people, and pray for their remission. In that which he says, it is enough, there is indeed an asteismus or litotes, by which the Apostle mitigates the harshness of the reproach, in the way that Christ says to the disciples, indulging in sleep at the time of the passion, it is enough. Mark 14. verse 41. and the Prophet Ezekiel by the command of God says to his hearers. Let all your abominations suffice you, O house of Israel ch. 44. v. 6. Let it suffice you, Princes of Israel, cease to drive out my people ch. 45. v. 9. By τὸ θέλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν he understands the same thing which in the preceding verse he understood by ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπων, namely the lust for sinning and depraved concupiscences, which men alienated from God follow, of which kind the Gentiles were. For those who are nothing else than men, who are not regenerated by the Holy Spirit, they delight in sins and wallow securely in the mire of flagitious acts. The little word ἐθνῶν the Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] of the profane from the root [consult facsimile image] he polluted, he profaned, because the Gentiles were held by the people of God as polluted and impure. Matthew 6. v. 7. ch. 10. v. 5. ch. 18. v. 7. etc.

Πεπορευμένους The Vulgate rendered, those who walked. In the Greek it is, going, proceeding, walking, as Augustine cites in Epistle 99. for it is the fourth case, which is construed with the preceding verb κατεργάσεσθαι, and is resolved into a verb of the second person, if we read ὑμῖν. There is, however, in this verb a customary metaphor, by which the course of human life is described through a journey or travel, and πορέυεσθαι are said to be in sins, who pass their life in sins. Thus they are called ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ πορέυεσθαι 2. Peter 2. verse 10. and κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιθυμίας πορέυεσθαι 2. Peter 3. verse 3. Jude verse 16. and 18.

who securely indulge in the concupiscences of their own flesh, to whom are opposed πορευόμενοι ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασι τοῦ θεοῦ Luke 1. v. 6. who establish not the desires of the flesh, but the will of God and the divine law as the norm of their actions, as the Apostle describes them in V. preceding. The interlinear gloss seeks emphasis in the word walking, that the Gentiles were stable in one vice, but walked from vice to vice. The Syriac omitted this word.

Ἐν ἀσελγίαις the Vulgate rendered, in luxuries. The use of this word is frequent in the New Testament Mark 7. vers. 22.Rom. 13. vers. 13.2. Corinth. 12. vers. 21.Galat. 5. vers. 19.Ephes. 4. vers. 19.2. Peter 2. vers. 7. & 18.Jude vers. 4. where it is referred to among the works of the flesh, which dominate in unregenerate men. Wisdom 14. vers. 26. it is joined with μοιχεία ἀσελγὴς which is petulant, forward. Also lascivious, who petulantly indulges in lusts. Lucian, ἀσελγέστεροι τῶν ὄνων more lascivious than asses: for this animal is most lustful. Budaeus says τὸ ἀσελγεὶ is placed for obscenity and the flagitious habit of debaucheries. They wish it to be denominated τὸν ἀσελγέα from a certain city Selge, and they say that here it is στερητικὸν because all the inhabitants of that city were upright and modest, while others on the contrary τὸ α say it is ἐπιτατικὸν saying, that all those citizens were petulant, lascivious, and wicked. ἀσέλγειαν Philo takes it for lasciviousness and forward lust, lib. 1. on the life of Moses, writing διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀσελγείας καὶ ἀκολασίας through an obscene woman, forward lust, petulance. It is therefore more correctly rendered by lasciviousness and forwardness, or by forward lasciviousness than by luxury; and this name embraces every kind of obscenity and lust, when interior lust is betrayed by forward words and gestures. Luther rendered it, in Unzucht. The Syriac expresses it by the Greek name ἀσωτίας, which our Apostle uses in the following verse, as does Paul Ephes. 5. vers. 18.Tit. 1. vers. 6. It is however ἀσωτία luxury or riot, just as it is said of the prodigal son Luke 15. vers. 13. that he lived ἀσώτως. It is called ἄσωτος from ἀστερητικῷ & σώξειν, to declare him, who saves nothing for himself, whom we call profuse and prodigal. In the Chaldean paraphrase Prov. 23. v. 21. אסיט is ἄσωτος glutton, reveller, as Münster rendered it in the Chaldean and Rabbinic Lexicon. Herodian lib. 1. ἀσωτίας καὶ κραιπάλας, Athenaeus lib. 11. τὰς μέθας καὶ τὰς ἀσωτίας.

joins. Arist. lib. 4. Ethic. cap. 1. ἄσωτος is ἀκρατὴς καὶ εἰς ἀκολασίαν δαπανηρὸς incontinent and spending on luxury, καὶ δι' αὐτὸν ἀπολλύμενος and destroying himself by himself. Clem. Alex lib. 2. paedag. cap. 1. ἀσώτους says it is said as if ἀσώστους alien from salvation, who destroy body, soul, and faculties.

Ἐπιθυμίαις. He understands depraved concupiscences, depraved desires, from which the external works of the flesh proceed. These v. 2. he called in the preceding ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπων concupiscences of men namely of the depraved, not yet reborn, who are nothing else than men. Lyranus. Just as he denotes external acts of intemperance regarding Venus through luxuries: so he denotes internal acts, when the faculty for external ones is lacking, through concupiscences. The Syrian omitted it in the version.

Ἐν οἰνοφλυγίαις. The Vulgate rendered vinolentiis, for which in some Codices it is read viciously, violentiis, οἰνόφλυξ is said, who bubbles with wine, who belches wine i. e. wine-bibbing, drunken, greedy for wine, thence οἰνοφλυγία vinolentia, immoderate desire for wine, Philo lib. 1. de vita Mosis. οἰνοφλυγίαι καὶ ὀψοφαγίαι καὶ λαγνείαι καὶ ἄλλαι ἀπλήρωτοι ἐπιθυμίαι. Oecumenius explains τὰς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶνον ἀκρατεῖς ὁρμὰς. The LXX use the word οἰνοφλυγεῖν for he drank, he gorged himself with wine, or rather he is wine-bibbing and drunken, he delights in the disease of drunkenness Deut. 21. v. 20. Esai. 56. v. 12. It is signified therefore by the name οἰνοφλυγίας a disease of the mind given to wine. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] in drunkenness, in which way also August. Epist. 99. and Luther in the German version. In Trunctenheit. סבא

Ἐν κώμοις. Vulg. as also August. most correctly in comessationibus. Κῶμος is a convivial drinking-bout, from which someone finally falls into κῶμα into a deep sleep, says Eustathius. It is also called κῶμος a luxurious banquet, after supper outside or after the time of the midday meal, not instituted for honest recreation, but for luxury, pleasure and lasciviousness, from which the name Comessationis is derived among the Latins, although by the word κῶμος something more is signified than by the word comessatio, see every kind of amorous lasciviousness, levity and wantonness, which appears in men heating up with wine: for from wine they arise to lascivious dances; to obscene songs, wanderings through the streets and crossroads, and even to those absurd actions which a drunken crowd is accustomed to institute in Comedies. For it is gathered from Aristophanes' Plutus and Xenophon's Symposium, that in these κώμοις they were once accustomed to carry garlands, sometimes also torches, but sometimes also αὐλητρίδας and ὀρχηστρίδας to lead with them. κῶμος is also called a feast, which was performed with great hilarity by revelers in honor of Bacchus, according to Dionysius in his description of the world, and the god presiding over such revelries or the wantonness and impudence of reveling men, according to Philostratus. Paul Rom. 13. vers. 13. Gal. 5. v. 21. κώμους & μέθας, just as Peter in this place κώμους καὶ πότους joins them, from which it is gathered that by the name κώμου is understood an inordinate greed for devouring, just as Luther also rendered it. Fresseren. Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, Epistle 456, κῶμον says it is the song of the flute, which with more generous wine stimulates to pleasure and lust and changes the banquet into a foul and obscene theater, and through certain cymbals and instruments adapted for deceits, soothes and beguiles the guests. Suidas κῶμον says it is μέθην. Sap. 14. v. 23. ἐμμανεῖς κώμους ἄγειν the Gentiles are called, when they institute luxurious banquets and insane revelries. 2. Maccab. 6. vers. 4. ἀσωτία & κῶμοι are joined. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] in stench, because luxurious banquets draw vomit and stenches with them. Marc. 7. v. 22. and Galat. 5. v. 19. the Syrian renders the Greek ἀσέλγεια. with this word.

Ἐν πότοις Vulg. in drinking bouts. Aug. hom. 20. among 50. in drinking. By this name, when joined with κώμοις, are denoted luxurious drinking parties, in which one drinks to a number and competes in drinking Esai. 5. v. 11. and 22. an inexhaustible gluttony for drinking and an insane zeal for continuing the drink. Prov. 23. v. 30. ἰχνέυοντες ποῦ πότοι γίνονται anxiously investigating where drinking parties are being instituted. Vulg. who are eager for draining cups. Luth. Die da kommen auszusauffen/was eingeschencket ist. In Lucian φίλος πό των καὶ ἀφροδισίων is said, who is delighted by wine and Venus. The Syrian rendered [consult facsimile image] which signifies a banquet, to which music is applied from the root [consult facsimile image] he sang.

Moreover, it is a synecdochical expression, since from one part the whole luxury of banquets is understood, in which, besides exquisite foods, music and every kind of delight is present. Rom. 13. vers. 13.Galat. 5. vers. 21. The Syriac interpreter expresses the Greek κώμους, with this word, whence also Tremellius in this place translates revelries. Luth. Sàufferen. Lyranus, so that he may distinguish it from οἰνοφλυγίαις, takes it as concerning inebriating drinking bouts without wine. But it is more elegant to take οἰνοφλυγίας concerning a vicious habit and affection, and πότους concerning the act of drinking.

Καὶ ἐν ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαις. Vulg. illicit idol worships. But the Greek is ἐμφατικώτερον, nefarious idol worships, by which the honor owed to GOD is transferred to creatures and fictitious Divinities, which sin is most severely prohibited in the first commandment of the decalogue. The Syriac rendered in the worship or service [consult facsimile image] of Demons, so called from devastation, because the gods of the nations are Demons Psalm. 96. vers. 5. August. in the same place in illicit idol servitudes, homil. 20 among 50 nefarious idol servitudes. Luth. in greulichen Abgo tterenen. Thus, therefore, the Apostle recalls to the minds of those converted to CHRIST the horrendous sins in which they lived before their conversion in gentilism, and from that he draws an argument for his exhortation to the pursuit of a holy life. Parallel passages are Roman. 13. vers. 12. The night has passed, and the day has drawn near; let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light. vers. 13. As in the day let us walk honestly, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in beds and impurities, not in contention and emulation. Ephes. 2. vers. 11. Be mindful that you were once Gentiles in the flesh, etc. cap. 4. vers. 17. This I say and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk as the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their sense vers. 18. having their intellect darkened by darkness vers. 19. who ἀπηλγηκότες have delivered themselves to impurity unto the operation of all uncleanness.

Latin:

SUFFICIT ENIM PRAETERITUM TEMPUS AD VOLUNTATEM GENTIUM CONSUMMANDAM HIS, QUI AMBULAVERUNT IN LUXURIIS, DESIDERIIS, VINOLENTIIS, COMESSATIONIBUS, POTATIONIBUS & ILLICITIS IDOLORUM CULTIBUS.

Connexio. 1. Dixerat in V. praeced. quod reliquum in carne, i. e. quod vitae tempus adhuc superest, non iuxta hominum desideria, sed iuxta Dei voluntatem transigendum esse, illud declarat per antithesin vitae prioris ante conversionem ad Christum iuxta gentium voluntatem transactae.

2. Continetur autem in hac oppositione argumentum exhortationis, à temporis circumstantia sumtum. Iamdum bonam vitae partem mundo & carni, imò ipsi Diabolo consecrastis, aequum est, ut residuam vitae partem Deo consecretis, iuxta ipsius voluntatem eam unicè conformando.

3. Potest etiam dici argumentum esse ductum à qualitate personarum. Ante vestram ad Christum conversionem, cum adhuc versaremini, in crassis ignorantiae tenebris perpetratione gravissimorum peccatorum voluntati gentium vos conformastis, nunc verò salutari Dei cognitione illustratis, vitam, & mores mutare convenit; hoc tempus alios mores postulat. Immutati estis per renovationem, proinde etiam vitam debetis mutare. Gentes coeco impetu feruntur, quò prava libido eas ducit, vos autem gentilismo renunciastis, & Christo nomina dedistis. Ergò non debetis, quod vitae reliquum, ad gentium voluntatem conformare.

4. Iohannes Huss textum Apostolicum sic ordinat. Ex carnis mortificatione quatuor utilitates consequimur, quas Apostolus tangit in praesenti. Primò consequimur, Christi capitis nostri conformationem, ut sicut ipse passus est pro nobis, ita & nos pro ipso patiamur. Quantum ad hoc dicit Apostolus. Christo igitur passo in carne & vos eâdem cogitatione armamini. Secundò consequimur peccatorum expulsionem, de qua dicit Apostolus. Qui passus est in carne, desiit à peccatis. Tertiò consequimur divine voluntatis impletionem, quae voluntas Dei est nostra sanctificatio &c. de hac dicit Apostolus, ut iam non hominum desideriis, sed voluntati Dei quod reliquum est in carne vivat temporis. Quartò consequimur nostrae mentis reformationem, ut si in praeterito nos conformavimus huic seculo vivendo secundùm desideria carnis, iam ad futurum debemus nos conformare Deo. Quantum ad hoc, dicit Apostolus, sufficit enim praeteritum tempus &c.

Dispositio. Apostolus primò in genere describit vitam ante conversionem ad Christum actam, videlicet quod gentilibus eam confirmaverint. Secundò enumeratione aliquot vitiorum in specie ἐξηγητικῶς declarat, qualis fuerit illa gentilium vita.

Expositio textus. Ἀρκετὸς γὰρ ἡμῖν ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος τοῦ βίου τὸ θέλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατεργάσεσθαι. Vulg. reddidit. Sufficit enim praeteritum tempus ad voluntatem gentium consummandam. Sed Graeca propriè sic habent. Sufficit enim nobis, praeteritum tempus vitae voluntatem gentium operatos fuisse. Erasmus sensum respiciens sic vertit. Sat enim est nobis, quod ante acto vitae tempore voluntatem gentium patraverimus. Syrus hoc modo. Sufficit enim tempus illud, quod praeteriit, in quo operati estis voluntatem gentium. Augustinus Epist. 99. ad Evodium locum his verbis adducit. Sufficit enim praeteritum tempus ad voluntatem hominum consummatum.

Pronomen ἡμῖν vulgata, uti etiam Augustinus, praetermittunt, dubio procul, quia durum fuit visum, Petrum per ἀνακοίνωσιν sese annumerare illis, qui gravissima eiusmodi scelera olim perpetrarunt. Quidam respondent, esse enallagen personarum, quâ pronomen primae personae positum sit pro pronomine secundae personae, qualis etiam occurratHebr. 2. v. 3. Simpliciùs respondetur praeferendam esse illam quorundam Codicum ac nominatim Regii Iectionem, quae habet ὑμῖν in secunda persona. Nam 1. in V. subsequente 4. habetur itidem pronomen secundae personae μὴ συντρεχόντων ὑμῶν. 2. in v. 1. praeced. itidem loquitur Apostolus in secunda persona, καὶ ὑμεῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἔννοιαν ὁπλίσασθε. 3. Syrus etiam hoc loco reddidit in secunda persona. Sufficit tempus, quod prateriit, in quo operati estis voluntatem gentium. 4. Caietanus quidem dicit, Petrum se aliis annumerare, quamvis talis non fuerit, ut admonitio faciliùs admittatur: ac Cornelius à Lapide ad h. l. sic annotat. Ex modestia & ut lenior sit increpatio, Petrus se gentibus annumerat, cùm ipse gentilis non fuerit, multò minus gentiliter vixerit. Praepostera foret humilitas, si Petrus sese annumerare voluisset horum coetui, qui gentium voluntatem secuti in luxuriis ambularunt. Longè dispar ratio est, quando Esaias cap. 64. v. 6. & Daniel c. 9. v. 5. & suo & totius populi nomine peccata coram Deo confitentur, eorumque remissionem orant. In eo quod ait, sufficit, est quidem asteismus sive liptotes, quâ mitigat Apostolus exprobrationis asperitatem, quo fere modo Christus ad discipulos, tempore passionis somno indulgentes, dicit, sufficit.Marc. 14. vers. 41. ac Propheta Ezechiel ex mandato Dei auditoribus suis dicit. Sufficiant vobis omnes abominationes vestrae ô domus Israelcap. 44. v. 6.Sufficiat vobis, Principes Israel, desinite exturbare populum meumcap. 45. v. 9. Per τὸ θέλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν idem intelligit, quod in vers. praeced. per ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπων, videlicet peccandi libidinem & pravas concupiscentias, quas sectantur homines à Deo alieni, cuiusmodi erant gentiles. Qui enim nihil aliud sunt quàm homines, qui non sunt per Spiritum Sanctum regeniti, illi delectantur peccatis & in coeno flagitiorum sese securè volutant. Voculam ἐθνῶν Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]profanorum à rad. [consult facsimile image]polluit, profanavit, quia gentiles à populo Dei pro pollutis & impuris habebantur.Matth. 6. v. 7.cap. 10. v. 5.cap. 18. v. 7. &c.

Πεπορευμένους Vulgata reddidit, his qui ambulaverunt. In Graeco est, euntes, incedentes, ambulantes, ut citat Augustinus Epist. 99. est enim casus quarti, qui construitur cum praecedente verbo κατεργάσεσθαι, ac resolvitur in verbum secundae personae, si legamus ὑμῖν. Est autem in hoc verbo metaphora usitata, quâ vitae humanae cursus per profectionem sive iter describitur, ac πορέυεσθαι in peccatis dicuntur, qui vitam in peccatis transigunt. Sic dicuntur ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ πορέυεσθαι2. Petr. 2. vers. 10. & κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιθυμίας πορέυεσθαι2. Petr. 3. vers. 3.Iudae vers. 16. & 18.

qui carnis suae concupiscentiis securè indulgent, quibus opponuntur, πορευόμενοι ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασι τοῦ θεοῦLuc 1. v. 6. qui normam suarum actionum non carnis desideria, sed Dei voluntatem & legem divinam statuunt, ut in V. praeced. Apostolus eos describit; Glossa interlinearis in verbo ambulandi emphasin quaerit, quod gentiles fuerint in uno vitio stabiles, sed de vitio in vitium ambulaverint. Syrus hanc vocem praetermisit.

Ἐν ἀσελγίαις Vulgata reddidit, in luxuriis. Frequens est huius vocis usus in Nov. Testam. Marc. 7. vers. 22.Rom. 13. vers. 13.2. Corinth. 12. vers. 21.Galat. 5. vers. 19.Ephes. 4. vers. 19.2. Petr. 2. vers. 7. & 18.Iudae vers. 4. ubi refertur inter opera carnis, quae in hominibus non renatis dominantur. Sap. 14. vers. 26. coniungitur cum μοιχεία ἀσελγὴς est petulans, protervus. Item lascivus, qui petulanter indulget libidinibus. Lucianus, ἀσελγέστεροι τῶν ὄνωνasinis lasciviores: est enim hoc animal libidinosissimum. Budaeus τὸ ἀσελγεὶ dicit poni pro obscoenitate & stuprorum flagitiosa consuetudine. Denominatum voluntτὸν ἀσελγέαab urbe quadam Selge, aiuntque a hîc esseστερητικὸνquod omnes eius urbis incolae probi & modesti essent, aliis contraτὸ α esse ἐπιτατικὸνdicentibus, omnesque illos cives fuisse petulantes, lascivos atque improbos.ἀσέλγειαν pro lascivia & proterva libidine accipit Philo lib. 1. de vita Mosis, scribens διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀσελγείας καὶ ἀκολασίας per mulierem obscoenam libidinem protervam petulantiam. Rectiùs ergò redditur per lasciviam ac proterviam, vel per protervam lasciviam quàm per luxuriam; & complectitur hoc nomen omne genus obscoenitatis & libidinis, quando procacibus verbis & gestibus interior libido proditur. Lutherus reddidit, in Unzucht. Syrus exprimit per Graecum nomen ἀσωτίας, quo in seq. vers. Apostolus noster utitur, ut & Paulus Ephes. 5. vers. 18.Tit. 1. vers. 6. Est autem ἀσωτίαluxus vel luxuria, sicut de filio prodigo dicitur Luc. 15. vers. 13. quòd vixerit ἀσώτως. Dicitur autem ἄσωτος ab ἀστερητικῷ & σώξειν, ut eam declaret, qui nihil sibi servet, quem profusum ac prodigum vocamus. In Chald. paraph. Prov. 23. v. 21.אסיט est ἄσωτοςlurco, comessator, ut Münsterus in Lexico Chaldaico & Rabinico reddidit. Herodianus lib. 1. ἀσωτίας καὶ κραιπάλας, Athenus lib. 11. τὰς μέθας καὶ τὰς ἀσωτίας.

coniungit. Arist. lib. 4. Ethic. cap. 1. ἄσωτος est ἀκρατὴς καὶ εἰς ἀκολασίαν δαπανηρὸς incontinens & in luxum expendens, καὶ δι' αὐτὸν ἀπολλύμενος & per se ipsum se perdens. Clem. Alex lib. 2. paedag. cap. 1. ἀσώτους ait dici quasi ἀσώστουςà salute alienos, qui corpus, animam, facultates perdunt.

Ἐπιθυμίαις. Intelligit pravas concupiscentias, desideria prava, ex quibus opera carnis externa prodeunt. Eas v. 2. praeced. vocavit ἐπιθυμίας ἀνθρώπωνconcupiscentias hominum scil. pravorum, nondum renatorum, qui nihil aliud sunt quàm homines. Lyranus. Sicut externos actus intemperantiae circa Veneres denotat per luxurias: ita internos actus, quando facultas externorum deest, denotat per concupiscentias. Syrus in versione praetermisit.

Ἐν οἰνοφλυγίαις. Vulgata reddidit vinolentiis, pro quo in quibusdam Codd. vitiosè legitur, violentiis,οἰνόφλυξ dicitur, qui vino bullit, qui vinum eructat i. e. vinosus, ebriosus, vini avidus, inde οἰνοφλυγίαvinolentia, immodicae vini cupiditas, Philo lib. 1. de vita Mosis. οἰνοφλυγίαι καὶ ὀψοφαγίαι καὶ λαγνείαι καὶ ἄλλαι ἀπλήρωτοι ἐπιθυμίαι. Oecumenius explicat τὰς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶνον ἀκρατεῖς ὁρμὰς. LXX. verbo οἰνοφλυγεῖν utuntur pro סבאpotavit, vino se ingurgitavit, vel potius vinosus & ebriosus est, morbo ebrietatis delectaturDeut. 21. v. 20.Esai. 56. v. 12. Significatur ergò οἰνοφλυγίας nomine morbus animi vino dediti. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]in ebrietate, quo modo etiam August. Epist. 99. & Lutherus in versione Germanica. In Trunctenheit.

Ἐν κώμοις. Vulg. ut & August. rectissimè in comessationibus.Κῶμοςest compotatio convivalis, ex qua aliquis tandem incidit inκῶμαin profundum somnum, inquit Eustathius. Dicitur etiam κῶμοςconvivium luxuriosum, post coenam extra vel post tempus prandii, non ad honestam recreationem, sed ad luxum, voluptatem & lasciviam institutum, ex quo nomen Comessationis apud Latinos deductum, quamvis voce κῶμος aliquid ampliùs significetur, quàm voce comessatio, vid. omne amatoriae lasciviae levitatis ac proterviae genus, quod apparet in hominibus vino incalescentibus: à vino enim exurgunt ad lascivas saltationes; ad obscoenas cantationes, discursationes per plateas & compita, adeòque ad absurdas illas actiones, quas ebria turba in Comaediis instituere solet. Colligitur enim ex Aristoph. Plutone & Sympos. Xenophontis, in his κώμοιςgestare olim solitos fuisse coronas, interdum & faces, nonnunquam vero &αὐλητρίδας ac ὀρχηστρίδαςsecum ducere. Dicitur etiam κῶμος festum, quod magna hilaritate à comessabundis in honorem Bacchî peragebatur, apud Dionys. de situ orbis, ac Deus praeses huiusmodi comessationum seu lasciviae proterviaeque comessabundorum hominum, apud Philostratum. Paulus Rom. 13. vers. 13.Gal. 5. v. 21.κώμους & μέθας, sicut hoc loco Petrus κώμους καὶ πότους coniungit, ex quo colligitur, κώμου nomine inordinatam vorandi aviditatem intelligi, sicut etiam Lutherus reddidit. Fresseren. Isidorus Pelusiota lib. 1. Epist. 456. κῶμον dicit esse tibiae cantum, qui cum largiore vino ad voluptatem & libidinem extimulat ac convivium in foedum & obscoenum theatrum mutat, atque per cymbala quaedam & instrumenta ad fraudes accommodata, convivas mulcet ac delinit. Suidas κῶμον dicit esse μέθην.Sap. 14. v. 23.ἐμμανεῖς κώμους ἄγειν gentiles dicuntur, quando luxuriosa convivia & insanas comessationes instituunt. 2. Maccab. 6. vers. 4.ἀσωτία & κῶμοι coniunguntur. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]in foetore, quia convivia luxuriosa vomitus & foetores secúm trahunt. Marc. 7. v. 22. & Galat. 5. v. 19. reddit Syrus hac voce Graecum ἀσέλγεια.

Ἐν πότοις Vulg. in potationibus. Aug. hom. 20. inter 50. in potatione. Denotantur hoc nomine cum κώμοις coniuncto luxuriosae compotationes, in quibus ad numerum bibitur & potando certatur Esai. 5. v. 11. & 22. inexhausta potandi ingluvies & insanum continuandi potûs studium. Prov. 23. v. 30.ἰχνέυοντες ποῦ πότοι γίνονται solicitè investigantes, ubi compotationes instituantur. Vulg. qui student calicibus epotandis. Luth. Die da kommen auszusauffen/was eingeschencket ist. Apud Lucianum φίλος πό των καὶ ἀφροδισίων dicitur, qui vino & Venere delectatur. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] quod significat convivium, cui Musica adhibetur à rad. [consult facsimile image]cecinit.

est autem locutio Synecdochica, siquidem ex una parte totus conviviorum luxus intelligitur, in quibus praeter exquisitos cibos praesens est Musica & omne delitiarum genus. Rom. 13. vers. 13.Galat. 5. vers. 21. Syrus interpres hac voce exprimit Graecum κώμους, unde etiam Tremellius hoc loco vertit comessationes. Luth. Sàufferen. Lyranus, ut distinguat ab οἰνοφλυγίαις accipit de potationibus inebriativis sine vino. Sed concinnius est οἰνοφλυγίας de vitioso habitu & affectu, πότους de potandi actu accipere.

Καὶ ἐν ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαις. Vulg. illicitis idolorum cultibus. Sed Graecum est ἐμφατικώτερον, nefariis idolorum cultibus, quibus honor DEO debitus ad creaturas & fictitia Numina transfertur, quod peccatum in primo decalogi praecepto severissimè prohibetur. Syrus reddidit in cultu vel servitio[consult facsimile image]Daemoniorum, à vastatione sic dictorum, quia Dii gentium sunt Daemonia Psalm. 96. vers. 5. August. d. l. in illicitis idolorum serritutibus, homil. 20. inter 50. nefandis idolorum servitutibus. Luth. in greulichen Abgo tterenen. Sic ergò Apostolus conversis ad CHRISTUM in mentem revocat horrenda peccata, in quibus ante suam conversionem in gentilismo vixerunt, & ex eo argumentum ducit exhortationis ad sanctae vitae studium. Loca parallela sunt Roman. 13. vers. 12.Nox praecessit, dies autem appropinquavit, abiiciamus ergò opera tenebrarum, & induamus arma lucis.vers. 13.Sicut in die honestè ambulemus, non in comessationibus & ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus & impudicitiis, non in contentione & aemulatione.Ephes. 2. vers. 11.Memores estote, quod aliquando eratis gentes in carne &c.cap. 4. vers. 17.Hoc dico & testificor in Domino, ut iam non ambuletis, sicut gentes ambulant in vanitate sensus suivers. 18.tenebris obscuratum habentes intellectumvers. 19.quiἀπηλγηκότεςsemetipsos tradiderunt impudicitiae in operationem omnis immunditiae.

## 4:4
IN WHICH THEY ARE ASTONISHED THAT YOU DO NOT RUN WITH THEM INTO THE SAME CONFUSION OF LUXURY, BLASPHEMING.

Connection. 1. A new argument for exhortation sought from the very judgment of the impious. The impious, offended by your amendment and struck by the novelty of the matter, are astonished. This very thing ought to confirm you in the purpose of a holy life, for that which displeases the wicked cannot but be good.

2. He amplifies the impiety of the Gentiles, of which he had treated in the preceding verse, in that they not only continue to stick in the most filthy mire of sins, but are also disturbed by the amendment of others, and blaspheme the same.

3. The Apostle knew that weaker Christians are not a little moved by the fact that the Gentiles, after their conversion to Christ, not only renounce their friendship, but even pursue them with reproaches and insults. He therefore fortifies their minds with this προθεραπιεία, so that they might not be disturbed by those perverse and preposterous judgments of the impious and their blasphemous speeches, and much less allow themselves to be drawn back into the society of their former vices.

Disposition. He amplifies the amendment of those converted to Christ from two events, namely, the offense of those from whose morals they had withdrawn, and the blasphemies of the same.

Exposition of the text. Ἐν ῷ ξενίζονται. Vulg. in which they marvel. Certain Latin codices read, in which they now stand astonished. August. Epist. 99 to Evod. in which they are stupefied. The Greek properly has, in which they are strangers, in which way the Vulgate Interpreter himself rendered the word ξενίζεσθαι below v. 12.. Meanwhile, he also correctly expressed the sense in this place by the word they marvel. For those are called ξενίζεσθαι, by the Greeks who are disturbed with wonder on account of some new, unusual, or strange thing, whence the Greek Scholia on this passage explain ξενίζονται by θαυμάζουσι, and α. The Syrian rendered it by [consult facsimile image] from the root [consult facsimile image] he wondered, he was astonished. Matth. 8. v. 10. Ioh. 3. v. 7. It also signifies he murmured, he was indignant Marc. 10. v. 41. 1. Corinth. 11. v. 10. which signification can likewise be accommodated to this place. The word ξενίζεσθαι taken properly signifies to lodge, to be received as a guest Act. 10. v. 6. 18. and 32. cap. 21. vers. 16. by metalepsis it is put for that which it is accustomed to happen to guests and travelers. For just as they, contemplating citadels, houses, harbors, monuments, and other things not seen before, are struck and marvel at the novelty and strangeness of the thing: so the nations, seeing a sudden change of life and morals in men converted to Christ, are travelers, i.e., they marvel as at a new and strange thing, and are offended from there; it seems to them insolent and strange that those converted to Christ have departed from their former way of life. Acts 17. verse 20. The Athenians say to Paul, ξενίζοντα τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν, you bring certain new and strange things to our ears. 2. Macc. 9. verse 6. ξενίζουσαι συμφοραὶ are called new calamities. ἡ φύσις τῇ ἀμετρῷ μεταβολῇ ξενίζεται the Greeks say. Nature is disturbed by excessive change. Budaeus in his commentaries p. 1096, from two passages of Polybius, proves that ξενίζεσθαι is the same as to be stunned and to marvel at a thing as unusual, unheard of, and strange. Polyb. book 1. ξενιζόμενοι ταῖς τῷν ὀργάνων κατασκευαῖς. book 5. ξενισθεὶς καὶ διαπορήσας ἐπὶ πολὺν χρόνον διὰ τὸ παράδοξον, where, however, it should rather be rendered passively, to be brought into admiration and stupor on account of the novelty of the thing. In the vernacular language likewise, that which is unusual and unexpected is accustomed to be called strange, whence Luther in this place rightly rendered it, Das befrembdet sie. ἐν τῷ for it is placed in this place δεικτικῶς, in which i.e., concerning which they marvel, or that is what they marvel at; they marvel about that thing or for that reason. A similar Hebraism occurs John 9. v. 30. ἐν τούτῳ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν, this is a wonderful thing. The Syrian rendered it, And behold now they are stunned.

Μὴ συντρεχόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν αὐτῷν τῆς ἀσωτίας ἀνάχυσιν. The Vulgate rendered it, you not concurring with them into the same confusion of luxury. August. in the same place, you do not concur into that confusion of luxury. By the word συντρέχειν he insinuates that carnal men flow together with a most fervent course toward intemperance. Nor is it absurdly thought that in particular there is a regard for the feast of Bacchus, to which the Gentiles were accustomed to concur with a certain insane impetus, and in it to practice those unspeakable crimes which Peter enumerates in the preceding verse. The Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael, which Tremellius in this place rendered by to become foolish. But from Rom. 1. v. 27. it appears that it is more rightly translated to burn up through an insane namely lust, for luxuria in Greek is not ἀσέλγεια, which in the preceding verse the Vulgate Interpreter rendered by luxuria, but ἀσωτία, which properly signifies luxury, or profusion. The Syrian retained the Greek name and added, in the former ἀσωτία. Nor is there in the Greek σύγχυσιν confusion, as the Vulgate rendered it, but ἀνάχυσιν, which properly signifies refusion, by which they think it is denoted, that Christians do not refund, i. e. do not respond to allurements, provocations, and dishonest solicitations: It could also be thought that by this word the fervor of lust and intemperance is expressed, with a metaphor drawn from the sea overflowing and pouring out waters beyond its channel. Some translated it by profusion. The Greek Scholia explain it by σύγχυσιν. Confusion, when things of a different kind are mixed and confounded among themselves without order, Act. 19. v. 29. which exposition fits beautifully with the gluttony of the luxurious and the heap of crimes among the Gentiles. Hesychius and Suidas say that ἀνάχυσιν among other things signifies the βλακείαν καὶ ἔκλυσιν of the mind and the dissolution of strength, softness, which meaning fits this passage beautifully. For ἀσωτία finally dissolves the powers of the mind and body. βλασφημοῦντες. Vulgate blaspheming. Some take it concerning the insults and reproaches with which the Gentiles pursued those converted to the Christian faith by this name, because with their former manner of living changed, they seem alien from all humanity and common society. βλασφημεῖν is said, as if βλάπτειν τὴν φημὴν, to harm the reputation of another, in which meaning it is taken Roman. 3. v. 8. 1. Corinth. 4. v. 13. But it is likely that those slanderers did not stop at the persons of the Christians, but had also slandered the Christian religion itself, as if in it and with it no one could exercise cheerfulness and live by the example of others, and for this reason had blasphemed God himself, the author of the Christian religion, in which meaning the word βλασφημεῖν is taken Matth. 9. v. 3. cap. 26. v. 65. Rom. 2. v. 24. etc. The Syrian, for the sake of clarity, arranges the text thus. And behold now they are astonished and blaspheme you in that you do not burn with them in the same former debauchery.

Latin:

IN QUO PEREGRINANTUR NON CONCURRENTIBUS VOBIS IN EANDEM LUXURIAE CONFUSIONEM BLASPHEMANTES.

Connexio. 1. Novum exhortationis argumentum petitum ab ipso impiorum iudicio. Impii vestra emendatione offensi ac rei novitate perculsi stupent. Idipsum in sanctae vitae proposito vos confirmare debet, non potest enim non esse bonum, quod malis displicet.

2. Amplificat impietatem gentium, de qua in praeced. vers. egerat, quòd non solùm in peccatorum coeno turpissimo haerere pergant, sed etiam aliorum emendatione turbentur, eandemque blasphement.

3. Noverat Apostolus, non parum moveri Christianos infirmiores, quod gentiles post conversionem ipsorum ad Christum, non modo eorum amicitiae renuncient, verùm etiam convitiis & contumeliis ipsos persequantur. Munit igitur hac προθεραπιεία ipsorum animos, ne perversis & praeposteris illis impiorum iudiciis, ac blasphemis sermonibus turbentur, multò vero minus ad pristinorum vitiorum societatem sese pertrahi patiantur.

Dispositio. Amplificat conversorum ad Christum emendationem ex duobus eventis, offensione sc. eorum, à quorum moribus recesserant, & eorundem blasphemiis.

Textus expositio. Ἐν ῷ ξενίζονται. Vulg. in quo admirantur. Quidam Codd. Lat. legunt, in quibus nunc obstupescunt. August. Epist. 99. ad Evod. in quo stupescunt. Graeca propriè habent, in quo peregrinantur, quo modo inferiùs v. 12. ipse Interpres vulgatus verbum ξενίζεσθαι reddidit. Interim sensum etiam hoc loco rectè expressit per verbum admirantur. Dicuntur enim Graecis ξενίζεσθαι, qui ob rem aliquam novam, insolentem aut peregrinam cum admiratione turbantur, unde Scholia Graeca h. l. ξενίζονται explicant per θαυμάζουσι, ac α Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image]admiratus est, obstupuit.Matth. 8. v. 10.Ioh. 3. v. 7. significat etiam obmurmuravit, indignatus fuitMarc. 10. v. 41.1. Corinth. 11. v. 10. quae significatio itidem huic loco accommodari potest. Verbum ξενίζεσθαι propriè acceptum significat diversari, hospitio excipiAct. 10. v. 6.18. & 32.cap. 21. vers. 16. per metalepsin ponitur pro eo, quod hospitibus ac peregrinantibus contingere solet. Ut enim illi arces, domus, portus, monumenta, aliaque priùs minimè visa contemplantes, rei novitate & insolentiâ perculsi admirantur: ita gentes subitam vitae & morum mutationem in hominibus ad Christum conversis videntes, peregrinantur i. e. tanquam rem novam & peregrinam admirantur, atque inde offenduntur; videtur ipsis insolens ac peregrinum, quòd conversi ad Christum à pristino vitae genere discesserint. Actor. 17. vers. 20. Athenienses ad Paulum dicunt, ξενίζοντα τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν,nova & peregrina quaedam infers auribus nostris.2. Macc. 9. vers. 6.ξενίζουσαι συμφοραὶ dicuntur novae calamitates.ἡ φύσις τῇ ἀμετρῷ μεταβολῇ ξενίζεται dicunt Graeci. Natura nimia mutatione perturbatur. Budaeus in comm. p. 1096. ex duobus locis Polybii probat, ξενίζεσθαι esse idem quod stupere & rem ut insolitam, inauditamque admirari & peregrinam. Polyb. lib. 1. ξενιζόμενοι ταῖς τῷν ὀργάνων κατασκευαῖς. lib.: 5. ξενισθεὶς καὶ διαπορήσας ἐπὶ πολὺν χρόνον διὰ τὸ παράδοξον, ubi tamen passivè potiùs reddendum, in admirationem & stuporem adduci ob rei novitatem. In lingua vernacula itidem, quod est inusitatum & inopinatum, vocari solet peregrinum, unde Luth. hoc loco rectè reddidit, Das befrembdet sie.ἐν τῷ enim ponitur hoc loco δεικτικῶς,in quo i. e. de quo admirantur, sive illud est, quod mirantur; ea de re vel eam ob rem admirantur. Similis Hebraismus occurrit Iohan. 9. v. 30.ἐν τούτῳ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν,hoc mirabile est. Syrus reddidit. Et ecce nunc obstupescunt.

Μὴ συντρεχόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν αὐτῷν τῆς ἀσωτίας ἀνάχυσιν. Vulg. reddidit, non concurrentibus vobis in eandem luxuriae confusionem. August. d. l. non concurrere vos in eam luxuriae confusionem. Verbo συντρέχειν insinuat, carnales homines fervidissimo cursu ad intemperantiam confluere. Nec absurdè cogitatur, in specie haberi respectum ad Bacchi festum, ad quod insano quodam impetu gentiles concurrere solebant, inque eo nefanda illa flagitia exercere, quae Petrus versu praeced. enumerat. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael, quod Tremellius hoc loco reddidit per stultescere.
