Cui officium aliquod in Ecclesia vel etiam Politia commissum, non agatremissè & languidè, sed summo studio, fideliter & quantis potest viribus Rom. 12. v. 8.Qui exhortatur in exhortando, qui praeest in solicitudinev. 11.Studio non pigri. Et quia nullius est felix conatus & utilis unquam, Consilium si non detque, iuvetque Deus, ideò per serias preces divinam illuminationem, gubernationé & directionem solicitè expetat.

27. Ut in omnibus nostris actionibus, ita quoquc in officii Ecclesiastici administratione gloriam Dei velut unicum & summum nobis praefixum habeamus scopum. 1. Cor. 10. v. 31.Omnia in gloriam Dei facite; in quem locum Theodoretus sic commendatur. Pulchrè omnia comprehendit & sedere, & ambulare, & disserere, & misereri & docere, ut unus omnium sit scopus gloria Dei. Quia enim totum, quod sumus, possumus, agimus, habemus, à Deo est, quia munere divino, quod sumus, omne sumus, ideò meritò omnia nostra studia, actiones & conatus nostros omnes ad ipsius gloriam unicè referre debemus.

28. Tunc autem verè DEUS in officii nostri operibus glorificatur, quando nihil quicquam tentamus fiduciâ propriarum virium, sed divinam gratiam & Spiritus sancti auxilium imploramus, quando non quaerimus eruditionis vel eloquentiae gloriam in verbo Dei tractando, 1. Cor. 1. v. 17. quando ex sincera dilectione ad protimi salutem omne nostrum studium convertimus, quando totum Deo tribuimus, quicquid boni ac salutaris in officio agimus. 1. Cor. 15. v. 10.2. Cor. 3. v. 5. &c. Beda in h. l. Honorificatur Deus in actibus nostris, cum omne quicquid benè & secundùm voluntatem eius facimus non hoc nostris meritis, sed gratiae tribuimus; è contra autem mala, quae gerimus, nostrae solùm malitiae vel ignorantiae deputamus.

29. Quia Deus non potest verè glorificari, nisi fide praelucente officii opera perficiantur, ideò in omni officio vocationis requiritur verbum, cui fides innitatur, ut conscientia possit esse certa, haec opera Deo placere. Rom. 14. v. ult.Hebr. 11. v. 6.

30. Ut non possumus DEO placere nisi in CHRISTO; ita quoque non potest DEUS à nobis glorificari, nisi in CHRISTO & per CHRISTUM. Sicut à DEO per CHRISTUM omnia beneficia ad nos descendunt, ita quoque in humili gratiarum actione per Christum omnia ad DEI gloriam referri debent. Bernh. serm, 13. in Cant. Ad locum, unde exeunt, revertantur flumina gratiarum, ut iterum fluant; remittatur ad suum principium coeleste profluvium, quò uberius terrae refundatur.

## 4:9
BE HOSPITABLE TO ONE ANOTHER WITHOUT MURMURING.

Connection. 1. This is the third virtue to which the Apostle exhorts those converted to Christ, namely, hospitality.

2. To the exhortation to charity, which is the source and mother of all virtues to be exercised toward one's neighbor, the Apostle adds an exhortation to hospitality, which is the primary fruit of love and a virtue subordinated to charity: for it is a work of charity, among other things, to receive needy strangers into one's home, to refresh them with food, and to perform all offices of humanity for them.

3. Lyranus on this passage notes as follows: Because charity ought to be shown in work, otherwise it would not be true, according to what Gregory says, homily 20: The love of GOD is never idle; for it works great things if it exists; but if it refuses to work, it is not love; therefore hospitality is added.

4. Peter knew and remembered that he had heard from the mouth of the Master that hospitality is also enumerated among the works of charity and mercy to be publicly proclaimed on the day of judgment Matth. 25. v. 35. I was a stranger, and you took me in; therefore he adds the precept of hospitality to the precept of charity.

5. Arnobius, book 8 against the Gentiles, mentions regarding the Pontics or those dwelling by the Pontus, that they were inhospitable. Therefore, lest Christians, through conversation with them, should contract a partnership in this vice, Peter exhorts them to hospitality.

Exposition of the text. φιλόξενοι εἰς ἀλλήλους. The Vulgate rendered it, hospitable to one another. The Greek properly has, toward others. ἄξενοι those are called inhospitable, who are alienated in mind from receiving strangers into hospitality. Opposed to them are φιλόξενοι, who they are prompt and ready to receive strangers with hospitality, who treat guests in a friendly manner, and show them all the duties of humanity. The Syriac rendered κατὰ πόδα. Be lovers of hospitality. But the Apostle is not speaking of that pompous hospitality which men exercise in inviting the wealthier to unnecessary banquets, Luke 14. verse 11. nor of that civil hospitality by which those things which are necessary for the sustenance of life are provided to strangers in public inns for a just price; but of that Christian and holy hospitality by which Christians, out of sincere charity, promptly receive needy strangers into their homes, especially those who are exiles on account of the profession of the true religion, embrace them kindly and lovingly, cherish them as members of Christ and fellow citizens of the Church, and provide for them with food, drink, clothing, and other things necessary for the sustenance of life, which virtue the Apostles also commend to Christians elsewhere. Rom. 12. verse 13. τὴν φιλοξενίαν διώκοντες. Heb. 13. verse 2. τῆς φιλοξενίας μὴ ἑπιλανθάνεσθε. 3. Epist. v. 5. you do faithfully whatever you work toward the brothers and this toward strangers ἄνευ γογγυσμῶν. The Vulgate rendered, without murmuring, in which way Gregory also cites it in homily 7 on Ezekiel, but in the Greek it is plural without murmurings, although two Royal Codices also have the singular ἄνευ γογγυσμοῦ. Hugo thinks that this προσδίορισμὸν can be referred also to those who are received with hospitality, so that they may be content with what is provided, and grateful toward those who receive them. But it is more correctly referred to those who exercise hospitality. For by this προσδιορισμὸν the Apostle explains the form and manner of exercising this virtue, namely that we ought to exercise works of mercy, and among them also hospitality, with a prompt, indeed a cheerful and glad mind, for forced services do not please God. γογγύζειν is to murmur, to speak against tacitly, to contradict with a certain signification of impatience and hatred, Matt. 20. verse 11. Luke 5. verse 30. John 6. verse 41. 43. and 61. chap. 7. verse 32. 1. Cor. 10. v. 10. hence γογγυσμὸς murmur, or murmuring John 7. v. 12. Acts 6. v. 1. Phil. 2. v. 14. The LXX use it for תלונות from the root לון to complain, to murmur Ex. 16. v. 7. and following. The Syriac in this place rendered it by [consult facsimile image] from the root [consult facsimile image] he murmured, he muttered. Matt. 20. verse 11. John 6. verse 41. etc.

When therefore Peter commands that hospitality ἄνευ γογγυσμῶν be exercised, he then prohibits: 1. Occult detraction and clandestine slanders, by which those who unwillingly receive them into hospitality are accustomed to injure the reputation of strangers. 2. Tacit murmuring and unjust complaints. For those who do not provide hospitality to strangers with a ready mind, but unwillingly and as if compelled, complain and lament about the scarcity of their household goods, about the difficulties of the times, about the abundance of expenses to be spent on strangers, or even about the manners of the strangers. 3. Odious reproaches of the benefits conferred upon strangers. Conversely, he commands that we receive strangers into hospitality with a ready and cheerful mind, and that we, as it were, congratulate ourselves on the occasion of exercising this excellent virtue. The parallel passages are: Rom. 12. v. 8. ὁ ἐλεῶν, ἐν ὸλαρότητι. 2. Cor. 9. v. 7. μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἣ ἐξ ἀνάγκης. ἱλαρὸν γάρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεὸς. Philip. 2. vers. 14. πάντα ποιεῖτε χωρὶς γογγυσμῶν.

Latin:

HOSPITALES INVICEM SINE MURMURATIONE.

Connexio. 1. Tertia haec est virtus, ad quam Apostolus conversos ad Christum hortatur, videlicet hospitalitas.

2. Exhortationi ad caritatem, quae est fons & mater omnium virtutum erga proximum exercendarum, subiicit Apostolus exhortationem ad hospitalitatem, quae est dilectionis primarius fructus ac virtus caritati subordinata: caritatis enim opus est inter caetera peregrinos egentes in domum recipere, cibo reficere, & omnia humanitatis officia eis praestare.

3. Lyranus ad h. l. sic annotat. Quia caritas debet ostendi in opere, aliter non esset vera, secundùm quod dicit Gregorius homil. 20. Amor DEI nunquam est otiosus, operatur enim magna, si est; si autem operari renuit, amor non est, ideò subditur hospitalitas.

4. Noverat & meminerat Petrus, fe ex ore Magistri audivisse, inter caritatis & miscericordiae opera in die iudicii publicè praedicanda etiam recenseri hospitalitatem Matth. 25. v. 35. Hospes eram, & collegistis me, ideò praecepto caritatis subiungit praeceptum hospitalitatis.

5. Arnobius lib. 8. contra gentes de Ponticis sive Ponti accolis memorat, quòd fuerint inhospitales. Ne igitur Christiani ex conversatione cum illis vitii huius consortium contraherent, Petrus eos ad hospitalitatem exhortatur.

Textus expositio. φιλόξενοι εἰς ἀλλήλους. Vulgat. reddidit, hospitales invicem. Graeca propriè habent, alii erga alios. ἄξενοι dicuntur inhospitales, qui animo ab excipiendis hospitio peregrinis sunt alieno. Illis opponuntur φιλόξενοι, qui promti & parati sunt ad peregrinos hospitio excipiendos, qui hospites amicè tractant, & omnia humanitatis officia eis exhibent. Syrus reddidit κατὰ πόδα.Estote amantes hospites. Loquitur autem Apostolus non de pomposa illa hospitalitate, quam homines in invitandis ditioribus ad convivia non necessaria exercent, Luc. 14. vers. 11. nec de civili illa hospitalitate, quâ peregrinis in diversoriis publicis pro iusto precio ea, quae ad vitae sustentationem necessaria sunt, exhibentur; sed de Christiana illa & sancta hospitalitate, quâ peregrinos egenos, maximè vero propter religionis verae professionem exules Christiani ex sincera caritate promtè in aedes suas recipiunt, eos benignè & amanter complectuntur, tanquam Christi membra & Ecclesiae concives fovent, ac de cibo, potu, vestimentis & aliis ad vitae sustentationem necessariis illis prospiciunt, quam virtutem etiam alibi Christianis Apostoli commendant. Rom. 12. vers. 13.τὴν φιλοξενίαν διώκοντες.Hebr. 13. vers. 2.τῆς φιλοξενίας μὴ ἑπιλανθάνεσθε. 3. Epist. v. 5. fideliter facis, quicquid operaris in fratres & hoc in peregrinosἄνευ γογγυσμῶν. Vulg. reddidit, sine murmuratione, quo modo etiam citat Gregorius homil. 7. in Ezech. sed in Graeco est plurale sine murmurationibus, quamvis etiam duo Regii Codices habeant singulare ἄνευ γογγυσμοῦ. Hugo existimat, posse huncπροσδίορισμὸνreferri ad eos etiam, qui hospitio excipiuntur, ut sint appositis contenti, & erga suscipientes grati. Sed rectiùs refertur ad eos, qui exercent hospitalitatem. Per hunc enim προσδιορισμὸν explicat Apostolus formam & modum huius virtutis exercendae, videlicet quod animo promto, imò hilari ac laeto misericordiae opera, & inter ea etiam hospitalitatem exercere debeamus, coacta enim servitia Deo non placent. γογγύζεινest murmurare, tacitè obloqui, cum quadam impatientiae & odii significatione contradicere,Matth. 20. vers. 11.Luc. 5. vers. 30.Iohan. 6. vers. 41.43. & 61.cap. 7. vers. 32.1. Corinth. 10. v. 10. inde γογγυσμὸςmurmur, ob murmuratioIohan. 7. v. 12.Actor. 6. v. 1.Phil. 2. v. 14. LXX. utuntur pro תלונות à rad. לוןquerulari, murmurareEx. 16. v. 7. & seqq. Num. 17. v. 10. Syrus h. l. reddidit per [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image]murmuravit, mussitavit.Matth. 20. vers. 11.Iohan. 6. vers. 41. &c.

Quando ergò Petrus hospitalitatem ἄνευ γογγυσμῶν exerceri praecipit, tùm prohibet. 1. Occultam maledicentiam, & clancularias obtrectationes, quibus famam peregrinorum laedere solent, qui inviti eos hospitio excipiunt. 2. Tacitum murmur & iniquas querelas. Qui enim non promto animo, sed inviti & quasi coacti peregrinis hospitium praebent, conqueruntur ac quiritantur de rei familiaris penuria, de temporum difficultatibus, de copia sumtuum peregrinis impendendorum, vel etiam de moribus peregrinorum. 3. Odiosas exprobrationes beneficiorum in peregrinos collatorum. Contra vero praecipit, ut animo promto & hilari peregrinos hospitio excipiamus, nobisque de occasione exercendae huius praeclarae virtutis quasi gratulemur. Loca parallela sunt. Rom. 12. v. 8.ὁ ἐλεῶν, ἐν ὸλαρότητι.2. Cor. 9. v. 7.μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἣ ἐξ ἀνάγκης. ἱλαρὸν γάρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεὸς.Philip. 2. vers. 14.πάντα ποιεῖτε χωρὶς γογγυσμῶν.

## 4:10
AS EVERY MAN HATH RECEIVED THE GIFT, EVEN SO MINISTER THE SAME ONE TO ANOTHER, AS GOOD STEWARDS OF THE MANIFOLD GRACE OF GOD.

Connection. 1. This is the fourth virtue to which the Apostle exhorts Christians, διακονία & κοινωνία of spiritual gifts, which likewise is a certain species and offspring of charity.

2. From the exhortation to hospitality, which pertains to the works of corporal mercy, he passes to an exhortation by which he admonishes Christians concerning the ready χαρισμάτων communication of those things given to each one divinely, which pertains to the works of spiritual mercy.

3. He had said that hospitality and other offices of charity toward one's neighbor were to be exercised without murmurings. Truly, nothing is more apt and efficacious for restraining those murmurings than the consideration of the first origin from which all those things by which we benefit our neighbor descend, namely, that we are not liberal with our own, but with another's, and that we dispense that which has been committed to us by the Lord.

4. This precept is general, pertaining to all states of all orders, by which the Apostle admonishes Christians that each one according to the gift which he has received from GOD, should serve his neighbor, and contribute to the common use what seems to him peculiar and proper, since all are members of one and the same mystical body. To this general precept the Apostle soon adds παραγγέλματα special ones.

Disposition of the text. The Apostle insinuates three arguments of exhortation, why we ought to expend our gifts for the use of our neighbor. 1. Because we have received them from GOD, therefore it is fair that we should liberally pour them back into others. 2. Because we are not the Lords of them, but stewards appointed by GOD to dispense them, therefore it is fair that we should distribute them according to the will of GOD. 3. Because those gifts are various, and not all things are given to one, but some to some, so that individuals may be more prompt to communicate their own things with others.

Exposition of the text. Ἓκαστος καθὼς ἒλαβε χάρισμα εἰς ἑαυτοὺς αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες. Vulg. As each one has received grace, administering it to one another. But in the Greek it is χάρισμα, which properly signifies a gift given out of grace, and διακονοῦντες, which is ministering. By the word χαρίσματος. are understood 1. Ministering gifts, which are not given by GOD to all the reborn, as sanctifying gifts are, but only to some, so that by their legitimate use they may serve others, and contribute the same to the common use of the Church, from which they are also called ministering. The Scholastics call them graces freely given. The Apostle recounts a quite long catalog of them 1. Cor. 12. v. 4. There are divisions of graces, but the same Spirit &c. v. 7. But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for utility (for the edification of the Church) v. 8. To one indeed is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, but to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit. v. 9. To another faith in the same Spirit, to another the grace of healings in the same Spirit. v. 10. To another the working of powers, to another Prophecy, to another the discernment of Spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of speeches. 2. Diverse functions in the Church, and virtues necessary for their administration, as we shall demonstrate afterwards.

Καθὼς ἒλαβε, from GOD, as 1. Cor. 12. v. 11. is added. But all these things one and the same Spirit works, dividing to individuals as he wills. Ephes. 4. v. 7. To each one of us grace is given according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Thence the Syrian explicitly added [consult facsimile image] to GOD. The same person indeed omitted the mark of comparison ὡς, which is nevertheless emphatic in this place, for it signifies among other things, as we have received freely, so also, let us give freelyMatth. 10. v. 8.

Ἐις ἑαυτοὺς αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες. A variety of reading occurs here. For some Codices read αὐτῷ διακονοῦντες, so that the sense may be, that grace or that gift i.e. by that gift ministering or serving one another. But the more approved and more numerous Codices have αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες ministering that, so that the sense may be. Just as each one is endowed with some gift given to him by GOD, by which he might be useful to others, let him minister that one to another, who has need of it, or expend it by ministering. Moreover, the little word διακονοῦντες is very emphatic, since it includes the meaning of ministry. Matth. 4. v. 11.cap. 8. v. 15.cap. 20. v. 28.Luc. 22. v. 26.Ioh. 12. v. 2. &c. Therefore the Apostle implies that on account of those gifts no one ought to exalt himself above others, or affect lordship over others, but of his own accord constitute himself a minister of others, and thus use the gifts divinely granted to him not only promptly, but also with true humility and modesty for the benefit of others. The Syrian has. Each one of you, the gift which he received from God [consult facsimile image] [consult facsimile image] let him supply to his neighbors, let him serve his neighbors with it [consult facsimile image] the root proper to the Syrians and Chaldeans signifies he served, he ministeredMatth. 25. v. 44.Act. 13. v. 36. &c.

Ώς καλοὶ ὀικονόμοι ποικίλης χάριτος θεοῦ. The Royal Codex has, κληρονόμού heirs, so that it may correspond to the little word ἒλαβε But the more approved Codices read ὀκονόμοι, in which way the vulgate also rendered it, as good stewards, and the Syrian [consult facsimile image] stewards, house-managers, Matth. 20. v. 8.Luc. 16. v. 1. it is held joined [consult facsimile image]

By Χὰριν μετωνυμικῶς he understands χάρισμα a gift given out of grace, and therefore ποικίλης χάριτος to the Apostle in this place is the same as ποικίλων χαρισμάτων, as is evident from the preceding, whence the vulgate rendered it in both places grace. ποκίλης The vulgate rendered it multiform. But the Greek is more significant, Jerome book 1. against Iovin. chap. 4. rendered, various, Epist. 50. to Pamm. manifold. The Syrian [consult facsimile image] from the root [consult facsimile image] divided, separated, distinguished. Therefore the Apostle looks to a parallel passage 1. Cor. 12. v. 4. διαιρέσεις χαρισμάτων εἰσὶ there are divisions of gifts i. e. gifts are diverse and various, most greatly differing from one another; for they are called διαιρέσεις χαρισμάτων not so much from distributing, as from differing. Also to the parable of the Savior Matth. 25. v. 15.Luc. 19. v. 13.To one he gave five talents, to another however two, to another indeed one, to each according to his own ability. But whatsoever and how great soever gifts anyone has received, he ought to contribute them to the salvation of his neighbor and the Church, and thus in their dispensation and use demonstrate himself a faithful steward of the supreme Lord, whence Lyranus at this place annotates thus, as good stewards of the grace of God, conformed to your Lord, who gives freely and liberally. Parallel passages are Rom. 12. v. 6. ἒχοντες δέ χαρίσματα κατὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν διαφορὰ. Eph. 4. v. 7.To each one, grace is given according to the measure of the gift of Christ1. Cor. 12. v. 4.there are divisions χαρισμάτων, v. 5.divisions διακονιῶν. v. 6.divisions ἐνεργημάτων &c.

Latin:

UNUSQUISQUE SICUT ACCEPIT GRATIAM, IN ALTERUTRUM ILLAM ADMINISTRANTES, SICUT BONI DISPENSATORES MULTIFORMIS GRATIAE DEI.

Connexio. 1. Quarta haec est virtus, ad quam Apostolus Christianos hortatur, διακονία & κοινωνία donorum spiritualium, quae itidem caritatis est quaedam species ac suboles.

2. Ab exhortatione ad hospitalitatem, quae pertinet ad opera misericordiae corporalis transit ad exhortationem, quâ de promta χαρισμάτων divinitùs unicuique datorum communicatione Christianos admonet, quae pertinet ad opera misericordiae spiritualis.

3. Dixerat sine murmurationibus hospitalitatem & alia caritatis officia erga proximum esse exercenda. Nihil vero ad cohibendas illas murmurationes aptius & efficacius, quàm consideratio primae originis, ex qua omnia illa, quibus proximo benefacimus, descendunt, videlicet, quòd non simus liberales de proprio, sed de alieno, ac illud dispensemus, quod à Domino nobis commissum.

4. Praeceptum hoc generale est, ad omnes omnium ordinum status pertinens, quo Apostolus Christianos admonet, ut quisque iuxta donum, quod à DEO accepit, proximo serviat, & in communem usum conferat, quod ipsi videtur peculiare atque proprium, cùm omnes sint unius eius demque mystici corporis membra. Huie generali praecepto mox subiungit Apostolus παραγγέλματα specialia.

Textus dispositio. Tria insinuat Apostolus exhortationis argumenta, quare in proximi usum dona nostra debeamus impendere. 1. Quia à DEO ea accepimus, ideò aequum est, ut in alios eadem liberaliter refundamus. 2. Quia non sumus illorum Domini, sed ad ea dispensanda oeconomi à DEO constituti, ideò aequum est, ut ad DEI arbitrium eadem erogemus. 3. Quia dona illa sunt varia, nec uni omnia, sed alia aliis data, ut singuli ad sua cum aliis communicanda sint promtiores.

Expositio textus. Ἓκαστος καθὼς ἒλαβε χάρισμα εἰς ἑαυτοὺς αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες. Vulg. Unus quisque sicut accepit gratiam in alterutrum illam administrantes. Sed in Graeco est χάρισμα, quod propriè significat donum ex gratia datum, & διακονοῦντες, quod est ministrantes. Intelliguntur autem voce χαρίσματος. 1. Dona ministrantia, quae non omnibus renatis à DEO dantur, ut dona sanctificantia, sed quibusdam tantùm, ut legitimo eorum usu aliis inserviant, & in communem Ecclesiae usum eadem conferant, ex quo etiam ministrantia vocantur. Scholastici ea vocant gratias gratis datas. Eorum catalogum benè longum recenset Apostolus 1. Cor. 12. v. 4.Divisiones gratiarum sunt, idem autem Spiritus &c.v. 7.Unicuique autem datur manifestatio Spiritûs ad utilitatem (ad Ecclesiae aedificationem) v. 8.Alii quidem per Spiritum datur sermo sapientiae, alii autem sermo scientiae secundùm eundem Spiritum.v. 9.Alteri fides in eodem Spiritu, alii gratia sanitatum in eodem Spiritu.v. 10.Alii operatio virtutum, alii Prophetia, alii discretio Spirituum, alii genera linguarum, alii interpretatio sermonum. 2. Diversae functiones in Ecclesia, & virtutes ad illarum administrationem necessariae, ut postea demonstrabimus.

Καθὼς ἒλαβε,â DEO, sicut 1. Cor. 12. v. 11. additur. Haec autem omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus, dividens singulis prout vult.Ephes. 4. v. 7.Unicuique nostrûm data est gratia secundùm mensuram donationis Christi. Inde Syrus disertè addidit [consult facsimile image] à DEO. Idem vero omisit notam similitudinis ὡς, quae tamen hoc loco est emphatica, significat enim inter alia, ut sicut gratis accepimus, ita quoque, gratis demusMatth. 10. v. 8.

Ἐις ἑαυτοὺς αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες. Occurrit hîc lectionis varietas. Quidam enim Codices legunt αὐτῷ διακονοῦντες, ut sit sensus, illam gratiâ sive illo dono h. e. per illud donum alii aliis ministrantes sive inservientes. Sed probatiores & plures Codices habent αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες illud ministrantes, ut sit sensus. Prout quisque praeditus est aliquo dono a DEO sibi dato, quo utilis esse possit aliis, illud alius in alium, qui eo opus habet ministret, sive ministrando expendat. Est autem vocula διακονοῦντες perquàm emphatica, cum significationem ministerii includat. Matth. 4. v. 11.cap. 8. v. 15.cap. 20. v. 28.Luc. 22. v. 26.Ioh. 12. v. 2. &c. Innuit ergò Apostolus, quod propter dona illa nemo sese debeat supra alios efferre, aut dominium in alios affectare, sed aliorum ministrum sese sponte constituere, adeoque donis divinitùs sibi concessis non solùm promtè, sed etiam cum vera humilitate & modestia in aliorum commodum uti. Syrus habet. Unusquisque, ex vobis donum quod accepit à Deo[consult facsimile image][consult facsimile image]suppeditet proximis suis, inserviat eo proximis[consult facsimile image] radix Syris & Chaldaeis propria significat servivit, ministravitMatth. 25. v. 44.Act. 13. v. 36. &c.

Ώς καλοὶ ὀικονόμοι ποικίλης χάριτος θεοῦ. Regius Codex habet, κληρονόμούheredes, ut respondeat voculae ἒλαβε Sed probatiores Codices legunt ὀκονόμοι, quo modo etiam vulgata reddidit, sicut boni dispensatores, ac Syrus [consult facsimile image] dispensatores, oeconomi, Matth. 20. v. 8.Luc. 16. v. 1. habetur coniunctum [consult facsimile image]

Per Χὰριν μετωνυμικῶς intelligit χάρισμα donum ex gratia datum, ac proinde ποικίλης χάριτος Apostolo hoc loco idem est ac ποικίλων χαρισμάτων, ut constat ex praecedentibus, unde vulgata utrobique reddidit gratiam.ποκίλης Vulgata reddidit multiformis. Sed Graecum est significantius, Hieronymus lib. 1. contra Iovin. cap. 4. reddidit, variae, Epist. 50. ad Pamm. multiplicis. Syrus [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image]divisit, separavit, distinxit. Respicit ergò Apostolus ad locum parallelum 1. Cor. 12. v. 4.διαιρέσεις χαρισμάτων εἰσὶdivisiones sunt donorum i. e. dona sunt diversa & varia, maximè à se invicem diflerentia; dicuntur enim διαιρέσεις χαρισμάτων non tàm à distribuendo, quàm à differendo. Item ad parabolam Salvatoris Matth. 25. v. 15.Luc. 19. v. 13.Uni dedit quinque talenta, alii autem duo, alii vero unum, unicuique secundùm propriam virtutem. Quaecunque vero ac quantacunque dona quispiam accepit, illa debet ad proximi & Ecclesiae salutem conferre, adeoque in eorum dispensatione & usu sese fidelem supremi Domini oeconomum demonstrare, unde Lyranus ad h. l. sic annotat, tanquam boni dispensatores gratiae Dei, Domino vestro conformes, quidat gratis & liberaliter. Loca parallela sunt Rom. 12. v. 6.ἒχοντες δέ χαρίσματα κατὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν διαφορὰ.Eph. 4. v. 7.Unicuique, datur gratia secundùm mensuras donationis Christi1. Cor. 12. v. 4.divisiones suntχαρισμάτων,v. 5.divisionesδιακονιῶν.v. 6.divisionesἐνεργημάτων &c.

## 4:11
IF ANY MAN SPEAKS, AS THE ORACLES OF GOD. IF ANY MAN MINISTERS, AS OF THE ABILITY, WHICH GOD ADMINISTERS, THAT IN ALL THINGS GOD MAY BE GLORIFIED THROUGH JESUS CHRIST, TO WHOM IS GLORY AND DOMINION FOR EVER AND EVER, AMEN.

Connection. I. This is the fifth virtue, to which the Apostle exhorts Christians, especially those established in public offices, namely faithfulness in the administration of the duty committed to each one.

2. By Τὰ χαρίσματα in the preceding verse the Apostle understands not only sanctifying gifts, or graces freely given, but also diverse functions in the Church, and virtues necessary for their administration, as is gathered from parallel passages. Rom. 12. v. 6.Having χαρίσματα according to the grace, that is given to us, differences, or prophecy according to the analogy of faith.v. 7.or ministry, in ministering, or he that teacheth, in doctrine.v. 8.He that exhorteth, in exhortation; he that giveth, in simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.1. Cor. 12. vers. 4.there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.vers. 5.And there are differences διακονιῶν of administrations, but the same Lord.vers. 6.And there are diversities ἐνεργημάτων of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. Truly some think that one and the same gifts of God are called χαρίσματα, that a gratuitous donation may be indicated; διακονίας, that their use toward others may be indicated; ἐνεργήματα, that we may know those gifts to be efficacious. But it is more harmonious διακονίας & ἐνεργήματα to accept them as two distinct species χαρισμάτων, so that by διακονίας ecclesiastical offices may be understood; by ἐνεργήματα the virtues of working miracles. Eph. 4. vers. 8.He ascended up on high, he gave δόματα gifts unto men. vers. 11. And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers.1. Tim. 4. v. 14.Neglect not χάρισμα ἐν σοί, the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.2. Tim. 1. v. 4.Stir up τό χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ, the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. In all these places by χαρίσματα are understood not only ministering gifts, but also the ecclesiastical functions themselves, in which signification Peter also uses the word χαρίσματος in the preceding verse, and therefore he passes from the genus to the species, from the thesis to the hypothesis. Nor, however, does he enumerate all χαρισμάτων the species of them or many in detail, but he brings forward two as it were genera of them, under which, according to the custom used among the Hebrews, he comprehends many special charisms. Those indeed are, the one of speech, the other of ministry or action.

3. Lyranus brings forward such a connection. Because in the use of grace freely given a right intention is required, therefore it is added. If any man speak the words of exhortation, as the oracles of God i. e. let him attribute the whole good to God, and not to himself. If any man minister to the needy temporal goods, as of the ability which God giveth i. e. let him attribute this to God, who gave him the will and the faculty of doing this.

Disposition. A twofold exhortation is proposed in this verse. The former looks to the Doctors of the Church, whom he exhorts that in the Church they not propose human dreams, but divine oracles. The latter looks to whosoever performs any Ecclesiastical office, whom he exhorts that they may faithfully perform their office, and according to the strength which God deigns to supply from grace, may minister to their neighbor. He confirms both exhortations by the effect or the salutary consequence, namely the glorification of GOD through Christ, to which argument he attaches the δοξολογίαν customary to the Apostles.

Exposition of the text. Ἐι τις λαλεῖ Vulg. If any man speak. John Huss understands this in a general sense of all Christians, whom he thinks are to be admonished that they speak the words of GOD, so that the sense may be: Let your words be of GOD and in GOD, directed to the glory of God alone. Eph. 4. v. 29. Let no corrupt communication σαπρὸς (filthy, rotten, shameless, which shows that the soul is dead in sins, just as rottenness proves that an animal is dead, from which a foul odor exhales. Psal. 5. v. 11. Rom. 3. v. 13.) proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. Coloss. 4. v. 6. Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt ( lest it become σαπρὸς ) But the circumstances of the text and the parallel passage Rom. 12. v. 6. show that this exhortation is special, directed to those who perform the public duty of teaching in the Church. Therefore, the Apostle embraces both with the word λαλεῖν,, namely both the function of teaching itself, and the gifts necessary for duly performing this vocation, so that the sense may be: If anyone has received from GOD χαρίσματα for teaching (to which are referred λόγος σοφίας, λόγος γνώσεως 1. Cor. 12. v. 8. προφητεία, διάκρισις πνευμάτων, γένη γλωσσῶν, ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν vers. 10.) and is called to perform this duty in the Church (that he may prophesy, i.e., interpret Scripture, Rom. 12. v. 6. teach v. 7. exhort v. 8. and console), let him speak (for this word is to be understood from the preceding Rom. 12. vers. 8. whence the Syrian clearly expressed it) ὡς λόγια θεοῦ. The Vulgate rendered it as the words of God. In the Greek it is as the oracles of God, in which way the same Interpreter rendered the same little word Rom. 3. v. 2. The sense is that a Doctor of the Church ought not to bring forth human dreams, but divine oracles, that he ought not to preach anything in the Church which is not agreeable to the word of God, which exposition is gathered from the parallel passage Rom. 12. vers. 6. Having χαρίσματα according to the grace that is given to us, with difference, εἲ τε προφητείαν, κατὰ τὴν ἀνὰλογίαν τῆς πίστεως, that is, If any man has the gift of interpreting the Scriptures,1. Corinth. 14. vers. 29. let him institute the interpretation in such a way that it agrees with the articles of faith, and the more principal chapters of Christian doctrine, manifestly proposed in the clear places of Scripture.

Ἐί τις διακονεῖ. Vulg. If any man ministers. This διακονία is expounded in various ways. 1. Some take it concerning political offices, by that argument, that in the preceding member it had been acted concerning the office of Ecclesiastical teaching, and also that the MagistrateRoman. 13. vers. 4. is called θεοῦ διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν. 2. Oecumenius takes it concerning those who distribute food and other subsidies to poor brothers. 3. Some expound it specifically concerning that office, which the Deacons performed in the Apostolic and primitive Church, whose duty it was διακονεῖν τραπέζαις, Actor. 6. v. 2.to distribute the goods of the Church collected in common to the poor and widows. 4. Akin to this exposition is that some take this διακονίαν concerning the administration of the Sacraments, because those Deacons of the primitive Church were not excluded from the ministry of the word, and the administration of the Sacraments.Actor. 6. vers. 10.cap. 8. vers. 5. 5. Some take it, as a general precept pertaining to all Christians. Whoever ministers or serves his neighbor with any gift divinely granted to him. Beda in h. l. 6. From the circumstances of the text and parallel places Roman. 12. vers. 6. & 7.1. Corinth. 12. vers. 5. & 28. it is gathered, that by διακονίαν in this place is understood any ministries in the Church, distinct from the office of teaching, of which he had acted in the preceding member, so that the sense may be. If any man ministers serving the Church either by administering the Sacraments, or by taking care of the poor and the sick, or by governing morals, or by inspecting the state of the Church. Therefore there pertain to this διακονίαν τά χαρίσμα ἰαμάτων 1. Corinth. 12. v. 9. ἀντιλήψεις, κυβερνήσεις v. 28. and Διακονούντων under the name come μεταδιδόντες, προϊστάμενοι, ἐλεοῦντες. Roman. 12. v. 8. διακονοῦτες ταῖς τραπέζαις Actor. 6. v. 2. πρεσβύτερος προεστῶτες 1. Tim. 5. v. 17. etc. If any man therefore performs such any ministry in the Church.

Ὡς ἐξ ἰσχύος, ἧς χορηγεῖ ὁ θεὸς, as of the strength, which GOD supplies, understand διακονῄ let him minister, which word is to be repeated equally from the preceding, as the word λαλῇ loquaim in the former member. (In the Complutensian and Royal Bibles, for ᾖς, ὡς is read erroneously.) Indeed, a variety of expositions occurs also in this place. 1. Some refer it to the divine calling, so that the sense may be: Let him acknowledge himself called by GOD to this office, and made fit, therefore let him faithfully administer it. 2. Corinth. 2. v. 15. πρὸς ταῦτα τις ἱκανὸς; cap. 3. v. 6. ὁ θεὸς ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνου καινῆς διαθήκης, 2. Some judge it to be the opposite πολυπραγμοσὸνῃ, than in this very cap. v. 15. the Apostle enumerates most grave and enormous crimes, so that the sense may be: Let him not go beyond the limits of his calling, nor arrogantly attempt anything beyond his strength outside his calling. 3. Some accept it as a precept of humility and modesty, so that the sense may be: Let him not trust in his own prudence and industry, nor think that a prosperous success in his office is the work of his own powers, but let him seek the prudence and strength for acting from GOD, and perform his office in true and serious humility. Beda in h. l. Let each one expend for his neighbor every good that he can, so much the more humbly, as he most certainly knows that he cannot have from himself what he expends. Lyranus. Let him attribute this to GOD, who gave the will and the faculty of doing this. This exposition is confirmed by what follows, that GOD may be glorified. 4. Some accept it as a precept of fortitude, so that the sense may be, that he ought to minister in virtue, i. e. not only rightly and faithfully, but also valiantly, strenuously, generously, overcoming all difficulties, fearing no one's power or envy, knowing themselves to be ministers of GOD, and to be moved, ruled, and protected by Him. 5. Some accept it simply as a precept of faithfulness. If any ministry in the Church is committed to anyone, let him execute it as if from the virtue or powers which GOD supplies, h. e. let him not act remissly and languidly, but faithfully with all his strength; let him not hide his talent, nor bury the gifts given to him divinely, but let him administer the duty enjoined upon him so holily and sincerely, and direct everything to the edification of the Church and the utility of men, so that it may appear that GOD is working powerfully and effectively through this his ministry. This exposition is the simplest of all, to which the others, as not being adverse but subordinate to it, can also be accommodated. For what else is sought in a steward, than that he be found faithful 1. Cor. 4. v. 2. What follows also agrees beautifully with the same.

Ἵνα ἐν πᾶσι δοξάζηται ὁ θεὸς. Vulg. that in all things God may be glorified. In Greek, may be honored. The Syriac adds, that in all things [consult facsimile image] [consult facsimile image] which you are doing, (which προσδιορισμὸς transferred here from 1. Cor. 10. v. 31.) [consult facsimile image] God may be affected with honor, praised, celebrated. The particle ἵνα in this place is not only ἐκβατικὴ, demonstrating that from the faithfulness which we apply in administering our office, the honor and glory of God follows, but also αἰτιατικὴ, demonstrating the ultimate end, which everyone ought to have prefixed for himself in his calling, which is not our glory, but God's. For the Apostle seems to look back to the saying of the Master Matth. 5. v. 16. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father, who is in heaven, from which it is also gathered that τὸ έν πᾶσι is more rightly accepted here as a neuter referring to gifts and actions, than as a masculine referring to men. The parallel passage 1. Cor. 10. v. 31. and the Syriac version in this place also prove the same thing.

Διὰ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ. The Syriac has by the hand of Jesus Christ, which is a Hebrew phrase πλεοναστικὴ.

ᾧ ἐστὶν ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αὶώνων, Αμλὴν. To whom is glory, i. e. to whom alone all glory is owed, who is blessed and glorious, just as the Hebrews also say הקבה holy, blessed is he, that is, God worthy of all praise and proclamation: or היתה whose name is blessed. To whom also belongs κράτος strength, dominion, principality and power, for he himself is גבור mighty, Deuter. 10. vers. 17. שדי omnipotent, Gen. 17. v. 1. cap. 49. v. 25. The Syriac rendered it by a cognate noun [consult facsimile image] honor, because power is honorable. Peter seems to look back to the clause of the Lord's prayer, which he had heard from the mouth of the Master. Matth. 6. v. 13. ὃτι σου ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμὴν. That it is a genuine part of that prayer is evident from the fact that it is found in all Greek copies, that Chrysostom, Theophylact and Euthymius interpret it, that it exists in the Syriac paraphrase, that it is conformable The parallel passages of Holy Scripture &c. are 1. Paral. 29. v. 11.Yours, O Lord, is the magnificence and power and glory and victory and honor, for all things that are in heaven and on earth are yours; yours, O Lord, is the kingdom and the exaltation above every Prince.Rom. 11. v. 36. αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Αμὴν. cap. 16. v. 27. ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ἀμὴν Gal. 1. v. 5. ᾧ ἡ δόξα είς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν. Eph. 3. v. 21. αὐτᾧ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν χριστῷ Ιησοῦ εἰς πᾶσας τὰς γενεὰς τοῦ αἰῶνος τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν. Phil. 4. v. 20. τῷ δε θεῷ καὶ, πατρὶ ἡμῶν ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν. 1. Timoth. 6. v. 16. ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον, ἀμὴν 2. Timoth. 4. v. 18. ὧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Αμὴν. Hebr. 13. vers 21. ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν. 1. Petr. 5. vers. 11. αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν. 2. Petr. 3. vers. 18. αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς ἡμέραν αἰῶνος, ἀμὴν. Iudae v. 25. μόνῳ σοφῷ θεῷ σωτῆρι ἠμῶν δόξα καὶ μεγαλοσύνη, κράτος καὶ ἐξουσὶα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας, Αμὴν. Apocal. 1. v. 6. αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τό κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμὴν; from which it appears δοξολογίαν that this was familiar to the Apostles, and frequent in the Epistles. The little word Αμὴν in this place is not so much of one wishing, as of one asserting and confirming, as appears from the preceding particle ἒστι, in which meaning it is used here and there in the Evangelical History, when Christ says: Amen, Amen, I say to you, as also 2. Cor. 1. v. 20.the promises of God in Christ are ναὶ, & ἀμὴν, and it is rendered by the particle ἀληθῶς. Ierem. 28. v. 6.Luc. 21. v. 3. ( Marc. 12. v. 43.)

Latin:

SI QUIS LOQUITUR, QUASI SERMONES DEI. SI QUIS MINISTRAT, TANQUAM EX VIRTUTE, QUAM ADMINISTRAT DEUS, UT IN OMNIBUS HONORIFICETUR DEUS PER IESUM CHRISTUM, CUI EST GLORIA & IMPERIUM IN SECULA SECULORUM, AMEN.

Connexio. I. Quinta haec est virtus, ad quam Apostolus Christianos, praesertim in publicis officiis constitutos hortatur, videlicet fidelitas in muneris unicuique commissi administratione.

2. Per Τὰ χαρίσματα in versu praeced. Apostolus non solùm intelligit dona sanctificantia, sive gratias gratis datas, sed etiam diversas functiones in Ecclesia, & virtutes ad earum administrationem necessarias, ut colligitur ex locis parallelis. Rom. 12. v. 6.Habentesχαρίσματαsecundùm gratiam, quae data est nobis, differentiae, sive Prophetiam secundùm analogiam fidei.v. 7.sive ministerium, in ministrando, sive qui docet, in doctrina.v. 8.Qui exhortatur, in exbortando; qui tribuit, in simplicitate; qui praeest, in solicitudine; qui miseretur, in hilaritate.1. Cor. 12. vers. 4.divisiones sunt idem autem Spiritus.vers. 5.Et divisionesδιακονιῶνsunt, idem autem Dominus.vers. 6.Et divisionesἐνεργημάτωνsunt, idem vero Deus, qui operatur omnia in omnibus. Sanè quidam existimant, una atque eadem Dei dona vocariχαρίσματα,ut indicetur gratuita donatio;διακονίας,ut indicetur eorum usus ergaalios;ἐνεργήματα,ut sciamus, dona illa esse efficacia. Sed concinnius est διακονίας & ἐνεργήματα accipere, ut duas distinctas species χαρισμάτων, ut per διακονίας intelligantur officia Ecclesiastica; per ἐνεργήματα virtutes operandi miracula. Eph. 4. vers. 8.Ascendit in altum, de ditδόματαdona hominibus. vers. 11. Et ipse dedit quosdam quidem Apostolos, quosdam autem Prophetas, alios vero Evangelistas, alios autem Pastores & Doctores.1. Tim. 4. v. 14.Noli negligereχάρισμα ἐν σοί,quod tibi datum per Prophetiam cum impositione manuum Presbyterii.2. Tim. 1. v. 4.Exuscitesτό χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ,quod est in te per impositionem manuum mearum. In his locis omnibus per χαρίσματα intelliguntur non solùm dona ministrantia, sed etiam ipsae functiones Ecclesiasticae, in qua significatione etiam Petrus voce χαρίσματος in versu praeced. utitur, ac proinde transit à genere ad speciem, à thesi ad hypothesin. Nec tamen omnes χαρισμάτων illorum species aut multas particulatim enumerat, sed duo velut genera eorum prosert, sub quibus more apud Hebraeos usitato multa specialia charismata comprehendit. Ea vero sunt, alterum sermonis, alterum ministerii sive actionis.

3. Lyranus talem profert connexionem. Quia in usugratiae gratis datae requiritur intentio recta, ideo subditur. Si quis loquitur exhortationis verba, quasi sermones Dei i. e. totum bonum attribuat Deo, & non sibi. Si quis ministrat egentibus bona temporalia, tanquam ex virtute, quam administrat Deus i. e. attribuat hoc Deo, qui dedit sibi voluntatem & facultatem hoc faciendi.

Dispositio. Duplex proponitur in hoc versiculo exhortatio. Prior spectat ad Ecclesiae Doctores, quos hortatur ut in Ecclesia non proponant humana somnia, sed divina oracula. Posterior spectat ad quosvis officio aliquo Ecclesiastico fungentes, quos hortatur, ut fideliter officium suum faciant, & pro viribus, quas Deus ex gratia suppeditare dignatur, proximo ministrent. Utramque exhorrationem confirmat ab effectu sive consequente salutari, videlicet glorificatione DEI per Christum, cui argumento annectit δοξολογίαν Apostolis usitatam.

Textus expositio. Ἐι τις λαλεῖ Vulg. Si quis loquitur. Iohannes Huss. in genere de omnibus Christianis intelligit, quos admoneri existimat, ut loquantur sermones DEI, ut sit sensus. Sermones vestri sint de DEO & in DEO, ad solius Dei gloriam directi.Eph. 4. v. 29.Omnis sermoσαπρὸς (turpis, putris, impudicus, qui animam in peccatis mortuam esse ostendit, sicut putredo arguit animal esse mortuum, ex quo foetidus odor exhalat. Psal. 5. v. 11.Rom. 3. v. 13.) ex ore vestro non procedat, sed si quis bonus ad aedificationem fidei, ut det gratiam audientibus.Coloss. 4. v. 6.Sermo vester sit semper in gratia sale conditus ( ne fiatσαπρὸς) Sed circumstantiae textus ac locus parallelus Rom. 12. v. 6. ostendunt, hanc exhortationem esse specialem, directam ad eos, qui publico docendi munere in Ecclesia funguntur. Utrumque igitur complectitur Apostolus verbo λαλεῖν, videlicet tùm ipsam docendi functionem, tùm dona ad hanc vocationem ritè peragendam necessaria, ut sis sensus. Si quis accepità DEO χαρίσματα ad docendum (ad quae referuntur λόγος σοφίας, λόγος γνώσεως1. Cor. 12. v. 8.προφητεία, διάκρισις πνευμάτων, γένη γλωσσῶν, ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶνvers. 10.) & ad hoc munus in Ecclesia peragendum vocatus est (ut prophetet i. e. Scripturam interpretetur, Rom. 12. v. 6. doceat v. 7. exhortetur v. 8. & consoletur) is loquatur (hoc enim verbum ex praecedentibus subintelligendum Rom. 12. vers. 8. unde Syrus illud disertè expressit) ὡς λόγια θεοῦ. Vulgata reddidit quasi sermones Dei. in Graeco est tanquam eloquia Dei, quomodo eandem voculam idem Interpres reddidit Rom. 3. v. 2. sensus est, quod Doctor Ecclesiae non debeat humana somnia, sed divina oracula proferre, quòd non debeat quicquam in Ecclesia praedicare, quod non sit verbo Dei consentaneum, quae expositio colligitur ex loco parallelo Rom. 12. vers. 6.Habentesχαρίσματα secundum gratiam, quae data est nobis, differentiâ,εἲ τε προφητείαν, κατὰ τὴν ἀνὰλογίαν τῆς πίστεως, id est, Si quis habet donum interpretandi Scripturas,1. Corinth. 14. vers. 29. interpretationem ita instituat, ut congruat cum articulis fidei, & principalioribus doctrinae Christianae capitibus, in perspicuis Scripturae locis manifestè propositis.

Ἐί τις διακονεῖ. Vulg. Si quis ministrat. Variis modis haec διακονία exponitur. 1. Quidam accipiunt de politicis officiis, argumento eo, quòd in praecedente membro actum fuerit de officio docendi Ecclesiastico, quoque, MagistratusRoman. 13. vers. 4. dicatur θεοῦ διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν. 2. Oecumenius accipit de illis, qui alimenta alique, subsidia in fratres pauperes erogant. 3. Quidam exponunt in specie de officio illo, quo fungebantur Diaconi in Ecclesia Apostolica & primitiva, quorum munus eratδιακονεῖν τραπέζαις,Actor. 6. v. 2.bona Ecclesiae in commune collata pauperibus & viduis erogare. 4. Cui expositioni affine est, quòd quidam hanc διακονίαν accipiunt de administratione Sacramentorum, quia Diaconi illi Ecclesiae primitivae à ministerio verbi, & administratione Sacramentorum non erant exclusi.Actor. 6. vers. 10.cap. 8. vers. 5. 5. Quidam accipiunt, tanquam generale praeceptum ad omnes Christianos pertinens. Quicunque dono aliquo divinitùs sibi concesso proximo ministrat sive inservit. Beda in h. l. 6. Ex textûs circumstantiis & locis parallelis Roman. 12. vers. 6. & 7.1. Corinth. 12. vers. 5. & 28. colligitur, per διακονίαν hoc loco intelligi quaevis ministeria in Ecclesia, à docendi officio, de quo in praeced. membro egerat, distincta, ut sit sensus. Si quis ministrat Ecclesiae inserviens vel Sacramenta administrando, vel pauperum & aegrotorum curam agendo, vel mores regendo, vel Ecclesiae statum inspiciendo. Pertinent ergò ad hanc διακονίαν τά χαρίσμα ἰαμάτων1. Corinth. 12. v. 9.ἀντιλήψεις, κυβερνήσειςv. 28. ac Διακονούντων nomine veniunt μεταδιδόντες, προϊστάμενοι, ἐλεοῦντες.Roman. 12. v. 8.διακονοῦτες ταῖς τραπέζαιςActor. 6. v. 2.πρεσβύτερος προεστῶτες1. Tim. 5. v. 17. &c. Si quis ergò tali aliquo ministerio in Ecclesia fungitur.

Ὡς ἐξ ἰσχύος, ἧς χορηγεῖ ὁ θεὸς,tanquam ex virtute, quam DEUS suppeditat, subintellige διακονῄministret, quod verbum aequè ex praecedentibus repetendum, ac verbum λαλῇ loquaim in priore membro. (In Complutensibus & Regiis Bibliis pro ᾖς mendosè legitur ὡς) Occurrit vero etiam hoc loco expositionum varietas. 1. Quidam referunt, ad divinam vocationem, ut sit sensus. Agnoscat se à DEO ad hoc officum vocatum, & idoneum factum, ideò fideliter illud administret.2. Corinth. 2. v. 15.πρὸς ταῦτα τις ἱκανὸς;cap. 3. v. 6.ὁ θεὸς ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνου καινῆς διαθήκης, 2. Quidam censent, oppositum esseπολυπραγμοσὸνῃ,quam in hoc ipsocap. v. 15.gravissimis & enormibus delictis Apostolus annumerat, ut sit sensus. Non egrediatur vocationis limites, nec extra vocationem suam supra vires aliquid arroganter attentet. 3. Quidam accipiunt, ut praeceptum humilitatis & modestiae, ut sit sensus. Non confidat suae prudentiae & industriae, nec existimet, prosperum in officio successum esse opus suarum virium, sed agendi prudentiam & vires à DEO petat, & in vera ac seria humilitate officium suum faciat. Beda in h. l. Tantò humilius impendat quisque proximo omne bonum, quod potest, quantò certissimè novit, quòd à semetipso non potest habere, quod impendat. Lyranus. Attribuat hoc DEO, qui dedit voluntatem & facultatem hoc faciendi. Hanc expositionem confirmat, quòd sequitur, ut glorificetur DEUS. 4. Quidam accipiunt, ut praeceptum fortitudinis, ut sit sensus, debere eum ministrare in virtute, i. e. non tantaem rectè & fideliter, sed & valenter, strenuè, generosè, vincendo omnes difficultates, nullius potentiam vel invidiam timendo, scientes se DEI esse ministros, ab eoque, agi, regi & protegi. 5. Quidam accipiunt simpliciter, ut praeceptum fidelitatis. Si cui ministerium aliquod in Ecclesia commissum, exequatur illud, tanquam ex virtute sive viribus, quas DEUS suppeditat, h. e. non agat remissè & languidè, sed fideliter ex totis viribus; talentum suum non abscondat, nec dona divinitùs sibi data sepeliat, sed munus sibi iniunctum tàm sanctè ac sincerè administret, & ad Ecclesiae aedificationem ac hominum utilitatem omnia dirigat, ut appareat, DEUM per hoc suum ministerium potenter & efficaciter operari. Haec expositio est omnium simplicissima, ad quam etiam reliquae utpote eidem non adversae, sed subordinatae accommodari possunt. Quid enim aliud in dispensatore quaeritur, quàm ut fidelis inveniatur 1. Cor. 4. v. 2. Eidem etiam pulchrè congruit, quod sequitur.

Ἵνα ἐν πᾶσι δοξάζηται ὁ θεὸς. Vulg. ut in omnibus glorificetur Deus. In Graeco, honorificetur. Syrus addit, ut in omnibus[consult facsimile image][consult facsimile image]quae facientes estis vos, (qui προσδιορισμὸς huc translatus ex 1. Cor. 10. v. 31.) [consult facsimile image]honore afficiatur, laudetur, celebretur Deus. Particula ἵνα h. l. non solùm est ἐκβατικὴ, demonstrans ex fidelitate, quam in officio administrando adhibemus, consequi Dei honorem & gloriam, sed etiam αἰτιατικὴ, demonstrans ultimum finem, quem quilibet in vocatione sua sibi praefixum habere debet, qui est non nostra, sed Dei gloria. Videtur enim Apostolus respicere ad dictum Magistri Matth. 5. v. 16.Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant opera vestra bona, & glorificent Patrem vestrum, qui in coelis est, ex quo etiam colligitur, τὸ έν πᾶσι rectiùs hîc accipi, ut neutrum ac ad dona & actiones referatur, quàm ut masculinum & ad homines referatur. Idipsum etiam probat locus parallelus 1. Cor. 10. v. 31. & versio Syriaca h. l.

## 4:12
BELOVED, DO NOT BE SURPRISED AT THE BURNING (WHICH HAPPENS TO YOU FOR A TRIAL) AS THOUGH SOME STRANGE THING WERE HAPPENING TO YOU.

Connection. 1. The Apostle has hitherto exhorted the converted and the faithful to the mortification of the flesh and the innocence of life; now furthermore he exhorts them to sustain persecution, and to show patience under the cross. From this verse 12, therefore, begins the latter part of this chapter.

2. Lyranus hands down a connection of this kind. The Apostle had hitherto ordered the faithful in the matter of their neighbor in the communication of goods, now furthermore he orders them in the enduring of evils from the adversaries of the faith, whence by these he invites them to the glory of Martyrdom.

3. From the exhortation to the solicitous administration of the imposed function, he passes to an exhortation, already proposed before chap. 1. v. 6. & 7.chap. 2. v. 19. 20. & 21.chap. 3. v. 13. 14. & 17. by which he urges them to the tolerance of persecutions brought on account of the confession of Christ. For whoever applies due faithfulness and industry in an office, especially an Ecclesiastical one, is compelled to sustain the hatreds and persecutions of the world. Hence also the face of a lion is attributed to the four living creatures, by which the Apostles and their successors in the Ministry are denoted Ezechiel. 1. vers. 10. & Apocal. 4. vers. 7. because they ought to have an unbroken spirit against dangers, hatreds, and persecutions.

4. It is the duty of the pious to do good, and patiently to bear evil, therefore the Apostle adds to the exhortation to charity and hospitality an exhortation to the tolerance of adversities. Interlinear Gloss on this passage: Do these good things, and cease for no tribulation.

Disposition. The Apostle warns the faithful, lest they be offended or perturbed by persecutions, as if by a new and unusual thing, by an argument taken from the end, for the sake of which GOD sends such persecutions, which is the testing of our faith, for which reason he compares persecutions to fire, by which gold or silver is explored.

Exposition of the text. ἀγαπητοὶ. The Apostle imitates with this friendly address the example of his Colleagues, Paul Roman. 12. vers. 19.1. Corinth. 4. vers. 13.chap. 10. vers. 14.chap. 15. vers. 58.2. Corinth. 12. vers. 19.Phil. 2. vers. 12.chap. 4. vers. 1.Hebr. 6. vers. 9.James chap. 1. v. 16. & 19.chap. 2. v. 5.John Epist. 1.chap. 3. v. 2. & 21.chap. 4. vers. 1.7. & 11. & Jude vers. 3.17. & 20. indeed of Christ himself, who called his disciples τεκνία, i.e. ἀγαπητὰ. John 13. vers. 33. The Syrian rendered it, my beloved, as if it were in Greek ἀγαπητοί μου, as is had 1. Corinth. 10. vers. 14. &c.

Μὴ ξενίζεσθε τῇ ἐν ὑμῖν πυρώσει. The Vulgate rendered the word ξενίζεσθαι to be a sojourner. Above, verse 4, according to certain Codices it rendered to wonder. Bede also reads to wonder in this place, meanwhile he adds, that in certain Codices it is written to be a stranger. Cyprian in the book on the exhortation of Martyrdom chapter 9, and book 4 Epistle 59. Jerome in the commentary on chapter 4 of Amos likewise read to wonder. Tertullian in Scorpiacus chapter 12, Fulgentius 3 to Thrasimundus chapter 30 read to be terrified. The Syrian has the verb [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael, which signifies both to wonder and to be astonished Matt. 8. verse 10.Mark 6. v. 6.John 3. v. 7.Acts 2. v. 7. & 12.chapter 7. v. 31. where it is placed for θαυμάζειν & ἐκπλήττεσθαι. Peter himself expressed the force of this word best of all, when he added ἐξηγητικῶς, ὡς ξένου ὑμῖν συμβαίνοντος, as if a strange, that is, a new and unusual thing were happening to you. The sense therefore is, that the faithful ought not to be offended by persecutions, as if by a strange and unusual thing, that they ought not to be astonished and rendered thunderstruck by encroaching persecutions, as is accustomed to happen to those who fall into a strange, new, and unusual thing, about which they had not thought before. For from the antecedent the consequent is understood through a certain Metalepsis. Bede explains that ξενίζεσθαι in a double way. Do not wonder in the heat. Some, he says, Codices have. Do not be a stranger in the heat. However, the sense of both words is at hand, because neither should any faithful person wonder why he suffers the heat of tribulations in this life, who for a certain reason is therefore now tempted by tribulations, so that when he has been proved, he may be held worthy to receive the crown of the future life: nor should anyone therefore think himself a stranger and alien from the members of Christ, because he is struck by the adversities of the present age, since both the exit of the Lord's death, and in his Church never from the Protomartyr Abel up to the last elect, who is to be born at the end of the age, has the persecution of the unfaithful ceased, whence well when he had said, do not wonder in the heat, he added, as if something new were happening to you, because it is very ancient and frequent for the elect of GOD to tolerate the adversities of the present life for eternal salvation. The ordinary Gloss in almost the same way. If you suffer the heat of tribulations, do not therefore think that you are exiles from the members of Christ, and do not wonder about the evils brought upon you. Oecumenius in this place. Do not consider this strange from the friends of GOD, since this is proper and glorious to them, that they may be proved like gold by the fire of tribulations. Lyranus departs a little further from the genuine meaning of the word. Do not, he says, be a stranger, i. e. be alienated from the faith. Thus it is explained commonly, it can also be explained otherwise, more literally thus: Do not be strangers, i. e., be removed in body by fear of imminent death. But since we have the interpretation of the Apostle himself, we look around in vain for others.

The Vulgate rendered the little word πύρωσιν as fervor, Tertullian in the same place as burning; Cyprian and Jerome in the same place as ardor. Apocal. 18. v. 9. and 18, the Vulgate rendered by conflagration. πυροῦσθαι is to be burned, to burn, to be ignited Eph. 6. v. 16.2. Petr. 3. v. 12.Apocal. 1. v. 15.cap. 3. v. 18. therefore πύρωσις is a burning, an ignition. It is known in the Holy Scriptures that by fire are denoted more serious afflictions of every kind, for the reason that they are as troublesome to flesh and blood as fire is to the body. Ps. 17. v. 3.Psal. 66. v. 10.Esa. 48. v. 10.Dan. 12. v. 10.Zach. 13. v. 9. hence πύρωσις in this place is used for the more serious afflictions which the pious are compelled to sustain in this life in the flesh, and especially for the persecutions which they sustain on account of the confession of the name of Christ; as is evident from v. 14. and 16. The LXX use it for כור, which signifies a crucible or a furnace, in which gold is tested by fire. Proverb. 27. vers. 21. The Syrian rendered ἐξηγητικῶς by [consult facsimile image] which signifies temptations, just as the Greek Scholia also explain ἐν πυρώσει, i. e. ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ, which happens through tribulations, as if through fire. But πύρωσις does not properly signify temptation or exploration, but burning, i. e. serious affliction. Furthermore, when the Apostle says, μὴ ξενίζεσθαι τῇ ἐν ὑμῖν πυρώσει, he signifies that that burning or affliction befalls and is sent upon the pious, and as it were seizes them, just as fire seizes and inflames combustible material. The Vulgate omitted that ἐν ὑμῖν entirely; the Syrian supplied the ellipsis of the particle οὔσῃ. For he rendered it thus: Do not be astonished because of the temptations [consult facsimile image] which are or which happen to you. Cyprian, book 4, Epistle 6: Do not marvel at the burning happening to you.

Πρὸς πειρασμὸν ὑμῖν γινομένῃ. These words are interposed as if by a parenthesis, and contain the reason why the pious ought not to marvel or be astonished at the persecutions brought upon them, as if at a strange and unusual thing, namely because they are divinely sent for a very good end. The Royal and Complutensian codices read, which to that it may be a temptation to you. But in the Greek it is γινομένῃ, more correctly therefore Tertullian in the same place a burning, which is happening in you for a temptation. Cyprian a burning happening to you, which is done for your temptation. Whence the Syrian cast it to the end of the verse, thus ordering the text. Do not be astonished because of the temptations, which happen to you, as if some strange or foreign thing were happening to you, because they are done for your probation. Πειρασμὸς signifies probation and exploration, which is done through afflictions and persecutions, just as gold is accustomed to be proved and examined by fire, whence between πύρωσιν and πειρασμὸν there is a sweet paronomasia. Sap. 3. v. 5. God ἐπείρασεν αὐτοὺς, tempted them and found them worthy of himself, vers. 6. as gold in the furnace ἐδοκίμασεν αὐτοὺς he proved them. Iac. 1. v. 2. Count it all joy my brethren, ὃταν περιπέσητε πειρασμοῖς ποικίλοις, v. 3. knowing ὃτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν. v. 12. Blessed is the man, who endures πειρασμὸν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς. 1. Petr. 1. v. 6. having been grieved a little in various πειρασμοῖς. v. 7. ἵνα τὀ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως πολὺ τεμιώ τερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου, διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου εὐρεθῆ, which places are parallel to this one of ours, and show, that πειρασμὸν respects faith, which like precious gold is proved through the fire of tribulation.

Latin:

CARISSIMI, NOLITE PEREGRINARI IN FERVORE (QUI AD TENTATIONEM VOBIS FIT) QUASI NOVI ALIQUID VOBIS CONTINGAT.

Connexio. 1. Exhortatus fuit hactenus Apostolus conversos & fideles ad carnis mortificationem & vitae innocentiam; iam portò exhortatur eos ad sustinendam persecutionem, & praestandam in cruce patientiam. Ab hoc igitur versiculo 12. incipit posterior pars huius capitis.

2. Lyranus eiusmodi tradit connexionem. Ordinaverat hactenus Apostolus fideles ratione proximi in communicatione bonorum, iam porrò eos ordinat in perpessione malorum ab adversariis fidei, unde his invitat eos ad gloriam Martyrii.

3. Ab exhortatione ad solicitam functionis impositae administrationem, transit ad exhortationem, iam antè propositam cap. 1. v. 6. & 7.cap. 2. v. 19. 20. & 21.cap. 3. v. 13. 14. & 17. quâ ad tolerantiam persecutionum propter confessionem Christi illatarum eos hortatur. Quisquis enim debitam in officio praesertim Ecclesiastico fidelitatem & industriam adhibet, odia & persecutiones mundi sustinere cogitur. Inde etiam facies leonis tribuitur quatuor animalibus, per quae Apostoli & eorum in Ministerio successores denotantur Ezechiel. 1. vers. 10. & Apocal. 4. vers. 7. quia adversus pericula, odia & persecutiones infractum debent habere animum.

4. Piorum est agere bonum, & patienter ferre malum, ideò exhortationi ad caritatem & hospitalitatem subiungit Apostolus exhortationem ad tolerantiam adversitatum. Glossa interlin. ad h. l. Haec bona facite, & pro nulla tribulatione cessate.

Dispositio. Admonet Apostolus fideles, ne persecutionibus offendantur aut perturbentur, tanquam re novâ & insolita, argumento petito à fine, propter quem DEUS persecutiones eiusmodi immittit, qui est fidei nostrae probatio, quam ob rem persecutiones comparat igni, quo exploratur aurum vel argentum.

Textus expositio. ἀγαπητοὶ. Imitatur hac amicâ compellatione Apostolus exemplum Collegarum, Pauli Roman. 12. vers. 19.1. Corinth. 4. vers. 13.cap. 10. vers. 14.cap. 15. vers. 58.2. Corinth. 12. vers. 19.Phil. 2. vers. 12.cap. 4. vers. 1.Hebr. 6. vers. 9.Iacobi cap. 1. v. 16. & 19.cap. 2. v. 5.Iohannis Epist. 1.cap. 3. v. 2. & 21.cap. 4. vers. 1.7. & 11. & Iudae vers. 3.17. & 20. imò ipsius Christi, qui discipulos suos vocabat τεκνία, sc. ἀγαπητὰ.Iohan. 13. vers. 33. Syrus reddidit, dilecti mei, ac si in Graeco esset ἀγαπητοί μου, uti habetur 1. Corinth. 10. vers. 14. &c.

Μὴ ξενίζεσθε τῇ ἐν ὑμῖν πυρώσει. Verbum ξενίζεσθαι vulgata reddidit peregrinari. Superiùs vers. 4. iuxta quosdam Codices reddidit admirari. Beda etiam hoc loco legit mirari, interim addit, in quibusdam Codicibus scriptum esse peregrinari. Cyprianus lib. de exhort. Martyrii cap. 9. & lib. 4. Epist. 59. Hieronymus in comm. cap. 4. Amos itidem legunt mirari. Tertullianus in Scorpiaco cap. 12. Fulgentius 3. ad Thrasimundum cap. 30. legunt expave scere. Syrus habet verbum. [consult facsimile image] in Ethpaël, quod & admirari & obstupesiere significat Matth. 8. vers. 10.Marc. 6. v. 6.Iohan. 3. v. 7.Actor. 2. v. 7. & 12.cap. 7. v. 31. ubi pro θαυμάζειν & ἐκπλήττεσθαι ponitur. Petrus ipse omnium optimè vim vocis huius expressit, quando ἐξηγητικῶς subiunxit, ὡς ξένου ὑμῖν συμβαίνοντος,ac si peregrinum, h. e. novum & insolitum quid vobis contingat. Sensus igitur, quòd fideles non debeant persecutionibus, tanquam re peregrinâ & insolitâ offendi, quòd ingruentibus persecutionibus non debeant obstupescere ac reddi attoniti, ut contingere solet illis, qui in rem peregrinam, novam & insolitam incidunt, de qua priùs non cogitaverant. Ex antecedente enim intelligitur consequens per quandam Metalepsin. Beda duplici modo illud ξενίζεσθαι exponit. Nolite mirari in fervore. Quidam, inquit, Codices habent. Nolite peregrinari in fervore. Utriusque autem verbi sensus in promtu est, quia neque, mirari fidelis quisque, debet, quare in hac vita fervorem patiatur tribulationum, qui certâ ratione ideò nunc tribulationibus tentatur, ut cum probatus fuerit, ad futurae vitae coronam percipiendam dignus habe atur: neque se aliquis ideò peregrinum & extraneum à Christi membris existimare debet, quia praesentis seculi feriatur adversis, cum & Domini exitus mortis, & in eius Ecclesia nunquam à Protomartyre Abel usque, ad ultimum electum, qui in fine seculi nasciturus est, infidelium persecutio cessaverit, unde benè cum dixisset, nolite mirari in fervore, addidit, quasinovi aliquid vobis contingat, quia valdè est antiquum & frequens, electos DEI vitae praesentis adversa pro aeterna salute tolerare. Glossa ordin. eodem ferè modo. Si patimini fervorem tribulationum, non ideò putetis, vos esse exules à membris Christi, & nolite mirari de illatis malis. Oecum. in h. l. Nolite hoc ab amicis DEI extraneum ducere, cum hoc eis proprium & gloriosum sit, quòd ut aurum igne tribulationibus probentur. Lyranus paulo longiùs à genuina verbi significatione discedit. Nolite, inquit, peregrinari, i. e. à fide alienari. Sic exponitur communiter, potest etiam aliter exponi magis literaliter sic. Nolite peregrinari, i. e. corpore elongari timore mortis imminentis. Sed eum habeamus Apostoli ipsius interpretationem, frustrà de aliis cireum spicimus.

Voculam πύρωσιν vulg. reddidit fervorem, Tertullianus d. l. ustionem; Cyprianus & Hieronymus d. l. ardorem.Apocal. 18. v. 9. & 18. vulgata reddidit per incendium.πυροῦσθαι est uri, ardere, ignitum esse Eph. 6. v. 16.2. Petr. 3. v. 12.Apocal. 1. v. 15.cap. 3. v. 18. ergò πύρωσις est ustio, ignitio. Notum est in Scripturis sacris, per ignem denotari graviores omnis generis afflictiones, propterea quod earni & sanguini tàm sint molestae, quàm corpori est ignis. Ps. 17. v. 3.Psal. 66. v. 10.Esa. 48. v. 10.Dan. 12. v. 10.Zach. 13. v. 9. inde πύρωσις hoc loco usurpatur pro gravioribus afflictionibus, quas pii in hac vita in carne sustinere coguntur, cumprimis vero pro persecutionibus, quas ob nominis Christi confessionem sustinent; ut patet ex v. 14. & 16. LXX utuntur pro כור, quod significat catinum sive fornacem, in quâ autum igne exploratur.Proverb. 27. vers. 21. Syrus ἐξηγητικῶς reddidit per [consult facsimile image] quod significat tentationes, sicut etiam Graeca Scholia explicant ἐν πυρώσει, h. e. ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ, quae fit per tribulationes, velut per ignem. Sed πύρωσις proprie non significat tentationem vel explorationem, sed ustionem, i. e. gravem afflictionem. Caeterùm quando Apostolus dicit, μὴ ξενίζεσθαι τῇ ἐν ὑμῖν πυρώσει, significat, ustionem sive afflictionem illam piis obtingere & immitti, eosque quasi apprehendere, sicut ignis materiam ustibilem apprehendit & inflammat. Vulg. illud ἐν ὑμῖν planè omisit, Syrus ellipsin particulae οὔσῃ supplevit. Sic enim reddidit. Ne obstupe scatis propter tentationes[consult facsimile image]quae sunt vel contingunt vobis. Cyprianus lib. 4. Epist. 6. Nolite mirari ardorem accidentem vobis.

Πρὸς πειρασμὸν ὑμῖν γινομένῃ. Haec verba quasi per parenthesin interponuntur, ac rationem continent, quare pii ob persecutiones ipsis illatas non debeant mirari, vel obstupescere, tanquam ob rem peregrinam & insolitam, nimirum quia optimo fine divinitùs immittuntur. Codices Regii & Complutensis legunt, qui ad tentationem vobis sit. Sed in Graeco est γινομένῃ, rectiùs ergò Tertullianus d. l. ustionem, quae agitur in vobis ad tentationem. Cyprianus ditiardorem accidentem vobis, qui ad tentationem vestram fit. Unde Syrus eareiecit ad finem versiculi, sic ordinans textum. Ne obstupescatis propter tentationes, quae contingunt vobis, tanquam alienum sive peregrinum quiddam eveniat vobis, quia ad probationem vestram fiunt.Πειρασμὸς significat probationem & explorationem, quae fit per afflictiones & persecutiones, sicut aurum igne solet probari & examinari, unde inter πύρωσιν ac πειρασμὸν est suavis paranomasia. Sap. 3. v. 5. Deus ἐπείρασεν αὐτοὺς,tentavit eos & invenit illos dignos se,vers. 6.tanquam aurum in fornaceἐδοκίμασεν αὐτοὺςprobavit illos.Iac. 1. v. 2.Omne gaudium existimate fratres mei,ὃταν περιπέσητε πειρασμοῖς ποικίλοις,v. 3.scientesὃτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν.v. 12.Beatus vir, qui suffertπειρασμὸν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς.1. Petr. 1. v. 6.modicum contristatiin variisπειρασμοῖς.v. 7.ἵνα τὀ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως πολὺ τεμιώ τερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου, διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου εὐρεθῆ, quae loca huic nostro sunt parallela, & ostendunt, illum πειρασμὸν respicere fidem, quae instar preciosi auri per ignem tribulationis probatut.

## 4:12-19 Questions and observations
It is asked here 1. Why the Apostle, about to exhort to patience, premises, ἀγαπητὸι; Resp. 1. Oecumenius gives this reason. By the name itself he signifies that they are not held in hatred by GOD because afflictions befall them, but that they are very dear to him and are loved vehemently. Prov. 3. v. 12. Hebr. 12. v. 6. Apoc. 3. v. 19. 2. He had premised v. 8. the exhortation to mutual charity: therefore by his own example he shows that he sincerely embraces those to whom he writes with the same.

Q. 2. Why does he exhort again to patience? Resp. διὰ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν ἀνάγκην 1. Corinth. 7. v. 26. Those converted to Christianity, especially from Judaism, were hateful to the Gentiles, partly in the name of their nation, partly of their religion, since they were also held in hatred by their own fellow tribesmen 1. Thessal. 2. vers. 14. against these hatreds and persecutions brought on by hatreds, their minds had to be armed and fortified with patience.

Q. 3. Why does he add, πύρωσιν that that affliction happens for πειρασμὸν; Resp. to mitigate the pain of the burning, indeed Think, not for your destruction or condemnation, but that this burning of the cross happens to you for a trial and probation, and therefore is sent to you for a salutary end. Look to the example of Abraham your father, whom GOD likewise tempted Genes. 22. vers. 1. but not for evil, but for good. Iacobi 1. vers. 13.

Q. 4. What is understood by ἀποκάλυψιν τῆς δόξης Χριστοῦ ? Resp. The Apostle insinuates by this, that although Christ, placed at the right hand of the heavenly Father, which is the right hand of power and glory, is glorious in himself, yet in the members of his mystical body he does not yet show that communication of glory, but that on the day of the final judgment, when he is to come in the glory of his Father Matth. 16. vers. 27. with power and great glory cap. 24. vers. 30. in his glory cap. 25. vers. 31. he will finally manifest his glory publicly before Angels and men. The glory of Christ is indeed revealed to the blessed souls of the saints, released from the prison of the body, but the full, perfect, and universal revelation will follow on the day of judgment, when the souls of the blessed, united in turn to their bodies, will see their Savior in glory, and will triumph with him and in him against all enemies, glorified in their resurrected bodies. Col. 3. v. 4. When Christ shall appear your life, then you also shall appear with him in glory. 1. Ioh. 3. v. 2. when he shall appear, we shall be like him. Hence the interlinear Gloss says, then at last that revelation of the glory of Christ will follow, when every veil shall be taken away, which will happen on the day of judgment. Esai. 25. vers. 7. And God will swallow up on the mountain he will destroy the surface of the covering, with which all peoples are covered, and the veil, with which all nations are veiled.v. 8.he will swallow up death forever, and the Lord will take away the tear from every face, etc.

Q. 5. How can it be gathered from the endurance of reproaches and calamities, brought on without merit, that the Spirit of God rests upon him who patiently sustains them? Resp. Because the carnal man is prone not to bear reproaches, but to return them; when, therefore, reproaches and curses brought on account of the name of Christ are patiently tolerated, this is an argument that such a man is regenerated by the Holy Spirit, and consequently also a temple of the Holy Spirit. By this reason God is glorified in the body and Spirit of the reborn 1. Corinth. 6. v. 20. The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of gentleness and meekness,Gal. 6. v. 1. and μακροθυμία & πρᾳότης are the fruits of the Spirit Galat. 5. v. 22. who therefore patiently tolerate reproaches on account of the name of Christ, by that very fact show that the Spirit of Christ dwells in them.

Q. 6. On what occasion does Peter exhort those to whom he wrote, that none of them should suffer as a thief, or a murderer? Resp. Certain persecutors wished to appear to Christians not to be inflicting persecutions simply because they were Christians, but on account of misdeeds; hence they burdened Christians with fabricated crimes and misdeeds, both so that they themselves would not be considered cruel and unjust, and so that Christians would not obtain the glory of martyrdom among their own. Thus it is recorded of Nero, that he transferred the crime of the burning of the city of Rome, which he himself had incited, onto the Christians. Peter therefore gravely exhorts the Christians, that none of them should commit either murder, or theft, or any other crime for which civil laws have established penalties, lest the crime of one be spread by the persecutors to the remaining Christians.

Q. 7. Why does he make mention of murder in particular? Resp. Because the crime of infanticide and of the Thyestean feast was objected to Christians by the Gentiles, as Minutius mentions in Octavius, Tertullian in Apologeticus c. 9, Justin in his oration to Antoninus Pius, Athenagoras in his Apology for the Christians.

Q. 8. Why of theft? Resp. Because certain martyrs were compelled to suffer extreme punishment along with this infamous class of men, so that they might appear to be partners in guilt as they were partners in punishment, for which purpose the Jews also led Christ out to the place of punishment between two thieves.

Eusebius book 6. Ecclesiastical History chapter 40. from the Epistle of Dionysius, Bishop of Alexandria, to Fabius, Bishop of Antioch, concerning the struggles of those who endured martyrdom at Alexandria under the Emperor Decius. A certain Egyptian, Nemesion, is denounced as a companion of robbers; having cleared himself of this calumny as being most foreign to him before the Centurion, he is accused of Christianity, and on this account, bound, he comes before the governor. The most iniquitous judge, however, having afflicted him with tortures and scourges twice as bitterly as the robbers, burns him among the robbers, and renders him blessed and honored by the example of Christ.

Q. 9. Who is properly ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος; Resp. The Vulgate rendered it, a coveter of other men's matters. Estius defends that version, annotating thus on this passage: Mere curiosity about other men's affairs is not among the crimes which are accustomed to be punished by public laws, of which the Apostle speaks here. Therefore, a coveter of other men's matters is understood, namely with effect, that is, greedily gaping after other men's things and taking them where he can. But because it could be objected that mention of this crime had already been made before under the name of theft, Estius adds, this crime differs from theft, because it is not simple theft, but theft or rapacity joined with fraud. It would therefore be called a coveter of other men's matters ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος, because he who covets something, reaches for it. But it is more correctly understood as πολυπραγμοσόνῃ, by which someone invades the boundaries of another's office, strives to take care of those things which pertain to him not at all, thrusts himself into the calling of others without a legitimate calling, and studies to reform everything, when nevertheless he neither understands them nor has been ordered to do them. He proves this explanation. 1. The composition of the word itself. For what else is ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος, than ἀλλοτρίων ἐπίσκοπος, or ἀλλότριος ἐπίσκοπος, one who takes upon himself another's administration, as Budaeus translates in the Areopagite. 2. The exposition of the ancients. Tertullian in Scorpiacum chapter 12 rendered it, a spy of another's affairs. Cyprian in book 4, Epistle 6, and Augustine in the unfinished exposition of the Epistle to the Romans, doing the business of others. 3. The circumstance of time and place. The Apostle writes to those Christians who lived in the midst of Jews and Gentiles. Therefore, without a doubt, certain Christians out of thoughtlessness, rashness, and levity inquired too curiously into the actions of the infidels, as being their neighbors, rebuked them by their own judgment, and wished to be their judges, which did not pertain to their calling.

Q. 10. Why does the Apostle ἀλλοτριοεπισκπην rank [this] among the most serious crimes, for which deserved punishments are owed by the laws? Resp. Some think that Peter is listing in this place not only crimes more serious and prohibited by the laws, but also any others whatsoever that are less becoming to Christians. It could, says Estius, be understood simply as the curiosity of other people's affairs, which renders a man odious, so that Peter is not enumerating only those things which are punished by the laws, but also those by which the minds of men are irritated to do harm. But it is more correctly said that πολυπραγμοσύνην is rightly and deservedly numbered among the most serious sins. 1. Because GOD has distinguished the states and orders of life with grave counsel, whence θεομαχεῖν are rightly called those who transgress the boundaries of the office entrusted to them, and without a calling mix themselves into the offices and business of others. Paul repeats this three distinct times. As God has called each one, so let him walk 1. Cor. 7. v. 17.20. & 24. 2. Those who are curiously busy about the affairs of others easily fall into quarrels and disputes, from which far greater evils arise later. 3. Those who are curious about the affairs of others and things that do not pertain to them are for the most part neglectful of their own.
