But others in this way: Because that which is of the honor, glory, and virtue of GOD, and which is His Spirit, rests upon you. Others, because the Spirit of glory and of GOD rests upon you. But also the word ἀναπάυεται some Latin Codices render by the present, which agrees with the Greek; some by the past, who read ἀναπέπαυται, some by the future, who read ἀναπάυσεται. Tertullian in Scorpiacus cites the passage thus: Because the glory and the Spirit of GOD shall rest upon you. Cyprian, book 4, Epistle 6: Because the name of the majesty and virtue of the Lord rests upon you. For πνεῦμα he reads ὄνομα, as Pamelius advises. The Syrian rendered it, because the Spirit of glory or the glorious [Spirit] of GOD rests upon you. The more common and more used reading is that which our Codices have, ὅτι τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐφ ὑμᾶς ἀναπάυεται. Erasmus advises that this passage can be explained in two ways. In one way, that τὸ τῆς δόξης is taken separately for glory, in which way the Vulgate Interpreter takes the passage, thus rendering it: Because the glory and the Spirit of GOD rests upon you. In the other, that the nominative τὸ πνεῦμα is applied equally to the two preceding genitives, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, the Spirit of glory and of GOD rests upon you. If we wish to embrace the former explanation, it could be thought that the name of glory has respect to that peculiar presence of the Lord in the tabernacle of the covenant. For when the gracious presence of GOD in the tabernacle of the covenant was manifested by some external symbol, then the glory of the Lord was said to appear, Exodus 16. verse 10.chap. 40. v. 34.Lev. 9. verse 23.Numbers 14. v. 10. etc. For as the glory of the LORD in the tabernacle of the covenant typically and

he appeared visibly: so the same dwells through faith and invisibly in all who are truly pious. Ephes. 3. vers. 17. But the latter exposition is more in agreement with the text, as the series of words τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα, shows, which the Syrian also confirms, who, with the conjunction removed, rendered it: The Spirit of the glory of God, or the glorious Spirit of God rests upon you. He calls him the Spirit of glory, not only because he is glorious and praiseworthy in himself, but also because he is the author of our glorification, and therefore he opposes this Spirit of glory to the reproaches and ignominy which are inflicted upon the pious by the world, just as also the Spirit of God, or as 1. Cor. 2. v. 12. Paul speaks, the Spirit which is of God, is opposed to the spirit of the world, by which persecutors, driven and impelled, afflict the pious with reproaches and ignominy on account of the name of Christ. Therefore, the Apostle gives in these words the reason why he called those who are afflicted with reproaches on account of the name of Christ blessed, namely, because the Spirit of God rests upon them, since to patiently sustain reproaches and any adversities whatsoever on account of the name of Christ is an infallible sign of the indwelling Holy Spirit, and he in whom the Holy Spirit graciously dwells cannot but be blessed. And since that Spirit of God is also the Spirit of glory, he therefore consoles and animates believers, who are sustaining reproaches for Christ, against all the ignominy of the world, and confirms them that for the transitory ignominy of the world there is to be rendered to them at some time a heavenly glory that will never die or cease, since to the sons of God is also owed a heavenly inheritance. For those in whom the Spirit of God dwells, they are the sons of God, Rom. 8. v. 16. Gal. 4. v. 6. Therefore, also to those in whom the Spirit of God dwells, the heavenly inheritance is owed, which alone can be most firmly opposed as a consolation to all the reproaches, hatreds, and adversities of the world. The word ἀναπάυεται. also looks to this. For the Apostle alludes to the passage Esa. 11. v. 1. There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. vers. 2. And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him. He signifies, therefore, that the pious have been made partakers of the same [Spirit] with Christ, and therefore have been received by the heavenly Father into the sons of God, therefore because they have been partakers of the Spirit of Christ in sufferings, therefore they will also communicate with Christ in glory through the gift and indwelling of the same Holy Spirit. The word ἀναπάυειν, also hints, which is used concerning the gracious indwelling of the Holy Spirit in the pious, that the Holy Spirit [gives] the rest of conscience, interior joy, and life-giving may supply consolation to the pious in the cross, concerning which that word is used Matth. 11. v. 28.1. Cor. 16. v. 18.2. Cor. 7. v. 13.Philem. v. 7.20. Those who read the name δυνάμεως of virtue inserted into the Apostolic text, refer it to the victory which believers through faith in the cross report over the Devil and his instruments. Gloss. ordin. ad h. l. The Spirit of Christ rests upon you, and in the present in part for doing good, and in the future perfectly for rewarding: which is of honor, so that also in the present you may be honorable in good works, and in the future participants of the honor of Christ; and which is of glory in the present a pure conscience, in the future without all corruption as much in soul as in body; and which is of virtue both in the present and in the future over the Devil and his members. Lyranus ad h. l. Honor is referred to a virtuous work, glory to the testimony of a good conscience, but virtue indeed to the triumph had over the Devil. His Spirit rests upon you, by dwelling in you spiritually, or rests upon you, as a rider upon a horse, leading it according to his pleasure: Thus the Holy Spirit leads such ones according to his instinctRom. 8. vers. 14. The name of virtue can also be referred to the strengths and power which GOD supplies for bravely tolerating reproaches and other calamities.

Κατὰ μὲν αὐτοὺς βλασφημεῖται, κατὰ δὲ ὑμᾶς δοξάζεται. These are not held in the Latin Codices, nor in the Syriac paraphrase, nor in Tertullian in Scorpiacus, where he brings forward this whole passage: whence Lorinus takes it for an addition. Meanwhile they are a genuine part of the text, because they are held in all Greek Codices, and in the commentaries of the Greek Fathers, as Oecumenius testifies. Indeed, Cyprian also in book 4, Epistle 6, brings forward this passage, although with words a little different from the Greek, for he reads in this way. Which indeed according to them is blasphemed, but according to us is honored, so that it may be referred to the τὸ ὄνομα name, which precedes it in him. But because in the Greek τὸ πνεῦμα, precedes, therefore it is more correctly referred to the Spirit, and consequently it is to be supplied from the idiom of the Hebrews ὃ, which Spirit of God is indeed blasphemed among them, but among you is glorified, in which way Oecumenius also explains it. Certainly those words βλασφημεῖται, δοξάζεται are indeed taken impersonally in this sense, as far as it pertains to them, curses are cast upon you; as far as it pertains to you, however, glory happens to you, for while they falsely you they accuse and cast reproaches upon the undeserving, upon them indeed confusion is poured back, but to you it is glorious to suffer as the undeserving for the name of Christ. Some refer this to Christ, of whom mention is made in the beginning of the verse, whose name and doctrine is blasphemed by the impious and persecutors, but is glorified by the pious and among the pious, because they constantly confess his name and patiently sustain persecutions on account of him. But it is more correctly referred to the Spirit of God, who is said to be blasphemed among the impious and persecutors, because the reproaches and insults brought upon the pious on account of the name of Christ do not cease in the pious, but redound upon the Spirit of God himself, who is in them, while they cry out that the profession of the Christian religion, which the pious embrace by the leading and impulse of the Holy Spirit, is apostasy, heresy, sedition, contumacy toward the Magistrate, etc., while they slander the word, which is the word of the Holy Spirit, and thus slander the Holy Spirit himself, while they hold in mockery whatever is suggested to them by the Holy Spirit for the consolation of the pious, while they blaspheme the pious, who are the temples and dwellings of the Holy Spirit, and thus blaspheme the Holy Spirit himself. But the Holy Spirit is said to be glorified by the pious and among the pious, because they embrace the word of the Gospel, which is the word of the Holy Spirit, and by this faith they glorify the Holy Spirit, because by the virtue and gift of the Holy Spirit they remain constant in the confession of the truth, and do not allow themselves to be moved from it by any reproaches or persecutions, and because by their example they invite others to constancy, which redounds to the glory of the Holy Spirit. Moreover, the Apostle confirms the immediately preceding sentiment with these words, signifying that it ought to suffice for the pious as a support for patience, that the Spirit of GOD dwelling in them testifies that they themselves are blessed on account of the reproaches which they sustain for the confession of the name of Christ, since through this patience and constancy of theirs the Holy Spirit is glorified. He also meets their tacit objection, who could say that in those reproaches nothing less than the Spirit of glory appears. The Apostle answers that a distinction must be made between the judgment of the world and the judgment of the pious, which is conformed to the word of God. Among the persecutors indeed the Holy Spirit is blasphemed, while they heap reproaches and adversities upon you on account of the name of Christ, but among you he is glorified, because your tolerance and constancy in the cross redounds to the glory of the Holy Spirit. At the same time, however, the Apostle insinuates that the Holy Spirit those reproaches and blasphemies, inasmuch as they are against himself redundant, he will avenge with temporal and eternal punishments in the impious unless, led by serious repentance, they are converted to Christ.

Latin:

SI EXPROBRAMINI IN NOMINE CHRISTI, BEATI ERITIS, QUONIAM GLORIA & SPIRITUS DEI IN VOBIS REQUIESCIT: (APUD ILLOS QUIDEM BLASPHEMATUR, APUD VOS VERO GLORIFICATUR.)

Connexio. 1. Praeter ea, quae in praecedentibus adduxerat, quatuor affert consolationis argumenta, quibus piorum in cruce patientiam confirmat. Primum desumtum est à causae bonitate. Non ob flagitia quaedam vestra, sed ob confessionem Christi probra & adversitates sustinetis. Quàm ergô carus vobis Christus, tàm gratum vobis essc debet pro Christo & propter Christum aliquid pati. Alterum ab eventus utilitate. Beati eritis, omnia vobis in bonum cedent.Rom. 8. v. 28. Tantum abest, ut persecutores salutem vobis eripere possint, ut eandem etiam praeter suam voluntatem promovere cogantur. Tertium à tolerandi facilitate. Adversitates, quas pii propter Christum sustinent, evidens testimonium ferunt, quòd Spiritus Dei in illis habitet & requiescat. Spiritus autem Dei ad ferendam crucem & ipsam mortem tolerandam eum, in quo requiescit, id oneum & paratum facit. Quartum à peccati, quod persecutores committunt, gravitate. Adversarii sibi persuadent, in vos solos convitia & calumnias sese emovere, sed recidunt illae in ipsum Spiritum Dei, qui in vobis habitat, & quem vestra in cruce patientiâ & constantia glorificatis.

2. Quoniam probra & convitia, quae superiùs v. 4. blasphemiarum nomine denotaverat, quibus confessores Christi ab adversariis onerantur, animos ingenuos plus turbant, quàm vel facultatum direptio, vel corporis cruciatus, ideò etiam huic malo consolationem Apostolus adhibet.

3. Lyranus eiusmodi profert connexionem. Apostolus ordinans fideles in perpessione mali, ab adversariis fidei illati, hactenus induxerat eos ad confidentiam, iam porrò tollit erubescentiam.

Textus expositio. Ἐι ὀνειδίζεσθε ἐν ὀνόματι Χριστοῦ. Tertull. in Scorpiaco cap. 12. Si dedecoramini. Cyprianus lib. 4. Epist. 6. Si improperatur vobis. Vulgata Si exprobamini, minùs Latinè, si probris &

convitiis afficimini. Potest quidem hoc accipi limitativè, velut determinatio opprobriorum. Non enim quaevis afflictiones & probra in partem beatitudinis computanda, sed ea solùm, quae propter confessionem Christi, & propter iustitiam in bona causa piis nihil talis merentibus ingeruntur. Interim quia Apostolus hîc in specie agic de piis, fervori persecutionis in hac vita expositis, & quia in seq. demum versiculo illam limitationem subiungit, ideò haec verba rectiùs accipiuntur assertivè. Quia in Christi nomine probris, conviciis & maledictis afficimini. Ita usurpatur vocula εἰMatth. 6. v. 30.cap. 10. v. 25.Actor. 11. v. 17.cap. 26. v. 23.Rom. 5. v. 10.cap. 6. v. 5.cap. 8. v. 31. &c. in quibus & similibus locis non tàm conditionaliter, quàm assertivè particula εἰ usurpatur.

Pro ὀνειδίζεσθαι Syrus habet [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image] ex Hebraeo חסר, quod benignitatem, & per ἀντίφρσινprobrum significat: hoc autem loco in posteriori significatione usurpatur.

Ἐν ὀνόματι ponitur pro διὰ ὂνομαpropter nomen Christi, i. e. propter confessionem nominis Christi, quia vos profitemini Christianos, ut exponitur v. 16. Matth. 5. v. 11. redditur, ἒνεκα τοῦ χριστοῦ. Syrus pro nomine Messiae.

Μακάριοι. Vulgatus de suo addidit, eritis, quod non est in Graeco. Existimavit, respectum haberi ad futuram regni coelestis beatitudinem, quae probra, propter Christi nomen illata, patienter sustinentibus promissa. Sed quia Petrus haec verba desumsit ex ore Magistri Matth. 5. v. 11.Μακάριοι ἒστε, ὃτι ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσι καὶ εἴπωσι πᾶν ῥῆμα καθ' ὑμῶν, ψευδόμενον, ἒνεκεν ἐμοῦ, qui locus huic nostro parallelus, ideò rectiùs subintelligitur verbum praesentis temporis, beati estis, quo modo etiam hunc locum citat Cyprianus lib. 4. Epist. 6. Si improperatur vobis in nomine Christi, beati est is, vid. ob spem certissimam mercedis amplissimae, in coelis vobis repositae. Pari ratione Apostolus noster absolurè loquitur superiùs c. 3. v. 14.Sed & si quid patiamini propter iustitiam, beati, sc. estis. Rationem h. l. addit, quia Spiritus Dei in vobis requieseit, qui de gratia Dei interiore suo testimonio vos confirmat, vivificam consolationem vohis suppeditat, & de secutura coelestis vitae gloria vos certos reddit, ut sic quaevis adversa non solùm patienter, sed etiam laeto animotolerare possitis.

Ὅτι τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐφ' ὑμᾶς ἀναπάυεται. Varia hîc occurrit lectio non solùm in Latinis, sed etiam Graecis Codicibus. Quidam enim Codices ita legunt, uti modò verba adduximus. Regii duo & alius inserunt nomen δυνάμεως, legentes hoc modo, ὅτι τῆς δόξης καὶ δυνάμεως καὶ τό τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα, ἐφ' ὑφᾶς ἀναπάυεται. Sed & pro praesenti ἀναπάυεται Complutensis & Regius habent perfectum ἀναπεπάυται. Similis varietas occurrit in Codicibus Latinis. Quidam enim sic legunt. Quoniam gloria & Spiritus DEI in vobis requiescit. Quidam verò hoc modo. Quoniam quod est honoris, gloriae & virtutis DEI, & qui est Spiritus eius, super vos requiescit. Alii, quoniam Spiritus gloriae & DEI super vos requiescit. Sed & verbum ἀναπάυεται quidam Codices Latini reddunt per praesens, quod Graeco congruit; quidam per praeteritum, qui legerunt ἀναπέπαυται, quidam per futurum, qui legerunt ἀναπάυσεται. Tertullianus in Scorpiaco locum sic citat. Quoniam gloria & DEI Spiritus requiescet in vobis. Cyprianus lib. 4. Epist. 6. Quia maiestatis & virtutis Domini nomen in vobis requiescit. Pro πνεῦμα legit ὄνομα, ut monet Pamelius. Syrus reddidit, quia Spiritus gloriae vel gloriosus DEI super vos requiescit. Communior & magis usitata lectio est, quam habent nostri Codices, ὅτι τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐφ ὑμᾶς ἀναπάυεται. Erasmus monet locum hunc bifariam exponi posse. Uno modo, utτὸ τῆς δόξηςseparatim accipiatur pro gloria, quo modo accipit vulgatus Interpres locum, sic reddens. Quoniam gloria & Spiritus DEI in vobis requiescit. Altero, ut nominativusτὸ πνεῦμαadhibeatur ex aequo duobus genitivis praecedentibus,τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ,Spiritus gloriae & DEI requiescit in vobis. Si priorem expositionem amplecti velimus, cogitari posset, nomen gloriae respectum habere ad peculiarem illam Domini in tabernaculo foederis praesentiam. Quando enim symbolo quodam externo gratiosa DEI in tabernaculo foederis praesentia manifestabatur, tùm gloria Domini apparere dicebatur, Exodi. 16. vers. 10.cap. 40. v. 34.Lev. 9. vers. 23.Numer. 14. v. 10. &c. Ut enim gloria DOMINI in tabernaculo foederis typicè &

visibiliter apparuit: ita eadem per fidem & invisibiliter habitat in omnibus verè piis. Ephes. 3. vers. 17. Sed posterior expositio magis congruit textui, ut ostendit series verborum τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα, quam comprobat etiam Syrus, qui sublatâ coniunctione reddidit. Spiritus gloriae Dei, vel Spiritus gloriosus Dei in vobis requiescit. Vocat autem Spiritum gloriae, non solùm quia gloriosus & laudabilis est in se, sed etiam quia est nostrae glorificationis autor, ac proinde hunc Spiritum gloriae opponit probris & ignominiae, quae piis à mundo infertur, sicut etiam Spiritus Dei, vel ut 1. Cor. 2. v. 12. Paulus loquitur, Spiritus qui ex Deo est, opponitur Spiritui mundi, quo persecutores acti & impulsi pios, ob Christi nomen probris & ignominiâ afficiunt. Reddit igitur Apostolus in his verbis rationem, quare eos, qui ob nomen Christi probris afficiuntur, beatos dixerit, nimirùm, quia Spiritus Dei super eos requiescit, siquidem propter Christi nomen probra, & quaevis adversa patienter sustinere, est signum infallibile inhabitantis Spiritus sancti, in quo autem Spiritus sanctus gratiosè habitat, non potest non beatus esse. Cumque Spiritus ille Dei sit etiam Spiritus gloriae, ideò consolatur & animat credentes, propter Christum probra sustinentes, contra omnem mundi ignominiam, ac confirmat ipsos, quòd pro transitoria mundi ignominia ipsis aliquando reddenda sit coelestis, & nunquam intermoritura vel desitura gloria, siquidem filiis Dei debetur etiam hereditas coelestis. In quibus autem habitat Spiritus Dei, illi sunt filii Dei,Rom. 8. v. 16.Gal. 4. v. 6. Ergò etiam illis, in quibus habitat Spiritus Dei, debetur haereditas coelestis, quae vel sola consolatio omnibus mundi probris, odiis & adversis firmissimè opponi potest. Eò etiam respicit verbum ἀναπάυεται. Alludit enim Apostolus ad locum Esa. 11. v. 1. Egredietur virga de radice Iesse, & virgultum de radice eius ascendet. vers. 2. Et requiescet super eum Spiritus Domini. Significat ergò, pios eiusdem cum Christo participes factos, ac proinde in filios Dei à Patre coelesti esse receptos, proinde quia Spiritus Christi participes fuerint in passionibus, ideò in gloria quoque per eiusdem Spiritus sancti donum & inhabitationem cum Christo communicaturos. Innuit etiam verbum ἀναπάυειν, quod de gratiosa Spiritus S. in piis habitatione usurpatur, quòd Spiritus sanctus quietem conscientiae, interius gaudium & vivificam consolationem piis in cruce suppeditet, de qua verbum illud usurpatur Matth. 11. v. 28.1. Cor. 16. v. 18.2. Cor. 7. v. 13.Philem. v. 7.20. Qui nomen δυνάμεως virtutis textui Apostolico insertum legunt, reserunt illud ad victoriam, quam credentes per fidem in cruce à Diabolo & eius organis reportant. Gloss. ordin. ad h. l. Spiritus Christi requiescit super vos, & in praesenti exparte ad benè operandum, & in futuro perfectè ad remunerandum: quod est bonoris, ut & in praesenti sitis honorabiles in bonis operibus, & in futuro participes honoris Christi; & quod est gloriae in praesenti pura conscientia, in futuro sine omni corruptione tàm in anima, quàm in corpore; & quod est virtutis & in praesenti & in futuro super Diabolum & membra eius. Lyranus ad h. l. Honor refertur ad opus virtuosum, gloria ad bonae conscientiae testimonium, virtus vero ad triumphum de Diabolo habitum. Spiritus eius super vos requiescit, in vobis spiritualiter habitando, vel requiescit super vos, sicut sessor super equum, ducens eum secundùm suum libitum: Sic Spiritus sanctus inducit tales secundùm suum instinctumRom. 8. vers. 14. Potest etiam nomen virtutis referri ad vires & robur, quod suppeditat DEUS ad probra & caeteras calamitates fortiter tolerandas.

Κατὰ μὲν αὐτοὺς βλασφημεῖται, κατὰ δὲ ὑμᾶς δοξάζεται. Haec non habentur in Codicibus Latinis, nec in Syriaca paraphrasi, nec apud Tertullianum in Scorpiaco, ubi totum hunc locum adducit: unde Lorinus habet pro additamento. Interim sunt genuina textus pars, quia habentur in omnibus Codicibus Graecis, & in Graecorum Patrum commentariis, teste Oecumenio. Quin & Cyprianus lib. 4. Epist. 6. locum hunc adducit, quamvis verbis à Graeco paululùm diversis, legit enim hoc modo. Quod quidem secundùm illos blaesphematur, secundùm nos autem honoratur, ut referatur ad τὸ ὄνομα nomen, quod apud ipsum praecedit. Sed quia in Graeco praecedit τὸ πνεῦμα, ideò rectiùs ad Spiritum refertur, ac proinde supplendum ex Hebraeorum idiotismo ὃ,qui Spiritus Dei apud ipsos quidem blasphematur, apud vos vero glorificatur, quo modo etiam Oecumenius exponit. Sanè quidem verba illa βλασφημεῖται, δοξάζεται accipiunt impersonaliter hoc sensu, quod ad illos quidem attinet, maledicta in vos iaciuntur; quod ad vos autem, gloria vobis contingit, dum enim illi falsò vos accusant & in immerentes probra coniiciunt, in illos quidem refunditur confusio vobis autem gloriosum est ob Christi nomen immerentes pati. Quidam referunt ad Christum, cuius in principio versiculi fit mentio, eius nomen ac doctrina ab impiis & persecutoribus blaspbematur, à piis vero & apud pios glorificatur, quia nomen eius constanter confitentur & propter ipsum persecutiones patienter sustinent. Sed rectiùs ad Spiritum Dei, qui dicitur apud impios & persecutores blasphemari, quia probra & contumeliae propter nomen Christi piis illatae non desinunt in piis, sed in ipsum Spiritum Dei, qui in ipsis est, redundant, dum professionem religionis Christianae, quam ductu & impulsu Spiritus sancti pii amplectuntur, clamant esse apostasian, haeresin, seditionem, contumaciam erga Magistratum &c. dum verbum, quod est Spiritus sancti verbum, calumniantur, & sic ipsum Spiritum sanctum calumniantur, dum ludibrio habent, quicquid ad piorum consolationem ipsis à Spiritu sancto suggeritur, dum pios, qui sunt Spiritus sancti templa & habitacula, blasphemant, adeoq; ipsum Spiritum sanctum blasphemant. A piis vero & apud pios Spiritus sanctus dicitur glorificari, quia verbum Evangelii, quod est verbum Spiritus sancti amplectuntur, & hac fide Spiritum sanctum glorificant, quia virtute & dono Spiritus sancti in veritatis confessione manent constantes, nec ullis probris vel persecutionibus ab ea sese dimoveri patiuntur, & quia exemplo suo alios ad constantiam invitant, quod in gloriam Spiritus sancti cedit. Confirmat autem his verbis Apostolus sententiam proximè praecedentem, significans, ad patientiae fulcrum debere piis sufficere, quôd Spiritus DEI in ipsis habitans testetur, beatos ipsos esse propter probra, quae ob confessionem nominis Christus sustinent, cum per hanc patientiam & constantiam ipsorum Spiritus sanctus glorificetur. Occurrit etiam tacitae eorum obiectioni, qui poterant dicere, in probris illis nihil minus quàm Spiritum gloriae apparere. Respondet Apostolus, distinguendum esse inter iudicium mundi, & iudicum piorum, verbo Dei conforme. Apud persecutores quidem Spiritus Sanctus blasphematur, dum ob Christi nomen probra-& adversa vobis ingerunt, sed apud vos glorificatur, quia vestra in cruce tolerantia & constantia in Spiritus sancti gloriam cedit. Simul vero insinuat Apostolus, Spiritum sanctum probra & blasphemias illas, utpote in ipsummet redundantes, poenis temporalibus & aeternis in impiis vindicaturum nisi seriâ poenitentiâ ducti ad Christum convertantur.

## 4:15
BUT LET NONE OF YOU SUFFER AS A MURDERER, OR A THIEF, OR A SLANDERER, OR A COVETER OF OTHERS' GOODS.

Connection. 1. The Apostle admonishes the faithful not to commit anything unworthy of the Christian profession, or contrary to honest laws, otherwise it would come to pass that they not only bring back no glory from adversities, but also procure ignominy and infamy for themselves and the Christian name.

2. He shows what kind of cross is glorious for the pious, namely that which is not brought on because of crimes, but which is imposed upon them without merit on account of the name of Christ; thus therefore ἐξηγητικῶς by antithesis he declares what it is to be afflicted with reproach or other injuries in the name of Christ or on account of the name of Christ.

3. In the Greek there is the particle γὰρ, which shows ἀιτιολογικῶς that this little verse is joined with the preceding one. Therefore the Apostle explains the reason why he had spoken only of that kind of reproach and affliction which is brought on account of the name of Christ, namely because the pious ought not to summon a cross upon themselves through misdeeds, nor commit anything for which they might deservedly seem to be punished.

4. Bede likewise accepts it as an exhortation to patience in persecutions. As a slanderer, he says, he suffers, who at the time of his passion is unbridled in injury to his persecutor, from Gregory, book 3 of the Morals, chapter 12 (otherwise 16).

5. Lyranus offers this kind of connection. In the preceding verses the Apostle removes shame in words, here he removes shame in deeds: for those who suffer for their own crimes are reasonably ashamed.

Exposition of the text. Μὴ γάρ τις ὑμῶν πασχέτω ὼς φονεὺς, ἡ κλέπτης. The Vulgate rendered it adversatively. But let none of you suffer as a murderer. The Syriac in almost the same way. [consult facsimile image] μόνον or πλὴν only let no one of you suffer as a murderer. Tertullian in Scorpiace, chapter 12. Provided that none of you suffer, But in the Greek there is the particle αἰτιολογικὴ γὰρ, which fits the context very well, as we showed in the connection. I said that through the reproaches cast upon you undeservedly for the name of Christ by the impious, the Holy Spirit resting upon you is glorified, and thus from those reproaches of the enemies glory comes to you: I said that indeed because I know that you suffer those curses and any adversities whatsoever not because of certain enormous crimes, but because of the confession of Christ, for if any of you were to suffer as a wrongdoer, that would result neither to the glory of the Holy Spirit nor to your own.

Ἡ κακοποιὸς. The Vulgate rendered it, as a slanderer. But in the Greek it is, or a wrongdoer, in which way also Tertullian in Scorpiacus, ch. 12, and Cyprian in book 3 of Testimonies, ch. 37, read it. The Syriac rendered it [consult facsimile image] a perpetrator of evils. Moreover, κακοποιὸς in general, is said of one who affects his neighbor with evils, who harms his neighbor through injury, especially in the safety of the body. John 18, v. 30. concerning Christ, whom they had accused of sedition, the Jews say: If this man were not κακοποιός we would not have brought him to you. 1 Pet. 2, v. 12. they speak against you as κακοποιοῖς, and v. 14. ch. 3, v. 16. for the punishment of κακοποιῶν, from which it is understood that κακοποιοὺς are called criminals who, because of their enormous crimes disturbing civil society, incur the punishments of the Magistrate. Prov. 12, v. 4. The LXX call a woman κακοποιὸν who affects her husband with shame by indecent acts. ch. 24, v. 19. they are called κακοποιὸι מרעים malignant and harmful men, whose zeal is to do evil, κακοποιεῖν, Gen. 31, v. 29. and elsewhere it is everywhere to inflict evil upon a neighbor. In particular κακοποιὸς is said of one who harms a neighbor with sorceries and incantations, which for that reason are also called maleficia. Synesius, Epistle 57, αἱ κακοποιὸι δυνάμεις maleficent powers. The Royal Codex reads κακοῦργος without variation of sense. For κακοῦργος or κακόεργος, ὁ τὰ κακὰ ἐργαζόμενος is said a wrongdoer, a criminal, a wicked person. Demosthenes τοὺς κλέπτας καὶ τοὺς ἀλλου κακούργους ἐπὶ θανάτῳ εἰσάγουσι 2 Tim. 2, v. 9. κακοποθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος; in particular thieves are called κακοῦργον Luke 23, verse 32. as those who strip men of life and goods. ἣ ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος. The Syriac omitted this member entirely. The Vulgate rendered it, as a coveter of other men's things. In the Greek it is properly, an inspector of other men's things, By what name these are properly denoted, we shall see in the questions.

Latin:

NEMO AUTEM VESTRUM PATIATUR, UT HOMICIDA, AUT FUR, AUT MALEDICUS, AUT ALIENORUM APPETITOR.

Connexio. 1. Admonet Apostolus fideles, ne quid committant Christiana professione indignum, aut legibus honestis contrarium, alioqui fore, ut non solùm nullam ex adversis reportent gloriam, sed etiam ignominiam & infamiam sibi & Christiano nomini concilient.

2. Ostendit, quae crucis species piis sit gloriosa, videlicet ea, quae non propter scelera infertur, sed quae ob Christi nomen praeter meritum ipsis imponitur, sic ergò ἐξηγητικῶς per antithesin declarat, quid sit in nomine Christi vel propter Christi nomen probis aliisve iniuriis asfici.

3. In Graeco est particula γὰρ, quae ostendit, ἀιτιολογικῶς hunc versiculum cum praecedente coniungi. Explicat ergò Apostolus rationem, quare de illo duntaxat probrorum & afflictionum genere locutus fuerit, quod propter Christi nomen infertur, nimirum quia pii non debeant sibi ipsis per maleficia crucem accersere, neque quidquam committere, propter quod meritò videantur plecti.

4. Beda itidem accipit ut exhortationem ad patientiam in persecutionibus. Tanquam maledicus, inquit, patitur, qui passionis suae tempore in sui iniuriam persecutoris effrenatur, ex Gregorio lib. 3. moral. cap. 12. (al. 16.)

5. Lyranus eiusmodi profert connexionem. In praecedentibus tollit Apostolus erube scentiam in verbis, hîc tollit erubescentiam infactis: illi enim qui patiuntur pro suis criminibus, rationabiliter erubescunt.

Textus expositio. Μὴ γάρ τις ὑμῶν πασχέτω ὼς φονεὺς, ἡ κλέπτης. Vulgata reddidit adversativè. Nemo autem vestrûm patiatur ut homicida. Syrus eodem ferè modo. [consult facsimile image]μόνον vel πλὴνtantummodò ne quis ex vobis patiatur tanquam homicida. Tertullianus in Scorpiaco. cap. 12. Dum ne quis vestrûm patiatur, Sed in Graeco est particula αἰτιολογικὴ γὰρ, quae contextui optime congruit, ut in connexione ostendimus. Dixi, per probra in vos immerentes ob Christi nomen ab impiis coniecta, Spiritum sanctum in vobis requiesentem glorificari, adeoque ex probris illis hostium gloriam vobis contingere: id vero ideò dixi, quia novi, vos illa maledicta & quaevis omninò adversa non propter enormia quaedam flagitia, sed propter confessionem Christi pati, si quis enim vestrûm ut maleficus pateretur, id nec ad Spiritus sancti nec in vestram gloriam cederet.

Ἡ κακοποιὸς. Vulgata reddidit, ut maledicus Sed in Graeco est, aut maleficus, quo modo etiam Tertullianus in Scorpiaco, c. 12. Cyprianus lib. 3. testim. c. 37. legunt. Syrus redd. [consult facsimile image]patrator malorum. Dicitur autem κακοποιὸςin genere, qui malis proximum afficit, qui per iniuriam proximo nocet, praesertim in corporis incolumitate. Ioh. 18. v. 30. de Christo, quem seditionis accusaverant, dicunt Iudaei. Nisi hic essetκακοποιόςnon adduxissemus eum ad te.1. Petr. 2. v. 12.obtrectant vobis tanquamκακοποιοῖς, & v. 14.c. 3. v. 16.in vindictamκακοποιῶν, ex quo intelligitur, κακοποιοὺς vocari facinorosos, qui ob enormia sua flagitia societatem civilem turbantia in poenas Magistratus incurrunt. Prov. 12. v. 4. LXX. mulierem κακοποιὸν vocant, quae indecentibus actibus maritum pudore afficit. c. 24. v. 19. vocantur κακοποιὸιמרעים homines maligni ac noxii, quorum studium est malè agere, κακοποιεῖν,Gen. 31. v. 29. & alibi passim est malum proximo inferre. In specieκακοποιὸς dicitur, qui veneficiis & incantationibus, quae propterea etiam maleficia vocantur, proximo nocet. Synesius Epist. 57. αἱ κακοποιὸι δυνάμειςmaleficae potestates. Regius Codex legit κακοῦργος sine sensus variatione. Dicitur enim κακοῦργος vel κακόεργος, ὁ τὰ κακὰ ἐργαζόμενοςmaleficus, facinorosus, improbus. Demosth. τοὺς κλέπτας καὶ τοὺς ἀλλου κακούργους ἐπὶ θανάτῳ εἰσάγουσι2. Tim. 2. v. 9.κακοποθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος; in specie latrones dicuntur κακοῦργονLuc. 23. vers. 32. ut qui homines vitâ & bonis exuant. ἣ ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος. Syrus hoc membrum penitùs omisit. Vulgata reddidit, ut alienorum appetitor. In Graeco propriè est, rerum alienorum inspector, quo nomine quinam propriè denotentur, in quaestionibus videbimus.

## 4:16
BUT IF AS A CHRISTIAN, LET HIM NOT BE ASHAMED, BUT LET HIM GLORIFY GOD IN THIS NAME.

Connection. He opposes to the dissuasion an exhortation to the tolerance of afflictions, brought upon one without merit on account of the profession of the Christian name, into which exhortation he inserts an argument from the salutary consequence, which is the glorification of God, because by such afflictions patiently endured for Christ's sake, God is glorified.

Exposition of the text. εἰ δὲ ὡς χριστιανὸς to wit πάσχει, if he suffers as a Christian, that is, if because he professes himself a Christian or a disciple of Christ, either by persons constituted in public office, or by private individuals, some evil is brought upon anyone. The Syrian retained the Greek name [consult facsimile image] μὴ αἰσχυνέσθω, let him not be ashamed, let him by no means consider that ignominious for himself, let him not be suffused with shame on that account, the Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] which corresponds to the Hebrew ביש he was ashamed, he was put to shame. Lyranus adds, let him not be ashamed for this reason, because it is a virtuous work, which is not shameful, but rather honorable.

Δοξαζέτω δὲ τόν θεὸν ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτω. The Vulgate rendered, but let him glorify God in this name, in which way also the Syrian translates. But in the Greek it is, in this part, although the Royal Codex substitutes ὀνόματι for μέρει & adds the particle καὶ ἐν ὀνόματι τούτω. The sense is the same in both. He who suffers as a Christian, let him submit himself to the holy & good will of God, and not only let him not be ashamed, but let him also rejoice; and not only let him rejoice, but let him also consider it glorious for himself to suffer for Christ's sake, and let him give thanks to God, because He judged him worthy, that he should suffer something for the name of Christ, and that He worked patience in his heart through the Holy Spirit. Acts 5. v. 41. The Apostles went rejoicing from the presence of the Sanhedrin, because they were counted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus. Phil. 1. v. 29. To you it is given for Christ, not only that you may believe in him, but that you may also suffer for him. Therefore let him glorify God & ascribe the whole glory of patience to Him in this part, to wit, of the passions in that measure of the cross, which falls to him by the ordination of God. Or even in this name, whether it be taken concerning the name of Christ himself, on account of whose confession he suffers, and in whom we ought to glorify God v. 11. in which way Lyranus accepts it, annotating thus on this place, because he will not only be called a Christian, but also a faithful witness of Christ through Martyrdom; or whether the name be taken for the cause.

Latin:

SI AUTEM UT CHRISTIANUS, NON ERUBESCAT, GLORIFICET AUTEM DEUM IN NOMINE ISTO.

Connexio. Dehortationi opponit exhortationem ad tolerantiam afflictionum, ob Christiani nominis professionem praeter meritum illatarum, cui exhortationi inserit argumentum à salutari consequente, quod est Dei glorificatio, quia eiusmodi afflictionibus propter Christum patienter toleratis Deus glorificatur.

Textus expositio. εἰ δὲ ὡς χριστιανὸς scil. πάσχει,si ut Christianus patiatur, hoc est, si ideo quia se Christianum sive Christi discipulum profitetur, vel à personis in publico officio constitutis, vel à privatis mali aliquid alicui infertur. Syrus retinuit Graecum nomen [consult facsimile image]μὴ αἰσχυνέσθω,non erubescat, nequaquam id sibi ducat ignominiosum, non propterea pudore suffundatur, Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] quod respondet Hebraeo בישerubuit, pudefactus est. Lyranus addit, ideo non erubescat, quia est opus virtuosum, quod nonesterubescibile, sed magis honorabile.

Δοξαζέτω δὲ τόν θεὸν ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτω. Vulg. reddidit, glorificet autem Deum in isto nomine, quo modo etiam Syrus vertit. Sed in Graeco est, in parte hac, quamvis Regius Codex pro μέρει substituat ὀνόματι & addat particulam καὶ ἐν ὀνόματι τούτω. Sensus utrobiq; idem. Qui ut Christianus patitur, subiiciat se sanctae & bonae Dei voluntati, nec solùm non erubescat, sed etiam gaudeat; nec solùm gaudeat, sed etiam gloriosum sibi ducat propter Christum pati, ac Deo gratias agat, quod dignum ipsum iudicaverit, ut propter nomen Christi aliquid patiatur, quodque patientiam in ipsius corde per SS. operatus fuerit. Actor. 5. v. 41.Ibant Apostoli gaudentes à conspectu Synedrii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Iesu contumeliam pati.Phil. 1. v. 29.Vobis donatum est pro Christo, non solùm ut in eum credatis, sed ut etiam pro illo patiamini. Glorificet ergò Deum & totam patientiae gloriam ei adscribat in parte hac, scilicet passionum in demenso illo crucis, quod ex Dei ordinatione ipsi obtingit. Vel etiam in hoc nomine, sive illud accipiatur de ipso Christi nomine, propter cuius confessionem patitur, & in quo debemus Deum glorificare v. 11. quo modo accipit Lyranus, ad h. l. sic annotans, quia non solùm vocabitur Christianus, sed etiam fidelis Christi testis per Martyrium; sive nomen pro causa accipiatur.

## 4:17
FOR THE TIME IS COME, THAT JUDGMENT MUST BEGIN AT THE HOUSE OF GOD. AND IF IT FIRST BEGIN AT US, WHAT SHALL THE END BE OF THEM THAT OBEY NOT THE GOSPEL OF GOD?

Connection. 1. He brings forward two other arguments for the exhortation to patience. The former is taken from the decree and will of God, to whom it has seemed good to chastise his beloved children in this age. Wherefore, since the cross is sent in by the fatherly counsel of God, it is certainly also to be tolerated with filial patience. The latter is taken from the most grievous punishment, which awaits the persecutors. He confirms this argument from the lesser. If the judgment of God begins at us believers, that is, if God chastises and corrects his beloved children in this life, what will be the end of those who refuse to receive the Gospel by faith, when they also persecute the confessors of the Gospel, what at length is to be expected, or rather feared, by them?

2. He explains at the same time the reason why one ought to glorify God, if anyone suffers as a Christian, because hence he is known to be of the house and family of God Hebr. 12. v. 6.Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth: and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.

3. He also amplifies that consolation which the goodness of the cause, for which we suffer, brings to us, when we sustain persecution on account of Christ and his Gospel. This, he says, is the common lot of the whole Church, therefore none of us ought to seek for himself another lot in this world.

4. Finally, through the latter argument he meets the scandal which the pious might receive from persecutions, when they see that they are perpetually pressed by the burden of the cross, while the impious and persecutors meanwhile luxuriate in every abundance of things. The Apostle truly admonishes the pious, that they ought to fortify themselves against this scandal, and not look at the present state of the impious, but at their end.

Exposition of the text. Ὅτι ὁ καιρὸς τοῦ ἂρξασθαι τὸ κρίμα αὐτοῦ οἲκου τοῦ θεοῦ. Some codices read, ὅτι καὶ ὁ καιρὸς Because it is also the time, so that a new method of exhortation may be insinuated. Kαιρὸς It signifies not simply time, but an opportune time Acts 1. v. 7. Moreover, the Apostle looks to the will and ordination of God, according to which whatever happens to or is sent upon the faithful, happens to them at an opportune time.

By τὸ κρῖμα the Apostle understands paternal chastisements, which God sends with a salutary plan either because of preceding sins, or because of the remnants of sin still remaining in the flesh of the reborn, which are therefore called κρίματα, because with respect to others they are public signs of divine judgment against sins. Numbers 12. verse 14. 2. Samuel 12. v. 14. With respect to the reconciled themselves, they are memorials of the past, and cautions for the future; hence the Greek scholia say that κρῖμα, is used here, not ἀντὶ κατακρίματος but ἐξετασίας. In this meaning the word κρίματος is used 1. Corinthians 11. v. 31. For if we would judge ourselves, we should not indeed ἐκρινόμεθα be judged. v. 32. κρινόμενοι δέ, But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. 1. Peter 4. v. 6. For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.

By the house of God the Apostle understands the Church, and the true members of the Church, according to the Pauline phrase 1. Timothy 3. v. 15. Hebrews 3. v. 6. When therefore he says, that the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God, he then means this. Let no one complain that he suffers unjustly and undeservedly. For although persecutors and the impious, who afflict Christians, do not have a just cause for inflicting such evils, nevertheless before God no one is innocent. Exodus 34. v. 7. Therefore eyes are to be lifted to God and it is to be thought that God exercises his judgment in the cross through these very persecutors and the impious even upon his beloved sons and his household. It is to be thought that that judgment indeed begins with Christians and the household of God, but will finally be completed in the reprobate and persecutors. For τὸ ἄρξασθαι is a relative term, and therefore it insinuates, that this judgment indeed begins at the house of God, that is, that the faithful and true members of the Church are subject to the cross in this life before others, but in the impious outside that the house of God is at some time to be completed and finished. εὶ δε πρῶτον ἀφ' ἡμῶν, τὶ τὸ τέλος τῶν ἀπειθούντων τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίῳ; If, however, judgment must begin from us, namely the domestics of God and the faithful, what will be the end, that is, how miserable will be the outcome of those who not only refuse to embrace the Gospel of Christ by faith, but moreover also persecute its confessors? There is an exaggeration in the interrogation. If God afflicts his beloved sons and his domestics in this life more than others, what will happen to the unbelievers and ἀθέοις, to those who are aliens from the family of God. Eph. 2. v. 12. He will at some time pour out upon them all his wrath like a flood of waters, like a cataclysm 2. Thess. 1. v. 5. and following, and will compensate for the slowness of the punishment with its gravity. τῶν ἀπειθούντων The Vulgate rendered it, of those who do not believe. But the Greek is ἐμφατικώτερον, for positive unbelief is signified, and the stubborn contempt of the Gospel of those who refuse the Gospel preached to them, and are unwilling to believe it, and by this reason judge themselves unworthy of eternal life. Act. 13. v. 46. The Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael. who do not suffer themselves to be persuaded, so as to obey and acquiesce to the Gospel.

Latin:

QUONIAM TEMPUS EST, UT INCIPIAT IUDICIUM A DOMO DEI. SI AUTEM PRIMUM A NOBIS, QUIS FINIS EORUM, QUI NON CREDUNT DEI EVANGELIO?

Connexio. 1. Duo alia exhortationis ad patientiam afferr argumenta. Prius desumtum est à Dei decreto & voluntate, cui visum est, dilectos suos filios in hoc seculo castigare. Quare cum paterno Dei consilio crux immittatur, utique etiam filiali patientiâ est toleranda. Posterius desumtum à gravissima poena, quae manet persecutores. Hoc argumentum confirmat à minori. Si iudicium Dei incipit à nobis fidelibus, h. e. si dilectos fuos filios Deus in hac vita castigat atque corripit, quis finis erit eorum, qui Evangelium fide recipere renuunt, quando & confessores Evangelii persequuntur, quid ipsis tandem expectandum, vel potiùs metuendum erit?

2. Exponit simul rationem, quare Deum glorificare debeat, si quis patiatur ut Christianus, quia hinc cognoscitur esse de domo & familia Dei Hebr. 12. v. 6.Quem diligit Dominus, castigat: flagellat autem omnem filium, quem recipit.

3. Amplificat etiam consolationem illam, quam nobis affert causae, pro qua patimur, bonitas, quando propter Christum, & Evangelium eius persecutionem sustinemus. Haec, inquit, est communis sors totius Ecclesiae, nemo igitur nostrûm aliam sibi in hoc mundo sortem expetere debet.

4. Denique per posterius argumentum occurrit scandalo, quòd pii ex persecutionibus accipere possent, quando vident, se crucis onere perpetuò premi, impiis & persecutoribus interim in omni rerum abundantia luxuriantibus. Admonet vero Apostolus pios, ut contra hoc scandalum sese muniant, non praesentem impiorum statum, sed finem eorum intueri debere.

Textus expositio. Ὅτι ὁ καιρὸς τοῦ ἂρξασθαι τὸ κρίμα αὐτοῦ οἲκου τοῦ θεοῦ. Quidam Codices legunt, ὅτι καὶ ὁ καιρὸςQuia & tempus est, ut insinuetur nova exhortationis ratio. Kαιρὸς non simpliciter tempus, sed oportunum tempus significat Act. 1. v. 7. Respicit autem Apostolus ad voluntatem & ordinationem Dei, iuxtaquam quicquid fidelibus obtingit vel immittitur, oportuno tempore ipsis obtingit.

Per τὸ κρῖμα intelligit Apostolus castigationes paternas, quas vel ob peccata praecedentia, vel ob peccati reliquias in carne renatorum adhuc residuas salutari consilio Deus immittit, quae ideò vocantur κρίματα, quia respectu aliorum sunt publica indicia iudicii divini adversus peccata. Numer. 12. vers. 14.2. Samuel. 12. v. 14. respectu ipsorummet reconciliatorum sunt memorialia praecedentium, & cautelae futurorum, inde Graeca scholia dicunt, κρῖμα, hîc usurpari, non ἀντὶ κατακρίματος sed ἐξετασίας. In hac significatione vox κρίματος usurpatur 1. Corinth. 11. v. 31.Quod si nos ipsos diiudicaremus, non utiqueἐκρινόμεθαiudicaremur.v. 32.κρινόμενοι δέ,cùm iudicamur autem, à Domino corripimur, ne cum mundo damnemur.1. Petr. 4. v. 6.propter hoc & mortuis evangelizatum est, ut iudicentur quidem secundùm homines in carne, vivant autem secundùm Deum Spiritu.

Per domum Dei intelligit Apostolus Ecclesiam, ac vera Ecclesiae membra, iuxta phrasin Paulinam 1. Tim. 3. v. 15.Hebr. 3. v. 6. Quando ergò dicit, tempus esse, ut iudicium incipiat à domo Dei, tùm hoc vult. Nemo queratur, se iniustè & immerentem pati. Quamvis enim persecutores & impii, qui Christianos affligunt, non habeant iustam eiusmodi mala inferendi causam, tamen coram Deo nemo innocens est.Ex. 34. v. 7. ad Deum igitur oculi elevandi & cogitandum, Deum in cruce suum exercere iudicium per ipsos persecutores & impios etiam in dilectos suos filios & domesticos suos. Cogitandum, iudicium illud inchoari quidem à Christianis & domesticis Dei, tandem vero in reprobris & persecutoribus completum iri. Est enim τὸ ἄρξασθαι vocabulum relativum, ideoque insinuat, à domo Dei iudicium quidem hoc incipere, h. e. fideles & vera Ecclesiae membra prae aliis in hac vita cruci esse subiecta, sed in impiis extra domum Dei constitutis aliquando complendum & finiendum esse. εὶ δε πρῶτον ἀφ' ἡμῶν, τὶ τὸ τέλος τῶν ἀπειθούντων τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίῳ;Si autem primum à nobis, scil. domesticis Dei ac fidelibus iudicium incipere debet, quis finis, h. e. quàm miserabilis erit exitus eorum, qui Evangelium Christi fide amplecti non solùm renuunt, sed insuper etiam eius confessores per sequuntur? Exaggeratio est in interrogatione. Si Deus dilectos suos filios &domesticos suos in hac vita prae aliis affligit, quid futurum incredulis & ἀθέοις,à Dei familia alienis.Eph. 2. v. 12. in illos aliquando totam suam iram aquarum, cataclysmi instar effundet 2. Thess. 1. v. 5. & seqq. ac tarditatem supplicii gravitate compensabit. τῶν ἀπειθούντων vulgata reddidit, eorum qui non credunt. Sed Graecum est ἐμφατικώτερον, significatur enim incredulitas positiva & pertinax Evangelii contemtus eorum, qui Evangelium sibi praedicatum renuunt, eique credere nolunt, atque hac ratione seipsos vitâ aeternâ indignos iudicant. Act. 13. v. 46. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael. qui non patiuntur sibi persuaderi, ut oboediant & acquiescant Evangelio.

## 4:18
AND IF THE RIGHTEOUS IS SCARCELY SAVED, WHERE WILL THE UNGODLY AND THE SINNER APPEAR?

Connection. 1. He illustrates the antithetical comparison, brought forward in the immediately preceding verse, by the testimony of Scripture.

2. He shows what the end of the ungodly will finally be, of which he had treated in the preceding verse, namely, that before the judgment of God they will at some time not be able to stand, but will pay the penalties away from his sight. 2. Thessal. 1. vers. 9.

Exposition of the text. Καὶ εἰ ὁ δίκαιος μόλις σώζεται, ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται; By τὸν δίκαιον he understands him who, justified by faith in Christ, strives for righteousness, who fights the good fight, retaining faith and a good conscience 1. Tim. 1. vers. 18. & 19. To him he opposes the man ἀσεβέα καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸν, who is alien from faith in Christ and the worship of God, but on the contrary is held by a zeal for sinning, and is wholly given over to sins; both names seem to be taken from in the human forum, and transferred to the divine forum. For ὁ δίκαιος is a guilty person who is innocent, but ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς, is a guilty person who is the source ὑπόδικος He says concerning the just, that μόλις σώζεται. The Word σώζεται the Vulgate expressed by the future, shall be saved, but in the Greek it is the present, as also Prov. 11. v. 31. among the LXX Interpreters, from which passage Peter took this sentence. The Syrian likewise rendered it in the present [consult facsimile image] is saved, lives, in which way Augustine also cites it in his enarrations Psal. 6. And if the just man indeed with difficulty be saved, which reading of the present tense also occurs in certain more corrected Latin Codices. By τὸ μόλις σώζεται it is signified that for the pious the entrance into the kingdom of heaven is not opened except through many tribulations Acts 14. vers. 22. that for the pious on the way which leads to eternal salvation, great difficulties, pressures, and straits occur, that they cannot enter except with great labor and trouble through the narrow gate and the strait way which leads to life Matt. 7. vers. 13. Luke 13. vers. 24. which explanation is gathered from the preceding verse. For this first member of this little verse, if the just man with difficulty is saved, corresponds to the first member of the preceding verse. If the judgment of God begins from us, so that the sense may be: If the just man is not saved except through the judgment of God chastising his sins? Thus the little word μόλις is used Acts 14. vers. 18. μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους, not except with great labor and difficulty did they quiet the crowds. chap. 27. vers. 7. μόλις ἤλθομεν, not except with great labor and trouble, since the wind was hindering us, did we arrive at the place called Good Harbor. Wisd. 9. vers. 16. μόλις εἰκάζομεν those things which are on earth, and which are in our hands, we find μετὰ πόνου, where the latter is ἐξηγητικὸν of the former. Among Xenophon μόλις πῶς is taken for that which is scarcely, with difficulty, with a certain difficulty. Grammarians hand down that μόλις is the same as μόγις but it is deduced from μόγιστà μόγος, which πόνον, μόχθον, κακοπάθειαν signifies, thence μογὲω I endure labors, I suffer miseries, all of which show that the little word μόλις is most rightly referred to the cross and adversities, which the pious, striving for eternal life, are compelled to endure in this life.

Ποῦ φανεῖται; The Vulgate rendered, where shall they appear. But in the Greek it is singular, where shall he appear? so that we may understand that the same person is called a sinner and the impious, that is, the unbelieving and the one turned away from GOD. Some refer to the house of GOD, of which mention was made in the preceding verse, so that the sense may be, he will nowhere be able to have a place in the House of GOD, that is, in heaven. But the house of GOD in the preceding verse is not used for heaven or the house of glory; but for the house of grace, for the household of GOD, in whom He dwells by grace in this life. It is therefore more correctly understood concerning the judgment of GOD from Psalm 1. v. 5. The impious shall not stand or be able to stand in judgment, so that the sense may be: If the righteous is scarcely saved, how shall the impious be able to stand in the judgment of God, so that he is not cast out from His face and adjudged to eternal punishments. Lyranus in this place: Where shall he appear? Indeed nowhere, because they shall be hidden in the deep of hell. Some wish the phrase to be taken from those who, being ill-conscious of themselves, fear to appear in judgment, but it is more correctly said to be taken from those who, on account of their misdeeds, cannot stand before the judgment, but are compelled to hear the condemnatory sentence. This whole sentence is taken from the version of the LXX Interpreters Prov. 31. v. 31. where it is held in the same number of words: εἰ ὁ μὲν δίκαιος μόλις σώζεται, ὁ ἀσεβής καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται.

Latin:

ET SI IUSTUS VIX SALVATUR, IMPIUS & PECCATOR UBI PAREBUNT?

Connexio. 1. Illustrat collationem antitheticam, vers. proximè praecedente allatam, Scripturae testimonio.

2. Ostendit quis futurus tandem impiorum finis, de quo in v. praeced. egerat, videl. quòd coram Dei iudicio aliquando non poterunt consistere, sed poenas ab ipsius conspectu luent. 2. Thessal. 1. vers. 9.

Textus expositio. Καὶ εἰ ὁ δίκαιος μόλις σώζεται, ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται; Per τὸν δίκαιον intelligit eum, qui fide in Christum iustificatus iustitiae studet, qui militat bonam militiam, retinens fidem & bonam conscientiam 1. Tim. 1. vers. 18. & 19. Illi opponit hominem ἀσεβέα καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸν, qui à fide in Christum & cultu Dei alienus, contrà vero peccandi studio tenetur, & peccatis totus est deditus, utrumque nomen videtur desumtum à foro humano, & translatum ad forum divinum. Nam ὁ δίκαιος est reus insons, sed ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς, est reus fons ὑπόδικος De iusto dicit, quod μόλις σώζεται. Verbum σώζεται vulgata expressit per futurum, salvabitur, sed in Graeco est praesens, ut etiam Prov. 11. v. 31. apud LXX. Interpretes, ex quo loco Petrus hanc sententiam desumsit. Syrus itidem reddidit in praesenti [consult facsimile image]servatur, vivit, quo modo citat etiam Augustinus in enarr. Psal. 6.Et si iustus quidem vix salus sit, quae lectio praesentis temporis etiam occurrit in quibusdam Codicibus Latinis correctioribus. Per τὸ μόλις σώζεται significatur, quòd piis non nisi per multas tribulationes ingressus in regnum coelorum pateat Actor. 14. vers. 22. quòd piis in via, quae ducit ad salutem aeternam, magnae occurrant difficultates, pressurae & angustiae, quòd non nisi magno cum labore & molestia per angustam portam & viam arctam, quae ad vitam ducit, ingredi possint Matth. 7. vers. 13.Luc. 13. vers. 24. quae explicatio colligitur ex versu praecedente. Nam hoc prius membrum huius versiculi, si iustus vix salvatur, respondet priori membro praecedentis versiculi. Siiudicium Dei à nobis incipit, ut sit sensus. Si iustus non nisi per iudicium Dei castigantis illius peccata salvatur? Ita usurpatur vocula μόλιςActor. 14. vers. 18.μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους, non nisi magno cum labore & difficultate sedaverunt turbas. cap. 27. vers. 7.μόλις ἤλθομεν,non nisi magno cum labore & molestiae, quippe prohibente nos vento, pervenimus ad locum Boniportus dictum.Sap. 9. vers. 16.μόλις εἰκάζομενea quae in terra, & quae in manibus, invenimusμετὰ πόνου, ubi posterius est ἐξηγητικὸν prioris. Apud Xenophontem μόλις πῶς accipitur pro eo, quod est aegrè, difficulter, cum quadam difficultate. Grammatici tradunt, μόλις idem esse quod μόγις deducitur autem μόγιστà μόγος, quod πόνον, μόχθον, κακοπάθειαν significat, inde μογὲωlabores tolero, aerumnas patior, quae omnia ostendunt, voculam μόλις rectissimè referri ad crucem & adversitates, quas pii ad vitam aeternam contendentes in hac vita tolerare coguntur.

Ποῦ φανεῖται; Vulgata reddidit, ubi parebunt. Sed in Graeco est singulare, ubi comparebit? ut intelligamus, eundem dici peccatorem & impium, id est, incredulum & à DEO aversum. Quidam referunt ad domum DEI, cuius in praeced. vers. facta fuit sit sensus, nuspiam in Domo DEI, idest, in coelo habere poterit locum. Sed domus DEI in vers. praeced. non usurpatur coelo sive domo gloriae; sed pro domo gratiae, pro domesticis DEI, in quibus per gratiam in hac vita habitat. Rectius igitur accipitur de iudicio DEI ex Psalm. 1. vers. 5.Non stabunt vel stare poterunt impii in iudicio, ut sit sensus,. Si iustus vix salvatur, quomodo impius stare poterit in Dei iudicio, ut non proiiciatur à facie eius & aeternis suppliciis adiudicetur. Lyranus in h. l. Ubi comparebit? quidem nustpiam, quia in profundo inferni absconditi erunt. Quidam volunt, phrasin desumptam esse ab illis, qui malè sibi conscii verentur in iudicio comparere, sed rectiùs dicitur desumta ab illis, qui ob malefacta sua non possunt coram iudicio stare, sed coguntur sententiam damnatoriam audire. Desumta est tota haec sententia ex versione LXX. Interpretum Prov. 31. v. 31. ubi totidem verbis habetur: εἰ ὁ μὲν δίκαιος μόλις σώζεται, ὁ ἀσεβής καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται.

## 4:19
THEREFORE ALSO THOSE WHO SUFFER ACCORDING TO THE WILL OF GOD, LET THEM COMMEND THEIR SOULS TO A FAITHFUL CREATOR IN WELL-DOING.

Connection. 1. The Apostle concludes συμπεράσματι διδακτικῷ the exhortation made to those by whom persecution and afflictions are to be tolerated in this life on account of the name of Christ. Luther in this place: This is the final admonition of D. Peter to those by whom affliction is to be endured on account of the will of God.

2. In this conclusion he repeats the argument, taken from the will of God, and at the same time mixes in another twin one, of which one is taken from the truth of the divine promises. God most kindly wills to preserve our souls in persecutions, because He is faithful in keeping His promises: the other is sought from the omnipotence of GOD. GOD is also able to preserve our souls in persecutions, because He is their omnipotent creator, for preservation is nothing other than the continuation of being.

3. The Apostle also instructs those who suffer persecution how they ought to conduct themselves in it. 1. Let them acknowledge that afflictions are not sent upon them except by the will of God. 2. Let them commend the outcome to God in true patience and humility. 3. Let them not depart from the zeal of doing good on account of their hardships. 4. In all these things let them imitate the example of Christ.

4. He had said in v. praeced. the righteous is scarcely saved, from this he gathers that all Christians, especially those who suffer persecution, ought to commend their souls to God and depend entirely upon God, and by no means exalt themselves or trust in their own strength. The Ordinary Gloss on this passage: Because judgment begins at the house of the Lord, and because through many tribulations it is necessary to enter into the kingdom of God, therefore this remains for those who are to suffer, that when they suffer according to what God wills, that is, for the sake of righteousness, they should commend their souls to God, presuming nothing of themselves, so that He may both purge them here according to what He wills, and make them blessed in the future, because He is faithful in rendering good things to those whom He has created.

Exposition of the text. ὥστε καὶ οἱ πάσχοντες κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. The little word ὥστε shows that this conclusion is inferred from the preceding. The Syrian rendered it [consult facsimile image] for this reason. By τοὺς πάσχοντας some understand specifically those who resist even unto blood, Hebr. 12. vers. 4. to whom afflictions even unto death are brought by evil men, which they gather from the following, because such persons are commanded πάχοντες to commend their souls to God. But it is more correctly taken generally of any kind of persecution, whether one sustains reproaches, or the plundering of goods, or prisons, or the very punishment of death for the name of Christ, as is understood from the preceding, from which this exhortatory conclusion is deduced vers. 12. 14. & 15. nor does the precept about commending souls to God stand in the way, since it is general, pertaining to all who in any way suffer persecution. προσδιορισμὸν added κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ some wish to be joined with the following, so that the sense may be that this is the will of God, that they should commend their souls to God on the cross; but it is more correctly joined with the preceding, as is evident from cap. 3. v. 17. so that the sense may be, to whom according to the will of God afflictions are sent: for the Apostle warns again those who suffer that all afflictions proceed from the will of God. ὡς πιστῷ κτίστη παρατιθέσθωσαν τας ψυχὰς ἑαυτῶν The Vulgate rendered it. Let them commend their souls to a faithful creator. The Greek properly has. As to a faithful creator, i.e., let them deposit their souls with a faithful creator. Truly, in some codices ὡς is absent and it is read simply πιστῷ κτίστῃ. But this particle is held in more approved codices, and is expressed by the Syrian through a prefix, nor is it added idly, for it expresses the cause on account of which those who suffer ought to deposit their souls with God, namely, because He is their creator and faithful guardian, to whom therefore the custody of souls, as a certain precious deposit, can most safely be commended. Some translate the word κτίστῃ as possessor, so that it may be derived from κτάω I possess, but it is more correctly rendered creator, so that it may be derived from κτίζω I create, which agrees more with the verb παρατιθέσθωσαν. for therefore he commands our souls to be commended into the protection and custody of God like a precious deposit, because God is their founder, and therefore He will by no means repudiate His work commended to Him and deposited with Him. But according to His most truthful promise He will both want to preserve them, as the most faithful; and will be able, as the most powerful. By ψυχὰς some understand life, by a certain μετωνυμίαν, because life is the effect of the soul united to the body, which meaning is not infrequent in the Scriptures Matth. 2. v. 20.c. 6. v. 25.cap. 10. v. 39. etc. some understand those very ones who suffer persecution Act. 2. v. 41. & 43.c. 7. v. 14.Rom. 13. v. 1. etc. by a certain species of Synecdoche, because the soul is the other, and the same more important part of man. But the soul is more correctly accepted, Matth. 10. v. 28.c. 11. v. 29. which the Apostle commands to be commended to God the founder in the whole of life and even in death itself, since it cannot be killed by persecutors, but separated from the body it remains still surviving. By the verb παρατιθέσθωσαν the Apostle looks back to psal. 31. v. 6. into your hand אפקיד I will commend or I commend (for פקד among other things also signifies he deposited, he commended, he committed something to someone to be saved and guarded, thence פקדון a deposit, a thing which is deposited with someone Levit 6. vers. 2.) my spirit, which the LXX rendered thus.

εἰς χεῖράς σου παραθήσομαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου, which words Christ repeats on the cross Luc. 23. v. 46. The Apostle therefore sends back those who suffer persecution according to the will of God to the example of Christ, who commended his soul as a noble deposit into the hands of his heavenly Father, and on the cross taught that the same must be done by us. To this also pertains what is added ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐα, The Vulgate rendered it, in well-doing, to which version corresponds what is held in the two Books of Kings, the plural ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐαις, and in the Syriac version, in good works. But the more approved Codices have the singular ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ. Some understand this specifically of beneficence toward one's neighbor, because Christians in persecutions ought not to pray for evils for their enemies, much less return them, but by the example of Christ praying for his crucifiers Luc. 23. vers. 34. to render good to them for evils, Matth. 5. vers. 44. Luc. 6. vers. 27. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, pray for those who persecute and slander you. Rom. 12. vers. 21. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. But it is more correctly taken in a general sense regarding the pursuit of good works 1. Petr. 2. vers. 15. which includes beneficence toward one's neighbor as a species, so that the sense is that because of persecutions one must not depart from the pursuit of good works, but the pursuit of virtues must be joined with the tolerance of evils, so that we may thus demonstrate ourselves to be true Christians and genuine sons of God, on the cross. 1. by constantly confessing the name of Christ. 2. by glorifying God vers. 16. 3. by praying for persecutors. 4. by showing faith from good works Iae. 2. vers. 18. Thus therefore the Apostle repeats what he had said before vers. 15. that those doing evil should not be afflicted because of their misdeeds, but as Christians, who demonstrate their faith by good works. Gloss. ordin. in h. l. in well-doing, not because of sins. The Syrian arranges the text otherwise, but without any variation of sense. Who suffer according to the will of God, let them commend their souls to him in good works as to a faithful creator.

Latin:

ITAQUE & HI, QUI PATIUNTUR SECUNDUM VOLUNTATEM DEI, FIDELI CREATORI COMMENDENT ANIMAS SUAS IN BENEFACTIS.

Connexio. 1. Concludit Apostolus συμπεράσματι διδακτικῷ exhortationem factam ad eos, quibus ob Christi nomen persecutionem & afflictiones in hac vita tolerandae. Lutherus in h. l. Haec ultima est D. Petri admonitio ad eos, quibus propter voluntatem Dei perferenda afflictio.

2. In hac conclusione repetit argumentum, à voluntate Dei desumtum, simulque aliud geminum admiscet, quorum unum desumium à veritate promissionum divinarum. Deus benignissimè vult animas nostras in persecutionibus conservare, quia fidelis est in servandis suis promissis: alterum petitum est à DEI omnipotentia. DEUS etiam potest animas nostras in persecutionibus conservare, quia est omnipotens earum conditor, conservatio enim nihil aliud est, quàm essendi continuatio.

3. Instruit etiam Apostolus eos, qui persecutionem patiuntur, quomodo in ea sese gerere debeant. 1. Agnoscant, afflictiones non nisi Dei voluntate sibi immitti. 2. Eventum in vera patientia & humilitate Deo commendent. 3. à studio benefaciendi propter aerumnas minimè discedant. 4. In hisce omnibus exemplum Christi imitentur.

4. Dixerat in v. praeced.iustum vix salvari, ex eo colligit, omnes Christianos praecipuè eos, qui persecutionem patiuntur, animas suas Deo commendare, & in solidum à Deo pendere, nequaquam vero se extollere, autsuis viribus confidere debere. Glossa ordin. in h. l. Quia, incipit iudicium à domo Domini, & quia per multas tribulationes oportet ingredi inregnum Dei, itaque hoc restat illis passuris, ut quando patiuntur secundùm quod Deus vult h. e. propter iustitiam, commendent animas suas Deo, nil de se praesumentes, ut & hic secundùm quod vult purget, & in futuro beatificet, quia fidelis est bona reddendo illis, quos creavit.

Textus expositio. ὥστε καὶ οἱ πάσχοντες κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ. Vocula ὥστε ostendit, hanc conclusionem ex praecedentibus inferri. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]propter hoc. Per τοὺς πάσχοντας quidam speciatim intelligunt eos, qui usque ad sanguinem resistunt,Hebr. 12. vers. 4.quibus affictiones usque ad mortem à malis hominibus inferuntur, quod colligunt ex sequentibus, quia iubentur huiusmodiπάχοντεςanimas suas Deo commendare. Sed rectiùs generaliter accipitur de quovis persecutionum genere, sive quis probra, sive bonorum rapinam, sive carceres, sive ipsum mortis supplicium ob Christi nomen sustineat, ut intelligitur ex praecedentibus, ex quibus haec conclusio exhortatoria est deducta vers. 12.14. & 15. nec obstat praeceptum de animabus Deo commendandis, quippe quod generale est, pertinens ad omnes, qui quovis modo persecutionem patiuntur. προσδιορισμὸν adiectum κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ quidam coniunctum volunt cum sequentibus, ut sit sensus, hanc esse Dei voluntatem, ut commendent animas suas Deo in cruce; sed rectiùs coniungitur cum praecedentibus, ut constat ex cap. 3. v. 17. ut sit sensus, quibus iuxta Dei voluntatem afflictiones immittuntur: denuò enim monet Apostolus eos, qui patiuntur, omnes afflictiones à Dei voluntate procedere. ὡς πιστῷ κτίστη παρατιθέσθωσαν τας ψυχὰς ἑαυτῶν Vulgata reddidit. Fideli creatori commendent animas suas. Graeca proprie habent. Tanquam fideli creatori i. e. apud fidelem creatorem deponant animas suas. Sanè in quibusdam Codicibus abest ὡς ac simpliciter legitur πιστῷ κτίστῃ. Sed habetur haec particula in probatioribus Codicibus, ac exprimitur à Syro per praefixum, nec est otiosè adiecta, exprimit enim causam, propter quam hi, qui patiuntur, animas suas apud Deum deponere debeant, nimirum, quia est earum creator & fidelis custos, cui proinde tutissimè animarum velut praeclari cuiusdam depositi custodia commendari possit. Vocem κτίστῃ quidam vertunt possessori, ut sit deducta à κτάωpossideo, sed rectius redditur, creatori, ut sit deducta à κτίζωcreo, quod magis congruit cum verbo παρατιθέσθωσαν. ideò enim animas nostras in Dei tutelam & custodiam instar praeclari depositi commendari praecipit, quia Deus est earum conditor, ac proinde opus suum sibi commendatum & apud se depositum minimè repudiabit. Sed iuxta veracissimam suam promissionem eas conservare & volet, ut fidelissimus; & poterit, ut potentissimus. Per ψυχὰς quidam intelligunt vitam, per quandam μετωνυμίαν, quia vita est animae corpori unitae effectus, quae significatio in Scripturis non est infrequens Matth. 2. v. 20.c. 6. v. 25.cap. 10. v. 39. &c. quidam intelligunt illos ipsos, qui persecutionem patiunturAct. 2. v. 41. & 43.c. 7. v. 14.Rom. 13. v. 1. &c. per speciem quandam Synecdoches, quia anima est hominis alterae, eademque potior pars. Sed rectiùs accipitur anima, Matth. 10. v. 28.c. 11. v. 29. quam Deo conditori in tota vita & in ipsa etiam morte Apostolus commendari iubet, cum à persecutoribus ea occidi non possit, sed à corpore separata maneat adhuc superstes. Verbo παρατιθέσθωσαν respicit Apostolus ad psal. 31. v. 6.in manum tuamאפקידcommendabo vel commendo ( פקד enim inter alia etiam significat deposuit, commendavit, ad servandum & custodiendum aliquid alicui commisit, inde פקדוןdepositum, res quae apud aliquem deponiturLevit 6. vers. 2.) Spiritum meum, quod LXX. sic reddiderunt.

εἰς χεῖράς σου παραθήσομαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου, quae verba Christus in cruce repetit Luc. 23. v. 46. Remittit igitur Apostolus eos, qui persecutionem iuxta Dei voluntatem patiuntur, ad exemplum Christi, qui animam suam velut praeclarum depositum in manus Patris sui coelestis commendavit, ac in cruce idem nobis faciendum esse docuit. Eò etiam pertinet, quod additur ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐα, Vulgata reddidit, in benefactis, cui versioni congruit, quod in duobus Regiis habetur plurale ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐαις, ac in Syriaca versione, in operibus bonis. Sed probatiores Codices habent singulare ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ. Quidam hoc in specie intelligunt de benesicentia erga proximum, quòd Christiani in per secutionibus nò debeàt hostibus suis mala precari, multò minus referre, sed exemplo Christi pro crucifixoribus suis orantisLuc. 23. vers. 34.bona pro malis eis reddere,Matth. 5. vers. 44.Luc. 6. vers. 27.Diligite inimicos vestros, benedicite devoventibus vos, benefacite his, qui oderunt vos, orate pro persequentibus & calumniantibus vos.Rom. 12. vers. 21.Noli vinci à malo, sed vince in bono malum. Sed rectiùs in genere accipitur de studio bonorum operum. 1. Petr. 2. vers. 15. quod beneficentiam erga proximum tanquam speciem includit, ut sit sensus, quod ob persecutiones non sit à studio bonorum operum discedendum, sed cum malorum tolerentia coniungendum esse studium virtutum, ut sic veros Christianos & genuinos Dei filios nos demonstremus, in cruce. 1. nomen Christi constanter confitendo. 2. Deum glorificando vers. 16. 3. pro persecutoribus orando. 4. fidem ex bonis operibus ostendendo Iae. 2. vers. 18. Sic ergò repetit Apostolus, quod antea dixerat vers. 15. ne malè agentes ob malefacta affligantur, sed tanquam Christiani, qui fidem suam bonis operibus demonstrant. Gloss. ordin. in h. l. in benefactis, non propter peccata. Syrus textum aliter ordinat, sed sine ulla sensus variatione. Qui patiuntur secundùm voluntatem Dei, commendent ei animas suas in operibus bonis tanquam creatori fideli.

## 5:1
THE ELDERS THEREFORE WHO ARE AMONG YOU, I BESEECH, A FELLOW-ELDER AND WITNESS OF THE SUFFERINGS OF CHRIST, AND A PARTAKER OF THE GLORY THAT IS TO BE REVEALED IN THE FUTURE.

Connection. 1. After the Apostle had in general exhorted all those to whom he writes, from v. 8 of chapter 3 up to the end of the preceding chapter 4, to holiness of life, Christian charity, and especially to the tolerance and patience of afflictions, he returns to a special exhortation, or to personal and hypothetical places, such as he had also treated in the second and third chapters. As therefore there he had first admonished the subjects chap. 1 v. 13. Secondly the servants chap. of the same v. 18. Thirdly the wives chap. 3 v. 1. Fourthly the husbands chap. of the same v. 7 of their duty. Now furthermore he addresses the Presbyters and the younger men, and likewise informs them of the debt of their office. Thus therefore the Apostle passes from the political and economic state to the Ecclesiastical state.

2. The Apostle had said chap. immediately preceding v. 11. If any man speaks, as the oracles of God. If any man ministers, as of the strength which God supplies, which precepts directly and properly pertain to those who are constituted in the Ecclesiastical ministry, this exhortation therefore he declares more abundantly in this place.

CHAPTER V.

3. Toward the end of the preceding chapter, he had exhorted those who suffer according to the will of God, that they should commend their souls to God, their faithful creator, in good works. But because this salutary admonition can be known only from the instruction of the Ecclesiastical ministry, and can be brought into practice only from its serious inculcation, therefore the Apostle now furthermore admonishes those who perform the Ecclesiastical Ministry of their duty.

Disposition of the text. About to exhort those who perform the office of teaching in the Church to the diligent care of the flock committed to them, he premises three arguments for the exhortation, which all and each are deduced from the person of the exhorter. First, he calls himself a fellow-presbyter. Second, a witness of the sufferings of Christ. Third, a partaker of the heavenly glory to be revealed in its own time. What force of concluding may be in the individual arguments will appear later.

Exposition. Πρεσβυτέρους τοὺς ἐν ὑμῖν παρακαλῶ. The Royal and another Codex add the illative particle οὖν, which the Syrian Interpreter also has [consult facsimile image] as does the Vulgate translation. The elders therefore I beseech, by which reason the connection of this exhortation with the preceding ones might be expressly insinuated, but all the remaining Codices read simply πρεσβυτέρους τοῦς ἐν ὑμῖν. Lorinus, out of supine ignorance, thought the little word [consult facsimile image] in the Syriac text signifies but, when the particle [consult facsimile image] in the Syriac text is placed for οὖν, [consult facsimile image] and the relative pronoun I is joined with the verb [consult facsimile image] I ask, I beseech. Tremellius rendered it but. But [consult facsimile image] placed absolutely is an adversative conjunction Matt. 1. v. 12.18. etc. when however it is joined with [consult facsimile image] it is illative and connective, corresponding to the Greek οὖν Matt. 7. vers. 20.chap. 12. v. 12. etc. He understands but the Apostle by Presbyters [refers to] them, whom the Holy Spirit has placed over the flock as Bishops to feed the Church of GODAct. 20. v. 28. who labor in the word and doctrine.1. Timoth. 5. v. 17. who are the teachers of the Church, and governors of morals, whence Jerome in Epistle 85 to Evagrius rightly warns, that Presbyter in this place, just as also in the Acts of the Apostles and in the Pauline Epistles, is not a name of age, but of office and dignity, that which is evidently gathered from the precept of feeding, given to these Presbyters in the following verse, whence also Bede, following Jerome, calls these Presbyters Pastors of the Church. Just as, he says, the Lord commanded blessed Peter to have care of his whole flock, that is, of the Church, so Peter himself rightly commands the following pastors of the Church, that each one should protect the flock of GOD which is with him with solicitous governance. He adds moreover τοὺς ἐν ὑμῖν, to signify that he is addressing determinately and specifically those Presbyters who at that time were performing the duty of teaching in the Churches of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,1. Petr. 1. vers. 1. the precept itself meanwhile is general, pertaining to the Presbyters of all times and places. Hugo warns, that the Apostle by this formula of speaking wished to admonish the Presbyters of humility, since he does not say, Presbyters, who are over you, but who are in you, or among you. But this is more subtle than true, for immediately in the following verse the Apostle uses the same formula of speaking concerning the flock committed to these Presbyters. And even if κυριότης and the primacy of Monarchical power is deservedly denied to Presbyters, nevertheless ἐξοχὴ and the primacy of honor cannot be denied to them, and therefore Pastors cannot and ought not to be in every way equalized to the flock.

Παρακαλῶ The Vulgate rendered it I beseech, that which John Huss explains: by sacred things or through all sacred things I pray. The Syrian likewise rendered it by [consult facsimile image] requesting, beseechingMatth. 8. vers. 5.Rom. 12. vers. 5. The interlinear Gloss deduces from it this doctrine, that Elders are to be besought.1. Tim. 5. vers. 1. Do not rebuke an Elder, but beseech him as a Father, the younger as brothers. And indeed the word παρακαλῶ sometimes obtains the meaning of beseeching,Matth. 8. vers. 5.31. & 34.cap. 14. vers. 36.cap. 18. vers. 29. & 32. &c. meanwhile, however, more often, especially in the Acts and Apostolic Epistles, it also has the meaning of exhortingActor. 2. vers. 40.capitis 11. vers. 23.cap. 14. vers. 27.

Roman. 15. vers. 30.cap. 16. vers. 17. in the same way it is also used by Peter in this very Epistle cap. 2. vers. 11.cap. 5. vers. 12. whence Luther followed it in this place in the German version. The LXX likewise use סית for it, which signifies to stimulate, to persuade Deuter. 13. vers. 6. Meanwhile, both significations can be joined, as in cap. 2. vers. 11. so also in this place. I exhort, and if it is right, I pray and beseech.

ὁ συμπρεσβύτερος. Jerome in Epist. 85 rendered it, fellow-presbyter. The Complutensian Codex substituted ὡς for ὁ, as a fellow-presbyter.
