Bonus pastor praebere debet ovibus suis pabula salutaris doctrinae doctè; exempla bonae conservationis sanctè, subsidia caritatis piè. Pascat verbo, pascat exemplo, pascat orationum suffragio. Bernh. Epist. 201.

12. Exemplo Christi, qui sevocat Pastorem bonumIoh. 10. v. 11. discendum, quomodo oves pascendae. Ezech. 34. v. 15.Ego pascam oves meas &c. dicit Dominus:v. 16.Quod perierat, requiram; quod errans erat, reducam; quod confractum fuerat, alligabo; quod infirmum fuerat, consolidabo, & quod pingue & forte est, custodiam & pascam illas in iudicio.

13. Non sufficit gregem ad salutaria pascua ducere, sed lupos etiam ab ovili oportet abigere. Nihil differt à lupo, qui pro oribus non vigilat contra lupum. Luth. tom. 2. Ien. f. 3816. Bonus pastor piis carminibus gregem nutrit; arma, quae ad impietatis eversionom faciunt, negligere non solet, imò vero cantillans, quae sunt Spiritus, etiam in lupos arma capit.

14. Sola Christi doctrina est salutare animae pabulum. Veri ergò Pastores non sunt, qui vel à docendi officio penitùs abstinent, vel humana somnia velut mortifera venena ovibus proponunt.

15. Ut Pastores dicuntur esse in grege, sic grex vicissim dicitur esse in Pastore. Nimirum quia & caritatis & officii vinculo Pastor gregi & grex Pastori est coniunctus.

16. Omnia quidem, quae sunt in coelo ac terra, Dei sunt, interim Ecclesia est ipsius peculium & hereditas, ipsius ovile & cara possessio. Hoc ipsum vel maximè excitare potest ac debet Pastores ad vigilantiam, quod sciant, gregem sibi commissum esse gregem DEI, id est, à DEO electum, & gregem Christi, id est, à Christo redemtum.

17. Episeopatus unus est & indivisus, cuius pars à singulis in solidum tenetur, inquit Cyprianus lib. de simpl. Praelat. Singulis pastoribus portio gregis adscripta est, quam regat unus quisque, & gubernet rationem sui actus Domino redditurus, inquit idem lib. 1. Epist. 3.

18. Pastores Ecclesiae non solùm debent ποιμαίνειν sed etiam ἐπισκοπεῖν, pascendi praeceptum laboris; inspiciendi prudentiae & vigilantiae ipsos admonet. August. lib. 19. de Civ. DEI cap. 9. Episcopatus nomen est operis, non honoris,ἐπισκοπεῖνenim est superintendere, ut intelligat non se esse Episcopum, qui praeesse dilexerit, non prodesse. Isid. Pelusiota lib. 1. Epist. 149. Episcopus ex ipso nomine perspectum, quod speculari eum oporteat, atque omni ex parte oculum esse omnia prospicientem, neque quid quam negligentem Bernh. in sententiis. Pastorum est vigilare super gregem, propter tria necessaria, videlicet ad disciplinam, ad custodiam, ad preces. Ad disciplinam, propter morum correctionem, ne grex commissus propria molestiâ deficiat. Ad custodiam, propter Diabolicam suggestionem, ne hostili seducatur calliditate. Ad preces, propter tentationum instantiam, ne vincatur à pusillanimitate.

19. Illud ἐπισκοπεῖν etiam hoc requirit, ut Pastor non solùm prospiciat omnibus, sed etiam singulis. Actor. 20. v. 28.Attendite universo gregi, in quo vos Spiritus sanctus posuit Episcopos pascere Ecclesiam Dei &c.v. 31.propter quod vigilate, memoriâ tenentes, quoniam per triennium nocte & die non cessavi cum lachrymis monens unumquemque vestrûm.Ezech. 3. v. 17.cap. 33. v. 7.Fili hominis, speculatorem dedite domui Israël (in genere) v. 18.Si dicente me ad impium (in specie) morte morieris, & non annunciaveris ei, sanguinem eius de manu tua requiram.Hebr. 13. v. 17.Obedite praepositis vestris, ipsi enim vigilant, quasi rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri. De Gregorio Thaumaturgo Episcopo Neocaesariensi Gregorius Nyssenus in ipsius vita memorat, quod singulos erudierit ad virtutem suo statui congruam. Iuvenes hortabatur ad modestiam, senes ad patientiam, servos ad obedientiam, ut erga Dominos fideles & morigeri essent, dominos ad clementiam, ut erga subditos se humanos exhiberent, pauperes ad contemtum opum, ut veras divitias censerent esse virtutes, divites ad beneficentiam, ut eleëmosynas egenis facerent, cogitantes, se opum non esse dominos, sed dispensatores, mulieribus pudicitiam, pueris obedientiam, parentibus disciplinam inculcabat; moerentibus consolationem, dubiis consilium, afflictis opem afferebat, omnibus omnia factus.1. Cor. 9. vers. 23.

20. Gregor. Nazianz in Apol. cum dixisset, illud quod vi ac necessitate exprimitur, minimè laudandum esse, subiungit praesentem adductum locum. Proinde vel maximè id lex nostra & legislator noster sanxit, ut grex non coactè, sed spontaneè, ac libenti animo pascatur. Ambrosius in Psal. 118. octon. 14. exponens verba Psalmographi. Voluntaria oris mei beneplacita fac Domine &c. multis ostendit, plurimùm referre, utrum ex voluntate quid facias, an ex necessitate, quod placeat DEO, & urget cumprimis locum Apostolicum 1. Cor. 9. v. 17.Si volens hoc ago, mercedem habeo, ibid. Dominus operationes servulorum suorum spontaneas probat potiùs, quàm coactas, ideò ex servis liberos facit, ut magis voluntatum nostrarum munera, quàm necessit atum obsequia conferamus. Quò etiam referri potest illud, quod Petrus hoc loco liberalem animum & affectum in officio Pastorali requirit.

21. Beda in h. l. sic commentatur. Coactè providet, qui propter rerum temporalium penuriam, non habens unde vivat, idcirco praedicat Evangelium, ut de Evangelio vivere possit. Contra spontaneè providet, qui nullius rei terrenae, sed tantùm supernae mercedis intuitu verbum DEI praedicat. Postea addit, religionis opera cuncta spontanee debere fieri, id quod declarat exemplo Israëlitarum in V. T. Iuxta illud, inquit, exemplum constructionis tabernaculi, quod praesentem Ecclesia constructionem praetendit, ubi & omnis multitudo filiorum Israël obtulit mente promtissimâ atque devotâ primitias Domino ad faciendum opus tabernaculi sponte propriâ cuncta tribuens, & ipsi artifices sponte sua obtulerunt se ad faciendum opus.

22. Ἀισχροκερδεία in omni vitae statu, cumprimis vero in Ministerio Ecclesiastico detestanda. Dicuntur autem illi αἰσχροκεοδῶςgregi providere, qui quaestus gratia tàm sanctum ministerium exercent, & ex curae pastoralis officio ditari quaerunt. Beda in h. l. Turpis lucri gratiâ providet gregi DEI, qui propter quaestum & terrena commoda praedicat, cum religionis opera cuncta spontaneè fieri debeant. De eiusmodi variis Pastoribus gravissimae extant in Prophetis querelae. Esai. 56. v. 11.Canes impudentissimi nescierunt saturitatem, ipsi Pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam, omnes in viam suam declinaverunt, unusquisque ad avaritiam suam.Ierem. 6. v. 13.cap. 8. v. 10.A minore usque ad maiorem omnes avaritiae student, & à Propheta usque ad Sacerdotem cuncti faciunt mendacium.Ezech. 13. v. 19.propter pugillum hordei & fragmen panis prophanant me coram populo meo &c. mentientes populo meo credenti mendaciis.Ezech. 34. v. 2.Vae pastoribus Israël, qui pascebant semetipsos!Mich. 3. v. 5.Haec dicit Dominus super Prophetas, qui seducunt populum meum, qui mordent dentibus suis & praedicant pacem: & si quis non dederit in ore eorum quippiam, sanctificant super eum praelium.1. Tim. 6. v. 5.existimant, quaestum esse pietatem. Contra vero fideles Pastores sic describuntur, quod sint ab hoc vitio alieni quàm maximè Num. 16. v. 15.1. Sam. 12. v. 3.Act. 20. v. 33.1. Tim. 3. v. 3.Tit. 1. v. 7. Hieronymus ad Nepotianum. Obsecro te, & repetensiterum iterumque monebo, ne officium Clericatus genus antiquae militia putes, id est, ne lucra seculi in Christi quaeras militia, ne plus habeas, quàm quando Clericus esse caepisti &c. Sunt nonnulli Clerici, qui possideant opes sub Christo paupere, quas sub locuplete & fallace Diabolo non habuerant, ut suspiret eos Ecclesia divites, quos mundus tenuit antè mendicos &c. Negotiatorem Clericum & ex inope divitem, ex ignobili gloriosum quasi quandam pestem fuge. Bernh. Epist. 24. ad Gilbertum Episcopum vera illa & indubitata sapientia est, quae turpia lucra contemnit, & indignum sibi iudicat, eodem cum idolorum servitute contubernio frui.

23. Ecclesia tenetur Pastoribus stipendia solvere & quidem liberaliter, ne penuria sit ipsis neglecti officii vel etiam sectandae αἰσχροκερδείας occasio. 1. Cor. 9. v. 7. & seqq. Galat. 6. v. 6.1. Timoth. 5. v. 17. & 18.

24. Tres sunt Ministerii Ecclesiastici pestes, ἀεργία, αἰσχροκερδεία & φιλοπρωτεία,ambitio, Tyrannis ac dominandi libido. Epist. Ioh. 3. v. 9.

25. Ut ergò Presbyteris turpis lucri, ita quoque dominii cupiditas est interdicta. Cogitent, se non esse Ecclesiarum dominos, sed ministros, 1. Cor. 4. v. 21.Omnia vestra suntv. 22.Sive Paulus, sive Apollo, sive Cephas &c. omnia vestra sunt. Cogitent sibi demandatum, ut gratiam divinitùs sibi datam aliis ministrent. Sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiae DEI.1. Petr. 4. v. 10.Cogitent, Pastoribus illis maledictionem denunciatam, qui cum austeritate ac saevitia imperantEzech. 34. v. 4.qui alligant onera gravia & importabilia & imponunt in humeros hominum, digito autem suo nolunt ea movere.Matth. 23. v. 4. Cogitent, se eo fine praeesse, ut emineant sanctitate, & aliis praeluceant humilitate, non autem ut ostentent suam potestatem & severitatem. Cogitent, non absolutum in gregem dominium, sed pascendi eius curam sibi iniunctam. Lyranus in h. l. Presbyteri non sint elevati per superbiam natione praelationis.

26. Ecclesia est hereditas & peculium Domini. Christus Ecclesiam sibi suo sanguine acquisivit.Act. 20. v. 28. ipse ergò solus est Ecclesiae Dominus. Culturam, huius vineae suae aliis elo cavit, ipse vero solus est & manet Dominus. Matth. 21. v. 33.

27. Pastores non solùm docere debent verbo, sed etiam exemplo; velut vivam pietatis & virtutis imaginem se exhibeant, in studio ac stadio virtutis auditores suos praeeant. Ioh. 10. v. 4.Pastor ante oves vadit, & oves illum sequuntur.Phil. 3. vers. 17.Imitatores mei estote.2. Thessal. 3. vers. 9.Non quasi non habuerimus potestatem, sed ut nosipsos daremusτύπονvobis ad imitandum nos.1. Timoth. 4. v. 12.Esto typus fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate, in fide, in castitate.Tit. 2. vers. 7.In omnibus teipsum praebeτύπονbonorum operum in doctrina, integritatem, gravitatem, incorruptelam: in quem locum Hieronymus sic commentatur. Optat Paulus, ut Timotheus;

aut quicunque praelatus sit instar archetypi sive primariae formae, ex qua viva virtutum simulachra lineamentis vitae honestae in se translatis exprimuntur. Ea igitur debet esse Pastoris vita, ut non solùm quie. quid loquitur, sed etiam quicquid agit, sit auditorum doctrina. Quomodo possunt alios informare, qui in seipsis informes & monstrosi inquit Lyranus in h. l. Monstrosa autem res est gradus summus & animus infimus; Sedes prima & vita ima; lingua magniloqua & vita oticsa; sermo multus & fructus nullus; vultus gravis & actus levis; ingens autoritas & nutans stabilitas, ut scribit Bernhardus lib. 2. de considerat. ad Eugenium cap. 8. Quod sumus professione, actione potiùs, quàm nomine demonstremus, ut nomen congruat actioni, actio respondeat nomini, ne sit nomen inane & crimen immane: ne sit honor sublimis & vita deformis; ne sit deifica professio & illicita actio; ne sit religiosus amictus & irreligiosus profectus; ne sit gradus excelsus & deformis excessus; ne habeatur in Ecclesia Cathedra sublimior, & conscientiae Sacerdotis reperiatur humilior; ne locutionem simulemus columbinam, & mentem habeamus caninam, inquit Ambrosius lib. de dignit. Sacerd. cap. 3. tom. 4. oper. f. 179.

28. Auditores secuti suos Pastores in via pietatis & virtutis itidem fiant τύποι aliis fidelibus. 1. Thess. 1. v. 6.Imitatores nostri facti estis & Domini.vers. 7.ita ut facti sitisτύποςomnibus credentibus in Macedonia.

29. Fidi Pastores in hoc seculo loco praemii, odia & ingratitudinem mundi reportare solent, igitur in futurum seculum extra hunc mundum respiciant, & Satanae ac mundi odiis opponant promissa praemia coelestia, apud Christum reposita, quorum spe omnia pericula & adversa vincere, seque ad officium summa diligentia exequendum excitare debent. Luth. in h. l. Officium Pastorum nimis sublime est, quàm ut in hac vita compensari possit, in coelo copiosa merces ipsis parata.Dan. 12. v. 3.Matth. 25. v. 21.2. Tim. 4. v. 8.

30. Christus est Princeps Pastorum, Pastor primarius, magnus Pastor ovium Hebr. 13. v. 20. imò unusEzech. 34. v. 23. ipsius oves sunt propriae, ipsius etiam Pastores reliqui sunt proprii, pariter cum ovibus ipsius sanguine redemti. Act. 20. v. 28. Bened. Arias in h. l. Christus est princeps Pastorum iure, munere, exemplo.

31. Praemium coeleste à Pastorum principe fidelibus Pastoribus promissum, & suo tempore reddendum, vocatur corona iustitiae 1. Timoth. 4. vers. 8. tùm quia Christus perfectà suâ obedientiâ ac iustitiâ eum promeruit, tùm quia Deus eam promisit fideliter sibi servientibus, ac sanctitati & iustitiae studentibus 1. Corinth. 9. vers. 25.corona vitaeIac. 1. v. 12.Apoc. 2. v. 20. quia illi, quibus haec corona dabitur, verae & aeternae vitae participes reddentur; & corona gloriae h. l. quia gloriosos & illustres eos reddet, quibus à Christo imponitur.

32. Coronae nomen de tribus potissimùm fideles pastores monere potest. Primò, quòd certamen non exiguum in Ministerio ipsis propositum. 2. Timoth. 2. v. 5.Qui certat, non coronabitur, nisi legitimè certaucrit. Nam nisi certanti nulla corona datur. 2. quòd post certamen exantlatum praemia coelestia ipsis sint expectanda. Finis pugnae fortis est victoria; victoriae consequens corona. 3. quòd praemia illa futura sint aeterna. Lyranus in h. l. Vita aeterna corona est, quia nec principium nec finem habet.

33. Horum omnium consideratio ad alacritatem in obeundo munere Pastores excitare debet. Longè maius praemium fidelibus Pastoribus à Christo promissum, quàm Iacobo in gregibus soceri pascendis tam graviter occupato. Gen. 31. v. 31. Gregorius lib. 7. Epist. 48. Si sic laborat & vigilat, qui pavit oves Laban, quanto labori, quantisque vigiliis debet intendere, qui pascit oves Dei? cui etiam divina & coelestia praemia sunt promissa.

34. Quò plura sunt fidelis Pastoris requisita, quò rariora sunt fidelium Pastorum exempla, quò maiora praemia fidelibus Pastoribus promissa, eò maior debet esse gregis Dominici erga fideles Pastores reverentia.

35. Iuniores subiecti esse debent senioribus, patiantur se ab eis moneri, utpote longo rerum usu edoctis & affectuum dominio minùs obnoxiis, reverentiam & obedientiam illis exhibeant, ac sanctis eorum monitis pareant.

36. Hoc conforme est mandato divino Lev. 19. vers. 32.Coram cano capite surgas, & honora personam senis; conforme hoc est iuri Naturae, rectae rationi, dictis & exemplis saniorum gentilium, qui Credebant hoc grande nefas & morte piandum. Si iuvenis vetulo non assurrexerat.

OMNES AUTEM INVICEM HUMILITATEM INSINUATE, QUIA DEUS SUPERBIS RISISTIT, HUMILIBUS AUTEM DAT GRATIAM.

Connexio. 1. Exhortationi speciali ad Presbyteros officii dignitate, & iuniores aetate directae subiungit Apostolus exhortationem generalem ad omnes cuiuscunque status, conditionis & aetatis homines directam, in qua primùm omnium humilitatem omnibus commendat.

2. Praeceperat Apostolus, iuniores debere subiici senioribus. Hoc praeceptum quasi quadam correctione amplificat, quâ illud ad omnes extendit, ac hypothesin ad thesin transferendo omnes per humilitatem sibi iuvicem subiectos esse debere asserit. Beda in h. l. Ne Praelati audientes (iunioribus dari subiectionis praeceptum) putarent, solummodo subditis suis, & non etiam sibi debitae humilitatis iura esse servanda, continuò generaliter admonendo subiecit; omnes autem humilitatem insinuate.

3. Pestis obedientiae est superbia, nisi enim subigantur alti & elati illi Spiritus, quibus homo turget, nemo alteri cedere volet ideò postquam Apostolus iuniores exhortatus fuerat ad subiectionem & reverentiam erga seniores, & ipsos & in genere omnes ad humilitatem exhortatur.

Dispositio. Proponitur in hoc versiculo. 1. Apostolica exhortatio. 2. Exhortationis ratio. Exhortatio duplex est. 1. ad subiectionem mutuam. 2. ad superbiae fugam. Ratio exhortationis petita est à consequentibus tùm superbiae, tùm humilitatis ἀντιθετικῶς sibi invicem oppositis.

Expositio. πάντες δὲ ἀλλήλοις ὑποτασσόμενοι τὴν ταπεινοφροσύνην ἐγκομβώσασθε. Vulgata reddidit. Omnes autem invicem humilitatem insinuate. Sed in Graeco textu additur ὑποτασσόμενοι;omnes invicem subiecti seu subiicientes vos, est enim praesentis temporis participium, vel ut quidam Codices legunt ὑποτάσσεσθεvos subiicite. Adversativam δὲ quidam Codices omittunt, unde quidam Interpretes hanc veluti correctionem ἀσυνδέτως adiectam statuunt. Sed habetur in probatioribus & pluribus Codicibus, ac omninò eam requirit universalitas praecepti, per quandam quasi correctionem speciali praecepto subiecti, ut subaudiatur vocula μᾶλλον. Omninò iuniores debent subiici senioribus, sed omnes potiùs sibi mutuò debent subiici. Syrus Interpres non solùm voculam δὲ, sed etiam universalem πάντες ut & participium ὑποτασσόμενοι prorsus omisit, proinde non statuit hîc novum praeceptum, sed cum praecedente praecepto iunioribus in specie dato illud coniungit, hoc modo. Et vos iuniores subdite vos senioribus vestris, & amicite vos intrinsecus demissione mentis unus erga alium. Sed Syriaca versio, cum sit rivulus, fonti Graeco non debet praeiudicare. De significatione verbi ἐγκομβώσασθε plurimum variant Interpretum sententiae. 1. Vulgata reddidit Insinuate. Eam sequitur Beda in comm. Omnes, inquit, iubentur humilitatis insinuare virtutem. Videtur vetus Interpres legisse ἐγκολπώσασθε,insinu recondite, sinu distento comprehendite. In sinu semper & pectore ferte tanquam rem carissimam, vel ut glossa interlinearis exponit, in sinu semper habete. Insinuare in hac significatione apud probatos scriptores Latinos non occurrit, sed aliud ipsis significat, quod Lyranus & Iohannes Huss. sic expressit. Insinuate i. e. exterius opere ostendite, non tantum mente habete. Lyranus. Verbis & operibus demonstrate, ut excitetis vos mutuò ad opera humilitatis. Alii, insinuate. i. e. vestro exemplo in aliorum sinum mittite. Salmero versioni Latinae fulcrum quaesiturus sic exponit. Insinuare propriè est coniungere & quasi latenter & cautè in sinum se immittere. Sed quilibet videt, hanc significationem esse alienam. Quis enim dixerit, quod latenter & cautè in sinum humilitatis nos immittere debeamus? aut quomodo haec significatio deduci potest ex verbo Graeco ἐγκομβώσασθε? 2. Syrus reddidit per verbum [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael, quod bis usurpatur in N. T. Act. 12. v. 8. ubi in Graeco est περιβάλου τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου involve te operimento tuo, & hoc loco, amicite vos intrinsecus[consult facsimile image] quod Syrus ἐξηγήσεως causâ addidit, ut emphasin praepositionis ἐν in verbo ἐγκομβώσασθε exprimeret. Congruit haec involvendi ac induendi significatio cum usu verbi ἐγκομβώσασθε apud Graecos scriptores. Pollux l. 4. cap. 18. scribit, τῇ τῶν δούλων ἐξωμίδι προσκεῖσθαι καὶ ἱματίδιον τὶ λευκὸν, quod ἐγκόμβωμα sive ἐπίβλημα nominetur.

Hesychius ἒγκομβωθείς exponit δεθεὶς & ἐγκεκόμβωται affert pio ἐνειληταί Item κομβώσασθαι exponit στολίσαθαι ac κόσσυμβοι sive κοσσύμβην dicit fuisse ἐγκόμβωμα καὶ περιζωμα Ἀιγύπτων. Hanc significationem videtur secutus Oecumenius, qui reddidit, vobis circumdate. Sic ergò metaphora ducta esset à genere vestimenti in nodum constricti, quo servi olim utebantur, quod ἐγκόμβωμα vocabatur, ut sit sensus. Induite humilitatem & omni exparte eam amplectimini, sicut vestis totum corpus tegit. Instar vestis modo constrictae humilitatem vobis coniunctam retinete, ne uspiam excutiatur. Simili phrasi utitur Apostolus Col. 3. v. 12.ἐνδύσασθαι ταπεινοφροσύνην. 3. Huic expositioni cognata est ea, qua ἐγκομβώσασθε exponitur innodate, illigate h. e. arctè vobis astringite humilitatem. Ut enim ante monuimus, genus illud vestimenti, quod ἐγκόμβωμα dicebatur, in nodum solebat constringi. Henricus Stephanus ex veteri quodam Lexico citat, ἐγκόμφωμα esse τὸν δεσμόν τῶν χειριδων. Suidae, ὁκόμβος, (ex quo κόμβωμα & ἐγκόμβωμα) ἐστι τῶν δύο χειριδίων, ὃθαν τις δήσῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἲδιον τράχηλον. Erasmus reddidit, infixam habete humilitatem. Tam arctè constricta debet esse humilitas, ut nec Diabolus ipse hoc vinculum solvere possit. Eodem modo Vatablus. Humilitatem vobis infixam habete, vel arctè seu nodis illigatum tenete. Pagninus. Humilitatem vobis illigatam habete, nam κόμβοςnodum significat. Camerarius in not. ἐγκομβὼσασθεdevincite, compingite. Sensus igitur erit. Humilitatem arctissimis nodis illigate & innodate, ne elabatur. Huc referri potest, quòd κόμβος Hesychio idem est quod κόσυμβος i. e. ἀνάδεσμα, ὅπερ αἱ κρισσαὶ φοροῦσιν ὃμοιον ἀσπιδίσκῳ. Suidae est itidem ἀνάδεσμος & χιτὼν κρισσωτὶς. Pro nodo & ἀναδέσματι accipitur Exod. 28. v. 39. ubi οἱ κόσυμβοι τῶν χιτώνων ἐκ βύσσου nodi tuniearum ex bysso, pro quibus Hebraici textus versio habet, stringes ei tunicam ex bysso, Pollux lib. 2. titulo de tonsura & crinibus, pro crinium nodo accipit. In eod. cap. Exod. vers. 4.χιτὼν κοσυμβωτὶς est tunica nodis substricta. 4. Ab hac expositione non multùm abit ea, quâ ἐγκομβώσασθε exponitur pro ornate vos. Nam vestis non solùm corpus tegit, sed etiam ornat. Ac στολίσασθαι, per quod Hesychius verbum ἐγκομβώσασθαι exponit, significat non solùm vestiri, sed etiam ornari. Suidae κομβώματα sunt τὰ καλλωπίσμαθαornamenta.

Biblia Regia hoc loco pro ἐγκομβώσασθε legunt ἐγκομπώσασθε; apud Suidam vero ἐγκομπώσασθαι exponitur per στολίσασθαι. Sic ergò fores sensus. Estote intus ornati humilitate. Quamvis verò Beza in annot. tertiam significationem repudiet tanquam tralatitiam & huic loco minimè convenientem, tamen cum trium harum posteriorum significationum exempla sint allata, eaedemque invicem minimè pugnent, sed sint subordinatae, ideò nulla ex illis simpliciter repudiari potest.

Ταπεινοφροσύνη in malam quidem partem Coloss. 2. v. 18. usurpatur, ubi coniungitur cum θρησκεία τῶν Αγγέλων. ac cap. eiusd. vers. 23. ubi coniungitur cum ἐθελοθρησκείᾳ καὶ ἀφειδία σώματος, significat ergò stolidam animi demissionem, sed in aliis Scripturae dictis virtutem illam Christianam notat, imò fundamentum omnium virtutum, quando quis modestè de se sentit & est animo demisso, ὁ γὰρ ταπεινόφρων ἒστιν ὁ ταπεινὰ φρονῶνAct. 20. v. 19.Eph. 4. v. 2.Phil. 2. v. 3.Col. 3. v. 12. Syrus h. l. reddidit per [consult facsimile image]humilitatem, mansuetudinem, lenitatem &c. mentis, hae enim virtutes sunt cognatae ὃτι ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται, ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσι χάριν, Locus desumtus est ex Prov. 3. v. 34. iuxta LXX. Interpp. nisi quod pro ὁ θεὸς ibi legitur κύριος. Iisdem verbis hanc sententiam citat Iacobus cap. 4. v. 6. in textu Hebraeo apud Salomonem habetur. Ipse deludet illusores, & mansuetis dabit gratiam; sed sine ulla sensus variatione.

Ὑπερήφανοι dicuntur homines superbi ac fastuosi. Luc. 1. v. 51.Rom. 1. v. 30.2. Tim. 3. v. 2. Eustathius tradit ὑπερήϕανος habere pleonasmum literae η, ut sit quasi ὑπέρϕανος ab ὑπερϕαίνομαιsuper alios emineo. Qui enim superbus est atque arrogans, supra caeteros se conspiciendum praebet, supra eos videlicet se attollens. Apud Demosthenem in Midiam, ὑπερηϕανία καὶ ὑπεροψία coniunguntur ut ἰσοδυναμοῦντα. Eustathius participium ὑπερηφανέοντες apud Homerum Iliad. λ. exponit ὑπερφρονοῦντες, ex superbia enim contemtus aliorum nascitur. LXX. utuntur pro גאה vel גאיוןtumidus, fastuosusIob. 40. vers. 7.Psal. 93. v. 2. &c. pro גבהsublimisPs. 100. v. 7.ὀφθαλμὸι ὑπερήφανοι, quos Esai. 5. vers. 15. vocant ὀφθαλμοὺς μετεώρους, pro זר vel זרון superbus, elatus à rad. זורintumuit, efferbuit prae superbiaPsal. 118. v. 21.51.69. &c. Ier. 43. v. 2. pro רם vel מרוםelatus, elevatus,2. Reg. 22. v. 28.Iob. 38. v. 15. &c. superbia enim ex oculis, verbis, gestibus & vestibus elucet; ac undiquaque per omnia corporis membra sui vestigia relinquit. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image]illis qui sese elevant atque, exaltant,ὑψοῦσιν ἑαντοὺς, ut vocantur Luc. 18. Vers. 13.

Verbum ἀντιτάσσεσθαιest militare, ex adverso quasi aciem instruere, praelio obsistere. Plutarchus in Caesare de Bruto loquens. άντιταχθεὶς δὲ Αντωνίῳ καὶ φιλίππῳ, ἀντιτά-ττεσθαι, inquit Budaeus, sicut &άντιπαρατάττεσθαιest ex adverso instrui in acie ut sinistrum cornu adversariorum dextro nostro; inde οἱ ἀντιτεταγμένοιdicuntur hostes, &ἡ ἀντίταξιςest aciei adversus hostem instructio. Haec significatio pulchrè huic loco congruit. Superbi enim sunt veluti invasores divinae gloriae, dum ad se rapiunt, quod est Dei; invasoribus antem & raptoribus vis armata opponi consuevit. Ambrosius in Psal. 118. octon. 7. tom. 4. fol. 464. Deus suae contumeliae propulsator veluti speciale quoddam certamen adversus superbiam suscipit. Emphasis huius verbi exponitur Iud. 2. v. 15.Quocunque egrediebantur Israëlitae, manus Domini erat contra illos in malum, ut non possent stare coram inimicis suis, ut colligitur ex versu praeced. Deus ipse aciem contra Israelitas instruebat, ac hostibus ipsorum victorias concedebat, contrà vero Israelitarum conatibus obsistebat. Deinde ἀντιτάσσεσθαι in genere significat resistere, repugnare, adversari, sive id fiat verbis, sive factis, Act. 18. v. 6.ἀντίτασσομένων αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων.Rom. 13. Vers. 2.ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν.Iac. 5. Vers. 6.ὁ δίκαιος ἀντιτάσσεται ὑμῖν. quae significatio itidem huic loco accommodari potest. Deus enim & verbis & factis superborum conatibus adversatur, eosque impedit. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image]occurrit, adversatus est,Act. 17. vers. 17. inde [consult facsimile image]ἐνάντιος.adversarius, inimicusIoh. 19. v. 12.quia Deus superbiam & superbos odio habet.

Per ταπεινοὺς intelliguntur hoc loco ταπεινόφρονες, τοῖς ὑπερηθανοις oppositi, ut docet antithesis. Significat ergò non tàm humilem statum, quàm demissum animum & humilem affectum, in qua significatione usurpatur Matth. 11. v. 29.Luc. 1. v. 52. &c. In textu Hebraeo Prov. 3. v. 34. habetur vocula עניים quod propriè signficat mansuetos, quia humilitas est mansuetudinis mater, inde צניZach. 9. v. 9.Matthaeus cap. 21. v. 5. reddidit πραΰς. LXX. ταπεινὸς utuntur pro דכאי־רוח qui sunt compressi sive humiles Spiritu.Psalm. 33. v. 18. pro צנוע quod significat eum, qui est animo demisso & humiliato. Prov. 11. v. 2. pro שפלhumiliatusPsal. 137. v. 7.Ezech. 21. v. 25. &c. Syrus habet nomen [consult facsimile image] quod itidem significat ταπεινὸν & πρᾷονhumilem & mansuetum.Matth. 5. v. 5.cap. 11. v. 28.cap. 21. Vers. 5.12. v. 16.1. Thess. 2. v. 7.

Χάρις in Scripturis significat. 1. favorem. 2. dona ex gratia data. Utraq; significatio hîc locum habet. Deus enim humilibus dat gratiam, apud alios facit eos gratiosos & caros, ut emergant, sicut de Iosepho dicitur Gen. 39. v. 4.invenit gratiam in oculis Potipharis domini sui. Cumulat etiam eos gratiae muneribus sive χαρίσμασι, ut appareat, ipsos Deo & hominibus caros esse.

## 5:2
FEED THE FLOCK OF GOD WHICH IS AMONG YOU, PROVIDING NOT BY CONSTRAINT, BUT WILLINGLY ACCORDING TO GOD, NEITHER FOR THE SAKE OF FILTHY LUCRE, BUT VOLUNTARILY.

Connection. 1. Having set forth three arguments of exhortation, he submits the exhortation itself, and explains the office of the Presbyters with the word of feeding.

2. He knew that it had been said to him by Christ ἀρχιποιμένι, feed my sheepJohn 21. verse 17.. Therefore, the care of feeding the sheep which he knew had been commended to him by Christ, he calls the Presbyters into its fellowship.

Disposition. To the exhortation. 1. He inserts a new argument, taken from the condition of the sheep to be fed. The sheep, which I commend to you to be fed, are the flock of God, that is, God redeemed them with his own bloodActs 20. v. 28. he himself also as the supreme Shepherd will at some time demand an account from you, how you have fed this flock of his.Ezek. 34. v. 10. I will require my flock from their hand.Heb. 13. v. 17. They themselves watch as those who are to render an account for your souls. 2. He also prescribes the manner in which the Presbyters ought to perform the office demanded of them. First, let them feed their flock, let them not be ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοποι, but let them look after the flock committed to their faith. Second, let them take care of the flock committed to them, not by constraint, but voluntarily, and not for the sake of filthy lucre, but with a ready mind.

Exposition. ποιμαίνατε. That the office of Presbyters of feeding is expressed by the word, Peter in this follows both the Prophets of the O. T. Jer. 3. v. 15. I will give you pastors according to my heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine.c. 23. v. 1. Woe to the pastors who destroy and scatter the flock of my pasture, says the Lord.v. 2. therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel to the pastors, who feed my peoplev. 4. I will raise up Pastors over them, and they shall feed them, (to which also pertain the Prophetic sayings, in which the Prophetic office of Christ, which he was to perform in the days of his flesh, is described by the word of feeding Cant. 1. v. 7. Isa. 40. verse 11. Ezek. 34. v. 2. & 23. Mic. 5. v. 4. Zech. 11. verse 4.) and Christ himself, from whom he had heard the command given to himself, feed my sheepJohn 21. verse 17. and Paul the Co-Apostle Act. 20. v. 28.Take heed to all the flock, over which the Holy Spirit has placed you as bishops to feed the Church of God, which He has acquired with His own blood, which passage is clearly parallel to this one of ours.

τὸ ἐν ἡμῖν πόιμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ. That τὸ ἐν ἡμῖν Erasmus, Calvin, and others translate thus, as much as in you lies, so that the sense may be, direct all your nerves and whatever ability God has bestowed upon you toward this, that you may rightly feed the flock committed to your faith. But 1. if Peter had intended this, he would have said τὸ καθ' ὴμᾶς, or as it is held Rom. 2. v. 18. τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν. 2. in the verse immediately preceding he used the same phrase concerning the Presbyters Πρεσβυτέρους τοὺς ἐν ὑμῖν παρακαλῶ, where that exposition does not have a place. 3. Peter knew that it was not said to him by Christ, feed as much as in you lies my sheep, but absolutely and simply, feed my sheep. 4. The Syriac rendered it, feed the flock of God [consult facsimile image] entrusted to you. 5. Such qualifications, as much as in you lies, as much as you can, do not agree with these precepts and exhortations concerning the works of an office being rightly performed, because those would rather relax than excite the mind of him to whom the exhortation is directed. It is therefore more rightly rendered, who is among you or with you, who is with you, namely with whom you are one body, one Church, just as the Vulgate also rendered it, who is in you, from which version it does not depart much that some render this phrase, who depends on you, just as it is said in Sophocles, ἐν σοι ἐσμέν, we depend on you. Benedict Arias interprets in you as among you yourselves, because the flock of God is in individual men or because individuals belong to this flock. But this is forced.

For ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ some codices read ποίμνιον τοῦ Κυρίου,, some τοῦ Χριστοῦ.. But most codices have τοῦ θεοῦ,, in which way the Syriac also reads, feed the flock [consult facsimile image]. Peter took this προσδιορισμὸν from the mouth of Christ Iohan. 21. v. 17. and the Apostles Act. 20. 28. and by it he intimates, first, that he is speaking of a divine and spiritual flock, and consequently that the word ποιμνίου is taken metaphorically in this place. Secondly, that this flock is Christ's own, inasmuch as He laid down His soul for it Iohan. 10. v. 15.. Thirdly, that pastors are occupied with the goods of another and concerning this flock they must one day to Him whose own it is, that is, to the supreme Pastor. an account must be rendered, all of which pertains to this, that the solicitude and diligent care of feeding the flock may be the more commended to Pastors. ἐπισκοποῦντες. The Vulgate rendered it, providing. The Greek words properly have, intending, or as Jerome reads in Epist. 85 to Evagrius, superintending, for it is said ἐπισκοπεῖν, he who takes care of some thing or person, and looks out for him regarding necessary things, Hebr. 12. v. 15. ἐπισκοποῦντες diligently taking heed, solicitously attending, lest anyone be wanting to the grace of God. The LXX use for דרש he inquired with solicitous care Deut. 11. v. 12. The Syrian rendered it in this place by [consult facsimile image] which signifies he visited, he had care, whence [consult facsimile image] Bishop, visitor, curator, by which name our Apostle uses in this very Epistle cap. 2. v. 25. He alludes to that very name in the word ἐπισκοποῦντες, as if he wished to say, be mindful of your name, respond to your name, show by the thing itself that you are Bishops, diligently and solicitously attending to what is fitting for each age, sex, condition, and state, and with provident care taking heed, lest the wolf invade and tear apart the flock committed to you, i.e., lest Satan through heretics infect the hearers committed to your faith with false doctrine, or stir up public scandals among them, by impelling them to impropriety of life and morals. Therefore, this passage is parallel to that Apostolic one Act. 20. v. 28. προσέχετε attend to yourselves and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as Bishops to feed the Church of God, which He acquired with His own blood. v. 29. For I know, that after my departure grievous wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock. Augustine, book 19 of the City of God, chapter 19, explains the force of the word in this way. ἐπισκοπεῖν If we wish, we can say in Latin to superintend, so that he may understand that he is not a Bishop who has loved to preside, not to be useful. Ambrose, on the dignity of the Priesthood, chapter 6, interprets Bishop as over-inspector. Some wish this appellation to descend from the metaphorical word צפה Watchman, by which in the O.T. the Prophets are called. Es. 52. v. 8. 56. v. 10. Ierem. 6. v. 17. Ezech. 3. v. 17. c. 33. v. 2. Os. 9. v. 8. because they foresaw future things and warned the people about them, just as a watchman sees from afar the arrival of an enemy, and with a sign given warns the inhabitants of the city about it. Any Ministers of the Church are called watchmen, because they ought to attend both to themselves and to the flock and to admonish the unruly and impenitent concerning future temporal and eternal punishments.Ezech. 3. v. 18. Spigelius in his commentary on the verses of Gunther mentions, that the Athenians called those Bishops, that is, Watchmen, whom they sent to watch what good and evil, what just or unjust was being done in each of the subject cities, to which he refers c. Episcopatum caus. 8. q. l. which meaning can not inappropriately be applied here. For thus Isidore interprets the name of Bishop in book 7 of the Etymologies, 12. and it is cited in c. Cleros dist. 21. The term Bishop is so called from this, because he who is made a Bishop superintends, namely, bearing the care of his subjects, σκοπεῖν for in Greek, is said in Latin to intend. For Bishops in Greek are interpreted in Latin as watchmen. For a watchman is a person set in charge in the Church, so called for this reason, that he may watch and look out for the life and morals of the peoples placed under him, and those whom he has approved as good he confirms by honoring, those whom he has discovered to be vicious, he amends by rebuking, as Prosper adds in book 2 of the Contemplative Life, c. 2. μὴ ἀναγκαστῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ἑκουσίως, The Vulgate not by constraint, but willingly. ἀναγκαστῶς is said to be done, which someone does unwillingly, forced, and out of necessity, ἀναγκάζειν for it is to force, to compel, to drive. Among Thucydides ἀναγκαστοὶ ἐκβάντες are called not voluntary, unwilling. But because he acts perfunctorily and negligently who acts according to the prescription of necessity; and because he proceeds slowly and coldly in acting who undertakes to carry out some matter forced and unwillingly, therefore the Apostle leaves it to be understood here from the antecedent the consequent, and warns the Presbyters not to perform the office of feeding sluggishly and with weariness. The Syrian added to the participle ἐπισκοποῦντες the adverb [consult facsimile image] spiritually, which some establish to be a gloss added to the text, by which it is signified that the discourse here is about the spiritual care of souls. Some wish that the Syrian placed that for that which is added in certain Greek Codices and all Latin ones, according to God. But it is more correctly said that he himself wished to declare ἐξηγητικῶς, which he adds a little later [consult facsimile image] not in violence, not by constraint, from the root [consult facsimile image] he bound.Ephes. 4. vers. 16. For those things which we do forced and out of necessity, they do not proceed from a free and spontaneous Spirit. Hence τῷ ἀναγκαστῶς τὸ ἑκουσίως, which Jerome

Epist. 85. rendered voluntarily. Thus also in Paul, that which is done κατὰ ἀνάγκτην, and that which is done κατὰ ἐκούσιον are opposed to one another in Epist. ad Philem. vers. 14. and those are called ἑκουσίως ἁμαρτάνειν Hebr. 10. vers. 26. who sin with full will, not out of ignorance or infirmity, but out of set malice, where however it is treated properly and specifically of the sin against the Holy Spirit. The LXX use for בנדבה voluntarily, in spontaneous will I will sacrifice to thee Psalm. 54. vers. 8. But the force of the little word ἑκουσίως is beautifully explained Exodi 36. vers. 2. whom his heart lifted or raised up to approach the work. Welche ihr hertz darzu trug. Luth. Die sich willig dar erboten. Arist. 5. Ethic. λέγω δὲ ἑκούσιον ὃ ἄν τις τῶν ἐφ᾽ αὐτῷ ὄντων εἰδὼς καὶ μὴ ἀγνοῶν πράττῃ. Opposed to it is ἀκούοιον not voluntary, not proceeding from our will. A passage parallel to this of ours exists. 1. Corinth. 9. vers. 17. εἰ ἑκὼν, if I do this willingly (if I have evangelized) I have a reward; but if ἄκων unwillingly, a dispensation is committed to me, that is, nevertheless the dispensation of preaching the Gospel is committed to me, and therefore unless I faithfully perform it, I am not going to have a reward, but a punishment.

After the little word ἑκουσίως in the two Royal [manuscripts] and another, κατά θεὸν, is added, which the Latin Codices also have. Jerome reads the same in Epist. 85. Ephrem Syrus tom. 2. paraen. 47. Synod VII. can. 4. Gregory part. 2. Curae pastoralis 7. and Bede in comment. h. l. where among other things he writes thus. Spontaneously and according to God he feeds the flock of God, who preaches the word of God with a view to no earthly thing, but only to the heavenly reward. The interlinear Gloss explains, that they may preach nothing but the divine, Gregory seems to refer to moderation in bodily and external matters, lest on account of that the Prelate, when he in no way satisfies the need of his subjects, kills himself with the sword of ambition. John Huss explains it in three ways. The little word according to, he says, either denotes the material cause, that nothing but the divine may be preached, against those who preach lies for the sake of gain: or the formal cause, that they may preach by keeping the form which Christ kept by preaching and providing; or the final cause, that they may preach for the sake of God, namely by establishing the glory of God as the end of preaching, and not for the sake of temporal things. A fourth can be added, that they may understand that they are rendering obedience to God in this calling, and therefore let them institute all things according to the will of GOD and for the glory of GOD. But because most Greek Codices do not have this προσδιορισμὸν added, it is deservedly held as foreign and alien, and therefore the Latin man complains in vain that these two words are missing in the Greek text and the Syriac edition. μηδὲ αἰσχροκερδῶς. Vulg. not for the sake of filthy lucre, Syriac, not in filthy lucre. Others prefer to translate, not basely affecting gain, not following filthy lucre, but the matter returns to the same thing. A parallel passage exists Tit. 1. vers. 7. A bishop must be μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ, not given to filthy lucre, for which 1. Timoth. 3. v. 3. it is said, a bishop must be μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ, ἀλλὰ ἀφιλαργυρον, from which it is understood that φιλαργυρίαν avarice or the desire of accumulating gold or silver and αἰσχροκερδίαν are synonymous for the Apostle. Tit. 1. vers. 11. he resolves the compound little word into two simple ones, when he says concerning the Pseudo-Apostles, διδάσκοντε ἃ μὴ δεῖ αἰσχροῦ κέρδους χάριν for the sake of filthy lucre.

Ἀλλὰ προθύμας, The Vulgate rendered, but willingly. Erasmus with ready minds, others, with a prompt mind. Syriac, from your whole heart, in which way also Luther. Von hertzen Grund. πρόθυμος is said, he who is prompt and prepared to do something Rom. 1. v. 15. & προθυμία is alacrity & promptness of mind, Actor. 17. v. 11. 2. Corinth. 8. v. 11. & following. 9. v. 2. The emphasis of this little word is beautifully explained. 1. Paral. 29. v. 17. ἐν ἁπλότητι καρδίας μου προεθυμήθην ταῦτα πάντα, καὶ νῦν τὸν λαόν σου τὸν εὑρεθέντα ὧδε εἶδον ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ προθυμηθέντα σοι. Between the preceding ἑκουσίως & προθύμως there does not seem to be much difference, unless one wishes to say that τὸ προθύμως intensifies the meaning of ἑκουσίου. Moreover, the Apostle opposes to it that which is done by constraint and for the sake of filthy lucre τὸ ἑκούσιον καὶ πρόθυμον, because both, he who by constraint, i.e., compelled by poverty, so that he may have wherewith to live, undertakes the pastoral office; and he who for the sake of filthy lucre, so that he may become rich, exercises it, does not do it from the heart, nor from a spontaneous Spirit, so that he may procure the salvation of the sheep, but for the sake of private advantage. Bede in his commentary on this place: He provides for the flock of God for the sake of filthy lucre, who preaches on account of gain and earthly advantages, since all works of religion ought to be done spontaneously. John Huss from Gilbert on this place: He is not spontaneous, whom poverty urges; or voluntary, whom greed draws.

A parallel passage exists Hebr. 13. v. 17. Obey your leaders, for they themselves watch as those who are to render an account for your souls, so that μετὰ χαρᾶς they may do this with joy, and not with groaning.

Latin:

PASCITE, QUI IN VOBIS EST, GREGEM DEI, PROVIDENTES NON COACTE, SED SPONTANEE SECUNDUM DEUM, NEQUE TURPIS LUCRI GRATIA, SED VOLUNTARIE.

Connexio. 1. Expositis tribus exhortationis argumentis ipsam exhortationem subiicit, ac verbo pascendi Presbyterorum officium exponit.

2. Noverat, à Christo ἀρχιποιμένι sibi dictum esse, pasce oves measIohan. 21. vers. 17. Quam ergò ovium pascendarum curam à Christo sibi noverat commendatam, in eius societatem Presbyteros vocat.

Dispositio. Exhortationi. 1. inserit novum argumentum, à conditione ovium pascendarum desumtum. Oves, quas pascendas vobis commendo, sunt grex Dei, h. e. Deus suo sanguine eas redemitAct. 20. v. 28.ipse etiam ut summus Pastor rationem à vobis aliquando exiget, quomodo hunc gregem suum paveritis.Ezech. 34. v. 10.Requiram gregem meum de manu eorum.Hebr. 13. v. 17.Ipsi vigilant quasi rationem pro anim abus vestris reddituri. 2. Praescribit etiam modum, quo Presbyteri officio sibi demandato fungi debeant. Primò pascant suum gregem, non sint ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοποι, sed gregi suae fidei commisso prospiciant. Secundò agant gregis sibi commissi curam, non coactè, sed voluntariè, nec turpis lucri gratiâ, sed promto animo.

Expositio. ποιμαίνατε. Quod Presbyterorum officium pascendi verbo Petrus exprimit, in eo sequitur tùm Prophetas V. T. Ierem. 3. v. 15.Dabo vobis pastores iuxta cor meum, & pascent vos scientia & doctrinâ.c. 23. v. 1.Vae pastoribus qui disperdunt & dissipant gregem pascua meae, dicit Dominus.v. 2.ideò haec dicit Dominus Deus Israël ad pastores, qui pascunt populum meumv. 4.suscitabo super eos Pastores, & pascent eos, (quò etiam pertinet dicta Prophetica, in quibus Propheticum Christi officium, quo in diebus carnis suae functurus erat, pascendi verbo describitur Cant. 1. v. 7.Esa. 40. vers. 11.Ezech. 34. v. 2. & 23.Mich. 5. v. 4.Zach. 11. vers. 4.) tùm Christum ipsum, ex quo sibi praeceptum audierat, pasce oves measIoh. 21. vers. 17. tum Paulum CoApostolum Act. 20. v. 28.Attendite universo gregi, in quo vos Spiritus S. posuit Episcopos pascere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit suo sanguine, qui locus huic nostro planè parallelus.

τὸ ἐν ἡμῖν πόιμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ. Illud τὸ ἐν ἡμῖν Erasmus, Calvinus & alii sic vertunt, quantum in vobis est, ut sit sensus, huc intendite omnes nervos & quicquid facultatis vobis Deus contulit, ut gregem fidei vestrae commissum rectè pascatis. Sed 1. si Petrus hoc voluisset, dixisset τὸ καθ' ὴμᾶς, vel ut habetur Rom. 2. v. 18.τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν. 2. in versu proximè praecedente eadem phrasi de Presbyteris usus fuerit. Πρεσβυτέρους τοὺς ἐν ὑμῖν παρακαλῶ, ubi expositio illa locum non habet. 3. Petrus noverat, sibi non esse à Christo dictum, pasce quantum in te est, oves meas, sed absolutè & simpliciter, pasce oves meas 4. Syrus reddidit, pascite gregem Dei [consult facsimile image]traditum vobis. 5. Praeceptis & exhortationibus hisce de operibus officii ritè peragendis non conveniunt eiusmodi mortificationes, quantum in te est, quantum potes, quia illae potiùs remitterent, quàm excitarent animum eius, ad quem exhortatio dirigitur. Rectiùs ergò redditur. qui apud vos vel penes vos est, qui vobiscum est, videlicet cum quo unum corpus, una Ecclesia estis, sicut & vulgata reddidit, qui in vobis est, à qua versione non multum abit, quod quidam hanc phrasin reddunt, qui à vobis pendet, sicut apud Sophoclem dicitur, ἐν σοι ἐσμέν,abs te pendemus. Bened. Arias in vobis interpretatur, intravos ipsos, quia in singulis hominibus sit grex Dei seu quod pertineant singuli ad hunc gregem. Sed hoc coactum.

Pro ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ quidam Codd. legunt, ποίμνιον τοῦ Κυρίου, quidam τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Sed plerique Codd. habent τοῦ θεοῦ, quo modo etiam Syrus legit, pascite gregem[consult facsimile image] Desumsit hunc προσδιορισμὸν Petrus ex ore Christi Iohan. 21. v. 17. & Co Apostoli Act. 20. 28. eoque innuit, primò se de divino ac spirituali grege loqui, ac proinde vocem ποιμνίου metaphoricè hoc loco accipi. Secundò gregem hunc esse Christi proprium, utpote qui animam suam pro eo posuerit. Iohan. 10. v. 15. Tertiò pastores versari in bonis alienis & de hoc grege ei, cuius proprius est, h. e. summo Pastori aliquando rationem reddendam esse, quae omnia eò pertinent, ut solicitudo & diligens pascendi gregis cura Pastoribus eò magis commendetur. ἐπισκοποῦντες. Vulg. reddidit, providentes. Graeca propriè habent, intendentes, sive ut Hieronymus legit Epist. 85. ad Evagrium, superintendentes, dicitur enim ἐπισκοπεῖν,qui curam alicuius rei vel personae agit, eique prospicit de necessariis,Hebr. 12. v. 15.ἐπισκοποῦντεςdiligenter caventes, solicitè attendentes, ne quis desit gratiae Dei. LXX. utuntur pro דרשsolicitâ curâ inquisivitDeut. 11. v. 12. Syrus reddidit hoc loco per [consult facsimile image] quod significat visitavit, curam habuit, unde [consult facsimile image]Episcopus, visitator, curator, quo nomine Apostlolus noster utitur in hac ipsa Epist. cap. 2. v. 25. Ad illud ipsum nomen in verbo ἐπισκοποῦντες alludit, ac si dicere velit, memores estote nominis vestri, respondete nomini vestro, reipsâ ostendite, vos esse Episcopos, diligenter & solicitè attendentes, quid cuique aetati, sexui, conditioni & statui conveniat, ac providâ curâ caventes, ne lupus gregem vobis comissum invadat ac diripiat h. e. ne Satanas per haereticos auditores fidei vestrae commissos falsâ doctrinâ inficiat, aut publica scandala inter eos excitet, ad vitae ac morum improbitatem eos impellendo. Parallelus igitur est hic locus illi Apostolico Act. 20. v. 28.προσέχετεattendite vobis & universo gregi, in quo vos Spiritus S. posuit Episcopos pascere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit suo sanguine.v. 29.Ego enim scio, quoniam intrabunt post discessionem meam lupi graves in vos, non parcentes gregi. Augustinus lib. 19. de Civ. Dei cap. 19. vim vocis hoc modo explicat. ἐπισκοπεῖνsi velimus, Latinè superintendere possumus dicere, ut intelligat, non se esse Episcopum, qui praeesse dilexerit, non prodesse. Ambros. de. dign. Sacerd. cap. 6. Episcopum interpretatur super inspectorem. Quidam volunt, hanc appellationem descendere à voce metaphoricaצפהSpeculator, quâ in V. T. Prophetae appellantur.Es. 52. v. 8.56. v. 10.Ierem. 6. v. 17.Ezech. 3. v. 17.c. 33. v. 2.Os. 9. v. 8.quia praeviderunt futura & populum de illis monuerunt, ficut speculator è longinquo videt adventum hostis, ac signo dato urbis incolas de eo admonet. Quivis Ecclesiae Ministri dicuntur speculatores, quia debent & sibiipsis & gregi attendere ac immorigeros & impoenitentes de futuris poenis temporalibus & aeternis admonere.Ezech. 3. v. 18. Spigelius in comm. ad versus Guntheri commemorat, Athenienses eos vocasse Episcopos, id est, Speculatores, quos speculatum mittebant, quid in unaquaque subditarum civitatum boni malique, aequi aut iniqui ageretur, quò refert c. Episcopatum caus. 8. q. l. quae significatio haud inconcinnè hûc accommodari potest. Sic enim Episcopi nomen interpretatur Isidorus lib. 7. Etymolog. 12. & citatur c. Cleros dist. 21. Episcopi vocabulum inde dictum est, quia ille, qui efficitur Episcopus, superintendat, scilicet curam gerens subditorum,σκοπεῖνenim Graecè, Latinè intendere dicitur. Episcopi enim Graecè, Latinè speculatores interpretantur. Nam speculator est praepositus in Ecclesia, ideò dictus, eò quod speculetur & prospiciat populorum infra se positorum vitam & mores, ac quos bonos probaverit honorando confirmat, quos deprehenderit vitiosos, arguendo emendat, ut addit Prosper lib. 2. de vita contempl. c. 2. μὴ ἀναγκαστῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ἑκουσίως, Vulg. non coactè, sed spontaneè.ἀναγκαστῶς fieri dicitur, quod quis facit invitus, coactus & ex necessitate, ἀναγκάζειν enim est cogere, compellere, adigere. Apud Thucydidem ἀναγκαστοὶ ἐκβάντες dicuntur non voluntarii, inviti. Quia vero defunctoriè & negligenter agit, qui ad praescriptum necessitatis agit; & quia lentè ac frigidè in agendo progreditur, qui coactus & invitus rem aliquam peragendam in se suscipit, ideò Apostolus ex antecedente hîc intelligendum relinquit consequens, ac monet Presbyteros, ne segniter ac cum toedio pascendi officio fungantur. Syrus participio ἐπισκοποῦντες addidit adverbium[consult facsimile image]spiritualiter, quod quidam statuunt esse glossema textui additum, quo significatur, de spirituali animarum cura hîc sermonem esse. Quidam volunt, Syrum illud posuisse pro eo, quod in quibusdam Codicibus Graecis & omnibus Latinis additur, secundùm Deum. Sed rectiùs dicitur, ipsum ἐξηγητικῶς declarare voluisse, quod paulo pòst subiicit [consult facsimile image]non in violentia, non coactè, à rad. [consult facsimile image]ligavit.Ephes. 4. vers. 16. Quae enim coacti & ex necessitate facimus, ea non proficiscuntur ex Spiritu libero & spontaneo. Inde τῷ ἀναγκαστῶς τὸ ἑκουσίως, quod Hieron.

Epist. 85. reddidit voluntariè. Sic etiam apud Paulum sibi invicem opponuntur illud, quod fit κατὰ ἀνάγκτην, & quod fit κατὰ ἐκούσιονin Epist. ad Philem. vers. 14. ac ἑκουσίως ἁμαρτάνειν dicuntur Hebr. 10. vers. 26. qui plenâ voluntate, non ex ignorantia vel infirmitate, sed ex destinata malitia peccant, ubi tamen propriè & in specie de peccato in Spiritum sanctum agitur. LXX. utuntur pro בנדבהvoluntariè, in voluntate spontanea sacrificabo tibiPsalm. 54. vers. 8. Pulchrè vero explicatur vis voculae ἑκουσίωςExodi 36. vers. 2. quem levavit vel extulit cor suum ad appropinquandum operi. Welche ihr hertz darzu trug. Luth. Die sich willig dar erboten. Arist. 5. Ethic. λέγω δὲ ἑκούσιον ὃ ἄν τις τῶν ἐφ᾽ αὐτῷ ὄντων εἰδὼς καὶ μὴ ἀγνοῶν πράττῃ. Illi opponitur ἀκούοιον non voluntarium, non profectum ex nostra voluntate. Locus huic nostro parallelus extat. 1. Corinth. 9. vers. 17.εἰ ἑκὼν,si volens hoc ago (evangelizavero) mercedem habeo; si autemἄκωνinvitus, dispensatio mihi credita est, id est, nihilominus tamen dispensatio praedicandi Evangelium mihi concredita est, ac proinde nisi fideliter ea fungar, non mercedem habiturus sum, sed poenam.

Post voculam ἑκουσίως in Regiis duobus & alio additur κατά θεὸν, quod habent etiam Codices Latini. Idem legunt Hieronymus Epist. 85. Ephrem Syrus tom. 2. paraen. 47. Synodus VII. can. 4. Gregorius part. 2. Curae pastoralis 7. & Beda in comment. h. l. ubi inter caetera sic scribit. Spontaneè & secundùm Deum pascit gregem Dei, qui nullius rei terrenae, sed tantùm supernae mercedis intuitu verbum Dei praedicat. Glossa interlinearis explicat, ut nihil nisi divinum praedicent, Gregorius videtur referre ad moderationem in re corporali & externa, ne propter illam Praelatus, cum subiectorum inopiam minimè satiat, se mucrone ambitionis occidat. Iohannes Huss tripliciter exponit. Vocula secundùm, inquit, vel denotat causam materialem, ut nihil nisi divinum praedicetur, contra illos, qui mendacia praedicant propter quaestum: vel causam formalem, ut praedicent servando formam, quam Christus servavit praedicando & providendo; vel causam finalem, ut praedicent propter Deum, videlicet Dei gloriam finem praedicationis statuendo, non autem propter temporalia. Potest addi quartum, ut intelligant, se Deo in hac vocatione praestare obedientiam, ac proinde secundùm DEI voluntatem & ad DEI gloriam omnia instituant. Sed quia plerique Codices Graeci hunc προσδιορισμὸν non habent adiectum, meritò pro peregrino & alieno habetur, ac proinde frustrà Latinus duas hasce voces in textu Graeco & & editione Syra desiderari conqueritur. μηδὲ αἰσχροκερδῶς. Vulg. neque turpis lucri gratiâ, Syrus, non in turpi lucro. Alii malant vertere, non turpiter affectantes lucrum, non sectantes turpe lacrum, sed res eòdem redit. Locus parallelus extat Tit. 1. vers. 7.Episcopum oportet esseμὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ,non turpis lucri cupidum, pro quo 1. Timoth. 3. v. 3. dicitur, Episcopum oportet esse μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ, ἀλλὰ ἀφιλαργυρον, ex quo intelligitur φιλαργυρίαν avaritiam sive auri argentive cumulandi cupiditatem & αἰσχροκερδίαν esse apud Apostolum synonyma. Tit. 1. vers. 11. voculam compositam resolvit in duas simplices, quando de Pseudo Apostolis dicit, διδάσκοντε ἃ μὴ δεῖ αἰσχροῦ κέρδους χάριν turpis lucri gratiâ.

Ἀλλὰ προθύμας, Vulgata reddidit, sed voluntariè. Erasmus animis propensis, alii, promto animo. Syrus, ex toto corde vestro, quo etiam modo Lutherus. Von hertzen Grund.πρόθυμος dicitur, qui ad aliquid faciendum promtus est ac paratus Rom. 1. v. 15. & προθυμία est alacritas & promtitudo animi,Actor. 17. v. 11.2. Corinth. 8. v. 11. & seqq. 9. v. 2. Emphasis huius voculae pulchrè exponitur. 1. Paral. 29. v. 17.ἐν ἁπλότητι καρδίας μου προεθυμήθην ταῦτα πάντα, καὶ νῦν τὸν λαόν σου τὸν εὑρεθέντα ὧδε εἶδον ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ προθυμηθέντα σοι. Inter praecedens ἑκουσίως & προθύμως non videtur multum discriminis intercedere, nisi quis velit dicere, τὸ προθύμως significationem ἑκουσίου intendere. Opponit autem Apostolus illi, quod fit coactè & turpis lucri gratiâ τὸ ἑκούσιον καὶ πρόθυμον, quia uterque, tùm qui coactè, i. e. inopiâ compulsus, ut habeat unde vivat, pastorale munus suscipit; tùm qui turpis lucri gratiâ, ut dives evadat, illud exercet, non ex animo, nec ex Spiritu spontaneo illud facit, ut ovium salutem procuret, sed privati commodi causâ. Beda in comm. h. l. Turpis lucri gratiâ providet gregi Dei, qui propter quaestum & terrena commoda praedicat, cum religionis opera cuncta spontaneò fieri debeant. Ioh. Hussus ex Gilberto in h. l. Non est spontaneus, quem paupertas urget; aut voluntarius, quem cupiditas trahit.

Locus parallelus extàt Hebr. 13. v. 17.Obedite praepositis vestris & ipsi enim vigilant quasi rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri, utμετὰ χαρᾶςcum gaudio hoc faciant, & non gementes.

## 5:3
NEITHER AS DOMINEERING OVER THE CLERGY, BUT BEING MADE EXAMPLES TO THE FLOCK FROM THE HEART.

Connection. 1. The Apostle continues in describing the manner in which Presbyters ought to perform their office, and after he had taught in the preceding verse that two vices ought to be absent from the pastoral duty, namely, first ἀεργίαν weariness, sloth, and sleepiness in caring for the flock, to which he had opposed eagerness; secondly αἰσχροκερδίαν or avarice, to which he had opposed προθυμίαν, now he touches upon a third as well, namely, the lust for domineering, arising from ambition.

2. He disapproved of those who seek gain in the ministry, now furthermore he censures those who seek honor in the same. There is a great kinship between both vices, and one by consent draws the other with it. For he who out of ambition desires to domineer over his hearers, he seeks a multitude of ministers, pomp of garments, splendor of banquets, etc., for which matter he has need of money, obtained by base gain. Deservedly, therefore, after forbidden gain, he also forbids domination, because the desire for dominion draws with it the desire for gain, and vice versa.

Disposition. Just as in the preceding verse he had opposed ἀντιθετικῶς to one another, ἀναγκαστῶς & ἑκουσίως; αἰσχροκερδῶς & προθύμως, so in this verse he opposes κατακυριεύειν τῶν κλήρων, & τύπον γίνεσθαι τοῦ ποιμνίου. to one another. For those who arrogate dominion to themselves do not shine before their hearers with the example of a holy life, and especially of humility, but they compel them by command. Bede on this passage: Being made an example of the flock, so that, namely, the humility which you desire your subjects to have both toward you and toward one another, you yourselves may first both show in act and keep in your heart entirely.

Exposition of the text. μηδ᾽ ὡς κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων. Vulg. neither as domineering over the clergy, or over the Clergy. Most correctly. For although τὸ κατακυριεύειν seems to signify tyrannical domination, since the preposition κατὰ is almost always taken in a bad sense, nevertheless from the passage By the parallel Matt. 20. vers. 25.Luc. 22. vers. 25. it is understood that not only the abuse of lordship, but lordship itself is forbidden to Presbyters, for as Christ there, so in this place Peter, having been taught by Christ, forbids the Ministers of the Church, the successors of the Apostles in the office of teaching, that they should not preside over their hearers in the way that a political Magistrate presides over subjects by lording and exercising coercive power. Hence the Vulgate version rendered it simply not lording it over the Clergy; the Syriac in the same way, not as [consult facsimile image] lords of the flock. And Paul not only denies τὸ κατακυριέυειν, but also τὸ κυριέυειν to himself and the remaining Apostles and ministers of the Church, when he says 2. Corinth. 1. vers. 24. οὐ κυριέυομεν ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως, just as also Actor. 19. vers. 16. κατακυριέυειν is used simply for lordship or prevailing.

By τοὺς κλήρους the Apostle understands the same thing as by τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ in the preceding verse, namely the assemblies of the faithful and portions of the Lord's flock, which fell to individual Bishops to be fed, just as the Syriac also rendered it by [consult facsimile image] flock, which little word it had used in the preceding verse. A twofold reason for the appellation can be given. First, the Israelite Church in the O. T. was called the inheritance of the Lord, the peculiar treasure of the Lord, the rod of inheritance &c.Deut. 9. vers. 29.thy people and thine inheritancec. 32. v. 9.2. Sam. 21. v. 3.Bless the inheritance of Jehovah, whom he chose as a peculiar treasure.Psal. 33. vers. 12.Blessed is the people, whom the Lord chose for an inheritance to himselfPsal. 74. v. 2.thou hast redeemed the rod of thine inheritance.Ps. 78. v. 71.Israel his inheritance &c.Esa. 19. v. 25.my inheritance Israel &c. namely because it was God's own, and dear to him like an inheritance, which falls to someone by lot, for κλῆρος properly signifies a lot. Because therefore the Christian Church in the N. T. succeeded the Israelite Church of the O. T., therefore it also is deservedly called the lot and inheritance of the Lord, because Christ acquired it with his own blood Actor. 20. vers. 28. Secondly, because those portions of the Lord's flock fell to the Bishops as if by lot, just as in the division of an inheritance each person's portion comes to him by lot. The Israelites in distributing the land of Canaan used the lot by God's ordinance Psal. 78. vers. 55. whence the parts, which had fallen to individual tribes, were called κλῆροι or lots.Iud. 1. v. 3.20. v. 14. Jerome in his Epistle to Nepotianus, Ephrem vol. 2, paraenesis 37, the VII Synod canon 4, Bernard book 2 de consideratione 5, and Epistle 247, read Clergy, having changed the plural noun into the singular, but all Greek Codices have the plural τῶν κληρῶν, which does not lack emphasis, as is evident from what has been said.

Ἀλλὰ τύποι γινόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου. Some Latin Codices read, but form of the flock. But in the Greek it is the plural, forms of the flock, in which way also the more correct Latin Codices, both ancient and recent, read. The sense is that Presbyters ought to propose themselves to their flock as it were as types, forms, and certain patterns of the Christian life and of all virtues, but especially of humility, so that the hearers may always have before their eyes a mirror of good works proposed to them, which they may contemplate; and a pattern of a holy life, which they may imitate, whence the Syrian correctly expressed the sense, rendering the text thus that you may be to them [consult facsimile image] a form and good pattern, to which they can and ought to conform themselves. For [consult facsimile image] is formed from the root [consult facsimile image] he assimilated himself, he was made like. Parallel passages are 1. Tim. 4. vers. 12.Be a type of the faithful in word, in conversation, in charity, in Spirit, in faith, in chastity.Phil. 3. vers. 17.Be imitators of me and observe those who walk so, as you have us τύπον a form.2. Thessal. 3. vers. 9.that we might give ourselves to you τύπον to imitate us.Tit. 2. v. 7.In all things showing yourself a type of good works, in doctrine, integrity, gravity, incorruptness. The Vulgate version here adds, from the soul, in which way also Jerome Epist. 2 and Idacius against Varim. read, which Lyranus explains thus, that humility may be true, not feigned. But προσδιορισμὸς that is held neither in the Greek text, nor in the Syriac paraphrase, and the ancients citing this passage, the VII Synod can. 4, Ephrem, and Bernard in the said places, omit the same.

Latin:

NEQUE UT DOMINANTES IN CLERIS, SED FORMAE FACTI GREGIS EX ANIMO.

Connexio. 1. Pergit Apostolus in describendo modo, quo Presbyteri officio suo fungi debeant, ac postquam in versu praecedente duo vitia à pastorali munere abesse debere docuerat, videl. primò ἀεργίαν taedium, ignaviam ac somnolentiam in curando grege, cui opposuerat alacritatem; secundò αἰσχροκερδίαν sive avaritiam, cui opposuerat προθυμίαν, iam tertium quoque tangit, videl. dominandi libidinem, ex ambitione ortam.

2. Improbavit eos, qui in ministerio quaerunt lucrum, iam porrò taxat eos, qui honorem in eodem quaerunt. Utriusque vitii magna est cognatio, & unum per consensum secum trahit alterum. Qui enim ex ambitione in auditores dominari appetit, ille quaerit ministrorum copiam, vestium pompam, conviviorum splendorem &c. quam ad rem opus habet pecuniâ, turpi lucro comparatâ. Meritò igitur post interdictum lucrum etiam interdicit dominatum, quia cupiditas dominii trahit secum cupiditatem lucri, & vice versâ.

Dispositio. Sicut in praecendente versiculo ἀντιθετικῶς sibi invicem opposuerat, ἀναγκαστῶς & ἑκουσίως; αἰσχροκερδῶς & προθύμως, ita in hoc versiculo invicem opponit κατακυριεύειν τῶν κλήρων, & τύπον γίνεσθαι τοῦ ποιμνίου. Qui enim dominium sibi arrogant, non praelucent auditoribus suis sanctae vitae, & cumprimis humilitatis exemplo, sed cogunt eos imperio. Beda in h. l. Forma gregis facti, ut vid. humilitatem, quam subditos & ad vos & ad invicem habere desideratis, ipsi priùs & actu monstretis & in animo servetis ex integro.

Expositio textus. μηδ᾽ ὡς κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων. Vulg. neque ut dominantes in cleris, sive in Cleros. Rectissimè. Quamvis enim τὸ κατακυριεύειν Tyrannicum dominatum significare videatur, cùm praepositio κατὰ ferè in malam partem accipiatur, ex loco tamen parallelo Matt. 20. vers. 25.Luc. 22. vers. 25. intelligitur, non tantùm abusum dominatus, sed ipsum etiam dominatum Presbyteris prohiberi, ut enim ibi Christus, ita hoc loco Petrus à Christo ita edoctus Ministris Ecclesiae, Apostolorum in officio docendi successoribus prohibet, ne eo modo praesint auditoribus suis, quo Magistratus politicus dominando & imperium coactivum exercendo subditis praeest. Inde vulgata versio simpliciter reddidit non dominantes Cleris; Syrus eodem modo, non tanquam[consult facsimile image]domini gregis. Ac Paulus non solùm τὸ κατακυριέυειν, sed etiam τὸ κυριέυειν sibi & reliquis Apostolis ac Ecclesiae ministris derogat, quando dicit 2. Corinth. 1. vers. 24.οὐ κυριέυομεν ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως, sicut etiam Actor. 19. vers. 16.κατακυριέυειν simpliciter pro dominatu seu praevalescentia usurpatur.

Per τοὺς κλήρους intelligit Apostolus idem, quod per τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ θεοῦ in vers. praecedente, videlicet coetus fidelium ac gregis Dominici portiones, quae singulis Episcopis pascendae obtingerunt, sicut etiam Syrus reddidit per [consult facsimile image] gregem, quâ voculâ in praeced. vers. usus erat. Ratio appellationis dari potest duplex. Primò, Ecclesia Israelitica in V. T. dicebatur hereditas Domini, peculium Domini, virga hereditatis &c.Deut. 9. vers. 29.populus tuus & hereditas tuac. 32. v. 9.2. Sam. 21. v. 3.Benedicite hereditati Iehovae, quam elegit in peculium.Psal. 33. vers. 12.Beatus populus, quem elegit Dominus in hereditatem sibiPsal. 74. v. 2.redemisti virgam hereditatis tuae.Ps. 78. v. 71.Israël hereditatem suam &c.Esa. 19. v. 25.hereditas mea Israël &c. nimirum quia fuit Dei propria, ipsique cara instar hereditatis, quae alicui sorte obtingit, nam κλῆρος propriè sortem significat. Quia ergò Ecclesia Christiana in N. T. Ecclesiae Israelitae V. T. successit, ideò ipsa quoque meritò vocatur sors & hereditas Domini, quia Christus eam proprio suo sanguine acquisivio Actor. 20. vers. 28. Secundò, quia portiones illae Dominici gregis Episcopis veluti sortitò obtigerunt, sicut in hereditatis divisione unicuique sua portio per sortem obvenit. Israelitae in distribuenda terra Canaan ex Dei ordinatione utebantur sorte Psal. 78. vers. 55. unde partes, quae singulis tribubus obvenerant, vocabantur κλῆροι sive sortes.Iud. 1. v. 3.20. v. 14. Hieronymus in Epistola ad Nepotianum, Ephrem tom. 2. paraen. 37. VII. Synodus can. 4. Bernhardus lib. 2. de consid. 5. & Epist. 247. legunt, in Clerum, mutato nomine plurali in singulari, sed Graeci Codd. omnes habent plurale τῶν κληρῶν, quod non caret Emphasi, ut ex dictis constat.

Ἀλλὰ τύποι γινόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου. Quidam Codd. Latini legunt, sed forma facti gregis Sed in Graeco est plurale, formae facti gregis, quo modo etiam correctiores Latini Codices tùm vetusti tùm recentiores legunt. Sensus est, quod Presbyteri seipsos veluti typos, formas & exemplaria quaedam vitae Christianae ac virtutum omnium, cumprimis vero humilitatis gregi suo proponere debeant, ut auditores sibi semper ob oculos propositum habeant speculum bonorum operum, quod intueantur; & exemplat vitae sanctae, quod imitentur, unde Syrus sensum rectè expressit, textum sic reddens ut sitis eis[consult facsimile image]forma & exemplar bonum, cui sese conformare possint ac debeant. Formatur enim [consult facsimile image] à rad. [consult facsimile image]assimilavit se similis factus fuit. Loca parallela sunt 1. Tim. 4. vers. 12.Esto typus fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate, in Spiritu, in fide, in castitate.Phil. 3. vers. 17.Imitatores mei estote & observate eos, qui ita ambulaent, sicut habetis nosτύπονformam.2. Thessal. 3. vers. 9.ut nos ipsos daremus vobisτύπονad imitandum nos.Tit. 2. v. 7.In omnibus teipsum exhibens typum bonorum operum, in doctrina, integritatem, gravitatem, incorruptelam. Vulgata versio hîc addit, ex animo, quo modo etiam legunt Hieronymus Epist. 2. & Idacius contra Varim. quod Lyranus sic explicat, ut humilitas sit vera, non ficta. Sed προσδιορισμὸς ille nec in textu Graeco, nec in Syriaca paraphrasi habetur, ac veteres hunc locum citantes Synod. VII. can. 4. Ephrem. & Bernhardus d. locis. eundem praetermittunt.

## 5:4
AND WHEN THE PRINCE OF PASTORS SHALL APPEAR, YOU SHALL RECEIVE A NEVER-FADING CROWN OF GLORY.

Connection. 1. After he prescribed the manner of administering the Pastoral office, he returns to the confirmation of the exhortation, and brings forward a new argument, sought from the useful consequence, namely, the heavenly glory, which he teaches is promised to faithful Pastors in place of a gratuitous reward, and therefore is to be certainly expected.

2. He had said in v. 1 that he was κοινωνὸν τῆς δόξης ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι μελλούσης.. He now declares this κοινωνίαν more broadly, and teaches that it pertains to all Presbyters faithfully performing their office.

3. This can also be referred to the arguments of the exhortation, because he calls Christ the Prince of Pastors. For by that very thing he shows that absolute power over the flock of the Lord does not belong to Presbyters, but that they themselves are secondary Pastors, subject and subordinate to Christ the Prince of Pastors, to whom they also will at some time be compelled to render an account of the office administered by them.

Exposition of the text Καὶ φανερωθέντος τοῦ ἀρχιποιμένος. And when the Prince of Pastors shall have appeared. By the Prince pastor or Prince of pastors he understands Christ, of whom he had said in c. 2. v. 25, you have turned to the shepherd and Bishop of your souls, whom Paul Hebr. 13. v. 20. calls the great shepherd of the sheep. He is called ἀρχιποιμὴν, not only because he excels in dignity among all the remaining pastors, but also because he has power over all the rest, for all the remaining pastors are subject to his command and power, they administer the pastoral office in his name and place, and they themselves will also at some time be compelled to render an account of the administration of their office. This name is read as attributed to the Moabite King 2. Reg. 3. v. 4. by the author Theodoret. The Syrian rendered it [consult facsimile image] i.e. שר הרועים prince of Pastors: By φανέρωσιν he understands the final coming of Christ to judgment, just as it is also called by this name elsewhere in the Scriptures Col. 3. vers. 4. ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ 1. Ioh. 2. v. 28.3. v. 2. to which the cognate name ἀποκαλύψεως 1. Cor. 1. v. 7.2. Thess. 1. v. 7.1. Petri. 1. v. 7. & 13.c. 4. v. 13. & ἐπιφανείας 2. Thess. 2. v. 8.1. Tim. 6. v. 14.2. Tim. 4. v. 1.Tit. 2. v. 13. The Syrian has the verb [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael when that Prince of Pastors shall reveal himself.

Κομιεῖσθε τὸν ἁμαράντινον τῆς δόξης στέφανον. Ἀμαράντος is a herb that is perpetually green, never withering. It is therefore called στέφανος ἁμαράντινος an unfading crown, in distinction to the crowns which are given in this age to victors in war, or to boxers in the wrestling school, or to runners in the stadium 1. Cor. 9. v. 24. For those crowns are woven from corruptible flowers and leaves, which a little later wither and droop, whence they are said to receive στέφανον φθαρτὸν v. 25. But that heavenly crown, which will be given to faithful Presbyters by Christ the supreme judge of the contest, will never wither, or droop, or grow old, but will retain its greenness and vigor forever. It is called στὲφανος δόξης a crown of glory, either by such a phrase as occurs in Rom. 4. v. 11. so that it is a genitive of species, you will receive glory, which will be as it were a crown; or that the genitive is placed in the place of an adjective, you will receive a crown of glory i. e. a very glorious and illustrious one. 2. Tim. 4. v. 8. it is called a crown of righteousness. Iac. 1. v. 12. Apocal. 2. v. 10. it is called a crown of life. The Vulgate rendered the word κομεῖσθε as you will receive. The Greek properly has, you will carry away. as the Interpreter also translates c. 1. v. 9. The Syrian added [consult facsimile image] ἐξηγήσεως from him, because Christ the just judge will place that crown of righteousness, of life, and of glory upon his faithful servants. Compare those things which were said above at v. 4. of the first chapter.

Latin:

ET CUM APPARUERIT PRINCEPS PASTORUM, PERCIPIETIS IMMARCESCIBILEM GLORIAE CORONAM.

Connexio. 1. Postquam modum administrandi Pastorale officium praescripsit, redit ad exhortationis confirmationem, ac novum affert argumentum, petitum à consequente utili, videl. gloriâ coelesti, quam gratuiti praemii loco fidelibus Pastoribus promissam, ac proinde certò expectandam esse docet.

2. Dixerat v. 1. se esse κοινωνὸν τῆς δόξης ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι μελλούσης. Hanc κοινωνίαν latiùs iam declarat, & ad eandem omnes Presbyteros officio suo fideliter fungentes pertinere docet.

3. Potest etiam hoc ad argumenta exhortationis referri, quod Christum vocat Principem Pastorum. Eo ipse enim ostendit, Presbyteris non competere absolutam in gregem Domini potestatem, sed ipsos esse Pastores secundarios, Principi Pastorum Christo subiectos & subordinatos, cui etiam aliquando rationem officii à se administrati rationem reddere cogantur.

Textus expositio Καὶ φανερωθέντος τοῦ ἀρχιποιμένος. Et cùm apparuerit Princeps Pastorum. Per Principem pastorem sive Principem pastorum intelligit Christum, de quo in c. 2. v. 25. dixerat, conversi estis ad pastorem & Episcopum animarum vestrarum, quem Paulus Hebr. 13. v. 20. vocat pastorem ovium magnum. Is vocatur ἀρχιποιμὴν, non solùm quia dignitate inter omnes reliquos pastores eminet, sed etiam quia potestatem in reliquos omnes habet, eius enim imperio & potestati reliqui pastores omnes sunt subiecti, eius nomine & loco pastorale officium administrant, ipsi etiam aliquando rationem de officii sui administratione reddere cogentur. Legitur hoc nomen attributum Regi Moabitico 2. Reg. 3. v. 4. autore Theodoreto. Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] h. e. שר הרועיםprinceps Pastorum: Per φανέρωσιν intelligit novissimum Christi ad iudicium adventum, sicut etiam alibi in Scripturis hoc nomine appellatur Col. 3. vers. 4.ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ1. Ioh. 2. v. 28.3. v. 2. cui cognatum nomen ἀποκαλύψεως1. Cor. 1. v. 7.2. Thess. 1. v. 7.1. Petri. 1. v. 7. & 13.c. 4. v. 13. & ἐπιφανείας2. Thess. 2. v. 8.1. Tim. 6. v. 14.2. Tim. 4. v. 1.Tit. 2. v. 13. Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael cum seipsum Princeps ille Pastorum revelabit.

Κομιεῖσθε τὸν ἁμαράντινον τῆς δόξης στέφανον. Ἀμαράντος est herba perpetuò virens, nunquam marcescens. Vocatur ergò στέφανος ἁμαράντινοςcorna immarcessibilis, ad differentiam coronarum, quae in hoc seculo dantur victoribus in bello, vel pugilibus in palaestra, vel cursoribus in stadio 1. Cor. 9. v. 24. Coronae enim istae nectuntur ex floribus & foliis corruptibilibus, quae paulo pòst mercescunt & flaccescunt, unde dicuntur accipere στέφανον φθαρτὸνv. 25. Sed corona illa coelestis, quae fidelibus Presbyteris à Christo summo agonotheta dabitur, nunquam marcescet, vel flaccescet, vel veterascet, sed virorem & vigorem suum in aeternum retinebit. στὲφανος δόξηςcorona gloriae vocatur, vel phrasi eâ, qualis occurrit Rom. 4. v. 11. ut sit genitivus speciei, percipietis gloriam, quae erit veluti corona; vel ut genitivus ponatur loco adiectivi, percipietis coronam gloriae i. e. valde gloriosam & illustrem. 2. Tim. 4. v. 8. vocatur corona iustitiae.Iac. 1. v. 12.Apocal. 2. v. 10. vocatur corona vitae. Verbum κομεῖσθε Vulgata reddidit percipietis. Graeca propriè habent, reportabitis. uti vertitidem Interpres c. 1. v. 9. Syrus ἐξηγήσεως causa addidit [consult facsimile image]ab eo, quia Christus iustus iudex coronam illam iustitiae, vitae & gloriae fidelibus suis servis imponet. Confer ea, quae superiùs dicta ad v. 4. capitis primi.

## 5:5
LIKEWISE YOU YOUNGER PEOPLE BE SUBJECT TO THE ELDERS.

Connection. 1. After he had commended the faithfulness of the office to the Presbyters or Elders, he prescribes obedience and subjection to the younger ones. Bede in this place: After he taught how the elders should preside, it was fitting that he should also instruct the younger ones to obey their fatherly provision.

2. Just as above in 3, after he had prescribed the rules of life for wives, he also admonishes husbands of their duty, because of the mutual relationship which exists between both: so also in this place he descends from the Presbyters or Elders to the duty of the younger ones.

Exposition. ὁμοίως. The word of likeness requires equal diligence in this age in executing the parts of the office demanded of them, from which it is left to be understood that equal rewards of diligence are also to be expected by them. The Syrian rendered it by a copulative particle. And you younger ones.

Νεώτεροι The Vulgate rendered it younger ones. The Greek properly has Younger ones. By these younger ones, opposed to the Presbyters or Elders, he understands those who are younger in age, since he had previously spoken of Presbyters or Elders, who are such by office, namely, of Bishops and Pastors of the Church. Therefore, he uses the appellation πρεσβυτέρων in a different signification than before, namely, in a somewhat more general signification. You younger ones be subject to the Elders, whether they be such by dignity of office or by age. The word ὑποτάγητε has a reciprocal signification. Subject yourselves to the younger ones, in which way the Syrian also rendered it [consult facsimile image] in the Ethpael from the quadriliteral root [consult facsimile image] which is from the prosthetic [consult facsimile image] and [consult facsimile image] he served. By the name of subjection, the Apostle embraces every kind of subjection and duty which the younger owe to the Elders, namely, that they ought to rise for the Elders, honor them with words, gestures, and the work itself, obey their admonitions and comply with them, yield to them, and thus hold their venerable gray hair in esteem.

Latin:

SIMILITER ADOLESCENTES SUBDITI ESTOTE SENIORIBUS.

Connexio. 1. Postquam Presbyteris sive Senioribus fidelitatem officii commendasset, iunioribus obedientiam & subiectionem praescribit. Beda in h. l. Postquam seniores quomodo praeessent, docuit, oportebat ut etiam iuniores ad obediendum paternae eorum provisioni instrueret.

2. Quemadmodum superiùs in 3. postquam uxoribus vitae regulas praescripserat, etiam viros sui admonet officii, propter mutuam, quae utrisque intercedit relationem: ita etiam hoc loco à Presbyteris sive Senioribus ad iuniorum officium descendit.

Expositio. ὁμοίως. Vox similitudinis parem in hac aetate requirit diligentiam in exequendis officii sibi demandati partibus, ex quo intelligendum relinquitur, paria etiam ipsis expectanda esse diligentiae praemia. Syrus per particulam copulativam reddidit. Et vos iuniores.

Νεώτεροι Vulgata reddidit adolescentes. Graeca propriè habent iuniores. Per hosce iuniores, Presbyteris sive Senioribus oppositos, intelligit eos, qui aetate iuniores sunt, cum priùs de Presbyteris sive Senioribus locutus sit, qui officio tales sunt, videl. de Episcopis & Ecclesiae Pastoribus. Ergò in alia significatione πρεσβυτέρων appellatione utitur quàm priùs, vid. in significatione paulo generaliore. Vos iuniores subditi estote Senioribus, sive officii dignitate sive aetate tales sint. Verbum ὑποτάγητε significationem habet reciprocam. Subiicite vos iunioribus, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit [consult facsimile image] in Ethpael à rad. quad. [consult facsimile image] quae est ex [consult facsimile image] prosthetico & [consult facsimile image]servivit.
