## 5:13
THE CHURCH THAT IS IN BABYLON, ELECT TOGETHER WITH YOU, SALUTETH YOU, AND MARCUS MY SON.

Connection 1. This is the other part of the conclusion, consisting of ἀσπασμοῖς, such as also occur in the Pauline Epistles toward the end of them. Rom. 16. v. 16. All the churches of Christ salute you. v. 21. Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you. ὁ συνεργός μου, 1. Cor. 16. v. 19. The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house. v. 20. All the brethren salute you. 2. Cor. 13. v. 15. All the saints salute you. Phil. 4. v. 21. The brethren which are with me greet you. v. 22. All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household. Col. 4. v. 10. Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus. v. 12. Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you. v. 14. Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you. Compare 2. Tim. 4. v. 21. Tit. 3. v. 15. Philem. v. 23. & 24. Hebr. 13. v. 24. And likewise in the Epistles of John, Epist. 2. v. 13. Epist. 3. v. 15.

2. In those salutations the Apostle at the same time indicates the place where he wrote this Epistle, namely in Babylon.

3. These excellent salutations contain in themselves a consolatory argument to be opposed to persecutions, namely, that they may see their perseverance in faith and salvation is a care to the remaining faithful, and they [commend] them through prayers συναγωνίζεσθαι. For a salutation is nothing other than some pious vow.

4. Bede warns, that therefore mention is made of the Church in Babylon, so that the Apostle may confirm what he had saidvers. 9.knowing that the same sufferings are accomplished in that brotherhood which is in the world. Well, says B, Peter, while he exhorts his hearers to the tolerance of present adversities, says also that the Church, which is established with him in Babylon, that is, in the confusion of tribulations, and yet he confirms that it is gathered, to show that the holy city of God in this life cannot be immune from the intermingling and pressure of the city of the Devil, which Babylon signifies.

5. Iohan. Huss. determines that these salutations were added to the conclusion for this purpose, that through them this Epistle might be rendered more commendable and pleasing.

Disposition. A double salutation is proposed in this verse. The former is general, namely of the whole Church, gathered and assembled in Babylon: the latter is special, namely of Mark, Peter's beloved son.

Exposition of the text. Ἂσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτὴ, The Vulgate rendered it. The Church which is in Babylon, co-elect, saluteth you. The noun ἐκκλησίας is not indeed added αὐτολεξεὶ in the Greek text, meanwhile ἐξηγήσεως is rightly added for the sake of the Latin Vulgate version, as also by the Syriac paraphrast, for it is to be understood concerning the noun συνεκλεκτὴ. For co-elect, some Latin Codices viciously read collected, which although it agrees with the thing itself, for indeed this Church, whose salutation is announced, was gathered and collected in Babylon, yet it does not agree with the Greek text, which has συνεκλεκτὴ, which Jerome in the catalogue of writers under the word Mark renders co-elect, that is, elected together with you. Erasmus rendered it, partner of your election. The Syrian simply rendered it [consult facsimile image] elect, from the root [consult facsimile image] which not only signifies ἐκλέγειν he choseMarc. 13. vers. 20.Luc. 6. v. 13.Act. 1. v. 2. etc. but also συλλέγειν he gathered, Matth. 13.

v. 29.40. & 48. The Apostle seems to look back to that which he had called them, to whom he writes, in cap. 1. huius Epist. v. 1. ἐκλεκτοὺς; because therefore the Babylonian Church was a sharer of the same benefit, thence he calls it συνεκλεκτὴν. For the word ἀσπάζειν the Syrian has the word [consult facsimile image] he sought, he asked, joined with the noun [consult facsimile image] peace, which phrase is peculiar to the Syrians in the meaning of greeting. Matth. 5. v. 47.Marc. 9. v. 15.Rom. 16. v. 3. &c. because in a greeting we are accustomed both to ask our neighbor about his prosperous state, and also to pray for every prosperity for him.

Καὶ Μάρκος ὁ υἱος μου. He makes mention of Mark, because he had him in his company & fellowship at that time with him.

Latin:

SALUTAT VOS ECCLESIA, QUAE EST IN BABYLONE COELECTA, & MARCUS FILIUS MEUS.

Connexio 1. Altera haec est pars conclusionis, constans ἀσπασμοῖς, quales etiam in Paulinis Epistolis sub calcem earum occurrunt. Rom. 16. v. 16.Salutant vos omnes Ecclesiae Christi.v. 21.Salutat vos Timotheusὁ συνεργός μου,& Lucius & Iason & Sosipater cognati mei &c.1. Cor. 16. v. 19.Salutant vos Ecclesiae Asiae, salutant vos in Domino multùm Aquila & Priscilla cum domestica sua Ecclesia.v. 20.Salutant vos omnes fratres.2. Cor. 13. v. 15.Salutant vos omnes sancti.Phil. 4. v. 21.Salutant vos, qui mecum sunt fratres.v. 22.Salutant vos omnes sancti, maximè qui de Caesaris domo sunt.Col. 4. v. 10.Salutat vos Aristarchus &c. & Marcus.v. 12.Salutat vos Epaphrasv. 14.Salutat vos Lucas Medicus carissimus & Demas. Confer. 2. Tim. 4. v. 21.Tit. 3. v. 15.Philem. v. 23. & 24.Hebr. 13. v. 24. Itemque in Epistolis Iohannis Epist. 2. v. 13. Epist. 3. v. 15.

2. In illis salutationibus Apostolus simul indicat locum, ubi hanc Epistolam scripsit, videlicet in Babylone.

3. Praeclarae hae salutationes continent in se argumentum consolatorium persecutionibus opponendum, videl. quod, videant suam in fide perseverantiam & salutem reliquis fidelibus esse curae, ac eosdem per preces ipsis συναγωνίζεσθαι. Salutatio enim nihil aliud est, quàm pium aliquod votum.

4. Beda monet, ideò mentionem fieri Ecclesiae in Babylone, ut confirmet Apostolus, quod dixeratvers. 9.scientes, easdem passiones ei, quae in mundo est, fraternitati perfici. Bene, inquit, B, Petrus, dum suos auditores ad tolerantiam hortatur adversitatum praesentium, dicit & Ecclesiam, quaesecum est in Babylone constitutam, id est, in confusione tribulationum, & tamen collectam eam esse confirmat, ut ostendat, sanctam Dei civitatem in hac vita à permixtione & pressura civitatis Diaboli, quam Babylonia signat, immunem esse non posse.

5. Iohan. Huss. salutationes hasce eo fine in conclusione adiectas statuit, ut per eas haec Epistolamagis commendabilis & grataredderetur.

Dispositio. Duplex salutatio in hoc versiculo proponitur. Prior est generalis, videlicet totius Ecclesiae, in Babylone collectae & congregatae: Posterior specialis, videlicet Marci dilecti petri filii.

Textus expositio. Ἂσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτὴ, Vulgata reddidit. Salutat vos Ecclesia, quae est in Babylone coëlecta. Nomenἐκκλησίας non quidem additur αὐτολεξεὶ in textu Graeco, interim ἐξηγήσεως causâ rectè additur à vulgata versione Latina, ut & paraphraste Syro, subintelligendum enim circa nomen συνεκλεκτὴ. Pro coelecta quidam Latini Codices vitiosè legunt collecta, quod quamvis rei ipsi congruat, verè enim haec Ecclesia, cuius salutatio nunciatur, erat in Babylone congregata & collecta, non tamen congruit textui Graeco, qui habent συνεκλεκτὴ, quod Hieronymus in catalogo scriptorum in verbo Marcus reddit conelecta, id est, un à vobiscum electa. Erasmus reddidit, vestrae electionis consors. Syrus simpliciter reddidit [consult facsimile image]electa, à rad.[consult facsimile image] quae non solùm significat ἐκλέγεινelegitMarc. 13. vers. 20.Luc. 6. v. 13.Act. 1. v. 2. &c. sed etiam συλλέγεινcollegit, Matth. 13.

v. 29.40. & 48. Videtur Apostolus respicere adid, quod in cap. 1. huius Epist. v. 1. eos, ad quos scribit, vocaverat ἐκλεκτοὺς; quia ergò Ecclesia Babylonica eiusdem beneficii erat consors, inde eam vocat συνεκλεκτὴν. Pro verbo ἀσπάζειν Syrus habet verbum [consult facsimile image]petiit, interrogavit, coniunctum cum nomine [consult facsimile image]pax, quae phrasis Syris peculiaris est in significatione salutandi. Matth. 5. v. 47.Marc. 9. v. 15.Rom. 16. v. 3. &c. quia in salutatione tùm de statu prospero solemus proximum interrogare, tùm etiam omnem prosperitatem ei precari.

Καὶ Μάρκος ὁ υἱος μου. Marci ideò mentionem facit, quia eum in comitatu & consortio tùm temporis secum habuit.

## 5:14
GREET ONE ANOTHER WITH A HOLY KISS. GRACE BE TO YOU ALL, WHO ARE IN CHRIST JESUS. AMEN.

Connection. 1. This is the third part of the conclusion, namely προτροπὴ an exhortation to a holy kiss, as also the fourth, namely εὐχὴ an Apostolic vow.

2. The exhortation to a holy kiss is found joined in the same place in the clauses of certain Pauline Epistles. Rom. 16. v. 16.Greet one another with a holy kiss. Compare 1. Cor. 16. v. 20.2. Cor. 13. v. 12.1. Thess. 5. v. 26. &c.

3. That symbol of mutual love & benevolence was customary to Oriental peoples, namely the holy kiss, it was a confirmation of the greeting.

4. It was solemn for all the Apostles to conclude an Epistle with a pious vow. Rom. 16. v. 24.2. Thess. 3. vers 18.The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.1. Cor. 16. v. 23.The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.2. Cor. 13. v. 13.The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.Gal. 6. v. 18.The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.Eph, 6. vers. 23.Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.vers. 24.Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ in sincerity and incorruptness.

Amen.Philip. 4. v. 23.Philem. v. 25.The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, Amen.Coloss. 4. v. 18.2. Timoth. 4. v. 22.Grace be with you, Amen.1. Thess. 5. v. 28.The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you, Amen.Tit. 3. v. 15.Hebr. 13. vers. 25.Grace be with you all, Amen.Iohannes Epist. 3. v. 15. uses this formula. Peace be to thee. These variations can usefully admonish one of many things.

Disposition. There are two parts of the verse. 1. προτροπὴ to the holy kiss. 2. εὐχὴ the Apostolic vow.

Exposition of the text. Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἀγάπης. The Vulgate rendered it: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The Royal codex reads likewise ἐν Φιλήματι ἁγίῳ, and the Syriac rendered it in the same way [consult facsimile image] [consult facsimile image] with a holy kiss, which without doubt was taken from parallel passages Rom. 16. v. 16.1. Corinth. 16. v. 20.2. Corinth. 13. v. 12.1. Thessal. 5. v. 26. in all of which is read ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ. But the more approved and more numerous Greek codices read ἐν φιλήματι ἁγάπης, with a kiss of charity, although between a kiss of Christian charity and a holy kiss there is in reality no difference. It was the custom of Eastern peoples that they should salute one another with mutual kisses. The Persians did this especially, as did also the Hebrews, from whom this custom flowed down to the Christians, for the first Christians were Hebrews. Peter calls that kiss the kiss of love, because it was accustomed to be used for the attestation of it. Paul calls it a holy kiss for the difference from a worldly and carnal kiss. In turn, Peter calls it the kiss of love, because it ought not to be hypocritical, but to have proceeded from a pious, honest, candid mind, and from a breast full of sincere love. Paul calls it a holy kiss, because it ought not to savor of carnal affections, nor of Venus-like sweetnesses, but of the Holy Spirit of God, the author of all holiness and Christian charity. εἰρήνη ὑμῖν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν χριστῷ Ιησοῦ, Ἀμὴν. The Vulgate rendered it: Grace be to you all that are in Christ Jesus. But in the Greek it is, Peace be to you all, in which way the Syriac also rendered it, which formula of saluting, customary to the Hebrews, was transferred by the Apostles into their Epistles, and placed either at the beginning or at the end of the Epistles. Most frequently, however, they join χάριν καὶ εἰρήνην Roman. 1. vers. 7. 1. Corinth. 1.

ver. 3.2. Cor. 1. ver. 2.Eph. 1. ver. 2.Phil. 1. ver. 1.Col. 1. ver. 21. Thess. 1. ver. 1.2. Thess. 1. ver. 2.Philem. ver. 3.1. Pet. 1. ver. 2.2. Pet. 1. ver. 2.Rev. 1. ver. 4. where by χάριν is understood reconciliation with God, by εἰρήνην peace of conscience, flowing forth from that reconciliation. Sometimes χάρις, ἔλεος καὶ εἰρήνη are joined 1. Tim. 1. ver. 2. 2.Tim. 1. ver. 2.Tit. 1. ver. 4.2. John ver. 3. where by τὸ ἔλεος of the one remitting, by χάριν the grace of God, conferring benefits of every kind of spiritual nature, by εἰρήνην the tranquility of conscience, drawing its origin from that grace and mercy, is signified. Sometimes it is said absolutely and simply, εἰρήνη ὑμῖν. Eph. 6. v. 23. 3. John v. 15. which formula is taken from the salutation used by Christ in the days of his flesh, especially after the resurrection. Luke 24. v. 36.John 20. v. 19.21. & 26. where by the name of peace, through a Hebraism, all kinds of goods are understood, among which stands out peace with GOD, and peace with one's own heart. But the word πληθυνθειῃ must be supplied from chap. 1. v. 2. and from the Epistle of Jude ver. 2. peace be multiplied to you.

Luther, in the German version, rendered the words τοῖς ἐν χριστῷ Ιησοῦ placed absolutely in the third person. But because the pronoun of the second person ὑμῖν, precedes, therefore the Vulgate more correctly rendered it in the second person. Peace to you all, who are in Christ Jesus, namely, united to him by true faith and living members of his mystical body. Interlinear Gloss: to all the Churches throughout the world. The Syrian, through a certain correction as it were, rendered it: Peace to you all, to those (I say) who are in Christ. Carthusian: You who are united through faith and charity. But in the Greek, no mention of charity is made.

Latin:

SALUTATE INVICEM OSCULO SANCTO. GRATIA VOBIS OMNIBUS, QUI ESTIS IN CHRISTO IESU. AMEN.

Connexio. 1. Tertia haec est conclusionis pars, videl. προτροπὴ exhortatio ad osculum sanctum, ut & quarta videl. εὐχὴ votum Apostolicum.

2. Exhortatio ad osculum sanctum ibidem in clausulis quarundam Epistolarum Paulinarum subiunctum invenitur. Rom. 16. v. 16.Salutate invicem in osculo sancto. Confer. 1. Cor. 16. v. 20.2. Cor. 13. v. 12.1. Thess. 5. v. 26. &c.

3. Symbolum illud mutuae caritatis & benevolentiae Orientalibus populis usitatum, osculum sc. sanctum, fuit, confirmatio salutationis.

4. Pio voto Epistolam concludere solenne fuit omnibus Apostolis. Rom. 16. v. 24.2. Thess. 3. vers 18.Gratia Domininostri Iesu Christi cum omnibus vobis. Amen.1. Cor. 16. v. 23.Gratia Domini Iesu Christi vobiscum.2. Cor. 13. v. 13.Gratia Domini Iesu Christi, & caritas Dei & communicatio Spiritus sancti sit cum omnibus vobis. Amen.Gal. 6. v. 18.Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi cum Spiritu vestro fratres. Amen.Eph, 6. vers. 23.Pax fratribus & caritas cum fide à Deo Patre & Domino Iesu Christo.vers. 24.Gratia cum omnibus, qui diligunt Dominum nostrum Iesum Christumἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳsincerè & incorruptè.

Amen.Philip. 4. v. 23.Philem. v. 25.Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi cum Spiritu vestro, Amen.Coloss. 4. v. 18.2. Timoth. 4. v. 22.Gratia vobiscum, Amen.1. Thess. 5. v. 28.Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christ vobiscum, Amen.Tit. 3. v. 15.Hebr. 13. vers. 25.Gratia cum omnibus vobis, Amen.Iohannes Epist. 3. v. 15. hac formula utitur. Pax tibi. Hae variationes de multis utiliter admonere possunt.

Dispositio. Partes versiculi duae sunt. 1. προτροπὴ ad osculum sanctum. 2. εὐχὴ votum Apostolicum.

Textus expositio. Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἀγάπης. Vulgata reddidit. Salutate invicem in osculo santo. Regius codex itidem legit ἐν Φιλήματι ἁγίῳ, ac Syrus eodem modo reddidit [consult facsimile image][consult facsimile image]in osculo sancto, quod dubio procul desumtum ex locis parallelis Rom. 16. v. 16.1. Corinth. 16. v. 20.2. Corinth. 13. v. 12.1. Thessal. 5. v. 26. in quibus omnibuslegitur ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ. Sed probatiores & plures Codices Graecilegunt, ἐν φιλήματι ἁγάπης,in osculo caritatis, quamvis inter osculum caritatis Christianae & osculum sanctum reipsâ nihil sit discriminis. Orientalium populorum consvetudo erat, ut se invicem mutuis osculis salutarent. Id inprimis faciebant Persae, uti etiam Hebraei, à quibus hic mos promanavit ad Christianos, nam primi Christiani erant Hebraei. Osculum illud Petrus vocat osculum dilectionis, quia ad eius contestationem adhiberi solebat. Paulus vocat osculum sanctum ad differentiam osculi mundani & carnalis. Vicissim Petrus vocat osculum dilectionis, quia non debeat esse hypocriticum, sed ab animo pio, honesto, candido, & ex pectore sinceri amoris pleno profectum. Paulus vocat osculum sanctum, quia non debeat sapere carnales affectus, nec suavia Venerea, sed Spiritum Deisanctum, omnis sanctitatis & Christianae caritatis autorem. εἰρήνη ὑμῖν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν χριστῷ Ιησοῦ, Ἀμὴν. Vulg. reddidit. Gratia vobis omnibus, qui estis in Christo Iesu. Sed in Graeco est, Pax omnibus vobis, quo modo etiam Syrus reddidit, quae salurandi formula Hebraeis nsitata ab Apostolis in Epistolas ipsorum fuit translata, ac vel in principio vel calce Epistolarum collocata. Frequentissimè tamen χάριν καὶ εἰρήνην coniungunt Roman. 1. vers. 7. 1. Corinth. 1.

vers. 3.2. Corinth. 1. vers. 2.Eph. 1. vers. 2.Philip. 1. vers. 1.Coloss. 1. vers. 21. Thessal. 1. vers. 1.2. Thessal. 1. vers. 2.Philem. vers. 3.1. Petr. 1. vers. 2.2. petr. 1. vers. 2.Apoc. 1. vers. 4. ubi per χάριν intelligitur reconciliatio cum Deo, per εἰρήνην pax conscientiae, ex reconciliatione illa promanans. Quandoque coniunguntur χάρις, ἔλεος καὶ εἰρήνη1. Timoth 1. vers. 2. 2.Timoth. 1. vers. 2.Tit. 1. vers. 4.2. Iohan. vers. 3. ubi per τὸ ἔλεος λremittentis, per χάριν gratia Dei, omnis generis beneficia spiritualia conferentis, per εἰρήνην tranquillitas conscientiae, ex illa gratia & mifericordia originem trahens, significatur. Quandoque absolutè & simpliciter dicitur, εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.Ephes. 6. v. 23. 3. Ioh. v. 15. quae formula petita est ex salutatione Christo in diebus carnis suae, praesertim post resurrectionem usitata. Luc. 24. v. 36.Iohan. 20. v. 19.21. & 26. ubi pacis nomine per Hebraismum omnis generis bona, inter quae eminet pax cum DEO, & pax cum corde proprio intelliguntur. Supplendum vero ex cap. 1. v. 2. & ex Epist. Iudae vers. 2. verbum πληθυνθειῃpax vobis multiplicetur.

Verba τοῖς ἐν χριστῷ Ιησοῦ absolutè posita Lutherus in vers. German, reddidit in tertia persona. Sed quia praecedit pronomen secundae personae ὑμῖν, ideò vulgata rectiùs in secunda persona reddidit. Pax vobis omnibus, qui estis in Christo Iesu, videlicet verâ fide ipsi uniti & viva corporis eius mystici membra. Gloss. interl. omnibus per orbem terrarum Ecclesiis. Syrus per quandam quasi correctionem reddidit. Pax vobis omnibus, iis (inquam) qui sunt in Christo. Carthus. Qui per fidem & caritatem uniti estis. Sed in Graeco non fit caritatis mentio.
